project_description: The investment comprises (i) an A loan up to US$40 million and (ii) a B1 loan up to US$60 million to Agricola Alvorada S.A. (Alvorada), an agribusiness group in Mato Grosso, Brazil, engaged in warehousing, grain trading, logistics and agro-input retail. Proceeds will fund traceable grain sourcing, partially a corn ethanol plant, drying automation, and eucalyptus plantations supplying biomass to warehouses and the plant.
sponsor_shareholders: Jarbas Weiss is the controlling shareholder of Alvorada and Bunge is a minority shareholder, having entered the partnership in 2017.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of (i) an IFC A loan up to US$40 million and a (ii) B Loan up to US$60 million.
location_description: The Project will be developed in Mato Grosso, Brazil.
development_impact: The Project supports Alvorada’s expansion of grain storage capacity, traceable sourcing, and working capital through its input-for-grains barter model, strengthening farmers’ access to markets and financing in Mato Grosso, Brazil. Storage capacity will increase , helping address regional bottlenecks, while the farmer base expands and benefits from both financing and technical assistance via the Company’s in-house agronomy team. The Project contributes to food security, economic growth, and job creation through increased grain commercialization, corn ethanol production, and biomass initiatives, while delivering environmental benefits from greater energy efficiency and reduced emissions. The Project also supports innovation and competitiveness in Brazil’s corn ethanol sector.
additionality: IFC will provide both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality includes (i) long term financing, and (ii) resource mobilization (PCM). Non-financial additionality encompasses: (i) Standard setting: IFC will support the Company in aligning its environmental and social practices with IFC’s Performance Standards and (ii) Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC’s upstream/advisory team will train suppliers and technical assistants on regenerative agriculture, including conversion of degraded land and improved livestock intensification, and will promote the use of DDG (a corn-ethanol byproduct) to enhance resource efficiency.

project_description: The proposed project entails the financing of a greenfield, world-scale ammonia and granular urea complex in Argentina, with an installed capacity of approximately 2.1 million tons per annum (tpa) of granular urea (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Fertil Pampa S.A.U. (the Project Company) is a special purpose vehicle wholly owned by Pampa Energia S.A. (Pampa or the Sponsor), a leading integrated energy company in Argentina and one of the country's largest natural gas producers and power generators, with active participation in the oil and gas and electricity value chains. Pampa is publicly traded on the Buenos Aires and New York Stock Exchanges.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost stands at approximately US$3.2 billion. The IFC financing package of up to US$850 million includes: (i) an IFC A Loan of up to US$300 million, and (ii) an IFC B Loan / Parallel Loan of up to US$550 million.
location_description: The Project is located in Argentina, in the Ingeniero White industrial area of BahBlanca, Province of Buenos Aires, within an established petrochemical corridor and Pampa's integrated industrial platform, adjacent to existing Pampa Energia assets, with proximity to gas pipelines, high-voltage transmission, seawater intake infrastructure and the deep-water export port of Ingeniero White.
development_impact: The most important, expected development outcome of the Project is increasing the regional supply of fertilizers, achieving an annual production capacity of up to 2.1 million tons. IFC anticipates that this expanded output will benefit up to 270,000 farmers across Brazil and Argentina. Beyond the Project itself, IFC expects the intervention to increase competitiveness in the agricultural input market due to demonstration and replication effects and supply-chain complementarities between agricultural production and agricultural inputs, as well as supporting resilience in a critical context by generating net foreign revenues and helping support the Argentina’s external position.
additionality: IFC will provide both financial and non-financial value. On the financial side, IFC will provide long-term hard currency financing with a tenor beyond what the Project Company can currently secure from local and international commercial banks; IFC will further mobilize third-party capital through its B Loan and coordination with IDB Invest. From a non-financial perspective, IFC will act as Mandated Lead Arranger, structuring a bankable project finance package for the Project. The Project will benefit from IFC's standard-setting role in developing the Project's environmental, health and safety practices in line with international best practice and the IFC Performance Standards.

project_description: IFC proposes a €140 million debt package to Balfin Group, an existing IFC client. This investment will support: (i) entry into Ukraine and the South Caucasus region with Balfin's retail business; and (ii) tourism development in Albania. The debt package will be structured as secured loans, expected to be committed in three separate phases over the next three years: (i) up to €57mn to finance the energy efficient expansion of TEG; (ii) up to €50mn for capex and working capital of retail expansion outside Albania, including in Ukraine and Southern Caucasus; and (iii) up to €33mn for tourism development through a hotel in the city of Vlora.
sponsor_shareholders: Balfin is a leading diversified conglomerate based in Albania with operations in the Western Balkans, Austria, and, more recently, North America. Established in 1993, it is fully owned by Mr. Samir Mane. Balfin owns 97% of TEG with the remaining shares held by First Investment Services (3%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total needs for the Project are estimated at about €400 million.
location_description: Albania, Ukraine, and the Caucasus.
development_impact: The Project’s most significant expected development outcome is its economy-wide effect through job creation, formalization, and the strengthening of local supply chains. By supporting the expansion of modern retail and tourism, the Project is expected to generate broader spillover effects through increased demand for local goods and services, higher operational standards, workforce skills development, and improved productivity across the value chain. Beyond these outcomes, IFC expects the Project to enhance competitiveness by demonstrating the commercial viability of higher-value tourism, modern retail formats, and resource-efficient buildings. The Project is expected to support Albania’s transition toward more sustainable, year-round tourism while serving as a demonstration effect for sustainable private investment in the region.
additionality: IFC will provide financial additionality through long-term financing and mobilization, enabling investments with extended development. Non-financial additionality will include support for the enhancement of environmental and social standards. IFC has provided advisory support to Balfin on EDGE Advanced certification, promoting resource-efficient building design and helping establish a benchmark for sustainable tourism development in Albania.

project_description: IFC proposes an up to US$30 million Sustainability-Linked Loan (SLL) to Liberian American Poultry (LAP) and Modern Mills of Liberia (MML), collectively referred to as the Companies. The investment will support capacity expansion and provide working capital for both companies. Specifically, MML will double its flour milling capacity to 300 tonnes per day, while LAP will increase its table egg production from 750 to 1,500 cartons per day.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 2018, MML is a leading flour mill in Liberia. In addition to flour milling, the company produces animal feed, which is primarily supplied to its sister company, LAP, as part of an integrated feed-to-egg business model. LAP is Liberia's leading table egg producer. MML and LAP are majority-owned (51%) by West African Premier Investment LLC (WAPI), an investment fund of the Siblani family. Mr. Henri Chaoul holds a 24% stake in MML and a 19% stake in LAP, with the remaining shares held by other minority investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost of US$42.5 million includes US$27.8 million in CAPEX (US$12.0 million for MML and US$15.8 million for LAP) and US$14.7 million in working capital for both companies. The project will be financed through a US$30 million IFC loan and US$12.5 million of Sponsor equity contributions.
location_description: Both companies are located in Liberia. MML is situated near the Freeport of Monrovia, while LAP is located in Bomi County, in the north-western part of the country.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is the impact on stakeholders — specifically, improved food security for consumers through the local production and broad distribution of quality, safe, and affordable wheat flour and poultry products. Beyond these direct project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will foster greater competitiveness in the poultry market through demonstration effects and replication by other market participants.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC is providing financing on terms not otherwise available in the local market, complemented by IDA PSW BFF that add value by better addressing risks, and eventually lowering the cost of capital for the Project. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC, through advisory services, will provide expertise, innovation, knowledge to improve operational efficiency of the Companies and align its operations with industry best practices

project_description: IFC investment consists of an equity investment in the form of common shares of an aggregate amount of up to INR 1,420 million (equivalent to approximately US$15.0 million), including as an anchor investor in Milky Mist’s initial public offering (IPO). IPO proceeds are expected to support expansion and modernization of the Company’s manufacturing facility in Tamil Nadu, purchase of visi-coolers, chocolate coolers and ice-cream freezers, repayment or pre-payment of the Company’s existing borrowings, and general corporate purposes (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Milky Mist is sponsored by Mr. Sathishkumar T, and Ms. Anitha S. Pre-IPO, the Sponsor Group holds 93.0%, Temasek holds 5.2%, and other investors hold the remaining 1.8% of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will invest via a subscription to common shares in Milky Mist’s IPO, including as an anchor investor. The IPO is expected to raise approximately INR 15,530 million, equivalent to US$164.0 million. IFC will invest an aggregate amount of up to INR 1,420 million (equivalent to approximately US$15.0 million) in the IPO.
location_description: The Project is located in Perundurai, in the state of Tamil Nadu of India.
development_impact: The Project is expected to: (i) improve access to nutritious value-added dairy products for Indian consumers, particularly base-of-the-pyramid populations; (ii) strengthen livelihoods of smallholder dairy farmers through increased milk procurement, improved market access, and continued technical support; (iii) generate economy-wide benefits through job creation and investments in dairy processing, logistics, procurement, and distribution infrastructure; and (iv) enhance competitiveness in India’s value-added dairy sector by expanding domestic production of higher-value dairy ingredients, supporting import substitution, innovation, and broader sector development.
additionality: The Project is expected to: (i) provide growth capital to support Milky Mist’s expansion in value-added dairy products, cold-chain infrastructure, and nationwide distribution without increasing leverage; (ii) catalyze additional private capital and support successful IPO execution through IFC’s role as an anchor investor, strengthening investor confidence and market liquidity; and (iii) enhance the Company’s environmental and social management systems, supplier management practices, grievance mechanisms, and implementation of GBVH and child safeguarding measures aligned with IFC Performance Standards and international good practices.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment package of up to US$42 million is to support BB Energy Group Holding Ltd. (“BB Energy” or the “Group” or the “Sponsor”), a leading global independent energy trading company, in implementing its US$64 million Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) expansion program across the DRC, South Africa, and Zambia (the “Project”). In the DRC, BB Energy will develop a greenfield LPG import terminal in Boma, a filling plant in Kinshasa, and associated distribution infrastructure to promote clean cooking. In South Africa, BB Energy will acquire an ownership stake in an LPG bulk distributor and expand its operations through investments in storage and distribution capacity. In Zambia, BB Energy has acquired the LPG assets of a leading LPG distributor in Lusaka and grow through investments in storage and distribution infrastructure.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1963, BB Energy is a family-owned enterprise that is owned, controlled and managed by members of the Bassatne family. The Group is executing the Project through Deux Rivieres Holding (DRH), its sub-holding company for the LPG expansion. DRH is wholly owned by BB Energy Downstream Ltd (BBED), a key subsidiary of BB Energy, focused on the petroleum downstream sector.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project cost is estimated at US$64 million and will be financed by US$21 million equity from the Sponsor equity, while the balance of funding will be from the proposed IFC investment package. The proposed IFC financing package consists of an IFC A loan of US$30.15 million, an IDA Private Sector Window (PSW) subordinated loan of US$11.03 million loan and an equity investment in DRC of US$1 million.
location_description: The Project is located across three countries: the Democratic Republic of Congo, South Africa and Zambia. In the DRC, the Project will be located in Boma along the Congo River, and Kinshasa. In Zambia, the Project will be situated in Lusaka. In South Africa, the Project will be located in the Gauteng province.
development_impact: The most significant project-level outcomes include improved access to cleaner cooking fuel alternatives, as well as the generation of economy-wide value added and employment. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the potential for this project to promote greater competitiveness through expanded private sector participation and the entry of a multinational LPG company into markets with very limited supply of LPG.
additionality: IFC’s involvement with the support of IDA PSW LCF is expected to contribute both financially and non-financially. Financial additionality is delivered through the provision of extended-tenor funding that remains largely unavailable in the domestic banking sector. Non-financial additionality comprises risk mitigation via the equity stake in DRC project, knowledge, innovation, capacity building, and standard-setting, including guidance to strengthen the Company’s capacity to manage E&S risks.

sector: Other Vegetable Oil Crops (Coconut, Rapeseed, Peanut, Sunflower, etc.)
project_description: The Project targets agri feedstock produced regionally in the Republic of Congo (Congo), Mozambique and Angola from crops grown on severely degraded land and intermediate crops in rotation with food crops, certified under EU Renewable Energy Directive (EU-RED III) standards. Production is carried out by aggregators working with local farmers and commercial farmers on their own land. Feedstock is processed in oil extraction plants (Agri Hubs), by Eni Natural Energies S.p.A. (Ene), a subsidiary of Eni S.p.A. (Eni), the Italian integrated energy company operating across the energy value chain in 62 countries with over 32,000 employees. Ene is responsible for producing vegetable oil for shipment to biorefineries of Eni in Italy. Extraction by-products from the feedstock are sold to animal feed and fertilizer market. To meet EU sustainability requirements, Eni’s biofuel supply chains are certified under ISCC-EU and the Italian National Scheme (INS).
sponsor_shareholders: Ene is wholly owned by Eni - an integrated energy company operating across the energy value chain in 62 countries with over 32,000 employees. It has significant exploration and production activities in conventional oil and gas, markets gas and liquefied natural gas (LNG), and is expanding into new energies and decarbonisation services, including solar and wind power, biofuels, biochemistry, Carbon Dioxide (CO2) capture and sequestration, and research into new energy paradigms such as magnetic fusion and chemical recycling of plastics. In 2020, Eni developed a decarbonization strategy https://www.eni.com/en-IT/sustainability/decarbonization.html and an action plan to reach net zero Scope I and II GHG emissions by 2035 and Scope III emissions by 2050. It also aims for decarbonized gas to represent at least 90% of total production beyond 2040.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Project Cost: US$400 million. The proposed IFC investment is a corporate loan of up to US$250 million for IFC’s own account, plus up to US$150 million mobilized from other parties. Beneficiaries: ENI Natural Energies S.p.A. Sucursal em Angola; ENI Natural Energies Congo S.A.U.; ENI Natural Energies Mozambico S.r.L Use of Proceeds: Financing proceeds will support general corporate purposes in Angola, Mozambique and Congo, including: (i) construction and operation of agro-processing hubs and related logistics to collect and process oilseeds into oil and cake, including through third-party hubs; (ii) tolling fees; (iii) agri-equipment purchases, including mechanization components and agri-inputs, for use by farmers and aggregators; (iv) working capital to source oilseeds from local farmers, aggregators and intermediaries and (vi) other related financing needs agreed by the parties, provided they align with the Paris Climate Agreement objectives.
location_description: ENE Congo’s agri-hub is located in Loudima. The proposed location for ENE Mozambico’s agri-hub is Namialo. ENE Angola currently does not have a planned agri-hub.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are benefits to farmers and increased value added and jobs in Angola, Mozambique, and the Republic of Congo. Beyond direct project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater market competitiveness primarily via demonstration and replication channels, showcasing viable models for establishing certified biofuel feedstock supply chains in underdeveloped markets.
additionality: (i) Financing Structure: IFC will provide up to $250 million long-term loans whose size and duration are unavailable in the investment market for agribusiness companies. The financing is expected to strengthen the Project’s financial soundness, creditworthiness, and governance. (ii) Resource Mobilization: IFC is expected to play a catalytic role in mobilizing up to US$150 million Parallel Loan. (iii) Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC and Eni will promote best agricultural practices through advisory support and a multi-country food security study.

project_description: The proposed Project is an equity investment of up to US$25 million in Jumia Technologies AG (“Jumia” or the “Company”), Africa’s leading e-commerce platform and the first African technology company to list on a major global exchange, namely the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). The proposed project aims at accelerating Jumia’s growth across its core markets.
sponsor_shareholders: Jumia is a publicly traded company, with the majority of its shares held by retail investors, with several institutional investors holding each less than 10 percent of Jumia’s shares. The Company is currently led by Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Francis Dufay and Executive Vice President (EVP) of Finance and Operations Antoine Maillet-Mezeray, supported by an executive team spanning finance, operations, technology, and commercial functions, as well as country CEOs across its key African markets.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project is an equity investment of up to US$25 million.
location_description: Cote d'Ivoire, Africa Region
development_impact: IFC anticipates that the Project will preserve and expand access to markets for businesses, of which a significant share are MSMEs, and consumers across its core African markets, while strengthening the resilience of the e-commerce ecosystem within the region. By supporting Jumia's path to profitability, IFC helps sustain the presence of Africa's leading e-commerce platform and demonstrates a commercially viable business model for the sector. The Project is expected to drive improved sales opportunities for merchants and greater product availability for consumers, while also expanding micro-entrepreneurship opportunities for independent workers, including J-Force agents, drivers, and pickup point operators, thereby contributing to more inclusive economic participation in markets characterized by high rates of informal employment.
additionality: IFC financial additionality centers around providing primary capital to the Company as the sole anchor investor in the private placement for sustaining its platform efficiencies and path to profitability. Non-financial additionality involves providing targeted expertise around impactful strategic initiatives like vendor financing, warehouse solarization, fleet electrification and broader market enablement program for women entrepreneurs, J-Force agents and gender vendor education. Moreover, IFC will work with the Company to implement E&S improvements to align Jumia’s operations with IFC’s Performance Standards through a detailed E&S Action Plan (ESAP).

company_name: HIWA RAUF FOR INVESTMENT AND DEVELOPMENT
project_description: Hiwa Rauf for Investment and Development Ltd. (HRID or the “Company”) is a real estate development company established in 2012 in Iraq. HRID is planning to establish an EDGE-certified mixed-use real estate project in Slemani, Iraq comprising residential towers, a mall, a commercial building, a hotel, and a performance center (the “Project”). The Project is expected to be supported by the Concessional Capital Window for non-IDA FCS countries (CCW-FCS) as described in the Blended Finance Section. It will be developed over two phases where IFC financing will initially be directed towards the first phase with potential subsequent financing to follow later.
sponsor_shareholders: HRID is fully owned by Mr. Hiwa Rauf.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed financing package includes a senior loan from its own account of up to US$20 million, potential syndication of up to US$20 million, and is expected to be supported by the Concessional Capital Window for non-IDA FCS countries (CCW-FCS) with a subordinated loan of up to US$25 million (the “Loans”). The Loans will be used to partially finance the cost of the Project’s first phase of US$177 million and will have a tenor of 9 years with a sculpted repayment profile.
location_description: The Project will be development in Slemani, Iraq.
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase access to high-quality mixed-use commercial property and housing, while generating environmental benefits through reductions in energy and water consumption as well as GHG emissions. By expanding the supply of modern, resource-efficient real estate assets, the Project is expected to support improved urban infrastructure and contribute to more sustainable urban development. In addition, the Project is expected to enhance market competitiveness by supporting the growth of a leading real estate developer, encouraging other market participants to enter and expand, and promoting higher sustainability standards across the real estate sector.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to provide both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality includes the provision of a long-term financing structure that is not readily available in the local market, as well as resource mobilization through B1/parallel loans to support the Company’s growth and funding needs. On the non-financial side, IFC will support the strengthening of the Company’s environmental and social management systems. IFC’s involvement is also expected to contribute knowledge, innovation, capacity building, and support in EDGE certification.
Company Name: HIWA RAUF FOR INVESTMENT AND DEVELOPMENT

project_description: The proposed IFC investment aims to support Dorado Free Zone Company (UAE), a leading cashew processor with operations in Cote d'Ivoire, in expanding its processing capacity through the development of a new 50,000 MT p.a. cashew processing plant in Yamoussoukro, Cote d'Ivoire.
sponsor_shareholders: Dorado FZCO is a UAE-incorporated holding company, owned 90% by Mr. Venkatesan Rajkumar (founder and Chairman) and 10% by Mr. Vigneshwar Rajkumar (Managing Director). The Project Company, Bluejay Nuts SARL (Cote d'Ivoire), is a wholly owned subsidiary of Dorado FZCO.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$18 million, comprising a US$15 million IFC corporate loan and US$3 million in sponsor equity.
location_description: The new plant will be built in Yamoussoukro, Cote d'Ivoire.
development_impact: The Project will expand cashew processing in Cote d’Ivoire, strengthening smallholder market access, job creation, and domestic value addition. Local processing currently accounts for about 40% of total production, with the majority exported as raw cashew nuts; the investment will increase this share through modern, mechanized and vertically integrated operations. Dorado’s scale, market leadership, and deployment of scalable innovations are expected to catalyze sector-wide replication and product diversification.
additionality: IFC will provide long term financing on terms that are otherwise not available for agribusinesses in Cote d'Ivoire. IFC will also provide expertise, innovation, knowledge to align its operations with industry best practices with greater emphasis on corporate governance and cashew sector supply chain management.

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: IFC will support the investment program of KONCAR d.d. (KONCAR or the Group, together with its subsidiaries), which includes investments in new production capacity for critical grid equipment, logistics infrastructure, energy efficiency, research and development capabilities, and other initiatives that support the Group’s growth (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Zagreb, Croatia, KONCAR is a leading South-East European industrial and engineering group that designs, manufactures, and services equipment for critical energy and transport infrastructure. KONCAR is listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange. Its shareholder base consists predominantly of local institutional investors, including pension funds and insurance companies, with no single controlling shareholder.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s financing is an up to €120 million A Loan. Total Project cost is estimated at €370 million.
location_description: All investments under the Project are planned to be made in Croatia.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to expand access to critical grid infrastructure, create quality engineering and manufacturing jobs, and support workforce upskilling and industrial development in Croatia. Beyond the Project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater resilience, competitiveness, and sustainability in the European electrical equipment sector through demonstration effects and strengthened regional supply chains.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided through long-term financing and mobilization of private capital. Non-financial additionality is provided through enhanced environmental and social standards and potential workforce advisory support.

project_description: IFC is considering an investment package of up to ZAR300 million (~US$18 million) in a special purpose vehicle (“Pula SPV”), managed by Live Easy Property Management (Pty) Ltd (“Live Easy” or “the Company”), a South African property development and management company specializing in affordable urban rental housing (the “Project”). The Company’s offering is based on a “nano-unit” concept — compact, self-contained apartments with a kitchenette and bathroom. Live Easy’s model involves acquisition of underutilized or distressed office buildings and converting them into residential rental assets, typically complemented by amenities such as laundromats, gyms, common areas, and Wi-Fi. To date, Live Easy has delivered 5,516 nano units and has additional units currently under development. These projects have been financed through a series of standalone SPVs backed by South African institutional investors, with Live Easy serving as investment and property manager, whilst its parent company, Twentyfive 15 (Pty) Ltd (“Twentyfive”), provides development management services. Proceeds will be used by the Pula SPV to acquire and refurbish/convert properties into additional affordable nano rental units and to fund related project costs, targeting low- and middle-income households primarily in Johannesburg and Pretoria.
sponsor_shareholders: Live Easy is a wholly owned subsidiary of Twentyfive, which is owned 60% by Mr. Jeffrey Froom and 40% by Mr. James Huff (together, the “Sponsors”) through their respective family trust vehicles. The shareholders of the Project company (the Pula SPV) are expected to include Twentyfive (4.5%), Kagiso Capital (24%)—an existing institutional investor in a prior SPV—IFC (up to 20%), and other institutional investors (51.5%). These shareholdings are indicative, as fundraising for the Pula SPV is ongoing; however, IFC’s common equity participation will be capped at 20%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at ZAR3.2 billion (~US$194 million) and will be financed through a combination of equity, quasi-equity and debt. IFC’s proposed financing package will comprise (i) a quasi-equity investment via a ZAR175 million preference note (~US$11 million) and (ii) an equity investment of ZAR125 million (~US$7 million) in common shares of Pula SPV, for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Republic of South Africa
development_impact: The Project will expand access to well-located, secure, and affordable rental housing in Gauteng, where shortages are most acute. It targets low- and middle-income households and will provide quality units with amenities in central locations, helping reduce residents’ transport costs and commuting times. It also applies a circular-economy approach by repurposing underutilized office buildings into residential units. This adaptive reuse avoids emissions associated with demolition and new construction, while retrofits will incorporate energy-efficiency measures. The Project will strengthen competition in South Africa’s rental housing market by increasing the supply of affordable, well-located units for low- and middle-income households. It will help scale the emerging nano-unit segment, demonstrating the viability of this model while supporting urban regeneration in Gauteng.
additionality: The proposed IFC financing has both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is delivered through long-term equity and quasi-equity financing that meets the capital requirements of the Pula SPV. Financing in the form that IFC is providing is not readily available on the local market. Regarding non-financial additionality, IFC will also support the client in strengthening corporate governance structures and improving environmental and social (E&S) standards across its operation.

project_description: IFC proposes to provide an unfunded financial guarantee of up to MXN2,125 million, covering the mezzanine (second-loss) tranche of a reference portfolio performing SME loan exposures originated by BBVA Mexico, S.A., Institucion de Banca Multiple, Grupo Financiero BBVA Mexico (BBVA Mexico). The transaction is structured as a Significant Risk Transfer (SRT) - Bursatilizacion Sintetica. IFC’s guarantee will enable the Bank to use the regulatory capital freed up through the reference portfolio to generate more risk-weighted assets and support its origination lending activities.
sponsor_shareholders: BBVA Mexico, S.A., Institucion de Banca Multiple, Grupo Financiero BBVA Mexico is the leading universal financial institution in Mexico, operating across all banking segments corporate, commercial, SME, government, retail, private, and personal banking. As of March 2026, the Bank serves 34 million customers through a network of 1,635 branches, 14,381 ATMs, and 44,718 employees, and is 99.97% owned by Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria S.A. (BBVA Spain), which is publicly listed on the Madrid Stock Exchange with 62% held by public investors and 38% by institutional investors. As of April 2026, BBVA Mexico holds a 25.5% market share in performing loans nearly double that of its closest peer at 14.6% and a 24.0% market share in deposits. The Bank's total performing loan portfolio stood at approximately US$107.9 billion as of April 2026. Total deposits reached approximately US$110.1 billion, with 83% in demand deposits reflecting strong retail franchise fundamentals. BBVA M?co is the undisputed leader in SME financing in the country, holding a 33.7% national market share in SME lending as of early 2026 and serving over 1.1 million of approximately 1.5million banked SMEs, representing around 64% penetration. The bank's dominance is also reflected geographically, ranking first in 29 out of 32 states and across all seven divisions, with particularly strong positioning in underserved regions where financial inclusion gaps persist, including market shares of 41.9% in the South and 36.8% in the Southeastareas where access to credit remains most constrained for SME borrowers. BBVA Mexico maintains strong investment-grade credit ratings: BBB+ (Stable) by Fitch, BBB (Stable) by S&P, A3 (Negative) by Moody's, and mxAAA on local scales. The Bank is regulated by the Mexican National Banking and Securities Commission (CNBV) and supervised at the consolidated group level by the European Central Bank (ECB).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC's investment takes the form of an unfunded financial guarantee of up to MXN2,125 million on the mezzanine tranche of the reference SME portfolio
location_description: Mexico
development_impact: Project Outcome: Increased Access to Finance for SMEs, including underserved regions and women SMEs. The Project is expected to contribute to the WBG Scorecard Indicator: (12.2) Millions of people and businesses using financial services, of which (%) are women. The Project expands access to finance for SMEs in Mexico, which face an US$186 billion financing gap (16% of GDP) and where 29% of firms report credit constraints. Through regulatory capital relief enabled by the SRT, BBVA Mexico can redeploy released capital to support firm growth, productivity, and employment, while improving capital efficiency without increasing leverage. The Project strengthens the capacity to expand SME lending, particularly to Women SMEs and underserved regions such as the South and Southeast. It also promotes scalable, data-driven lending platforms within regulated banks, with IFC supporting their expansion and replication to improve SME access to finance. Contribution to Market Creation: Increasing Market Resilience The Project forms part of a broader IFC program across LAC aimed at strengthening resilience through innovative capital tools. Demonstration effects may catalyze additional SRT issuances, attract private investors, and enable institutions to free up capital for inclusive credit growth without issuing new equity or Tier II capital, contributing to long-term financial sector resilience.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC's financial additionality arises from its provision of an innovative SRT structure not currently offered by any other financial institution in Mexico or the broader LAC region. By offering an unfunded financial guarantee of up to US$100 - US$115 million on the mezzanine tranche of an SME portfolio, IFC enables BBVA Mexico to obtain regulatory capital relief while retaining ownership of the underlying assets and without increasing balance-sheet leverage. This is also the inaugural SRT for BBVA Mexico, reinforcing the innovation dimension of IFC's involvement. IFC's participation also has the potential to mobilize additional private investors into similar structures, supporting future replication and deepening of the local structured finance ecosystem. The mobilization ratio is 3.5x the guarantee amount. Non-Financial Additionality — Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: Beyond the financial instrument, IFC delivers non-financial additionality through its structuring expertise, risk-transfer capabilities, and global SRT track record. IFC supports BBVA Mexico in refining the transaction structure, eligibility criteria, reporting standards, and verification procedures per international best practices, enhancing the Bank's internal risk management and capacity to execute future capital-optimization tools.

company_name: AT & S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik Aktiengesellschaft
project_description: AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik Aktiengesellschaft (AT&S or the Company) is a leading global manufacturer of High-Density Interconnect (HDI) Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) and Integrated Circuit (IC) substrates, which are critical components in modern devices and applications. The proposed IFC investment consists of subscription by IFC for an amount of €15 million (approximately US$17.5 million equivalent) to convertible perpetual bonds issued by AT&S. The proceeds of IFC’s investment will be earmarked for financing the capital expenditure and associated working capital requirements for expansion of: (i) PCB manufacturing capacity in Nanjangud, Karnataka, India; and (ii) IC substrates capacity in Kulim, Kedah, Malaysia (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: AT&S is publicly listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange with 64.29% of shares held by public shareholders on a free float basis. The balance 35.7% is owned by two private foundations (Androsch Private Foundation and Dorflinger Private Foundation).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed transaction involves an IFC investment of €15 million in convertible perpetual bonds issued by AT&S. The investment will support the Company in its expansion plans in India and Malaysia.
location_description: Nanjangud, Karnataka, India and Kulim, Kedah, Malaysia
development_impact: (A) Project Level: The most significant expected Project level outcomes are economy-wide effects and stakeholder effects. By localizing production of advanced printed circuit boards and IC substrates, where reliance on imported components remains significant, the Project will increase domestic value addition, support foreign exchange savings, create employment throughout the extended value chain, and enhance industrial competitiveness. The Project will also deepen local supplier ecosystems by supporting the upgradation and qualification of domestic vendors. (B) Market Creation: Beyond the Project, the investment is expected to strengthen supply chain resilience in a market dominated by low-end production and imports, reducing reliance on imported advanced boards for priority sectors, and demonstrate the commercial viability of higher-value manufacturing, supporting market development and future investment.
additionality: (A) Financial additionality: The investment will strengthen the Company's capital base and will also support using funds raised in developed markets for investments in emerging markets. (B) Non-financial additionality: In an underdeveloped supply chain, IFC will leverage its relationships to support the Company building local partnerships. IFC will also provide guidance on implementation of IFC Performance Standards across the Company's India operations, improving the Company's ability to manage E&S risks and strengthening the capacity of the local supply chain.
Company Name: AT & S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik Aktiengesellschaft

project_description: IFC is considering providing up to US$150 million from IFC's own account (the IFC Loan), and up to US$250 million mobilized from parallel lenders, as part of a proposed senior unsecured loan facility of up to US$400 million to Ronesans Holding A.S. (RHOL or the Company), a leading Turkish conglomerate operating across five core divisions: construction, real estate, infrastructure, renewable energy, and industrials. The proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, including potential equity contributions to hospital public-private partnership (PPP) projects in Central Asia (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: RHOL is a family-owned business. It is owned by Dr. Erman Ilicak, President Emeritus of Ronesans Holding and his sister, Ipek Ilicak Kayaalp, Chair of the Board of Directors of Ronesans Holding, who together hold 98.71% of the Company. The remaining 1.29% is held by IFC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total financing is up to US$400 million, comprising (i) up to US$150 million from IFC's own account and (ii) up to US$250 million mobilized from parallel lenders.
location_description: The proceeds will be utilized by RHOL for its operations in Turkiye and Central Asia.
development_impact: The Project will directly contribute to job creation and value addition in the local economy through RHOL's business expansion, creating employment across management, technical, and support roles. The Project will also contribute to the wider economy through supplier linkages and local procurement. In terms of market outcomes, the Project is expected to enhance competitiveness in the construction sector through competitive pressure, by strengthening a key international contractor that delivers high-quality work across major infrastructure, commercial real estate, and healthcare facility projects. Its continued growth will raise performance benchmarks across the market, encouraging other firms to improve quality, adopt more efficient practices, and offer more competitive pricing.
additionality: IFC's involvement is expected to contribute to both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided through (i) a financing structure with longer tenors and grace periods otherwise not available in local markets, and (ii) IFC mobilizing up to US$250 million in additional financing from parallel lenders. Non-financial additionality is provided by (i) standard setting with respect to environmental and social performance, through an ESAP to address identified gaps, and (ii) knowledge, innovation, and capacity building to support RHOL's continued institutional development

company_name: IENTC, S. de R.L. de C.V.
project_description: The proposed investment entails a local currency-denominated (Mexican Pesos) senior loan of up to US$30 million equivalent in MXN to IENTC S. de R.L. de C.V. (IENTC or the Company) to finance the expansion of its fiber-optic backbone and metro network, enhancing capacity, connectivity and redundancy across Mexico (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: IENTC, established in 2011, is a fast-growing wholesale and B2B broadband operator based in Queretaro, Mexico that designs, builds, owns, and operates fiber backbone and metro networks, complemented by indefeasible rights of use on third-party dark fiber.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is approximately up to $100 million, from which IFC Investment from its own account would be up to US$30 million.
location_description: The Use of Proceeds of the project will be applied in Mexico.
development_impact: The project is expected to enable the Company in expanding its fiber optic backbone and metro network, which is expected to directly contribute to increasing the capacity of broadband networks in the country. This could then also indirectly facilitate improved access to quality digital connectivity for individuals and businesses in Mexico. Beyond the project, the project is expected to increase the competitiveness of Mexico’s wholesale and retail fixed broadband markets by strengthening the competitive dynamics in broadband markets in the country. The expansion of a wholesale market challengers' network is expected to not only encourage competition in the wholesale segment, but also lower costs for retail operators and reinforcing competition in the downstream retail market serving customers.
additionality: IFC is expected to mobilize approximately US$15 million through Credit Insurance Products, thereby enabling participation from private insurers that would not otherwise take exposure to this risk profile or to local currency in this context. This approach helps crowd in private capital in the context of weakened investor confidence and demonstrates a scalable mechanism to mobilize funding under constrained market conditions. IFC is further expected to support the Company in building on its foundational E&S and HR systems in through an ESAP aligned with IFC Performance Standards, thereby exceeding current industry standards.
Company Name: IENTC, S. de R.L. de C.V.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$50 million A Loan to Zebra Manufacturing Limited (“Zebra Manufacturing”) and Future Africa International Trading FZE (“Future Africa”) (together, the “Borrowers”) to finance (i) the development of a Hilton-branded hotel in Lusaka, Zambia (“Hilton Lusaka”); and (ii) development of a warehousing facility in Djibouti (“Djibouti Warehouse”) (together, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Zebra Manufacturing is owned by Mr. Yemane Berhe Weldeslassie (50%) and Mr. Daniel Berhe Weldeslassie (50%). Future Africa is owned by Mr. Daniel Berhe Weldeslassie (100%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated cost of the Project is up to US$97 million. IFC plans to provide a loan of up to US$50 million.
location_description: The Hilton Lusaka is located in Lusaka, Zambia and the Djibouti Warehouse is located in the Djibouti Damerjog Industrial Development Free Trade Zone, Djibouti.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are economy-wide effects via jobs creation and value added and stakeholder effects with increased business opportunities and capacity building for domestic suppliers. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater market competitiveness via competitive pressure and demonstration effects, while strengthening the resilience of the grain supply and distribution logistics in the Horn of Africa region.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via scarce long-term financing, which is otherwise not readily available in the local market. Non-financial additionality is provided via setting of ESG standards and capacity building through IFC advisory.

company_name: Hebei Huatong Wires and Cables Group
sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$60 million senior loan to Hebei Huatong Wires and Cables Group Co., Ltd. (Huatong Group or the Company) and its subsidiaries, HT International Trading Services PTE. LTD. (Huatong Singapore), Everwell Cable and Engineering Company Ltd. (Everwell Tanzania) and Everwell Cameroon Cables and Engineering.SA (Everwell Cameroon), to expand its manufacturing capacity in electric cables in Cameroon, and Tanzania. The project scope includes i) expand Huatong Group’s existing copper and aluminium cable production capacity in Tanzania; and ii) meet the working capital needs of its Cameroon plant (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Huatong Group is a leading global manufacturer of wires and cables company registered in China, with manufacturing plants in 6 countries globally. Huatong Singapore, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Huatong Group, is the investment holding platform for the Company’s offshore assets. Everwell Cameroon produces low- and medium-voltage cables in Cameroon. Everwell Tanzania is East Africa’s leading wire and cable producer in Tanzania. Huatong is a company listed on the Shanghai stock exchange, the ultimate beneficiary owners of the Company are members of the Zhang family, who collectively holds 35 percent of the shares, with Wenyong Zhang owning 17 percent as a Board Member, Wendong Zhang holding 14 percent as the Board Chairman, and other family members holding 4 percent. The remaining 65 percent is owned by individuals and institutional investors with all its shares trading on the Shanghai stock exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at US$60 million and will be financed by: the proposed US$60 million A loan from IFC.
location_description: The project sites are located in Douala, Cameroon, and Mkuranga, 45 km south of Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
development_impact: The Project will improve access to quality insulated wires and cables in key African markets, support national electrification plans, and reduce reliance on costly imports. It is expected to create 920 direct and 2,580 indirect jobs in Tanzania and Cameroon, enhance domestic industrial value, and boost foreign exchange through increased exports. The Project is expected to enable downstream power-sector development and support the expansion of electricity access in Tanzania, where capital expenditures are concentrated. The Project is also expected to expand electric cable production markets in Tanzania and Cameroon by scaling up domestic production and generating demonstration effects for other market players.
additionality: IFC provides both financial and non-financial additionality. The financial additionality is provided through long-term financing distributed across two countries in SSA, which local banks struggle to provide. Non-financial additionality is provided by enhancing the Company’s environmental and social (E&S) management systems in line with IFC’s performance standards (PSs) and enhancing the Company’s workplace gender equality and inclusion policies through potential IFC gender advisory support.
Company Name: Hebei Huatong Wires and Cables Group

project_description: The proposed IFC's financing consists of a senior secured Tajik Somoni (TJS)-denominated financing package of up to US$15 million equivalent (the IFC Financing) to Iroda Invest LLC (Iroda or the Company). Established in 2024, Iroda is a flour milling and oil bottling company in Tajikistanand is part of the Farovon Group (Farovon or the Group) - Tajikistan's largest integrated food producer. The IFC Financing will support Iroda's investment program which includes flour mills, oil bottling facilities, storage and associated working capital. The project is expected to be supported by the IDA21 Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (PSW LCF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Iroda Invest LLC is majority owned by the Bobojonov, Samandarov, and Mirzomansurov families, founders of the Group. Minority stakes are held by two long-serving senior managers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The investment program for Iroda Invest is estimated at US$37.4 million to be financed by (i) IFC Financing, (ii) Sponsor's equity and (iii) internal cash generation.
location_description: The Project is located in the Bobojon Gafurov district of the Sughd region, Republic of Tajikistan.
development_impact: The project will increase production capacity for flour and vegetable oil in Tajikistan, increasing food supply and availability in the market, thereby improving consumer access to safe staple food. In addition, the project is expected to contribute to the economy of Tajikistan through value addition, backward linkages to other sectors of the economy, while creating additional employment opportunities. Lastly, IFC anticipates that by supporting a leading flour producer in Tajikistan, the project helps to sustain progress towards increased competitiveness of the flour milling sector and the food processing market in Tajikistan.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial: i. Financial Additionality: IFC, enabled by the IDA PSW LCF, will provide long-term local currency financing (7 years with a 2-year grace period) in the form of a Sharia-compliant Commodity Murabaha. This type of financing is currently unavailable in the local market, thereby materially reducing FX risk for a staple-food producer. ii. Non-Financial Additionality: IFC will help improve Iroda's existing Environmental & Social (E&S) standards in line with IFC Performance Standards and industry best practices. IFC’s involvement is also expected to materially mitigate state-intervention risk. ESG, CG, and food-safety advisory support, IFC will strengthen institutional quality, helping ensure that development outcomes are delivered through a financially sustainable business. This includes diagnostic and potential follow-up advisory engagements related to corporate governance, gender, and financial management.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an up to US$25 million (M) A-Loan under Expedited Processing for Existing Clients to IFC’s client Edita Food Industries S.A.E (“Edita” or the “Parent Company”), and its subsidiaries Ahramat Al-Nile for General Trading and Food Industries Ltd. (formerly TJA) (the “Company” or “Edita Iraq”), Edita Participation Cyprus Ltd. (“Edita Cyprus”) and Edita for Trade and Distribution S.A.E (together the Co-Borrowers). The loan will be used to support (i) new operations in Iraq by financing the expansion of production lines, equipment, property, and working capital, aiming to more than double capacity and fully commission new lines by 2028 and (ii) Edita’s operations in Egypt with working capital.
sponsor_shareholders: Edita is a listed company in Egypt. It was founded and is led by Hani Berzi. His family’s investment vehicle, Quantum Investment B.V., is the controlling shareholder of Edita with about 45%, followed by Koenigsweg Holdings Ltd. (around 10%) and Rimco Egt Investments LLC (around 10%), both of which are financial investment entities holding significant minority stakes in the company. The remaining shareholding is made up of free float, some institutional investors, public and other investors. Edita Iraq is a Baghdad-based snack manufacturer owned 51% by Tuama Jebur Abbas (TJA) and 49% by Edita Investments Holding LTD, an Abu Dhabi Global Markets (ADGM) company wholly owned by Edita.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide an up to USD25 million senior loan to finance Edita’s expansion to Iraq and working capital requirements.
location_description: Iraq, Egypt
development_impact: The Project will grow Edita’s production capacity and operations in Iraq. IFC anticipates that this will contribute to Iraq’s economy by generating jobs, increasing processing capacity, adding value to domestically sourced cereals, creating inter-sector linkages, and generating revenue to the Government of Iraq through VAT, corporate income taxes, etc. In addition, the Project is expected to localize a well-known foreign brand in Iraq, through a “South-South” regional integration to build up additional local production capacity, ultimately introducing new product lines to diversify its current offering in the market beyond cakes and bakeries. This should enhance operational capacity and improve competitiveness in the market among mid-income consumers as well as within the premium snacks segment.
additionality: IFC will provide long-term hard currency financing, which is not readily available to agribusinesses and food manufacturers in the local market, which typically provide shorter term facilities and require significant collateral. Moreover, IFC will provide specific global expertise in food manufacturing, drawing on its prior experience supporting Edita’s operations in Egypt and Morocco, to ensure efficient deployment and scaling of Edita’s manufacturing processes in Iraq. Through its involvement, IFC will also support the Group to align its operations with IFC Performance Standards.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment supports Marquardt GmbH (“Marquardt” or “the Company”) in financing the (i) expansion capex including equipment purchase and building and (ii) working capital needs of its automotive mechatronic and automation component production facility in Tunisia operated through its local subsidiary, Marquardt Automotive Tunisie S.a.r.l.
sponsor_shareholders: Marquardt Group (the Group) is a German global supplier of mechatronic systems, serving primarily the automotive and electrical industries. The product portfolio spans a broad range of applications, from vehicle access and ignition systems to energy management solutions and industrial switching components, serving leading automotive original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and manufacturers in the power tools and home appliance sectors. Marquardt has maintained a manufacturing presence in Tunisia since 1991, producing electrical switches and mechatronic components across three facilities and supporting the Group’s research and development activities. The Tunisian operations employ approximately 2,000 people (of which over 60% are female). This positions the Tunisian subsidiary as a strategically integrated part of the Group's global supply chain.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide up to EUR 52 million A-Loan to support Marquardt Tunisia capex program.
location_description: Marquardt Tunisia operates three manufacturing facilities, 2 in El Agba and 1 in El Fejja NEOPARK industrial zone, all in the greater Tunis area.
development_impact: The development impact is provided through: increasing value added and job creation by scaling up advanced automotive manufacturing and expanding supply chain linkages with domestic SMEs; enhancing human capital through structured training in technical and managerial competencies, digital upskilling, and partnerships with universities and technical institutions; and reinforcing Tunisia's competitiveness as an advanced automotive manufacturing hub, encouraging further multinational entry and FDI into the sector.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing Structure: IFC is providing long-term financing with a tenor exceeding what is currently available from commercial banks in Tunisia, commensurate with the cash flow dynamics of the automotive sector and Marquardt's planned capital expenditure build-out and ramp-up. Non-Financial Additionality: (A) Risk Mitigation: IFC's involvement provides a confidence signal that encourages Marquardt to sustain and scale its investment in Tunisia despite a challenging macroeconomic environment, while signaling to other investors and OEMs that Tunisia remains a viable long-term manufacturing destination. (B) Standard Setting: IFC will support Marquardt in greening its operations and strengthening E&S standards beyond local regulatory requirements.

project_description: IFC is considering a US$400m financing package to Fruitist Holdings Inc. (“Fruitist” or the “Company”) to (i) support the Company’s capital and operational expenditures as well as working capital requirements in Peru, and (ii) refinance existing debt (the “Project”). The capital and operational expenditures will include the replacement of older, conventional varieties of blueberries, with newer, elite varieties.
sponsor_shareholders: Fruitist is privately held, with a distributed shareholding, including the founders Steve Magami (Chairman and CEO) and Thomas Snyder, early investors, family offices, and private financial institutions. No individual shareholder owns more than 10% of the Company
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s financing package consists of (i) a US$100m IFC A-loan and (ii) a US$300m B-Loan to be mobilized from commercial banks and potentially other Development Finance Institutions.
location_description: Olmos and Morrope municipalities, Lambayeque, Peru
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate economy-wide effects in terms of job creation and value addition and have positive environmental effects through building adaptive capacity. Beyond the Project, IFC expects its financing to contribute to strengthening the resilience of the blueberries sector in Peru by implementing improvement in climate resilience through adopting new blueberry varieties that have superior performance against climate events.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the Project will be both financial and non-financial, including longer tenor financing, resource mobilization, provision of advisory services and implementation of IFC's environmental and social standards to strengthen governance and sustainability practices.

project_description: IFC is considering an investment of up to US$40 million or its KZT equivalent in a senior secured private placement bond (the IFC Investment) to be issued by Samal Finance LLC (Samal Finance), a subsidiary of KazFoodProduct LLC (KFP or the Group). The IFC investment will support Group’s multi-year investment program, focused on expanding of the Group`s confectionary business and addressing increased working capital requirements.
sponsor_shareholders: Samal Finance is a financing entity and a wholly owned subsidiary of KFP. Founded in 1998, KFP is an existing IFC client in Kazakhstan and a leading Kazakhstan-based agrifood group operating across deep wheat processing, meat production and processing, and confectionery. The Group comprises 20+ subsidiaries and employs over 5,000 people nationwide. KFP sells its products domestically and exports to over 10 countries. KFP is controlled and majority owned by Mr. Yerlan Baimuratov (30%) and Balapanov family (53%) and Mr. Alikhan Talgatbek (5%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed financing is a US$40 million investment in a privately placed bond to partially fund KFP’s US$63 million investment program (the “Project”), including: (i) capital expenditures during 2025–2027 to increase confectionery production capacity by 20%, reaching more than 100 Kt per year; and (ii) working capital needs for confectionary and agribusiness.
location_description: The Project will be implemented by KFP’s two subsidiary companies: Joint Stock Company “Bayan Sulu”, located in Kostanai region, northern Kazakhstan, and Joint Stock Company “Asia AgroFood”, located in Chemolgan, Almaty region.
development_impact: The Project is expected to contribute to Kazakhstan’s economic development by supporting job creation, increasing value addition, and strengthening linkages across key sectors such as agriculture, logistics, and transportation. By sustaining and expanding the operations of a major local confectionery producer, it will help enhance domestic production capacity and support export activity, thereby contributing to foreign exchange generation. In addition, the Project will promote greater food availability and improve access to nutritious food products in both Kazakhstan and neighboring markets, including through the production of fortified goods. Furthermore, it will support inclusive employment, particularly for women, and advancing initiatives that promote gender equality in the workplace. Finally, the Project is expected to enhance competitiveness in the local food processing industry by sustaining a strong domestic player and supporting a more dynamic and competitive market environment.
additionality: The proposed IFC financing has long term and local currency features that are currently not widely available in the market; it will also help further catalyze private sector investment, strengthen capital market development and support Kazakhstan’s sustainable growth. By providing local currency financing, IFC will help the Group to address FX mismatch risk, without which the Group’s long-term development plans could be impeded. IFC will offer Financial Management Advisory services for KFP to strengthen its financial reporting and management practices. Additionally, IFC will support and guide KFP to implement and maintain policies for the Project in line with Performance Standard. IFC`s guidance will help KFP to strengthen its environmental and social practices, including among other things, aligning EHS procedures with IFC standards, conducting Atmosphere Explosible (ATEX) and OHS assessments with corrective actions, implementing a robust supply chain management system addressing key risks, establishing policies on gender-based violence and harassment, introducing a formal worker grievance mechanism, and enhancing group-wide OHS performance through independent audits and targeted improvements.

project_description: The IFC is considering an US$11 million corporate finance package to Djeliba Leisure Group (DLG), a group comprised of four Gambian companies acting as co-borrowers - Djeliba Leisure Group Ltd, Balafon Company Ltd, EON Company Ltd, and International Tourism Investment Ltd – to support hotel expansion, refurbishment, and energy efficiency improvements. The financing comprises an IFC A-Loan and subordinated loans from International Development Association Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) and the Concessional Capital Window (CCW). Proceeds will support a US$20.76 million investment program across four beachfront hotels in The Gambia: Balafon Beach Resort; Kombo Beach Resort; TUI BLUE Tamala hotel; and Kalimba Beach Resort. Djeliba Leisure Group Ltd. Use of financing proceeds will cover construction of new rooms and room refurbishment across the four hotels; upgrades to employee welfare facilities; and installation of a 1.8MW solar photovoltaic (PV) system with battery energy storage to supply solar power exclusively for on-site hotel operations at three hotels. All four hotels are expected to receive EDGE certification.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group is a private limited company co-owned equally by Malleh Sallah and Omar Jawara.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost of US$20.76 million, will be financed with Sponsor equity (US$9.76 million) and IFC A-Loan (US$11 million).
location_description: The Project is located at Banjul, in Gambia.
development_impact: The project is expected to generate economy wide benefits through both direct and indirect job creation and contributions to GDP; employment impacts through the creation of high quality jobs in hotel operations; and environmental gains in the form of energy and water savings, as well as reductions in GHG emissions, achieved through the green certification of hotel assets. The employment impact is also inclusive, reflecting the client’s commitment to significantly increase the proportion of female employees. In addition, IFC anticipates that the investment will strengthen competitiveness in the hospitality sector, particularly in the mid to upscale segment, by fostering competitive pressure. It will support the client’s a shift away from a mass “sun, sea, and sand” tourism model toward a more diversified, higher value offering, with strong potential for replication and scale up within the local market by other players.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is through the provision of a long-term facility with an extended grace period, better aligning debt service obligations with DLG’s cash flow profile, which is otherwise not readily available in the local market. Non-financial additionality is provided via capacity building through IFC advisory in financial management, EDGE advisory and through the implementation of comprehensive Environmental & Social management systems.

project_description: Allied Chemicals Share Company (Allied) is Ethiopia's largest domestic manufacturer of industrial chemicals, headquartered in Addis Ababa with three manufacturing facilities in Ethiopia. Founded in 2008, the company produces 18 chemical and mineral products and serves over 1,300 customers across Ethiopia, including large FMCG manufacturers and beverage companies. The Project involves the construction and commissioning of a greenfield NPK/NPS fertilizer blending plant in Adama, Ethiopia the first privately owned compound fertilizer facility in the country. IFC is providing a financing package of up to US$17 million, comprising an IFC A Loan of US$11 million structured as a Local Currency Linked Loan in Ethiopian Birr and supported by an IDA-PSW Blended Finance Facility swap subsidy, and US$6 million mobilized from parallel lenders.
sponsor_shareholders: Allied Chemicals was founded by Mr. Rajesh Gupta (the Sponsor), who, along with his family, owns ~70% of the company. The other shares are held by an IFC investee fund manager, Ascent Capital, which holds ~30% of the company's shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at ETB 3.69 billion (approximately US$33.98 million) and will be financed on a 50/50 debt-to-equity basis. The Sponsor is investing up to US$16.98 million in equity, and IFC is providing up to US$17 million in debt financing.
location_description: Adama Industrial Zone, Oromia Regional State, Ethiopia approximately 90km east of Addis Ababa.
development_impact: The development impact is provided through: Increasing value addition and job creation by expanding domestic fertilizer production, expanding the domestic supply-chain to include more upstream steps; Increasing access and affordability of a critical agricultural input in a market with substantial failures; Increasing the competitiveness of Ethiopia's agricultural sector, by establishing Ethiopia's first fertilizer blending facility, reducing vulnerability to external shocks, and boosting agricultural productivity through more intensive fertilizer use.
additionality: Financial Additionality: (A) Financing Structure: IFC is providing long-term financing for the Project commensurate with project needs and typically not readily available in the domestic market for manufacturing companies. This long-term financing is crucial to the Project’s success, given the need to ramp up production. (B) Mobilization: IFC will also mobilize funding from a local bank in Ethiopia. Non-financial Additionality: (A) Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: Through the Upstream Advisory engagement, IFC will connect Allied to 3,000 farmers for a pilot to demonstrate the product’s efficacy to mitigate risk by establishing product trust and demand prior to full-scale entry. (b) Standard Setting: IFC will help Allied improve its E&S standards.

project_description: Indorama Corporation Pte. Ltd. (Indorama or the Group), a Singapore-based holding company, is a long standing strategic IFC client. Over the last three decades IFC and Indorama have partnered to enter high-risk markets, during which time Indorama has evolved into one of the world's fastest-growing fertilizer, petrochemical, and fiber companies. As part of its growth strategy, Indorama is expanding its footprint into the Middle East and North Africa through the development and construction of a greenfield phosphatic fertilizer complex in Ain Sokhna, Egypt. The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$174 million debt financing package to Indorama Misr Fertilizers SAE (IRM) for developing a greenfield integrated phosphate-based fertilizer facility in Ain Sokhna, Egypt (the Project). The expected investment cost of the Project is US$520 million which will include a sulfuric acid plant (SAP), a phosphoric acid plant (PAP) and a granulation unit to produce di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) and mono-ammonium phosphate (MAP), NPK fertilizers and associated infrastructure. The Project is expected to produce 600,000 tonnes per annum of phosphate-based fertilizer.
sponsor_shareholders: Indorama, headquartered in Singapore, is a global leading producer of essential materials. It was established in 1975 in Indonesia by its founder, M.L. Lohia, and his son, S.P. Lohia with its first operations in Indonesia as a cotton yarn spinning company. In 1991, Indorama diversified into the production of polyester fibres from petrochemical derivatives, and subsequently into the production of PET resins. Today, Indorama manufactures, through its subsidiaries, a multitude of products including nitrogen fertilizers, phosphate fertilizers, agriculture inputs, polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, textiles, cotton fibre and medical gloves. Indorama ranks as the 5th largest global fertiliser producer, the 4th in synthetic gloves, and the 1st in PET (excluding China) and it is the largest producer of urea fertilizers in Sub-Saharan Africa, the largest producer of polyolefins in West Africa. Indorama Group has footprint across 38 countries in Asia, Europe, CIS, Africa, and North America, and a workforce of 50,000 employees. Indorama also owns a 32% share in IVL, a global player in chemical intermediate products (PET, fibers and chemical solutions) with manufacturing facilities in the Americas, Europe, Asia, in addition to Egypt.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The expected investment cost of the Project is US$520 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to US$174 million debt package comprising of (a) US$100 million IFC A loan and (b) mobilization of US$74 million in the form of B Loans to IRM Egypt. The balance of required funding will come from parallel lenders and equity / shareholder loans.
location_description: The Project will be located at Ain Sokhna in Egypt.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes include a substantial increase in the domestic supply of fertilizers in both India and Brazil, economy-wide value added and job creation, and environmental effects driven by climate mitigation measures. Beyond the project-level impact, IFC expects the Project to enhance the competitiveness of Egypt’s fertilizer industry by fostering the adoption of resource-efficient state-of-art technologies to improve its global competitiveness and further expand its export.
additionality: IFC's financial additionality stems from IFC’s long-term financing package to support the growth and financial sustainability of the Project. IFC will also help IRC Egypt implement E&S standards and assess climate impact of the Project and define longer-term climate goals and priorities making the Project eligible for a SLL.

project_description: The proposed investment is an A Loan of up to US$165 million (partially de-risked through an MCPP credit insurance cover) alongside US$135 million mobilized from B/parallel lenders to four Moroccan subsidiaries of the Pickalbatros Group (the “Group”), one of Africa’s largest and most diversified hospitality platforms with 39 hotels and ~16,000 keys across Egypt and Morocco. The Proposed investment will finance (i) the acquisition of the three assets, (ii) the refurbishment and upgrade of both newly acquired and selected existing hotels, and (iii) refinancing of existing debt, with implementation over 2026–2028. The Project includes sustainability-linked features tied to environmental performance improvements, with refurbishment expected to deliver energy and water efficiency gains, contributing to IFC’s climate objectives.
sponsor_shareholders: The Pickalbatros Group was established in 1992 by Mr. Kamel Abou-Ali (the “Sponsor”), an Egyptian businessman. The four Moroccan subsidiaries of the Groupare directly and indirectly owned by the Sponsor and his family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project costs of US$386 million, will be financed with Sponsor equity (US$86 million) and debt (US$300 million).
location_description: The Project is located in Morocco (Marrakech, Agadir and Casablanca).
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are economy-wide effects through jobs creation, domestic purchases, value addition, and linkages to other sectors of Morocco’s economy. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will help strengthen sustainability initiatives in Morocco’s hospitality sector.
additionality: Financial Additionality Innovative Financing Structure: The Moroccan financial market has limited access to long-term financing, particularly for sustainable and green bond investments. IFC’s investment of up to US$200m provides a longer tenor up to 10 years that is typically not available in the domestic market, improving financial stability and supporting the project’s sustainability. Non-Financial Additionality Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC will assist Pickalbatros, through Upstream advisory engagement and potential investment, to develop its overall Sustainability Framework (SF) and accordingly, obtain EDGE green building certification for its key assets, thereby strengthening the environmental sustainability of its existing portfolio and future brownfield assets to be acquired. Standards Setting: IFC will help improve Pickalbatros’s ESG practices, strengthening its position as a leader in sustainable hospitality and ensuring alignment with international best practices. IFC’s upstream engagement will support designing a new ringfenced Holding company for Morocco operations, ensuring adherence to sound ESG practices on all its operations in Morocco. Also, IFC’s investment and advisory support will help catalyze Morocco’s green/blue tourism finance, setting a precedent for future sustainable financing and attracting both domestic and international investors.

project_description: Insulet Corporation (Insulet or the Company) is a MedTech company specializing in diabetes management solutions. The Company is planning to establish its first manufacturing facility in Latin America, dedicated to the production of its flagship product, the Omnipod insulin management system, a tubeless insulin delivery device for people living with diabetes (the Project). The new manufacturing facility will be located within Savia Sur, a light industrial park in Heredia, Costa Rica, developed by Portafolio Inmobiliario (Portafolio or the Developer). The proposed IFC investment consist of a US$97 million A Loan, to support the construction of the facility's coldshell. The Borrower will be 3-101-939148 SA (Savia SPV), a special purpose vehicle responsible for managing the assets of the industrial park where the plant will be located.
