sponsor_shareholders: Insulet Corporation is publicly listed. 3-101-939148 SA is controlled by Portafolio Inmobiliario S.A, a Costa Rican leading real estate developer of industrial, corporate, commercial, residential and mixed-use projects in the Central American Region.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proceeds of the IFC loan will be used to partially finance the construction of Insulet's new plant in Costa Rica. The new plant is expected to go live in 2029.
location_description: The Project is located in Savia Industrial Park in Heredia, Costa Rica.
development_impact: Costa Rica shows a mixed performance in productive integration and human capital. Only 61% of manufacturing inputs are domestically produced, indicating limited local value chains despite a strong export-oriented sector. Human capital indicators are solid, but labor outcomes lag, with just 49% skilled workers and high unemployment. Project Outcomes: The most significant expected project level outcomes are increased formal employment and foreign exchange generation in Costa Rica, through the construction of a greenfield manufacturing facility. Market Outcomes: Beyond direct project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will strengthen market competitiveness in Costa Rica’s med-tech sector through demonstration and replication effects. By enabling domestic production at scale of an advanced drug-delivery medical device integrating disposability with embedded electronics, an activity not currently undertaken at scale in the country, the Project is expected to catalyze supplier upgrading, skills spillovers, and deeper local linkages, supporting the gradual transition of Costa Rica’s med-tech ecosystem toward higher-value and more technologically complex manufacturing.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality comes from IFC’s provision of a USD financing and mobilizing a significant financing package. Non-financial additionality will be provided through knowledge transfer, innovation, and capacity building, as well as standard setting through strengthening the client’s environmental and social risk management and disclosure practices in line with IFC Performance Standards and international best practice.

project_description: The proposed investment is a senior A Loan of up to EUR 40 million to Naval Holding Limited (Naval Groupor, The Group), a diversified industrial conglomerate with headquarters in Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) and operational leadership based in Luanda, Angola. The investment supports Naval Group's expansion of its Angolan subsidiary, Foodtec Industria Alimentar, Lda (Foodtec, The Company), a leading food manufacturer in Angola operating a wheat mill and pasta lines (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Naval Group has operations in food distribution, construction materials, industrial and agricultural supplies. The Group is a family business owned by Simon Ghebrebhan Tecleab and Ghebrebhan Tecleab.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide a senior loan of up to EUR40 million to finance Foodtec's EUR57 million facility expansion in Angola.
location_description: Angola
development_impact: The Project is anticipated to increase domestic value addition and job creation through up- and down-stream linkages with related sectors and increase food security for consumers through increased local production and distribution of quality and safe food products. The investment is expected to sustain market resilience against shocks by supporting Foodtec's expansion and utilization of grain handling and milling capacities. Angola and neighboring countries such as Zambia, the DRC, Namibia and Botswana have underdeveloped food systems and mostly import food products which make them vulnerable to shocks such as forex fluctuations and volatility of prices of food and raw materials. These aggravate food shortages and losses and food insecurity which the investment intends to address.
additionality: Financing structure: IFC will offer long-term Euro financing structure on terms otherwise not available in the local market (8years tenor and 2 years grace). IFC, through upstream and advisory services, will provide expertise, innovation, knowledge to improve operational efficiency of Foodtec, and align its operations with industry best practices with greater emphasis on product quality and sustainability.

company_name: Dogus Cay ve Gida Maddeleri Uretim Pazarlama Ithalat Ihracat A.S.
project_description: Established in 1985, Dogus Cay ve Gida Maddeleri Uretim Pazarlama Ithalat Ihracat A.S. (“Dogus Cay” or “The Company”) is a leading Turkish food and beverage (F&B) producer with a diversified portfolio spanning chips, tea, sugar, tomato paste, and soft beverages. The Company operates 15 large-scale production facilities with nationwide distribution, mainly serving modern retail and traditional trade channels in the domestic market. The project entails financing of Dogus Cay’s investment program in Turkiye which includes capacity increase and efficiency investments in chips operations, capacity increase in tomato paste operations and vehicle purchases for distribution operations (“The Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsor is Karakan Yatirim Holding A.S. (“The Sponsor”) which owns Dogus Cay’s majority shares. The Sponsor is established in Turkiye and is privately owned by Karakan Family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide an A-Loan up to EUR250 million to finance The Project.
location_description: The proposed IFC investment is planned to be utilized in the Company’s facilities in Turkiye.
development_impact: The project is expected to deliver broad economic benefits by creating new jobs, contributing to Turkiye’s economy through backward linkages with other sectors of the economy including agriculture, transportation, and logistics, as well as improving farmers’ livelihoods by expanding market access and providing technical assistance. Beyond direct outcomes, IFC’s financing is anticipated to sustain competitiveness within the savory snacks of Turkiye’s confectionery segment.
additionality: IFC provides a long-term financing with a tenor of up to 8 years including a up to 2-year grace period, which is not readily available in Turkiye. With the proposed IFC loan, Dogus Cay will repay €120 million bridge loan, originally incurred in 2024 and 2025 as part of its corporate investment program, converting it into a long-term financing matching its cash flow with its debt servicing obligations. The total face value of EUR syndicated loans in Agribusiness over the past 12 months was 0.03 billion USD. There were no EUR corporate bond issuances at a corresponding rating of B+/- in Agribusiness sector over the past 12 months. IFC will strengthen the Company’s E&S standards, linkages to farmers as well as institutional capacity and corporate governance standards of a family-owned business.
Company Name: Dogus Cay ve Gida Maddeleri Uretim Pazarlama Ithalat Ihracat A.S.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to US$80 million debt facility to be committed in phases to Netafim Ltd (“Netafim” or “the Company”) a global manufacturer and provider of drip irrigation equipment and solutions, headquartered in Israel and with operations in 110 countries.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is majority-owned by Orbia Advance Corp SAB de CV (“Orbia”), and the remaining stake is held by a kibbutzim entity called Netafim Hatzerim Holdings – Cooperative Association for Irrigation and Drippers Ltd (founder).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment an of up to US$80 million debt facility, to support the Borrower’s working capital needs in connection with its operations in Brazil, Colombia and Africa (the “Project”).
location_description: The Project is located in Colombia, Brazil and Africa.
development_impact: Summary – The main project outcomes derive from positive environmental effects in improving irrigation water efficiency by introducing or replacing traditional irrigation with more efficient micro-irrigation methods. At the market level, IFC anticipates that the investment will contribute to the resilience of the global food supply market by demonstrating modern, efficient irrigation systems in targeted regions, which not only increase water efficiency but also aims to improve crop yields and farmer incomes.
additionality: Financial Additionality: - Mobilization: Netafim is looking to expand its financing sources for its emerging market expansion strategy. IFC will mobilize US$30 million through a B loan from other development or commercial banks which would not be available if not for IFC´s participation and would help to further diversify the Company´s funding sources. Non-financial additionality: - Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: Netafim is expanding in emerging markets where the penetration of drip irrigation is still low. Netafim values IFC’s local presence, global experience, and connections to help support its entry into these markets.

sector: Soap and Cleaning Compound (Soap, Detergent, etc.)
project_description: IFC is considering a total funding package of up to US$20 million to Movit Products Limited (“Movit” or the “Company” or the “Borrower”), a leading personal care and hygiene manufacturer in Uganda. The Company currently manufactures from its plant in Uganda and sells a wide range of personal care and hygiene products across ten African countries. The funds will be used to i) establish a greenfield manufacturing plant in Tanzania and provide working capital for the new operations under Movit Products (Tanzania) Limited (a co-borrower); and ii) finance equipment purchases and working capital for the Company’s Uganda operations (the “Project”). The new facility will manufacture personal care and hygiene products for the Tanzanian market and neighbouring countries, complementing the Company’s existing operations in Uganda. The project is expected to strengthen regional manufacturing capacity, improve access to affordable personal care and hygiene products, reduce reliance on imports, and support job creation and regional value addition in Eastern and Southern Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: Movit Products Limited (Uganda) is owned by Simpson Birungi (96.5%), Jackson Turyatunga (2.0%) and Grace Katushabe (1.5%). Movit Products (Tanzania) Limited is owned by Simpson Birungi (64.8%), Jimson Birungi (17.6%), and Jackson Turyatunga (17.6%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at approximately US$21.5 million, and is expected to be financed by: (i) IFC ‘A’ Loan of up to US$12 million, and (ii) B2/MCPP Trust Loan of up to US$8 million, mobilized under IFC’s Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) (together with IFC ‘A’ Loan, the “IFC Loan”, and (iii) US$1.5 million from the Company’s internally generated cash.
location_description: The new manufacturing facility is being established on a greenfield site located in Kibaha, Tanzania, whilst the new equipment for Uganda will be installed at the existing factory site in Wakiso District, Uganda.
development_impact: Assessment of Project Outcomes - Economy-Wide Effects. The Project is expected to generate approximately 349 direct jobs at the client company, alongside additional indirect employment effects through backward supply chain linkages and induced impacts from increased consumer spending. Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation - Competitiveness. The IFC investment is expected to enhance the competitiveness of Tanzania’s hygiene and personal care sector through demonstration effects that showcase the investment potential of the FMCG sector for other regional and multinational market participants.
additionality: The proposed IFC financing has both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is delivered through long-term financing, comprising a loan with a tenor of up to eight years. Regarding non-financial additionality, IFC can support Movit by sharing FMCG sector insights, operational expertise, and global lessons learned from comparable markets through its Industry Specialist, helping drive market expansion and operational efficiency. IFC will also support the client in strengthening corporate governance structures and improving environmental and social (E&S) standards across its operations.

project_description: The proposed investment is an unfunded risk participation for up to €50 million in a €150 million bilateral facility extended by Societe Generale Paris (“SG”) for Touton S.A. (“Touton” or the “Group”), leading global cocoa, coffee and vanilla commodity trader for more than 150 years, to finance the procurement and export of traceable cocoa mainly from IDA Countries; Cote d’Ivoire, Ghana and Cameroon (the Facilities, the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Touton is a leading France-headquartered agro-industrial group with a global footprint spanning 15 offices worldwide. It is among the world’s top cocoa traders, purchasing approximately 350,000 metric tons of cocoa annually and accounting for around 8% of global cocoa trade. Cocoa is the core of the Group’s business, representing about 75% of its total revenues, with total trading volumes ranging between 300,000 and 400,000 metric tons of cocoa bean equivalents per year. Touton has a long-established presence across key producing origins and is one of the largest exporters of cocoa from Cote d’Ivoire as well as one of the leading exporters from Cameroon, reflecting its strong sourcing, logistics, and market positioning in major cocoa-producing regions. Societe Generale (“SG”) is a leading global Trade and Commodity Finance (“TCF”) bank with strong growth ambitions in the agricultural commodities sector. Its Paris platform specializes in transactional trade finance, supported by dedicated and experienced transaction monitoring teams, and is widely recognized by the market for the quality of its structuring, execution, and risk management capabilities. SG is a strategic partner for IFC, leveraging its extensive international network and its strong commitment to sustainability and ESG standards. The bank has a long-standing relationship with Touton, having financed the Group for over 33 years with an excellent performance and credit track record.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost will be up to EUR 150 million with IFC’s investment of up to EUR50 million in the form of an unfunded participation.
location_description: The proposed facility will involve trade transaction mainly in West Africa.
development_impact: The anticipated development impacts of the Project include: (i) improving smallholder farmers’ access to the cocoa market in West Africa by supporting continued local sourcing of traceable and sustainably produced cocoa beans; (ii) strengthening financial integration across the cocoa value chain through enhanced access to structured trade and working capital finance; and (iii) reinforcing West African countries’ competitiveness in global cocoa markets by promoting local value addition and higher environmental and sustainability standards.
additionality: IFC will be providing short-term liquidity in the Agri-supply chain, at a time of restricted availability in terms of country and obligor limits across West Africa affecting Agri supply chain liquidity.

project_description: The proposed investment (“Investment”) consists of a 10-year, upto US$90 million senior secured facility to Akij Carriers Limited and Akij Sea Line Limited (the “Companies” or the “Borrowers”), affiliated to Akij Shipping Line Limited (“Akij Shipping” or “ASLL”), a large, diversified conglomerate owned by Mr. Sheikh Jasim Uddin and his family (the “Promoter”). The Investment shall be for financing the acquisition of 3-4 second-hand ultramax bulk carriers and will support the Company’s fleet renewal, decarbonization and expansion program (the “Project”). The facility will be structured as an A loan of up to US$60 million and B1 loans of up to US$30 million. The shipping business is across eight entities based in Bangladesh, Singapore & UAE and currently operates 10 dry bulk vessels. All of these ships are managed and chartered by Akij Shipping Lines Pte Ltd (Akij Shipping Singapore).
sponsor_shareholders: Akij Group, a major Bangladeshi conglomerate, began as a jute trading business in the late 1940s, founded by Sheikh Akij Uddin (late father of the Promoter), and later became a leading local diversified conglomerate. In 2020, following the division of Akij Group's family assets among the five sons of the founder, the Companies and its affiliated shipping entities were spun off from Akij Group and integrated into Akij Resource Limited (“Akij Resource”). Under Akij Resource group, currently over 8,000 people are employed and operates in diversified industries such as building materials, logistics, travel, commodity trading, agricultural processing, IT, communications as well as shipping sectors, generating c. US$578 million in revenues in FY2025. The Promoter is Mr. Sheikh Jasim Uddin, the Managing Director of Akij Resource and Faria Hossain (wife of Mr. Sheikh Jasim Uddin), the Chair of Akij Resource.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated cost of 3-4 second-hand Ultramax bulk carriers and retrofitting of existing vessels is US$138.5 million to be financed with 65% debt and 35% equity. The debt will be provided from IFC A-Loan of US$60 million and rest US$30 million to be mobilized from parallel lenders. IFC intends to commit an initial tranche of US$40 million in FY’26, with subsequent commitments in FY’27 subject to Akij Shipping progressing with vessel identification and negotiation.
location_description: The Companies that will be owning the vessels, are based out of Dhaka, Bangladesh.
development_impact: The Project will contribute to improving access to reliable, efficient freight shipping services in Bangladesh, job creation and environmental co-benefits. At the market level, the Project is expected to enhance the competitiveness of the maritime logistics sector in Bangladesh through reinforced efficiency and quality standards and sustained competition.
additionality: IFC has both financial and non-financial additionality for the transaction. IFC’s financial additionality stems from its role in providing long-term financing in line with the business model of the Companies, which is not available in the market. Non-financial additionality stems from IFC’s technical assistance provided in the areas of market assessment, environmental and social (E&S) capacity building, digital and operational integration, fleet modernization and decarbonization, corporate governance (CG) standards, and gender advisory.

project_description: The proposed investment is a senior loan of up to USD40 million to Carrinho Empreendimentos, S.A. (Carrinho). Carrinho is the holding of an Angolan family-owned business (the Carrinho Group or the Group) integrating operations across the food value chain (origination, storage, processing, distribution and retail). The investment will support the Group’s expansion, including the extension of its wheat flour mill, the construction of a warehouse at its industrial complex in Benguela, the construction of a central kitchen in Luanda, the purchase of new trucks and the implementation of SAP software in its stores (the Project). . The Project is the continuation of Carrinho Group’s long-term import substitution program, started in 2016-2019 with the successful establishment of a state-of-the-art industrial complex with 19 factories (flour, biscuits, pasta, edible oil, various packaged foods, animal feed, etc.) at the mouth of the Lobito corridor.
sponsor_shareholders: Carrinho Empreendimentos, S.A. is fully owned by the Carrinho family. Nelson Carrinho, Rui Carrinho, the sons of the founder, respectively own 49.9% and 40%. Leonor Carrinho, the founder, her daughter Elsa and her granddaughter Stelavic respectively own 8.0%, 2.0% and 0.1%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide an up to USD40 million senior loan to finance the Group’s USD52.1 million capex program on its industrial sites in Angola.
location_description: Angola
development_impact: The investment is expected to increase production of wheat flour and derivatives, thereby contributing to local food security. It will also contribute to local economic activity, both through backward linkages for suppliers (including smallholder farmers) and job creation, as the Group’s production capacity expands. The Group's prominent role in wheat flour production the sector is expected to increase competitive pressure on other market players.
additionality: IFC will provide long-term hard currency financing, which is not readily available to agribusinesses in the local market. IFC has been providing extensive advisory support to the Group since 2021, supporting Carrinho to create market linkages for farmers in the poultry and feed grain sectors and provide them with training and extension services. The Group has also implemented a platform to support MSM) development across the agribusiness value chain and has received support on gender awareness. The advisory project will continue through 2026 with support to enhance Carrinho's digital platform. Through its involvement, IFC will also support the Company to align its operations with IFC Performance Standards.

company_name: WEST INDIAN OCEAN CABLE COMPANY LTD
project_description: The West Indian Ocean Cable Company (WIOCC) Group is a top pan-African digital infrastructure provider, offering open-access data centres and high-capacity fibre networks across Africa. WIOCC Holding Company Ltd, its parent company, provides wholesale broadband connectivity linking African countries to Europe and beyond. WIOCC Holding Company has been a client of IFC since 2007. The proposed IFC investment comprises a senior secured sustainability-linked loan (“SLF”) of up to US$20.8 mn to WIOCC’s subsidiaries: WIOCC Mauritius (“WIOCC MU”) (US$ loan) and OADC PropCo South Africa (“OADC SA”) (ZAR loan), jointly referred to as “WIOCC Group”. Both entities are existing IFC clients under the 2024 SLF loans (#48053 and #49887) https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/48053/wiocc-slf-loan and WIOCC MU is a client under IFC’s 2020 loan (#44202); https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/44202/rse-covid-wiocc . IFC also holds a 10% equity stake in WIOCC Holding Company; WIOCC III equity in 2022 ( https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/41580/wiocc-iii ); This current project is considered an extension of WIOCC SLF loan (#48053) and OADC SLF Loan (#49887) which also sought to enhance connectivity and data hosting services for individuals and businesses in Africa. Proceeds from the new transaction will support WIOCC in expanding its network through further deployment of subsea and terrestrial cables to extend coverage in South and West Africa and increase data center capacity, primarily in Nigeria and South Africa as well as leverage the existing metro infrastructure to expand its Open Access Metro business improving fiber connections to estates and businesses for ISPs in Lagos and other States of Nigeria.
sponsor_shareholders: WIOCC Holding Company Limited (WHCL) is currently owned by a private equity Fund, African Capital Alliance, IFC, Management and 10 African telecommunication operators namely: Dalkom Somalia, Djibouti Telecom SA, Lesotho Communications Authority, Mocambique Telecom, S.A, Office National Des Telecommunication du Burundi, Telkom Kenya Limited, Tel-One (Private) Limited, Uganda Telecom Limited, BoFiNet, and Zanzibar Telecom Public Limited Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$577 million, to be financed with a combination of equity, new debt (US$65 million), and internal cash generation supported by already signed customer contracts. IFC’s proposed financing package includes, a US$ denominated sustainability-linked loan of up to US$10 million equivalent and a Rand denominated sustainability-linked loan of up to Rand 185 million (approximately US$10.7 million equivalent).
location_description: WIOCC is incorporated in Mauritius. The Project will involve the development of data centers in South Africa, Nigeria, and DRC, terrestrial fiber in Nigeria as well as the purchase of additional subsea capacity across Africa.
development_impact: WIOCC has been an investee of the IFC since 2008, with its most recent investment being the WIOCC SLF Loan which sought to bolster the Company's growth in connectivity and data center expansion across Nigeria, South Africa, and the DRC. The project's ex-ante rating was Good, based on a score of 60. This new investment builds upon this earlier project by introducing a new fiber to premises business model in Nigeria whilst facilitating further investments in terrestrial and submarine connectivity and data centers. The Project Outcomes will derive from its stakeholder effects to increase the capacity of broadband services in Sub-Saharan Africa, resulting in improved quality of broadband internet for end-users. These outcomes would be achieved by supporting the Company in its strategy of scaling up its new fiber to premises business in Nigeria while expanding its submarine cable capacity and terrestrial fiber infrastructure to cover up to 10 African countries. The project is also expected to improve access to data hosting services for businesses by expanding data center capacity in South Africa, Nigeria and DRC. Beyond the Project, and focusing on the Nigerian market, the Market Outcomes will derive from the capacity of this project to increase the competitiveness of the broadband market in Nigeria through competition channels. Through this project, the Company is expected to demonstrate the viability of rolling out fiber access connections, including by expanding its take-or-pay wholesale model, resulting in competitive pressure on its competitors to roll-out more fiber and potentially replicate the business model. The project could thereby also improve ISPs’ ability to compete downstream and offer improved retail services to end-users.
additionality: IFC additionality in this transaction is primarily financial and involves (i) the Financing Structure based on IFC providing a loan denominated in US$ and local currency, as well as (ii) Resource mobilization for the loan tranches, with Proparco and EAIF as co-investors in this transaction.
Company Name: WEST INDIAN OCEAN CABLE COMPANY LTD

project_description: Agrofertil S.A. (Agrofertil or the Company) is a crop input distributor and agronomic services provider headquartered in Ciudad del Este, Paraguay. Founded in 1993, Agrofertil has been an IFC client since 2011. The Company assists farmers, cooperatives and small distributors by providing technical support, agricultural inputs and preharvest financing. The proposed investment consists of an A loan facility of up to US$40 million per year, structured as one-year commitments with annual clean ups. The proposed project is to support the operations of Agrofertil and enhance its capacity to provide farmers with preharvest financing and technical advice (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: he Company is controlled by the Sarabia family, a leading participant in the Paraguayan agribusiness sector with over three decades of operating experience. Mr. Jose Marcos Sarabia, Mr. Antonio Ivar Sarabia, and Mr. Paulo Sergio Sarabia collectively hold, on an indirect basis, an 86.5% equity stake in Agrofertil.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an “A loan” facility of up to US$40 million per year, structured as one-year commitments with annual clean ups.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Ciudad del Este, Paraguay, and operates 30+ distribution centers and silos.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to improve access to pre-harvesting financing, technical assistance and market for farmers, strengthen global food security, and have positive environmental effects. Beyond the Project, IFC expects its financing to contribute to enhancing the competitiveness of the agricultural inputs market in Paraguay by spearheading the digitization of farming through ramping up the rollout of the first integrated smart agri platform in Paraguay.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the Project will be both financial and non-financial, including: i) financing structure; ii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building; and iii) standard setting.

project_description: The proposed project consists of an equity investment of up to €100 million (of which up to €68 million at the first close) in Alcazar Energy Partners III (“AEP-III” or “the Fund”), a closed end infrastructure fund with target fund size of €900 million managed by Alcazar Energy Management Services (Alcazar), engaged in developing and investing in utility-scale renewable energy projects across select emerging markets. AEP-III will invest in a diversified portfolio of utility-scale renewable energy projects across Middle East, North Africa, Turkey, Eastern Europe and Central Asia.
sponsor_shareholders: The fund will be managed by Alcazar Energy Partners III GP S.a r.l.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment comprises of an equity investment of up to €100 million in the Fund (of which up to €68 million at the first close).
location_description: AEP-III will invest across select emerging economies in Middle East, North Africa, Turkey, Eastern Europe and Central Asia.
development_impact: The development outcomes of the Project come from environmental effects through GHG emissions mitigation by adding low carbon sources of energy generation in the target markets. The Project is also expected to strengthen the sustainable finance market by promoting equity instruments that support sustainability outcomes; and enhance resilience through diversification of the power mix and promote long term energy security.
additionality: IFC’s investment will help AEP-III in reaching its fundraising target by helping mobilize capital from new investor base, including private institutional investors. Furthermore, IFC’s IFC involvement will enhance Fund’s capacity and credibility through promoting good environmental and social risk management practices aligned with IFC Performance Standards.

project_description: Genica Inovacao Biotecnologica S.A. (Genica or the Company) is a biological agricultural inputs developer and manufacturer, headquartered in Piracicaba, Sao Paulo, Brazil. Founded in 2015, the Company has established itself as one of Brazil's leading innovators in the biologicals sector, developing and commercializing proprietary biopesticides, biostimulants, inoculants, and regenerative agriculture solutions.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was co-founded by Fernando Reis, an agronomic engineer, and Prof. Dr. Carlos Labate from the University of Sao Paulo in Piracicaba. Since its founding in 2015, Genica has raised institutional capital from SP Ventures, Faro FIP, Mosaic, and Mitsubishi’s Agrex.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of a US$10 million equity investment in Genica as part of its Series D funding round.
location_description: The investment will be made in Brazil, with the Company headquartered and operating its R&D and manufacturing facilities in Piracicaba, Sao Paulo.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate jobs and value addition to the Brazilian economy, improve access to biological inputs, technical assistance, and credit for farmers, and to generate positive environmental effects. Beyond the Project, IFC expects its financing to contribute to improving the competitiveness of the agricultural input market in Brazil by catalyzing the development of the next generation of biologicals.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the Project will be both financial and non-financial, including: i) IFC own account equity; ii) standard setting; iii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building

project_description: The proposed investment comprises a US$10 million equity investment in the Caribbean Community Resilience Fund Equity Fund (CCRF Equity Fund or the CCE), a regional impact investing fund with a target size of US$60 million (scalable to US$100 million). The fund will invest catalytic development and scale-up capital in the Caribbean region in key climate resilience sectors in Renewable Energy, Electric Grid/Vehicle, Energy Efficiency, Blue Economy and Climate Smart Agriculture, across multiple countries of the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) i.e. Antigua & Barbuda, Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Grenada, Guyana, Jamaica, St. Kitts & Nevis, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Bahamas, St. Lucia, Suriname, and Trinidad & Tobago (The Project). The Project is expected to be supported by the IFC Frontier Opportunities Fund (FOF) as described in the Blended Finance Section. The CCE is a sub-fund of the CCRF, a new 10-year closed-end impact investment fund launched by the Fund Manager, Sygnus Capital Limited, and the anchor investor, the CARICOM Development Fund (CDF) in January 2024.
sponsor_shareholders: Sygnus Capital, a leading Pan-Caribbean alternative asset manager, was established in 2016 and headquartered in Jamaica with over US$600 million in assets under management. Sygnus has close to 90 professionals located across Jamaica, Saint Lucia, Puerto Rico and the United States.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is seeking to invest up to US$10 million comprising (i) up to US$5 million for its own account in the Senior C Tranche and (ii) up to US$5 million blended finance investment from the IFC FOF in the Junior D tranche.
location_description: The CCE will invest in Antigua & Barbuda, Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Grenada, Guyana, Jamaica, St. Kitts & Nevis, St. Lucia, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Bahamas, Suriname, and Trinidad & Tobago.
development_impact: The project will provide access to equity for mid-market companies in the Caribbean by supporting a fund that aims to scale companies targeting sustainability outcomes. In addition, the project is expected to enhance resilience in the Caribbean region by enabling critical investments across key infrastructure sectors and demonstrating alternative low-carbon technologies that diversify the regional energy mix, given that electricity generation in the Caribbean remains heavily reliant on fossil fuels.
additionality: IFC's additionality will be provided through its own account equity, as IFC’s commitment will help the Fund reach its target size. IFC support at the second close will be needed to mobilize capital from private investors at the third close, enabling the Fund to upsize its target size. Further, IFC will play a key role in standard-setting by improving the fund's environmental and social risk management system and by advising on gender practices, complementing the support provided by other DFIs.

project_description: The group of companies known as PRAN Group (PRAN or the Group) was established in 1981. The Group is a leading branded food and beverage group and the largest Agro processer in Bangladesh. PRAN is a well-known household brand in Bangladesh and produces more than four hundred food products across multiple categories including juices, drinks and beverages, dairy, confectionary, snacks, grains, spices, and frozen foods. PRAN exports to 145 countries across the world. IFC will provide long-term US Dollar financing to be utilized to support expansion plans across the two group companies, Pran Dairy Limited (PDL) and Mymensingh Agro Limited (MAL).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsors and shareholders of the Project companies consist of the children of the late Pran Group founder Major General Amjad Khan Chowdhury, Mr. Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, and Ms. Uzma Chowdhury (together, Sponsors).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to provide debt financing of an A Loan of US$35 million to PDL and MAL. The proposed A Loan has a tenor of 7 years with a 2-year grace period.
location_description: The Project is located in Bangladesh.
development_impact: Bangladesh continues to face food insecurity and nutrition challenges, alongside a large base of consumers with limited purchasing power. The Project is expected to strengthen market access for smallholder dairy farmers by expanding the company’s supplier network, supported by supply chain development, farmer training, feed support, and improved access to credit. It is also expected to increase the availability of safe, nutritious dairy products and lower sugar beverages for consumers. More broadly, the Project is anticipated to contribute to job creation, stronger formal employment, higher agricultural productivity, and wider economic linkages in Bangladesh. Besides, the beverage market is currently characterized by very high sugar consumption, with the vast majority of carbonated and dairy beverages containing high sugar levels, posing material health concerns. The Project aims to introduce and scale lower-sugar beverages through PRAN, a market leader, setting a visible benchmark that could catalyze broader industry reformulation over time.
additionality: IFC’s role combines long-term foreign-currency financing and targeted advisory support. Financial additionality is the provision of long-term US Dollar funding—limited in the local market—structured to match the project’s cash-flow needs and support PDL’s and MAL’s expansion. Non-financial additionality includes technical assistance to strengthen the dairy supply chain, reduce food loss and waste, improve product nutrition through fortification, and support gradual sugar reduction—helping set stronger industry benchmarks in Bangladesh

sector: Municipal Finance - Water, Wastewater, District Heating, and Waste [Project only]
project_description: The proposed Project is a loan to the City of Johannesburg (COJ or the City) of 750 million South African Rands (ZAR), equivalent to approximately US$47 million, with a tenor of 15 years. The proceeds of the loan will partially fund the City's capital investment program for water storage and distribution, including reservoir upgrading and refurbishment, pipe replacement, bulk mains rehabilitation and upgrading, metering, and pressure management equipment (the Project) to be implemented over FY2025/26 to FY2026/27.
sponsor_shareholders: The City, located in the Gauteng Province, is one of the most advanced commercial cities in Africa and the engine room of the South African and regional economy. The City provides electricity, water, waste and sanitation, and transport services to its residents. The City's water sector faces a number of challenges: most recently, water supply disruptions have become more frequent due to the constrained water supply from Rand Water and the need for system maintenance and repairs. Addressing the water infrastructure maintenance backlog is a crucial step towards improving water security and service delivery.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC's proposed loan of ZAR750 million (about US$47 million) will partially fund the City’s water storage infrastructure upgrade and refurbishment and water distribution infrastructure replacement and upgrading program. This is part of the City’s FY2025/26 and FY2026/27 water capital expenditure programs, of ZAR1.70 billion and ZAR1.96 billion respectively.
location_description: COJ is located in the northeastern part of South Africa, within the province of Gauteng.
development_impact: At the project level, the proposed investment focuses on improving water service delivery, water conservation, and demand management through a dedicated set of sub-projects to upgrade, refurbish and rehabilitate reservoir infrastructure and bulk water mains and other ageing assets. The interventions also target the reduction of non-revenue water (currently estimated at ~45%) through systematic pipe replacement and metering, which is expected to strengthen the financial viability of the utility while also easing demand pressures on the network. Beyond immediate outcomes, the pipeline of projects executed by the COJ are designed to build the city's long-term resilience by closing the investment gap in the water sector and creating the capacity necessary to meet future growth in water demand. The Project is also expected to yield demonstration effects to other large metros in South Africa to design and implement similar programs for improved water service delivery and demand management.
additionality: IFC's additionality stems from: (i) Financing structure: IFC will provide a ZAR-denominated loan with a tenor of 15 years which would be otherwise difficult for the client to obtain from commercial financiers. The tenor is aligned with the capital intensive nature of the investment program; (ii) Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: Under the Cities initiative, IFC will leverage its global experience to support COJ through advisory services, in areas to be determined.

project_description: The Facility for Energy Inclusion (FEI and/or the Fund) is a pan-African structured debt fund dedicated to financing decentralized renewable energy (DRE) projects in Africa. The Fund has total assets under management (AUM) of c.US$361 million and has, to date, deployed c.US$482 million in DRE assets within 25 countries, supporting multiple enterprises and creating jobs across the continent. Building on this, the Fund is looking to upsize to US$750 million AUM to further its impact across the region and deliver on an expanded mandate to increase access to affordable energy through investments in solar home systems, in addition to existing investments in other DRE subsectors, including mini-grids, small to medium scale independent power producer projects, telecommunications energy servicing companies, and commercial & industrial (C&I) energy operators. This is aligned with the World Bank Group’s M300 initiative. IFC’s proposed investment is an equity investment of up to US$40 million in the upsized Fund, subject to the total own account exposure not exceeding 20% of total Fund size and IFC not being the largest investor (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: FEI is managed by Cygnum Capital Group, an experienced investment banking and asset management firm with a strong record in frontier and emerging markets across sub-Saharan Africa. Cygnum Capital Group was established in 2018 and operates across four business lines, including (i) asset management, with total AUM of US$1.4 billion across 7 funds, (ii) financial advisory, (iii) corporate and investment banking, and (iv) sovereign finance, serving clients across multiple sectors. Limited Partners (LPs) in the Fund comprise African Development Bank (AfDB), KfW, Norfund, the European Commission (acting through AfDB as implementing agent), the Clean Technology Fund (acting through AfDB as implementing agent), and the Fund General Partner. IFC will become an LP through this investment.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total capital to be raised to reach the Fund’s target size of US$750 million is up to US$389 million, split into US$154 million in equity and up to US$235 million in debt. IFC’s investment is an equity investment of up to US$40 million. IFC seeks to mobilize up to US$150 million additional investments for the Fund.
location_description: FEI targets investments in DRE projects across Africa. IFC’s investment and other mobilized funds will be deployed in DRE investments across the region, with a focus on lower income countries.
development_impact: The Project will provide access to affordable and quality electricity supply to C&I and residential customers in Sub-Saharan Africa by financing renewable energy solutions. Most of the high and medium probability pipeline is targeting investees with operations in multiple countries. The electricity sector in target markets faces significant challenges including very low access, comparably high costs, and low quality of service. The Fund will provide debt financing to DRE solutions covering a wide range of sectors and customers of varying scale, from residential, to SMEs, corporates, and utilities. The Project also supports renewable energy solutions displacing power supplied by more carbon intensive sources (e.g., diesel gensets, electricity grids, kerosine) and is expected to reduce GHG emissions.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this project is anticipated to be financial. This includes providing senior equity of up to US$40 million that is not readily available in the market to support a specialized DRE debt platform of this size and profile. IFC is expected to play an anchor role in mobilizing additional equity which will enable the Fund to reach target size, while continuing its investment in countries that face higher inherent risks at a reasonable price for the borrower.

project_description: The proposed investment in Alema Koudijs Feed PLC (AKF or the Company) is to support the Company's expansion program on the existing feed mill in Bishoftu, Ethiopia (the Project). The Project is expected to be supported by the International Development Association's Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA-PSW LCF), as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: AKF is owned by De Heus Animal Nutrition BV (51%) and Alema Farms PLC (49%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is expected to be approximately US$12.3 million. The proposed investment is an own account A Loan of Up to US$10millionequivalentin Ethiopian Birr (ETB).
location_description: The Company's feed mill and the Project are based in Bishoftu, Ethiopia.
development_impact: Economy-wide effects: The project boosts Ethiopia's economy though increased local value addition and job creation, promoting local feed production. By strengthening linkages with suppliers, it supports economic diversification and addresses unemployment challenges. Stakeholder effects: Livestock farmers benefit from better-quality compound feeds and technical support. The project helps address crop and livestock productivity gaps but faces supply risks due to conflict in key regions. Market creation effect: The investment introduces innovations in feed formulation, marketing, and bulk storage to strengthen Ethiopia's livestock feed market. By using food processing byproducts, Alema Koudijs lowers costs and improves margins, while expanded storage ensures supply stability. Aligned with national and World Bank initiatives, the project fosters systemic changes, though competitor capacity limitations may constrain broader scalability.
additionality: Financial Additionality - Financing structure: IFC will provide the Company with a US$10 million equivalent local currency denominated long term financing otherwise not available in Ethiopia for agribusiness projects like the one proposed. Non-financial Additionality - Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC's involvement in the Project will benefit the Company through IFC's global industry knowledge, and connection with IFC's global network of players in the animal feed/livestock value chain and associated industries. The support will help address the current corporate governance and Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) compliance gaps in the sector and align AKF's operations with IFC Performance Standards and industry best practices. The Project will be complemented by an Advisory Services program to support the Company's biodiversity and child labor risk mitigation measures.

project_description: Provision of up to USD [100] million senior loan to AlDau Hospitality BV (AlDau Hospitality or the Company) or to its fully owned subsidiaries as part of a larger financing package amounting to up to USD [265] million equivalent, which is expected to be provided in parallel with local and/or international financial institutions, including the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). The loan will(i) finance the development of a new 400-key hotel in West Cairo in the vicinity of and overlooking the Grand Egyptian Museum and the Pyramids of Giza, (ii) refinance/consolidate existing debt (iii) finance other Capex-related investments, including acquisition of land and buildings and refurbishment Capex and (iv) fund future capex.
sponsor_shareholders: AlDau Hospitality, subsidiary of AlDau Development BV, is a leading hospitality company in Egypt, with a portfolio of 5 hotels under 2 complexes spanning over the Giza and Red Sea Governorates with a total of 1,800+ keys, while it intends to develop a new 400-key hotel in West Cairo. The Company is part of ADD Properties (formerly known as Aldau Development), the real estate arm of a larger multiline conglomerate owned by the Sami Saad family and active in a broad spectrum of business lines including commercial & residential real estate, food & beverage, engineering & contracting and passenger car assembling and trading.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide an up to USD [100] million senior loan to finance the project
location_description: The new hotel will also be located in Cairo.
development_impact: The tourism sector is an important contributor to the Egyptian economy. IFC expects that the Project will contribute to both direct and indirect employment creation, forex earnings to Egypt, and further contribute to Egypt’s economy through value addition, supply chain development, domestic purchases of goods and services, and local linkages to other sectors of the economy.
additionality: IFC's involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide scarce long-term hard currency financing with a tenor and grace period not available in the market. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will contribute to helping the Company improve its capacity in the areas of E&S and corporate governance.

project_description: Incorporated in 2021, Redcliffe Lifetech Private Limited (Redcliffe or the Company) is a fast-growing, pan-India diagnostics service provider operating through a hub-and-spoke model to deliver quality and affordable pathology and radiology services, with a focus on Tier II and Tier III cities. IFC is proposing an equity investment of up to US$30 million (INR equivalent) in Redcliffe to support the Company's growth plans, including acquisitions and capital expenditure (the Project).The Project represents an opportunity for IFC to support the expansion of a pan-India, omni-channel, integrated diagnostics and radiology platform, while improving access to quality diagnostic services for patients with non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in underserved markets.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is led by founders, Aditya Kandoi (Founder and CEO) and Dheeraj Jain (Founder and Non-Executive Chairman), who collectively hold ~19% shareholding in the Company on a fully diluted basis. The company also is a portfolio company of LeapFrog Investments, Chiratae Ventures India, Impact Fund Denmark (IFDK), Alkemi Growth Capital LLP, and HealthQuad Fund, amongst others.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment is an equity investment of up to $30 million in INR equivalent through Compulsorily Convertible Debentures (CCDs).
location_description: The Company’s registered office is located in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India. It has ~76 labs and ~1500+ collection centers all over the country.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is increased access to high-quality, affordable diagnostics in India. At the market level, the investment is expected to contribute to sustaining the development of India’s diagnostics market by augmenting and expanding Redcliffe’s digital-first, direct-to-consumer hub-and-spoke model of diagnostic services. As India's population has rapidly grown, so has its need to deliver high-quality healthcare services. While the performance of India's health system has improved, significant gaps remain in access to and the quality of healthcare. Communicable diseases like dengue fever and chikungunya are still widespread, while the burden of non-communicable diseases continues to rise. Greater investment in healthcare infrastructure, technology, and the workforce is needed. Redcliffe aims to address the gaps in access to diagnostics by providing affordable diagnostic tests through its “digital-first” front end and extensive lab network. The Project will support the Company's expansion by supporting its growth plans through financing the acquisition of regional diagnostic and radiology platforms and capital expenditure. The Project’s efforts to acquire and augment these radiology companies and integrate them into its digital direct-to-consumer diagnostics model are expected to improve access to diagnostics in India, particularly in Tier II and Tier III cities. At the market level, the Project is expected to contribute to increasing the competitiveness of the diagnostics sector in India. By augmenting Redcliffe's business model with greater radiology capabilities through acquisition, the Project will help sustain the development of India's fragmented diagnostics market to consolidate, formalize while being affordable.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality is provided through IFC’s own account equity. IFC’s quasi-equity investment of up to US$30 million (INR equivalent) is expected to provide long-term, patient growth capital to enable the Company’s organic and inorganic expansion, while strengthening the Company’s balance sheet, creditworthiness, and institutional governance. IFC’s participation is also expected to have a signaling effect with other institutional capital providers, supporting the Company’s ability to diversify funding sources as it scales and prepares for an IPO. Non-financial additionality is provided through knowledge, innovation and capacity building. Through IFC’s healthcare advisory and active engagement, IFC will work with the Company to (i) assess and implement operational improvement opportunities, including strengthening systems and processes for quality management and service delivery as the platform scales; (ii) support institutionalization of governance, internal controls, and reporting frameworks appropriate for a scaled network; (iii) strengthen the Company’s environmental and social (E&S) capacity and management systems in line with IFC Performance Standards; and (iv) support diligence of identified acquisition targets during appraisal, to ensure that inorganic growth is executed with appropriate operational, governance, and E&S rigor and is aligned with intended development outcomes. IFC’s engagement with the company on PPRR efforts under the GCPH will potentially enable the company to position itself as a thought leader in the industry and access new business opportunities related to advanced disease surveillance and diagnostics.

project_description: Manuka SpA (“Manuka” or the “Company”) is a Chilean milk producer located in southern regions of Los Lagos and Los Rios, operating a pasture-based dairy production model. Manuka is a founding member of Campos Australes, Chile’s second-largest dairy cooperative, which has grown to represent approximately 80 predominantly small-scale farmers. IFC’s proposed investment will support Manuka’s investment program, including the rearing of youngstock and investments in soil fertility and pasture productivity, and limited refinancing (the “Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Manuka was founded in 2005 by over 100 New Zealand dairy farmers who collectively maintain a majority ownership. No investor individually holds control.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of an IFC A-loan of up to CLP 55 billion (approximately US$65 million equivalent) to support Manuka’s investment program, including the rearing of youngstock and investments in soil fertility and pasture productivity, and limited refinancing.
location_description: Investments will be made at Manuka’s dairy farms, located in the southern regions of Los Rios and Los Lagos (Chile).
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate economy-wide effects in terms of job creation and value addition and have positive environmental effects by improving soil fertility. At a market level, IFC expects its financing to contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of the dairy farming sector in Chile by further strengthening and showcasing the New Zealand-style pasture grazing system with superior productivity and cost competitiveness.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is both financial and non financial. Financially, IFC will provide long term financing through a sustainability linked loan to support Manuka’s investment program and capital mobilization. Non financially, IFC may support the Project through targeted advisory services to the cooperative, alongside the adoption of IFC’s environmental and social standards to further strengthen sustainability practices.

project_description: New Hope Singapore Pte Ltd (NHS, or the Company) is one of the largest animal feed producers in Southeast Asia. NHS is a wholly owned subsidiary of New Hope Liuhe Co., Ltd. (“NHLL”), part of the New Hope Group (“the Group”), a long-standing strategic partner of IFC. NHS serves as the overseas arm of the Corporate, owning and operating 48 facilities including 39 operational feed mills and several broiler breeding farms and hatcheries, across 14 countries outside China. IFC will provide an A Loan of up to US$150 million, to support the Company's capital expenditure and working capital needs for planned new feed mill production lines in Bangladesh, Cambodia, Egypt, Nepal, and Viet Nam (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: NHS is wholly owned by New Hope Liuhe Co., Ltd. (NHLL). Mr. Liu Yonghao and family is the sponsor and controlling shareholder of NHLL.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be US$214 million. IFC's proposed investment is an A Loan of up to US$150 million. The balance of the Project cost will be financed by internal cash generation.
location_description: The Project is located in Bangladesh, Cambodia, Egypt, Nepal, and Viet Nam.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the stakeholder (farmers, distributors) and economywide effects (local value addition, job creation). Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that investment will have deepening market catalytic effects in improving sector competitiveness.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality will be provided via financing structure not otherwise available for agribusinesses in the local markets. Non-financial additionality is supplied via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment aims to support M'Bouna, a leading wheat flour miller in Mali with ~30% market share, through an 8-year senior-secured 10 million loan to implement Phase 2 of its expansion program. The project will finance the construction of a 4.3 MW solar PV plant with 12.16 MWh storage and the acquisition of fuel-efficient trucks, reducing high energy and logistics costs driven by Mali's unreliable grid and diesel dependence. This follows a successful first expansion that increased milling capacity to 500 tons/day and added a feed line. The investment will strengthen the company's competitiveness, energy security, and operational efficiency while supporting food-security resilience in Mali. The Project is expected to be supported by IDA PSW and IFC's Concessional Capital Window (CCW) as described in the Blended Finance section.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Sanankoroba (34 km south to the capital Bamako), M'Bouna is the largest flour mill producer in Mali, holding around 30% market share. This 100% family-owned business was established by Mr. Abdoulaye Hamidou Cisse, 65 years old, a reputable Malian entrepreneur and sole shareholder of M'Bouna SA. The Company is now run on a day-to-day basis by his son Mohamed Cisse who is the Managing Director.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The package will comprise (i) an 8-year (incl. 3-year grace) A Loan of up to EUR 5 million, and (ii) an equivalent loan of up to EUR 5 million from IDA Private Sector Window and CCW-21, subordinated in payments and liquidation to IFC’s A loan. The total Project cost is EUR 33.8 million and includes (i) Phase 1 (completed): EUR 22.8 million capex related to the expansion of the flour mill capacity and (ii) Phase 2: up to EUR 11 million senior-secured loan to fund capex for the solar power plant (EUR 7.5 million), purchase a strategic fleet of 30 wheat delivery trucks (EUR 3 million) and a contingency of 5% (EUR 0.5 million). Phase 2 will be funded by IFC (EUR 10 million) and Internal Cash Generation (EUR 1 million).
location_description: The project is located in Sanankoroba, ~34 km south of the capital city, Bamako
development_impact: The project is expected to contribute to domestic food security by enabling additional production of fortified wheat flour. It will generate employment opportunities by creating new direct jobs in a context with high levels of employment informality. The project will also produce environmental co-benefits, supporting climate mitigation through renewable energy generation, which is expected to reduce the Company’s emissions and the carbon intensity of its wheat flour production. The project is expected to deliver positive market outcomes by enhancing competitiveness in the wheat flour production sector, by expanding the adoption of cost-saving business practices (solar energy generation, in-house transportation) that will reduce production and logistics costs and address key supply-side bottlenecks.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing Structure: The proposed financing package of €10M, with an 8-year tenor and 3-year grace period, is not readily available to agribusinesses on the local market. This includes support from blended finance. From December 2024 to December 2025, there were neither EUR syndicated loans nor EUR corporate bond issuances at a corresponding rating of B+/- in Mali. Non-financial Additionality: Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC is exploring provision of advisory services to support the Company with engaging smallholder farmers and cooperatives at its farm in Selingue, with a particular focus on women, and technical and agronomical support for the nucleus farm. IFC will support M’Bouna to hire Corporate Governance and E&S advisors, and may provide technical assistance for the establishment of the Baking Academy. Standard-setting: With support from IFC, the Company will improve its E&S standards to comply with IFC Performance Standards, including implementation of an ESAP.

sector: Other Support Activities for Transportation (Grain Terminals, Cargo Terminals)
project_description: Leap India Food & Logistics Private Limited (“Leap India” or “Sponsor”) is a leading Indian company specializing in modern agricultural warehousing and logistics. With over 30% market share in India, it is developing a national network of agri-storage silos under the Food Corporation of India (FCI)’s Public Private Partnership (PPP) program. The project entails the construction of scientific storage silos with a total capacity of 1.725 million metric tonnes (MMT), under a 32.25-year PPP concession with the FCI.
sponsor_shareholders: Leap India is ultimately held 40% by Government of Singapore Investment Corporation Affiliates (GIC- through Dagenham Investment Pte Limited), 33.48% by Mr. Rajeev Akshay Karthikeyan (Co-founder), 22.32% by Mr. Anurag Malempati (Co-founder) and 4.2% by Siemens Project Ventures GMBH (Siemens).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Leap India is raising debt financing of up to INR equivalent of US$ 180 million, of which IFC is considering a straight senior loan of up to INR equivalent of US$ 80 million.
location_description: Leap India is registered in the state of Tamil Nadu, India with corporate headquarters in Telangana, India. It's projects are located across various states in India.
development_impact: The Project is expected to improve access to modern logistics infrastructure for agricultural commodities in India and reduce food loss resulting in lower greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. At the market level, the Project is expected to enhance the competitiveness of the agriculture supply chain by scaling efficient logistics solutions to serve India’s national food schemes, leading to enhanced food security.
additionality: IFC's additionality is both financial and non-financial. IFC’s investment will provide critical debt financing to Leap to expand modern steel silo infrastructure in India, strengthening the efficient procurement, storage, and distribution of foodgrains under national food security programs. In addition, IFC’s own account investment is expected to catalyze mobilization of private capital from parallel lenders, leveraging its participation and signaling effect. Beyond financing, IFC will provide technical guidance to strengthen Leap’s E&S risk management framework, including the development and implementation of action plans aligned with IFC Performance Standards (PSs).

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a corporate debt facility to OCP SA (“OCP” or the “Company,” https://www.ocpgroup.ma/ ) to finance the development of an inland phosphogypsum (“PG”) storage facility of up to 22 million tons capacity capacity, with a storage height of 60 m, in Jorf Lasfar, Morocco (the “Project”). OCP generates PG as a by-product in the production of phosphoric acid for phosphate fertilizers. The Project helps support sustainable PG management.
sponsor_shareholders: OCP S.A., a state-owned enterprise, is a fully integrated phosphate fertilizer producer with operations at every stage from mining to processing to sales of phosphate products. The Company is the largest producer and exporter of phosphate rock and phosphoric acid globally. OCP’s shareholders are the Moroccan State and other minority shareholders with, respectively, 94.12% and 5.88% ownership.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project’s costs is approximately EUR190 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to EUR95 million.
location_description: The Project is located on the Company’s fertilizers production site in Jorf Lasfar, Morocco.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is to store phosphogypsum (PG) instead of discharging it into the ocean via outfalls, and to enable future valorization options that could improve resource preservation. Beyond these project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote competitiveness in fertilizers industry through introducing a necessary step for future valorization of PG that can be scaled via replication channels.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is in the form of: (i) Financing structure; (ii) Resource Mobilization; (iii) Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building; and (iv) E&S standard-setting.

project_description: Founded in 1982, GDM Argentina S.A. is a leading global seed genetics company specializing in high-productivity soybean and other crop varieties. The IFC Project will support the breeding R&D program in Argentina, helping GDM Argentina to develop new seed varieties that aim to increase yield in corn, soybean and wheat, which helps to reduce the agri carbon footprint.
sponsor_shareholders: GDM is 100% owned by the Bartolome family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$50mn. The proposed IFC investment is a US$50 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: R&D activities are held in rural areas in Argentina suitable for soybean, corn and wheat production.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to improve access to high yielding seeds for farmers, to generate positive climate adaptation effects, and to produce economy wide effects in terms of job creation and value addition. Beyond the Project, IFC expects its financing to contribute to improving the resilience of the soybean, corn and wheat farming sectors in Argentina by demonstrating innovations in seed variety development with far-reaching impact on agricultural sector resilience.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the Project will be both financial, including: i) financing structure; ii) resource mobilization; iii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building; and iv) standard setting.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment aims to support Societe Diarra Negoce (“SDN” or the “Company), a Mali-based agribusiness and logistics operator, in developing a new milling complex in Banankoro, Koulikoro region (the “Project”). The Project will comprise: (i) a 300 tons-per-day wheat flour mill; (ii) 20,000 MT of grain storage capacity; and (iii) a 2.3MW solar power installation. The total Project cost is estimated at €18.6 million, covering both capital expenditure and associated working capital. The Project is expected to benefit from blended finance support through the IDA Private Sector Window (PSW) and IFC’s Concessional Capital Window (CCW), as described in the Blended Finance section.
sponsor_shareholders: SDN is incorporated in Mali as a private limited company. The Company is wholly owned by the founder, Mr. Sekou Diarra.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project is estimated at €18.6 million. IFC will provide a €13 million corporate loan facility, consisting of: (i) a €6.5 million IFC A loan; (ii) a €4.875 million IDA PSW BFF loan; and (iii) a €1.625 million CCW-21 loan, as described in the Blended Finance Section. The remaining financing will be provided by the sponsor.
location_description: The Project will be located on SDN’s existing site in Banankoro, Koulikoro region, about 15-20 km from Bamako.
development_impact: (i) The Project will expand consumer access to safe, high-quality wheat products in Mali, where demand is high and growing, thereby contributing to improving local food security in a country with a high Global Hunger Index score. The Client may also implement a fortification program, which would add essential micronutrients that would help to combat widespread malnourishment. (ii) The bran produced as a by-product of wheat milling is a critical raw material input for animal feed production, which will increase as a result of the Project, benefiting the animal protein value chain. The Project is also expected to contribute to local economic activity through value addition and direct and indirect job creation. IFC expects this Project to increase the competitiveness of wheat flour production in Mali by expanding production and introducing new business practices.
additionality: IFC’s financial additionality stems from its ability, with support from the IDA PSW BFF, to provide long term financing that is otherwise unavailable to agribusiness companies in the local market. Non financial additionality will be delivered through IFC advisory support, including planned engagements on food safety and financial management to strengthen the Company’s capacity. IFC will also help the Company strengthen its environmental and social practices to meet IFC Performance Standards.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a US$20 million A Loan to Grupo Agronorte (“Agronorte” or the “Company”), a family-owned business based in Tocantinopolis, Tocantins, in northern Brazil. Agronorte is an agribusiness group operating across animal feed production, grain trading and logistics, agro-retail stores and grain storage services. The project aims to support the acquisition and restart of operations of an animal feed plant in Tres Coracoes, Minas Gerais, Brazil, previously owned by ADM (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Agronorte is owned by the Goncalves Carvalho Family. The founder, Gilmar Goncalves Carvalho holds the majority of the Company and the remaining is owned by his wife and their three sons.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of an IFC A loan for IFC’s own account of US$20 million.
location_description: The project will be developed in Tres Coracoes, Minas Gerais, Brazil.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate jobs and value addition to the Brazilian economy, and improve access to feed for farmers. Beyond the Project, IFC expects its financing to contribute to improving the competitiveness of the animal nutrition sector in Brazil by showcasing the transformation of a regional producer to become a nationally relevant producer and exporter.
additionality: IFC will provide both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality includes (i) long-term financing, (ii) resource mobilization (PCM). Non-financial additionality encompasses (i) corporate governance advisory and (ii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building from IFC global knowledge and expertise in environmental and social matters.

project_description: Interoc S.A. and its subsidiaries (Interoc or the Group) is a mid-sized multinational agribusiness group of Ecuadorian origin with over 30 years of experience specializing in high-yield maize and rice seeds and crop protection solutions. The Group operates with a vertically integrated model and a strong focus on research and development, enabling it to deliver differentiated products and technical assistance to farmers and distributors. Interoc has a regional presence across Ecuador, Peru, Colombia, and Central America. The proposed project will finance the development of a rice seeds germplasm program allowing the Group to distribute the first hybrid rice seed variety in the Andean Region, with higher yields and improved resilience to climate variability, while also strengthening the Group’s capacity for the production and distribution of hybrid maize seeds.
sponsor_shareholders: Interoc is fully owned by Mr. Felipe Antonio Custer Hallet, a well-known member of the business community in Peru. The Custer family arrived in Peru over a hundred years ago and has had investments in multiple industries across the country.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$20m. IFC is proposing an A Loan of up to US$20m for IFC's own account to support the Company in the development of the project.
location_description: Investments will be made at Interoc's facilities located in Ecuador, including sites in the provinces of Santa Elena, Guayas, and Los Ríos. These include the San Rafael seed multiplication farm, the Palestina research facilities, and the Buena Fe seed processing and distribution facility, which are located in established agricultural area.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to improve access to high-yield hybrid maize and rice seeds and technical assistance for farmers, and to generate economy wide effects in terms of job creation and value addition. Beyond the Project, IFC expects its financing to contribute to improving the resilience of the rice production sector in Ecuador by catalyzing productivity improvement through supporting the launch of the first hybrid rice seeds in the country.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the project will be both financial and non-financial: (i) Financial additionality will be provided through the provision of long-term financing with a tenor not readily available in the market. (ii) Non-financial additionality will be provided in the form of (a) knowledge sharing and capacity building through advisory services focused on reducing Interoc's operational carbon footprint and strengthening climate resilience, and (b) standard setting by supporting the Group with guidance to adopt good practice standards, including enhancing labor practices at its farm facilities and implementing improvements to its environmental and social management system.

sector: Household Appliances (Including Refrigerators, Laundry Machine, Dishwashers, etc.)
project_description: Dreame Technology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd (“Dreame”, or the “Company”), established in 2017 and headquartered in Jiangsu province, China, is a fast-growing developer and manufacturer of energy-efficient cleaning and small home appliances. IFC will provide an A Loan of up to US$60 million, to support the Company’s planned development of a local ecosystem for product development, procurement, production, and distribution in Southeast Asia – initially focused on Viet Nam, Malaysia, and Thailand (the Project). IFC will also mobilize additional term lending from commercial banks.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Yu Hao is Dreame’s single largest shareholder, with direct ownership of 31.15%. His total effective stake amounts to 62.30%, while the remaining financial investors hold minority stakes in the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment is an A Loan of up to US$60 million.
location_description: The Project is located in developing countries in Southeast Asia.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the economywide effects, stakeholder (employee) effects, and stakeholder (supplier) effects. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that investment will have deepening market catalytic effects in improving sector competitiveness.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality will be provided via financing structure and resource mobilization, including a parallel loan from commercial banks. Non-financial additionality is supplied via standard setting including enhancement in E&S standards.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to $40m senior loan, with $20m being for IFC’s own account and $20m mobilized, to Nile Agriculture Company S.A.E. (“NAC”), to be guaranteed by Nile Sugar Company S.A.E. (“NS” or the “Company”, and together with NAC, the “Obligors” or “NSG”. NS, founded by the Sawiris family (the “Sponsors”) in 2006, is a leading Egyptian beet sugar refinery producing white sugar and its by-products, including molasses and beet pulp. IFC’s loan will be used to finance the development of 13,711 feddans (5,760 hectares) land in Minya, Egypt to cultivate sugar beet and improve its supply chain sustainability, together with required relating infrastructure, machinery and equipment, and working capital (the “Project”). The Project will directly and indirectly help address increased sugar consumption in Egypt through local production vs. imports.
sponsor_shareholders: NS is a well-established Egyptian joint stock company engaged exclusively in sugar production within Egypt. Its main shareholders, Mr. Naguib Sawiris and Mrs. Yousriya Loza who, own, directly and indirectly, 99.6% of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s own account exposure is US$20 million within a total financing package of US$40 million to be utilized to finance NAC’s US$68.5 million investment program.
location_description: Egypt
development_impact: Stakeholders-Farmers: IFC expects the Project to increase access to beet inputs and output markets for smallholder farmers. The Project, through an out-grower scheme, is expected to provide beet seeds, credit and transportation services to 25,000 farmers while also training farmers to adopt climate smart production and post-harvest management practices, which is also expected to standardize quality and consistency of supplies while minimizing losses.
