Environmental effects: The Project is expected to make a significant contribution to addressing acute climate challenges through solutions that are on a low-carbon and climate-resilient pathway leading to reduction of GHG emissions. The total climate finance portion of the Project is estimated at 54.0%, with 53.1% contributing to climate adaptation and 0.9% contributing to climate mitigation. Economy wide effects: The Project is expected to increase domestic value addition and create jobs along the supply chains through up- and down-stream linkages with related sectors. Competitiveness: The investment will generate market-deepening effects by increasing beet sugar processing, while introducing innovations that significantly improve production and processing performance and efficiencies and maintain the requisite food safety requirements. The scalability of the vertical integration model and adoption of high yielding beet varieties is expected to promote wider adoption across the sector, fostering a growing ecosystem that supports development and integration of farmers in beet supply chains while catalyzing adoption of sustainable practices.
additionality: Financial additionality: Financing structure: IFC offers financing on terms not otherwise available for agribusiness in the local markets. Non-financial additionality: Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC's global industry knowledge will help align the Company's operations with IFC Performance Standards and industry best practices. The expertise in beet farm management will enable the Company to run farm operations efficiently.

company_name: Global Infrastructure Partners Emerging Markets Fund II LP (Cayman)
country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: The proposed investment is for a commitment of up to US$100 million, along with a proposed co-investment envelope of US$75 million, in the Global Infrastructure Partners Emerging Markets Fund II (the “Fund” or “EM II”), a fund focusing on investments in infrastructure assets or business across four sectors: Energy, Transport, Digital and Water/Waste.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by Global Infrastructure Partners (“GIP”), a leading infrastructure investor.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment is up to US$100 million, along with a proposed co-investment envelope of US$75 million.
location_description: The Fund will invest across emerging markets primarily in Asia, Latin America, and the countries comprising the Gulf Cooperation Council (“the Target Countries”) and up to 15% of Fund commitments outside the Target Countries, which may potentially include Africa, and Central and/or Eastern Europe
development_impact: Expected development impact outcomes include i) increased access to equity financing across emerging markets, addressing critical infrastructure needs and delivering increased access to quality infrastructure; and (ii) scaling private capital mobilization that supports emerging market infrastructure needs.
additionality: IFC’s commitment is expected to support the mobilization of additional private institutional capital, enhance the Fund’s ability to scale infrastructure platforms across emerging markets , and reinforce the application of international governance, environmental and social standards across portfolio companies. IFC’s engagement will further contribute through its advisory expertise, convening role, and collaboration on ESG integration and innovative financing structures, strengthening development outcomes and supporting sustainable private sector infrastructure investment across emerging markets.
Company Name: Global Infrastructure Partners Emerging Markets Fund II LP (Cayman)
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: Grands Hotels de Mauritanie SA (GHM), is a special purpose vehicle (SPV) set up for the development of a 200-key Edge-certified upper upscale business hotel in Nouakchott, Mauritania to be operated by Marriott International under the Sheraton brand (the “Project”)
sponsor_shareholders: SNIM (62 percent shareholder of GHM) is a State-owned Enterprise (SOE) responsible for managing Mauritania’s mining assets and is the country’s largest company with revenues estimated at ~US$1.3 billion (12 percent of Mauritania nominal GDP). The other two shareholders (Al Raja Holdings and Wafa Holdings, each holding a 19 percent stake in GHM) are two of Mauritania’s largest private sector conglomerates (active in construction, banking, transport, agribusiness, real estate, and mining).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be up to US$90 million. The Proposed investment is an up to US$15 million equivalent in EUR for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project is located in Nouakchott (Mauritania).
development_impact: The Projet is expected to have positive Project-level outcomes through improved access to business infrastructure and suppliers through supply chain development. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater competitiveness in the tourism sector in Mauritania through improved availability and quality of product and service offerings in the market.
additionality: IFC's financial additionality is delivered through provision of long-term financing with maturity not readily available in the market. Non-financial additionality is delivered through provision of technical expertise including implementation of ESMS and provision of technical guidance on green building standards along with necessary support for EDGE certification.

project_description: The proposed project is an equity investment of up to $5 million in a healthcare technology platform, Carpl.AI, Inc (CARPL or the Company). Launched in 2021, the Company operates a global artificial intelligence (AI) marketplace and orchestration platform that accelerates the adoption of AI models in radiology and healthcare systems, improving patient outcomes.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded by Dr. Vidur Mahajan. Its shareholders include the founder, early employees, individual angel investors and an institutional investor.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC equity investment is up to US$5 million.
location_description: CARPL’s operations are based out of New Delhi, India and it serves clients worldwide. It plans to expand further in emerging markets including in India and Latin America.
development_impact: Project outcomes involve increased access to AI-enabled radiology tools for healthcare providers in emerging markets including in India and in Latin America, resulting in improved diagnostic capacity and health outcomes. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that the investment will contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of the healthcare sector in the target emerging markets, by deepening the diagnostics segment by inducing market-wide uptake of AI-based technologies for radiology and by enabling framework and capacity building channels.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is expected to be primarily non- financial and expected to include (i) knowledge, capacity building and innovation; and (ii) standard setting. Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building will involve IFC’s support to enable Company’s scale-up in emerging markets, by connecting the Company with healthcare providers that could become potential customers. Furthermore, IFC is expected to provide advice to the Company on regulatory and data policies across emerging markets. Standard setting involves IFC support to enhance its corporate governance and environmental and social practices.

project_description: Tecnomyl S.A. (“Tecnomyl” or the “Company”) is an agrochemicals producer and wholesale distributor, headquartered in Villeta, Paraguay. Founded in 1991, the Company has over 30 years of experience formulating and commercializing post-patent crop protection products such as herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, and fertilizers. The proposed investment consists of: (i) an “A” loan facility of up to US$20 million to support the construction and expansion of a biological products plant in Villeta, the development of a logistics center in Ciudad del Este, and to finance related working capital needs; and (ii) an “A” loan facility of up to US$100 million to be made available through five one-year commitments of up to US$20 million each to support the operations of Tecnomyl (the “Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is fully owned by the Sarabia family which has more than 30 years of experience in the Paraguayan agribusiness sector. Its president and founder, Jose Marcos Sarabia, has a 62% shareholding stake.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of: (i) an up to US$20 million long-term A loan; and (ii) an up to US$20 million A Loan, renewable each year, for a total of five years.
location_description: The investments will be made in Paraguay, with the biologicals plant located in Villeta and the logistics center located in Ciudad del Este.
development_impact: The Project will support Paraguay’s economy by establishing a biological inputs plant and a logistics center, contributing to new employment and higher value added. It will also expand the use of biological crop protection products, improving soil health, strengthening resilience to climate shocks, and promoting more sustainable farming practices.
additionality: In addition to providing long-term financing, IFC will bring value through advisory services to promote and expand the use of biological products in Paraguay. Tecnomyl will adopt IFC's environmental and social standards to strengthen sustainability practices.

project_description: IFC’s investment is up to €60 million in bond(s) to be issued by Titan Global Finance UK PLC, a subsidiary of Titan SA (Titan or the Company). The Project comprises financing of Titan’s investment program in Albania, Bulgaria, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Serbia (the Project Countries), including energy-efficiency solutions, low-CO2 cement alternatives, fly ash processing and utilization, and increased use of alternative fuels.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1902 and headquartered in Greece, Titan is an international producer of cement and building materials. The Company operates a network of more than 260 facilities in over 15 countries across four continents. Titan’s shares have been listed on Euronext Brussels, Euronext Paris, and the Athens Exchange since 2019. As of December 15, 2025, the founding shareholders – the Papalexopoulos and Canellopoulos families - held 48.9 percent of shares. The remainder consisted of treasury shares of 5 percent, and balance in free float.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: On January 9, 2026, IFC’s board authorized an investment of up to €60 million in bond(s) to be issued by Titan Global Finance UK PLC. IFC’s investment will be used for Titan’s capex program in the Project Countries, including energy-efficiency solutions, low-CO2 cement alternatives, fly ash processing and utilization, and increased use of alternative fuels. On 4 February 2026, IFC invested €15 million in Titan’s 5-year bond. The IFC Investment represented 4% of the total issue size of €350 million. The bond will be listed on the Irish Stock Exchange.
location_description: Project assets are located in Albania, Bulgaria, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Serbia.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level development outcomes are: (i) environmental effects via greenhouse gases reduction through increased use of AF, supplementary cementitious materials and energy efficiency projects, and (ii) economywide effects through value creation by advancing circular economy principles and increasing productivity through improvement in supply chain management. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will address critical sustainability challenges and carbon reduction objections.
additionality: IFC’s role lies in enhancing investor participation and strengthening Titan’s access to long-term capital to advance its investment roadmap. IFC is also providing upstream advisory support to enable the use of fly ash to reduce costs by lowering clinker and emissions in cement production, hence promoting circularity, resource efficiency, and strengthening industrial competitiveness.

project_description: IFC will support part of the investment program of Adriatic Marinas d.o.o. (the Company), which includes developing a sports and wellness-focused hotel, food and non-food retail, a creative industry space, an outpatient clinic, and related infrastructure in Montenegro (The Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Adriatic Marinas d.o.o., based in Montenegro, is a mixed-use developer, wholly owned by PM Holdings One Person Company LLC. PM Holdings One Person Company LLC (together with its subsidiaries, the Group), based in the United Arab Emirates, is indirectly wholly owned by the Investment Corporation of Dubai (ICD). ICD is a sovereign wealth fund of the Government of Dubai.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s financing package comprises an €85 million A Loan and a €65 million B Loan to the Group. Total project cost is estimated at €150 million. IFC will benefit from a guarantee from ICD Hospitality & Leisure LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of ICD.
location_description: All investments under the Project are planned to be made in Tivat, Montenegro.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to create jobs, increase business opportunities, and build the capacity of local suppliers, particularly small and medium enterprises. Beyond the Project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater market competitiveness and sustainability in the tourism sector via competitive pressure and demonstration effects.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via scarce long-term financing to the Group that is not otherwise readily available in the local market. Non-financial additionality is provided via capacity building through standard setting in E&S management.

project_description: IFC is supporting Estithmar Holding Q.P.S.C. (“Estithmar” or “the Group”), a leading diversified Qatari group listed on the Doha stock exchange, with a financing package of up to US$249 million. The IFC financing will be used for i) developing and putting into operations a 321-room hotel (“Project Hotel”) within a residential and hospitality complex, which is being constructed by the Group in Baghdad, Iraq, and ii) corporate purposes to support the balance sheet of the Group and its operations in emerging markets, together (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Estithmar was listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange in 2017, with a market capitalization of US$3.9 billion, as of December 2025. Its controlling shareholder is the founding Al-Khayyat family?and its companies (78.2%), with the remaining shares held by public and other institutions and retail investors (21.8%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated Project cost is US$531 million, which includes US$411 million to be deployed for the development of the Project Hotel, with US $249 million of the total Project cost amount to be covered by the proposed IFC investment. The proposed IFC investment consists of (i) $129 million to fund the Project Hotel; and (ii) $120 million corporate tranche to strengthen the Group’s balance sheet and support the Group’s initiatives in emerging markets.
location_description: The Project is located in Baghdad, Iraq and Doha, Qatar.
development_impact: The most significant project-level outcomes include: (i) stakeholder effects on customers through increased purchases from local suppliers; and (ii) economy-wide effects through direct/indirect job creation and GDP contribution. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment will promote greater market competitiveness of Iraq’s hospitality sector.
additionality: Financial Additionality: The IFC Investment is structured to provide efficient support to Estithmar's investment in Iraq. The IFC Investment tenor is up to 10 years with a tailor-made sculpted repayment schedule which is not be readily available for Estithmar through its local banking network. Non-Financial Additionality: IFC will provide the Group with best practices and lessons learned from its global hospitality portfolio. In addition, IFC will also extend gender advisory services to support the Group to improve inclusive workplace practices. IFC's engagement is expected to provide guidance to enhance the Group's capacity to manage environmental and social (E&S) risks in accordance with IFC's Performance Standards (PS).

sector: Grocery Retail (Supermarkets, Hypermarkets, Convenience Stores etc.)
project_description: The proposed IFC’s financing consists of a senior secured loan of up to US$50 million or its equivalent in Euros (the IFC Loan) to Umai Group LLC (Umai, the Company or the Borrower), the largest retailer in the Kyrgyz Republic and LogoPark LLC, a newly established company (LogoPark or the Co-Borrower, and together, the Companies or Co-Borrowers). The IFC Loan will fund the Companies’ US$68 million investment program for 2026–2028, including US$33 million for the construction of 29,000m2 A-class distribution center by LogoPark near Bishkek and US$35 million for Umai’s capital expenditures to open new stores and redesign existing formats across the Kyrgyz Republic, an IDA country (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The Companies are solely owned by Snowbird Resources Ltd, a Cyprus-based intermediary holding company, wholly owned by Visor International DMCC (Visor). The Visor Group was established in 2001 and since 2016, Visor has been incorporated, registered and domiciled in the Dubai Multi Commodity Centre (UAE). Visor is a leading private equity holding company in Central Asia which specializes in active ownership and strategic investments across telecom, banking, FMCG, and renewables in Kazakhstan and the Kyrgyz Republic.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$68 million to be financed by the IFC Loan of up to US$50 million, with the remaining US$18 million to be financed through the internal cash generation of the Companies.
location_description: The Project will be implemented in the Kyrgyz Republic: the new distribution center will be built near Bishkek and the new stores across the country.
development_impact: The Project will increase consumer access to high-quality, affordable products, help modernize the Kyrgyz Republic’s grocery retail sector, drive efficiency gains in distribution, and enhance supply chain capacities.
additionality: IFC will provide large-scale, long-term financing with tenor, currency, and size uncommon in the local market. IFC will also strengthen the Companies’ E&S management, support international quality standards, and advise on EDGE certification, helping Umai’s new distribution center become the first EDGE-certified building in the Kyrgyz Republic.

project_description: IFC’s investment is up to €155 million (US$180 million) in senior, unsecured Eurobonds to be issued by VGP NV (VGP or the Company). The proceeds will finance the development of new low-carbon, energy-efficient industrial and logistics (I&L) properties in Romania and Serbia (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Antwerp, Belgium, VGP is a pan-European developer of I&L assets, operating in 18 countries with more than 100 parks and employing over 400 people. VGP is listed on Euronext Brussels Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s board authorized an investment of up to €155 million in the EU taxonomy-aligned Eurobonds of VGP. The proceeds of IFC’s investment will support development of energy-efficient, grade-A I&L parks in Serbia and Romania. On 16 January 2026, IFC invested €60 million in VGP’s 6-year green Eurobond. The IFC First Investment represented 10% of the total issue size of €600 million. The green Eurobond will be listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange (EuroMTF).
location_description: Serbia and Romania.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the stakeholder effects from increased access to quality I&L infrastructure that supports job creation, and improved resource efficiency of green buildings. Beyond the Project, the IFC investment is expected to contribute to enhance capital markets competitiveness by supporting the issuance of EU taxonomy-aligned corporate bonds.
additionality: IFC's role lies in enhancing private sector investor participation and knowledge, innovation and capacity buildings through IFC’s potential advisory offerings.

project_description: The proposed project involves two risk sharing facilities with Standard Chartered Bank (the “Bank” or “SCB”) for two trade finance facilities of up to US$230 million to support ETC Group (“ETG”) agri commodity trader’s export of cash and food grains, storage, and import of fertilizers in Sub Saharan Africa. IFC’s investment amount will be up to US$40 million. The Project will support the purchase, storage and sales of agri commodities and fertilizers in SSA countries such as Malawi, Benin, Kenya, Tanzania, etc. Commodities financed by the project are bought from mostly smallholder farmers in SSA and sold to wholesalers, cooperatives, NGOs and governments in various IDA countries and into the international market.
sponsor_shareholders: Standard Chartered Bank: a leading international banking group, with a presence in 54 of the world’s most dynamic markets. Its purpose is to drive commerce and prosperity through its unique diversity, and its heritage and values are expressed in the brand promise, here for good. Standard Chartered PLC is listed on the London, Hong Kong, Bombay (Mumbai) and India’s National stock exchanges. ETG: Since establishment in 1967, ETG has developed into a global player with a presence in more than 45 countries, spanning 6 continents. The Group has a diverse portfolio of expertise across various industries, encompassing agricultural inputs, chemicals, logistics, processing, food and food ingredients, energy, metals, technology and supply chain optimization. Over 7 000 employees contribute every day to achieve our vision and purpose, and live our values of Respect, Integrity, Pursuit of Excellence, Leadership and Meritocracy. ETG’s verticals are structured in a manner to emphasize focus and optimize strategic growth opportunities. ETG adapts and grows responsibly as a diversified enterprise, creating a sustainable future for all it's stakeholders. Ultimate beneficial owners of ETG together controlling 52.51% are Mr Mahesh Patel (Chairman), Mr Ketan Patel (Joint Group CEO) and Mr Birju Patel (Joint Group CEO). Other key stakeholders are Mitsui & Co Ltd via its African arm i.e MIT African Management Limited (31.9%) and Public Investment Corporation (13.9%) with the balance held by Executive Directors (1.69%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost will be up to US$230 million with IFC’s investment of up to US$40 million in the form of a funded and unfunded risk participation.
location_description: Standard Chartered is headquartered in London, United Kingdom, and has offices in 54 countries. The Bank’s Trade Risk Distribution is managed out of its Singapore hub. The proposed project will involve trade transactions mainly in east, south and west Africa.
development_impact: The anticipated development impacts of the Project are: (i) support of commodity trade finance for importers/exporters in emerging markets; (ii) increased access to trade finance for critical commodities, especially in the agro-commodity sector in emerging market; and (iii) Enhances competitiveness and market creation in agri-finance by linking funding sources to a regional commodity trader, improving access for farmers and agri-traders, and strengthening the value chain through better connectivity and imports of essential goods.
additionality: The proposed investment is an opportunity for IFC to help provide short-term liquidity to agri supply chain across Africa. IFC's support would continue encouraging greater activity in IDA countries and support smaller traders and processors.

project_description: The proposed investment is a senior loan of up to €11 million to Star Bright Holdings Limited (“Star Bright” or the “Group”) for its capital expenditure at its Kenya and Ethiopia farms and across group operations including but not limited to environmental and sustainability initiatives such as setting up water recycling at the packhouses and installation of energy efficient lighting (together “the Project”). Star Bright, domiciled in Mauritius, specializes in summer flowers production in East and Southern Africa under the “Marginpar” brand. The Group operates 10 flower farms in Kenya and Ethiopia, with a production output of ~220 million stems a year that are exported to the Europe and Asian markets. In addition, the Group sources flowers from three partner farms in Tanzania and four partner farms in Zimbabwe.
sponsor_shareholders: Star Bright is majority owned by PE funds, AgriVie and Norfund with 42% and 25%, respectively followed by co-Founder Richard Fernandes (19%) and Rob Koning (6%) with balance held by other minority shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide an up to €11 million senior loan to finance the Group’s €15.4 million capex program on its farms in Kenya and Ethiopia.
location_description: Ethiopia and Kenya.
development_impact: The primary anticipated outcome is the broad economic impact, including increased domestic value addition, job creation, and foreign exchange generation. In addition, IFC expects its financing to enhance market competitiveness through demonstration effects and opportunities for replication.
additionality: IFC will offer financing on terms that are not otherwise available to agribusinesses in the market. This funding is intended to strengthen the Company’s balance sheet, improve working capital management, and lower the impact of high local bank interest rates. Through its involvement, IFC will bring global industry expertise and access to its international network in the floriculture value chain and related sectors. This support will also help the Company align its operations with IFC Performance Standards and industry best practices.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an A Loan of up to US$70 million to Votorantim Cimentos S.A. (“VC” or the “Company”), a leading cement producer based in Brazil. The proposed project aims to support the modernization of the Salto plant by installing additional cement griding capacity as well as setting up: (i) a new cement silo; (ii) two bulk loading points; (iii) an interconnection of cement silos and; (iv) a new electrical substation. The completion of the project is expected by 2026.
sponsor_shareholders: Votorantim Cimentos S.A. is wholly owned by Votorantim S.A., a Brazilian multinational conglomerate, whose shareholders are members of the Ermirio de Moraes family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of an IFC A Loan, structured as a Sustainability Linked Loan, of up to US$70 million dollars to finance the Project.
location_description: The Salto plant is in the municipality of Salto de Pirapora in the state of Sao Paulo, southeast of Brazil.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to create positive environmental effects by reducing carbon intensity of cement production in the Company's Brazilian operation with a larger use of alternative fuels and by strengthening its commitment to a global decarbonization pathway. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to have a powerful market demonstration effect by incentivizing the issuance of sustainability linked loans in the cement sector, thus catalyzing more demanding standards in the industry.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality derives from the provision of long-term financing not otherwise readily available in the market and by the implementation of a sustainability linked loan, an innovative instrument that the company has introduced to the cement sector in Brazil. Non-financial additionality is provided via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building as IFC will (a) support the Company's decarbonization efforts, (b) help the client improve environmental and social standards and knowledge, and (c) through Gender Advisory Services, implement a Gender Assessment and customized Action Plan, aligned with IFC’s gender agenda, SDGs and VC's corporate goals, with targeted strategies to promote employee engagement, productivity, and inclusive practices for female workers.

project_description: The proposed investment is an 8-year IFC A-Loan to Fermav Industries (the “Company”), a subsidiary of Groupe SONOCO, S.A (“SONOCO”, the “Group”) a client based in Conakry, to support a greenfield poultry project in Guinea. The Group is a repeat IFC client since 2019 and is a Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) player and leader in the wheat milling industry. SONOCO has other subsidiaries and Fermav is the subsidiary dedicated to the integrated poultry farm. The ESRS and ESAP for the original project can be found in https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/40276/sonoco. IFC’s loan will support an integrated poultry operation consisting in three mains components: (i) the development of poultry facilities in Daboyah (including a breeding facility, several breeding houses and a hatchery with incubators) on the outskirts of Kindia town, (ii) the construction of a slaughterhouse in Massayah, and (iii) the construction of the feed mill in Sanoyah. Construction of all the facilities has commenced with some being nearly completed and others expected by March 2027.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group is owned by the Diallo family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide an up to $20 million senior loan to finance the Company’s $49 million investment program.
location_description: Guinea.
development_impact: The Project aims to enhance food security in the country by boosting local industrial production of fresh, safe, and affordable poultry products. It will also strengthen local poultry supply chains and support farmers, leading to increased productivity, higher incomes, and improved nutrition, while promoting a more inclusive and resilient agrifood system in Guinea.
additionality: IFC is offering financing options that are not typically available for greenfield agribusiness projects in Guinea, including a long-term senior loan. Additionally, IFC will contribute technical expertise and global experience in the poultry processing sector to help bring the Company's operations in line with international standards. Insights gained from similar projects will also provide valuable support throughout the Project's implementation.

project_description: OCI Terrasus Sdn. Bhd. (“OCI TRS” or the “Company”) is a leading global producer of traceable polysilicon and is headquartered in Kuching, Sarawak, Malaysia. The Company currently operates a polysilicon production facility in Bintulu, Sarawak, Malaysia. As of November 30, 2025, OCI TRS employed 1,101 people in Malaysia. The proceeds of the Project will be used to support: (i) the Company’s equity contributions into a joint venture with Tokuyama Corporation for the development of a semiconductor-grade polysilicon production facility in Bintulu, Sarawak, Malaysia; and (ii) the Company’s electricity procurement for its existing operations.
sponsor_shareholders: OCI TRS is a wholly-owned subsidiary of OCI Holdings Inc. (“OCIH”). OCIH is a leading Korean conglomerate headquartered in Seoul, Republic of Korea, with diversified operations across renewable energy, advanced materials, energy solutions, and urban development. OCIH is publicly listed on the Korea Exchange. OCIH’s largest shareholder is the Lee Family, including its Chairman, Mr. Lee Woo-hyun and his family members, with a combined shareholding of 29.33 percent as of September 30, 2025. The remaining shareholding of 70.67 percent is owned by institutional and public investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$474 million and will be partly funded with an IFC A Loan of up to US$150 million.
location_description: Sarawak, Malaysia
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the economywide, stakeholder (employee), and environmental effects. Beyond project outcomes, IFC expects the investment to have a transformational effect on the market’s resilience through its role in laying the foundation for a regional semiconductor ecosystem and transforming Southeast Asia into a strategic front-end player.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC will provide a long-term A Loan to meet the long payback period typically required for such projects. Standard Setting: IFC will apply its Environmental and Social (E&S) Performance Standards and corporate governance expertise to ensure the Project adheres to international best practices in sustainability, occupational safety, and community relations.

project_description: The proposed investment is an unfunded risk participation through the Global Structured Trade Finance Program (GTST) of up to EUR 30.25 million to Guan Chong Cocoa Côte d’Ivoire (GCC CI or the Company) to provide traceable cocoa working capital requirements in Côte d’Ivoire (the Project). GCC CI is a subsidiary of Guan Chong Berhad (GCB or the Sponsor) is a manufacturer of cocoa-derived food ingredients. The unfunded risk participation of up to EUR 30.25 million will be made available within a EUR 60.5 million revolving trade finance facility to be arranged by Société Générale Côte d’Ivoire (“SGCI” or the “Bank”), on terms to be agreed between the parties.
sponsor_shareholders: Guan Chong Berhad (GCB or the Sponsor) is Asia’s largest and the world’s fourth-largest manufacturer of cocoa-derived food ingredients. GCB was founded in 1985 and incorporated in its current form in 2004. Strategically headquartered in Malaysia and listed on Bursa Malaysia since 2005, GCB integrates activities from bean sourcing and grinding in origin countries to downstream processing in major consumer markets, thereby gaining control over quality, cost, and sustainability across the entire value chain. Societe General Cote d’Ivoire is a subsidiary of Societe General S.A “SG” and the largest Bank in Cote d’Ivoire. It is a regional systemic bank in Cote d’Ivoire and in the West Africa Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). SG started its operations in Cote d’Ivoire in 1941, opening 3 main branches in Abidjan, before creating Societe General de Banques de Cote d’Ivoire (“SGBCI”) in 1962 as a commercial bank who mainly focused on the Retail & Public/Corporate segments and rebranding itself as SGCI in 2019. The Bank is today a complete universal bank, offering a wide range of products and services to its clients.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s unfunded risk participation of up to EUR 30.25 million, is within a EUR 60.5 million revolving trade finance facility to be arranged by SGCI.
location_description: Cote d’Ivoire
development_impact: The anticipated development impacts of this Project are: (i) increasing access to the cocoa market by farmers in Côte d’Ivoire, maintaining local sourcing of traceable and sustainably produced cocoa beans, (ii) promoting local cocoa production and processing and therefore increasing domestic value addition, and creating more jobs; and (iii) maintaining Côte d’Ivoire’s market position through local value addition and higher sustainability practices.
additionality: The proposed investment is an opportunity for IFC to fund traceable cocoa volumes in West Africa. IFC’s funding IFC will also support GCB’s efforts to improve the operational efficiency of its suppliers and help align the Group’s operations to support its sustainability industry practices.

project_description: The proposed investment is a nine-year local currency unsecured senior loan facility to PT Link Net Tbk (“Linknet”), a leading FiberCo in Indonesia. The proceeds will be used for refinancing and funding the company’s expansion.
sponsor_shareholders: Link Net is 82.1% owned by Axiata Group Berhad (Axiata): (a) 75.4% by wholly owned Axiata Group Companies; and (b) 19.2% by XLSmart (joint controlled between Sinar Mas and Axiata). Rated BBB (Stable) by S&P and Baa2 (Stable) by Moody’s, Axiata is one of Asia's largest regional telecommunications providers with approximately 170 mn customers across 7 countries in South and Southeast Asia. Axiata has been listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange since 2008.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total size of IFC investment is up to US$350 mn in IDR-equivalent which will be used to i) refinance part of Link Net’s existing debt, and ii) fund the capex program for expansion of Link Net’s FTTH network and migration of the existing cable HFC network to FTTH.
location_description: Link Net’s future expansion will be in Indonesia.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is to increase access to quality fixed broadband connectivity for households and businesses by expanding a high-speed fiber broadband network, driving greater adoption of digital services and enabling country’s digital transformation and economic growth. Further, the project has the potential to result in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions savings through energy savings. Beyond the project outcomes, this investment is expected to deepen competitiveness in the market for fixed broadband Internet in Indonesia, through demonstration and replication of an innovative business model. By scaling up the open-access wholesale FiberCo model, the transaction introduces a novel approach to shared infrastructure that reduces costs, minimizes duplication, and enhances efficiency in broadband expansion.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists of mobilizing debt from parallel lenders in the context of the company’s financial constraints, enabling it to address immediate challenges and support its growth trajectory. Non-financial additionality involves Standard setting by (i) providing guidance to the company’s efforts to align its E&S practices with IFC’s performance standards and (ii) helping the company improve gender diversity and representation in its workforce.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an unfunded risk participation facility of up to US$50 million to Absa Bank Ghana LTD (“Absa Ghana”). The facility is part of a broader syndicated package supporting four Ghanaian banks to finance the purchase of traceable cocoa beans from smallholder farmers via leading Licensed Buying Companies (“LBCs”). The facility will be used to provide working capital to four major LBCs.
sponsor_shareholders: Absa Ghana is one of the leading banking subsidiaries of Absa Group Limited, a prominent pan-African financial services group with a presence in 12 countries and over 42,000 employees. Absa Ghana is a leading bank in Ghana with a strong focus on corporate, retail, and small and medium-sized enterprise banking, supported by a nationwide distribution network and a growing customer base.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost and amount: IFC’s risk participation is US$50 million for a total portfolio of US$140 million. Nature of IFC’s investment: The project consists of an unfunded and uncommitted Risk Participation Agreement with a maturity of up to one year and is renewable annually for up to 4 years in aggregate, at IFC’s option.
location_description: The project is located in Ghana, where Licensed Buying Companies (LBCs) operate across both regional and district levels.
development_impact: Contribution to Market Creation: Resilience: IFC anticipates that the Project will contribute to the resilience of Ghana’s cocoa sector currently affected by inadequate finance straining the ability of traders to sustain cocoa sourcing from farmers and that could ultimately affect Ghana’s ability to maintain its global market position as a major supplier of cocoa. To monitor progress against this outcome, IFC will track the number of private sector participants benefiting from the project and monitor the total value of cocoa exported by Ghana. Project outcome: Stakeholder effects: Increased Access to Finance: IFC anticipates that the facility will increase liquidity in the agri supply chain and access to finance for farmers by providing the participating banks with an efficient and competitive risk mitigating tool to accept a higher degree of lending risk. Credit to Ghana’s agricultural sector is even lower relative to the contribution it makes to the country’s GDP, where many lenders lack the risk tolerance and/or expertise to lend to small holder farmers The project is expected to reach over 139,000 farmers in the value chain of the LBCs. To monitor progress against this outcome, IFC will track the volumes of US$ commodities financed by the facility and volumes of MT cocoa trade supported.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing structure: Leveraging IFC’s AAA rating, the proposed facility is designed to address the regulatory capital and single obligor exposure limits that are presenting severe constraints to Ghana’s Cocoa pre-export financing efforts at present. Non-Financial Additionality: Frameworks: catalyzing regulatory change: IFC’s involvement in the financing of the cocoa sector catalyzes changes in the regulatory framework as it opens doors to a new financing instrument currently not available in the market, mitigating credit risk and adding value by enhancing financing facilities to the private sector following the Central Bank of Ghana approval to treat the IFC guarantee in banks’ working capital facilities as deductible for purposes of computing single obligor limit (“SOL”).

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$80 million A Loan to MIDROC Ethiopia PLC (“MEP” or the “Company”) to finance (i) the refurbishment of the Sheraton Addis; and (ii) the development of new Sheraton Hotel (jointly, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: MEP is owned by Sheikh Mohammed Hussein Ali Al-Amoudi (75%) and Mrs. Sofia Saleh Al-Amoudi (25%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated cost of the Project is up to US$116 million. IFC plans to provide a loan of up to US$80 million.
location_description: The Project is located in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are (i) sustained and increased access to formal employment opportunities; (ii) economy-wide effects, including indirect job creation and value-added in the local economy; and (iii) environmental effects through green building certification. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that the investment will sustain ongoing growth in the hospitality sector in Ethiopia.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality will be provided through the longer tenor US$ financing on terms otherwise not available in the local market, especially for foreign currency loans. Non-financial additionality will be provided through knowledge sharing to assist in implementing green building standards and EDGE certification. And other advisory services are being considered. The Company will improve its environmental and social standards to meet IFC Performance Standards.

project_description: IFC’s Board of Directors approved an up to US$40 million (or equivalent in Georgian Lari) long term financing package for Tegeta Motors LLC (Tegeta), Georgia’s leading automotive trade and repair services company. The financing will be deployed in two phases, beginning with a first investment of up to US$20 million to support Tegeta’s GEL 260 million Sustainability Linked Bond (SLB). IFC’s financing will support Tegeta’s investment program, which includes (i) expanding its fleet with hybrid and electric vehicles, to grow its sales, leasing, and rental activities; and (ii) refinancing maturing obligations to enhance financial resilience.
sponsor_shareholders: Tegeta is privately owned by Mr. Temur Kokhodze, a Georgian entrepreneur who established the Company in 1995.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: On December 18, 2025, IFC’s Board of Directors approved an investment of up to US$40 million (or equivalent in Georgian Lari) in long-term financing. IFC acts as a strategic investor in Tegeta’s inaugural GEL 260 million SLB by subscribing for up to US$20 million (equivalent in GEL) for its own account as the first investment under the financing package. The SLB has a five‑year tenor, with amortization of 50 percent of the principal on December 16, 2028, and final maturity on December 16, 2030. The SLB is publicly offered and listed on the Georgian Stock Exchange. In addition to the investment in the SLB, IFC has earmarked up to US$20 million (or equivalent in GEL) in follow-on long-term financing for Tegeta, to be provided within 24 months from the initial investment. This follow-on financing may take the form of either loans or additional bond purchases, depending on market conditions and company needs.
location_description: Georgia
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes include direct and indirect job creation and broader value addition across Georgia’s economy. Georgia faces structural employment challenges, including high unemployment among youth and rural populations, limited formal job opportunities, and vulnerability to external shocks. Creating and preserving quality jobs is critical for inclusive growth, reducing poverty, and supporting economic resilience. The Project will also accelerate car fleet modernization by replacing Georgia’s aging, highly polluting vehicles with cleaner, safer alternatives. Beyond the project-level effects, IFC expects the investment to catalyze innovation in Georgia’s capital markets, enhancing sector competitiveness.
additionality: IFC brings both financial and non-financial additionality. Financially, the proposed investment will strengthen Tegeta’s balance sheet by converting shorter-term bonds into a long-term local-currency bond, improving the Company’s financial sustainability and reducing refinancing risk. IFC’s participation in a five-year GEL bond will help set a precedent for local-currency corporate bonds and help deepen the domestic capital market, while the sustainability-linked element - an innovative instrument in Georgia’s market - provides an additional layer of impact that helps to mobilize three to four times IFC’s investment. Non-financially, IFC will deliver targeted advisory support as follows: (i) on workforce development: assess recruitment, retention, and career advancement practices to foster an equitable workplace for men and women; and (ii) on operational efficiency: reduce energy and water consumption at select facilities to lower costs and improve resource efficiency. Tegeta will develop Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) aligned with IFC performance standards. This will enable Tegeta to better identify and manage environmental and social risks across its operations and enhance compliance with best practices.

project_description: Brookfield India Real Estate Trust (BIRET) is an institutionally managed office real estate investment trust, comprising a portfolio of ten Grade A office assets and a mall. These assets cover a total operating leasable area of 24.6 million square feet across key business districts in India. BIRET was listed on Indian exchanges in February 2021. IFC has invested INR 6,000 million (about US$ 67 million) of debt and INR 1,500 million (about US$ 17 million) of equity. The proceeds shall be utilized for the refinancing of any present or future debt, refurbishment expenses, asset upgrade, working capital requirements and/or acquire stabilized and income-generating office assets (the “Project”). IFC may consider additional financing at a later stage, subject to satisfactory project performance, corporate approvals, and disclosure requirements.
sponsor_shareholders: BIRET is part of the existing investment portfolio of IFC, with IFC having invested INR 8,350 million in equity in December 2024. BIRET is managed by Brookprop Management Services Private Limited (Investment Manager), and the trustee is Axis Trustee Services Limited. BIRET is sponsored by BSREP India Office Holdings V Pte. Ltd. (Sponsor), an affiliate of Brookfield Corporation (Brookfield Group). The Investment Manager and BIRET are part of Brookfield Group. Brookfield Corporation’s asset management business is one of the leading global alternative asset managers, with over US$ 1 trillion in AUM across real estate, infrastructure, renewable power, private equity, and credit, with an AUM of US$272 billion in real estate (over 500 msf). In India, Brookfield Group has a diversified portfolio of ~55 msf of assets in 10 cities, including BIRET portfolio of assets. BIRET is listed on the Indian stock exchanges. Brookfield Group owns ~25 percent shareholding in BIRET, and other investors own the remaining ~75 percent as on September 30, 2025.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: BIRET has raised INR 35,000 million of equity funds through the Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) and INR 20,000 million through debt. Out of this, IFC has made an equity investment of INR 1,500 million, resulting in IFC holding about 4.7 percent stake in BIRET together with its stake from a previous investment and a debt investment of INR 6,000 million.
location_description: BIRET's assets include ten integrated business parks and one independent mall located across Delhi National Capital Region (NCR), Mumbai, Kolkata and Ludhiana. BIRET has acquired Grade A commercial office spaces in Bengaluru and in future it can expand to other south Indian cities such as Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level effects are a) stakeholder effects on tenants through increased access to high quality Grade A offices which supports the GCC ecosystem, potentially contributing to job creation and upskilling relevant for youth; and (b) environmental effects through improved resource efficiency resulting from EDGE Advanced building certification, sustainability linked loan for BIRET, and reductions in GHG emissions. IFC also anticipates that the investment will promote greater sustainability in India's real estate sector.
additionality: The IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. IFC's financial additionality stems from providing financing structure with sustainability linked incentives and resource mobilization. Non-financial additionality comes through knowledge, innovation, capacity building, and standard setting.

project_description: FIBRA Macquarie Mexico (FIBRA MQ) is a publicly listed Mexican real estate investment trust with a US$1.4 billion market capitalization, headquartered in Mexico City that primarily focuses on the acquisition, development, leasing, and management of industrial real estate assets.
sponsor_shareholders: FIBRA MQ is publicly listed with a US$1.4 billion market capitalization. Macquarie Asset Management Mexico S.A. de C.V. (MAM) and its affiliates hold a 4.8% shareholding in FIBRA MQ, with the remaining 95.2% being free float. FIBRA MQ is externally managed by the Macquarie Group through its asset management division and through MAM, a Mexican management company. The Macquarie Group is a reputable global asset manager of Australian origin, managing more than US$590 billion in total assets under management globally.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost stands at US$600 million consisting of a US$50 million A-Loan to finance FIBRA MQ’s 2025-2027 investment program in industrial parks, and a US$550 million parallel syndicated facility to refinance upcoming debt maturities.
location_description: The Project will be developed in Mexico.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the generation of additional quality industrial infrastructure, and energy-efficiency improvements to existing and new buildings. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater market competitiveness via demonstration and replication channels, by increasing access to sustainable finance and advancing the practice of portfolio decarbonization through demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: The proposed Project is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided by capital mobilized by IFC and enabling access to the REIT’s required long-term US dollar bullet financing structures. Non-financial additionality will be provided through capacity building on decarbonization and improved ESG standards.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a loan of up to INR 20,700 million (the INR equivalent of US$250 million) in tranches to Nexus Select Trust. The investment will be structured as a Sustainability-Linked Bond (SLB) with climate-related Sustainability Performance Targets (SPTs). The proceeds will be used for acquisitions (directly or indirectly through its SPV’s), repayment/ refinancing of financial indebtedness (NXST or its SPV’s), and/or extending loan to its SPV’s for enhancement works of NXST’s properties or undertaking construction, payment of fees and issue expenses and other general corporate purposes. NXST is a AAA rated (by CRISIL - S&P affiliate and ICRA - Moody’s affiliate) Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) and is India’s only listed REIT in the retail space. Its portfolio comprises of 17 Grade-A urban consumption centers (UCCs or malls) across 14 cities spanning 9.9 million square feet (msf) of leased retail area, two hotel assets (354 keys), three office assets (1.3 msf) and one renewable power plant (15 MW - AC). Nexus Select Mall Management Private Limited is the Investment Manager (IM) to NXST.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor of NXST is Wynford Investments Limited, an affiliate of Blackstone Inc. The Sponsor and Sponsor Group i.e., Blackstone (through its affiliates) holds 22% of the total units in NXST as of September 30, 2024. The Investment Manager is majority held by Blackstone through its affiliates. Blackstone is one of the world’s leading investment firms and a global alternative asset manager with diverse interests across multiple asset classes including real estate, private equity, infrastructure, etc. across the globe.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment of up to INR 20,700 million (~US$250 million) through subscription to non-convertible, listed debt securities to be issued by NXST. The proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes including payment of fees and issue expenses, acquisitions (directly or indirectly through it’s SPV’s), repayment/ refinancing of financial indebtedness (NXST or its SPV’s), and/or extending loan to its SPV’s for enhancement works of NXST’s properties or undertaking construction.
location_description: Several cities across India
development_impact: By incentivizing NXST to reduce GHG emissions and make its portfolio assets more energy efficient, the Project will contribute to reducing the impact of climate change. The Project will also demonstrate and promote greater sustainability in the real estate sector in India.
additionality: IFC proposes to provide a long-term, innovative financing instrument that is not common in the Indian market especially in the real estate sector, in a relatively new asset class in India. IFC is also providing guidance on development of a Sustainability-Linked Financing Framework and on selection of Sustainability Performance Targets.

project_description: Sustainable Development Investment Company SAOC (SDIC) was established for the purpose of developing The Sustainable City Yiti (TSCY) in Oman. TSCY is a mixed residential and commercial development extending over approximately 100 hectares in proximity of the Yiti village, c.40 km East of Muscat. TSCY includes a marina, two hotels, 132 serviced apartments, 300 houses, and the Plaza District - which consists of 17 buildings with 1,225 apartments, c.13,400 m2 of office space and c.14,600 m2 of commercial space. TSCY will also include shared services (general urban infrastructure, a water desalination plant, waste management plant, solar photovoltaic power generation systems, district cooling etc.) and facilities for use by residents and non-residents of the city (a mosque, school, sport facilities, public beach, equestrian and autism centers).
sponsor_shareholders: SDIC is a joint venture between SEE Holding and OMRAN Group, created to develop TSCY. SEE Holding is a Dubai-based real-estate development company specialized in the construction and management of residential districts with a low carbon footprint. SEE Holding has so far developed sustainable cities in Dubai, Sharjah and Abu Dhabi, and is finalizing construction of TSCY in Muscat. OMRAN Group is Oman's national tourism development company, a state-owned enterprise established in 2005 and wholly owned by the Oman Investment Authority. The company serves as Oman’s master developer for tourism and real estate projects with its policies aligned with the goals of Oman Vision 2040.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost of the Plaza District of the city is c.US$370 million. The proposed IFC Murabaha financing to SDIC comprises of: (i) an A-Loan of up to US$100 million; and (ii) mobilization of B/Parallel loans up to US$100 million.
location_description: TSCY extends over approximately 100 hectares in proximity of the Yiti village, which is c.40 km East of Muscat, Oman.
development_impact: The proposed investment will: (i) create jobs, whilst boosting local economic activity and tax revenues, (ii) increase availability of affordable residential accommodation in the country, (iii) set a regional benchmark for climate-smart urban development by integrating green building principles, renewable energy, and water-efficient systems, and (iv) introduce cost-effective, sustainable standards for urban infrastructure, encouraging private sector investment and advancing Oman’s sustainability goals. Overall, the Project aims to institutionalize climate-aligned practices in urban planning and infrastructure delivery.
additionality: IFC is providing SDIC with an 8-year Islamic Finance Murabaha Loan package, including a 2-year capital grace period, to complete the Plaza District which is a key component of the broader city. IFC will also assist SDIC in obtaining EDGE and APEX Green Building certifications and ensure SDICs alignment with the IFC Performance Standards through the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP) agreed.

project_description: The project entails a debt financing package of up to US$80 million to Green Esteel Pte. Ltd. (“Green Esteel”, the “Company” or “Borrower”), a leading integrated steel manufacturing group based in Singapore. The Company engages in steel manufacturing, fabrication, and trading businesses across Southeast Asia. The Project will support the replacement and refurbishment of equipment at an existing integrated steel mill in Malaysia. This includes dismantling an obsolete electric arc furnace and installing a new electric arc furnace, as well as dismantling existing rolling mill lines and installing a new rolling mill line. The IFC investment will support the Company’s production of low-carbon steel and contribute to the low-carbon transition of the construction and manufacturing sectors in Southeast Asia.
sponsor_shareholders: Green Esteel is beneficially owned by Mr. You Zhenhua with an interest of approximately 87.8%. By ownership, Green Esteel is 20.2% owned by Deep Source Holdings Limited, a Hong-Kong listed investment holding company that primarily engages in the processing, distribution, and commodities trading. Mr. You Zhenhua is the ultimate beneficiary for Deep Source Holdings Limited. The remaining 4.2% of interest in Green Esteel is owned by other shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at US$117 million, which will be funded by IFC’s debt financing package of up to US$80 million and equity contributions from Green Esteel and other shareholders.
location_description: The Project is located in Pasir Gudang, Johor, Malaysia.
development_impact: The Project has benefited from climate adjustment. The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the economywide, stakeholder (employee), and environmental effects. Beyond project outcomes, IFC expects the investment to have a catalytic effect on the market by demonstrating that through technology and value-added products, Malaysia's steel industry can achieve greater profitability and stability. The Project outcomes consist of economywide effects on value addition and job preservation, employee effects through upskilling with the latest electric arc furnace (EAF) technology, as well as environmental effects through greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions by implementing EAF for steel production. The Project also aims to enhance resilience in Malaysia's steel sector by demonstrating a turnaround of a dormant facility to become a fully functioning, competitive one. These enhancements will enable the Company, and by extension the broader industry, to better absorb shocks, adapt to evolving challenges and sustain stable operations amid overcapacity and shifting regulatory and environmental requirements.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via financing structure. Non-financial additionality is supplied via standard setting. Financial additionality includes: Financing structure - IFC's financing will play a crucial role in reviving the dormant facility by providing essential capital that was unavailable through traditional avenues. This infusion is particularly significant as it offers long-term stability through a longer-tenured loan, providing the Company much-needed financial flexibility during its critical restart and refurbishment phase. Non-financial additionality includes: Standard setting - The steel value chain also represents some environmental and social risks, in which IFC's performance standards and E&S Action Plan will ensure the Company enhances its management of the high-risk areas of the operations.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an A Loan, B Loans and Parallel Loans of up to US$850 million to Acelen Industrial S.A. (“Acelen” or the “Company”), a subsidiary of Acelen Energia Renovável S.A. The proposed project aims to support the construction of a new seed-to-fuel biorefinery in Bahia, Brazil (the “Project”), with a capacity of 20 kbpd using Hydroprocessed Esters and Fatty Acids (HEFA) technology to produce Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and Renewable Diesel (RD).
sponsor_shareholders: The project’s sponsor is Acelen Energia Renovavel S.A., established in 2023 by Mubadala Capital, the investment arm of Abu Dhabi’s sovereign wealth fund (SWF) Mubadala Investment Company, to expand its presence in Brazil’s biofuels sector and support the global energy transition.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of (i) an IFC A loan for IFC’s own account of up to US$250 million, and (ii) Parallel Loans and B loans totaling up to US$600 million.
location_description: The project will be developed in a brownfield industrial area in Sao Francisco do Conde in Bahia, Brazil.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to have economy-wide effects through the creation of direct and indirect employment opportunities, enhancing skills and knowledge of workers from low-income areas, and contributing to foreign exchange earnings in Brazil. Beyond the Project, IFC expects to strengthening of the sustainability of the aviation sector by establishing one of Brazil’s first large-scale SAF production segments with strong demonstration effects for other market players.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality through: (i) resource mobilization; (ii) standard setting on E&S management system; and (iii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building through an upstream engagement.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment in NDR Smart Spaces Private Limited (NDR Smart or Company) is by means of subscription to the Compulsory Convertible Debentures (CCDs) or Preference Shares issued by the Company of up to US$ 25 million (INR equivalent) and debt investment of up to US$ 25 million (INR equivalent). The proceeds will be used by the Company to acquire and develop green warehouses in India. NDR Smart is a newly incorporated subsidiary of NDR Warehousing Private Limited (NDRWPL). Currently NDRWPL is undergoing a demerger process to transfer its warehouse development business to NDR Smart, for better governance, simplified administration and management. NDRWPL is one of the leading warehousing developers in India having developed and leased approx. 20 Mn sq. ft as of December 2025. NDRWPL is also the sponsor of NDR InvIT Trust (a listed regulated AAA rated entity) that has a right of first offer with the Company (“ROFO”) to purchase completed leased warehouse assets.
sponsor_shareholders: NDR Smart is a subsidiary of NDRWPL. NDRWPL is closely held Mr. N Amrutesh Reddy (97%) and Mrs. N Srithi Reddy (3%). Mr. Reddy has over 24 years of experience in end-to-end supply chain logistics, particularly in warehousing. He has been with the NDR Group since 1998 and has been associated with Continental Warehousing Corporation (CWC) since 2009. He has been on the board of directors of the Company since 1998.20
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment of up to US$50 million (INR equivalent) will be used for equity and debt contribution towards construction of warehouses, purchase of under development warehouses, land for construction of warehouses and working capital and general corporate purposes in accordance with Applicable Laws.
location_description: The warehouses associated with project will be located across India across key consumption centres including Mumbai, Pune, Ahmedabad, Surat, Kolkata, Lucknow, Kanpur, Ghaziabad, Hosur, Coimbatore, Kochi, Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is the increased access to high quality logistics infrastructure in India. Other project-level outcomes are the environmental benefits of reaching Advanced EDGE certification in commercial buildings. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater market competitiveness in warehousing and logistics, as well as cold storage, by supporting the consolidation of a fragmented market and enabling high quality business infrastructure.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is both financial and non-financial. IFC’s financial additionality lies in its own-account investment into NDR Smart by subscribing to its CCDs/Preference Shares and debt to finance the development and sale of warehousing space. IFC will also mobilize additional financing from commercial banks and investors. IFC’s non-financial additionality lies in its contribution to the Sponsor’s knowledge through which the Sponsor will improve its gender diversity and inclusion standards and providing technical expertise, knowledge and toolkits to the client towards assessment and target setting for Advanced EDGE certification.

project_description: IFC will support Arboreal S.A. (the “Company”) with a financing package of US$40 million for several key initiatives focused on enhancing value-add products and operational efficiency including: (i) installation of a thermally modified timber (TMT) production line, (ii) deployment of a biomass/briquette system for byproducts and sawdust, and (iii) general capital expenditures at the Tacuarembó plant. Additionally, the Project will refinance Arboreal’s existing debt. Arboreal’s current operations include a sawmill and mass timber production facility.
sponsor_shareholders: Arboreal is privately held, with principal shareholders Matias Albergo (CEO and Director, 26.57%) and Mark Crandall (Director, 24.91%). Beneficial ownership is structured through direct holdings and Cyprus-based entities or trusts, in compliance with IFC’s eligible jurisdiction guidelines.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s financing package consists of (i) a US$20m IFC A-loan and (ii) a US$20m B-Loan to be mobilized from commercial banks.
location_description: The project will be developed in Tacuarembó, Uruguay.
development_impact: The Project is expected to create significant positive development effects by generating jobs and environmental benefits, driving economic growth through expanded mass timber production, increased value-added and export earnings, and supporting industrial innovation and sustainable construction practices. It will also advance climate mitigation by expanding sustainably sourced mass timber, which acts as a carbon sink and replaces carbon-intensive materials, supporting Uruguay’s low-carbon development goals and catalyzing sustainability in the housing sector.
additionality: In addition to providing long-term financing, IFC will bring value through upstream/advisory services. Arboreal will adopt IFC's environmental and social standards to strengthen governance and sustainability practices.

project_description: The proposed investment is for up to US$30.7 million (“IFC Loan”) to Popular Pharmaceuticals PLC. (“PPL” or the “Company” or the “Borrower”) in Bangladesh. Founded in 2006, PPL is a well-established, mid-sized pharmaceutical manufacturer in Bangladesh. The Company ranks 9th by revenue in Bangladesh pharma market. PPL belongs to Popular Group, which is a leading, family-owned healthcare conglomerate in Bangladesh with a 41-year track record across diagnostics, pharmaceuticals, hospitals, and medical education The IFC Loan proceeds will be used to finance working capital, primarily for the procurement of raw materials, which are mostly imported. The transaction aims to ensure uninterrupted supply of essential medicines during a period of financial sector stress and credit tightening in Bangladesh. A long-term US$-denominated loan will enable the Company to navigate the current financial sector stress and credit tightness and maintain continuity of operations.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsors include Dr. Mostafizur Rahman and his children – Mr. Murtuza Rahman, Mr. Sardin Rahman, and Ms. Sadia Rahman (collectively referred to as the “Sponsors”). The Sponsors are the ultimate beneficial owners of the 100% of the shareholding in the Borrower.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment will support the import requirements of the Company.
location_description: The Company’s factory is located in Gazipur, 23 kilometres north of Dhaka, in Bangladesh.
development_impact: The most significant project-level outcome is improved access to high-quality pharmaceutical products in Bangladesh. Although healthcare access has improved, it still lags behind regional peers such as India and Indonesia, reflecting persistent challenges in achieving equitable healthcare delivery. The burden of noncommunicable diseases has risen sharply, placing additional pressure on the health system, while unstable macroeconomic conditions have further strained its capacity. The Project responds to these challenges by supporting the company in implementing its short-term growth plans, which include a significant increase in sales, particularly in the hormone segment, thereby improving access to essential treatments for patients across the country.
additionality: IFC provides financial additionality through a US$ loan with a tenor of 6 years, including 1.5 years of grace period to support PPL's working capital requirement needs for raw material imports. Besides, IFC will advise on efficiency, gender inclusion, and inclusive workplace practices through gender advisory. Further, IFC will support adoption of Performance Standards and an ESMS, strengthening E&S practices in the sector.

project_description: IFC is considering providing a senior A-loan of up to US$60mn (“IFC Loan”) to Fatima Fertilizer Company Limited (“Fatima Co” or the “Company”) which will be used to import raw materials, machinery, and pay for technical services from international providers for the Company's operations (“Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Fatima Co is one of Pakistan’s leading fertilizer companies with the second largest installed capacity representing 30% of the overall fertilizer sector and 44% of the phosphate-based fertilizer subsegment. The Company was established in 2003 and is listed on Pakistan stock exchange. It operates three manufacturing plants in the Punjab province with combined nameplate production capacity of 2.57 million tons per annum (MTPA). Its flagship plant is located in Sadiqabad and operated directly, while two smaller ones in Multan and Sheikhupura are operated through fully owned subsidiaries. The Company’s main shareholders are Fatima Group (owning 58.9%) and Arif Habib Group (owning 33.6%), with the remaining 7.5% owned by the general public. Fatima Group is a conglomerate engaged in commodities trading, manufacturing of fertilizers, textiles and sugar, as well as in the mining and energy sectors. Arif Habib Group started its activities in the financial services sector and later also became an investor in industrial sectors (fertilizers, cement, steel and power generation) and engaged in real estate development and management.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost will be financed by a senior “A” loan of up to US$60 million to be provided by IFC under annual commitments of up to US$60 million per year for up to three years. Each commitment of the loan will be repaid by the Company at its anniversary and then, at IFC’s discretion, an additional US$60 million loan will be committed at the beginning of the subsequent year. At any time, IFC exposure to the Company will not exceed US$60 million.
location_description: The Company’s operations take place in Pakistan. The IFC loan will be used for the Sadiqabad plant.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are the economywide effects via value addition, job preservation, and import substitution, contributing to FX savings. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will contribute to increasing the resilience of Pakistan and the global food supply chain.
additionality: Financial Additionality - Financing structure: Critical US$ liquidity support amidst prevailing FX constraints in Pakistan is needed to finance the Company's working capital, maintenance capex and fees to be paid to technical services providers. IFC will provide financing on terms not otherwise available in the local market, with one year tenor, renewable for up to two additional years. Non-financial Additionality - Standard setting: IIFC conducted a diagnostic for Fatima's E&S considerations. Based on the diagnostic, IFC will support Fatima Co to align its operations with IFC Performance Standards and industry best practices on E&S aspects.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$50 million A Loan (the Loan) to support Consolidated Tourist & Hotel Investments (CTHI, the Company, the Borrower) to finance the development of the Explorer by Elewana brand through refurbishment of two existing Sopa Lodges together with an expansion of one of those existing lodges in Tanzania.
sponsor_shareholders: CTHI is part of SafariCo Group (SafariCo, the Group), a leading diversified East African safari operator that owns and operates (i) safari lodges in Kenya and Tanzania under the brands Elewana Collection, Explorer, and Sopa Lodges, (ii) a destination management company covering East Africa and with offices in Kenya, Tanzania, and Rwanda under the brand Cheli & Peacock Safaris, and (iii) a company operating scheduled, itinerised aviation safaris in Kenya and Tanzania which operates under the brand SkySafari.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated project cost is approximately US$72 million, of which IFC will be financing US$50 million via the Loan.
location_description: The Project is located in Serengeti National Park and Ngorongoro Conservation Area in Tanzania.
development_impact: Project Outcomes for the Project include: Stakeholder Effects: Employees: The labor market in Tanzania is largely informal, with an informal employment rate of 93.6%. The level of assessed vulnerability in employment (informal work arrangements, limited social protection or safety nets) is also high: 89.3% among women and 78.8% among men, higher than the average for Sub-Saharan Africa. The Project will sustain existing direct jobs and create new jobs, as well as seasonal employment opportunities. These are formal jobs with training and benefits, which are scarce in the local communities. Economy-wide Effects: This Project is expected to have positive economy-wide impacts, including job creation, contribution to GDP, and higher revenues for the Government of Tanzania and its agencies, including Tanzania National Parks and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority. The refurbishment of SXR and NXR will allow the Group to maintain and even expand its positive economic impact on local communities, and the extension of the existing NXR to include N20 will create new business opportunities for local suppliers. Environmental Effects: Environmental stewardship is essential to maintain the sensitive ecosystem of wildlife conservation areas. This Project will contribute to climate change mitigation through green building practices, by achieving EDGE Basic certification for SXR, NXR, and N20. The Project's contribution to market creation includes: Sustainability: The green buildings ecosystem in Tanzania is still very nascent, and lags behind that of neighboring Kenya. Additionally, existing use of EDGE (or similar green building certifications) in the safari sub-sector is limited. This Project will contribute to market sustainability by demonstrating the viability of green building practices, particularly for facilities in remote areas. This demonstration effect should encourage other accommodation operators to adopt green building practices on their own properties.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing structure: IFC is providing financing with a 10 year tenor that is not immediately available on the local market. Non-financial additionality: Standard-setting: IFC will support EDGE certification for SXR, NXR, and N20, as well as support for EDGE Gender certification. Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC will provide labor & workforce advisory services to strengthen the client’s HR function.

project_description: Engro Fertilizers Limited (Company), incorporated in Pakistan and a manufacturer and distributor of fertilizers, is seeking a general-purpose corporate loan in local currency. IFC has been invited to arrange a financing package comprising of a Partial Credit Guarantee (PCG), to be issued by IFC in favor of a commercial bank, which is providing a local currency loan to Engro Fertilizers (Project).
