In addition, the Project is supported by the IFC-Canada Facility for Resilient Food Systems (FRFS) to de-risk the investment.
sponsor_shareholders: Engro Fertilizers is one of Pakistan's leading fertilizer producers. Its main products include urea, di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) and specialty fertilizer blends. It is the second largest urea producer and second largest distributor of DAP in Pakistan. It operates three manufacturing plants with a combined production capacity of 2.38 million tons per annum. Engro Fertilizers is a subsidiary of Engro Corporation (56.3% ownership), one of the largest conglomerates in Pakistan. Engro Corporation has a significant presence in various sectors including fertilizers, petrochemicals, energy, food, and telecommunications infrastructure. Engro Fertilizers' other shareholders include financial institutions (12.3%), general public (20.9%), and others (10.5%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be US$190 million, which will be financed through a PKR-denominated loan of PKR33.6 billion (equivalent to approximately US$120 million) from a commercial bank. The proposed IFC investment comprises of an unfunded PCG of up to PKR33.6 billion (equivalent to approximately US$120 million), to be issued by IFC in favor of the commercial bank. The proposed PCG will cover 100% of the principal portion of the commercial bank's loan to Engro Fertilizers.
location_description: The proposed investment will support the Company in Pakistan, where all its operations are based.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are i) stakeholder effects by expanding fertilizer access through a direct distribution model complemented by digital solutions and the provision of technical assistance; and ii) economy-wide effects by sustaining value addition and employment through facilities turnaround. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the Project to strengthen sector resilience by demonstrating the impact of digital technologies and direct-to-farmer approaches in improving efficiency, transparency, and farmer engagement.
additionality: IFC will provide financial and non-financial additionality to the Project. Financial Additionality - providing a pioneering PCG, with support from FRFS, enabling a commercial bank to provide a long-term local currency loan that can otherwise not be arranged due to capital constraints and exposure limits applicable on large conglomerates. Non-Financial Additionality - supporting alignment of the Company’s operations with IFC’s Performance Standards (PS) on environmental and social (E&S) aspects, setting a benchmark for sustainable practices and encouraging sector-wide adoption.

project_description: IFC intends to lead Boost Holdings’ equity fundraising with a proposed equity investment of US$20 million. Boost is a Malaysian digital bank, e-wallet and payment solutions provider. The use of proceeds will be dedicated to sustaining the Company’s growth.
sponsor_shareholders: Boost (the “Company”) was launched in 2017 by Axiata Digital, an IFC client and one of Asia's largest telecoms conglomerates. The Company has evolved into a Fintech ecosystem primarily offering Small Medium Enterprise (SME) and Consumer lending products in Malaysia, but also e-wallet and payment solutions. In partnership with RHB Bank, it secured a digital bank license in 2022, launched Boost Bank in 2024 and commenced lending through the bank in 2025. The Company also operates a small supply chain financing platform in Indonesia. Current shareholding includes Axiata Group, Great Eastern and Mitsui & Co.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is US$20 million in equity by IFC.
location_description: The Company is registered and has operations in Malaysia.
development_impact: Expected development impact through: (i) Improved Access to Finance for SMEs in Malaysia by introducing credit products to support SMEs; (ii) Increased Access to Retail Credit for Individuals in Malaysia, by offering a Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) solution to consumers that provides them with access to credit; (iii) Enhancing the MSME lending market in Malaysia through increased competitive pressure through introducing a scalable, fully digital lending product that uses proprietary data for alternative credit scoring, expanding access to underserved segments.
additionality: IFC’s additionality consists of: (i) own account equity; (ii) risk mitigation; and (iii) standard setting.

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: The proposed investment is a senior, unsecured, sustainability-linked A loan of up to €150 million (the “IFC Loan”), committed in two tranches: (1) Tranche 1: up to €100 million, and (2) Tranche 2: up to €50 million to KOSTAL Mobility Holding SE (the Company). The Company is a Tier I player in the global automotive industry, known for innovative electronic solutions and leading the mobility transition.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a fully owned subsidiary of Leopold Kostal GmbH & Co. KG (the Group), a German family business that develops high-quality electronic and mechatronic systems for automotive and industrial use. Founded in 1912, KOSTAL Group operates in 64 locations across 24 countries. In 2024, the KOSTAL Group employed over 20,000 people.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed €150 million loan investment consists of: (i) Tranche 1, which will support the Company’s capital expenditures and working capital needs in Bulgaria, North Macedonia, Poland, and Ukraine for 2025 – 2027. This includes research and development, product upgrades, and investments in energy-efficient machinery and specialized equipment; and (ii) Tranche 2, which is intended to help restart and grow the production in Ukraine once conditions allow, expected to be committed at a subsequent stage, but no later than December 2027 (the “Project”).
location_description: Bulgaria, North Macedonia, Poland, and Ukraine.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes include the generation of economy-wide value added and job creation, including direct and indirect effects across the economy and increased exports across Bulgaria, North Macedonia, Poland, and Ukraine. Beyond the Project-level impact, IFC expects the Project to drive innovation across the supply chain.
additionality: IFC will provide both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC is providing financial additionality through a longer-term loan with an extended grace period beyond local market norms, structuring it as the Company's first Sustainability-Linked Loan tied to the sustainability targets, and through resource mobilization. IFC will also provide non-financial additionality via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building, particularly through support in the development of KOSTAL Mobility's first sustainability-linked framework and standard setting for ESG best practices.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment supports Sahara Energy Resource Limited (“SERIOM” or “the Company”) in implementing a multi-country LPG infrastructure expansion program and strengthening access to trade finance for trading and delivering LPG and refined products across Sub-Saharan Africa. The Project comprises two integrated components: (i) Long-Term Project Finance – LPG Storage Terminals IFC will support the development of four greenfield LPG storage terminals located in: Tema, Ghana (6,000 MT) Apapa, Nigeria (15,000 MT) Mombasa, Kenya (30,000 MT) Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (6,000 MT) Sahara will use special purpose vehicles (“SPVs”) in each country to implement these assets, which address major storage gaps, reduce logistics costs, and expand access to clean cooking fuels. (ii) Participating as a lender or risk participant in Trade Finance Facilities In parallel, IFC will participate in trade finance facilities arranged by commercial banks to support the Company’s procurement, shipments, importation, storage, and distribution of oil and gas products (LPG, LNG and other refined petroleum products) across Africa and working capital needs.. These facilities help ensure reliable and competitive energy supply across multiple African markets. Together, the long-term project finance component and the trade-finance participation will create a unified financing package that expands LPG access, strengthens supply chains, and promotes energy security in Sub-Saharan Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: Sahara Group ( “Sahara” or the “Group”) is a leading African energy and infrastructure conglomerate headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria. Since its founding in 1996, the Group has grown into a vertically integrated platform operating across the upstream, midstream, downstream, and power sectors, with a presence in more than a dozen African and international markets. Sahara Energy Resource Limited is the Group’s principal trading arm and the counterparty for IFC’s investment. The Company’s operations span LPG vessels, storage facilities under development, gasoline blending assets, and a broad trading footprint across Africa. For the LPG terminals, Sahara will use dedicated SPVs in each of the four project countries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: LPG Infrastructure Investment: IFC will provide up to US$150 million including US$100 million IFC A-Loan and up to US$50 million in mobilization to support Sahara’s LPG infrastructure expansion across Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, and Tanzania. The overall capital cost of the multi-country program is estimated at US$218–347 million, covering the development of four new LPG storage terminals through country-level SPVs. Trade Finance Participation: In addition, IFC will participate with up to US$105 million in multiple trade finance facilities arranged by commercial banks to support Sahara’s procurement, shipments, storage, and distribution of oil and gas products (LPG, LNG and other refined petroleum products) across Sub-Saharan Africa, and the Company’s general working capital needs.
location_description: The Project spans four African countries for the LPG infrastructure component and multiple African countries under the trade finance component. Infrastructure Sites: Tema, Ghana – 6,000 MT Apapa, Nigeria – 15,000 MT Mombasa, Kenya – 30,000 MT Dar es Salaam, Tanzania – 6,000 MT Trade Finance Footprint: Côte d’Ivoire DRC Gabon Guinea Conakry Kenya Nigeria Senegal Sierra Leone and other African markets per facility utilization
development_impact: Expanded Access to Clean Cooking: The new LPG terminals will improve availability and reliability of LPG across four countries, enabling millions of households to transition from biomass fuels to cleaner alternatives. Strengthened Energy Security: The additional storage capacity will reduce logistics bottlenecks, vessel waiting times, and supply disruptions, resulting in more consistent access to LPG and other essential fuels. Enhanced Trade Finance Liquidity: By supporting critical trade finance lines, IFC will help maintain stable energy imports into several African markets, including IDA and FCS countries, during periods of constrained liquidity. Climate and Environmental Benefits: Increased LPG consumption displaces firewood and charcoal, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, mitigating deforestation, and improving indoor air quality. Market Efficiency and Competition: The Project will help create a more competitive and efficient LPG market by expanding private sector-led storage capacity and improving supply-chain integration.
additionality: Financial Additionality • IFC provides long-term financing for LPG infrastructure that is scarce in the market. • IFC’s participation in trade-finance facilities mobilizes significant commercial capital and supports sustained energy-sector financing in Sub-Saharan Africa. • The combined offering reduces Sahara’s overall cost of capital and consolidates multiple financing needs under a coherent structure. Non-Financial Additionality • IFC will support Sahara in aligning its operations with international environmental, social, and governance standards. • IFC provides technical expertise in energy logistics, multi-country infrastructure development, and E&S risk management. • The Project is expected to contribute to broader market creation by expanding private investment and improving competitiveness in the LPG value chain.

project_description: IFC is considering an equity investment of up to US$13 million in Breadfast Inc. (“Breadfast” or “Company”), a leading online grocery and quick commerce brand in Egypt. The proposed project aims to accelerate Breadfast’s expansion in the country.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company’s shares are held by its founders — Mostafa Amin, Muhammad Habib, and Abdallah Nofal — alongside leading global institutional investors, venture capital funds, and strategic partners with deep expertise in technology, consumer markets, and emerging economies. The Company is currently raising a pre-Series C round to finance infrastructure development and accelerate growth.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC equity investment is up to US$13 million.
location_description: Breadfast’s headquarters are located in Cairo, Egypt, which serves as the Company’s primary market.
development_impact: Breadfast’s expansion is anticipated to contribute to job creation, both directly and indirectly, through the establishment of new facilities and the onboarding of delivery agents. Additionally, the project is expected to broaden market access for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the retail distribution sector. Breadfast’s platform will enable SMEs to reach more customers and benefit from essential services such as inventory tracking, marketing, and distribution, supporting their business growth. The project also aims to enhance the competitiveness of Egypt’s retail market by encouraging innovation and digitalization, addressing challenges such as market fragmentation, limited product selection, and inconsistent service quality.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is both financial and non-financial. By providing long-term equity in a market with limited venture funding, the project enables Breadfast’s growth and product expansion, and IFC’s involvement also encourages other investors to join future funding rounds. IFC will also work with Breadfast to implement robust environmental and social standards aligned with international best practices.

sector: Household Appliances (Including Refrigerators, Laundry Machine, Dishwashers, etc.)
project_description: Arcelik A.S. (Arcelik or the Company) is a major Turkish white goods manufacturer with global operations. Arcelik would like to proceed with an investment program in Turkiye which is comprised of (i) expenditures linked to improving earthquake resilience of Arcelik’s six production facilities (ii) financing of two newly built solar power plants for captive use, (iii) research and development expenditures (the Project). The Project is planned to be funded with an IFC senior unsecured A Loan package of up to EUR200 million (the IFC Loan).
sponsor_shareholders: Arcelik's current ownership structure is as follows: Koc Group (57.2%), Burla group (17.6%), Arcelik (10.2%), and publicly listed shares on Borsa Istanbul (15.0%). Koc Holding is the leading industrial conglomerate of Turkiye, mainly engaged in the energy, automotive, consumer durables, and finance sectors. Koc Holding is majority-owned by the Koc family of Turkiye, while the remaining shares (26.9%) of Koc Holding are publicly listed.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is expected to be EUR 200 million, to be financed fully with the IFC Loan in two equal tranches.
location_description: The IFC Loan will be fully used in Türkiye.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project’s development outcomes to include (i) environmental / climate effects: reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions; and (ii) economywide effects: foreign exchange generation, employment and domestic value addition. The anticipated market-level outcome is the enhancement of Turkish home appliances sector’s sustainability by supporting a leading company in issuing its first sustainability-Linked Loan (SLL) with targets set by the Science-Based Target initiative (SBTi).
additionality: IFC’s financial additionality will be delivered mainly by its countercyclical provision of a five-year loan financing, which may not be readily in Türkiye’s market, especially in large volumes. IFC’s non-financial additionality will be delivered by proving guidance and incentives for Arçelik to achieve its ambitious and quantitative sustainability targets for its first SLL.

project_description: The proposed investment is comprised of a senior secured A-Loan of up to €45 million and an unfunded risk participation through the Global Structured Trade Finance Program (GTST) of up to €30.25 million to Guan Chong Cocoa Côte d’Ivoire (GCC CI or the Company) and GCB Cocoa Singapore Pte (GCB Singapore or the Co-Borrower) to support the expansion of an existing cocoa processing facility and provide traceable cocoa working capital requirements in Côte d’Ivoire (the Project). GCC CI and GCB Singapore are subsidiaries of Guan Chong Berhad (GCB or the Sponsor). The unfunded risk participation of up to €30.25 million is within a €60.5 million revolving trade finance facility to be arranged with a bank, which will be partially secured by inventory under a collateral management agreement.
sponsor_shareholders: Guan Chong Berhad was founded in 1985 and incorporated in its current form in 2004. It is headquartered in Malaysia and has been listed on Bursa Malaysia since 2005. GCB integrates activities from bean sourcing and grinding in origin countries to downstream processing in consumer markets, thereby gaining control over quality, cost, and sustainability across the cocoa value chain.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed senior secured A-loan of up to €45 million from IFC's own account will fund the second phase of expansion of an existing cocoa processing facility in San Pedro, Côte d’Ivoire. IFC’s unfunded risk participation of up to €30.25 million is within a €60.5 million revolving trade finance facility to be arranged with a bank. The total estimated project cost is €106 million, which includes expansion capex and additional working capital.
location_description: The cocoa processing facility is in San Pedro, Côte d’Ivoire’s second-largest port, and was established by GCB in 2018, with operations commencing in 2023.
development_impact: The anticipated development impacts of this Project are: (i) increasing access to the cocoa market by farmers in Côte d’Ivoire, maintaining local sourcing of traceable and sustainably produced cocoa beans, (ii) promoting local cocoa production and processing and therefore increasing domestic value addition, and creating more jobs; and (iii) maintaining Côte d’Ivoire’s market position through local value addition and higher sustainability practices.
additionality: The proposed investment is an opportunity for IFC to fund traceable cocoa volumes in West Africa. IFC’s funding IFC will also support GCB’s efforts to improve the operational efficiency of its suppliers and help align the Group’s operations to support its sustainability industry practices.

project_description: The proposed transaction involves an equity investment of up to INR 4.3 billion (approximately US$50 million equivalent) in GFCL EV Products Limited (GFCL EV or Company) in the form of Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares (CCPS). IFC CCPS shall be converted to common shares at the time of Qualified Public Offering or other qualified liquidity event or equity financing round. GFCL EV is a newly established Indian manufacturer specializing in chemicals for Lithium-ion Battery (Li-B) cells used in electric vehicles (EV) and stationary battery energy storage systems (BESS). GFCL EV is focused on the manufacture of electrolytes, salts, binders and Cathode Active Material (CAM). These materials go into Li-B cells and most either contain, or are based on, fluorine chemistry. The Company was established as a wholly owned subsidiary of Gujarat Fluorochemicals Limited (GFL or the Sponsor), an Indian chemical manufacturer with over 30 years of experience in fluorine chemistry. The Sponsor established GFCL EV with the aim of leveraging its manufacturing experience in fluorinated chemicals and backward integration into critical raw materials, to offer a cost-competitive alternative to global battery cell manufacturers looking to diversify their supply chain. The Company has began investing in a manufacturing facility in Gujarat, Maharashtra, close to the Sponsor's existing chemicals manufacturing facility. In addition, GFCL EV is also planning to establish a second facility in Oman in the future. The proposed IFC investment aims to support the Company's manufacturing facility in Gujarat, India (the Project), which is currently undergoing phased commissioning. The proposed IFC investment will promote domestic value-added manufacturing within India's Li-B supply chain, facilitate the creation of direct and indirect green jobs, and contribute to the availability of critical raw materials essential for transport electrification and BESS, thereby enhancing supply chain resilience and global competitiveness.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor, GFL, is a leading Indian manufacturer specializing in fluoropolymers, specialty chemicals, and refrigerants. Established in 1987, GFL has grown into a key player in the global fluorochemicals market, serving a wide range of industries including automotive, electronics, and pharmaceuticals. The company is publicly listed and maintains active listings on both major Indian stock exchanges. In GFL, the sponsor group holds a 62.57% stake, while the remaining shareholding is distributed among mutual funds (10.05%), foreign institutional investors (4.61%), and the general public (22.77%). Currently GFL owns 96.87% shares in GFCL EV. The remaining shares are held by several prominent family offices of major Indian business conglomerates.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: GFCL EV plans to invest approximately US$709 million in its manufacturing facility in India, with the implementation scheduled in phases through FY29. IFC’s proposed investment of up to INR 4,300 million (approximately US$50 million equivalent) in form of CCPS will support the initial phase, while the remaining funding requirement will be met through a combination of subsequent equity raise and internal accruals.
location_description: The manufacturing unit for the Project is located in Jolva, Gujarat, India.
development_impact: Assessment of Project Outcomes: The Project aims to strengthen domestic manufacturing of critical Li-B components in India, thereby reducing reliance on imports and supporting the expansion of the BESS and EV sectors. As India’s demand for Li-B cells continues to grow, the Project is expected to contribute to import substitution and position the country as a competitive exporter of battery materials. It will also promote greater local sourcing of raw materials, reaching up to 100% for select components such as PVDF (binder) and electrolytes. Beyond its economic impact, the Project will generate approximately 250 high-skilled direct jobs and create additional employment across the broader supply chain. It will further invest in workforce development to address skills gaps in this emerging sector, equipping local engineers and technicians with expertise in advanced chemical processes, materials science, and quality control. These efforts are expected to contribute meaningfully to India’s employment objectives and support its transition to a low-carbon economy. Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation: The Project aims to support the emergence of India as a competitive player in the global battery materials market by localizing the production of key Li-B components. In the context of a highly concentrated global supply chain, the Project will contribute to diversification efforts by establishing India’s first integrated battery materials facility, enhancing supply chain resilience and reducing production costs. Anchored in a rapidly growing domestic EV ecosystem and aligned with planned greenfield cell manufacturing investments, the Project is expected to catalyze broader development across the battery value chain. It will also facilitate deeper integration of India into global EV supply networks through exports, positioning both as strategic manufacturing and export hubs.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists of the provision of long-term, flexible capital through CCPS, a financing instrument that remains scarce in India’s chemical sector. The Project requires patient and back-end loaded financing to enable successful scale-up without placing undue pressure on early-stage financial performance. IFC’s participation also plays a catalytic role in mobilizing additional long-term capital for this capital-intensive venture, which may have otherwise faced delays in securing adequate financing. Non-financial additionality includes standard setting and capacity building in environmental and social (E&S) management. Given the complexity of industrial processes and materials involved in this greenfield operation, IFC’s engagement will support the Company in aligning with international E&S standards. IFC will assist the Company in formulating and implementing an Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP), ensuring best practices are embedded across operational areas as the project becomes fully operational.

project_description: IFC is considering an equity investment in Ingenix.AI LTD (Ingenix, or the Company) to support the development of an AI-platform for clinical drug development that helps pharmaceutical companies predict clinical trial outcomes, improve efficiency, and bring new treatments to patients faster.
sponsor_shareholders: Shares of the Company are held by investment vehicles of founders Piotr Surma and Adam Dancewicz, as well as Venture Capital firms Inovo VC and OTB Ventures.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC has previously invested US$1.25 million in Ingenix via its Upstream program and is now considering converting its initial investment into shares of the Company.
location_description: The Company’s operating headquarter is Poland.
development_impact: In terms of Project outcomes, the Company is expected to create high-skill jobs in Poland, thereby delivering a key contribution to innovation in Poland. The Project is also expected to help provide access to AI-enabled clinical trial software, including in emerging markets, thereby reducing the barriers to R&D among pharmaceutical companies, and potentially resulting in productivity gains and reducing the overall cost of clinical drug development. In terms of market outcomes, the Project is expected to contribute to increasing the competitiveness of the global market for AI-enabled clinical trial software. The company is expected to increase quality competition in this market, which ultimately is expected to drive competitors to increasingly enter and scale the solutions across new geographies, including emerging markets.
additionality: IFC’s financial additionality involves the provision of own account equity as well as resource mobilization, against the background of limited venture capital available in Polan for pre-product, pre-revenue companies operating in regulated sectors in Poland. On the non-financial side, IFC will provide knowledge, capacity building and innovation by providing networks to enable the company to increase its market access and onboard customers in emerging markets. IFC will also offer guidance on corporate governance and social environmental practices, thereby enabling the company to align with best practices.

company_name: THE BIOLOGICALS AND VACCINES INSTITUTE OF SOUTHERN AFRICA (PTY) LTD
project_description: The proposed investment seeks to support, the Biologicals and Vaccines Institute of Southern Africa ('Biovac' or the 'Company'), a South African biopharmaceutical company based in Cape Town, to expand its suite of products which includes partnering with international vaccine entities through technology transfer agreements for fill and finish manufacturing of vaccines on the continent as well as an end to end scale up of an internally developed Oral Cholera Vaccine (OCV). The project will entail developing a new state-of -the-art “green” facility for end-to-end manufacturing to manufacture up to 250 million doses of vaccines per year, thus helping reduce Africa’s over dependence on imported vaccines. It will be comprised of (i) one glass vial fill & finish suite, (ii) one drug substance suite, for the manufacturing of inactivated OCV, and (iii) one blow-fill-seal (plastic line) for Fill & Finish of OCV and other vaccines (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Biovac is 47.5%-owned by two South African government agencies, namely the Technology Innovation Agency (‘TIA’) with 12.5% and the Department of Science, Technology and Innovation (‘DSI’) with 35%. The balance of Biovac’s 52.5% is held by a Biovac Consortium (Pty) Limited which consisting of private investors, who amongst others includes Dr Makhoana Morena (Biovac’s CEO).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be up to US$253 million. IFC’s proposed investment in Biovac is an “A” loan of up to US$20million and Parallel Loans of up to US$90 million, with a tenor of up to twelve years. The remaining Project costs is expected to be funded through a mix of grant, venture debt and equity.
location_description: The funds will be used in Biovac’s current facilities and a new site, both located in Cape Town, South Africa.
development_impact: The project outcomes rating is Very Strong based on the Project’s efforts to improve access to high quality vaccines in sub-Saharan African countries. The building of primary vaccine production capacity will increase access to vaccines, specifically the OCV vaccine. Additionally, the expansion of secondary vaccine manufacturing capacity and investments in R&D will increase access to new and higher quality vaccines in SSA countries and create direct and indirect employment opportunities. The rating for market outcomes is Very Strong. IFC expects the Project to strengthen the stability of local vaccine manufacturing in SSA, fostering a more self-reliant, responsive, and equitable supply chain by decreasing dependence on imports and supporting a sustainable local supply. By securing and accelerating vaccine availability, and by developing local expertise and regulatory capacity (including achieving WHO prequalification), the Project aims to boost the region’s resilience to global disruptions, enhance epidemic response, and support long-term self-sufficiency in SSA health systems
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality is provided through financing that is not readily available in the market and through direct and indirect mobilization. Non-financial additionality is provided through sharing pharmaceutical expertise, as well as industry best practices in improving the Company’s E&S practices.
Company Name: THE BIOLOGICALS AND VACCINES INSTITUTE OF SOUTHERN AFRICA (PTY) LTD

project_description: The proposed investment is an equity commitment of up to US$40 million in Perfin Infrastructure Fund II (Offshore) LP (together with its parallel vehicles “Fund II” or the “Fund”). Fund II is a Latin America infrastructure fund with a high Brazil concentration, managed by Perfin Infra Administração de Recursos ltda (“Perfin Infra” and, together with its affiliates “Perfin”). The target size of the Fund is R$3.3 – R$3.9 billion (US$600 – 700 million) and will be Perfin Infra’s first time securing commitments from non-Brazilian Limited Partners (“LP”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by Perfin Infra, an independent investment manager focused on infrastructure investments in Brazil operating since 2016. Founded in 2007, Perfin has US$6.6 billion of assets under management.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Perfin expects to raise US$700 million to the Fund. IFC's proposed investment is for up to a total equity investment of US$40 million in the Fund.
location_description: The Fund will primarily make investments in Brazil and may opportunistically consider investments in other South American countries.
development_impact: The Fund will increase access to quality infrastructure in Brazil. Brazil faces significant infrastructure challenges across multiple sectors. The Fund will address these infrastructure gaps by investing in key segments including but not limited to power generation and transmission; water and sewage; logistics and toll roads. Beyond the project, the Fund's success will strengthen the infrastructure finance market in Brazil by scaling the use of infrastructure equity funds.
additionality: IFC's international anchoring role will be critical to mobilizing capital from other international institutional investors, signaling the validity of the fund's model and providing assurance that IFC's Environmental & Social (“E&S”), integrity, and governance standards have been fully integrated into its operations. IFC will also support the Fund Manager in establishing its Environmental and Social Management System (“ESMS”) to meet IFC requirements and Performance Standards and to strengthen its climate-related policies and risk management.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an equity investment of up to US$30 million in the South Africa-domiciled African Transition Acceleration Fund (the “Fund” or “ATAF”) managed by African Infrastructure Investment Managers (“AIIM” or the “Fund Manager”) to provide early-stage capital to accelerate the development of energy transition businesses and ecosystems in Africa. ATAF has identified three core thematic verticals: clean electrons, clean molecules and sustainable transport. The project is expected to be supported by Frontier Opportunities Fund (FOF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Created in 2000, AIIM is a subsidiary of Old Mutual Limited, a leading South African financial services provider with operations in 15 countries across 3 continents and assets under management of US$84.4 billion as of June 2025. AIIM, established in 2000, is one of the largest dedicated infrastructure fund managers in Africa with assets under management of US$3.4 billion. AIIM focuses on 3 megatrends driving infrastructure demand with high growth potential in Africa: (i) digitization: data centers, fiber to the home and towers; (ii) energy transition: commercial & industrial (C&I) as well as utility scale renewable energy platforms; and lastly (iii) mobility and logistics: bulk-handling infrastructure and temperature-controlled logistics. AIIM has a 40+ strong investment professionals’ team across 5 offices: Cape Town, Johannesburg, Nairobi, Lagos and Abidjan.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund has a total committed capital target of US$ 200 million with a hard cap of US$ 250 million. IFC’s proposed investment is for up to US$ 25 million in senior equity in ATAF.
location_description: The Fund will make investments across various countries on the African continent.
development_impact: The Fund aims to provide increased access to equity and value creation for small to mid-market companies, supporting them to scale while delivering sustainability outcomes. Private Equity (PE) investment in Africa remains amongst the lowest across all regions, representing only three percent of the total PE investment in emerging markets. As there are relatively few regional fund managers serving the Africa PE market, with most of them heavily reliant on support from development finance institutions, this new fund offering from an established fund manager into the region could help signal the commercial viability of the PE model, alongside delivering sustainability outcomes and attract sustainability-linked institutional investment into Africa.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Own account equity: IFC’s equity investment will help the Fund reach its first close of US$100m, addressing key challenges in Africa’s fundraising landscape, including high risk perception, foreign exchange volatility, and economic uncertainty. With international investors withdrawing from the African Private Equity ("PE") market, even experienced regional fund managers struggle to raise capital without strong support from the development finance institutions. Resource mobilization: IFC will assist ATAF in reaching its US$200-250m fundraising target by mobilizing capital from a new investor base, including institutional investors. IFC's anchor role will validate the Fund’s strategy and reassure investors that IFC's Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) policies will be integrated into the Fund's operations. Non-Financial Additionality Standard Setting: Given IFC’s previous engagement with AIIM, IFC will review gaps in the Fund’s Environmental and Social standards to establish if IFC is required to support specific actions with the Fund Manager. Additionally, improvements in climate related policies and processes may be explored during appraisal. This additionality will only be supported if specific incremental actions are committed by IFC to improve practices.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support PLP Properties Ltd (PLP or the Company) develop a 170-room 3-star Hampton by Hilton branded-hotel at the Kotoka International Airport in Accra, Ghana (the Project). The Project hotel is expected to receive an EDGE-advanced certification.
sponsor_shareholders: PLP is jointly owned by the Feghali (75%) and Nassar (25%) families, under the leadership of Bernadette Abou Daher Feghali and Jean Assad Nassar.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost of US$29 million, will be financed with Sponsor equity (US$19 million) and debt (US$10 million).
location_description: The Project is located at the Kotoka International Airport, Accra in Ghana.
development_impact: Job Creation and Skills Development: The project will create direct jobs during the construction phase and full-time positions during operations. Supply Chain Strengthening: The hotel's food and beverage supplies will be sourced locally. This strategy will benefit Ghanaian SMEs, particularly those in agribusiness and retail sectors, by providing them with stable demand and growth opportunities. Consumer Benefits: The Hampton by Hilton-branded hotel will offer affordable yet high-quality accommodations. This will enhance service standards and accessibility for both domestic and international travelers. Economy Wide Effects: The project is expected to create direct jobs starting from the construction phase and additional indirect jobs via increased supply chain activity generated by hotel operations. The increased spending by employees and travelers in the hotel will translate into economic growth and employment. Sustainable Infrastructure: The hotel will incorporate EDGE-certified green building practices, significantly reducing energy and water consumption. This will set a new standard in the hospitality industry. Climate Contribution: The project aligns with Ghana's environmental sustainability goals by promoting resource-efficient hotel infrastructure. This alignment supports the country's broader climate objectives. Market Expansion: The introduction of an internationally recognized mid-scale hotel brand will stimulate competition in the hospitality sector. Demonstration Effect: The success of this project could serve as a model, encouraging further private sector investments in the hospitality industry, particularly in segments that are currently underserved. Resilience and Sustainability The global brand, will set a new benchmark for hotel quality and service within Ghana's market and strengthen the resilience, sustainability of supply chains in the region.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via scarce long-term financing to the Group, which is otherwise not readily available in the local market. Non-financial additionality is provided via capacity building through IFC advisory. Financial Additionality: Financing structure: IFC will provide an A-loan of up to US$10 million with a 12-year tenor and a 3-year grace period. This financial structure is difficult to secure in Ghana's financial market, making it a unique offering not only for the Company, but also for the hospitality sector. Over the past 12 months, Ghana recorded USD 0.47 billion in syndicated loans, including USD 0.01 billion in the Services sector, while no USD corporate bond issuances at a B+/- rating were recorded, either overall or in the Services sector. Non-Financial Additionality: Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC will play a key role in supporting the company to adopt best practices in hotel operations, financial structuring, and green building standards. This will include labor advisory, training and innovative approaches, and corporate governance advisory to enhance operational efficiency. Standards setting: The IFC will assist the project in implementing robust environmental and social (E&S) governance frameworks. This includes EDGE certification, which signifies excellence in sustainable construction and operational practices.

project_description: The proposed investment is a risk-sharing facility with Banco Santander S.A. and its affiliates (“Santander”) and Santander Bank Polska S.A. and its affiliates (“Santander Polska”) in a portfolio of supply chain finance-related assets for up to US$500 million with IFC investment of up to US$250 million (the “Project”). The Project falls under the Global Supply Chain Finance (GSCF) Program, a supply chain finance program launched by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) in December 2022. The GSCF supports open account trade in the emerging markets by providing funded or unfunded risk participation in partner banks’ facilities. The project is part of a crisis response initiative, through which IFC plays a countercyclical role when markets experience turbulence due to the negative economic impacts of the ongoing global food and energy crisis, compounded by rising inflation and increased tariff barriers.
sponsor_shareholders: Banco Santander is a leading banking partner for institutions with global and regional needs, a prominent player in retail and commercial banking, and a valued financial institution in its home market of Spain. Santander operates in over 40 countries and jurisdictions, providing corporations, governments, investors, institutions, and individuals with a broad range of financial products and services.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project will be in an amount up to US$500 million with an underlying portfolio of supply chain finance assets that will be risk-shared by Santander and IFC. The IFC Investment will be in amount of up to US$250 million.
location_description: The supply chain finance assets in the portfolio will be originated globally by Santander and/or its affiliates or subsidiaries.
development_impact: The proposed project is expected to provide financing to emerging market suppliers in the face of economic, trade, and supply chain disruptions caused by the ongoing crisis.
additionality: The Project helps reduce the effects of de-risking and ensure that a global systemically important bank stays engaged or expands their SCF presence in EMs. Under the GSCF, IFC will provide funded or unfunded risk participation in partner banks’ facilities given: (i) IFC's track record of crisis response efforts; (ii) its network of partner banks that support global emerging markets; (iii) its set of programs aimed at investing both large scale and transactional financing for trade and supply chain finance in emerging markets; and (iv) its ability to support private sector beneficiaries to address liquidity constraints in response to the market shocks

project_description: The proposed investment is a US$20m IFC unfunded participation under a Risk Sharing Facility (“RSF”) in an up to US$60m uncommitted transactional secured revolving trade finance Facility for 3-years with annual renewals with Banque Internationale de Commerce -BRED (Suisse) SA (“BIC-BRED” or “the Bank”) for Agro Companies International (“Agro Companies” or the “Group”). The RSF will finance Agro Companies’ grain trading working capital needs, mainly (i) cargoes on water with secured bills of lading (“BLs”), (ii) storage in warehouse at destination with Stock Monitoring Agreement (“SMA”), and (iii) receivables on African buyers mainly covered by prime insurers. It will be processed under the Global Warehouse Finance Program (“GWFP”) with delegated authority from the Board.
sponsor_shareholders: Agro Companies is a family-owned trading group based in Geneva, established in 1983 by M. Jean-Christophe Egli. It is today wholly owned by his daughter, Rachel Boubet-Egli. The Group has become the leading supplier of wheat to many countries in West & Central Africa, including Ghana, Cameroon, Guinea-Conakry and Togo. The Group is composed of 6 operating entities: (i) AgroHall, a wheat purchasing entity in Canada, (ii) Ifaco Grain, the main wheat trading entity, (iii) Ifaco Feed, the feed trading entity, (iv) Agri Company SA (Agrico), (v) Agro Industries SA, and (v) York Overseas, the shipping company of the Group. Banque Internationale de Commerce -BRED (Suisse) SA (‘BIC-BRED’ or the ‘Bank’) is based in Geneva and is a wholly owned subsidiary of BRED Banque Populaire, Paris. The Bank was initially established as a branch in 1991 then obtained a full banking license in August 2015 from the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA). The mission of the Bank is to assist the development of companies engaged in the trade of energy, agricultural and metal commodities. BIC-BRED covers four sectors including Financial Institutions, FX & Trading, Trade Finance and Corporate Finance & Business Solutions.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total investment by the Bank is US$60m in an uncommitted transactional secured trade finance Facility for 3-years with annual renewals to be fronted by BIC-BRED in favor of Agro Companies International group entities. IFC’s investment as a disclosed risk participant will be for an amount of up to US$20m (i.e. 1/3rd of BIC-BRED Bank’s share).
location_description: Africa Region
development_impact: The Project is expected to: (i) increase the supply of wheat to African millers in the destination countries to produce wheat products; (ii) increase the supply of animal feed (soya bean, corn) to destination countries; (iii) increase technical support from the Group to millers to improve food safety and quality; and (iv) increase (in-kind) financing to millers to ensure continuity in commodity trading. To measure progress against this outcome, IFC will track the: (i) volume of products supplied to customers; and (ii) number of customers reached. The Project is expected to have catalytic effect of stimulating industry-wide best practices in grain trade financing, grain sourcing and processing, and facilitating food quality and safety improvements, moving the sector toward greater competitiveness from domination by large players to more participation by mid-sized players. To measure progress against this outcome, IFC will track the number of private sector banks providing support to the Group (which should increase or at least remain stable).
additionality: IFC’s proposed investment consists of a $20 million risk sharing facility with BIC-BRED to increase their available credit facility to $60 million for AGRO COMPANIES to finance more trade flows. BIC-BRED had limits on facility size that prevented the Bank from financing large cargoes of wheat and feed when the prices were high. With IFC, larger financing have become possible. In addition, IFC’s involvement is expected to contribute to the reinforcement of the Group’s environmental and social practices, in line with IFC’s Performance Standards and industry best practices.

project_description: The proposed project entails an IFC equity and debt investment of up to US$18.75 million (approximately INR 1,650 million) each, aggregating to up to US$37.5 million (approximately INR 3.33 billion), in Invesdian Pte. Ltd., a newly established student housing platform (the Platform or the Company) to be managed by SPIRE Investment Manager Pte. Ltd. (SPIRE) ( https://spireim.com/ ). Roche Holdings Ltd., Mauritius, wholly owned by Mr. Shapoor Pallonji Mistry will serve as the Sponsor of the Platform. The Platform is focused on the development, ownership, and operation of a portfolio of purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) projects catering to students of higher education institutions (HEIs) in India.
sponsor_shareholders: Incorporated in 2025, Invesdian Pte. Ltd. is presently wholly owned by Mr. Padmakumar Unnikrishnan, a Director of SPIRE. Upon execution of the definitive agreements, ownership of the Company will be transferred to Roche Holdings Ltd., prior to investment by other incoming investors, including IFC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be about US$300 million (approximately INR 26.4 billion) and IFC's investment will be in the form of equity shares and optionally convertible debentures or non-convertible debentures.
location_description: Across multiple cities and towns in India.
development_impact: The expected development impact include: (i) Stakeholder Effects (Tenants): The project will increase the availability and quality of housing for students, addressing a critical need for safe and secure accommodation and supporting the retention of students in higher education institutions in India. The PBSA developments will be located in well-connected areas of major education hubs, improving safety, quality of life, and indirectly contributing to higher graduation rates. The project will also promote gender inclusion as the Platform’s portfolio is expected to include female-only hostels, (ii) Environmental Effects: As part of the project, the client will pursue EDGE Certification for the PBSA portfolio, ensuring energy efficiency and reducing greenhouse gas emissions compared to comparable local buildings, and (iii) Economy-wide Effects and Contribution to Market Creation: The development of ~20,000 beds of PBSAs will lead to direct job creation during and after construction. The increase in demand for building materials and other supply chain linkages, including building management and cleaning services, increased tax revenues, and potential improvements in infrastructure, may lead to indirect job creation.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the proposed project is both financial and non-financial: (i) Financial additionality will be provided through a long-term financing structure and resource mobilization. This investment will strengthen the Company's financial soundness, creditworthiness, and governance, and enhance overall confidence in the PBSA market. IFC also expects to mobilize third-party capital into the Platform, and (ii) Non-financial additionality will be provided through supporting the Platform in improving environmental and social practices and in developing an Environmental and Social Action Plan, including Fire and Life Safety standards. In addition, IFC's Green Building Specialist will work with the Company to explore opportunities to pursue EDGE certification for its PBSA developments.

project_description: The proposed investment in ZZ2 Beherend Pty Limited (“ZZ2” or the “Group”) is to finance expansion of avocado production, expansion of tomato production in net houses, investments in solar energy for its farm operations and refinance part of its existing debt (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: ZZ2 is owned by Bertie Van Zyl Trust (95%) and Amsodebe Trust (5%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment package comprises of (i) Senior A loan of ZAR900m (US$52m) in Bertie van Zyl Pty Limited (ZZ2’s subsidiary); and (ii) redeemable non-convertible preference shares (“preferred equity”) of ZAR100m (US$5.8m) in ZZ2.
location_description: Investments under the Projects are planned to be in South Africa.
development_impact: (i) generate value added and create 522 direct jobs and 670 indirect jobs along the value chain (ii) strengthen the local economy by generating forex inflows through increased exports (iii) reduce Green House Gas (GHG) emissions through the expansion of renewable energy use (solar energy) and reduction of food loss (iv) improve competitiveness of vegetables and fruits market through increased production and diversified product offerings and vertical integration to increase productivity and quality of products in an environment constrained by climate change (v) strengthen integration of local value chains with global value chains.
additionality: (i) provision of preferred equity rarely available in the market for agribusinesses (ii) support ZZ2 to align its operations with IFC Performance Standards and industry best practices in operational sustainability and resource (water and energy) efficiency.

project_description: The proposed investment comprises senior unsecured sustainability linked-debt by IFC, for its own account, of up to THB 2.8 billion (approximately US$85 million equivalent) through subscription to senior unsecured Sustainability-linked Bonds (SLB) proposed, to be issued by CPNREIT as part of public issuances in one or more tranches.
sponsor_shareholders: CPNREIT is the largest retail focused Real Estate Investment Trust in Thailand with a portfolio of 12 high grade assets across the country. Established in 2017, CPNREIT assets include 7 shopping malls, 4 office buildings and 1 hotel with a combined Gross Leasable Area of over 365,000 square meters. Central Pattana Public Company (CPN) is the largest unitholder in CPNREIT and the property manager for the assets.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s debt investment of up to THB2.8 billion (approximately US$ 85 million equivalent) will go towards payment of the 1st 10 years of the leasehold extension on Central Rama 2, a shopping mall in Bangkok and CPNREIT’s largest asset by Gross Leasable Area with 99,330 square meters of Gross Leasable Area.
location_description: Thailand
development_impact: The most significant anticipated project-level outcomes are improved access to longer-term financing in Thailand and positive environmental effects from improved energy and water use. REITs open an alternative stream of capital that otherwise would not be available, by mobilizing financing from a wider pool of capital market investors. By enabling a relatively novel bond instrument, the Project will help deepen Thailand’s domestic capital market.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the proposed project is both financial and non-financial. IFC’s participation through long term financing through the 7 year tenor will enhance investor confidence, enabling CPNREIT to secure the financing needed to accelerate its green transition. The longer tenor will provide the Company with greater flexibility to advance its portfolio decarbonization efforts and support Thailand’s ambitious GHG reduction targets. IFC's non financial additionality will be in the form of knowledge, innovation, and capacity building support via IFC's U/A engagement.

project_description: The proposed project is an unfunded risk-sharing facility with Standard Chartered Bank (“SCB”) in a portfolio of supply chain finance-related assets for up to US$500 million with IFC participation of up to US$250 million (the “Project”). The Project falls under the Global Supply Chain Finance (GSCF) Program, launched by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) in December 2022. GSCF supports trade in the emerging markets by providing funded or unfunded risk participation in partner banks’ facilities. IFC risk participation is up to 50% of eligible assets in the facility (up to $250 million for IFC’s own account) and will mobilize SCB for the balance. This Facility aims to further improve access to Supply Chain Finance (SCF) in Emerging Markets (EM)s, including providing pre-shipment finance, bringing working capital benefits to local suppliers.
sponsor_shareholders: Standard Chartered is a leading international banking group, with a presence in 53 of the world’s most dynamic markets. Its purpose is to drive commerce and prosperity through its unique diversity, and its heritage and values are expressed in the brand promise, here for good. Standard Chartered PLC is listed on the London, Hong Kong, Bombay (Mumbai) and India’s National stock exchanges.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project will be in an amount up to US$500 million with underlying portfolio of supply chain finance (SCF) assets that will be risk-shared by Standard Chartered and IFC on a pre-agreed basis.
location_description: The supply chain finance assets in the portfolio will be originated globally by Standard Chartered Bank and/or its affiliates or subsidiaries.
development_impact: The Project is expected to expand the availability of working capital for EM suppliers and allow SCB to deliver funding to suppliers including SMEs. The Project will provide pre-shipment finance to bring working capital benefits to local suppliers, which will help the market for working capital financing for local suppliers become more competitive.
additionality: IFC’s risk participation helps reduce the effects of de-risking and ensure that a global systemically important bank stays engaged or expands their SCF presence in EMs.

project_description: IFC will provide a senior secured loan of up to US$33 million equivalent (the IFC Loan) to subsidiaries of Eurasia Group AG (EG AG, the Group), a Swiss-based group that distributes and services John Deere and other Western-made agricultural machinery in Kazakhstan and the Kyrgyz Republic. The IFC Loan will finance the construction of new service centers in Astana, Almaty, and Pavlodar in Kazakhstan, and in Bishkek in the Kyrgyz Republic (the Project). The IFC Loan will be committed as follows: (i) up to US$30 million equivalent to Eurasia Group Kazakhstan LLC (EG KZ), and (ii) up to US$3 million equivalent to Eurasia Group Kyrgyzstan LLC (EG KZ, together with EG KZ, the Companies).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1998, EG AG’s subsidiaries - Eurasia Group Kazakhstan LLC (100% owned through the intermediate holding company MEGAS Invest LLC) and Eurasia Group Kyrgyzstan LLC (99.99% owned) - are the exclusive dealers of John Deere and distributors of other premium-brand agricultural machinery in Kazakhstan and the Kyrgyz Republic. EG AG is 100% owned by the Swiss-based holding company Eurasia Swiss Holding AG.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at up to US$38.8 million, which will be primarily funded by the IFC Loan of up to US$33 million, with the remaining US$5.8 million to be financed through the Group’s internal cash generation.
location_description: The Project will be implemented in Astana, Pavlodar, and Almaty in Kazakhstan, and Bishkek in the Kyrgyz Republic.
development_impact: The expected Project-level outcomes include increased access to advanced agricultural equipment for farmers, economy-wide benefits through job creation, and stimulation of downstream linkages along the distribution and service chains. The Project is also expected to enhance competitiveness and efficiency in the agricultural machinery and services market in Kazakhstan and the Kyrgyz Republic through demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality stems from IFC’s provision of long-term financing in local currency equivalent, which is not readily available in the local market. Non-financial additionality includes setting standards on environmental and social (E&S) practices, as well as knowledge, innovation, and capacity building through the proposed advisory services.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a financing package of up to US$16 million to the Fideicomiso Irrevocable de Desarrollo Inmobiliario y Administración Araya (the “Trust”), a trust established to develop a lower-middle-income greenfield housing project in Punta Cana, Dominican Republic (“DR”). The project comprises the development of 77 small residential buildings, for a total of 462 apartments (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Trust is jointly controlled by its two beneficiaries: (1) Fondo de Inversión Cerrado de Desarrollo de Viviendas en la Republic Dominicana I (the “Fund”; 70% stake), a public closed-end investment vehicle focused on financing affordable and tourism-related housing projects across the DR; and (2) Grupo BAK, S.R.L (the “BAK”; 30% stake), a housing developer with 49 years of experience fully owned by the Briseno family, mainly Mariano Briseno via BK2006 Inc.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost is US$60.3 million (DOP 3,619 million). The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$16 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Punta Cana, Dominican Republic.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to increase access to housing and generate positive environmental effects in the Dominican Republic. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing to deepen the competitiveness of the Dominican Republic's housing sector by demonstrating the feasibility of adopting resilient and green building standards and allocating units to underserved populations, such as women.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the proposed project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality is provided through financing structure, providing financing at terms that are not readily available in the market for middle-income housing development. Non-financial additionality is provided through knowledge, innovation, and capacity building, as IFC will provide international E&S best practices through the implementation of an E&S Action Plan (ESAP) and provide its global expertise in green buildings for the Project to obtain EDGE or equivalent green building certifications, as well as building resilience.

country: Middle East, Pakistan, and Afg Region
project_description: The proposed investment involves an equity participation into Catalyst MENA Climate Fund II (CMCF2 or the Fund) to be established by Catalyst Investment Management (Catalyst MENA). CMCF2 would be the second infrastructure fund established by Catalyst MENA following the successful raise of US$57 million in Catalyst MENA Clean Energy Fund I (CMCF1), an infrastructure fund launched in 2016. The Fund's target size is US$150-200 million with a first close target of US$70-85 million. It will focus on climate mitigation, climate adaptation and energy transition themes in the form of inter alia renewable energy infrastructure, energy storage, energy efficiency and water-related projects across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), with a primary focus on Jordan, Egypt, Tunisia and Morocco.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 2006, Catalyst MENA is the first investment manager in the MENA region to focus exclusively on renewable energy, energy efficiency, and energy/water technology. The Catalyst MENA team brings a combined investment experience of over 100 years, with the core team contributing more than 70 years of expertise. Catalyst MENA was among the first MENA-focused sponsors to develop solar photovoltaic (PV) Independent Power Producer (IPP) projects, starting with a 23MW project in 2014. In the long-term, it aims to develop and invest in a portfolio of over 500MW of renewable energy projects, having already contributed to more than 170MW of projects in Jordan and Egypt. Most of Catalyst MENA’s core team have worked together for over 17 years. They have deployed over US$47 million of equity into solar projects.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund is domiciled in Luxembourg with a target final size of US$150-200 million and a target 1st close of US$70-85 million by end-December 2025. The Fund targets a balanced portfolio of greenfield and brownfield projects (capped at 25% of the total commitments), spanning various development stages, from early-stage to selecting operating assets. The proposed IFC investment is to provide up to US$15 million equity participation into CMCF2.
location_description: The Fund will invest in a diversified portfolio of renewable energy projects, primary solar PV, with a predominant geographic focus on MENA, particularly Egypt, Jordan, Tunisia, and Morocco.
development_impact: The expected project-level outcomes include Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions mitigation through displacing more carbon-intensive and expensive power sources, as well as implementing energy-efficient solutions. At the market level, the Project is expected to strengthen the climate finance ecosystem in MENA by promoting climate-focused equity instruments that support sustainability outcomes and power sector resilience in the target markets.
additionality: IFC’s equity investment of up to US$15 million in CMCF2 will enable the Fund to expand into new markets with growing demand for greenfield renewable energy projects, while also helping mobilize third-party investors toward its US$150–250 million target. Beyond financing, IFC’s involvement will enhance the Fund’s capacity and credibility through potential advisory support on gender and social inclusion, strengthening investor confidence in high-risk markets through its due diligence and long-term commitment to renewable energy, and promoting good environmental and social risk management practices aligned with IFC Performance Standards (PS), including development of an E&S management system (ESMS).
Country: Middle East, Pakistan, and Afg Region

sector: Grocery Retail (Supermarkets, Hypermarkets, Convenience Stores etc.)
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an A-loan of up to US$15mn equivalent in Nigerian Naira (NGN), supported by IDA PSW Local Currency Facility (“IDA PSW LCF”). The proposed IFC loan is to support an expansion to open 25 new stores (the “Project”). Through its expansion plan, Justrite aims to become the leading supermarket retail brand in Nigeria.
sponsor_shareholders: Justrite Limited was founded in 2000 by Ayodele Patrick Aderinwale and his wife Oluwatosin Temitayo Aderinwale. In 2022, Africinvest, a pan-African private equity fund, acquired a 40.4% stake in Justrite Limited. As a result of this acquisition, Ayodele Patrick Aderinwale and his wife Oluwatosin Temitayo Aderinwale currently have a 28.3% shareholding each while Omoboye Fajeku owns the remaining 2.9%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$24 million and the proposed IFC investment is an A-loan of up to US$15mn equivalent in Nigerian Naira (NGN).
location_description: All the Project sites will be located in the Southwestern States of Nigeria including Lagos, Oyo, Osun, and Ogun.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcomes are the stakeholder effects on increased access to modern retail. The project is also expected to generate employee effects through quality job creation, and environmental effects through EDGE-certification of stores. Beyond the project outcomes, the IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater market competitiveness via competitive pressure and capacity building channels. The project benefits from an inclusion adjustment due to expected increases in the female employee share in the workforce, and a climate adjustment.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality consists of providing innovative financing structures to support Justrite’s growth and meet its funding needs. On non-financial additionality, IFC will focus on standard setting and knowledge, innovation, and capacity building.

company_name: Allianz Asia Pacific Infrastructure Credit Fund S.A., SICAV-RAIF.
project_description: The proposed investment entails an investment of up to US$60 million for IFC’s own account in Allianz Asia Pacific Infrastructure Credit Fund (the “Fund”) to be launched by Allianz Global Investors (“AGI”) with a target fund size of US$500 million. The Fund will focus on providing senior secured loans to medium-sized, high-growth infrastructure companies in emerging markets across the Asia-Pacific region. Up to 40% of the investment is expected to be allocated to climate finance, supporting sustainable infrastructure projects.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund is structured as a Luxembourg-based investment company with variable capital (société d'investissement à capital variable). AGI’s Luxembourg branch serves as the Fund’s authorized Alternative Investment Fund Manager (the “AIFM”) and will receive non-discretionary advice from Allianz Global Investors Singapore Ltd., a Singapore-based private company owned by AGI. Founded in 1998, AGI is a global asset management firm and a wholly owned subsidiary of Allianz SE, one of the world’s largest financial services providers, specializing in insurance and asset management. AGI is present across Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the US, with offices in financial hubs such as London, Paris, Munich, Frankfurt, Zurich, Luxembourg, New York, Singapore, and Mumbai.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment entails an investment of up to US$60 million for IFC’s own account in a US$500 million target private credit fund to be launched by AGI.
location_description: AGI is headquartered in Frankfurt, Germany. The Fund will be advised by Allianz Global Investors Singapore Ltd. Allianz Global Investors Singapore Ltd team is based in Singapore and Mumbai. The Fund will focus on investments in emerging Asian markets, primarily Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, and the Philippines in Southeast Asia, as well as India in South Asia.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcome is increased access to finance for mid-market infrastructure projects in emerging Asia, including for climate assets; increased renewable energy supply and access to data hosting centers; and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction. Beyond the Project level outcomes, the contribution to market creation is that IFC anticipates that the Project will strengthen the competitiveness of the private credit market in the infrastructure mid-market space.
additionality: Financial Additionality: IFC’s own account equity: IFC’s proposed own-account investment of up to US$60 million would provide essential capital to support the launch of AGI’s first infrastructure focused strategy in emerging Asia. Resource Mobilization: IFC’s commitment will play a catalytic role in attracting additional institutional capital to the Fund. Non-financial additionality: Standard setting: IFC will support AGI in enhancing its Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) and climate risk management system to meet global best practices, tailor them for infrastructure projects, and improve impact measurement and reporting in line with international standards.
Company Name: Allianz Asia Pacific Infrastructure Credit Fund S.A., SICAV-RAIF.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a purchase by IFC, for its own account, of a senior unsecured Colombian peso-linked bond to be issued by Bogotá Distrito Capital (“Bogotá” or “the Municipality”) for an amount of up to US$125 million. IFC proceeds will be used for funding the Municipality’s obligations under the Linea 2 del Metro de Bogotá (in English, Bogota Metro Line 2 – BML2), being developed by the Bogotá Metro Company (EMB).
sponsor_shareholders: Bogotá is Colombia’s capital city and the fourth largest metropolis in Latin America, playing a pivotal role in the country’s economy. It contributes over a fourth of its GDP and employs more than a fifth of its workforce.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Bogotá will issue a Colombia peso-linked bond of up to US$600 million with a 10-year maturity and amortization scheduled in the final three years. IFC will anchor the issuance by purchasing up to US$125 million of the bond.
location_description: Bogotá, Colombia.
development_impact: The project is expected to improve access to quality urban transport for underserved populations— enabling shorter travel times to jobs, educational opportunities and economic inclusion—alongside reducing environmental footprint for Bogotá's mass transit system. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its investment will have a demonstration effect and contribute to financial resilience of municipal entities, capital markets integration, and will encourage further placement of sustainable finance instruments in Colombia and Latin America and the Caribbean.
additionality: IFC's additionality through the Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality will be provided in the forms of: (i) an innovative financing structure, as the Project will incorporate a sustainable finance instrument in debt capital markets into Bogotá's funding strategy, providing necessary funding for the Municipality's landmark projects; and (ii) resource mobilization, as IFC's participation as an anchor investor will leverage IFC's global experience in sustainable finance instruments and mobilize commercial and institutional investors, signaling credibility and stability to ensure a successful placement of Colombia's first offshore green bond by a municipality. Non-financial additionality will be provided in the form of non-commercial risk mitigation. As an anchor investor, IFC will provide confidence to international investors, mitigate execution risks, and strengthen the Municipality's ability to achieve its targeted issue size, even in volatile market conditions.

project_description: The CBL Group (the Group) is one of Sri Lanka’s largest food manufacturing conglomerates and produces high quality confectionary and convenient nutrition. CBL Investments Limited (CBLI) is the holding company of the CBL Group. The Group operates in 3 main food businesses – (i) confectionaries which is the Group’s largest business and includes biscuits, chocolates and cakes; (ii) packaged (convenience) foods which includes nutri-foods, cereals, soy-based products, soups, noodles and porridges in original, value added and ready to eat formats; and (iii) natural foods which includes coconut-based products (largely coconut milk), fruit products and spices for export. The proposed investment entails three loans of up to US$40 million to CBLI, and Ceylon Biscuits Limited (CBL) and CBL Global Foods Limited (GFL), two wholly owned subsidiaries of CBLI, for the purpose of funding the Group’s growth plans.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsors of the CBL Group are the Wickramasingha family (Sponsors). The Chairman is Mr. Ramya Wickramasingha, and the Group Managing Director (MD) is Ms. Sheamalee Wickramasingha. Family members of the Wickramasinghe family own the majority of the shareholding of the holding company CBLI. CBL and GFL are each wholly owned subsidiaries of CBLI.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The loan proceeds will be used for expansion plans of the Group, which include (i) acquisition of a coconut milk and desiccated coconut (DC) manufacturing plant in Sulawesi region of Indonesia; and (ii) increasing production and distribution capacity of biscuits in Ghana.
location_description: Ghana, Indonesia
development_impact: Financial Additionality: Long-term USD funds: IFC will provide a long-term US Dollar 7-year loan with a grace period of 24 months, which is not available in the local market for CBL. Non-Financial Additionality: IFC has engaged extensively with CBL through multiple advisory engagements and this investment transaction is a direct result of IFC’s advisory work with this client. CBL is interested to avail of IFC’s advisory services in Ghana which will focus on increasing the number and role of women in the distributor network.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality stems from IFC providing long-term US dollar funding which is not readily available in the local market. Sri Lanka has restricted access to foreign currencies, including the US dollar, due to the economic crisis. IFC’s involvement has been crucial in providing counter-cyclical financing through foreign direct investment (FDI) for the Group’s international expansion plans. Non-financial additionality comprises knowledge, innovation, and capacity building. IFC has engaged with the Group through multiple advisory engagements, and this investment transaction is a direct result of IFC’s advisory work with the Group to improve the efficiency of their distribution and retailer network. IFC is present in discussions with the Group to provide gender advisory support to develop and increase the number of women in its distribution network overseas. IFC is also discussing potential advisory services regarding fortifying some of its cereal products with essential nutrients. In addition, IFC has reviewed and prepared an action plan meet to align the Group with IFC’s Performance Standards.

company_name: MR. D.I.Y. Holding (Thailand) Public Company Limited
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an equity investment of up to THB 810 million (approximately US$25.0 million equivalent) as an anchor investor in the Initial Public Offering (“IPO”) of MR D.I.Y. Holding (Thailand) Public Company Limited (“MRDIYT” or the “Company”) (the “Project”). The Company will be listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (“SET”). MRDIYT opened its first store in 2016 and has since grown to become a leading home improvement and lifestyle retailer in Thailand. The Company offers mass-market consumers convenient access to a wide variety of essential household items at affordable prices. As of June 30, 2025, the Company operated 1,027 “MR. D.I.Y.” stores in all 77 provinces across all regions in Thailand. The Company is targeting to open more than 600 new stores from 2025-2027, with the majority to be located in rural and underserved regions of Thailand.
sponsor_shareholders: MRDIYT is part of a collective network of entities that carry on retail operations under the brand name of “MR. D.I.Y.” in Thailand, Malaysia, Brunei, Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines, Cambodia, India, Vietnam, Spain, Turkey, Bangladesh, Poland and South Africa as at June 30, 2025 (the “MR. D.I.Y. International Network”). Except for MRDIYT, the controlling interest in the MR. D.I.Y. International Network is held by Tan Yu Yeh and Tan Yu Wei (“TYY and TYW”) and related entities. Following the IPO, the Company’s largest shareholders are expected to be (i) TYY and TYW; (ii) Ms. Titanan Sun and Mr. Jhomphong Tomongkhon; and (iii) MR. D.I.Y. Co., Ltd , an entity controlled by TYY, TYW, Ms. Titanan Sun and Mr. Jhomphong Tomongkhon.
