total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an equity investment of up to THB 810 million (approximately US$25.0 million equivalent) as an anchor investor in the IPO of MRDIYT. The Company will use primary proceeds from the IPO to (among others) support its store network expansion and increase its warehouse and distribution capacity.
location_description: Thailand
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are improved access to affordable and good quality home improvement retail products and economy-wide impact based on potential jobs creation and value-added. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater market competitiveness via competitive pressure and demonstration effects.?
additionality: IFC’s investment is expected to provide both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality consists of IFC's own-account equity. Through supporting the Company's IPO, IFC will help to Company to access long-term patient capital that is needed for its expansion plans, but is not readily available through the public equity market, as illustrated by the low number of listings on the SET in 2025. Non-financial additionality consists of standard setting to support the Company's transition to a publicly listed company. IFC will assist the Company to align its operations with IFC’s Performance Standards and international standards.
Company Name: MR. D.I.Y. Holding (Thailand) Public Company Limited

project_description: The proposed investment is a local currency-linked senior/unsecured loan facility of up to US$81 million (approximately MWK 140.5 billion equivalent) to Illovo Sugar (Malawi) plc (ISM or the Company). The loan has an 8-year term with a c.1.5-year grace period. The loan is supported by the International Development Association Private Sector Window (IDA PSW) in the form of local currency hedging and will benefit from a corporate guarantee from the Company's ultimate parent Associated British Foods plc (the Guarantor or ABF) over the life of the loan.
sponsor_shareholders: ISM is listed on the Malawian Stock Exchange with ABF as the largest shareholder with c.76% of share capital held through Sucoma Holdings Limited. A c.11% shareholding is held by Old Mutual Assurance Company (Malawi) with the remaining stake held by public investors. ABF is listed on the London Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed loan will be committed in two phases. The first phase is an investment of up to US$36 million to finance the upgrade of bulk water irrigation infrastructure at the Company's Nchalo Sugar Estate, connecting to the World Bank's Shire Valley Transformation Program (SVTP) irrigation project. The second phase is an investment of up to US$45 million for a boiler replacement and debottlenecking in the sugar mill factory. The first phase investment is expected to be supported by a Water Purchasing Agreement between Illovo Sugar (Malawi) plc and the Government of Malawi, which is anticipated to be signed shortly.
location_description: The proposed first phase investment of US$36 million will be used to fund the upgrade of the water irrigation infrastructure at the Company's Nchalo Sugar Estate which is located in the southern part of Malawi. The proposed second phase investment of US$45m million will be used to expand the current factory capacity at the Nchalo Estate.
development_impact: The project is expected to have significant development impacts in Malawi, primarily in terms of job creation and domestic value addition, contributing to broader economic growth as well as positive environmental effects. It aims to enhance the competitiveness and sustainability of the sugar market. Additionally, the investment is anticipated to have market-catalyzing effects, supporting the success of the World Bank's Shire Valley Transformation Program (SVTP). However, potential climate events could pose challenges to the SVTP's implementation. Overall, the project is poised to contribute positively to the host country's development by fostering economic resilience and environmental sustainability.
additionality: With support from the IDA PSW LCF, IFC will provide the Company with local currency-denominated financing on terms (size, tenor, and structure) that are otherwise unavailable in the country. This transaction structure will also provide the Company with the foreign exchange needed for capital purchases, which is currently in critically short supply. IFC will also help further align the Company's operations with IFC's Performance Standards (PSs) and industry best practices.

company_name: TURKIYE SISE VE CAM FABRIKALARI ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: The IFC Financing will help finance the Company’s solar and flat glass capex including refinancing of short-term loans availed for its implementation and working capital needs in Türkiye.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1935, Sisecam Group, headquartered in Turkiye is a leading glass and soda ash manufacturer. The company operates 45 production facilities across 14 countries, with an annual production capacity of 8.1 million tons of glass and 5 million tons of soda ash. Sisecam oversees more than 50 affiliated companies spanning five core business divisions: architectural glass, industrial glass, glass packaging, chemicals, and glassware. Approximately 58% of Sisecam is owned by Türkiye Is Bankasi A.S. and its related entities, while the remaining shares are publicly traded on Borsa Istanbul.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project, with a total estimated cost of US$600 million, will support flat and solar glass manufacturing, contributing to the growth of renewable energy solutions and meeting increased demand for solar glass, while also increasing the energy efficiency of the existing plant operations. The IFC Financing will be allocated as follows: (i) refinancing of short term loans secured to implement a greenfield flat and solar glass manufacturing capacity increase in Tarsus Municipality; (ii) cold repairs of its flat glass line in Mersin City; (iii) working capital requirements in its glass operations in Türkiye and refinancing of its upcoming Eurobond payment (together the “Project”). The Project will support solar glass manufacturing, contributing to the growth of renewable energy solutions and meeting increased demand for solar glass, while also increasing the energy efficiency of the existing plant operations The IFC financing is aligned with the Paris Agreement and is structured as an incentive-based loan with ambitious sustainability-linked performance indicators tied to gender and climate targets. IFC Financing may be disbursed in US Dollars or Euros through one or more commitments
location_description: IFC Financing will be used entirely for Sisecam's glass businesses in Turkiye (both for capex and working capital).
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good with a score of 52. The expected project-level outcomes are (i) environmental / climate effects: reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through investments in solar supply chain (solar glass) and efficiency improvements through cold repair of existing flat glass furnace; and (ii) economy-wide effects: foreign exchange savings, skilled job creation and domestic value addition due to production of higher margin goods. The anticipated market-level outcome is the enhancement of Turkish glass manufacturing sector’s adoption of practices that are not yet fully mainstreamed in the sector such as water use standards and gender inclusive practices or female employees. The investment has the potential to catalyze a broader market shift towards development impact-related financial instruments such as incentive-based loans, sustainability-linked loans, and bonds for other Turkish manufacturers in his sector through demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC will deliver both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC’s financial additionality will mainly be through countercyclical provision of financing as Sisecam's access to longer term funding is constrained due to the country’s current volatile and liquidity-strained market, coupled with the recent increase in Sisecam’s leverage and associated credit rating downgrades. The IFC Financing, with a tenor of seven years, will enhance Sisecam’s financial resilience and extend the weighted average life of its debt portfolio, enabling pursuit of investments with long gestation periods. The expected mobilization component (58 percent of the total Project cost) will further strengthen IFC’s financial additionality. IFC’s non-financial additionality will be delivered by guiding and incentivizing Sisecam to achieve its ambitious and quantitative sustainability targets and position the Company for its first sustainability-linked loan (SLL) in the medium-term. Additionally, IFC`s extensive expertise in Environmental and Social (E&S) related matters will lead to Sisecam aligning its E&S policies and procedures with IFC’s Performance Standards. These constitute part of IFC’s longstanding and ongoing guidance to Sisecam on sustainability and E&S matters.
Company Name: TURKIYE SISE VE CAM FABRIKALARI ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: The proposed investment is for a commitment of up to US$100 million, along with a proposed co-investment envelope of US$100 million, in the Actis Energy 6 Fund (the “Fund” or “AE6”), a US$6 billion (target) fund primarily investing in power generation, electricity transmission and distribution, and other energy-related and/or distribution businesses.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by Actis EU Management Sarl (“Actis”). Actis is a leading private equity investor in growth markets.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment in the Fund is up to US$100 million, along with a proposed co-investment envelope of US$100 million.
location_description: The Fund will invest across growth markets, including Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa, and Central and Eastern Europe.
development_impact: Expected development impact outcomes include (i) increased access to energy financing across emerging markets, addressing energy transition needs; and (ii) deepening the competitiveness of the emerging markets energy market through expanding equity financing.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the project will be both financial, consisting in helping to attract additional resources for the Fund from other institutional investors, and non-financial, anchored in providing knowledge, innovation and capacity building on its strategic partnership with Actis to support the Fund more effectively invest and operate across a wider range of emerging markets .

project_description: The proposed transaction entails an investment of up to INR 12,840 million (approximately US$150 million equivalent) in the form of subscription to Non-Convertible Debentures (NCDs) issued by SignatureGlobal (India) Limited (Signature or the Company). The Company is developing an integrated township project comprising of residential houses, commercial and industrial plots located in Sohna, Haryana (the Daxin project). The proposed loan will be utilized to partly finance the development of Daxin project and other future middle-income housing projects in India (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor family includes Mr. Pradeep Aggarwal (Chairman of the Company), Mr. Ravi Aggarwal, Mr. Lalit Aggarwal and Mr. Devender Aggarwal. The Sponsor family holds 69.63 percent of the total share capital of the Company while the balance is held by financial institutions and the public.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC's investment of up to approximately US$150 million in equivalent INR will be used to part finance (i) the Daxin project; (ii) purchase land around the Daxin project; and (iii) other upcoming housing projects of the Company. The Company will fund the balance amount required for the Project through internal accruals.
location_description: The Daxin project is located in Sohna, Haryana and the upcoming housing projects are proposed to be located in Haryana or Delhi National Capital Region (NCR).
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects via increased access to quality middle-income housing and industrial plots (ii) environmental effects via improved efficiency in energy and water usage which will be verified by EDGE or higher green building certification. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment to promote competitiveness in the Indian housing sector by exerting competitive pressures on developers to improve the quality of their projects. The Project will also have demonstration effects on other developers that will be incentivized to expand in smaller micro-markets, adapt their mixed-use business model, and cater to the underserved middle-income populations.
additionality: IFC’s financial additionality comes through resource mobilization, and financing structure. IFC will provide capital required primarily for land acquisition and construction finance which is not readily available in the market. Non-financial additionality (knowledge, innovation, and capacity building): IFC will help Signature obtain EDGE or higher certification, helping improve energy efficiency and optimizing water usage.

project_description: The proposed investment is through Non-Convertible Debentures (“NCDs”) of up to INR 13,125 million (US$150 million equivalent) issued to DCM Shriram Limited (“DCM Shriram” or the “Company”) to partly finance the Company’s capex plan for FY25 to FY27 (the “Project”). The Project is expected to comprise (i) aluminum chloride and calcium chloride production facility at a new site in Jhagadia, Bharuch, Gujarat; (ii) maintenance, project capex and refinancing of loans for the sugar mills at Loni, Hariawan and Ajbapur and distillery plants in Ajbapur and Hariawan (all in Uttar Pradesh) (iii) maintenance and project capex for chlor-alkali production in Kota, Rajasthan; and (iii) long-term working capital of the Company.
sponsor_shareholders: DCM Shriram is an integrated Indian company present in three major segments (i) agri-rural business (sugar, ethanol, urea, hybrid seeds, crop protection and plant nutrition products),(ii) chemicals (caustic soda, chlorine, calcium carbide, aluminum chloride, polyvinyl chloride (PVC)) and Fenesta Building Systems. DCM Shriram is owned and managed by three Shriram brothers – Mr. Ajay S Shriram, Mr. Vikram S Shriram and Mr. Ajit S Shriram (together “Sponsors”) who collectively have a 66.5% shareholding in DCM Shriram. The Company is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) in India and has a market capitalization of US$2.2 billion (as on 30th June 2025). Detailed shareholding structure of the Company as on 30th June 2025 is presented in the table below.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment comprises of a senior, secured loan of up to US$150 million in INR equivalent through unlisted NCDs with a tenor of 10 years (with 2 years of grace period).
location_description: The Project comprises multiple locations of the Company’s existing manufacturing facilities; for sugar at Ajbapur, Loni, and Hariawan, distillery plants at Ajbapur and Hariawan, all in Uttar Pradesh, and for chemicals business at a new location near its existing facility at Bharuch in Gujarat as well as its existing chlor-alkali at Kota in Rajasthan.
development_impact: The Project is expected to generate significant economy-wide value added and employment, enhance the sustainability of India’s chemical industry, and promote the adoption of sustainable finance. It will expand production capacity, introduce high-value products like aluminum chloride, create direct and indirect jobs, stimulate ancillary industries, and demonstrate sustainable practices such as renewable energy integration, energy optimization, and use of alternative fuels.
additionality: (i) IFC’s long tenor funding will provide adequate cushion to weather the inherent cyclicality of the industry; (ii) The loan will incentivize the Company to develop a sustainable finance framework and achieve the sustainability targets while also having a strong demonstration effect in the hard-to-abate chemicals sector; (iii) IFC will assist the Company in its implementation of the agreed Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP), in the form of providing inputs from its subject experts and sharing technical guidelines; (iv) Through a decarbonization advisory program, IFC will help evaluate the techno-commercial feasibility of options for reducing the Company’s carbon footprint, including electrification, afforestation, potential for CO2 capture, etc.

project_description: Catramp SA, a leading warehousing and logistics operator in Cameroon with facilities in Douala and Kribi seeks to invest €10.1 million to expand and modernize its sites and launch operations into Chad and CAR. The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) through a First Loss Guarantee (FLG). The Project will be financed through a proposed €7.5 million IFC senior loan benefitting from a 21% IDA PSW FLG, and €2.6 million shareholder equity.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Justin Talom, who owns 70% of Catramp directly and 15% through his holding company T’s Corporation. The remaining 15% are held by Jean Kuate, a local entrepreneur.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed €10.1m project involves (i) the expansion and refurbishment of existing warehousing and open storage facilities in Douala and Kribi and (ii) a greenfield expansion into the underserved landlocked FCS markets of Chad and Central African Republic (CAR). It will be financed by €7.5m senior debt and €2.6m equity. Senior debt will be provided by IFC and the equity will be injected prior to the debt disbursement.
location_description: The Company has sites in Douala and Kribi(Cameroon).
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcomes are stakeholder effects on tenants through increased access to high-quality warehouses. The Project is expected to increase the Grade A warehousing and storage space for rent in Cameroon, Chad, and CAR. This expansion will effectively address the shortage of high-quality warehousing infrastructure in these countries. Additionally, the project is expected to create jobs and add economic value through collaboration with local suppliers and a commitment to employing the local workforce. The Project is also expected to promote greater competitiveness and integration in the target countries’ warehousing and storage sector. By supporting a new player in the small-scale warehousing segment entering FCS markets, the Project will generate significant demonstration effects, promoting greater interest and competition in these countries. Integration between the target countries and the rest of the world will also be stimulated.
additionality: Financial additionality - Financing structure: IFC will provide long-term financing through an A loan of up to EUR 7.5 million, with an 8-year tenor including a 2-year grace period, which is not readily available in the target markets. In Central Africa, the average loan tenor is approximately six years, and over the past year, there have been no EUR-denominated syndicated loans or corporate bonds rated B+/- issued in Cameroon, Chad, or the Central African Republic (CAR). Additionally, there have been no EUR corporate bond issuances or syndicated loans in the services sector across these countries during the same period. The proposed financing structure will therefore better match the cash flow needs of the Group’s subsidiaries in Cameroon, Chad, and Central Africa Republic, and allow reasonable time to develop and ramp up the storage and handling business. Non-financial additionality - Non-commercial risk mitigation: IFC’s strong market reputation, ability to identify viable projects, and convening power will be instrumental in structuring and de-risking this initiative, thereby instilling confidence in Catramp regarding its successful realization. The project aims to facilitate the client’s entry into conflict-affected countries like Chad and the CAR, where heightened risk perceptions currently diminish investor confidence. Chad faces significant security challenges due to ongoing conflicts, while CAR's political volatility is intensified by the concentration of power within a small elite, exacerbating ethnic tensions and perceptions of social exclusion. IFC will guide Catramp SA in navigating these complex environments, helping to mitigate associated risks, and enhancing the likelihood of project success. This strategic guidance, combined with IFC’s thorough due diligence and meticulous project structuring, will offer reassurance, empowering the client to launch operations with confidence and optimize their investment potential.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A/B loan to Pandurata Alimentos Ltda (Bauducco or the Company). Bauducco, founded in 1952, is a baked products company headquartered in Brazil, producing long shelf-life bread, panettones, toasts, and other baked products. The Company produces baked products under 3 complementary brands (Bauducco, Visconti and Tommy) to target different consumer segments. Bauducco is currently carrying out an investment program of about US$40 million comprised of a small soft bun bread (“Bisnaguinhas”) production line and climate investments (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Bauducco is fully owned by the Bauducco family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at about US$40 million, and IFC’s investment consists of an A loan of up to US$20 million and a B loan of up to US$20 million.
location_description: The Project will be carried out in the Bonsucesso and Extrema plants, located in Guarulhos (Sao Paulo state) and Extrema (Minas Gerais state), respectively.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to support Brazil’s development by creating jobs and adding value to the economy, while improving food security through increased bread availability via a new production line. The Project is also expected to promote social sustainability and inclusiveness in the baked goods sector by demonstrating advanced production technology that can expand access in underserved regions.
additionality: IFC's additionality arises from providing long-term financing on terms not readily available in the market, mobilizing complementary commercial funding, and introducing an incentive-based loan structure. Additionally, IFC will enhance the Company's E&S practices and procedures by supporting the Company in the implementation of the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP).

project_description: The project consists of an equity investment for a minority stake in Candela Technology AB (“Candela”, or the “Company”), a company that manufactures electric foiling vessels at the forefront of electrifying marine transport. Candela is a first-mover in the space and its ferry (P-12 model) is the first electric hydrofoil to receive regulatory approval and operates in Stockholm’s public transport system. IFC is proposing up to €8 million in equity financing to support the Company’s expansion into Emerging Markets.
sponsor_shareholders: Candela Technology AB is a privately owned company incorporated in Sweden. Current major shareholders include the founder Gustav Hasselskog as well as financial investors like EQT Ventures and SEB.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing up to €8 million equity investment as part of the Company’s current fundraising.
location_description: Poland, Central and Eastern Europe (“CEE”).
development_impact: Assessment of Project Outcomes: Economy-wide effects - The Project is expected to generate direct value added and employment opportunities within the client company in Poland, while also fostering economy-wide value added and job creation through supply chain linkages and consumption-driven effects. Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation: IFC's investment in Candela is expected to catalyze the development of a new segment within Poland's vessel manufacturing industry - electric passenger vessels -through strong demonstration, replication, and capacity-building channels. If the Company's commercial deployment in developing countries proves successful, it is expected to demonstrate the technical and economic feasibility of the technology, foster broader market acceptance, and promote higher sustainability standards and practices across the passenger vessel industry.
additionality: IFC will provide primarily non-financial additionality encompassing transfer of knowledge, innovation promotion and capacity building and non-commercial risk mitigation. IFC's involvement will support the Company in scaling up its operations and workforce in developing countries by transferring global best practices in manufacturing, e-mobility, and climate technology to new geographies. Furthermore, IFC's involvement will help ease perceived risks associated with Candela's expansion into emerging markets, where regulatory frameworks and market conditions for electric marine transport are still developing.

project_description: Hygenco Green Energies Private Limited (Hygenco or the Company), originally founded in October 2020 as Hygenco Private Limited (HPL), is a green industrial gases company that develops, designs, executes, and operates green hydrogen (GH) Projects (GH Project). The Company plans to develop a platform of GH Projects that will be fully or partially owned by Hygenco and associated renewable energy generation plants (RE Project). Hygenco will undertake such projects through project-specific SPVs.
sponsor_shareholders: Hygenco's key promoters and co-founders are Mr. Amit Bansal, Mr. Anshul Gupta and Mr Ashish Gupta, who together with associates, collectively hold a 51% equity shareholding in the Company. The remaining 49% shareholding is owned by the SVL-SME Fund (SEBI Registered Alternate Investment Fund managed by SBICAP Ventures Ltd), an impact investment vehicle managed by a subsidiary of the State Bank of India.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to invest up to US$50 million in the Company as part of its ongoing fundraising in the form of quasi-equity, of which upto US$25 million is contributed by IFC as implementing entity of Blended Concessional Finance.
location_description: Company will operate at multiple locations across India. Please refer to ESRS for details.
development_impact: The Project is expected to deliver significant benefits across multiple dimensions. By financing the expansion of the Company’s green hydrogen (GH) platform, it will enhance access for downstream industries through a pioneering Green Hydrogen-as-a-Service (GHaaS) model offered under long-term contracts, providing a substantial cost advantage over grey hydrogen. This model will particularly benefit mid-size companies that lack the capital, technical expertise, and scalability to develop GH projects independently, enabling them to decarbonize without the burden of upfront investment. Currently, most hydrogen consumed in India is grey hydrogen, a major source of greenhouse gases. Therefore, the Project will help to cut CO2 emissions by replacing it with clean, green hydrogen. In addition, the Project is expected to create direct and indirect high-skilled jobs, contributing to local economic growth and workforce development in advanced clean energy technologies. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote sustainability and demonstrate a new, commercially viable pathway to decarbonization. It will also stimulate the development of new production ecosystems and value chains in the nascent green hydrogen sector through demonstration effects in the region, helping to accelerate market adoption and reduce barriers for future entrants.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC is expected to provide both financial and non-financial additionality. On the financial side, IFC will offer patient equity capital that is not readily available in the market, strengthening the Company’s ability to expand, take risk, leverage resources, and enhance corporate governance. IFC’s participation will also support the Company’s capital structure and facilitate the mobilization of long-term financing and other capital for this capital-intensive business—mobilization that may otherwise be delayed without IFC’s involvement. On the non-financial side, IFC will support the Company in implementing environmental and social (E&S) standards in line with IFC Performance Standards and industry best practices, while also contributing to the Company’s growth plans through IFC’s global industry knowledge and connections across the green hydrogen value chain and related industries.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment involves an equity investment of up to US$53 million in The Reforestation Strategy (the “Strategy”), which will be managed by BTG Timberland Investment Group (“TIG”). This investment will allow IFC to get equity exposure to all the assets of the Strategy and would support the acquisition of land, the establishment of FSC-certified commercial tree farms, and restoration efforts to preserve and enhance biodiversity, primarily in Brazil, Chile and Uruguay (the “Project”). The financing is expected to enable the protection and restoration of 135,000 hectares of natural forest, the planting of 200 million trees on 135,000 hectares of degraded land, and the generation of more than 36 million forest carbon offsets over 15 years. The Strategy targets raising up to US$1 billion in equity.
sponsor_shareholders: TIG is one of the world’s largest timberland investment management organizations with more than US$7.3bn in assets and 1.2mn hectares under management in North and South America. TIG will commit a sizable ticket and will be the investment manager of the Strategy. TIG is a wholly owned subsidiary of BTG Pactual. Founded in the early 1980s, BTG Pactual is a publicly-listed diversified global investment company based in Sao Paulo, Brazil.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Proposed IFC commitment of up to US$53 million into the Strategy.
location_description: The Strategy will make investments mainly in Brazil and Uruguay, and potentially in Chile, Colombia and Paraguay.
development_impact: The Strategy is expected to pioneer commercially viable models for carbon-sequestration through conservation and restoration of degraded land in LAC. Beyond the project, the Strategy’s success will demonstrate that private equity (PE) can deliver financial returns while implementing large-scale carbon removal through Nature-based Solutions (NbS). This will in turn de-risk the market for future entrants and encourage other large managers to launch dedicated NbS funds in Emerging Markets.
additionality: As part of IFC’s financial additionality, IFC’s investment will support the Strategy in achieving its target size of US$1 billion and mobilize additional capital by providing comfort to potential (as well as existing) investors that IFC's Performance Standards will be integrated into the Strategy's operations. For its non-financial additionality, IFC will leverage its expertise in the regions where the Strategy operates to support the region’s biodiversity outcomes.

sector: Grocery Retail (Supermarkets, Hypermarkets, Convenience Stores etc.)
project_description: The proposed investment is an IFC financing package of up to US$10 million to AZZA CJSC (“AZZA” or the “Company”) to finance a portion of the components for a new industrial bakery plant, the largest in Azerbaijan, and the roll-out of new stores across Azerbaijan (the “Project”). The Project is expected to be supported by Blended Finance, as described in the Blended Finance section. AZZA is the largest baked goods manufacturer, the largest gastronomy retailer and the largest importer of European confectionary products in Azerbaijan.
sponsor_shareholders: AZZA is the largest baked goods manufacturer, the largest gastronomy retailer and the largest importer of European confectionary products in Azerbaijan. AZZA is majority owned by Mr. Zohrab Aslanov.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is up to an US$10 million financing package. The preliminary allocation of the proposed financing package under consideration is as follows: (i) up to US$5.5 million from IFC’s own account and (ii) up to US$4.5 million from Canada GROW program.
location_description: Azerbaijan
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to contribute to increased formal employment and value addition in the retail sector and along the supply chain, as well as to emission reductions through investments in high-efficiency bakery equipment in production facility and energy-efficient refrigeration units across retail stores. Beyond the Project, IFC investment is expected to enhance market competitiveness by supporting the growth of specialty retail chains with vertically integrated value chains and by fostering capacity-building initiatives in the retail market in Azerbaijan.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality consists of providing a long-term financing structure that is not readily available in the market to support AZZA’s growth and meet its funding needs. Non-financial additionality consists of capacity-building and standard setting by supporting AZZA’s E&S, corporate governance, and gender initiatives.

project_description: sCamposol S.A. (Camposol or the Company) is a leading multinational agribusiness company specializing in the production, processing, and export of high-quality fresh fruit. Camposol’s agricultural operations extend across Peru, Colombia, Uruguay, and Chile, with a vertically integrated business model that ensures quality control across the entire supply chain. The proposed financing package is intended to support Camposol’s long-term growth strategy by funding strategic investments to expand and modernize its blueberry operations and to proactively address upcoming debt maturities. The investment forms part of the Company’s broader plan to enhance productivity and resilience by gradually replacing traditional blueberry varieties with its own proprietary genetics.
sponsor_shareholders: Camposol is 100% controlled by the Dyer Family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at approximately US$466 million, with an IFC investment of up to US$140 million, comprising: (i) a US$64 million IFC A-Loan (of which US$18 million are insured under the A-Loan RSU program); (ii) a US$36 million MCPP Trust loan; and (iii) a US$40 million B-Loan to be mobilized from Rabobank.
location_description: Camposol's main operations and new investments will be located in the city of Trujillo, La Libertad, Peru.
development_impact: The Project is expected to generate significant positive development effects by enhancing Peru’s agricultural productivity, strengthening climate resilience, and supporting inclusive economic growth. IFC’s financing will enable Camposol to expand and modernize its operations while introducing innovative, climate-resilient agricultural practices that can serve as a benchmark for the broader agribusiness sector in Latin America.
additionality: IFC’s participation will enable Camposol to implement its 2025–2026 investment plan while promoting climate resilience and sustainability in Peru’s agribusiness sector. In addition to providing long-term financing, IFC will bring value through its global expertise in climate-smart agriculture, helping Camposol maintain its leadership in the blueberry agribusiness and demonstrate the viability of climate-resilient production models in Peru’s fruit export sector.

project_description: IFC is considering providing a follow-on financing to Almaty International Airport (AIA) after IFC’s initial investment (Project #43007) committed in September 2021 to support AIA’s capex program, aimed at rehabilitating and upgrading critical airside infrastructure. This includes: (i) rehabilitation of the existing runway to improve safety, (ii) construction of a new taxiway to reduce aircraft turnaround time, (iii) construction of additional aircraft parking stands and a cargo apron, and (iv) modernization of auxiliary infrastructure (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: AIA is majority owned by TAV Havalimanlari Holding A.S. (TAV), with 85% shareholding, and the remaining 15% shares are held by Kazakhstan Infrastructure Fund (KIF), managed by VPE Capital (collectively, the “Sponsors”). Established in 1997, TAV is a leading international airport operator with more than 22,000 employees and a portfolio of 15 airports along with interests in other aviation related activities such as commercial activities, duty free, catering and ground handling at various airports around the world. Aéroports de Paris owns 46.1% shareholding the company, while 49.9% is listed in Borsa Istanbul. Finally, Tepe Insaat Sanayi A.S. retains 4.1% shareholding. KIF is a Kazakhstan-focused private equity infrastructure fund, managed by VPE Eurasia GP Limited, which is a special purpose vehicle 100 percent owned by VGL Limited (the holding company for VPE Capital).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated to be around US$360 million which will be funded by a combination of debt and internally generated cash. The IFC contemplates to provide US$30 million from its own account and mobilize another US$30 million using its Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP)/Credit Insurers. IFC may also provide interest rate swaps.
location_description: The Project is located approximately 15 kilometers northeast of Almaty, Kazakhstan.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to improve the safety, security and operational standards across key areas of AIA’s infrastructure and service. The airport has experienced a larger increase in passengers and extreme climate situations have negatively impacted its key infrastructure. It is also expected to improve resilience, as the investment program seeks to enhance and expand the airport’s infrastructure and systems to adequately manage the risks stemming from adverse weather conditions.
additionality: IFC’s long-term financing and mobilization ensures access to long-term financing in US$ for a much-needed project for aviation safety in the largest airport of Central Asia. IFC will continue to provide support to AIA to comply with E&S standards.

project_description: Getmobil Teknoloji Anonim Sirketi (“Getmobil or the Company”) is a smartphone refurbishment platform serving the Turkish market. The Company operates a B2B platform, which provides end-to-end digital infrastructure to offline SME smartphone vendors enabling them to source used electronics, refurbish them as per government standards and sell them to customers nationwide via digital channels. Getmobil also has a retail presence through its B2C e-commerce platform, “Getmobil.com”. IFC is considering an equity investment of up to US$6 million in Getmobil (“the Project”). The funding will support Getmobil’s expansion in Türkiye.
sponsor_shareholders: Getmobil was co-founded by Mehmet Uygun and Zeynep Uygun. Notable existing shareholders include Dutch Founders Fund II, 212 I, LLC, TechOne Ventures and Arya VC
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering an equity investment of up to US$6 million. Getmobil is raising a US$15 million funding round to accelerate its expansion in Türkiye.
location_description: Getmobil is headquartered in Istanbul, Türkiye, and operates in Türkiye.
development_impact: IFC anticipates that the Project will result in improved access to markets for Small and Medium Enterprises (“SME”) in the second-hand technology retail sector in Türkiye, resulting in revenue growth and productivity gains, and improved access to affordable quality handset devices. The Company is expanding a digital platform that enables the sales and refurbishment of second-hand handset devices by linking SMEs to certified refurbishment centers, providing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) tools, financing, and digital payments to expand reach, boost revenues, and support formalization. For consumers, the platform offers affordable, high-quality refurbished handsets – priced below both new devices and refurbished options of similar quality – while ensuring consistent standards. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Company’s expansion will promote greater competitiveness of the market for refurbished electronic devices in Türkiye, by deepening the digital refurbished electronics segment, via demonstration and replication channels.
additionality: IFC additionality in this Project is expected to be financial and non-financial. Financial additionality involves own account equity. Noting that VC availability in Türkiye is higher compared to other emerging markets, IFC’s role as a co-leading investor will be critical to support the Company’s expansion plan in the country and support its future fundraising efforts. IFC’s participation will also help mobilize capital, providing comfort to other investors that the Company will achieve its final fundraising targets. Non-financial additionality involves standard setting, as IFC will support the Company in upgrading its Environmental, Health & Safety and Human Resources practices, while also strengthening its employee grievance mechanisms related to gender-based violence.

company_name: Access Bank Ghana Cocoa Risk Participation
project_description: The proposed investment consists of an unfunded risk participation facility of up to US$61 million to Access Bank Ghana PLC (“Access Bank Ghana”). The facility is part of a broader syndicated package supporting four Ghanaian banks to finance the purchase of traceable cocoa beans from smallholder farmers via leading Licensed Buying Companies (“LBCs”). The facility will be used to provide working capital to six major LBCs: AgroECOM & Unicom/ECOM, Nyonkopa/Barry Callebaut, Eliho/TOUTON, FedCo/SUCDEN & Barry Callebaut, CJ Commodities/SUCDEN, and Adikanfo/SUCDEN.
sponsor_shareholders: Access Bank Ghana PLC is majority owned by Access Bank Nigeria Plc (93.4%), with staff and other minority shareholders holding the remainder.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s risk participation is US$61 million for a total portfolio of US$112 million.
location_description: Access Bank Ghana operates across 56 branches in 9 of Ghana’s 16 regions, serving over 1.8 million customers.
development_impact: Contribution to market Creation: Resilience: IFC anticipates that the Project will contribute to the resilience of Ghana’s cocoa sector currently affected by limited adequate finance straining the ability of traders to sustain cocoa sourcing from farmers and that could ultimately affect Ghana’s ability to maintain its global market position as a major supplier of cocoa. To monitor progress against this outcome, IFC will track the number of private sector participants benefiting from the project and monitor the total value of cocoa exported by Ghana. Project outcome: Stakeholder effects: Increased Access to Finance: IFC anticipates that the facility will increase liquidity in the agri supply chain and access to finance for farmers by providing the participating banks with an efficient and competitive risk mitigating tool to accept a higher degree of lending risk. Credit to Ghana’s agricultural sector is even lower relative to the contribution it makes to the country’s GDP, where many lenders lack the risk tolerance and/or expertise to lend to small holder farmers The project is expected to reach over139,000 farmers in the value chain of the LBCs. To monitor progress against this outcome, IFC will track the volumes of US$ commodities financed by the facility and volumes of MT cocoa trade supported.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing structure: Leveraging IFC’s AAA rating, the proposed facility is designed to address the regulatory capital and single obligor exposure limits that are presenting severe constraints to Ghana’s Cocoa pre-export financing efforts at present. Non-Financial Additionality: Frameworks: catalyzing regulatory change: IFC’s involvement in the financing of the cocoa sector catalyzes changes in the regulatory framework as it opens doors to a new financing instrument currently not available in the market, mitigating credit risk and adding value by enhancing financing facilities to the private sector following the Central Bank of Ghana approval to treat the IFC guarantee in banks’ working capital facilities as deductible for purposes of computing single obligor limit (“SOL”).
Company Name: Access Bank Ghana Cocoa Risk Participation

company_name: Patria Latam Reforest Fund I Fundo de Investimento em Participacoes Multiestrategia IS
project_description: The investee will be a special purpose entity (the SPE) capitalized by Patria Reforest Fund I (the Fund) and potentially IFC, along with other investors. The SPE will provide financing to a portfolio of afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation (ARR) sub-projects in Brazil, including Productive Restoration and Ecological Restoration projects, with an initial focus on greenfield projects in the Atlantic Rainforest biome. The financing would enable the restoration of 12,000 hectares of reforestation, and generate 1.5 million carbon removal credits over 15 years. The strategy is targeting to raise up to US$100-200 million equity and up to US$40-85 million debt. The Project is expected to be supported by the Frontier Opportunities Fund (FOF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: The strategy will be managed by Kamaroopin, a wholly owned entity of Patria Investments Limited (Patria). Patria was founded in 1988 and is one of Latin America’s largest and most diversified alternative asset managers. With over US$46 billion in assets under management, Patria has built a strong track record across private equity, credit, infrastructure, real estate, and public equities. Patria has been publicly listed on the NASDAQ since 2021 and is an existing IFC client.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment in the SPE is comprised of: (i) US$20 million senior debt; (ii) US$2.5 million equity investment for IFC’s own account; (iii) US$2.5 million in the form of junior equity and (iv) potential mobilization of up to US$90 million to be recognized under IFC’s core mobilization guidelines.
location_description: The SPE will focus on financing projects located in Brazil, with an initial focus in the Atlantic Rainforest biome in Brazil.
development_impact: The Project is expected to deliver substantial environmental and social benefits by supporting carbon sequestration through ARR initiatives in Brazil’s Atlantic Rainforest biome, one of the most degraded ecosystems in the country. By restoring native vegetation and implementing agroforestry systems on degraded lands, the Project will not only generate carbon credits but also enhance biodiversity, reduce soil erosion, and improve water quality. It aims to catalyze a shift from traditional commercial forestry and agriculture to sustainable silviculture and perennial crop systems, fostering long-term climate resilience, strengthening local livelihoods, and promoting a regional bioeconomy. Through this integrated approach, the Project contributes to low-carbon development pathways and adaptive capacity.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality stems from structuring, where IFC will offer a longer tenor than is commonly available in the market and repayment terms have been tailored to align with the cash flow generation cycle of the underlying assets. IFC will also provide an own-account equity investment in the Project. IFC’s role as an anchor investor also serves to validate the strategy and catalyze the mobilization of additional private capital. Non-financial additionality is equally significant. The Fund’s investment team will benefit from IFC and the broader World Bank Group’s deep expertise in carbon markets, facilitating alignment with evolving market standards and the development of credible, high-impact carbon investment strategies. Further, IFC will support the Fund in adopting best-in-class environmental and social (E&S) practices in accordance with IFC’s Performance Standards (PSs) and uphold integrity principles aligned with IFC’s integrity Deal Acceptance Criteria (DAC) for carbon projects. Patria will also leverage IFC’s Plataforma ELOS (Brazil2Equal Program), a peer learning platform aimed at demonstrating how greater gender and racial equity can enhance climate performance in Brazil’s private Agriculture and Forestry sectors.
Company Name: Patria Latam Reforest Fund I Fundo de Investimento em Participacoes Multiestrategia IS

project_description: The project is a US$25 million equity investment in Seraya Partners Fund II (SEA) LP, in the Southeast Asia sleeve of a new infrastructure fund (the “Fund”) established by Seraya Management Private Limited (“Seraya”). The Fund will invest in the energy transition and digital infrastructure sectors via two separate Developed Asia (“DA”) and Southeast (“SEA”) sleeves. The DA sleeve will invest in developed countries in Asia, i.e. Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Singapore and South Korea. The SEA sleeve will invest in emerging markets in Southeast Asia i.e. Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand and Viet Nam.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by Seraya, which is an Asia-focused fund manager focusing on the digital infrastructure and energy transition sectors. Established in 2020, Seraya is headquartered in Singapore, with offices in Kuala Lumpur, Tokyo, and Seoul.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund aims to raise US$1-1.5 billion. IFC’s proposed investment is for an equity investment of up to US$25 million in the Fund’s SEA sleeve.
location_description: The Fund’s SEA sleeve will focus on investing in SEA markets including Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, and Viet Nam.
development_impact: The Fund’s SEA sleeve aims to increase access to quality infrastructure in Southeast Asia to address significant gaps in infrastructure in emerging markets. In this context, the Fund will invest in platforms across Malaysia, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia across core sectors of digital infrastructure and energy transition. In addition to strengthening the infrastructure equity market in emerging markets, the Fund’s success will demonstrate the commercial viability of the equity fund model and open new pathways for institutional investors to invest in the region
additionality: IFC’s own account equity will be critical in supporting a viable first close, given this is Seraya’s first emerging markets (“EM”) focused fund, combined with a relatively short track record of investing in SEA target markets. Further, the Fund’s target size for the SEA sleeve will require mobilizing additional capital from institutional investors and other development finance institutions. However, there is perceived risk among investors viz. the governance and E&S requirements for a thematic fund like Seraya, and IFC’s anchor role as the leading global EM investor will provide certainty that IFC’s ESG and Performance Standards will be integrated into the Fund’s operational procedures. Finally, IFC will work with Seraya to enhance the Fund’s E&S policies and practices to further align it with the IFC E&S requirements and industry best practices.

project_description: Established in 1994, The Arab Palestinian Investment Company (“APIC” or the Company) is an investment holding company registered in the British Virgin Islands and the West Bank and listed on the Palestinian stock exchange since 2014. The Company has several business lines including trade, distribution (including food products, medical supplies, and automobiles), manufacturing, and services across the Middle East and Türkiye.
sponsor_shareholders: APIC’s shareholding structure is diverse, with the top three shareholders collectively holding 27.2% of the Company’s share capital. Mr. Tarek Aggad, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board and his affiliates together own circa 20.4% of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is US$120 million, comprising: (i) US$29 million to finance both capital expenditures and working capital investments across the Company’s subsidiaries, including the expansion of warehouse capacities in its medical and FMCG distribution businesses, increased capacity at its aluminum processing and sanitary tissue plants, and sustainability measures through the installation of solar power systems for both captive and grid use; (ii) US$91 million to refinance existing debt. IFC’s investment consists of a US$15 million own-account participation in the bond.
location_description: IFC’s contribution to the APIC bond will support select capex and expansion plans of APIC’s subsidiaries in the West Bank territories.
development_impact: The Project is anticipated to yield significant outcomes, including (i) stakeholder effects from improved access to food, energy and medical products and (ii) economy wide effects by contributing to employment creation and value addition. Beyond the Project level outcomes, IFC anticipates the investment will strengthen market resilience by providing liquidity to the Palestinian economy at a time of uncertainty and economic strain.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality stems from the provision of a financing structure to support the Company’s expansion of its storage and distribution capacity, including implementation of energy-efficient systems, and development of a solar power plant. Non-financial additionality is comprised of knowledge, innovation and capacity building through four advisory engagements, as well as in the standard setting and alignment with E&S standards and industry best practices.

project_description: The Project consists of the financing of the second development phase of the seven airports in Cabo Verde currently operated by VINCI-owned Cabo Verde Airports S.A. (CVA or the Concessionaire) under a 40-year concession (the Project or Phase 1-B). CVA took over the airports' operations from the former public operator ASA on 24-Jul-2023, upon the achievement of Concession Commencement Date (CCD) under the Project's Concession Agreement (CA) signed between CVA and the government of Cabo Verde (GoCV or the Grantor) on 18-Jul-2022. At CCD, CVA launched the first development phase for the airports (Phase 1-A). Phase 1-B was triggered under the CA on 2-Jan-2025 (the Investment Trigger Date), after the airports' annual traffic of 3.0 million pax in 2024 exceeded the level of 2.8 million pax reached in 2019 before the COVID-19 pandemic. The scope for Phase 1-B includes works to improve and expand passenger terminals, the extension of the runway at one of the international airports, and environment-related investments to optimize utility costs.
sponsor_shareholders: VINCI Airports S.A.S. (VA) and ANA - Aeroportos de Portugal S.A. (ANA) own 70% and 30% of CVA, respectively. Headquartered in Paris, VA is the largest airport operator globally, with 72 airports in 2024 across Europe, South Asia, Latin America, North America, and Africa, and handling 318 million pax in 2024. ANA, a 100% subsidiary of VA, is Portugal's lead airport operator, with 10 airports under concession.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project's total cost for Phase 1-B is estimated at EUR289 million (out of which (a) EUR45 million for the second instalment of the upfront concession fee to the government of Cabo Verde and (b) EUR173 million for the estimated EPC cost). IFC's proposed investment is an IFC sustainability linked A loan of up to EUR60 million and the provision of interest rate swaps covering part of the loan amount.
location_description: The Project is located on seven islands of the archipelago of Cabo Verde, which is composed of nine inhabited islands. The islands where the airports are located are Sal, Boa Vista, Santiago (Praia), Sao Vincente, Sao Filipe, Sao Nicolau and Maio.
development_impact: The Project has an AIMM rating of Good. The most significant project outcomes are (i) improved access to aviation services in the country to meet rising demand and (ii) economy-wide effects, through their impact on value-addition and job creation in the tourism sector. Beyond Project outcomes, the Project's contribution to market creation rating is Strong based on the following: (i) the continued expansion of the airport will deepen the competitiveness of Cabo Verde's tourism sector; (ii) enhanced waste and wastewater management also mitigates tourism-related environmental impacts, setting a model for other infrastructure operators.
additionality: IFC additionality is both financial and non-financial. IFC's financial additionality stems from providing long-term EUR financing with a 20-year A loan to support a strategic asset for Cabo Verde's tourism sector. IFC's non-financial additionality stems from Standard Setting, to bring the Company's Environmental and Social (E&S) practices in compliance with IFC's Performance Standards (PS). The Project ESAP will include (i) a detailed assessment of the airports' climate fiscal risks (to better align the Project with the Equator Principles) and (ii) a cumulative impact assessment on the Project's impact of tourism on the freshwater resources and waste management infrastructure in the area of influence of the airports aligned with IFC PS1 requirements.

company_name: Dogus Otomotiv Servis ve Ticaret A.S.
sector: Grocery Retail (Supermarkets, Hypermarkets, Convenience Stores etc.)
project_description: IFC is providing up to EUR 100 mn or TRY equivalent in the form of a senior, unsecured corporate loan (IFC Loan) to Dogus Otomotiv Servis ve Ticaret A.S. (“Dogus Otomotiv”, “DOAS”, or the “Company), a new IFC client. The IFC Loan will be used to finance the Company’s purchase of electric vehicles (EV), thereby reducing the proportion of Internal Combustion Engine (ICE), and for working capital and/or other corporate needs.
sponsor_shareholders: The main shareholder of Dogus Otomotiv is Dogus Holding (the “Holding”), controlling 60.5% of shares, while the rest of the shares are publicly traded on Borsa Istanbul since 2004.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The IFC investment consists of an up to EUR 100 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: DOAS is headquartered in Sekerpinar, Türkiye with its dealer network spread across the country.
development_impact: Project Outcomes: Economy-wide effects: The Project will support the continued growth of the automotive industry in Türkiye by (i) increasing demand for EVs; (ii) increasing demand for goods and services provided by local suppliers; and (iii) creating more skilled new employment opportunities. Environmental effects: The Project will contribute to increasing energy efficiency and GHG emission reduction by supporting the dissemination of EVs in the Turkish automotive market. Market Creation: Competitiveness: IFC anticipates the Project to enhance the competitiveness of the automotive retail industry through demonstration and replication channels. The Project will enable the Company to increase its EV sales at scale, which will support the distribution of a more efficient and environmentally sustainable product in the market. As the Company is the third largest automotive retailer in Türkiye, the Project should serve as a catalyst for other firms to also enter and expand its EV operations to remain competitive. Sustainability: IFC anticipates the Project to contribute to greater environmental sustainability in the automotive retail market through demonstration and replication channels. The Project is expected to catalyze the adoption of resource efficient solutions among other automotive suppliers in Türkiye.
additionality: Financial additionality Financing structure: IFC will provide financing on terms not readily available in the local market, including a 6-year tenor. The terms of the proposed financing will better match the cashflows of the Company's business, improve its debt profile, and enhance its access to complementary capital thereby reducing its vulnerability to domestic financial and banking shocks. IFC's financing will also help diversifying the Company's capital structure, which currently has low debt levels, mainly provided by local financial institutions. Non-financial additionality Standard Setting: The Project will help the Company enhance its E&S management system in line with international best practices. IFC's E&S specialist will provide guidance on IFC Performance Standards.
Company Name: Dogus Otomotiv Servis ve Ticaret A.S.

company_name: Dai Dung Metallic Manufacture Construction and Trade Corporation
project_description: Dai Dung Metallic Manufacture Construction and Trade Corporation (“DDC” or the Company”) is a leading Vietnamese provider of mechanical engineering solutions, including consultancy, fabrication and Engineering, Procurement and Construction (“EPC”) of building structures for large-scale and technically complex projects both in Viet Nam and internationally. IFC’s proposed investment will fund the construction of two new factories in Ho Chi Minh City and Thanh Hoa provinces between 2024 and 2026 (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: DDC is owned by Nam Phat Long Co., Ltd, Mr. Trinh Tien Dung and his family members, and other shareholders. Nam Phat Long Co., Ltd. is wholly owned by Mr. Trinh Tien Dung and his family members.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed up to VND1,000 billion (approximately US$38 million) quasi-equity investment will fund the construction of two new factories in Ho Chi Minh City and Thanh Hoa provinces between 2024 and 2026. The estimated Project cost is US$152 million, which includes expansion capex for the two new factories and additional working capital.
location_description: Viet Nam
development_impact: At the Project level, the Project is expected to create direct jobs in Viet Nam and to support additional jobs through indirect effects in logistics, transportation, and other related activities in the value chain. Additionally, the Project is expected to train the new workforce on advanced structural engineering skills, fabrication techniques which involve familiarity with heavy machinery and processes specific to large components. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote competitiveness by: (i) increasing value addition; (ii) demonstrating capability in producing large structures; and (iii) providing engineering services for complex projects such as large-scale constructions, renewable energy and offshore wind.
additionality: Financial additionality is provided via long-term quasi-equity investment that aligns with the cash flow needs of large-scale expansion and helps the Company diversify its funding sources. Non-financial additionality is provided via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building where IFC will support DDC in developing a decarbonization roadmap, adopting energy efficiency measures, applying environmental and social (E&S) best practices, and pursuing EDGE building certification.
Company Name: Dai Dung Metallic Manufacture Construction and Trade Corporation

sector: Grocery Retail (Supermarkets, Hypermarkets, Convenience Stores etc.)
project_description: IFC is proposing to provide Dali Discount AG (Dali or the Company) with an up to US$10.07 million quasi-equity financing. Dali is a hard discount retailer in the Philippines, dedicated to making everyday essentials affordable for all. Established in 2020, Dali follows a no-frills, small-format, limited-assortment model with a strong focus on private-label products. Today, Dali operates more than 1,000 stores across Luzon island.
sponsor_shareholders: Dali’s shareholders include its management team alongside financial investors such as the Asian Development Bank, Creador, DEG, Navegar, Pavilion Capital, and Venturi Partners, among others.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering a quasi-equity investment of up to US$10.07 million to enable the Company to scale its business.
location_description: The Company is operating on Luzon, Philippines.
development_impact: IFC anticipates that the Project will improve consumer access to affordable, quality household products. It is also expected to support local suppliers through the development of stronger supply chains, while generating positive impacts across the wider economy. More broadly, the proposed investment aims to enhance market competitiveness by scaling up the hard-discount retail model, raising quality standards, and reinforcing supply chains.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists of providing IFC's own-account equity to support the company's growth and meet its funding needs, which is especially relevant given the relatively limited availability of venture capital in the Philippines. IFC's proposed investment is also expected to strengthen fundraising dynamics and the capitalization table. On the non-financial side, IFC will contribute through standard setting, knowledge, innovation, and capacity building, by helping to strengthen the company's environmental and social standards.

project_description: The proposed investment is up to US$20 million IFC A-Loan to Continental Blue Investment Ghana Limited (“CBI” or the “Company”), for the operation of a 400,000 tons per year Limestone Calcined Clay production plant, regarded as the largest flash calciner in the world (the Project). CBI is a leading cement producer in Ghana and recently completed the expansion of its cement grinding capacity from 0.6 million tons per year (mtpy) to 1.4 mtpy. This financing will support the implementation of the Project to ramp up the production of Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3) in Ghana. The Project is aimed at expanding and localizing cement production by partially substituting imported clinker with the calcined clay, thereby significantly reducing CO2 emissions and catalyzing a shift toward more sustainable cement production in the region.
sponsor_shareholders: CBI is a leading cement manufacturer in Ghana established in 2017 and operating in Tema’s industrial zone, Ghana. CBI is a subsidiary of CBI SA, a Swiss holding company that owns 70% of the business. CBI SA is a 50/50 joint venture between Heidelberg Materials and F. Scott AG. Minority shareholders in CBI Ghana include Norwegian (Norfund) and Danish (IFU) state-owned investment funds, and FLSmidth, Denmark.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is US$66.7 million, financed with (i) US$38 million debt including IFC A-loan, and (ii) US$28.7 million in shareholders’ equity.
location_description: The Project is located in Tema, Accra. The Company also owns the rights to calcined clay deposits in Togorme, North Tongu District, Volta Region in Ghana.
development_impact: The Project is expected to deliver strong development impact by fostering inclusive economic growth, enhancing environmental sustainability, and promoting market innovation in Ghana’s cement industry. The Project will generate both direct and indirect employment and stimulate local supply chains. By substituting clinker with locally available calcined clay, the Project will reduce reliance on imported materials, lower production costs, and contribute to more affordable cement in Ghana. The Project will reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with cement production, aligning with Ghana’s climate goals. Its innovative production process meets global standards and is expected to catalyze broader market transformation by encouraging other industry players to adopt similar low-carbon technologies.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality includes long-term USD financing for up to 7 years tenor, while non-financial additionality encompasses offering the enhancement of the overall environmental, health and safety practices, and Advisory Services to access the carbon markets.

project_description: IFC is proposing to provide Ayala Land, Inc. (ALI or the Company) with up to 14.3 billion Philippine Pesos (PHP) (equivalent to approximately US$250 million) in local currency on IFC’s own account in the form of sustainability-linked financing (SLF) with up to an 8-year tenor. The IFC proceeds will be earmarked for the construction of ALI’s selected commercial properties. The proposed SLL is an extension of IFC’s support to ALI’s sustainability initiatives. In addition, IFC will mobilize capital from other lenders to support ALI in greening and strengthening the resilience of ALI’s commercial property portfolio.
sponsor_shareholders: Ayala Land is a long-standing IFC strategic client and partner in establishing the sustainability-linked finance framework in the Philippines. It is the largest property developer in the Philippines, with more than 10,000 hectares of land bank and a solid track record in developing large-scale, integrated, mixed-use, and sustainable estates. With a footprint spanning 53 estates nationwide, Ayala Land has a diverse real estate portfolio composed of developing residential, office, commercial and industrial properties for sale, as well as properties for lease such as shopping centers, offices, hotels, resorts, warehouses, co-living and co-working spaces. Additionally, Ayala Land is engaged in services such as construction, property management, and other property-related investments. ALI is listed on the Philippines Stock Exchange (PSE). ALI’s largest shareholder is Ayala Corporation (AC), a diversified business conglomerate in the Philippines with operations in real estate, financial services, telecommunications, industrial technologies, power, infrastructure, healthcare, education, and technology ventures.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an up to PHP14.3 billion (equivalent to approximately US$250 million) in local currency SLF with a tenor of up to 8 years to ALI.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Makati City, Metro Manila, Philippines.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are (i) increased access to modern quality commercial space and (ii) environmental effects through improved resource efficiency of green buildings. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment will promote sustainability by facilitating the use of sustainable financial products and adoption of resource efficient and resilient building standards.
additionality: Financial Additionality – Sustainable Finance and Resource Mobilization: The IFC financing will be an SLF, an underdeveloped instrument in the Philippines. This SLF will encourage broader SLF participation through mobilizing capital from other lenders. Non-Financial Additionality – Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will provide support to ALI in evaluating the resilience of its commercial properties through the Building Resilience Index toolkit, and integrating this toolkit into institutional practice. IFC will also support ALI to improve labor practices at institutional level, including inviting ALI to participate in IFC’s Respectful Workplace Trainings.

project_description: IFC’s proposed investment is a senior A loan of up to RMB540 million (approximately US$75 million) to Great Rich Technologies Limited (“GRT”, or the Company), a leading manufacturer of precision coated functional materials and polymer film materials, to support a manufacturing plant for innovative film materials in Çorlu, Türkiye (the Project). The innovative film materials produced are expected to play a crucial role in reducing industrial carbon footprints in its targeted markets, including Türkiye, the Middle East and Europe, while also creating skilled jobs through localized production.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is controlled by its founder and Chairman, Mr. Yongnan Zhou (the Sponsor), who holds a 50.8 percent stake. China Development Industrial Bank (CDIB) Capital Group, an investment company based in Taiwan, China holds 12.2 percent and Compal Group, an original design manufacturer for consumer electronics based in Taiwan, China holds 3.2 percent. The remaining shares are publicly traded.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$382 million. IFC’s proposed investment is a senior A loan of up to RMB540 million (approximately US$75 million) to the Company.
location_description: The Project is to be located in Çorlu, Türkiye.
development_impact: The project outcomes consist of economywide effects on value addition, increasing foreign exchange revenue and employment creation. The Project is also expected to drive stakeholder effects through sourcing from local domestic suppliers, a large portion of which are Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will have deepening market catalytic effects by promoting competitiveness.
additionality: i) Long-term cross-border financing beyond what is available in the local market; (ii) Mobilization of a Development Finance Institution to help the Company diversify its sources of financing; and (iii) Standard settings and sharing of best practices in Environmental and Social (E&S) aspects.

project_description: IFC is proposing to anchor an emerging market focused sidecar fund (the “EM Sidecar”), with IFC contributing US$100 million and mobilizing additional amounts via IFC’s Asset Management Company (“AMC”). The EM Sidecar will be managed by Appian Capital Advisory Limited or one or more of its affiliates (collectively, “Appian” or the “Fund Manager”) and will co-invest with the Fund Manager’s Appian Natural Resources Fund III and Appian Credit Strategies Fund I (together “the Funds”), as well as potential successor funds, in metals, mining and adjacent industries projects in emerging markets (“EM”). The commodities that the Funds and the EM Sidecar will target include those that are primarily linked to energy transition and technology-linked commodities. The EM Sidecar will have an opt-out right for IFC policy considerations, including alignment with IFC Performance Standards.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 2011 by Michael W. Scherb, Appian is a leading global Metals and Mining Fund Manager with US$3.6 billion in assets under management. Appian has 10 offices worldwide and employs approximately 90 professionals, including a 28-person technical team, representing the largest technical team in the market. Uniquely, Appian is not a pure capital allocator, but also a leading builder and operator of projects in a technically intensive sector.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of a US$100 million equity commitment to anchor the EM Sidecar to be managed by the Fund Manager, along with additional private capital mobilization via AMC.
location_description: The EM Sidecar will make co-investments with the Funds in emerging markets, including jurisdictions spread across Latin America and Africa.
development_impact: The EM Sidecar is expected to have positive fiscal impacts by boosting government revenue and contributing to GDP growth in countries with varying levels of macroeconomic stability. Additionally, mining projects can be significant drivers of economic activity in remote areas and support quality jobs over the life of the mine. Appian’s 21 portfolio assets to date have created a total of approximately 5,000 direct jobs, with over 80% of these jobs filled locally. In addition, the EM Sidecar will help strengthen the competitiveness of the EM equity market to support mineral development critical to global economic growth. The availability of public capital for mining projects in emerging markets is low due to limited availability of capital overall – typically due to long lead times, high capital requirement and political risk. The EM Sidecar will demonstrate a commercially viable model to mobilize private capital for developing metals and mining projects in emerging markets, including into nascent Private Equity markets.
additionality: IFC additionality is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality involves supporting the Funds to mobilize additional capital from new investors, including institutional investors. Non-financial additionality includes supporting Appian to enhance the Fund’s Sustainability Procedures. IFC will also support the Funds in ensuring consistent application of Environmental, Social and Governance practices, which is a key concern for institutional investors. IFC’s anchor investor role will therefore help mobilize other investors seeking exposure to the metals and mining sector in EMs in a way that is consistent with high ESG standards.

project_description: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC (“Hikma” or the “Company” or together with its subsidiaries “the Group”) is a pharmaceutical company incorporated in the United Kingdom (UK) and listed on the London Stock Exchange. While the Group was founded in Jordan in 1978, Hikma has expanded its footprint with successful operations across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, North America and Europe with 29 manufacturing plants in 10 countries. Hikma is a long-standing IFC client since 1987 whereby support was primarily provided for the Company’s investments in the MENA region. IFC provided a financing package (the “Financing Package”) to Hikma Finance USA LLC (the “Borrower”), a wholly owned subsidiary of Hikma. Proceeds of the IFC Loan (as defined below) and the Bond (as defined below) which, for the avoidance of doubt, is limited to IFC’s subscription of US$50 million in the Bond, will be used to support the Company’s general corporate purposes including acquisitions, capital expenditure, working capital needs, and any investment in research and development in the Middle East region, as well as debt refinancing of the Group (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Hikma is a publicly traded company and has been listed on the London Stock Exchange since November 2005.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Financing Package entails (i) a 6-year senior unsecured A loan of US$250 million, to the Borrower – processed under IFC project Hikma Loan 2025 (#51629) (the “IFC Loan”); and (ii) a subscription of US$50 million in the Borrower’s US$500 million bond (the “Bond”), in which IFC played an anchoring role – processed under IFC project Hikma Bond (#51148).
location_description: The Financing Package would primarily support Hikma’s existing operations in the Middle East region.
development_impact: The most significant expected project level outcomes are increased access to higher quality pharmaceuticals in the Middle East region. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates this investment to result in greater competition among pharmaceutical manufacturers across the Middle East, which is expected to increase local production of higher quality and more advanced final form pharmaceuticals.
