additionality: - Financial Additionality - Financing Structure: IFC will provide Hikma with long-term financing of six years, allowing Hikma to better plan its capital allocation, and strengthen its overall financial resilience. Resource Mobilization: IFC's participation in the Bond will provide credibility and confidence to investors, supporting Hikma's long-term funding strategy during a time when the bond market was experiencing volatility and uncertainty. Additionally, IFC may mobilize a certain portion of the IFC Loan through private credit insurance under the MCPP RSU program, thereby attracting additional capital investors to the Project. - Non-Financial Additionality - Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: The Company sees IFC as a strategic long-term partner, offering not only essential financing but also industry expertise, global network access, and guidance to navigate the evolving challenges of the pharmaceutical sector. Currently, IFC is working with Hikma exploring resource efficiency, sustainability, and digitization opportunities.

company_name: Amber Dragon Ukraine Infrastructure Fund I SCSp
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an equity investment of up to €40 million (approximately US$45 million equivalent) (subject to 20% of total commitments) in Amber Dragon Ukraine Infrastructure Fund I, L.P., an infrastructure fund targeting €350 million in total commitments (“the Fund”). The Fund will be jointly managed by Amber Fund Management Limited (“Amber”) and Dragon Capital Advisors Limited (“Dragon”, Amber and Dragon together “The Fund Manager”). The Fund will focus on the reconstruction and modernization of Ukraine’s critical infrastructure and will invest in energy transition (renewable energy generation, transmission and distribution, storage), digital infrastructure (data centers, telecom towers, fiber networks), as well as transport and logistics (ports, roads, rail, industrial parks, cold storage facilities, intermodal terminals). Amber is a well-established global infrastructure fund manager with a strong presence in Central and Eastern Europe. Dragon Capital is a Ukraine-based investment group with deep local roots and a strong track record in private equity and real estate in Ukraine. The Fund Manager JV combines Amber’s infrastructure expertise with Dragon’s local market knowledge to effectively navigate Ukraine’s challenging investment climate. IFC’s investment in the Fund is expected to be supported by Blended Finance contributors under the Economic Resilience Action Program (ERA) for Ukraine, as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Amber is part of Boyd Watterson Global Asset Management Group LLC, a global diversified infrastructure, real estate, and fixed income business. Founded in 2009 Amber has made over 175 infrastructure investments globally across equity-focused and impact-focused funds. Dragon Capital was founded in Kyiv in 2000 by Czech investor Tomas Fiala and has since grown into Ukraine’s leading investment group, providing a comprehensive range of products in equities and fixed income sales, trading and research, investment banking, private equity, and asset management to institutional, corporate and private clients. The group is also an active private equity investor in Ukraine.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC investment is expected to be an equity investment of up to €40 million to support the first close of the fund.
location_description: The Fund will only invest in Ukraine.
development_impact: The Fund will increase access to equity capital leading to the development of critical infrastructure to support emergency energy stability, transport, logistics, and digital services—preserving market activity and catalyzing economic recovery and the creation of jobs as the first infrastructure fund to reach first close amid the invasion.
additionality: IFC's equity will be critical to support the Fund reach its first close in a challenging fundraising environment given the exposure to high geopolitical risks in Ukraine. IFC will have an anchoring role in the Fund's first close and will be critical to mobilize capital from other DFIs and institutional investors.
Company Name: Amber Dragon Ukraine Infrastructure Fund I SCSp

project_description: Grupo Neolpharma (“Neolpharma” or “the Group”) is a family-owned pharmaceutical company primarily operating in Mexico. It offers over 250 branded and generic medicines across various therapeutic areas, including central nervous system (CNS) diseases, cardiovascular diseases, oncology, and diabetes. In 2021, IFC financed Neolpharma’s initial expansion plan, encompassing the construction of a new injectables facility in Mexico City, the expansion of an active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) production plant in Ecatepec, Mexico, and other related expenditures (#39128). IFC is now proposing a new $70 million long-term corporate loan to support Neolpharma’s further expansion plan in Mexico (“the Project”). The Project includes (i) the acquisition, refurbishment, and reactivation of the NeolSym Civac API plant in Morelos (“API Plant”); (ii) the construction of a new injectables facility in Toluca to provide drug manufacturing services for a third party (“CMO Plant”); and (iii) technological upgrades and new equipment for Neolpharma’s existing plants, including the refurbishing of corporate offices.
sponsor_shareholders: Neolpharma is fully owned by the Ocampo family. The founder, Mr Efren Ocampo, is the main shareholder across all companies of the Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost is estimated at approximately US$123 million and will be financed by a combination of internal cash generation and financial debt. The proposed IFC investment consists of a corporate A loan of up to US$70 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project will be developed in Mexico.
development_impact: - Increased access to high-quality medicines: The Project is expected to make a strong contribution to improving access to quality pharmaceuticals in Mexico, addressing significant gaps in healthcare access and quality. By expanding domestic production of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and injectables, the project strengthens the local supply of essential medicines, potentially reducing reliance on imports and potentially mitigating stock-outs in public healthcare facilities. - High demonstration effect on the importance, technical feasibility and financial sustainability of the API industry: The Project is poised to advance the evolution of Mexico’s healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors by demonstrating the feasibility and benefits of local API production in a market that currently relies heavily on imports. Neolpharma’s acquisition and modernization of an API plant, combined with its vertically integrated production model, could serve as a replicable example for other firms.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality is provided through financing that is not readily available in the market. Non-financial additionality is provided through sharing pharmaceutical expertise, as well as industry best practices and improving the Company’s environmental and social (E&S) practices.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is up to US$70 million financing package for SK leaveo Co., Ltd. (“SK leaveo” or the “Company”), a biodegradable materials producer in South Korea. SK leaveo is a subsidiary of SKC Co., Ltd. (“SKC”). The IFC financing package comprises of: (i) equal to US$40 million from IFC’s own account; and (ii) up to US$30 million mobilization from other investors. Proceeds from the proposed IFC investment will be used to support SK leaveo in constructing biodegradable material production facilities in Hai Phong, Viet Nam (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Suwon-si, Gyeonggi-do, South Korea, SKC is a holding company, and its subsidiaries are engaged in the businesses of semiconductors, chemicals, and materials. Other shareholders of SK leaveo include Daesang Corporation and TBM Co., Ltd.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project’s cost is estimated to be US$500 million, a part of which will be funded by the IFC financing package of up to US$70 million.
location_description: The proposed IFC investment will be utilized in Viet Nam.
development_impact: At the Project level, the Project will: (i) increase value addition and manufacturing complexity in the plastic packaging sector; (ii) create new direct/indirect jobs; and (iii) contribute to reducing landfill waste and greenhouse gas emissions. At the Market level, the Project will contribute to enhancing Viet Nam’s competitiveness in the global bioplastics market through increased export of biodegradable materials.
additionality: Financial additionality includes: (i) a patient capital that is not typically available in the local market and appropriate for such a greenfield project; and (ii) mobilization of investment from other investors. Non-financial additionality includes standard-setting and aligning of the Company’s E&S considerations to the industry best practices and IFC Performance Standards.

sector: Pulp and Paper Hygiene Products (Tissues, Diapers, Wipes, Feminine Care, Nonwovens, etc)
project_description: Pehart is a leading producer of tissue paper in Romania, operating two plants in Petresti and Dej. It manufactures jumbo rolls as well as finished products, including toilet paper and kitchen rolls, which are sold under own brands and private labels. The proposed Project comprises the following components: (i) buyout of Pehart, (ii) capital expenditures to install new converting lines and improve energy efficiency, and (iii) refinancing of existing debt.
sponsor_shareholders: Pehart combines three legal entities – Pehart Tec Grup SA, Pehart Tec Tissue SA, and Samus Constructii SA, which are virtually fully owned by Abris Capital Partners via Abris CEE Mid Market Fund II LP fund. After the buyout, Pehart will be owned by a consortium led by INVL Baltic Sea Growth Fund, the main private equity fund in the Baltics.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at €308 million, and IFC will fund from its own account and from the account of participants a total of up to €95 million in the form of a sustainability-linked senior secured loan, and an unsecured loan. The remaining funding will be provided by commercial banks, equity investors, and Pehart.
location_description: Romania.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are (i) environmental effects through the reduction of GHG emissions through the improvement of the paper drying process, and (ii) economy-wide impact through job creation and value addition in Romania. Beyond these outcomes, IFC expects that the Project will promote sustainability by showcasing the financial benefits of adopting energy efficiency solutions in the tissue production industry.
additionality: IFC will provide both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is in the form of resource mobilization and an innovative financing structure, which includes the first sustainability-linked loan to Pehart, and a mezzanine instrument. IFC will also provide non-financial additionality via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building, especially in the areas of sustainability and gender equality, as well as standard setting for ESG best practices.

project_description: The proposed investment is an unfunded risk-sharing facility with Standard Chartered Bank (“SCB”) in a portfolio of supply chain finance-related assets in up to eight countries in Africa for up to US$300 million with IFC investment of up to US$150 million (the “Project”). The Project falls under the Global Supply Chain Finance (GSCF) Program, a supply chain finance program launched by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) in December 2022. The GSCF supports trade in the emerging markets by providing funded or unfunded risk participation in partner banks’ facilities. IFC will risk participate of up to 50% of eligible assets in the facility (up to $150 million for IFC’s own account) and will mobilize SCB for the balance. This Facility aims to support more than 300 suppliers in both domestic and global value chains and over the time period indirectly support over a million farmers in the target countries The eligible Trade assets will be across corporate clients in Africa. The project is expected to be supported by the IDA Private Sector Window’s Blended Finance Facility (“IDA PSW-BFF”).
sponsor_shareholders: Standard Chartered is a leading international banking group, with a presence in 53 of the world’s most dynamic markets. Our purpose is to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, and our heritage and values are expressed in our brand promise, here for good. Standard Chartered PLC is listed on the London and Hong Kong stock exchanges. For more stories and expert opinions please visit Insights at sc.com. Follow Standard Chartered on x.com/StanChart, linkedin.com/company/standardchartered/, and facebook.com/StandardChartered.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project will be in an amount up to US$300 million with underlying portfolio of trade finance assets that will be risk-shared by Standard Chartered and IFC on a 50-50% basis.
location_description: The supply chain finance assets in the portfolio will be originated in up to eight countries in Africa, including Ghana, Cote D’Ivoire, Kenya, Egypt, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania and Zambia.
development_impact: Over its three-year life, the Project is expected to support over US$1.5 billion in trade financing. This volume will be directed at a diversified mix of companies and SMEs – following a ramp-up period. The financing will impact over 300 suppliers, companies in Africa, and over 1 million farmers indirectly. In markets where less than 20% of business loans are extended to SMEs, this intervention is designed to help these firms overcome long-standing financing constraints and better integrate into global supply chains by leveraging innovative trade financing structures. Moreover, the trade transactions will benefit some of the key sectors such as manufacturing, pharma, agricultural commodities, and food processing amongst others in the region.
additionality: Innovative Financing Structure: through the Project, IFC will support SCB in establishing a trade finance unfunded risk-sharing facility on a portfolio basis in the Africa region, which would allow a substantially larger number of suppliers, some of whom are traditionally not considered bankable, to receive financing and to reduce financing gaps for these SMEs.

project_description: IFC is considering extending a fixed rate loan, linked to local currency, of up to US$15 million to TWM PNG Limited (“TWM” or the “Borrower”), a leading waste management service provider in Papua New Guinea (“PNG”), to support the expansion and upgradation of the Integrated Waste Management Facility (“IWMF”) located at Roku near Port Moresby in PNG, particularly including, but not limited to, the introduction of new incinerator, wastewater treatment equipment as well as the expansion of engineered landfill (the “Project”). The project is expected to be supported by the IDA PSW (IDA PSW) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: TWM is a leading waste management company operating the sole IWMF of its kind in PNG and in the Pacific Islands region. Founded in 2011, TWM is a family run business wholly owned by Mr. Kori Chan and Mr. Michael Chan through Chan Corporation Limited. The business interests of Chan Corporation span property investment, marine transport, waste management and environmental services.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project involves a 9-year senior, secured Papua New Guinea Kina (PGK) of up to US$ 15 million from IFC’s own account. The Project is intended to optimize existing operations with new equipment and upgradation with appropriate technical specifications and expand its waste processing capacity. Total capex requirements for upgradation and expansion is approximately US$22.4 million.
location_description: TWM and the Project are located in Roku site (Central Province) near Port Moresby in Papua New Guinea
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase access to integrated waste management services for large commercial and industrial players in PNG and increase the volume of industrial and hazardous waste that is treated. At the market level, the Project contributes to increasing sustainability by demonstrating an integrated business model for the treatment of hazardous industrial waste and support the business case for circularity
additionality: IFC additionality is financial and non-financial. IFC will provide long-term debt financing in local currency, which is not readily available for private companies in the waste management sector. IFC financing will enable TWM to upgrade and expand its waste management operation. In addition, IFC will continue its upstream engagement to strengthen TWM capability to implement a waste incinerator and expand its business towards the recovery of materials from waste.

project_description: The proposed investment entails a EUR9 million IFC Loan to SANIFER SARLU and KIBO SARLU (jointly the “Companies”). The IFC Loan will support i) the development of five new stores (three SANIFER stores and two KIBO stores); ii) the implementation of Sage X3 ERP system; and iii) the partial refinancing of the Borrowers’ outstanding working capital credit facility (jointly the “Project”). SANIFER specializes in the import, distribution, and retail of construction, and home improvement materials while KIBO operates modern grocery retail stores.
sponsor_shareholders: The Companies are both fully owned by TALYS SAU (the “Group”), a family-owned business based in Madagascar. The Group is fully owned by Mr. Féride Hassanaly and Mr. Eric Hassanaly.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The IFC financing package is in the form of an A Loan of up to EUR9 million.
location_description: All the Project sites will be located in the country of Madagascar. The Project sites for SANIFER Ivato, KIBO Ivato, and SANIFER Bypass will be in Antananarivo while the Project site for SANIFER Nosy Be and KIBO Nosy Be will be in the island of Nosy Be.
development_impact: The project is expected to increase access to affordable, high-quality goods for consumers and create job opportunities for the local people. Further, the opening of five new stores will provide business opportunities for local suppliers and increase the companies' usage of transportation and logistics services. Beyond the direct project outcomes, IFC's financing is also expected to strengthen market competitiveness through competitive pressure.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality consists of providing longer-term financing as part of the proposed financing structure. The non-financial additionality comprises of (i) green building advisory services to help the Companies achieve EDGE certification for two newly constructed stores; and (ii) supporting the Companies in strengthening their capacity for environmental and social risk management.

company_name: Fideicomiso de Titulacion para Inversion en Renta de Bienes Raices
project_description: Founded in 2018, Patrimonio en Fideicomiso - Decreto Legislativo N°861, Título XI – Fideicomiso de Titulización para Inversión en Renta de Bienes Raíces – Fibra PRIME (“Prime”) is the first and largest Real Estate Investment Trust (“REIT”) in Peru. It is focused on the acquisition, leasing, and management of real estate assets and is listed in the Lima Stock Exchange. IFC is considering providing a US$70 million senior secured financing package, including a secured IFC A Loan of up to US$40 million and a B/Parallel Loan of up to US$30 million, to support Prime’s 2024-2026 investment plan. This includes the acquisition of office assets, efficiency improvements to achieve green building certifications, and debt refinancing.
sponsor_shareholders: Prime is externally managed by Administradora Prime SA (APSA), and both were founded by the Mariategui family. Currently, APSA is 99.08% owned by Ignacio Mariategui, the founder and CEO of APSA. Prime’s main investors include: (i) institutional and corporate investors representing 75% of the total shareholding value, including insurance companies, private investment entities, among others; and (ii) more than 670 individual retail investors representing the remaining 25%. APSA has 0.56% of Prime’s outstanding shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost stands at US$70 million consisting of a US$70 million senior secured financing package to finance Prime’s 2024-2026 investment program.
location_description: Prime is headquartered in Lima, Peru. The project is located in Peru.
development_impact: The Project is expected to provide increased access to high quality industrial space and office space. The Project is also expected to generate positive environmental effects through higher resource efficiency of green buildings. Beyond the Project, the investment will promote greater sustainability in Peru’s commercial property sector. This investment also has the potential to enhance competitiveness by supporting the growth of the leading REIT in the market.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality consists of providing innovative financing structure and resource mobilization to support FP’s growth and meet its funding needs. On non financial additionality, IFC will focus on knowledge, innovation, and capacity building.
Company Name: Fideicomiso de Titulacion para Inversion en Renta de Bienes Raices

project_description: The proposed investment involves IFC investment of up to INR 4,250 million (US$50 million equivalent) in wholly owned subsidiaries of TVS Emerald Limited (“TVS Emerald” or the “Company”), including Emerald Haven Life Spaces 2 Private Limited (previously known as Radial (Phase II) IT Park Private Limited), Emerald Haven Life Spaces 3 Private Limited (previously known as Radial (Phase III) IT Park Private Limited) and Emerald Haven Properties Private Limited for part financing development of middle-income housing projects in India (the “Project”). The first project is located on the Pallavaram-Thoraipakkam Radial Road, Chennai and the second project is located in Sathanur, Bengaluru. Other middle-income housing projects will be located in Chennai and Bengaluru and will be jointly identified by the Company and IFC. The housing projects will be green building certified and are expected to include development of 4,000 – 5,000 housing units.
sponsor_shareholders: Incorporated in 2010, TVS Emerald Limited is in the business of residential real estate in India and is part of an Indian multinational conglomerate operating in automobiles, auto components, financial services, and real estate. The Company is focused on the residential market in Chennai and Bengaluru and operates under the brand “TVS Emerald”. The Company has delivered projects with saleable area of over 5 million sq.ft. till date and is currently developing a portfolio of over 8.5 million sq.ft.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be about INR equivalent of ~US$621 million and IFC’s investment will be in the form of INR denominated Non-Convertible Debentures (NCDs).
location_description: The first project is located on the Pallavaram-Thoraipakkam Radial Road, Chennai and the second project is located in Sathanur, Bengaluru. Other projects will be located in Chennai and/or Bengaluru and will be jointly identified by the Company and IFC.
development_impact: Project-level impact includes (i) increased access to quality housing for middle income populations; and (ii) environmental effects via improved efficiency in energy and water usage as a result of EDGE certification for properties identified under this Project. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment to promote competitiveness in the Indian housing sector by providing i) competitive pressures on developers already operating in the target micro-markets to improve the price and quality of their projects and (ii) demonstration effects to other developers that will be incentivized to expand in smaller micro-markets, adapt their business model to achieve economies of scale and cater to middle-income populations.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the proposed Project is both financial and non-financial. IFC will provide long-term financing to purchase land that is not readily available in the local market. Non-financial additionality will be provided through technical guidance to the Company to develop capability in green buildings.

project_description: The proposed project entails IFC's equity investment of up to US$60 million in the Asia Environmental and Social Infrastructure Fund (AESI Fund or the Fund) to be managed and promoted by AEW and Natixis Investment Managers (together referred to as the Sponsors). The Fund seeks to raise up to US$500 million to provide debt financing to infrastructure projects in emerging East Asia Pacific and South Asia regions, with emphasis on green and sustainable infrastructure projects. At least 50% of the funds will be earmarked for renewable energy projects.
sponsor_shareholders: AEW, one of the world’s largest real estate and private debt investment managers, is expected to act as the Fund Manager for the Fund, with its subsidiary, AEW Private Debt Hong Kong Limited, to be appointed as the investment advisor. AEW has over 860 employees, with its main offices located in Boston, London, Paris and Singapore. As at 31 March 2025, AEW managed a global portfolio of € 77.6 billion of asset under management in the real estate and private debt markets. AEW is a wholly owned subsidiary of Natixis Investment Managers, which is 100% owned by the Group BPCE, the second largest French retail banking group and is mutually owned.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project entails IFC's equity investment of up to US$60 million in the AESI Fund. The Fund will provide debt financing to infrastructure projects in emerging East Asia Pacific and South Asia regions, with emphasis on green and sustainable infrastructure projects. At least 50% of the funds will be earmarked for renewable energy projects.
location_description: The AESI Fund is domiciled in Luxembourg and can make private debt investments in infrastructure projects across East Asia Pacific and South Asia regions, including countries such as India, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore, and South Korea.
development_impact: The development impact of the Project will be delivered through an increase in climate finance stemming from the Fund’s climate investments in Asia. The Project will also promote greater market sustainability via demonstration and replication of the Fund mobilizing funds from institutional investors to provide long-term debt to finance infrastructure assets in emerging markets in Asia.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Under the proposed investment, IFC will provide own account investment of up to US$60 million to the Fund to support infrastructure finance in emerging markets in Asia, which is not easily available. IFC’s anchor investment is expected to mobilize a minimum 4x IFC’s investment amount by signaling confidence in emerging markets infrastructure debt as an asset class. Non-Financial Additionality: IFC will provide guidance and experience in structuring the Fund as well as developing a credible impact reporting framework. IFC will also provide technical guidance to help strengthen the Fund’s capacity to manage E&S risks in accordance with IFC Performance Standards and will support the design and implementation of a robust E&S Management System.

project_description: IFC is considering a €16 million senior loan investment to AFISA Food Industry S.A. and AFISA Flour Mills S.A. (together referred to as AFISA or Company) and their parent company, Trans Afrique General Trading FZCO (TransAfrique). The proposed financing will support their working capital requirements for (i) wheat imports to support expanded milling capacity, and (ii) growth of their rice and sugar import business. Incorporated in 2010 in Dubai, TransAfrique operates across five sectors—flour milling, food commodity imports, transport/logistics, construction, and real estate—with a presence in Cameroon, Chad, and other Central African countries.
sponsor_shareholders: AFISA is owned by TransAfrique. TransAfrique is wholly owned by the Elnefeidi Group, a Sudanese family-run conglomerate led by Amin Bashir Elnefeidi (Board President) and Ahmed Bashir Elnefeidi (Group CEO).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an IFC A loan of up to €9 million and a subordinated loan from IFC acting as the Implementing Entity of the Canada – IFC Facility for Resilient Food Systems (FRFS) for up to €7 million.
location_description: The Company has manufacturing units located in Douala, Yaounde, and Ngaoundere, Cameroon.
development_impact: Project-Level Impact: Economic Effects: The Project aims to boost domestic wheat flour production, enhancing value addition and job creation through up- and downstream linkages. It is expected to stimulate Cameroon’s food processing sector and support economic diversification. Customer Impact: By increasing the availability of safe, quality, and affordable wheat products, the Project will improve consumer access and strengthen food security. Market Creation – Competitiveness & Resilience: The Project will promote investment in local food processing, reduce import reliance, and showcase the viability of expanding domestic wheat flour production. It is also expected to drive adoption of best practices in post-harvest handling and strengthen resilience of both local and global food supply chains.Project-level Impact: Economy-wide effects: The Project, through import substitution efforts, is expected to increase domestic value addition and create more jobs (direct and indirect) through up- and downstream linkages in Cameroon, by expanding domestic wheat flour production. The Project is expected to bring a much-needed boost to the food processing sector and contribute to diversifying and strengthening the local economy. Stakeholders – Customers: The Project is expected to increase end consumer access to safe, quality, and affordable wheat products in the country, and therefore contribute to improving food security. Contribution to market creation - Competitiveness/Resilience: IFC expects the Project to increase competitiveness of the market through increased investment in food processing to bolster domestic food marketing and reduce reliance on food imports. The Project will demonstrate the potential to expand wheat flour production and marketing in the country to increase supplies and ensure adoption of industry best post-harvest handling and storage practices. The Project is also expected to contribute to building resilience.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC is considering offering long-term financing on terms not otherwise available in Cameroon (7 years with a 2-year grace period), potentially alongside concessional blended finance from Canada's Facility for Resilient Food Systems (FRFS). If approved, the €16 million package including a subordinated blended finance loan of €7 million and IFC’s proposed €9 million senior loan, could enhance the project’s bankability by helping mitigate key risks in a fragile and conflict-affected environment. These include execution risks tied to major expansion, raw material supply and price volatility, and limited collateral availability. Notably, there have been no EUR syndicated loans or corporate bond issuances in Cameroon in the past 12 months. Non-Financial Additionality – Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC is also considering providing technical assistance to support AFISA in aligning its operations with IFC Performance Standards and international best practices, particularly in environmental, social, health, and safety areas. In addition, IFC is exploring the possibility of offering advisory support through a last-mile retail initiative targeting female beignet (fried doughnut) vendors—core customers of AFISA’s flour. This initiative would aim to strengthen their business and financial management capabilities.

project_description: New Anthoney's Farms Private Limited (NAF or the Company) is a poultry farming business in Sri Lanka and consists of a feed mill, breeder farms, a hatchery, broiler farms, a network of out-growers for broiler farming, a slaughterhouse, a further processing unit, and retail shops under the Anthoney's brand. Established in 1986 as a small farm with 1,000 birds and a manual production facility, NAF has grown over the past 40 years to become one of the largest players in Sri Lanka's poultry industry. It is currently implementing a capital expenditure program for capacity expansion, improvement in operational efficiencies and expansion of its own retail network (the Project). The IFC investment will be for the purpose of partially funding this Project, in the form of a C Loan (in US$) up to US$ 5 million with an option to convert into equity shares of NAF. NAF's wholly owned subsidiary, New Anthoney's Feeds Limited and affiliate, Anthoney's Meatlery (Pvt.) Limited will be co-borrowers to the C Loan. The Project is expected to be supported by the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP), as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: NAF is a family-owned business, privately held by the founder, Mr KA Emil Stanley and his wife, Mrs SMD Marie S Lakshmee. One co-borrower, New Anthoney's Feeds Limited is a wholly owned subsidiary of NAF and the other co-borrower, Anthoney's Meatlery (Pvt.) Limited is an affiliate of NAF. There are no other companies or affiliates of the NAF Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed Project plan runs over 6 years from FY2025 to FY2030 and has a total estimated cost of US$22 million. Proposed investment of US$10 million will fund part of the Project cost. The proposed investment is a US$10 million C Loan (in US$) from IFC and GAFSP with an option to convert into equity shares of NAF. NAF's subsidiary, New Anthoney's Feeds Limited and NAF's affiliate Anthoney's Meatlery (Pvt) Limited will be co-borrowers to the C loan.
location_description: Sri Lanka
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to (i) contribute to enhancing food and nutrition security in Sri Lanka through increasing the availability of and access to poultry meat to consumers in Sri Lanka; (ii) generate stakeholder effects for farmers as suppliers through improved livelihoods, access to market, and technical assistance and (iii) generate economy-wide effects by contributing to employment creation and stimulating forward and backward linkages with related sectors. Beyond the Project outcomes, IFC anticipates that the Project will generate a market deepening effect in the natural chicken production segment. By improving operational efficiency for a leading player in the natural poultry production sector in Sri Lanka and demonstrating viability of the Project, it can catalyze other players in the sector to replicate natural chicken production.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is expected to come from both financial and non-financial sources of additionality. Financial additionality stems from IFC providing long-term financing in hard currency and grace period that is not readily available in the local market. Non-financial additionality comes from standard setting relating to E&S standards, and knowledge, innovation, and capacity building through proposed advisory services.

project_description: The proposed project entails the financing of Paraguay’s first green hydrogen project, the Villeta 145MW production facility, designed to produce up to 260,000 tons per annum (tpa) of green calcium ammonium nitrate (CAN), a low-carbon fertilizer (the Project). The project is expected to be supported by the Green Climate Fund (“GCF”) and by IFC’s Frontier Opportunities Fund (“FOF”) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: ATOME Paraguay SAE (the Project Company) is a wholly owned subsidiary of ATOME Energy PLC (ATOME or the Sponsor), a UK-listed company focused on the development of greenfield green hydrogen projects for the purpose of producing, marketing and distributing green fertilizers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost stands at approximately US$620 million. IFC’s financing package includes (i) a C Loan of up to US$25 million for IFC’s own account, complemented with a mezzanine loan of up to US$50 million provided by IFC in its capacity as accredited entity of the Global Green Climate Fund, and (ii) the subscription of preferred shares in ATOME Paraguay of up to US$25 million for IFC’s own account including IFC’s FOF.
location_description: The Project is located in Paraguay, 30 kilometers to the south of Villeta municipality, within an industrial area in development, near the eastern bank of the Paraguay River and approximately 3km east of the border with Argentina.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects such as the development of a domestic green fertilizer industry, which is expected to reduce farmers’ reliance on grey alternatives in Paraguay and the wider region, thereby enhancing the sustainability and security of the food supply chain; and (ii) economy wide effects, which are expected to materialize through direct and indirect job creation. On the market front, the Project is expected to generate strong demonstration effects by illustrating the commercial viability of green fertilizers, thereby catalyzing broader market adoption of sustainable production practices.
additionality: IFC will provide both financial and non-financial aspects. On the financial side, IFC's involvement will include concessional financing designed to address barriers associated with the innovative nature of the Project, such as elevated capital expenditures for equipment and uncertainties surrounding commercial sustainability. From a non-financial perspective, IFC will play a pivotal role in mitigating non-commercial risks within an emerging sector that lacks a robust track record of financing. By leveraging its institutional expertise, IFC will support the Client in evaluating the feasibility and creditworthiness of the transaction while facilitating the development of an adequate financial structure. Additionally, the Project will benefit from IFC's technical and multidisciplinary expertise in the green hydrogen and fertilizer industries, offering critical insights into technology selection, project design, supply chain optimization, and power market dynamics.

project_description: The proposed Project involves IFC investment of up to INR 4,200 million (US$50 million equivalent) in wholly owned subsidiaries (“SPVs”) of Birla Estates Private Limited (“BEPL” or “Birla” or the “Company”) for the development of two middle-income housing projects in India (“Project”). The first project is located in Kalwa, Thane and will primarily consist of middle-income housing with some office and retail spaces. The second project will be a middle-income housing project located in Manjri, Pune. The projects will be certified green and will include an estimated development of 6,000 – 9,000 housing units.
sponsor_shareholders: Setup in 2016, Company is a Mumbai based developer with presence across India. Company is a subsidiary of Aditya Birla Real Estate Ltd (formerly known as Century Textiles and Industries Ltd) and part of the Aditya Birla Group (“the Group”). The Group is one of India’s oldest and largest conglomerates with presence in metals, telecom, financial services, cement, fashion, retail, renewable energy, textiles, paper and real estate amongst other sectors. The Company is primarily focused on the residential segment with some presence in office real estate. It has a pan India presence across North, West and South India with Mumbai as its primary market. In a relatively short span of 8 years the Company has created an ongoing portfolio of 13.96 million square feet and development pipeline of additional 21.10 million square feet as on 31 March 2025.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The overall project cost is US$1,096mn. IFC investment will be in the form of INR denominated non-convertible debentures (“NCDs”).
location_description: The Project is expected to be located across various cities in India. The identified projects are located in Kalwa, Thane and Manjri, Pune.
development_impact: IFC investment in the identified projects are a mix of affordable and middle-income housing. 68% of IFC investment to be tagged Climate. The investment will increase access to quality housing for middle-income populations by building 6,000 - 9,000 green homes. Further, as part of Thane project, ~5% of additional housing units will be developed for the economically weaker sections.
additionality: Financial additionality IFC’s own account equity: Long-term equity capital is not readily available for housing developers in India. IFC’s provision of long-term patient capital will enable the company increase housing supply at mid-income price points while promoting investor confidence is a sector where private capital finance is inadequate. Non-financial additionality Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will help Birla obtain green building certification for this project, helping them improve energy efficiency and optimizing water usage.

project_description: Magazine Luiza S.A (“Magalu” or the “Company”) is the largest brick-and-mortar retailer in Brazil, with a nationwide presence and the second-largest e-commerce retailer in the country, holding a 17 percent market share as of 2023. IFC’s proposed financing would enhance Magalu’s technology infrastructure to strengthen its marketplace, logistics, and service ecosystem. The project will also benefit local suppliers by integrating underserved MSMEs into Magalu’s marketplace, giving them access to a wider consumer base, digital tools and infrastructure. Additionally, the Project will be gender-tagged to reflect Magalu's commitment to increase female representation within its technology department. The IFC investment will be structured as an incentive-based loan, with Magalu committing to significantly increase its e-waste collection and recycling efforts over the next five years.
sponsor_shareholders: Magazine Luiza S.A. has been listed on the Brazilian Stock Exchange (B3) since 2011 at the highest corporate governance standard (“Novo Mercado”). Magalu is majority-owned by the founding families, Trajano and Garcia, who control 57% of the company, while 1% is under treasury and 42% is in the public float.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment in Magalu comprises an (i) A loan for IFC’s own account in the amount of up to US$100 million equivalent in Brazilian reais (BRL) and (ii) a B loan of up to US$50 million
location_description: The investment will be implemented at Magalu's headquarters in São Paulo, primarily supporting its technology initiatives, with nationwide impacts on the company’s operations.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate (i) effects on suppliers through increased business opportunities and integration into the modern retail supply chain and (ii) stakeholder effects on female employees through increased access to quality jobs and skill development opportunities. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Project will further promote competitiveness in the retail sector through enabling innovative business models and increasing competition in the market.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this project will be both financial and non-financial: (i) Financial additionality will be provided through the provision of long-term financing, which is not readily available for the retail sector in Brazil, and an innovative financing structure in the form of an incentivized-based loan with a target related to circularity of electronic waste. IFC will also play an active and direct role in mobilizing B-lenders and credit insurance from international private insurance companies. (ii) Non-financial additionality will be provided in the form of (i) standard setting by providing guidance to Magalu to adhere to good international environmental, health, and safety practices, and (ii) knowledge sharing and capacity building through Magalu’s engagement in IFC’s Equality in Education and Employment (E3) peer learning platform, which aims to support the recruitment of women in technology roles.

project_description: IFC is considering an equity investment in Senegalese AI healthcare startup KERA Health Platforms (KERA or Company). Launched in 2023, KERA offers a multitude of products for stakeholders in the healthcare ecosystem.
sponsor_shareholders: Shares of the Company are held by its founders Moustapha Cissé, Papa Sow, and Hosam Mattar, several undisclosed angel investors from the technology space, as well as a few venture capital firms. The Company has previously raised a pre-Seed round and is now raising its Seed round to finance its product development and growth.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC equity investment is up to US$10 million.
location_description: Kera’s operating headquarter is in Dakar, Senegal. Senegal is currently Kera’s primary market, however the company seeks to expand to member countries of the West African Economic and Monetary Union.
development_impact: IFC's investment in KERA health is expected to support the growth of the Company's digital products in Senegal. At the project level, the Project is expected to expand access to quality health services and coverage in Senegal, particularly targeting underserved populations such as informal workers and women. This is anticipated to reduce out-of-pocket health expenditures and improve service quality through faster payments and embedded healthcare services, enabled by AI. At the market level, the project is expected to contribute to the growth of Senegal's AI ecosystem and stimulate innovation in the health insurance sector, thereby encouraging broader adoption of digital, quality-enhancing solutions, beyond the Company.
additionality: IFC's additionality is expected to be both financial and non-financial. Under financial additionality (own account equity), IFC is catalyzing a substantial Seed round with an up to US$10 million equity investment, catalyzing funding in an underdeveloped venture capital market. Under non-financial additionality (standard setting), IFC will support the Company in strengthening its corporate governance standards.

project_description: United Solar Polysilicon (FZC) SPC (“USP”) is a special purpose vehicle implementing a greenfield 100,000 tonnes per annum (TPA) solar-grade polysilicon manufacturing facility located in Sohar, Oman (the Project or Company).
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Longgen (Sam) Zhang (a US citizen) is the founder of USP and the key Sponsor for the Project. Mr. Zhang is a seasoned industry veteran, having 20+ years of senior management experience in US listed entities in the solar PV value chain. Other shareholders include IDG Capital (a leading private equity firm with global operations), and USP Management. Future Fund of Oman (sovereign wealth fund platform managed by Oman Investment Authority) has also invested in USP in form of convertible debt. IFC’s planned equity investment will come alongside additional equity USP is raising.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is c.US$1.6 billion to US$1.8 billion. The proposed IFC financing to the Project comprises of: (i) an A-Loan of up to US$200 million; (ii) mobilization of up to US$400 million through B-Loans and/or parallel loans; and (iii) Preferred Equity to United Solar Holdings (parent company of USP) of up to US$50 million.
location_description: The USP facility is located in Sohar Free Zone, Oman.
development_impact: The proposed Project will create domestic value addition and employment, diversify Omani exports, and manufacture globally 40GW of solar modules annually. Additionally, USP will catalyze the creation of a new solar PV ecosystem in Oman and the wider GCC region, enhancing competitiveness and reducing reliance on oil and gas. Furthermore, the Project will expand the global resilience of the polysilicon value chain, by providing additional supply through a new location.
additionality: IFC's additionality covers 4 main areas: (i) The IFC loan, featuring a maturity of up to 10 years (including a 1-year capital grace period), offers longer-term, patient capital that surpasses the financing terms typically available from other financial institutions; (ii) IFC's involvement provides optimal support to the capital structure, facilitating the mobilization of long-term financing and additional capital for this capital-intensive business; (iii) IFC has entered an advisory mandate to evaluate bankability gaps and offer recommendations to improve the Project's bankability. Additionally, the Company is eager to collaborate on advisory services to develop action plans focused on carbon reduction, resource efficiency, and the integration of clean energy; and (iv) With IFC's involvement, the Company will accelerate the alignment of its operations with the best global practices in labor and hazardous waste management within the polysilicon industry. IFC's proposed upstream advisory engagement will identify key environmental and social gaps relative to the IFC Performance Standards and recommend mitigation measures to be implemented during the final construction phase and early operations, thereby enhancing the Project's bankability for international lenders. Additionally, IFC's extensive global experience in the solar PV supply chain will support benchmarking the Project against leading global efficiency standards in polysilicon production.

project_description: IFC is considering a loan to support Celulosa Arauco y Constitución S.A. (“Arauco”) for the construction and operation of the Sucuriú Project, an industrial pulp plant in Inocência, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. The facility will have an annual production capacity of 3.5 million tons of short-fiber pulp, supported by 400,000 hectares of eucalyptus plantations, with operations expected to begin in late 2027.
sponsor_shareholders: Arauco is a privately held company fully owned by Empresas Copec S.A. (“Copec”), a Chilean conglomerate with operations in energy and natural resources. Copec is indirectly controlled by the Angelini family, which holds a combined 45.3% stake through various entities. Other shareholders include the Matte Group, free float shareholders on the public exchange, pension funds, and other private investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at approximately US$4.6 billion for the pulp mill, with additional potential investments related to forestry and other associated facilities. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A Loan of up to US$250 million and a B Loan of up to US$350 million.
location_description: The pulp mill will be located in the municipality of Inocencia, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate jobs and value addition, and to have positive environmental effects from sustainable forest management and renewable energy generation. At the market level, the Project will help strengthen the competitiveness of Brazil’s pulp and paper sector by putting pressure on other players to replicate zero waste to landfill technology and other designs that optimize energy and resource efficiency.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality comes from the provision of long-term financing and resource mobilization. Non-financial additionality comes from the adoption of best E&S practices in line with IFC E&S Performance Standards to support the Project´s sustainability goals

company_name: FRAPORT TAV ANTALYA YATIRIM YAPIM VE ISLETME A.S.
project_description: Fraport TAV Antalya Yatirim,Yapim ve Isletme A.S. (the “Company”) is a Turkish joint-stock company owned by TAV Havalimanlari Holding Anonim Sirketi (“TAV Airports”) and Fraport AG Frankfurt Airport Services Worldwide (“Fraport”), respectively. On December 28, 2021, the Company entered into a 25-year Lease Agreement with the General Directorate of State Airports Authority (“DHMI”), for the operations and expansion of Antalya Airport (ICAO: AYT), starting on 1st of January 2027. Antalya airport is one of the largest leisure-oriented airports in Europe, with a current capacity of circa 40 million passengers. The Project entails the expansion of the Antalya Airport to a capacity of approximately 80 million in three phases.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsors are Fraport and TAV Airports, with 49% and 51% ownership of the Company, respectively, and a joint management control structure. Fraport is a leading international airport operator with about 19,000 employees and 24 airports under management and provides services to 30 airports globally. Fraport also provides services such as traffic and terminal management, ground handling, security, and real estate and facility management at various airports around the world. Fraport is publicly listed in the Frankfurt Stock Exchange. Established in 1997, TAV Airports is a leading international airport operator with over 22,000 employees and currently managing a portfolio of 15 airports and with interests in other airport related activities such as commercial activities, duty free, catering and ground handling at various airports around the world. TAV Airports is publicly listed in the Istanbul stock exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is estimated at approximately €3.4 billion to be financed by a combination of equity and debt. The proposed investment entails a long-term project finance package consisting of a loan of up to €300 million from IFC’s own account and a B loan of up to €250 million for the account of the participants. This financing will support the Company in refinancing the existing €2.3 billion bridge loan raised for the expansion of AYT.
location_description: The Project is in the city of Antalya in Türkiye.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate significant stakeholder impacts in terms of improved access and quality of the airport's landside and airside services, as well as positive government revenue and economy-wide impacts derived both from the operation and from the activities enabled mainly in the aviation and tourism sectors. The anticipated market creation effect is to preserve Türkiye's role in the global and regional tourism market.
additionality: IFC long-term financing and mobilization from development financial institutions and/or commercial banks is expected to send a positive signal and provide investor comfort within the Turkish market.
Company Name: FRAPORT TAV ANTALYA YATIRIM YAPIM VE ISLETME A.S.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support EDK Group (“EDK” or the “Group”) expand its grocery retail business, Low Price, and refinance part of its existing debt to improve its capital structure (“the Project”). The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA[20] Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Groupe EDK SA, the holding company of the Group is fully owned by M. Demba Ka. Low Price, the Group grocery retail business is fully owned by Groupe EDK SA.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be up to EUR25 million. IFC will provide an A-loan of up to EUR25 million including up to EUR15 million in local currency to be used exclusively for Low Price.
location_description: The Project is located in Senegal.
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase consumers’ access to modern retail formats including in less served areas of Senegal, outside Dakar. The Project will also have beneficial effects on suppliers and various positive economy-wide effects, including job creation and value addition.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC's financial additionality is delivered through the provision of long-term financing with maturity not readily available in the market, needed for Low Price expansion. IFC's non-financial additionality is delivered through the provision of technical expertise through the implementation of comprehensive Environmental & Social management systems and the provision of advisory services such as the Financial Management Advisory solution.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support Carrefour Medical (“CM” or the “Company”) increase supply capacity, complete its headquarter with technical and training centers for equipment maintenance and technical engineers, and put in operation its recently built dialysis kit production plant (the “Project”). The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA[20] Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF) and Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Carrefour Medical specializes in the supply, installation, and maintenance of healthcare equipment and consumables. The Company is fully owned by M. Saliou Mboup, which also owns the COSEMAD group, which operates in strategic sectors such as healthcare, food, construction, energy, and industry.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be up to EUR31.2million. IFC will provide an A-loan of up to EUR18 million in two tranches including up to US$13.2 million in local currency (XOF) and up to EUR6.5 million. The remaining portion of the Project will be funded by the Project Sponsors.
location_description: The Project is located in Senegal.
development_impact: The Project is expected to improve access to medical equipment and consumables thus improving healthcare outcomes for patients. The Project is also anticipated to create employment opportunities for skilled labor in medical consumables manufacturing, and equipment distribution and servicing. The Project will help demonstrate efficiencies achieved through vertical integration of medical consumable production.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC's financial additionality is delivered through the provision of long-term financing with maturity not readily available in the market, needed by the Company. IFC's non-financial additionality is delivered through the provision of technical expertise through the implementation of comprehensive Environmental & Social management systems.

sector: Other Textile Products (Including Industrial and Medical Products)
project_description: Drylock Technologies Brasil Ltda. (“Drylock” or the “Company”) is a Brazilian-based manufacturer of private label personal hygiene products, with a portfolio ranging from baby care and feminine care to adult care. In response to growing demand, Drylock plans to expand its capacity in the country by constructing a new, state-of-the art, and eco-friendly plant in the broader São Paulo region (the “Project”). The Project will feature the latest clean technology, delivering high-quality products at lower costs to the Brazilian market.
sponsor_shareholders: Drylock is a wholly owned subsidiary of Drylock Technologies NV, a global leader in personal hygiene product manufacturing. Headquartered in Zele, Belgium, it employs over 3,700 people in 10 production plants worldwide, including locations in the Czech Republic, Spain, Italy, the US, Brazil, and Russia. It is primarily owned by Bart Van Malderen, a seasoned Belgian entrepreneur with extensive experience in the hygiene industry, who holds a 75% stake through Belgium-based holding VM Invest NV. The remaining 25% is owned by Sofina SA, a Belgian asset manager listed on the Brussels stock exchange, which focuses on long-term investments, directly or through private equity funds, in companies with growth potential and sustainable business models across sectors such as technology, healthcare, consumer goods, and financial services.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$30 million, which IFC is proposing to finance through an A Loan of up to US$30 million.
location_description: The Project will be located in the peri-urban area of the city of Capivari, located approximately 140 kilometers northwest of São Paulo.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes include increased purchases from domestic suppliers including SMEs and economy-wide GDP and job creation. Beyond the project-level impact, IFC expects the Project to enhance the competitiveness of Brazil’s baby and adult care products sector by increasing the availability of high-quality and cost-effective private labels.
additionality: IFC will provide both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality includes long-term financing, while non-financial additionality encompasses offering the enhancement of the overall environmental and safety performance.

sector: Metal Can and Other Metal Container (Including Aluminum Beverage Cans)
project_description: IFC plans to provide a senior secured loan of up to US$18 million to East Can Solution LLC (the “Company”). The IFC loan will be used to finance the construction of a new aluminum can production plant in Uzbekistan, which will have an annual capacity of approximately 550 million cans (the “Project”) and will supply leading beverage manufacturers within the country.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Shuhrat Ergashev, a respected Uzbek entrepreneur, wholly owns the Company directly and indirectly.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated total project cost is around US$57 million. The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$18 million equivalent senior, secured 7-year loan.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. The Project is located in Yangi Avlod Special Industrial Zone of Tashkent.
development_impact: The expected project-level outcomes are Economy-wide Effects: by promoting local production of aluminum cans, the Project is expected to contribute to increased value addition, which will be strengthened through the adoption of cost-efficient production methods, and employment creation. IFC anticipates that the Project will also strengthen domestic supply chains in Uzbekistan and will contribute to import substitution. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that this investment will contribute to the development of metal packaging industry in Uzbekistan, which relies heavily on imports. The Project represents the first large-scale opportunity for the development of Uzbekistan's metal packaging sector, with the potential to showcase the country’s cost competitiveness in this industry.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial additionality and comes in the form of (i) financing structure through longer tenor; (ii) standard setting; and (iii) knowledge, innovation, and capacity building through advisory services. Financial additionality: Financing Structure: IFC will provide long term local currency financing (7 years with 2-years grace) on terms otherwise not available in the local market. Non-Financial additionality: (i) Standard setting: IFC will help improve its existing E&S standards in line with IFC Performance Standards and industry best practices; (ii) Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC is exploring potential advisory engagements related to decarbonization and corporate governance.

project_description: The proposed investment is a funded participation by IFC for up to US$30 million (“M”) in a secured revolving syndicated borrowing base trade finance facility (the “Facility) for TOI Commodities SA, Switzerland (“TOI” or the “Company”) to finance TOI’s pre-export working capital needs in Moldova and Romania (the “Project”). The Project is for up to three (3) years with annual cleanup and commitment, which will be processed under IFC’s Global Warehouse Finance Program (“GWFP”) with the delegated authority from IFC’s Board of Directors.
sponsor_shareholders: Aragvi Holding International Limited, a holding company domiciled in Cyprus (“Aragvi” and together with its direct and indirect subsidiaries, “the Group” or the “Sponsor”) owns 100% in TOI. Headquartered in Romania, the Group first entered the Moldovan market in 1998, initially as a commodity trader. Over the years, the Group has grown substantially through acquisitions and investments. In addition to being the leading originator, processor and exporter of agri-commodities in Moldova, the Group has expanded its origination and processing activities into Romania, Serbia and Ukraine.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed loan amount will be up to US$30 M for its own account as a lender in the syndicated Facility to support the Group’s export related trade operations across Moldova and Romania. The total Project cost is around US$260M.
location_description: Moldova, Romania and Switzerland.
development_impact: The proposed Project is expected to (i) provide increased access to finance for an agricultural player operating in a key sector of the Moldovan and Romanian economies; (ii) support the Group’s growth and generation of higher export revenues, a major source of export income in Moldova.
additionality: (i)Financial additionality is driven by IFC’s countercyclical role by financing a funding gap after crisis driven retrenchment by lenders since February 2022. (ii) Non-financial additionality from IFC's contribution to improving the Company’s environmental and social practices, in line with IFC’s Performance Standards and industry best practices.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to Papua New Guinea Kina (PKG) 70 million A Loan to Wonye No 2. Limited (the “Company”), a joint-venture company established for the development of a greenfield commercial property in Mount Hagen, Papua New Guinea. The IFC financing will be used to complete construction of a single storey mixed use retail development with total lettable area of 11,646 square meters (the “Project”). The project is expected to be supported by the IDA PSW Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a joint venture between Steamships Trading Company (“Steamships”) and Tininga Ltd (“Tininga”). Steamships is a diversified leader in shipping, transport, property and hospitality operation in Papua New Guinea. Steamships is dual listed on the Port Moresby Stock Exchange and Australian Securities Exchange, and is a subsidiary of John Swire & Sons Ltd, a diversified global group headquartered in the United Kingdom. Tininga is one of the largest companies in Mount Hagen, with operations across retail, wholesale and distribution, and property.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project has a total cost of approximately PGK 200 million. The proposed IFC loan will finance 35 percent of the total project cost, with the remainder to be financed by the joint venture shareholders.
location_description: The Project is located in Mount Hagen, Papua New Guinea.
development_impact: The most significant project-level outcomes include (i) increased tenant access to high quality modern retail facilities, (ii) supplier effects on development of modern supply chain, and (iii) environmental effects through enhanced energy efficiency. Beyond the Project outcomes, IFC expects the investment to foster competitiveness in the commercial property and retail sectors, through demonstration and capacity building.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality consists of providing innovative financing structure to support the company’s growth and meet its funding needs. On the non-financial additionality side, IFC’s investment will support the Company in adopting IFC’s E&S and corporate governance Performance Standards, positioning the Company for sustainable long-term growth, as well as encouraging the adoption of similar standards by tenants of the Project.

company_name: CIMKO CIMENTO VE BETON SANAYI TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Çimko Çimento ve Beton San. Tic. A.S. (Cimko), a leading local cement manufacturer in Türkiye, launched a US$300 million 5-year Eurobond (the Eurobond) to be used to (i) refinance Cimko’s existing short- to medium-term debt, (ii) fund Cimko’s mostly sustainability-focused capital expenditures over 2025-2027; and (iii) general corporate purposes, including upgrades in management information systems and working capital financing (the Project). IFC participated in this debut issue with a subscription of US$50 million as an anchor investor.
sponsor_shareholders: Sanko Holding, ultimately owned by the Konukoglu Family, is Cimko’s main shareholder. Sanko Holding is a Turkish industrial conglomerate with operations in a wide range of industries including textile, flexible packaging, cement, renewable energy, textile recycling, etc.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is US$300 million and was partially funded by the subscription of US$50 million for IFC’s own account. The remaining funding was provided by development finance institutions including EBRD and Finance in Motion and other investors.
location_description: The Project will be implemented in three cities of Türkiye: (i) Adiyaman and Kahramanmaras, two cities in Southeastern Türkiye that were hit hard by the two February 2023 earthquakes, and (ii) Bartin, in Northern Türkiye.
development_impact: • Reduction in the Carbon Footprint: The Project will support greening of the cement operations in Cimko’s three plants in Türkiye by improving energy intensity, emissions intensity, carbon intensity and increasing share of alternative fuel use. • Deepening of Sustainability Practices: The Project will advance the sustainability practices of the local cement market in Türkiye by (i) increasing use of biomass-containing waste, (ii) improving effective waste/fuel management, (iii) reducing the clinker/cement ratio through optimizing clinker quality parameters and use of alternative additives; and (iv) upgrading utility water lines.
additionality: • Financing structure: IFC, by playing a countercyclical role, provides long-term financing which is difficult to procure in the local market for the proposed amount and tenor. In addition, IFC helps mobilize the remaining funds as an anchor investor with long experience with Cimko and Sanko Holding. • Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC has been providing guidance & advice on broader capital market transactions, including bond issuance, as a result of which Cimko issued its debut Eurobond. IFC will also continue advising Cimko on adopting state-of-the-art equipment and practices in sustainability and help Cimko achieve its greening targets in line with Türkiye’s national sustainability strategy.
Company Name: CIMKO CIMENTO VE BETON SANAYI TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: Etana is a leading pharmaceutical company in Indonesia with vaccine and pharmaceutical products focused on the treatment and prevention of various (i) non-communicable diseases, including cancer and kidney disease, and (ii) infectious diseases. The Project will support the Company’s expansion plans to increase local production capacity of vaccines and biological drugs.
sponsor_shareholders: Etana was founded in 2014 by its President Director, Mr. Nathan Tirtana. The Company’s senior management, led by Mr. Tirtana, collectively is the largest shareholder in the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is estimated to cost up to US$60 million, including IFC’s investment of up to US$30 million and mobilization of up to US$30 million from other investors.
location_description: Jakarta, Indonesia
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcome is an improvement in access to affordable and quality pharmaceutical products in Indonesia. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that this investment will contribute to strengthening competitive pressures in the Indonesian pharmaceutical market by demonstrating the effectiveness of the Company’s ability to increase its domestic production of critical pharmaceutical products.
additionality: Financial additionality: IFC is providing long-term patient capital to address the Company’s funding needs and support its continued growth. The Project requires upfront capital expenditure and a long lead time to generate cash flows, given the timeline for construction, technology transfers and regulatory approvals. Non-financial additionality: IFC is expected to leverage its global experience to facilitate the sharing of best practices and to provide guidance to Etana as it scales up its operations. The Company is also expected to leverage IFC’s global network to connect with new potential partners or principals globally.

sector: Soap and Cleaning Compound (Soap, Detergent, etc.)
project_description: The proposed investment is a US$25m A loan to Cepsa Quimica SA’s affiliate companies, aimed at expanding its manufacturing operations for chemicals and additives in home and laundry care segments in Nigeria. CSCHEM Limited (HoldCo) has two operating companies (OpCo), SIL Chemicals Limited (SIL) and Reliance Chemical Products Limited (RCPL), which are involved in manufacturing and selling chemical products and trading detergent chemicals in Nigeria. The investment involves two key expansions. First, the sulphonation plant will be upgraded to significantly increase the production of HLAS, an essential raw material for detergent manufacturing. This expansion aims to meet the rising demand in Nigeria and reduce dependence on imports. Second, a new regenerative furnace will be installed at the sodium silicate glass plant to boost the production of sodium silicate solids. Sodium silicate is a versatile chemical used in various industrial applications, including detergents, adhesives, and paper products. Both expansions are designed to strengthen local manufacturing capabilities and support the growth of related industries in the region.
sponsor_shareholders: CSCHEM Limited is 70% owned by SIL Holdings Ltd and 30% owned by CEPSA Quimica SA. CEPSA is one of the leading producers of LAB globally and is owned by Mubadala Investment Company in UAE and Carlyle Group since 2019.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project is expected to cost US$61 million including (i) IFC A loan of US$25 million (ii) US$20 million in commercial bank term loan from the Development Finance Institution, Nigeria (iii) US$16m equity.
location_description: The Project locations are in the industrial zone in Agbara and Ikorodu, Nigeria.
development_impact: The Project will expand the production capacity in Nigeria of specialty chemicals, generating direct and indirect domestic value addition through increased output and economic activity in the Company’s value chain. Moreover, the Project will create full-time direct and indirect jobs in Nigeria and will make the consumer goods markets in Nigeria more competitive, by enhancing raw material supply, quality, and diversity locally, and reducing reliance on costly imports.
additionality: IFC’s participation will result in financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided through a financing structure with longer tenor and grace periods that are not readily available in the local financial markets, particularly in the context of challenging global economy. Non-financial additionality is provided through improvement in the overall performance in accordance with the IFC Performance Standards.

project_description: ISA Lab (“ISA” or the “Company”) is a tech enabled healthcare services Company in Brazil. It offers vaccination, testing, infusion, clinical visits, and chronic disease management. ISA operates a B2B/B2B2C model connecting individual medical professionals (“ISAs”) to patients and it’s compensated by insurance companies and out-of-pocket. It has a decentralized model and a network of independent healthcare professionals currently operating in 65 cities across Brazil.
sponsor_shareholders: ISA was founded by Fernando and David Pares. Notable existing shareholders include Canary, Vox Capital, MatterScale, Kortex Ventures, Yaya and Scale-Up Ventures.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering an investment of up to US$15 million in ISA in the form of direct equity.
location_description: ISA is headquartered in São Paulo, Brazil, with operations primarily in Brazil.
development_impact: The Project is expected to result in improved access to quality healthcare services for privately-insured patients in Brazil, by expanding a digital platform that integrates patients with independent healthcare professionals to provide at-home healthcare services, thereby offering enhanced convenience of accessing medical care. The Company’s expansion plan involves onboarding additional independent healthcare professionals, specifically nurses, thereby enabling them to access part-time, flexible employment opportunities. The Company is scaling one of the leading, asset-light digital platforms in Brazil that provides at-home care for a large share of services typically provided by traditional healthcare organizations. A successful scale up is expected to induce such traditional providers to up their game, e.g., through the development of digital distribution channels (incl. via partnerships), as well as induce digital-first competitors to add more services to their offering. Ultimately, this is expected to trigger broader innovation and digitalization across the Brazilian healthcare market, and the expansion of the at-home care segment in Brazil.
additionality: IFC will provide the following financial and non-financial Additionality. IFC will lead the Series B investing round by providing a venture capital investment of US$15 million to support the Company’s expansion in Brazil. IFC will leverage its board seat to provide strategic guidance and support in shaping the company’s long-term growth plans. By connecting the company to its extensive network of insurance companies and HealthTech investments in Brazil and other regions, IFC will facilitate business development and enable valuable knowledge sharing as the company scales. IFC is also expected to provide the Company with the following support: (I) IFC has conducted a Rapid Quality Assessment to assess how the Company manages patients’ safety and quality of care standards. IFC will work with the Company to strengthen its quality management system, to align the Company’s processes to international standards.
