(II) IFC will improve the Company’s Environmental & Social (E&S) practices by: (a) implementing an E&S Action Plan aligned with IFC Performance Standards and World Bank Group Guidelines; (b) include prohibitions on sexual and workplace harassment, as well as child and forced labor in its procurement processes; (c) develop a Child Protection Policy for children accessing services via the Company's home program. (III) IFC will work with the Company to strengthen its corporate governance standards.(IV) IFC support from the gender team is under discussion with the Company.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a subscription to a Sustainability-Linked Bond (“SLB”) of up to EUR120 million (approximately US$136 million) to be issued by Techtronic Industries Company Limited (“TTI” or the “Company”). Proceeds from the proposed SLB will be used to expand TTI’s operations in Viet Nam (the “Project”), mainly for the construction of a second factory at Saigon High-Tech Park. The proposed SLB will help reduce the Company’s greenhouse gas emissions and promote gender inclusion.
sponsor_shareholders: TTI is a leading manufacturer of power tools and equipment for industrial workers in professional settings and for consumers. The Company owns a comprehensive product portfolio under 13 well-known brands, including Milwaukee, the Company’s flagship product for the professional segment. The Company’s largest shareholders are Mr. Horst Julius Pudwill and his family, who together own approximately 22% stakes in the Company. The Company’s current management team owns approximately 2.82% in the Company through a share awards scheme. The Company’s remaining approximately 75.18% shareholding are held by public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project's cost is estimated to be US$200 million, a part of which will be funded by the IFC financing of up to EUR120 million (approximately US$136 million).
location_description: The proposed IFC investment will be utilized in Viet Nam.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes include economy-wide effects, such as enhancing local value addition and product complexity in Viet Nam, which will lead to innovative product development, make significant contributions to its GDP, and generate direct and indirect employment opportunities. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the proposed investment to catalyze market effects by deepening supplier development and R&D investments. This will be achieved by integrating local suppliers into the global value chain and addressing technical capability gaps in Viet Nam’s power tools industry.
additionality: Financial additionality is primarily provided through IFC's technical expertise to help structure TTI's first SLB, including the preparation of a sustainability-linked bond framework, as well as IFC’s subscription to TTI’s inaugural SLB issuance, which could potentially mobilize future sustainability-linked financings issued by TTI. Non-financial additionality will be in the form of knowledge and capacity-building support to TTI. This includes providing technical guidance on the gender performance target included in the sustainability-linked bond framework and potential gender-related engagements to expand TTI's initiatives to recruit, retain, and progress female staff. Through this Project, TTI will also adopt IFC's Environmental & Social Performance Standards and Good International Industry Practices.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment of up to US$100M unsecured loan as part of a US$155M debt package (6 years, including a 2-year grace) to ETC Group (“ETG” or “the Group” or “the Company”) to support the expansion of its edible oil facilities in Malawi, Rwanda and Zambia as well as general working capital purposes (the “Project”). IFC is to mobilize at least US$55M through its syndication partners. ETG is an existing IFC client. They are a vertically integrated agricultural supply chain manager involved in the origination, procurement, warehousing, logistics of multiple agricultural commodities and processing of consumer products. It is active in over 26 African countries, as well as in India, China and South East Asia and has additional trading, merchandising and/or treasury desks in Europe, the Americas and the Middle East
sponsor_shareholders: Ultimate beneficial owners of ETG together controlling 52.51% are Mr. Mahesh Patel (Chairman), Mr. Ketan Patel (Joint Group CEO) and Mr. Birju Patel (Joint Group CEO). Other key shareholders are Mitsui & Co. via its African arm MIT African Management Limited (31.9%) and Public Investment Corporation (13.9%) with the balance held by Executive Directors (1.69%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated project cost is US$155M. IFC will support the Project with an investment of up to US$100M in the form of an unsecured loan. In addition, the Project will mobilize at least US$55M from syndication partners.
location_description: A portion of the funds will be used to finance the development and operations of the edible oil plants in Malawi, Rwanda and Zambia. The remaining funds are expected to be utilized mainly in Sub Saharan Africa to finance ETG's trading flows in agri commodities including fertilizer, pulses, grains and oilseeds among others.
development_impact: The Project is anticipated to positively impact the economies of Malawi, Rwanda and Zambia in terms of value addition and job creation. The economic growth of these countries is on an upward trajectory but unemployment, especially youth unemployment, remains high. The creation of quality jobs is therefore an urgent social demand and responds to a pressing need for diversification in the economy IFC financing will help with implementation of the edible oil plants in the three countries which will increase value addition, create jobs and promote local edible oil production to bridge the significant gap between local demand and supply. The Project is also expected to increase consumer access to quality and affordable edible oils, while also increasing access to the soybean markets by farmers in Malawi and Zambia. At the market level, the Project will introduce measures by a leading edible oil producer that will increase market resilience to shocks through local production of edible oils and efficiency improvements. The sizable increased in soybean cake production in Malawi and Zambia will also have a favourable impact on the animal feeds market.
additionality: IFC offers long term financing structure on terms that are otherwise not available in Malawi, Zambia and Rwanda. Over the past 12 months, there were neither US dollar syndicated loans nor corporate bonds issuance in the three countries. Through this investment, IFC will also provide expertise, innovation and knowledge to establish the edible oil production capacities including its operational efficiency and climate impact.

project_description: PT Medela Potentia (Medela or the Company), is one of Indonesia's largest healthcare and pharmaceutical distribution companies. Medela was established in the 1980s as the distribution arm of PT Dexa Medica (Dexa), a leading pharmaceutical manufacturer in Indonesia. Medela and Dexa (collectively referred to as the Group) are currently owned by the Soetikno family (the Sponsor). The proposal is for IFC to be a lead investor in the IPO and to invest own account equity in Indonesian Rupiah (“IDR”) of up to a maximum of (i) IDR520 billion (approximately US$35 million equivalent); or (ii) 30% of the total IPO size (the “Project”). The Company plans to use proceeds from the IPO to expand its operations in Indonesia and to pursue a regional expansion strategy. As a lead investor, IFC will support the Company's IPO and help it to develop its E&S and governance standards.
sponsor_shareholders: The Soetikno family founded Medela and its sister company, Dexa, a pharmaceutical manufacturing company. Concerned by Indonesia’s scarce supply of medicines, the family established Dexa in Palembang, South Sumatra, in 1969. In the 1980s, Medela was established as a separate distribution company for Dexa due to the government’s regulation that required the separation between manufacturing and distribution.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Proceeds from the IPO will be used to finance Medela’s expansion capex and working capital needs over the next five years, along with potential strategic acquisitions.
location_description: Medela is headquartered in Jakarta and has a countrywide coverage in Indonesia.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are increased access to high quality health products (i.e., pharmaceuticals, medical devices) in Indonesia. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment will increase competition between competitors operating at scale.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality consists of the provision of IFC’s own account equity to support the Company in its expansion plan and resource mobilization by serving as a lead investor in its IPO. Non-financial additionality is comprised of knowledge, innovation, and capacity building provided by IFC’s information sharing of best practices and potential partners.

company_name: GOVERNMENT OF THE PROVINCE OF CORDOBA
sector: Municipal Finance - Transport and Roads [Project only]
project_description: The proposed investment is a sustainability-linked senior loan of up to USD 200 million to Provincia de Cordoba (the “Province” or “Cordoba”) to finance the expansion of National Route (RN) 8 and RN A005. These roads will serve as critical bypass routes for Rio Cuarto, the second-largest city in the Province (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project implementing agencies are: (i) the DPV (Dirección Provincial de Vialidad), who is responsible for the design and preparation of tender documents for this project; (ii) the ACIF (Agencia Cordoba de Inversion y Financiamento), responsible for the execution of the loan and launching the tender process; and (iii) DNV DNV (Dirección Nacional de Vialidad), responsible for the operation and maintenance of the roads once the project has been completed. The Borrower will be the Province of Cordoba, and the Legal Agreements will be signed by the Governor or other representative of the Province. The Province of Cordoba is the 2nd most populated out of Argentina’s 23 provinces.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed transaction will finance the expansion of National Routes (RN) 8 and A005, with a total project cost of USD 228 million. These roads serve as vital bypasses for Río Cuarto, a key commercial and service center in a dynamic agricultural-livestock region that strategically links the Pampa and Cuyo areas.
location_description: The project is located in Rio Cuarto, the second-largest city in the Province of Cordoba. The Province of Cordoba is located in the center of the country. Neighboring provinces are (clockwise from the north): Santiago del Estero, Santa Fe, Buenos Aires, La Pampa, San Luis, La Rioja and Catamarca. All investments will be implemented in the Capital City of Cordoba and the Alpa Corral region.
development_impact: The project will contribute to (i) reduce travel time and congestion ii) enhance safety for drivers and pedestrians, and (iii) avoid GHG emissions. The Project introduces an innovative instrument that contributes to unlock the sustainable debt financing market for subnational infrastructure in Argentina, and promotes resilience. IFC is supporting Cordoba through advisory services to develop a Sustainability-Linked Financing Framework aligned with international standards. It is helping define KPIs and SPTs tied to the Province’s goals on gender-based violence and emissions. The Province is expected to increase coverage of its network of support services (Punto Mujer) to prevent and reduce gender-based violence.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is strong both from a financial and non-financial perspective. IFC will play a countercyclical role and provide corporate debt financing through an innovative instrument -. e.g., the first Sustainability-Linked Loan (SLL) subnational government in Latin America and the Caribbean - and will play a key role in mobilizing commercial lenders which would otherwise limit exposure or not finance subnational infrastructure in Argentina. IFC debt financing package and mobilization is critical to finance the Province of Cordoba’s Road infrastructure and sustainability strategy, amid a challenging macroeconomic context and limited fiscal space. IFC is providing advisory support for the development of a robust Sustainability Framework, which is aligned with international principles and enhances the Province’s ability to access commercial finance linked to sustainability goals. Similarly, IFC is providing advisory support to enhance the Province’s capacity to identify and mitigate road safety and E&S risks to improve quality of subnational infrastructure Projects.
Company Name: GOVERNMENT OF THE PROVINCE OF CORDOBA

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a US$60 million financing package, to support Jalles Machado S.A. (“Jalles” or the “Group”), a leading sugar, ethanol, and renewable energy producer in Brazil, with three mills located in the states of Goias and Minas Gerais (Jalles Machado, Otavio Lage and Santa Vitoria mills) with a total of 9.0 million tons of crushing capacity and a cogeneration capacity of 174.5 MW.
sponsor_shareholders: Jalles is listed in Brazilian stock exchange B3 under the Novo Mercado segment. The Group's majority shareholder is the Lage family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an A loan of up to US$60 million equivalent in BRL. The proceeds of the IFC loan will be used to support an investment program to improve the productivity of the fields surrounding the Santa Vitoria mill (the Project).
location_description: The Project is located in Santa Vitoria, which is in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
development_impact: The Project has an AIMM rating of Good. IFC expects the Project to have environmental effects through increased bioenergy production and improved agricultural yields. The Project will also generate economy wide impact through job creation and value addition. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment has the potential to contribute to promoting resilience of Brazil's sugar and ethanol sector through demonstrating climate smart agri practices, including the use of a diversified set of seed varieties.
additionality: The proposed IFC loan has both financial and non-financial additionality. The financial additionality stems from the provision of long-term financing with tenors that are scarce to the Company in the market. Non-financial additionality centers on the adoption of IFC's environmental and social Performance Standards.

project_description: The Project aims to support Liquid Telecom Holding Limited (“Liquid” or the “Company”) at raising US$220 million in ZAR equivalent to be borrowed by their South African subsidiary Liquid Telecom South Africa (“LTSA”). IFC is providing up to ZAR 1,029 million as part of the Company's effort to strengthen its balance sheet structure. This will include the refinancing of Liquid’s existing ZAR debt and drawn portion of the US$ revolving credit facility, extending tenors and moving away from a single maturity, as well as potentially repurchasing a portion of its bond (the “Project”). The Project is taking place in a context where Liquid is undergoing a capital rebalancing exercise. Liquid is a strong Telco partner in South Africa and across the African continent. Since its establishment in 2004, Liquid has anchored the development of the broadband market in Africa with its presence across the region. The Project will help ensure the continuity of Liquid’s endeavor to bridge the connectivity gap in Africa and enhance the resilience of the fixed broadband market in its countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Liquid is the leading pan-African provider of wholesale voice, wholesale data, and internet protocol (IP) services, and an existing IFC client, and provides internet services across the African continent.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Term Loan amount is up to $220 million ZAR equivalent. The proposed IFC investment is for an up to ZAR 1,029 million investment in the Term Loan, for IFC's own account..
location_description: Liquid Telecom South Africa is the South African subsidiary of Liquid. Liquid is a Pan-African company with operational locations across Africa.
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase Liquid’s capacity to enhance customer connections through last-mile connectivity. While this investment mainly consists of refinancing existing debt associated with activities in Sub-Saharan Africa, this will enable the Company to unlock more free cash flow for capital expansion plans across Africa over the next few years. Such expansion includes furthering Liquid’s fiber network and digital footprint of services across countries of operation. Beyond the Company, this project is expected to enhance the resilience of the broadband market in Africa by supporting a large player to face headwinds and continue its growth strategy which aims to increase broadband capacity for retail operators in the Pan-African markets including South Africa, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Kenya, Zambia and DRC.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is primarily financial and will be demonstrated through supporting Liquid in its ambitious plan to strengthen its balance sheet by improving the Company’s current debt structure through upsizing the ZAR Term Loan and moving away from the single maturity debt profile. IFC’s support during this process will be essential to ensure that Liquid can continue its growth plan to be one of the most relevant broadband and connectivity players on the continent.

project_description: The proposed IFC’s financing consists of a senior secured Kyrgyz Som (KGS)-denominated loan of up to US$20 million equivalent (the IFC Loan) to Adal Azyk LLC (AA or the Company), the largest sausage producer and integrated poultry farm in the Kyrgyz Republic, an IDA country, with about 55% market share in the fast-growing Kyrgyz sausage market, and a highly competitive position in the country’s poultry market. The IFC Loan will help fund the US$33 million investment program aimed at expansion of poultry operations in 2024-2026, including construction of 48 broiler sheds, and a new feed mill (the Project). The Project will be implemented by Agro Kush LLC (AK), a subsidiary of AA. The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA PSW Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: AA is majority owned by the Orumbayev family (89%), with the remaining 11% shares belonging to Mrs. Valentina Alymkulova.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total cost to implement the Project is estimated at US$33 million to be financed by (i) IFC’s proposed senior secured loan of up to US$20 million denominated in KGS for its own account; and (i) internal cash generation of the Company.
location_description: AA is headquartered in the outskirts of Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic. The Project is to be implemented by AK in Issyk Kul and Chui regions of the Kyrgyz Republic.
development_impact: The expected project-level outcomes are: (i) Economy-wide Effects: by promoting local production of poultry meat, the Project is expected to contribute to increased value addition, employment creation and stimulate downstream linkages with related sectors. The Project will also create indirect jobs for MSMEs in the product value chains, and support import substitution; (ii) Stakeholder – Consumer: the Project is expected to increase consumer access to affordable, safe and higher quality poultry products therefore contributing to food security in the country. The expected market-level outcomes are resilience/competitiveness: the Project is expected to catalyze adoption of best practices that improve efficiency in operations and competitiveness of the market. The Project will also help supply Kyrgyz Republic with a reliable supply of affordable animal protein. The low volume of local poultry production has exposed the Kyrgyz Republic’s vulnerability to import restrictions from neighboring countries.
additionality: IFC’s expected additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial and comes in the form of (i) financing structure through longer tenor; (ii) standard setting; and (iii) knowledge, innovation, and capacity building through advisory services. Financial additionality: Financing Structure: IFC, enabled by the IDA PSW LCF, will provide long term local currency financing (7 years with 2-years grace) on terms otherwise not available in the local market. Non-Financial additionality: (i) Standard setting: IFC will help improve its existing E&S standards in line with IFC Performance Standards and industry best practices thereby setting the bar for competitors; (ii) Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC is exploring potential upstream and advisory engagements related to corporate governance, decarbonization, and reduction of chicken mortality.

project_description: The proposed investment comprises an International Finance Corporation (IFC) A-loan of up to US$60 million in INR equivalent, to Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (“GVMC”), an urban local body in the state of Andhra Pradesh. GVMC is responsible for the civic infrastructure and administration of the city of Visakhapatnam. The proposed investment would finance the development of Madhurawada Sewerage System in the northern part of the city as it is one of the fastest growing executive capital area in the city. The project involves the development of sewage collection network, sewage pumping stations, lift stations, and sewage treatment plant. The benefits of the proposed project are increased sustainability of sanitation services, improved environmental outcomes, mitigation of greenhouse gases, and cost efficiency.
sponsor_shareholders: GVMC is the civic body that governs the city of Visakhapatnam , which is the largest city of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh . The executive power of the GVMC is vested in the Municipal Commissioner , an Indian Administrative Service officer appointed by the Government of Andhra Pradesh .
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Out of total project cost of US$67 million, IFC will invest up to US$60 million (in INR equivalent) through subscription of non-convertible debentures issued by GVMC.
location_description: The project will be covering the Madhurawada region of Visakhapatnam city in Andhra Pradesh, India.
development_impact: IFC’s investment will increase access to sanitation services in Visakhapatnam City through the expansion of the sewerage network, and the development of a wastewater treatment plant and sewerage pumping station, that will contribute to reduce and mitigate pollution generated by untreated wastewater. Beyond the Project, IFC's investment is expected to demonstrate the financial viability of India’s municipalities' urban infrastructure projects using commercial debt, enhancing the municipalities’ likelihood for accessing financing in the future from commercial investors.
additionality: IFC additionality is both financial and non-financial. IFC financial additionality stems from the provision of long-term debt financing without a sovereign guarantee. IFC non-financial additionality stems from Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building which is focused on delivery of advisory services encompassing (i) the preparation of a Climate Action Plan, (ii) recommendations based on the APEX tool to prioritize municipal projects based on impact and guidelines on which technologies to use for water/wastewater treatment, (iii) recommended STP and sewerage network design; as well as Standard Setting, to bring the Company's Environmental and Social (E&S) practices in line with IFC's Performance Standards (PS).

project_description: The Project is a combination of investment preparation and proposed financing to Eneris Alpha S.A., a Luxembourg based company and sole owner of a leading Warsaw-based group with vertically integrated waste management operations in Poland. (“Eneris” or the “Company”). IFC’s pre-investment support to the Company focuses on development of Eneris’ long-term sustainability and circular economy strategy and strengthening of corporate E&S capacity to support the Company’s growth ambitions.
sponsor_shareholders: Eneris is a private company, currently indirectly and wholly owned by Mr. Artur Dela, a Polish-born entrepreneur who first entered Poland’s waste management sector in 2015 through acquisition of Veolia Uslugi dla srodowiska and significantly expanded it by developing new product lines in waste management, thereby strengthening its position among the sector’s leaders in Poland.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC seeks to provide an up to EUR 80 million financing to Eneris Alpha S.A. The IFC's proposed investment will be used to finance greenfield circular economy projects and strategic acquisitions in the waste management sector in Poland, including municipal and industrial waste collection, sorting and recycling, battery recycling, hazardous waste management, biogas plants, as well as strengthening of the Company's capital structure.
location_description: The Borrower is headquartered in Luxembourg, while its Polish operating subsidiaries conduct business within Poland.
development_impact: The Project will increase access to waste management infrastructure and services, and environmental effects through a reduction in GHG emissions. At the market level, the Project is expected to improve sustainability by introducing a modern waste management and value-addition system that supports the development of a circular economy in Poland.
additionality: Through the proposed investment IFC will support the expansion of Eneris, a waste management company in Poland with operations across collection, treatment, recycling and landfilling of waste. The Project would provide both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide innovative financing tailored to the Company’s growth plans. Non-financial additionality derives from the application of IFC’s knowledge and expertise in waste management through pre-investment engagements facilitating application of its Performance Standards to mitigate E&S risks and improvement of operational standards.

sector: Other Textile Products (Including Industrial and Medical Products)
project_description: The proposed investment is a financing package consisting of: (i) an IFC A-loan of up to EUR50 million to Sunmart Trading FZCO Dubai (Sunmart) and Senbai Holdings FZCO, Dubai (Senbai, together the Borrowers); and (ii) an equity investment of US$30 million in Softcare Limited (Softcare or the Company), which is also the guarantor of IFC’s proposed loan to Sunmart and Senbai. Sunmart and Senbai are fully-owned subsidiaries of Softcare, which itself is a subsidiary of Sunda Enterprise Limited (“Sunda”). The proceeds from IFC’s debt and equity investments will be used to finance the capacity expansion of baby diapers and sanitary pads factories with a total project cost of US$155 million. The proceeds will be used to finance new production lines for baby diaper and sanitary pad within existing factories in Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, and Zambia (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Sunda is a leading Africa-focused, manufacturing and trading company, and operating in the FMCG, building materials, and metal hardware product segments. Incorporated in July 2024 in the Cayman Islands, Sunda became the new holding company for the business formerly known as Sunda Group Co., Limited. (Sunda Hong Kong) after a restructuring of Sunda Hong Kong. Softcare is a fully-owned subsidiary of Sunda and serves as the holding company for the business of baby and feminine hygiene products focusing on the development, manufacturing and sales of baby and feminine hygiene products such as baby diapers, baby pants, sanitary pads and wet wipes. Softcare published its application proof of the prospectus on the website of the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited on January 27, 2025. Sunmart is principally engaged in the procurement and trading of raw materials. Senbai is an intermediate holding company of Softcare’s operating subsidiaries for baby and feminine hygienic operating assets overseas, including Africa, Latin America, and Central Asia. Sunda’s ultimate beneficial owners are Mr. Yanchang Shen, the founder, CEO and Chairman of Sunda, and Ms. Yanjuan Yang, the spouse of Mr. Shen. They collectively own 100 percent of Sunda and 66.35 percent of Softcare according to the application proof of the prospectus of Softcare. The rest 33.65 percent of Softcare is currently beneficially owned by the shareholders who are then senior management members and employees of Sunda and its subsidiaries. These shareholdings will be diluted proportionally after the IFC investment for all Softcare’s shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at US$155 million and will be financed by: (i) the proposed EUR50 million (equivalent to US$53 million) A loan from IFC; (ii) the proposed US$30 million equity from IFC; and (iii) US$72 million of internal cash generation from Softcare.
location_description: Nairobi, Kenya; Accra, Ghana; Lusaka, Zambia; Pwani, Tanzania.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes include increased access to diapers and sanitary pads in target countries and enhanced career prospects and skill development opportunities for employees. Beyond project outcomes, IFC anticipates that the Project will improve the competitiveness of Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) sectors, particularly in baby diapers and sanitary pads, in Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, and Zambia by demonstrating the substantial business opportunities available within these markets.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality: 1) Financing structure: IFC will provide a substantial amount of long-term hard currency financing, to be deployed across multiple countries in different regions of Africa, which is not readily available through local banks due to shallow financial markets and limited appetite for cross-border financing. 2) IFC own account equity: IFC equity investment provides Softcare with necessary patient capital to fuel its forthcoming growth phase and market expansion in Africa and beyond. The instrument is well suited for the capital intensive and long-term nature of Softcare’s strategic objectives in countries with limited industrial infrastructure. Furthermore, the instrument strengthens Softcare’s ability to take risk, leverage resources, and improve corporate governance. 3) Non-commercial risk mitigation, including trusted partnership: IFC’s local presence and business network in Africa would provide comfort and help mitigate sovereign and regulatory risks, especially those related to repatriation and regulation issues. World Bank Group’s brand and good relationship with the local governments will enhance the credibility of the Company and the Project. 4) Standard setting: The Company expects that partnership with IFC will enable them to further strengthen best practices in environmental and social (E&S). IFC will conduct a diagnostic on the Company’s environmental, social, and governance practices, and provide guidance to improve any actions on par with international standards.

project_description: IFC will partially guarantee the receivables of Soufflet Agro Ukraine CJSC from farmers and grain buyers and provide liquidity support for the operations of InVivo Group direct and/or indirect subsidiaries in Ukraine (“Project”). The Project is expected to be supported by Blended Finance contributors under the Economic Resilience Action (“ERA”) Program for Ukraine – the Netherlands, as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: SouffletAgro Ukraine CJSC, based in Ukraine, is a subsidiary of InVivo Group, based in France. InVivo Group is a leading agribusiness player in Europe owned by Union InVivo. Union InVivo is a union of cooperatives in France.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide (i) two risk-sharing facilities partially guaranteeing up to 30 million of SouffletAgro Ukraine CJSC's receivables from Ukrainian farmers and up to 10 million of its receivables from grain buyers and (ii) up to 50 million loan to InVivo Group.
location_description: Investments under the Project are planned to be made in Ukraine.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to contribute to global food security by supporting grain origination in Ukraine and exporting to, among other regions, developing countries in Africa, Asia, and the Middle East. The Project will also support jobs and the livelihoods of Ukrainian farmers and generate value addition and employment to the Ukrainian economy. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing will contribute to promoting resilience in Ukraine’s agribusiness sector.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality in this Project largely stems from the provision of counter-cyclical financing to a client with whom IFC has had a long-term partnership; IFC’s support for Ukraine’s agricultural production, which will provide a strong positive signal to other potential investors; and IFC’s global presence and knowledge.

project_description: The proposed investment is a USD15M unsecured income participating loan, in GMED Holding B.V. (the Company under creation, the Borrower) a holding medical technologies (medtech) manufacturing and distribution company, to support (i) growing its existing subsidiaries' operations in Egypt and (ii) the company's expansion plan in tofive East African countries as a medtech distributor (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded by Dr. Sayed Shaker in 1983. Currently, in Egypt, Dr. Sayed's son, Amr Shaker (the Sponsor) along with his family own 100% of Egyptian Company for Medical Industries (EGF), Egyptian Group for Exports & Imports (EGI), Egyptian Group for Corporate Services (EGCS), and 50% of Fresenius Medical Care Egypt (FMCEG) (collectively known as “EGMED”). Regionally, the Shaker family will own 100% of entities created for the expansion into East Africa. As part of this transaction, the group of Companies will be restructured into a Holding Company that will directly or indirectly mirror the above ownership stakes.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment is an up to USD15M Unsecured Income Participating Long-term Loan (the “C Loan”).
location_description: Egypt 19 Ebad El Rahman St. Heliopolis Cairo, Egypt. As of December 2024, EGMED operates four manufacturing plants in Cairo, Egypt in addition to nine distribution centers. The above address is the Head Office in Egypt.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is an improvement in access to quality medical products and equipment in Egypt and East African countries, notably in Kenya, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Rwanda and Uganda. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that its financing will contribute to increasing the competitive pressures of the Egyptian and East African medical equipment distribution market, by supporting the Company’s business-as-usual operational model of integrating high value-added services with medical device distribution, and internationalization through sole distributorship and principal diversification.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists of the provision of long-term finance to support the Company’s expansion of its medical distribution segment which will contribute to providing quality medical products and equipment in Egypt and East African countries. Non-financial additionality is comprised of knowledge, innovation, and capacity building provided by IFC’s information sharing on local markets and regulatory insights for local and regional expansion through acquisition, and standard setting provided by supporting the Company in developing a comprehensive E&S system and corporate governance strategy.

project_description: The proposed project entails an investment in a senior tranche of asset-backed securities (the “ABS”) to be issued by a Special Purpose Vehicle (“SPV”) to be established under the laws of Thailand (subject to regulatory approval). The senior tranche will be collateralized by a pool of receivables originated by SeaMoney (Capital) Co., Ltd. (the “Company”) under the Nano loan license regulated by the Bank of Thailand. The senior tranche will be of up to US$75 million or equivalent in local currency (“LCY”). The investment shall comprise of IFC’s own account, and mobilization. The purpose of the proposed IFC investment is to support the Company's lending program to micro borrowers and small business owners, with at least [60%] earmarked to women borrowers (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: SeaMoney (Capital) Co., Ltd. is a financial services provider offering lending products to the low to middle income population in Thailand, including women. SeaMoney (Capital) Co., Ltd.’s parent company, Sea Limited, is listed on the NYSE and operates Shopee, the largest e-commerce platform in Southeast Asia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project entails an investment in a senior tranche of ABS of upto US$75 million or equivalent in LCY to be issued by an SPV to be established under the laws of Thailand. The investment shall comprise of IFC’s own account of upto US$50 million and mobilization to support the Company's lending program to micro borrowers and small business owners, with at least [60%] earmarked to women borrowers. The total issuance including the junior tranche will be of up to US$100 million.
location_description: The investment will finance the Company’s digital lending program for productive purposes in Thailand.
development_impact: The development impact of the Project will be delivered through increased access to support low-income individuals and microentrepreneurs, especially women borrowers.
additionality: Financial Additionality: The structure is a tailored securitization which will be customized to suit the Company’s funding needs. IFC, through this investment, will support diversifying the Company's funding base. Furthermore, IFC will help the Company to raise additional needed funding through resource mobilization. Non-financial Additionality: IFC will help the Company develop its environmental and social (“E&S”) standards to mitigate E&S risk and share with the Company its global knowledge on responsible finance, consumer protection, microfinancing and digital solutions.

project_description: Couvoir Amar (“CA”) and Africaine de Production Animale (“APRAN”) (collectively referred to as the “Companies” or “COUVOIR AMAR”) aim to integrate the value chain through the establishment of an animal feed plant, additional breeder farms, and chicken broiler facilities. The project will focus on improving feed production and broiler farming efficiency.
sponsor_shareholders: Couvoir Amar and APRAN are owned by Mr. Serigne Amar and his siblings.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$10.12 million. IFC will provide a EUR 5 million A loan equivalent in currency XOF (8-year A loan including a 3-year grace period), with a subsidy for a rate buy-down from the GAFSP Local Currency Pilot facility, amounting to approximately 5% of the total project cost.
location_description: The company’s headquarters are in Keur Massar, Senegal. All company activities are located in the Thies region, and the new feed mill will specifically be based in the Special Economic Zone of Diass.
development_impact: The proposed investment is aligned with IFC’s strategic approach to Agribusiness. It will enhance food and nutrition security by improving access to poultry products in Senegal. The Project is also expected to contribute to the surrounding community through the new jobs created to operate the expanded facilities and along the poultry supply chain. Project level outcomes: (i) Stakeholder (farmers) - increased farmer’s access to poultry inputs such as DOCs and feeds to improve productivity; (ii) Stakeholder (consumers) - contribute to food security by increasing the volume of protein-rich poultry products sold to consumers and improving dietary diversity of households in Senegal and (iii) Economy wide effects - increased value addition and direct job creation along the poultry value chain. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to contribute to increasing competitiveness of the sector in Senegal.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing structure: IFC offers long term financing on terms that are otherwise not available in Senegal (8 years tenor with 3 years grace), and GAFSP LCF that adds value by mitigating the risks of currency depreciation, convertibility/transferability and provide a viable local currency rate. Over the past 12 months, the total face value of Euro syndicated loans was 0.11 billion. However, there were no Euro corporate bond issued during the period. Further, there were neither EUR syndicated loans nor corporate bonds issued in Agribusiness sector. Non-financial Additionality: Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC, through advisory services, will help strengthen COUVOIR AMAR biosecurity at the poultry farms and hatchery, and food safety at the feed mill. Additionally, IFC assessment will help strengthen the Company’s E&S management system, in line with international standards.

project_description: The proposed project is an investment of up to US$100 million in the Green Investment Partnership (GIP or the Fund). GIP is a structured debt fund focused on providing debt financing to marginally bankable green infrastructure projects in emerging Asia, with an initial focus on Southeast Asia (SEA). GIP will be managed by Pentagreen Capital Fund Management Pte. Ltd. (the Fund Manager or Pentagreen FM). The Fund Manager is wholly owned by Pentagreen Capital Pte. Ltd. (Pentagreen), a Singapore-based company that is owned by HSBC Holdings Plc and Temasek Holdings on a 50:50 basis. GIP seeks to raise up to US$1 billion to provide senior secured loans, unsecured loans, mezzanine, subordinated loans, and investments into debt securities, for marginally bankable sustainable infrastructure projects. The senior, mezzanine and junior tranches in the Fund’s capital stack are expected to respectively comprise 50%, 30% and 20% of total Fund commitments.
sponsor_shareholders: Pentagreen Capital Fund Management Pte. Ltd. is a wholly owned subsidiary of Pentagreen and is expected to act as the Fund Manager for the GIP. Incorporated in 2021 in Singapore, Pentagreen (formerly known as Sustainable Infrastructure Capital Pte. Ltd.) is a 50-50 joint venture between Temasek and HSBC formed with an initial capital of US$150 million. Pentagreen officially launched its business in August 2022.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project is an investment of up to US$100 million in GIP. GIP seeks to raise up to US$1 billion to provide senior secured loans, unsecured loans, mezzanine, subordinated loans, and investments into debt securities, for marginally bankable sustainable infrastructure projects. The senior, mezzanine and junior tranches in the Fund’s capital stack are expected to respectively comprise 50%, 30% and 20% of total Fund commitments.
location_description: Pentagreen is domiciled in Singapore. The proposed project is a fund investment into marginally bankable infrastructure projects across Southeast Asia and India. The current pipeline includes projects in Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Malaysia, Laos, Cambodia and India.
development_impact: Environment effects – Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction: The Project will contribute to reduced GHG emissions in Asian emerging countries with a large power generation carbon footprint. Stakeholder effect – Increased access to climate finance: The Project will lead to environmental benefits of GIP’s investments in emerging economies and will support access to climate finance in the target markets for a range of climate projects. Competitiveness: IFC anticipates that the Project will promote competition in the climate finance space for infrastructure sector, by helping create mechanisms to draw long-term financing for renewable energy, sustainable transport, waster, water and circular economy solutions. Through demonstration and replication, the Project is expected to help crowd-in private capital for climate financing activities through new funds and investors.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality stems from financial structuring, given IFC’s expected role helping the Fund reach its target size. Non-financial additionality includes knowledge sharing and E&S advisory services and capacity building for the Fund Manager if needed.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a US$30m A Loan to Grupo Naturasol (the “Group”) to finance the acquisition of new production lines on its potato and corn processing businesses.
sponsor_shareholders: Grupo Naturasol is a Mexican group involved in the production and commercialization of cereal bars, nuts, processed potatoes and corn-based products, and the purchase, processing and distribution of honey, honey-based products and jams. Grupo Naturasol’s shareholders are Mr. Ulises Armando Vigil Silva (founder) and Ms. Selma Valdez Cazares
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project Cost is estimated at US$30 million and IFC’s investment consists of an A loan of up to US$30 million.
location_description: The Project is located in the State of Mexico, where the production facilities and distribution centers are located.
development_impact: The Project is expected to generate environmental effects through improving water efficiency and economy-wide impact through job creation and value addition. The Project is also expected to contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of Mexico's private label food processing sector by helping to shift the sector toward a more productive and sustainable production model.
additionality: IFC is providing long-term financing supporting Naturasol’s liquidity and enabling critical capex for the food processing industry. In addition, IFC will contribute to strengthening the Company's Environmental and Social practices through the adoption of IFC's Performance Standards.

company_name: America Industria e Comercio de Embalagens Ltda.
project_description: America Embalagens S.A. (“America”, or the “Company”) is one of the leading Brazilian manufacturers of plastic closures and rigid plastic packaging, serving the food & beverages, personal care, household and beauty markets. Headquartered in the state of Rio Grande do Sul (South Brazil), the Company operates four plants, three in Brazil and one in Argentina. America is undergoing an expansion project to increase its capacity in Brazil.
sponsor_shareholders: America is fully controlled by the Ling Family through its holding company Évora S.A. America has a dedicated management team and a board of directors with independent members, operating separately from the other companies within Évora S.A.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing an A/B Loan of up to US$70 million to support America’s capital expenditure and related working capital at one of its plants located in Brazil, aimed at increasing capacity of innovative plastic preforms (tubes) used in the beauty and personal hygiene industries.
location_description: Investments will be made at America’s facility located in the São Paulo state, Brazil.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project will contribute to generate environmental effects driven by the adoption of advanced technology facilitating a substantial increase in the utilization of recycled plastic. The project is also expected to generate economy-wide effects through the creation of value added and employment opportunities. Beyond the Project, IFC expects that the investment will have a powerful market demonstration effect and incentivize other market participants to adopt innovative technologies that enable a substantial reduction in plastic usage within the personal care product packaging sector.
additionality: IFC is providing long-term financing and mobilization through a B loan. In addition, the Company will benefit from targeted support to enhance environmental and social standards, the provision of Sustainability Linked Financing, and the potential development of a comprehensive Gender Action Plan and EDGE certification, subject to further consultation with the Company.
Company Name: America Industria e Comercio de Embalagens Ltda.

project_description: The proposed investment is a secured financing of up to Euro (€) 9.2 million to Menema Guinée Sàrl (the ‘Company’), a leading Guinean family-owned manufacturer of mattresses, plastic household goods and wooden furniture. IFC’s financing supports the capacity expansion of the Company’s operations and associated working capital needs. The project is expected to be supported by the IDA Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (“IDA PSW BFF”), as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was established by the Guinean Ly family in the early 1980s and currently employs 337 individuals. The ownership of the company is equally divided between Mr. Kadialiou Ly and Mr. Elhadji Thierno Ly, each holding a 50 percent share.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is €15 million comprising of (i) an IFC A-Loan of up to €4.6 million; and (ii) a concessional loan of up to €4.6 million subordinated to the A Loan from IFC, acting in its capacity as the implementing entity of IDA PSW BFF.
location_description: Menema's current location is in Manéah, 50 kilometers west of the capital, Conakry. The new expansion site is in Kassognah, 40 kilometers west of Conakry.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes include stakeholder effects, economy-wide effects, and environmental benefits. Beyond this Project, IFC anticipates that its investment will promote sustainability through increased recycling of plastics.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via the Project’s financing structure through long-term debt financing, which is not readily available from the local banking sector. Non-financial additionality is supplied via standard setting and knowledge, innovation and capacity building.

company_name: ISQ Growth Markets Infrastructure Fund II (UST), L.P.
project_description: The proposed project comprises a US$75 million equity investment in ISQ Growth Markets Infrastructure Fund II (“the Fund”), an infrastructure fund established by I Squared Capital (“ISQ”). The Fund will generally focus on the key sectoral themes of Digital, Energy Transition, Transportation and Logistics, Environmental (waste management and sustainable water), and Social infrastructure in certain jurisdictions that are not member states of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (the “OECD”), as well as the following members of the OECD: as determined by the General Partner in its sole discretion, certain Asia Pacific jurisdictions, including Australia, the Republic of Korea and Japan, and certain Latin American jurisdictions, including Chile, Colombia and Mexico (collectively, the “Target Jurisdictions”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by ISQ, which is an independent fund manager specialized in investing and managing infrastructure assets globally. Established in 2012, ISQ is headquartered in Miami, and operates across more than 70 countries via offices in Abu Dhabi, London, Munich, New Delhi, Sao Paolo, Singapore, Sydney and Taipei.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund aims to raise US$3.0 billion. IFC’s proposed investment is for up to a total equity investment of US$75 million in the Fund.
location_description: The Fund will primarily make investments in Target Jurisdictions.
development_impact: The Fund aims to increase access to private equity capital and value creation for infrastructure projects in Target Jurisdictions, addressing significant infrastructure gaps in emerging markets jurisdictions. The Fund will support infrastructure needs by investing across areas of: transport and logistics, digital infrastructure, and energy transition and efficiency in countries including India, Brazil, Philippines, Indonesia, Thailand, and Colombia. The initiative aims to strengthen the infrastructure equity market in emerging markets, demonstrating the commercial viability of such investments and attracting more institutional investors.
additionality: IFC additionality is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality involves supporting the Fund to mobilize additional capital from new investors, including institutional investors and other development finance institutions (DFIs). Non-financial additionality includes supporting ISQ to enhance the Fund’s Sustainability Procedures. Further, IFC will act as a strategic partner, providing ongoing support and feedback on sensitive and critical issues in Target Jurisdictions. For instance, as needed, IFC will introduce ISQ to market participants, technical experts, other key stakeholders, or coordinate meetings with IFC’s Industry Specialists and relevant teams in target markets. IFC’s presence as a key investor in the Fund provides comfort and ensures the Fund will be managed and pursue an investment strategy in adherence to international standards and adequate risk mitigation.
Company Name: ISQ Growth Markets Infrastructure Fund II (UST), L.P.

project_description: IFC is considering an investment comprising an up to US$12.0 million “A” loan and a US$12.0 million subordinated loan from IFC acting as the implementing entity of the International Development Association’s Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility for a total financing package of US$24.0 million to Mackie Building Materials (“MBM”) and MACCEM Industries SL Limited (“MACCEM”). This will be used to part finance the construction and operation of a cement grinding plant in Hastings, Sierra Leone. This backward integration project is expected to increase supply of locally produced cement and improve cost competitiveness. The project is expected to be supported by an International Development Association Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (“IDA PSW BFF”) as described in the Blended Finance section.
sponsor_shareholders: Both MBM and MACCEM are 100% owned by Mr. Ahmed Mackie (the Sponsor) and his immediate family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$36.5 million. IFC’s proposed investment comprises an (i) up to US$12.0 million A loan and (ii) up to US$12.0 million concessional subordinated loan from IFC acting in its capacity as the implementing entity of IDA PSW BFF. The IDA PSW BFF loan will help close the funding gap and de-risk IFC's investment by being subordinated in payments and liquidation to the IFC A loan.
location_description: Hastings, Sierra Leone.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are: (i) economy-wide effects through substantial value-addition, direct and indirect employment generation, foreign exchange savings while enabling import substitution; and (ii) competitiveness through the localization of a segment of cement manufacturing in Sierra Leone, significantly reducing cement costs, thereby establishing a substantial competitive advantage. In addition to incorporating advanced grinding technology, the project is expected to generate significant demonstration effects by encouraging the adoption of renewable energy solutions, as a portion of IFC’s financing will be used for the installation of solar PV.
additionality: IFC, with the support of IDA PSW BFF, will (i) provide long-term financing that is not otherwise available in the market; (ii) provide guidance to upgrade the client’s environment, health, and safety practices in line with international best practices; (iii) assist with strengthening financial reporting and corporate governance practices; and (iv) propose interventions to address gender-based gaps identified.

sector: Household Appliances (Including Refrigerators, Laundry Machine, Dishwashers, etc.)
project_description: This project is proposed under IFC's Global Trade Supplier Finance program (“GTSF” or the “Program”) approved by the IFC Board on September 21, 2010 (Original Project #28723) and an additional increase approved on December 15, 2022. Under GTSF, IFC provides short-term financing to suppliers, (“Suppliers”), in emerging markets selling to large companies, (“Buyers”), on open account terms. Under this project, IFC will provide financing to Suppliers of Controladora Mabe, S.A. de C.V., (“Mabe” or “the Company”), through E-Factor Network platform (“EFN”), an independent Mexican supply chain finance platform with experience in the electronic factoring business.
sponsor_shareholders: Mabe is a private company based in Mexico. The company designs, manufactures, and distributes household appliances including refrigerators, stoves, washing machines, and other kitchen appliances and serves customers in Mexico and Latin American and Caribbean. Mabe is owned by individual shareholders and Haier
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is US$50 million, senior, unsecured, funded, uncommitted, revolving, short-term, GTSF facility for Mabe's suppliers based in Mexico and other emerging markets.
location_description: GTSF-approved jurisdictions, including Mexico.
development_impact: Not Applicable
additionality: Financial Additionality: The Project would provide much needed affordable US$ based, short-term funding to suppliers located in emerging markets.

project_description: The proposed transaction includes IFC investment of up to US$20 million equivalent local currency debt to WorldLink Communications Limited (WCL) and its wholly owned subsidiary, Data World Limited (DWL). As Nepal's leading Internet Service Provider (ISP) with approximately 33% market share in the fixed broadband segment, WCL serves over 940,000 retail broadband households and 10,000 enterprise customers across 73 of Nepal's 77 districts. Expanding into the enterprise data center business through DWL, the company leverages nearly 30 years of operational experience, with key management personnel having been with WCL for over two decades.
sponsor_shareholders: Worldlink’s founder and largest shareholder, Mr. Dileep Agrawal, leads the promoter group, which holds a majority stake in the company. Institutional investors, including British International Investment and Dolma Impact Fund. In November 2024, WCL secured a €10 million equity commitment from Finnfund.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total planned capital expenditure (capex) for FY25-FY28 is $64 million, primarily allocated towards Fiber to the Home (FTTH) expansion ($43 million, 66%) and Data Center (DC) infrastructure ($21 million, 34%). Funding sources include loans from IFC and other lenders for FTTH ($14 million, 22%) and DC development ($15 million, 23%), while equity and internal accruals contribute $35 million (55%).
location_description: Spread across Nepal. Please refer to ESRS for details.
development_impact: The project benefits from inclusion adjustment. The most significant expected project-level outcome is to increase access to quality broadband Internet and data hosting services for households and businesses. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will support the creation of a competitive market for data hosting services via demonstration and replication channels. IFC anticipates that the Project Outcomes are Very Strong, derived from increased access to quality fixed broadband connectivity for households, by connecting households with high-speed Internet, a substantial share of which are located in underserved areas and were previously unconnected. Further, the Project is also expected to increase access to data hosting services for businesses, by rolling out core and edge data center facilities in the Country. These outcomes have the potential to result in higher availability of digital services for individuals and thereby support enhanced productivity growth for businesses. this investment is expected to support the creation of a competitive market for data hosting services in Nepal by inducing market entry through demonstration and replication of a nascent business model and technological innovation. As part of this investment, the Company is introducing the wholesale data center business model outside metropolitan areas to support rural connectivity and serve both hyperscalers and local market with data hosting facilities. A successful expansion is expected to demonstrate the commercial viability of this business model at scale in this nascent market, thereby supporting the entry of independent DC providers or new hyperscalers.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists of (i) providing a longer-tenor investment than what is available from the banking system in an IDA market, and (ii) mobilizing additional debt from parallel lenders leveraging a PCG structure that enable the company to reach its fundraising target. Non-financial additionality involves (iii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building by leveraging advisory services to help the Company make contributions to its selected Sustainable Development Goals on climate, gender and reduced inequalities; and (iv) Standard setting by providing guidance to the Company to strengthen its corporate governance (CG) framework.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an A-loan of up to US$24.3 million equivalent Nigerian Naira (NGN) to NSIA Advanced Medical Services Limited (“MedServe” or “the Company”), to expand its medical diagnostic and cancer treatment services, which comprises the roll-out of 13 new diagnostics health centers, 3 oncology (cancer) centers and 3 catheterization (cardiology) labs, across 13 states in Nigeria (the Project). The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF), as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 2022, MedServe is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA) via its wholly owned healthcare platform company, Nigeria Health Development and Investment Company (NHDIC), collectively the Project Sponsors. Following the successful pilot of an oncology center and two medical diagnostic centers over the last 5 years, MedServe was established to house, consolidate and execute NHDIC’s business plan for medical diagnostic and cancer treatment. The proposed Project represents the first of two phases to establish 23 modern medical diagnostic centers, 3 oncology centers, and 7 catheterization laboratories across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones. NHDIC’s mandate is to address the infrastructure gap in the Nigerian health sector, elevate standards, improve manpower, and improve health indicators. NHDIC works with both the private and public sector, focusing on tertiary health care provision, diagnostic services and medical manufacturing.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project cost is estimated at US$154.1 million and will be financed by US$129.8 million in equity by the Project Sponsors, while the balance of funding will be from the proposed IFC debt package. The proposed IFC financing package consists of a US$24.3 million IFC A loan with a US$/NGN cross-currency swap support from IDA PSW LCF.
location_description: The Project will be rolled-out across 13 states in Nigeria: including Akwa-Ibom, Bauchi, Delta, Enugu, Kaduna, Kwara, Oyo, Lagos, Plateau, Rivers, Sokoto, Yobe, and Federal Capital Territory, in Nigeria.
development_impact: The Project will contribute to alleviating the burden of NCDs such as cancers, cardiovascular diseases and other allied health conditions for patients and create direct and indirect job opportunities, including for medical professionals. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that this investment will promote competitiveness in the healthcare (oncology and medical diagnostic) market by demonstrating the model of co-location, cross subsidization of treatment cost; entry into an underdeveloped and highly specialized healthcare market with a growing demand, and upskilling medical personnels in an underdeveloped specialty. This is expected to catalyze significant movement among other private healthcare providers in the market.
additionality: The Project will contribute to alleviating the burden of NCDs such as cancers, cardiovascular diseases and other allied health conditions for patients and create direct and indirect job opportunities, including for medical professionals. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that this investment will promote competitiveness in the healthcare (oncology and medical diagnostic) market by demonstrating the model of co-location, cross subsidization of treatment cost; entry into an underdeveloped and highly specialized healthcare market with a growing demand, and upskilling medical personnels in an underdeveloped specialty. This is expected to catalyze significant movement among other private healthcare providers in the market.

project_description: NSG UK Enterprises Limited (“NSG UK” or “the Company”), a leading global glass producer has invited IFC to consider providing up to US$160 million sustainability-linked corporate loan to finance its capital expenditures in Poland and corporate level research and development (R&D) focused on decarbonization initiatives (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1918 and headquartered in Tokyo, Nippon Sheet Glass Co. Ltd. (“NSG Group”) is a well-diversified global manufacturer of glass and glazing products for the automotive, architectural, and technical glass markets, ranking among the top five global producers in these markets. With manufacturing operations in about 30 countries and sales in over 100 countries, it employs approximately 25,000 people worldwide. NSG Group is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. NSG UK Enterprises (“NSG UK” or the “Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of NSG Group, manufactures architectural and automotive glass products. With over 150 years in business, the Company has 19 float glass lines, 16 automotive glass plants, and sizeable downstream glass operations in over 20 countries throughout America, Europe, and Asia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment consists of a US$160 million A Loan to finance (i) an investment program to expand production and products in Poland and (ii) corporate-level research and development (R&D) focused on decarbonization initiatives to support the Group meeting its climate targets (the “Project”).
location_description: NSG plants in Sandomierz (float line and automotive) and one (automotive) at Chmielow in Poland, and R&D facilities in Merseyside, UK.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are economy-wide effects, namely an increase in value addition and exports in Poland and employment generation. Beyond these outcomes, IFC expects the investment to transform the sector of glass for photovoltaics (PV), and to diversify the global supply chains of PV modules.
additionality: IFC will provide both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality will be achieved through the Project’s financing structure, as the proposed loan improves the Company’s debt maturity profile, and through resource mobilization. IFC will also provide non-financial additionality via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building, particularly through structuring the investment as a sustainability-linked instrument. Discussions are ongoing to incorporate a gender perspective, as IFC is exploring gender advisory engagement with NSG UK to support the Company’s gender inclusion initiatives.

project_description: XSD International Paper SDN. BHD (“XSD” or the “Company”), founded in 2018, is a leading coated duplex board and grey board manufacturer in Malaysia which uses recycled material as raw material. XSD commenced production in March 2022 and currently operates one production line for coated duplex board with a designed capacity of 350,000 tons per annum (TPA). A second production line for grey board, with a capacity of 150,000 TPA, is under construction and is expected to be commissioned by 2Q25 (i.e. the period from April 1 to June 30, 2025). IFC’s proposal consists of an up to US$70 million Senior Secured A-Loan to XSD. IFC’s proceeds are expected to support the Company for the development of: (i) a biomass cogeneration plant to generate electricity and steam; and (ii) a third production line for duplex board paper with a capacity of 300,000 TPA. The construction of the cogeneration plant is ongoing and the commissioning of the same is expected in 2Q25. The construction of the third production line for coated duplex board is anticipated to commence at the end of 2025 and get completed by 1Q27.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was established by Mr. Li Shengfeng, also the founder of XSD Zhejiang, formerly one of China's largest duplex board producers with a total production capacity of 1.3 million TPA. In 2018, following a government decision to rezone the industrial area for residential use, Mr. Li sold all the assets of XSD Zhejiang and launched the Company in Malaysia. Mr. Li has over 25 years of experience in the paper industry. 99% of the shares in the Company are owned by Mr. Li Shengfeng while 1% is owned by another individual, namely, Mr. Lu Chengying.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project consists of the capital expenditure for: (i) a cogeneration plant with an estimated outlay of US$45 million; and (ii) a new duplex board production line which will have a capacity of 350,000 TPA with an estimated outlay of US$105 million. IFC will finance the Project with a senior secured loan of US$70 million split into investment of US$35 million each for the capex of the co-generation plant and new duplex board production line respectively. The residual cost of the Project will be financed through equity contribution and/or internal cash generation.
location_description: No 441, Bangunan XSD International Paper Sdn Bhd, 09400 Padang Serai, Kedah, Malaysia.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to have environmental effects through production of renewable energy for own consumption through financing a cogeneration unit. The Project will also generate economy wide impact through job creation and value addition. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment has the potential to contribute to promoting sustainability in Malaysia’s paper and pulp industry by demonstrating the environmental benefits and commercial viability of cogeneration.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC is providing financing for its own account at longer tenors than those readily available in the market. IFC’s A Loan will have a 7-year tenor with a two year grace period, which is longer than what the Company can obtain from local commercial banks. Standard setting: IFC will help the Company further strengthen its existing E&S practices , particularly in the areas of labor and working conditions and resource efficiency and pollution prevention, in line with IFC's performance standards and international best practices.

project_description: Copeval is Chile's largest agricultural input distributor reaching 50,000 farmers through its 24 stores and 3 distribution centers strategically spread across the country's agricultural regions. Copeval provides agricultural inputs such as crop protection products, fertilizers, seeds, machinery, irrigation equipment, fuel, and animal feed for the fruit, grain, cattle, and dairy sectors. It also provides intermediation services, logistic services, technical assistance, and training for farmers. IFC will be supporting Copeval's permanent working capital needs that are essential to finance the pre-harvest inputs and services to its network of farmers. IFC will subscribe securitized senior notes in CLP equivalent to up to US$25 million that will be structured through a securitization of Copeval's farmers receivables.
sponsor_shareholders: Copeval is a publicly listed company in the Santiago Stock Exchange, with three families (Martino, Bozzo and Ariztia) holding a ~54% shareholding interest, IFC a 16.8% shareholding interest and the balance atomized among several investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$25 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of a subscription of securitized senior notes for up to US$25 million in CLP equivalent to finance Copeval’s permanent working capital needs.
location_description: Copeval is headquartered in San Fernando, Chile. The Company has 24 branches and 3 distribution centers located throughout the major agricultural regions of Chile.
development_impact: The Project is expected to provide essential financing to ensure continuous provision of critical agricultural inputs to farmers, in particular small-scale farmers. Beyond the Project, the investment has the potential to contribute to promoting resilience of Chile’s agricultural sector through sustaining the provision of key agricultural inputs and deepening the use of securitization of agricultural receivables as a financial product to help stabilize the input distribution market.
additionality: IFC offers Copeval long-term local currency financing through a securitization structure, enabling competitive-cost financing by selling a pool of receivables with a better rating than Copeval itself. Additionally, IFC will conduct a corporate gender and inclusion assessment to identify workforce strengths and opportunities, forming an Action Plan to foster inclusion, enhance engagement, and boost productivity. IFC will also help Copeval develop and promote gender-smart corporate practices and policies.

project_description: Brookfield India Real Estate Trust (BIRET) is an institutionally managed office real estate investment trusts, comprising a portfolio of ten Grade A office assets and a mall. These assets cover a total operating leasable area of 24.3 million square feet across key business districts in India. BIRET was listed on Indian exchanges in February 2021. IFC has invested INR 8,350 million by subscribing to units of BIRET through the recently concluded Institutional Placement under the SEBI REIT Regulations (“QIP”), the proceeds from which shall be utilized for the partial or full prepayment or repayment of the outstanding borrowings of BIRET and companies held by it and general purposes including towards funding growth opportunities and strategic initiatives and acquisitions or such other objects as may be set out in the placement document (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: BIRET is managed by Brookprop Management Services Private Limited (“Investment Manager”), and the trustee is Axis Trustee Services Limited. BIRET is sponsored by BSREP India Office Holdings V Pte. Ltd. (Sponsor”), an affiliate of Brookfield Corporation (“Brookfield Group”). The Investment Manager and BIRET are part of Brookfield Group. Brookfield Group is a global alternative asset manager with a presence in real estate, infrastructure, renewable energy, and private equity with an AUM of US$272 billion in real estate (over 500 msf) as on September 30, 2024. In India, Brookfield Group has an AUM of approximately US$10 billion in real estate as on June 30, 2024. Its Indian office real estate business has a diversified portfolio of ~55 msf of assets in 10 cities, including BIRET portfolio of assets. BIRET is listed on the Indian stock exchanges. Brookfield Group owns ~40 percent shareholding in BIRET, and other investors own the remaining ~60 percent as on September 30, 2024.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: BIRET has raised INR 35,000 million of equity funds through the QIP. Out of this, IFC has made an equity investment of INR 8,350 million, resulting in IFC holding about 5 percent stake in BIRET. The immediate use of the proceeds will be for debt paydown and general corporate purposes as set out in the placement document. BIRET’s Sponsor group provides access to c.26 million square feet of high-quality office assets in places like Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Pune. A lower leverage is expected to create headroom for future acquisitions and support BIRET’s long-term strategy of acquiring stabilized, income-generating office assets and funding capital expenditures to upgrade its existing portfolio.
location_description: BIRET’s assets include ten integrated business parks and one independent mall located across Delhi National Capital Region (NCR), Mumbai, Kolkata and Ludhiana.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level effects are a) increasing access to modern and sustainable Grade A office buildings, which supports the GCC ecosystem, potentially contributing to job creation and upskilling relevant for youth; and (b) environmental effects through improved resource efficiency resulting from EDGE Advanced building certification, net-zero carbon targets, and reductions in GHG emissions. IFC also anticipates that the investment will promote greater sustainability in India's real estate sector.
additionality: The IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. IFC’s financial additionality comes through IFC’s own account financing, resource mobilization, and innovative financing structure. This stems from bringing patient equity capital into India’s nascent REIT asset class. Non-financial additionality comes through knowledge, innovation, capacity building, and standard setting.

project_description: Background: Prishtina Mall (PM or the Mall) is a super-regional mall with a GLA of ~115,000 m² located on the outskirts of Pristina, Kosovo. Construction began in 2019 (on a greenfield site); it opened in March 2023 and is currently occupied by over 200 retail units, including anchor tenants such as Intersport, H&M, Zara/Inditex, LC Waikiki, New Yorker and entertainment venues, such as HyperActive (south-Eastern Europe’s largest indoor amusement park). The Mall construction was financed mainly through equity investment from shareholders. IFC’s financing will help settle dues to construction contractors, finance expenditures for fit-out of new tenants, fund installation of solar power and investments to improve operational efficiency, in addition to refinancing existing capital providers.
sponsor_shareholders: Prishtina Mall Sh.A. is owned by 14 shareholders with business entities across various industries. All shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners (UBO) are local businessmen in Kosovo. The shareholding structure is presented below:
