total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide a senior debt package of up to €80 million with a tenor of up to 10 years. The debt package will comprise an A Loan of up to €45 million from IFC’s own account, and €35 million from B and/or Parallel loans.
location_description: Prishtina Mall is located approximately 10km from the city center of Pristina, the Kosovo capital. It is connected to Pristina by a major highway and served by a bus route.
development_impact: Project Outcomes: Economy-Wide: (i) direct job creation and contribution to GDP as well as indirect effects across the distribution chains; (ii) higher tax revenues for local government and; (iii) increased value added for local products. Environmental effects: By enabling energy-friendly, EDGE-certified infrastructure on Prishtina Mall, IFC expects the project to improve energy and water efficiency and reduce GHG emissions. Contribution to Market Creation: Competitiveness: Modern retail penetration of 31% in Kosovo is low compared to +80% in the developed European nations. IFC anticipates that the Project will increase competitive pressures that affect the market through expansion and subsequent increases in the offering of good quality and standardized retail infrastructure across the catchment areas.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing Structure: The proposed IFC investment will provide long-term financing. Innovative Financing: IFC will provide climate finance loan in a country where capital markets for such finance are not developed. Resource mobilization: mobilization of debt to help complete the financing needs. Non-Financial Additionality: Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC will support PM in improving corporate governance and support on green building standards. Standard Setting: IFC will help PM further elevate its existing E&S standards, particularly the L&FS standards, in line with IFC's PSs and international best practices.

company_name: Shandong Weigao Group Medical Polymer Co., Ltd.
project_description: Shandong Weigao Group Medical Polymer Co., Limited (“Weigao” or the “Company”) is a leading manufacturer of single-use medical consumables in China. The proposed investment is a debt financing package including up to US$250 million equivalent IFC A Loan to support Weigao in (i) expanding manufacturing capacity in consumables products in China; (ii) expanding into Southeast Asia, especially in Indonesia, through enhanced sales and marketing activities and localization of product manufacturing; and (iii) new product R&D to expand its product offerings including chronic disease management and health informatics (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Weigao is 46% owned by Weigao Holding Co., Limited (“Weigao Holding” and the “Sponsor”), while the remaining shares are owned by public (52%) and employee ownership plan (2%). Mr. Xueli Chen, the former Chairman and founder of Weigao Holding, directly and indirectly owns an aggregated 51% of Weigao Holding. The remaining 49% of Weigao Holding are owned by other current and former senior management team and minority shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed financing package comprises of an A Loan of up to US$250 million and mobilization of up to US$100 million from other development finance institutions, as well as potential core mobilization from other financial institutions.
location_description: The Project is located in Weihai, Shandong Province, China and developing countries in Southeast Asia.
development_impact: Project outcomes (stakeholders, Economy-wide): This Project will enhance access for patients in China and other developing countries to affordable and quality medical consumables. The Company has cost advantages brought by operational flexibility, the capability to manufacture raw materials, and the quality control management with high level of automation, enabling the introduction of affordable and quality medical consumables in China and Southeast Asian countries. The Project is also expected to benefit employees through creating direct and indirect employment opportunities. Market creation outcomes (competitiveness): The Project is expected to contribute to strengthening competitive pressures in the Chinese and Southeast Asian medical devices market, particularly for manufacturers and investors intending to enter the single-use medical consumable space. Additionally, this Project would demonstrate new opportunities for medical devices manufacturers in China, which could facilitate significant movements of other medical devices manufacturers to upgrade their facilities. The Company's overseas expansion will also support the development of local medical device industries to those countries.
additionality: Financing structure: IFC will provide a long-term financing option for the Company to upgrade of its production facilities and overseas expansion. Such long-term financing is not readily available to firms in the health sector, and is a particularly acute constraint for companies with overseas expansion plans, where unfamiliarity means long-term financing is even harder to obtain in destination countries. Resource Mobilization: The proposed IFC financing will include a mobilization component which will broaden Weigao's international financing base. This is considered a critical foundation as the Company looks to significantly scale up its presence in Southeast Asia. Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC will solidify the Company’s expansion strategy in Southeast Asia given IFC's in-depth understanding of the markets and local context. Standard Setting: IFC will strengthen the Company’s capacity to manage E&S matters, bringing the Company’s E&S standards to a level above common market practice in China’s medical devices industry, as well as the Company’s participation in a regional program on promoting workplace gender equality and respectful workplace practices.
Company Name: Shandong Weigao Group Medical Polymer Co., Ltd.

company_name: Otokoc Otomotiv Ticaret ve Sanayi A.S.
project_description: Otokoç Otomotiv Ticaret ve Sanayi A.S.(“Otokoç” or the “Company”), incorporated in Turkiye and the largest car retailer and rental company in Türkiye, is undertaking an investment program. IFC has been invited to provide debt financing to fund Company’s investment plan (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1928, Otokoç is the largest car retailer and rental company in Türkiye engaged in: (i) selling multiple international brands namely Ford, Volvo, Fiat, Alfa Romeo, Jeep, and Maserati; (ii) car rental services under major brands like Budget and Avis (iii) used car sales for sale of second hand cars defleeted from its rental segment and sourced from third parties; and (iv) other revenue streams from: car service, car spare parts sales etc. Otokoc currently operates at 405 points in 9 countries between Eastern Europe and Central Asia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC financing comprises of an unsecured A loan of up to US$150 million for first tranche and up to US$450 million for all tranches in own account financing.
location_description: The proposed financing will support the company’s investment program in Turkey and in the future potentially in Kazakhstan.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are: (i) stakeholder effects via increased access to cost-efficient and sustainable EVs for customers, and (ii) economy-wide effects: job creation and value-addition through knowledge sharing and the establishment of standards for local suppliers, boosting their skills and efficiency and facilitating their growth. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment to promote competitiveness in the Turkish automotive sector by deepening EV penetration thereby exerting competitive pressures on rivals and supporting greater diversity in EV offerings with improved affordability for customers.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality: (i) Financial additionality is provided via scarce long-term financing to the Company that is otherwise not readily available in the local market. The proposed financing is expected to enhance the Company’s cash flows, improve its debt profile, and increase access to complementary capital, thereby reducing vulnerability to domestic financial and banking shocks. (ii) Non-financial additionality is provided via capacity building through standard setting in E&S management.
Company Name: Otokoc Otomotiv Ticaret ve Sanayi A.S.

project_description: Grupo Farinter Internacional S.R.L. (“Farinter” or the “Group”) is a family-owned, private company headquartered in Honduras engaged in the distribution and retail of pharmaceutical and consumer products. Farinter has presence across the region with distribution centers and pharmacy stores in Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador, Costa Rica, and Panama. IFC proposes to provide a long-term loan to finance its strategic plan which includes (i) the acquisition of companies in the pharmaceutical sector in Central America; and (ii) the construction of two new distribution centers in Honduras and Nicaragua. The IFC loan will be disbursed to Farinter’s subsidiaries in Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, and Costa Rica (jointly the “Co-Borrowers”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Co-Borrowers are fully owned by Grupo Farinter International S.R.L. The Farinter group headquarters are in Honduras, and the parent company is majority owned by the Faraj family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment consists of an A Loan on IFC’s own account which will finance the acquisition of companies in the pharmaceutical sector in Central America and the construction of two new distribution centers in Honduras and Nicaragua.
location_description: The Project is located in Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and Panama. Farinter is headquartered in Tegucigalpa, Honduras and has presence in Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador, Costa Rica, and Panama.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is an increase in access to quality and affordable pharmaceutical products in Central American countries through the semi-automation of distribution services and continued production of licensed products. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that this investment will promote competitiveness in these countries’ pharmaceutical distribution markets, by scaling output through an important distributor and introducing more pharmaceutical products in these markets. IFC will monitor the following indicators: (i) total number of members of the board of directors; (ii) number of female members of the board of directors; (iii) total number of senior management positions; (iv) number of females in senior management positions; (v) total direct employment in operations and maintenance; and (vi) female direct employment in operations and maintenance.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC will support the expansion of a vertically integrated pharmaceutical companies in Central America to ensure the sustained availability of quality health products in the region. IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide the Group with long-term debt financing, with terms and conditions not readily available in Honduras. IFC will also help the Group with the certification of the two new distribution centers in Honduras and Nicaragua under EDGE standards and provide corporate governance advisory to improve its control environment.

company_name: CIMSA CIMENTO SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: The proposed IFC’s financing (the IFC Loan) is to be provided to Çimsa Çimento San. ve Tic. A.S. (Cimsa or the Company), a publicly listed cement and building materials manufacturer with global footprint thanks to its operations in Türkiye, Germany, Italy, Spain, USA and Cyprus. The IFC Loan, structured as a Green Loan, will help fund Cimsa’s multi-year investment program aimed at decarbonizing its plants in Türkiye (the Project). The Project is to be completed by 2027 and comprises (a) modernization investments (including reduction in clinker usage by increased use of additives in cement production); (b) energy efficiency investments (incl. system changes for increased use of alternative fuels and waste heat recovery improvements); and (c) ground-mounted solar panel installations for captive use.
sponsor_shareholders: Cimsa is majority owned by Haci Ömer Sabanci Holding A.S. of Türkiye (SAHOL) which holds 54.5% of its share capital, 9.0% of Cimsa is owned by Akcansa Cimento San. ve Tic. A.S., an affiliate company to SAHOL, and the remaining 36.5% is publicly traded on Borsa Istanbul. SAHOL is a leading, diversified Turkish conglomerate involved in financial services, energy, retail, and manufacturing sectors. A number of Sabanci Family members control an aggregate of 47.6% shareholding of SAHOL, with the remaining 52.4% of shares being free float on Board Istanbul.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The IFC Loan will finance Cimsa’s multi-year decarbonization investment program with an estimated cost of US$118 million. In addition to the proposed IFC Loan, which consists of up to US$70 million senior unsecured A loan for IFC’s own account, EBRD’s senior loan of EUR25 million and Cimsa’s internal cash generation will finance the Project.
location_description: Headquartered in Istanbul, Cimsa will carry out the Project in its three integrated plants in Mersin, Eskisehir and Afyon, Türkiye.
development_impact: The Project’s expected development impact will include: (i) contribution to Türkiye’s GDP through capacity expansion and the increased output of higher value-added cement production; (ii) direct and indirect employment creation; (iii) reduction of the greenhouse gas emissions in the cement production of a Company that is the second largest exporter of white cement globally; and (iv) overall enhanced competitiveness in the Turkish cement sector via its adaptation to the requirements of its EU export markets.
additionality: IFC will play a counter-cyclical role by providing long-term financing in a challenging macro environment and help the Company diversify its funding base. In addition to providing a positive signal to the market at a time when risks about Turkish corporates are elevated, IFC is expected to support Cimsa enhance its environmental and social (E&S) standards and improve its resource utilization with a reduced carbon footprint.
Company Name: CIMSA CIMENTO SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: IFC intends to lead AND Global’s Series B equity fundraising with a proposed equity investment of up to US$7 million. AND Global is a Mongolian MSME digital lender and global technology provider. The use of proceeds will be dedicated to sustaining the Company’s growth.
sponsor_shareholders: Launched in 2017, AND Global, through their subsidiary LendMN, operates an unsecured on-balance sheet digital lending business providing loans to informal MSMEs (sole proprietors) in Mongolia. AND Solutions, a subsidiary of AND Global, provides Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions to financial institutions in South-East Asia, including intelligent data processing, customized credit rating, loan management system and innovation platform. Current shareholding includes founders, employees (through ESOP), strategic investors such as Marubeni Corporation and SBI Holdings, and other minority shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is up to US$7 million in equity by IFC as part of a fundraising round to enable the Company to scale its business.
location_description: The Company is registered in Singapore and has operations in Mongolia.
development_impact: The project is expected to increase the access to quality finance for MSMEs by supporting the growth of AND Global's operations and loan book through LendMN. Clients, mostly individuals using loans for productive purposes, start with lower limits and short maturities, but can graduate to larger revolving credit lines after establishing a good track record of timely payments. The investment seeks to increasing the number of clients and loan amounts in a country with limited access to credit for rural and informal microenterprises. Additionally, the project is expected to enhance the competitiveness of the MSME lending market in Mongolia by demonstrating effective lending practices. LendMN’s digitalized credit analysis and tiered loan system enable it to serve smaller and informal MSMEs. Via demonstration effects and by offering its technology to other lenders, it encourages NBFIs to digitize their processes and better serve underserved MSMEs.
additionality: IFC is providing financial additionality through its own account equity investment. IFC further provides non-financial additionality by supporting and guiding AND Global in terms of institutionalizing their corporate governance, policies, and best practices, as well as by bringing its industry partnerships, global networks, and industry expertise to help mitigate regulatory, transactional, and country-specific risks, and to further improve underwriting, collection, among introducing other best practices.

company_name: CORPORACION INMOBILIARIA VESTA, S.A.B. DE C.V.
project_description: Corporación Inmobiliaria Vesta, S.A.B. de C.V. (“Vesta”) is a leading Mexican real estate company specializing in high-quality industrial properties (IPs) and providing common infrastructure and services (energy, water, wastewater, and waste management) to tenants. Vesta negotiated a new senior unsecured credit facility of US$ 545 million, comprising of: (i) a US$345 million in term loans and a (ii) US$200 million revolving loan. IFC contributed with US$100 million to the facility. IFC co-structured and co-led the facility together with certain commercial banks. The financing is structured as a Sustainability-Linked Loan (SSL) with a spread reduction incentive tied to achieving specific certification objectives. The proceeds will partially fund Vesta’s 2025-2026 investment program (“the Project").
sponsor_shareholders: Vesta is a leading real estate Mexican company focused on the development and operation of high-quality industrial properties, including both warehousing and industrial parks serving light manufacturing, logistics, and last mile tenants. Founded in 1998, the Company is deemed one of the main players in the sector. As of September 2024, Vesta owned 221 operational Class A industrial buildings, with a total GLA of 39.1 million sqft. Vesta is recognized for its high-quality operations and strong corporate governance, which has enabled the Company to attract both local and international institutional investors. Vesta is a publicly traded corporation listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV) and in the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) markets with a total of 94.2% of floating shares. The Company went public in 2012, raising US$ 286 million in its initial public offering (IPO) on the BMV, followed by three additional offerings that raised ~US$ 680 million. In 2023, Vesta listed American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) on the NYSE, raising ~US$ 600 million in its first listing and in a subsequent follow-on offering.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total facility size stands at US$545 million. IFC contributed with US$100 million to the facility.
location_description: Vesta is headquartered in Mexico City. The project is located in Mexico.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects on customers through increased access to high-quality industrial assets, and (ii) environmental effects through improved resource efficiency of green buildings. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater sustainability in Mexico’s property sector. As one of the largest industrial asset developers, the potential portfolio-wide greening of Vesta will provide a highly visible demonstration case and spur further competition among other institutional real estate players, which could have a catalytic impact on the industrial real estate market in the country.
additionality: IFC will be providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Through this Project, IFC will provide long-term financing, with a sustainability-linked loan structure, to support the Company’s green expansion, while mobilizing additional third-party funds. Non-financial additionality will be provided via an IFC advisory engagement, specifically through GRIP, which will help the Company develop and implement its decarbonization strategy. IFC will also share knowledge with Vesta to help enhance their Environmental and Social (E&S) policies and procedures in line with IFC Performance Standards (PSs).
Company Name: CORPORACION INMOBILIARIA VESTA, S.A.B. DE C.V.

project_description: The proposed investment is an unfunded risk participation of up to US$40 million equivalent in Ghana Cedis (GHS) in a US$80 million (equivalent in GHS) package of uncommitted unsecured self-liquidating facilities extended by Société Generale Ghana (SG Ghana or the Bank) to selected Ghana cocoa Licensed Buying Companies (LBCs). IFC's investment will support the financing by the Bank of leading LBCs for the procurement of traceable cocoa beans from smallholder farmers.
sponsor_shareholders: Société Generale Ghana is the 12th largest bank in Ghana by total assets (3.4% market share) and 5th largest by total loans (5% market share) (September 2024). The Bank is the 7th largest subsidiary in terms of both deposits and loans out of the 15 Société Générale (SG) African subsidiaries. In Ghana, SG Ghana has a customer base of over 200,000 across 42 branches in all 16 regions, with a historic strong franchise in the corporate segment of the market, however diversifying into SMEs. The Bank is listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE) with market capitalization of US$92 million.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC's investment is an unfunded risk participation of up to US$40 million equivalent in Ghana Cedis (GHS) in a US$80 million (equivalent in GHS) package of uncommitted unsecured self-liquidating facilities extended by Société Generale Ghana (the Bank) to selected Ghana cocoa Licensed Buying Companies. IFC participation is for one-year and can be recommitted up to 3 times.
location_description: Republic of Ghana
development_impact: IFC anticipates that the Project will contribute to enhance the resilience of Ghana's cocoa sector currently affected by limited adequate finance straining the ability of traders to sustain cocoa sourcing from farmers. This in turn could ultimately affect Ghana's ability to maintain its global market position as a major supplier of cocoa. The Project is expected to increase liquidity in the agriculture supply chain and access to finance for farmers by providing SG Ghana with an efficient and competitive risk mitigating tool to accept a higher degree of lending risk. Credit to Ghana's agricultural sector is even lower relative to its contribution to the country's GDP, where many lenders lack the risk tolerance and/or expertise to lend to smallholder farmers.
additionality: IFC's Role and Additionality is expected to be both Financial and Non-Financial. Leveraging IFC's AAA rating, the proposed facility is designed to address the regulatory capital and single obligor exposure limits that are presenting severe constraints to Ghana's Cocoa pre-export financing efforts at present. IFC's involvement in the financing of the cocoa sector catalyzes changes in the regulatory framework as it opens doors to a new financing instrument currently not available in the market, mitigating credit risk and adding value by enhancing financing facilities to the private sector. IFC may also provide advisory support to help de-risk Ghana's cocoa sector by helping reduce key social and environmental risks associated with financing of the sector.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to €2 million to First African Company SA FAC in Cameroon (“FAC” or the “Company”) to finance capex and working capital needs for expansion and operational improvement in yogurt and juice production facility (the “Project”). FAC is a leading dairy and fruit juice company in Cameroon and a market leader in affordable sachet yogurt segment. The Project?may be supported?by Canada – IFC Facility for Resilient Food Systems (“Canada FRFS”), subject to obtaining the necessary internal approvals, as described in the Blended Finance section.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Martin Ngouchet, the founder and CEO, is a seasoned entrepreneur in Cameroon with over 20 years of experience in business management. He owns 97% of FAC. FAC has two related companies: (i) Promodis Afriq SA (food import/distribution), managed and 29% owned by Mr. Martin and (ii) First African Logistics (transport service), managed and 100% owned by Mr. Martin.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is €2.4 million. The proposed investment is a €1 million IFC A Loan and a €1 million concessional loan from Canada FRFS.
location_description: The Company has a manufacturing units located in Douala, Cameroon.
development_impact: (i) Economywide effects: Economy-wide: Competitive local manufacturing of beverage products will support domestic value addition and job creation through up-and downstream linkages in the dairy and fruit juice value chains (The Project will create more full time direct jobs and support indirect jobs in the supply chain). (ii) Stakeholder - Customers: The Project is expected to increase access to affordable, safe, quality (hygienically packed) and protein-rich dairy products which contribute to improving nutrition and health in the country. Consumers will also benefit from increased access to fruit juice. (iii) Contribution to market creation- competitiveness: The Project could serve as a catalyst in showcasing the potential of domestic vertical integration to other investors in the FMCG industry via demonstration effect of business models to increase competitiveness via local processing of beverage products.
additionality: Financial additionality: Financing structure: IFC will provide a long-term loan with a sufficient grace period, which is not readily available to agribusiness in the local market. The loan will be structure to fit the project that needs sufficient time for preparation. Non-financial additionality: Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity building: IFC will provide technical, environmental, and social (E&S), health, and safety expertise to improve overall environmental and safety performance, to align the company’s operation with IFC performance standards and industry best practices. IFC could also provide support in financial management through advisory services.

project_description: The proposed investment is a senior debt facility comprised of a €30 million long-term loan and a €10 million short-term loan to Nuvibev SGPS, S.A. (Nuvibev or the Group) and its key subsidiaries namely Refriango – Indústria e Comércio Geral, Lda. (Refriango), Luanday – Comércio e Serviços, Lda. (Luanday), and Wayfield - Trading Internacional S.A. (Wayfield) (Refriango, Luanday and Wayfield together the Companies). The investment will assist in sustaining employment and consumer goods production and contribute to drinking water security in Angola (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Nuvibev is a subsidiary of Nuvigroup SGPS, S.A, owned by Mr. Luis Vicente and Ms. Clélia Vicente.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Group is Angola's market leader in non-alcoholic ready to drink (NARTD), and the Project supports the Companies' €70 million investment program to achieve NARTD growth.
location_description: Refriango and Luanday are the Group's beverage production arm and distribution arm respectively, and both companies are located in Luanda, Angola. Wayfield is the Group's procurement arm located in Lisbon, Portugal.
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase value addition and lead to job creation in the NARTD market in Angola. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will contribute to increasing competitiveness of the market by introducing improved business practices through demonstration, replication, and competition.
additionality: IFC provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via financing terms not otherwise available to agribusinesses in Angola. Non-financial additionality is provided via technical expertise to improve corporate governance.

project_description: Rima Industrial S.A. (“Rima” or the “Company”) is a leading Brazilian producer of silicon-, ferroalloys- and magnesium-based products. IFC’s proposed financing would support improvements in Rima’s forestry division (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Rima was founded in 1974 by CEO Ricardo Vicintin. The Vicintin family maintains full ownership of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A Loan of up to US$25 million to support (i) replanting of eucalyptus trees on existing plantations, (ii) purchase of forestry equipment, and (iii) other forestry-linked expenditures.
location_description: Investments will be made in Rima’s forestry division in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
development_impact: The Project will support the decarbonization efforts of the Company by financing green initiatives in the metallurgy global market, through improving forest productivity by adopting new eucalyptus clones that are optimal for charcoal production.
additionality: Financial additionality will be provided through IFC's nine-year tenor to reflect the long investment period of the Project, which requires planting eucalyptus trees and only harvesting six years afterwards. Non-financial additionality will be provided through (i) the Company's adoption of good practice E&S standards in line with the IFC performance standards. and (ii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building in IFC's partnership in the Company's innovative studies on charcoal production.

project_description: The Project seeks to provide a combination of investment and investment preparation support to Zagrebacki Holding d.o.o. (“ZGH” or the “Company”) to facilitate holistic transformation of Zagreb’s waste management, road maintenance and construction and green landscaping sectors into modern, efficient and sustainable system that incorporates circular economy principles and advance the development of green cities agenda. The Project strengthens strategic partnership with the Company, building on IFC’s EUR72.5m subscription as an anchor investor into a EUR305m Sustainability Linked Bond issuance in July 2023.
sponsor_shareholders: ZGH is a diversified multi-utility holding company fully owned by the city of Zagreb (the “City”), which provides essential municipal public services, including waste management, roads maintenance and reconstruction, landscaping, water treatment, gas supply and distribution and others.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC plans to provide straight senior loan to ZGH for up to EUR60 million. IFC loan will finance circular and smart waste management infrastructure, including lower emission trucks and auxiliary equipment for separate collection and transportation of segregated municipal, green and construction waste fractions for treatment and recycling, biowaste pre-treatment infrastructure, innovative information and communication (“ICT”) technologies to optimize waste management operations across the whole system, as well as equipment for road maintenance and green landscaping. The holistic solution should reduce landfill disposal as well as contribute to net GHG and methane emission reduction due to lower-emission technologies, less fuel consumption in all three sectors, improved biowaste and material recycling. IFC’s investment is complemented by comprehensive investment preparation engagement which supports ZGH with developing long-term circular waste management and digitalization strategy, designing innovative technical solutions for the Project, facilitating recyclable materials offtake, exploring carbon offsetting opportunities and enhancing operational practices, including applying WBG procurement framework.
location_description: The Project is located in Zagreb, the capital of Croatia.
development_impact: The Project upgrades the quality of waste management, road maintenance and green landscaping services in Zagreb and enables its transition into a holistic, efficient and sustainable system with circular economy principles. The main expected project-level outcomes are stakeholder effects through the improvement in the quality of municipal infrastructure and services and environmental effects through a reduction in GHG emissions. At the sector level, the Project is expected to have replication potential for similar circular waste management initiatives in the region and encourage further investments.
additionality: The Project provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided through supporting the most sizable investment in waste, road maintenance and green landscaping space over the past 10 years in Zagreb and multi-faceted use of proceeds. Non-financial additionality derives from the application of IFC’s knowledge and experience in the waste management sector through investment preparation engagement, helping the Company to improve its capacity and operational standards.

project_description: Founded in 1993 and headquartered in Liaoning, 3SBio Inc. (“3SBio” or the “Company”) is a pioneer in the Chinese biotechnology industry that is primarily involved in the development of biopharmaceutical products to meet significant unmet medical needs in the areas of cancer and its supportive care, nephrology and other diseases or conditions. The proposed investment will support 3SBio to fund: (i) the expansion of its research and manufacturing facilities in Liaoning Province, a frontier province in Northern China, and Guangdong Province; and (ii) Company’s expansion overseas in emerging market (the “Project”). The Project is expected to support the improved access to innovative, yet affordable, biopharmaceutical products in China and other developing nations.
sponsor_shareholders: 3SBio is 21.62% owned by its founder, Chairman and the Sponsor Dr. Jing Lou and his spouse Lily Xing. While another 5.7% is owned by employees, the rest 72.7% is public float.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is estimated to cost US$470 million and will be funded by the IFC loans of up to US$200 million equivalent in RMB with 7-year tenor, and the Company’s internally generated cashflow.
location_description: The Project locations are primarily in Liaoning and Guangdong provinces in China.
development_impact: Project level: enhance access for patients in China and other developing countries to affordable and quality biologic products; direct and indirect job creation, particularly for skilled labor in biopharmaceutical R&D and related fields. Market level: contribute to competitive pressures in the Chinese biopharmaceutical market and demonstrate new opportunities for pharmaceutical companies in the sector. The Company’s overseas expansion will also support the development of local biopharmaceutical industries by providing affordable and quality biologics to those countries.
additionality: IFC's Role and Additionality: (i) long-term financing beyond what is available in the market; (ii) share local knowledge and resources with client to help the Company expand to other emerging markets; and (iii) standard settings and sharing of best practices in Environmental and Social (E&S) aspects.

project_description: The proposed project consists of an equity investment of up to US$ 30 million in Evolution Fund III (EVIII or the Fund), established by the Mauritian private equity firm Inspired Evolution Managers Limited (“the Fund Manager” or “Inspired Evolution”) to invest in renewable energy (solar, hydro, wind and battery energy storage systems) development platforms and towards growth capital in energy resource efficiency companies. The Fund’s strategy is aimed at accelerating the clean energy transition and increasing energy access in Africa through renewable and sustainable energy.
sponsor_shareholders: Inspired Evolution was founded in 2007 through the merger of Capital Evolution created by Christopher Clarke and Inspired Funds created by Wayne Keast. By gradually buying out other initial partners, Christopher Clarke and Wayne Keast became full owners of the equity in 2018 with a 50% equity stake each. In 2024, they offered equity ownership to include Steven Faure, a new partner in the business, who is now a 10% shareholder with Christopher Clarke and Wayne Keast retaining a 45% equity stake each.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund has a total committed capital target cap of US$ 400 million. IFC’s proposed investment is for up to US$ 30 million in EVIII.
location_description: The Fund will make investments predominantly across various countries in sub-Saharan Africa, and potentially select countries in North Africa.
development_impact: The main project-level outcome/development impact is increasing access and reliability of clean electricity supply to households and businesses in Africa. Eighteen of the 20 countries with the largest access deficits in 2022 are in Sub-Saharan Africa. Even when available, grid electricity supply is highly unreliable, leading to frequent load shedding, outages, and reliance on diesel generators. The Fund is expected to support the expansion of utility-scale, grid-connected independent power producer platforms and projects, decentralized commercial and industrial private off-takers, off-grid solutions, and energy-as-a-service microgrid infrastructure-type offerings, clean energy and resource-efficiency technology-based businesses with potential economy-wide effects. In addition, the Fund will invest in large-scale energy-efficient cold chain solutions businesses, which will aid in alleviating food insecurity and waste by allowing the transport of perishable foods around the region as and when needed. Complementarily, the project supports the expansion of clean energy solutions that will reduce GHG emissions by displacing more carbon-intensive energy sources, with an identified pipeline of 3.6 GW of renewable energy investments across Africa.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is expected to be both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists in providing patient equity to help the Fund reach its target final closing size. Such patient capital is not readily available for infrastructure investments amid uncertainty on the global economic outlook and monetary tightening, which are likely to constrain capital flows to emerging markets. Non-financial additionality involves (i) non-commercial risk mitigation by providing comfort to additional investors considering investing in the Fund, (i) Knowledge of the regulatory environments and power sectors in the West Africa region, and (iii) Capacity Building to strengthen the Fund’s capacity to manage associated E&S risks by IFC Performance Standards.

company_name: SHANDONG ZHAOWEI STEEL TOWER CO., LTD.
project_description: The Project entails a proposed IFC A Loan investment of up to USD20 million in Woda Metal Industry Plc. (“Woda”) based in Ethiopia. Woda will be the beneficiary of the IFC funds. The use of proceeds is for permanent working capital requirements to support Woda’s manufacturing expansion of its steel-based power transmission and telecommunication towers and cables in Ethiopia.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is the Chinese-based Shandong Zhaowei Steel Tower Company Ltd. (“Zhaowei”). Zhaowei, founded in 2007, manufactures transmission and telecommunication towers, cables and other steel structures. Zhaowei’s principal shareholders are Mr. Li Jin, founder and Chairman, and Mr. Wang Hongqi. Woda was founded in 2015 and is majority owned by Zhaowei.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at USD20 million. The proposed investment is an A-loan for IFC’s own account of up to USD20 million.
location_description: The Project will be in Woda’ existing plants in the Woda Industrial Park, Sheger-Sub City, Sebeta City, about 21 kilometers west of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
development_impact: The proposed investment aims to support electrification and connectivity efforts in Ethiopia, which are important due to the growing population and infrastructure developments. The primary expected project-level outcomes include economy-wide and environmental effects. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will enhance the resilience of the local steel structure and cables value chain to better support critical infrastructure and the expansion of the telecom and power industries in Ethiopia.
additionality: IFC's expected involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality will be provided through longer tenor financing to support Woda's expansion and permanent working capital needs. Non-financial additionality will be through supporting Woda in adopting best practices in corporate governance and environmental and social procedures.
Company Name: SHANDONG ZHAOWEI STEEL TOWER CO., LTD.

project_description: The proposed project entails IFC’s equity investment of up of ZAR350 million (approximately US$19.4 million equivalent in s a cornerstone investor in an Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Boxer Superstores Pty Limited (“Boxer” or “the “Company”) (“The Project”). Boxer is the leading soft discounter in South Africa, with a focus on serving the low to middle-income populations in underserved rural, urban, and peri-urban areas across the country. It is currently a wholly owned subsidiary of Pick n Pay Stores Limited (Pick n Pay or the Group), which is one of the largest grocery retailers in South Africa. Established in 1977 as a conventional wholesaler trading in essential commodities like maize meal, rice, sugar, oil, and beans, Boxer was acquired by Pick n Pay in 2002 when it had 35 stores. Since then, Boxer has grown significantly, becoming a national-scale retail brand with 477 stores, including 296 supermarkets, as of February 2024. Total equity expected to be raised from the IPO is up to ZAR8.0 billion (approximately US$ 470 million) to support Pick n Pay’s recapitalization and Boxer’s expansion in the medium term. The Project will be a continuation of IFC’s systematic efforts to promote inclusive growth in South Africa and signal confidence in Boxer’s inclusive business model and the South African capital markets. IFC’s cornerstone participation in the IPO is expected to crowd in other investors to further support the Boxer strategy focusing on providing affordable grocery products to the low to middle-income segment in South Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: Boxer is a leading discount retailer in South Africa focused on low- to middle-income groups within underserved rural, peri-urban, and urban areas across the country. Boxer operates in all nine provinces of South Africa, with a particularly strong presence in Kwazulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape. The Company manages 477 stores with over 600,000 square meters of gross lettable area and has six distribution centers. Boxer is currently a wholly owned subsidiary of Pick n Pay Stores Limited (Pick n Pay or the Group). Pick n Pay is listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) with a market capitalization of US$760 million and annual revenues of US$6 billion as of February 29, 2024. The Group operates various store formats, including supermarkets, clothing stores, and an online platform, all under the banners of Pick n Pay and Boxer.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project is an equity investment of up to US$30 million equivalent in ZAR to participate in Boxer IPO as a cornerstone investor. The target amount to be raised by the Boxer IPO is ZAR8.0 billion (US$ 470 million).
location_description: South Africa
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are improved access to affordable and good quality retail products and economy-wide impact based on potential value-added and job creation. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will deepen discount retail penetration and enhance the quality and diversity of affordable products in the catchment areas through the growth of a market leader and increased competition.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project will be both financial and nonfinancial. Financial additionality will be provided through IFC's own account equity; patient capital through the public equity markets, which is otherwise not available, as evidenced by the declining number of listings in the local stock market. Non-financial additionality is provided via (i) boosting investor confidence by IFC investing in an IPO in South Africa at a time when the country is implementing key reforms, (ii) signaling effect from IFC’s role as a cornerstone investor, in the IPO of a Company focused on serving the lower economic population, (iii) strengthening the environmental & safety practices of a company that will be listed publicly and (vi) strengthening and diversifying Boxer’s supply chain through best practices and capacity building through sector knowledge

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a senior, secured loan of up to US$100 million to two companies in the JK Tyre Group comprising an A loan of up to US$30 million to JK Tyre and Industries Limited (“JK Tyre” or the “Company”), and up to US$70 million to Cavendish Industries Limited (“Cavendish”), a majority owned subsidiary of JK Tyre, together referred to as the “Borrowers”. The Borrowers are amongst the top four tyre manufacturers in India and amongst the top 19 tyre manufacturers globally by revenues. Proceeds from the investment will be utilized for brownfield expansion of the Borrowers and to refinance and extend the maturity of existing debt of Cavendish (the “Project”). IFC’s investment is proposed to be classified as a Sustainability Linked Loan (“SLL) which will provide performance related incentives to the Company to achieve corporate wide decarbonization and sustainability targets.
sponsor_shareholders: The Borrowers are amongst the leading tyre manufacturers in India. JK Tyre is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange and has a market capitalization of approximately US$1.2 billion as of November 29, 2024. The Promoter Group holds 50.5 percent of the total share capital of JK Tyre while the balance is held by financial institutions and public. The Promoter Group holds the Company’s share mainly through Bengal and Assam Company Limited, which is a listed non-banking financial company. Dr. Raghupati Singhania is the Chairman and Managing Director, and Mr. Anshuman Singhania is the Managing Director of the Company. Cavendish is a majority owned, unlisted subsidiary of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is ~US$200 million which includes capital expenditure to increase their tyre manufacturing capacity and refinancing of existing debt of the Borrowers. The proposed IFC investment comprises senior, secured A loan of up to US$100 million. Of the total loan proceeds of US$100 million, up to US$30 million will be to JK Tyre to fund its capital expenditure and up to US$70 million will be to Cavendish with US$ 20 million to fund Cavendish’s capital expenditure and up to US$50 million to refinance and extend the maturity of its existing high-cost debt.
location_description: The Company’s corporate office is located at 3, Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, New Delhi, 110002. The capital expenditure to be financed by IFC’s loan will be at JK Tyre’s manufacturing facility at Banmore in the state of Madhya Pradesh and Cavendish’s manufacturing facility at Laksar in the state of Uttarakhand.
development_impact: Based on the widening gap between local demand and local production, the Indian Government, through the Rubber Board of India, has launched an initiative to cater to significant self-sufficiency of the country’s natural rubber requirements. The Government, along with 4 tyre manufacturers including the Company, are working on a pilot project which targets undertaking additional planting rubber across additional 200 thousand hectares in non-traditional areas such as the North-East. The collaboration is expected to (i) foster domestic production of rubber, (ii) create opportunities and improve livelihoods of previously underserved segments of society, (iii) skill and train additional farmers in collaboration with the Rubber Board, (iii) financially support the provision of planting materials, and (iv) strengthen the Indian tyre industry’s resilience against supply chain disruptions and pricing of a key raw material.
additionality: (i) IFC’s long tenor funding will help stabilize the balance sheet of the Borrowers and provide adequate cushion to weather the inherent cyclicality of the industry; (ii) The loan, which is structured as a SLL, will incentivize the Company to develop a sustainable finance framework and achieve the sustainability targets; (iii) IFC will assist JK Tyre to formulate and implement its Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP) to strengthen social/labor management systems and de-risk natural resource supply chains; (iv) Through a decarbonization advisory program, IFC will help evaluate the techno-commercial feasibility of options for reducing the Company’s carbon footprint; and (v) IFC will share technical knowledge and best practices on increasing diversity and inclusion within the Company through the India Gender Collaborative, an IFC-led peer learning initiative for the private sector.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment to ECOM Agroindustrial Corp. Ltd. (ECOM or the Company) of up to US$230 million comprises: (1) a US$200 million 4-year A Loan facility that is renewable annually; and (2) a US$30 million 4-year C Loan that is renewable annually after the first 2 years. Use of proceeds are aimed at funding working capital for ECOM's cocoa business in Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana. At the first renewal of the A Loan facility, IFC will increase its investment by up to US$50 million and will arrange a syndicate for an amount up to US$150 million. ECOM is an existing IFC client. The investment would enable ECOM to strengthen its balance sheet; sustain offtake volumes and finance cocoa farmers; and invest into its sustainable cocoa supply chain.
sponsor_shareholders: ECOM is a leading commodity trader incorporated in Switzerland with operations in 40 countries in Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America and the United States. ECOM operates in sectors that are dominated by smallholder farmers and provides support to its coffee and cocoa suppliers to increase their productivity and access certification programmes. The Group is a significant player in the global coffee, cocoa and cotton trades. ECOM Agroindustrial Corporation Ltd is a family-owned company founded in Barcelona, Spain in 1849.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Up to US$280 million from IFC own account and up to US$150 million through syndication.
location_description: ECOM Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana.
development_impact: The Project is anticipated to positively impact access to cocoa markets by smallholder farmers. The direct offtake opportunities provided to smallholders is expected to increase earnings from cocoa sales by sustaining sustainability programmes and accessing premium markets, and consequently improve livelihood of farm households in Cote d’Ivoire and Ghana who supply cocoa to the Company. The Company provides pre-harvest support to farmer suppliers for fertilizers, pruning, and farm upkeep. At the Market level, the Project is anticipated to improve competitiveness through ECOM's sustainable cocoa supply chain practices. This will catalyze adoption of similar practices by competitors and therefore aligning operations with industry best practices.
additionality: IFC working capital financing will increase the resilience of the Company during cocoa commodity price spikes. Through this investment, IFC will have the opportunity to bring its industry and E&S expertise to validate ECOM's performance, providing advisory services where required.

project_description: Sunshine Healthcare Lanka Limited (“SHL” or “the Company”) is an integrated pharmaceutical player with operations across the value chain including (i) Pharma and Medical Devices import and distribution; (ii) Pharma Manufacturing; (iii) Pharma Retail (Pharmacies); and (iv) Distribution. The proposed IFC investment is an equity investment of up to LKR 3,270 million in SHL to support the Company in its growth plan to increase its pharma manufacturing capacity, augment its medical devices import segment, and expand its pharma retail footprint over the next three years (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: SHL is a subsidiary of Sunshine Holdings PLC (“SUN”), a diverse conglomerate with interests in healthcare, consumer goods and agribusiness. SUN is an existing IFC client: IFC made a US$ 5mn investment in its consumer segment in 2021. SUN’s majority shareholder is G. Sathasivam and his family
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed transaction comprises an equity investment which will support the Company in its growth plan to increase its pharma manufacturing capacity, augment its medical devices import segment, and expand its pharma retail footprint. The Company plans to incur a total capex of US$10 million for its growth plans which is expected to be funded through the proposed IFC equity investment.
location_description: Sri Lanka
development_impact: The Project is expected to lead to an increase in access to health products in Sri Lanka through increased local production of respiratory health products, placement of diagnostic analyzer in hospitals for early detection and prevention of disease, automation of central logistics infrastructure, and expansion of retail footprint. IFC anticipates that financing the only pharmaceutical producer of metered dose inhalers (“MDI”) in Sri Lanka will support greater market resilience as spillover effects accrue to the pharmaceutical supply chain and potential local pharmaceutical manufacturers in this market, facilitating import substitution in the largely import-dependent market. The Project is also expected to contribute to the resilience of the pharmaceutical manufacturing market in Sri Lanka. The Project will promote greater stability of the MDI supply chains in Sri Lanka by improving the operational efficiency of the only local producer of MDI, reducing the reliance of the public sector on importation.
additionality: IFC’s additionality stems mainly from its countercyclical role during crises which in this instance comprises IFC’s long-standing experience with rapid crisis response efforts, its ability to support real sector clients to address liquidity constraints, its ability to help clients re-direct supply chains and its support to continued employment in countries of operations.

project_description: This project is proposed under IFC’s Global Trade Supplier Finance program (“GTSF” or the “Program”) approved by the IFC Board on September 21, 2010 (Original Project #28723) and an additional increase approved on December 15, 2022. Under GTSF, IFC provides short-term financing to suppliers, (“Suppliers”), in emerging markets selling to large companies, (“Buyers”), on open account terms. Under this project, IFC would purchase, at a discount, US$ denominated Principal Approved Payables/invoices owed by Nestrade S.A. (“Nestrade” or “the Company) to its suppliers in several emerging markets via CRX Markets AG (“CRX”), a leading global supply chain finance platform (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Nestrade, a subsidiary of Nestlé S.A, provides procurement services on behalf of its affiliates worldwide
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is US$100 million, senior, unsecured, funded, uncommitted, revolving, short-term, GTSF facility that will provide early payment to Nestrade’s coffee suppliers in emerging markets such as Brazil, Colombia, Kenya, and Ethiopia.
location_description: GTSF-approved jurisdictions, including Brazil, Colombia, Kenya, Ethiopia, and other emerging market countries.
development_impact: N/A
additionality: Financial Additionality: Access to sustainable finance for suppliers located in emerging markets, some of whom otherwise would not be able to obtain affordable financing. The proposed facility will be priced based on the credit rating of Nestrade, making it more affordable for suppliers who may also be facing credit limit issues from their banks which in turn hinders their growth. IFC’s financing is in addition to what suppliers can access currently from their existing banking relationships and as it is off-balance sheet and as such does not add to their debt load. Non-financial Additionality: IFC participation will reinforce Nestlé’s commitment to increase procurement of coffee from suppliers that comply with Nestlé’s Responsible Sourcing criteria. IFC will also provide input and guidance to Nestlé on further strengthening Nestlé's Responsible Sourcing Standard. This will help inform and influence the broader universe of Nestlé suppliers as well as suppliers of other global food and beverage companies, supporting replication and scale up beyond the individual participating suppliers.

project_description: Anhui Huaheng Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (AHB or the Company) is a leading manufacturer of amino acids and other bio-based products in the People’s Republic of China (PRC). IFC is proposing to provide up to RMB 500 million (equivalent to US$70.5 million) in the form of a Green Loan (the Loan) to Qinhuangdao Huaheng Bioengineering Co., Ltd. (QHB), a wholly-owned subsidiary of AHB. The IFC proceeds will be used to fund the capex and working capital needs of malic acid and L-Tryptophan production (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Ms. GUO Henghua is the Founder and Chairwoman of AHB, holding a stake of 27.15%. The remaining shares are held by individuals, institutional investors and other investors from public market, with each representing less than 5% of the shareholding of AHB.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project is estimated to cost approximately US$105 million, among which IFC will finance up to RMB 500 million (equivalent to US$70.5 million) and the remaining will be covered by the Company’s internal cash.
location_description: Qinghuangdao, Hebei Province, PRC
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are: (i) environmental effects through greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction through lower-emission manufacturing processes; and (ii) economywide effects through value addition, exports and job creations. Furthermore, the Project is expected to contribute to market creation through promoting product complexity and the shift towards more sophisticated manufacturing capabilities in China, with potential to replicate in other emerging markets.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality consists of providing long-term green finance to support the Company’s expansion into new amino acid and organic acid types, which will provide more climate-friendly and cost-effective solutions to producing nutritional ingredients. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will provide knowledge and guidance to the Company to strengthen its sustainability performance, facilitate its future aspirations in bringing affordable nutrition to a broader emerging market, and help the Company improve its E&S standards.

project_description: IFC is seeking to invest in a privately placed unsecured bond (the “Bond”) of up to US$90 million to be issued by Municipality of Ulaanbaatar (“MUB”), the subnational entity of the capital city of Mongolia. The investment entails (i) an own account IFC investment of up to US$65 million and (ii) an investment by IFC-Canada Blended Climate Finance Program (“BCFP”) of up to US$25 million. The proceeds of the financing will be used for the procurement by the MUB of the supply and construction for the 50MW/200MWh Battery Energy Storage System (“BESS”) project. The BESS is designed to store electricity during off-peak times and supply it during peak times (the “Project”), reducing recurrent blackouts during peak demand in the winters and provide grid stabilization.
sponsor_shareholders: Ulaanbaatar, the capital city of Mongolia, is the country’s primary economic hub with over 40% of the population, 63% of registered businesses and generating over 65% of the national GDP. MUB is the largest subnational entity in Mongolia and has a wide mandate of infrastructure service provision to its citizens. The project will be owned by a special purpose vehicle which will be fully owned by MUB or a 100% MUB-owned subsidiary.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, together with BCFP will invest up to US$90 million in the Bond issued by MUB.
location_description: The project is located in the outskirts of Ulaanbaatar at Baganuur district.
development_impact: The main Project outcomes are increasing the supply of reliable electricity in the Ulaanbaatar municipality and reducing electricity shortages which result in frequent blackouts. Beyond these effects, the investment can contribute to the resilience of the power sector by integrating energy storage solutions designed to smooth power production and mitigate interruptions during peak demand, as well as reduce the country’s need for expensive electricity imports. In the future, the expansion of BESS capacity in the MUB’s central grid will prevent curtailment of renewable energy (RE) projects and facilitate the integration of RE capacity into Mongolia’s power mix.
additionality: IFC has both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC’s financial additionality stems from its role as the first international development institution to invest in the domestic bond issued by Municipality of Ulaanbaatar (MUB) without a sovereign guarantee. Non-financial additionality is driven by Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building and Standard Setting through executing this first of a kind transaction as well as engagement with Advisory Services pertaining to MUB’s debt management practices and credit rating, as well as the delivery of Environmental and Social (E&S) academy training to ensure standard setting .

project_description: The proposed investment is an IFC financing package of up to US$80 million to LLC Astarta Agro Protein, a subsidiary of Astarta Holding PL? (together, “Astarta” or the “Company”), to help finance the construction of a soy protein concentrate (SPC) production plant in central Ukraine (the “Project”). The Project is expected to be supported by Blended Finance, as described in the Blended Finance Section. Astarta is one of the leading integrated agricultural producers and processors in Ukraine, which operates crop growing, soybean processing, sugar production, cattle farming and milk production, and biogas production.
sponsor_shareholders: Astarta Holding PLC is listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, with major shareholders including the Ivanchyk family (41.47%) and Fairfax Financial Holdings (29.91%), while the remaining shares are distributed among other shareholders and are subject to trading at the Warsaw Stock Exchange, with no single shareholder holding 10% or more (as of November 12, 2024).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering providing to the Company a corporate long-term financing package that will comprise of: (i) a senior A Loan (“A Loan”) of up to US$50.7 million for IFC’s own account, (ii) a senior unsecured loan of up to US$24.4 million from IFC, acting in its capacity as an implementing entity of the Economic Resilience Program for Ukraine (“ERA”), supported by the Netherlands (the “ERA NL Loan”), and (iii) a B Loan (“B Loan”) of up to US$40 million for the account of participants, provided that the combined amount of the A Loan, ERA NL loan, and B loan would not exceed US$80 million. IFC’s A Loan would be supported by a first-loss guarantee (“FLG”) of up to US$25.4 million from the from the European Commission’s Ukraine Investment Framework (“EC-UIF”) and IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity of ERA NL and/or the ERA Program for Ukraine – supported by France (“ERA France”) as further described in the Blended Finance Section.
location_description: Ukraine
development_impact: The Project is expected to generate employment and value-added to the economy, support jobs and the livelihoods of farmers in Ukraine, and have climate mitigation effects through renewable energy generation and adoption. Beyond the Project, IFC investment is expected to contribute to promoting competitiveness of Ukraine’s soybean sector and broader agribusiness sector by pioneering a higher value-added soybean product and helping to catalyze the transition of Ukraine’s agribusiness sector from a commodity-driven sector to a value-added one.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the project will be both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists of the financing structure and resource mobilization. IFC is contemplating a loan with a long tenor, tailored to support project viability in a high-uncertainty context, with de-risking through blended finance. Leveraging its knowledge of the company and the sector, IFC is expected to mobilize additional funds to support the project. Non-financial additionality consists of non-commercial risk mitigation as well as knowledge, innovation, and capacity building. Through upstream engagement, IFC assisted the Company in obtaining a market study for SPC, preparing the project’s business plan, and assessing its commercial attractiveness. Additionally, IFC’s support for Ukraine’s agricultural production will send a strong positive signal to other investors, providing reassurance in a challenging FCS market.

company_name: Joincare Pharmaceutical Group Industry Co., Ltd.
project_description: Founded in 1992 and headquartered in Shenzhen, Joincare Pharmaceutical Group Industry Co., Ltd. (“Joincare”, “Company”) is a diversified pharmaceutical manufacturer of chemical drugs, active pharmaceutical ingredient and intermediates, biological drugs and diagnostic reagents and equipment. The proposed investment will support Joincare to fund: (i) the expansion for development and production capacity of APIs and finished formulations in Henan and Guangdong provinces, China; and (ii) investment, including working capital needs, related to key therapeutic areas (together, the “Project”). The additional production capacity created by the Project will enable the Company, given its vertical integration and scale, to produce APIs and intermediates at lower cost and improve the affordability and availability of pharmaceutical products in China and in emerging markets.
sponsor_shareholders: The controlling shareholder of Joincare is Mr. Baoguo ZHU and his spouse, Ms. Guangxia LIU. Mr. Zhu founded the Company in 1992 and owns 45.5% of the Company together with Ms. Liu. The remainder 54.5% are held by public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is estimated to cost US$275 million and will be funded by the IFC loan of up to US$100 million equivalent, and the Company’s internally generated cashflow.
location_description: The Project locations are in China.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good, based on an AIMM score of 53. Project level: improve the accessibility to a wide range of affordable and quality pharmaceutical products in China and developing countries; direct and indirect job creation, particularly for skilled labor in pharmaceutical R&D and related fields. Market level: contribute to competitive pressures in the Chinese pharmaceutical market and demonstrate new opportunities for pharmaceutical companies in the sector.
additionality: IFC’s Role and Additionality: (i) long-term financing beyond what is available in the market; (ii) share local knowledge and resources with client with the potential of an Upstream engagement to help the Company expand to other emerging markets; and (iii) standard settings and sharing of best practices in Environmental and Social (E&S) aspects.
Company Name: Joincare Pharmaceutical Group Industry Co., Ltd.

company_name: THANH THANH CONG BIEN HOA JOINT STOCK COMPANY
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a senior loan of up to US$50 million to Bien Hoa Consumer Joint Stock Company (“BHC”). BHC is a subsidiary of Thanh Thanh Cong - Bien Hoa Joint Stock Company (“TTC AgriS”). The proceeds from the IFC loan will be used to (i) relocate BHC’s legacy refinery in Bien Hoa province, Viet Nam and build a state-of-the-art modern sugar refinery and logistics hub in Tay Ninh province, incorporating a new warehouse for raw and refined sugar; and (ii) fund BHC’s procurement of imported raw sugar (collectively, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam, TTC AgriS is the largest producer of sugar and its by-products in Vietnam. Its main products include refined sugar, raw sugar, functional sugar, liquid sugar, organic sugar, and rock sugar. TTC AgriS is a public company listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange. Its major shareholders include Thanh Thanh Cong Investment Joint Stock Company, Legendary Venture Fund 1, Mrs. Huynh Bich Ngoc, and Mrs. Dang Huynh Uc My.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be in excess of US$50 million, and IFC is considering the provision of an A Loan of up to US$50 million to support the Project.
location_description: The Project is located in Tay Ninh Province, Viet Nam.
development_impact: Environmental Effects: The Project is expected to generate positive environmental effects by reducing greenhouse gas emissions through relocating a legacy sugar refinery to a state-of-the-art modern refinery and replacing coal-fired boilers with biomass boilers. TTC AgriS has a stretch target to reach net zero by 2035 across its whole operation, well ahead of the Vietnamese national commitment of 2050. To achieve the net zero goal, the Company is planning to reduce emissions at its sugar refineries by using 100% biomass as feedstock for boilers. Economy-wide Effects: The Project is expected to generate new jobs and value added to the Vietnamese economy. Contribution to Market Creation - Competitiveness or Sustainability: The proposed investment will improve processing efficiency and increase productivity via enabling economies of scale. This would consequently support the competitiveness of the Vietnamese sugar industry as well as contribute to further growth in exports. The Project may also contribute to promoting the sustainability of Viet Nam’s sugar sector by demonstrating the economic/environmental feasibility of biomass feedstocks.
additionality: IFC will provide long-term financing, which would not be readily available in the market. In addition, IFC is assisting BHC to bring its operations in line with IFC’s Performance Standards and international standards by benchmarking the operations against IFC requirements and recognized quality certification schemes.
Company Name: THANH THANH CONG BIEN HOA JOINT STOCK COMPANY

project_description: IFC is proposing to provide a senior A-loan of up to US$20mn (the “IFC Loan”) to fund Novatex’s working capital requirements for import of raw materials, machinery, and related services to support the Company’s existing operations (the Project). IFC will also play a catalyst role and mobilize parallel loans of up to US$40mn in LCY (the “Parallel Loan”)
sponsor_shareholders: Established since 1948, G&T Group, the majority shareholder in Novatex, is one of the largest export houses in Pakistan engaged in manufacturing of textiles, plastics, and downstream chemicals for over 70 years.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The IFC investment consists of an up to US$20 million equivalent A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Novatex is headquartered in Karachi, Pakistan, with manufacturing facilities located at Karachi, Faisalabad and Sheikhupura
development_impact: The Project is expected to help sustain Company's on-going operations allowing it to continue to support economic activity, preserve jobs and build capacity in its supply chain (local sugarcane farmers, MSME retailers, and distributors etc) to withstand shocks and stresses arising from COVID-19's disruption of supply chains and rising inflation.
additionality: IFC will play an important counter-cyclical role by offering US$ financing to the Company which is not available in the local market is providing much need liquidity to fund its working capital requirements. IFC will further support Novatex to align its operations with IFC Performance Standards and industry best practices on E&S aspects.

project_description: The proposed investment is a debt facility to Sococim Industries (‘Sococim’, ‘Company’ or the ‘Borrower’), the largest integrated cement manufacturer in Senegal to fund working capital and additional capital expenditures related to kiln modernization at its existing facility near Dakar, Senegal. Sococim is a subsidiary of Vicat S.A, (‘Vicat’, ‘Sponsor’, or the ‘Guarantor’), an existing and strategic client for IFC, and one of the top global cement makers. IFC’s facility will enable Sococim to replace and modernize part of its existing capacity with a modern fuel-efficient kiln (the ‘Project’) with Best Available Technology. Further, the Project will enable the Company to replace all of its clinker imports.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is Vicat Group (EPA: VCT), an integrated global cement manufacturer that is listed on Euronext Paris with market cap of €1.6 billion. As of FY2023, it operates in 12 countries and employs ~10,000 people, with 66% of revenues (of €3.9 billion) realized in Europe and the Americas (France, US, Italy, Switzerland, and Brazil) and 34% in emerging markets (Kazakhstan, Egypt, Senegal, Mali, Mauritania, India, Turkey).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project Cost related to the kiln modernization is expected to be up to €291 million. IFC’s financing is of up to €75m in IFC A-loan.
location_description: Sococim is located in Rufisque on the outskirts of Dakar.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are climate change mitigation and economy-wide effects. IFC expects the Project to contribute to the improved sustainability of cement production in West Africa through the dissemination of production processes compliant with the most demanding international sustainability standards and through the increased availability of less polluting alternative fuels.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via financing structure (long-term financing that is not otherwise available). Non-financial additionality is provided via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building as IFC will support the Company's E&S endeavors including its carbon strategy.

project_description: Azalai Group (Azalai or the Group) is a regional player in the hospitality sector which owns and operates 9 upscale and mid-scale business hotels in in West Africa. To fill the gap in the provision of region wide upscale branded hotels that meet international standards, Azalai aims to expand in capacity and geographically through: (i) the renovation and expansion of Azalai Hotel Independance (AHI) in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso and (ii) the refinancing of a portion of the recently completed Azalai Hotel Dakar (AHD), in Dakar, Senegal (iii) the renovation of the Azalai Grand Hotel in Bamako, Mali (the Project). The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA PSW Blended Finance Facility (BFF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Azalai Hotel SA, the Mali-based holding company (the Holding) of the Azalai Group is a private owned company whose majority shareholder is Mr. Mossadeck Bally, a Malian entrepreneur. Other shareholders include: (i) PE funds, (iii) private investors; and (iv) Azalai staff. AHD and AHI and SGH, under which GHB is held, are three subsidiaries of the Holding.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost for the three hotels is estimated at €82.7million. The total proposed IFC investment is a €10million Corporate C loan in the Holding that is comprised of €5 million from IFC own account and €5 million from IDA PSW BFF. The remaining balance will be provided by the shareholders and other lenders to AHD, AHI and GHB
location_description: AHD is located on the Corniche Ouest in Dakar, Senegal, while AHI is in the business center of Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, and GHB is in the center of the District of Bamako, Mali.
development_impact: IFC expects that this project will deliver economy-wide effects through job creation and value-addition and supplier effects by increasing access to markets for SMEs in the target countries. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will improve the competitiveness of the tourism sector in the Sahel region by improving the quality of hotel services in the target countries
additionality: IFC's participation will provide financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide a long-term loan (5-year tenor) which is not readily available for the company in the local markets of the target countries. The proposed financing structure will therefore better match the cash flow of the underlying businesses, improve the company’s debt profile, and enhance its access to complementary capital amid a challenging macroeconomic environment. Additionally, IFC will help the company improve its standards in the area of corporate governance.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is in the form of a financing package of up to US$30 million to Kazyon Retail Sarlau (Kazyon Morocco), with Tawfeer for Food Products (Kazyon Egypt) being a Co-Borrower, to support Kazyon Morocco’s expansion plan which includes the roll out of new stores and Distribution Centers in Morocco (the Project) .Kazyon Morrocco started operations in 2023 and currently operates one DC and 102 stores as of end of August 2024. Kazyon Morocco is a wholly owned subsidiary of Kazyon Limited UK (Kazyon), which is also the 100% owner of Kazyon Egypt, the largest grocery retailer in Egypt with more than 7,000 employees, five DCs and 935 stores as of end of August 2024.
sponsor_shareholders: The company was founded in 2014 by Mr. Hassan Heikal. Kazyon’s shareholders include: (i) ADP III, a fund managed by Development Partners International (35.5%), (ii) Challender Universal Limited (20.6%) and Supreme Universal Holdings (9.1%), both owned by members of Qatar Royal Family and (iii) HE Partners Limited, owned by Mr. Hassan Heikal (7.9%), (iv) Red Hawk Long Term Investments Limited, owned by EFG Hermes and a charitable foundation in the United Kingdom (8.3%), with the remaining 18.6% ownership held by several institutional and individual investors.
