total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing an 8-year financing package in the form of an A Loan of up to US$30 million to support Kazyon Morocco’s investment program over the next three to five years.
location_description: Kazyon Morocco is headquartered in Casablanca. The company’s DC is located in Mohammedia city between Casablanca and Rabat in the region of Casablanca-Settat, with its stores network spanning across Casablanca and Rabat. Kazyon Morocco plans to expand into new cities like Tangier and Marrakesh.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are improved access to affordable quality retail services and economy-wide impact based on potential value-added and job creation. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will deepen modern retail penetration and improve the quality of retail services in the catchment areas via increased competition and demonstration channels.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality consists of providing innovative financing structure to support Kazyon’s growth and meet its funding needs. On the non-financial additionality side, IFC will focus on capacity building and standard setting.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a financing package equivalent to US$4.5 million to be provided in local currency (HTG) to Caribbean Bottling Company S.A. (“CBC” or the “Company”), a bottling company headquartered in Croix Des Bouquets, Haiti. CBC is one of the leading manufacturers and distributors of: (i) water and related products; (ii) juice beverages under the brand “Frooty”; (iii) iced tea under the brand “Brizz”; and (iv) isotonic drinks under the brand “Active”. The Company employs over 500 people and commercializes its products through a well-established distribution network. The project consists of the acquisition of solar panels, a battery system, and a backup diesel generator to reduce energy costs and the carbon footprint of the Company (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Barrau family, Jacques Villejoint and Jean Phillippe Dufort own an aggregate shareholding interest of 69% in the Company, with the balance being owned by minority shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at approximately US$4.5 million equivalents in HTG, for which IFC is proposing to participate with an A Loan of up to US$4.5 million from IFC’s own account.
location_description: The investments will be made in CBC’s plant in Croix Des Bouquets (Ouest Department, Haiti).
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate positive environmental effects through supporting the Company’s energy transition to solar power systems. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing will contribute to promoting resilience in Haiti’s food processing sector by demonstrating the feasibility of adopting renewable energy solutions.
additionality: IFC’s long term investment will enable the Company to properly execute its energy transition plan. IFC’s additionality in this Project comes in the following forms: long-term financing structure, providing technical and market knowledge and expertise related to energy transition, and supporting the Company on good international industry practices in line with IFC Performance Standards through implementation of the Environment and Social Action Plan (ESAP).

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: IFC is considering an equity investment in Rondo Energy, Inc. (“Rondo” or the “Company”). The company enables industrial decarbonization via its proprietary thermal battery systems that are designed for seamless integration with existing industrial equipment and processes. By utilizing a low-cost storage medium that can be rapidly charged, Rondo can harness low-cost renewable electricity and deliver clean industrial heat for a variety of sectors and industries.
sponsor_shareholders: Rondo’s shareholders include established climate tech investment funds like Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Energy Impact Partners as well as Aramco Ventures, Microsoft, Rio Tinto, H&M, the Siam Cement Group, and others.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC to invest up to US$15m in equity.
location_description: Rondo is headquartered in Alameda, California, United States, and serves industrial clients in many regions and industries. The proposed investment by IFC will be used for business expansion to additional markets.
development_impact: Rondo's thermal batteries enable the decarbonization of industrial heat, one of the largest sources of CO2 emissions globally. The Company's technology allows the use of variable, carbon-free electricity instead of fossil fuels to deliver superheated air or steam or to produce electricity via a turbine.
additionality: IFC will support Rondo's scale-up strategy by facilitating and potentially financing partnerships with IFC's network of manufacturing and industrial clients in Emerging Markets. IFC already helps manufacturers implement and finance strategies aimed at decarbonizing their operations, with an emphasis on initiatives that promote the use of renewable and alternative energy through the use of emerging technologies.

company_name: AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn. Bhd.
project_description: The proposed investment is a sustainability linked loan (SLL) of up to US$400 million (or equivalent in Euros), including up to US$250 million (or equivalent in Euros) for IFC’s own account and up to US$150 million (or equivalent in Euros) in potential mobilization, to AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn. Bhd. (“AT&S Malaysia” or the “Company”). AT&S Malaysia is a wholly owned subsidiary of AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik Aktiengesellschaft (“AT&S Austria”). AT&S Austria is a leading global manufacturer of high-end printed circuit boards (PCBs) and integrated circuit (IC) substrates. AT&S Malaysia was incorporated in June 2021 to house greenfield integrated circuit (IC) substrate manufacturing plant in Kulim, Malaysia for some of the key customers. IFC’s financing will be utilised to fund the capital expenditure and associated start-up costs / effects (i.e. the expenses until the commencement of mass production) for the first phase of this plant (the “Project”). AT&S Austria has a focus on sustainability and targets to reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 38% by 2030/31 (compared to a baseline of 2021/22). The Project is aligned with the goals of the Paris Agreement.
sponsor_shareholders: AT&S Malaysia is a 100% owned subsidiary of AT&S Austria. AT&S Austria was founded in 1987 and is currently listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange with a market cap of US$905 million (as of October 10, 2024). Mr. Hannes Androsch and Mr. Willi Dorflinger, along with the related entities own 35.68% of the shares in AT&S Austria while the remaining 64.32% (as of March 31, 2024) of the shares are owned by public shareholders on a free float basis.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the Project is estimated at approximately US$ 1 billion which will be financed by (i) up to US$250 million (or equivalent in Euros) A Loan for IFC’s own account; (ii) up to US$150 million (or equivalent in Euros) in potential mobilization through B1 Loan and/or Parallel Loans to be provided by other lenders; and (iii) equity and customer advances for the remaining balance.
location_description: The Project location will be Kulim, Kedah, Malaysia
development_impact: (A) Project Level: The most significant expected Project level outcomes are employment generation and increase in value addition. The Project will install IC substrate manufacturing with much higher value addition than the existing semiconductor operations in Malaysia, such as PCB and low-end substrates. The semiconductor sector creates high-value jobs and high multiplier effects. (B) Market Creation: Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote competitiveness by contributing to building a more advanced semiconductor ecosystem in Malaysia. IFC anticipates that the Project will promote integration effects in the semiconductor sector in Malaysia, providing demonstration effects to other market players.
additionality: (A) Financial Additionality: IFC’s financial additionality stems from offering a long-term loan (tenor of 7 years with a grace period of 2 years) which aligns with the intrinsic investment and return profile for the Project. Furthermore, IFC’s loan is a SLL which will incentivize the Company to fulfill its sustainability targets. (B) Non-Financial Additionality: IFC will provide guidance on international best practices and support the implementation of the E&S Action Plan (ESAP). These practices are designed to improve the Company’s ability to manage E&S risks and strengthen the capacity of the local supply chain.
Company Name: AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn. Bhd.

project_description: The Project entails a proposed IFC A Loan investment of up to USD20 million in Abyssinia Group of Industries (“Abyssinia” or the “Group”), a leading steel producer in Ethiopia, Kenya, and Uganda, which will support the capacity expansion, backward integration, decarbonization efforts, and working capital needs of Abyssinia. It also entails IFC mobilizing local currency parallel loans to strengthen the Group’s financial position with longer tenors (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Mr. Jateen Patel, a Kenyan businessman. Mr. Patel and his family hold a majority stake in the Group. The Group started its operations in Ethiopia in 2003 and has since expanded its footprint to Kenya and Uganda. The Project will be implemented by Abyssinia Iron & Steel Ltd in Kenya and by Abyssinia Cold Rolling Mills PLC in Ethiopia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at USD70 million. The proposed investment is an A-loan for IFC’s own account of up to USD20 million.
location_description: The Project will be located in the Group’s existing plants in Mariakani, Kenya and in Bishoflu, Ethiopia
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are economy-wide and environmental effects. Beyond the Project, IFC expects its investment to improve the resilience of the steel value chain in the target industries by strengthening backward and regional integration and implementing renewable energy for energy security.
additionality: IFC's involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality will be provided through longer tenor and mobilizing local capital. Non financial additionality will be through supporting the Group in developing a green financing framework in addition to technical advice on implementing the greening of its operations.

project_description: The proposed investment is for up to US$40 million (“IFC A Loan”) to Samuda Food Products Limited (“SFPL” or the “Company”) in Bangladesh. The IFC loan will support setting up a greenfield soybean seed crushing plant with a capacity of producing 540 metric tons per day (MTPD) crude degummed soybean oil and 2,370 MTPD of soybean meal (the “Project”). The Project will improve food safety by boosting the domestic processing of soybeans, supplying crude edible oil for cooking and other edible purposes, and providing soybean meal to local feed producers to support local production of animal protein.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsors include Mr. Mohammad Mustafa Haider, Ms. Farzana Afroze, and Ms. Rizwana Afroze (collectively referred to as the “Sponsors”).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$83.2 million and is proposed to be financed with long-term debt totalling US$58.3 million and the balance of US$24.9 million will be financed through equity. IFC will provide a senior-secured A Loan of up to US$40 million.
location_description: The Project is located in Mirsarai Economic Zone, approximately 70 km north of Chittagong port, Bangladesh.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to (i) contribute to improved food security for consumers through increasing the availability of edible oils and soybean meal to support poultry production in Bangladesh; and (ii) generate economy-wide effects through employment creation and stimulate forward linkages with related sectors. Beyond the Project outcomes, IFC anticipates that the Project will help to reduce food supply volatility in Bangladesh through competitive local production, thereby improving resilience.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is expected to come from both financial and non-financial sources of additionality. Financial additionality stems from IFC providing long-term financing and grace period that is not readily available in the local market. Non-financial additionality comes from standard setting relating to E&S standards, and knowledge, innovation, and capacity building to reduce wastages during production.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A / B loan financing package to Aperam S.A. (“Aperam”). Aperam is a global player in manufacturing and recycling stainless, electrical, and specialty steel which operates key industrial plants in France, Belgium and Brazil, with customers worldwide.
sponsor_shareholders: Aperam is listed on Euronext Amsterdam and the Luxembourg Stock Exchange. Aperam was created in 2011 by the spinoff of the stainless steel assets of ArcelorMittal, a leading steel and mining company. The Mittal family owns 40.33% of Aperam, with the remainder owned by the public and no individual shareholder owning more than 5%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an A/B loan to Aperam of up to €250 million to support an investment program for Aperam Bioenergia. The program involves the expansion of the production of charcoal, wood, seedlings and seeds from Aperam’s eucalyptus forests in Minas Gerais, Brazil.
location_description: Aperam Bioenergia, Minas Gerais, Brazil
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to have climate mitigation effects through reducing the carbon footprint of steel manufacturing by expanding sustainable forest management and improving charcoal production efficiency and waste utilization. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that IFC financing will contribute to promoting environmental sustainability by showcasing efficiency improvement for charcoal production and pioneering commercial scale production of bio-oil from charcoal production waste.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality through: (i) long term financing; (ii) innovative financing structure; iii) mobilization; (iv) standard setting on E&S policy and practices; and (v) knowledge, innovation and capacity building.

project_description: The proposed investment is senior secured loan of up to US$4.22 million in Meticais equivalent for Higest Moçambique, Lda (“Higest” or the “Company”), a leading integrated poultry company in Mozambique. The funding is to support the second phase of Higest’s expansion program (the “Project”), consisting of (i) a 40% increase in its hatchery’s capacity, and (ii) upgrading its out-growers’ operations. Founded in 1993, Higest is a family-owned business producing and selling Day-Old-Chicks (DOC), poultry feed and frozen chicken meat, with the following yearly nameplate capacity: 126,720 MT for feed, 18 million units for DOC and 8,538 MT for frozen/processed chicken. The project is expected to be supported by IDA PSW LCF, as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Higest is 95% owned by Manuel Teixeira de Almeida, wife and his sons. Mr. de Almeida is a Portuguese entrepreneur with an economics background with more than 40 years of experience in the poultry sector.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$27 million, of which 16% will be funded with IFC’s A Loan, and 84% is funded by local banks and internally generated cash under the first phase of the Project. The IFC proposed investment consists of a secured loan of up to US$4.22 million and will be denominated in MZN with support from the IDA PSW LCF.
location_description: The project is in Machava, Maputo Province in Mozambique.
development_impact: The Project will support a leading poultry producer to expand operations while improving production and processing efficiencies all the while maintaining requisite food safety standards. Competitive pressures on other sector players will lead to the adoption of these measures, gradually reducing the informal share of production, to push the market toward formalization. These efficiency improvements are showcased through environmentally controlled sheds, own grain handling and storage to manage costs and streamline grain procurement and storage, automated bulk feed dispatch system, and breeder farm improvements to match the increasing demand for broiler hatching eggs currently sourced from neighboring countries. Moreover, it will increase smallholder farmer’s access to poultry inputs such as DOCs and feed to improve productivity. This is combined with greater distribution of DOCs in remote areas alongside farmer trainings to enhance adoption of best production practices. It is also expected to contribute to food security by increasing the volume of protein-rich poultry products sold to consumers and improving dietary diversity of households in Mozambique. The project will offer a long-term loan not available in the market, complemented by IDA PSW BFF that add value by better addressing risks, and eventually lowering the cost of capital for the Company.
additionality: Financing structure: IFC offers long term financing structure on terms that are otherwise not available in Mozambique (8years with 2 years grace), and IDA PSW LCF that adds value by mitigating the risks of Meticais (MZN) depreciation, convertibility/transferability and provide a viable local currency rate via concessionally priced swap. Over the past 12 months, the total face value of US dollar syndicated loans was 0.2 billion. However, no US dollar corporate bond issued during the period. Further, there were neither US dollar syndicated loans nor corporate bond issued in Agribusiness sector. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC, through advisory services, will provide expertise, innovation, knowledge to improve operational efficiency of Higest, and align its operations with industry best governance, financial and information management, and environmental and social practices. IFC’s support to implement poultry farm management practices to increase productivity and improve production and supply chain efficiencies, is expected to strengthen Higest’s resilience to shocks.

company_name: LG Innotek Vietnam Haiphong Co., Ltd
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a Sustainability-Linked Loan (“SLL”) of up to US$200 million to LG Innotek Vietnam Haiphong Co., Ltd. (“LGI VN” or the “Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of LG Innotek Co., Ltd. (“LGI” or the “Sponsor”). Proceeds from the proposed SLL will be used to expand the Company’s production capacity for smartphone camera modules as part of the approximately US$1 billion capex program to build a new factory in Trang Due Industrial Park, Hai Phong, Viet Nam (the “Project”). The proposed SLL will help reduce Greenhouse Gas (“GHG”) emissions.
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, LGI is one of the leading electronic components manufacturers, focusing on optic solutions for smartphones, substrates for semiconductors, as well as automotive components. The Sponsor is listed on the Korea Exchange and is 40.79% owned by LG Electronics of South Korea as of December 31, 2023.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project’s cost is estimated to be US$1 billion, a part of which will be funded by an IFC A Loan of up to US$200 million.
location_description: The proceeds from the proposed IFC investment will be utilized in Viet Nam.
development_impact: At the Project level, the Project will: (i) contribute to GHG emissions reduction; and (ii) create new jobs. At the Market level, the Project will contribute to enhancing Viet Nam’s competitiveness through export capacity expansion and knowledge spillovers.
additionality: Financial additionality includes: (i) a long-term tenor that is above what is available in the market and appropriate for such a greenfield project; and (ii) the first SLL for LGI. Non-financial additionality includes knowledge, innovation, and capacity building, where IFC will work with LGI on the sustainability-linked financing framework.
Company Name: LG Innotek Vietnam Haiphong Co., Ltd

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a Senior Secured Loan of: (i) up to US$ 96 million, and (ii) up to EUR 55 million to Orascom Development Egypt (“ODE” or the “Company”), a leading tourism and property developer in Egypt. The proposed SLL will provide ODE with long-term financing to help implement its energy renovations, capital expenditure program, and renovation of its strategic hotel assets in El Gouna, including the Movenpick Hotel, and strengthen its financial wherewithal by replacing short-term debt with more long-term patient debt (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1995 by Eng. Samih Sawiris, ODE has grown to become one of the leading players in the Tourism and Property space in Egypt. ODE has a portfolio of 24 hotels with 5,055 rooms, primarily in El Gouna and Taba Heights. The Company has a total land bank of 5,025 hectares (“ha”), of which 2,415 ha has yet to be developed and 1,136 ha is under development. ODE is listed on the Egypt Stock Exchange (“EGX”). The Company is 75% owned by Orascom Development Holdings (“ODH”) with 25% on free float at EGX. ODH is 76.4% by Eng. Samih Sawiris family with 23.6% on free float at the Swiss Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost is estimated to be up to US$ 96 million and EUR 55 million. IFC will provide (i) an A- Loan of up to US$85.4 million, (ii) an A loan of up to EUR 45.2million. of which IFC expects to share risk for EUR 20 million on unfunded basis with a credit insurer, and (iii) will mobilize US$ 10.6 million and EUR 9.8 million through Managed Co Lending Portfolio Program (“MCPP”).
location_description: ODE operates in Egypt. Most of the Company’s hotels are located is in El Gouna in the Red Sea area.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are environmental effects resulting from improvements to the water and energy efficiency of ODE’s hotel portfolio which will result in reduction in GHG emissions. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment will promote adoption of green building standards mainly amongst hotel developers and operators.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality will be provided through the longer tenor US$ and EUR financing on terms otherwise not available in the local market, especially for foreign currency loans. Non-financial additionality will be provided through the knowledge sharing to (i) assist in implementing green building standards and EDGE certification; and (ii) strengthen gender-based violence (GBV) grievance procedures, which will contribute to improving female workers’ health, safety, morale, and stress levels.

project_description: SAFCO Venture Holdings Limited BVI (“SAFCO Venture” or the “Company”) is a company established to own and operate biodiesel and sustainable aviation fuel (“SAF”) production facilities in Pakistan. Through its subsidiary Bio Tech Energy Pte Ltd (“BTE”), SAFCO Venture owns and operates a 50,000 tons per annum (tpa) biodiesel manufacturing facility in Sheikhupura, Pakistan.
sponsor_shareholders: SAFCO Venture is owned by Taimur Shaikh, Ali Shaikh (together, the “Sponsors”). SAFCO Pakistan is 100% owned by SAFCO Venture. SAFCO Venture will be the IFC investee company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$121 million. The proposed IFC investment is a financing package of up to US$35 million, consisting of (i) up to US$30 million in the form of preference shares and shareholder loans, of which US$10 million is contributed by IFC as implementing entity of Blended Concessional Finance (“The Preferred Equity”), and (ii) up to US$5 million in A-loan, to SAFCO Venture Holdings Limited.
location_description: The Project is located in an industrial area at 14-Km, Sharaqpur road, District Lahore, in Pakistan adjacent to BTE’s biodiesel manufacturing facility.
development_impact: The Project is anticipated to yield significant outcomes, including: (i) environmental effects through Green House Gas (GHG) emission savings and (ii) economywide effects through the creation of 300 highly skilled jobs and the generation of export revenue for the country. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment will promote sustainability by supporting the growth of the sustainable aviation fuel sector and circular economy model to curb the growth of carbon emissions in the aviation sector.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will be providing the Company with patient equity capital and support the capital structure for a greenfield project in a nascent sector. IFC non-financial additionality will be achieved through (i) supporting the Company in establishing E&S standards in line with IFC Performance standards and industry best practices and (ii) providing specialized advisory services in gender and corporate governance.

project_description: The project entails financing to the Municipality of Guatemala City (“MGC”) to address the city’s infrastructure bottlenecks by funding capital expenditures in (1) water infrastructure, such as small greenfield water treatment plants (“WTP”), as well as the rehabilitation and expansion of an existing groundwater extraction facility managed by the municipal water company EMPAGUA; (2) modernizing the city’s traffic light system through the installation of smart traffic lights and associated software and infrastructure upgrades to the existing control center, managed by the MGC’s Regulatory Entity for Transportation and Traffic - EMETRA and (3) assessing the feasibility of installing urban cycling routes and the deployment of a public bicycle system, managed by the Department of Urban Mobility, Planning Management of the MGC (together, the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The Municipality of Guatemala (MGC) is an autonomous state body responsible for the planning, implementation and administration of services and infrastructure in Guatemala City.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at GTQ [280] million (c.US$[35] million eq.). The proposed IFC investment entails a single asset unfunded risk participation (“URP”) for an amount in GTQ not to exceed 75% of a senior local currency loan of GTQ [280] million (c.US$[35] million eq.) amortizable by January 14th, 2028 (the “Covered Loan”) to MGC. The Covered Loan is provided by Banco Industrial.
location_description: The Project is located in Guatemala City and within the premises of EMPAGUA in surrounding municipalities, namely San Miguel Petapa.
development_impact: Stakeholder effects: The Project increases availability of drinking water in the MGC. The Project supports municipal investments by EMPAGUA, including the construction of greenfield Water Treatment Plants (WTP) and the rehabilitation of the infrastructure network in Guatemala City. These investments will optimize the use of surface water and provide an alternative to alleviate exploited groundwater resources. IFC expects these investments to add capacity to treat drinking water, which will increase the volume of drinking water supplied to MGC. Hence, benefiting users with improved potable water availability (50 l/day) and resilience to climate change vulnerabilities. Environmental effects: The Project is expected to treat contaminated surface water to address water scarcity and climate change vulnerabilities. In this sense, the Project provides a short-term solution to preserve critical surface water resources under stress and secure a more stable water production that is less sensitive to climate change. The Project supports the construction of greenfield WTPs, which will add capacity to treat surface contaminated water. This will enable EMPAGUA to treat contaminated surface water in Guatemala City, which would become available for reuse in a water scarce context. Hence, improving the availability of treated drinking water sources to adapt to the stress of climate-driven drought in the short-term, while the municipality develops integral long-term solutions to holistically address water scarcity.
additionality: Financial Additionality Resource Mobilization. IFC's guarantee (75 percent of the US$35.0 million loan) enables the mobilization of US$8.8 million (25% of the total transaction) from the largest domestic bank in Guatemala (Banco Industrial). Although the municipality could potentially negotiate the financing with Banco Industrial without IFC's involvement, the guarantee's risk mitigation effect allows Banco Industrial to lower the spread offered to the Municipality of Guatemala. Non-financial additionality Knowledge, innovation and capacity building. IFC is providing comprehensive support to the client to ensure the technical soundness and adequate procurement of the projects supported by the Covered Loan's use of proceeds. Through its Advisory Services IFC is supporting EMPAGUA (local water utility and implementing agency) to conduct feasibility studies for both potable and wastewater treatment projects. The feasibility studies provide the technical basis (topographic surveys, hydraulic and hydrological assessment, basic structural design, etc.) to determine the specifications for bidding documents to be used at the procurement stage. Standard Setting. IFC works with the client to strengthen E&S capabilities and ensure procedures are applied consistently and adequately to the projects supported by the Covered Loan's use of proceeds. Furthermore, IFC will support the client in improving gender standards and practices. IFC has identified gaps within municipal entities like EMPAGUA and EMT in areas like women's leadership and policies and procedures for women users and local communities. IFC is under discussions to provide advisory services to these entities as part of this investment. Update: This potential advisory support has not advanced beyond initial discussions.

project_description: IFC proposes a debt investment comprising a senior secured A loan of up to US$60 million to Renata PLC (the Company or Renata) with a tenor of up to six years, including a one-year grace period, to finance working capital needs of the Company (the Project). Renata PLC is one of the leading pharmaceutical companies in Bangladesh. The sponsors, Sajida Foundation, with a majority shareholding of 51.09% (as at 30th June 2023 and as at 31st March 2024) acquired the business 30 years ago from Pfizer. Renata has grown to become the fifth-largest pharmaceutical company in Bangladesh by revenues. The Project supports the ongoing operations of the Company in manufacturing and distributing essential medicines and helping the importation of key materials for those products during uncertain macroeconomic conditions, such as higher prices of raw materials and foreign exchange shortages. This will enable continued and appropriate access to pharmaceuticals for patients in need in Bangladesh, support the Export growth ambitions of the Company, in addition to preserving the skilled workforce of the Company.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsors of Renata is Sajida Foundation, who acquired the business 30 years ago from Pfizer in 1993, with a majority shareholding of 51.09%. Other Shareholders include Business Research International Corp (21.34%), Domestic Financial Institutions (12.46%) and General Public (15.11%). SAJIDA Foundation is a non-government, non-profit voluntary organization registered with: Registrar of Joint Stock Companies registration no. S1403(37)/91 dated 08/05/1991 NGO Affairs Bureau registration no. 984 dated 31/10/1995 Micro credit Regulatory Authority registration no. 00251-00155(Ka)- 00155, dated 16/03/2008 The General Body of SAJIDA comprises of 26 members who are involved in policy making, approval of the annual audit report, budget planning and electing the Governing Body. Members of the General Body who are also Directors of Renata PLC include:
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes a debt investment comprising a senior secured A loan of up to US$60 million to Renata PLC with a tenor of up to six years, including a one-year grace period.
location_description: Bangladesh
development_impact: Assessment of Project Outcomes: The project aims to improve access to affordable and quality pharmaceutical products in the country. Bangladesh has made progress in healthcare access, including pharmaceuticals, but recent macroeconomic events have affected the performance of pharmaceutical companies. The project will support the company in securing USD, thereby mitigating the foreign exchange risk as well as foreign currency liquidity risk related to the importing of raw materials, ensuring adequate supplies of essential pharmaceuticals. The project is expected to preserve employment opportunities and measure progress through tracking sales of pharmaceutical products. Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation: The project aims to strengthen the competitiveness of the Bangladesh pharmaceutical industry and its export potential. The pharmaceutical industry in Bangladesh has grown rapidly, however it is highly dependent on the import of raw materials, making it vulnerable to external shocks. The project will support the company's export strategy as the company is one of the leading exporters in Bangladesh and has the potential to open untapped export markets, positioning Bangladesh as a competitive player in the global pharmaceutical market. The progress of this outcome will be measured by tracking the value of Bangladesh's pharmaceutical exports.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists of the provision of scarce long-term finance in United States Dollars (USD) in the context of severe foreign exchange shortages in Bangladesh. Non-financial additionality is comprised of knowledge, innovation, and capacity building as well as standard setting, provided by supporting the Company’s improvement in operational efficiency, women employment, and environmental and sustainability management. IFC will support Renata to improve gender diversity and inclusion in its workplace by providing recommendations, guidance, and tools to improve policies and practices to support workplace participation of all genders, particularly women through its Partnership for Women’s Employment, a peer learning initiative for select private sector companies in Bangladesh.

project_description: The proposed investment is an IFC A loan to Mersin Water & Sewage Administration ( MESKI), backstopped by a guarantee from Metropolitan Municipality of Mersin (MMM or City). IFC's financing will support 10 subprojects including the: (i) expansion and technology upgrade of 4 existing wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs); (ii) construction of 2 new WWTPs; and (iii) installation of 4 deep-sea discharge pipelines (collectively the Project). The Project willadd 30% (46 million cubic meters per annum) to the existing WWTP capacity in the City.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1995, MESKI is the public water utility of the Mersin city, providing water and wastewater services to ~1 million subscribers. MESKI is 100% owned by the Metropolitan Municipality of Mersin. The City is the eleventh largest of the country's metropolitan areas, serving a population of nearly 1.9 million inhabitants. MESKI has a good credit profile and a self-sustaining business model, operated by an experienced administration that has been able to maintain a prudent financial management and adequate liquidity. The Board of Directors of MESKI is composed of Mr. Vahap Secer, the Mayor of MMM and Chairman of the Board; Mr. Irfan Korkmaz, General Manager of MESKI; Mr. Nizamettin Yildirim; Mr. Seyfettin Atar; and Professor Dr. Orhan VeliAlici.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated to be around EUR 100 million across the ten sub-projects. The proposed investment is an IFC A loan of up to EUR 45 million in equivalentTurkish Lira with a 15-year tenor. The Project is expected to be supported by the Clean Technology Fund, as described in the Blended Finance section.
location_description: The ten subprojects are located across five semi-rural and touristic districts of Mersin city including Tarsus, Erdemli, Silifke, Akdeniz, and Bozyazi.
development_impact: The Project adds wastewater treatment capacity to a municipality recently exposed to surging population growth due to internally displaced people from the 2023 earthquake, and refugees from both Syria and Ukraine. The main expected project-level outcomes are from stakeholder and environmental effects by providing increased access and quality of wastewater treatment and other additional positive effects such as an integrated wastewater management system to prevent water contamination and potential waste-to-energy options. The anticipated market creation effects stem from financial integration, as IFC is offering its first blue loan to a municipality and its first blue loan in the infrastructure sector in MCT. Given the funding challenges facing most water utilities, this is expected to have demonstration and replication effects for other municipalities.
additionality: IFC's additionality is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality is provided through long-term financing in local currency. Financing of this type for infrastructure is limited, and maturities in the subnational market have declined. Non-financial additionality derives from the application of IFC’s knowledge and experience in the water sector and in supporting MESKI in aligning the transaction with the requirement of blue finance and qualifying it as a blue loan. IFC’s participation also supports the application of its Performance Standards to mitigate E&S risks and includes an upstream engagement aimed at strengthening MESKI’s capacity through the E&S Academy.

project_description: On September 24, 2024, IFC supported the inaugural 5-year green bond issuance by voestalpine AG (voestalpine or the Company, together with its subsidiaries, the Group) of €500 million with an own account subscription of €75 million. It will be listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange.
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Linz, Austria, the Company is a leading global steel and technology Group with a combined materials and processing expertise, operating in 50 countries across six continents and employing over 51,000 people. voestalpine is listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: On September 19, 2024, IFC’s board authorized an investment of up to €150 million in the green bonds of voestalpine. The proceeds of the Green Bond will be used for CAPEX aimed primarily at achieving GHG emission reductions, but also for other eligible investments. The eligibility criteria are defined in voestalpine’s Green Financing Framework (GFF).
location_description: Brazil, Poland, Romania.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes lie in reducing the climate footprint of steel production and steel products used in downstream manufacturing in various customer industry segments. Beyond the Project, the IFC Investment is expected to contribute to the growing availability of sustainable financing instruments for decarbonization in the iron and steel sectors.
additionality: IFC’s role lies in resource mobilization as sustainability advisor and anchor investor.

project_description: The proposed project entails an IFC investment as an anchor investor in Asia Debt Opportunities Fund II (ADOF II or the Fund). The Fund will focus on distressed debt, special situations, asset-backed credit portfolios as well as single assets and will have a life of up to 8 years. ADOF II will be managed by GI Capital Management Ltd (GICAM or the Company), a Japan-based manager with US$754 million of Assets under Management (AUM) and over 20 years of credit experience. The Fund is targeted at US$300 million, with first close aimed at US$100 million. IFC’s investment is proposed at the lower of up to US$30 million or up to 15% of the Fund commitments. ADOF II’s geographical scope will be pan-Asia spanning across various sectors and asset classes.
sponsor_shareholders: GI Capital Management Ltd. (GICAM or the Company) is an alternative asset management and advisory boutique headquartered in Tokyo, Japan. Founded in 2010, GICAM has since grown into a licensed broker-dealer and multi-class asset manager with AUM of US$754 million. GICAM has three business areas: (1) Fund placement and Distribution Business, (2) Asset Management Business, and (3) Investment Advisory and Consulting Business to Institutional Investors and Asset Managers. The Company’s capital as of March 2024 is JPY50 million (~US$ 330,000).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is IFC’s investment in the Fund up to the lower of US$30 million or 15% of the Fund total commitments. The total size of the Fund is targeted at US$300 million.
location_description: GICAM is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan. The eligible countries of the IFC’s investment into the Fund shall include Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mongolia, Nepal, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand and Viet Nam.
development_impact: Project Outcomes Stakeholder effects – Increased access to finance for financially stressed companies: The Project will provide up to US$300 million financing in loans to mid-market companies, enabling them to recover their business operations, avoid liquidation, and preserve jobs. Stakeholder effects – Enable Financial Institutions (FIs) Dispose non-performing loans (NPLs) and borrowers to normalize their obligations: NPLs pose challenges for both lenders and borrowers as they restrict credit availability, disrupt credit allocation, erode market confidence, and hinder economic growth. In this context, the Fund will acquire NPLs from FIs and allow them to release capital and thus increase their capacity to lend. The Project will also reduce the costs, for FIs, of managing these distressed assets and refocus their attention to their core lending activities. Through this Project, IFC will also help to bring the financially distressed but viable businesses in the target countries back to creditworthiness and regain access to finance, while preserving jobs. Contribution to Market Creation Competitiveness: IFC anticipates that the Project will promote greater competitiveness in the distressed assets and special situations financing segment, by supporting the development of an alternate financing channel like private credit funds in this segment. Through demonstration and replication, IFC expects that the Project will attract potential investors and new funds in the private credit space to enter and crowd-in more private capital to scale up lending to distressed assets and special situations, contributing to the secondary market development across Asia. By supporting the growth and expansion of GICAM, IFC will demonstrate the viability of providing special situations financing to businesses and will encourage other players to enter this segment.
additionality: Financial Additionality IFC’s Own Account Equity: IFC will be the anchor investor for the Fund, investing up to US$30 million or maximum 15% out of a total fund size of US$300 million. The Fund will focus on distressed debt, special situations, asset-backed credit portfolios and single asset investments across Asia. IFC’s anchor investment will facilitate the successful first closing of the Fund and enable GICAM to start investing in accordance with the Fund’s investment objective. Resource mobilization: IFC will play a key role in mobilizing financing from other investors in the Fund through its anchor investment, sending a strong signal to the market and boosting potential investors’ confidence in the Fund. IFC investment will also help diversify GICAM’s investor base that would have been otherwise difficult to mobilize in the absence of IFC’s anchor investment. Non-Financial Additionality Standard setting: IFC’s participation will support the application of international best practice for E&S standards and risk mitigation. GICAM is expected to develop an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) to assess key E&S risks related to investment in distressed companies and special situation transactions. IFC will help foster best practices applicable to special opportunities funds, including the adoption of IFC E&S risk assessment, mitigation, and monitoring procedures for all the investments made by the Fund. All investments by the Fund will be subject to applicable performance requirements including IFC’s exclusion list, relevant national E&S laws and regulations and IFC performance standards. IFC will support GICAM in adhering to higher standards of implementing climate transition and physical risk assessments in line with Paris Alignment methodology.

company_name: BORCELIK CELIK SANAYII TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Borçelik Çelik Sanayii Ticaret A.S. (“Borcelik”, the “Company”), founded in 1990, is the second largest private sector flat steel manufacturer and galvanized steel producer in Turkiye (https://www.borcelik.com/en). The Company has a production capacity of 1.5 million (m) tons of hot dip galvanized steel, cold-rolled steel, and hot-rolled steel, all of which are industrial raw materials that serve the automotive, white goods, and construction sectors, among others. Borcelik’s main plant is located in Gemlik (near Istanbul in Turkey) on a 240,000 square meter (sqm) area. Two smaller steel service centers are located in Bursa (20k sqm) and Manisa (10k sqm). IFC is considering a financing package of up to US$210M to Borcelik to finance the modernization and expansion program as well as working capital requirements, which will include the installation of a 1.6 mt Pickling Line and Tandem Cold Mill (PLTCM) upstream line combined with a 0.5 mt Continuous Galvanizing and Annealing Line (CGAL) downstream line (“Project”). The IFC loan will be committed in two phases over a period of 3 years, with the first phase consisting of a senior, corporate A loan of up to US$80M, a MCPP Trust Loan of up to US$50M, and a B1/Parallel loan of up to US$30M, and the second phase consisting of an A Loan and B1/Parallel loan of up to US$50M.
sponsor_shareholders: Borçelik is a JV between i) Borusan Holding A.S., a diversified Turkish conglomerate with primary operations in steel manufacturing and distribution of cars and industrial machinery; and ii) ArcelorMittal, one of the largest global steelmakers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost to implement the Project (including working capital) is estimated at up to US$530 million. IFC is considering a financing package of up to US$210M in senior loans that will be committed in two phases over a period of 3 years, with the first phase consisting of a senior, corporate A loan of up to US$80M, a MCPP Trust Loan of up to US$50M, and a B1/Parallel loan of up to US$30M, and the second phase consisting of an A Loan and B1/Parallel loan of up to US$50M.
location_description: The Project will be located on the industrial premises/land adjacent to the Gemlik Plant in Turkey.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are economy-wide effects through value addition, export increase, employment creation, and environmental effects. Beyond the Project outcomes, IFC anticipates the Project will support competitiveness in key manufacturing industries for Türkiye – notably the automotive and white goods sectors by strengthening the steel value chain.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via the Project's financing structure and resource mobilization, which are not readily available from the local banking sector. Non-financial additionality is provided via knowledge, innovation and capacity building, and standard setting.
Company Name: BORCELIK CELIK SANAYII TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: The proposed investment comprises senior unsecured sustainability linked-debt by IFC, for its own account, of up to THB4.6 billion (approximately US$125 million equivalent) through subscription to senior unsecured Sustainability-linked Bonds (SLB) proposed, to be issued by CPN as part of public issuances in one or more
sponsor_shareholders: CPN is a leading real estate developer with a strong presence in the retail property sector in Thailand. With over 40 years of experience, CPN has the largest retail footprint in the country, covering 20 provinces and holding a 22% market share in terms of leasable area. CPN is part of the Central Group, one of Thailand's largest conglomerates, with a vast property network and over 5,700 employees. CPN's property portfolio includes retail-led mixed-use developments, comprising shopping malls, residences, office buildings, and hotels, with a total net lettable space of 2.3 million sqm. Nearly half of CPN’s portfolio is located in provinces outside of the Bangkok Metropolitan Area.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s debt investment of up to THB4.6 billion (approximately US$125 million equivalent) will go towards green refurbishing of selected properties, increasing green building certifications, and refinancing existing debt.
location_description: Thailand
development_impact: The main expected project-level outcomes are environmental effects via improved resource efficiency of green buildings, and stakeholder effects due to increased access to high-quality modern retail services in Thailand’s suburban and rural areas. IFC expects the project to catalyze sustainability in the Thai retail property sector via demonstration and replication channels, given CPN’s high visibility and market leading position in the sector.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the proposed project is both financial and non-financial. IFC will provide long-term financing through a 7-year SLB, which will be CPN's first public issuance of SLB. IFC’s non-financial additionality will be in the form of knowledge, innovation, and capacity building support to CPN via IFC’s U/A engagement.

project_description: The proposed Investment is an up to US$ 20 million financing facility to Bismark Maritime Limited (“Bismark” or the “Company”), a Papua New Guinean-owned shipping company, operating in the domestic/inter-islands cargo transportation market. The financing will support Bismark’s plans to acquire two younger multipurpose cargo vessels (MPVs), in order to increase the cargo carrying capacity. The newly acquired vessels are expected to be more efficient in terms fuel consumption and green-house-gas emissions. The project is expected to be supported by the IDA PSW Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Bismark is a private 100% family-owned business. The Founder and Managing Director of Bismark is Hamish Gordon Sharp. Hamish (Jamie) William Sharp is the Chief Executive Officer.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment in Bismark is a secured IFC A-loan of up to US$ 20 million equivalent in Papua New Guinea Kina (PGK).
location_description: Bismark operates solely in Papua New Guinea and connects the major domestic ports of the country. The Company is headquartered in Lae city, the economic hub of the country.
development_impact: The Project will improve the quality of maritime freight shipping services, and in turn enable an increased access to critical goods in coastal communities of Papua New Guinea (PNG). At the market level, IFC investment will contribute to increasing the resilience of inter-island domestic shipping and logistics consumption hubs and also provide point to point service between small-medium sized ports. This “last-mile” connectivity at competitive rates is a key element to enabling the functioning of maritime trade, which the larger vessels of main liners cannot service due to infrastructure constraints (iii) Inclusiveness: The Company provides a critical service to the fresh food producers in highland for local. The upgrade incapacity in sustainable transport infrastructure would increase its outreach to suppliers.
additionality: Financial additionality Financing structure: IFC will provide a long-term debt facility to fund the capacity expansion and fleet renewal of the business. Private companies in PNG have limited access to long-term fixed-rate capital and only a limited number of lenders are providing shipping financing. IFC financing provided will be in local currency helping improve the sustainability of the Project by matching the currency of the revenues with debt obligations. IFC will help the client scale up operations to meet growing demand. Resource mobilization: IFC’s involvement is expected to help mobilize additional funds needed for the Project. Potential investors value IFC’s experience in the sector and due diligence in adequately mitigating structuring, technical and implementation risks. Non-Financial additionality Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: The proposed investment is expected to be the first asset-based financing which is not available in the local financing market. The introduction of such financing to the Company and validation by IFC will allow it to access financing for its future fleet renewal program. IFC is also expected to provide technical assistance through pre-investment to develop a sustainability strategy for Bismark, support Bismark to comply with environment and social standards for its operations. Standard-setting: As this is the first engagement with Bismark, IFC will work with the Company to meet IFC Performance Standards, thereby enhancing the overall standard and rigor of E&S standards followed by the Company.

project_description: The proposed project consists of an up to ZAR1 billion (~US$52 million) loan with a 8-year tenor to Balwin Properties Limited (Balwin or the Company) to fund Balwin’s original land acquisition and the infrastructure preparatory work and of up to 4,500 apartments at its development, Mooikloof City. This includes the financing of the external bulk infrastructure services such as water, sewer, electricity, roads, and stormwater which is required for the top-structure development of the apartments. The facility will also refinance the existing short-term loans previously taken by Balwin for the project.
sponsor_shareholders: Balwin was established in 1996 and is one of the largest sectional title residential property developer in South Africa focused on development and sale of sectional title apartments. The company has been at the forefront of efforts to close the burgeoning gap of low-to-middle-class housing across different provinces of South Africa. In addition to its residential Build-to-Sell business, Balwin has also established several complimentary businesses that leverages its developments, including fibre installation, rental of apartment units and solar power generation. Since its inception it has successfully completed and sold over 50,000 apartment units and currently develops approximately 2,000 to 3,000 units each year. Balwin also has the largest number of IFC EDGE certifications by any property developer globally with over 22,810 units registered for EDGE certification and with 14,328 of these already EDGE Advanced. The Company is listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and the largest shareholders are held by its founder and CEO Stephen Brookes (33.07%), and its Managing Director, Rodney Gray (9.29%). Other shareholders include Reggie Kukama, Non-Executive Director (9.09%); GRE Africa Ltd (7.58%); Nedbank Group (5.49%); Ulrich Gschnaidtner, Chief Projects Officer (1.05%) and Jonathan Bigham, CFO (0.02%). The rest of the shareholding is held publicly.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project involves a 8-year loan of up to ZAR1 billion (~US$52 million) from IFC. It will support the phased development of Mooikloof City by funding Balwin’s original land acquisition, bulk infrastructure investments and the development of up to 4,500 apartments.
location_description: The Mooikloof City project is located east of Tshwane (Pretoria) in Gauteng, South Africa.
development_impact: Stakeholder effects (customer access): The project will increase access to quality housing for low-to-middle-income households, helping to alleviate South Africa's housing shortage. Environmental effect: The project aims to achieve IFC EDGE Advanced certification, requiring at least 40% energy savings and 20% water savings, thereby reducing GHG emissions.
additionality: (i) Financial Additionality- Financing Structure: IFC will provide long-term financing not readily available for the Company in the local market. IFC financing will better match the cash flow of the infrastructure investments required by Balwin to deliver large scale housing and enhance its access to complementary capital needed for the home developments. (ii) Risk Mitigation: IFC's financing to Balwin will serve as an endorsement, boosting confidence in South Africa's housing sector and attracting additional investors. The South African housing market is battling a number of challenges including worsening business sentiment and a 15 year high in mortgage rates. IFC’s investment is expected to serve as demonstration effect to investors that the industry remains resilient and help crowd in more investors to the sector. (iii Standard Setting: This will include support to improve environmental and social (E&S) best practices. IFC’s due diligence included a comprehensive review of E&S practices and policies of Balwin and support the Company’s plan to deliver IFC’s EDGE Advanced residential developments in the country.

company_name: PROMOTORA DE VIVIENDAS INTEGRALES, S.A. DE C.V.
project_description: The Project involves IFC financing for up to MXN 1,150 million (~US$ 58 million) through an A-Loan and Partial Credit Guarantee (“PCG”) from IFC’s own account to Vinte Viviendas Integrales, S.A.B. de C.V. (“Vinte”), a real estate homebuilder. The proposed project aims to support Vinte’s acquisition of Servicios Corporativos Javer S.A.B. de C.V. (“Javer”), CAPEX, and debt reprofiling to expand development and construction of EDGE-certified green homes for entry-level and middle-income housing across Mexico.
sponsor_shareholders: Vinte is a leading real estate developer in Mexico focused on urban development and home building. The company is publicly traded (BMV: VINTE) with a diversified investor base including co-founders (61.5% controlling stake) and institutional investors such as Proparco, IFU, and IDB Invest
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost of MXN 7,700 million (~US$ 390 million) is expected to be financed by a combination of potential public and private bond issuances of MXN 2,650 (~US$ 134 million), financial debt of MXN 2,550 million (~US$ 129 million), and additional equity capital of MXN 2,500 million (~US$ 127 million). IFC will finance up to MXN 1,150 million (~US$ 58 million) through an A-Loan and PCG and mobilize funds by enhancing the credit profile of the financing package.
location_description: Vinte and Javer currently have combined presence in 11 states in Mexico, including Nuevo Leon, Estado de Mexico, Jalisco, Quintana Roo, Queretaro, Aguascalientes, Hidalgo, Puebla, Tamaulipas, Baja California, and Morelos.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects via increased access to quality low to middle-income housing in Mexico (ii) environmental effects via improved efficiency in energy and water usage on new and existing properties of the integrated company. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment to promote competitiveness in the Mexican housing sector by exerting competitive pressures on other developers to expand the supply of green homes in the lower-middle income segment and by demonstrating its commercial profitability.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the proposed Project is both financial and non-financial. IFC will provide scarce long-term financing to the Company that is not readily available in the local market and mobilize funds by enhancing the credit profile of the financing package. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will provide technical guidance on green buildings including EDGE and the Building Resilience Index (BRI).
Company Name: PROMOTORA DE VIVIENDAS INTEGRALES, S.A. DE C.V.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to EUR500 million financing package comprising (i) an unsecured, straight senior loan (“A” loan) of up to EUR150 million from IFC and; (ii) mobilization of parallel loans of up to EUR350 million to Aspen Treasury Ireland Limited (ATIL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Aspen Pharmacare Holdings Limited (Aspen or the Company). The financing will support: (i) Aspen’s corporate financing program to assist the Company in expanding its capacity to deliver medicines, diabetes insulin and paediatric vaccines in Africa; the Company’s investment in ongoing product development and acquisition of product portfolios; (iii) the Company’s investments in emerging markets manufacturing capabilities; and (iv) to refinance existing debt and strengthen the Company’s balance sheet.
sponsor_shareholders: ATIL is a wholly owned subsidiary of Aspen that centrally manages the group’s syndicated loan programs. Aspen is listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), the Company’s shareholding is a mix of the founders, institutional investors and domestic and international asset managers. Aspen’s co-founders, Stephen Saad and Gus Attridge, own 12.8 percent and 4.3 percent of the Company, respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment in Aspen through ATIL is an unsecured IFC “A” loan of up to EUR150 million and parallel loans of up to EUR350 million, with a tenor of up to seven years, to be disbursed in Euros.
location_description: The proposed investment is a corporate finance loan to ATIL, acting as treasury company to Aspen, which has a global presence in both emerging and developed markets.
development_impact: The project outcomes rating is Strong based on the improved access to healthcare products such as medicines, insulin and vaccines to countries in Sub-Saharan Africa. The Project will support the increase in access to medicines, insulin and vaccines in the African region by supporting a large manufacturer in setting up partnerships to manufacture and distribute locally. The contribution to market creation rating is Very Strong based on the project's expected contribution to the regional healthcare systems' resilience, by supporting the development of vaccines, and human insulin manufacturing capabilities in Africa, along with other critical medicines.
additionality: Additionality: Financial Additionality: Financial additionality is provided through the Project’s financing structure; longer-term euro-denominated financing from IFC on terms otherwise not available in the local market. Non- Financial Additionality: Non-financial additionality is provided through (i) support to the Company in developing a decarbonization roadmap, and (ii) sharing best practices to address gender-based violence and harassment in the workplace.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an A Loan of up to BRL150 million in BRL equivalent to Kepler Weber Industrial S.A. (“Kepler”, “KW” or the “Company”), the leading company in the storage and post-harvest solutions sector in Latin America. The Company has requested IFC to finance its BRL150 million capital expenditure plan for 2022-2024 which includes the expansion of manufacturing capacity, plant modernization and productivity improvements (“The Project”). The IFC investment is also expected to be structured as an Incentive Based Loan focused assisting the company in obtaining the EDGE Gender Certification and developing a Sustainability Linked Framework based on EDGE’s Action Plan.
sponsor_shareholders: The Borrower Kepler Weber Industrial S.A. is a privately held corporation, whose sole shareholder is Kepler Weber S.A. with 100% participation in its share capital. The Guarantor Kepler Weber S.A is listed company in the São Paulo Stock Exchange. As of March 11, 2024, Kepler’s shareholding structure is comprised of 60.2 percent of free-floating shares with the remaining shares being held by Trigono Capital, an asset management firm, with 21.7 percent, the Heller Family, with 11.6 percent, Tarpon Investimentos, an independent asset manager in Brazil, with 4.9 percent, and treasury shares, with 1.7 percent.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is estimated at US$30 million dollars. The proposed IFC investments consist of an IFC A Loan of up to the total required amount.
location_description: Investments will be made at Kepler’s existing facilities located in Panambi (Rio Grande do Sul) and Campo Grande (Mato Grosso do Sul).
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to contribute to improved food security for consumers by increasing the production of modern, efficient grain storage silos in Brazil, which will help alleviate infrastructure bottlenecks in Brazil resulting in increased availability of food to the market. The Project will also preserve and create employment both directly and in the supply chain and increase value addition in the Brazilian economy. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing will contribute to promoting resilience in the global food supply market
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality derives from the provision of long-term financing materially longer than the Company’s most recent issuance and from its potential innovative structuring as an incentive-based loan, an instrument that aims to support the Company in the development and implementation of its gender-related strategy. Non-financial additionality is provided via standard setting as IFC will introduce the Performance Standards to the Company

project_description: The proposed investment is for up to US$100 million (“IFC Loans”) to Meghna Re-Rolling and Steel Mills Limited (“MRSL” or the “Company”) in Bangladesh. IFC’s financing package will support setting up a greenfield steel plant with a melting capacity of 1.4 million Metric Tons per year and a rolling capacity of 0.9 million Metric Tons per year (the “Project”). The Project will use more than ninety percent scrap steel as input with its energy-efficient electric arc furnace (EAF) technology, thereby helping Bangladesh increase circularity in the steel sector and reduce the carbon foot print of the final product.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsors include Mr. Mostafa Kamal, his wife Mrs. Beauty Akhter, and their grown-up children - Ms. Tahmina Binthe Mostafa, Ms. Tanjima Binthe Mostafa, Mr. Tanveer Ahmed Mostafa and Tasnim Binthe Mostafa (collectively referred to as the “Sponsors”). The Sponsors are the ultimate beneficial owners of hundred percent of the shareholding in the Borrower.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$372 million and is proposed to be financed with long-term debt totaling US$224 million and the balance of US$148 million will be financed through equity. The Project involves a 9-year senior loan comprising of US$46.02 million from IFC’s own account and US$53.98 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP). The loan will have a tenor of 9 years, including a 3-year grace period on principal repayments.
location_description: The Project will be located in Cumilla Economic Zone, Cumilla, 40 kilometers south of Dhaka, in Bangladesh.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are economywide effects through value addition and employment, as well as productivity and skillset improvement. Beyond these outcomes, IFC expects that the project will promote competitiveness through expansion into a less developed Southwestern region.
additionality: Financing structure: IFC provides financial additionality through a US$ loan with a tenor of 9 years, including 3 years of grace period. This long tenor is not readily available for manufacturing projects in Bangladesh. In absence of IFC financing, MRSL would have to seek financing from a local commercial bank and would usually receive shorter tenor (up to 5 years) which could strain the cash flows and affect viability of the Project. E&S Standard-setting: IFC will have an opportunity to identify and help close any gaps in the ESG performance of the Company. Through ESAP and other associated measures prescribed by IFC, the Company will make improvements and align its operations with industry best practices.

sector: Garment and Apparel (Without Fabric , Excluding Footwear)
project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support Royal Apparel EPZ Limited (RAL), Royal Garment Industries EPZ Limited (RGI) and Royal Clothing EPZ Limited (RCL), (together, the Royal Garments Group of Companies, Royal or the Group), a Kenyan garments manufacturing company based in Athi River, to expand the Cut-Make-Trim (CMT) operations in Kenya by constructing a new factory (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Royal is 100%-owned by Mr. Omprakash Shukla, a Kenyan businessman who has been in the textiles and apparel sector for 32 years. He started his career in the export business prior to joining the business first garment factory as a general manager.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at US$20 million. IFC’s proposed investment in Royal is a US$15 million corporate A loan to support the Group in implementing the Project, with the balance of US$5 million through Equity.
location_description: The funds will be used in the Royal factory located in the Athi River Export Processing Zone in Nairobi, in the Republic of Kenya.
development_impact: The project helps finance a Kenyan garments manufacturer to expand its operations. Economy-wide effects: The textiles and apparels sector is a strategic priority in Kenya's economic development agenda. The project is expected to have various positive economy-wide effects including (i) the direct creation of 3,700 formal manufacturing jobs, mostly for women in underserved population groups, and a larger number of indirect jobs, (ii) the generation of valuable foreign exchange earnings for Kenya from increased exports through the expansion of CMT operations. Stakeholder effects: The Project is expected to employ people primarily coming from underserved, low-income populations with limited education and skills, and no formal employment history. Beyond providing jobs, the IFC investment will help enhance employees’ technical and soft skills through various training programs and policies. Additionally, the Group is also committed to creating a more inclusive workforce, particularly for women. Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation - Competitiveness: The Project is expected to boost the Group's productivity, thereby improving Group's overall competitiveness. This improvement in a domestic apparel producing company will be achieved through a multi-pronged approach including optimization of sewing line staffing, automation of specific tasks and integration of real time data analytics. Furthermore, training local staff on these tools will create a pool of skilled professionals, benefiting the entire industry in Kenya. The project is anticipated to have meaningful demonstration effects, as improvements in productivity and export expansion are likely to encourage other domestic companies in Kenya's textile and apparel sector to adopt similar approaches.
additionality: Financial additionality - Financing Structure: (i) IFC will provide customized financing with two tranches to match the CMT ramp-up (in US$) with 7-year tenor (including 2-year grace period) which is not readily available to the Company in the local market; (ii) IFC will potentially provide concessional financing which will help de risk the project given the limited available security package. Non-Financial additionality - Knowledge Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will help Royal strengthen the workplace policies for the female workforce (i.e. gender) through the Kenya2Equal program. Standard setting - During Project implementation and supervision, IFC will provide technical, environmental and social (E&S), health and safety expertise to improve the overall environmental and safety performance as well as introduce international best practices to the client.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support Pee Cee Holding Ltd (the Company or PCH), a Sierra Leone-based consumer goods group to develop its subsidiary, Pee Cee Agriculture (PCA), an integrated onion farming business spanning 500 hectares (ha) in Lungi (the Project). The Project total cost is US$16 million and will be financed 25% by Sponsor equity (US$4 million) and the remaining by IFC and IDA PSW. The proposed investment entails a 7-year senior secured loan of up to US$12 million. The project is expected to be supported by IDA PSW, as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Pee Cee Holding Ltd (PCH) is a privately owned consumer goods group established more than 50 years ago in Sierra Leone. It is one of the country’s largest importers, manufacturers, and distributors of fast-moving food and non-food consumer products (FMCG), operating primarily within Sierra Leone. PCH was founded by Mahesh Nandwani (current CEO), a Sierra Leonean citizen, renowned businessman, and philanthropist. Pee Cee Holding Ltd is 100% owned by the Nandwani family. Pee Cee Agriculture (PCA), the ultimate beneficiary of the proceeds from IFC loan is owned 80% by PCH with 20% unsubscribed.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project is estimated at US$16m comprising: (i) US$12m capex for machinery and storage facility, and (ii) US$4m for start-up costs (funded by PCH). The proposed investment is a 7-year (including a 2-year grace period) senior secured loan of up to US$12m, consisting of US$6m each of IFC A loan and IDA PSW BFF Loan, subordinated to IFC A loan both in payment and liquidation. PCH is the main borrower, and its affiliates (Jolaks Manufacturing Limited, Pee Cee & Sons, Pee Cee Agriculture, Pee Cee Industries, and Milla Group) are co-borrowers.
location_description: Pee Cee Agriculture (PCA), a 500-hectare commercial onion farm, is located in Lungi, Porto Loko District, approximately 50 km from the capital city, Freetown. The proceeds of IFC’s loan will be directed to this farm.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Excellent for the following reasons: Project-level impact: (i) Stakeholders – Customers: The project is expected to increase consumer access to safe, quality, and affordable vegetable products in the country, and therefore contribute to improving food security. The vegetable products have nutrition benefits to consumers, a source of protein, vitamins and minerals to combat the widespread malnourishment among vulnerable populations in a country whose hunger situation is serious according to the Global Hunger Index; and (ii) Economy-wide effects: The Project, through import substitution efforts, is expected to increase domestic value addition and create more jobs (direct and indirect) through up- and downstream linkages in Sierra Leone, by expanding irrigated production and warehousing/storage of vegetable products such as onions. The Project is expected to bring a much-needed boost to the food processing sector and contribute to diversifying and strengthening the local economy; Market-level Impact: IFC expects the Project to increase competitiveness of the market through increased investment in irrigated production and warehousing of food products to bolster food marketing and reduce reliance on food imports. The Project will demonstrate the potential to expand irrigated vegetable production and marketing in the country to increase supplies and ensure adoption of industry best post-harvest handling and storage practices.
additionality: Financial additionality – Financing structure: IFC will provide a long-term loan with a sufficient grace period, which is not readily available to agribusinesses in the local market. The loan will be structured to fit the needs of a new mechanized farming project that needs sufficient time for preparation and ramp-up. The IDA PSW subordinated loan also gives sufficient cushion to provide the necessary cover for the IFC senior tranche. Non-financial additionality – Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC is expected to provide advisory services. PCH is interested in financial management and corporate governance advisory support while PCA would like gender and E&S advisory services. The advisory work will be phased and dependent on PCH and PCA's capacity to balance these engagements with other business priorities.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to €250 million syndicated term loan (1-year maturity, renewable/re-committed annually, for up to 4 years in aggregate) by IFC to SUCDEN Cote d’Ivoire (“SUCDEN-CI” or the “Company”) and its parent company SUCDEN S.A (the “co-Borrower” and, jointly with SUCDEN-CI and other subsidiaries, “SUCDEN” or the “Group”) to finance the procurement and export of cocoa beans from Cote d’Ivoire (CI).
sponsor_shareholders: SUCDEN S.A. and SUCDEN Cote d’Ivoire.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: €250 million, distributed as follow: €120 million from IFC’s own account, and €130 million mobilized (€80 million from FMO and €50 million from OPEC fund).
location_description: Cote d’Ivoire.
development_impact: The most significant Project level outcomes are stakeholders - improved livelihood for smallholder farmers. IFC's investment in the project is expected to support the livelihoods of a significant number of smallholder farmers in Cote d'Ivoire who supply cocoa beans to SUCDEN. Cocoa farming is a critical sector for the country's economy, but many cocoa farmers in Cote d'Ivoire are among the poorest in the country. SUCDEN's pre-harvest finance provides farmer suppliers with access to funds for fertilizers, pruning, and farm upkeep, and IFC is discussing an Advisory Services program to support SUCDEN's efforts towards compliance with the European Union Deforestation Regulation.
