Beyond the Project, IFC expects SUCDEN's sustainability programs to cocoa farmers to positively impact cocoa quality, the efficiency and effectiveness of cocoa production, and the supply of sustainable and traceable cocoa. These outcomes can contribute to promoting the competitiveness and sustainability of the cocoa sector in Cote d'Ivoire.
additionality: The investment provides IFC with the opportunity to assess the E&S performance of SUCDEN Cote d’Ivoire and identify potential gaps for alignment with international best practices.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan financing package to Sao Martinho S.A. (Sao Martinho). Founded in the 1930’s by the Ometto family, Sao Martinho is a sugar, ethanol and renewable energy producer in Brazil. Sao Martinho currently operates three sugar mills in the state of Sao Paulo and one distillery in the state of Goias. .
sponsor_shareholders: Sao Martinho is listed in Brazilian stock exchange B3 under the Novo Mercado segment. The Company’s majority shareholders and sponsors are the Ometto family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an A loan to Sao Martinho of up to US$165 million to support an investment program in the Santa Cruz Mill related to the construction of a biomethane plant, and sugarcane planting and crop treatment needs.
location_description: Santa Cruz Mill
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to have environmental effects by contributing to climate mitigation through production of biomethane. The Project will also generate economy wide impact through job creation and value addition. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will contribute to environmental sustainability by demonstrating the commercial feasibility of producing biomethane from vinasse.
additionality: The proposed IFC loan has both financial and non-financial additionality. The financial additionality stems from the provision of long-term financing with tenors that are not readily available to the Company in the market. Non-financial additionality centers on the adoption of IFC's environmental and social Performance Standards.

project_description: The proposed investment is a package of €68.1 million to support the expansion of La Joie de Hicha S.A (“Hicha”), a subsidiary of Agro Care Projecten B.V. (“ACP” or the “Company”) in Tunisia. IFC would finance the second phase of the Hicha’s two-phase development in Akarit, Tunisia, which includes (i) the construction of glass greenhouses; (ii) a desalination plant; (iii) a combined heat and power system; and (iv) a warehouse.
sponsor_shareholders: Agro Care Beheer B.V. (“ACB”, “Sponsor”), a leading Dutch greenhouse tomato grower founded in 1997, based in Maasdijk, Netherlands. The main shareholders of ACB are NPM Capital N.V., Cornelis van Veen, Andrianus Phlipus J. Van. ACB owns 100% of ACP, which in turn owns ACP owns 88.4% of Hicha directly and indirectly while, Mr. Najib Zerrouk, a Tunisian entrepreneur, ultimately owns the remaining 11.6% in Hicha.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at up to €107 million. IFC’s proposed financing includes an A-loan of up to €39 million and a syndicated loan of up to €29.1 million
location_description: Hicha is located in Akarit, Tunisia, close to the Gabes area.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate positive environmental effects through improved water use efficiency as well as economy wide effects in terms of value added and job creation to the Tunisian economy. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will contribute to promoting the resilience of agribusiness sector in the country by demonstrating the feasibility of using desalinated water as an alternative water supply source for agriculture.
additionality: Financing structure: IFC is providing long-term financing which is not available locally for agribusiness companies at comparable terms to enable the Company to expand its operations. Resource mobilization: IFC will mobilize up to €30 million. Standard setting: IFC will support the Company on good international industry practices in line with IFC Performance Standards through implementation of the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP).

project_description: Maistra Hospitality Group (“MHG”, or the “Company”) is one of the leading tourism companies in Croatia. As part of its capital expenditure program for 2024-2027, the Company will invest in (i) the reconstruction of Hotel Marjan, a landmark property next to the UNESCO World Heritage Site in Split, and (ii) the refurbishment, upgrade, and merger of its campsites in Vrsar to establish Vrsar Holiday Village (together, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Maistra Hospitality Group combines two legal entities – Maistra d.d. and HUP-Zagreb d.d. The Company is the second largest owner and operator of hotels, resorts, and campsites in Croatia. Currently, it has 34 assets, ranging from budget to landmark, located along the Adriatic coast and in the capital, Zagreb.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at €343 million. It will be funded by a blue sustainability-linked senior secured loan of €200 million from IFC’s own account, and €143 million from MHG.
location_description: The Project is located in Vrsar (Istria region) and Split (Dalmatia region), Croatia.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects on suppliers based on increased and sustained business opportunities, (ii) employee effects through creating quality jobs and promoting skills development, and (iii) environmental effects through ambitious reduction of GHG emissions, improved resource efficiency of green buildings, and adoption of sustainable tourism practices. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment to promote sustainability in the tourism sector through demonstration and competition channels.
additionality: IFC will provide both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is in the form of an innovative financing instrument, a long-term blue sustainability-linked loan, which would be the first for MHG. IFC will also provide non-financial additionality by helping the Company to (i) set and achieve the sustainability targets under the Project, including identifying opportunities for resource efficiency gains, (ii) build internal capacity to access climate funding in the future, and (iii) support MHG in improving the environmental and social (E&S) systems and practices in line with IFC’s Performance Standards (PS).

project_description: IFC is providing support to MCS Mongolia (MCS or the Company), a strategic IFC client and the largest private sector group in Mongolia, in the completion of (i) a sustainable food production project that consists of an arable farm, a cattle feedlot and downstream processing; and (ii) A new green office tower planned for central Ulaanbaatar that will be known as ICC Tower.
sponsor_shareholders: MCS is one of the largest diversified business groups in Mongolia operating in (i) civil engineering, (ii) healthcare, (iii) information technologies, (iv) maintenance and security services, (v) agriculture, and (vi) real estate development. MCS also owns a 31% share in Mongolian Mining Corporation which is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. MCS was founded in 1993 by two brothers, MrOdjargalJambaljamts and Mr Od Jambaljamts. The founders own 88% of the company, and the remaining shares are owned by existing and former senior management. MCS Group has been a client of IFC since 2008.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment of up to US$60 million is comprised of a US$40.5 million A Loan and US$19.5 million syndicated loan from the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP).
location_description: The proceeds from the proposed Project will be deployed within Mongolia.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project level effects are (i) stakeholder effects through improved food security for consumers through increased access to quality, affordable and nutritious grain and meat products, (ii) environmental effects through the reduction in GHG emissions and improved resource efficiency provided by green buildings. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater resilience and competitiveness in the livestock and crop production subsectors.
additionality: IFC’s Additionality includes (i) longer term financing that is not readily available for the Company in the local market, and (ii) provision of IFC advisory services to support the education and training of Metagro's suppliers and the implementation of a supply chain management system for Metagro’s agricultural production operations.

project_description: The investment involves the purchase by IFC, for its own account, of unsecured debt instruments, in a principal amount of BRL300,000,000 with an up to 5 years tenor and bullet principal payment at maturity, issued in the Brazilian capital markets by Natura Cosméticos S.A. (Natura or the Company) (the Project). These debentures will be labelled as sustainability-linked debentures (in accordance with the Sustainability-Linked Bond Principles of 2023, issued by the International Capital Market Association – ICMA) with Natura committing to increase its sourcing from the Amazon to 49 new bioingredients by 2027, up from 44 ingredients as of 2023.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1969 in São Paulo, Brazil, Natura is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Natura & Co Holding S.A (Natura & Co), which is publicly traded on Brazil's B3 stock exchange. Natura & Co is under the control of five families, including the three co-founding families, which collectively hold 38% of Natura & Co’s shares. Of the remaining shares, 47% are freely traded on the stock market, while institutional investors (such as BlackRock, Dynamo, and Aikya, each holding approximately 5%) own the rest.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The issue was sized at BRL 1.326 billion with a coupon equal to 100% of the CDI rate plus a spread of 1.2%. The proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, with Natura allocating an amount at least equal to the proceeds from IFC's investment for (i) the development and sourcing of bioingredients from the Amazon, (ii) enhancements to manufacturing and distribution infrastructure at its Cajamar operations in the state of Sao Paulo, and (iii) the purchase of equipment for product line updates and growth, all within Brazil.
location_description: Brazil.
development_impact: Assessment of Project Outcomes - Supplier Effects. The Project is expected to stimulate the local supply chain through the development of novel Amazonian ingredients leveraging biodiversity and by scaling up procurement from the Amazonian bioeconomy. The Amazon rainforest constitutes a vital component of the Earth's natural infrastructure and plays a critical role in regulating the planet's climate system and biodiversity. Despite its ecological significance, Amazon rainforest has witnessed a rise in deforestation rates since 2012, with soybean production and cattle ranching identified as key contributors. Over the past two decades, Natura has cultivated a sustainable value chain within the Amazon biome through collaboration with small-scale agroextractivist communities. The Company sources nearly half of its raw materials from Amazonian suppliers, solidifying its model as a globally recognized example of economic use of the standing forest. Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation - Inclusiveness. At the market level, IFC expects that the Project will incentivize other companies to adopt sustainable sourcing practices from Amazon. This has the potential to unlock economic opportunities for marginalized populations within the region. Collaborating with small-scale agroextractivist communities can improve the livelihoods of these underserved groups, while simultaneously promoting sustainable practices that contribute to the well-being of the Amazon ecosystem.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project will be both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality is provided in the form of (i) resource mobilization, derived from mobilization of additional funding to support investments in the Amazon, attracting other professional investors through IFC’s role as an anchor investor, and (ii) an innovative financing instrument in the form of a sustainability-linked bond with sustainability performance targets linked to sourcing from the Amazon. Non-financial additionality will be provided in the form of (i) standard setting by providing guidance to Natura to adhere to best international environmental, health, and safety practices, and (ii) knowledge sharing and capacity building through an existing upstream engagement to support Natura’s suppliers.

project_description: IFC is proposing to provide Ayala Land, Inc. (ALI or the Company) with up to US$250 million equivalent in Philippine Pesos (PHP) in the form of an up to 8-years sustainability-linked loan (“SLL”). The IFC proceeds will be earmarked to refurbish a subset of ALI’s commercial property portfolio. The proposed SLL will help ALI to (i) establish the largest EDGE Zero Carbon portfolio globally; and (ii) reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
sponsor_shareholders: ALI is a leading property developer in the Philippines, with more than 11,000 hectares of land bank and a solid track record in developing large-scale, integrated, mixed-use, and sustainable estates. With a footprint spanning 52 estates nationwide, Ayala Land has a diverse real estate portfolio composed of developing residential, office, commercial and industrial properties for sale, as well as properties for lease such as shopping centres, offices, hotels, resorts, warehouses, co-living and co-working spaces. Additionally, Ayala Land is engaged in construction, property management and other property-related investments. ALI is listed on the Philippines Stock Exchange. ALI’s largest shareholder is Ayala Corporation, a diversified business conglomerate in the Philippines with operations in real estate, financial services, telecommunications, industrial technologies, power, infrastructure, healthcare, education, and technology ventures.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$250 million equivalent in Philippine Pesos (PHP) SLL with a tenor of up to 8 years to ALI.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Metro Manila, Philippines.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are (i) environmental effects through improved resource efficiency of green buildings and (ii) increased access to modern quality commercial space through substantial renovations of the shopping malls. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment will promote sustainability by facilitating the use of green financial products and adoption of green building standards.
additionality: Financial Additionality - Innovative Financing Structure: The IFC financing will be structured as a SLL, which is an underdeveloped instrument in the Philippines. IFC will act as the anchor (sole) investor in ALI's first SLL. Non-Financial Additionality - Knowledge, Innovation and capacity building: IFC will support the Company to develop and implement a robust sustainability-linked financing framework, and identify the assets and appropriate KPIs for the proposed SLL. IFC will also support the Company to attain EDGE certifications for its portfolio.

project_description: Summa Turizm Yatirimciligi A.S. (“Summa”, or the “Company”) is a Turkish contractor operating in 15 countries with a strong focus on Africa. Summa has four lines of business: (i) turn-key construction projects, (ii) investment projects such as shopping centers, hospitals, hotels etc., (iii) build-operate-transfer (“BOT”) and public private partnership (PPP) concessions/schemes, mainly for airports and hospitals and (iv) mining investments. The project entails financing of (i) a hotel investment in Senegal, and (ii) Summa’s working capital and capex need for its construction projects in African countries acceptable to IFC (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Summa’s current ownership structure is as follows: Mr. Selim Bora owns 42.41% shareholding; Mr. Sinan Bora owns 41.22% shareholding in Summa respectively. The remaining shares are owned by Mr. Osman Ozkan at 10.00%, and Mr. Okan Sargin at 6.37%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Approval IFC will provide an A Loan up to EUR50 million to finance the Project.
location_description: The hotel will be located in Diamniadio, Senegal.
development_impact: Project-level: (i) stakeholder effects: The Project is expected to create positive impact on (a) employees mainly through recruitment, and training, (b) suppliers via development of local supply chains for construction materials and technical services, and (c) customers via increased access to quality construction services in the target countries. (ii) economy-wide effects: The Project is expected to create jobs and economic value-add during construction and operational phases, as well as indirect effects across the construction services supply chain. Market impact: The Project is expected to contribute to competitiveness through support of a leading regional construction company to modernize, develop internal capacities, and expand its application in new geographies across the Sub-Saharan Africa.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide scarce long-term financing and enhance the Company’s access to complementary capital. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will help Summa improve its capacity in areas of E&S and corporate governance.

project_description: Shanghai Desano Bio-Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd (“Desano”, “the Company”) is a leading Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (“API”) and Finished Dosage Formulation (“FDF”) manufacturer in China, focusing on producing antiretroviral (“ARV”) drugs to address the global public health challenge of Human Immunodeficiency Viruses (“HIV”). The proposed investment is a US$100 million equivalent A loan to the Company’s subsidiaries to support: (i) the construction of a new API/FDF manufacturing facility in Bangalore, India, and (ii) the expansion of an existing API manufacturing facility in Jiangxi Province, China (a frontier region), for ARV drugs targeting low- and middle-income countries (the “Project”). The Project intends to play a key role in reducing the treatment cost of HIV patients globally and enhancing the resilience of pharmaceutical supply chain through localized production.
sponsor_shareholders: Desano is 54.28% directly and indirectly owned by its co-founder Shengping Xu. The rest is owned by employees and institutional private equity investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$150 million, which will be funded by the IFC loans of up to US$100 million equivalent in RMB with 7-year tenor and the Company’s internally generated cashflow.
location_description: The Project locations are in Jiangxi Province in China (a frontier region) and in Bangalore in India.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is an improvement in access to affordable and quality APIs and FDFs of ARV drugs in China, India and other developing countries, especially those used in the treatment of HIV. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that this investment will contribute to strengthening the resilience of the Chinese and Indian pharmaceutical markets, particularly for manufacturers of APIs and FDFs of ARV drugs, by demonstrating the Company’s business model of cost competitiveness in China and the localization of producing these products in India.
additionality: Financial additionality consists of the provision of long-term financing to support the Company’s expansion of production capacity in China and a cross-regional investment in constructing a manufacturing facility in India. Non-financial additionality is comprised of (i) knowledge, innovation, and capacity building, including information sharing on the local market for Desano’s overseas expansion in India; (ii) advisory on a group-wide insurance risk policy and risk management; (iii) supporting the Company in developing gender-related policies and practices to increase the proportion of women in its workforce and female board representation in both China and India and engagement in IFC’s women’s employment advisory project, India Gender Collaborative program, to leverage best practices, tools and workshops on gender and inclusion; and (iv) standard setting provided by supporting the Company in developing a comprehensive environmental and social (E&S) management system for its new facilities.

project_description: Ideal Development for Manufacturing Industries (“IDMI”, the “Company”, the “Client”) is a special purpose company established in 2021 to develop a minimum 2 million tons per annum (mtpa) greenfield phosphate rock beneficiation plant in Eshidiya, Jordan on a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT) basis (the Project). IDMI won its rights in a 2020 tender and signed its BOOT contract with Jordan Phosphates Mines Company (JPMC or the Off-taker), where JPMC is the sole off-taker of the final product.
sponsor_shareholders: IDMI is fully owned by Jordanians: (i) 50% by Lugain for Ideal Business Administration, (ii) 25% by Al Oudat for Consultation, and (iii) 25% by Mr. Rami Fakhouri (together “the Sponsors”).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC Investment will partially finance the Project’s cost of up to US$83 million. IFC may invest up to US$30 million in long-term A-Loan alongside a local commercial bank as a parallel lender. The long debt will have a tenor of up to 6.5 years, to be repaid in equal semi-annual installments. IFC may also invest up to US$4.0 million in equity or quasi-equity alongside the Sponsors.
location_description: The Project is located in Eshidiya, Jordan.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good, based on an AIMM score of 53. On an unadjusted basis (i.e., without the likelihood factor), the full potential AIMM score could reach 64. The most significant expected project-level outcomes are economy-wide effects through preservation of value-added and employment. Beyond Project-level outcomes, IFC’s investment will promote resilience in the food value chain through enabling the continued and reliable supply of fertilizers.
additionality: Summary: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via the Project's financing structure, not available in the local banking sector. Non-financial additionality is provided via standard setting. Financial Additionality: Financing structure: The proposed engagement will enable IFC to perform its countercyclical role in Jordan where liquidity is strained, especially for a greenfield project. IFC will provide a long-term USD-denominated corporate loan with a tenor of up to 6.5 years. Resource Mobilization: IFC will help mobilize a commercial loan equal in size and under the same terms as the IFC financing. Non-Financial Additionality: Standard-setting: Throughout the appraisal and supervision of the Project, IFC will share its expertise in environmental and social risk management, labor and working conditions, pollution prevention, and community health, safety, and security, and will be introducing international best practices to the client, in a context where domestic laws and/or market practice might not entirely enforce such practices.

company_name: Comercializadora PepsiCo S. de R.L. de C.V.
project_description: This project is proposed under IFC’s Global Trade Supplier Finance program (“GTSF” or the “Program”) approved by the IFC Board on September 21, 2010 (Original Project #28723) and an additional increase approved on December 15, 2022. Under GTSF, IFC provides short-term financing to suppliers, (“Suppliers”), in emerging markets selling to large companies, (“Buyers”), on open account terms. Under this project, IFC will provide financing to Comercializadora PepsiCo Mexico S. de RL de CV and other Mexican subsidiaries of PepsiCo (“PepsiCo Mexico” or “the Company”) that are based in Mexico and other emerging market countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Comercializadora PepsiCo Mexico S. de RL de CV and other Mexican subsidiaries of PepsiCo is a leading convenient food and beverage company in North America & Latin America, with a portfolio of iconic brands, including Cheetos, Doritos, Lay’s, Gamesa, Sabritas, and Tostitos.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project (‘the Project”) within the GTSF facility is expected to be US$75 million for PepsiCo Mexico’s Suppliers in Mexico and other emerging markets
location_description: GTSF-approved jurisdictions, including Mexico and other emerging market countries.
development_impact: Not Applicable
additionality: Not Applicable
Company Name: Comercializadora PepsiCo S. de R.L. de C.V.

project_description: B5 Plus is one of the largest manufacturers and suppliers of steel-related products in Accra, Ghana. The proposed investment is an up to US$50mln financing package to B5 Plus Limited (“B5 Plus” or “the Company”) to fund: (i) refurbishing and repurposing of a newly acquired Steel Plant at Tema Freezone to produce rebars and wire rod coil; (ii) installation of a wire rod mill at Tema Freezone; (iii) development of a 10 MW solar plant in the Prampram facility; and (iv) funding of working capital needs, together (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: B5 Plus was founded by Mukesh and Tanuja Thakwani (the “Sponsors”), who own 49% and 51% of the company respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$50mln and will be funded by IFC financing package of up to US$50mln.
location_description: The project sites are located at Tema, 30km south of Accra and Prampram,15 km of Tema / Republic of Ghana.
development_impact: Economy-wide effects: The Project will support domestic value addition in the iron and steel sector, and is expected to create about 1,900 direct jobs and a large number of indirect jobs (e.g., transportation, scrap handling, among others). The Project will conserve scarce foreign exchange reserves for the Ghanaian Government, by way of import substitution through increased local production of steel. Stakeholder effects: While customers will benefit from a broader range of steel products, the main effects on stakeholders will be on suppliers, mainly SMEs, and distributors working with the Company, who will benefit from additional scrap procurement and increased purchases of the finished product. The Project will also contribute to the abatement of pollution and reduced emissions of greenhouse gases, due to greater use of steel scrap in the production process, and the increase in the share of solar energy in the Company’s energy mix. Competitiveness: The adoption of more resource efficient manufacturing processes, and increase in higher value-added output, is expected to create competitive pressures on other market players in Ghana to upgrade the efficiency of their processes and business models, through direct effects on selling prices, or replication and demonstration effects.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing Structure: IFC is providing a long-term foreign currency funding, which is not easily available in the local market. Non-Financial Additionality: (i)E&S Standard Setting: IFC will help the client develop a comprehensive E&S management systems and procedures and align its operations with IFC Standards and industry best practices. The Company will set standards which will demonstrate best practices for the sector. (ii)Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC’s global experience in the steel sector will assist the Company, including work related to decarbonization and energy efficiency. The Project will serve as an example to the Ghanaian and African steel industry.

company_name: Gencau Sao Paulo -Industria e Comercio de Ingredientes Alimenticios Ltda
project_description: Gencau Sao Paulo Indústria e Comércio de Ingrediente Alimentícios Ltda. (“Gencau” or the “Company”) is a family-owned cocoa processing company which focuses on supplying traceable, sustainable, and high-quality cocoa products. Gencau is headquartered in Brazil with operations in the states of Pará, Bahia and Sao Paulo. IFC’s proposed investment will support Gencau’s growth in sustainable cocoa sourcing and processing (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Gencau was founded in 2019 by Ernesto Ary Neugebauer and current CEO Adriano Sartori Pedroso, who maintain full ownership together with their families.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of a preferred share instrument of up to US$8 million equivalent to support Gencau in (i) increasing its cocoa bean sourcing in the states of Pará and Bahia and (ii) expanding its processing capacity at its three cocoa processing facilities (the “Project”).
location_description: Investments will be made at Gencau’s facilities located in Medicilandia (state of Pará), Ibirapitanga (state of Bahia) and Tambaú (state of Sao Paulo).
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate positive climate mitigation effects by promoting agroforestry in the supply chain and provide access to market and technical assistance for farmer suppliers. At the market level, IFC expects the Project to increase the competitiveness of Brazil’s cocoa processing industry by supporting an innovative player focused on sustainability.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality comes from the provision of IFC own account equity. Non-financial additionality comes from standard setting in terms of supporting the Company to implement good practice E&S standards and corporate governance standards, as well as knowledge, innovation and capacity building in upstream work and risk management.
Company Name: Gencau Sao Paulo -Industria e Comercio de Ingredientes Alimenticios Ltda

project_description: FIBRA Macquarie Mexico (FIBRA MQ) is a publicly listed Mexican real estate investment trust with a US$1.3 billion market capitalization, headquartered in Mexico City that primarily focuses on the acquisition, development, leasing, and management of industrial real estate assets. The proposed project entails an up to US$150 million sustainability linked “A” loan with a tenor of up to seven years to FIBRA MQ to develop its 2023–2025 investment program in industrial parks. This includes the development of new green industrial assets in markets such as Mexico City Metropolitan Area, Monterrey, Ciudad Juarez, Reynosa, and Tijuana for a total of 2 million square footage in gross leasing area (GLA). It also includes energy efficiency upgrades in existing properties through IFC’s Green Pathways for Real Estate Institutional Portfolios (GRIP) decarbonization program (both capital expenditure and advisory initiatives together are defined as the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Fibra MQ is publicly listed with a US$1.3 billion market capitalization. Macquarie Asset Management Mexico S.A. de C.V. (MAM) has a 4.8% shareholding in Fibra MQ, with the remaining 95.2% being free float. The FIBRA is externally managed by the Macquarie Group through its asset management division and through MAM, a Mexican management company. The Macquarie Group is a reputable global asset manager of Australian origin, managing more than US$540 billion in total assets under management globally.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost stands at US$150 million consisting of a US$150 million A-Loan to finance FIBRA MQ’s 2023-2025 investment program in industrial parks.
location_description: FIBRA MQ is headquartered in Mexico City. The project is located in Mexico.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects on customers through increased access to high-quality industrial assets; and (ii) environmental effects through improved resource efficiency of green buildings. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater sustainability in Mexico's property sector. As one the largest industrial asset-focused FIBRAs, the potential portfolio-wide greening of Fibra MQ will provide a highly visible demonstration case and spur further competition among other institutional real estate players, which could have a catalytic impact on the industrial real estate market in the country.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the Project is both financial and non-financial. Through the Project, IFC will provide long-term financing with an innovative sustainability-link loan structure to support the Fibra MQ’s green expansion. In addition, IFC's support through GRIP would further enable Fibra MQ to tap into the climate finance market. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will help the Company develop a decarbonization strategy, build internal capacity to implement energy-efficient upgrades, and obtain green building certification for new and existing assets.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a senior secured sustainability-linked loan of up to INR 12,000 million (US$150 million equivalent) through subscription to non-convertible listed debt securities/ debentures to be issued by Mindspace Business Parks REIT (Mindspace or the MREIT). MREIT is a AAA (local rating) rated Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) and is one of India’s largest Grade A office portfolios spanning 26.3 million square feet (msf) of (completed) leasable area across 5 integrated business parks and 5 independent office buildings. It has a presence across the key business districts of Mumbai, Hyderabad, Pune and Chennai. K Raheja Corp Investment Managers Pvt. Ltd. has been appointed as the Manager to Mindspace REIT.
sponsor_shareholders: Mindspace Business Parks REIT is sponsored by Anbee Constructions LLP and Cape Trading LLP which are part of K Raheja Corp Group (KRC). KRC is one of the largest real estate developers in India. KRC is a leading player across commercial and residential real estate, retail destinations (through Shoppers Stop), malls (through Inorbit malls), and hospitality (through Chalet Hotels).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s debt investment of up to INR12,000 million (~US$150 million) will be used for general corporate purposes including for payment of fees and issue expenses, repayment of existing financial indebtedness, direct or indirect acquisition of properties and for providing loans to the SPVs for meeting their construction related expenses, working capital or general corporate requirements, repayment of their financial indebtedness, and/or acquisition of commercial properties directly or indirectly in accordance with Applicable Laws.
location_description: Mumbai, Hyderabad, Pune and Chennai
development_impact: By incentivizing MREIT to reduce GHG emissions and make its office properties more energy efficient, the Project will contribute to reducing the impact of climate change. The Project will also demonstrate and promote greater sustainability in the real estate sector in India.
additionality: IFC proposes to provide a long-term, innovative financing instrument that is not common in the Indian market especially in the real estate sector, in a relatively new asset class in India. IFC is also providing guidance on development of a Sustainability-Linked Financing Framework and on selection of Sustainability Performance Standards.

project_description: The Project consists of an investment by IFC in the form of an A loan of up to US$60 million equivalent in PT Gunung Rajapaksi Tbk (GRP or the Company). GRP is a leading steel producer in Indonesia involved in the production of crude steel from EAF to mainstream and downstream flat steel products. The Company primarily serves the growing domestic demand for steel in Indonesia. The Project will fund GRP’s capital expenditure to expand its upstream, middlestream and downstream capacity to produce coated steel, along with investments to increase energy efficiency. The climate component of the Project is assessed as 92 percent of the total Project cost, and the Project is aligned with the goals of the Paris Agreement.
sponsor_shareholders: Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) in September 2019, GRP has a market capitalization of IDR5.01 trillion (US$308 million) as of May 29th, 2024. The Company (under a different name) was founded by six siblings in 1970 in Medan, Sumatra Province and later moved to Jakarta in 1991. Currently, first- and second-generation members of the founding family, directly and indirectly own 90.3 percent of GRP shares. The remaining 9.7 percent is held by the public.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed financing will comprise up to US$60 million (equivalent in IDR) in the form of a senior-secured A loan with a seven-year maturity. The proposed investment will be used to fund capital expenditure and working capital needs associated with GRP’s flat steel business, including (i) downstream capacity expansion through the set-up of a new steel coating line; (ii) cost efficiency and productivity improvement measures related to existing?equipment; and (iii) scrap inventory.
location_description: The project location is at GRP’s manufacturing facility in Cikarang Barat, West Java Province, Indonesia.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good, based on an AIMM score of 53. On an unadjusted basis (i.e., without the likelihood factor), the full potential AIMM score could reach 64.
additionality: Financial Additionality? / Financing Structure: IFC will provide long-term 7-year funding with a 3-year grace period, which is difficult to obtain in the local market. The Company could only secure commercial financing with shorter tenors, which is not suitable for financing capex needs. Non-financial Additionality? / Standard setting: IFC is working with the Company to develop its E&S practices in line with WBG requirements especially around organizational and labor conditions and setting standards for the management of emissions and pollution.?

project_description: The proposed investment is a senior secured loan of up to INR 8,350 mn (approx. US$100 mn equivalent) to be provided towards Infopark Properties Limited (“IPL” or the “Company”) for refinancing of outstanding debt (the “Project”). The Ramanujan Intellion Park (formerly called “Ramanujan IT City” or “RITC” and hereinafter referred to as the “Project Asset”). The Ramanujan Intellion Park is a special economic zone (SEZ) in Chennai, mainly offering six Grade-A offices.
sponsor_shareholders: IPL is owned by Tata Realty and Infrastructure Limited (TRIL, 51% stake) and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB, 49% stake) (the “Sponsors”). TRIL, incorporated in 2007, is one of the leading real estate and infrastructure development companies in India.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment of INR 8,350 mn (US$ 100 mn) will be utilized for refinancing of the existing NCDs of INR 19,000 mn.
location_description: The Project location is in India.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project level effects are environmental effects through continued resource efficiency resulting from sustained adherence to green building certification. At the market level, The Project has the potential to promote the competitiveness of the Indian commercial real estate sector by incentivizing decarbonization efforts and adoption of internationally accepted green building standards.
additionality: IFC will provide financial additionality by providing long-term financing. IFC will also provide non-financial additionality by helping the company obtain EDGE certifications for the Project’s assets

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: The project entails a debt financing package of up to US$75 million to Li & Fung Limited (“L&F Limited”), Li & Fung (Trading) Limited (“L&F Trading”) and Air8 Pte. Ltd. (“Air8”) (L&F Trading and together with Air8 and L&F Limited, the “Borrowers”). Li & Fung is the world’s leading supply chain solutions partner. It specializes in responsibly managing supply chains of high-volume, time-sensitive goods for leading retailers and brands worldwide. Air8 is a supply chain financing solution provider, under LFX, focused on sustainability. The company connects SME suppliers with funders across borders, leveraging deep apparel and merchandise sector expertise, and promotes ESG asset creation to align funders’ capital with their ESG goals. The Project will support the Borrowers’ expansion of service offerings to its buyers and suppliers on supply chain solutions and supply chain financing for the benefit of suppliers in developing countries in Asia (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Borrowers are owned and controlled by Golden Lincoln Holdings II Limited (“GLH”). GLH is ultimately 60% controlled through voting power by Dr. William Fung and a trust set up for the benefits of the family members of Dr. Victor Fung (the “Fung Family”). By ownership, GLH is 30.14% owned by the Fung Family and 63.08% owned by GLP, a global real estate logistics provider and investment manager based in Singapore. The remaining 6.78% is owned by JD.com, a leading e-commerce platform based in China.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated to be US$150 million and IFC is proposing a debt financing package of up to US$75 million.
location_description: The Project will be located amongst developing countries in Asia.
development_impact: Project-level Impact - Stakeholder effects: The Project will provide increased access to finance for suppliers, mainly for SMEs. Emerging market suppliers will have greater access to finance, thereby optimizing their working capital and improve business efficiency. Market-level Impact - Resilience: The Project will support suppliers to become more resilient by providing a cost-competitive financing solution that enhances transparency and visibility over the industry’s value chain.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is in the form of: (a) Financing Structure: IFC will provide the Borrowers (i) long-term financing to fund their long-term growth, thereby increasing its service offerings, and (ii) long-term financing to accelerate the supply chain financing program and help alleviate the working capital challenges faced by suppliers. (b) Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will share its experience in emerging market trade finance with the Borrowers. IFC can also connect textile clients to the Borrowers, which may facilitate future partnerships. (c) Standard Setting: IFC will share international E&S best practices with the Borrowers, which will raise the E&S performance of suppliers working with the Borrowers.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment will support Minth Group Limited (“Minth” or the “Company”), a leading auto parts manufacturer to set up electric vehicle (“EV”) battery housing production facilities in Serbia and Poland (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Minth's is publicly listed in the Hong Kong Stock Exchange and the Company's controlling shareholders are Mr. CHIN Jong Hwa and his wife Ms. WEI Ching Lien who collectively hold 38.7% of the shares. The rest is public float.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is part of Minth’s EUR598 million capital expenditure program to establish the Company’s auto parts manufacturing base in Europe. IFC is providing a financing package of up to EUR200 million which includes an 8-year A loan up to EUR200 million to be supported by up to EUR100 million credit insurance and up to EUR21.5 million MCPP loan.
location_description: Loznica and Sabac, Serbia; Szprotawa, Poland
development_impact: Project-level outcomes are: (i) increased employment and value addition in Serbia’s and Poland’s economies through the near-shoring of a strategic automotive component for the transition to sustainable mobility, and (ii) the upskilling of the workforce in advanced manufacturing technologies. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to: (i) fast-track significant improvements in the resilience of the European EV ecosystem, by helping near-shore the production of a critical component in EV battery systems, and lowering reliance on a few global suppliers, and (ii) to unlock high gains in economic complexity, in particular for Serbia.
additionality: (i) IFC will provide long tenor financing package for the Company to set up new facilities in Serbia and Poland. (ii) IFC will help arrangement mobilization to unlock additional capital to fund the Project. (iii) IFC will share knowledge and best practices in the E&S management systems. (iv) IFC intends to support the Company’s future plans to build an aluminum value chain in Serbia.

country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: The proposed IFC investment comprises three loans totaling up to US$315 million equivalent (“the Project”) to three subsidiaries (the “Borrowers”) of Cormoran de Bilbao S.L. (“Roemmers” or the “Group”). The Project will be committed over a period of two years in the form of three senior secured corporate loans, including: (i) a US$45 million loan to be disbursed in USD to Laboratorios Siegfried S.A.S. (“Siegfried Colombia”) and Laboratorios Siegfried S.A. (“Siegfried Panama”) to partially finance the acquisition of Activa, S.A de C.V., Activa Energy, S.A. de C.V., and Activa Guatemala, S.A. de C.V. (together “Pharmedic”), a pharmaceutical manufacturing company based in El Salvador with operations in Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua (“Phase 1”), (ii) a US$20 million to be disbursed in Colombian Pesos (c. COP 78.0 billion) to Siegfried Colombia, of which US$5 million (c. COP 19.5 billion) will be own account and US$15 million (c. COP 58.5 billion) mobilized to support its capacity expansion in Colombia through the construction of a new manufacturing facility (“Phase 2”), and (iii) a US$250 million loan to be disbursed in Mexican Pesos (c. MXN 4.2 billion) to Siegfried Rhein, S.A. de C.V. (“Siegfried Mexico”), of which US$100 million (c. MXN 1.7 billion) will be own account and US$150 million (c. MXN 2.5 billion) mobilized, to support the construction of a new manufacturing facility in Mexico and potential acquisitions in Mexico (“Phase 3”). Siegfried Colombia, a fully owned subsidiary of Roemmers, is a leading pharmaceutical company focused on the development, manufacture and commercialization of over-the-counter medicines, prescription drugs and personal care products (mostly branded generics). With two manufacturing plants in Colombia and 840 employees, Siegfried Colombia is focused mainly on cardio, neuro, women’s health, and primary care therapeutic areas. Approximately 95% of Siegfried Colombia’s revenues are generated in Colombia, and the rest is exported to Central America, Ecuador, and Peru. Founded 45 years ago, Siegfried Mexico is a Mexico-based, pharmaceutical company fully owned by Roemmers focused on the development, manufacture, and commercialization of branded generic medicines. Siegfried Mexico (and its affiliates in Mexico) owns two manufacturing facilities located in Queretaro, Mexico. It is one of the leading domestic pharmaceutical companies in Mexico, primarily focused on prescription generics, with a portfolio of over 100 brands covering the following therapeutic areas: analgesics, antibiotics, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, women’s health, central nervous system, and pediatrics. The Company has one of the largest pharmaceutical sales forces in Mexico and employs more than 1,600 people.
sponsor_shareholders: The Borrowers are fully-owned by Grupo Roemmers (“Roemmers”), one of the largest pharma players in LAC based in Argentina with operations in twelve countries. Roemmers’ shareholders are: Pablo Roemmers - 49 percent; Alberto Roemmers - 49 percent; and Alejandro Roemmers – 2 percent. On August 2018, IFC committed a US$31 million Senior Loan to finance the expansion of Roemmers’ in Brazil (Farmoquimica, IFC/R2017-0341), on January 2019, IFC committed a US$75 million Senior Loan to Siegfried Mexico (IFC/R2018-0346), and on April 2022, IFC committed a US$30 million Senior Loan to Siegfried Colombia and Siegfried Panama (IFC/R2022-0041).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost is estimated at approximately US$338 million (US$68 million for Phase 1, US$20 million for Phase 2 and US$250 million for Phase 3). The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$315 million facility to be committed over a period of two years in the form of three senior secured corporate loans (US$45 million for Phase 1, US$20 million for Phase 2, and US$250 million for Phase 3) of which US$150 million is own account and US$165 million mobilized through B or parallel lenders.
location_description: El Salvador, Colombia and Mexico.
development_impact: The project has an AIMM rating of Excellent, based on an AIMM score of 74. On an unadjusted basis (i.e., without the likelihood factor), the full potential AIMM score could reach 88. The most significant expected project-level outcome is an increase in access to affordable and quality pharmaceutical products in Central American countries, through increased production and introduction of new products in Colombia, Mexico and several Central America (CA) countries. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that this investment will promote competitive pressures in the pharmaceutical markets in Colombia and Central America, by scaling output through an important pharmaceutical manufacturer and introducing more pharmaceutical products in these markets.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC will support the expansion of a family-owned regional pharmaceutical group to ensure the sustained availability of affordable and quality health products in the LAC region. IFC’s additionality in this Project comes in the following forms: financing structure and resource mobilization, providing global industry expertise and knowledge related to enhancing resource efficiency and gender equality, and expertise and knowledge through monitoring the development and implementation of an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS), in line with IFC Performance Standard (PS) requirements.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: IFC's proposed project consists of an investment package of up to US$40 million of equity in Actis Asia Climate Transition Fund (the “Fund” or “AACT”), a Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) Article 9 classified infrastructure fund focused on the reduction of greenhouse-gas emissions as a path to net zero by investing in renewable energy infrastructure, energy solutions and sustainable transportation primarily in emerging markets across the Asia-Pacific region.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by Actis GP LLP (“Actis”), a leading private equity investor in emerging markets.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is a proposed equity commitment of up to US$40 million for IFC’s account.
location_description: The Fund will make investments across various countries in South / Southeast Asia.
development_impact: The Fund will address climate mitigation by investing in projects that facilitate the transition to a low-carbon future. The fund will achieve this by developing renewable energy and other emerging technologies such as energy storage, alternative fuels, smart-meters, cooling-as-a-service, and EV charging infrastructure. Beyond the project, raising of a new dedicated sustainability fund will send a strong signal by demonstrating the commercial viability of sustainability focused investing and attract sustainability-linked institutional investment into these regions.
additionality: IFC’s financial additionality will support Actis to close its first climate strategy fund and reach sufficient final scale to develop a well-structured portfolio. The thematic areas of energy efficiency and sustainable transport are still in an early stage of development within the region and dedicated sustainability funds as yet receive limited interest from commercial investors at sufficient scale for funds such as AACT to raise without DFI support. IFC will also provide non-financial additionality by drawing from its experience in energy markets and sustainable investing to support AACT provide greater value added to its investee companies.

project_description: CapitaLand India Trust (CLINT or the Trust) is a prominent commercial real estate trust in India, with a portfolio of 19.6 million square feet of completed properties, comprising nine business parks, one logistics park, and three industrial facilities and is listed on the Singapore Exchange (“SGX”). IFC is proposing to invest up to 200 million Singapore dollars (approximately US$150 million) to the Trust through CLINT’s trustee-manager, CapitaLand India Trust Management Pte. Ltd. (the Trustee-Manager).
sponsor_shareholders: CLINT is managed by the Trustee-Manager, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Singapore-listed CLI, a leading global real estate investment manager that is part of the CapitaLand group and one of Asia’s largest diversified real estate groups, owning and managing real estate assets in several countries. CLI is also listed on the SGX.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a sustainability-linked unsecured loan of up to 200 million Singapore dollars (approximately US$150 million ) to CLINT through the Trustee-Manager.
location_description: The Project Location will be India spread across office parks in 5 cities of Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai, and Pune.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level effects are environmental effects through reduced GHG emissions and improved resource efficiency. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the proposed investment will increase access to sustainable office space in India promoting greater sustainability in India's real estate sector through a demonstration and replication.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project stems from both financial and non-financial aspects. IFC's financial additionality stems from the tenor and nature of the SLL, which is not readily available in the market. Non-financial additionality is through knowledge sharing and capacity building. IFC will provide essential support to CLINT to enhance its sustainability strategy, by helping to design a sustainability-linked financing framework and selecting specific sustainability KPIs and SPTs for the SLL.

company_name: JERONIMO MARTINS COLOMBIA S A S
project_description: Ara Tiendas (“Ara”), a chain of neighborhood retail stores in Colombia, has requested IFC to provide a long-term loan to partially finance the construction of two distribution centers which will be EDGE-Advanced certified (the “Project’) to provide logistic support to its stores.
sponsor_shareholders: Jeronimo Martins SGPS SA is a Portugal-based group engaged mainly in the food retail business. The Group focuses on distribution and sale of food and other consumer good products, employing more than 134,000 people across 3 countries – Portugal, Poland and, Colombia –. The Group owns a portfolio of brands in these countries, including Biedronka and Hebe in Poland; Pingo Doce and Recheio in Portugal and Ara Tiendas in Colombia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to provide an A loan of up to US$120 million in local currency to partially finance this investment plan.
location_description: The Project will be developed in the Bogota and Cali regions of Colombia.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to increase customer access to affordable and high-quality retail services, meeting the increasing demand for more affordable retail services in Colombia, environmental effects, as well as significant economy-wide effects through the creation of direct jobs and increased demand for goods and services from local businesses. At the market level, IFC expects the Project to contribute to improving the competitiveness of the grocery retail market, especially the discount segment, in Colombia through demonstration channels.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project will be both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality will be provided through the provision of long-term financing which is not readily available for the retail sector in Colombia. Non-financial additionality comes from IFC assistance in building the capacity in the areas of green buildings and green loans.
Company Name: JERONIMO MARTINS COLOMBIA S A S

project_description: Good Karma Group of Companies Private limited (“Holding Company”, “Parent Company”) has undertaken the construction and development of a greenfield apartment complex in Kathmandu Nepal totalling 186 apartments, of which 56 serviced apartments are proposed to be operated by Marriott International (the “Operator”, ”Marriott”) and the balance 130 apartments will be sold to the general public. The 56 serviced apartments (the “Project”) will be owned by the sponsors under a 100% subsidiary company of the Parent Company named Good Karma Hospitality Pvt. Ltd. (“Company”).
sponsor_shareholders: Good Karma Hospitality Pvt. Ltd., incorporated in February 2024, is 100% subsidiary of the Parent Company. The Parent Company, incorporated in September 2020, is 100% owned by Mr. Karma Tenzing and his siblings. The shareholding structure is: Mr. Karma Tenzing (53.3%); his brother Mr. Mukhia Gurung (36.7%); and his sister Ms. Sonam Gurung (10.0%) (collectively the “Sponsors”).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to fund upto US$7 million to finance the 56 serviced apartments to be owned by the Sponsors under Borrowing Company and operated by Marriott.
location_description: The Project location is Maharajgunj, Kathmandu, Nepal.
development_impact: Summary: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are (i) Economy-wide effects through employment creation and value addition and (ii) environmental effects through its impact on GHG emissions reduction. At the market level, it will improve the competitiveness of the Nepal tourism industry. Project Outcomes Economy-wide effects: The Project, which supports the development of serviced apartments in Kathmandu is expected to have various positive economy-wide effects, including direct job creation, contribution to GDP, and higher tax revenues for the government. It is anticipated that the Marriot serviced apartments will employ about 48 people for its operations and about 80 people during its construction phase. The construction and operation of the apartments is expected to create opportunities for local suppliers including those specializing in cements, steel, blocks, tiles, plumbing and other related services. Environmental effects: The Project will support resource efficiency initiatives of a leading player in Nepal, including deployment of energy friendly technology and equipment, and the obtention of EDGE certifications, thereby reducing the overall GHG emissions of the apartments. Additionally, given Nepal’s sustainability to earthquakes, the company has adopted Seismic Damper walls across the building to enhance its structural resilience, becoming the first residential apartment building in the country to do so. Contribution to Market Creation Competitiveness: This Project will improve competitiveness of the tourism market in Nepal by introducing a new long-stay offering and attracting new developments and investments into the segment through demonstration and replication channels. It supports current efforts to diversify product offerings in Nepal’s tourism industry through the introduction of a branded serviced apartments to meet the needs of a different class of tourists that are currently not served by existing hotels.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing structure: IFC will provide a long-term loan (12 years) with an extended grace (4 years), which is not readily available for the company in the local market. Non-Financial Additionality: Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: Through this engagement, IFC will help the company improve its capacity in the areas of (i) management contract negotiations (ii) labor standards (iii) corporate governance and (iv) green and resilient buildings. Standard setting: IFC will help the company improve its E & S standards, in line with IFC’s performance standards.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to IDR 851 billion (US$53 million equivalent) sustainability-linked loan (SLL) facility to various subsidiaries of PT Nirvana Wastu Pratama (NWP or the Company) with a maturity of up to 11 years. The loan will be used for the refinancing of NWP’s retail mall and hotel property assets in Indonesia. NWP is a rapidly expanding consumer real estate platform focused on retail and logistics properties in Indonesia. It currently has 53 properties – 36 in operation and 17 under development – with a combined gross floor area (GFA) of 1.24 million square meters (sqm) upon completion. NWP is backed by strong institutional investors, led by Warburg Pincus (majority ownership of 54%), a leading global private equity firm with a proven track record of investing in Asia real estate across multiple asset classes.
sponsor_shareholders: NWP was established in 2015 as a joint venture between Warburg Pincus (through its affiliate, Adventure Holdings BV) and PT City Retail Developments Tbk, a publicly listed company on the Indonesian Stock Exchange. In 2019, NWP raised an additional US$200 million equity from Warburg Pincus, Korean Teacher's Credit Union (KTCU), and CITIC, of which the transaction formed the current ownership structure with Warburg Pincus becoming the largest controlling shareholder with a 53.78% stake in the Company. Currently, the Company’s shareholding is as follow: (i) Warburg Pincus – 53.78%, (ii) PT City Retail Developments Tbk – 32.48%, (iii) KTCU – 10.30%, and (iv) CITIC – 3.44%. Warburg Pincus is a leading global private equity firm with a proven track record of investing in Asia real estate across multiple asset classes. Today, Warburg Pincus is a globally integrated private partnership focused solely on private equity with more than US$84 billion in assets under management (AUM) and US$62 billion in total assets. Warburg Pincus' Asia real estate AUM stands at approximately US$7 billion.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at US$106 million which will be funded by (i) the proposed IFC A Loan of up to US$53 million, and (ii) financing from other financial institution.
location_description: The Project will be located across several provinces in Indonesia, including Greater Jakarta, East Kalimantan, West Kalimantan, South Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan, and South East Sulawesi.
development_impact: The main expected project-level outcomes are environmental effects via improved energy and water use efficiency. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote sustainability in the Indonesian retail property sector via demonstration and replication channels. Supporting a leading retail developer in Indonesia to green its portfolio will provide a highly visible demonstration case which could have a catalytic impact on the retail and logistics property market in the country.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the proposed Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality will be provided via a long-term financing structure that is not readily available in the market. Non-financial additionality will be provided via knowledge innovation and capacity building to help the company improve its standards to achieve EDGE certifications.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a US$30 million financing package, to support Grupo Zilor (“Zilor” or the “Group”), a leading sugar, ethanol, and renewable energy producer in Brazil, with three mills located in the Sao Paulo state. The investment will support the expansion of its cogeneration capacity in one of its plants called Barra Grande from 62.9 MW to 142.9 MW (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1946, the Group owns three mills with a combined installed capacity to crush up to 12.3 million tons of sugarcane per year while employing 3,581 people. Zilor is a member of the sugar and ethanol cooperative and trader, Copersucar, which commercializes 100% of its sugar and ethanol production. In addition, the Group sells energy directly to the grid and has a business line focused on the production of yeast-based natural ingredients for human consumption and animal nutrition. Zilor is majority owned by the Zillo family, with a 71% shareholding interest, and the remaining 29% is held by the Lorenzetti family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The investment plan is estimated at US$60 million, for which IFC will provide an A Loan of up to US$30 million equivalent. The remaining portion was financed through a debenture issuance in July 2022.
location_description: The Project is located in the Sao Paulo state, Brazil, in the Lencois Paulista municipality, where the Barra Grande mill is located.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good, based on an AIMM score of 58. On an unadjusted basis (i.e., without likelihood factor), the full potential AIMM score could reach 64. IFC expects the Project to have climate mitigation effects through expanding the Company’s electricity cogeneration using biomass and increasing the sale of renewable energy to the grid. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing will contribute to promoting resilience in Brazil’s power sector through diversification of electricity generation sources.
additionality: The proposed IFC loan has both financial and non-financial additionality. The financial additionality stems from the provision of long-term financing with seven years to eight-year tenor that are not available to the Company in the market. Non-financial additionality centers on the adoption of IFC’s environmental and social PS.

company_name: INDORAMA VENTURES GLOBAL SERVICES COMPANY LIMITED
project_description: The proposed investment is for an IFC A loan of up to US$250 million to Indorama Ventures Global Services Limited (IVGS or the “Company”). In 2020, IFC had provided a US$300 million loan package consisting of a US$150 million IFC A loan and parallel loans of US$150 million from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Deutsche Investitions- und Entwicklungsgesellschaft (DEG) to IVGS (Board reference no. IFC/R2014-0206). IVGS, incorporated in Thailand is a subsidiary of Indorama Ventures Public Company Limited (“IVL” or the “Group”), is one of the world’s leading intermediate petrochemicals producers, with a global manufacturing footprint across Africa, Asia Pacific, Europe and Americas. The Company’s product portfolio is classified into 3 segments: Combined PET (CPET), Integrated Oxides & Derivatives (IOD) and Fibers.
sponsor_shareholders: IVL is a global intermediate petrochemical producer and one of the largest vertically integrated polyester value chain producers in the world, serving global brands in diversified end-use markets including food, beverages, mobility, personal care and health care. IVL is headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand, and geographically diversified with over 147 operating sites in 33 countries across five continents and employs over 26,000 employees. IVL is a publicly listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand. The Lohia Family (SP Lohia and his brother Aloke Lohia), are the largest shareholders of IVL with a 64.75% holding while the balance 35.25% of the shares are held by institutional and retail shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$250 million and will be funded with an IFC A Loan of up to US$250 million.
location_description: The Project will be implemented across IVL’s existing and planned manufacturing facilities in Thailand, Indonesia and India.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects, where the Project aims to fulfil the demand for recycled PET; (ii) economywide effects, where the Project seeks to create value through a circular economy of PET waste and create employment; and (iii) environmental effects, where the Project diverts plastic waste away from environment and channels them to recycling processes. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the potential to encourage more PET bottle producers to establish recycling operations.
additionality: Financial: IFC will provide a long-term A loan to meet the long payback period typically required for such projects. Non-financial: IFC has supported IVL in developing its first “Blue Loan Framework,” which was externally certified to cover the financing of future IVL plastic circular economy projects. IFC will continue to support IVL in other knowledge areas.
Company Name: INDORAMA VENTURES GLOBAL SERVICES COMPANY LIMITED

project_description: Mapletree Investments Pte Ltd (Mapletree) is a global real estate development, investment, and management company headquartered in Singapore. Mapletree is now developing green Grade A warehousing infrastructure in Viet Nam (the Project), which will be executed by a private fund platform to be established by Mapletree (the Fund). The proposed investment is an A Loan of up to US$250 million to support the Fund in developing and constructing modern logistics warehousing assets in Viet Nam, all of which are expected to achieve green building certifications. Additionally, IFC will mobilize parallel loans of up to US$350 million on a best-efforts basis to finance the Fund’s development activities in India and/or Viet Nam.
sponsor_shareholders: The proposed investment is expected to be provided to certain special purpose vehicles incorporated in Singapore and Viet Nam directly and indirectly owned by the Fund.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed financing package comprises of an A Loan of up to US$250 million, and Parallel Loan of up to US$350 million.
location_description: The Project location will be in Viet Nam.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project level effects are (i) stakeholder effects through increased access to quality logistics space in the target cities, and (ii) environmental effects through the reduction in GHG emissions and improved resource efficiency. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater sustainability in the commercial real estate sector in Vietnam.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via a long-term financing structure and resource mobilization. Non-financial additionality is provided through technical assistance on enhancing E&S standards and green buildings.

company_name: LATAMCC Fund Manager Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V
project_description: The Project involves an IFC senior loan of MXN 2,940 million (~US$ 175 million) from IFC’s own account to a group of trusts associated with 6 individual residential properties managed by LATAMCC Fund Manager Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V (“CCLA” or the “Company”), a real estate asset manager. The proposed project aims to support the development, construction, and rental operation of 6 high rise multifamily residential, 4 in the Mexico City area and 2 in Monterrey, to be EDGE/EDGE Advance certified. Once construction is completed on each project, CCLA will manage the rental operations through its wholly owned Nomad Living entity.
sponsor_shareholders: CCLA develops and operates high-quality residential housing for multifamily rent in Latin America. It was co-founded in 2015 by CIM Group (50 percent), with vast experience in US multifamily, and Compass Group (50 percent), an asset manager focused on Latin America.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost of MXN 6,319 million (~US$ 375 million) will be financed by a combination of the IFC loan of MXN 2,940 million (~US$ 175 million) and the remaining with CCLA managed equity.
location_description: Four properties will be located in the Mexico City area and two in Monterrey, Mexico.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects via increased access to quality housing (ii) environmental effects via improved efficiency in energy and water usage as a result of EDGE certification for properties identified under this project. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment to promote competitiveness and sustainability in the Mexican housing sector.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the proposed Project is both financial and non-financial. IFC will provide scarce long-term financing to the Company that is not otherwise readily available in the local market and allow it to diversify funding sources. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will provide technical guidance to the Company to develop capability in green buildings.
Company Name: LATAMCC Fund Manager Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to US$12 million loan to Sierra Leone Flour Mill Limited (“SLFM” or the “Company”) guaranteed by BSB International Limited (“BSB” or the “Guarantor”, together with SLFM referred to as the “Group”) to support SLFM’s US$19.2 million project for the expansion of its (i) milling capacity from 150 metric tons (MT) of wheat per day to 450 MT and (ii) storage capacity from 8,400 MT to 28,400 MT at its factory located in Cline Town, Freetown, Sierra Leone (the “Project”). The Project may be supported by the Canada-IFC Facility for Resilient Food Systems (Canada FRFS”), subject to obtaining the necessary internal approvals, as described in the Blended Finance section.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Amadu Juldeh Sowe, the Founder and CEO, is a seasoned entrepreneur in Sierra Leone with over 35 years’ experience in business management and development. He owns 100% of SLFM and BSB.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$19.2 million. The proposed investment is a US$6 million IFC A Loan and a US$6 million concessional loan from Canada FRFS.
location_description: The Project is located in Cline Town in Freetown (Sierra Leone).
development_impact: Project-level Impact: Project Outcome: The Project will increase consumer access to (fortified) wheat products and therefore contribute to food security and nutrition in Sierra Leone where prevalence of undernutrition, stunting and wasting is high. Protein intake per capita and day is also low. IFC expects the Project will increase value addition and create direct and indirect jobs along the Project’s supply chain. Market Outcome: The Project will increase resilience in the market by building capacity in the Company’s supply chain to withstand shocks and stresses related the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and climatic change affecting cereals production. This is expected to have significant impact as the Company is a major player in food distribution in the country.
additionality: Financial additionality – Financing structure: IFC will provide a long-term loan with a sufficient grace period, which is not readily available to agribusinesses in the local market. The loan will be structured to fit the expansion project that needs sufficient time for preparation and ramp-up. Non-financial additionality – Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC will provide technical, environmental, and social (E&S), health, and safety expertise to improve overall environmental and safety performance, to align the Company's operations with IFC performance standards and industry best practices.

company_name: CONSEIL REGIONAL DE GUELMIM OUED NOUN
project_description: The proposed investment consists of up to US$40 million loan or its equivalent in Euros to Region Guelmim-Oued Noun (RGON), one of the 12 Regions of Morocco, to support and co-finance capital expenditure projects included in its current and previous Regional Development Programs (RDP) (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project’s sponsor and borrower of the proposed IFC financing is the Region of Guelmim-Oued Noun.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s financing consists of up to US$40 million or its equivalent in Euros for IFC’s own account. The proceed of the loan will partially fund capital expenditure projects included in the Region’s RDP.
location_description: The Project is located in the Region of Guelmim-Oued Noun, Kingdom of Morocco.
development_impact: The expected project-level outcome is driven by the positive effects on stakeholders, achieved through enhancing the quality of the Region’s infrastructure, enhancing accessibility and coverage of critical urban infrastructure as well as upgrading existing assets. This investment will also support the objectives of the Regional Development Program aiming to generate 50,000 jobs, play an important role in reducing unemployment, while also directly contributing to enhancing the Region’s GDP. Beyond the Project, at the market level, this investment is expected to contribute towards further opening of Morocco’s subnational infrastructure financing to private investors by providing a continued strong commitment and signal for potential participants.
additionality: IFC’s financial additionality is derived from providing long-term, non-sovereign guaranteed, debt financing, which is not available to sub-national entities in Morocco from commercial sources. IFC’s non-financial additionality is driven by standard setting through assisting the Region improve its E&S systems in line with IFC Performance Standards and strengthen its institutional capacity through long term advisory engagement.
Company Name: CONSEIL REGIONAL DE GUELMIM OUED NOUN

project_description: The Project consists of a corporate debt facility to OCP SA (“OCP” or the “Company,” https://www.ocpgroup.ma/) for the design and construction of a 219km pipeline to bring the desalinated water produced in OCP’s existing and future desalination plants in Jorf Lasfar to reservoirs located near its extraction sites in Khouribga (the “Project”). With a capacity of 80 million m3 p.a., the pipeline is designed to transfer desalinated water to several discharge locations at Beni Amir Expansion, Khouribga Basin and Beni Amir wash plant. The Project is part of OCP’s sustainability strategy that aims to supply 100% of its water needs from non-conventional sources by 2024.
sponsor_shareholders: OCP SA, a state-owned enterprise, is a fully integrated phosphate fertilizer producer with operations at every stage from mining to processing to sales of phosphate products. The Company is the largest producer and exporter of phosphate rock and phosphoric acid globally. OCP’s shareholders are the Moroccan State and other minority shareholders with, respectively, 94.1% and 5.9% ownership. OCP SA (“OCP” or the “Company,” https://www.ocpgroup.ma/) launched in 2022 its green investment program, with clear objectives to (i) supply OCP with 100% non-conventional water by 2024, (ii) ensure the supply of drinking water to neighboring towns, and (iii) engage in the development of high value-added agricultural activities.
