The Project will be implemented by OCP, through its 100%-owned subsidiary OCP Green Water.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at approximately US$486 million. The proposed IFC investment comprises up to EUR 100m A-Loan for IFC’s Own Account.
location_description: The Project pipeline will be installed between Jorf Lasfar and Khouribga, mostly following the same route as the slurry pipeline owned and currently operated by OCP.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome lies in the increased accessibility of desalinated water serving OCP operations, agriculture needs, and the surrounding communities along with the associated positive environmental effects. Beyond the Project, IFC’s financing will contribute to increasing resilience in the water sector to future shocks in Morocco and support the use of non-conventional water sources at large scale
additionality: IFC’s additionality is in the form of: (i) Financing structure; (ii) Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building; and (iii) E&S standard-setting.

project_description: The proposed project consists of an equity investment of up to $50 million in PI Fund V (Ontario), L.P. (or any parallel fund or feeder fund, together PIF V or the Fund), controlled by Patria Investments Limited (“Patria), a leading investment firm in Latin America and the Caribbean (“LAC”). PIF V will make equity investments in a diversified portfolio of infrastructure assets across LAC, aiming to address infrastructure bottlenecks, gaps, and inefficiencies to serve the growing needs of the population and businesses while bolstering a wider use of international best practices in Environmental & Social (“E&S”) standards.
sponsor_shareholders: Patria was established in 1988 and is one of the largest fund managers in Latin America with assets under management of $31.8 billion as of December 2023. Listed on the Nasdaq Stock Exchange (ticker - PAX), Patria has a global presence with offices in 10 cities across four continents. With 18 years of operating infrastructure experience, Patria has managed five infrastructure specific funds with ~$5.4 billion of committed capital to 30 infrastructure projects.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund was launched with a target size of $2.5 billion. IFC’s proposed investment is for up to $50 million in equity in PIF V.
location_description: LAC with a focus on Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Mexico, and Chile
development_impact: Stakeholders: Increased access to private equity capital and value creation for infrastructure projects across LAC. Patria will target investments that address infrastructure bottlenecks, gaps, and inefficiencies within the LAC region. Competitiveness: Strengthening the competitiveness of the infrastructure equity market in LAC, through supporting the expansion of private equity financing. IFC's support to Patria will demonstrate the ability for infrastructure equity funds to scale up and demonstrate sustained commercial viability, attracting greater institutional investors into infrastructure equity in LAC.
additionality: Financial Own account equity: Patria recognizes IFC's role as a reference investor, catalyzing investments from a new investor base. In recent years, macro-uncertainty and high-risk perception has led to many investors leaving the LAC market, making fundraising for regional mandate funds more challenging. Attracting new institutional investors is required for Patria to reach the target size of Fund V. Resource mobilization: IFC will assist Patria in mobilizing capital from institutional investors and other Development Finance Institutions by providing Patria insight into institutional investors' requirements and helping strengthen the Fund's ESG practices. Non-Financial Knowledge, capacity building: Patria values IFC as a strategic partner and will seek IFC's feedback on sensitive and critical issues. IFC may also introduce experts, key stakeholders, IFC Industry Specialists, etc., and/or provide Advisory/Upstream services for initiatives that require regulatory considerations. Standard setting: IFC will identify gaps in the Fund's E&S standards, support the implementation plan, and work with Patria to strengthen and integrate its climate/Paris Alignment strategy.

project_description: The proposed investment comprises (i) an equity investment of up to MAD410 million (approximately US$41 million equivalent) in Retail Holding SA (RH, or Group); and (ii) an equity investment of up to US$15 million in Compagnie de Distribution de Cote d'Ivoire (CDCI). This will support the Group's operations through (i) the purchase of a minority stake of common shares in the Group from exiting financial investors alongside other investors and (ii) the subscription of common shares in CDCI to finance an organic expansion plan. IFC's investment will contribute to the Group's objective to expand and strengthen RH's regional presence in Morocco and Cote d'Ivoire.
sponsor_shareholders: Retail Holding is a leading diversified Moroccan investment holding company operating in fast-moving consumer goods and food retail. RH and its subsidiaries hold strong positions in high-growth markets in Morocco. Based in Rabat, the Group has grown steadily since its establishment in 1985 to become a significant economic player and one of the leading employers in Morocco's private sector, with nearly 12 thousand employees. The Group also has a presence in Cote d'Ivoire, through CDCI. The Group is majority owned by Best Financière (50.6%) and whose beneficial owners are two Moroccan families, the Bennani and Hadni families.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$56 million broken down into two equity components: (i) an equity investment of up to MAD410 million (approximately US$41 million equivalent) in Retail Holding SA (RH); and (ii) an equity investment of up to US$15 million in Compagnie de Distribution de Cote d'Ivoire (CDCI).
location_description: The project will be located in both (i) Morocco for the first component of the investment, and (ii) Cote d'Ivoire for the second component.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are stakeholder effects through increased access to affordable and high-quality food products in Morocco and Cote d'Ivoire, especially in underserved areas. The Project is also expected to support economic activity and job creation in both countries. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment, along with several other projects in the pipeline targeting various links along the global food supply value chain, as well as corresponding responses from the World Bank, will promote greater resilience in the global food supply market as part of the GFSP. Platform-level indicators specifically tracked by the Project are long-term global food price inflation and the percentage of countries with food inflation above five percent.
additionality: IFC's involvement is expected to deliver both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via (i) IFC's Own Account Equity - IFC will provide scarce patient equity capital not readily available in the local market to match the growth plan and cash flow of the underlying businesses and improve the Group's creditworthiness profile, and (ii) Resource mobilization – IFC will enhance the Group's access to complementary capital. Non-financial additionality is provided via (i) Risk mitigation - IFC will help mitigate non-commercial risks through its support in attracting potential private institutional investors via the Equity Mobilization Program, and (ii) Standard Setting – IFC advisory services will support the Group to strengthen corporate governance and E&S practices, and facilitate the implementation of the gender Advisory program.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to US$10 million to support Ferme Jambo (the “Company”) in Southern DRC in expanding into irrigated wheat cultivation and milling. The Project will be executed over two phases from 2023-27. Phase 1 (2023-25): investment consisting of (i) farm machinery and irrigation equipment for 1.5 k ha and 4 ton/ hour wheat flour milling line). Phase 2 (2026-27) has assets like Phase 1, financed by US$10 million. Phase 2 commitment will be contingent on the satisfactory completion of Phase 1.
sponsor_shareholders: Ferme Jambo is part of Group Jambo, founded in 2004 in Lubumbashi. It is ultimately owned 50-50 by Rajesh Fatania and Arun Datwani. Rajesh Fatania has served as the Managing Director. He has lived in the DRC for the last 20 years.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$27.7 million, financed by US$20 million to support the acquisition of farming equipment, center pivot irrigation systems, and wheat milling lines in two phases from 2023 to 2027. The proposed IFC financing package for phase 1 consists of a US$5 million IFC A loan and a US$5 million loan from the IFC Facility for Resilient Food Systems (FRFS).
location_description: The project is located on Ferme Jambo’s site in Lubumbashi, Katanga, DRC, near the border with Zambia.
development_impact: Project level impacts Economy-wide effects: The Project is expected to generate additional value-added and an estimated 5,150 direct and indirect jobs along the Project's supply chain. Stakeholders (consumers): The Project is expected to increase food security by providing increased access to quality, hygienically packed maize flour at affordable prices supported by a robust regional retail network. Market level impacts: IFC anticipates the investment will contribute to strengthening the longer-term resilience of the DRC’s food market and help improve the global food supply market's ability to withstand future shocks.
additionality: Financial additionality Financing structure: IFC will provide longer tenor term loans on terms not otherwise available for agribusinesses in the local market (8 years and three years grace) and blended finance from IDA-PSW. The sector is experiencing financial challenges due to limited commodity-based financing by commercial banks. The proposed IDA-PSW support will adjust the risk-return profile of the transaction while facilitating a strong impact on the economy and consumers. Non-financial additionality Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC, through advisory services, is expected to improve the knowledge, innovations, and capacity of the client to implement industry best E&S and HSE practices at the manufacturing facilities and to the manufacturing facilities acquire requisite food safety certifications leading to improved product quality and safety.

project_description: IFC is proposing to provide an A-loan of up to US$25 million to Armstrong ZE (“Armstrong ZE” or “Company”), to partially finance the establishment of a greenfield tyre manufacturing facility near Karachi, Pakistan at an overall cost of US$ 92 million (the “Project”). The Project aims to address the under-served replacement tyre market in Pakistan, predominantly reliant on imports and the informal sector. The plant, with a production capacity of 1.4 million tyres annually, will focus on producing Armstrong brand tyres for passenger cars and light truck segments.
sponsor_shareholders: The shareholding of the Project will be held by the Hussain and Yusufzai families of Pakistan (collectively the “Sponsors”) directly and indirectly. The Sponsors also own Zafar Enterprises in Pakistan and Zafco Holdings in the UAE, both operating in the tyre distribution business.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated Project cost is up to US$92 million which will be funded by Sponsors’ equity, local currency loans and an up to US$25 million A Loan from IFC.
location_description: The Project will be built on a 50.25 acres land parcel, located on the outskirts of Karachi, Pakistan.
development_impact: The Project is anticipated to yield significant outcomes, including: (i) stakeholder effects through increased access to affordable and reliable tyres, and (ii) Economy-wide effects through local value addition, economic activities, and job creation while preserving foreign exchange reserves through import substitution. Beyond the Project outcomes, IFC anticipates that the Project will improve competitiveness in the tyre manufacturing industry by fostering innovative production capabilities, introducing advanced technology, and adhering to international safety standards.
additionality: IFC’s additionality encompasses both financial and non-financial aspects. IFC is providing long-term US$ financing with a customized repayment structure to match the Project’s cash flows which is not readily available in the local banking sector. IFC’s non-financial additionality will be achieved through providing climate and resource efficiency advisory to the Company to enhance the Project’s environmental sustainability and minimize its environmental impact. Furthermore, IFC will help the Company develop its environmental, health, safety and social practices in line with the World Bank standards.

project_description: The Project is to support the City of Cape Town Metropolitan Municipality’s (“CCT” or the “City”) FY24/25 capital investment program, through a proposed IFC loan of up to the lower of ZAR2.8 billion or US$150 million (in South African Rands equivalent) with an up to 20-year tenor. The investment aims to support the City’s FY24/25 capital investment program for infrastructure assets, which comprises primarily upgrades, replacements and expansion of sanitation and water supply infrastructure, roads, electrical infrastructure, and transport assets, amongst others. The capital investment program forms part of the City’s ten-year infrastructure plan, under which the City aims to address key infrastructure gaps to deliver quality basic services to its growing population and enable inclusive economic growth.
sponsor_shareholders: CCT is the second largest municipality in South Africa from a revenue and expenditure standpoint. The City, located in the Western Cape Province of South Africa, is the country’s second most populous city and the legislative capital of South Africa. It is a key economic hub, with world-class infrastructure and dynamic economic activity across various sectors, including finance, insurance, property and tourism.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The City plans to raise up to ZAR8 billion (around US$421 million) through loans to finance its FY23/24 and FY24/25 capital expenditure program of ZAR25.3 billion (around US$1.3 billion). IFC’s proposed loan of up to the lower of ZAR2.8 billion or US$150 million in ZAR equivalent will partially finance the FY24/25 program.
location_description: CCT is located in the Western Cape Province of South Africa.
development_impact: The Project supports: i) improving the quality of infrastructure services in the City through infrastructure upgrades, replacements and expansion; and ii) improving CCT’s financial resilience through supporting the City’s revenue base and improving operational efficiency.
additionality: IFC will help CCT to better align debt maturities with the lifespans of its infrastructure assets by providing a longer tenor investment than is currently available in the market. Prior to this Project, IFC supported the City to identify and assess solutions to improve energy services and climate change mitigation.

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: Epic Group Holdings Limited and its subsidiaries (“Epic” or the “Company”) are leading apparel manufacturers in Bangladesh and one of the top chino manufacturers globally. Epic is now expanding its operations in Bangladesh and establishing presence in India. The proposed investment will provide Epic with a debt financing package of up to US$120 million in the form of a sustainability-linked loan and a green loan with sustainability-linked features, that will be used to support its expansion in India and Bangladesh.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is wholly owned by Ranjan Mahtani, Sunil Daryanani, and Dinesh Virwani.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed financing package comprises of an A Loan of up to US$60 million, a B Loan of up to US$23.57 million and a senior loan of up to US$36.43 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP).
location_description: The project is located in Dhaka in Bangladesh and the State of Odisha in India.
development_impact: Project-level Impact - Economywide: The Project will provide direct and indirect employment in addition to creating higher value addition in the apparel sector in India and Bangladesh. The Project is expected to employ more female workers while providing more career opportunities to its female employees. Epic Group's expansion into India will help to create more employment opportunities to fill the current employment gap in India. Project-level Impact - Environmental effects: The proposed financing will be structured as a green and/or sustainability-linked loan to promote climate change awareness. The structure will also align with Epic Group's vision to carry out its environmental roadmap. Market-level Impact - Competitiveness: The Project will help Bangladesh and India move towards higher value-added production and greater competitiveness. It will demonstrate that a manufacturer who produces higher value-added products, focusing on sustainability and operating more complex process technology, will retain its competitive advantage.
additionality: Financial Additionality - Financing structure: IFC will provide long-term financing in a form of green loan and / or sustainability-linked loan that is not readily available to the Company. This will be the first time the Company is entering into a long-term financing package that has sustainability features. Non-financial Additionality - Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will share its global experience and industry knowledge in the garment manufacturing sector. IFC has extensive investment experience in India, which will help the Group to enter this new market and better achieve its business and financial goals. IFC will share international E&S best practices with the Company by implementing an E&S Action Plan.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment will support Salcomp Technologies India Pvt Ltd. (“Salcomp Tech”), a leading manufacturer of consumer electronics parts to set up new manufacturing capacities of top modules and back frames for mobile devices in Chennai, India. (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Salcomp Tech is 100% owned by Salcomp Plc, which is a Finland based holding company. Salcomp Plc is a wholly owned subsidiary of Lingyi iTech (Guangdong) Co., Ltd. (“Lingyi” or the “Company”) which is a leading manufacturer of precision parts and chargers for consumer electronic products from China. Lingyi’s controlling shareholder is Ms Fangqin Zeng, who owns 60.5% shares in the Company and the remaining shares are public floats.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is US$250 million and IFC is providing a 7-year A loan up to US$150 million to fund the Project.
location_description: Chennai India
development_impact: Project-level: (i) stakeholder effects on female employees through upskilling and promoting more women to managerial roles; and (ii) economywide effects via transition from lower-skilled assembly to skill-intensive precision production. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will create demonstration effect to local manufacturers for their value addition in production.
additionality: (i) Long term nature of the IFC loan for Salcomp Tech to scale up operation in India; (ii) IFC Gender and Inclusion Team to share technical knowledge and best practices for increasing diversity and inclusion in Salcomp Tech.

project_description: IFC committed a EUR75 million A-Loan on March 29, 2024, to Ülker Biskuvi Sanayi A.S. (“Ülker”). The IFC Loan will support Ülker’s multi-year corporate investment program. IFC also had an approval to invest EUR75 million, by subscribing to a US$-denominated senior unsecured fixed rate Eurobond to be issued by Ülker. As a result of the book building that took place on July 1, 2024, IFC has been allocated US$65 million of the notes issued (the IFC Subscription). Proceeds of the IFC Subscription will be used to refinance working capital needs of Ülker’s facilities located in Topkapi and Gebze in Türkiye, and its subsidiary Hamle`s factory in Kazakhstan.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1944, Ülker is the market leader, producer and exporter of snacks and other food products in Türkiye with an overall market share of 34% and is also one of the largest in the Middle East and Central Asia. The Company has been listed on Borsa Istanbul (“BIST”) since 1996. Shares of Ülker are represented as follows: 47.2% of its issued capital is owned by pladis (100.0% of which is owned by Yildiz Uluslararasi Gida Yatirimlari A.S.), 6.7% of its issued capital is owned directly by Yildiz Holding A.S., 6.4% by the Ülker Family members, whereas 39.7% are free float shares under BIST.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of an unsecured senior A-loan of EUR75 million and a subscription of US$65 million to Ülker’s US$-denominated senior unsecured fixed rate Eurobond from IFC’s own account. The IFC Loan will support Ülker’s multi-year corporate investment program which includes: (a) structural improvements for its factories Topkapi and Gebze in in Türkiye to make them earthquake resilient; (b) sustainability targeted investments for resource efficiency and Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions reduction in the same two factories in Türkiye and Hamle in Kazakhstan; and (c) maintenance capex for Hamle Company Ltd. LLP (“Hamle”), Ülker’s subsidiary in Kazakhstan. The proceeds from IFC Subscription, on the other hand, will be utilized towards working capital needs of Ülker’s factories located in Topkapi and Gebze in Turkiye, and its subsidiary Hamle`s plant in Kazakhstan.
location_description: The structural strengthening measures will take place in Ülker’s factories in Istanbul and maintenance capex for Hamle will take place in its factories in Kazakhstan. Working capital financing will be utilized in Ülker’s Topkapi and Gebze plants in Türkiye, and its subsidiary Hamle`s plant in Kazakhstan.
development_impact: Expected Project-level outcomes are contribution to the value addition to the operating countries economy and creation jobs in countries with high unemployment rates and positive environmental effects driven largely by climate adaptation measures and mitigation measures. In addition, part of the investment will be used towards earthquake strengthening works in the existing factories in Istanbul (Topkapi, Gebze) which are expected to result in enhancement in safety standards and creation of temporary construction employment opportunities. Beyond the Project level, IFC expects the investment to increase the resilience of the sector through adoption of sustainability measures and improving buildings to withstand earthquakes. Finally, investment in Kazakhstan Hamle factory will cover process enhancements and technological adjustments which are expected to lead to greater efficiency in resource utilization as well as improvement of safety environment at the factory.
additionality: Financial Additionality: IFC is extending financing to a manufacturing group during a period of economic instability in Turkiye that is specifically tailored for the structural needs of the Company, and which is not readily available in the Turkish financial markets. The loan will be structured in line with Sustainability-Linked Loan Principles, tying targets to sustainability indicators, which will lay the groundwork for future sustainable finance alternatives. Non-Financial Additionality: With IFC oversight, Ülker will further align its E&S policies and procedures with IFC Performance Standards while strengthening its E&S requirements applying to its direct and indirect third-party suppliers from whom Ulker is sourcing its raw materials in Turkey and in other origins. These measures will further improve Ulker’s operational efficiencies and E&S performance at targeted facilities and mitigate its raw material sourcing risks.

project_description: The proposed investment is a partial credit guarantee (“PCG”) covering a senior secured corporate loan (the “Covered Loan”) to be provided by Banco Santander (Uruguay), S.A. (“Santander”) to finance the acquisition of the world’s largest passenger electric ferry (the “Project”). The Project will be owned and operated by Los Cipreses S.A. (the “Company” or “Buquebus”), a Uruguayan passenger and vehicle river transport company operating in the Rio de la Plata area between Uruguay and Argentina under the “Buquebus” commercial name. IFC will help structure this financing as a blue loan, which would make this landmark transaction as the first blue loan in Uruguay.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a privately-owned maritime passenger company founded in 1979 in Uruguay, operating between Argentina and Uruguay using the Rio de la Plata waterway to connect Buenos Aires (BsAs) in Argentina to Colonia and Montevideo in Uruguay. The Company follows major international safety regulations and has a positive track record over its history. Buquebus is majority owned (99.9%) by its founder Mr. Juan Carlos López Mena, who continues to lead the Company as its president.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost is estimated at approximately US$170 million, out of which around US$107 million will be financed through the Covered Loan. IFC’s investment will be in the form of a PCG, covering up to US$ 67 million of the Covered Loan.
location_description: The Project will transport passengers between Buenos Aires and Colonia de Sarmiento across the Rio de la Plata riverway.
development_impact: The main direct anticipated impact is the positive environmental effect, as the electric ferry will replace diesel vessels in the Colonia to Buenos Aires route, hence reducing the carbon footprint of ferry transportation in such area. Beyond the project, the main expected market effect is that it will constitute a proof of concept for the implementation of mid-large scale electric ferries in Latin America and the Caribbean.
additionality: IFC’s PCG is providing financial additionality to Buquebus by enabling the mobilization of the Covered Loan provided by Santander. IFC’s PCG effectively mitigates Santander's exposure to the risk associated with the transaction. Domestic banks have been unable to provide a PCG for this project due to unfamiliarity with the product. IFC's non-financial additionality derives from supporting in the structuring of the Covered Loan as a “blue loan” (expected to be the first in Uruguay) and providing guidance on management of E&S risks in line with IFC Performance Standards, helping the Company to improve its practices.

sponsor_shareholders: CCI is the sixth-largest bottler of TCCC globally, with operations in 11 countries including Turkey, Kazakhstan, Pakistan, Iraq, Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Jordan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Syria. With 30 bottling plants and 146 production lines, CCI produces, distributes and sells five categories of beverages: soft drinks, water, juices, energy drinks and teas. CCI is a public listed company with 28.9% shareholding being publicly traded, 50.2% owned by Anadolu Group, 20.1% owned by TCCC and 0.8% owned by Ozgorkey Holding.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment comprises of an A Loan of up to US$250 million in own account financing.
location_description: The proposed investment will support the Company’s investment program in Turkey, Uzbekistan, Iraq and Tajikistan.
development_impact: The most significant project-level outcomes are expected to be: (i) economy-wide effects through value addition, and employment creation; and (ii) mitigation of climate change by reducing the carbon footprint of CCI’s operations. In addition, the Project also has a Gender flag given CCI’s commitment to reduce the gender gap across all levels and a target of 35 percent female new hires by 2030 across all subsidiaries. Beyond the Project-level outcomes, IFC anticipates that the Project will also contribute to the competitiveness in its countries of operations via (i) putting competitive pressure on domestic players to improve the efficiency; and (ii) providing a demonstration effect to decarbonize operations.
additionality: IFC will provide financial and non-financial additionality to the Project. Financial Additionality: IFC is providing a 6-year loan with a 1-year grace period; such long-term financing is not readily available in Türkiye, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Iraq. Non-financial Additionality: i) Knowledge management and capacity building: IFC will provide ongoing guidance to bring CCI's operations in Iraq, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan in line with IFC's Performance Standards.

sector: Other Vegetable Oil Crops (Coconut, Rapeseed, Peanut, Sunflower, etc.)
project_description: The proposed investment is an A Loan of up to US$10 million equivalent in Ethiopian Birr (ETB) to Shemu PLC (“Shemu” or the “Company”), a leading manufacturer of edible oil and household goods (soap & detergent) based in Dire Dawa in eastern Ethiopia. IFC’s financing will support Shemu to expand its refinery capacity to 950 TPD (tons per day) and improve operational efficiency through investing in logistical assets (“Project”). The Project may be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF), subject to obtaining the necessary internal approvals, as described in the Blended Finance section.
sponsor_shareholders: Shemu PLC is a private limited company incorporated in Ethiopia wholly owned by its founder Mr. Kahsay Wolday and his family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is expected to be approximately US$30 million. The proposed investment is an own account A Loan of up to US$10 million equivalent in Ethiopian Birr (“ETB”). The proposed ETB loan will be provided under the signed Framework Agreement between IFC and the National Bank of Ethiopia.
location_description: The Company’s refinery and the Project are based in Dire Dawa, a city in eastern Ethiopia.
development_impact: Project level impact: i) Economy-wide: The Project supports Ethiopia’s ambition to develop a competitive industry by improving the efficiencies of its refined oil operations and supporting marketing efficiency. Local refining will support domestic value addition and associated job creation; ii) Stakeholders: The Project is expected to increase the volume of fortified refined edible oil and therefore contribute to addressing Ethiopia’s challenges of food security and nutrition. With the proposed expanded production of the refinery, the Company will continue to produce refined oil fortified with vitamins A and D which are essential micronutrients to humans, which contributes to reducing the prevalence of micronutrient deficiencies among consumers. Market level impact: i) Competitiveness: The Project will contribute to addressing the challenges of CPO supply chain disruptions by establishing backward integration of local peanut supply chain to increasingly source peanuts from smallholder farmers and gradually replace CPO imports. This will demonstrate the possibility of import substitution if the companies remain competitive in terms of selling oil at prices below or at par with the import parity prices. Other market players are likely to follow suit by also sourcing edible oils locally to remain competitive. ii) With the support of IFC’s advisory, the adoption of improved peanut production practices will be demonstrated by the Company rolling out a farmer support program to help farmers achieve higher productivity through the introduction of improved production technologies (e.g., improved seed varieties), customized fertilizers, input financing system, and training on pre-and post-harvest management practices to improve peanut quality and reduce aflatoxin contamination.
additionality: Financial additionality – i) Financing structure: A facility with USD disbursement and local currency repayment is currently not available in Ethiopia; ii) IFC is proposing a 7-year loan, including 2.5 year grace period, and such long-tenor financing with a grace period is not readily available in Ethiopia. Non-financial additionality – i) Standard Setting: IFC will assist the Company in facilitating the development of a robust Integrated Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) system to close any existing gaps including the development of an E&S management system responsive to the requirements of PS1 and extend the scope of the E&S oversight of the Company to include its primary suppliers; ii) Corporate Governance: The Company, still fully owned by the founder family, will be supported to professionalize its organization structure; iii) Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC will help build capacity through the provision of Advisory Services, focusing on food safety practices, financial management and resource use efficiency of the Company’s operations.

project_description: The proposed transaction entails an investment of up to INR 12.50 billion (approximately equivalent to US$150 million) in the form of subscription to Non-convertible Debentures (NCDs) issued by Grasim Industries Limited (“the Company” or “Grasim”). The proposed loan will be utilized to finance the Company’s ongoing capital expenditure program for the paints business and working capital needs for the paints business of the Company (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Kumar Mangalam Birla and his family directly & indirectly hold ~43% shareholdings and are the sponsors of the Company. The balance shareholding is widely held by institutional investors and other public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Grasim is investing approximately US$1.2 billion across 6 new paints manufacturing plants, which will be implemented in a phased manner till FY25. IFC’s investment would be used to fund up to INR 12.50 billion (equivalent to approximately US$150 million) and the balance would be funded through equity raise and internal accruals.
location_description: The manufacturing units for the Project will be in India at the following locations: Ludhiana (Punjab), Panipat (Haryana), Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu), Chamarajnagar (Karnataka), Mahad (Maharashtra) and Kharagpur (West Bengal).
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good based on an AIMM score of 58. On an unadjusted basis (i.e., without the likelihood factor), the full potential AIMM score could reach 64. Economywide effects (value addition): IFC’s investment will support adoption of cutting-edge technology and processes which will minimize waste and reduce carbon footprint. Economywide effects (employment): IFC’s investment will create additional 2,810 jobs over next few years. Environmental Effects: IFC’s funding is structured as a sustainability linked loan (SLL) which will incentivize the Company at a corporate level to increase the use of RE power and reduce dependency on freshwater. Competitiveness: Grasim aspires to be the second-largest player in the decorative paint sector through a pan-India distribution network which will drive growth in rural markets, promote the shift from unorganized to organized markets, and encourage manufacturing efficiency among other players.
additionality: IFC funding will provide long term SLL, incentivizing the Company to undertake decarbonization and sustainability measures, which any other commercial financing is unlikely to encourage. IFC funding is also climate finance compliant based on the joint Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) Common Principles for Climate Finance tracking. Given Grasim’s position as a market leader, the adoption of these measures will have a demonstration effect across other hard-to-abate, carbon emitting companies in the manufacturing sector. IFC will also provide inputs on the sustainability framework to the Company. Further, IFC will provide support in environment and social (E&S) standard setting comparable to good international industry practices (GIIP). Among other things, IFC’s environmental and social action plan (ESAP) will strengthen the Company’s: (i) occupational health & safety (OHS) and process safety management (PSM) systems; (ii) documented operational E&S management systems (ESMS); (iii) contractor management systems; (iv) process emission standards specifically for Ammonia and volatile organic compounds (VOC); and (v) stakeholder engagement and community grievance mechanism.

project_description: Grupo Farmanova Intermed (“GFI” or the “Group”) is a private, family-owned group engaged in pharmaceutical distribution, commercialization, and retail both for human and animal health. GFI is headquartered in Costa Rica with operations throughout Central America and the Caribbean. As part of its growth in the region, GFI is investing in capital expenditure to consolidate its distribution operations into a single facility, acquiring licenses for commercialization of medications in the region, and other general corporate proceeds including working capital and repayment of debt (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: GFI was founded in 1983 by Dr. Rodrigo Salas, who maintains a majority of ownership. GFI remains a private, Costa Rican family-owned group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of a US$20 million convertible C loan to support (i) capex related to a new centralized, semi-automated logistics center, (ii) acquisition of new licenses for commercialization around the Central American and Caribbean region, and (iii) general corporate proceeds including working capital and reprofiling of existing debt.
location_description: Investment will be made at the combined corporate headquarters and centralized distribution center at the Verbena Logistics Park in San Jose, Costa Rica.
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase access to pharmaceutical products in Costa Rica as well as other Central American and Caribbean countries, through the centralization and semi-automation of distribution services and the introduction of new in-licensed products. Moreover, IFC anticipates that this investment will promote competitiveness in these countries’ healthcare market, by scaling output through an important distributor and introducing new pharmaceutical products in a number of countries which will generate increased pressure for competitors to scale-up their operations and increased availability of much-needed medications.
additionality: IFC will provide the Group with long-term financing not readily available in the country. Non-financial additionality will be delivered in the form of (i) knowledge, innovation and capacity building through the DigiPharma Advisory program, supporting the Company in its digital transformation journey, (ii) standard setting by supporting GFI in adhering to best international environmental, health, and safety (EHS) practice, and (iii) additional IFC knowledge sharing regarding corporate governance and other corporate matters.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan to Companhia Melhoramentos Norte do Parana (the “Company” or “CMNP”). CMNP is a Brazilian sugar, ethanol (S&E), and bioenergy company that operates 3 mills in the states of Parana and Sao Paulo (Jussara, Nova Londrina and Vale do Paraná mills) with a total of 8 million tons of crushing capacity and a cogeneration capacity of 121 MW.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is majority-owned by the Mesquita Souza family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an A loan of up to BRL 250 million. The proceeds of the IFC loan will be used by used to support an investment program to improve the productivity of the fields surrounding Vale do Parana mill (the “Project”).
location_description: The Project is located in Vale do Parana, Suzanópolis, which is in the state of Sao Paulo.
development_impact: The Project has an AIMM rating of Good, based on an AIMM score of 58. On an unadjusted basis (i.e., without likelihood factor), the full potential AIMM score could reach 64. IFC expects the Project to have environmental effects by contributing to increased biofuel production, and climate mitigation and adaptation through increased bioenergy production, yield increase, and adoption of climate smart practices. The Project will also generate economy wide effects through job creation and value addition. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment has the potential to contribute to strengthening resilience of Brazil’s sugar and ethanol sector, as well as the power sector through diversification of energy mix.
additionality: The proposed IFC loan has both financial and non-financial additionality. The financial additionality stems from the provision of long-term financing with tenors that are scare to the Company in the market. Non-financial additionality centers on the adoption of IFC's environmental and social Performance Standards.

project_description: The proposed long-term secured A-Loan of up to USD 35.5 million (the “Loan”) will be part of the multi-bank facility to Oasis-33 Mixed Use Development Company (the “Company”). The Company is a mixed-use real estate company responsible for developing, constructing, and operating Ayla Marina Village, which includes three hotels and retail stores within the Ayla development complex in Aqaba, Jordan. The Loan will be used by the Company to i) fund capital expenditure and complete the construction of a new hotel and ii) reprofile existing debt that was used to partly fund the construction of the existing two hotels and retail stores (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is fully owned by Ayla Oasis Development Company (AODC), which was established in 2003 to own and develop the entire Ayla development complex. In turn, AODC is more than 95 percent owned by Arab Supply Trading Company and Al Maseera International Company. Palm Beach Investment Company and Aqaba Special Economic Zone Authority (“ASEZA”) hold the remaining stake. ASEZA is the government organization responsible for the management, regulation, and development of the Aqaba Special Economic Zone in Jordan.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment is an A-loan of up to USD 35.5 million, which will be part of a multi-bank facility for the Company to fund the Project.
location_description: The Project is located in Aqaba, Jordan
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good, based on an AIMM score of 53. On an unadjusted basis (i.e., without the likelihood factor), the full potential AIMM score could reach 64. The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects on suppliers, through the purchase of goods and services from local SMEs and (ii) environmental effects via reduction in GHG emissions by improving the water and energy efficiency of the newly constructed hotel as well as greening the upcoming pipeline of projects. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment to promote Integration in the Jordanian tourism sector by maintaining the operation of existing infrastructure and supporting the completion of the hotel component of an integrated tourist destination project in Aqaba, Jordan, facilitating improved access to tourism infrastructure and related services for visitors and attracting more international tourists into region.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the proposed Project is both financial and non-financial. IFC will provide scarce long-term financing to the Company to fund its capital expenditure that is not otherwise readily available in the local market. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will provide technical guidance to the Company to develop capability in the areas of E&S and green buildings along with improvements to the Company’s gender efforts.

project_description: Shandong Intco Recycling Resources Company Limited (“Intco” or “the Company”) is an innovative manufacturer of recycled polystyrene (r-PS) and recycled polyethylene terephthalate (r-PET) headquartered in China. It produces and sells an extensive range of finished products including picture frames, original framed paintings and other artwork, mirrors, architectural panels, and other home finishings. The proposed IFC investment will support Intco to construct a greenfield multi-material plastic reprocessing site in Malaysia, as well as supporting the working capital needs of its operations (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Intco’s single largest shareholder, the founder and Chairman, Mr. Fangyi Liu (the “Sponsor”) holds a stake of 44.3%. The remaining 3.3% shares are held by ESOP and 52.4% by public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at approximately US$123 million. IFC’s proposed investment is a senior “A” loan of up to US$70 million or equivalent RMB.
location_description: Mukim Tanjong Duabelas, Daerah Kuala Langat, Selangor, Malaysia.
development_impact: The Project has an anticipated AIMM rating of Good, based on an AIMM score of 66. On an unadjusted basis (namely, without the likelihood factor), the full potential AIMM score could reach 88. The most significant expected project-level outcomes are stakeholder and environmental effects through increased domestic sourcing of recycling waste and associated circular economy benefits. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment will promote sustainability in the plastic waste value chain through demonstration effects.
additionality: Financial Additionality: 1. Innovative financing instrument (Blue Loan): The proposed IFC loan provides the long-term capital necessary for the Company to sufficiently scale up its recycling operations. In addition to the longer tenor and grace period, IFC’s financing will potentially help the Company complete a landmark climate-related financing, which will be Malaysia’s first-ever Blue Loan. Non-financial Additionality: 1. Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: With deep expertise in the plastic recycling industry, IFC can advise Intco on strategic planning and product innovation. IFC can leverage its global platform to introduce potential business partners, particularly in other emerging markets, as the Company broadens its sourcing and manufacturing operations globally. 2. Standard setting: IFC’s performance standards and the Project environmental and social action plan will ensure that the Company enhances its management of the risk areas of the operations. In addition to helping the Company develop an E&S management system, IFC is also helping Intco invest in risk mitigation measures in the areas of occupational health and safety (OHS) and life and fire safety (LFS).

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of up to US$100 million A-Loan (in BRL equivalent of approximately BRL 500 million) to Randon S.A. Implementos e Participações (“Randoncorp” or the “Group”) the largest manufacturer of trailer and semi-trailer in Latin America, and a leading global producer of motion control systems (through its subsidiary Fras-Le Mobility) and auto-parts. The loan will partly support the Group’s 2023-25 capex plan related to Randoncorp’s ESG commitments, which consist of sustainability-related investments aimed at reducing GHG emissions, improving OHS within the Group’s factories, and increasing the number of women in leadership positions.
sponsor_shareholders: Randoncorp was founded in 1949 in Caxias do Sul, Brazil, and has become a global reference in the trailer, semi-trailer, and autoparts business lines. The Group is publicly listed in the Brazilian Stock Exchange (tickers: RAPT4, RAPT3) and has approximately 61% of shares in the free float. The Randon founding family, via DRAMD Participações (“DRAMD”), holds approximately 39% of the Group’s shares. Note that Fras-Le Mobility is also publicly listed in the Brazilian Stock Exchange (ticker: FRAS3) and has approximately 34% of shares in the free float. Randoncorp owns approximately 53% of Fras-Le Mobility’s shares and the remaining 13% is owned by DRAMD directly.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$100 million to be financed with an A Loan of up to US$100 million.
location_description: Investments will be made at Randoncorp’s and Fras-Le’s manufacturing plants in Brazil.
development_impact: The Project will support (i) the decarbonization efforts of the Group by improving its resource efficiency for its manufacturing operations and Randon's GHG emission reduction targets; (ii) a more inclusive workforce in Brazil; and (iii) improvements in occupational health and safety improvements in Brazil's car and truck manufacturing sector. Moreover, the Project will support the continued growth of the automotive industry in Brazil, in addition to enhancing the market competitiveness of the industry through demonstration and replication.
additionality: IFC's financing will be structured as a Sustainability-Linked Loan, which will be the first of its kind for Randon, and is still relatively new for domestic lenders in Brazil. Thus, the loan will be structured with a variable spread, where the interest rate will be linked to the Group's performance in terms of reducing GHG emissions in line with its Sustainability-Linked Framework (as cleared by a third-party opinion). IFC will also provide financing at longer tenors and support the diversification of Randon's lender base, mostly local banks and local retail investors, supporting its road toward accessing international markets. Furthermore, IFC would help Randon implement IFC’s E&S Performance Standards.

company_name: BTG Pactual Timberland Investment Group, LLC
project_description: The Latin American reforestation strategy (the “Strategy”) was established in 2021 by the BTG Pactual Timberland Investment Group (“TIG”) to focus on greenfield climate-positive forestry. The geographic focus of the Strategy is Latin America, mainly Brazil and Uruguay. The Strategy’s objective is to protect, restore and plant trees on approximately 280,000 has of degraded land for timber production and restoration of natural forests, managing forests sustainably. Additional revenues are expected to come from carbon removal credits and manufacturing of FSC-certified wood products.
sponsor_shareholders: TIG, a wholly owned subsidiary of BTG Pactual, is one of the world’s largest Timberland Investment Management Organizations (“TIMO”), with US$ 6.4 billion in assets & commitments and 1.2 million hectares under management in North and South America (as of December 31, 2023). TIG has been appointed as the Strategy’s Manager (Investment Manager) and BTG Pactual will be a co-investor of the Strategy. A vehicle designated by TIG will act as General Partner of the Strategy..
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$120 million of which IFC will contribute with US$50 million.
location_description: The Project is located in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to have climate mitigation effects through forest restoration, afforestation, and sustainable forest management. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates contributions to promote environmental sustainability by financing among the largest initiatives to restore and preserve native forest in the ecologically important Cerrado biome in Brazil.
additionality: Financial Additionality: (i) Financing structure: Availability period and grace period, which is not readily available in the market and aligns with the Strategy’s timeline to commit the equity funding, close the property acquisitions, and match the cash flow generation cycle. (ii) Resource Mobilization: Tranche from third-party investors managed by IFC, which would not be available to the Strategy without IFC participation, diversifying its funding sources. (iii) Innovative Financing Structure: The loan will be structured in compliance with Sustainability-Linked Loan principles, in which the interest rate would vary in accordance with ESG KPIs Non-financial Additionality (i) Standard setting: IFC will support the Strategy in the adoption of good practice E&S principles in line with IFC's Performance Standards which will help the Strategy to strengthen the identification and mitigation of E&S risks inside the farm (e.g., health and safety of workers, management of hazardous materials) and in its area of influence (e.g., gender based violence and harassment (GBVH), stakeholder engagement) and ensure its operations meet best-in-class practices in line with expectations of its investors. (ii) Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: TIG will benefit from IFC's biodiversity risk management through the application of IFC PS6 to provide evidence of gains in biodiversity values in the areas managed by the Strategy. Applying IFC´s Performance Standards in this innovative TIMO represents a unique opportunity to set up higher standards across the entire industry.
Company Name: BTG Pactual Timberland Investment Group, LLC

project_description: ComBio Energia S.A. (“ComBio” or the “Company”), established in 2008, is one of the leading providers of renewable thermal energy solutions from biomass in Brazil. ComBio’s business model consists in installing biomass boilers inside its clients’ facilities, managing its operations and maintenance, and sourcing of the feedstock from renewable and sustainable sources. The Company’s biomass powered steam boilers provide a renewable and cost-effective alternative for industrial clients, reducing CO2, sulfur and nitrogen air emissions in comparison to existing diesel-based boilers. The proposed IFC investment comprises a financing package of up to US$72 million for the purchase and installation of (i) four boilers for two Ingredion Brasil Ingredientes Industriais Ltda.(“Ingredion”) facilities in Mogi Guacu and Balsa Nova, and (ii) a new boiler at Pirelli Pneus Ltda. (“Pirelli”) facility in Campinas (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: ComBio is a private company domiciled in Brazil. Approximately 67% of the shares of the Company are held by the five founding shareholders. The remaining is held by two private equity funds (Lightrock and SPX Capital), with a combined approximately 31% stake in the Company, and five executives who joined as shareholders through the Company’s Long-Term Incentive Program.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project has a total cost of approximately US$81 million equivalent and IFC is proposing an up to US$72 million financing package (IFC Own Account A Loan and Mobilization).
location_description: The Project facilities are located in the municipalities of Mogi Guacu and Campinas (state of Sao Paulo) and in the municipality of Balsa Nova (state of Parana).
development_impact: Project outcomes Environmental Effect: The Project will replace existing boilers that use fossil fuel by modern boilers fueled by biomass sourced from sustainable sources. The switch to renewable energy and enhanced resource efficiency will lead to reduction in CO2 emissions. Economy wide effects: The Project is expected to generate jobs and value addition to the Brazilian economy. Contribution to Market Creation Sustainability: The industrial sector requires large amounts of thermal energy to power its operations. The Project will support the provision of a cost-effective and environmentally friendly solution for switching to biomass boilers and contribute to environmental sustainability.
additionality: Financing structure: IFC is providing financing at longer tenors than those readily available to the Company in the market. Innovative Financing Structure: IFC is aiming at including an incentive-based structure linked to climate-related/sustainability KPIs. Mobilization: Under the proposed financing package IFC is aiming to mobilize funding. Non-Financial Additionality Standard setting: ComBio will benefit from the adoption of best E&S practices in line with IFC's Performance Standards.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support Duval Group (“Duval” or the “Group”) to build and operate a mixed-use property building complex that will consist of a serviced apartment hotel, office space, as well as shopping, food & beverage and restaurants area, to be located in Plateau, the business district of Abidjan, Cote d’Ivoire (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Terasson Invest, the Project entity, is fully owned by Duval Group. Duval Group is a well-established French conglomerate with core activities in real estate and hospitality. Duval Group is owned by the Duval family, including amongst others, Eric Duval, the Group’s founder and chairman, Pauline Duval, Co-Executive Director and Louis-Victor Duval, Co-Deputy Executive Director.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be up to EUR 64 million. IFC will provide an A-loan of up to EUR 16.3 million and will mobilize up to another EUR 16.3 million from other lender(s). The remaining portion of the Project will be funded by Duval Group.
location_description: The Project is located in Abidjan, Cote d’Ivoire.
development_impact: The Project is expected to contribute to improve businesses' access to quality and modern urban infrastructure through new commercial property developments and will contribute to job creation and contribution to GDP as well as indirect effects across the distribution chains. The Project is also expected to improve energy and water use efficiency by deploying energy friendly materials, technology, and equipment, thereby reducing the Project's GHG emissions.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC's financial additionality is delivered through the provision of long-term financing in line with the Project's needs and the mobilization of other lender(s) to meet the Project financing needs. IFC's non-financial additionality is delivered through the provision of technical expertise through the implementation of comprehensive Environmental & Social management systems and the provision of green building advice to achieve EDGE standards.

project_description: The group of companies known as PRAN Group (PRAN or the Group) was established in 1981. The Group is a leading branded food and beverage group and the largest agro-processer in Bangladesh. PRAN is a well-known household brand in Bangladesh and produces more than four hundred food products across multiple categories including juices and drinks, snacks, dairy, spices, grains, and frozen foods. PRAN exports to 145 countries around the world. IFC will provide long-term US Dollar working capital financing to be utilized across the two group companies, Pran Dairy Limited (PDL) and Habiganj Agro Limited (HAL).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsors and shareholders of the Project companies consist of the children of the late Pran Group founder Major General Amjad Khan Chowdhury, Mr. Ahsan Khan Chowdhury and Ms. Uzma Chowdhury (together, the Sponsors).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to provide debt financing comprising of an A Loan of US$30 million to HAL and PDL. The proposed A Loan has a tenor of up to 6 years with a 2-year grace period, and will be guaranteed by two other group companies, Pran Agro Limited and Mymensingh Agro Limited.
location_description: Bangladesh
development_impact: 1.Project Outcome- Economic-wide Impacts- The project will increase value addition and job creation from the HAL and PDL operations under the Pran Group, enable the companies to increase exports through the provision of long-term US Dollar working capital. The two Companies' direct employment is expected to grow from 15,501 in 2023 to 22,501 in 2027. 2.Market Creation- ?Resilience- The project investment will provide a working capital loan to sustain operations for a client that is the market leader in Bangladesh in several food categories that it operates in and in a tough economic environment where the country is facing a shortage of US dollars. IFC expects this project may serve to have a demonstration effect, leading to the provision of more USD working capital loans by other international lenders to support similar companies to sustain their operations in the current environment
additionality: 1. Financial Additionality-?-Financing Structure: IFC will provide PDL and HAL, sister concerns of Pran Group, with a USD working capital loan, filling a crucial gap at a time when local banks are struggling to secure USD for their clients. IFC is proposing a US Dollar loan of up to US$30 million with a tenor of 6 years, including a 2-year grace period, to support the companies' working capital requirements for raw material imports and ensure the long-term stability of their operations. ?2. Non-Financial Additionality-Knowledge, Innovation and capacity building: (i)IFC will provide advisory services to develop Pran’s smallholder sourcing supply-chain in Bangladesh for key commodities (casava, dairy, rice) working with 10,000 smallholders as well as developing decarbonization opportunities in Pran’s agro-processing operations through resource efficiency and circular economy assessments. (ii) IFC will continue to help improve E&S food safety and good agricultural practice standards of the Pran Group and its farmer suppliers and support in improving efficiency and reducing food loss and waste, a key aspect of IFC's additionality for Pran. (iii) IFC will support PRAN to improve gender diversity and inclusion in their workplace by providing recommendations, guidance, and tools to improve policies and practices to support workplace participation of all genders, particularly women through its Partnership for Women’s Employment, a peer learning initiative for select private sector companies in Bangladesh.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to US$25 million risk participation by IFC in an up to US$50 million 3-year uncommitted annual revolving, commodity backed, secured, trade finance facility (“Facility”) extended by ABSA Bank Limited (“Absa” or the “Bank”) to Valency International Pte Ltd (the “Company” or “VIPL”) to support its subsidiaries in financing pre-export storage of raw cashew nuts (RCN), cocoa, sesame, shea nuts, ginger and soya beans sourced directly or indirectly from smallholder farmers in Nigeria, Ghana, Tanzania and Cote d'Ivoire. The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA Private Sector Window’s Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW-BFF) to de-risk the investment.
sponsor_shareholders: Valency International Pte Limited is a Singapore-based vertically integrated agricultural supply chain manager operating in Africa, Middle East, Europe, India and South-East Asia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment will be in the form of an uncommitted-risk participation of up to US$25 million in ABSA’s existing facility (US$50 million) with the Company.
location_description: The Project will support the Company’s operations in Nigeria, Ghana, Cote d’Ivoire and Tanzania.
development_impact: (i)The Project is expected to enable continued access to finance for smallholder farmers and small and medium-size commodity traders through the Group’s procurement activities in Tanzania, Cote d’Ivoire, Nigeria, and Ghana. (ii) IFC expects the Facility to contribute to the strengthening of financial integration of the commodity value chains in the target countries by maintaining continuity and connections between cross-border private sector financial institution, local farmers, cooperatives and exporter.
additionality: (i) Financial additionality driven by IFC’s countercyclical role in providing short-term liquidity to the agribusiness value chains, at a time of restricted availability in terms of country and obligor limits across Africa (ii) Non-financial additionality from IFC's contribution to improving the Company’s environmental and social practices, in line with IFC’s Performance Standards and industry best practices

company_name: KUCUKCALIK TEKSTIL SANAYII VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: IFC will provide a senior secured loan of up to US$50 million equivalent in EUR (the “IFC Loan”) to Küçükçalik Tekstil Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (“Kucukcalik”, the “Company”), a vertically integrated textile manufacturer and exporter of home textiles operating in Türkiye and Egypt. The IFC Loan will finance the Company's investment program, which entails: (i) installing a semi-continuous polymerization plant to produce polyethylene terephthalate (PET) / polyester chips, (ii) expanding yarn spinning capacity from 60 tons per day to 100 tons per day in two phases (the first phase up to 85 tons per day); (iii) installing a textile recycling facility; (iv) implementing a 2.2MW rooftop solar PV, and (v) associated working capital needs (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is 100% privately owned by the Küçükçalik family from Türkiye.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is expected to be up to US$50 million, which will be primarily funded by the IFC Loan at an amount of up to US$50 million consisting of: (i) up to US$30 million EUR equivalent A Loan on own account and (ii) up to US$20 million EUR equivalent syndicated loans.
location_description: The Project is located in Sakarya and Bursa, Türkiye.
development_impact: The expected Project-level outcomes are economy-wide effects through value-addition, job creation and exports. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to spur renewed competitive pressure in the Turkish synthetic fabric manufacturing industry through increased value addition and diversification in the raw materials used for the home textile sector.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via a financing structure not readily available in a challenging financial market. Non-financial additionality will be provided via standard setting, as IFC makes its expertise available in environmental and social standards.
Company Name: KUCUKCALIK TEKSTIL SANAYII VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an A-loan of up to US$8.5 million to Pharmakina S.A. (“Pharmakina” or “the Company”), one of the world’s principal manufacturers of quinine (the active agent in anti-malaria drugs), with its operations based in Bukavu, the Eastern region of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The funds will be used to (i) modernize and upgrade existing processing facilities, (ii) expand production capacity, (iii) increase working capital, and (iv) refinance the Company’s existing bank loan.
sponsor_shareholders: Pharmakina is majority-owned by AlphaTalents Africa LP (ATA) via Pharmeg, an investment holding that owns 99.9% of Pharmakina S.A. ATA acquired a 57.5% shareholding of Pharmeg in 2023, and the two companies are together the Project Sponsors. ATA is an investment company supporting the creation and growth of profitable, sustainable, and impact-centric agribusiness ecosystems in Africa (including auxiliary sectors such as healthcare) with long-term capital.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project cost is estimated at US$20.9 million and will be financed by US$12.4 million in equity, while the balance of funding will be from the proposed IFC debt package. The proposed IFC financing package consists of a US$4.25 million IFC A loan and a US$4.25 million loan from IDA Private Sector Window Blended Finance (IDA PSW BFF).
location_description: The project is located on Pharmakina’s site in Bukavu, South Kivu, near the border with Rwanda.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is increased access to affordable and quality pharmaceutical products in DRC by extracting high-quality quinine from the bark of cinchona. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates financing the principal quinine-based pharmaceutical producer in DRC, supporting greater market resilience as spillover effects accrue to the pharmaceutical supply chain in these markets.
additionality: IFC’s involvement with the support of IDA PSW LCF is expected to contribute to both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality is provided through a long-term debt facility not readily available in the local market. Non-financial additionality comprises knowledge, innovation, capacity building, and standard-setting provided by IFC's engagement with the Company to provide further guidance to strengthen the Company’s capacity to manage E&S risks in accordance with IFC’s performance standard.

country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: The project consists of a venture debt investment of up to US$20 million in Habi, a leading PropTech platform in Latin America. Habi is building the digital infrastructure to support an efficient residential real estate market in Latin America. The investment will be used to refinance and reprofile existing debt, and support Habi’s continued growth.
sponsor_shareholders: Habi is a privately owned company with operations in Colombia and Mexico. Habi’s holding company, MCN Investments, Ltd, the intended recipient of IFC’s investment, is incorporated in the Cayman Islands. Current major shareholders include Softbank, Inspired Capital and co-founders Brynne McNulty Rojas & Sebastian Noguera Escallon.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a US$20 million loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Latin America and the Caribbean (“LAC”).
development_impact: The project is expected to improve access to quality homes, by refurbishing homes, integrating mortgage origination, and enhancing the efficiency of the home ownership trading process using inhouse data algorithms, reducing administrative requirements, and enhancing the speed of turnaround. The majority of the Company’s customers are first time house owners and a material share are in the lower-middle income strata. IFC also anticipates that the project will enhance the competitiveness of the residential housing market, via demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC aims to provide its expertise on environmental and social standards, insurance, and gender, to enable the Company to upgrade its practices in these areas and align with international standards. Sustainability: The Company is a real estate platform that purchases, remodels, and resells residential homes. In this context, the Company has agreed to collaborate with IFC to build a strategy to integrate green building standards into its remodeling operations, targeting water and power consumption reductions. Insurance: The Company is subject to professional liability and cybersecurity risks; IFC will advise the Company on acquiring insurance packages that appropriately mitigate such risks. Gender: Against the background of underrepresentation of women in house ownership, IFC will assist the Company to better understand how gender gaps affect its user base, with a longer-term objective of designing products aimed at increasing the share of women users of the platform.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: The proposed investment is an IFC investment as an anchor investor for the lower of US$60 million or 20% of the total commitments in ADM Asia Secured Lending Fund III LP (ASLF III – Elkhorn or the Fund), which will be established and managed by Asia Debt Management Hong Kong Limited (ADM Capital or the Sponsor) and provide debt financing to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in emerging Asia that have strong fundamentals but have limited access to traditional lending (the Project). ASLF III – Elkhorn is a successor fund to Asia Secured Lending Facility Ltd (ASLF I) in 2012 and ADM Capital Somei Lending Platform Ltd (ASLF II) in 2016, in both of which IFC was an anchor investor. The Fund aims to support the development of smart cities to enable a smooth transition to urbanization across emerging Asia, reducing strain on resources and supporting the delivery of more efficient, competitive, sustainable economies through technology and innovation.
sponsor_shareholders: ADM Capital is a private credit manager with a strong track record of providing debt to financially stressed SMEs across emerging and developed Asia markets for over 25 years since its inception in 1998. ADM Capital has an asset under management in private credit of about US$1.9 billion as of June 2023. An ADM Capital group entity will act as the general partner of the Fund, and several limited partners are expected to participate in the first closing of the Fund alongside IFC’s investment.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is IFC’s investment in the Fund at the lower of US$60 million or 20% of the total commitments in the Fund. The total size of the Fund is targeted at US$300 million.
location_description: ADM Capital is headquartered in Hong Kong SAR, China. The Fund will invest in SMEs in emerging markets in Asia. The eligible countries of the Fund’s investment initially include Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mongolia, Nepal, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
development_impact: Project Outcomes: Stakeholder Impact – Increased access to finance for financially stressed and distressed SMEs Contribution to Market Creation: Competitiveness - supporting the development of an alternate financing channel like private credit funds
additionality: IFC’s own account equity: IFC will provide up to US$60 million or 20% of the total commitment of the Fund as an anchor investor Resource mobilization: IFC will play a key role in mobilizing financing from other investors in the Fund through its anchor investment, sending a strong signal to the market and boosting potential investors’ confidence in the Fund. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC will support ADM in improving its capacity and developing a framework to identify and build its green finance portfolio, such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, green buildings and other climate-eligible assets. Standard setting: IFC will support ADM in adhering to higher standards of implementing climate transition and physical risk assessments in line with Paris Alignment methodology. In addition, IFC will support ADM to develop its capacity to assess and integrate the nature-based risks, and have these publicly available to industry stakeholders including the potential investors in the form of TNFD reporting. Further, IFC will support ADM with establishing Paris-aligned GHG targets.

project_description: The IFC investment consists of a green syndicated financing package with sustainability linked features of up to €500 million with a 5-year tenor for NE Property B.V. (NEPC or the Company), an existing IFC client and a wholly owned subsidiary of NEPI Rockcastle (NEPIRC or together with its subsidiaries, the Group), the largest retail property landlord and operator in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) (the IFC Loan). The proceeds of the IFC Loan will be allocated to refinance an existing portfolio of green-certified retail assets in Bulgaria and Romania (the Project Countries), in accordance with the use of proceeds criteria and selection process described in NEPIRC’s Green Finance Framework, and more specifically, used to repay the Company’s outstanding Eurobond due on November 23, 2024 (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: NEPIRC is incorporated in the Netherlands and listed on the Main Board of the JSE and on Euronext Amsterdam (share code NRP). The ownership of NEPIRC’s shares, as at the latest practicable date prior to the publication of the present Summary of Investment Information, in so far as it is known to NEPIRC, is as follows: (i) Public Investment Corporation 18.25%; (ii) Fortress Real Estate Investments Limited 16.19%; (iii) State Street Bank and Trust Company (Custodian) 7.88% and (iv) JP Morgan (Custodian) 6.21%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: On December 20, 2023, IFC committed a partial tranche of approximately €387 million, consisting of (i) a 5-year senior unsecured loan of €225 million from IFC’s own account; (ii) a 5-year senior unsecured syndicated loan of €115 million; and (iii) a 5-year senior unsecured loan of approximately €47 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program. Subsequently, on April 26, 2024, IFC committed a second tranche of approximately €58 million under the 5-year syndicated loan facility.
location_description: Bulgaria and Romania
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcome is increased access to high-quality green retail infrastructure in the Project Countries, achieved amongst others through the delivery of low-carbon and modern property retail space. Additionally, the Project is expected to have positive environmental effects, particularly through improved energy efficiency of the buildings. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will facilitate the connection between the Commercial Real Estate sector in the Central and Eastern Europe region and the broader financial markets.
additionality: IFC will provide a countercyclical loan to NEPIRC to balance out capital markets challenges caused by the geopolitical tensions in the region, inflationary pressures and consequential rising interest rates. This unsecured facility will be innovatively structured as a green loan with sustainability-linked features. The interest rate of the IFC Loan will be adjusted annually based on climate targets to reduce the intensity of both GHG emissions and energy consumption. IFC will also play an important role in mobilizing financing from third-party lenders. This will help the Company diversify its financing sources and gain access to a sustainable unsecured funding. IFC will also provide upstream advisory support to NEPIRC in advancing its decarbonization, sustainability, and equality strategies. Firstly, IFC will help identify, manage, and disclose building-resilience risks using IFC’s BRI tool. Secondly, through the GRIP program, IFC will help identify measures to reduce embodied emissions. Thirdly, IFC will support NEPIRC to prepare for and attain EDGE Gender certification, which will help the Group enhance its workforce diversity and promote inclusivity.

company_name: MARTUR SUNGER VE KOLTUK TESISLERI TICARET VE SANAYI ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Martur Sunger ve Koltuk Tesisleri Ticaret ve Sanayi A.S. (“Martur” or the “Company”) engages in design and manufacturing of seats as well as other interior parts for passenger cars and light commercial vehicles. Martur has production facilities in Turkiye, Romania, Morocco, Algeria, and Slovakia. The project entails financing of Martur’s investment program in Turkiye which includes expansion and maintenance capex during the period of 2024-2027 (the “Project”). The expansion capex will include Martur’s new machinery and equipment purchases required for its products, majority of which will be used in electric vehicle production.
