sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsor is Martur Fompak Holding A.S. (“Martur Fompak Holding” or the “Sponsor”) which owns Martur’s majority shares. Martur Fompak Holding’s main area of focus is automotive parts industry through Martur and its subsidiaries. The Sponsor is established in Turkiye and is privately owned by Ustunberk Family. Martur’s current shareholding structure is as follows: 84.4% by Martur Fompak Holding, 5.4% by IFC and 10.2% by Ustunberk Family members, Martur Fompak Holding companies and management.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide an A Loan up to EUR40 million to finance the Project.
location_description: The proposed IFC investment is planned to be utilized in the Company’s facilities in Türkiye.
development_impact: Economy-wide effects: The Project is expected to increase value-addition, employment, exports, and economic activity in Martur’s supply chain. Competitiveness: The Project is expected to modernize Martur’s operations, enhance firm-level productivity and develop its production lines for electric vehicle components, enabling the Company to preserve its competitive position in the global markets.
additionality: IFC will play a countercyclical role in a volatile market where access to longer-term financing and liquidity is strained.
Company Name: MARTUR SUNGER VE KOLTUK TESISLERI TICARET VE SANAYI ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support Institut Pasteur de Dakar (“IPD”, the “Company” or the “Sponsor”) scale up vaccine production capacity in Africa and manufacture up to 300 million doses of vaccines per year. This will be achieved through the construction of a multi-vaccines plant in Diamniadio, Senegal providing for drug substance manufacturing and fill & finish capacities (the “Project”). The project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: IPD is a biomedical research center and vaccine manufacturer created in 1923. It is a private not-for-profit foundation under Senegalese law. IPD was jointly created and is jointly managed by the Government of Senegal and Institut Pasteur, France. IPD’s mission is to contribute to public health in Africa, especially in Senegal, through research, teaching, medical, epidemiological, and biological training, as well as vaccine production. The Project is expected to be implemented through a Project special purpose vehicle to be established and to be majority owned by IPD (“NewCo”).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be up to US$252 million. IFC’s proposed investment in the Project comprises (i) an “A” Loan from IFC, and (ii) mobilization of “B” and/or “Parallel” Loans from other lenders, totalling up to US$80 million to be committed in phases, to NewCo. The remaining Project costs is expected to be funded through a mix of grant and public financing.
location_description: The Project is located in Diamniadio, Senegal.
development_impact: The Project is expected to help address the critical supply gap of vaccines in Africa as it creates additional manufacturing capacities and is expected to contribute to meeting the continent’s future needs for vaccines. The Project is expected to help strengthen the future resilience of the region health systems and supply chain and reduce the continent dependence on imports.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC will support a vaccine manufacturer scale up operations to respond to the vaccines needs of the continent. IFC's financial additionality is delivered through the provision of long-term financing in line with the Project’s needs and at a time vaccines manufacturers are expected to play a critical role, and mobilization of additional financing for the Project. IFC's non-financial additionality is delivered through the provision of technical expertise through IFC’s Upstream engagement to support the Project development phase and the implementation of Environmental & Social management systems.

company_name: KARSAN OTOMOTIV SANAYII VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: The proposed investment is a senior A-Loan of up to EUR 35m (the IFC Loan) to Karsan Otomotiv Sanayii ve Ticaret A.S. (“Karsan”, or the Company), a Turkish manufacturer of conventional and electric light commercial vehicles (“LCVs”) and buses. The IFC Loan aims at (i) refinancing Karsan’s transition to electric vehicles (“EV”) including the acquisition of EV-linked intellectual property rights; and (ii) financing working capital requirements linked to EV sales (the “Project”). Karsan is a manufacturer and seller of commercial vehicles and spare parts with a special focus on conventional and electric LCVs and buses. The Company operates in four main fields: (i) strategic partnerships (including manufacturing, marketing, sales, and after-sales services for brands, which target growth in the region), (ii) contract-based production (iii) original equipment manufacturing, and (iv) integrated & industrial solutions.
sponsor_shareholders: Karsan is owned by Türkiye-based Kiraça Holding A.S. (Kiraca Holding) with a 58.5% shareholding. Kiraca Holding is owned by the Kirac family. Kiraca Holding engages in automotive and in other industrial sectors with proprietary brands in automotive, automotive spare parts, and energy solutions. Karsan’s shares are publicly traded on the Istanbul Stock Exchange with a free float of 39.4%. Mr. Inan Kirac’s own direct shareholding is 2.0%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project Cost of EUR 35 million, which is expected to be financed by the IFC Loan, is detailed as follows: (i) refinancing Karsan’s transition to EV including the acquisition of EV-linked intellectual property rights (EUR 10m); and (ii) financing working capital requirements linked to EV sales (EUR 25m).
location_description: Karsan has 3 plants in Bursa, Türkiye.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good based on an AIMM score of 53. The most significant, expected project-level outcomes are: (i) economy-wide effects through value addition; (ii) an increase in exports; and (iii) job creation. Beyond the project-level outcomes, IFC anticipates that the Project will promote competitiveness by strengthening Türkiye’s position in the global automotive value chains.
additionality: IFC provides both financial and non-financial additionality to the Project. IFC’s financial additionality stems from: (i) the financial structure of the IFC Loan, which is not readily available from commercial banks in Türkiye and (ii) the countercyclical role of IFC. IFC’s non-financial additionality stems mainly from its standard setting. IFC will share its expertise by introducing international best practices to Karsan in areas such as Environmental and Social (E&S) risk management, Corporate Governance (CG) and Human Resource (HR) practices as well as the development of a gender action plan to identify actions to be taken for improvements.
Company Name: KARSAN OTOMOTIV SANAYII VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: KES Group Corporation (“KES” or “the Company”) is the largest Vietnamese producer of engineered wood panels, focusing on Medium Density Fiberboard (“MDF”) products and the leading provider of innovative solutions for the construction and interior industry. The Company currently has an annual MDF production capacity of 500,000 m3, an annual flooring production capacity of 6.5 million sqm and an annual melamine paper printing and dipping production capacity of 40 million sqm. The proposed IFC financing will support the Company’s vertical integration strategy, provide funding for a new warehouse and maintenance capex and working capital for MDF production (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: KES’ major shareholders are Kim Tin Investment Joint Stock Company, Mrs. Trinh Thi Xuan and Mrs. Tran Thi Kim Quy.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$92 million, of which will be funded by: (i) US$60 million IFC loan; and (ii) US$32 million from the Company’s internal cash generation.
location_description: The Project location is in Viet Nam.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate economy-wide effects from job creation and economic value-added through supporting the Company’s vertical integration strategy, and positive environmental effects from using wood waste as inputs in MDF production. At the market level, IFC expects the Project will create competitive pressures on other wood panel producers in Vietnam to optimize their cost structures and improve operation efficiency, accelerating the consolidation of the wood panel market.
additionality: Financing structure: IFC will provide longer-term USD debt financing than available in the local market. The financing from IFC is aligned with the Company’s longer duration capital expenditure cashflow payback timelines. Standard setting: IFC will help enhance KES’ sustainability by developing a comprehensive Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP) whose implementation will strengthen the Company’s Environmental and Social practices and procedures in MDF production.

project_description: The proposed investment entails a 7-year facility to Axtel S.A.B. de C.V. (Axtel” or “Company”) for up to US$60 million comprised of an A loan of US$40 million and mobilization of the balance. IFC’s financing will support a market leader providing critical digital connectivity and digital transformation services by extending the Company’s maturities, strengthening its balance sheet, and providing funds to invest in new Capex.
sponsor_shareholders: Controladora Axtel S.A.B. de C.V., an independent vehicle listed on the Mexican stock market, owns 53.9% of Axtel. The remaining shares 46.1% of shares are directly listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange (26.3%) and owned by a group of shareholders (19.8%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment entails a 7-year corporate loan to Axtel for up to US$60 million comprised of an A loan of US$40 million and a US$20 million mobilization component.
location_description: The Project location will be Mexico.
development_impact: The development impact thesis derives from the Company’s potential to (i) increase access to reliable quality connectivity for businesses, including SMEs; (ii) increase employment opportunities, especially for women; (iii) increase the competitiveness of the market for broadband connectivity in Mexico by fostering competition; and (iv) enable the economic transformation via nearshoring opportunities by strengthening the integration of the Mexican economy in the global value chains through digital connectivity.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality involves resource mobilization with a longer tenor. Non-financial additionality stems from providing (i) gender advisory services and (ii) support to develop and implement an integrated environmental and social management system that aligns with good international industry practices and IFC’s Performance Standards

sector: Tour Operators (i.e., Arranging and Assembling Tours)
project_description: Aqua Expeditions Pte. Ltd. (“Aqua” or the “Company”) operates soft-adventure environmentally sustainable cruises in remote and emerging destinations. Presently the Company operates in the in the Peruvian Amazon, the Galapagos Islands, Cambodia, Vietnam, and Indonesia. The Company is considering an expansion into Tanzania-Eastern Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded by Francesco Lorenzo Galli Zugaro (CEO) and Fred Brown. The company is owned by Mr. Galli Zugaro, Mr. Fred Brown and Bison Capital, a US-based investor.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost of the Tanzania-Eastern Africa expansion is US$45 million. The proposed financing for the expansion will include a secured IFC loan of up to US$40 million.
location_description: Tanzania-Eastern Africa
development_impact: The Project is expected to (i) Increase access to markets for suppliers via local sourcing opportunities and improved efficiency through capacity building (ii) Economy-wide effects through job creation, contribution to GDP and higher tax revenues for the government. At the market level, the Project has the potential to promote the integration of the tourism sector by supporting the introduction of cruise tourism as a new market segment.
additionality: IFC will provide financial additionality by providing long-term financing that is not readily available in the local market.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a debt facility to Precious Shipping Public Company Limited (“PSL” or the “Company”), to be drawn down over the next 24 months to support the Company’s plan to purchase up to six dry bulk carrier vessels (“Project Vessels”). Each Project Vessel will be owned and operated under a special purpose company (all six special purpose companies are collectively called “Project Companies”). The Project Companies will be wholly owned by PSL.
sponsor_shareholders: PSL is one of the world’s largest pure dry cargo ship-owning companies operating in the geared (10,000 to 69,000 dead weight tonnage) sector of the tramp freight market. PSL currently operates 34 dry bulk ships and four cement carriers with a total capacity of 1.7 million dead weight tonnage. PSL is a member of the GP Group, a 155-year-old diversified Thai conglomerate with businesses across shipping, pharmaceuticals, construction, and mining sectors. PSL was established in 1989 and was listed on Stock Exchange of Thailand in 1993. PSL is an existing IFC client through project #45146 (https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/45146/psl-ultratech).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC financing involves senior loans with an overall tenor of up to 10 years, to the Project Companies comprising: (i) up to US$35 million from IFC’s own account, (ii) up to US$35 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP), and (iii) up to US$60 million syndicated loans consisting of IFC B loans for the account of B loan participants and/or parallel loans from parallel lenders. The loans will be secured by the assets, cashflows and shares of the Project Companies and guaranteed by PSL as the parent entity.
location_description: PSL corporate offices are in Thailand, while the Project Companies will be incorporated in Singapore. The dry bulk vessels are expected to transport various dry bulk commodities worldwide.
development_impact: The Project has an anticipated AIMM rating of Satisfactory. The main project outcome stems from positive environmental effects with the acquisition of six dry bulk vessels that will be more fuel efficient than the average fleet of PSL. Beyond the Project, the investment is expected to help enhance financial integration by demonstrating a more efficient financing structure for the acquisition of dry bulk vessels in the secondhand market, given the limited availability of newbuild vessels as a result of constraints from shipyards.
additionality: Financing structure: IFC is providing long-term USD-denominated financing with an overall tenor of up to 10 years including 3-month grace period not readily available in the domestic market for the shipping industry. The financing structure helps contribute to the Company’s commercial viability within a highly cyclical sector with volatile rates. Resource mobilization: IFC as mandated lead arranger will help mobilize a total debt package of up to US$130 million, including parallel and/or IFC B loan of up to US$60 million. IFC’s participation is expected to help provide comfort to commercial lenders. Standard-setting: IFC will continue providing technical support and guidance to PSL on the implementation and improvement of the environmental & social standards in accordance with IFC Performance Standards. IFC will help ensure the design and implementation of a selection criteria for the acquisition of any secondhand ships in line with IMO requirements and IFC PS.

project_description: The proposed investment is a debt facility to Kioo Limited (Kioo or the Company), a leading glass container producer in East Africa. Kioo produces both flint and colored glass for its domestic market in Tanzania, where it has dominant market share, and export markets in Eastern, Central, and Southern Africa, and the Indian Ocean Islands. Its customers include leading beverage multinationals. The project will support the planned capacity expansion of Kioo in its existing production facility in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (the Project). The expansion will enable the Company to meet increasing demand for glass containers in the region. The key components of the Project are addition of a new production line and addition of transportation equipment.
sponsor_shareholders: Kioo is wholly owned by African Developments Limited, an associate company of the Madhvani Group. The Madhvani Group have been based in Uganda for over 100 years and are one of the leading business groups in East Africa with interests in Uganda, Rwanda, Tanzania, the Middle East, and India across agribusiness, power, insurance, real estate, tourism, and other sectors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at approximately US$60 million. The proposed IFC investment will comprise an A loan of up to US$45 million.
location_description: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the generation of foreign exchange revenue for Tanzania, increased local value addition, and employment. IFC estimates that the Project will generate indirect and induced jobs along the different value chains as the supply and logistics networks are expected to grow significantly due to the expansion. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to continue strengthening the integration of manufacturing industries on a regional scale, by further optimizing regional supply chains of glass packaging, which could serve as catalysts for developing additional downstream linkages, for instance, with the emerging beverage, food, pharmaceutical, perfume and cosmetics industries in Eastern and Southern Africa.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via a financing structure that is not readily available locally to fund expansion investments. Non-financial additionality is provided via knowledge, innovation and capacity building, as IFC is supporting the Company with an advisory service package to determine a suitable business model to increase the collection and reuse of glass containers (cullet). IFC will also advise on energy efficiency measures in the context of the decarbonization roadmap under preparation.

project_description: IFC will finance the establishment by InVivo Group of two new malt processing plants in Johannesburg, South Africa, and Pleven, Bulgaria, along with its working capital needs in Bulgaria, Poland, South Africa and Romania (Project).
sponsor_shareholders: InVivo Group is a leading agribusiness player in Europe. It is owned by Union InVivo, a national union of French cooperatives.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide a total financing package of €200 million, to be financed by IFC’s net A Loan of around €150 million and the remaining will be a combination of a trust loan, with IFC acting in its capacity as the implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP), or credit insurance.
location_description: Investments under the Project are planned to be made in South Africa, Bulgaria, Romania, and Poland.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Satisfactory to Good. At the project outcome level, IFC expects the Project to have climate mitigation impact with energy efficiency and renewable energy designs in the new plants in Project countries, as well as job creation and benefits to farmers. Beyond the project, IFC expects the Project to contribute to promoting sustainability in the agribusiness sector in Project countries.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality in this Project largely stems from the provision of financing in the longer range of tenors available in the market to a client that IFC has had a long-term partnership with; and from IFC’s global presence & knowledge.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of up to US$200 million A-Loan to Localiza Rent a Car S.A. (“Localiza” or the “Company”), a regional leader in the vehicle rental business headquartered in Brazil with a presence in Latin America. The loan will partly support the Company’s 2023 capex plan, which consists of purchasing more efficient flex-fuel vehicles (biofuels-based) to renew and expand its existing fleet.
sponsor_shareholders: Localiza was founded in 1973 in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, and operates one of the largest vehicle-rental networks in South America. The Company is publicly listed in the Brazilian Stock Exchange (ticker: RENT3) and has approximately 79% of shares in the free float. Localiza founders (the Mattar and Brandão Resende families), jointly hold approximately 14.7% of the Company’s shares. Following a business combination with Companhia de Locacão das Americas (“CLA”) in September 2022, CLA’s founders also became shareholders of Localiza, with approximately 5.7% of the common equity.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$200 million, to be financed with an A Loan of up to US$200 million.
location_description: Investments will be made at Localiza’s vechicle fleet in Brazil.
development_impact: The Project will support the continued growth of the automotive industry in Brazil, in addition to enhancing the market competitiveness of the car rental industry through demonstration and replication. The Project will also contribute to increasing energy efficiency and process improvements to reduce GHG emissions by supporting the Company's decarbonization targets.
additionality: IFC's financing will be structured with a variable spread, where the interest rate will be linked to the Company's performance in terms of developing a Sustainability-Linked Framework with KPIs and targets to be validated by Science-Based Targets Initiative, and further reducing GHG emissions driven by compliance with such climate-related KPI. This would be the first of its kind for Localiza. IFC will also support the diversification of Localiza's lender base, mostly local banks and local retail investors, supporting its road toward accessing international markets. Furthermore, IFC would help Localiza implement IFC’s E&S Performance Standards.

project_description: IFC is considering up to a US $30 million IFC “A” Loan and up to a US$20 million mobilized in B/Parallel loans to Melcom Limited (“the Company”), a leading retailer in Ghana. The company currently has a network of 60+ retail stores, and a network of warehousing & storage assets (including cold-rooms) , as well as an e-commerce business in Ghana. The funding is to support the expansion and upgrade of its operations which includes: (i) the development of 22 new stores of approximately 128,000 m2 retail space (EDGE certified), built on Melcom’s existing land bank. (ii) installation of 5-6MW of rooftop PVC solar across 22 stores, (ii) expand warehousing and storage assets (including cold-rooms) to support its own retail operations, as well as its wholesale operations to smaller retailers (iv) upgrade of the company’s e-commerce platform, and IT systems, and operational systems (.i.e.; storage, handling, delivery, etc.) to support its expansion, and working capital (the Project). The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a family-owned business. It is owned by the wife of the late founder, Mrs. Sheila B. Khubchandani (30%) and their daughters, Mrs. Rani M. Melwani (25%) and Mrs. Sonya R. Sadhwani (25%). The balance shareholding is held by the founders’ sons-in-law, Mr. Mahesh A. Melwani (10%) and Mr. Ramesh M. Sadhwani (10%), who together established Melcom with the founder over 30 years ago.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$61 million equivalent in Ghanaian cedi, comprising of (i) up to US$30.0 million “A” loan; (ii) up to US$20.0 million in “B”/“Parallel” loans and (iii) US$11.0 million funded through internal cash within the Company. The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (“IDA PSW LCF”) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
location_description: The proceeds will be utilized for Melcom Limited in Ghana.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are: (i) economy-wide effects through job creation, higher tax revenues for local government and increased value added for local products; (ii) stakeholder effects through improving consumers’ access to modern retail in underserved areas; (iii) environmental effects through reducing CO2 emissions associated with electricity generation by developing 6-7MW of solar rooftop equipment across existing and new stores. Beyond these outcomes, IFC expects the Project result in an increase in competitive pressures that affect the market through expansion and subsequent increase in offering of good quality and standardized retail services across the catchment areas.
additionality: IFC's involvement with the support of IDA PSW LCF is expected to contribute to both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via an innovative financing structure (long-term financing and grace periods that are not otherwise available). Non-financial additionality is provided by (i) IFC providing technical expertise and guidance with respect to the implementation of solar rooftop systems; (ii) IFC's E&S teams for organizational and operational best practices; (iii) IFC supporting the Company with EDGE certification of stores and (iii) through IFC advising on gender enabling policies.

project_description: The proposed Project consists of a financing package made up of (i) an equity commitment of up to US$ 50 million and (ii) a corporate finance loan of up to US$100 million in favour of Lagos Free Zone Company (LFZC or the Company) which is a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) covering an area of 842hectares in Lagos, Nigeria.
sponsor_shareholders: Project Sponsor is Tolaram Pte Ltd, a holding company headquartered in Singapore with diversified business interests in consumer goods, fintech, infrastructure and industrials. It has a presence across Asia, Africa and Europe. LFZC is 96.72% owned by Tolaram Pte Ltd and 3.28% owned by its employees.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed financing package consists of (i) an equity investment of up to US$50 million and (ii) a corporate finance loan of up to US$100 million.
location_description: The Project is located in Lagos, Nigeria.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are stakeholder effects through increased access to high-quality industrial spaces for tenants, capacity building for suppliers, and economy-wide effects through creating high-quality formal jobs and economic value-add. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment to have the potential to promote the integration of domestic firms in Nigeria to international markets and improve the connectivity of the Lekki peninsula axis of Lagos state, by supporting the development of a large scale Special Economic Zone project in Nigeria with demonstration potential.
additionality: IFC's additionality is through (i) Own account equity: IFC is providing risk capital to a free trade zone in Nigeria, acting as an anchor equity investor in view of a planned listing in the near term; (ii) Non-commercial risk mitigation: an IFC investment is expected to help attract major international manufacturers to the Lagos Free Zone as this is the first economic zone being developed by Tolaram; (iii) Frameworks—catalyzing policy or regulatory change: IFC Advisory Services is completing an upstream engagement that is geared towards the improvement of the legal, regulatory and institutional framework for all Special Economic Zones in Nigeria; and iv) Standard setting in E&S and Corporate Governance related matters.

project_description: The proposed investment is a debt package which consists of an IFC A loan of up to EUR5.6 million and a Blended Finance (BF) senior loan of up to EUR5.6 million (the “IFC Loan”) to support the expansion and diversification program of Société Lierkang Diaguissa en Guinee SARL (the “Company” or “Solidiagui”), one of the leading fruit juice companies in Guinea-Conakry. IFC would finance the (i) expansion of the current juice beverage production capacity and (ii) installation of a dairy products line within the existing production hall to produce yoghurt and liquid milk (“the Project”). Solidiagui has been distributing beverage brands including ‘Sagiko’ juice and ‘Incolac’ milk products since 2009, then started manufacturing its own brand ‘Fruitalos’ and ‘Sagiko’ juice under license upon completion of its factory in 2021.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is managed and wholly owned by the founder/CEO: Mr. Souleymane Sow (60%), and his brother/Deputy CEO: Mr. Ibrahima Sow (40%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: ?The total project cost of US$ 22 million includes (i) Capex: US$10.5 million for Phase I and US$5 million for Phase II, (ii) working capital of US$5 million and (iii) refinancing of an existing bank loan of US$1.5 million, out of which US$8 million for Capex for Phase I was invested in 2023.
location_description: The project is in the Company’s existing industrial site, in Dubreka (Guinea), in a radius of 10 km from Conakry.
development_impact: The Project will increase consumer access to dairy and juice beverage products and therefore contribute to food security and nutrition in Guinea where prevalence of undernutrition, stunting and wasting is high. Protein intake per capita and day is also low. IFC expects the Project will increase value addition and create jobs. IFC’s analysis of the Project suggests average multiplier effects on the value-added dimension, with an overall value addition estimated at US$3,5million, including 150 direct jobs and 300 indirect and induced jobs along the Project’s supply chain. The investment, complemented by IFC Advisory, will increase competitiveness in the market supporting (i) local dairy processing to gradually substitute imports; (ii) expansion of canned juice production line; and (iii) technical and operations improvements in terms of adoption of plant and food safety standards of a leading player in Guinea’s dairy and fruit juice industry, with demonstration and replication potential.
additionality: On financial additionality, IFC will be providing the Company with long-term financing on terms otherwise not available in Guinea (8-year tenor with 3-year grace) and blended finance from IDA PSW BFF to adjust the risk-return profile of the transaction. IFC’s non-financial additionality consists of providing Food Safety Advisory to support the implementation of a Food Safety Management System (FSMS) that complies with ISO22000 standards in juice beverage production and dairy plant design, while enhancing operational efficiency and strengthening Solidiagui’s corporate governance. The support will help align Solidiagui’s operations with IFC performance standards and industry best practices.

company_name: DOUJA PROMOTION GROUPE ADDOHA COTE D'IVOIRE SA
project_description: The proposed investment is a corporate A loan (the Loan) of up to EUR 25 million equivalent in local currency (XOF) in Douja Promotion - Groupe Addoha Cote D’Ivoire (Douja CIV or the Company), a leading housing developer in Cote D’Ivoire which primarily develops build-to-sell affordable housing units along with mid- to high-end housing in Cote D’Ivoire. The Company is a fully owned subsidiary of Groupe Addoha Douja Promotion (Addoha Group) – a Moroccan real estate developer. The Loan will be used to partly finance the development of about 4,700 build-to-sell affordable housing units in the Company’s project in Lagoona City.
sponsor_shareholders: Douja CIV is 100% owned by Addoha Group which is listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange. Addoha Group is majority owned by Mr Anas Sefrioui (64.8%), followed by RCAR (Régime Collectif d’Allocation de Retraite) with 5.1% and the rest is free float (30.1%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The cost of the Project is estimated at EUR 158 million which IFC will support with a EUR 25 equivalent in XOF million, senior loan package. Within the scope of the Project, IFC’s financing will be directly used to support the development of housing in Lagoona City, Abidjan, Cote D’Ivoire.
location_description: The Project will be located in Yopougon in Abidjan, Cote D’Ivoire
development_impact: Project Outcomes – Stakeholder effects: (i) Effects on consumers: The Project entails supplying about 4,700 affordable housing units for sale in Abidjan, Cote D’Ivoire, thereby promoting increased access to affordable housing for the consumers; (ii) effects on local communities: The large-scale development is also expected to create potential economy-wide effects in the local community, creating demand for building materials, durable goods used for equipment and furnishing, and other relevant services in the area. Contribution to Market Creation: Competitiveness: Project will demonstrate that good quality housing in the affordable segment can also be profitable; and can be replicable to serve the underserved population. The success of the Project can help alleviate the commercial risk perceived by banks and investors for affordable housing developments in Cote D’Ivoire, by demonstrating a strong case for the commercial viability of these projects, which will improve access to financing for the developers by crowding in more private capital into the sector. Through these demonstration effects, the Project will contribute to developing the depth and diversity of residential offerings in the market, thereby promoting competitiveness in the CI housing sector.
additionality: IFC financial additionality is through the provision of a long-term facility with a long grace period, which is not readily available in the local market. Developers in the market largely rely on secured shorter term loans to finance their housing projects. The proposed financing structure will better match the cash flows of the underlying business, improve the Company's debt profile, and enhance access to complementary capital. Furthermore, IFC is expecting to play a role in non-financial additionality through its global expertise in providing affordable housing and E&S standard setting.
Company Name: DOUJA PROMOTION GROUPE ADDOHA COTE D'IVOIRE SA

project_description: IFC is considering a total funding package of US $55.0 million for Eastern Focus Investments Limited (the “company”), Conifer Holdings Limited, Polytanks Ghana Limited and Sonnex Packaging Nigeria Limited (as “co-borrowers). The company and co-borrowers are part of the Mohinani Group. The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (“IDA PSW BFF”), as described in the Blended Finance section below. The funds will be used to help the company (i) develop two plants (one in Ghana and another in Nigeria), each with capacity of 15,000 tons per annum (tpa), to recycle polyethylene terephthalate (PET) from plastic waste into recycled pellets (rPET), and (ii) working capital support for the Company in the chemicals and polymers trading and distribution business.
sponsor_shareholders: Mohinani Group was founded in Ghana in 1966 by the late Ramchand Mohinani and has 3 major business lines: (i) manufacturing of plastics and packaging; (ii) trading and distribution of chemicals and polymers; and (iii) general goods trading and distribution of electronics, tires, motor bikes. The group is run by three brothers; Ashok Mohinani, Anil Mohinani and Sunil Mohinani. The Group holds its business through two separate holding companies – Eastern Focus Investments Limited (EFI) which owns all the Group’s manufacturing and chemicals trading subsidiaries in Africa and International business (UAE and Hong Kong); and Conifer Investments which owns all the Group’s consumer and electronics trading business in Africa. Polytanks Ghana Limited is a 100% wholly owned subsidiary of Eastern Focus Investments Limited and Sonnex Packaging Nigeria is a 100% wholly owned subsidiary of Confier Holdings Limited.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$55.0 million, comprising of (i) up to US $30.0 million IFC A Loan and (ii) up to a US $25.0 million B2/MCPP Trust Loan, mobilized under the IFC’s Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (the MCPP); together the IFC Loan. Additional support will be provided by the IDA20 PSW; the latter will provide a first loss guarantee of a portion of the IFC loan.
location_description: The proceeds will be utilized for Polytanks Ghana Limited in Ghana and in Sonnex Packaging Limited in Nigeria. Working capital facilities will be utilized by Eastern Focus Investments Limited in the chemicals and polymers trading and distribution business.
development_impact: The Project, through contributing towards creating circular economic solutions, allowing the offset of up to 100% of virgin plastic resins to produce PET bottles, will directly contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and reducing plastic pollution. The Project will also contribute to the wider economy through value-addition, job creation and supplier effects. In terms of market creation, effects can be expected both in the short term on the domestic integration of the plastics supply chain, thanks to the launch of a circular process that replaces imports of virgin resin, and in the longer term on the wider sustainability of plastics manufacturing operations, by encouraging other PET bottle producers to backward integrate through the establishment of recycling operations.
additionality: IFC's involvement with the support of IDA PSW is expected to contribute to both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided through (i) a financing structure with longer tenors and grace periods otherwise not available in local markets, and (ii) IFC mobilizing additional financing for the Project. Non-financial additionality is provided by (i) technical expertise and guidance in rPET operations, including PET waste management and collection schemes and (ii) standard setting with respect to corporate governance and gender enabling policies.

sector: Other Vegetable Oil Crops (Coconut, Rapeseed, Peanut, Sunflower, etc.)
project_description: As part of the corporate zero net emissions strategy launched in 2020, Eni S.p.A. (Eni) is targeting net zero carbon emissions by 2050. This target will be achieved through a variety of fully decarbonized products, combining environmental and financial sustainability with a strong focus on technological leadership built on years of research and innovation. As part of this strategy, through its affiliate Eni Kenya B.V. (“the Company”), Eni has initiated a biofuel project in Kenya. The Project involves contractual engagement of third-party farmers and aggregators to supply oil seeds (feedstock) into Eni-owned agri-processing plants, where these seeds will be processed to produce vegetable oils for export to Eni bio-refineries in Italy and further refined into different bio-energy products (biofuels). Eni will develop and oversee supply chains for the agri-hubs, including ~200,000 ha of oilseeds production, and reaching over 200,000 smallholder farmers through contracted aggregators. The biofuels will be International Sustainability and Carbon Certification (ISCC) certified as advanced biofuels, being produced from “low indirect land-use change” (“Low ILUC”) feedstocks that do not compete with food production because these non-edible oilseeds, like castor and croton, are grown on degraded lands not suitable for food production and/or are grown in rotation/inter-cropping with food crops.
sponsor_shareholders: Eni Kenya B.V. is wholly owned by Eni International B.V., which in turn is wholly owned by Eni. Eni, formed as a result of the transformation of Ente Nazionale Idrocarburi, a public agency, pursuant to Law No. 136 of February 10, 1953, is an integrated energy company with operations in 62 Countries and a workforce of 32,188 (11,310 abroad) as of December 31st, 2022. Eni operates in oil, natural gas, and energy in general, with a particular focus on renewable energies, and is active in the development of circular economy projects, forest conservation and CO2 capture and storage. In June 2020, the Board redefined the Company’s organisational structure, launching a new arrangement consistent with the corporate mission and the new long-term strategy, aimed at transforming the company into a leader in the production and sale of decarbonised energy products. Eni is subject to the control of Italy’s Ministry of the Economy and Finance, through stakes held directly in the Company (with 4.667%) and indirectly (27.731%) through Cassa Depositi e Prestiti S.p.A. (CDP S.p.A.), a company controlled by the Ministry. The balance of the shares (with 67.602%) is held by institutional investors, retail, and treasury shares. Eni is a company that issues shares listed on Euronext Milan operated by Borsa Italiana S.p.A. and securities traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in the United States.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$213 million, consisting of capital investments to construct and operate the agri-processing plants in Kenya and related working capital needs. IFC is considering providing up to US$210 million senior loan financing package to ENI Kenya B.V. for its agri-business activities, including a potential mobilization piece of up to US$75 million earmarked for potential other lenders.
location_description: Eni Kenya B.V.’s first and second agri-processing plants have been built respectively in the Kenyan counties of Makueni and Kwale while the third one is planned to be built in the county of Nakuru. The location of the fourth agri-processing plant is yet to be confirmed.
development_impact: Project Outcomes: Stakeholders: Farmers - IFC expects the Project to improve livelihoods for up to 200,000 smallholder farmers by providing inputs, mechanization, logistics, certification, training, etc., and access to markets to farmers by off-taking up to 600,000 Mt oilseeds p.a. Economy-Wide Effects: IFC expects the Project to strengthen linkages with farmers and improve employment and domestic value addition through economywide linkages. Market Creation: Sustainability: Biofuels are among the available options to decarbonize transport in the short to medium term, especially for aviation, marine, and heavy-duty vehicles. The Project will contribute to the biofuel value chain development in Kenya, promoting the production of biofuel from oilseeds without competing with food production and increasing market uptake.
additionality: Financial additionality: Financing structure –IFC is considering supporting the Project with long-term funding needed for ramp up of operations and structuring supply chain financing in collaboration with one or more local banks. Non-financial additionality: Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building - IFC will provide MAS advisory services to support the establishment and coordination within the required supply chain. It will also support the implementation of good agricultural practices, professionalization of farmer aggregators and the provision of services required in the implementation of the different crops.

country: Cen Afr, and Anglophne W Africa Region
project_description: Afropa Liberia Inc. (“Afropa” or the “Company”) is a leading beverage and food distribution company in Liberia. The proposed Project is a $20 million debt financing package, comprised of a $10 million A-loan from IFC and a $10 million loan from the IDA20 IFC-MIGA Private Sector Window’s Blended Finance Facility (“IDA PSW-BFF”), aiming to finance the expansion of the Company in Liberia and Sierra Leone. The Company is implementing a $33 million project, aiming to (i) increase its water bottling capacity in Liberia; (ii) refurbish a newly acquired water bottling plant in Sierra Leone; and (iii) finance working capital needs (the “Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Joseph Barbar owns 100% of Afropa (Liberia). Afropa has two subsidiaries: Liberty Investment Limited (Liberia) and Grafton Investment Limited (Sierra Leone). Afropa owns 100% of Liberty Investment and 85% of Grafton Investment. 15% of Grafton Investment is owned by Afropa’s local partner.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost of $33 million includes (i) capex of $30.4 million; and (ii) working capital of $ 2.6 million. The proposed investment is a $10 million of IFC A-loan and a $10 million of IDA PSW-BFF loan.
location_description: The Project is located in Monrovia (Liberia) and Grafton (Sierra Leone).
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to enhance the economy through job creation and added value from its expanded operations. This increased capacity will directly address Sierra Leone and Liberia's pressing need for safe and clean drinking water. Moreover, the Project will have environment impacts in terms of increased water and energy use efficiency. Beyond the Project-level impact, IFC anticipates the Project will contribute to increasing the competitiveness of the bottled water market by exerting competitive pressures on other bottled water producers in Liberia and Sierra Leone to optimize their cost structures and improve the distribution model and operation efficiency.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality stems from the provision of longer-term financing that supports the company’s capital-intensive expansion plans. Non-financial additionality comes from IFC’s support to align the Company’s operations with IFC’s Performance Standards.
Country: Cen Afr, and Anglophne W Africa Region

project_description: Warehouses de Pauw NV (WDP or the Company), a listed Belgian Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT), has requested IFC to provide a long-term loan to support the building of semi-industrial and logistics property throughout various cities in Romania (the Project) over the next few years.
sponsor_shareholders: WDP is a listed Belgian Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) that develops, owns, acquires, and manages logistics, warehouses, and class A semi-industrial property. It has a portfolio of assets covering, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg, and Romania.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is around €900 million and entails the Company's capital expenditures in Romania. IFC’s proposal to provide a green financing package of up to €300 million consists of (i) a senior loan from IFC’s own account, (ii) a senior loan from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP), and (iii) a senior syndicated loan, to partially finance this investment plan.
location_description: Romania
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects through increased access to modern and high-quality logistics and business infrastructure, and (ii) environmental effects, through the development of green certified buildings. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater integration in Romania’s industrial property sector via demonstration and replication channels.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided through long-term innovative financing structure and resource mobilization. Non-financial additionality is provided via knowledge sharing and capacity building as well as standard setting for ESG best practices.

project_description: The proposed investment is for IFC to be the sole subscriber to an up to FJD 27.0 million (approximately US$11.8 million) corporate bond issued by Tappoo Holdings Limited (“THL”), a leading diversified business group in Fiji, with operations including retail, wholesale, manufacturing, automotive and hospitality. Proceeds will be used to support THL to develop green buildings to meet its need for additional retail and warehousing space (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: THL is a family owned business through a nominee company in Fiji, which has 7 individual and equal shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing to be the sole subscriber to the proposed corporate bond of up to FJD 27.0 million (approximately US$11.8 million equivalent). The project is expected to be supported by the IDA PSW Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
location_description: The project is located in Suva, Fiji.
development_impact: Project-level impact: (i) stakeholder effects on employees through increased jobs and gender equity (ii) stakeholder effects on suppliers through increased demand, and (iii) environmental effects, through the development of green certified buildings. Market-level impact: (i) promote sustainability in Fiji’s commercial property sector via demonstration and replication channels; and (ii) contribute to deepening of the capital markets in Fiji.
additionality: IFC's additionality includes (i) long-term financing with innovative financing structure, which is not readily available in the market; (ii) standard setting of best ESG practices, including gender and corporate governance; and (iii) capacity building for the adoption of green building standards.

sector: Garment and Apparel (Without Fabric , Excluding Footwear)
project_description: This project is proposed under IFC’s Global Trade Supplier Finance program (“GTSF” or the “Program”) approved by the IFC Board on September 21, 2010 (Original Project #28723) and an additional increase approved on December 15, 2022. Under GTSF, IFC provides short-term financing to suppliers, (“Suppliers”), in emerging markets selling to large companies, (“Buyers”), on open account terms. Under this project, IFC will provide financing to Hugo Boss AG (“Hugo Boss” or “the Company”) for Suppliers based in Vietnam, Bangladesh and other emerging market countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Hugo Boss is a leading European apparel, footwear, accessories, and fragrance brand founded in 1924. Hugo Boss is listed on Frankfurt Stock Exchange and NASDAQ with majority of shares free float held by retail and institutional investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project (‘the Project”) within the GTSF facility is expected to be US$50 million for Hugo Boss’s Suppliers in emerging markets.
location_description: GTSF-approved jurisdictions, including Vietnam, Bangladesh and other emerging market countries.

sector: Other Textile Products (Including Industrial and Medical Products)
project_description: Fitesa Naotecidos S.A. (“Fitesa” or the “Company”) is one of largest global manufacturers of nonwoven fabrics for hygiene, medical, and industrial sectors. With headquarters in Porto Alegre, southern Brazil, Fitesa operates 22 plants and 5 innovation centers across 12 countries. Fitesa is undergoing an expansion project to increase its capacity in Brazil.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded by Mr. Sheun Ming Ling in 1973. Fitesa continues to be fully owned by the Ling family. The Company has independent management.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing an A Loan of up to US$60 million to support Fitesa’s capital expenditure and related working capital at its three major plants in Brazil, aimed at increasing capacity of innovative nonwoven materials.
location_description: Investments will be made at Fitesa’s facilities located in São Paulo and Rio Grande do Sul states, Brazil.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project will contribute to generate direct indirect value-addition through its impact on supply chain and consumer spending. The project is anticipated to have an environmental impact, as it aims to implement measures and innovative technologies to increase the use of climate-resilient production processes. At the market level, the Project may contribute to enhancing the competitiveness of the non-woven textile industry in Brazil.
additionality: IFC is providing long-term financing to Fitesa, which is not so readily available in the market. In addition, the Company will benefit from IFC's Environmental and Social performance standards and IFC's sectoral knowledge.

project_description: CHO Group, (“CHO” or the “Company”), was established in 1996 and is a leading olive oil producer in Tunisia. The Company’s facilities are mainly located in the region of Sfax, Tunisia, and its destination markets span over 50 countries worldwide. CHO retains a workforce of over 950 employees. The proposed Project of equity injection will enable CHO, while strengthening its balance sheet and reducing its costs, to continue implementing its strategic plan aiming to enhance its global market position and ensure and diversify sourcing of raw material beyond Tunisia. ?
sponsor_shareholders: CHO was created in 1996 by three entrepreneurs, Mr. Abdelaziz Makhloufi, Mr. Moncef Rekik, and Mr. Abderazzak Tounsi. The original founders own directly or indirectly about 88.5 percent of shares. The remaining is held by SICAR Invest.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is up to US$20 million common equity and mobilization of up to US$50 million equity from co-investors.?
location_description: Sfax, Tunisia.
development_impact: The proposed project will (i) strengthen CHO's balance sheet, enabling the effective execution of its strategic plan on reducing raw material costs, focusing on high-margin products, diversifying sourcing, and geographic expansion, (ii) improve the livelihoods of both olive farmer suppliers and MSME olive oil suppliers, and (iii) generate positive environmental impacts by supporting CHO's initiatives toward green transformation, promoting the development of smart, efficient irrigation systems tailored to specific olive varieties and production conditions. Beyond the project, the project is expected to enhance the competitiveness of Tunisia's olive oil sector by supporting CHO, the market leader, in its efforts to grow, diversify production, improve yields, and expand into new export markets through a vertically integrated business model.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is both financial and non-financial and comes in the form of (i) financing structure through equity not readily available in Tunisia for agribusiness companies; (ii) resource mobilization; (iii) standard setting; and (iv) knowledge, innovation, and capacity building through advisory services. IFC expects the Project to strengthen linkages with suppliers, improve employment and domestic value addition through economy-wide linkages, and generate positive environmental impacts via the promotion of irrigation systems. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater competitiveness in the olive oil sector in Tunisia.

sector: Garment and Apparel (Without Fabric , Excluding Footwear)
project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support Star Garments Group (Private) Limited (“Star Garments” or the “Company”), a Sri Lankan garments manufacturing company and wholly owned subsidiary of Charles Komar & Sons to build a greenfield Cut-Make-Trim (CMT) operation in Togo through a newly formed subsidiary (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Star Garments Group is 100% owned by Charles Komar & Sons, a US-based family-owned group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at US$25 million. IFC’s proposed investment in Star Garments is a US$7.5 million corporate A-loan and a US$7.5m subordinated loan provided by International Development Private Sector Window (“IDA PSW”) to support the Company in implementing the Project.
location_description: The funds will be used in the Star Garments factory located in the Arise Industrial Zone, Plateforme Industrielle d’Adetikope (PIA) in Lome, in the Republic of Togo.
development_impact: The project helps finance a Sri-Lanka garments manufacturer to expand its operations in Togo. Economy-wide effects: The Ready-Made Garments (“RMG”) sector in West Africa was badly hit during the onset of the pandemic and it is gradually recovering. Against this backdrop, the Project is expected to have various positive economy-wide effects, including i) domestic and regional value addition, from increased exports through the expansion of the CMT operations; ii) the direct creation of 2,000 formal manufacturing jobs, mostly for women, and a larger number of indirect jobs. These effects will be assessed in detail during the appraisal. Employee effects resulting from training and coaching will also be assessed for their materiality. Contribution to market creation and market competitiveness: The Project is expected to improve the sector competitiveness through the expansion of the CMT operations to achieve scale, and therefore improve the efficiency of apparel production in the West Africa region, including through backward integration (the 2nd phase of the Project). As the first mover in the Togolese market with operations at scale, Star Garments can serve a significant demonstration effect, and support the case for developing the textiles sector in West Africa. This could have significant ripple effects, attracting other investors and players in the region, and permitting the West African textiles sector to follow the trajectory of other successful cases (Bangladesh and Sri Lanka).
additionality: Financial additionality – Financing structure: IFC will provide a long-term loan with a sufficient grace period, which is not readily available to the company in the local markets. The loan will be structured to fit the needs of a greenfield apparel project that needs sufficient time for construction and ramp-up. The IDA PSW subordinated loan also gives sufficient cushion to provide the necessary cover for the IFC senior tranche. Non-financial additionality- Standard Setting: IFC will provide technical, Environmental Health, and Safety expertise to improve overall environmental and safety (E&S) performance as well as introduce the international best practice to the client. IFC will also help SGG strengthen the workplace policies for the female workforce (i.e., gender advisory).

project_description: IFC is supporting (i) expansion of modern food retail in several Western Balkan countries (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, and North Macedonia) by helping Schwarz Group to launch its operations in these new markets; and (ii) the Group’s existing retail operations in Romania, Moldova, Bulgaria, Croatia and Serbia (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Schwarz Group, a privately held retail chain based in Germany. It operates mostly in Europe under the Lidl and Kaufland brands. The borrower is SG Finance & Treasury Limited, the Irish treasury subsidiary of the Schwarz Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost to be incurred in the 2023 financial year is estimated at about EUR500 million. The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$250 million equivalent in EUR A loan (the IFC Loan) for IFC’s own account to partially finance the Project.
location_description: Investments under the Project are planned to be made in different cities of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Romania, Moldova, Bulgaria, Croatia and Serbia.
development_impact: The Project is expected to (i) increase customer access to high-quality affordable food; (ii) improve food safety standards and enhance the quality of retail offerings; and (iii) improve energy and water use efficiency. At the market level, IFC anticipates the Project will improve the competitiveness of the retail sector in target countries by improving food quality standards and facilitating the adoption of green building standards in the retail property sector.
additionality: IFC will provide financial additionality by offering an innovative and flexible financing instrument that is not readily available in the local markets of the Project countries. IFC will also provide non-financial additionality by mitigating Schwarz Group’s non-commercial perceived country risks associated with new market entries and by strengthening the long-term partnership between both institutions.

project_description: The proposed investment is a corporate finance loan of up to Euro250 million to ARISE Integrated Industrials Platform Ltd (“ARISE IIP” or “ARISE”) and four (4) of its subsidiaries. The funds will be used for Special Economic Zone (SEZ) and Industrial Park developments in (i) Glo Djigbé Industrial Zone (GDIZ) in Benin, (ii) Platforme Industrielle Du Congo (PIC) in the Republic of Congo, (iii) Bugesera Sprecial Economic Zone (BSEZ) in Rwanda, and (iv) Plateforme Industrielle d’Adétikopé (PIA) in Togo collectively referred to as the Project. The IDA PSW Blended Finance Facility is expected to support the project as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: ARISE shareholders are Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) and Africa Transformation and Industrialization Fund (ATIF), who own 75.92% and 24.08%, respectively. AFC is a multilateral financial institution created and owned by African sovereign states, with a minority private sector ownership, and operated in line with private sector governance principles. ATIF is a management and employee-sponsored fund led by Mr. Gagan Gupta, ARISE's Founder and Chief Executive Officer. ATIF is registered in the United Arab Emirates and regulated by the Abu Dhabi Global Market
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: ARISE is executing a Euro 870 million investment program across four (4) countries (Benin, Congo, Rwanda, and Togo). The proposed IFC Euro 250 million financing package consists of an IFC A-Loan of Euro 63 million, B/parallel loans of Euro 107 million, and an IDA PSW loan of Euro 80 million. The financing for each country will be (i) GDIZ Benin with Euro 100 million, (ii) PIC Republic of Congo with Euro 80 million, (iii) BSEZ Rwanda with Euro 40 million, and (iv) PIA Togo with Euro 30 million.
location_description: The Project locations are in countries with ARISE subsidiary operations. In Benin, the Project is located in Tori-Bossito and Ze, about 45 km from Cotonou along the interstate national road. In the Republic of Congo, the Project is located in Loango, approximately 15 km West of Pointe Noire and adjacent to the Atlantic Ocean. In Rwanda, the Project is located in the Bugesera district, about 50 km South of Kigali, near the new Bugesera airport, and 10km before the Burundi border. In Togo, the Project is in the municipality of Zio 1 (Cantons of Dalavé and Kpomé), approximately 27 kilometers (km) from the City of Lomé.
development_impact: Through the proposed investment, IFC will support ARISE, a company with a unique business model that goes beyond providing Industrial real estate but also deploys several core operational offerings and services to accelerate the industrialization of its host countries. The African continent remains the least industrialized part of the world despite being a global source of raw commodities- such as agro products, solid minerals, and fuels for energy. The region continues to export most of its commodities in unprocessed raw forms, losing significant opportunities to add value locally, create jobs, capture wealth, and increase economic complexity. ARISE provides a complete package\ecosystem of services to increase value addition on local commodities across Africa -by offering industrial real estate, commodities sourcing, investment promotion, one-stop-shop regulatory support, export market linkages, skills development of local communities, etc. ARISE’s zones are therefore set up to industrialize value chains and facilitate domestic processing of raw commodities, such as soya, cashews, cotton, and wood, amongst others (rather than continue raw exports of commodities). The most significant expected project-level outcomes are stakeholder effects through increased access to high-quality industrial spaces for tenants and supply chain development. The Project is expected to have significant economy-wide effects by providing high-quality formal jobs and contributing to GDP via value addition in agricultural commodities. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment has the potential to promote greater integration of agricultural value chains in the target countries via demonstration and replication channels. The large-scale nature of this project will provide an obvious demonstration case, which could have a catalytic impact on the industrial property market in the target countries.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide scarce long-term financing that better matches the cash flow of the underlying businesses, improves the Company’s debt profile, and enhances its access to complementary capital. IFC will also help build the company's capacity in food safety management to support tenants within its zones, smallholder farmer financing, and green building standards.

project_description: Marifala, Guinea’s first furniture company, plans to construct (i) an industrial complex located in the industrial zone of Maférenyah (~60 km from Conakry) that will enable the company to consolidate its operations and triple its capacity, and ii) 4 retail outlet stores: 3 in Conakry in Guinea and 1 in Bamako in Mali (“The Project”). The Project total cost is US$20 million and will be financed 35% by Sponsor equity (US$7 million) and the remaining by IFC and IDA PSW. The proposed investment entails an 8-year senior secured loan of up to EUR12 million (c. US$13 million).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 2007 and based in Conakry, Galerie Marifala Sarlu (Marifala or the Company) is Guinea's leading furniture company. They design and produce furniture and doors for retail and office markets. Marifala is managed and fully owned by Mr. Abdoulaye Diallo (Sponsor). Initially an importer, the Company expanded into furniture production in 2018, becoming the only in-country producer in Guinea. Marifala plans to start exporting to neighboring countries from 2024.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost of US$20 million will be financed with 35% from Sponsor equity (US$7 million) and the remaining from IFC and IDA PSW (US$13 million). This includes US$15.6 million for the industrial complex, US$3.2 million for the retail outlet stores, and US$1.2 million for working capital. The proposed investment is an 8-year senior secured loan of up to EUR12 million (approximately US$13 million). The loan amount consists of €6 million from IFC A loan and €6 million from IDA PSW BFF Loan.
location_description: The industrial complex will be situated in the Mafreyah industrial zone, located ~60 km outside of Conakry, Guinea. Three out of the four showrooms envisioned in this Project will be located in Conakry. The fourth showroom is planned for Mali at a later stage.
development_impact: Project level outcomes: (i) Stakeholder (customers) - Increased timely access to quality and affordable furniture products by consumers through customized mass domestic production; and (ii) Economy wide effects - increased value addition and job creation along the furniture supply chain. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to contribute to increasing competitiveness of the sector in Guinea.
additionality: Financial additionality: Financing structure -The proposed investment is an 8-year (including 2.5-year grace period) senior secured loan of up to €12M (equivalent to ~US$13M), consisting of €6M A loan from IFC and of €6M loan from IDA PSW BFF. Access to long-term financing locally is limited and when existing are not comparable to IFC's terms due to constraints faced by local banks. Non-financial additionality: IFC will deploy industry expertise to strengthen E&S practices across the Company’s operations by aligning them with IFC performance standards and industry best practices. Further, IFC Upstream/Advisory will support MariFala to establish its own concession forestry operations in Guinea, enabling the Company to source solid wood in a traceable and sustainable manner that meets IFC performance standards.

project_description: Grupo Cieno (“Cienogroup”, “Cieno” or the “Group”), founded 30 years ago, is a private, family-owned group based in Bogota, Colombia engaged in: (i) private healthcare plans; (ii) hospitals and health services; and (iii) pharmaceutical manufacturing .
sponsor_shareholders: Cieno Group is 100% controlled by the Barrero family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost stands at COP125bn (~US$31 million equivalent) and IFC investment consists of an up to US$25 million A loan (or COP equivalent), IFC’s own account.
location_description: Cienogroup’s operations are located in Colombia.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are (i) increased availability of quality healthcare services, (ii) increased access to quality healthcare products, and (iii) direct/indirect job creation. There is also potential to strengthen competitive pressures in the health sector in Colombia.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide Cienogroup with long-term financing that is not readily available in the country. It will also help the group's digital transformation journey and implementation of international best practices.

project_description: The proposed Project involves a total investment of up to US$40 million (in equivalent INR) to Sunteck Realty Limited (Sunteck or the Company) and/or its subsidiaries for developing housing projects. The IFC financing will be used for expansion of the Company’s operations, including for part-financing 4-6 housing projects to be mutually identified by the Company and IFC primarily in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) in India (altogether the “Project”). The housing projects are expected to be green housing projects in the suburbs of Mumbai and will help develop these micro-markets and strengthen the Company’s presence in these locations.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment is for up to US$40 million (in equivalent INR) in the form of quasi-equity through financial instruments to be used for part financing housing projects mutually identified by IFC and Sunteck mostly in the MMR.
location_description: The projects are expected to be located across various suburbs in the MMR.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are (i) increased access to good quality housing in underserved micro-markets and (ii) environmental effects through improved energy and water efficiency. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will enhance competitiveness in the market through (i) competitive pressures on developers already operating in the target micro-markets to improve the price and quality of their projects and (ii) demonstration effects to other developers that will be incentivized to expand in smaller micro-markets, adapt their business model to achieve economies of scale.
additionality: (i) Non-financial additionality: IFC will support the Company in developing new residential EDGE-certified green buildings. IFC will provide advice for the Company to achieve this target and improve its green building framework so that it can attain, in a systematic fashion, both the development of green projects and the implementation of cost-efficient, energy-saving upgrades on some of the ongoing developments. (ii) Financial additionality: IFC will provide long term financing tailored to the cash flows of the housing project(s) which is not easily available in the market.

company_name: Africa50 Infrastructure Acceleration Fund I LP
project_description: The proposed equity investment is for up to US$20 million in Africa50 Infrastructure Acceleration Fund I LP (the “Fund” or “IAF”) set up by Africa50 Infrastructure Investment Partners I Manager Ltd (the “Fund Manager”) to invest in value-add infrastructure assets in Africa and with a core focus across Power & Energy, Water & Sanitation, Transport & Logistics, and Digital & Social infrastructure. The Fund Manager is a subsidiary of Africa50, the Fund’s sponsor.
sponsor_shareholders: Africa50 Infrastructure Investment Partners I Manager Ltd is registered in Mauritius and was created by Africa50 in 2021. Africa50 is a pan-African multilateral institution created by the African Development Bank (AfDB) and currently capitalized by 31 African governments, two African central banks, and the AfDB.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Manager’s objective is to raise a total of US$500 million for the Fund. IFC’s proposed investment consists of an equity investment of up to US$20 million as a Limited Partner in the Fund.
location_description: The Fund is domiciled in Mauritius and will target investments in or substantially benefiting Africa. The Fund will have a pan-African focus.
development_impact: The main development outcomes at the Fund level are expected to stem from increased access to private equity capital, value creation for established companies, contribution to reducing carbon emissions, and positive economic and social impact in the countries and communities where the Fund invests in Africa, especially in the infrastructure sector. Private Equity (PE) investment in Africa remains amongst the lowest across all regions, representing less than 3 percent of the total private equity investment volumes in emerging markets over five years from 2018 to 2022. Within this context, IFC expects that the Fund will support around 10 companies across Africa, within thematic areas focused on Digital & Social infrastructure; Power & Energy; Transport & Logistics; and Water & Sanitation. Beyond the Fund’s intended investment activities, IFC expects the Fund’s success to increase financial integration and capital mobilization within Africa’s PE market by introducing new domestic institutional investors and attracting more international institutional capital into the private equity segment. Deepening the segment’s links to domestic institutional capital that is aligned with making long-term investments will be an important step towards the longer-term sustainability of the PE market in Africa.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is expected to be both financial and non-financial. IFC’s financial additionality will support the Fund in achieving its first and final close targets. Fundraising in the Africa region faces a number of challenges including high risk perception, foreign exchange risk impacting commercial returns, and economic uncertainty. IFC will provide non-financial additionality by reducing non-commercial risk and encouraging participation from additional investors. IFC’s entry as an anchor investor into the first close, in combination with expected support from other DFIs, will help signal confidence in the first-time fund manager and will provide comfort to institutional investors that are looking to come in at subsequent closes.
Company Name: Africa50 Infrastructure Acceleration Fund I LP

project_description: The Project consists of an up to US$150 million equity linked notes issuance whose proceeds will support PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GoTo or Company) of which it is proposed that IFC invests up to US$125 million as an anchor investor. The proceeds will be utilized to strengthen and grow the Company’s offering across its three business segments including e-commerce, on-demand services (transport and food delivery) and financial solutions, and further promote the unique integrated technology solutions business model of GoTo.
sponsor_shareholders: GoTo is a listed company with a diversified shareholding. GoTo’s senior management and founders has majority voting control: (i) Andre Soelistyo (Co-Founder); (ii) Kevin Bryan Aluwi (Co-Founder of Gojek); (iii) William Tanuwijaya (Commissioner / Co-Founder of Tokopedia); and (iv) Melissa Siska Juminto – (President, e-Commerce), who are all Series B shareholders. Under GoTo’s dual-class voting structure, the holders of Series A shares and Series B shares have the same rights with the exception being that of voting rights (each Series A and B shares having 1 and 30 votes respectively).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project consists of an up to US$150 million equity linked notes issuance of which it is proposed that IFC invests up to US$125m as an anchor investor.
location_description: GoTo is one of the largest digital ecosystem in Southeast Asia with over 65 million annual transaction users (ATUs), 15 million registered merchants and 2.6 million registered driver-partners. IFC's investment will be part of the funding that will fund capex and operational expenses and will be primarily in Indonesia.
development_impact: Project Outcomes - Supplier Effects – Increased Access to Clients and Improved Efficiency via Adoption of Digital Technologies: The Project will facilitate local suppliers/retailers’ access to a wider and more reliable customer base, which will contribute to strengthening the supply chain in the region. Furthermore, MSME merchants will also benefit from the improved operational efficiency via adoption of digital merchant solutions. Market Creation – Integration: The Project will promote greater integration of domestic suppliers by helping them to reach buyers beyond their traditional customer base. The success of the Project could help boost confidence in online businesses, potentially scaling up business opportunities for smaller retailers in the region.
additionality: Own-account equity: IFC’s financial additionality will be through providing essential capital to address the Company’s funding need and support its continued growth. Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC will leverage its global experience to provide support to the Company as it scales up operations to meet its sustainability ambitions.

company_name: Operadora y Procesadora de Productos Marinos Omarsa S.A.
project_description: Omarsa (the “Company”) is one of the leading integrated shrimp producers and processors in Ecuador. The proposed investment will support the development of 536 hectares of state-of-the-art farms in their Puna location (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Omarsa's majority shareholders and Project sponsors are the Vanoni family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC Investment consists of up to US$ 20 million “A” loan.
location_description: Development of 536 hectares (ha) of shrimp in Puna location.
development_impact: • Export-oriented sector development.
