The Project will contribute to the development of a competitive export-oriented sector with extensive linkages throughout the value chain that is key for Ecuador's economy. • Private sector development. IFC's funding will support further professionalization of a family-owned business as the company expands as one of the sector's regional leaders. • Stakeholder effects. The Project contributes to the improvement of global food security by increasing the production and export of high-nutritionist food. This will translate into an increase of people fed per year over the life of the project. • Job creation. Omarsa currently employs about 7,155 people. The investment will generate value for the Ecuadorian economy through direct and indirect employment opportunities. • Reducing supply volatility. Through this intervention, IFC hopes to promote the resilience of the global food supply market and contribute to stabilizing global food supply and prices.
additionality: • Long-term financing. IFC will provide tailor-made long-term financing that is not readily available in Ecuador in competitive terms. • Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building. IFC will potentially provide resource efficiency advisory services to the company. • E&S policy and practices. IFC will support Omarsa to further improve its environmental and social standards and strengthen the Company's compliance with IFC’s Performance Standards and global best practices.
Company Name: Operadora y Procesadora de Productos Marinos Omarsa S.A.

project_description: The proposed project consists of an equity investment of up to US$ 30 million in equity in the South African-domiciled African Infrastructure Investment Fund 4 (the “Fund” or “AIIF4”) managed by African Infrastructure Investment Managers (“AIIM” or “the Fund Manager”) to invest in value-add infrastructure assets in Africa, with a focus on Sub-Saharan Africa, in three thematic areas: Digitization; Energy Transition; Mobility and Logistics (“the Project”). AIIF4 will target investments in growth capital assets to facilitate enhanced investment returns.
sponsor_shareholders: AIIM, was established in 2000 and is one of the largest dedicated infrastructure fund managers in Africa with assets under management of US$2.7 billion. AIIM is a subsidiary of Old Mutual Limited a leading African financial services provider with operations in 17 countries across 3 continents and assets under management of US$82 billion. With 22 years of operating infrastructure experience, AIIM has managed 7 funds and returned US$1.3 billion to limited partners (LPs) to date.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund was launched with a target size of US$ 500 million. IFC’s proposed investment is for up to US$ 30 million in equity in the Fund.
location_description: Pan-Africa with a focus on South Africa, Kenya, Cote d’Ivoire, Senegal, Morocco and Egypt.
development_impact: The main Project outcomes are expected to stem from the Fund’s ability to set and meet sector-specific commitments around improving access efficiency and/or quality of infrastructure in the targeted countries with a focus on digitization, energy transition, and logistics. The Project may also deliver positive environmental effects such as reduced GHG emissions. The Fund’s pipeline is diversified across nine sub-sectors, with a large exposure to renewable energy and projects located in IDA countries where infrastructure capacity is inadequate to support economic growth. The investment may also strengthen competitiveness in the relevant sectors by demonstrating the viability and efficiency of private sector engagement as the targeted markets face massive investment needs in digitization, energy, and logistics to sustainably meet growing demand. In addition, it could also enhance financial integration by helping deepen financing structures to catalyze investments to emerging markets.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is expected to be both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists in providing patient equity to support the fundraising round of a Fund Manager specialized in the infrastructure investing in Sub-Saharan Africa, the region with the lowest private equity fundraising globally, with only US$12 billion raised between 2017 and 2021. IFC’s financial additionality is further strengthened by potentially co-investing in underlying projects subject to meeting specific criteria. Non-financial additionality involves non-commercial risk mitigation by providing comfort to additional investors through signalling that the Fund will be managed in adherence to international standards, and with adequate risk mitigation leveraging its experience investing in the targeted emerging markets. Furthermore, IFC is expected to provide technical expertise to strengthen the Fund’s capacity to manage environmental and social (E&S) risks by participating on the E&S Subcommittee.

project_description: Facility for Energy Inclusion (“FEI” or the “Fund”) is a dedicated pan-African decentralized renewable energy (“DRE”) focused structured debt fund. The Fund provides debt financing to companies operating in the small to mid-scale distributed power sub-sectors, including Commercial and Industrial (“C&I”), Telecom Energy Service Companies (“T-ESCO”), Mini-Grids (“MGs”) and small Independent Power Producers (“IPPs”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund’s limited partners are The African Development Bank, the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development through KFW and Norfund. The AfDB also invested on behalf of the Clean Technology Fund and the European Commission. The Fund has existing credit from African Development Bank and the Austrian Development Bank. The Fund’s Project Preparation Facility (“PPF”) is funded by the Global Environment Facility through the African Development Bank and provides returnable grant funding to fund due diligence and preparatory costs prior to financial close of transactions FEI is seeking to lend to. The Fund Manager is Cygnum Capital, founded in 2008, Cygnum Capital, formerly Lion’s Head Group, (“CG” or the “Fund Manager”) is an experienced asset manager in green investments with an extensive track record in Africa. It has 70+ dedicated professionals spread across their offices in London, Nairobi, Lagos, Dubai and Amsterdam. CG currently manages 5 funds with US$740mn of AUM, partnering with leading DFIs and institutional investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed financing package of up to US$80mn is comprised of: (i) an IFC A loan of up to US$30mn; (ii) a Trust loan of up to US$20mn from the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (“MCPP”); and (iii) concessional senior Blended Finance (“BF”) loans of up to US$30mn, of which up to US$22.5mn from IDA20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (“IDA20 PSW BFF”), and up to US$7.5mn from Finland – IFC Climate Change Program (“IFC-FIN”).
location_description: Pan Africa Fund
development_impact: The main project-level outcomes are expected to stem from the stakeholder effects through increased access to affordable and quality electricity supply to C&I customers, residential customers (through mini grid or IPPs) and other users of DRE solutions in Africa. The project will also have positive environmental effects stemming from the provision of solar solutions displaying power supplied by more carbon intensive sources. Beyond the project, the investment is expected to demonstrate the viability of a model that offers senior long-term debt structured as asset finance, equipment finance or project finance to DRE customers for the implementation of renewable energy solutions, with the potential of leading to replication in the target markets.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is expected to be both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists in providing medium-term debt that is not readily available in the market to support the largely nascent DRE industry in Africa. The financing will be supported by blended finance which will enable the Fund to reach target size, while continuing its investment in countries that face higher inherent risks at a reasonable price for the borrower. IFC is also expected to mobilize financing from MCPP. IFC’s participation is expected to contribute to non-financial additionality through standard setting by supporting the adoption and implementation of a framework to manage environmental and social risks and impacts from the Fund’s investments.

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: The proposed investment is to contribute to a financing package of up to US$40 million (“IFC Loans”), including IFC A loan for up to US$10 million, Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) of up to US$10 million and a loan from the IDA PSW Blended Finance Facility (“IDA PSW BFF”) which is subordinated in liquidation, of up to US$20 million to Badsha Textiles Limited (BTL) belonging to Badsha Group, the largest yarn manufacturer in Bangladesh and one of the top-tier, vertically integrated sweater and woven garment manufacturing and exporting groups in Bangladesh. The IFC Loans will support setting up of a greenfield spinning mill with a production capacity of 70,373 MT per year to manufacture premium cotton, viscose, blended cotton, cotton denim, poly cotton yarns (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: BTL belongs to Badsha Group. Established in 2004, Badsha Group, comprising four companies, is a family-owned business, founded by Mr. Md Badsha Mia who, along with his wife Mrs. Asma Begum, and his grown-up children Mr. Kamal Uddin, Ms. Sharmin Sultana and Mr. Mohiuddin Ahmed.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$160.9 million and is proposed to be financed with a debt to equity ratio of ~60:40 as follows: long-term debt of US$97.3 million and equity of US$63.7 million in the form of internal cash generation. IFC loans will be of US$40 million comprised of A Loan US$10 million, MCPP financing of up to US$10 million, IDA PSW BFF loan of US$20 million, with a tenor of 8 years including 2 years grace period. The balance US$57.3 million debt will be provided by other long term lenders.
location_description: The Project is located in Habiganj, approximately 150 kms northeast of Dhaka City, in Bangladesh, an IDA country.
development_impact: Economy-Wide Impacts: The Project will enable Badsha Group to further expand the capacity of it spinning operations, strengthen its manufacturing supply chain, and ensure better quality control. IFC anticipates that the Project will contribute to Bangladesh’s economy by helping the downstream entities of the Group as well as other RMG exporters of the country to produce higher value-added garments. The Project also has a strong employment effect and will create thousands of additional direct and indirect jobs and female employment in the value chain. Competitiveness: By increasing the local availability of high-quality yarn, the Project would reduce the lead time in the knitting and RMG sector, which is a key requirement of international buyers, and thereby contribute to preserving Bangladesh’s competitiveness as a global player in the textile and apparel market.
additionality: (i) IFC will provide financial additionality through a US$ loan with a tenor of 8 years, including 2 years of grace period. The Company requires the long tenor loan to have the necessary financial flexibility to implement advanced manufacturing technology and investments in resource efficiencies. (ii) IFC is expected to provide concessional financing which will make the financing affordable for the client. (iii) The Group will continue implementing recommendations from Partnership for Cleaner Textile (PaCT) and Better Work

company_name: Aditya Birla Fashion And Retail Limited
project_description: The proposed transaction entails an investment of up to INR7.5 billion (approximately US$91 million) in the form of subscription to Non-Convertible Debt securities (NCDs) issued by Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (“ABFRL” or the “Company”). The NCDs will be rated, listed, unsecured, redeemable, and denominated in Indian Rupees. In May 2023, ABFRL entered into definitive agreements to acquire TCNS Clothing Co. Limited (“TCNS” or the “Target”). The proposed investment will be utilized towards the acquisition of TCNS and the long-term working capital needs of the Company.
sponsor_shareholders: The Aditya Birla Group family with 55.47% shareholdings is the sponsor of the Company. Being a listed company, the balance shares are held by financial institutional investors and the public.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The cash outflow for acquisition is estimated at INR 16.50 billion, (approximately US$200 million), of which IFC’s proposed investment would fund up to INR7.5 billion and the balance is proposed to be funded through ABFRL’s internal accruals and equity.
location_description: The Project location will be India.
development_impact: The Project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects on female employees through increased access to quality jobs and skill development opportunities and (ii) effects on suppliers through increased business opportunities and integration into the modern retail supply chain. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote competitiveness and inclusiveness through demonstration and replication channels.
additionality: IFC’s additionality stems from: • Financing Structure: IFC is providing longer tenor debt that matches the payback period of the acquisition, which is longer than what is usually available for acquisition financing. • Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC will engage the Gender advisory team to conduct gender advisory and help build capacity for a gender-inclusive ABFRL workforce. IFC will provide technical support for the Company in achieving the EDGE certification, which would support the Company’s sustainability strategy on gender and diversity. • Standard Setting: The Company will benefit from IFC’s expertise in Environmental and Social (E&S) standards, and IFC will share international best E&S practices with the Company.
Company Name: Aditya Birla Fashion And Retail Limited

project_description: The Project is a container terminal with capacity of 3.3 million Twenty-foot equivalent unit (“MTEU”) located in Damietta Port on the Mediterranean Sea in Egypt (“Project”). The Project will be carried under a 30-year Concession Agreement granted by the Damietta Port Authority (“DPA”) under the Ministry of Transport (“MoT”) . Construction is expected to begin in end of 2023 with initial operations expected to commence in January 2025.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project will be developed by Damietta Alliance Container Terminal S.A.E. (the “Company”), a special purpose vehicle incorporated in Egypt, owned (39%) by Hapag-Lloyd AG (“HLAG”), (29.5%) by Eurogate International GmbH (“Eurogate”), and (29.5%) by Contship Italia S.p.A. (“Contship”, together the “Sponsors”), and 1% by Middle East Logistics & Consultant Group S.A.E and Ship & C.R.E.W. S.A.E each. HLAG is one of the largest ship liners and operates the fifth-largest fleet of container ships worldwide. By the end of 2022, HLAG had c. 14,200 employees in more than 400 offices in 135 countries, and its vessels carried 11.8 MTEU, on par with 2021. HLAG is also a founding member of THEA, one of the biggest shipping alliances worldwide, which includes HLAG, Yang Ming, Ocean Network Express, and Hyundai Merchant Marine. Eurogate is a top 15 independent operator of container terminals in Europe with twelve terminals located in Germany, Russia, Italy, Portugal, Cyprus, and Morocco and a total capacity of 16.9 MTEU and 69 container gantries, including Germany’s only deep-water container terminal. Eurogate has a longstanding relationship with HLAG through its operations in the German ports of Hamburg, Bremerhaven, and Wilhelmshaven, the three largest ports in Germany, and it also operates HLAG’s West-Med transshipment volumes at the TangerMED port in Morocco. Contship is a subsidiary of Eurokai, one of the shareholders of Eurogate, and is currently controlled by Eurokai (66.6%) and Eurogate (33.4%). Contship operates (directly and indirectly) four port terminals with 23 STS cranes and 12 mobile cranes, one rail hub, and transport companies. On a standalone basis in the Italian market, the group handled a total of 1.5 MTEU containers with a market share of 16% in 2021.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at c. US$665 million, financed with c. 70% by debt and 30% by equity. The debt is to be funded with senior loans from IFC, EBRD, DEG, AIIB, and Proparco. The proposed IFC investments include (i) A Loan for up to US$125 million and (ii) Risk Management Products in the form of interest rate swaps with a loan equivalent exposure of c. US$10 million.
location_description: The Project will be located in Damietta Port on the Mediterranean Sea in Egypt at around 70km from Port Said at the northern end of Suez Canal and 200km from the Greater Cairo Area.
development_impact: The main project-level effect is enhanced access and quality of port services in Egypt through an increase in Port Damietta capacity and operational efficiency with catalyzed economywide effects. Beyond the Project, at the market level, this investment is expected to contribute to enhanced integration through connections to local and new international markets to play a more prominent role in Egypt’s trade while expanding transshipment through connecting additional shipping lines. This will further support the integration and economic development of the east-Mediterranean region to help position Egypt as a global hub for logistics and trade.
additionality: Through this Project, IFC's strong financial additionality is derived a counter-cyclical financing and mobilization role through parallel lending, helping raise additional long-term financing for the project. Therefore, this would send a strong signal to other investors and easing concerns of investing in the infrastructure sector at the time when country risks are heavily emphasized. IFC non-financial additionality is driven by standard setting to achieve adequate E&S performance in line with IFC performance standards.

project_description: The Proposed loan of up to EUR4 million (EUR2 million own account and EUR2 million from IDA PSW) to Société Malienne de Biscuiterie SARL (SOMABIS or “the Company”), the only established biscuit manufacturer in Mali, is to support the Company’s investment program and includes a EUR 6.6 million project. This project will expand the company’s production capacity on a new site with the installation of a new state-of-art production line of biscuit of 1,200 kg per hour (compared to the current line of 650 kg per hour) and a production line of wafers of 500kg per hour, which will be a new business segment for the Company. The new site is in the new industrial zone of Banancoro (in the outskirt of Bamako) and will host two warehouses for the plant and an administration building. The project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) in the amount of up to EUR2 million as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: SOMABIS is as limited liability corporation which was established in 2010 by Moussa Djigue (30% shareholding) and his brother Boubacar Djigue (20%), with the financial support of their father Hassan Djigue (20%), who built a family business in food and textile trade, and also of a close family friend, Amadou Golfa (30%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at EUR6.6 million. IFC’s proposed financing is an A loan of up to EUR2 million and a subordinated loan from IDA PSW of EUR 2 million. The uses of funds include i) capex to fund the Company’s new site construction project as well as ii) working capital requirements.
location_description: The new site is in new industrial zone in the outskirt of Bamako.
development_impact: Project level outcomes: (i) Stakeholder (consumers) - Increased access to fortified biscuits by consumers and therefore contribute to improving nutrition in Mali which has a high prevalence of malnutrition; and (ii) Economy wide effects - increased value addition and job creation along the supply chain. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to contribute to increasing competitiveness of the sector in Mali.
additionality: Financial additionality: Financing structure - the Project consists of A loan of up to US$2million from IFC and a similar amount from IDA PSW repayable within 8 years and with 3 years grace. This kind of long-term financing is not readily available in the local market and is much needed given the country’s macro-economic situation (inflationary pressures and tightened financing from local banks and fragile political/business environment). Non-financial additionality: (i) Knowledge, innovation and capacity building - IFC will leverage the expertise of its agribusiness team to provide advisory support on food safety and fortification practices and plant design review to help acquire Green Building certification; and (ii) Standard setting - the Project is one of the first IFC investments in the food manufacturing sector in this FCS country, which will be an excellent opportunity to set standards especially on the environmental, health, safety, and social levels. IFC is also expected to improve corporate governance of the family-owned company, aligning its operations with IFC standards and industry best practices.

project_description: MAN Holding SAL and Man Holding Limited (together, Man Holding or the Company), a leading integrated Engineering, Procurement and Construction (“EPC”) company in the Middle East region, is undertaking, through its subsidiaries, industrial, commercial and infrastructure projects in GCC, Middle East, North & Western Africa. IFC will provide a senior secured A-Loan of up to US$15.0 million to support the Company in growing its project backlog across the Middle East & Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: Man Holding is a regional EPC company established in 1971 in Lebanon. It is a leading construction company in Lebanon and a landmark builder in the Middle East & Africa with a diverse portfolio covering residential, commercial and infrastructure projects. Man Holding SAL is incorporated in Lebanon and consolidates the group’s operations in Lebanon while Man Holding Limited is incorporated in Guernsey and consolidates operations outside Lebanon. Both entities are owned by Man Holding Luxembourg SCS, which is ultimately owned by Noel, Thierry, Patrick and Aida Abi Nader. The Company employs over 400 skilled professionals and over 3,000 blue-collar workers across different countries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment will be through a senior secured A-Loan of up to US$15.0 million. The Company will use the loan proceeds to support its capacity expansion program by growing its project backlog across the Middle East & Africa.
location_description: The proposed IFC investment will support the working capital requirement of the group in bidding and undertaking construction projects across multiple countries in the Middle East and Africa. These include Lebanon, Jordan, Iraq, Mali, Ghana, Senegal and Ivory Coast among others.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are (i) increased access to quality construction services for infrastructure and properties development in MEA and (ii) access to skills development for local employees and contract workers. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote competitiveness in the construction market through the adoption of new technologies and the introduction of higher quality standards, with demonstration potential.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via the provision of financing structure that is not readily available in the market. Non-financial additionality is provided via (i) capacity building for new market operations and ESG risk management, and (ii) non-commercial risk mitigation through IFC’s stamp of approval which will provide comfort to other investors.

project_description: In July 2023, IFC committed an A-Loan (the ‘IFC Loan’) under the COVID-19 Real Sector Crisis Response Envelope (“RSE”) of US$50 million (“mn”) (eqvt. in Euro) to Coca Cola Beverages Pakistan Limited (“CCBPL” or the “Company”). The IFC Loan will finance the Company’s working capital requirements and support its maintenance capex (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsors are two publicly listed entities: The Coca-Cola Company (“TCCC”), incorporated in the USA, and Coca-Cola Icecek A.S. (“CCI”), incorporated in Turkey. Both are the major shareholders of CCBPL, each owning 49.6% of its shares, with management control with CCI.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The IFC investment consists of an up to US$50 million equivalent A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: CCBPL is headquartered in Lahore, Pakistan, with 7 manufacturing facilities located at Karachi, Rahim Yar Khan, Multan, Lahore, Gujranwala, Faisalabad and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
development_impact: The Project is expected to help sustain Company’s on-going operations allowing it to continue to support economic activity, preserve jobs and build capacity in its supply chain (local sugarcane farmers, MSME retailers, and distributors etc) to withstand shocks and stresses arising from COVID-19’s disruption of supply chains and rising inflation.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is driven by its countercyclical role during the current stressed macro-economic conditions in the country. IFC is providing much-needed liquidity to the Company to fund its increase in working capital requirements and the maintenance capex. IFC will also explore advisory engagements to support implementation of the Company’s gender and sustainability strategy.

project_description: OCP SA (“OCP” or the “Company,” https://www.ocpgroup.ma/ ) plans to design, install and operate greenfield, captive solar power plants at two of the Company’s phosphate mines in central Morocco, with a cumulative installed capacity of 400 MWp including at least 100 MWh of battery storage. The Project is part of an effort from OCP to achieve 100% of green energy.
sponsor_shareholders: OCP SA, a state-owned enterprise, is a fully integrated phosphate fertilizer producer with operations at every stage from mining to processing to sales of phosphate products. The Company is the largest producer and exporter of phosphate rock and phosphoric acid globally. OCP’s shareholders are the Moroccan State and other minority shareholders with, respectively, 94.1% and 5.9% ownership. As part of its sustainability strategy, OCP plans to become carbon neutral by 2040. The Company has increased the share of clean sources in its total energy consumption from 30 percent in 2017 to 47 percent in 2022. Within the electricity segment, OCP sourced 87 percent of its electricity from clean sources in 2022 (cogeneration – 76 percent; and wind – 11 percent), while 13 percent was supplied by ONEE via the national grid. OCP plans to source 100% of its electricity needs through wind, solar (including battery storage) and cogeneration by 2030.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at US$380 million. The proposed IFC investment comprises a senior Green Loan of up to EUR100 million to the Company.
location_description: The captive solar power plants and associated storage will be installed on lands owned by the Company in Benguerir and Khouribga.
development_impact: The Project is expected to: (i) provide cleaner and cheaper energy during both day and evening peak hours (thanks to battery storage) compared to electricity sourced from the grid and (ii) contribute to market creation through: (a) demonstration effect from the first large scale solar PV and battery energy storage project in Morocco and largest in North Africa, (b) enhancing competitiveness of Moroccan industry by allowing the Company to offer more sustainable products, (c) improving resilience of food supply system by enabling increased global supply of less carbon-intensive fertilizers.

project_description: The proposed loan of up to EUR6 million (the IFC Loan) to Tewfik El Najem Driss SA (the “Company”, the “Borrower” or “TND”), leading importer and distributor of food products in Mauritania, is to support the Borrower’s investment program and includes a EUR21.3m poultry greenfield project on the outskirts of Nouakchott to supply the local market with eggs, frozen/fresh broiler chicken, and feeds. In addition, the Project is supported by the IDA20 IFC-MIGA Private Sector Window’s Blended Finance Facility (“IDA PSW-BFF”) to de-risk the investment, as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: TND is 75% owned by Telmidy El Najim Driss, a Mauritanian entrepreneur (the “Sponsor”), and 25% by the Fund for Export Development in Africa (“FEDA”), a subsidiary of Afreximbank.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at EUR21.3 million. IFC’s proposed financing is an A loan of up to EUR6 million. The uses of funds include i) capex to fund the Company’s feedmill construction project as well as ii) working capital.
location_description: The Project has various sites, located in a radius of 53 km from the capital Nouakchott.
development_impact: By promoting local production (import substitution) of poultry, the Project is expected to contribute to employment creation and stimulate downstream linkages with related sectors. The Project will also create indirect jobs through business opportunities for local MSMEs in the poultry and eggs distribution channels and service providers. To measure progress against EBITDA and wages) as well as average poultry and egg prices in Mauritania. Stakeholder - Consumer: The Project is expected to increase access to food supplies for consumers therefore contributing to food security of Mauritania which relies on imports for essential foods. The expected positive consumer impacts include lower (affordable) product prices and higher quality local products. To measure progress against these outcomes, IFC will track the volumes of poultry and eggs (MT) sold by the project. Beyond the project level, IFC expects the investment to improve resilience in The global food supply value chain is under considerable strain caused by the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The pandemic’s effects are adding to this pressure as input producers and distributors face increasing working capital needs and farming operations struggle with rising input prices. Through this intervention, IFC hopes to sustain the resilience of the global food supply market by supporting a key player TND in obtaining financing. Parallel WBG support to promote risk mitigation, coherent food policies, and stronger safety nets, will contribute to reducing food insecurity and market resilience. To measure progress against this outcome, IFC will track global flood inflation metrics and the supply of key commodities.
additionality: IFC is supporting TND in its expansion in its operations. On financial additionality, IFC is providing long term financing in Mauritania at tenors that are otherwise not easily available in the market and helping the firm gain traction for its fundraising. IFC's non-financial additionality consists of i) IFC’s technical expertise, global knowledge of the industry and markets, as well as lessons learned from other integrated poultry projects. Also, ii) IFC advisory service is exploring the potential application of MAS’s successful training program aimed at TND’s newly formed operation team for technical skills as well as for capacity building as week as iii) aligning meet the best practice in areas as animal welfare, use of antimicrobials, or food safety management systems with best international practices.

company_name: OMNIUM DES INDUSTRIES ET DE LA PROMOTION
project_description: The Project entails a proposed IFC green loan facility of up to EUR45 million to subsidiaries of the Omnium des Industries et de la Promotion Group (OIP, and together with its subsidiaries, the Group), a leading cement producer in Morocco and West Africa, to support the green capex program of the Group in the Sahel. The Project, whose primary objective is to finance climate investments, will be implemented through Ciments de l'Afrique (CIMAF), the Group’s sub-Saharan African subsidiaries, and will include the construction of a limestone calcined clay cement (LC3, a low-carbon cement) plant in Burkina Faso and solar PV projects in Burkina Faso, Chad, and Mali, aiming to promote the decarbonization of the Group’s operations.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsor is Mr. Anas Sefrioui, a Moroccan businessman with interests in the real estate and cement industries. Mr. Sefrioui owns 100% of OIP (a holding company incorporated in Morocco), 100% of CIMA Holdings (a holding company incorporated in Luxemburg), and 100% of the CIMAF subsidiaries. The Project will be implemented by CIMAF Bobo Dioulasso, CIMAF Burkina Faso, CIMAF Chad and CIMAF Mali. These subsidiaries are owned 70% by OIP and 30% by CIMA Holding, with the exception of CIMAF Mali, which is owned 90% by OIP and 10% by CIMA Holding.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at EUR50 million. The proposed investment is an A-loan for IFC’s own account for up to EUR45 million.
location_description: For CIMAF Bobo Dioulasso, the Project will be located on the existing cement plant site in Bobo Dioulasso, Burkina Faso. For CIMAF Burkina Faso, the Project will be located on the existing cement plant site in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. For CIMAF Mali, the Project will be located on the cement plant in Dio Gare, near Bamako, Mali. For CIMAF Chad, the Project will be located on the existing cement plant in N'Djamena, Chad.
development_impact: Project outcomes (Environment), economy-wide: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are environmental effects, namely reducing the carbon intensity of cement production in CIMAF’s operations, and strengthening the commitment to rolling out in West Africa its corporate decarbonization framework, and economy-wide effects, in terms of increased domestic value addition and employment. On another note, some import substitution effects are worth mentioning, since the Bobo Dioulasso plant will replace costly clinker imports from overseas with locally produced calcined clay. Market outcomes(Sustainability): Beyond the Project, IFC expects that the investment will contribute to improve the sustainability of cement production in West Africa through dissemination of the relatively novel LC3 technology, and larger use of captive solar energy facilities at cement plants and grinding stations.
additionality: Financial additionality (Financing structure): IFC is providing a set of straight senior loans with 8-year tenor and 2-year grace period under a single common terms agreement (CTA). This loan structure aligns with the Project’s implementation timeline and longer payback for decarbonization costs, an arrangement not available in Morocco, or the host countries’ financial markets. Non-financial additionality (Standard setting): With IFC’s involvement, CIMAF will pursue the alignment of West African cement operations with state-of-the-art developments in the industry, notably through the implementation of its decarbonization framework, and improvements in corporate governance, and EHS. IFC’s advisory services has signed an advisory engagement letter with the Group in July 2023 to assist it in developing a decarbonization roadmap and a green financing framework and obtain a second-party opinion (SPO) to facilitate the green loan structure for the Project. Moreover, and during Project implementation, IFC E&S team’s monitoring will contribute to ensuring adherence to emissions reduction and resource efficiency standards.
Company Name: OMNIUM DES INDUSTRIES ET DE LA PROMOTION

project_description: Lion’s Head Investments AD (“LHI” or the “Company”) is a commercial property investment platform in Bulgaria and Romania, established in 2017 (https://www.lhinv.eu/). The Company currently owns and operates five office buildings situated in prime locations, two in Sofia and three in Bucharest. LHI plans to expand its portfolio to the rapidly growing logistics and light industrial market in the Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) region. As part of this strategy, LHI will be acquiring income generating assets and developing new projects in Bucharest, Sofia and other key transportation hubs in Romania and Bulgaria. The Project comprises: (i) acquisition and development of the aforementioned logistics assets, as well as (ii) partial refinancing of and capital expenditure in the existing office portfolio. The logistics assets are expected to be certified with the IFC’s Advanced Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies (EDGE) green building certification. The Project will be supported by a sustainability-linked financing package of €150m from IFC’s own account as well as from IFC acting in its capacity as the implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program.
sponsor_shareholders: LHI is majority owned by Old Mutual Property, which is part of Old Mutual Limited, a major South African financial conglomerate, and by AG Capital (AGC) Group, a leading regional real estate group. Old Mutual Limited is a publicly listed company with the South African Public Investment Corporation holding 17% and BlackRock holding 6%; remaining shareholders hold less than 5%. AGC is controlled by Christo Iliev, the founder of AG Capital Group, and is a real estate focused group of companies with presence in Romania, Bulgaria and Poland. AGC has commercial and residential real estate platforms and partners with international institutional investors in the CEE region.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed sustainability-linked investment consists of a financing package of €150m, comprised of: (i) a long-term senior secured loan of €45m from IFC’s own account, (ii) a long-term senior secured loan of €65m from IFC acting in its capacity as the implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program, and (iii) a convertible instrument of €40m from IFC’s own account. IFC financing will be used towards: (i) the acquisition of income generating assets as well as the development of new projects in the logistics and the light industrial market (€140m), as well as (ii) partial refinancing and refurbishment of the existing office portfolio (€110m).
location_description: Project assets are located in both Romania and Bulgaria, including the capital cities of Bucharest and Sofia, as well as their surrounding counties/provinces and other key hubs in the two countries.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level development outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects through increased access to modern and high-quality logistics and business infrastructure, and (ii) environmental effects, through the development of green-certified buildings. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater financial integration in Bulgaria and Romania’s commercial and warehousing property sector via demonstration and replication channels.
additionality: IFC will provide long-term financing with optional conversion to equity, a rare tenor and structure for the local market. The IFC loans incorporate sustainability-linked features based on the funded warehousing properties' EDGE Advanced certification (marking Lion's Head Investments' first SLL engagement). IFC will also provide non-financial additionality by helping Lion's Head Investments elevate its sustainability reporting and corporate governance, as well as improve the green credentials of its portfolio and achieve EDGE certification for its assets.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of subscriptions to sustainability-linked bonds (“SLB”) of up to approximately US$150 million (in VND equivalent), of which US$50 million will be issued by Thanh Xuan Joint Stock Company and US$100 million will be issued by BIM Land Joint Stock Company (“BIM Land”). The proposed IFC investment is earmarked for (i) the development of Thanh Xuan valley project, which includes a hotel complex under the InterContinental brand, shophouses, and infrastructure of the project; and (ii) InterContinental Hotel and Regent Hotel in Phu Quoc.
sponsor_shareholders: BIM Land is a leading tourism and property developer in Vietnam that focuses on identifying and developing new tourism destinations in the country – it was one of the first companies to invest in the Ha Long bay area and Phu Quoc island and has played an instrumental role in the tourism development of these areas. BIM Land’s largest shareholder is BIM Group Joint Stock Company, a conglomerate in Vietnam with business interests in real estate, renewable energy, industrials, aquaculture, and consumer services. BIM Group was founded by Mr. Viet Quoc Doan and his wife Ms. Hien Thi Khong.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing to be the sole subscriber to the proposed SLBs of up to US$150 million (in VND equivalent).
location_description: The Project is primarily located in Vinh Phuc province and Kien Giang province of Vietnam.
development_impact: At the Project level, the Project is expected to create direct jobs and improve local businesses’ access to high-quality and modern urban infrastructure. In addition, it is expected to improve energy and water use efficiency by deploying energy-friendly, EDGE-certified infrastructure, thereby reducing the Project’s GHG emissions. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will improve quality standards in the Vinh Phuc’s accommodation sector. Through competitive pressure, existing players are expected improve their service standards, product quality, and safety and hygiene measures.
additionality: Financial additionality will be provided via financing structure with long-term tenor that is not readily available in the market to better match the cashflow profile and via financing instrument with this being Vietnam’s first local currency SLB. Non-financial additionality will be provided via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building where IFC will work with BIM Land on the sustainability-linked financing framework and on the targets where applicable.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$20 million A Loan (“the Loan”) to support Centum Real Estate Limited (“CRE”, “the Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of Centum Investment Company Plc (“CIC”, “the Sponsor”), to finance its development of 1,940 affordable housing units in Two Rivers Development (“Two Rivers”), a prime mixed use urban node located within Kenya’s Diplomatic Blue Zone in northern Nairobi (“the Project”). The Project will address the obvious and increasing affordable housing market gap in Kenya.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is the wholly owned subsidiary of CIC. CIC is a private equity and real estate investment company headquartered and domiciled in Kenya and its shares are listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE:CTUM) and on the Uganda Securities Exchange (USE: CENT).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated project cost is approximately US$91 million, of which IFC will be financing US$20 million via the Loan.
location_description: The Project is located in Two Rivers, a prime mixed use urban node located within Kenya’s Diplomatic Blue Zone in northern Nairobi and where the Company currently resides.
development_impact: Project outcomes for the Project include: Stakeholder effects: (i) Effects on consumers - The Project is expected to supply up to 1,940 affordable housing units within the investment period by a developer who is increasingly going down-market. The increase in access to quality housing at lower-priced points will help address the shortage of housing in Kenya and benefit families who currently cannot afford quality housing in the market; (ii) Effects on suppliers - With a larger scale of construction, there will be an increase in demand for building materials; (iii) Effects on local communities - those who live in the area will benefit from urban infrastructure such as roads, electricity, water and sanitation that were developed as a result of the Project. Economy-wide effects: The Project will create direct and indirect jobs through the construction of the housing projects. Local suppliers of building materials and other services will also benefit from the increased demand. The Government of Kenya may also benefit from higher tax payments from imports and company income. Environmental effects: Reaching efficiency in residential housing is an important step towards addressing climate change. Globally buildings account for 40% of GHG emissions and are an important consumer of energy. The Project is expected to improve energy efficiency, reducing GHG emissions. All developments will use EDGE standards requiring a minimum of 20% savings on water usage, energy usage, and embodied energy. The Project’s contribution to market creation includes: Competitiveness: The market for affordable housing in Kenya is underdeveloped. The limited provision of affordable housing is primarily driven by supply-side constraints due to: (i) high building costs and regulatory costs for approval processes; and (ii) limited access to finance for developers. The Project will demonstrate to other developers that good quality housing can be profitable and successful in a more affordable market segment, which could lead to more investments in the sector.
additionality: Financial additionality - Financing structure: IFC’s provision of long-term debt funding, which would otherwise not be available in the market from strictly commercial investors as the sector is considered highly risky. IFC’s involvement will also offer a “stamp of approval” to the Company and is expected to crowd in more investors to the affordable housing space in Kenya. Non-financial additionality - Knowledge innovation and capacity building: IFC will provide advice on green building standards as well as support for Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies (EDGE) certification. CRE will also benefit from IFC’s deep knowledge and expertise in housing, including tools such as Pillar Advisory as well as leveraging IFC network with key actors in the sub-sector.

company_name: Emerging Markets Infrastructure Fund II KS
project_description: The proposed project consists of an equity investment of up to US$50 million in Emerging Markets Infrastructure Fund II (“EMIF II” or “the Fund”) established by A.P. Moller Capital (“the Fund Manager”) to invest in critical transport infrastructure and renewable energy assets. The Fund’s strategy is aimed at tackling food security, supply chain disruptions, and global warming in selected South / Southeast Asian and African countries.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by A.P. Moller Capital. The Fund Manager was founded in 2017 and is a majority-owned affiliate of A.P. Moller Holding, part of the A.P. Moller Group. It is owned 58.6% by A.P. Moller Holding (Danish holding company that also owns 42% of A.P. Moller Maersk) and is a value-add infrastructure fund manager incorporated in Copenhagen and with offices in Copenhagen, Dubai, and Singapore.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund has a total committed capital target cap of US$ 1.0 billion and a hard cap of US$ 1.5 billion. IFC’s proposed investment is for up to US$ 50 million in EMIF II.
location_description: The Fund will make investments across various countries in South / Southeast Asia and Africa.
development_impact: The main project-level outcomes are expected to stem from the fund’s ability to set and meet sector-specific commitments around improving access and/or quality of infrastructure, mostly in transport/logistics but also renewable energy, in the targeted countries where capacity remains inadequate to efficiently support economic activity. Beyond the project, the investment has the potential to strengthen competitiveness in the relevant sectors by supporting expansion of private equity financing. The targeted markets face massive investment needs in transport/logistics and renewable energy to sustainably meet growing demand and the project could enhance spatial integration through investment in key logistics infrastructure as well as financial integration by helping deepen financing structures to catalyse investments in emerging markets.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is expected to be both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists in providing patient equity to help the Fund reach its target final closing size. Such patient capital is not readily available for infrastructure investments amid uncertainty on the global economic outlook and monetary tightening, which are likely to constrain capital flows to emerging markets. Non-financial additionality involves non-commercial risk mitigation by providing comfort to additional investors considering investing in the Fund and Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building.
Company Name: Emerging Markets Infrastructure Fund II KS

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a financing package of up to US$42 million to Bacao SAS (“Bacao” or the “Company”) to finance the development of approximately 3,800 hectares of cacao plantations and post-harvesting facility in the Meta region of Colombia (the Project). Bacao is an agroforestry cacao company that seeks to produce sustainable cacao by creating inclusive and climate-smart productive ecosystems that will not only contribute to rehabilitate degraded lands but also benefit local communities.
sponsor_shareholders: Bacao, established in Colombia, is a subsidiary of Andean Cacao GmbH, domiciled in Switzerland, which in turn is owned by Mars Nederland B.V., ECOM Agroindustrial Corp. Ltd., Amazonas-AI Fund SCS, SICAV-FIAR and 12Tree GmbH.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide an up to US$10.5 million senior loan for its own account and mobilize an up to US$10.5 million from the IFC-Canada Blended Finance Climate Program and up to US$21 million loan from parallel lender(s).
location_description: The Project will be developed in Cabuyaro, in the Meta department of Colombia.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to provide access to market and technical assistance for farmers, generate positive environmental impacts by conducting agroforestry cacao production on degraded land, and produce economy-wide effects with employment creation, plantation expansion, and post-harvest facility development. At the market level, IFC expects the Project to promote Colombia’s integration into the global cacao market and trade diversification through developing sustainable cacao production and exports.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality comes from the provision of tailored long-term financing. Non-financial additionality comes from standard setting in terms of supporting the Company to implement best practice E&S standards and the potential adoption of the Green Financing Framework.

project_description: Yara Oil SA (the “Company”) is a privately owned Malian company founded in 1983. Yara is transitioning from distributing fuel to the mining sector (B2B) to expanding its presence in the retail segment. The Project aims to support Yara Oil expand its retail business by building new 20 fuel distribution stations. With this engagement Yara Oil intends to take the first steps towards energy transition in Mali, including piloting electric vehicles charging stations, solar panels to power the service stations, and distribution of small-scale clean energy solutions nationwide.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is the Yaranangore Family, shareholders of YARA OIL SA in Mali.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at EUR 20.7 million. The proposed IFC’s financing is a EUR 12.2 million package consisting of EUR 6.1 million A loan and IDA PSW Subordinated loan of EUR 6.1 million.
location_description: The 20 service stations will be distributed nationwide in Mali, including urban, peri-urban, and rural areas.
development_impact: Development Impact includes increasing access to modern retail fuel stations, supporting economic activity, job creation, and contributing to Mali’s local economy the Project is expected to promote competitiveness in the retail fuel sector, improve the quality of fuel and non-fuel retail products, and introduce new green standards.
additionality: IFC and PSW support for Yara Oil encompasses (1) financial additionality with long-term financing, (2) knowledge and capacity building through financial management and clean energy advisory services, (3) standard-setting in fuel retail practices, and (4) promoting environmentally and socially responsible operations for sustainable growth.

project_description: The proposed investment is a senior secured A Loan of up to US$23.3 million to Johnvents Industries Limited (“Johnvents” or the “Company”), a Nigerian cocoa processing and trading company. The investment will support the Company’s US$46.1 million expansion plan in (i) increasing production capacity to 120 metric tons per day cocoa processing capacity; (ii) expanding gas power plants; (iii) fleet acquisition; and (iv) working capital (together, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is owned 51 percent by Capital Sage Holdings (the “Group” or the “Guarantor”), a holding company with operations in agribusiness, healthcare services and financial services and 49 percent directly by John Alamu (the “Sponsor”), the Founder and Group Managing Director. The Group is in turn owned 90 percent by the Sponsor, and 10 percent is held by two Directors of the Group, Sam Oduwole and Oluyemisi Shittu. Prior to setting up Johnvents, the Sponsor was working at The International Institute of Tropical Agriculture in the monitoring and evaluation team where he saw the gap in providing inputs and access to markets to farmers, hence the establishment of Johnvents. Mr. Alamu has over 8 years of industry experience in Nigeria. He has been active in growing the operations of the Company with the support of an experienced team of professionals (with c.10 average years of industry experience) with a special attention on quality control and food safety.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is US$46.1 million; made up of c. (i) US$13.3 million from the Sponsor and internal cash generated (already invested in 2022); (ii) US$9.5 million from local commercial bank (already invested); and (iii) IFC’s proposed investment package comprising (a) a US$14.8 million A Loan from IFC (of which US$6.3 million is provided in Naira equivalent with the support of International Development Association Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF)), and (b) a US$8.5 million loan from Global Agriculture and Food Safety Program (GAFSP).
location_description: The Project will be located within the existing land area of the Company’s operations situated in the city of Akure, the capital of the state of Ondo, Nigeria; where the Company has warehouses and existing cocoa processing facilities.
development_impact: The Project outcomes assessment is based on the predicted growth in demand for cocoa and cocoa-related products globally, the Company's leading position in the local market, and the favorable outlook of the regulatory environment. Project outcomes are composed of the following: Stakeholder – farmer suppliers: IFC expects that the Project will improve farmers' livelihoods through increased cocoa sourcing and technical and financial assistance. Economy-wide effects: IFC expects that the project will lead to an annual increase in GDP. The project is also expected to create direct, indirect, and induced jobs along the value chain, with more permanent jobs being created directly through the expansion of processing capacity, and additional jobs in input provision, technical assistance, and supplies and services for the cocoa processing plants. The market creation rating is Moderate with Medium likelihood of achievement. The likelihood is supported by the large untapped potential of cocoa processing capacity in the country, and the favorable projection of global demand for sustainably and transparently sourced cocoa products, which together provide comfort on the potential growth of Nigeria’s cocoa industry. The likelihood is tempered by the intensive investments required to establish and operate cocoa processing plants and for other market players to adapt a similar business model in the country. The Project’s contribution to market creation is as follows: Competitiveness - IFC expects the Project will have a positive impact on Nigeria’s cocoa industry competitiveness through the support to the Company’s processing capacity expansion and increase the volume of sustainable and traceable cocoa production.
additionality: Summary : IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality comes from the provision of long-term financing with a structure not readily available in the market. Non-financial additionality comes from standard setting in terms of supporting the Company to implement best practice E&S standards and providing knowledge, innovation and capacity building. Financial additionality : Financing structure - The proposed investment is a patient senior loan of up to US$20 million with a tenor of 8 years (with 2 years grace) to implement a capex program and meet working capital needs. This kind of financing is not readily available for agribusinesses in Nigeria. According to IFC’s analysis, over the past 12 months in Nigeria, there were two USD-denominated syndicated loans provided to corporates, with a combined face value of 0.365 billion USD and tenors of one year each; there was one USD-denominated corporate bond issued at a corresponding rating by companies, with a face value of 0.05 billion USD and maturity at issuance at five years. None of the loans provided or bonds issued over the past 12 months was in the Agribusiness sector. Non-financial Additionality : Standard setting - IFC will provide expertise in food safety, environment, and social standards to align the Company’s operations with industry best standards. Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building - IFC Advisory Services will support the Company about their engagement scope (e.g., deploying the agribusiness leadership program (ALP) to train farmer organizations/groups to strengthen their capabilities; organize the Last Mile Retailer (LMR) training of their distributors emphasizing on food safety and providing agronomic support including good agricultural practices (GAP) to add value to the Company’s farmer engagement initiatives, etc.).

company_name: THE BIOLOGICALS AND VACCINES INSTITUTE OF SOUTHERN AFRICA (PTY) LTD
project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support, the Biologicals and Vaccines Institute of Southern Africa ('BioVac' or the 'Company'), a South African biopharmaceutical company based in Cape Town, to expand its suite of products which includes partnering with Pfizer-BioNTech through a tech transfer agreement for fill and finish manufacturing of vaccines on the continent thus helping reduce Africa’s over dependence on imported vaccines (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: BioVac is 47.5%-owned by two South African government agencies, namely the Technology Innovation Agency (‘TIA’) with 12.5% and the Department of Science and Innovation (‘DSI’) with 35%. The balance of BioVac’s 52.5% is held by a BioVac Consortium (Pty) Limited which consisting of private investors, who amongst others includes Dr Makhoana Morena.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment in BioVac is an “A” loan of up to ZAR120million (equivalent to approximately US$7m) with a tenor of up to nine years.
location_description: The funds will be used in BioVac’s facilities located in Cape Town, South Africa.
development_impact: The project helps finance a South African manufacturer of healthcare products. Assessment of Project Outcomes: The project outcomes rating is based will be based on the project’s support in the production of vaccines. This production responds to the large gap that has arisen due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Stakeholder Effect: Increased Access to Healthcare Products – The global shortage of medical products has led to a worldwide competition of these supplies, making it difficult – particularly in developing countries – to purchase quality drugs and medicines at affordable prices. Economy-wide Effect: Direct Jobs Created and Gross Value Added – IFC financing will support only manufacturer capable of full end-to-end of vaccines manufacturing in Africa. The project will help support delivery of healthcare supplies that is likely to result in the creation of new jobs and/or economic linkages to the rest of the economy. To measure progress against this outcome, IFC will track direct jobs created, gross value-added, and taxes in the country of production. Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation - Resilience: Currently, healthcare markets in emerging markets face a range of vulnerabilities. With COVID-19, these markets are under significant strain as service providers face exponential growth in treatment requirements and increasingly depleted supplies. To measure progress against this outcome, IFC will track improvements in functioning of supply chains and/or emergence of logistics infrastructure to support healthcare markets.
additionality: Standard Setting: Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC will bring to the table potential market access to clients, including member countries of the World Bank Group, expertise, and industry knowledge which will be critical in supporting BioVac's growth plans. IFC will seek to introduce the Company to potential strategic partners who will enhance its manufacturing operations by providing technical guidance and financial support as needed. IFC support in impacting procurement standards by Africa CDC, GAVI, WHO, and other agencies involved in vaccine procurement E&S Standard Setting: : IFC will help the Company to strengthen E&S systems both for the existing operations, promote climate-smart systems for a “green-rated” manufacturing facility. Financial additionality: Long-term financing and countercyclical role: IFC is providing long-term financing for immediate needs and beyond what BioVac is currently able to obtain in the market, given that it operates in a space that several lenders perceive as high risk.
Company Name: THE BIOLOGICALS AND VACCINES INSTITUTE OF SOUTHERN AFRICA (PTY) LTD

project_description: In 2022, IFC committed a new senior unsecured A-Loan (the ‘IFC Loan’) of up to US$40 million eqvt. to Coca-Cola Beverages Pakistan Limited (‘CCBPL’ or the ‘Company’), to refinance the outstanding balance of IFC's existing loan to the Company and top up the overall Loan amount. The IFC Loan will i) fund CCBPL's expanded working capital needs, which have arisen due to COVID; ii) partially finance the Company's capital expenditure program, which COVID delayed; and iii) facilitate a long-term cross-currency swap to hedge the Company's hard currency debt exposure against the anticipated Pakistan Rupee (‘PKR’) devaluation (the ‘Project’).
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsors are two publicly listed entities: The Coca-Cola Company (“TCCC”), incorporated in the USA, and Coca-Cola Icecek A.S. (“CCI”), incorporated in Turkey. Both are the major shareholders of CCBPL, each owning 49.6% of its shares, with management control with CCI.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of an up to US$40 million equivalent A Loan for IFC’s own account for corporate uses.
location_description: CCBPL is headquartered in Lahore, Pakistan, with 6 manufacturing facilities located at Karachi, Rahim Yar Khan, Multan, Lahore, Gujranwala and Faisalabad.
development_impact: Consistent with the RSE Facility, the proposed AIMM score is 53. The investment will preserve 3,800 existing jobs and the new plant will create 200 direct jobs and up to 2000 indirect jobs (10x multiplier) and strengthen linkages with local sugarcane farmers, MSME retailers, and distributors. The investment also facilitates South-South FDI.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in the proposed investment is driven by its countercyclical role during crises providing liquidity for anticipated increase in working capital requirements and financing for continuity of investment plans. The team will also investigate IFC's advisory engagement to develop and enhance the supply chain in rural areas of KPK, Northern Pakistan and to see if CCBPL may benefit for IFC advisory in energy and water efficiency.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is US$130 million financing package to MHP SE and its subsidiaries (collectively, MHP or the Company) to support the Company’s plans to (i) refinance its US$500 million Notes due in May 2024, and (ii) upgrade and expand its agricultural waste-to-energy (WTE) plant in the Vinnytsia region of Ukraine in order to increase biomethane production (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1998, MHP is a leading international food and agrotech group, and the largest producer of poultry, culinary, and processed meat products in Ukraine. MHP has been listed on the London Stock Exchange since 2008. Mr. Yuriy Kosyuk is the founder, CEO, and controlling shareholder of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is US$552 million. It will be funded with an IFC A loan of up to US$130 million to be supported by Blended Finance contributors, as described in the Blended Finance section.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Kyiv, Ukraine. The WTE plant is in the village of Vasylivka, Haisyn district, Vinnytsia region, Ukraine.
development_impact: The Project is anticipated to help address the food security crisis both within Ukraine and globally by sustaining and supporting the Company’s production and export of poultry and other agricultural products. The Project is expected to also sustain jobs and livelihood of employees of the Company and enable MHP to continue having a significant impact on Ukraine’s agribusiness value chain. The WTE plant component of the Project is expected to help promote the use of renewable energy sources and demonstrate the feasibility of biomethane production in Ukraine.
additionality: Financial additionality will be through critical support in the form of long-term debt to the Company, in the context of contracted availability of liquidity and long-term financing in Ukraine The proposed investment is part of the ERA Program, which aims to provide essential support to Ukraine’s private sector, including liquidity support to private sector companies in Ukraine that play a critical role in preserving jobs, exports, and fiscal revenues and providing the population with essential goods and services. The non-financial additionality will be through non-commercial risk mitigation and standard setting to support the Company in aligning with good international industry practices in line with IFC Performance Standards through implementation of the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP).

project_description: The proposed investment is up to US$30 million A-loan and mobilization of up to US$15 million to Edita Food Industries S.A.E. (the “Company” or “Edita Egypt”), Edita Participation Cyprus Ltd. (“Edita-Cyprus”), and Edita Trade and Distribution S.A.E. (the Co-Borrowers). The loan will support Edita’s (i) capital expenditure requirements in Egypt and Morocco, (ii) working capital requirements, and (iii) potential expansion in Africa and the Middle East regions (“Project”). The Company has been listed on the Egyptian Exchange (“EGX”) and the London Stock Exchange (“LSE”) since 2015.
sponsor_shareholders: The main shareholders of the Company are Quantum Investment BV holding, fully owned by the Berzi family, 42.67 percent of the Company’s share capital, the Bank of New York Mellon (acting as depositary bank for shares traded in the London Stock Exchange), managing 11.7 percent of the Company’s share capital, Kingsway Fund Frontier Consumer Franchises holding 9.11 percent of Company’s share capital, RIMCO EGT Investment LLC holding 5.35 percent of Company’s share capital, in addition to several shareholders holding 31.17 percent of the Company’s share capital.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to US$30 million and mobilization of up to US$15 million.
location_description: The project is located in the existing operations of Edita in Egypt and Morocco and potentially in other locations in Africa and the Middle East regions that are yet to be determined.
development_impact: IFC's investment will help in (a) sustaining over 7,000 jobs in Egypt and creating over 400 jobs in Edita’s production and supply chain; (b) developing sustainable and efficient supply chains in Egypt, Morocco, and other markets in Africa and MCT regions, as Edita will continue to support and develop distributors and local suppliers of inputs, leading to efficient supply chains in these markets; and (c) IFC expects the Project to increase resilience in the market by building Edita’s capacity to withstand shocks and stresses from forex shortage and inflation.
additionality: Through the proposed investment and the potential accompanying advisory service package, IFC will help a leading food processor grow into a solutions provider in its industry for the benefits of mostly consumers in MENA region. IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial (financing structure) and non-financial (non-commercial risk mitigation, including trusted partnerships, and standard setting).

company_name: INDORAMA ELEME FERTILIZER AND CHEMICALS FZE
project_description: The Indorama Corporation (“Indorama” or the “Group”), a Singapore-based holding company, is a long standing, repeat IFC client. Over the last 3 decades, IFC has supported Indorama’s entry into high-risk markets, helping it grow from a mid-sized, domestically focused business into one of the world’s fastest growing petrochemical and fibre companies. In June 2016, Indorama successfully completed a 1.4 million metric ton per annum (“MMTPA”) urea fertilizer facility (“Line 1”) in Nigeria via Indorama Eleme Fertilizer and Chemicals Limited (IFL or the Company), making it the first major fertilizer export plant in Nigeria and one of the few in Africa. For Line 1, IFC provided a US$150 million (“mn”) A Loan, a US$75mn B Loan and mobilized US$150mn from several development finance institutions (“DFIs”). IFL constructed a second urea fertilizer line located at the same site as Line 1, which increased capacity from 1.4 MMTPA to 2.8 MMTPA (“Line 2”). To support Line 2, IFC arranged in June 2018, financing totalling US$1 billion (“bn”), comprising of US$120mn A Loan, US$550mn B Loan, and US$330mn parallel loans. Line 2 was completed in April 2021. Both Line 1 and 2 projects are in operation, with capacity to produce a combined 2.8 MMTPA of urea. IFC also financed the construction of a Feed Conditioning Unit (“FCU”), an add-on gas processing facility to Line 2. IFC provided a US$35mn A Loan and mobilized US$115mn in B/Parallel loans from commercial banks and other DFIs. Indorama is now planning the construction of a third urea fertilizer line within the same complex as Lines 1 and 2 in Port Harcourt, Nigeria, which will increase current capacity from 2.8 MMTPA to 4.2 MMTPA (“Line 3”). A dedicated jetty/port terminal with sufficient capacity to export all the Line 3 urea, and to be located approximately 20 kilometres from the IFL site, is also planned (“Line 3 Jetty”) (“Line 3” and “Line 3 Jetty” together the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Indorama is a long standing IFC client based in Singapore, which has grown into a global business entity with US$29.6 bn in revenues. Indorama was established in 1976, and it is wholly owned by Mr. S.P. Lohia and family. Indorama manufactures polyester, polyethylene terephthalate (“PET”) resins and bottles, polyester intermediates, polyethylene, polypropylene, spun yarns, fabrics, disposable gloves, hygiene, and fertilizers. Indorama is the world’s largest producer of polyester and PET resins as well as one of the fastest growing global petrochemical producers with a presence in 39 countries across 175 sites across Asia, Europe, Africa, and Americas.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project Cost is estimated at US$1.250 bn. IFC is leading the debt financing package comprising of (i) US$285mn IFC A loan; (ii) up to US$870mn in mobilization of B/parallel loans from commercial banks/development finance institutions, including available Trust Loans; and (iii) IFC B2 loans provided under IFC’s Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (“MCPP”) of up to US$95mn.
location_description: Port Harcourt, Nigeria
development_impact: The Project will promote (i) increase in value addition and export revenue for the Nigerian economy; (ii) direct and indirect employment; (iii) strong environmental sustainability by redirecting polluting wasted flared gas to productive use as feedstock; (iv) improvement in accessibility and supply of quality fertilizer to farmers; and (v) the resilience of the global food supply market through increased availability of urea.
additionality: IFC's participation will (i) provide long-term financing beyond what is generally available in the market, which is key in this sector; (ii) mobilize large amounts from other developmental financial institutions and commercial banks; (iii) continue support to a strategic client as it expands in Sub-Saharan Africa and in the fragile Niger Delta region; (iv) provide in-house technical, insurance, and EH&S expertise; and (v) help define long-term climate priorities for the Project.
Company Name: INDORAMA ELEME FERTILIZER AND CHEMICALS FZE

project_description: The proposed transaction entails an investment of up to US$100 million of senior secured A Loan to SRF Limited (the “Company”). The proceeds of the loan provided by IFC shall be used for financing capital expenditure towards specific identified projects in the Company’s specialty chemicals business, all at Dahej in the state of Gujarat being undertaken at a capital expenditure of US$112 million (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is currently listed on Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange. The majority ownership of the Company is with Arun Bharat Ram and his family (the Sponsors), including his son and the current Managing Director, Ashish Bharat Ram. The Sponsor family has a 50.53% shareholding, and the balance is held by public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost includes capital expenditure of approximately US$112 million, of which IFC will provide a senior secured A Loan in the form of an External Commercial Borrowing in the amount of up to US$100 million.
location_description: The Company will use the IFC funding for its operations in Dahej, in the state of Gujarat, India.
development_impact: The project-level outcomes include economy-wide benefits through increased employment and value addition. IFC estimates that the Project will increase manufacturing direct value addition in India’s GDP and contribute to the economy through indirect and induced effects along the chemicals value chain. The Project will also create additional jobs thanks to the expansion through indirect and induced effects along the value chain. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to promote competitiveness in India’s chemical sector, especially in agrochemicals and pharmaceuticals intermediates, through increased efficiencies along the value chain and production processes, and product diversification.
additionality: IFC will provide additionality via risk mitigation through a trusted partnership over the long term, as well as support in standard setting, as the Company moves to strengthen its environmental, social, and governance (“ESG”) practices. IFC is also working on structuring a potential decarbonization advisory program with the Company to help further reduce their carbon footprint.

company_name: IHS Kenya CIV Green Housing SCSp
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an equity co-investment package by IFC of up to €19.3 million (~ US$ 20.9 million) to invest along with IHS Kenya Green Housing Partnership LLP and IHS Kenya Green Housing SCSp (the “Fund”) in the development and acquisition of approximately 5,000 newly developed, resource efficient, green affordable housing properties in Kenya (the “Project”). The proposed IFC investment will consist of up to €10 million (~ US$ 10.9 million) from IFC’s own account and up to US$10 million equivalent in € (~€9.3 million) from IFC acting as the implementing entity of the UK-IFC Market Accelerator for Green Construction Program (MAGC). IFC will provide equity for the development of affordable housing projects with an initial focus on the Nairobi Metropolitan Area and selectively in other Kenyan Counties. The Fund will be managed by IHS Kenya Green Housing Fund GP Limited (“GP”), through its main investment management team based in Nairobi. IFC will utilize a “sidecar” investment structure by using a newly created special purpose vehicle that will have IFC as its only limited partner co-investing alongside with the Fund in selected investments.
sponsor_shareholders: Investment Housing Solutions group of companies (collectively, “IHS”) is a private equity firm focused on affordable housing in Africa. IHS is an asset manager of four affordable housing funds in the Southern African region and owns a listed REIT in the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. IHS has developed a solid track record in the African affordable housing space with operations across four countries in the Sub-Saharan African region (South Africa, Namibia, Botswana and Kenya). IHS is a wholly owned subsidiary of U.S. based Hunt Companies, Inc., a real estate and infrastructure fund manager.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund has a target equity investment of up to €130 million (~US$ 140 million) from various institutional investors, of which IFC expects to invest up to €19.3 million (~ US$ 20.9 million) in equity, but not to exceed 20% of total fund size. This investment will be in the form of a co-investment package with up to €10 million for IFC’s own account and up to US$10 million equivalent in Euros from IFC acting as the implementing entity of MAGC.
location_description: The Fund will invest in real estate projects, with an initial focus on Nairobi County in Kenya and a minimum of 15% of the Fund’s committed to areas outside Nairobi, Kenya.
