development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects on customers through increased access to affordable housing, as well as potential effects on suppliers through increased business opportunities and on local communities that will benefit from the accompanied urban infrastructure development, and (ii) environmental effects, through reduction in GHG emissions via improved resource efficiency. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the investment will promote competitiveness of the residential property market in Kenya through the demonstration and replication effects for affordable green housing
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via the long-term financing structure which is not readily available in the market. Non-financial additionality is provided via capacity building for green building standards and sharing IFC expertise in the affordable housing sector.
Company Name: IHS Kenya CIV Green Housing SCSp

project_description: On 6 July 2023, IFC submitted an offer to subscribe for EUR 72.5 million, equivalent to US$ 78.7 million, as an anchor investor, into a EUR 305 million, 5-year sustainability-linked bond (SLB), issued by Zagrebacki Holding d.o.o. (“ZGH”, or the “Issuer”). The issuer has accepted the offer and has allocated the bonds to IFC. The bond issue date is 11 July 2023. The Issuer is a municipal utility holding company, 100% owned by the City of Zagreb, whose subsidiaries provide essential municipal services such as waste disposal and treatment, water supply, and gas distribution. The Bond proceeds will be used to refinance an existing 7-year bond with a bullet maturity date of 15 July 2023.
sponsor_shareholders: ZGH is solely owned by the City of Zagreb, which is issuing a guarantee for the bond.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total issuance size is EUR 305 million (equivalent to US$ 331 million) with the proceeds being used for refinancing of the existing bond. IFC investment of EUR 72.5 million constitute around 24% of the total issuance. It is expected that IFC investment will allow the Issuer to implement climate-related projects.
location_description: City of Zagreb, Croatia.
development_impact: The main Project-level outcome is the improvement in municipal waste management in the city of Zagreb. At the market level, IFC investment in the issuance of the first Sustainability-Linked-Bond (SLB) by a municipal utility in Croatia will contribute to deepen the domestic capital market, encourage additional placement of sustainable finance instruments, and increase integration of infrastructure to capital markets in the Western Balkans through demonstration effects.
additionality: IFC has both financial and non-financial additionality associated with the proposed investment. IFC financial additionality is driven by an innovative financing structure and resource mobilization that would allow a municipal utility access to sustainable finance instruments for the first time. IFC will play the role of an anchor investor and leverage its global experience in sustainable finance instruments to mobilize local commercial and institutional investors, ensuring a successful placement of the first SLB in Croatia’s domestic capital market by a municipal company like ZGH. The SLB issuance would contribute to diversify ZGH funding sources and provide the necessary financial flexibility to implement its Sustainability Strategy focused on critical municipal investments. IFC’s non-financial additionality derives from its role in ensuring prudent debt management and the establishment of a strategic partnership with the city of Zagreb and ZGH that will pave the way for future investments to address municipal challenges.

sector: Integrated Textile Operation (Spinning, Weaving/Knitting, but no Garment )
project_description: The proposed investment consists of a senior, secured debt financing package arranged by IFC for an aggregate amount of up to US$150 million or its EUR equivalent (the IFC Financing) to the following three companies in Turkiye: (i) Sanko Tekstil Isletmeleri Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (Sanko Tekstil) – a vertically integrated premium yarn manufacturer; (ii) Super Film Ambalaj Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (Super Film) – an export-oriented flexible packaging manufacturer; and (iii) Cimko Cimento ve Beton San. Tic. A.S. (Cimko) – a leading local cement manufacturer (together, the Project Companies). The IFC Financing will partially finance (i) the construction of a ring spinning mill to be certified as a green building and a recycling facility with roof-top solar panel installations at Sanko Tekstil; (ii) the construction of a greenfield plant to be certified as a green building at Super Film, (iii) several energy efficiency and renewable energy investments at Cimko; and (iv) some earthquake recovery investments by the Project Companies (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Sanko Holding is the main shareholder of Sanko Tekstil, Super Film and Cimko. The holding is ultimately owned by the Konukoglu Family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is expected to be up to US$245 million, which will be primarily funded by the IFC Financing at an amount of up to US$150 million consisting of: (i) up to US$100 million or its EUR equivalent A Loan on own account and (ii) up to US$50 million or its EUR equivalent syndicated loans. The remaining balance is to come from the internal cash generation by the Project Companies and/or additional debt from Sanko Holding’s relationship banks.
location_description: The Project will be implemented in three cities of Turkiye, two of which were hit hard by the two earthquakes in February 2023. Sanko Tekstil’s and Cimko’s investments will be in the epicenters of the earthquakes, Gaziantep and Kahramanmaras, respectively, while Super Film’s investments will be in Kirklareli in the Marmara Region of Turkiye.
development_impact: • Job Creation and Exports: The Project will generate economy-wide effects including enabling growth in exports and job creation. In addition, jobs along the value chain of the Project Companies will be supported through indirect and induced effects in less developed cities of Turkiye. • Reduction in the Carbon Footprint of the Turkish Manufacturing Industry: The Project will support critical exporting sectors for the Turkish economy (textiles and flexible packaging) and help greening of the operations at the Project Companies by enabling them to utilize state-of-art efficient technologies and increase renewable energy in production. • Competitiveness: The Project will improve competitiveness of the local textiles, flexible packaging; and cement industries by (i) supporting increased circularity and use of recycled content in production at Sanko Tekstil, (ii) enabling capacity/product portfolio optimization at Super Film to better meet growing demand for more sustainable/environmental products in Europe; and (iii) helping implement a decarbonization strategy to increase use of renewable sources and alternative fuels with improved resource efficiency at Cimko.
additionality: • Provision of long-term financing: IFC, by playing a countercyclical role, will provide long-term financing which is difficult to procure in the local market for the proposed amount and tenor. • Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: The Project Companies will directly benefit from IFC’s expertise on adopting climate-smart production techniques, improving the environmental footprint of their current operations; and green loan financing framework development.

project_description: Napino Auto and Electronics Limited (Napino or the Company) is a leading manufacturer of electrical and electronic components for the 2-wheeler automobile industry in India. Its key product profile includes electronic control units, regulator rectifiers, electronic fuel injection systems, instrument clusters, electronic mobility components including converters, chargers, battery management systems and others. It has a 30+ year track record of supplying to leading OEMs in India with R&D-driven proprietary solutions. The proposed project will (i) part finance a capex plan, primarily for expanding existing capacity in plants(brownfield expansion); (ii) finance setup of a greenfield plant in Hosur-Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu in India; (iii) finance the capex for setting up the motor manufacturing plant at Halol, Gujarat in India and (iv) strengthen company’s balance sheet by repaying debt taken to finance purchase of shares from a minority investor.
sponsor_shareholders: Napino is promoted by Vipin Raheja and family (“Promoters”) who own 100% of the Company currently.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project size is US$57 mn which will be funded through mix of IFC equity of upto US$40 mn, debt from other local banks and internal accruals.
location_description: The Company has eight manufacturing units and two R&D centers located across India in Hardiwar, Bhiwadi, Manesar, Pune, Halol and Bengaluru. The capex will be primarily for expanding capacity (brownfield) in Manesar, Halol and Haridwar, and to setup a greenfield plant in Hosur-Krishnagiri
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are economywide effects. The project will increase value addition and employment in the auto sector by helping the Company to diversify into the EV segment Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to contribute to the integration of advanced EV manufacturing capabilities, the scaling-up of the EV ecosystem in India, and the smooth transition of the auto industry from fossil fuel powered vehicles to EV.
additionality: IFC's additionality stems from (i) financing structure in an evolving sector, (ii) standard setting of governance frameworks and environmental and social (E&S) practices to further strengthen best practices in E&S and make it on par with international standards, and (iii) mitigate the perception of risk in the eyes of other potential institutional investors in the sector by signaling confidence in the Company and the prospect of E-2W in India.

project_description: Zhende Medical Co. Ltd. (“Zhende” or the “Company”) is a leading medical supplies manufacturer in China and has played a crucial role in protecting front-line healthcare workers worldwide during the pandemic by providing critical medical supplies, including personal protective equipment (PPE), surgical gowns and masks. The Company is planning to construct a medical supply manufacturing plant near Nairobi, Kenya. This facility will primarily produce medical supplies such as gowns, gauze, syringes, and other basic medical consumables for the region. The proposed IFC loan is a A loan of up to US$70 million equivalent.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Jianguo LU, the founder and chairman of Zhende (the “Sponsor”), and his wife, Ms. Zhenfang SHEN, collectively control 52.15% of the Company’s shares as the largest shareholder.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project will be implemented in two phases, to be primarily funded by the IFC loan, with the remaining amount funded by the Company’s internal cash generation and cash balance. The cost of phase I is expected to be US$60 million and the cost of phase II is to be finalized after land purchase. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to US$70 million equivalent.
location_description: The project facility is to be constructed in Nairobi, Kenya.
development_impact: Project level: benefits to consumers from the production of medical consumables; job creation along with skill training opportunities for the local industry in Kenya. Market level: market resilience via demonstration and replication channels.
additionality: IFC’s Role and Additionality: (i) long-term financing beyond what is available in the market; (ii) provision of advice in the form of Upstream engagement, to help the Company expand into other emerging markets; and (iii) standard settings and sharing of best practices in Environmental and Social (E&S) aspects.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment involves a 10-year senior secured loan of up to US$130 million to Aarti Industries Limited (“the Company” or “AIL”). The proposed loan will be utilized towards capacity expansion, modernisation and debottlenecking initiatives (“the Project”) in Jhagadia and Dahej, in the state of Gujarat, India, which consists of: (i) expansion of nitro toluene capacities at Jhagadia, (ii) expansion of ethylation capacities at Dahej, (iii) setting up of a chloro-toluene and its derivatives plant at Jhagadia, (iv) setting up of multi-purpose plants and pilot plants for customized manufacturing at Jhagadia, and (v) expansion and debottlenecking of other existing capacities at Jhagadia and Dahej. IFC’s loan is structured as a Sustainability Linked Loan (SLL) and builds in incentives for the Company to meet agreed emission reduction targets.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded in 1984 by four entrepreneurs, namely, Mr. Chandrakant Gogri, Mr. Rajendra Gogri, Mr. Parimal Desai and the late Mr. Shantilal Shah (the “founders”). The founders along with their families and related group entities own 44.16% of total shareholding (as of March 31, 2023) in the Company and are together the sponsors of AIL. Being a publicly listed company, the balance of shares are held by financial institutional investors and other public investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be approximately US$338 million. IFC will fund US$130 million in the form of a senior loan. The balance US$208 million will be funded through loans from other banks and internal cash generation of the Company.
location_description: Jhagadia and Dahej, in the state of Gujarat, India.
development_impact: The most significant project-level outcomes are economy-wide benefits through increased employment and value addition, and GHG emissions reduction. The Project will contribute to increasing domestic value addition in India’s specialty chemical sector through production of downstream and value-added products. The most significant effect of the Project on the market is through its scale expansion, backward integration, and the Company’s drive to push innovation through manufacturing of products that are currently imported. The Project is also expected to achieve reduction in total GHG emissions through a combination of measures including partial coal replacement with biomass; increase in share of renewable power in energy mix and increase in waste heat utilization.
additionality: IFC will provide a long-term, US$ loan with a 3-year grace period that is not freely available in the local market, especially for the manufacturing sector. Further, IFC will provide support in standard setting, as the Company moves to strengthen its environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices. IFC’s funding will also incentivize the Company to undertake several decarbonization measures aimed at reducing coal consumption and GHG emissions, which any other commercial financing is unlikely to incentivize.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to €100m syndicated term loan on a Unsecured Covenant Light basis (1-year maturity, renewable/re-committed annually, for up to 4 years in aggregate) by IFC to SUCDEN Cote d’Ivoire (“SUCDEN-CI” or the “Company”) and its parent company SUCDEN S.A (the “co-Borrower” and, jointly with SUCDEN-CI and other subsidiaries, “SUCDEN” or the “Group”) to finance the procurement and export of cocoa beans from Cote d’Ivoire (CI). The project is expected to be supported by the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP) and IDA20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA-PSW BFF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: SUCDEN S.A. and SUCDEN Cote d’Ivoire.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: €100 million (including parallel loan and mobilization).
location_description: Cote d’Ivoire
development_impact: The most significant Project level outcomes are stakeholders - improved livelihood for smallholder farmers. IFC's investment in the project is expected to support the livelihoods of a significant number of smallholder farmers in Cote d'Ivoire who supply cocoa beans to SUCDEN. Cocoa farming is a critical sector for the country's economy, but many cocoa farmers in Cote d'Ivoire are among the poorest in the country. SUCDEN's pre-harvest finance provides farmer suppliers with access to funds for fertilizers, pruning, and farm upkeep, and IFC is considering providing advisory services to farmers in the form of training on financial literacy, farm management, and good agricultural practices. Beyond the Project, IFC expects SUCDEN's sustainability programs to cocoa farmers to positively impact cocoa quality, the efficiency and effectiveness of cocoa production, and the supply of sustainable and traceable cocoa. These outcomes can contribute to promoting the competitiveness and sustainability of the cocoa sector in Cote d'Ivoire.
additionality: The investment provides IFC with the opportunity to assess the E&S performance of SUCDEN Cote d’Ivoire and identify potential gaps for alignment with international best practices.

project_description: The Project consists of an up to US$15 million equivalent in Indonesia Rupiah (“IDR”) minority equity investment in PT. Tawada Healthcare (“Tawada” or the “Company”), a profitable, high-growth Indonesian medical devices distribution and manufacturing company. The proceeds will be used to support the Company’s capital expenditure for development of its manufacturing facility, acquisitions, and working capital as follows: (i) c.50% of the proceeds towards the acquisitions of one or several companies with medical device distribution and/or manufacturing capabilities that will leverage the Company’s existing platform; (ii) c.20% of the proceeds towards capital expenditure to build its manufacturing capabilities in Batang Central Java Province, in an established industrial park; and (iii) c.30% of the proceeds will be used to fund the Company’s working capital as it grows its scale.
sponsor_shareholders: Tawada is a private company which is (i) 65% owned by Satrija Sumarkho (the “Sponsor”) through PT Triputra Berjaya; and (ii) 35% owned by Capsquare Asia Partners Fund II, L.P. through Apollo Clinical Enterprise Limited. The Sponsor founded Tawada in 1999 and had reacquired majority stakes in 2021 when Navis Capital exited their investment in the Company. Capsquare Asia Partners Fund II, L.P. is an Indonesian private equity fund which acquired 35% of the Company in 2021.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project consists of an up to US$15 million common equity.
location_description: Tawada is one of the largest medical device companies in Indonesia with over 700 employees present across the country with 13 branch offices, 15 sales offices, and 14 warehouses. IFC’s investment will be primarily in Indonesia.
development_impact: The development impact of the proposed project is evaluated against its contribution to the goals of the GHP Platform. The project responds to the challenges of manufacturing and distribution during the COVID-19 pandemic, which placed enormous pressure on healthcare systems. The challenges of distributing medical products are greater in countries with difficult geographies like Indonesia. Through this project, IFC will support a leading domestic distributor and will help to build its manufacturing capabilities for medical consumables and basic equipment. There is also expected to be an impact on market resilience. This impact will occur through strengthening the supply chain to deliver medical devices across Indonesia, consolidating a market that is currently highly fragmented.
additionality: Financial additionality IFC’s own account equity: The proposed investment will support the Company’s capital expenditure needed for business expansion and the construction of a new manufacturing facility located in Central Java, Indonesia. IFC’s long term investment horizon will help the Company to focus better on its business expansion and operation. In addition, with their plan for IPO in the next 1-2 years, IFC’s presence will provide a stamp of approval on the Company’s financial soundness, creditworthiness, and governance. Non-financial additionality Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: Tawada will benefit from IFC's global healthcare sector expertise and network, as it plans to expand beyond distribution to manufacturing. IFC will provide the Company with best practices and lessons learned from IFC's global health portfolio. The Company can also leverage IFC’s global network to connect with new potential partners or principals globally. Standard setting: IFC will assist the Company to bring its operations in line with IFC’s Performance Standards and international standards by benchmarking the operations against IFC requirements and recognized quality certification schemes.

project_description: Olam Palm Gabon S.A. (“OPG” or the “Company”) is a palm oil company in Gabon established in 2011 as a joint venture between food and agribusiness company Olam Global Holdings (60%) and the Republic of Gabon (40%) to develop and operate palm oil plantations in Gabon. The Company’s has developed six plantations covering 63,330 ha of land, associated crude palm oil (“CPO”) mills, a refinery, and other associated facilities (the “Project”). The plantations consist of ca. 57,300 ha in Awala, Mouila and Ndende developed from a greenfield stage (now fully planted), and about 6,000 ha in Makouke acquired from SIAT Gabon in 2016. About 106,000 ha (50% of the total concessions awarded to OPG) are set-aside for the voluntary protection of High Conservation Value areas, including community use zones. The proposed IFC investment is a project finance loan with use of proceeds to support an investment of up $350 m to Olam Palm Gabon (“OPG” US$350m) of which US$150 m would be from IFC’s own account and the remaining amount to be syndicated and financed by IFC’s Parallel lenders. The proceeds will be used for (i) the maintenance of the entire palm oil project which includes OPG’s 63,330 ha of developed palm oil plantations (Awala, Makouke, Mouila Lot 1, 2 and 3, and Ndende), three palm oil mills and kernel crushing plants (KCPs) at Awala, Mouila Lot 1 and 3, crude palm oil (CPO) refinery in Lambarene, and all ancillary facilities (e.g. biogas co-generation power plant at the Awala mill, 24,000 ha drip irrigation system at Makouke and Mouila Lot 1, 2 and 3, CPO bulking station at Owendo port, worker’s accommodations, Crop Protection Products (CPP) and fertilizers warehouses, and maintenance workshop), (ii) capital expenditure (CAPEX), including the construction of a bio-diesel plant and refinery at Owendo port, construction of a 4th mill at Mouila Lot 2 or 3, including a kernel crushing plant, roll-out of the remaining 20,000 ha of drip irrigation project at Makouke and Mouila plantations, biogas co-generation power plants at three mills, namely Mouila Lot 1, 3 and at the proposed 4th mill, and other maintenance, logistics, and building additions/upgrades) (the “Project”), and (iii) partial repayment of the shareholder loan from the sponsors.
sponsor_shareholders: OPG is a palm oil joint venture between Olam Group Holding (60%) and the Government of Gabon (40%), established in 2011. Olam Group Holding is part of Olam Group Limited, a global agribusiness group listed on the Singapore Exchange (SGX).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is arranging an up to US$350 million syndicated senior loans financing package to OPG which includes US$150 million for IFC’s own account and US$200 million in parallel loans from Parallel Lenders.
location_description: The Project is located in the following sites in the Gabonese Republic: palm oil plantations and CPO mills in Awala, Mouila, Ndende and Makouke and CPO refinery in Lambarene. Detailed locations are listed in below link at Olam Group ’s website (“View Our Plantation Locations”): https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/viewer?mid=14dfeS1Tch4LqkIOi-8Io8445tOeggRf5&ll=-0.17200352574736424%2C10.995013000000004&z=7.
development_impact: Main Project Level Development Impact: (i) Economy wide effects - Increased value added and job creation: The Project through the up- and down-stream linkages in expected to increase value added and create jobs. OPG currently has approximately 4,810 Gabonese employees on its payroll, with around one third of staff being female, making OPG the largest private sector employer in Gabon. Part of the job are taken up by villagers from the surrounding communities (about 10% of the workforce). The Project is also expected to create about 20,000 indirect jobs along the value chain in ancillary functions and services, and to stimulate the growth and professionalization of Gabon’s agriculture sector, alleviating Gabon’s significant reliance on food imports. (ii) Diversifying Gabonese economy away from fossil fuel/oil: The Project will contribute toward diversifying Gabonese economy by developing a sector with potential for long-term competitiveness and significant linkages throughout the rural economy. The Project will provide a new source of export revenue for Gabon away from fossil fuels which are declining in production volume and is particularly important to supporting the economy’s resilience to global movements in commodity prices. (iii) Stakeholders – Improved food security for consumers through increased access to palm oil: Domestic and regional consumers will benefit from improved access to a versatile oil which is used in a broad range of products, including edible oil uses. Edible oil, as one of the key food staples, accounts for a significant share of household expenditures amongst “Base of the Pyramid” consumers in the region. Competitive local production of palm oil would therefore contribute to Gabonese and regional food security. (iv) Stakeholders – increased access to palm oil markets: The Project is expected to expand offtake opportunities for smallholder oil palm farmers. The Project will onboard an additional 2,000 smallholders. Main Market Level Development Impact: (i) Competitiveness: The Project will significantly scale up Gabon’s palm oil production capacity and expand access to premium export markets. The production of RSPO-certified palm oil in Gabon may attract other responsible investors to the West and Central Africa region while increasing exports to other markets with stringent product standards. The implemented E&S standards are critical to the palm oil sector which is sensitive to E&S risks, especially those related to biodiversity, deforestation and social impacts including access to land. The efforts undertaken by the Project in this regard include participatory community mapping, use of Free, Prior, and Informed Consent negotiations with local communities, and concession management and planting schemes guided by High Conservation Value assessments which will result in the protection and rehabilitation of large tracts of forest, wetlands, and other natural habitat of high conservation value. As such, the Project can serve as a good practice demonstration example for other investors in Gabon and elsewhere in West and Central Africa, contributing to increasing competitiveness of the sector. (ii) Integration. The export orientation of the proposed investment may not only integrate Gabon into the regional and global palm oil value chains but also relieve some of the broader constraints and bottlenecks to trade, as Olam – via Gabon Special Economic Zone - has made significant investments in related logistics and infrastructure.
additionality: IFC can play a substantial role in developing the sustainable palm oil sector in Africa and in supporting the Gabonese economy to diversify away from crude oil. IFC’s additionality is as follows: Financial additionality: (i) Financing structure and resource mobilization: The financing package provided by IFC is tailored to the needs of the Project and the industry specifics. 12-14-year tenors (depending on the facility) that match the palm oil’s gestation cycle in this specific market can only be provided by IFC and other Development Finance Institutions participating in the syndication. Non-financial additionality: (ii) Standard setting: Appropriate management of E&S risks and issues is central to the sustainability of the sector and represents significant value addition from IFC which has dedicated substantial resources to design an appropriate framework to guide its palm oil engagements. IFC is planning to partner with the WBG to position this investment in the context of broader efforts to promote sustainable biodiversity/forestry management in Gabon as well as to promote employability/vocational training/human resource development in the country. This good practice example is particularly important in a high forest cover country like Gabon. (iii) Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC is exploring the provision of various value-adding Advisory Services.

project_description: The proposed Project with Absa Bank Limited (“Absa” or the “Bank”) is a) an up to ZAR2bln (equivalent to US$112mln); and b) an up to USD40mln working capital support to eligible suppliers of a large manufacturing company (the “Company”). The Project falls under the Global Supply Chain Finance (GSCF) Program, a supply chain finance program launched by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) in December 2022. The GSCF supports open account trade in the emerging markets by providing funded or unfunded risk participation in partner banks’ facilities. The project is part of a crisis response initiative, through which IFC plays a countercyclical role when the markets experience the turbulence due to the negative economic impacts of the ongoing global food and energy crisis.
sponsor_shareholders: Absa is a leading Pan-African financial services group offering banking, insurance and financial products and services to individuals, corporates and small and medium enterprises clients. Headquartered in Johannesburg, south Africa, it is the third largest commercial bank in South Africa with operations in Botswana, Ghana, Kenya, Mauritius, Mozambique, Uganda, Tanzania, Seychelles, and Zambia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is up to US$152mln of which IFC’s proposed risk participation is up to US$76mln to finance the eligible suppliers of a large manufacturing company.
location_description: The Bank and the Company are headquartered in Johannesburg, South Africa. All eligible suppliers are domestic South African companies, of which the majority are micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSME).
development_impact: The proposed project is expected to provide financing to South African suppliers in the face of economic, trade, and supply chain disruptions caused by the ongoing crisis.
additionality: IFC's additionality is driven largely by its countercyclical role when the markets experience the negative impact due to the crisis. Under the GSCF, IFC will provide funded or unfunded risk participation in partner banks’ facilities given: (i) IFC's track record of crisis response efforts; (ii) its network of partner banks that support global emerging markets; (iii) its set of programs aimed at investing both large scale and transactional financing for trade and supply chain finance in emerging markets; and (iv) its ability to support private sector beneficiaries to address liquidity constraints in response to the market shocks.

project_description: The proposed investment (Project) is for a debt facility of up to US$100 million comprising (i) US$50 million IFC A Loan and (ii) US$50 million mobilized by MCPP One Planet, to support Crescent Investment Management III Ltd. (Crescent Point), the General Partner for Crescent Asia Consumer and Deep Value Fund III, L.P. (the Fund or Fund III). Crescent Point is forming a hotel and resorts management platform to acquire and manage hospitality assets within large Southeast Asian countries such as Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam, plus other attractive hospitality markets such as Maldives. IFC will help Crescent Point to implement Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies (EDGE) certification of the hotels under the project. The first investment identified under the Crescent Loan Project is the acquisition and retrofitting of a resort in the Baa Atoll, Maldives.
sponsor_shareholders: Crescent Point and its affiliates (CP Group) manages consumer-focused private equity funds with a geographic focus in China and Southeast Asia started in 2003. Over the last 20 years, CP Group has invested over US$2.0 billion in over 50 companies. CP Group is headquartered in Singapore and has four local offices including Shanghai, HCMC, Jakarta and Manila currently.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Crescent Point’s capital deployment is expected to require investment of approximately US$350 million which IFC will support with an up to US$100 million-equivalent senior loan package, comprising IFC A loans and debt mobilization.
location_description: Baa Atoll, Maldives and other sites to be confirmed, within the eligible countries.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good. The most significant, expected project-level outcomes are (i) Economy-wide effects through the creation and preservation of employment and value addition in the hotel sector and its supply chain, and (ii) Environmental effects through energy and water savings. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote financial integration through demonstration and replication channels.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC will provide countercyclical financing to the Platform and its subsidiaries in Singapore and Maldives at a time when commercial lending to the tourism sector has been negatively affected by the heightened risk perception and the challenging business environment during the COVID-19 pandemic. By providing the necessary capital through a senior debt facility with a tenor of up to 11 years including a 4-year grace period, IFC will help to facilitate the refurbishment and reopening of hotel assets in a timely and sustainable manner, thereby supporting the recovery of the tourism sector in the target countries. Resource mobilization: IFC will mobilize third-party funds from MCPP. This funding will enhance the Fund’s access to international complementary capital, thereby reducing its dependence on domestic banks and vulnerability to financial market shocks.

project_description: The investment consists of a senior, unsecured, syndicated green loan with sustainability linked features for an aggregate amount of up to €500 million to support the expansion of CTP N.V. (CTP and the Company) in Bulgaria and Poland (the Project Countries) (the Project). The Project is aimed to (i) respond to the increased demand from clients in need to upgrade to low-carbon Grade-A industrial and logistics (I&L) building stock and enhance the resilience of their supply chains following the disruptions of the past years, and (ii) catalyze energy-efficient and environmentally friendly development and construction practices as part of a longer-term development agenda in the Project Countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1998, CTP is listed on the Euronext stock exchange in Amsterdam and majority owned (i.e., c.76%) by co-founder and CEO, Mr. Remon Vos.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: On May 4, 2023, IFC committed a partial tranche of €280 million, consisting of (i) a 7-year senior loan of €117 million from IFC’s own account; (ii) a 5-year senior syndicated loan of €117 million; and (iii) a 7-year senior loan of €46 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (the IFC First Investment). The IFC First Investment will support the development of energy-efficient, green-certified I&L infrastructure in the Project Countries. Subsequently, on September 5, 2023, IFC committed a second tranche of €45 million, consisting of (i) a 7-year senior loan of €33 million from IFC’s own account; and (ii) a 5-year senior syndicated loan of €12 million (the IFC Second Investment). Both the IFC First Investment and the IFC Second Investment will support the development of energy-efficient, green-certified I&L infrastructure in the Project Countries.
location_description: Bulgaria and Poland
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are (i) stakeholder effects through increased access to modern and high-quality logistics and business infrastructure, and (ii) environmental effects, through reduction in energy and water use. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Project has the potential to promote greater sustainability in the Project Country's I&L property sector via demonstration and replication channels. Given its leadership position in the market, the potential portfolio-wide greening of CTP will provide a highly visible demonstration case, which could have a catalytic impact on the institutional real estate market in the Project Countries.
additionality: IFC will provide a countercyclical loan to balance out disruptions in the capital markets caused by the geopolitical tensions in the region. The IFC Loan will have a longer tenor than the terms available in the market, and innovatively structured as a green loan with sustainability-linked features, with the interest rate tied to the Company meeting environmental impact-based key performance indicators. Additionally, IFC will play an important role in mobilizing financing from third party lenders, as well as helping the Company diversify its sources of financing. Furthermore, IFC will support CTP to (i) identify, manage and disclose building resilience risks using IFC’s Building Resilience Index; (ii) advance CTP’s green agenda by assessing and providing recommendations on CTP’s decarbonization ambitions, targets and implementation strategy; (iii) expand the use of rooftop photovoltaic systems across CTP’s portfolio by addressing regulatory and infrastructure bottlenecks within the Project Countries; and (iv) introduce CTP to the Green Loan Principles and the Sustainability-Linked Loan Principles of the Loan Market Association.

project_description: Tridem Pharma SAS (“Tridem”), together with Guilin Pharma, are planning to expand their pharmaceutical production capacity and distribution capabilities in French-speaking Africa through the construction of a regional pharmaceutical distribution hub in Cote d’Ivoire and the greenfield construction of a local drug manufacturing facility in Cote d’Ivoire (the “Project”). The manufacturing facility in Cote d’Ivoire will primarily be used to manufacture life-saving anti-malaria drugs. The proposed IFC investment comprises of two A loans to the local subsidiaries of Tridem and Guilin Pharma for the implementation of the Project. Tridem is a French pharmaceutical distribution company with a substantial presence in Africa, which offers distribution solutions for pharmaceutical manufacturers, including regulatory affairs and licensing, promotion, distribution. Guilin Pharma is a Chinese pharmaceutical company and a leading producer of anti-malarial products, with its products being made available in over 80 countries globally.
sponsor_shareholders: Shanghai Fosun Pharmaceutical (Group) Co., Ltd (“Fosun Pharma”) is the Sponsor for the Project, which is a 100% shareholder of Tridem and a 96% shareholder of Guilin Pharma. Fosun Pharma is 35.83 percent indirectly owned by Fosun International Limited, with the remaining 64.17 percent held by public shareholders. Mr. Guangchang GUO is the ultimate controlling shareholder of Fosun Pharma with an indirect interest of 22.3 percent.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is expected to be up to EUR90 million, which will be primarily funded by the IFC A loans and the remaining from internally generated cash and equity injection from the Sponsor. The proposed investment consists of two A loans totalling up to EUR50 million to the local subsidiaries of Tridem and Guilin Pharma.
location_description: The Project will be implemented in Abidjan, Cote d’Ivoire.
development_impact: Project-level: (i) increase access to pharmaceutical products, including life-saving anti-malaria drugs, in the African continent; and (ii) create employment opportunities and economic linkages with additional gross value added. Market creation: support greater resilience of health systems in the Africa continent as spillover effects accrue to the healthcare supply chains in markets of the project scope.
additionality: (i) long-term financing beyond what is available in the African markets; (ii) knowledge sharing as the Company sets up physical presence in some of the Project countries for the first time; and (iii) standard setting and sharing of best practices in Environmental and Social (E&S) aspects.

project_description: In May 2023, IFC committed a senior unsecured 5-year A-Loan of EUR75 million to meet additional working capital requirement of Royal FrieslandCampina N.V (“RFC” or the “Company”) in emerging markets including Pakistan, and to match the cashflow generation ability of the Company. IFC’s loan will help address the impacts of high commodity prices resulting from COVID-19 related supply chain disruptions and support the Company’s ability to preserve the sourcing, processing and distribution of dairy products across emerging markets including Pakistan.
sponsor_shareholders: Based in the Netherlands, RFC is wholly owned by Zuivelcooperatie FrieslandCampina, Europe's largest cooperative with 15,703 member farmers from the Netherlands, Germany and Belgium.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan for IFC’s own account of an up to EUR 75 million equivalent.
location_description: The Project will support the Company in mainly emerging markets including Pakistan.
development_impact: IFC loan will support the continued sourcing, processing, and distribution of dairy products to ensure a steady supply of essential dairy products for consumers in emerging markets including Pakistan thus increasing food security and supply chain resilience to withstand market shocks.
additionality: IFC’s additionality is driven by its countercyclical role during crises providing liquidity for anticipated increase in working capital requirements and financing for continuity of investment plans.

project_description: IFC will provide a senior secured loan of up to US$3 million (the “IFC Loan”) to Tajero Group (“Tajero”, the “Group”) as an allocation under the IFC’s COVID-19 response facility. The IFC Loan will support the increase in working capital requirements of Tajero's core import and distribution business and newly launched diaper production. This project is linked to Tajero WrCap #40023 ( https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/40023/tajero-wrcap ).
sponsor_shareholders: Tajero Group is primarily owned by Mr. Abdurakhmon Gaibullozoda (the “Sponsor”), Tajikistani entrepreneur. Mr. Gaibullozoda started in sales in a local food store in 1992, which he purchased in 1995. Since then, the Sponsor has gradually become the largest food importer and distributor of Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) products for suppliers from Russia, Turkey, Kazakhstan and Europe.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is ~US$11.5 million, the working capital needs for FY23. IFC has been invited to provide an A loan package of US$3.0 million, and the balance will be funded by Sponsor loan (US$4.6 million), Loans from other lenders (US$1.0 million) and Internal cash generation (US$2.4 million).
location_description: Dushanbe, Sughd and Khatlon regions, Tajikistan
development_impact: The expected Project-level outcomes are improved access to affordable quality products and economy-wide impact based on potential value-add and job creation. The investment is expected to promote resilience in the market by creating competitive pressure on other players to strengthen their distribution networks and facilitating vertical integration in the retail market via demonstration channels.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment will provide financial additionality via provision of US$ denominated long-term financing which is limited for private sector companies in the market. Additionally, IFC will advise and support the Group in areas such as E&S matters as it continues its expansion.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an IFC A Loan of up to US$20 million to Farmaenlace (the Company), a leading pharmaceutical retailer and distributor based in Ecuador. The proposed IFC Loan will finance the development of a new distribution center in Llano Grande following green building practices (seeking EDGE certification), the expansion of the Company’s pharmacy network across the country and the refinancing of the Company’s short-term lines (“The Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Farmaenlace is wholly owned by two Ecuadorian families, 50% Ortiz family and 50% Espinosa family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consist of an IFC A Loan of up to US$ 20 million dollars to finance the Project.
location_description: The Llano Grande distribution center is located in the capital city of Ecuador, Quito. The expansion of the pharmacy network will take place across 23 out of the 24 provinces of Ecuador (except Galapagos).
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to improve the access to affordable healthcare products to consumers in Ecuador provinces, including in more rural areas. The Project is expected to create new jobs and has the potential to promote economic linkages to the rest of the economy. Increased investments in a new distribution center will have direct, indirect and induced multiplier effects on the economy by adding value across supply chains. At the market level, the Project will contribute to the regional healthcare system resilience by supporting the Company to expand and increase its capacity to respond to future health crises.
additionality: IFC will expects to provide both financial and non-financial additionality. On the financial side, IFC will provide long-term funding not readily available to Farmaenlace in tenors beyond 5 years. On the non-financial side, IFC can support the Company by provide guidance from industry specialists on global best practices and in relation to its environmental, health and safety standards.

project_description: Founded in 2016, and headquartered in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire, ANKA (or “the Company”) is a social e-commerce enabler that offers a platform for merchants of Africa-related creative industry products to sell, ship and get paid globally. The majority of merchants using ANKA’s platform are small businesses based in Africa, while buyers are spread across the Americas, Europe, Africa and Asia notably. IFC is considering an investment of up to EUR3 million in ANKA, and the project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility. The funding will primarily be used to expand the Company’s operations in Cote d’Ivoire.
sponsor_shareholders: ANKA was initially founded by Moulaye Taboure and Kadry Diallo. Notable existing shareholders include Proparco, Saviu Ventures Limited, Investisseurs & Partenaires (I&P), BESTSELLER Foundation, and the Joe & Clara Tsai Foundation (Bluepool).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Proposed IFC investment of up to US$3.4 million, supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility, is to fund the Company’s operations and expansion plans in Cote d’Ivoire and other IDA eligible countries.
location_description: Cote d’Ivoire
development_impact: IFC anticipates that the Project would result in improved access to markets for creative entrepreneurs, potentially resulting in improved livelihoods, by scaling a social e-commerce platform that connects creative entrepreneurs in West Africa with buyers from international markets through quality logistics services, secured means of payments and improved digital literacy. Beyond the Project, this investment has the potential to strengthen the integration of creative industries in Francophone Africa into global value chains, via enabling framework channels, as successful expansion would enable creative products from the target countries to become more visible in international markets, thereby resulting in increased creative exports.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists in the provision of patient capital not readily available for the Company due to the limited availability of venture capital in Cote d’Ivoire and other target markets. Non-financial additionality involves the provision of knowledge, innovation and capacity building as well as Corporate Governance and E&S standard setting.

project_description: The proposed investment is a US$75 million equivalent A loan to a wholly owned subsidiary of China Sunshine Paper Holdings Company Limited (“Sunshine Paper” or “the Company”), a producer of multipurposed packaging paper in China, to increase an additional 300,000 tons production capacity of biomechanical pulp from wheat straws, and industry-pioneering initiative that would replace virgin and waste pulp in an ecological and energy-saving manner, and its related working capital needs (the “Project”). The Company has been listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange since 2007.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Dongxing Wang, the founder and Chairman, owns 12.8% of the Company through an offshore structure. A further 20.9% is owned by other minority shareholders under a concert parties agreement. The remaining 66.3% is owned by public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$140 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of US$75 million equivalent in local currency, with the remaining project cost funded by Company’s internal cash.
location_description: The project will be located near the company’s headquarter and the existing bio-mechanical pulp operation in Changle Development Zone, Weifang City, Shandong Province.
development_impact: At the Project level, the Project is expected to create income generating opportunities for farmers, as the Company will procure raw material inputs (wheat straws) from local farmers. The Project is also expected to produce economy-wide effects, with employment creation through capacity expansion. At the market level, IFC expects the Project to promote the competitiveness of China’s paper and pulp market through competition channels. If successful, the Project will demonstrate the economic viability as well as environmental benefits of biomechanical pulping from wheat straws to other companies in the sector.
additionality: IFC’s additionality includes: (i) provision of long-term financing that will match the Project’s long ramp-up period, which is not readily available; (ii) sharing of industry knowledge and best practices; and (iii) support of the Company to adopt improved practices, including on environmental and social risk management.

company_name: SK HI-TECH BATTERY MATERIALS POLAND SP.Z O.O
sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: The proposed IFC investment involves a 7 year senior loan of up to $300 million to SK hi-tech battery materials Poland sp. zo.o. (“SK Poland”), comprising (i) an A loan of between US$150 million and US$200 million (but no more than US$200 million) for IFC’s own account; and (ii) a syndicated loan of between US$100 million and US$150 million (but no more than US$150 million). SK Poland is the Polish subsidiary of SK ie technology Co. Ltd (“SKIET” or the “Company”), a manufacturer of lithium-ion battery separators (“LiBS”), a key component of batteries used in electric vehicles (EVs). Currently, SKIET has a total LiBS manufacturing capacity of 1.53bn square meters (sqm) across 4 production facilities in 3 countries, i.e. South Korea, China and Poland. SKIET is listed on the Korea Stock Exchange since May 2021 with a market capitalization of US$3.5 billion equivalent (as of March 13, 2023). IFC’s investment will support the on-going construction and expansion of SK Poland’s production facility in Dabrowa Górnicza, Poland to meet the fast-growing demand for electric vehicles batteries in Europe (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: SKIET was established in April 2019 after being spun off from its parent company SK Innovation Co. Ltd. (the “Sponsor”). It was then listed on the Korea Stock Exchange in May 2021, and the Sponsor holds a shareholding of 61.2% in the Company. Both SKIET and SK Innovation are part of the SK Group, a South Korean conglomerate with combined revenue of around $140bn. SK Group is active in the energy, petrochemicals, semiconductors, telecommunications, e-mobility batteries, and electronic materials industries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project will cost $750 million and will be funded with (i) a senior loan from IFC of up to US$300 million comprising an A loan of between US$150 million and US$200 million (but no more than US$200 million) for IFC’s own account, and a syndicated loan of between US$100 million and US$150 million (but no more than US$150 million), (ii) a $280 million loan from another lender and (iii) $170 million of internal cash generation / equity injection from SKIET.
location_description: Dabrowa Górnicza, Silesia, Poland
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the improvement in Poland’s industrial complexity through local production of a strategic component that requires an advanced manufacturing technology, and the increase in job quality and manufacturing skills in a critical segment for the decarbonization of mobility in Europe. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to fast-track significant improvements in the resilience of the European EV ecosystem, by supporting a first mover in near-shoring production of a critical component in an EV battery cell, and to enable the development of an EV components hub in eastern and central Europe, lowering dependency on a few global suppliers.
additionality: Longer Tenor: The IFC loan will carry a longer tenor than the other existing loans to the Company. This would enable it to maintain the same level of rapid capex deployment required to provide enough supply of separators. Resource Mobilization: The IFC loan will be complemented by a syndicated loan of up to US$150 million, hence enabling the Company to attract sufficient financing to successfully complete its financial plan. Standard setting: IFC will help SK Poland strengthen its existing E&S management system and capabilities in line with IFC’s Performance Standards.
Company Name: SK HI-TECH BATTERY MATERIALS POLAND SP.Z O.O

project_description: The proposed transaction entails an equity investment of up to INR 6,000 million (approximately US$73 million) in the form of compulsorily convertible instruments in a proposed new wholly owned subsidiary (“Mahindra LMM” or the “Company”) of Mahindra & Mahindra Limited (“M&M” or the “Sponsor”). This subsidiary will be newly incorporated to house M&M’s last mile mobility business (LMM). Mahindra LMM plans to incur a total capex of US$113 million over the next 3-4 years towards development and manufacturing of its portfolio. IFC will finance US$73 million which will go towards capex, working capital requirements, etc. for the electric vehicle (EV) business of LMM, by way of an equity investment in the form of compulsorily convertible instruments (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor, M&M, is the flagship company of the Mahindra Group which is one of India’s oldest and most reputed business groups with a footprint in 100+ countries and ~260,000 employees.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project capex is approximately US$113 million. IFC will fund up to approximately US$73 million, which will go towards capex, working capital requirements, etc. in the form of compulsorily convertible instruments.
location_description: The Project location will be India.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are income and livelihood effects for customers. The Project will increase access to E-3Ws (including passenger and cargo delivery vehicles) across India, supporting income and livelihoods of micro-entrepreneurs and will also contribute to localized air pollution benefits for the drivers of the E-3W vehicles. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to contribute to the integration of advanced EV manufacturing capabilities, the scaling-up of the EV ecosystem in India, and the smooth transition of the auto industry from fossil fuel powered vehicles to EVs.
additionality: IFC's additionality stems from (i) financing structure in an evolving sector, (ii) standard setting of governance frameworks and environmental and social (E&S) practices in a newly created company, in discussion with M&M and in consonance with M&M’s existing corporate governance and ESG standards, and (iii) knowledge transfer by leveraging the World Bank Group's expertise in the EV sector and potentially addressing gender gaps in employment.

project_description: Agence de Prestations Maritimes (“APM”) is an integrated provider of real estate warehousing/storage for rent and logistical services. APM provides end to end supply chain services to over 200 local and international customers active over a wide array of sectors ( retail, manufacturing, agriculture) out of the of Kribi and Douala ports. APM currently employs 190 full time staff. The Company has set up a representative office in N’Djamena (Chad) and has a similar plan for Central African Republic (“CAR”) whose importers and exporters face some of the challenges encountered by Chadian customers and also depend heavily on Douala and Kribi for its foreign trade. The Project consists of i) the expansion of APM’s existing warehousing facilities in the Douala Port area, ii) the construction of additional warehousing facilities in Douala’s largest industrial zone, iii) the construction of a wood park the Kribi port area and iv) the refinancing of existing long term local currency LT debt facilities. The project is expected to be supported by the IDA 20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: APM is 30% owned by its CEO Gabriel Manimben, followed by Messac Kwete (25%), Roch Mbanya (14%), Steve Yoh (11%), Joseph Faufack (10%) and five other shareholders for the remaining 9%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at EUR12 million. The proposed IFC investment is a EUR10 million financing package made up of a loan in the amount of up to EUR5 million from IFC of its own account and a loan of up to EUR5 million from IFC as implementing entity of IDA PSW BFF.
location_description: The Project location is in Cameroon and in particular in the cities of Douala and Kribi.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level impact is the effect on tenants/firms who will benefit from modern and high-quality warehouses through efficiency improvement. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will contribute to improving regional market integration, by facilitating the flows of goods and merchandise to and from Cameroon, Chad, Central African Republic (CAR) and other global markets.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality comes from IFC providing debt financing that is not available in the local market. Non-financial additionality comes from IFC support to help the company to build internal capacity to deal with E&S issues and improve its corporate governance.

company_name: Labaid Cardiac and General Hospital Limited
project_description: The proposed investment is to contribute up to US$8.1 Million loan equivalent in Bangladesh Taka (BDT) to Labaid Cardiac and General Hospital (“LCGH” or the “Company” or the “Borrower”) as a senior-secured A loan from IFC (the “A Loan”). The project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (PSW LCF). IFC Loan will be used by the Company to set up a new 100 bed multi-specialty hospital in the emerging residential area of Uttara, a large suburb located 15 kilometers north of Dhaka city. The Project will improve access to affordable, high quality care for patients living in Uttara and neighboring areas by offering a variety of treatments that are currently not available or difficult to access in the vicinity. The Project will increase competitiveness in the sector as the new hospital will pursue accreditation from leading international bodies and enhance the standard of care through a strong demonstration effect. The Project is expected to contribute to employment creation by generating 500 direct jobs.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsors include Dr. A. M. Shamim, his wife Dr. Sucharita Ahmed, his mother Mrs. Saleha Ahmed, his son Dr. Shakif Shamim, his son Mr. Wasif Farhan and his daughter Ms. Tashfia Farheen Parisha (collectively referred to as the “Sponsors”). The sponsors directly or indirectly own 100% of the Borrower.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$13.4 Million and is proposed to be financed with long-term debt totalling US$8.1 Million and the balance ~US$5.4 Million will be financed through equity. Proposed IFC A Loan has a tenor of 10 years including 3 years of grace period
location_description: The Project is located in Uttara, 15 kilometers north of Dhaka City, in Bangladesh, an IDA country.
development_impact: Stakeholders - patients: Given the extent of unmet demand in the country with an average of 8 beds per 10,000 people compared to WHO recommendation of 30 beds per 10,000 people greater private sector participation is needed in setting up new hospitals and IFC expects that the Project will be a step in this direction. At present there are no 100 bed multi-specialty hospitals operational in the area and to access such care patients travel for more than 2 hours to the center of Dhaka city making it highly inconvenient and expensive. IFC expects the Project to provide care to over 105,000 patients on an annual basis providing them a continuum of services across outpatient, inpatient, diagnostics and pharmacy. Economy wide effects: The Project is expected to generate value added and direct jobs as well as indirect jobs through business opportunities for local Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) as service providers. Competitiveness: The Project is expected to result, through demonstration effects, in increased competitiveness of the hospital sector. The Company's plans to pursue accreditation for this hospital from leading international bodies will help raise the bar on quality of care across the industry, potentially forcing the inefficient market players to up their game and motivating larger competitors to improve their quality practices
additionality: (i) IFC will provide financial additionality through a BDT loan with a tenor of 10 years, including 3 years grace period from the Commitment date. The Company requires the long tenor loan to have the necessary financial flexibility to pursue a project with high gestation. (ii) IFC’s several advisory offerings in Quality, Energy Efficiency and Benchmarking can support the company’s efforts to improve operational efficiencies, and better inform its longer-term strategic decisions (iii) IFC will have an opportunity to identify and help close any gaps in the ESG performance of the Company through ESAP and other associated measures prescribed by IFC, the Company will make improvements and align its operations with industry best practices
Company Name: Labaid Cardiac and General Hospital Limited

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an A Loan of up to US$150 million to Votorantim Cimentos S.A. (“VC” or the “Company”), a leading cement producer based in Brazil. The proposed project aims to support the modernization of the Salto plant by upgrading existing equipment and expanding its co-processing capacity to increase the use of alternative fuels (“The Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Votorantim Cimentos S.A. is wholly owned by Votorantim S.A., a Brazilian multinational conglomerate, whose shareholders are members of the Ermirio de Moraes family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investments consist of an IFC A Loan of up to US$ 150 million dollars to finance the Project.
location_description: The Salto plant is located in the municipality of Salto de Pirapora in the state of Sao Paulo, southeast of Brazil.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to create positive environmental effects by reducing the carbon intensity of cement production in the Company's Brazilian operation with a larger use of alternative fuels and by strengthening Votorantim Cimentos' commitment to its global decarbonization pathway. At the market level, the Project is expected to have a strong demonstration effect by incentivizing other players to replicate VC's funding strategy by issuing sustainability linked loans, with the goal of attaining the demanding climate related standards of the industry.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality derives from the provision of long-term financing not otherwise available in the market and by the implementation of a sustainability linked loan, an innovative instrument currently being utilized solely by the Company in the Brazilian cement sector. Non-financial additionality is provided via knowledge, innovation and capacity building as IFC will support the Company's decarbonization efforts through an engagement that will (a) support the evaluation of VC’s pipeline of climate investment projects and (b) provide inputs on VC’s alternative fuels sourcing strategy.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support Duval Group (“Duval” or the “Group”) and its subsidiary, Duval Great Lakes, build and operate a mixed-use property building complex that will consist of a shopping, food & beverage and entertainment area, a service apartment hotel, as well as office, co-working and conference space to be located opposite the Kigali Convention Center in Kigali, Rwanda (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Duval Great Lakes, the Project entity, is majority owned by Duval Group. The other shareholder is Vicky Murabukirwa. Duval Group is a well-established French conglomerate with core activities in real estate and hospitality. Duval Group is owned by the Duval family, including amongst others, Eric Duval, the Group’s founder and chairman, Pauline Duval, Co-Executive Director and Louis-Victor Duval, Co-Deputy Executive Director. Vicky Murabukirwa is a real estate professional in Rwanda.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be up to close to US$70 million. IFC will provide an A-loan of up to US$17.5 million and will mobilized up to another US$17.5 million from other lender(s). The remaining portion of the Project will be funded by Duval Group and possibly other equity investors.
location_description: The Project is located in Kigali, Rwanda.
development_impact: The Project is expected to contribute to improve businesses’ access to high-quality and modern urban infrastructure through new commercial property developments and will contribute to job creation and contribution to GDP as well as indirect effects across the distribution chains. The Project is also expected to improve energy and water use efficiency by deploying energy friendly materials, technology, and equipment, thereby reducing the Project’s GHG emissions.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC's financial additionality is delivered through the provision of long-term financing in line with the Project's needs and the mobilization of other lender(s) to meet the Project financing needs. IFC's non-financial additionality is delivered through the provision of technical expertise through the implementation of comprehensive Environmental & Social management systems and the provision of green building advice to achieve EDGE standards.

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: Industria Sudati de Compensados Ltda. (the “Company” or “Sudati”) is a Brazilian exporter of plywood and producer of Medium Density Fiberboard (“MDF”). Sudati operates 5 industrial facilities across the southern states of Parana and Santa Catarina. Sudati is constructing a new MDF Production line at its existing MDF plant in Santa Catarina, Brazil.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded in 1998 by Luiz Sudati and his wife Tatiane Sudati, and they remain the sole shareholders. Luiz Sudati is the company’s CEO.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing an A Loan of up to US$30 million and a B Loan of up to US$ 30 million to support Sudati’s expansion of a new MDF production line and related working capital.
location_description: Investments will be made at Sudati’s facilities located in Otacilio Costa, Santa Catarina, Brazil.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to provide stable access to market and technical assistance for farmer suppliers. At the market level, the Project will help strengthen the competitiveness of Brazil’s wood panel sector by introducing advanced designs that increase operating efficiency.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality comes from the provision of long-term financing and resource mobilization. Non-financial additionality comes from Environmental & Social standard setting and knowledge, innovation and capacity building.

project_description: Liquid Telecommunications Holdings Limited (“Liquid” or the “Sponsor”), via its local subsidiaries (including Liquid Telecom South Africa and Liquid ECG Infraco) has rolled out extensive broadband services in various provinces. The Project entails the provision of broadband services, initially using microwave, before fully transitioning to fiber once the deployment is completed. During the initial 3 years, Liquid ECG Infraco will be rolling out over 7,000 kilometres of fiber. Liquid plans to implement the project through a wholly-owned special purpose vehicle (“SPV”). The project activities have commenced since mid-2022, and to date there has been a roll-out of 2,700 kilometres of fiber.
sponsor_shareholders: Liquid is the leading pan-African provider of wholesale voice, wholesale data, and internet protocol (IP) services, and an existing IFC client, and provides internet services across the African continent and in particular across various provinces in South Africa.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost approximately ZAR 1.45 billion (approximately US$82 million) and will be financed through a combination of senior debt to be incurred by the Company and internally generated funds from the Sponsor.To support the Project, IFC intends to invest up to ZAR 900 million (or its equivalent in US$) consisting of (i) a Loan in the amount of up to ZAR 450 million (or its equivalent in US$); and (ii) financing in the form of (a) an MCPP Trust Loan and/or a B2 Loan in the amount of up to ZAR 450 million (or its equivalent in US$); or (b) alternatively, a Parallel Loan of up to ZAR 450 million.
location_description: The project will be based in South Africa.
development_impact: This Project is expected to result in (i) increased access to quality digital connectivity for individuals and businesses; (ii) improved access to education, healthcare, and public services; and (iii) jobs for workers through the expansion of high-speed Internet infrastructure to connect government agencies in a region that is among the least connected in South Africa. Beyond the Project, this investment is expected to strengthen the integration of the digital ecosystem in South Africa by enabling the connectivity of underserved areas through e-government services.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is primarily financial and involves (i) financial structure based on the provision of a local currency A loan under a structuring that enables the client to execute its expansion plan while meeting the covenants of its existing debts, and (ii) resource mobilization through MCPP given the limited availability of credit that matches the debt profile of the client in the local market.

project_description: The Project is to support the City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality’s (“CoJ” or the “City”) FY22/23 capital investment program, through an IFC’s proposed 15-year senior loan of up to US$100 million (in South African Rands equivalent). The investment aims to support CoJ’s FY22/23 capital investment program for infrastructure assets, which comprises primarily of upgrades, replacements and expansion of energy, water and sanitation, and transport infrastructure. The capital investment program is a high priority for CoJ, South Africa’s largest metropolitan city, in improving the quality of infrastructure services and life for its residents. This investment will also assist the City in providing enhanced access to public services and infrastructure to underserved areas.
sponsor_shareholders: CoJ is the largest municipality in South Africa from a revenue and expenditure standpoint. It is located in the Gauteng Province of South Africa and is one of the most advanced commercial cities in Africa and the engine room of the South African and regional economy. CoJ is a city with a unique, African character, world-class infrastructure in the fields of telecommunications, transportation, water and power, and with globally competitive health care and educational facilities.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: CoJ plans to raise up to ZAR1.83 billion (around US$100 million) through IFC’s proposed loan to finance a portion of its FY22/23 capital expenditure program of ZAR6.38 billion (around US$348 million).
location_description: CoJ is located in the Gauteng Province of South Africa.
development_impact: The Project and advisory services support: i) Improving the quality of infrastructure services in SA's largest city though infrastructure upgrades, replacements and expansion; and ii) Improving COJ's financial resilience by increasing cost recovery in the power and water sectors.
additionality: IFC will help COJ to better align debt maturities with its infrastructure assets by providing a longer tenor investment than is currently available in the market. IFC will also seek to provide advisory services to COJ, thus supporting efforts to improve sustainability and strengthen development effects.

sector: Fruit and Vegetable Preservation or Processing (Canning, Freezing, Drying, Jams, etc.)
project_description: Sugal Chile Limitada (“Sugal Chile” or the “Company”) is the Chilean subsidiary of the Sugal Group (the “Group”), a tomato paste producer and exporter. The Group sources tomato in Spain, Portugal and Chile, and processes c.a.1.8 million tons of tomatoes per year. The proposed IFC investment is composed of an up to USD25 million A loan and an up to USD25 million MCPP loan for Sugal Chile to finance its capex program and permanent working capital, including (i) a new tomato paste production line in Talca, (ii) the maintenance of the Tilcoco Plant, (iii) decarbonization of energy consumption, and (iv) processes reengineering (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Sugal Group is ultimately owned by the Ortigão Costa family, who founded the Group in 1957 and holds a 94% shareholding interest. The balance is held by a minority shareholder.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project Cost is estimated at USD50 million which IFC is seeking to support through an A loan of up to USD25 million and an MCPP loan of up to USD25 million.
location_description: The Project is located in Talca and Tilcoco, in the Maule and Libertador Bernardo O’Higgins regions of Chile, respectively.
development_impact: The development impact of the project is driven by the support that Sugal Chile provides to the farmers, in addition to the environmental effects reducing GHG emissions and generating energy and water efficiencies. The Project has the potential to have a market impact through resilience, IFC anticipates that projects under the Global Food Security Platform ("GFSP") will contribute to maintaining and strengthening resilience in the global food supply market.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing structure: Sugal Chile has been financing all its needs with local banks and on terms that entail shorter maturity than would be desirable for their business. IFC would bring diversification of funding sources as well as longer-tenors not ready available in the local market. Resource Mobilization: IFC would mobilize funds from managed third-party funds (MCPP) which would not be available if not for IFC´s participation and which would help to further diversify the Group´s funding sources. Non-Financial Additionality: Standard Setting: IFC will share international best practices in E&S and will support Sugal Chile to keep improving its standards. Energy and water efficiencies: IFC will explore advisory services opportunities on energy and water efficiency.

sector: Re-Rolling and Drawing of Purchased Steel
project_description: Kandil Steel S.A.E (“KS” or the “Company”) is the leading downstream flat steel supplier in Egypt and having export capacity. The proposed investment is an IFC A loan of up to US$25 million to finance the Company’s permanent working capital needs, the “Project”.
sponsor_shareholders: KS is owned by the Kandil family (86.2%), Marubeni Itochu Steel Inc, Japan (10.1%), and JFE Steel Corporation, Japan (3.7%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated project cost is US$25 million, of which IFC will fully finance through an A loan.
location_description: Kandil Steel S.A.E is headquartered in Egypt and operates two main production facilities domestically: Kama for Coating and Manufacturing located in 10th of Ramadan, and Galva Metal located in El Obour City. The two production facilities manufacture the same products except for pre-painted products which are only manufactured at Kama Coating.
development_impact: The Project will enable the Company to maintain capacity utilization rates, hence preventing reduction in output and preserving direct value-addition to the Egyptian economy. In addition, IFC’s investment will support the Company to preserve its current employment levels. Beyond project outcomes, IFC anticipates the Project will promote resilience in the domestic steel market through preserving the operations of a critical supplier of flat steel products in Egypt
additionality: IFC’s additionality will be financial and non-financial. IFC is providing US$ liquidity for working capital funding that is scarce in the market. IFC's non-financial additionality will be derived from supporting the Company develop and implement its decarbonization program, which includes renewable energy, energy efficiency, and efficient hydrogen and acid production components
