country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: Lentesplus (or the “Company”) was founded in 2013 in Colombia. The Company is an omnichannel platform that commercializes eyewear products (ophthalmic glasses, sunglasses, and contact lenses). It operates in Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Mexico, under the brand Lentesplus, and, in Brazil, under two brands (i) NewLentes, contact lenses e-commerce and (ii) Livo, eyewear retailer.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company’s co-founders are Jaime Oriol and Diego Mariño. The Company’s investors include Inversiones Oranda, Palm Drive Capital, Ignia Ventures, Empire Group, and InQlab, among others.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to invest US$ 10 million in the Company as a convertible note as part of the Company’s current fundraising, with additional capital to be provided by current investors of the Company and other external investors.
location_description: The Company has offices in São Paulo and Bogotá and currently operates in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Argentina.
development_impact: IFC anticipates that the Project would result in improved access to eyewear products for individuals in Latin America, potentially improving health outcomes related to vision care. Beyond the Project, this investment has the potential to improve the competitiveness of the eyewear market across Latin America by sustaining affordability.
additionality: IFC’s Additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists in the provision of financing as part of the Company’s round in Latin America, where fundraising for late stage venture capital deals remains challenging. Non-financial additionality involves the provision of knowledge, support with innovation and capacity building, and standard setting.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

company_name: Sama Al Manar for General Trading, Animal and Agriculture Production, Industrial Production, Oils
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a financing package of up to US$112.5 million, composed by an A-loan of up to US$66 million for IFC’s own account, a B1-loan of up to US$31.5 million, and a parallel loan of up to US$15 million. The proposed financing package intends to support the development of a US$205.5 million agro-industrial complex, including soybean crushing plant and warehouses at Berth 4 of the Umm Qasr Port in Iraq (the Project). The project will have a full corporate guarantee from Tiryaki Agro Gida Sanayi Ve Ticaret A.S. (“Tiryaki” or the “Sponsor”) which is a leading agricultural commodity trading company in Türkiye. Sama Al-Manar for General Trading Company (the “Project Company) of which Tiryaki is a shareholder, will execute the Project. Tiryaki is a previous IFC portfolio client, with 2 previous transactions.
sponsor_shareholders: Sama Al Manar for General Trading is a partnership between Tiryaki Agro (54%), Fatih Tiryakioglu, a shareholder in Tiryaki Agro (1%), and Hussein Al-Khazraji (45%), an Iraqi national, with experience in agriculture grain trading in Iraq.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering an A-loan of up to US$66 million for its own account. IFC is also syndicating a B-loan of up to US$31.5 million and a parallel loan of up to US$15 million. The financing package is divided into two tranches: The first tranche of US$45 million, with an 8-year tenor, to be used to fund the capex requirements. The second tranche of US$67.5 million to be used to fund permanent working capital needs, through a 5-year annually revolving facility. The total project cost to develop the agro-industrial complex is US$205.5 million. The remaining project cost will be financed from internally generated cashflow, at the project company level, in addition to sponsor equity.
location_description: The project is located in the backyard of Berth 4 of the Umm Qasr Port in Basra in the South of Iraq. The project site covers an area of approximately 171,000 m2.
development_impact: the Project is expected to contribute to improved food security for consumers through increasing the availability of maize and soybean meal to support poultry production in Iraq, and to generate economy wide effects through employment creation, value addition, and contribution to economic and export diversification. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing, as part of IFC’s Global Food Security Platform, will promote greater resilience in the global food supply market.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC provides a long-term loan in two tranches with an 8-year tenor for the first tranche and a 5-year annual revolving facility for the second tranche Resource Mobilization: IFC B Loan of up to US$31.5 million and Parallel Loan of up to US$15 million Non Financial Additionality: IFC supports the Company in the implementation of good E&S practices.
Company Name: Sama Al Manar for General Trading, Animal and Agriculture Production, Industrial Production, Oils

project_description: IFC has provided an equity investment of up to INR 2,400 million (approximately US$30 million) in JK Tyre & Industries Limited (“JK Tyre” or “the Company”), in the form of equity securities. The Company is implementing a capital expenditure plan of about US$158 million between FY21-25 to increase the production capacity of truck and bus radial (TBR) tires and passenger car radial (PCR) tires by more than 10 percent, from 32 million tires per annum to 35 million tires per annum. Of this, in FY24, the Company will implement capital expenditure of U$68 million along with resource efficiency projects (the “Project) and the proposed IFC investment will support the Company in implementing the Project.
sponsor_shareholders: JK Tyre was incorporated in 1976 by late Shri Hari Shankar Singhania and is amongst the top four tire manufacturers in India and the top 25 globally. JK Tyre is one of the flagship companies of the JK Group. The Company is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange and has a market capitalization of more than US$ 490 million as of September 2022. The Promoter group and family hold 56.3 percent of the total share capital of the Company and the balance is held by financial institutions and public. The promoter group holds the Company’s share mainly through Bengal and Assam Company Ltd., a listed non-banking financial company Dr. Raghupati Singhania is the Chairman and Managing Director and Anshuman Singhania is the Managing Director.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The IFC investment comprises an equity investment of up to INR 2,400 million (equivalent to US$ 30 million) by subscribing to equity securities issued by the Company. Considering the surge in demand and the near full capacity utilization of its existing facilities, JK Tyre has an ongoing capital expenditure plan of about US$158 million for increasing the capacity of its TBR and PCR production facilities in India by more than 10 percent, from 32 million tires per annum to 35 million tires per annum. The expansion is being implemented in a phased manner over FY21-25. In FY24, the Company is implementing capital expenditure of U$68 million as well as resource efficiency projects (the “Project). Additionally, the Company is strategically bringing down its leverage and strengthening its balance sheet. The IFC investment will support the Company in successful implementation of the Project and strengthening of its balance sheet.
location_description: The Project will be located at the Company’s existing manufacturing facilities in India; Banmore, and Laksar.

project_description: Boston Metal (“BM” or the “Company”, https://www.bostonmetal.com/) was created in 2012 with technologies licensed from Massachusetts Institute of Technology. The Company patented the Molten Oxide Electrolysis (MOE), a technology that can be used to reduce the carbon footprint of steel production and to produce high-value metals, such as tin, tantalum and niobium. The MOE technology, is an electro-chemical process, which uses direct electric current and an anode to separate chemical compounds into their constituent parts, eliminating the need for coal in steel production. MOE can make use of low- and mid-grade iron ore fines and iron slag that are unsuitable for low-emission steel making with incumbent technologies. MOE can also be used to recover high value metals from mine slags. Boston Metal research and development (R&D) facilities are located in an industrial neighborhood in Massachusetts, United States (US) where MOE modular cells of different sizes are routinely redesigned and reconfigured as part of the Company’s MOE scale up R&D process. In addition, Boston Metal is planning to ramp up production of steel at its new industrial demonstration plant, begin its construction in 2024 and start commercial operations in 2026. The location of the new plant has not been decided yet. In 2022, Boston Metal established a subsidiary in Minas Gerais, Brazil, where MOE technology will be used to recover high-value metals from mining slag. The project will be built in the municipality Coronel Xavier Chaves. In addition to the plant, the project will include the civil works for the connection to the electrical grid which is located around 500 meters away from the project site. The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$20M equity investment as part of a Series C round to further develop and commercialize the MOE platform and expand BM’s operations in the United States and Brazil.
sponsor_shareholders: The Series C round is led by ArcelorMittal, with participation from other investors, including Microsoft. Existing investors include strategic players such as Vale, BHP and BMW, climate-tech focused groups such as Energy Impact Partners and Breakthrough Energy Ventures, and deep-tech specialists such as The Engine.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an up to $20M equity investment as part of a Series C round to further develop and commercialize the Molten Oxide Electrolysis platform and expand Boston Metals’ operations in the United States and Brazil.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Woburn, Massachusetts and there is a project site in Coronel Xavier Chaves, Minas Gerais in Brazil.
development_impact: The development impact of the project will be via: (i) Project Outcomes (Stakeholders): Access to a steel production decarbonization technology for manufacturers, potentially resulting in improved access to offtake markets, and in the medium term some GHG emissions avoidance. (ii) Contribution to Market Creation (Sustainability): Creating a sustainable steel manufacturing sector in emerging markets, especially Brazil and India, via demonstration and replication channels.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this Project involves (i) knowledge, innovation, and capacity building by enabling the development and future commercialization of the Company’s technology in emerging markets; and (ii) standard setting, by helping the Company align its Environmental, Social and Governance standards with good international practices and IFC’s Performance Standards, and develop a framework to track its contribution to climate mitigation.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to EUR100 million (equivalent US$107 million) senior loan to Sunda Group Company Limited (Sunda or the Company) and its subsidiary company, Solipro Limited (Solipro), to support the Company’s capital expenditure and working capital needs in Africa. The proposed loan will finance Sunda’s investment program which seeks to expand its manufacturing operations in fast moving consumer goods (FMCG) and metal hardware production in Africa, including (i) a washing powder production factory in Ghana; (ii) distribution centers in Ghana; (iii) diaper/hygienic product factory expansions in Ghana, Guinea, Kenya, and Nigeria; and (iv) a hardware manufacturing factory in Cote d’Ivoire (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Sunda is a leading Africa-focused, manufacturing and trading company registered in Hong Kong, and operating in the FMCG, building materials, and metal hardware product segments. Solipro, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sunda, serves as Sunda’s centralized treasury and international procurement platform. The Company’s ultimate beneficiary owners are Mr. Yanchang Shen and Ms. Yanjuan Yang, the spouse of Mr. Shen, who collectively have 61.4 percent shareholding in the Company. Mr. Yanchang Shen is the founder, Chairman and CEO of Sunda. The remaining 38.6 percent is owned by employees.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at EUR160 million (equivalent US$171 million) and will be financed by: (i) the proposed EUR100 million (equivalent to US$107 million) A loan from IFC; and (ii) EUR60 million (equivalent to US$64 million) internal cash generation from Sunda.
location_description: Abidjan, Cote d’Ivoire; Accra, Ghana; Kindia, Guinea; Nairobi, Kenya; Ogun, Nigeria
development_impact: The most significant project-level outcomes are improved customer access to basic FMCG (hygiene products and detergents) and hardware products. Beyond the project, IFC expects that this investment will strengthen competitiveness of the basic FMCG sector in the West African regional market, through economies of scale, increased efficiencies along the supply chain, enhanced production capacity, and product diversification realized through the investment.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality: 1) Financing Structure: IFC will provide a substantial amount of long-term hard currency financing, to be deployed across multiple countries in different regions of Africa, which is not readily available through local banks due to shallow financial markets and limited appetite for cross-border financing. 2) Non-commercial risk mitigation: IFC will help mitigate sovereign and regulatory risks and enhance the Company’s credibility as it seeks to expand regionally. 3) Standard Setting: IFC will provide knowledge and advice to Sunda to strengthen its environmental and social (E&S) management systems and capabilities in line with IFC’s Performance Standards (PS) requirements.

project_description: Guangxi Yangxiang Co., Ltd (“GXYX” or the “Company”) is an existing IFC client engaged in pig farming and pig feed manufacturing business and is ranked among the top 10 pig producers in China. The Project is to support the incremental medium-term working capital needs by the Company’s feed and pig farms in Guangxi. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to CNY300 million (approximately US$47.3 million equivalent) and will be part of IFC Global Food Security Platform (GFSP) to strengthen the resilience of global food supply chains.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. YANG Xiang is the founder and controlling shareholder of the Company. Mr. Yang controls 74.5% shareholding of the Company through 37.2% direct stake and 37.3% indirect stake via acting-in-concert with other management. The other shareholders are 42 individual shareholders, Continental Feed, 2 university funds and 3 pre-IPO investment funds.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated to be approximately US$160 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to CNY300 million (approximately US$47 million equivalent) to the Company.
location_description: Guigang, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region
development_impact: The Project is assessed as part of IFC’s Global Food Security Platform (GFSP). IFC expects the Project to increase food security for consumers by sustaining and expanding the availability of pork, a main source of protein for consumers in China, and improve access to market and technical assistance for farmers. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater resilience in the global food supply market as part of the GFSP.
additionality: (i) financing structure, by providing a long-term local currency working capital loan in response to the global commodity price increases; (ii) knowledge, innovation and capacity development in animal welfare, antibiotics practices, corporate governance and decarbonization; (iii) E&S standard-setting.

project_description: The proposed investment is a US$30 million subscription in subordinated notes issued by Africa Impact Industrial, currently renamed to Bora Africa (“Bora” or the “Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of Grit Real Estate Income Group Limited, a public company headquartered in Mauritius (“Grit” or “GREIG”). Grit sees significant opportunities in the industrial real estate sub-sector and is creating a REIT-like vehicle, Bora Africa, which will invest in warehousing, prime logistics, light industrial, manufacturing, storage facilities, data centres and digital infrastructure real estate assets in Sub Saharan Africa (SSA). Grit will contribute its existing industrial portfolio of assets currently worth ~US$92 million (the “Seed Assets”), including: (i) Imperial Warehouse (Kenya), tenanted by Imperial Health Sciences, a SSA leader in healthcare supply chain management; (ii) the Orbit Facility leased to a leading household chemicals manufacturer in Nairobi; (iii) Bolloré Warehouse (Mozambique) tenanted by one of the world’s largest logistics groups; and (iv) three land bank assets in prime industrial nodes ready for greenfield development (Kenya). Bora Africa will then raise additional financing to execute a ~US$192 million pipeline of acquisition and new asset development opportunities in SSA. Grit is seeking IFC’s funding to support the acquisition and development of the industrial pipeline assets in Kenya, Mauritius and Nigeria (the “Pipeline Assets”). The balance of the financing required for the Pipeline Assets will be provided by Grit and co-investors in the form of equity and by private financial institutions in the form of senior debt.
sponsor_shareholders: Grit is a leading pan-African impact real estate company focused on investing in, developing and actively managing a diversified portfolio of assets (income producing assets of US$832.8 million as at 31 December 2022) in selected SSA countries (excluding South Africa). Grit holds its primary listing on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange (GR1T) and a secondary listing on the Stock Exchange of Mauritius (DEL.N0000). Grit is well known to IFC having secured a US$25 million IFC A Loan (Project #45002) that financed the Orbit Facility transaction.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Bora Africa will be seeded with assets currently worth ~US$92 million, then the vehicle will add pipeline assets worth ~US$192 million, of which IFC will be financing US$30 million via subordinated notes issued by Bora Africa.
location_description: While Bora Africa is domiciled in Mauritius, the assets in the vehicle will be located across four countries, namely Mauritius, Mozambique, Kenya, Nigeria and any other countries in Africa (excluding South Africa) agreed by Bora’s Board of Directors.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are i) environmental effects, through reduction in energy and water consumption, which will reduce GHG emissions; and ii) economywide effects through job creation, higher tax revenues and increased industrial output. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will facilitate the integration of the SSA real-estate market into regional and global financial markets through demonstration and replication effects for REIT and REIT-type vehicles.
additionality: Financial Additionality - Financing structure: IFC will provide scarce mezzanine funding, which is not readily available for GREIG (especially being a REIT-like vehicle with a high debt level) in the local market. The IFC facility will improve GREIG's debt profile and enhance its access to outside complementary capital, thus reducing its vulnerability to domestic financial and banking shocks. Non-Financial Additionality - Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC will provide technical knowledge and advice on green building standards as well as support to EDGE-certify the Project. IFC will also provide guidance to GREIG on the best practice E&S standards for the project.

sector: Pottery, Ceramic, and Plumbing Fixtures (Including Kitchenware)
project_description: The proposed investment is a debt facility to i) Tilemaster Investment Limited (Tilemaster, the Company or the Borrower), a Mauritius based holding company; and (ii) Brightsar Investment Limited (Brightstar, or CoBorrower, together with Tilemaster, the Borrowers), a Mauritius based holding company. Tilemaster and Brightstar manufacture and distributes ceramic tiles in Africa. Tilemaster is owned 51percent by Keda Industrial Group Co. Ltd (Keda) and 49percent by Sunda Group Co. (Sunda). Brightstar is wholly owned by Tilemaster. The proceeds of the debt facility will be used to finance Tilemaster’s corporate capital investment and long term working capital financing program. IFC’s loan proceeds will be dedicated to (i) expanding ceramic tile production and establish sanitary ware production in Ghana and (ii) setting up greenfield architectural flat glass plant in Tanzania (the Project). The Project will enable Tilemaster to localize ceramic tiles production in Africa and diversify its production base to manufacture associated building material products (such as sanitary ware and float glass).
sponsor_shareholders: Keda (51% shareholder of Tilemaster) is a leading global ceramic machinery manufacturer listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. Its core business segments include building materials machinery, building materials such as ceramic tiles, and lithium-ion battery. Sunda (49% shareholder of Tilemaster) is an Africa-focused manufacturing and trading company. Sunda has an extensive trading network that distributes building materials (ceramic tiles), consumer products (washing powders, diapers, sanitary towels) and hardware in more than 20 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa. It also has a growing manufacturing base with 15 manufacturing plants across 10 countries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be EUR200 million out of a total investment program of EUR370 million. IFC’s financing consists of up to EUR154 million in IFC A-Loan and up to EUR46 million from the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP).
location_description: a) Takoradi in Ghana; and b) Mkuranga in Tanzania.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the generation of direct and indirect employment and increase in value addition, and the improvement in manufacturing skills in several African countries. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to further strengthen the integration of the Ghanaian and Tanzanian economies into continental trade linkages, and to increase their industrial complexity.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via (i) providing a large unsecured loan in hard currency; and (ii) resource mobilization of up to EUR46 million via the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program. Non-financial additionality is provided via (i) mitigating sovereign and regulatory risks, and enhancing the Company’s credibility; and (ii) standard setting via an improved E&S risk management systems and capabilities.

project_description: IDA Private Sector Window’s Blended Finance Facility (“IDA PSW-BFF”) is expected to support IFC with a limit enhancement of up to US$400 million (“blended concessional finance co-investment”). Without the support provided by IDA PSW, IFC will not be able to support increase in trade volume, given the banks/countries exposure constraints, and/or high risk in booking trade finance in IDA/FCS countries. This support has become even more urgent in the context of rising commodity prices and declining insurance availability, which has resulted in increased unmet trade finance demand by clients. The project will not benefit from a subsidy, as it will earn a fee that is comparable to the market. As is the case with all of IFC’s blended concessional finance co-investments, this project has been assessed against the Enhanced Blended Concessional Finance Principles for DFI Private Sector Operations adopted by IFC and more than 20 other DFIs in 2017. Further information on these Enhanced Principles, IFC’s blended finance approach and governance and details and historical information on estimated subsidy levels in IFC’s blended finance portfolio can be found at: www.ifc.org/blendedfinance. To support this increase in trade volumes at this most critical time, IFC is open to engaging with other partner banks.
sponsor_shareholders: The proposal does not have a single company and/or sponsor, but rather, is expected to support more than 2,000 real sector participants (exporters/importers) as the sponsors. This proposal will rely on GTFP’s existing and new obligors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC as implementing entity of the IDA Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) is expected to support IFC with a revolving limit enhancement of up to US$400 million under Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP). The facility would enable additional trade finance of up to US$2 billion in IDA PSW eligible countries that would otherwise not happen in the current volatile environment, brought on by economic dislocations in the wake of overlapping war-related and post COVID-19 crises, global inflationary environment, and recession expectations in many parts of the world.
location_description: IDA PSW eligible countries.
development_impact: The project builds on GTFP's global platform, increasing access to trade finance to emerging markets. The project will provide increased access to trade finance to the Issuing Bank's customers, including both corporates and SMEs. On the market side, the project will improve overall market integration by (1) maintaining and expanding trade finance, financial linkages and trade across multiple markets through strengthening bilateral correspondent banking connections; (2) serving as an enabling platform to make new connections between local and international banks and their customers; (3) channeling new sources of capital to support EMDE trade flow through demonstration and replication of successful correspondent banking connections and being an example of a successful investment platform. In lower income/ IDA, fragile and conflict-affected countries, and smaller players in middle income countries, the project also builds, protects, and deepens trade finance networks by continually enabling individual trade transactions, which, over time, builds resilience of trade networks, trade, and income growth in these economies.
additionality: IFC’s additionality stems from its counter-cyclical role in its ability to continue its engagement with its extensive network of banking clients during crisis times, when other lending institutions or investors’ appetite is subdued, ensuring access to trade finance. This additionality is especially pronounced in the high-risk PSW countries, where the crisis impact is typically stronger than in higher income countries, due to pre-existing vulnerabilities and limited capacity of both governments and banks. Emerging market banks, particularly in PSW eligible countries, are in critical need of limit increases and liquidity to maintain their support to their trade finance clients amid increased risks. Availability of trade finance has decreased, as global banks and insurance companies have either reduced trade exposures or limited their risk exposure to EMDE counterparties, in the face of increasing risk perception following country defaults and downgrades. IFC in conjunction with PSW has a critical role to play in increasing the support to existing and new banks in IDA PSW markets. The project will enable trade financing of about $2 billion in IDA-PSW countries that would otherwise not happen. The Project is expected to help Issuing Banks strengthen their trade finance operations. In addition, issuing banks will benefit from IFC's technical expertise in redesigning its trade solutions and marketing materials.

project_description: The proposed investment is an A loan to Sansure Biotech, Inc. (Sansure, or the Company), to support its (i) increase in production capacity of in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) products in China, and (ii) expand into Southeast Asia and Africa through the setting up of local operations (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Sansure’s single largest shareholder is its Founder and Chairman, Dr. Dai Lizhong, who directly and indirectly owns 37.6 percent of the Company. The other shareholders of the Company are employees and public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost for the Project is estimated to be US$110 million, IFC will provide an A Loan of up to US$55 million equivalent. The remainder of the Project cost will be financed by the Company’s internal resources.
location_description: The Project is located in Hunan, China, Southeast Asia region, and Africa region.
development_impact: At the Project level, the Project is expected to increase access to affordable and quality IVD products for patients residing in China and developing countries in Southeast Asia and Africa, that would help enhance the outcome of medical treatments. The Project will also create local skilled employment opportunities and enhance domestic supply chain of IVD products. At the Market level, the Project is expected to contribute to increased competition in the IVD industry in China, Southeast Asia and Africa. Not only will increased competition benefit patients in these markets through increased supplies and enhanced affordability, it will also showcase the market opportunities, especially in the underserved markets in Southeast Asia and Africa, which could stimulate new entrants into these markets.
additionality: IFC’s Additionality includes: (i) provision of long-term financing that will match the Project’s long ramp-up period, which is not readily available, (ii) sharing of industry knowledge and best practices; and (iii) improving the Company’s environmental and social (“E&S”) performance through the adoption of an E&S Action Plan.

sector: Garment and Apparel (Without Fabric , Excluding Footwear)
project_description: The proposed investment is an A loan of up to US$20 million (“the IFC Loan”) to Hela Investment Holdings Ltd (“HIH” or “the Company”), a Mauritius-registered holding company. HIH is an indirect and wholly owned subsidiary of Hela Apparel Holdings PLC (“HAH” or “the Hela Group”), a Sri Lankan-headquartered multinational apparel manufacturer. HAH is publicly listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange and currently has 10 directly operated manufacturing facilities in Sri Lanka and Africa. HIH will use the IFC Loan to finance the long-term working capital requirement of the Hela Group and support the growth of its manufacturing operations.
sponsor_shareholders: Hela Investment Holdings Ltd is the Mauritian indirect and wholly owned subsidiary of Hela Apparel Holdings PLC, who will serve as the Project Sponsor. HIH will serve as the borrower of the IFC Loan. HAH is listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange (HELA.N0000).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated project cost is US$40.0 million, of which IFC will be financing up to US$20.0 million via an A Loan.
location_description: The Project will provide long-term working capital finance to HIH to support the continued growth of its operations in Kenya, Egypt, and Sri Lanka. The Hela Group’s Kenyan manufacturing facility is located in an Export Processing Zone in Athi-River, close to Nairobi, while its Egyptian operation is situated in the Alexandria Governorate, an area with a well-established skill base in apparel manufacturing that also hosts one of Egypt’s largest ports. The Hela Group operates 6 manufacturing facilities in Sri Lanka and its facility located in the Mawathagama Export Processing Zone will be the primary beneficiary of the IFC loan.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the preservation and generation of direct and indirect employment, the increase in value addition, and the improvement in manufacturing skills in Kenya, Egypt, and Sri Lanka. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to strengthen the resilience of key nodes of the global apparel industry in the verticals where the Hela Group is active.
additionality: Financial Additionality - Financing structure: IFC will provide a long-term loan with a grace period that is not readily available to the Hela Group either in Sri Lanka, due to the foreign currency shortages that the Sri Lankan lenders have been facing, particularly since March 2022, or in the local markets (Kenya and Egypt). The IFC Loan will also improve the Company’s debt profile and strengthen the assets base of HIH, which will enable the latter to autonomously access outside complementary capital, thus reducing its vulnerability to financial and banking shocks. Non-Financial Additionality - Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: During project supervision, IFC will provide technical expertise to improve overall E&S performance as well as introduce the international best practices to the Hela Group. Additionally, the Hela Group will be participating in an advisory package that is being prepared by the Gender Team and intends to bring together projects across leadership, employment, and access to assets for women entrepreneurs over a period of 4-5 years.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of up to US$35 million senior loan package to Maziwa and its subsidiaries (Pearl Dairy Farms Ltd or “PDFL” and Musty Distribution Limited or “Musty”, together “Pearl Dairy” or “the Company”) to finance the Company’s (i) capacity expansion plans in Uganda and in Kenya (US$ 21 million) including the upgrade and capacity increase of the powder milk plant in Uganda, and the acquisition of a packing plant in Kenya, and (ii) refinancing of existing Standard Chartered Bank loan in Uganda (US$ 14 million) (the “Project”). Pearl Dairy was established in 2009 in Uganda. Pearl Dairy’s product portfolio includes UHT milks, powder milks, flavored milks, yoghurts, butter, honey and more. The Company supplies its local market as well as most of East Africa. As of October 2022, the group employs c. 1,226 people (directly and through 3rd party), sources milk from over 15,000 farmers (2/3 in Uganda, 1/3 in Kenya) and distributes across the continent to retailers, wholesalers and end-consumers through 80 sales points in 2 operating countries.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded in Uganda by Mr. Kotecha and Mr. Kapoor, long-experienced businessmen in the region. In 2019, TPG Rise Fund, an impact Private Equity fund managed by global asset manager TPG, became a shareholder alongside the founders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, together with FMO, will provide a US$ 35 million long-term loan package to support the project. The project is expected to be supported by GAFSP, as described in the Blended Finance Section.
location_description: The Company’s operations are located in Western Uganda and Western Kenya.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to increase dairy productivity and smallholder farmers’ access to raw milk market in Uganda and Kenya. The Project will also contribute to food security by increasing the volume of dairy products sold to consumers. At the market level, the Project will help to strengthen the resilience of the dairy sector in the two countries by building capacity in dairy supply chain to withstand macro shocks and stresses related to droughts.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality comes from the provision of long-term financing. Non-financial additionality comes from the support to the Company on operational and strategic matters, and from the dairy farmer engagement program by IFC Advisory services.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a common equity investment of up to BRL160 million in Alvoar Lacteos (“Alvoar” or the “Company”), to support the Company’s expansion program, which includes the installation of new equipment, renovation of existing industrial units, construction of a new unit for cheese production and E&S improvements. Founded in January 2022, Alvoar is the company resulting from the merger of Betania Lacteos S.A. (“Betania”), a leading dairy producer in the Northeast of Brazil, and Embare Indústrias Alimentícias S.A. (“Embare”), a dairy producer with a strong industrial presence in the Midwest of Brazil.
sponsor_shareholders: Alvoar’s main shareholders are the Girao, Antunes and Schmidt families, and Arlon Group, a financial investment firm.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at BRL160 million of which IFC will contribute with BRL160 million.
location_description: Alvoar owns and manages industrial facilities in the Midwest and Northeast regions of Brazil.
development_impact: Project Outcome: Stakeholders - Consumers: Increased access to hygienically packed dairy products. Contribution to Market Creation: Resilience - Triggering new product offerings and supporting greater domestic value addition. IFC expects the Project to contribute to sustaining the resilience of the global food supply market by facilitating increased milk production and distribution in underserved areas of Brazil, a net importer of dairy products.
additionality: Financial additionality Financing structure: The proposed project consists of a common equity investment to support the Company’s expansion program, which includes the installation of new equipment, renovation of existing industrial units, construction of a new unit for cheese production and E&S improvements. Non-financial additionality Standard setting: IFC will support Alvoar to improve its environmental and social standards and streamline the Company’s operations to comply with IFC standards and industry best practices.

project_description: IFC is supporting Drenik ND d.o.o. (Drenik) in (i) developing the largest captive biomass power plant in Serbia to ensure stable energy supply for Drenik’s plant in Serbia and to materially reduce its CO2 footprint; (ii) refinancing its existing debt; and (iii) financing its permanent working capital needs (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Drenik, established in 1996 in Serbia, is a major tissue paper producer and distributor in the Western Balkans with production plants in Serbia and Hungary. It is fully owned by Mr. Igor Peric, a Serbian entrepreneur.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at over €100 million. The proposed IFC investment is comprised of an up to €60 million A Loan and an up to $50m equivalent in € MCPP Trust Loan to partially finance the Project.
location_description: Investments under the Project are planned to be made in Drenik’s plant located in Belgrade, Serbia.
development_impact: The most significant Project-level development outcomes are environmental effects through improved resource efficiency and greenhouse gas emissions reduction as a result of the biomass power plant. Beyond these outcomes, IFC expects that the Project will promote competitiveness in the paper and pulp industry, by generating demonstration effects to other players, and incentivizing companies to adopt strategies to lower their costs of energy.
additionality: IFC will provide long-term financing with a 10-year tenor not available from local banks. The A Loan will be complemented by the MCPP Trust Loan, which mobilization would be unlikely in the absence of IFC. IFC will also provide non-financial additionality by helping Drenik elevate its financial reporting, energy efficiency, corporate governance, and environmental and social standards.

sector: Household Textile Products (Including Drapes, Mattress Covers, Carpets, Towels, etc.)
project_description: Himatsingka Seide Limited (“HSL” or the “Company”) is one of the leading vertically integrated home textile manufacturing companies that designs, develops, manufactures and distributes a suite of home textile products. IFC is proposing a financing package of up to US$69 million equivalent to HSL. The proposed investment would be used towards (i) refinancing HSL’s existing long-term debt of approximately US$51.6 million, (ii) capital expenditure of approximately US$5.2 million towards debottlenecking of HSL’s terry towel capacity and (iii) approximately US$12.2 million towards corporate decarbonization exercise, (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded in 1985 by Dinesh Kumar Himatsingka. It is currently listed on both Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange. The majority ownership of HSL is with the Himatsingka family (“the Sponsors”) with about 48% shareholding, and the balance is held by public and institutional shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is approximately US$85 million. IFC will provide a financing package of upto US$69 million equivalent. The financing package will include (i) INR denominated Non-Convertible Debenture (NCD) of up to INR 4,600 million (approximately US$56.5 million) and (ii) and Foreign Currency Convertible Bond (FCCB) of up to US$12.50 million.
location_description: HSL will use the IFC funding for its operations in Hassan and Doddaballapur, both in the state of Karnataka, India.
development_impact: The Project will contribute to India’s GDP, both directly and indirectly through effects in the value chains (warehousing and logistics, cleaning, maintenance, design, R&D, marketing, mechanical and electrical engineering). The investment is also expected to create approximately 100 full time direct jobs in a formal setting, while indirect and induced employment will be created in the home textiles value chain. Additionally, the Project will enable decarbonizing the client’s steam and electricity generation processes, signaling to other market players the commercial feasibility of a low-carbon pathway in the Indian textile industry.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via financing structure (long-term financing that is not otherwise available). Non-financial additionality is provided via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building as well as standards setting to strengthen the Company’s environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices.

project_description: The proposed project involvesIFC investing INR 2,250 million (equivalent of approximately US$27.4 million) in mid-income and senior living residential projects developed by Ashiana Housing Limited (Ashiana or the Company) in India.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1979, by Late Om Prakash Gupta, Ashiana, is a well reputed real estate company having delivered over 23 million sq.ft. and over 15,000 units across affordable / mid-income housing segments. The Company is listed on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange ( BSE). The Company is currently managed by Mr. Om Prakash Gupta's sons, Vishal Gupta, Ankur Gupta and Varun Gupta (Sponsors) who collectively own 61%. As of December 2022, the Company has on-going projects, with 5.6 million sq ft of saleable area in 7 cities across India, including Jaipur, Jamshedpur, Gurugram, Bhiwadi and Chennai. In March 2018, IFC had committed INR1,500 million (~US$21 million at the time) to invest alongside Ashiana to develop affordable / mid-income housing and senior living housing in India. This has been almost fully disbursed towards projects in Jaipur, Gurugram and Chennai.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated to be about US$343 million and IFC's investment will be in the form of INR denominated Non Convertible Debentures.
location_description: Projects are expected to be located across various cities in India, including Jaipur (Rajasthan), Gurugram (NCR), Pune (Maharashtra) and Chennai (Tamil Nadu).
development_impact: The project’s most significant expected outcome is increased access to middle-income housing, particularly for senior citizens, addressing India’s growing need for quality housing driven by demographic shifts and urbanization. Despite this demand, the senior living housing market remains nascent, constrained by challenges such as limited understanding of development and financial viability, higher costs due to medical care and other amenities, and a lack of sector-specific incentives. Similarly, middle-income housing supply has been bottlenecked by bankruptcies among developers following tightened regulatory controls in 2016, leading to stalled construction in recent years. This project will add new units of senior and middle-income housing across various cities, aiming to improve living standards and alleviate critical housing shortages. Beyond the immediate project outcome, the Project is expected to promote competitiveness in the mid-income housing segment, especially in the senior housing class. AHL is the first mover in the senior housing segment, and the success of the Project across different tier 2 cities in India will strongly demonstrate financial viability of senior living housing at scale and in diversified locations across the country, as the existing small supply is concentrated in Southern parts of India. The Project will help in setting standards for senior friendly project designs and amenities and will attract other investors and developers to enter this market segment.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via provision of IFC's own account equity, long-term financing not readily available in the market. Non-financial additionality is provided via capacity-building by supporting the greening of its funded projects. Financial Additionality - IFC's Own Account Equity: Long-term equity capital is not readily available for housing developers in India. It is estimated that India's residential real estate market is expected to see a net annual capital shortfall of US$5 bn over the next 4-5 years. The Banks cannot lend for purchasing land due to regulatory constraints and NBFC financing to the sector has also reduced in recent years due to portfolio stress and liquidity issues. IFC is one of the few institutions providing long term patient capital to developers of affordable/mid-income housing. IFC's provision of equity capital at reasonable terms will enable Ashiana to increase housing supply at mid-income price points. In addition, IFC's continued support of the sector will promote investor confidence, in a sector where private capital finance is inadequate. Non-financial Additionality - Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will utilize its global expertise in Green Buildings for Ashiana to obtain green building certification for all units built under the Project. IFC will offer valuable inputs in the areas of energy, water and materials efficiency, helping reduce the greenhouse gas emissions of the housing sector.

project_description: Due to current status of Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves, private companies in Pakistan are facing challenges in securing US$ denominated letters of credit (LCs) to import essential raw materials and equipment for ongoing operations. Many companies are operating at reduced capacities and foreseeing shutdowns due to lack of inputs for production, which could lead to large scale job losses across industries in Pakistan. To address this critical and urgent issue, IFC proposes to make available an up to US$500 million (mn) in debt financing to select companies (the “Borrowers” or the “Corporates”) to finance their critical imports and related US$ expenses (the “Project”) required for business continuity. The Project is sector agnostic and individual borrowers are expected to be top tier companies with leading market position in their respective sectors and strong credit standing.
sponsor_shareholders: Borrower’s name and further details will be provided for each Borrower through Borrowers’ specific SII.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering arranging an up to US$500 million financing package, of which up to US$250 million will be for IFC’s own account and remaining amount will be mobilized from other development finance institutions.
location_description: Project will be located in Pakistan
development_impact: Implementation of the Project is expected to facilitate Borrowers’ access to US$-denominated funding, which will allow them to sustain their business operations and preserve direct and indirect jobs in their operations as well as in their value chains. The Project will support the resilience of the private sector in Pakistan.
additionality: IFC will play a counter-cyclical role as it is in a unique position to finance and mobilize US$ financing at a critical time. The Project will send a strong signal to the market and serve as a catalyst in mobilizing additional resources to support the private sector of Pakistan amid heightened macro risks.

project_description: The Project is an investment to support Redefine Properties Ltd. (Redefine or the Company), a South African-based REIT operating in the commercial, retail, and industrial property sectors. IFC will support the Company with a subscription of up to 750 million South African rand (about US$44.1 million) of its inaugural green bond issuance. The investment will help the Company finance retrofits, renovations, and other building improvements in its portfolio to make them environmentally sustainable, improve resource efficiency, and adopt environmentally sound technologies, in line with Redefine’s commitment to ensure that its debt is sustainably refinanced, and all its buildings are net zero carbon, water, and / or waste by 2050 (the Project). IFC’s investment is classified as 100 percent climate-related finance as it will be used exclusively on buildings with at least a Green Star 4 category certification (according to the Green Building Council of South Africa), or equivalent.
sponsor_shareholders: Redefine Properties Ltd - is a real estate investment trust (REIT) based in South Africa, focusing on developing and operating a portfolio of high-quality commercial property assets across retail, office, industrial, and specialized segments. Founded in 1999, Redefine is the second largest REIT listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE). Redefine’s shareholding is diversified, with entities with more than a 5 percent stake accounting for less than a 30 percent combined stake. The Company’s shares are traded on the JSE with a free float of 95 percent.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: On September 21, 2022, IFC invested ZAR750 million (about US$44.1 million) in Redefine’s maiden “use of proceeds” unsecured green bond issued under its ZAR30billion Domestic Medium Term Note program. The green bond included issuances of unsecured floating rate notes in multiple tenors, including a three-year, seven-year, and ten-year tenor. IFC participated in the issuance as an anchor bidder and received allocation in the seven- and ten-year notes. The bonds will be listed on the Johannesburg stock exchange. The green bond was oversubscribed and raised ZAR1.5 billion.
location_description: The Project will focus on greening of properties in South Africa.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are (i) increased access to grade A office space; and (ii) environmental effects through a reduction in energy and water consumption. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote financial integration through demonstration and competition channels.
additionality: IFC’s involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide a longer tenor (7 years or longer) local currency long-term financing, which is not readily available in the local market. Because the Company develops very-long term assets, obtaining funding with the appropriate tenor is essential to mitigate macroeconomic shocks and incentivize investment in durable quality assets. Furthermore, this is only the second green bond being issued in the country by a REIT, so its success will have a significant signaling effect on the market, specifically helping to crowd-in institutional investors to long term climate-focused financing for South Africa, a country which is looking aspiring to decarbonize, and reduce the impact of climate change on its economy. Non-financial additionality is delivered through knowledge, innovation, and capacity building. IFC’s expertise is instrumental in ensuring that the market views the proposed bond issuance as a genuinely “green” bond. IFC will develop a set of proceeds utilization conditions to ensure this, expecting the standards to be used by other REITs and corporates in the country.

project_description: IFC’s proposed investment is up to US$100 million to participate in a broader US$300 million syndicated secured revolving credit facility (the Revolving Credit Facility“ or “RCF”) to Westfalia Fruit International Limited (“WFIL” or the “Company” or “Westfalia”). The Company grows, sources, ripens, packs, processes and markets sustainably grown avocados all year round, and is a leading multinational supplier of fresh subtropical fruits and related processed products to Asia, Europe, the UK and the US. The proposed investment will support the Company’s US$300 million investment program comprising the following components: (i) investments in new facilities and in new markets such as China, India, Italy, Kenya, Spain, Tanzania and the US, with the investments in countries such as Italy, Spain and the US being part of the push-pull strategy to service production in developing countries; (ii) expansion of existing facilities mainly in Europe, South Africa and South America; (iii) expansion and maintenance of orchards and nurseries in key primary production areas (Colombia, India, Mozambique, South Africa, Mexico and Peru); and (iv) working capital.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a subsidiary of Hans Merensky Holdings (Proprietary) Limited (HMH), an existing IFC client (IFC/R2012-0367). HMH is a South African vertically integrated fruit and forestry business with a global footprint that is involved in farming, processing, and marketing of timber and fruits. HMH is owned by the Hans Merensky Foundation (40.02 percent), the Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) of South Africa (29.7 percent) and IFC (20 percent). The remaining shareholders are three Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (BBBEE) organizations namely Vuka Forestry Holdings (Vuka) (4.03 percent), Women Investment Portfolio Holdings (3.30 percent), and HMH Employee Share Ownership Plan (2.95 percent). HMH fully owns Westfalia Fruit (Pty) Ltd, which in turn owns 67.8% stake in WFIL. Other WFIL shareholders are: Caltha LLC (formerly Harvard University Foundation) (21.6%) and Inversiones Agroindustriales Limitada (10.6%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project will support WFIL’s US$300 million investment program comprised of: (i) planned acquisitions and investments in new facilities and in new markets such as Kenya, Tanzania, China, India, Italy, Spain, and the US, with the investments in countries such as Italy, Spain and the US being part of the push-pull strategy to service production in developing countries; (ii) expansion of existing facilities mainly in Europe, South Africa and South America; (iii) expansion and maintenance of orchards and nurseries in key primary production areas (Colombia, India, Mozambique, South Africa, Mexico and Peru); and (iv) working capital. IFC is looking to provide an own account A Loan of up to US$100 million in US dollars or Euros.
location_description: The proposed investment will support the Company’s capacity expansion and operational improvements in China, Colombia, India, Italy, Kenya, Mexico, Mozambique, Peru, South Africa, Spain, Tanzania and the US.
development_impact: Project Level impact: The Project is expected to: (i) Increase farmer outreach as a result of expanding avocado operations in Colombia and Mozambique and setting up greenfield avocado operations in India. (ii) Create additional employment and retain existing jobs in Colombia, India, and other project countries. Market level impact: The Project is expected to: (i) Increase competitiveness of the avocado sectors in the project countries, through demonstration effects and capacity building, as well as integrate them to the global value chain.
additionality: Financial Additionality: (i) Financing structure: IFC's proposed financing has a three-year with the option to extend by an extra year on two consecutive years. This structure is not readily available in the market. Non-financial Additionality: (i) Standard setting: IFC's engagement will support the Company in the implementation of good Environmental and Social (E&S) practices and its commitment to sustainable operations. (ii) Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC will provide the Company with country knowledge as it expand to new markets and advisory services on water efficiency measures for its facilities in South Africa.

project_description: Proposed investment is for a Sustainability Linked Loan to subsidiaries of X-Press Feeders Limited (XPF or the Company) for the purchase of three 7,000 TEU new-build container ships. Established in 1972, XPF is the largest independent feeder carrier. The Company operates a fleet of 111 vessels of which 56 are XPF owned. XPF currently runs 83 services across 183 ports in 71 countries across Asia, Middle East, Africa, the Americas, and Northern Europe. The three project vessels are expected to be commissioned in 2023 and 2024, will be registered under Singapore flag state and will be managed, operated, and crewed by XPF's subsidiary company Eastaway Ship Management Pte Limited (Eastaway).
sponsor_shareholders: The IFC financed Project Vessels are expected to be fully owned by XPF. XPF is privately held and 100 percent owned by Mr. Timothy Hartnoll.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project Vessels are expected to cost US$234 million, of which US$163 million is expected to be financed by debt in the form of a Sustainability Linked Loan from IFC and other financial institutions mobilized by IFC.
location_description: The IFC financed vessels are expected to be deployed on the China-India route.
development_impact: The investment is expected to support XPF's strategy to reduce GHG emissions across its operations. The IFC financed Project Vessels are expected to be more energy efficient and are expected to replace the older vessels in XPF's fleet. In addition to the IFC financed Project Vessels, and as part of the SLL, XPF will commit to reducing carbon emissions from its entire fleet, as well as reducing the use of plastics aboard its vessels. The Project is expected to help build momentum for the use of sustainable finance to accelerate the decarbonization of the maritime shipping industry.
additionality: IFC, as the lead arranger for the proposed loan, would be providing long term financing that is critical for XPF's large fleet renewal plan and would help diversify XPF's sources of financing at a time when the shipping sector is facing headwinds. In addition, IFC is expected to leverage its experience in sustainable finance to help XPF structure its first Sustainability-Linked Loan (SLL) and develop a sustainable finance framework. IFC is also expected to support XPF in upgrading procedures to help strengthen the Company's capacity to manage environmental and social risks, including along gender aspects, in accordance with IFC Performance Standards.

project_description: Ford Otomotiv Sanayi A.S. (Otosan or the Company) is a leading automotive manufacturer and is an existing IFC client. The proposed IFC investment is up to EUR150 million in 2022 and up to EUR90 million in 2023 to partially fund Otosan’s multi-year, €1.0 billion electric vehicle investment program, including the production of its new Ford Transit Custom commercial vehicle, a one-ton, medium-sized electric vehicle manufactured at the Yeniköy plant in Türkiye (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Currently, 18% of the Company's shares are publicly listed in Borsa Istanbul, while the remaining 82% is owned jointly by Koc Holding A.S. (“Koc Holding”) and Ford Motor Company (“Ford”). Koc Holding is majority owned by the Koc family of Turkey and the remaining shares (c. 26%) of Koc Holding are publicly listed. Koc Holding is the leading industrial conglomerate of Turkey, mainly engaged in five sectors namely, energy, automotive, consumer durables, and finance.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project which forms part of the Company’s multi-year investment program is estimated to cost around EUR1.0 billion. The proposed IFC investment are two A Loans of up to EUR150 million in 2022 and up to EUR90 million in 2023.
location_description: The Project is located in Kocaeli, Turkey.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good, based on an AIMM score of 58. On an unadjusted basis (i.e., without a likelihood factor), the full potential AIMM score could reach 64. The most significant project-level outcomes are expected to be: (i) economy-wide effects through value addition, an increase in exports, and employment creation; and (ii) stakeholder benefits through skill building and training for employees. Beyond the project-level outcomes, IFC anticipates that the Project will promote integration by introducing novel know-how in Türkiye’s automotive industry through higher value-added and more complex manufacturing processes. The Project is also expected to improve the country’s position in the GVCs.
additionality: Additionality: The main additionality of IFC is twofold: (i) IFC’s countercyclical role in Türkiye’s current volatile market environment where liquidity is strained. The IFC financing will enable Otosan to better manage its funding risk by ensuring tenor and currency match between its funding base and operations; and (ii) IFC’s reassessment of the Company’s E&S policies and practices in detail is expected to improve such policies and practices to international standards, particularly concerning contractors and supply chain management.

project_description: The proposed project is an equity investment of up to US$25 million in Ather Energy Private Limited (“Ather Energy”), a private limited company domiciles in India. Ather Energy is India’s leading electric two-wheeler manufacturer. Ather is the first Indian EV manufacturer to design its own vehicle from scratch and has a strong control over its value chain, ranging from R&D and design to manufacturing and services. Between January to December 2022, Ather sold ~59K vehicles, registering a 224% growth yoy.
sponsor_shareholders: Ather Energy was founded by Tarun Mehta (who currently serves as the Chief Executive Officer) and Swapnil Jain (who serves as the Chief Technology Officer) in 2013.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is an equity investment of up to US$25 million in Ather Energy Private Limited.
location_description: India
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase access to high quality and affordable electric two-wheelers in India, particularly in Tier II and Tier III cities, through scaling the company's production and distribution network. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC’s investment will contribute to market creation by supporting the alleviation of critical ecosystem obstacles as part of the programmatic approach and promote the production and distribution of E-2Ws through reaching scale in the Company’s distribution networks, as well as via demonstration and replication effects by other competitors.
additionality: IFC's Additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial by providing (i) patient equity in India where venture capital (VC) availability is abundant yet remains limited for EV startups; (ii) standard setting through alignment with IFC Performance Standards and international good practices, and (iii) knowledge, innovation, and capacity building since IFC can provide valuable knowledge by leveraging WBG’s expertise in the EV sector.

project_description: The IFC project is a ZAR1.0 billion (about US$54.5 million) investment in unsecured green bonds issued by Growthpoint Properties Ltd. (Growthpoint or the Company or the Group). Growthpoint is South Africa’s largest REIT listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, with total property assets of US$9.9 billion (ZAR160.8 billion) as of June 30, 2022. It operates in the commercial, retail, and industrial property sectors, and has operations across South Africa, Australia, Central and Eastern Europe, and the United Kingdom. The investment will support Growthpoint to (i) finance energy efficiency projects and renewable energy use across the Growthpoint portfolio; (ii) finance new green buildings; and/or (iii) refinance debt used to construct recently completed green buildings. The green bond issuances are a key part of Growthpoint's sustainability strategy and are aligned with its commitment to ensuring that all its portfolio buildings are carbon neutral by 2050. IFC investment is expected to be classified as 100 percent climate related as it will be used exclusively on buildings with at least Green Star 4 category certification (according to the Green Building Council of South Africa), or equivalent.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1987, Growthpoint Properties Ltd. (Growthpoint) is South Africa’s largest REIT, listed on the JSE with a market capitalization of US$2.6 billion (ZAR42.4 billion) as of June 30, 2022. Growthpoint owns and manages a diversified property portfolio valued at US$9.9 billion (ZAR160.8 billion) as of June 30 2022. The portfolio is also diversified across geography and sub-sectors, that is retail, office and industrial properties. Growthpoint’s portfolio comprised of the following: a) South Africa: (i) 408 directly owned properties in South Africa; (ii) a 50.0 percent interest in the V&A Waterfront, an iconic mixed-use development in Cape Town, South Africa; and (iii) a majority stake interest in Growthpoint Healthcare Property Holdings Ltd (“GHPH”), South Africa’s first healthcare Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT); (iv) 16.6 percent interest in Growthpoint Student Accommodation Holdings, which owns 7 student accommodation properties and 2 properties under development. b) Australia: a 62.2 percent interest in Growthpoint Properties Australia Limited, which owns 58 properties and is listed at the Australia Stock Exchange. c) Eastern Europe: a 29.4 percent interest in Globalworth Real Estate Investment Limited, which owns 71 properties in Poland and Romania. d) United Kingdom: a 60.8 percent interest in Capital & Regional Plc, which owns 6 properties e) Sub-Saharan Africa (ex-South Africa): a 16.3 percent interest in Lango Real Estate Limited (formerly Growthpoint Investec African Properties Fund), which owns 8 properties and 3 plots of land. Growthpoint’s shareholding is diversified, with entities with more than a 5 percent stake accounting for less than a 20 percent combined stake.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: On December 13, 2022, IFC invested ZAR1.0 billion (about US$54.5 million) as a sole investor in a privately issued green bond by Growthpoint. The green bond issuances were done under Growthpoint’s existing ZAR30 billion (US$1.76 billion equivalent) Domestic Medium-Term Note (DMTN) program which is registered at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. IFC investment was into unsecured floating rate notes with 7- and 10-year tenors that will be listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE).
location_description: The Project will focus on properties located in South Africa.
development_impact: The expected project-level outcomes are (i) environmental effects through a reduction in energy and water consumption, and (ii) increased access to grade-A office space and retail space. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote market sustainability through demonstration effects and by making other industry players follow to maintain competitiveness.
additionality: IFC's involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided through a longer-tenor local currency financing, which is not readily available in the local market. Since the Company develops long-term assets, obtaining funding with the appropriate tenor is essential. The proceeds will be used for the refinance of a green building within Growthpoint and the finance of other green eligible projects. IFC will also support Growthpoint in its ongoing work on developing a green bond framework, including adherence to South Africa's green finance taxonomy.

company_name: ASSAN ALUMINYUM SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Assan Aluminyum San. ve Tic. A.S. (Assan or the Company), established in 1988, is the largest manufacturer of aluminum flat-rolled products in Türkiye. The Company has launched a multi-year investment program with an estimated cost of US$130 million over a period of 2022-2024. The program, delayed due to the spillover effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, will modernize Assan’s operations, reduce carbon footprint, and expand processing capacity for flat rolled aluminum products and scrap by 60,000 tons per annum. It will also address the changing demand profile in its target markets post pandemic and eliminate imports of semifinished products. IFC will be partially advising and financing this program with a senior loan in form of an A Loan up to US$90 million that potentially will be structured as a Green Loan (the IFC Loan).
sponsor_shareholders: Kibar Holding A.S. (Kibar Holding) owns 95.5% of Assan while the remaining shareholding is owned by another company owned by the Sponsor (Assan Gayrimenkul Gelistirme ve Yatirim A.S.). Kibar Holding is wholly owned by members of the Kibar family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering an A Loan at an amount of up to US$90 million for IFC’s own account under the COVID-19 Crisis Response Facility. The Project was delayed due to the COVID-19 outbreak and can be only initiated by end of 2021. The remaining Project cost will be financed by the Company’s internal cash generation.
location_description: The Project locations are in the two plants of Assan in Türkiye: The first plant is in Tuzla/Istanbul while the second plant is in Dilovasi/Kocaeli.
development_impact: Through the capacity expansion (processing capacity increase for ingots and scrap by 60,000 tons per annum) and increase in exports, the Project will support higher value-addition and employment creation for the Turkish economy. Furthermore, by implementing measures to improve production efficiency, the success of the Project will incentivize Assan’s competitors and other players in the market to upgrade the efficiency of their operations and improve production capacity.
additionality: Provision of long-term financing: IFC will provide long-term financing which is difficult to procure in the local market for the proposed amount and tenor. Non-Financial Additionality: E&S capacity building and green loan financing framework development.
Company Name: ASSAN ALUMINYUM SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

company_name: AFRICA CONSERVATION AND COMMUNITIES TOURISM FUND, SCSP SICAV-RAIF
project_description: The Africa Conservation & Communities Tourism Fund, SCSp SICAV – RAIF (“ACCT” or the “Fund”) was established in 2021 as a structured debt vehicle providing loans to ecotourism businesses (safari operators, camps, lodges, hotels, etc.) in conservation areas in sub-Saharan Africa (the “Project”). ACCT is raising up to US$75m. The Fund is structured using a blended finance approach with three tranches of capital: a junior tranche, a senior tranche and a grant tranche. The ACCT Fund is a response to conservation threats resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic, with the specific aim of alleviating financial stress in the short to mid-term of well-managed conservation tourism businesses and increasing the conservation and community outcomes delivered by these businesses. As the impact of COVID-19 reduces, the ACCT Fund will also look at supporting operators who can catalyze significant financial flows to conservation activity in unutilized, or underutilized, ecologically important natural landscapes, to the benefit of the wildlife and communities who depend on them.
sponsor_shareholders: In addition to US$20m senior tranche capital seeded and committed by anchor investor The Nature Conservancy (TNC), the world’s largest conservation NGO, US$28.2m junior tranche capital committed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (“BMZ”) through KfW, US$2.0m grant capital committed by USAID, ACCT will have multiple investors and stakeholders, including IFC. The affairs of the Fund are managed and controlled by ThirdWay Conservation Partners I GP, S.à r.l. (“ThirdWay Conservation Partners”), who serves as general partner, and has appointed Innpact Fund Management S.A to act as the Fund’s external alternative investment fund manager (“External AIFM”). ThirdWay Conservation Partners is part of the ThirdWay Partners group of companies (“TWP”), an advisory and asset management firm focused on sustainable development with a track record in Africa. Founded in 2014, TWP has 3 core offerings, namely impact consulting and corporate finance as part of its advisory team, as well as asset management. The firm is made up of 30+ dedicated team spread across their offices in London, Madrid, Maputo, Nairobi and Johannesburg. TWP has advised on US$1billion plus of transactions over 50 advisory mandates. Across its Group, TWP currently manages or advises 3 investment vehicles, including the ACCT Fund.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: ACCT’s target is to raise a total of ~US$75m by the end of February 2023 to execute the Project. IFC proposes an investment of up to US$14m in the senior tranche of the Fund.
location_description: ACCT is a Luxembourg based fund, investing in sub-Saharan Africa.
development_impact: The project will improve conservation management activities for protected areas and deliver socio-economic impacts including job preservation in the conservation tourism sector and its supply chain. IFC expects that the success of the Project could help boost investor confidence, potentially scaling the availability of finance for projects in the conservation tourism sector through attracting new funds and investors.
additionality: The proposed financing structure will help strengthen the capital structure of the Fund. Funding in the target countries is not as readily available as local banks have become more risk averse in the face of the pandemic shock. IFC funding will help improve the risk profile of the Fund and crowd in private capital needed to finance and execute the Fund’s business plan. IFC’s investment in the ACCT Fund alongside other investors is expected to send a strong signal of confidence to other private institutional investors seeking to participate in the Fund and will be crucial in assisting the Fund to achieve viable close and size of at least US$70 million.1 Investor risk perception for sub-Saharan Africa continues to remain high with the region’s largest economies recently emerging from a protracted period of slow growth and policy uncertainty. Under these conditions, IFC’s support of the ACCT Fund is expected to improve the risk perception of both international and local investors, providing them with the comfort needed to participate in the Fund and assisting the Fund Managers in attracting more institutional capital.
Company Name: AFRICA CONSERVATION AND COMMUNITIES TOURISM FUND, SCSP SICAV-RAIF

project_description: IFC is considering an equity investment for the acquisition of up to 10% of ordinary shares of PAC Doverie A.D. (Doverie or the Company), the largest pension management company in Bulgaria. The investment will be in the form of a purchase of secondary shares from ATBIH GMBH, a 100% owned subsidiary of the Sponsor, VIENNA INSURANCE GROUP AG Wiener Versicherung Gruppe (VIG or the Sponsor).
sponsor_shareholders: Doverie is the largest PAC in Bulgaria with EUR 2.3 billion of assets under management as of June 30, 2022, servicing more than 1.2 million members in the country. The Company operates an extensive network of 61 branch offices and employs 343 staff. Doverie has its own sales network of approx. 200 sales people and additionally cooperates with more than 1,500 external sales agents and extensive third party distribution network. The Company is majority owned by VIG with a 92.6% ownership stake, while 6.8% is owned by the country’s largest confederation of trade unions (CITUB). VIG is the largest insurance group in Austria and one of the leading insurance groups in the CEE with more than 50 insurance companies in 30 countries. VIG is rated A+/stable by S&P as of December 2022 reflecting the Group’s strong capitalization, profitability, market position and liquidity. VIG’s principal shareholder is a mutual fund Wiener Städtische Wechselseitiger Versicherungsverein - Vermögensverwaltung - Vienna Insurance Group with approx. 72% shareholding while approx. 28% are freely floated on the Vienna, Prague and Budapest Stock Exchanges.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will purchase up to 10% of ordinary shares of the Company directly from ATBIH.
location_description: The Company is located in Sofia, Bulgaria.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is increased access to pension savings via an increase in the number of participants in the Company’s Voluntary Pension Fund (VPF) and an increase in VPF member contributions, brough about by the introduction of new digital marketing channels. Beyond the project-level outcomes, IFC anticipates that the Project will increase the competitiveness of the pension market by driving innovation and replication by pension companies in Bulgaria using digital channels to increase their memberships and active VPF member contributions.
additionality: IFC’s expected additionality in the project relates to: i) Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building, as IFC will use its global experience and know-how to support the Company in its digitalization efforts over the next five years, and ii) Non-commercial risk mitigation, as IFC’s presence in the market will help maintain an industry-supportive regulatory environment and support the future development of the second pillar.

project_description: OCP SA (“OCP” or the “Company”, https://www.ocpgroup.ma/ ) and/or its wholly owned subsidiary, OCP Green Energy SA, plan to design, install and operate four greenfield, captive solar power plants at two of the Company’s phosphate mines in central Morocco, with a cumulative installed capacity of 202 MWp (the “Project”). The plants will supply OCP’s mines with green electricity during daytime hours.
sponsor_shareholders: OCP SA, a state-owned enterprise, is a fully integrated phosphate fertilizer producer with operations at every stage from mining to processing to sales of phosphate products. The Company is the largest producer and exporter of phosphate rock and phosphoric acid globally.
