OCP’s shareholders are the Moroccan State and other minority shareholders with, respectively, 94.1% and 5.9% ownership. As part of its sustainability strategy, OCP plans to become carbon neutral by 2040. The Company has increased the share of clean sources in its total energy consumption from 30% in 2017 to 43% in 2021. Within the electricity segment, OCP sourced 87% of its electricity from clean sources in 2021 (cogeneration – 76%; and wind – 11%), while 13% was supplied by ONEE via the national grid. OCP plans to source 100% of its electricity needs through wind, solar (including battery storage) and cogeneration by 2030. The Project will be implemented by OCP and/or OCP Green Energy SA. OCP Green Energy SA was established in 2022 to develop the Company’s renewable energy generation activities.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at €159.2 million. The proposed IFC investment comprises a senior Green Loan of up to €100 million to the Company.
location_description: The four captive solar power plants will be installed on lands owned by the Company in Benguerir and Khouribga.
development_impact: The Project is expected to: (i) reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by an estimated 285,000 tCO2e per annum and provide a cleaner and more affordable source of electricity than can be currently sourced from the national electrical utility, ONEE; (ii) contribute to market competitiveness by increasing production of low-carbon fertilizers; and (iii) contribute to the resilience of Morocco’s electricity sector by diversifying the sources of power generation.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the Project is in the form of: (i) financing structure, (ii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building, and (iii) E&S standard setting.

project_description: The proposed project involves the second renewal of the existing two funded risk sharing facility with Standard Chartered Bank (the “Bank” or “SCB”) for two trade finance facilities of up to US$234 million to support ETC Group (“ETG”) agri commodity trader’s export of cash and food grains, storage, and import of fertilizers in Sub-Saharan Africa. IFC’s investment amount will be up to US$40 million. The Project will support the purchase, storage and sales of agri commodities and fertilizers in SSA countries such as Malawi, Benin, Kenya, Tanzania, etc. Commodities financed by the project are bought from mostly smallholder farmers in SSA and sold to wholesalers, cooperatives, NGOs and governments in various IDA countries and into the international market.
sponsor_shareholders: Standard Chartered Bank: Headquartered in London, Standard Chartered is a leading international banking group, with more than 86,000 employees, representing 130 nationalities and a 150-year history in some of the world’s most dynamic markets. It is one of the world's most international banks, with over 1,000 branches, offices and outlets in 60 countries across the globe. The group earns around 90% of its income and profits in Asia, Africa and the Middle East across Corporate, Institutional and Retail banking. As of December 31, 2021, Standard Chartered had total assets of US$ 828 billion, and net profit of US$2.3 billion. Standard Chartered PLC is listed on the London and Hong Kong Stock Exchanges as well as the Bombay and National Stock Exchanges in India and ranks among the top 30 companies in the FTSE-100 by market capitalization. The Top 5 Institutional Shareholders are Temasek Holdings, Hong kong Depositary Interests, BlackRock Investment Management UK, Dodge & Cox and Schroder Investment Management Ltd. As of August 1, 2022. Temasek Holdings (private) Limited (16.92% stake) and Hong Kong Depositary Interests (9.72% stake) are the two shareholders that own more than 5.0% ownership. The bank’s long-term ratings are A / A1 / A+ with stable outlook. ETG: established in 1967 in Kenya, the ETG is a vertically integrated agricultural supply chain manager involved in the origination, procurement, warehousing, transport, agriculture processing and consumer products. It is active in over 25 African countries, as well as in India, China and South East Asia. It has additional trading and merchandising desks in Europe, the Americas and the Middle East. ETG employs more than 7,000 people globally. The major shareholders are the Sponsors Ketan Patel, Mahesh Patel and Pradip Patel family trust and institutional investors Pembani Remgro (South Africa) and Mitsui & Co Ltd of Japan.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost will be up to US$234million with IFC’s investment of up to US$40 million in the form of a funded participation.
location_description: Standard Chartered is headquartered in London, United Kingdom, and has offices in 60 countries. The Bank’s Trade Risk Distribution is managed out of its Singapore hub. The proposed project will involve trade transactions mainly in east, south and west Africa.
development_impact: The facility is expected to continue having the following development impacts: (i) support of commodity trade finance for importers/exporters in emerging markets; (ii) increased access to trade finance for critical commodities, especially in the agro-commodity sector in emerging market; and (ii) improved market integration by facilitating intra-regional and south-south trade for commodities and enhancing connectivity of real sector firms into value chains.
additionality: IFC's risk participation will help provide short-term liquidity to agri supply chain across Africa. IFC's support would continue encouraging greater activity in IDA countries and support smaller traders and processors.

project_description: IFC proposes an equity investment of up to US$40 million and an additional co-investment envelope of up to US$30 million under the delegated authority framework, in Quadria Capital Fund III LP (the “Fund” or “Fund III”), a private equity fund dedicated to investments in the healthcare sector in South and Southeast Asia. The target Fund size is US$800 million (with a hard cap of US$1 billion). The Fund aims to provide equity to growth stage healthcare companies and will focus on strategic initiatives and operational improvements in its portfolio companies. The Fund will make investments in companies focused on the provision of healthcare delivery, life sciences, medical technology, and associated healthcare services. The Fund will be registered in the Singapore Islands as a limited partnership.
sponsor_shareholders: Quadria Capital Fund III GP is the general partner, Quadria Capital Investment Management Pte Ltd is the investment manager, and Quadria Capital Advisors Pvt Ltd is the investment advisor. The Managing Partners are Mr. Abrar Mir and Dr. Amit Varma who are also the shareholders of Quadria Capital Fund III GP. In addition, the Fund has two partners and eleven other investment professionals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Fund III is targeted at US$800 million (hard cap of US$1 billion) in total commitments by final close. IFC is proposing a limited partnership investment of up to US$40 million in the Fund.
location_description: Quadria Capital Investment Management Pte Ltd, the investment manager, is located in Singapore, and Quadria Capital Advisors Pvt Ltd, the investment advisor, is located in Delhi, India. The Fund’s investment and management team is located in those two locations. The Fund plans to invest across a number of developing countries in both South Asia and Southeast Asia, with an approximately even distribution across the two regions. Its current deal pipeline includes potential projects in both South and Southeast Asia.
development_impact: Stakeholders (Fund's portfolio companies) – Increased access to private equity capital and value creation for health sector focused mid-market companies in India and Southeast Asia region: The main Project Outcomes include increased access to private equity capital and value creation for mid-market companies in the Indian and Southeast Asian health sector and their ability to improve customers or patient health outcomes. South and Southeast Asia have strong unmet demand for quality healthcare. Following the strategy of its previous funds, the Fund plans to invest in quality, scalable businesses that address the mass market at an affordable price on a financially sustainable basis, thereby improving access to quality, affordable healthcare across Asia. Stakeholder (customers/patient health outcomes) – Increased access to affordable and quality health products and services for investees' customers: Quadria invests in healthcare companies that generate positive development impacts, contributing to increases in the provision of health services and improved access to affordable and quality health products. Investments by previous funds (Fund I and Fund II) have led to an increase in patients served by 11 million among a total of 34 million patients served by the Fund investee companies. Many of the invested companies have provided their services and products with 40 to 50 percent discounts for local patients. Fund III will continue its investment strategy, selecting companies in which development impact is intrinsically linked to its business model. Competitiveness – Increasing competitiveness in the South and Southeast Asian health market by promoting alternate funding options and demonstrating the ongoing viability of a healthcare-focused PE model: The private health sector provides more than half of the health services in the region, easing capacity constraints of the public health sector. However, in response to increasing demand for health services, further investment is needed. PE funds provide an alternate source of capital that supports funding options for scaling health services. Since 2017, around $12 billion across 132 deals has been invested by PE funds in healthcare across India and Southeast Asia, representing around 10 percent of PE activity in the regions. IFC expects that Fund III will build on the signal sent by Fund II, encouraging other fund managers to raise funds and reduce the reliance on DFI investors.
additionality: (i) Own Account Equity: IFC's support with a US$40 million equity investment will help the Fund reach its first close. A focused healthcare mandate is relatively unique within South and Southeast Asia. Quadria's specialty focus on raising a health sector focused fund is considered niche and less marketable than generalist funds, with DFIs expected to make up around 30 percent of first close. (ii) Non-commercial Risk Mitigation: IFC's role as a global institutional impact investor also provides unique signaling support to a multi-region sector fund like Quadria, as it will provide a consistent reference point for international investors and signal attractiveness for investors operating beyond a country-specific lens. (iii) Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will also support Quadria via knowledge sharing and standard setting. The Fund manager values IFC's deep health sectoral knowledge and global experience and has often leveraged IFC's healthcare expertise and networks to make better investment decisions and to formulate strategy for its investee companies. (iv) Standard Setting: IFC also supported the previous funds implement an ESMS and ensure alignment with IFC performance standards. Incrementally to this, IFC will work closely with Quadria to support them in promoting gender diversity within their investment team and portfolio. This will include developing internal mechanisms and targets to improve their pipeline of female investment professions and representation of females in Quadria's senior investment team, where there are currently no female Partners or IC members.

project_description: GS 25 Ltd. Liability Co.’s (“GS25 VN” or “the Company”) is one of the largest convenience store chain operators in Vietnam. IFC’s proposed investment will support GS25 VN’s expansion of its GS25 convenience store chain network in Vietnam (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: GS25 VN is ultimately 70% owned by Vietnam-based SonKim Retail Corp. (“SKR”) and 30% owned by South Korea-based GS Retail Co. Ltd. (“GSR”).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed VND460 billion (approximately US$20 million) quasi-equity investment will support GS25 VN’s 2022 – 2025 expansion of new GS25 convenience stores in Vietnam. The estimated Project cost is VND1,056 billion (approximately US$46 million), and includes the cost of construction, equipment, tools, supplies and store rental deposits.
location_description: Vietnam
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are increased access to modern retail for consumers, with improved product variety and services. By expanding its retail network, the Company will offer a more diverse selection of safe food and beverage products to a growing number of Vietnamese consumers. As a modern retailer, the Company will be able to ensure that products are sourced from trusted brands and suppliers. The Company’s expansion will provide local producers and importers with additional sales channels as well as help improve efficiency and operating standards up and down the supply chain through its requirements. With the planned new store openings, the Project is expected to generate a high number of jobs for employees in the stores, as well as indirect jobs for supply chain, logistics support and administration. Beyond The Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote competitiveness through the adoption of a cost-efficient, innovative business model enabling an ambitious expansion plan and generate competitive pressures on other modern retailers to increase their presence in areas where modern grocery retail penetration is low.
additionality: IFC’s Own Account Equity: IFC will provide early-stage long-term funding for GS25 VN’s expansion, which is not easily available in VN. IFC’s patient capital and long-term investment is much needed for the Company during this critical ramp-up period and will help strengthen the Company’s financial soundness and creditworthiness. Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC is aiming to provide Food Safety advisory support to GS25 VN, which will be important for the Company as it prepares to increase the proportion of its fresh food offering. Specifically, IFC Food Safety advisory could help the Company: (i) improve food safety practices in its stores, including acquiring international certifications as needed; (ii) reducing food loss & its reduced environmental footprint; and (iii) establish a supplier risk assessment program.

project_description: The proposed investment is for up to US$35 million equivalent loans to Tanveer Foods Limited (“TFL” or the “Company”). The financing is proposed to include up to US$21 million senior-secured A loan from IFC (the “A Loan”) alongside up to US$14 million from a GAFSP-subordinated loan (in liquidation) (the “GAFSP Loan” and altogether, the “IFC Loan”). IFC’s financing package will be used for setting up a greenfield automated rice mill with processing capacity of 1,000 Metric Tonnes Per Day (“MTPD”). The Project will also include the construction of an 80 MTPD rice bran oil plant and a husk-based co-generation plant, altogether the “Project”. The Project will improve food safety through the adoption of best technologies and practices in an otherwise largely unorganized rice sector in Bangladesh.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsors include Mr. Mostafa Kamal, his wife Mrs. Beauty Akhter and his grown-up children - Ms. Tahmina Binthe Mostafa, Ms. Tanjima Binthe Mostafa, Mr. Tanveer Ahmed Mostafa and Tasnim Binthe Mostafa (collectively referred to as the “Sponsors”). The sponsors are the owners of 100% of the shareholding in the Borrower.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at ~US$53 million and is proposed to be financed with long-term debt totalling ~US$35 million and the balance ~US$18 will be financed through equity. The proposed IFC investment package of US$35 million consists of an A Loan of up to US$21 million and a GAFSP-subordinated loan (the “GAFSP Loan”) of another US$14 million as described in the Blended Finance section. The two loans have a tenor of 8 years including a 2 years of grace period (from the commitment date).
location_description: The Project is located in Manikchak, Bogura in the northern region, a less economically developed part of Bangladesh, an IDA country.
development_impact: The Project is assessed under the Global Food Security Platform. Stakeholders –Consumers: The Project will contribute to increasing food security for consumers through increased production, processing, and distribution of hygienically packaged quality rice (staple food) in underserved areas of Bangladesh. The Project is expected to produce over 170,000 tons by 2027. Stakeholder- farmers: IFC expects that the Project's establishment of a rice milling facility in Bogura region will offer offtake opportunities for smallholder rice farmers, shortening storage periods through immediate purchases and improving the quality of paddy. IFC expects the Project to reach over 123,000 smallholders from a base of 2,600. Market impact -Resilience: The Project is expected to reduce rice supply volatility by preserving and re-directing production and keeping trade flow. IFC anticipates the Project, along with several other projects in the pipeline targeting various links along the global food supply value chain as well as corresponding responses from the World Bank, will enable the global food supply market to better withstand the price and supply shocks.
additionality: (i) IFC will provide financial additionality through a USD loan with a tenor of 8 years, including 2 years grace period from the Commitment date. The Company requires the long tenor loan to have the necessary financial flexibility to implement a more advanced manufacturing technology and investments in resource efficiencies. This kind of financing is not readily available in the market for agribusinesses (ii) IFC is expected to provide concessional financing with the support from GAFSP Blended Finance Facility which will make the financing affordable for the client. (iii) IFC will have an opportunity to identify and help close any gaps in the ESG performance of the Company through ESAP and other associated measures prescribed by IFC, the Company will make improvements and align its operations with industry best practices

company_name: THANH THANH CONG BIEN HOA JOINT STOCK COMPANY
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a 1-year US$20 million funded participation under a risk-sharing facility of up to US$40 million uncommitted secured revolving trade finance facility with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (“SMBC” or the “Bank”) for Thanh Thanh Cong - Bien Hoa Joint Stock Company (“TTC Sugar” or the “Company”). The facility is renewable annually for additional two years. The facility will be solely dedicated to finance (i) the Company’s import of raw sugar; (ii) storage in the approved domestic warehouse(s) with a Collateral Management Agreement (“CMA”); and (iii) sales to domestic and international customers (collectively, the “Project”). It will be processed under the Global Warehouse Finance Program (“GWFP”) with delegated authority from IFC’s Board of Directors.
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam, TTC Sugar is the largest producer of sugar and its by-products in Vietnam. The Company’s main products include refined sugar, raw sugar, functional sugar, liquid sugar, organic sugar, and rock sugar. The Company’s key shareholders include Thanh Thanh Cong Investment Joint Stock Company, Mrs. Huynh Bich Ngoc, and Mrs. Dang Huynh Uc My. Headquartered in Tokyo, SMBC is a leading global financial institution and a core member of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (“SMBC Group”). SMBC is one of the largest Japanese banks by assets, with strong credit ratings across its global integrated network spanning over 39 countries and regions, 15 of which are here in Asia. SMBC works across SMBC Group to offer personal, corporate, and investment banking services to meet the needs of its customers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$40 million, with the proposed IFC investment as a disclosed risk participant of up to US$20 million in an uncommitted secured trade finance facility for 1 year with annual renewals to be fronted by SMBC in favor of TTC Sugar.
location_description: The selected site(s) for the Project is (are) the designated warehouse(s) that is (are) owned by TTC Sugar and its subsidiaries and located in Vietnam.
development_impact: On a project level, the Project will benefit stakeholders along the sugar value chain. By improving access to finance for beneficiaries in Vietnam’s sugar value chain, the Project will enable the Company, distributors, and retailers to sustain operations and employment. At the same time, domestic and regional consumers’ access to sugar products would be ensured. On a market level, the Project will strengthen the competitiveness of Vietnam’s agribusiness sector, which is an important driver of the economy. Collateralized warehouse financing is relatively new in Vietnam; this facility will improve the Company’s sustainability procurement practices on importing goods, which enables the Company to expand its import capacity. The Project is also expected to have demonstration effects on other agribusiness players that will use similar facilities as well as local commercial banks that replicate this new type of financing.
additionality: IFC will provide a commodity-backed trade finance facility which is still nascent in Vietnam. IFC’s engagement will allow (i) SMBC to double the size of the proposed facility which is exceeding its own exposure limit in the country; and (ii) the Company to expand its capacity of importing raw materials to improve supply chain efficiency. This facility would be the first commodity-backed finance loan for the Company.
Company Name: THANH THANH CONG BIEN HOA JOINT STOCK COMPANY

project_description: Evermos (or “the Company”) is an Indonesian Sharia-compliant social commerce platform that connects brand principals (mainly Small and Medium Enterprises (“SMEs”)) to end-consumers via resellers. With a network of predominantly female resellers, the Company offers products from 1,000+ active brands to low-to-middle income consumers primarily in Tier 2-4 cities. The proposed investment would support Evermos’ growth initiatives in Indonesia.
sponsor_shareholders: Evermos was founded in 2018 by Arip Tirta, Iqbal Muslimin, Ghufron Mustaqim and Ilham Taufiq. Apart from the founders and IFC, some of the other key shareholders include Jungle Ventures and Alpha JWC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering an equity investment in Evermos of up to US$5 million from its own account and US$16 million through mobilization to support the Company’s growth Indonesia.
location_description: The Company is registered in Singapore and headquartered in Bandung, Indonesia.
development_impact: IFC anticipates that the Project would result in improved access to markets for individuals and businesses, especially local SME manufacturers. The Project is also expected to result in micro-entrepreneurship opportunities for individuals, especially women. Beyond the Project, this investment has the potential to contribute to supporting the inclusiveness of the e-commerce sector in Indonesia, via competition and innovation channels, by scaling up a tech-enabled social commerce platform in Tier 2+ areas that typically host underserved consumers with limited digital trust.
additionality: IFC’s additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists in the provision of patient equity and resource mobilization as part of the Company’s financing round in Indonesia, where VC availability has substantially increased, but remains more limited for social commerce ventures. Non-financial additionality comprises knowledge, innovation and capacity building, by connecting the Company with financial service providers to support resellers and suppliers, as well as providing gender advisory to the Company.

country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: IFC is considering providing an up to US$40 million loan to Knight Therapeutics Inc. (“Knight” or the “Company”), a pan-American (ex-USA) specialty pharmaceutical company headquartered in Canada with significant operations in Latin America, to partially finance the acquisition of the rights to manufacture, market and sell Exelon® (rivastigmine) in Canada and Latin America (the “Territory”), as well as an exclusive license to use the intellectual property and the Exelon® trademark, from Novartis within the Territory (the “Exelon Acquisition”). Exelon® is indicated for the symptomatic treatment of mild to moderately severe dementia in people with Alzheimer’s disease and Parkinson’s disease. Founded in 2014 in Montreal, Canada, Knight is pan-American (ex-USA) specialty pharmaceutical company that focused on acquiring or in-licensing and commercializing pharmaceutical products in Canada and Latin America. In 2019, Knight acquired a controlling stake in Grupo Biotoscana (“GBT”), a specialty pharmaceutical company with a presence across Latin America. In August 2020, Knight completed the 100% acquisition of GBT. With the GBT acquisition, Knight has expanded its operations in Latin America through a direct presence in 10 countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Knight was founded by Jonathan Ross Goodman, a successful businessman in the Canadian pharmaceutical market. Knight is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange. All shares of the Company are publicly traded, and Jonathan Ross Goodman owns directly and indirectly approximately 19.67% of common shares outstanding. Insiders own directly and indirectly approximately 20.23% as of August 31, 2022.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Knight acquired Exelon® for US$180 million (including a milestone payment of US$12 million upon the achievement of certain conditions). The acquisition has been financed with existing cash holdings of Knight complemented with an A Loan of up to US$40 million.
location_description: Exelon® will be sold across Knight’s platform in the Latin American region and Canada. As of September 2022, Knight has already started commercial activities in several relevant territories in the region, including Brazil and Colombia.
development_impact: Project outcomes: The Project helps respond to the existing and growing need for effective pharmaceuticals to treat dementia. Both Alzheimer's and Parkinson's are a fast-growing burden of disease in Latin America due to the rapidly aging population. Exelon® acts to reduce symptoms by slowing down the degradation of acetylcholine. Knight plans to actively promote Exelon® to revive a brand that has good brand equity and is accepted for its superior quality and tolerance. The patch form of Exelon® has been shown to have less side effects and provides convenience for patients and their caregivers, which is particularly important given the challenges patients with dementia face taking medication. Contribution to market creation: IFC anticipates that the Project will result in an increase in disease awareness, diagnosis and access to treatment in Brazil and other countries in Latin America through the improved promotion of the medication. Absent Knight's acquisition, access to Exelon® may have potentially been limited given the current under-investments in the product, and as a result knowledge of the effectiveness of the product and its market share could fall. The declining role of Exelon® would in turn lead to a further reduction in disease awareness, diagnosis, and access to treatment in the market. In particular, without Knight's acquisition, continued under-investment would cause a negative impact on the attractiveness of the market and would contribute to an under-developed market with less treatment options.
additionality: IFC is providing a multicurrency long-term financing package that is not readily available from commercial banks on a regional basis. In addition, IFC's network of clients and its global reach can provide Knight with expert support to identify and analyze new acquisition targets or expansion opportunities in Latin America and beyond.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of a long-term loan of up to CNY260 million (approximately US$40 million equivalent) to Anyou Biotechnology Group Co., Ltd. (“Anyou” or the “Company”). Headquartered in Taicang city of Jiangsu province, the Company is an existing IFC client in good standing and a leading animal feed producer in China. The Project entails expanding the Company’s eco-friendly and antibiotic-free feed (Eco-feed) capacity by 910,000 tons per annum in frontier regions in China (Guizhou, Gansu, Yunnan), and Hubei province.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Hung Ping is the Chairman and founder of Anyou. With more than 30 years of experience in the animal feed industry, Mr. Hung Ping has a great passion for pig industry development and has published many books about pig farming and animal nutrition. He is a well-respected animal nutrition expert in the industry. Mr. Hung Ping has a bachelor’s degree in animal husbandry from National Chung Hsing University, Taiwan, China. He is supported by a cadre of senior managers who have deep experience in the animal feed sector. Shareholders of Anyou include: (i) Anyou Group (China) Company Limited (46.3%); (ii) Jingning Bona LLP (16.1%); (iii) Xiamen Gaoli LLP (10.7%); (iv) Bangwan Consultancy Co., Ltd. (4.6%); (v) Jingning Shenghong LLP (4.2%); (vi) IFC (3.8%), (vii) Jingning Xingyuan LLP (3.2%); and (viii) Other 10 small shareholders owning less than 3% each (collectively 11.1%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$80 million. The proposed IFC investment is a CNY260 million (approximately US$40 million equivalent) long-term A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project is located in Anyou’s feed mills in key pig raising regions in China, including Guizhou, Gansu, Yunnan and Hubei province.
development_impact: Project level impact: Economy wide effects: The Project is expected to generate not only direct jobs from Anyou’s planned feed mills in 4 frontier provinces, but also indirect jobs along the animal feed value chain, due to the Project’s derived demand for raw material sourcing and ambient support services. Stakeholders–Farmers: At the current annual production level of 2 million tons of animal feeds, Anyou procures raw materials (mainly grains) indirectly from about 72,000 crop farmers through the corporate suppliers. The Project will increase the procurement of such raw materials, hence enhance crop farmers’ income accordingly. Market level impact: Sustainability and Competitiveness: The Project is expected to have a demonstration effect of improving the sustainability and competitiveness of the pig sector, as the use of antibiotic-free and eco-friendly feeds will reduce greenhouse gas footprint, contributing to sustainability of the pig value chain in a cost competitive manner.
additionality: IFC additionality stems from its ability to engage strategically with Anyou by offering the following financial and non- financial additionality. Financial additionality: IFC will provide a fixed-rate long-term local currency loan to the Company. This type of financing is not readily available locally for agribusinesses. The long loan tenor improves the Company’s debt maturity profile, and the fixed-rate local currency funding allows the Company to control the interest rate and currency risks. Non-financial Additionality—Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will engage with the Company to support continued improvement in ESG practices and identify further scope for enhancing Anyou’s sector knowledge and network in the emerging markets.

company_name: AL DOUH IRAQI COMPANY FOR CEMENT INDUSTRIES LLC
project_description: The proposed investment consists of a US$130 million financing package to Al Douh Iraqi Company for Cement Industries LLC (the “Company” or “Al Douh”) based in Al Muthanna city, Iraq and specialized in cement production. The funds will be used to finance the expansion of Al Douh’s plant from 1.5 million ton (“mt”) to 3.5mt per annum of Sulphates Resistant Cement (SRC) and Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC), (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is owned by members of the prominent Al Khawam family of Iraq with Mr. Hatam Al Khawam and Mr. Ali Al Khawam (the “Sponsors”) each owning 50% share. The Sponsors are well-respected and known members of Al Khawam family with over 20 years track-record of building successful businesses in Iraq and Jordan.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at US$220 million and will be financed through a combination of Sponsors equity and debt financing. IFC is proposed to arrange a financing package of up to US$130 million comprising of an (i) IFC A loan of up to $65 million and (ii) a mobilization tranche of up to $65 million.
location_description: The Project is located in the city of Samawa in the Southern Iraqi province of Muthanna.
development_impact: The Project will scale and strengthen local cement production capacity in Iraq, while generating jobs and strengthening economic linkages to other sectors. The Project is expected to create 800 jobs during the construction phase and 89 full-time jobs after commissioning.
additionality: The Project will scale and strengthen local cement production capacity in Iraq, while generating jobs and strengthening economic linkages to other sectors. The Project is expected to create 800 jobs during the construction phase and 89 full-time jobs after commissioning.
Company Name: AL DOUH IRAQI COMPANY FOR CEMENT INDUSTRIES LLC

company_name: FRAPORT TAV ANTALYA YATIRIM YAPIM VE ISLETME A.S.
project_description: Fraport TAV Antalya Yatirim,Yapim ve Isletme A.S. (the “Company”) is a Turkish joint-stock company owned by TAV Havalimanlari Holding Anonim Sirketi (“TAV Airports”) and Fraport AG Frankfurt Airport Services Worldwide (“Fraport”), respectively. On December 28, 2021, the Company entered into a 25-year Lease Agreement with the General Directorate of State Airports Authority (“DHMI”), for the operations and expansion of Antalya Airport (ICAO: AYT), starting on 1st of January 2027. Antalya airport is one of the largest leisure-oriented airports in Europe, with a current capacity of circa 40 million passengers. The Project entails the expansion of the Antalya Airport to a capacity of approximately 80 million in three phases.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsors are Fraport and TAV Airports, with 49% and 51% ownership of the Company, respectively, and a joint management control structure. Fraport is a leading international airport operator with about 19,000 employees and 24 airports under management and provides services to 30 airports globally. Fraport also provides services such as traffic and terminal management, ground handling, security, and real estate and facility management at various airports around the world. Fraport is publicly listed in the Frankfurt Stock Exchange. Established in 1997, TAV Airports is a leading international airport operator with over 22,000 employees and currently managing a portfolio of 15 airports and with interests in other airport related activities such as commercial activities, duty free, catering and ground handling at various airports around the world. TAV Airports is publicly listed in the Istanbul stock exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is estimated at approximately €3.4 billion to be financed by a combination of equity and debt. The proposed investment entails a long-term project finance package consisting of a loan of up to €300 million from IFC’s own account and a B loan of up to €250 million for the account of the participants. This financing will support the Company in refinancing the existing €2.3 billion bridge loan raised for the expansion of AYT.
location_description: The Project is in the city of Antalya in Türkiye.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate significant stakeholder impacts in terms of improved access and quality of the airport's landside and airside services, as well as positive government revenue and economy-wide impacts derived both from the operation and from the activities enabled mainly in the aviation and tourism sectors. The anticipated market creation effect is to preserve Türkiye's role in the global and regional tourism market.
additionality: IFC long-term financing and mobilization from development financial institutions and/or commercial banks will play a counter-cyclical role with a potential signaling effect on the Turkish market.
Company Name: FRAPORT TAV ANTALYA YATIRIM YAPIM VE ISLETME A.S.

company_name: INTERNACIONAL DE INVERSIONES, S.A.P.I. DE C.V.
project_description: The proposed investment consists of an unfunded Partial Credit Guarantee of up to MXN$500 million to Internacional de Inversiones S.A.P.I. de C.V. (“IDEI” or the “Company”), a property development company based in Mexico. The proposed project aims to support IDEI in its first ever public bond issuance to finance the development of new EDGE-certified green residential projects and to refinance the debt of existing green office buildings owned by the Company.
sponsor_shareholders: IDEI is a private company (Sociedad anónima promotora de inversión de capital variable). The De la Garza Evia family, founder of the Company, has a 55.8% shareholding interest. The remaining shares are held by other individual shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The bond issuance is estimated at MXN 1.0 billion. The proposed IFC investment consists of an unfunded Partial Credit Guarantee of up to MXN 500 million.
location_description: The buildings in the project are to be located in the city of Monterrey and neighboring areas, Nuevo Leon, Mexico.
development_impact: IFC expects the project to generate an increase in access to quality housing for middle-income populations and have positive environmental effects through reduction in energy and water consumption. At the market level, IFC anticipates that the Project will promote financial integration of the housing market through demonstration effects, where the Company will diversify its lender base through the issuance of the first Sustainability-Linked Bond (SLB) by a housing developer.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality comes from the provision of financing structure as IFC will support IDEI's first ever bond issuance and through the Partial Credit Guarantee allow IDEI to access a broader investor base. Non-financial additionality will be provided in the form of: (i) Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building as IFC will support the Company to achieve its first ever public issuance, expected to be classified as a Green Bond, while also sharing international best practices in environmental and social management to reinforce the Company’s ESG standards; and (ii) non-commercial risk mitigation, including trusted partnerships.
Company Name: INTERNACIONAL DE INVERSIONES, S.A.P.I. DE C.V.

project_description: Established in France in 1900, Groupe Soufflet (“Soufflet Group”) was privately-owned by the Soufflet family through Ets. J Soufflet SA, a holding company incorporated in France. Soufflet Group was a vertically integrated agribusiness group operating in wheat & barley value chains. In December 2021, Soufflet Group was acquired by InVivo Group (“InVivo”). InVivo is one of Europe's leading agricultural group, with a workforce of more than 13,000 employees. Established in 38 countries, InVivo operates across: Agriculture; Malting; Milling, Ingredients, Bakery / Pastry / Confectionery; Gardening and Food Distribution; International Grain Trading and Wine. In October 2021, IFC committed €50 million in A Loan to fund working capital needs of specific Soufflet Group (now, InVivo) subsidiaries in Bulgaria, Kazakhstan, Poland, Romania, and Ukraine. The existing loan is proposed to be increased by up to an A Loan of €65 million to support working capital needs and liquidity needs of InVivo in Ukraine .
sponsor_shareholders: InVivo is a leading agribusiness player in Europe. It is owned by Union InVivo – a national union of French cooperatives.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: With increased prices, InVivo’s working capital needs in the Ukraine only are expected to be €60 - 70 million. The proposed increase in IFC financing by up to €65 million in A Loan will support working capital and liquidity needs of InVivo in Ukraine.
location_description: The proposed increase in IFC financing of up to €65 million will be used in Ukraine.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is the impact on farmers' access to markets and quality inputs as well as its contribution to global food security.
additionality: IFC’s expected additionality in this Project largely stems from non-commercial risk mitigation and provision of working capital in counter cyclical times.

project_description: Afrigreen Debt Impact Fund (the “Fund” or “Afrigreen”) is an infrastructure senior debt fund offering financing solutions to implement small to medium on-and off-grid solar power plants, mostly to Commercial & Industrial (“C&I”) consumers in West and Central Africa (“W&C Africa”). The Fund will have a target cap size of EUR100.0 million with a hard cap at EUR125.0 million, and a maturity of 10 years. The Fund will invest in EUR, USD, and when relevant in local currency (in Nigeria and Ghana)
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund, formed as a Limited Partnership and domiciled in France, is managed by RGREEN INVEST S.A.S (the “Fund Manager”) and advised by Echosys Invest, a 50/50 joint venture between the FM and Echosys Advisory S.A.S. RGREEN INVEST is a European alternative investment Fund Manager regulated by the Autorité des Marchés Financiers with an exclusive focus on energy transition, adaptation to climate change and mitigation of its effects. Since 2013 RGREEN INVEST has supported over 1,500 projects in Europe for an installed capacity of more than 3.3 GW. Echosys Advisory S.A.S is a French advisory company specialized in renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, and industrial decarbonization. It was set up by Olivier Leruste and Alexandre Gilles, a team of former developers with 30 years of combined experience in the origination, structuring and financing of renewable energy projects across the globe (over 1.5GW of installed capacity in renewable energy).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an equity investment of up to EUR20.0 million as Limited Partner, comprising of (i) up to EUR10.0 million for IFC’s own account; and (ii) up to EUR10.0 million from IFC acting as implementing entity of the Finland-IFC Blended Finance for Climate Program (“Finland BFCP”). In addition, IFC will provide cross currency swaps (“CCS”) to the Fund in Nigeria and Ghana with the support of up to US$30.0 million from the International Development Association’s Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (“IDA20 PSW LCF”).
location_description: Afrigreen is a pan-African fund, with a focus on financing C&I consumers in W&C Africa.
development_impact: The Project is expected to improve the affordability of electricity supply for C&I customers in W&C Africa by supporting the development of ca. 90 megawatts of solar photovoltaic capacity. C&I customers in the target markets face high electricity costs due to high tariffs for grid electricity (e.g., Ghana and Senegal), as well as reliance on diesel generators in Sierra Leone and Nigeria. The Project will also contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution by displacing fossil fuel generation with a green source. At the market level, the Project is expected to enhance financial integration by supporting a debt fund with a standardized, scalable platform approach to help address a funding gap for small and medium C&I solar, thereby demonstrating a financing model that may be replicated by other lenders.
additionality: IFC’s additionality stems from the provision of own account equity, not readily available in the target markets, to the first debt fund exclusively focused on small- and medium-sized projects in the largely nascent solar C&I industry. IFC’s role as an anchor investor is expected to help catalyze participation in future funding rounds of institutional investors, who have appetite for infrastructure assets but lack in-house expertise to appraise investments individually. IFC’s non-financial additionality encompasses support to comply with rigorous E&S standards.

project_description: CapitaLand Ascott Trust (CLAS or the Company) is the largest hospitality trust in Singapore and Asia Pacific, with an asset size of S$7.6 billion as of June 30, 2022. CLAS is listed on the Singapore Exchange (“SGX”) and has an investment property portfolio that comprises mainly serviced residences, hotels, rental housing properties and student accommodation assets globally. IFC is proposing to invest up to US$115 million equivalent in a proposed up to 7-year sustainability-linked bond (“SLB”) issued by Ascott REIT MTN Pte. Ltd. under its S$2 billion Multicurrency Debt Issuance Programme.
sponsor_shareholders: CLAS’ sponsor, The Ascott Limited (Ascott or the Sponsor) is a leading international lodging owner-operator with more than 30 years of track record. Ascott is a wholly owned subsidiary of CapitaLand Investment, which is a leading global real estate investment manager with a strong foothold in Asia. CapitaLand Investment is listed on the SGX.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing to be the sole subscriber to the proposed SLB of up to US$115 million equivalent.
location_description: IFC’s investment will be earmarked for three serviced residence properties in Indonesia and the Philippines. The IFC-financed portfolio will be expected to meet Sustainability Performance Targets (SPTs), which are in line with CapitaLand Investment’s Sustainability Framework and comply with IFC Greenbuilding Definition and Sustainability-linked Bond Principles.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level effect is environmental effect through reduction in GHG emissions and resource efficiency. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater sustainability in the real estate sector in emerging East Asia Pacific (EAP) countries. CLAS's strong commitment to greening its properties will provide a highly visible demonstration case given its prominent position in the marketplace. This could help further the sustainability agenda of the institutional real estate market in emerging EAP.
additionality: Financial additionality will be provided via financing structure with a long-term tenor that is not readily available in the market. Non-financial additionality will be provided via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building where IFC will advise CLAS to enhance its Sustainability-linked Financing Framework where applicable.

project_description: The proposed investment is a debt facility to Sococim Industries(‘Sococim’, ‘Company’ or the ‘Borrower’), the largest integrated cement manufacturer in Senegal to fund a partial replacement and modernization at its existing facility near Dakar, Senegal. Sococim is a subsidiary of Vicat S.A, (‘Vicat’, ‘Sponsor’, or the ‘Guarantor’), an existing and strategic client for IFC, and one of the top global cement makers. IFC’s facility will enable Sococim to replace and modernize part of its existing capacity with a modern fuel-efficient kiln (the ‘Project’) with Best Available Technology. Further, the Project will enable the Company to replace all of its clinker imports.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is Vicat Group (EPA: VCT), an integrated global cement manufacturer with cement capacity of 35MTPA, is listed on Euronext Paris with market cap of €1.2billion. As of FY2021, it operates in 12 countries and employs ~9,500 people (in 16 cement plants in nine countries and five clinker grinding plants in three countries), with 63% of revenues (of €3.1billion) realized in developed markets (France, US, Italy, and Switzerland) and 37% in emerging markets (Kazakhstan, Egypt, Senegal, Mali, Mauritania, India, Turkey, and Brazil).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project Cost is expected to be up to €260 million. IFC’s financing of up to €120m in IFC A-loan and up to €120m equivalent in Parallel Loans.
location_description: Sococim is located in Rufisque on the outskirts of Dakar.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are economy-wide and environmental effects. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the project will contribute to improve the sustainability of cement production in West Africa through dissemination of production processes compliant with the most demanding sustainability international standards; and increased availability of low carbon fuels.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via financing structure (long-term financing that is not otherwise available). Non-financial additionality is provided via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building as IFC will support the Company’s E&S endeavors including its carbon strategy.

project_description: The proposed project consists in the establishment of the Transform Health Fund (“THF” or the “Fund”), a high impact healthcare focused debt fund. THF will seek to provide growth financing to and scale innovative care delivery models and supply chain businesses in the healthcare sector in Africa to achieve public health goals and improve resilience of the health infrastructure in the continent
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund General Partner will be a joint venture between AfricInvest Global Manco, a Mauritius limited liability company, focused on investing in Africa and the Health Finance Coalition, a Delaware limited liability company formed as a wholly own subsidiary of Malaria No More Fund, a Delaware Corporation and tax-exempt charitable corporation.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be up to US$100 million. IFC will provide financing of up to US$15 million in the form of subscription to preferred shares and mobilize funding from other financiers for up to US$45 million.
location_description: The Fund will make investments across the African continent
development_impact: The project will promote access to growth capital for Fund investees in a number of Sub-Saharan African countries. By providing investees with needed financing it will support them to respond to the large gap in the availability of appropriate quality health services and products in these countries. Many of the investees would otherwise face challenges accessing finance. By providing financing to these companies the project will thus expand access to healthcare services and products. Providing support to these companies can be expected to have broader impacts on the markets they operate in and so strengthen these markets competitiveness and resilience.
additionality: IFC’s participation in THF is timely and much needed given the challenging fundraising environment in Africa as a result of the economic fallout of the COVID-19 pandemic and suppressed investor sentiment, now somewhat recovering since 2021. The role of IFC will help to promote and facilitate the participation of third-party investors in THF and will enable the team to access the much-needed private sector funding for the scaleup. IFC’s involvement in helping to mobilize financing from international investors and development institutions will be a critical endorsement of the Fund’s credibility. Further IFC has various forms of non-financial additionality. This includes supporting the fund on E&S and corporate governance, as well as providing access to IFC’s global and regional industry knowledge and networks in the target investment sectors.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an A Loan and a B Loan of up to US$900 million to Suzano S.A. (“Suzano” or the “Company”), an integrated pulp and paper producer based in Brazil. The proposed project aims to support the construction of a new pulp plant with a 2.55 million tons per annum (mtpa) capacity, and the development of related forestry plantations in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil.
sponsor_shareholders: Suzano is a listed company with, as of September 30, 2022, 50.4% of shares in free float. The Feffer family, founder of the Company, and management have a combined 45.8% shareholding interest.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at BRL 19.3 billion (approximately US$3.7 billion). The proposed IFC investment consists of an IFC A Loan of up to US$250 million and an up to US$650 million B Loan.
location_description: The pulp mill will be located in the municipality of Ribas do Rio Pardo, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate economy-wide effects and to have positive environmental effects. At the market level, the Project will help strengthen the competitiveness of Brazil's pulp and paper sector by incentivizing other players to replicate zero fossil fuel technology and other designs that optimize energy and resource efficiency.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality comes from the provision of long-term financing and resource mobilization. Non-financial additionality comes from the adoption of best E&S practices in line with IFC E&S Performance Standards to support the Company´s sustainability goals.

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: Greenlam Industries Limited (“Greenlam”) is one of the leading decorative laminates brands in Asia. Greenlam is also India’s leading decorative-veneer brand and the only manufacturer of engineered wooden flooring and doors. It currently has two laminates manufacturing plants in Northern India (Rajasthan & Himachal Pradesh) with a total capacity of 15.6 million sheets/boards per annum. The proposed expansion involves setting up of greenfield manufacturing facilities for high-pressure laminates and particleboard to be housed in a wholly owned subsidiary of Greenlam - Greenlam South Ltd (“GSL” or the “Company”). The Project involves providing an IFC A Loan to GSL of up to US$ 25 million (INR 2,000 million) for setting up greenfield plant for new laminates lines with an operating capacity of 3.5 million sheets/boards per annum and the particleboard lines will have a capacity of 231,000 CMB per annum
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Greenlam. Greenlam is headed by Mr. Saurabh Mittal (Sponsor), the Managing Director and CEO, who possesses more than two decades of experience in the wood panel industry. The Company is a listed on the Bombay and National Stock exchanges of India and has a market capitalization of US$ 510 million as of October 07, 2022. As of June 30, 2022. the Sponsor and his family members own 53.8965% of Greenlam and the balance is owned by public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of setting up the greenfield manufacturing facilities for high-pressure laminates and particleboard (the Project) is US$111 million, of which US$39 million will be financed via equity from Greenlam. The balance will be funded through debt from IFC (up to US$25 million), Export Credit Agency Financing (EUR 25.459 million), and other local and international lenders in India.
location_description: The Project will be located in Naidupeta in Nellore District, Andhra Pradesh, India.
development_impact: The expected project-level outcomes are stakeholder effects, through contribution to employment and value-added to GDP in India. IFC anticipates that the Project will create significant jobs with the new upcoming capacity, including direct and indirect jobs. Contribution to market effects are to improve sector competitiveness through demonstration effects. The Project supports a market leader in laminate manufacturing to enter the particle board market, and expects to contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of the wood panels sector.
additionality: Through the proposed funding, IFC's involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide critical financing for the largest capex of the Company through a long-term debt financing that suits the Project's cashflows. IFC will also support Greenlam to adopt renewable agro-forestry practices in the particleboard manufacturing process.

sector: Household Appliances (Including Refrigerators, Laundry Machine, Dishwashers, etc.)
project_description: Arcelik A.S. (“Arcelik or the “Company”) is a major Turkish white goods manufacturer with global operations. The proposed investment is an IFC A loan of up to EUR150 million (the “IFC Loan”) which will fund Arcelik’s working capital needs in Turkey and construction of a new all-in-one facility by Singer Bangladesh Limited (“Singer”), Arcelik’s subsidiary in Bangladesh (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Arcelik’s current ownership structure is as follows: Koc Group (57.24%), Burla group (17.61%), Arcelik (9.97%), and publicly listed shares on Borsa Istanbul (15.18%). Koc Holding is the leading industrial conglomerate of Turkey, mainly engaged in the energy, automotive, consumer durables, and finance sectors. Koc Holding is majority-owned by the Koc family of Turkey, while the remaining shares (26.46%) of Koc Holding are publicly listed..
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is expected to be EUR290 million, while the proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to EUR150 million.
location_description: The Project will be located in Turkey and Bangladesh.
development_impact: The Project's expected development outcome includes (i) economywide effects, through exports and job creation, and (ii) promotion of sector integration in terms of novel productive capabilities and technology transfers in Bangladesh.
additionality: IFC’s expected additionality includes its counter cyclical role through provision of long-term financing and diversification of the Company’s funding base.

project_description: The proposed investment entails an up to US$150 million A loan and an up to US$100 million B loan to Eurofarma Laboratórios S.A. (Eurofarma or the Company), a life science manufacturing company headquartered in Brazil with presence across Latin America. The proceeds will be used to fund i) the construction of a greenfield pharmaceutical manufacturing plant in Montes Claros, Brazil to produce oral solids and antibiotics; and (ii) the equipment needed to do the fill and finish of the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine in Brazil (both investments together are defined as the “Project”). Eurofarma was founded in Sao Paulo, southeast of Brazil, in 1972 as a family business and has grown rapidly to become a regional manufacturer of prescription drugs, generic drugs and medicine solutions to public and private hospitals.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded in 1972 by Galliano Billi (1926-2020). Eurofarma continues to be fully owned by the Billi Family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$375 million and will be financed with an A Loan of up to US$150 million, a B Loan of up to US$100 million, other local bank loans and internal cash generation.
location_description: Investments will be made at Eurofarma’s new facility located in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil, and at Eurofarma’s existing facility in Itapevi, state of Sao Paulo, Brazil.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is an increase in access to vaccines and oral solids and antibiotics. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing could support greater market resilience as spillover effects accrue to the healthcare supply chains in these markets.
additionality: IFC is providing long-term financing to Eurofarma, which is not so readily available in the market. In addition, the Company will benefit from IFC's Environmental and Social performance standards and IFC's sectoral knowledge.

project_description: Shanghai Zhonggu Logistics Co., Ltd. (“Zhonggu” or the “Company”) is the second largest domestic trade multimodal container transportation company in China and is listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. Zhonggu started as a container shipping company and gradually began to provide multimodal container transportation by supplementing railway and truck transportation after the containers arrive at the ports. It targets to provide “door-to-door” services for its customers. As of 30 June 2021, Zhonggu operated a fleet of 109 container vessels (40 owned and 69 leased). Capacity-wise, it had approximately 160,000 TEU of ship capacity and approximately 390,000 TEU of container capacity. IFC is providing a green loan package of RMB 650 million to finance the Company’s purchase of new vessels and various types of containers to further enhance its capacity. The green loan package is expected to comply with the International Green Loan Principles.
sponsor_shareholders: As of 30 September 2021, Zhonggu’s largest shareholder was Zhonggu Shipping Group Co., Ltd. with 57.46% ownership. The second largest shareholder was Ningbo Guyang Investment Management Limited Partnershp with 7.01% ownership. The rest of shares (35.53%) are widely held by investors with less than 5% each.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at about US$1,088 million, which is to be financed by a combination of debt from both IFC and other financial institutions, as well as equity.
location_description: The proposed investment is to support purchase of vessels and containers used for domestic transportation within China.
development_impact: The project will support Zhonggu in expanding its operations through investment in vessels and containers, which will strengthen its multimodal transportation services and dry bulk containerization. The main project-level outcomes are the positive stakeholder effects of supporting increased volume of domestic cargo transported by expanded shipping capacity, and increased inland connectivity by supporting the Company’s strategic expansion of multimodal transportation. Moreover, by shifting transportation from roads to sea and rail, the project is also expected to lead to positive environmental outcomes. At the market level, the investment is expected to contribute to competitiveness by supporting private investments in the domestic shipping sector, and demonstrating the shift towards dry bulk containerization and multimodal transportation.
additionality: (i) The IFC green loan package will comply with the International Green Loan Principles. It introduces a new instrument to the Company and will help position the Company to issue green bonds compliant with the International Green Bond Principles in the future, which will enable the Company to access different pool of investors. (ii) IFC will support the design and implementation of a green financing framework, and will give recommendations to the Company on its sustainability framework and reporting. (iii) IFC will provide technical guidance to help strengthen the Company’s capacity to manage E&S risks in accordance with IFC PSs.

project_description: IFC is considering a US $6.0 million IFC “A” Loan to Kamal Steel Limited (“Kamal Steel”), a leading steel bar manufacturer in Tanzania. The funding will be utilized to support incremental working capital for steel production in Tanzania. The project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) in the amount of up to US$6.0 million as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Kamal Steel is owned by three brothers of the Gupta family from Tanzania: Gagan Santosh (48.8%), Sameer Santosh (51%) and Satyam Swatantra (0.2%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$12 million comprising of a (i) up to US$6.0 million “A” loan and (ii) up to US$6.0 million concessional loan subordinated to the “A” Loan from IFC, acting in its capacity as the implementing entity of IDA PSW BFF. IFC can only provide US$6.0 million based on the low value of the security package available. The IDA PSW BFF US$6.0 million loan will help close the funding gap and de-risk IFC’s investment by being subordinated in payments and liquidation to the IFC “A” loan.
location_description: The proceeds will be utilized for Kamal Steel in Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are: (i) economy-wide effects through value-addition and job creation in the target countries; and (ii) environmental effects through improved resource efficiency in production processes. Beyond these outcomes, IFC expects the Project to promote regional supply chains integration, enhance forward linkages, and support the growth of Tanzania’s construction and infrastructure sectors.
additionality: IFC’s involvement with the support of IDA PSW BFF is expected to contribute to both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is provided via financing structure (long-term financing that is not otherwise available). Non-financial additionality is provided by IFC’s E&S teams for organizational and operational best practices.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to US$3.75 million IFC A loan (“IFC Loan”) and an up to US$3.75 million IDA PSW Subordinated Loan (“PSW Loan”) (jointly the “Loans”) to Dembesh Hotel South Sudan Ltd (“Dembesh Hotel” or the “Hotel”). Dembesh Hotel is an independent owner operating a 50-key business hotel in Juba, the capital city of South Sudan. The Loans will be used to finance part of the Hotel’s US$20.05 million project involving a 30-room extension and refurbishment of the existing rooms (the “Project”). The balance of the funding will be provided by the majority shareholder Mr. Ayesheshim Teka Zeleke (the “Sponsor”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Hotel is 97% owned by Mr. Ayesheshim Teka who is also the sponsor of the Project. The remaining 3% is owned by Pur Chiengan Dakbai.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is US$20.05 million. IFC is expectd to provide a loan package of up to US$7.5 million to support the Project. The package will comprise: (i) a senior IFC A loan of up to US$3.75 million and (ii) a PSW IDA loan of up to US$3.75 million by IFC acting as Implementing Entity of IDA18 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility to help create quality jobs in South Sudan’s business tourism sector.
location_description: The Project is located in Hai Mission, Juba, South Sudan
development_impact: The most important project level outcomes are: (i) Economy wide effects: The Project which will support the expansion and modernization of the hotel is expected to have various positive economy-wide effects including: (a) direct job creation/preservation and contribution to GDP during the construction and operation phase of the hotel as well as indirect effects across the supply chains; (b) higher tax revenues for local government; (c) provision of infrastructure supporting the development of the tourism sector; and (d) increase in economic activities through increased international arrivals. These benefits will be important in South Sudan, where unemployment rates, exports are heavily dominated by oil and tourism & travel represent a small share of the GDP; and (ii) Stakeholder impacts: (a) Employees: The Project will also contribute to local skill development. Dembesh Hotel will provide training to all its employees, addressing the skills gap and (b) benefit local suppliers through increased linkages. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will facilitate market creation in terms of: (i) Competitiveness: The Project is anticipated to be the second internationally branded hotel to enter the market, contributing to the development of the country’s business infrastructure; and (ii) Integration: The Project has the potential to promote integration of local suppliers within domestic supply chains. As suppliers receive training and contingent to level of training they receive, they can expand their reach beyond the hotel and start working with other local players.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing structure: IFC will provide a long-term loan with a grace period, which is not readily available to the Company in South Sudan. The loan will improve the Company’s debt profile and enhance its access to outside complementary capital, thus reducing its vulnerability to domestic financial and banking shocks. Moreover, with the COVID-19 pandemic, funding for large projects is not readily available as local banks become more risk averse. Non-financial Additionality: Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC’s Guidance based on its expertise in TRP sectors will be valuable input to the Sponsor and the Project. IFC will use its expertise in Food Safety and Green Buildings to: (i) help the Project increase the quality and safety of the available local supply; and (ii) provide best practice assistance in terms of E & S Standards and implementation of the EDGE Green Building tool in a country where energy costs are extremely high. Team will explore potential for advisory engagements during appraisal.

project_description: The proposed transaction is an investment of up to US$90 million in convertible preferred shares of Elemental Holding S.à r.l., a company formed and incorporated in Luxembourg (“Elemental” or the “Company”). Elemental is a leading global player operating in the recycling stage of the Platinum Group Metals (“PGM”) and E-waste value chain. IFC’s proposed investment will be used to finance the Company’s growth plans through Mergers and Acquisitions (“M&A”) in developed and emerging markets, downstream projects, and other corporate purposes and transactions (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Elemental is a privately owned company established in 2011 and currently majority owned by EFF foundation settled by the Jarski family, with a minority stake being held by Mr. Przemyslaw Krych, a Polish businessman.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will be investing up to US$90 million in convertible preferred shares of the Company. IFC’s proposed investment is part of a total targeted capital raise of up to US$350 million, in the same instrument. Besides IFC, the Company is currently engaged with other development finance institutions and reputable private investors to secure funding for the private placement.
location_description: The Project involves acquisition of target companies (operating in upstream segment of metals recycling) in emerging and developed markets, and expansion into the downstream segment. The proceeds of IFC’s proposed investment will be used for financing M&A, including a potential acquisition of an existing company in an emerging market, downstream projects and other corporate purposes and transactions.
development_impact: The Project will contribute to the reduction in inadequate waste disposal and GHG emissions associated with primary mining and electricity generation as well as greater sustainability by demonstrating a successful circular economy business model.
additionality: IFC offers both financial and non-financial additionality in this transaction. IFC’s proposed investment will play a countercyclical role and allow Elemental to strengthen its capital position for organic growth and acquisitions. IFC’s non-financial additionality includes supporting the client’s ambitious expansion strategy by providing expertise in the waste management sector and sustainability as well as leveraging its regional knowledge and networks. IFC will also support Elemental on aligning with international Corporate Governance best practices and strengthen Company’s capacity to effectively manage E&S risks through the implementation of IFC Performance Standards.

project_description: The proposed investment entails an up to US$65 million A loan in BRL equivalent to União Química Farmacêutica Nacional S.A. (“UQ” or the “Company”), a life science manufacturing company headquartered in Brazil. The proceeds will be used to (i) expand production capacity with a focus on antibiotics, corticoids, anti-inflammatories, anesthetics, and others serving the hospital segment which had a spike in demand due to COVID-19 and supply disruptions; (ii) upgrade two existing plants to produce vaccines (both for COVID-19 and other uses); and (iii) finance working capital needs (all investments together are defined as the “Project”). With over 85 years of operations, the Company has grown into a diversified pharmaceutical manufacturer for human health (prescription drugs and OTC for retail and hospital clients), animal health and toll manufacturing.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded in 1936 and acquired by the Marques family in 1970. União Química continues to be fully owned by the Marques Family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$79 million and will be financed with an A Loan of up to US$65 million and internal cash generation.
location_description: Investments will be made at União Química’s existing facilities located in the states of São Paulo, Minas Gerais and the Federal District in Brazil.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is an increase in access to vaccines and much-needed medication in Brazil, including additional capacity for COVID-19 treatment medication. There is also expected to be an impact on market resilience through strengthening the supply chain to deliver medication and vaccines.
additionality: IFC is providing long-term financing to União Química, which is not so readily available in the market. In addition, there are important advisory engagements on Climate and Vaccine manufacturing. União Química will also benefit from IFC's Environmental and Social performance standards, corporate governance knowledge and sectoral experience.

project_description: The proposed investment is a corporate loan of up to €40m (the “IFC Loan”) to Balfin Group (“Balfin”). The IFC loan will (i) refinance existing debt of the Tirana East Gate mall (“TEG”); (ii) fund extension, refurbishment and other related capex of TEG; and (iii) recapitalization of TEG to finance Balfin’s retail parks projects (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Balfin is a leading diversified conglomerate based in Albania and a premium employer in the country. Established in 1993, it is fully owned by Mr. Samir Mane. Balfin owns 88.1% of TEG with the remaining shares held by Albanian American Enterprise Fund (8.9%) and First Investment Services (3%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total capital needs for the Project (including refinancing) is estimated at €51.7m
location_description: Albania
development_impact: Expected Project-level outcomes are increased supply of business enabling infrastructure, and increased access to modern retail for consumers. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Project will promote competitiveness in the retail market in Albania.
additionality: - Long term financing - Green buildings.

project_description: Anglesey Food LLC (“Korzinka” or the “Company”) is the leading food retailer in Uzbekistan, operating under the “Korzinka” brand name. The Project involves construction of the Company’s new distribution center in Tashkent with a total estimated project cost of approximately US$25 million (the “Project”). The Project will support the Company’s growth and help address the country’s developmental challenges by increasing consumer access to quality food via a nationwide, modern retail chain. The new distribution center will consolidate Korzinka’s logistics operations, increasing its operational efficiencies.
sponsor_shareholders: The majority shareholder of the Company is its founder, Mr. Zafar Khashimov, with the remaining shares owned by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated total project cost is around US$25 million. The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$25 million equivalent senior, secured, sustainability-linked 7-year loan, structured in compliance with Islamic finance principles.
location_description: The Project is located in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
development_impact: The Project will have significant development impact. The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are i) increased access to modern retail for consumers in Uzbekistan and ii) job creation and preservation. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Project will promote financial integration through enabling a loan aligned with Islamic Finance Principles.
additionality: IFC is providing financial and non-financial additionality. IFC’s financial additionality will be provided via: (i) An innovative sustainability-linked structure, (ii) a Shari’ah-compliant financing instrument not easily available to real sector companies in Uzbekistan, and (iii) long-term tenor that is not available in the local market. Non-financial additionality will be provided via knowledge, innovation, and capacity building where IFC will support the Company’s ambitions to obtain climate and gender EDGE certifications as well as improve its food safety standards.

project_description: BUA Cement PLC (“BUA” or “the Company”) owns and operates two cement plants i.e., one in Sokoto State, northwestern Nigeria known as the Kalambaina plant, and another one in the Edo State, in southern Nigeria. BUA is a listed company on the Nigerian Stock exchange, and one of the largest companies by market capitalization in the country. The project is BUA’s expansion of the Sokoto Kalambaina plant (“SKP”) (“the Project”). The Project includes i) expanding cement production capacity by 6 MTPA by constructing two modern, large-scale integrated cement lines i.e., lines 4 and 5 ii) constructing 120 MW (existing 50 MW plus new 70 MW) of captive gas-based power plants; iii) installing a 10 MW solar power plant; iv) expanding the cement distribution fleet; v) expansion of quarry operations including equipment and machinery to increase associated operations; vi) constructing additional storage silos, vii) building infrastructure in support of the use of liquified natural gas (LNG) allied to additional diesel storage tanks, and viii) working capital. Project implementation and construction is already ongoing.
sponsor_shareholders: BUA is a listed company on the Nigerian stock exchange, with publicly disclosed information on its financials and shareholding. At the time of this disclosure the company is majority owned and controlled by Abdulsamad Isyaku Rabiu (where he owns 56 percent of the shares directly, and an additional 35 percent indirectly). Mr. Abdulsamad Rabiu is a Nigerian businessman and chairman and majority shareholder of BUA Group, Headquartered in Nigeria. BUA Group is a leading conglomerate, with diversified investments spanning multiple sectors including – cement, sugar, pasta, rice, real estate development, port management, and steel.
