total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC seeks to provide up to US$500 million to the Company, which will be made up of US$150million in IFC A Loan and US$350million in mobilization from other lenders in B loans and Parallel loans.
location_description: Kalambaina, Sokoto State, Northern Nigeria.
development_impact: Through the proposed investment, IFC will support a leading cement manufacturer in Nigeria improve access to good quality cement at affordable prices in Northern Nigeria and neighboring land locked countries. IFC's additionality in this Project comes in two forms: (i) Economy wise and employment effects in the form of contributing to GDP by supporting domestic value addition to available natural resources (i.e., limestone and clay) and creating direct and indirect jobs ; and (ii) Improved access and sustainability in the form of eliminating longdistance trips to source cement for customers in Sokoto and other northern regions as well as support cleaner power generation solutions not widely present in the northern parts of Nigeria. The Project will also include provisions of IFC's value-add advisory services as outlined above.
additionality: IFC's involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide long dated financing that is not otherwise readily available in Nigeria. IFC will also mobilize other lenders into the Project. IFC will provide advice to the Company on how to raise operating standards in the cement operations in Nigeria- in the areas of E&S risk management to meet World Bank Group requirements; on initiatives to reduce CO2 emissions considering global commitments to the Paris accords; and also on corporate wide efforts to enhance gender related opportunities.

project_description: Founded in 1932, Maquinaria y Vehículos S.A. (Mavesa or the Company) is a family-owned, leading distributor of specialized vehicles from well-known brands including Hino and Citroen among others. The Company has a wide portfolio of mostly commercial vehicles, including buses, heavy-weight trucks, construction equipment, and light cargo vehicles utilized in multiple industries in Ecuador. The Company also owns and operates a network of 33 specialized vehicle shops and service centers across 12 cities, providing full after-sales services to customers. As part of its business model, Mavesa finances part of heavy-weight vehicles sales to its clients, mostly microentrepreneurs, who need long-term financing and competitive rates from the Company given their limited resources versus the relative high cost of the vehicle, and the fact that local banks don’t have sufficient appetite for the relative informality of the transportation activity. The proposed investment will be structured as a securitization-like structure of the Company’s loan portfolio, originated from the provision of heavy-weight vehicle financing to its clients, to partly finance Mavesa’s 2022-2024 investment plan related to working capital to finance the Company’s on-lending activities and growth post-COVID (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Mavesa is a private company ultimately majority owned by President Kleber Macleri Vaca, with a 98.8% shareholding interest, and his family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost stands at US$50 million and IFC’s investment consists of a financial package including a: (i) an A-Loan for an amount of up to US$30 million for IFC’s own account and; (ii) a “B2” loan for an amount of up to US$20 million for the account of participants under the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (“MCPP”) . The financing will be disbursed in a bankruptcy-remote trust which will purchase a portion of Mavesa’s loan portfolio.
location_description: Mavesa is headquartered in Guayaquil, Ecuador, and has regional presence in 12 cities in the country. The Project is located in Ecuador.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are the effects on consumers where the Company’s financing of heavy vehicles will enable microentrepreneurs to develop and run their businesses that would otherwise not be possible. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote competitiveness in the commercial vehicle retail industry in Ecuador.
additionality: Longer Tenor – IFC will be providing a long-term financing of 5-years which is not readily accessible for Mavesa given current market dynamics and relative informality of the segment where it operates. Resource mobilization – IFC will help mobilize funds for the Project (up to US$20 million). The "B2" Loan, will be provided at terms and conditions comparable to IFC’s “A” Loan under a structure currently not being replicated by local commercial banks in Ecuador, contributing to the development of a new financing product Standard Setting: As a first-time prospect, IFC will support Mavesa to enhance its E&S practices through the development and implementation of its E&S Management System in line with IFC’s E&S Performance Standards.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a senior secured syndicated loan package of up to €14 million to United Exports Limited (“UE” or “the Company”) and its subsidiaries. The proposed investment will support the Company’s €14 million investment program comprising of the following components: (i) fund frost mitigation measures on UE’s existing blueberry farms; (ii) support a blueberry farm expansion; and (iii) refinance existing debt (“the Project”). Established in 2004 in South Africa, the Company is involved in blueberries value-chain from farming, packing, processing, cooling, buying and selling. The Company sources blueberries from farms in South Africa and Zambia that it owns partially or entirely as well as from outsourced contract growers located in the Southern Africa region. United Exports focuses on the production and marketing of blueberries mainly to the export market. Its proprietary brand is OZblu® brand.
sponsor_shareholders: Born in South Africa, Mr. Roger Horak, an Australian national based in Australia, is the founder and ultimate owner of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, together with a syndication bank intends to provide a €14 million long-term loan package to support the Project.
location_description: The Company manages its farms that are located in the Western Cape, Gauteng and Limpopo provinces in South Africa as well as in Zambia.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to generate economy-wide effects from job creation and economic value-added through expansion. At the market level, the Project will help to strengthen the resilience of South Africa’s blueberry sector to frost and abnormal rainfall risk through, planting OZblu® varieties that fruit in alternate windows, R&D and implementation of innovative mitigation measures.
additionality: IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality comes from the provision of long-term financing and resource mobilization. Non-financial additionality comes from the support to the Company on its strategic and capital structure matters and possibly to provide a training program aimed at increasing the number of females in supervisory/middle management roles.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of a working capital loan of up to US$200 million to finance purchases of wheat, maize, and soya for delivery to Olam Global Agri Pte Ltd’s (Olam Agri) customers and processing operations in countries that rely on imports of these commodities. The proposed financing will support Olam Agri with sustaining commodity flows and contribute to food security mainly in West and Central Africa, South and South-East Asia, as well as Middle East and North Africa (MENA).
sponsor_shareholders: Olam Group Limited (OGL) – listed on the Singapore Stock Exchange – is a leading global agribusiness company that provides end-to-end supply chain solutions for a variety of agricultural raw materials and food ingredients. OGL’s key shareholders are Temasek Holdings (51.1 percent), Mitsubishi Corporation (14.4 percent), and Kewalram Chanrai Group (6.8 percent). Olam Agri is a subsidiary of Olam Group Limited that houses its commodity trading and agribusiness supply chain operations. Olam Agri’s product suite includes grains, oilseeds, wheat flour, animal feeds, edible oils, rice, cotton, rubber, and wood products. It is currently 100 percent owned by Olam, which has recently entered into an agreement to sell 35.4 percent of its ownership in Olam Agri to the Saudi Agricultural and Livestock Investment Company (SALIC).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of a senior corporate “A” loan for IFC’s own account of up to US$200 million to Olam Agri.
location_description: The proposed financing will support Olam Agri with sustaining commodity flows (wheat, maize and soy) and contribute to food security mainly in West and Central Africa, South and South-East Asia, as well as Middle East and North Africa (MENA).
development_impact: The Project will sustain flows of key food commodities of wheat, corn, and soy to over 10 countries in Africa, Asia, and Middle East regions. The most significant, expected project-level outcome is food security for consumers in countries affected by high food inflation. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater resilience in the global food supply market.
additionality: Financing Structure: The proposed financing is for the increased working capital requirements for key food commodities. As a result of the shocks from the war in Ukraine, working capital and trade financing needs for Olam Agri and other companies involved in crop production, trading and food processing, have increased following commodity price increases. Non-commercial risk mitigation, including trusted partnerships: IFC’s financing will provide confidence to the market on the commodity financing. Private sector companies in the agricultural commodities business are facing liquidity challenges. IFC has supported Olam through a number of investments over the past two decades.

company_name: EQUATORIAL COCA COLA BOTTLING COMPANY SL
project_description: The proposed investment is an up to €70 million package comprised of up to € 53million A-Loan from IFC’s own account and up to €17million equivalent loan from IFC acting as the implementing entity of the Canada IFC Blended Finance Program (“BCFP”) Loan to Equatorial Coca Cola Bottling Company SL (“ECCBC” or “the Company”).
sponsor_shareholders: ECCBC is a bottling company for The Coca Cola Company (“TCCC”) across 13 African countries including Morocco, Algeria, Ghana, Guinea Conakry, Cape Verde, Liberia, Gambia, Mauritania, Sierra Leon, South Sudan, Guinea Bissau, Equatorial Guinea and Sao Tome and Principe. With 27 production lines and 7 bottling plants, the Company produces, commercializes and distributes soft drinks, juices, energy drinks and malt. It was founded in 1997 in Equatorial Guinea and expanded through acquisitions. ECCBC’s main shareholder is the Daumeridian Invest, SL., which owns about 74% stake in the Company and The Coca-Cola Export Corporation (TCCEC) with about 26% stake.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is expected to be €80million and the proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to €53 million and a BCFP Loan of up to €17million and internal cash flow generation. The loans will be used to finance ECCBC’s sustainability CAPEX and working capital needs.
location_description: The proposed investment will support the Company’s capacity expansion program and sustainability initiatives in North Africa (Morocco and Algeria) and West Africa (Ghana, Cape Verde and Guinea Bissau) Regions.
development_impact: Project Outcomes: IFC expects the Project will: i) Create ~26 direct jobs plus about 6,510 indirect and induced jobs throughout the value chain, because of increased production and downstream effects on the retail value chain ii) Increase outreach and improve business of the distributors and retailers especially in the rural areas of West Africa iii) Contribute to a low-carbon pathway by virtue of more efficient compressors and manufacturing processes, especially the replacement of existing refrigerants by ones with zero global warming potential. Market Creation: i) Increase competitiveness in the beverage sector in North and West Africa through the demonstration of the business case for resource efficient production processes.
additionality: Financial Additionality i) Financing structure: IFC will provide a loan with a 7-year tenor including a 2-year grace period for climate-related investments, which is not readily available in North and West Africa. ii) Innovative financing / instruments: The IFC Green Loan is an innovative financing instrument both as the Company’s first green bond, and in the deployment of blended funds to attain sustainability targets. Non-Financial Additionality i) Knowledge management and capacity building: IFC will support the Group to improve E&S standards, through the advice of the IFC industry specialists in implementing sustainability measures.
Company Name: EQUATORIAL COCA COLA BOTTLING COMPANY SL

project_description: Agencias Universales S.A. (“AGUNSA” or the “Company”) is a leading logistics provider and operator in Latin America that is based in Valparaiso, Chile. The Company has over 30 years of experience in both Chilean and international markets, is present in more than 20 countries and has more than 70 subsidiaries and associated companies that provide services to large global clients. AGUNSA’s main business lines include logistics, agency services, and operation of ports and airports. The proposed investment consists of a US$70 million unsecured loan, comprised of an A loan of up to US$35 million and a B loan of up to US$35 million. The investment will finance AGUNSA’s planned capex program at Terminal II in Port of Valparaiso and will also support the Company’s efforts to refinance and consolidate upcoming debt maturities.
sponsor_shareholders: Agunsa is wholly owned by Grupo Empresas Navieras (“GEN”), a renowned Chilean conglomerate with operations in maritime logistics and infrastructure. As of Dec. 31, 2021, approximately 77.93% of GEN’s is directly or indirectly owned by a group of Chilean families with presence in the Company’s Board, including the Urenda family, among others.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investments consists of an up to US$70 million loan facility, with a 7-year door-to-door tenor. The facility is expected to support Agunsa in its efforts to consolidate its existing funding facilities, refinance upcoming debt maturities and support a portion of the Company’s ongoing capital expenditures.
location_description: Agunsa is headquartered in Chile and generates more than 56% of its revenues in the country, as of December 31, 2021. Proceeds are expected to be deployed in the consolidation of existing debts at the Chilean level and capital expenditures in Chile.
development_impact: Stakeholders - Access and Quality. The project will allow the continuity to the operation of Valparaiso’s Terminal 2 under a short-term concession, thus maintaining access and quality to port users. To maintain the terminal level of service the client has committed to purchase equipment to support vessel and land side operations for both containerized and general cargo. The project will also allow the company to continue growing its logistics services portfolio (warehousing, labelling, consolidation and deconsolidation of containers, pallets dismantling/assembly, temperature-controlled storage), which was up 8% in YoY basis, and to consider the potential expansion of its geographic footprint outside of Chile. Market Level - Competitiveness. The Project will contribute to maintaining market competitiveness by supporting a key player introducing innovative services and practices into Chile’s logistics sector. Agunsa is implementing technology solutions like a virtual trucking services exchange portal that contributes to improve asset utilization which results in lower vehicle operating costs per unit of cargo transported and can potentially result in lower costs to customers. In addition, the platform’s real time pricing increases price transparency for customers. The platform also increases reliability of trucking services by offering tracking cargo capabilities which adds visibility to the logistics chain. By demonstrating the business case of this innovative services, the project is expected to promote the development of a more sophisticated sector and effectively contribute to economic distance between Chile and its commercial partners. Logistics competitiveness is an important driver of economic growth in Chile and accounts for 11.5% of its GDP (2020). Market Level - Financial Integration. The Project will pioneer the use of a sustainability-linked loan (SLL) in the logistics services sector in Chile, contributing to their increased adoption and helping draw ESG investors to the sector. Agunsa’s pioneering SLL will contribute to market development by demonstrating the viability of this instrument for a company of its size and by providing a model for structuring similar loans in the Chilean market. Replicating the SLL would allow mid-size companies to tap into the demand for assets that have a positive environmental impact, in order to diversify sources of financing.
additionality: Financial Additionality. Innovative financing structure. IFC is developing a Sustainability-Linked Loan structure for this transaction. IFC will guide the client developing the corporate framework/procedures necessary to enable the SLL. This structure would introduce an innovative financing alternative into the client’s portfolio that can be replicated to obtain future financing with lenders in the domestic market, and for Agunsa to eventually become a capital markets issuer. IFC long-term financing is a solution to consolidate short-term debt currently distributed across multiple financing institutions. Similar financing solutions with the proposed tenor are scarce in the domestic market, particularly for mid-sized corporates and for companies in the logistics sector that are heavily exposed to the effects of the Covid pandemic. Non-Financial Additionality Standard setting. IFC will provide support and guidance to help strengthen the Company’s capacity to manage environmental and social (“E&S”) risks associated with the Project through the implementation of IFC Performance Standards.

company_name: EGE ENDUSTRI VE TICARET A.S. EGE SERBEST BOLGE SUBESI
project_description: The proposed investment consists of senior loan package up to EUR40 million(mn) to Ege Endustri ve Ticaret A.S. (Ege Endustri or Company). Established in 1964 in Izmir, Turkey, the Company is an export-focused, Turkish manufacturer of axles and suspension system components (e.g., axle housings, drive axles, tag axles, trailer axles, self-steering tag axle, front axles, and front axles components) and its products are mainly used in heavy commercial vehicles. As of December 31, 2021, the Company has a total manufacturing capacity of 280K pieces per year and employs over 600 staff. Company’s investment plans include (i) consolidation of existing two plants in a new plant based in Aegean Free Zone in Izmir, Turkey, (ii) increase production capacity of conventional and electrical axles with additional product lines and (iii) upgrade Company’s production technology (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Company’s main shareholder is Ege Endüstri Holding A.S. (Ege Endustri Holding) with 65% shareholding while the remaining 35% is free float. Ege Endustri Holding is indirectly controlled by Bayraktar family with a majority shareholding of 69% while other shareholders are Gurel Family and Mahmut Mahir Kusculu owing respectively with 29% and 2%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$59mn and includes Company’s greenfield plant capex in Turkey. The US$59mn Project cost will be financed by (i) IFC A loan of up to US$44mn (EUR40mn equivalent) and (ii) internal cash generation of US$15mn.
location_description: The Project will be located in Aegean Free Zone in Izmir, Turkey.
development_impact: Economywide effects-Increasing exports through value addition: Automotive (auto parts) industry is one of the primary drivers of Turkey’s exports and economic growth. In 2020, exports of vehicles and vehicle parts amounted to US$22.7 billion, representing 13% of total exports of goods and services. Vehicle parts, in turn, amounted to US$4.6 billion or 3% of total exports. Through the Project, the Company will increase its exports, directly contributing to improving Turkey’s current account deficit (CAD) – particularly important amid the volatile macroeconomic context experienced recently by the country. The Project is anticipated to contribute to the Turkish economy by both direct value addition, as well as through indirect effects induced in the value chain. Finally, IFC anticipates that through increased backward linkages, the Project will contribute to indirect employment in Ege Endustri’s supply chain. Integration: The automotive supplier industry is well developed in Turkey. In 2020, overall vehicle parts represented 2.6% of Turkish exports, valued at US$4.6 billion. The most important challenges faced by Turkish automotive suppliers are (i) subdued adoption of new technologies, which may result in lower value-added products and associated decline in margins, given the increase in global demand for technology-based products and (ii) limited strategizing and investment to develop the necessary capabilities and positioning to remain competitive in the future. It is imperative for the Turkish automotive supplier industry to prepare for the transition from traditional systems to higher-technology adoption, per the market dynamics as global automotive OEMs are ramping up their production of electric vehicles (EVs) and hybrid engine models. Ege Endustri has emerged as one of the leading players among Turkish automotive suppliers, through continuous investment in technology, research and development, cost competitiveness and capacity expansion. IFC’s Project will build on Ege Endustri’s ongoing strategy for the electrification of its products. The consolidation in a single facility of two existing plants and adoption of robotic equipment for automated manufacturing technology will enable the Company to achieve economies of scale and increased cost-efficiency, expanding the output capacity to produce axles and suspensions for e-trucks. The success of the Project will provide demonstration effects to other automotive suppliers in Turkey to improve their cost-efficiency, enhance operating standards, and expand capacity for local production of higher-technology products, which can potentially strengthen their forward linkages and integration with global OEMs. The Turkish automotive suppliers will be incentivized to follow suit, amid increasing pressures in the global supply chain as automotive industry leaders gradually increase the electrification of their products. Furthermore, in the long-term, Ege Endustri’s capacity expansion for e-truck components has the potential to support local OEMs of electrified heavy commercial vehicles in Turkey.
additionality: -Financing structure: The proposed engagement will enable IFC to perform its countercyclical role in the current volatile market environment in Turkey where the liquidity is strained. IFC will be providing a EUR corporate loan with a tenor of 8 years. The proposed IFC Loan will enable the Company to reduce its funding risk by providing a longer tenor and diversifying its funding base. -Standard setting: The Project will give IFC the opportunity to reassess the Company’s E&S policies and practices in detail and introduce corrective actions where necessary to bring them to international standards.
Company Name: EGE ENDUSTRI VE TICARET A.S. EGE SERBEST BOLGE SUBESI

country: Middle East, Pakistan, and Afg Region
project_description: The proposed project involves up to US$40 million of equity in Alcazar Energy Partners II ('AEP II'), a closed end infrastructure fund with a target size of US$500m. AEP II will invest in a diversified portfolio of renewable energy ('RE') projects across selected emerging markets with a primary focus on onshore wind, solar PV and storage in MENA, Eastern Europe and Central Asia.
sponsor_shareholders: Alcazar Energy Partners II GP S.r.l ('Alcazar Energy') headquartered in Luxembourg, will act as the Investment Advisor of AEP II.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Proposed IFC commitment of up to US$40 million.
location_description: The Fund will make investments across various countries in MENA, Eastern Europe and Central Asia.
development_impact: The main project-level effect is on stakeholders through the increased affordability of renewable energy capacity in the target markets as well as the associated environmental effects through decarbonizing power generation and displacing aging baseload. Beyond the project, the investment is expected to help enhance the power sector resilience through diversifying the energy mix in the target markets.
additionality: Through this Project, IFC's strong financial additionality is derived from providing equity investment that is not available in the market. In addition, IFC non-financial additionality is provided through risk mitigation and standard Setting
Country: Middle East, Pakistan, and Afg Region

project_description: IFC is supporting expansion of organized food retail in the lower-income consumer segments in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro and North Macedonia (the Target Balkan Countries) and addressing investment needs in the food retail sector in Romania and Moldova (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Schwarz Group, a privately held retail chain based in Germany and operating in different countries in Europe under the Lidl and Kaufland brands. The Project companies are Kaufland Romania S.C.S. and Lidl Stiftung & Co. KG, which are wholly owned by Schwarz Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost to be incurred in the 2022 financial year is estimated at over €600 million. The proposed IFC investment is an up to €175 million A loan for IFC’s own account to partially finance the Project.
location_description: Investments under the Project are planned to be made in different cities of Romania, Moldova and the Target Balkan Countries of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro and North Macedonia.
development_impact: The Project will enhance access to quality affordable food in the Target Balkan Countries, create jobs, including for vulnerable population and Ukrainian migrants, and contribute to strengthening the food supply chain in all project countries. The Project will also promote market competitiveness in the Target Balkan Countries by increasing penetration of modern retail and by demonstrating higher performance standards for energy efficiency in new stores and warehouses built as part of the Project.
additionality: IFC will provide a countercyclical loan during the war in Ukraine, which will strengthen the regional food supply chain and enhance access to quality affordable food for the vulnerable population. The loan will have a significantly longer tenor compared to the terms available in the local markets. IFC will also provide non-financial additionality by supporting Kaufland Romania's first ‘green' loan certification and helping Schwarz to pilot its first Zero Carbon Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies (EDGE) green building certification.

project_description: Agrocorp International (“Agrocorp” or the “Company”) is a mid-scale agricommodity trader headquartered in Singapore that is the largest supplier of wheat and pulses to Bangladesh. Agrocorp sources commodities from over 40 key origin countries and has customers in 30 countries, from Asia to Sub Saharan Africa. It trades over 12 million metric tons (MT) of commodities annually, dealing in staples such as pulses/legumes, wheat, rice, maize, soybeans, raw cashew, sugar, grains, oilseeds, and cotton.
sponsor_shareholders: Agrocorp is incorporated in Singapore as a private limited company. The company is wholly owned by the founders, Vijay Iyengar, Akila Vijay and Ravi Raghavan. This loan is being extended to the HQ entity in Singapore, with use of proceeds earmarked specifically to support the flow of wheat and pulses from Canada and Australia to Bangladesh.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at USD 32.5 million. USD 18 million will be provided via an own account A loan with the remaining USD 14.5 million coming from the International Development Association’s Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA-PSW-BFF), as further described in the Blended Finance Section.
location_description: The project will support Agrocorp’s trading flows of wheat and pulses going into Bangladesh.
development_impact: The Project will support the Company’s working capital facilities in Canada and Australia, ensure the smooth running of Agrocorp’s facilities, and increase flows of wheat and pulses towards Bangladesh. Access to working capital is essential for agri-processing. The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is the impact on consumers in Bangladesh through the provision of safe, nutritious, and calorie-rich staple food. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater market resilience via market enabling channels.
additionality: IFC’s financial additionality in this Project centers around provision of long-term working capital at longer tenors that are otherwise unavailable to the Company. This is complemented by non-financial additionality in the form of standard setting to continue strengthening the Company’s Environmental and Social (E&S) practices.

sector: Garment and Apparel (Without Fabric , Excluding Footwear)
project_description: The investment entails the expansion of the existing cut-make-trim (“CMT”) operations of DTRT Apparel Ltd (“DTRT”, or “the Company”) through the establishment of a new 31,000 sqm upgraded garment factory area to increase capacity from 50 sewing lines to 107 sewing lines by 2026 (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: DTRT is 48%-owned by its founding executives Skip Richmond and Marc Hansult. The remaining shareholders of the Company are Verod Capital Management (Fund III) and Red Bull GmbH, who hold 42% and 10% of the Company respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at US$12.26 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$4 million corporate A-loan and a US$4 million subordinated loan provided by International Development Association Private Sector Window (“IDA PSW”) to support the Company in implementing the Project.
location_description: The funds will be used in DTRT’s two CMT facilities located in Accra and in Tema, in the Republic of Ghana.
development_impact: Economy-wide effects- The Ready-Made Garments (“RMG” sector in West Africa was badly hit during the onset of the pandemic and it is gradually recovering. Against this backdrop, the Project is expected to have various positive economy-wide effects, including i) domestic value addition and grow exports from the region through the expansion of the CMT operations and increasing product complexity (including potential production of PPE); ii) the direct creation of 2,900 formal manufacturing jobs, mostly for women, and a larger number of indirect jobs. Contribution to market creation Market Competitiveness: The Project is expected to improve the sector competitiveness through the expansion of the CMT operations to achieve scale, and therefore improve the efficiency of apparel production in the West Africa region and through backward integration (the 2nd phase of the Project). The capacity for DTRT to produce fabric for other companies in phase 2 will create an additional opportunity to serve other apparel manufacturers on the African continent, particularly those that are increasingly focused on establishing West African CMT operations and would benefit from locally produced fabrics (e.g., Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, Cote d'Ivoire). As such, as the first mover in the Ghanaian market to integrate its operations at scale, DTRT can serve a significant demonstration effect, and case study for building the textiles sector in West Africa. This could have significant ripple effects, attracting other investors and players in the region, and permitting the West African textiles sector to follow the trajectory of other successful cases (Bangladesh and Sri Lanka) and to develop in ways that will not be possible without this type of first-mover investment.
additionality: Financial additionality- Financing Structure: (i) IFC will provide customized financing with multiple tranches to match the CMT ramp-up (in USD) with 6-year tenor (including 2-year grace period) which is not readily available to the Company in the local market; (ii) IFC will potentially provide concessional IDA PSW financing which will help de risk the project given the limited available security package. Non-Financial additionality- Knowledge Innovation and Capacity Building: (i) IFC will continue providing upstream support, to properly integrate the CMT with the upcoming fabric mill; (ii) IFC will help DTRT strengthen the workplace policies for the female workforce (i.e. gender). Standard setting- IFC can potentially enhance DTRT's E&S practices through IFC performance standards. IFC can do so during supervision by supporting the Company implement E&S action plan and recommendations.

company_name: BAF VIETNAM AGRICULTURE JOINT STOCK COMPANY
project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of (i) a VND600 billion convertible bond and (ii) a VND300 billion senior bond to BaF Vietnam Agriculture Joint Stock Company (BaF or the Company) to support the Company’s capacity expansion of its farm and food business across Vietnam (the Project). The Project is expected to provide BaF with a significant platform and presence in a fragmented market. With Vietnam’s pork sector severely impacted by African Swine Fever (ASF), BaF’s expansion is expected to contribute to a recovery of pork supply as well as an improvement in biosecurity across Vietnam.
sponsor_shareholders: The project Sponsors are (i) Mr. TRUONG Sy Ba, the Chairman and Founder of Tan Long Group Joint Stock Company (Tan Long Group), (ii) Tan Long Group, and (iii) Siba Holdings Joint Stock Company (Siba Holdings). Mr. Truong Sy Ba holds 88% ownership of Tan Long Group, and 98% ownership of Siba Holdings. Tan Long Group is the leading commodity trader of animal feed raw materials in Vietnam. Siba Holdings, an entity holding the farming, food, and technology assets of Mr. Truong Sy Ba, is the largest shareholder in BaF, with 20.5% ownership. Mr. Truong Sy Ba was appointed as the Chairman of BaF in March 2022.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is to support BaF’s 2021 – 2023 capex expansion plan totaling US$352.7 million equivalent and includes building and machinery for 13 sow farms, 18 hog farms, 2 feed mills, 1 slaughter and processing factory, and other costs for biological assets, systems, and office. The Project is expected to be funded by a combination of debt, quasi-equity / equity, and internal cash generation. The IFC investment will consist of a VND600 billion Convertible Bond (US$25.9 mn equivalent) and a VND300 billion senior bond (US$13.0 mn equivalent).
location_description: The Project includes the Company’s operations involving 13 sow farms, 18 hog farms, 1 slaughter and processing factory, and 2 feed mills at the following identified locations across Vietnam (locations not listed are as yet unidentified): Sow farms: Economic Village 2, Eatrol Commune, Song Hinh District, Phu Yen Province Hoi Thanh Base, Tan Hoi Commune, Tan Chau District, Tay Ninh Province Base 4, Suoi Day Commune, Tan Chau District, Tay Ninh Province Suoi Day Commune, Tan Chau District, Tay Ninh Province Dang Ha Commune, Bu Dang District, Binh Phuoc Province Po To Commune, Ia Pa District, Gia Lai Province Giai Xuan Commune, Tan Ky District, Nghe An Province Hog farms: Suoi Day Commune, Tan Chau District, Tay Ninh Province Hoa Hiep Commune, Tan Bien District, Tay Ninh Province Thanh Binh Commune, Tan Bien District, Tay Ninh Province Thung Base, Duc Binh Dong Commune, Song Hinh District, Phu Yen Province Slaughter and processing factory: Block B1 Minh Hung - Sikico Industrial Park, Dong No Commune, Hon Quan District, Binh Phuoc Province Feed mills: Nam Cam Industrial Park, Nghi Xa Commune, Nghi Loc District, Nghe An Province Nhon Hoa Industrial Park, Binh Dinh Province
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good. The Project is assessed as part of the overarching programmatic intervention (ASF Asia Recovery Program) to respond to the impacts of the ASF on the regional pork industry. The most significant, expected Project-level outcome resulting from this expansion is the impact on consumers from the provision of safe pork at the time of severe supply shortage as well as implementation of advanced biosecurity procedures at the new farms. At the market level, the Project, alongside other planned investment, and advisory interventions, is expected to promote market resilience through improvement of biosecurity and disease management, both by supporting industry consolidation and disseminating best practices among smaller players.
additionality: Financing structure: The proposed transaction is an investment of up to VND900 billion (US$39 million equivalent). This type of financing is not readily available in the Vietnam agribusiness sector. The financing package will help strengthen the Company's capital structure and improve liquidity. This is especially important during the current period of market disruption, as the industry has been severely affected by outbreaks of ASF and is experiencing additional turmoil stemming from the COVID-19 pandemic. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC is looking to provide technical expertise and facilitate knowledge sharing on animal welfare best practices. As part of this initiative, IFC is exploring an opportunity to provide advisory services to support the Company with designing and implementing a group housing transition for its pig farming operations. Standard setting: IFC will support BaF to implement best practices through raising the level of compliance to that of IFC's Performance Standards, European-level animal welfare standards, and industry best practices.
Company Name: BAF VIETNAM AGRICULTURE JOINT STOCK COMPANY

project_description: The proposed investment is a corporate loan to three Cabo Verdean group entities of the O?sis Atl?ntico? Group (OA), an established owner/operator, which has been running 4 and 5 star resort hotels for more than 25 years. The Co-Borrowers of this investment will be: (i) O?sis Atl?ntico Imobili?ria, S.A.; (ii) Sal H?teis, S.A., (iii) Hotelmar, S.A. The proceeds will be used to replace OA?s existing debt. The investment will enable OA to rationalize the lender group by repaying smaller lenders. It will also allow to: (i) enhance the Group?s financial structure, through longer maturities, mitigating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and provide operational liquidity for the Group during the anticipated sector recovery period (2021-2025);? and (ii) free up cash generation required to finance critical maintenance capex, which will ensure that the hotels remain compliant with the global best industry standards.
sponsor_shareholders: OA originated in the 1990?s as a vehicle to invest in hotels in Cabo Verde. At present, OA remains controlled by its founders and has been growing through acquisitions and by developing greenfield hotels. Currently it operates in:? (i) Cabo Verde, with three owned 4-star resorts and one owned 5-star resort; (ii) Brazil, with two leased 4-star resort hotels in the Northeastern city of Fortaleza, Cear? state; and (iii) Morocco, with a 5-star resort hotel, through a JV established in 2018 with a Moroccan partner (Med Hospitality), in the city of Sa?dia. OA is owned by 16 individuals and 2 entities representing 6 family offices. The largest 4 families collectively own over 87%: with 35.18% held by the Abade family, 24.27% held by the Pacheco family, 15% held by the Camacho family and 13% held by the N?brega family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is a 42 million debt package expected to be comprised of: (i) up to 10.5 million in and A loan from IFC's account; (ii) up to 10.5 million subordinated loan in USD equivalent from IDA PSW Blended Finance Facility; and (iii) up to 21 million in B loan/parallel loans (with a B loan of 7.5 million and parallel loans of 13.5 million).
location_description: Oasis Atlantico Imobiliaria and Sal H?teis are located in Santa Maria beach in Sal Island. Hotelmar is located in Praia city, Island of Santiago.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project outcome to be contribution to the recovery of tourism sector. Its development impact is expected through job preservation and purchase of goods and services from local SMEs and farmers. It will allow OA to mitigate some of the negative impact expected from the crisis, allowing OA not only to keep its staff on payroll but to pay their full contractual wages. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that the project has the potential to promote greater market resilience by limiting disruptions along supply chains and ensuring continued supply of goods and services in sectors affected by reduced demand, price reductions and FX rate volatility thereby mitigating the effects of the economic downturn.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC will support OA to preserve a strong and resilient hotel portfolio in CV, which is important in the context of hotels? contribution to job creation and their role as an essential part of Cabo Verde's economy. IFC's additionality in this Project comes mainly in two forms: (i) provision of customized long-term foreign currency financing which will address liquidity constraints in response to the COVID 19 pandemic. The PSW loan is required to make the financing structure more resilient to challenges of the difficult to predict post pandemic business and leisure tourism environment. The investment will also rationalize the lender group, making the financing structure more feasible from a security sharing perspective, and (ii) standard-setting with regards to environmental and corporate governance guidance in line with the best international practices to reform and modernize OA's structures and practices.

project_description: Zambeef Products Plc (“Zambeef” or the “Group”) is one of the leading agribusinesses with integrated operations in Zambia, focusing on cropping, stock feed production, animal breeding and rearing, meat processing, retail and distribution of meat products and stock feed. The investment supports the Company’s US$61.5 million capacity expansion program and resultant incremental working capital requirements.
sponsor_shareholders: Zambeef Products PLC is a listed Company on the Lusaka Securities Exchange (“LuSE”) and the Alternative Investment Market (“AIM”) of the London Stock Exchange. The majority shareholders are institutional investors consisting of: CDC (17.3%), African Life Financial Services (14.1%), National Pension Scheme Authority (8.1%), M & G Investment Management (8.1%), SBM Securities (5.2%) and other shareholders (47.2%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project Cost is expected to be c. US$61.5 million. IFC is looking to provide an own account A Loan of up to US$35 million in Zambian Kwacha (“ZMW”), hedged through cross-currency swaps provided by the IDA-PSW LCF. In addition, the project is expected to be supported by Blended Finance, as described in the Blended Finance Section. The remainder of the financing will be funded by internally generated funds.
location_description: The proposed investment will support the Company’s capacity expansion and operational improvements at Huntley farm , Chisamba, Lusaka and Chambatata farm in Mpongwe, Zambia.
development_impact: Project level impacts: (i) Economy wide effects: The project will expand Zambeef’s production capacity and allow the company to source more inputs from local suppliers thereby supporting domestic value addition and associated job creation. The estimates of increase in GDP, value added, and jobs will be assessed using IFC’s economic impact assessment framework. (ii) Stakeholders – Consumers: Increased access to quality and nutritious foods. The project will increase production of affordable quality, safe and nutritious meat products thereby increasing access to the products across the country especially among the largely BoP consumers. Coupled with investments in the distribution system, the project is expected to increase the volume of meat products sold to consumers. Market level impact: Competitiveness: Adoption of new production technology, changes in market structure and greater value addition. IFC expects the project, through demonstration and replication channel, to contribute to increasing the competitiveness of the food processing sector through the Client’s local processing of a range of food products. The project will support vertical integration by Zambeef and acquisition of on- and off-farm modern production technologies to expand production capacity and improve efficiency in production while ensuring product quality and safety. The project will ensure full implementation/acquisition of the requisite quality certifications. Taken together, these will show case the potential for vertical integration in the sector, adoption of modern and efficient production technologies to expand production of a range of food products at affordable prices. The project will not only shape the market structure by building the food processing base and market shares for the products but also reduce production costs and achieve economies of scale. This will encourage other players to replicate the business model to increase the competitiveness of the sector.
additionality: Financial additionality -Financing structure: long-term local currency funding when Zambia has a challenge in liquidity. Zambian banks are facing single borrower limit and could not provide adequate long-term capital to Zambeef. Non-financial additionality- Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: Zambeef will continue to tap into expertise of IFC in the development and implementation of E&S and climate smart practices, to align Zambeef’s operations with IFC performance standards and industry best practices.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a senior secured A Loan of up to USD 4.5 million to Bergman Industries Limited (“BM Group” or the “Group”), leading animal feed premix manufacturer and feed additives distributor with operations in Israel and Nigeria. The investment will support BM Group’s USD 4.9 million expansion in Nigeria in (i) increasing premix production capacity by 3000MT and concentrates production capacity by 2000MT in Nigeria; (ii) increasing the warehouse capacity by 2,600 m2; (iii) setting up a state-of-the-art laboratory; (iv) expanding the on-ground technical support team and enhancing the market outreach; and (v) meeting permanent working capital (together, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: BM Group is 100 percent owned by Rami Bergman (the “Sponsor”), the Founder and Co-CEO of BM Group. He has nearly four decades of industry experience.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is USD 4.9 million; IFC’s proposed investment consists of an A Loan of up to USD 4.5 million to BM Group supported by a 30 percent First Loss Guarantee from Global Agriculture and Food Safety Program (GAFSP).
location_description: The Project will be located in Ibadan, Nigeria within the existing land and area of operation where the Group has warehouses, premixes and concentrates production lines.
development_impact: The Project claims are stakeholders (farmers) as the primary claim via the provision of increased access to quality and affordable animal feed additives, and economy-wide effects on value added and job creation as the secondary claim. Beyond the project level, IFC expects the investment to promote market competitiveness in the livestock sector in Nigeria, by strengthening, through local production, the availability of key feed complements, such as salt licks, mineral blocks, and concentrates.
additionality: BM Group is interested in both financial and non-financial aspects of additionality that IFC brings to this Project. On financial additionality, IFC is providing long-term financing in Nigeria at tenors that are otherwise not readily available to private sector companies. IFC’s non-financial additionality centers around supporting BM Group’s operations, including through Advisory services to strengthen the corporate governance structure.

sector: Other Steel Products (Including Wire, Metal Sheets etc.)
project_description: Zener SA (Zener or the Company) is a full-service, integrated energy provider operating in Togo, across the LPG full value chain with the only seaborne LPG import facility for end-user distribution to industrial, commercial, and residential (urban and rural) markets, as well as export. The proposed investment is up to EUR 7 million (m) IFC A loan and mobilization of up to EUR 14m in Parallel loans, to finance (i) Zener’s LPG terminal capacity expansion and (ii) support the establishment of five gasoline retail stations for the distribution of white products, solar kits, and LPG bottles exchange (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Zener SA (Zener) was established in 2007 as Sodigaz SA. The name was changed in 2021 to Zener SA following a rebranding into an integrated energy provider. Zener was founded by Mr. Jonas A. Daou, a Togolese who owns 69.79% and the balance is owned by other Togolese individuals who are minority shareholders. An affiliate entity, Power and Gas Storage SA, Togo (PGS) will implement the expansion of the LPG terminal. The ultimate beneficiary of PGS is Mr. Jonas Daou, through another affiliate, called Oseor Sarl SA, Togo. All the entities are registered in Togo.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at EUR 24m, to be financed with EUR 21m debt. The IFC A loan is proposed for EUR 7m with up to 9-years tenor (including 3 years grace period).
location_description: The Project will be sited next to the existing operation of Zener in the industrial zone in Lome, while the filling stations will be across Togo at Agoè Deux lions (in lome) and Nyékonakpoè, Kpalimé/ Kpéta, Tsévié/Kpali, and Atakpamé/Avétè.
development_impact: According to the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2019, only 9.3% of the Togolese population consumed clean technologies for cooking. Firewood represents 99% of primary energy production , where more than 36% of the firewood is used by households for cooking. Heavy reliance on biomass fuels for household consumption entails severe negative health effects. These fuels are inefficient energy sources and produce a range of pollutants associated with detrimental health outcomes. While replacing biomass with LPG remains a switch to fossil fuels, this change represents an important step in the country’s move towards cleaner energy sources. The current use of biomass in Togo is unsustainable and contributes to the country’s high levels of deforestation. The most significant expected project-level outcomes are increased access to LPG products, with improvements in household’s air quality and resultant health effects, especially for women and children, especially in undeserved rural areas. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the Project will further promote Competitiveness of LPG production in the market through demonstration effects in other market players in improving LPG access, in particular to undeserved rural populations as an energy transition fuel.
additionality: IFC and the banks it will mobilize will provide foreign currency and long-term financing which is not readily available in the local market due to COVID-19 pandemic and send a "signaling mechanism" to other investors on climate related projects. IFC will contribute to the development of Zener’s environmental, health, safety and social practices in line with World Bank Group requirements.

project_description: Bocom Petroleum (“Bocom”) is a downstream distributor of petroleum products in Cameroon (i.e. LPG, lubricants, gasoline, diesel and kerosene). It operates its own network of 80 fuel stations throughout the country, as well as an LPG storage and cylinder filling plant, and a lubricant blending facility. Bocom owns the only private LPG coastal storage facility in Cameroon, which is essential for cooking gas distribution in the country, and necessary to promote clean cooking practices across the country. Bocom is also the only manufacturer of lubricants – through a blending process- in Cameroon (and Central Africa), which is essential to ensure the reliable supply of well-priced quality lubricants to various consumer segments in the country. Availability of quality lubricant’s ensures automobiles and machinery are efficiently run in Cameroon, with lower maintenance costs, prolongs useful lives of auto\machinery, and reduces unnecessary replacement costs. The Project entails the further diversification of Bocom from white products, and growth of its cleaner and higher value downstream product (LPG and Lubricants). It entails the expansion of Bocom’s LPG business through added storage and filling capacity in Douala, and establishing LPG centers across multiple provinces in the country, (which supports clean cooking across the country); and the expansion of its lubricants blending facility capacity in Douala. The project is expected to be supported by the IDA19 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Bocom is 100% owned by Mr. Bougne, a Cameroonian entrepreneur and businessman, and his family members.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at EUR50m. The proposed IFC investment is EUR50m financing package made up of EUR25m in IFC A Loan, EUR15m in IDA PSW loan, and EUR10m in B1 or parallel loan(s).
location_description: The Project location is in Cameroon and in particular in Douala, Yaoundé, Bansoa, Bertoua, Ngaoundere and Pitoa.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is increased access to LPG products to support clean cooking in underserved areas of the country. LPG use improves household’s air quality especially for women and children compared the widespread use of firewood or charcoal for cooking. The project will also increase access to high quality lubricants in a market where access to lubricants is quite poor in most of the country, and thereby, efficiency of automotives' engine combustion is low with the consequent detrimental effects on GHG emissions. Beyond these, the Project will also contribute to mitigate one of the deforestation drivers by displacing the use of unsustainable firewood and charcoal, support job creation in Cameroon and contribute to the country’s GDP through forward linkages with LPG retailers, and contribute significantly to improve the competitiveness of the LPG and Lubricants market in Cameroon through a sizable expansion in capacity, enhanced operational and distribution efficiency, and adoption of improved safety standards.
additionality: Financial Additionality: IFC will provide long-term finance which is not readily available in the local financial market. IFC will also mobilize EUR 15m to complete the financial plan. IFC's long-term financial commitment will allow the Company to continue with its expansion strategy amid increasing security risks in the country which negatively impact the supply of credit. Non-Financial Additionality: IFC will support the Project in terms of the adoption of international quality and safety standards in terms of health, safety and social practices, and corporate governance, which will help set an example for other market players to follow. Advisory Services: IFC to provide advisory services on (i) LPG value chain development to help Bocom develop sales and distribution models of LPG to maximize its reach in the country, and (ii) gender advisory to provide BOCOM’s leadership and HR team with the information, skills, and support to build a solid and impactful gender sustainability strategy.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to US$30 million in the form of funded participation (IFC Participation) in an up to US$80 million uncommitted secured trade facility (the Facility) arranged by Absa Bank Limited (acting through its Corporate and Investment Banking division) (Absa or the Bank) for Volcafe Ltd. (Volcafe or the Company) and its East African subsidiaries: namely, Kyagalanyi Coffee Limited (KCL) in Uganda, Taylor Winch Tanzania Limited (TWT) in Tanzania, and Taylor Winch Coffee Limited (TWK) in Kenya (the Project). The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA Private Sector Window’s Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW-BFF) to de-risk the investment.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1783, ED&F Man (the Group) is one of the largest traders of agricultural products with an annual revenue of over US$6.2 billion for FY2021 September. Sudzucker Holding GmbH owns strategic stake of 34.37%. The remaining 65.63% ownership is held by ED&F Man’s board, senior management and employees. ED&F Man’s coffee business, Volcafe, is one of the largest traders of Arabica and Robusta coffees providing beans for 80 billion cups of coffee a year.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Facility is an up to US$80 million uncommitted secured trade facility for the tenor of 12 months renewable twice. IFC Participation will be processed under the Global Warehouse Finance Program (GWFP) with delegated authority from the Board.
location_description: The Facility will finance the origination, processing, and storage and transport up to export port of coffee beans in Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya.
development_impact: The Project is expected to reach 77,000 farmers in Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya, safeguarding farmer livelihoods by providing access to markets and access to sustainable farming practices. Volcafe provides technical assistance and training to farmers through its “farming as a business” program, which aims to help farmers improve their coffee quality, farm productivity and yields, and train farmers on sustainable production, good agronomy, and making the best use of land. In addition, the program also helps them manage risks and exchange information with each other.
additionality: IFC has both financial and non-financial additionality in the Project. (i) Financial Additionality (Signaling Effect and Catalytic Role): IFC's participation sends a strong signal to the market and will play a role in the Facility's mobilization efforts by providing a stamp of approval for the Project structure and improve overall market perception. Furthermore, IFC's involvement provides comfort to other commercial lenders. (ii) Non-Financial Additionality (Knowledge Transfer, Innovation, and Capacity Building): IFC will contribute with its expertise to structure the transaction solidly. The adoption of IFC’s E&S Performance Standards would also promote broader sustainability standard setting in the industry.

project_description: The proposed transaction consists of a senior secured sustainability linked A Loan of BRL130 million with tenor of 8 years to Orizon Meio Ambiente S.A. (the “Company”), part of Orizon Valorização de Resíduos S.A., a leading waste management company in Brazil. The facility will be used for waste recycling and material recovery facilities (“MRFs”) and leachate treatment infrastructure, which are aligned with the circular economy concept. Orizon has assets located in several Brazilian states and has recently expanded its presence with the implementation of its organic and inorganic growth plan.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is controlled by Inovatec Participações S.A (52.6%), a company formed by (directly and indirectly): Milton Pilão, Ismar Assaly, Dalton Assumção Canelhas and Fábio Vettori. Milton Pilão and Ismar, as the largest shareholders, have past experiences as entrepreneurs in businesses unrelated to waste management. Ismar Assaly developed and sold a well-known canned tuna business (Gomes da Costa), and Milton Pilão’s family sold a manufacturer of equipment for the pulp and paper industry. Dalton Canelhas and Fabio Vettori are engineers with significant experience in Brazil.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC loan proceeds will be used for waste recycling and material recovery facilities (“MRFs”) and leachate treatment infrastructure, which are aligned with the circular economy concept. The total project cost amounts to BRL152 million, of which BRL140 million will be used for two MRFs and the remaining BRL12 million for two leachate treatment plants.
location_description: States of Rio de Janeiro and Pernambuco, Brazil. The MRFs will be located in Jaboatão dos Guararapes, state of Pernambuco, and São Gonçalo, state of Rio de Janeiro. The leachate plants will be located in São Gonçalo and Barra Mansa, both in the state of Rio de Janeiro.
development_impact: The direct anticipated impact of this project is to increase recycling capacity in Brazil while also contribute to GHG emissions reductions associated with the use of recovered materials. At market level, the project will be one of the first municipal solid waste management facilities to implement at scale materials recovery measures in Brazil and lead to increased adoption of this business model by other companies in the sector, further developing the circular economy concept. The Project will also pioneer the use of a sustainability-linked loan in the waste and environmental services sector in Brazil and in emerging markets, contributing to their increased adoption and helping draw ESG investors to the sector.
additionality: IFC offers both financial and non-financial additionality to Orizon. IFC is providing the company with the first Sustainability-Linked Loan (SLL) in the waste sector in Brazil. IFC will also share its global expertise to help the company integrate circular economy elements into its business model, and the Upstream team will assist Orizon in evaluating the potential diversification opportunities into new waste solutions. Finally, IFC’s involvement will improve the client’s access to financing by providing comfort to other potential investors in the Company’s recent restructuring and non-commercial risk mitigation measures.

project_description: City Group (“City” or the “Group”) is a leading player in processing and marketing of food commodities in Bangladesh. City entities provide Guarantee to Rupshi Flour Mills (#43149) an existing client in good standing. The proposed project, Rupshi Foods Limited (“RFL” or “the Company”) will vertically integrate the Group’s existing flour, sugar, and edible oil businesses with consumer products. The Company will produce candy and chocolate (6.4MT/day), cakes (181.6MT/day), biscuits and bakery items (100MT/day), condensed milk and powdered milk (70MT/day). The Company will be located in City Economic Zone, Rupshi, 30km from Dhaka (“the Project”) in the same economic zone as Rupshi Flour Mills.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Fazlur Rahman, along with his wife Mrs. Hamida Rahman and his grown-up children Mr. Md. Hasan and Ms. Shampa Rahman (together “the Sponsors”) founded City Group in 1972 to process and market essential food items in Bangladesh. Mr. Fazlur Rahman and Mr. Md. Hasan each owns 40% of the Company and Mrs. Hamida Rahman owns the balance 20%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Aggregate total Project cost is estimated at ~US$122.4 million and is proposed to be financed with long-term debt totalling US$83.3 million with the balance US$39.1 million through equity. Proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to US$20 million with a tenor of eight years including a two-year grace period.
location_description: The proposed Project will be located at in City Economic Zone at Rupshi which is 30 km from Dhaka in the Narayanganj district of Bangladesh.
development_impact: Project level impact (Economy wide effects): The Project will expand RFL’s processing capacities and allow the Group to source more inputs from local suppliers, which will support domestic value addition and associated job creation. Using IFC’s economic impact assessment framework we estimate that the Project will lead to an annual increase in GDP of US$ 239 million from 2030. This comprises 15,400 new jobs, 14,900 indirect jobs. The GDP (value added) multiplier is US$ 1.04 million per million US$ invested while the employment multiplier is 67 jobs per million US$ invested. Based on the financial model, revenue is projected to increase by 296 million US$. Market level impact (Competitiveness): Triggering new product offerings and supporting greater domestic value addition. IFC expects the project, through demonstration and replication channel, to contribute to increasing competitiveness of the consumer-packaged goods (CPG) sector and specifically in the production of dairy, bakery and confectionery products. The proposed investment will showcase the potential for domestic vertical integration downstream to take advantage of lower costs, security of supply and quality of inputs, and spearhead a replicable business model for other players with strong brand recognition, distribution strategy, lower cost of production per in-house production and scale of inputs, to increase their market shares through improvements in resource use efficiency, product diversity, quality and certification in a country where food quality and safety is a major concern. This will raise the bar in the CPG sector in Bangladesh and catalyze adoption of similar practices by other industry players.
additionality: Financial Additionality: The proposed investment is a patient senior loan of up to US$20 million with a tenor of 8 years (with 2 years grace) to implement a capex program. This kind of financing is not readily available for agribusinesses in Bangladesh. Non-financial Additionality- Standard setting: As this is a greenfield project, IFC will help the client develop a comprehensive ESAP plan and help close any gaps in the ESG standards of the Company and align Rupshi Food’s operations with IFC Standard and industry best practices., The Company will set standards which will demonstrate best practices for the sector commitment to environmental responsibility.

project_description: The proposed project consists of an A Loan of up to US$100 million and a B Loan of up to US$100 million, to Louis Dreyfus Company Finance B.V. (“LDC Finance” or the “Borrower”) for on-lending to Louis Dreyfus Company Brasil S.A. (“LDC Brasil”), to support a portfolio of eligible soy and corn farmers in Brazil that are committed to zero deforestation and conversion of native vegetation (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: LDC Finance is fully owned by Louis Dreyfus Company B.V. (“LDC” or the “Group”). The Group is owned by Louis Dreyfus family (55% ownership) and by the Abu Dhabi Developmental Holding Company PJSC (45% ownership).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at US$200 million, for which IFC will provide an A Loan of up to US$100 million and mobilize a B Loan of up to US$100 million.
location_description: The Project is expected to be located mainly in the states of Mato Grosso, Goias and Minas Gerais, Brazil.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome resulting from this investment is economic benefits for farmers and environmental impact by providing incentives for zero deforestation or conversion of natural habitat, building farmer capacity in certification, energy efficiency, and conservation agriculture for input use. At the market level, the Project will contribute to strengthening sustainability of the soybean and corn sectors in Brazil with the potential to demonstrate the feasibility of full traceability.
additionality: (i) Provision of long-term financing; (ii) Mobilization; (iii) E&S standards setting; (iv) Advisory services.

project_description: The proposed investment is a finance package of up to US$48.6 million comprised of: (i) approximately US$28.6 million of equity; and (ii) approximately US$20 million of secured ‘A’ Loan into Avacare Global (‘Avacare’ or the ‘Company” or the ‘Group’), an integrated distributor and manufacturer of pharmaceutical and healthcare consumable products in Sub-Saharan Africa. The investment provides patient capital and long-term financing to support the growth aspirations of the Company.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is majority owned by MJ Consultancy Services (the Sponsor) which represents the interests of Dr. Vikramkumar Naik (the Founder) and his family. An IFC investee fund, Amethis Fund II S.C.A. SICAR, holds a minority stake in the business.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is a finance package of up to US$48.6 million comprised of: (i) approximately US$28.6 million of common equity; and (ii) approximately US$20 million of a secured ‘A’ Loan.
location_description: Various countries in Sub-Saharan Africa.
development_impact: The project helps finance a manufacturer and supplier of pharmaceutical and healthcare consumable products in Africa. The most significant expected project-level outcome is an increase in access to healthcare supplies such as pharmaceuticals, healthcare consumables and disposables. The project will also likely result in the creation of new jobs and/or economic linkages to the rest of the economy. Beyond the project-level outcome, IFC anticipates that its financing could support greater market resilience as spillover effects accrue to the healthcare supply chains in these markets.
additionality: The proposed IFC financing has both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is delivered through long-term financing, comprising a loan with a tenor of up to ten years and an equity injection. Regarding non-financial additionality, IFC is expected to help the Company by sharing and transferring knowledge and global networks, as well as further strengthening corporate governance structures. IFC will also assist the Company improve environmental and social (E&S) standards across its operations.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to US$100 million unsecured, senior loan (“A” loan) to Imperial Capital Limited (“DTMC”), a wholly owned subsidiary of Imperial Logistics Limited (“Imperial” or the “Company” or the “Group”), an African focused provider of integrated market access and logistics solutions. The financing package will be used for general corporate and working capital purposes of the Group, growth capital expenditure and acquisitions across the Imperial Group.
sponsor_shareholders: DTMC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Imperial and forms part of the Group’s Group Treasury structure. Imperial is 100% owned by DP World Logistics FZE (“DP World”) via an intermediate South African holding company, Imperial Holdco (Pty) Ltd.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment in Imperial through DTMC is an unsecured IFC “A” loan of up to US$100 million with a tenor of up to seven years. The proposed investment is still subject to the agreement of commercial, and legal terms and conditions as well as regulatory approvals as required.
location_description: The proposed investment is a corporate finance loan to Imperial, which has a global presence in both emerging and developed markets and is Africa’s largest market access and logistics solutions provider.
development_impact: The project outcomes rating is composed of two claims: (i) Stakeholder Effect via increased access to healthcare products. The global shortage of healthcare supplies has led to worldwide competition for these supplies, making it difficult – particularly in developing countries – to purchase quality medical products at affordable prices. The Project will support operations in the Africa region, that will increase the distribution and sales of healthcare products that are needed in the response to COVID-19 and other diseases. The Project responds to the large need for improved healthcare logistics in Africa. This includes the need to improve cold-storage logistics as part of the roll out of COVID-19 and other vaccines; and (ii) Economy-wide effect via direct jobs created and gross value added. The project will help scale the production, distribution, and delivery of healthcare supplies that is likely to result in the creation of new jobs and/or economic linkages to the rest of the economy. To measure progress against this outcome, IFC will track direct jobs created.
additionality: The proposed IFC loan has both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality is delivered through long-term financing, comprising a loan with a tenor of up to seven years, for immediate needs. Non-financial additionality is expected to be evidenced by leveraging the presence and reach of IFC and the broader WBG in markets where the Company is seeking to grow. While experienced in Africa, Imperial has outlined is committed to its “Gateway to Africa” strategy which seeks to expand its operations on the continent.

project_description: The Project will provide financing to Enclave Power Company Limited (“EPCL” or “the Company”) to increase the attractiveness of the Tema Free Zones Enclave (“Tema FZ”) and Dawa Industrial Zone (“Dawa IZ”) by building (i) a 16.8 MWp capacity roof-top solar installation in Tema FZ (the “Solar Plant”), and (ii) the first phase of a water treatment plant in Dawa (the “Water Plant”) (together the “Project”). The Solar Plant and Water Plant will be implemented by Helios Solar Company Limited (“HSC”) and Southern Water Company Limited (“SWC”), respectively. EPCL is a private power distribution company and a subsidiary of LMI Holdings. It is responsible for distributing about 51.31 MW (Peak Average for 2021) of power purchased from the Volta River Authority to over 80 multinational and local manufacturing companies.
sponsor_shareholders: LMI Holdings (“the Sponsor”) is an industrial and property development group offering construction, land development, utilities and logistics services in Ghana. LMI is wholly owned by Mr. Kojo Aduhene, a Ghanaian entrepreneur.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$ 30 million. IFC is considering an investment of up to US$ 30 million from its own account to finance critical infrastructure to support LMI’s development plans in Tema FZ and Dawa IZ.
location_description: Funds will support LMI’s investments in Ghana, more specifically the Greater Accra Region. The projects will be located in Tema and Dawa, respectively ~30km East of Accra and ~64km North-East of Accra.
development_impact: The Project will improve the affordability of electricity supply in Tema FZ and Dawa IZ, improve the quality of water supply to the Dawa IZ, and reduce the associated CO2 emissions. The Project involves the construction of a 16.8 MWp rooftop solar installation that contributes to improving competitiveness of the industrial zones. It also adds a 4,000 m3/day water treatment plant, which will serve new tenants in the Dawa IZ with reliable potable water. At a market level, the Project will demonstrate the potential of on-site solar generation as a cost effective, reliable, and green alternative to thermal power from the grid. This investment will be the first private sector-led utility scale solar project developed by a Ghanaian company that can be replicated by other high-volume customers. The water facility also constitutes the first investment in Ghana to develop, build and operate a private-to-industries water treatment plant that can be replicated by similar large-scale facilities not adequately served by the water distribution network.
additionality: IFC’s additionality includes the provision of (i) US Dollar financing for a tenor beyond what is generally available in the market; (ii) Technical and E&S expertise to improve the overall E&S performance as well as introduce international best practice to the LMI group.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan to Pandurata Alimentos Ltda (Bauducco or the Company). Bauducco, founded in 1952, is a baked products company headquartered in Brazil, producing long shelf-life bread, panettones, toasts, and other baked products. The Company produces baked products under 3 complementary brands (Bauducco, Visconti and Tommy) to target different consumer segments. Bauducco is currently carrying out an investment program of about US$40 million over the next 2 years to expand its Bonsucesso plant to install an additional bread production line (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Bauducco was founded in 1952 and is fully owned by the Bauducco family
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at about US$40 million, and IFC’s investment consists of an A Loan of up to US$20 million.
location_description: The Project will be carried out in the Bonsucesso plant, located in Guarulhos, state of Sao Paulo
development_impact: The Project is expected to have positive economywide impacts in terms of job creation and value added, driven largely by the expansion of bread lines. In terms of market impact, Bauducco is expected to increase competitiveness of the sector through demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC expected additionality stems from its ability to engage strategically with the Company by offering a long-term financing facility at terms not readily available in the market. Additionally, IFC will enhance the Company’s E&S practices and procedures by supporting the Company in the implementation of the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP).

project_description: The proposed project involves a senior debt package of up to USD260 million to Seacom Limited (“Seacom” or the “Company”), a leading diversified, integrated digital infrastructure company with extensive broadband infrastructure across Africa. Seacom seeks to diversify from its subsea cable operations into the enterprise service provider market across the continent and refinance its short term debt with new longer-term debt (the “Project”). Through the Project, IFC will help one of the important digital infrastructure companies to increase its enterprise services capabilities to SMEs, medium and large corporates in South Africa, East Africa, and West Africa; leveraging its fiber network spanning 21,000 km (including 17,000 km on its submarine cable) as well as its strategic alliances on the 2Africa Cable and Equiano Cable. Seacom’s growth strategy will be achieved through strategic acquisitions and organic growth initiatives across its markets.
sponsor_shareholders: Project Company Seacom Limited is an established player in the African telecommunication sector, having brought the first subsea cable to Southern Africa in 2009.
