Since then, the Company has evolved in line with market dynamics and evolution into providing terrestrial transmission networks across several markets (including fragile and conflict-affected states (“FCS”) markets in the region. The Company is currently embarking on a five-year plan to diversify from its subsea cable operations in Southern, East and West Africa by building out its integrated enterprise business and expanding its footprint in the region. The Company is principally owned by Remgro (30%), IPS Cable System (40%), Convergence Partners (15%), and Sanlam (15%). Shareholders Remgro: Founded in 1968, Remgro is one of the leading investment holding companies in South Africa. It invests in listed and non-listed companies across various sectors and countries in Africa. To date, the company has invested about US$6.5 billion across its active markets and sectors. It also has other interests in the telecommunication sector in Africa., such as Dark Fiber Africa (“DFA”) and Vumatel (Pty) Limited. IPS Cable System (IPS): IPS is the industrial development arm of the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development (AKFED), formed in 1963. The company invests in financially sustainable and ethical projects capable of promoting economic development. To date, the company has more than $200m worth of assets in diversified sectors. Convergence Partners Investments (CPI): Established in 2006, CPI is an evergreen fund owned by the partners of Convergence Partners Africa, a highly respected investment management firm focused on Africa’s telecommunication and technology sectors. Convergence’s core strategy is premised on investing in companies focusing on inputs for the digital economy of sub-Saharan Africa, including digital technologies and ICT infrastructure. Convergence Partners Africa ha over US$400 million under management. Sanlam: Sanlam is a listed financial services provider in South Africa established in 1918. It is a diversified financial services group operating across several selected global markets. The company has over US$3 billion under management across the group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project costs are currently estimated at approximately USD 563 million. The proposed IFC investment includes an IFC A Loan of up to USD 100 million. IFC will also mobilize USD 160 million of debt from other commercial banks and parallel lenders for the Project. The balance will be funded by new equity and internally generated cashflow.
location_description: Seacom is domiciled in Mauritius. However, its main office is located in South Africa, and it has a presence in six other countries – Kenya, Djibouti, Uganda, Tanzania, Mozambique, and Rwanda. The Project will enable Seacom to expand its geographical footprint to at least another 12 African countries.
development_impact: The Project will contribute to the increased capacity of broadband networks and increased access, to IT services for businesses, potentially resulting in improved quality of broadband internet for end-users and enhanced productivity growth for businesses. The Project will also lead to increased competitiveness of the broadband market in selected countries, e.g., Ghana, via competition channels, and stronger economic integration in selected countries, e.g., South Africa and Kenya, by improving connectivity across value chains via the development of cloud/IT services. A successful expansion of submarine or terrestrial cable capacity under open access principles is expected to drop the wholesale price and level the playing field among retail operators, thereby improving the competitiveness of retail markets with a market-wide improvement in affordability and quality of connectivity in the relevant target countries.
additionality: The Project will benefit from IFC’s financial structuring and resource mobilization and nonfinancial additionality through standard-setting. IFC will provide up to USD 100 million while mobilizing up to USD 160 million in debt from MCPP, B-Loans, or Parallel Loans, in the form of long-term financing of up to 8 years for the Company to implement its expansion strategy. IFC will leverage its experience in aligning the Company’s E&S and Corporate Governance standards as part of the integration process after acquisitions as targeted in the business plan.

company_name: FONDO DE INVERSION COLECTIVA INMOBILIARIO VISUM RENTAS INMOBILIARIAS
project_description: IFC is considering providing an A Loan of up to COP 300 billion (approximately US$75 million equivalent) to “Fondo de Inversión Colectiva Inmobiliario Visum Rentas Inmobiliarias” (or “Visum”) to support Visum’s 2022 – 2024 investment program in Colombia.
sponsor_shareholders: Visum is managed by Visum Capital S.A.S. (“Visum Capital”), a professional team with extensive experience in the real estate sector in Colombia and in charge (directly or through third parties) of all origination, acquisition, development, and asset management aspects. Visum Capital is owned by BTG Pactual S.A. Comisionista de Bolsa S.A., a subsidiary of BTG Pactual, and Inverlink Estructuras Inmobiliarias S.A.S. (“Inverlink”). BTG Pactual is the largest investment bank in Latin America and Inverlink is a boutique investment bank in Colombia with more than 30 years of experience in the region. BTG Pactual and Inverlink are the Sponsors of the Project. Visum is owned by more than 1,200 investors including the Sponsors, pension funds, insurance companies, retail investors and family offices.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment of up to COP 300 billion, is part of Visum’s 2022-2024 investment plan.
location_description: Visum’s assets to be acquired and/or developed are located in Colombia, including but not limited to the cities and surrounding areas of Bogota, Cali, Medellín and Cartagena.
development_impact: Infrastructure development: The Project will improve firm’s access to high-quality and modern urban infrastructure through new potential industrial, office, healthcare, and retail property developments. Furthermore, the modern industrial warehouses established through the Project can contribute to efficiency gains and reduced operational costs for local businesses and supply chains. Class A developments can be significantly more efficient with lower operating costs than existing properties in the market. Environmental effects: All new developments will be certified as green buildings. In addition, Visum is expected to embark in a decarbonization pathway under the IFC GRIP (“Green Pathways for Real Estate Institutional Portfolios”) program, through which some existing buildings will be upgraded to attain energy efficiencies and reduce their carbon footprint and new acquisitions/developments will also have lower carbon footprint. Improving energy-efficiency in the commercial property sector is critical for coping with energy supply constraints while contributing to GHG emission reductions. Green Building (“GB”) Standards: The penetration of GB standards in Colombia remains low. The share of green buildings for new developments is currently at 4%, with an objective to reach 100 percent by 2030. Since 2011, the uptake for GB in Colombia remains mandatory, however, wide adoption of GB has proved a challenge due to (i) limited uptake of GB financing business by banks, (ii) very limited use of GB certification to two regions, Cundinamarca and Antioquia, (iii) lack of technical capacity and human capital in the GB area and (iv) lack of awareness by the government, FIs and leading developers.
additionality: Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: Visum will benefit from the implementation of IFC’s E&S compliance framework. In addition, IFC is expected to support Visum in defining and implementing its portfolio-level decarbonization strategy, under the recently launched GRIP Upstream program, which will guide on a systemic fashion, both the development of GB and the implementation of cost-efficient, energy-saving upgrades on existing properties, which in some cases could include obtaining certifications. Financing Structure: IFC will support Visum’s prospective access to debt financing by (i) expanding its financing at the corporate level, thereby reducing small scale debt at the asset level; and (ii) expanding the existing base of lenders (all local banks). Furthermore, IFC’s intended support under GRIP is expected to open the doors to green finance mechanisms such as ESG-linked loans and green bonds for Visum, as well as attract investors and tenants that have committed to climate goals.
Company Name: FONDO DE INVERSION COLECTIVA INMOBILIARIO VISUM RENTAS INMOBILIARIAS

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: M&J Group is one of the top tier denim garment manufacturing and exporting groups comprising of three cut and stitching plants and two washing plants. The proposed Project involves capacity expansion of three entities of M&J Group through increasing denim manufacturing capacity at Columbia Garments Limited (“CGL”) and Columbia Apparels Limited (“CAL”) and washing capacity at Columbia Washing Plant Limited (“CWPL”) (collectively the “Borrowers” or the “Companies”). The Borrowers’ capacity will increase from 11.65 million pieces per year to 15.45 million pieces per year for both readymade garments (RMG) and washing, with this expansion. The proposed expansion will be carried out at the existing locations of the three Companies in Gazipur, Bangladesh.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group is a family-owned business, founded by Late Mr. Mofizuddin Talukder, father of the principal Sponsors. The Companies have similar shareholding structure owned by the Sponsors – Mr. Salahuddin Ahmed (25% shareholding), Mr. Tarique Ahmed (33.3%), Mr. Munir Ahmed (33.3%), and Maheer Ahmed (8.3%). The Sponsors hold 100% stake in all the companies within the M&J Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Aggregate total Project cost is estimated at ~US$26.4 million and is proposed to be financed with long-term debt totalling US$11.7 million with the balance US$14.7 million through equity. Proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to US$11.7 million with a tenor of eight years including a two-year grace period.
location_description: The proposed expansion will be carried out at the existing premises of the respective three Companies in Gazipur, Bangladesh. CGL is located at Vogra whereas CAL and CWPL are located at Sreepur, and Bhabanipur, respectively within the Gazipur district.
development_impact: Economy-wide impacts: The Project will enable the Companies to move up the manufacturing complexity curve to more value-added products and services. IFC anticipates that the Company's operations will contribute to Bangladesh's economy through increased exports and backward linkages to the local supply chain. The Project also has a strong employment effect and will create thousands of additional direct and indirect jobs and female employment in the value chain. Competitiveness: This Project and IFC's sectoral programs in the RMG sector in Bangladesh are expected to contribute to preserving Bangladesh's competitiveness as a global player in the textile and apparel market, by helping Bangladesh move towards higher value-added production.
additionality: (i) IFC will provide financial additionality through a US$ loan with a tenor of 8 years, including 2 years of grace period. The Company requires the long tenor loan to have the necessary financial flexibility to implement a more advanced manufacturing technology and investments in resource efficiencies. (ii) IFC is expected to provide concessional financing which will make the financing affordable for the client. (iii) The Groups will continue implementing recommendations from Partnership for Cleaner Textile (PaCT), Better Work and Gear.

project_description: The proposed investment entails an up to US$45 million A loan to Industrial Pesquera Santa Priscila S.A. (“Santa Priscila” or the “Company”), a shrimp exporter in Ecuador. The proceeds will be used to (i) finance the acquisition of the California farm which entails 1,300 hectares of shrimp farms in the area of Naranjal close to Guayaquil; and (ii) connect this farm to the electrical grid, eliminating the use of diesel power generators in the pumping and automated aeration and feeding systems (the “Project”). The Company expects to decrease Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions while improving productivity levels in its shrimp ponds due to enhanced stability and quality of the oxygenation.
sponsor_shareholders: Santa Priscila’s majority shareholders and Project sponsors are the Salem family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$45 million and will be financed with a US$45 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project will be developed in the area of Naranjal close to Guayaquil.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is environmental improvement driven largely by Santa Priscila’s electrification project which is expected to significantly reduce Greenhouse Gas emissions by replacing energy from diesel power generators with electricity. Beyond the project level, IFC expects the investment to improve resilience of the sector through strong demonstration and replication effects, largely at primary production level. The investments in efficiency-improving automation and connection of the farms to the electrical grid will motivate other players to replicate similar practices.
additionality: IFC has both financial and non-financial additionality in the Project. Financial additionality is through providing patient long-term liquidity needed to grow Santa Priscila’s operations with tenors not available locally for agribusinesses. In addition, IFC will use its expertise to help the company raise its operating standards in terms of E&S, corporate governance, and insurance.

project_description: IFC's proposed investment comprises of up to US$5.4 million “A” loan, US$5.4 million “B” or Parallel loan and a US$10.8 million subordinated loan from IFC acting as the implementing entity of the International Development Association’s Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) for a total financing package of US$21.6 million to Fouta Cement Corporation (“Fouta Cement or “the Company”). This will be used to partially finance the construction and operations of a cement grinding plant in Monrovia. This backward integration project is expected to increase supply of locally produced cement and improve cost competitiveness. The project is expected to be supported by the International Development Association’s Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Fouta Cement is 100 percent owned by Fouta Corporation (“Fouta”). Fouta is engaged in the importation and distribution of rice, cement, steel rods and building materials, and is owned by 5 Liberian nationals. The Sponsors of the Project are (i) Mr. Hamidou Gnan who is the Founder and Managing Director of Fouta; and (ii) Mr. Mohammed Sow who is the President and Executive Director of Fouta.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposal is for IFC to provide a financing package of up to US$21.6mn comprising of: (i) IFC A Loan of up to US$5.4mn; (ii) IDA PSW subordinated loan of up to US$10.8mn; and (iii) B/Parallel loan of up to US$5.4mn. IFC’s own account financing represents about 48% of the total investment cost.
location_description: Freeport of Monrovia.
development_impact: (i) Economywide and employment effects: The Project will lead to the creation of jobs, including during the construction period and in the transportation and distribution network. Beyond the number of jobs created, the Project will support the continuous development of technical skills, which will improve the overall industrial capacity of the country. (ii) Market impacts- Competitiveness: IFC expects the investment to promote competitiveness in the Liberian cement market by allowing a key competitor to install a local grinding plant and thus retain competitive pressure on the dominant market leader.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC, with support from the IDA PSW BFF, will provide a long-term financing facility . IFC will also mobilize funds from other DFIs and/or commercial banks to complete the financial plan. Standards setting: IFC will support the Project to adopt international standard health, safety and social practices, as well as have a demonstration effect in the sector. Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC specialists will provide support in strengthening the Company’s operational efficiency. Moreover, the IFC Gender Team has advised the Client on developing a Sexual Harassment Policy and promoting more women into management positions.

project_description: Kordsa Teknik Tekstil A.S. (“Kordsa Turkey”) and its subsidiaries (together with Kordsa Turkey, “Kordsa”) is a leading Turkish group involved in the production of industrial nylon & polyester yarn, tire cord fabric and single end cord in addition to composite and construction reinforcement materials. The proposed IFC investment is up to US$110 million to fund (i) Kordsa’s investment program that will be undertaken in emerging markets between 2022 and 2025 to scale up research and development activities, acquire technology, improve operational efficiency and grow product capabilities in high margin products and (ii) increased permanent working capital need (the “Project”). Up to 25% of the proposed IFC investment will be utilized by Kordsa Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Kordsa Turkey in the US, for technology acquisitions. This component will benefit Kordsa’s operations in various emerging markets, such as Turkey, Brazil, Indonesia and Thailand.
sponsor_shareholders: Kordsa is majority owned by Haci Omer Sabanci Holding A.S. (“Sabanci Holding”) controlling 71.11% of the share capital. The remaining 28.89% is publicly listed in Borsa Istanbul. Sabanci Holding is one of Turkey’s leading conglomerates involved in financial services, energy, retail, and manufacturing sectors. While 49.1% of Sabanci Holding shares are on free float (listed in Borsa Istanbul), the remaining 50.9% of Sabanci Holding shares are owned by the Sabanci Family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to US$110 million for IFC’s own account. The IFC Loan will finance (i) Kordsa’s investment program in 2022 and 2025 and (ii) Kordsa’s increased permanent working capital needs.
location_description: Kordsa is headquartered in Turkey with manufacturing operations in five countries and the Project will benefit operations in various emerging markets, such as Turkey, Brazil, Indonesia, Thailand.
development_impact: The Project's expected development impacts include (i) higher export generation with increased sales, higher taxes; (ii) improved competitiveness of Kordsa; and (iii) job preservation and creation with skill development in a highly technical industry.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality includes its counter-cyclical role through provision of long-term financing and diversification of the group's funding base in addition to assisting Kordsa in improving its resource utilization with a reduced carbon footprint.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a senior loan of up to US$50 million composed by an A loan of US$30 million equivalent and a B loan of up to US$20 million, to support Usina Santa Adelia S.A.’s (“Santa Adelia” or the “Company”) investment plan for the 2022 and 2023. Santa Adelia is a leading sugar, ethanol, and renewable energy producer in Brazil, with two mills located in the Sao Paulo state. The investment will support (i) sugarcane replanting; and (ii) development and implementation of irrigation systems (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1943, the Company owns two mills with a combined installed capacity to crush up to 6 million tons of sugarcane per year while employing 3,100 people. Santa Adelia is a member of the sugar and ethanol cooperative and trader, Copersucar, which commercializes 100% of its sugar and ethanol production. In addition, the Company sells energy directly to the grid. Santa Adelia is majority owned by the Bellodi family with an 85.4% shareholding interests.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The investment plan is estimated at US$76 million, for which IFC will provide an A Loan of up to US$30 million equivalent and mobilize a B Loan of up to US$20 million. The remaining portion is expected to be financed through internal cash generation.
location_description: The Project is located in the Sao Paulo state, Brazil, where the Company owns and operates its two mills.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcomes are economy wide impact and environmental effects from increased ethanol production as well as renewable energy sales. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment has the potential to contribute to improving agricultural practices at the sector level and further strengthening its competitiveness through demonstration effect and replication.
additionality: • Long-term financing in local currency. • Mobilization of a B Loan. • Enhancement of the Company’s E&S practices.

project_description: Project is to construct and operate 1,061 green affordable housing units for rent across three housing developments in the Greater Johannesburg region (South Africa), over the next three years (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project will be developed and owned by AlleyRoads Holdings (Pty) Ltd (“AlleyRoads” or the “Company”). Founded in 2009, Alleyroads has developed over 3,000 residences to date, of which 1,850 are currently in its rental portfolio. The Company is 100% owned by the Airmid Investment Trust, with ultimate beneficiaries Mr. Ivan Pretorius (Founder and CEO) and his immediate family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be up to ZAR620 million (approximately US$42.1 million). IFC proposes a green A-Loan investment of up to ZAR 325 million (approximately US$20.9 million. The remaining balance will be provided by the Company shareholders in the form of equity.
location_description: The Project is located in Ekurhuleni and Midvaal municipalities, a large suburban region south east of Johannesburg, South Africa.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to increase access to good quality affordable housing in a market characterized by a large demand-supply gap. It will also contribute to job creation, training, and development of supply chains in the local community. Finally, demonstration and replication effects are expected by showcasing that green affordable housing projects in the rental space can be profitable and successful.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC will support a national property developer improve the local offering of quality affordable housing in the rental segment. IFC's additionality in this Project comes mainly in two forms: (i) provision of customized longer-term financing than Alleyroads is typically able to secure, and (ii) standard-setting with regard to implementation of E&S management systems, EDGE Advanced and READ.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of senior loan package up to USD35 million (mn) to Jubaili Holding for Investments SAL (“Jubaili” or the “Company”), the holding company of a leading importer, distributor and formulator of agrochemicals in Africa (the “Group”). The Group was established in 2002 by the Jubaili Family in Nigeria and expanded its geographical footprint to Ghana (2014), Uganda (2015), Tanzania (2016) and Kenya (2017). As of June 30, 2021, the Group employs over 2,300 people and sells to over 3,000 retailers, wholesalers, farmers and dealers through 80 outlets in the five operating countries. Jubaili’s investment plans include (i) capacity expansion plans in Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, Tanzania and (ii) permanent working capital needs (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Jubaili’s main shareholders are three siblings: Rajab Jubaili, Wissam Jubaili and Lara Jubaili with 40%, 40% and 20% shareholding respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The cost of the Project is estimated at USD35mn and IFC will support with a USD35mn senior loan. IFC’s financing will be used to support the Group’s expansion and working capital needs in Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda and Tanzania.
location_description: The Project will be located in Ibadan (Nigeria), Accra (Ghana), Kampala (Uganda) and Dar Es Salaam (Tanzania).
development_impact: Project level Impact: (i) Economywide effects: The Project will expand the Group’s production capacities and allow the Group to source more inputs from local suppliers, which will support domestic value addition and associated job creation. Using IFC’s economic impact assessment framework, we estimate that the project will lead to an average increase in annual GDP of US$217 million across the target countries, of which about US$26 direct value added, and US$192 indirect value added, as well as the generation of 1,600 direct jobs and 7,150 new indirect jobs. (i) Stakeholders - Increased outreach of distributors and retailers to smallholder farmers: The Project will improve the Group’s outreach to smallholder farmers through an expansion in its distribution networks in Nigeria and beyond. Specifically, scaling up blending and packaging operations will allow the the Group to increase the number of distributors and retailers reached by 7,200, in all turnover categories, from key accounts to medium and large agri-dealers to small-size retailers, not excluding the farmers that may be reached through market days or other training and extension services. The distributors will be strategically located, offering coverage across the individual countries, and increasing proximity to the customers, while also generating market intelligence for the Group. Further, the Group will be investing in ERP and warehouse inventory management systems, in the hope to enhance real time inventory management and, going forward, to experiment with digital and direct delivery models. Market level impact: (i) Competitiveness - Triggering new product offerings and supporting greater domestic value addition: IFC expects the Project, through the demonstration and replication channel, to contribute to increasing competitiveness of the crop protection sector in sub-Saharan Africa, through a first-mover company that will start local manufacturing of a select range of reliable herbicides in Ghana, Uganda, and Tanzania, and encouraging other companies to follow its lead and bring the production of quality crop protection closer to its final beneficiaries. The proposed investment will showcase the potential of domestic vertical integration in the crop protection industry in sub-Saharan Africa, and in particular spearhead a replicable business model for the crop protection sector in Anglophone West and East Africa. Market effects will play out through the example of a distributor company that evolves into a local manufacturer, thereby increasing its margins – as has been proved to be the case with the Group’s Nigerian operation – and steadily broadening up its market share. The Group’s strategy aims to shape the market, not only building on a regularly growing manufacturing base, in order to reduce costs and possibly attain economies of scale, but also enhancing its capacity development of retailers, both directly and indirectly through training of trainers and multimedia and digital content platforms.
additionality: Financial additionality: Innovative financing structure - IFC would provide the Group with a patient USD-denominated funding with a 8 years tenor including 2 years grace period to enable the Group to accomplish its vertical integration plan in the regions. This type of financing is not readily available locally for agribusiness companies. Non-Financial additionality: Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building - IFC will provide in-depth expertise in safer and effective crop protection products through its Industry Specialists. In addition, IFC Advisory Services, Environmental and Social Impact teams will explore environmentally safe certification requirements to ensure compliance with biopesticides market and organic agriculture industry standards. At appraisal IFC Advisory Services will brainstorm with the Company about the engagement scope (e.g. deploying the agribusiness leadership program (ALP); organize the Last Mile Retailer (LMR) training of their distributors and providing agronomic support including good agricultural practices (GAP). Standard setting: IFC could support a family owned Company improve its Corporate Governance practices.

country: Middle East, Pakistan, and Afg Region
project_description: Averda Holdings International Limited (?Averda or the ?Company?) is a leading waste management company based in the United Arab Emirates, servicing public and private sector customers across the GCC region and emerging markets in Africa and Asia, including Morocco, South Africa, Republic of Congo, and India.
sponsor_shareholders: Averda is a privately held company owned by the Sukkar Family through Envirohold Limited (62.7%), GrowthGate Capital Corporation BSC (33.3%) and the Grahne Family (4%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of a US$ 30 million A loan to finance development of waste recycling projects; and support general corporate and working capital needs.
location_description: Waste recycling projects proposed to be financed by IFC are located in Oman, Morocco and South Africa and use of proceeds for general corporate purpose will cover existing operations in the GCC region, Morocco, South Africa and the Republic of Congo.
development_impact: The investment is expected to (i) increase environmentally-sound waste treatment capacity in the target countries with focus on plastic recycling and help reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills; ii) increase material recovery and help prevent pollution through production of plastic pellets via mechanical recycling of plastics waste, displacing the production of the virgin materials and reducing GHG emissions; iii) contribute to market competitiveness by supporting private investment in the waste sector and demonstrating the role of plastic recycling plants in Oman, South Africa, and Morocco waste management systems.
additionality: IFC?s additionality in the project is both financial and non-financial. Financially, IFC will help Averda improve financial sustainability with access to capital and diversify the Company?s funding source at a time of high volatility due to the COVID-19 pandemic. IFC also plans to mobilize additional funding from lenders, thus attracting new partners and diversifying the Company's source of long-term funding. Non-financial additionality is provided through (i) knowledge sharing and capacity building, including leveraging the existing experience in solid waste and recycling, and ensuring that Averda adopts best corporate governance standards (ii) standard setting including IFC's environmental and social mitigation measures to manage environmental and social risks in line with IFC Performance Standards.
Country: Middle East, Pakistan, and Afg Region

project_description: The proposed IFC investment seeks to support Respublica Group (Pty) Ltd (“Company” or “RG”), a holding company that owns a 100% stake in each of Respublica Student Living (Pty) Ltd (“RSL”) and Respublica Management Services (Pty) Ltd (“RMS” or “Manco”). The Company is a leading student accommodation provider operating ~8,900 beds across South Africa. The Company is raising $34m initially with approximately US$23 million additional commitments. The initial commitment will allow the company to reduce the current debt raised to consolidate all its assets under RSL, and also to grow its portfolio through greenfield developments and conversions.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is currently 100% owned by Respublica Group Proprietary Limited (RG). Immediately before subscription, Bridgehead Real Estate Fund Proprietary Limited (BREF) owns 99.36% of RG with the balance being owned by management. BREF is a private real estate fund based in South Africa.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$57m million and will be funded with a combination of debt and equity. IFC will provide an equity of up to US$19 million, not to exceed 20% of total capital.
location_description: Republic of South Africa
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase acccess to affordable student housing in the underserved South African student housing market and responding to a significant gap in supply. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater competition in the affordable housing market segment via demonstration and replication channels.
additionality: IFC's additionality is driven by own account equity, resource mobilization and knowledge, innovation and capacity building factors. On own account equity front, IFC's investment will offer a stamp of approval from a recognized financial investor with a strong education and property track record. In terms of resource mobilization, IFC will assist the company to mobilize capital from other financial investors. IFC's non-financial additionality is driven by supporting the company to improve environmental and safety (E&S) best practices.

company_name: GENOMMA LAB INTERNACIONAL, S.A.B. DE C.V.
project_description: Founded more than 20 years ago, Genomma Lab (“Genomma” or the “Company”) is a Mexico-based, pharmaceutical company listed in the Mexican Stock Exchange with a presence in 18 countries across Latin America, and in the U.S.. It is focused on the development, manufacturing, distribution and sales of over the-counter (OTC) or non-prescription medicines and personal care (PC) products for the private market. The purpose of IFC’s proposed financing is to support Genomma’s approximately US$60 million expansion plan in Latin America over the next two years (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Genomma, a public company listed in the Mexican Stock Exchange. The main shareholder of the Company is Mr. Rodrigo Herrera (29 percent ownership), founder of Genomma Lab. The remaining shareholding is owned by international and local institutional investors and individuals, none of them own more than a 5 percent stake.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a US$60 million multi-currency and multi-country working capital (“WC”) facility in the form of a corporate A-Loan for IFC’s own account to fund the Company’s expansion in Latin America driven by increased demand of paracetamol, hand sanitizers, alcohol gel and other COVID-19-related products.
location_description: Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.
development_impact: Project-level : (i) increase access to quality and affordable medicines; and (ii) create employment opportunities and economic linkages with additional gross value added. Market creation : enhance resilience of supply chains for over-the-counter medical supplies.
additionality: Financial Structure . Multicurrency long term financing package which is not readily available in the region. IFC's global industry expertise and client network : Genomma aims to continue growing in the Latin America region. IFC can help the Company sharing knowledge on potential partners in new markets given IFC's pharmaceutical expertise in EMs, global network, and its local presence in many markets.
Company Name: GENOMMA LAB INTERNACIONAL, S.A.B. DE C.V.

project_description: Sodigaz is the largest distributor of LPG in Burkina Faso. It also operates fuel stations and is venturing into the solar power sector. The project entails the expansion of Sodigaz’s LPG operations, automation of certain manual operations, improvements in logistics, and installation of a solar power plant at a housing estate. The project is expected to be supported by the International Development Association’s Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: Sodigaz is owned by the Bolly family (71%) and African Infrastructure Investment Fund (29%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at EUR 17.7m. The proposed IFC investment is a EUR 8.4m XOF equivalent A loan (with support from IDA PSW LCF) and mobilization of a EUR 4m equivalent parallel loan.
location_description: The Project location is in Burkina Faso and in particular in Ouagadougou, Bobo-Dioulasso and Pamnoguin.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are increased access to LPG products, especially for rural households, with improvements in household’s indoor air quality contributing to improved health outcomes, especially for women and children. The Project will also contribute to improvements in the affordability and sustainability of electricity provision. Beyond these outcomes, the Project will promote competitiveness of the LPG market in Burkina Faso through a sizable expansion in capacity, enhanced operational efficiency, and the adoption of improved safety standards. The upgrade in the Company's distribution network is anticipated to lead to three main impacts in rural areas: (i) decreased leading time required for requalifying bottles and loading trucks; (ii) increased the availability of safe LPG cylinders, and (iii) improved distribution and retailing services.
additionality: Financial Additionality Financing structure: IFC will provide long-term financing in local currency (7-year with 2 years grace period), which is not readily available to the Company in Burkina Faso. IFC will also mobilize EUR 4m to complete the financial plan. IFC’s long-term financial commitment will allow the Company to continue with its expansion strategy amid increasing security risks in the country, which negatively impact the supply of credit. Non-Financial Additionality Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC will support the Company to adopt international good practice related to quality and safety standards in terms of health, safety, and social practices. IFC specialists will also provide technical assistance to the Company to ensure the solar installations meet international standards. Advisory Services: IFC to provide advisory on 3 key areas (i) the development of distribution models and value chains for clean energy solutions, (ii) improvement of efficiency of operations, and (iii) financial management.

project_description: The proposed investment is a US$20m IFC unfunded participation under a Risk Sharing Facility (“RSF”) in an up to US$60m uncommitted transaction secured revolving trade finance Facility for 3-years with annual renewals with Banque Internationale de Commerce-BRED (Suisse) SA (“BIC-BRED” or “the Bank”) for Agro Companies International (“Agro Companies” or the “Group”). The RSF will finance Agro Companies’ grain trading working capital needs, mainly (i) floating cargoes secured by the bills of lading (“BLs”), (ii) storage in warehouse at destination with Stock and Monitoring Agreement (“SMA”), and (iii) receivables on African buyers mainly covered by prime credit insurers. It will be processed under the Global Warehouse Finance Program (“GWFP”) with delegated authority from the Board.
sponsor_shareholders: Agro Companies is a family-owned trading group based in Geneva, established in 1983 by M. Jean-Christophe Egli. It is today wholly owned by his daughter and husband, Rachel and Erwan Boubet (50% each). The Group has become the leading supplier of wheat to many countries in West Africa, including Ghana, Cameroon, Burkina Faso and Togo. The Group is composed of 5 operating entities: (i) AgroHall, a wheat, feed products and pulses - purchasing entity in Canada, (ii) Ifaco Grain, the main wheat trading entity, (iii) Ifaco feed, the feed trading entity, (iv) Agri Company SA (Agrico), and (v) York Overseas, the shipping company of the Group. Banque Internationale de Commerce-BRED (Switzerland) SA (‘BIC-BRED’ or the ‘Bank’) is based in Geneva and is a wholly owned subsidiary of BRED Banque Populaire, one of the largest shareholders of BPCE Group. The Bank was initially established as a branch in 1991 then obtained a full banking license in August 2015 from the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA). The mission of the Bank is to assist the development of companies engaged in the trade of energy, agricultural and metal commodities. BIC-BRED covers the following business lines including Financial Institutions, Commodity Trade Finance and Corporate Finance.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Investment is US$60m in an uncommitted transaction secured trade finance Facility for 3-years with annual renewals to be fronted by BIC-BRED in favour of Agro Companies International group entities and whereby IFC’s investment as a disclosed risk participant will be up to US$20m (i.e. 1/3rd of BIC-BRED Bank’s facility).
location_description: Africa Region
development_impact: The Project is expected to: (i) increase the supply of wheat to African millers in the destination countries to produce wheat products; (ii) increase the supply of animal feed (soya bean, corn) to destination countries; (iii) increase technical support from the Group to millers to improve food safety and quality; and (iv) increase (in-kind) financing to millers to ensure continuity in commodity trading. To measure progress against this outcome, IFC will track the: (i) volume of products supplied to customers; and (ii) number of customers reached. The Project is expected to have catalytic effect of stimulating industry-wide best practices in grain trade financing, grain sourcing and processing, and facilitating food quality and safety improvements, moving the sector toward greater competitiveness from domination by large players to more participation by mid-sized players. To measure progress against this outcome, IFC will track the number of private sector banks providing support to the Company (which should increase or at least remain stable).
additionality: IFC’s proposed investment consists of a $20 million risk sharing facility with BIC-BRED to increase their available credit facility to $60m for AGRO COMPANIES to finance more trade flows. BIC-BRED had limits on facility size that prevented the Bank from financing large cargoes of wheat and feed at the current (high) price. With IFC, larger financing will be possible. Besides, the company had lost $125m of credit lines in 2019/20 that jeopardized their development. They had to replace this amount with existing and new lenders (including IFC). In addition, IFC’s involvement is expected to contribute to the reinforcement of the Group’s environmental and social practices, in line with IFC’s Performance Standards and industry best practices.

project_description: Lidl Discount S.R.L. (“Lidl”) is a discount food retailer in Romania and a subsidiary of D. Schwarz Beteiligungs-KG (“Schwarz” or the “Group”). The IFC loan will support Lidl’s investments in the COVID-19 pandemic induced improvements and expansion of its infrastructure and operations over the 2020-23 period (“Project”). This project is linked to Lidl Romania https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SPI/31466/lidl-romania
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Schwarz. Headquartered in Germany, Schwarz ranks among the top five food retail groups globally. Its network of approximately 13 thousand stores, operated under Lidl and Kaufland brands, spans 30 countries, mostly in Europe. The Group is a privately-held company. The Project company is Lidl, which is wholly owned by Schwarz.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at over €1 billion. The proposed IFC investment is an up to €85 million A loan for IFC’s own account to partially finance the Project (“RSE Loan”).
location_description: Investments under the Project are planned to be made in small and large cities throughout Romania.
development_impact: In the context of COVID-19 pandemic, IFC, through the crisis response financing, will help Lidl to: (i) increase access to quality products at affordable prices in remote and rural locations of Romania; (ii) grow domestic supplier base to minimize supply chain disruptions; and (iii) elevate food safety standards along the supply chain and safeguard employees in the stores to be built or modernized as part of the Project. By limiting supply disruptions, the Project promotes resilience in the food retail market.
additionality: IFC’s financial additionality includes the provision of a countercyclical loan with a long tenor of 10 years not widely available in the local market. IFC also provides non-financial additionality by supporting Lidl’s first 'Sustainability Linked' (SL) loan certification in Romania, in addition to green certification.

project_description: Established in 2004, Mavin Group Joint Stock Company (“Mavin” or “the Company”) operates in feed production, animal health, pig breeding, commercial pig farming and food processing. The Company’s operations are mainly in Vietnam. Mavin is a top 10 producer of animal feed in Vietnam and is among the largest locally built integrated players. Mavin’s integrated operations provides the Company with a competitive edge with its lower cost of production and strong biosecurity. The proposed IFC financing will support the expansion of Mavin’s pig breeding and commercial pig farming capacity and associated working capital requirements (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Mavin’s major shareholders are Mr. Dao Manh Luong (72.93%); Mr. Dao Manh Hoa (15.41%); Mr. Nguyen Anh Tuan (7.7%) and Dufort Future Enterprises Limited (3.9%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$90.6 million which would be funded by (i) VND1,200 billion (approximately equivalent to US$52 million) in Redeemable Convertible Dividend Preference Shares issued to IFC; and (ii) US$38.6 million of internal cash generation.
location_description: The Project location is in Vietnam
development_impact: The Project is assessed as part of the overarching programmatic intervention (ASF Asia Recovery Program) to respond to the impacts of the ASF on the regional pork industry. The most significant, expected Project-level outcome resulting from this expansion is the impact on consumers from the provision of safe pork at the time of severe supply shortage as well as implementation of advanced biosecurity procedures at the new farms. At the market level, the Project, alongside other planned investment, and advisory interventions, is expected to promote market resilience through improvement of biosecurity and disease management, both by supporting industry consolidation and disseminating best practices among smaller players.
additionality: Financing structure: The proposed transaction is a quasi-equity investment of up to VND1,200 billion (US$52 million equivalent). This type of financing is not readily available in the Vietnam agribusiness sector. The financing package will help strengthen the Company's capital structure and improve liquidity. This is especially important during the current period of market disruption, as the industry has been severely affected by outbreaks of ASF and is experiencing additional turmoil stemming from the COVID-19 pandemic. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC is looking to provide technical expertise and facilitate knowledge sharing on animal welfare best practices. As part of this initiative, IFC is exploring an opportunity to provide advisory services to support the Company with designing and implementing a group housing transition for its pig farming operations. Standard setting: IFC will support Mavin to implement best practices through raising the level of compliance to that of IFC's Performance Standards, European-level animal welfare standards, and industry best practices.

sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: IFC is invited to provide a US$7.5 million A loan and US$7.5m in B/parallel loans to Mammoth Foam Africa (“MFA” or the “Company”), a leading producer of polyurethane foam mattresses, spring mattresses and related foam and bedding products, operating through three subsidiaries in Kenya (Super Foam), Uganda (Euroflex) and Malawi (Vitafoam), to create a single consolidated group long-term loan, and to improve efficiency, expand production, and build storage capacity, among other capex investments.
sponsor_shareholders: MFA’s shareholders are Catalyst Mattress Africa (80%), Avuma (11%) and Foamex Holdings (9%). Catalyst Mattress Africa is a non-operational holding entity owned by Catalyst Fund II, a private equity fund mainly funded by Development Financial Institutions (CDC, EIB, IFC, PROPARCO, AfDB, DEG, etc.), and FISEA, a fund of the French Development Agency managed by PROPARCO.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$26.5 million, of which (i) US$21.9 million to refinance and consolidate into one long-term loan, a combination of short and long-term loans of the subsidiaries inherited from the consolidation process of these subsidiaries; and (ii) US$4.6 million capex to improve efficiency, expand production, and build storage capacity, among other investments (the “Project”). The Project will be financed with US$15 million debt, US$5.2 million working capital facility, and US$6.3 million equity to be contributed on a pro-rata basis from existing shareholders.
location_description: The proceeds will be utilized across the three operating subsidiaries of MFA that are located in: Ruiru, Kenya (Super Foam Limited); Kampala, Uganda (Euroflex Limited); and Blantyre, Malawi (Vitafoam (A) Limited).
development_impact: Assessment of Project Outcomes: - Economy-wide effects: The Project is expected to contribute to economic activity, direct job creation, and preservation of the existing high-quality jobs (1,000 employees) and the broader social fabric that the operations of the Company and the salaries contribute to. The Project also indirectly supports jobs and economic activity for local businesses that engage in the distribution of final products and sourcing of raw materials. - Stakeholders: Consumers in Kenya, Uganda and Malawi will benefit from improved affordability and access to a high-quality variety of bedding products. The Project will achieve this through (i) debt refinancing and expansion of raw materials storage capacity which will lower procurement cost of raw materials as a result of better working capital management, translating into improved affordability of final products sold; (ii) increased assistance to SMEs distributors through access to trade credits, which will intensify linkages in the value chain; and (iii) expansion in the number of retail distributors across the target countries as the Company grows its production. Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation: - Competitiveness: IFC anticipates that the investment will promote sector competitiveness in Malawi via the adoption of innovative manufacturing processes. Through the Project, MFA will expand its production capacity in Malawi, adopt novel technology and machinery, increasing its overall efficiency. Market impact in Kenya and Uganda is expected to be limited.
additionality: Financial Additionality: (i) Cross-Border Financing: IFC will help complete MFA’s strategic consolidation of its three operating subsidiaries, by regrouping at the corporate level all its long-term financing yielding centralized cash management; (ii) Loan Terms: IFC will provide a long-term loan with a 2-years grace period, which will reduce its vulnerability to domestic financial and banking shocks as well as enhanced working capital management. (iii) Resource Mobilization: IFC will help mobilize additional debt for the Company. Non-Financial Additionality: IFC will introduce its Lean Manufacturing Advisory to the Company as a possible complement to IFC’s financing to improve productivity.

project_description: Pier is Brazil’s first and largest full-stack insurtech. Pier began with a simple smartphone theft/robbery product in 2018, operating as an MGA, and they launched auto theft/robbery and roadside assistance product in 2020, and also became the first company to operate under the SUSEP sandbox digital insurer license.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company’s shareholder base is a diverse mix of strong local shareholders, notably Monashees (a leading Brazilian VC), Raiz Investimentos (A professional family office of Ivan Toledo, founder of Sem Parar), and Strategic investors including MELI Fund (Mercado Libre’s VC arm).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will invest $5M into the Company’s pre-Series C convertible round, to further invest in the growth of the Company as well as to ensure sufficient regulatory capital as the Company is becoming a fully licensed carrier.
location_description: Brazil.
development_impact: The Project has an AIMM rating of Good. The most significant, expected project-level outcome is improved access (to individuals) to theft insurance for smartphones and cars. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote competitiveness by demonstrating an innovative business model to reach new customers.
additionality: In this Project, IFC is providing non-financial additionality through knowledge, innovation and capacity building to support management on key strategies and decisions.

sector: Other Textile Products (Including Industrial and Medical Products)
project_description: Fitesa S.A. (“Fitesa” or the “Company”) is one of largest global manufacturers of nonwoven spunmelt textiles for medical, hygiene and industrial sectors. With headquarters in Porto Alegre, southern Brazil, Fitesa operates 23 plants and 5 innovation centers across 13 countries. Fitesa has been a key player in increasing the supply of nonwoven materials used in medical masks, respirators and other healthcare products whose demand has surged as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. Fitesa is undergoing an expansion project to increase its capacity in Brazil.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded by Mr. Sheun Ming Ling in 1973. Fitesa continues to be fully owned by the Ling family. The Company has independent management.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing an A Loan of up to US$50 million to support Fitesa’s capital expenditure and related working capital at its two major plants in Brazil, aimed at increasing capacity of nonwoven materials.
location_description: Investments will be made at Fitesa’s facilities located in São Paulo and Rio Grande do Sul states, Brazil.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is the increased delivery of raw materials for healthcare personal protective equipment ("PPE"). This will strengthen the availability of these materials in the region. IFC expects that its intervention will promote greater stability in healthcare provision by strengthening the supply chains relied upon to fill the growing need for medical supplies, especially PPE.
additionality: IFC is providing long-term financing to Fitesa, which is not so readily available in the market. In addition, the Company will benefit from IFC's Environmental and Social performance standards and IFC's sectoral knowledge.

company_name: ZENEX ANIMAL HEALTH INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED
project_description: The proposed IFC investment involves the purchase of equity shares of Zenex Animal Health India Private Limited (“Zenex” or the Company) from Multiples Private Equity Fund III (“Multiples”). Zenex commenced its business with the acquisition of the animal health business of Zydus Animal Health and Investments Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Cadila Healthcare Limited, which focused on the development, marketing and sale of drugs, vaccines and feed supplements for livestock, poultry, companion, and other animals, for markets in India and certain other countries. This has been funded by equity from investors including Multiples and with debt. Zenex is involved in the manufacturing, marketing, and sale of animal health products for the livestock and poultry segment.
sponsor_shareholders: Zenex is held by a consortium of investors including Multiples, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board and Rare Equity Private Limited.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed purchase of equity shares of Zenex is for up to INR1,200 million (approximately equivalent to US$16 million), together with IFC AMC Emerging Asia Fund (EAF)’s purchase of equity shares of Zenex for up to INR2,700 million (approximately equivalent to US$36.5 million). The aggregate IFC and EAF proposed investment is for up to INR 3,900 million (approximately equivalent to US$52.5 million).
location_description: The Project is located in India.
development_impact: Project-level impact: The growth of the Company will increase the production of quality pharmaceuticals for livestock and poultry, resulting in better yields and increased income for farmers. Market-level impact: The Project and Company’s growth will enable changes to existing markets that deliver sustainable development impact by promoting competitiveness through demonstration, replication, and competition.
additionality: IFC's additionality includes: (i) long-term patient capital while supporting the ownership transition, (ii) sharing its knowledge and experience in the agribusiness and pharmaceuticals sectors as the Company develops new products and providing guidance on Environmental and Social (E&S) aspects and (iii) potential advisory engagement.
Company Name: ZENEX ANIMAL HEALTH INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED

project_description: The Proposed Investment is a CHF 4 million equivalent corporate A Loan to the Nespresso Sustainability Innovation Fund (NSIF) to support Nespresso’s goal to further scale the farmer support provided through the AAA Sustainable Quality ProgramTM with a focus on the Reviving Origin program. At the same time, IFC will provide Advisory to support the implementation strategy in Uganda, Mozambique, and Zimbabwe. This Project will be IFC’s second collaboration with Nespresso, after successfully establishing the proof of concept in Ethiopia and Kenya.
sponsor_shareholders: The Nestlé Nespresso company, is an autonomous globally managed business of the Nestlé Group, founded in 1986. Nestle is a public Swiss multinational food and beverage company based in Vevey, Switzerland. The Nespresso Sustainability Innovation Fund (NSIF) was created in 2016 to facilitate investments in sustainability programs.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of an IFC A Loan for up to CHF $4 million to support Nespresso’s investments in the AAA program to restore coffee production in regions affected by adversity. IFC will provide Advisory to support the program’s implementation strategy.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Vevey, Switzerland. IFC loan will support Nespresso’s AAA program with a focus on the Reviving Origins program in Uganda and Mozambique. IFC will provide Advisory to support the program’s implementation strategy in Uganda, Mozambique, and Zimbabwe.
development_impact: The Project level outcome is the impact on farmers through: (i) adoption of sustainable coffee production practices and AAA sustainability standards; (ii) yield improvement; and (iii) domestic value addition through investments in processing facilities, leading to increased farm earnings through more reliable access to coffee markets including Nespresso. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that contribution to market creation will stem from better integrating underserved regions of the project countries into global value chains by setting up coffee buying points, processing facilities (wet/dry mills) close to the producers and demonstrating the business rationale for enhancing this type of physical infrastructure in the target areas to counter existing bottlenecks for revival of specialty coffee and sector development in general. The AS services contribute to demonstration effect largely at the production level through capacity building of farmers, motivating other sector players to establish or expand their engagement with smallholders to improve quality, increase coffee production, and to safeguard, revive and market rare and high quality coffee.
additionality: IFC will provide patient longer-term financing which is not readily available in Uganda and Mozambique. IFC's non-financial additionality centers around supporting Nespresso's operations through advisory services to strengthen the coffee supply chains and build farmer capacity as well as implementation of IFC Performance Standards to align the Company's operations with best international practices.

company_name: FCP DEUDA INFRAESTRUCTURA II SURA - CREDICORP CAPITAL
project_description: The proposed project entails an IFC equity investment of up to US$40m equivalent in COP (COP$150,000m) or up to 20% of the total commitments, as limited partner in an infrastructure debt fund managed by Unión para la Infraestructura S.A.S. (“UPI” or the “Manager”). This will be an IFC follow-on investment in compartment A of UPI’s second debt fund (the “Second Fund” or the “Fund”). The Second Fund will be earmarked to finance toll-roads and airports projects under the 4G and 5G infrastructure programs in Colombia (the “Project”). In December 2015, IFC committed COP$150,000m (US$48m) in UPI’s first debt fund (the “First Fund”), which provided senior debt financing to four projects under Colombia’s 4G toll-road concession program.
sponsor_shareholders: As in the First Fund, the Manager is a 50:50 joint venture (the “JV”) of Credicorp Capital Colombia S.A. (“CCC”) and Sura Invesment Management S.A.S. (“Sura IM”) with Sumatoria Gestión de Activos S.A.S. (“Sumatoria”), a Colombian investment bank specialized in infrastructure acting as advisor. CCC is a subsidiary of Grupo Credicorp, an important regional financial conglomerate based in Peru, and the controlling sponsor of Banco de Crédito del Perú, the largest commercial bank in the country with extensive track record in project finance. Sura IM is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sura Asset Management (“SUAM”). SUAM is part of Grupo Sura, one of the largest pension asset managers in Latin America, with operations in Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project entails an IFC equity investment of up to US$40m equivalent in COP (COP$150,000m) or up to 20% of the total commitments, as limited partner in the Fund.
location_description: The Fund will invest in toll-roads and airports projects under the 4G and 5G infrastructure programs in Colombia.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Satisfactory. The most significant, expected project-level outcome comes from the improved access to road infrastructure and it supported by the improved quality of finance for infrastructure projects through the provision of longer-tenor funding. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote competitiveness by fostering the creation of infrastructure debt funds as an investible asset class for institutional investors with a long-term focus and a complementary source of funding for infrastructure projects through demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: In this Project, IFC is providing both financial and non-financial additionality through the provision of equity, resource mobilization, and standard-setting. IFC's Own Account Equity: IFC will provide a direct equity investment of up to US$40 million. The Second Fund is expected to have on its investor base some of the largest pension funds and insurance companies in Colombia. While commercial banks were active in the financing of the 4G projects that have reached financial close, by providing about 62% of the financing needs, their high level of exposure to the infrastructure sector, coupled with increasing constraints in offering long tenors due to Basel III capital restrictions and the impact of COVID-19, limits their appetite and availability of funding for infrastructure projects in Colombia going forward. Resource mobilization: IFC's role of anchor investor will help catalyze investments from institutional investors. Also, IFC's participation will encourage increased participation of local institutional players in the financing of infrastructure and increasing sources of local currency financing. Standard-setting: IFC's previous engagement with the Manager served to help the Fund to work on environmental and social matters. Additionally, in this project IFC will work with the client to strengthen its management of Corporate Governance risks when it conducts its due diligence during investment review processes and in its portfolio management.
Company Name: FCP DEUDA INFRAESTRUCTURA II SURA - CREDICORP CAPITAL

project_description: Brightgene Bio-Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (“Brightgene” or the “Company”) is a leading Chinese pharmaceutical company that focuses on the research and manufacturing of high barrier generics, active pharmaceutical ingredients (“APIs”), and finished dosage forms (“FDFs”). The proposed IFC investment will support Brightgene’s expansion into Indonesia to meet the growing local demand in the country (the “Project”)
sponsor_shareholders: Brightgene’s controlling shareholders are its founder Mr. Jiandong Yuan, Ph.D. and his mother Ms. Weifang Zhong (collectively the “Sponsors”), who have combined shareholding of 45.85% in the Company. The remaining 54.15% are public floats.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be approximately US$100 million. IFC’s proposed investment is a senior, secured A loan of up to US$50 million.
location_description: Karawang New Industrial City, West Java Province, Indonesia
development_impact: Project level: The Project is expected to benefit patients in Indonesia through increase in the local production of quality pharmaceutical products. It is expected to make the health system more resilient to supply chain shocks of the kind that affected countries during the pandemic. The Project is also expected to benefit employees through the creation of local jobs along with skill training opportunities. Market level: The Project is expected to increase the competitiveness and resilience of the pharmaceutical markets in Indonesia. By supporting the introduction of relatively sophisticated production and the creation of a pool of well-trained workers with hands-on experience, the Project will lay the basis for further development of the pharmaceutical sector in Indonesia.
additionality: 1. Long-term financing and countercyclical role: IFC is able to lend on a long-term basis in USD which is not readily available from the existing banks and critical for the Project’s success, especially at this uncertain pandemic time. 2. Springboard to emerging markets: This will be BrightGene’s first overseas expansion plan. The Company may leverage IFC’s extensive experiences and resources in Indonesia to mitigate the execution risks. 3. Global industry knowledge: Pharmaceutical transportation and distribution requires significant effort and care (e.g., temperature control, timeliness, traceability, etc). IFC will share global industry knowledge and best practice in this area. 4. E&S standard-setting: IFC will help enhance BrightGene’s sustainability by developing a comprehensive E&S system. Its implementation will strengthen the Company’s E&S practices and procedures in its new production facilities and in raising the level of compliance to that of IFC’s Performance Standards.

project_description: Nam Long Investment Corporation (“NLG”, or the Company) is a leading affordable housing developer in Vietnam, who has 29 years of experience in construction and real estate and has developed more than 18,000 housing units in Ho Chi Minh City (“HCMC”) and surrounding provinces. Being one of the pre-eminent affordable housing developers in Southeast Asia, NLG has three product lines covering affordable apartment, premium affordable apartment and affordable townhouse. The Company mainly targets low- to middle-income households in Vietnam, with 84% of the Company’s total sales units in 2019 contributed by affordable and premium affordable apartment products.
sponsor_shareholders: NLG is listed on the HCMC Stock Exchange since 2013 and has a market capitalization of ~US$971 million as of November 2021. With a mission to develop affordable housing for the majority of Vietnamese, Mr. Nguyen Xuan Quang founded the Company in 1992 as one of the first non-state-owned enterprises in the real estate sector in Vietnam. After 29 years of development, Company today operates across the full value chain of real estate development. NLG has a diversified shareholder base. As of January 2021, Mr. Nguyen Xuan Quang and his relatives collectively own 17.7% of the shares as the largest shareholder. The other shareholders, including a Singapore-based real estate developer and public investors, own the rest of Company shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$ 411 million. The proposed IFC investment is a corporate bond of up to VND 1 trillion (approximately US$44 million equivalent).
location_description: The 190-hectare Project (Waterpoint Phase II) will be located in Long An, around 30km southwest of HCMC, Vietnam.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level effect is improved quality of life by giving the low-mid urban income population access to quality and affordable housing, schools, hospitals and commercial areas. The Project will also create jobs and positive environmental impacts. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that success of the proposed investment will encourage other developers to serve the low-mid urban income population in other secondary cities in Vietnam.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this Project comes in three forms: (i) financing structure; (ii) bond instrument; and (iii) knowledge innovation and capacity building. IFC will provide long-term funding in VND that will fit the cash generation profile of housing projects which is not available in Vietnam as local banks mostly offer floating rate financing at short or medium term from 3 to 5 years. In addition, financing through a bond diversifies the sources of funding and provides more flexibility in terms of the use of proceeds compared to traditional bank loans. Furthermore, IFC will provide technical knowledge and advice on greening Nam Long's pipeline of projects and provide an opportunity to offer IFC's new EDGE Green Urban Development (GUD) tool to help Nam Long reduce GHG impacts.

project_description: Financing to Laboratorios Siegfried S.A.S (“Siegfried-Col”) and Laboratorios Siegfried, S.A. (jointly the “Borrowers”) to support the execution of their strategic plan including: (i) Capex needed to upgrade the manufacturing plant owned by Siegfried-Col, (ii) working capital requirements for the commercialization of Novartis’ products in light of the recent license-in agreement signed between the Borrowers’ and Novartis; and (iii) reprofile the Borrowers’ existing debt with commercial banks to properly match the long-term nature of the investments undertaken by the Borrowers over the past years and free-up the cash needed to execute their strategic plan within the next 2-3 years (the “Project”). Siegfried-Col is a leading pharmaceutical company focused on the development, manufacture and commercialization of over-the-counter medicines, prescription drugs and personal care products (mostly branded generics). With two manufacturing plants in Colombia and 516 employees, Siegfried-Col is focused mainly on cardio, neuro, women’s health and primary care therapeutic areas. Approximately 95% of Siegfried-Col’s revenues are generated in Colombia, and the rest is exported to Central America, Ecuador, and Peru.
sponsor_shareholders: The Borrowers are fully-owned by Grupo Roemmers (“Roemmers”), one of the largest pharma players in LAC based in Argentina with operations in nine countries. On August 2018, IFC committed a US$31 million Senior Loan to finance the expansion of Roemmers’ in Brazil (Farmoquimica, IFC/R2017-0341) and on January 6, 2019, IFC committed a US$75 million Senior Loan to Siegfried in Mexico (IFC/R2018-0346). Roemmers’ shareholders are: Pablo Roemmers-49%; Alberto Roemmers-49%; and Alejandro Roemmers-2%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost is estimated at approximately US$36.3 million. The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$30 million corporate A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Colombia and Panama.
development_impact: This Project is being processed under the Global Health Platform (GHP). Project-level: Stakeholder effect: Increased Access to Healthcare Products. By financing the Project, IFC expects to benefit the middle-to-low income population in Colombia, Peru, Ecuador, and Central America from lower priced high-specialty medicines, consistent and high quality, and greater product variety. Economy-wide effect: Gross Value-Added – IFC financing will support a manufacturer located in Colombia. The project will help scale the production and delivery of healthcare supplies that is likely to result in the creation of new jobs and/or economic linkages to the rest of the economy. Market Creation: Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that its financing could support greater market resilience as spillover effects accrue to the healthcare supply chains in these markets.
additionality: Long-term financing: IFC is providing a long tenor loan that is not easily available in the market for transactions of this size. IFC’s long-term commitment to support the Borrowers expansion plan will also send positive signals to the market on the quality of the Management Team and operations, which will help the Company as it continues growing in Colombia and the LAC region. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: Siegfried-Col aims to continue expanding outside of Colombia. Through the support from IFC’s global industry expertise and client network, IFC can help the Company sharing knowledge on potential partners in new markets given IFC’s healthcare expertise in EMs, global network, and its local presence in many markets. Standard-setting by providing advice on E&S Best Practice and Gender Equity: IFC will share international best practices in E&S management and will support the Borrowers to keep improving its standards, including best practices on Gender Inclusion through a formal advisory project currently in discussion.

project_description: Crystal Crop Protection Limited (“Crystal” or the “Company”) is one of the major agrochemical players in India. Crystal manufactures and markets a broad range of crop protection products (insecticides, fungicides, and herbicides), as well as seeds and farm equipment, predominantly for the domestic India market. The Company is well-diversified across crops, has a large existing portfolio of generic crop protection products and is now strategically developing its own branded formulations. Crystal provides crop protection products that cater to entire lifecycle of crops from sowing to harvesting and assist the Indian farmer to maximize productivity and profitability. Crystal plans to (i) further expand Crystal’s own in-house manufacturing of active ingredients (“technicals”), which will help it to further backward integrate and reduce dependence on imports of technicals (ii) fund capital expenditure to expand capacity, improve IT infrastructure and automation in its plants, (iii) fund working capital requirement; (iv) setup solar plants in its production units to promote cleaner energy and reduce power costs, and (v) fund costs for domestic and global product registrations (all together, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Nand Kishore Aggarwal (Executive Chairman) and his son, Ankur Aggarwal (Managing Director), along with their families hold 94.7% of the Company. The remaining 5.3% is held by Crystal Crop Employee Welfare Trust.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost and Amount and Nature of IFC's Investment Pending
location_description: Headquartered in Delhi, the Company operates four formulation plants and two active ingredient plants across India and is in the process of installing a third active ingredient plant in Dahej, India.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are: (i) Stakeholder effects: The Project will improve farmers' productivity through better access to customized agrichemicals by enabling the development of formulations that are particularly well-adapted to local crop, soil, and environmental factors and through sale of affordable, generic pesticides. (ii) Economywide effects: The Project will create jobs and add value through backward linkages, where they will produce in-house the active ingredients required to produce their agrichemicals The Project will also create additional direct skilled jobs. The employees will learn new skills and technology to produce these active ingredients (iii) Competitiveness: The Project is expected to demonstrate backward integration, to improve cost control of the value chain, production efficiency as well as the ability innovate and produce high quality the products, and thus improving the sector's competitiveness.
additionality: IFC's support involves helping the Company raise patient, long-term equity financing and mobilizing equity from AMC (which manages private equity capital for its investors). IFC's presence, reputation and due diligence process provides comfort to future investors as the Company is preparing for its initial public offering (IPO). The equity investment will also strengthen the Company's environmental, social, and governance standards, and help mitigate potential environmental and safety risks resulting from the Company's operations. Such mitigations are critical in the agro-chemical industry.

project_description: Founded in Costa Rica, Corporación Stein (“Stein” or the “Company”) is a private, family-owned pharmaceutical group focused on the development, manufacture and commercialization of high-specialty generics. It has operating subsidiaries in six countries and sales in more than 20 countries across LAC, including all countries in Central America. Stein has a manufacturing facility in Costa Rica focused on the production of generics. The Company is also engaged in the commercialization of a diversified high-specialty portfolio that includes biosimilars, innovative products, and orphan drugs licensed from global pharmaceutical companies. The Company is focused on the institutional market with over 90% of revenues coming from the public sector. The proposed IFC’s financing aims to support Stein’s growth plan in LAC which includes expansion in the biosimilar, innovative, and orphan drugs segments through new licensing agreements and inorganic growth.
sponsor_shareholders: The Waserstein family fully owns Corporación Stein.
