total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC financing is a US$24 million equity investment in common shares of the Company to finance its strategic expansion plan in LAC focused on the growth of high-specialty products (biosimilars, innovative, orphan drugs) through new licensing agreements and inorganic growth strategies.
location_description: Latin America with a focus on Brazil, Costa Rica, Colombia, Chile, Ecuador, Mexico, Panama and Peru.
development_impact: Patients: Increased effectiveness of both the prevention and treatment of diseases. Biopharma drugs are particularly effective with late-stage, difficult to treat, chronic diseases such as cancer, diabetes, and hepatitis C, and immunological disorders. Biologics are better than existing chemical alternatives because they have higher efficacy outcomes and are more specific in targeting and hence, have fewer side effects. The Project responds to the gap through investing in a Company with capacity to bring biosimilars to developing countries where there is a low penetration of biologicals due to the high cost of innovative products and lack of interest of biosimilars producers to go to these markets. Competitiveness: Major multinational pharma companies, which were once considered traditional pharma companies, are now shifting into biotech on an unprecedented scale. However, most low- and middle-income countries lack access to biopharma products, and at the same time, face increasingly higher drug costs. Introduction of biosimilars has helped reduce drug costs (ranging from 30% to 75%) and increase access to treatment in several countries in Europe and EMs. Stein is planning to be one of the first companies to introduce biosimilars upon patent expiration in a number of therapeutic areas over the life of project, with a price discount to the innovator in the range of 50-60%.
additionality: IFC Own Account Equity: IFC's longer-investment horizon vis-à-vis other type of investors such as PEFs will enable Stein to properly execute its long-term plan. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: As Stein aims to continue expanding throughout LAC, IFC can help the Company sharing knowledge on potential partners in new markets given IFC's healthcare expertise in EMs, global network, and its local presence in many markets. In addition, IFC will bring international best practices in Corporate Governance based on IFC's experience working with family-owned companies in different markets. IFC's CG Advisory will help the Company to achieve a higher level of sophistication in corporate governance which is critical for the continuity of the business in the long run and for the achievement of Stein's medium to long term goals (e.g., internationalization, access to international markets). Standard Setting: IFC will help the Company establish appropriate environmental, social and governance standards.

project_description: Hikal Limited (the “Company” or “Hikal”) is a leading manufacturer of active intermediates and ingredients offering products to global pharmaceutical, crop protection, animal health and specialty chemical companies. The Company also provides discovery research and development support to companies in pharmaceuticals and crop protection. The Company is undertaking a multi-year capital expenditure plan across its facilities for product and capacity expansion (“Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Jai Hiremath and family with related entities hold 69% stake are the promoter shareholders. The Company is publicly listed in India and the balance is held by financial institutional investors and general public. The Project is being undertaken by Hikal Ltd.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to fund up to US$50 million to part finance the Company’s multi-year capital expenditure plan.
location_description: The Project will be located at the Company’s existing manufacturing facilities in India including in Mahad (Maharashtra), Taloja (Maharashtra), Panoli (Gujarat), Jigani (Karnataka) and Pune (Maharashtra).
development_impact: Climate Change and Resource Efficiency: This Project is expected to contribute to climate change mitigation by net reduction of GHG emissions through installations of rooftop solar panels, biomass briquette based boilers, and more efficient production processes that result in reduction of waste and lower consumption of water, electricity, and materials. Competitiveness: This Project is expected to contribute to increased competitiveness in the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals sectors as the Company works on innovation and expanding its product offering in the market.
additionality: Through the proposed funding, IFC's involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide a critical financial solution to the Company for one of its largest capital expenditures plans ever, through long-term financing that fits the project's timeline, risk profile and needs. Further, IFC's stamp of approval through its financing for the Company's sustainability initiatives, environment-friendly production facilities and resource-efficient processes will reinforce the Company's positioning as a sustainability-focused manufacturing partner for its target clientele. Lastly, IFC will explore Green Building advisory to the Company in order to obtain EDGE certification for identified buildings that will be part of the Project.

project_description: The proposed investment is a total of US$700 million senior loans, including IFC A plus B loans, to two Vietnam subsidiaries of Goertek Inc. (“Goertek”, “the Sponsor” or “the Guarantor”) for (i) the expansion of an existing production base in Bac Ninh, Vietnam and (ii) the construction of a new production base in Nghe An, Vietnam (together, the “Project”). Goertek Technology Vina Company Limited (“Goertek Bac Ninh”) will undertake the expansion in Bac Ninh and Goertek Precision Industry Vietnam Company Limited (“Goertek Nghe An”) will construct the greenfield in Nghe An (together “Goertek Vietnam”, the “Companies” or the Borrowers”).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Shandong, Goertek is a large manufacturer and supplier of acoustic electronics and components for world-leading consumer electronics brands. Goertek is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and currently is a major supplier of TWS (true wireless stereo) earphones and VR (virtual reality) products in the global value chain of consumer electronics. As of September 30 2021, the founder Mr. Jiang Bin and his brother Mr. Jiang Long together control 33.79% of the Sponsor through both direct shareholding and indirect beneficial ownership. The remaining 66.21% is owned by public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project will be funded by the IFC A plus syndicated B loans and Goertek’s internally generated cash. The proposed IFC investment is a 5-year senior loan of up to US$700 million in total with a grace period of 1 year.
location_description: The Project locations are in Bac Ninh Province and Nghe An Province in Vietnam.
development_impact: Economy wide effects: The Project is expected to support the development of the electronics value chain and contribute to the local economy through increased exports. Employment: The Project expects to create about 40,000 direct jobs along with skill training opportunities in the local markets, thus establishing a sizeable talent pool for future development of the local industry. Almost all employees of the Project are expected to be hired locally with female employment as a priority. All of them are expected to undergo professional training conducted by senior engineers and technicians of Goertek. Integration: The Project will help a major player in the global electronics value chain to expand into other emerging market, help to formalize the local electronics manufacturing sector up to export standards and enhance the local supply chain linkages. The know-how and expertise will be transferred at a scale needed to jumpstart other competitive manufacturing and supporting industries in the region. Its high E&S standards and production efficiency will also have market-wide demonstration effects and benefit other local players. Competitiveness: The Project will develop two full-fledged production sites in Vietnam for localized manufacturing of complicated smart devices and spur the competitiveness and growing innovation in the local economy. It will also facilitate the development of supporting industries by procuring more inputs from local suppliers in Vietnam and build up their capacity to support manufacturing with higher value-add.
additionality: IFC's additionality will mainly come from, i) mobilization: to provide and mobilize long-term USD loan financing to match the cash generation profile of the Project, which is critical for the success of the Project; ii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building: to enhance E&S standard setting for the Vietnam operations; to bring expertise on gender-smart policies and practices; and to support its engagement with local stakeholders and potential business partners.

project_description: The proposed loan of up to €9 million (the IFC Loan) to Industrie des Boissons du Sénégal (IBS or the Borrower), a still and carbonated soft drinks (CSD) processing company, is to support the Borrower’s investment program and includes: (i) expanding production capacity; (ii) implementing a packaging recycling program; (iii) Green building standards and certification, and (iv) working capital requirements.
sponsor_shareholders: IBS is an IFC existing client based in Senegal and majority-owned by the El Sahili family (the Sponsors) through SIFAKA. The founder, Mr. Kassim El Sahili, is joined by his two sons, Mr. Rouda El Sahili and Mr. Mohamed El Sahili in managing the business.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at €14 million. FC’s proposed financing is an A loan of up to EUR9 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The 52,000-sq. meter new project site is in Diamniadio, Senegal.
development_impact: The expected impacts are likely to center around: Consumers: Consumption of sugar-dense beverages (both CSD and juices) is associated with the negative nutritional outcomes for the consumers. The impacts could be mitigated by exploring reformulation or shifting production towards healthier choices. Direct and indirect employment: The Project is expected to generate 130 direct jobs and expand its local distribution and storage facilities to support small shops/kiosks (traditional trade). Environment: IBS will promote recycling, hence reducing the related carbon footprint and waste. There may be scope for market impacts along this dimension in the FMCG market in Senegal.
additionality: • IFC Industry Expertise: IFC brings (a) global industry knowledge based on previous transactions, and (b) Project implementation advice in line with best industry practices, sustainability and IFC’s Performance Standards. • IFC Advisory Services: IFC will potentially engage with IBS to identify/assess further investments in food safety, resource efficiency, renewable energy, water/waste reduction, and corporate governance succession planning.

company_name: WAYCOOL FOODS AND PRODUCTS PRIVATE LIMITED
project_description: The proposed project is an equity investment of up to US$15 million in WayCool Foods and Products Pvt Ltd (“WayCool” or the “Company”) based out of India. WayCool is a leading tech enabled business to business (“B2B”) ecommerce player in India that procures, processes and distributes fresh produce (fruits and vegetables), staples (like grains, pulses and sugar), processed food items including dairy and fast moving consumer goods (“FMCG”) to a diversified customer base of mom-and-pop stores (kirana stores), offline and online modern retailers and processors.
sponsor_shareholders: WayCool was founded by Mr. Karthik Jayaraman who currently serves as CEO and Mr. Sanjay Dasari. The Company’s key shareholders include: (i) the founders (Karthik Jayaraman and Sanjay Dasari) and management team; (ii) an impact fund Lightrock (through investing entities Aspada Investment Company; Lightrock India Holdings Ltd. and Lightrock Growth Fund I S.A.); (iii) a domestic VC fund Lightbox Ventures (Lightbox Ventures III); (iv) a Development Finance Institution FMO (NEDERLANDSE FINANCIERINGS MAATSCHAPPIJ VOOR ONTWIKKELINGSLANDEN N.V.) (v) Vishay Engineering & Holdings Private Limited (owned by Mr. Vinod Dasari); and other early and growth stage venture capital funds and angel investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Company is in the process of raising US$120 million of preferred equity. IFC is proposing to invest up to US$15 million in WayCool in preferred equity. IFC’s investment will support the expansion of WayCool’s business in India including investment in new products, technology and expansion of current operations.
location_description: WayCool Foods and Products Pvt Ltd is incorporated in India. The Company is primarily operational in six states in India namely Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telengana, Kerala and Maharashtra.
development_impact: Expected development impact includes: (i) Improved access to markets, potentially resulting in increased incomes for farmers and enhanced productivity growth for small retailers (ii) Increased integration of the food value chain in India, via competition and innovation channels.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists in the provision of patient capital and IFC's ability to continue to support future funding needs, particularly during the tough times brought on by the Covid-19 pandemic. Non-financial additionality involves knowledge, innovation and capacity building, provided by leveraging insights from previous investments, and connecting the Company with prospective clients.
Company Name: WAYCOOL FOODS AND PRODUCTS PRIVATE LIMITED

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: CNGR Advanced Material Co., Ltd. (“CNGR”, the “Company”) is an established producer of cathode precursors for lithium batteries and a major recycler of end-of-life batteries in China. The proposed IFC investment will support CNGR’s construction of recycling facilities for end-of-life batteries and scrapped materials in Tongren, Guizhou Province and integrated facilities in Qinzhou, Guangxi Province, both frontier regions in Southwest China (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: CNGR’s controlling shareholders are its founder and Chairman Mr Weiming Deng and his wife Ms Xiaoge Wu (the “Sponsors”), who have a combined stake of 66.24% through direct and indirect ownership. The remaining 33.76% shares are held by private equity funds, corporates and public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be approximately US$453 million. IFC’s proposed investment is a senior, secured A loan of up to US$150 million equivalent.
location_description: Tongren, Guizhou Province & Qinzhou, Guangxi Province, China
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is driven primarily by: (i) economy-wide effects, by creating value in the EV battery value chain through the expansion of recycling capacity and employment generation; and (ii) environmental effects from GHG emissions avoided through the recovery, refurbishment, and reuse of lithium-ion EV batteries. IFC expects the investment to increase Integration of EV battery recycling as an essential and inseparable part of East Asia's EV ecosystem by: i) supporting the top ternary precursor materials players in China; ii) developing the EV and components manufacturing ecosystem in East Asia, and; (iii) introducing an integrated EV battery ternary precursor materials producer-recycler model.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality stems from its ability to provide a long-term loan and mobilize additional funding sources to support CNGR's integrated business model. Moreover, IFC's E&S standards will help the Company adopt good international industry practices and support the sustainable development of the EV battery recycling industry along with the effective management the E&S risks associated with recycling activities.

project_description: The proposed investment will support Di’An Diagnostics Group Co., Ltd. (“Di’An”, “the Company” or “the Borrower”) to (i) expand and upgrade its existing ICL network and create 5 regional test centers through expansion of existing ICLs; (ii) add 5 “spoke” ICLs in second/third tier cities; (iii) build a manufacturing center for its self-developed In Vitro Diagnostic (“IVD”) products; (iv) fund R&D expenses to accelerate expansion in specialized testing and (v) build advanced IT infrastructure and data analytics function over the next five years (together, the “Project”). The additional testing capacity created by the Project will help to relieve capacity constraints at over-crowded public hospitals while expanding the types of testing available.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Hangzhou, Di’An operates one of the largest independent clinical laboratory (“ICL”) networks in China including some located in the frontier regions Yunnan, Inner Mongolia, Shaanxi, Gansu, etc., serving more than 20,000 medical institutions and 300 million people. The Company also engages in the business of diagnostic equipment and product distribution. The controlling shareholder of Di'An Diagnostics is Mr. Haibin Chen, who founded the Company in 2001 and owns 30.36% of Di'An Diagnostics Group (including 29.33% directly and 1.03% indirectly). Ms. Xu Min, who also founded the Company, directly owns 1.61% of the Company. The others are public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is estimated to cost US$350 million and will be funded by the IFC loan and internally generated cash. The proposed IFC investment is a 7-year senior unsecured A loan in RMB of up to US$150 million equivalent, with a grace period of 3 years.
location_description: The Project location is in China.
development_impact: Stakeholders: The most significant project outcome is the increased provision of quality and affordable diagnostics services in China. The Project also aims at relieving the overcapacity issue at tertiary hospitals in China while enhancing the testing service offerings at secondary and primary hospitals. Resilience: The Project will help increase overall testing capabilities and hopefully have a spillover effect in terms of building resilience against future pandemics in emerging markets around the world. Market Impact: The key market impact is the facilitation of reduction in prices of critical healthcare diagnoses through centralization and increased throughput and efficiency of lab testing. The project will lead to better quality and more accessible tests to the general public as well as demonstration effect to increase the number of market participants.
additionality: IFC's expected financial additionality in this Project, via our A Loan and potential mobilization, is our ability to provide long-term local currency financing that fills the tenor gap, matching the cash generation profile of the Project, and improving the Company's capital structure. IFC's expected non-financial additional is global knowledge and network. The Company has expressed an interest in engaging further with IFC global health quality experts to ensure they maintain their leadership position with respect to quality as they expand their footprint throughout China.

project_description: The proposed investment is a senior loan of up to INR3,750 mn (approximately US$51 mn) to Chalet Hotels Limited (Chalet or Company), an owner/developer of hospitality, commercial and retail assets. Chalet’s portfolio comprises of 7 upscale, upper upscale and luxury hotels including a serviced apartment project (together, 2,554 keys) as well as two commercial and two retail assets, across Mumbai, Bengaluru (Bangalore), Hyderabad and Pune. IFC’s loan will be used to (i) complete fairly advanced construction of a “green” IFC EDGE-certified commercial asset; (ii) refurbish and upgrade existing hotels and (iii) preserve operational liquidity at a time when hospitality cash flows have been devastated by the worst pandemic in a century.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is promoted by one of India’s largest and well-reputed property players, K Raheja Corp (KRC), which was established in 1996. The group is managed by brothers, Mr. Neel Raheja and Mr. Ravi Raheja (together with their father Chandru Raheja and KRC, the Sponsors) who have over 20+ years of experience in real estate development. KRC is the second largest commercial developer in India (developed area: 28 msf+ till FY20), with a sizable residential, retail and hospitality portfolio as well. The Sponsors hold 71.65% shareholding in the Company while domestic and foreign institutions hold ~22.4%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Company has a planned capex of US$109 mn in FY22 and FY23 which shall be used towards greenfield development of 2 commercial assets, the construction of which was halted due to COVID-19, repurpose existing retail space to office space, and refurbishment activities to maintain certain standards at its existing hotels. IFC’s loan of US$51.4 mn will be used by the Company for the completion of construction of commercial assets, for maintenance and refurbishment of its hotels and for general corporate liquidity needs at existing hotels.
location_description: Bengaluru, Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Hyderabad and Pune
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is derived from economy-wide effects by (i) preserving jobs at existing properties, (ii) restarting construction, which would result in the employment of hundreds of daily wage workers, as well as (iii) maintaining timely payments to suppliers including SMEs in the sector that is worst hit by the pandemic. The proposed investment will also (iv) promote greater market resilience in the tourism sector by demonstrating to other players that mixed-use developments create cross-demand and allow for more flexibility as the long-term nature of commercial lease contracts cushion volatility and seasonality of hospitality cash flows, altogether contributing to faster recovery from crises.
additionality: a. Financing Structure: IFC's additionality is demonstrated through its countercyclical role during crises, providing flexible and long-term financing to the Company at a time when commercial lending to the tourism sector has almost come to a standstill. In addition, IFC's loan will be used to renovate existing assets and prepare for the recovery as crisis abates. IFC's financing is also structured to accommodate the expected prolonged recovery of the tourism sector post-COVID. b. Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: Part of IFC's loan will be used to complete the construction of a commercial asset that will be EDGE (green)-certified. In addition, IFC has also engaged with the Company through its TechEmerge Sustainable Cooling Initiative. TechEmerge is an advisory program with an objective to accelerate the adoption of state-of-the-art cooling technologies, help reduce energy consumption and harmful GHG emissions, and drive commercial contract among providers of sustainable cooling solutions and established corporates, across emerging markets. IFC's Gender Advisory will also conduct a Gender Workforce Diagnostic through its Women's Employment Program to increase the number of women employed at Chalet's hotels. c. Standard Setting: IFC will provide support the Company to implement and maintain compliance with the IFC's Performance Standards on Environmental and Social (E&S) Sustainability. At present Chalet does not have a comprehensive E&S Management System in place. IFC will help Chalet to design and implement a robust ESMS in line with IFC's Performance Standards.

company_name: Operadora y Procesadora de Productos Marinos Omarsa S.A.
project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan to Operadora y Procesadora de Productos Marinos Omarsa S.A. (Omarsa or the Company). Founded in the 1977’s by the Vanoni family, Omarsa is one of the leading integrated shrimp producers and processors in Ecuador. The project involves the financing of part of the Company’s capex plan for 2021, consisting of (i) investments on shrimp farms to optimize the feeding process (including solar-powered feeding machines) and on the revamping of water pumping systems and (ii) an expansion on the cold storage facility and shrimp freezing equipment at the Las Brisas plant (the “Project”). These investments will allow the Company to improve its efficiency, in a scenario of low shrimp prices which were significantly affected by the Covid pandemic. The proposed financing will provide relief to the Company’s liquidity condition, which has an important portion of its debt concentrated in the short term.
sponsor_shareholders: Omarsa’s majority shareholders and Project sponsors are the Vanoni family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$14 million. The proposed financing is a US$13 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: All Omarsa’s operations are located in the Guayas province of Ecuador. The processing facility is located in Duran whereas the three farm facilities are located in Guayaquil.
development_impact: - Project impacts: Preserving extensive linkages throughout the value chain; maintaining direct and indirect jobs; increasing availability of high-quality protein. - Market impacts: Supporting the development of a competitive export-oriented sector; improving market practices regarding energy and resource efficiency.
additionality: - Long-term financing with tenors not readily accessible in Ecuador. - Counter-cyclical role to cope with Covid-19 impact. - Extending Environmental & Social standards.
Company Name: Operadora y Procesadora de Productos Marinos Omarsa S.A.

company_name: KADAT FOODS AND BEVERAGES PVT LIMITED
project_description: The proposed investment in Kings Beverages PVT Limited (KB or the Company) consists of: (i) a US$2.5 million A loan and (ii) a US $2.5 million loan from IFC in its capacity as implementing entity for the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP) Private Sector Window. The proposed financing will be used towards capital expenditures for the completion of the KB beverage factory located in Freetown, Sierra Leone, including two new fruit juice lines, one mineral water line as well as one carbonated soft drink (CSD) line (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: KB is a Freetown-based greenfield beverage drink company (mineral water, fruit juice, CSD) that was established by Mr Kishore Parwani and Mr Atul Nijhawan, two entrepreneurs of Indian descent, emanating from Dubai. Mr Parwani has been active in Sierra Leone since the 2000’s in the business of trading scrap metals before venturing go into fast-moving consumer goods distribution and beverage manufacturing in 2011. He then partnered with Mr. Nijhawan in 2016 to launch KB, to capture the growing demand for bottled water and non-alcoholic drinks. Mr Parwani and Mr Nijhawan are each involved in their own trading activities based in Dubai which are primarily engaged in scrap metals for Mr Parwani’s Krishna Global Impex General Trading LLC and chrome and manganese for Mr Nijhawan’s Globustarr Trading Company LLC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$13.7 million. IFC will provide US$5 million consisting of a US$2.5 million senior A loan and a US$2.5 million subordinated GAFSP loan.
location_description: The Project is located is located on 1.9 acres lot in Regent, 6 miles east of Freetown in Sierra Leone.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are its contribution to generating domestic value addition and job creation through investments in processing facilities, improving farmer livelihoods through more reliable access to markets, and strengthening the distributor networks. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that contribution to market creation will stem from (i) first mover operating the largest and first automated plant of its kind in Sierra Leone and using the latest technology and production standards to address local demand; and (ii) expected improvement in quality standards which will encourage competitors to up their game.
additionality: With the proposed investment, IFC is supporting KB in expanding its current operations and product lines in Sierra Leone. In particular, IFC financing will support capital expenditures to complete a partially built factory producing water and CSD as well as add fruit juices to the product lines. The investment is being complemented by IFC's Advisory Services. The project represents one of the first IFC engagements in the country's agribusiness sector and the Company is interested in both financial and non-financial aspects of IFC's additionality. IFC can provide long term financing at tenors that are otherwise not available to the private sector in Sierra Leone. IFC's non-financial additionality includes strengthening KB's operations through advisory services to improve supply chains and capacity of suppliers (mainly smallholder farmers) to supply quality raw materials for the new fruit juice line to the Company. Further, KB's implementation of IFC Performance Standards will ensure the Company's operations align with best international practices in the areas of food safety, operational efficiency, environmental and social standards and corporate governance.
Company Name: KADAT FOODS AND BEVERAGES PVT LIMITED

company_name: COMPAGNIE IVOIRIENNE POUR LE DEVELOPPEMENT DES TEXTILES SA
project_description: The Compagnie Ivoirienne pour le Dévelopement des Textiles (CIDT, the Company) is a cotton ginning company in Cote d’Ivoire (CDI) which is headquartered in Bouaké, the second largest city of the country. The company transforms raw cotton (seed cotton) into cotton lint/fiber which is mainly exported. The seed cotton is acquired from more than 30,000 smallholder farmers active in his exclusive area. IFC’s financing will be used to support CIDT’s expansion plan in CDI (the “Project) for: (i) Building a new 40,000 mtpa ginning plant in Tieningboué to increase the Company’s ginning capacity:; (ii) Upgrading its running plants in Bouaké, Mankono and Séguela; (iii) financing transport equipment which will improve the company’s operations and reduce reliance on third party.
sponsor_shareholders: CIDT is incorporated in Cote d’Ivoire as a private limited company. CIDT was a state-owned company founded in 1973 until up to January 2017 when the residual part of this historical company was privatized through a competitive bidding. COIC acquired 90 percent of stake while the Ivorian State kept the remaining 10 percent. The Parent Company, COIC, is also one of the 5 active ginning companies in CDI and is 100 percent owned by the Ivoirian businessman M. Kone Daouda Soukpafolo.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at around €25.6 million. IFC will provide a corporate facility of €15.4 million via an own account A Loan of €7.7 million with another €7.7 million from the Blended Finance Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP-PSW), as further described in the Blended Finance Section. The remaining financing is provided by the Company’s Internal Generated Cash.
location_description: As part of the Project, a 40,000 mtpa state-of-art plant will be built in Tieningboué (Mankono Region, central CDI). Other operations will take place in Mankono, Bouaké and Séguela.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are: (i) processing internally what is currently outsourced to 2 other processing ginneries; (ii) generating additional resources and expand farmer support to increase productivity since their interest is aligned with those of the farmers: the higher the volume, the better the margin since price is fixed and therefore not a lever of their profitability; (iii) searching for new sources of procurement, outside the contractual zones, and therefore reaching an additional segment of farmers who will benefit from increased incomes from producing cotton. The stakeholder effects for farmers will be enhanced through the provision of Advisory Services focused on capacity building and improved agricultural practices. Beyond the project level, IFC expects the investment to improve competitiveness in the cotton sector through strong demonstration and replication effects, largely at the processing and primary production levels. Capacity building of farmers will motivate processors in other zones to replicate similar practices with their suppliers.
additionality: IFC is supporting CIDT in its expansion in his operation zone. On financial additionality, IFC is providing long term financing in Cote d'Ivoire at tenors that are otherwise not easily available in the market and helping the firm gain traction for its fundraising. IFC's non-financial additionality consists of strengthening CIDT's operations in a challenging sector where market risks are high by : i) providing technical assistance opportunities which will cover cooperation with out-growers to improve productivity and ii) aligning their corporate governance, E&S and risk management with best international practices.
Company Name: COMPAGNIE IVOIRIENNE POUR LE DEVELOPPEMENT DES TEXTILES SA

project_description: Khaadi Corporation (SMC-Private) Limited (“Khaadi” or the “Company”) is a leading retailer of Pakistan with largest market share in formal apparel retail market. Khaadi started operations in 1998 with one store and has expanded its retail network to 62 stores in over 25 cities in Pakistan and 14 international stores in Qatar (1), UAE (6), Bahrain (1) and United Kingdom (6), to mainly cater to the South Asian communities in these countries. ? The Company is undertaking an expansion plan to (i) help grow its operations as it recovers from disruptions related to COVID-19 through expansion of footprint/retail space by adding stores in strategic locations in tier II and III cities across Pakistan, optimization of existing retail space, (ii) acceleration of global online sales, and (iii) expansion of the international store network (the “Project”) and has invited IFC to consider supporting its investment program.
sponsor_shareholders: Khaadi is a single member private limited company. Shamoon Sultan is the founder, Chief Executive Officer and sponsor of Khaadi, currently owning 100% of its capital. Shamoon pursued his formal education in Textile Design from a distinguished an arts college in Pakistan. He started his career by working for a prominent couture designer for a couple of years before setting up his own clothing line in 1998 under the brand name “Khaadi” which means “handlooms” in local language. Since its inception in 1998, Khaadi and Shamoon have won numerous local industry awards.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at approximately US$25 million. The proposed IFC investment includes a quasi-equity investment via convertible preference shares for up to US$25 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project will be located mainly in Pakistan.
development_impact: Implementation of the Project is expected to generate robust local demand for the labor-intensive textile industry, create ~850 direct and indirect jobs with up to 20% for women and enhance tax collection by encouraging formalization of retail and upstream activities. The Project has the potential to provide more job opportunities for female workers, both for those who work directly with the company and for the female workers in the supply chain such as local artisans, designers, and tailors. IFC anticipates that the Project will promote market integration by: i) improving standards across the value chain; ii) increasing access to market for local suppliers; iii) promoting development of retail infrastructure by creating demand for lease space and; iv) increasing formal retail penetration in Tier II/III cities. The expansion of Khaadi stores into Tier II and III cities of Pakistan will increase access to goods at attractive price-points and quality products otherwise not available outside large cities in the country.
additionality: IFC will be providing the Company with long-term patient capital not readily available locally for asset-light companies that will help strengthen the financial soundness, creditworthiness, and governance of the Company. IFC's equity financing will also provide confidence in Khaadi's minority shareholder rights as it progresses towards public listing. In addition, IFC will also assist the Company in establishing adequate Corporate Governance standards and E&S policies to ensure full compliance of the Project with IFC performance standards.

project_description: Founded in 2017, Toters (“TAN (Holding), Sal” or the “Company”) is an on-demand delivery platform operating in Lebanon and Iraq. The Group offers grocery, food, and convenience product delivery from a wide variety of more than 2,000 partner restaurants, coffee shops, bakeries, grocery stores, electronic stores, para-pharmacies, and flower shops, etc. via a Toters’ network consisting of thousands of couriers. IFC is considering an equity investment of US$5 million in Toters. The funding will primarily be used to expand the Group’s operations in Iraq.
sponsor_shareholders: Toters was founded by Tamim Al Khalfah, who currently serves as the CEO, and Nael Halwani, who currently serves as the COO. Existing shareholders in the Company include March Holding, B&Y Venture Partners, and Middle East Venture Partners.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Proposed IFC equity investment of up to US$5 million as part of the Series B financing round to fund the Group’s expansion in Iraq.
location_description: Toters is headquartered in Beirut, Lebanon and operates in both Lebanon and Iraq.
development_impact: The development impact of the project will be via: (i) Project Outcomes (Stakeholders): Improved access to goods for consumers, increased access to markets for merchants, and increased micro-entrepreneurship opportunities for couriers. (ii) Contribution to Market Creation (Competitiveness): Increased competitiveness of the retail distribution market in Lebanon and Iraq via demonstration and replication channels.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality will be via: (i) IFC's own account equity: IFC will provide patient risk capital in two markets where venture capital is not readily available; (ii) Non-commercial risk mitigation: IFC's investment is expected to give comfort to other investors; and (iii) Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC will share expertise and learnings from portfolio companies and network.

project_description: Founded in 2017, Brimore Holding B.V. (“Brimore” or the “Company”) is an assisted e-commerce platform in Egypt targeting mass market consumers. The Company utilizes a social commerce model to reach these underserved segments. IFC is considering an equity investment of US$5 million in Brimore. The funding will primarily be used to expand the Company’s operations.
sponsor_shareholders: Brimore was founded by Mohamed Abdulaziz, who currently serves as the CEO, and Ahmed Sheikha, who currently serves as the Chief Business Officer. Existing shareholders in the Company include Algebra Ventures (an IFC investee fund) and Endure Capital.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Proposed IFC equity investment of up to US$5 million as part of the Series A financing round to fund the Company’s expansion.
location_description: Brimore is headquartered in Netherlands and operates in Egypt.
development_impact: The development impact of the project will be via: (i) Project Outcomes (Stakeholders): Improved access to goods for consumers, increased access to markets for suppliers, and creation of microentrepreneurship opportunities for agents, who are primarily female. (ii) Contribution to Market Creation (Inclusiveness): Improving the inclusiveness of the Egyptian e-commerce sector by triggering replication of an innovative business model that enable market expansion to the underserved in a cost-effective manner
additionality: IFC's expected additionality will be via: (i) IFC's own account equity: IFC will provide patient risk capital; and (ii) Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC will share expertise and learnings from its portfolio companies and network.

project_description: Established in France in 1900, Soufflet is privately-owned by the Soufflet family through Ets. J Soufflet SA, a holding company incorporated in France. Groupe Soufflet (Soufflet, or the Group) is vertically integrated agribusiness group that operates in in wheat & barley value chains, together with rice and pulses sectors and advises wine growers. It has operations in 22 countries globally, including 9 ECA countries. The Group is a leading direct buyer of cereals in Europe and also operates in the international cereal markets. In the barley sector, it is one of the world’s top malt producers, with a presence in Europe, Asia, Africa and South America, while it is one of Europe’s leading wheat millers and an expert in developing tailormade ingredients. The Group also develops and manufactures enzymes and yeasts and is a significant player in the industrial bakery sector industry in France and Portugal and is also active in the fast food sector. The Group invests in research and innovation to enhance the value of agricultural resources.
sponsor_shareholders: Groupe Soufflet is a French family owned agri food group
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Soufflet’s average working capital needs in the Project Countries are €130 million. The proposed IFC financing amounts to a €50 million A-Loan to support such needs.
location_description: The IFC financing will be used in the five Project Countries - Ukraine, Romania, Bulgaria, Kazakhstan and Poland.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is the impact on farmers' access to markets and quality inputs as well as its contribution to global food security.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality in this Project stems largely from non-commercial risk mitigation and improvement of the Company's environmental and social practices. IFC's financial additionality relates to provision of working capital finance in a timely manner in a counter cyclical market affected the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_description: This project is proposed under IFC’s Global Trade Supplier Finance program (“GTSF” or the “Program”) approved by the IFC Board on September 21, 2010 (Project #28723). Under GTSF, IFC provides short-term financing to emerging market suppliers (“Suppliers”) selling to large domestic buyers or exporting to international buyers, by discounting invoices once they are approved by the Buyer. Under this transaction, IFC will provide financing to Suppliers of Wolverine World Wide, Inc. (“Wolverine” or “the Company”) that are based in Vietnam, Cambodia, India and other emerging market countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Wolverine is a leading global footwear Company. The company was started in 1883 and has been listed on the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) since 1965. Major shareholders of the Company are BlackRock Fund Advisors, the Vanguard Group and other institutional investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: GTSF facility with outstanding amount of up to US$15 million to finance suppliers of the Company.
location_description: Vietnam, Cambodia, India and other emerging market countries.

project_description: The proposed investment is an up to EUR600 million (approximately US$723 million) financing package comprising (i) an unsecured, straight senior loan (“A” loan) of up to EUR200 million (approximately US$241 million) from IFC and; (ii) mobilization of “B” and/or parallel loans of up to EUR400 million (approximately US$482 million) to Aspen Finance Proprietary Limited (AFPL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Aspen Pharmacare Holdings Limited (Aspen or the Company). The financing will help Aspen, South Africa’s largest pharmaceutical company, to refinance existing debt and strengthen the Company’s balance sheet, supporting Aspen’s operations including production of vaccines, and other therapies in African and emerging markets.
sponsor_shareholders: AFPL is a wholly owned subsidiary of Aspen which, inter alia, centrally manages the group’s syndicated loan programs. As a company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), Aspen’s shareholding is a mix of the founders, institutional investors and domestic and international asset managers. Aspen’s two co-founders, Stephen Saad (Group Chief Executive) and Gus Attridge (Deputy Group Chief Executive), own 12.5 percent and 4.2 percent of the Company, respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment in Aspen through AFPL is an unsecured IFC “A” loan of up to EUR200 million (approximately US$241 million) and “B” loans of up to EUR400 million (approximately US$482 million), with a tenor of up to seven years, to be disbursed in Euros.
location_description: The proposed investment is a corporate finance loan to AFPL, acting in its capacity as treasury company to Aspen, which has a global presence in both emerging and developed markets.
development_impact: The Project will refinance existing loans which funded the addition of sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity and the acquisition of related pharmaceutical products which are supplied to emerging markets. This has allowed for an increase of available supplies of healthcare products to treat, inter alia, COVID-19 patients, including the supply of COVID-19 vaccines at a time where demand exceeds supply.
additionality: The Project will refinance existing loans which funded the addition of sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity and the acquisition of related pharmaceutical products which are supplied to emerging markets. This has allowed for an increase of available supplies of healthcare products to treat, inter alia, COVID-19 patients, including the supply of COVID-19 vaccines at a time where demand exceeds supply. IFC's financial additionality is delivered through the provision of long-term, euro-denominated financing, comprising a loan with a tenor of up to seven years, for immediate needs. IFC will also mobilize funds from other DFIs and/or commercial banks for the Project. IFC's non-financial additionality is provided through the presence and reach of IFC and other WBG members, which could help increase the Company's access to clients, especially to partners keen on strengthening the local production of pharmaceuticals and vaccines in Africa.

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: Founded in 2002, GEM Co., Ltd. (“GEM”, the “Company”) is a leading waste recycler and manufacturer of lithium-based battery materials in China. The proposed investment is a RMB 500 million (approximately US$76 million equivalent) A Loan to support the Company’s construction of new recycling facilities in Hubei Province, a frontier region of China (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Kaihua XU, the founder and chairman of GEM (the “Sponsor”) and his wife Ms Min WANG collectively hold 11.0% of the Company’s shares as the largest shareholder.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is expected to be up to US$152 million, which will be primarily funded by the Company’s internal cash generation and cash balance, with the remaining amount funded by the IFC loan. The proposed investment is an A Loan of up to RMB 500 million (approximately US$76 million equivalent).
location_description: Jingmen, Hubei Province
development_impact: Project-level: (i) increase recycling capacities and promote circular economy; and (ii) create employment opportunities and economic linkages. Market creation: enhance integration of battery recycling practices.
additionality: IFC's Role and Additionality: (i) long-term financing beyond what is available in the market; (ii) standard settings and sharing of best practices in Environmental and Social (E&S) aspects.

project_description: Liquid Telecommunications (Jersey) Limited (“the Company” or “Liquid”) is a leading pan-African technology group with operations across 15 countries, primarily in Sub-Saharan Africa. Liquid has firmly established itself as the leading provider of pan-African digital infrastructure with an extensive network covering approximately 100,000 km. Liquid is redefining network, cloud, and cybersecurity offerings through strategic partnerships with leading global players, innovative business applications, smart cloud services and world-class security on the African continent. The Group also operates data centres in Johannesburg, Cape Town, Nairobi, Harare and Kigali, with a combined potential 19,000 square metres of rack space and 74 MW of power. The transaction comprises of a US$90 million equity investment to help company expand its data centre business. The investment would enable the Company to undertake it’s planned capital expenditure program over next few years to continue be the leading player supporting the digitization of Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: Liquid is a privately owned company which was established in 2004 as an independent telecommunications provider of international, voice, internet and data transmission using fibre and satellite technologies. The company is ultimately owned by shareholders including Royal Bafokeng Nation, CDC Group, Gateway Partners, the Masiyiwa Family, and management.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will be investing US$90 million in equity. The investment will be made through a mix of subscription to convertible preference shares and payment to certain holders of rights issue. Out of the total proposed investment (of US$90 million), approximately US$80 million would be injected into the company and the balance would be paid to certain shareholders.
location_description: The Project involves expansion of the Company’s data center operations across the African continent, including in South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, and Egypt.
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase access to data center capacity for businesses in regional hubs like South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria and Egypt, along with countries with larger gaps such as the DRC and South Sudan, that are digitally connected to these hubs. This has the potential to enable increased availability of quality digital services for individuals and enhanced productivity growth for businesses, recognizing some potential for increased GHG emissions. Beyond the Project, the investment is expected to strengthen integration of the African economy by enabling a faster growth of cloud computing services through expansion of data infrastructure.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists of the provision of patient equity to support the expansion of a data center business model that requires time to become profitable. IFC's own account equity will also support entry in nascent data center markets where demand takes time to build up at a time when a few existing shareholders have reached their exposure limit. Non-financial additionality involves non-commercial risk mitigation by providing comfort to a significant lender through a deleveraging of the Company.

sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: Newko Balkan SH.P.K (“Newko Balkan” or the “Company”), a Republic of Kosovo-based manufacturer of conveyor belts, seeks a senior IFC A loan of up to EUR4 million (the “IFC Loan”) to help fund (i) the Company’s COVID-related working capital needs and (ii) upgrade investments to increase efficiency and expand production operations (the “Project”). The Project will be IFC’s second engagement with the Company following IFC’s initial investment in 2010 to support Newko Balkan’s post-privatization ramp-up and refurbishment investments.
sponsor_shareholders: Newko Balkan is a wholly owned subsidiary of Ozer Konveyor Band Turizm Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (“Ozer Band”), a mid-sized Turkish conveyor belt manufacturer. Ozer Band is a family business owned by the Ozer family of Turkey.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost is expected to be EUR4 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to EUR4 million.
location_description: Newko Balkan has only one plant located 60 km away from Pristina, the capital city of Republic of Kosovo. The site is within the city of Suhareke in an urban area.
development_impact: The proposed south-south Project is expected to: (i) create additional jobs and preserve more than 230 direct jobs while increasing purchases from local suppliers; (ii) contribute to foreign exchange generation through strong export sales; (iii) benefit domestic consumers by ensuring access to lower cost, high quality locally produced conveyor belts; and (iv) promote the resilience of the conveyor belt production activities in Kosovo by supporting the only local conveyor belt producer.
additionality: The proposed IFC Loan will enable IFC to perform its countercyclical role in the current volatile market environment and will provide long-term funding which is not commonly available in the market. Furthermore, IFC will help the Company improve its E&S and corporate governance policies and practices and align its performance with best practice benchmarks.

project_description: The absence of safe, effective and well-functioning medical devices and equipment impairs health service provision, leads to poor patient outcomes and poses substantial health system risks. IFC’s funding will allow In?nity, a leading medical equipment distributor and service provider primarily in Ethiopia, to: Fill medical equipment orders from hospitals and clinics, including emergency care solutions. Provide the “patient capital” needed to maintain the necessary inventory level to minimize hospital equipment downtime and promote efficient use in both public and private hospitals. Continue to provide customers with good credit standing and steady patient flow, buy-now-pay-later option.
sponsor_shareholders: Infinity Advanced Technology Solutions PLC is majority-owned by Mr. Brook Fekadu, the founder and the CEO of the company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project Cost is expected to be c. US$3 million. IFC is looking to provide an own account A Loan of up to US$3 million in Ethiopian Birr (“ETB”), with support from International Development Association’s Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA-PSW LCF) subject to an approval from National Bank of Ethiopia.
location_description: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
development_impact: Project level impact: Improved access to high quality equipment for patients in Ethiopia. At present, access to foreign currency has limited private hospitals' ability to access high quality medical equipment which needs to be imported. The Project will expand Infinity's capacity to import and distribute medical equipment. The client will also provide training in the use of equipment to the hospitals/ clinics, ensuring patients receive adequate services. Market level impact: The Project will expand access to quality medical equipment for private, in addition to public, health services providers in Ethiopia. The equal footing through access to equipment via finance for both public and private, should help contribute to positioning the emerging private sector, increasing demand for private health services, and contributing to the development of a more competitive health services market.
additionality: 1. Financial Additionality: Financing Structure: a) A facility with USD disbursement and local currency repayment is currently not available in Ethiopia; b) IFC is proposing a 6-year loan, including a 2.5-year grace period. Such long-tenor financing with the grace period is not readily available in Ethiopia. 2. Non-Financial Additionality - Standard Setting: IFC will assist Infinity to strengthen its environmental, and social governance (ESG) standards.

project_description: On May 13, 2021, IFC’s board of directors authorize it to invest up to an aggregate of €150 million in 7 to 10-year, green, Eurobonds to be issued by CTP N.V. (CTP or the Company, or together with its subsidiaries, the Group) under CTP’s €8 billion Euro Medium Term Notes (EMTN) program (the Green Bonds). CTP will use the proceeds of IFC’s investment in the Green Bonds for the development of green-certified industrial and logistics properties in Romania and Serbia (the Project). The Group is the largest full-service owner-developer of prime industrial and logistics properties in the Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) region. CTPs primary market is in the Czech Republic, and it also has operations in Romania, Hungary, Slovakia, Serbia and Poland.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group was established in the Czech Republic in 1998 and developed into a major industrial and logistics real estate owner-developer in the CEE region. The Company is a public limited liability holding company incorporated under the laws of the Netherlands. CTP is the indirect parent of all property-owning companies of the Group. The Group is majority owned and controlled by Mr. Remon Vos.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: On June 21, 2021, IFC invested €42.5 million in CTP’s first 8-year green Eurobond issued under its EMTN program (the IFC First Investment). The IFC First Investment represented 8.5% of the total issue size of €500 million. The green Eurobond will be listed on the Euronext stock exchange in Dublin. On September 27, 2021, IFC invested €58.0 million in CTP’s first 10-year green Eurobond issued under its EMTN program (the IFC Second Investment). The IFC Second Investment represented 11.6% of the total issue size of €500 million. The green Eurobond will be listed on the Euronext stock exchange in Dublin. On July 1, 2022, IFC invested the last tranche of €49.5 million out of the total €150 million in a tap issue under CTP’s exiting senior secured green Eurobonds maturing in September 2031 (the IFC Third Investment). The green Eurobond will be listed on the Euronext stock exchange in Dublin.
location_description: Romania and Serbia
additionality: IFC's involvement is expected to have both financial and non-financial additionality. Through its participation in the Bonds, IFC is playing an important, market-signaling role to help extend the tenor of CTP's financing and catalyze the entry of other investors that will help the Group grow its commercial property business in line with market demands and better match the economic life of its commercial property portfolio. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will work with the Group to further improve its corporate governance policy to meet best practices. The Group will also optimize its sustainability policy, its group-level human resources policy as well as its formal procedure for addressing workers' grievances.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: NSG UK Enterprises Limited (“NSG UK” or “the Company”), a leading global glass producer, has invited IFC to consider providing up to US$40 million corporate loan to finance its subsidiary in Argentina, Vidrieria Argentina S.A. (“VASA”, a JV 51% NSG UK and 49% Saint-Gobain). The IFC Loan will finance the completion of the Company’s greenfield glass production plant in Argentina (partially financed by the IFC in 2019, Original Project, NSG Argentina #42550). This project is linked to project NSG Argentina #42550, https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/42550/nsg-argentina
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1918 and headquartered in Tokyo, Nippon Sheet Glass Co. Ltd. (“NSG Group”) is a well-diversified global manufacturer of glass and glazing products for the automotive, architectural and technical glass markets. NSG Group ranks among the global top 3 producers in each of its global core markets, with strong presence in automotive applications. With manufacturing operations in about 30 countries and sales in over 100 countries, it employs approximately 27,000 people worldwide. NSG Group is listed on the Tokyo stock exchange. NSG UK Enterprises (“NSG UK” or the “Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of Nippon Sheet Glass Co., manufactures architectural and automotive glass products. With more than 150 years in business, the Company has 18 float glass lines, 16 automotive glass plants, and large downstream glass operations in over 20 countries throughout America, Europe and Asia. Saint-Gobain, NSG UK’s JV partner in VASA, is a European and worldwide leader in flat glass, high performance materials, and construction products.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposed investment consists of a US$40 million A Loan to finance the completion and start of operations of the Company's greenfield (approximately 225,000 tons per annum) float glass production plant in Argentina.
location_description: The Project will be located in an industrial site in Cardales, approximately 70 kilometers north-west of Buenos Aires, Argentina.
development_impact: "The proposed loan will finance the completion of the Original Project. This will enable IFC to support Argentina's macro challenges by (i) supporting foreign direct investment (FDI); (ii) substituting imports and generating exports; (iii) adding value to domestic raw materials; and (iv) enhancing value chains."
additionality: IFC has financial additionality as long-term financing is not readily available to the Company under terms that are well aligned with the Project's cash flows given longer term nature of the investment and impact of COVID-19 pandemic. The Company is also considering an IFC advisory engagement for its subsidiaries to help identify energy efficiency opportunities.

company_name: TABREED ASIA CENTRAL COOLING COMPANY PTE. LTD.
project_description: The proposed investment is an equity investment of US$25 million by IFC for a 25% stake in a District Cooling Company (DCC or the Company), proposed to be set up in Singapore along with the National Central Cooling Company PJSC (Tabreed or Sponsor). Tabreed will hold 75% stake in the Company. The DCC will enter into long term concession agreements with major real estate developers to deploy district cooling (DC) technology in commercial, industrial, and retail establishments in India and other markets in Asia to deploy around 90,000 refrigeration tons (RT) of cooling capacity in the next 3-4 years.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor, Tabreed is amongst the world’s largest district cooling utilities, providing cooling service to government and private developers in UAE and Gulf Cooperation Council. Rated ‘Baa3’ and ‘BBB’ by Moody’s and Fitch Ratings, Tabreed is backed by well-established entities with ENGIE SA and Mubadala Investment Company holding 40% and 42% equity stake in the company respectively. It is listed on the Dubai Stock Exchange with a market cap of US$2.19 billion as on 15th May 2021. Tabreed currently delivers over 1.4 million RT of DC services across 86 projects. In 2020, their operations resulted in energy savings of 2.26 billion kWh and 1.35 million tons carbon dioxide emissions savings, when compared to conventional cooling systems.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Company will be capitalized with US$100 million of equity to be funded in the proportion of Tabreed’s and IFC’s shareholding. IFC will invest US$25 million in the form of newly issued common shares over the next 3-4 years. The Company targets building 90,000 RT of projects in India and other countries in Asia with an investment of upto US$300 million (US$100 million equity and balance in debt).
location_description: The initial focus market is India, but the Company would subject to approvals target other Asian geographies as well, at a later date.
development_impact: Space cooling is increasingly recognized as a development priority especially in emerging economies located in the tropical climate zone. India is experiencing a rapid growth in demand for space cooling, driven by population growth, urbanization, increasing incomes and rising urban heat. According to the India Cooling Action Plan, space cooling demand in India is expected to rise by 11 times from the year 2018 to the year 2038, leading to energy consumption and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions rising by 4x. The commercial real estate sector is expected to add 100 million RT in capacity during this period. The Company will pioneer the development of DC solutions at scale in India. These projects are expected to improve access to space cooling, reduce lifecycle cooling costs, decrease energy consumption, reduce peak power and refrigerant demand. The energy efficiency benefits are expected to lead to GHG emissions savings. IFC anticipates that the Company would contribute to faster market adoption of DC technology in the Asian countries by successfully demonstrating the commercial viability of the "cooling as a service" business model.
additionality: This investment will signal WBG's strong support for the adoption of DC technology in emerging markets, thus creating visibility and an enabling environment for further future investments in the sector. Through the proposed investment, IFC will provide patient capital, not readily available in the domestic market, to support this pioneering project. IFC may act a lead arranger to mobilise debt from other development finance institutions and commercial banks. In addition, IFC is providing targeted advisory support to map out and develop viable business models that will incentivize developers to adopt this technology. IFC will help the Company to mitigate environment and social (E&S) risks through the adoption of IFC Performance Standards and enhance corporate governance structures and processes in line with international best practices.
Company Name: TABREED ASIA CENTRAL COOLING COMPANY PTE. LTD.

project_description: Robust International (“Robust” or the “Company”) is a midscale agri-commodity trader headquartered in Singapore that specializes in niche commodities such as sesame, cashew, and ginger. The company is active in sourcing from across Sub-Saharan Africa. IFC’s financing will be used to support Robust’s expansion of operations in Nigeria (the “Project), where use of funds includes i) financing the construction of warehouse complexes and sesame processing facilities in Nigeria, and (ii) associated working capital to support increased sourcing and processing activity under the project.
sponsor_shareholders: Robust is incorporated in Singapore as a private limited company. The company is wholly owned by the founder, Chairman Naarayan Raaghavan, and his family. This project loan is being extended to Robust’s entity in Singapore, with use of proceeds earmarked solely for the project in Nigeria.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at around USD 25.7 million. IFC will provide a corporate facility of USD 18 million via an own account A Loan of USD 9 million with another USD 9 million from the International Development Association’s Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA-PSW-BFF), as further described in the Blended Finance Section. The remaining financing will be new equity injected by the client.
location_description: As part of the Project, an integrated complex with warehouses and sesame processing lines will be constructed in the Kano region, and a warehouse will be setup along the Lagos-Ibadan highway.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project outcomes are i) contributing to domestic value addition through investments in processing facilities, ii) improving farmer livelihoods through more reliable access to storage and offtake, and iii) benefitting the environment through reductions in GHG emissions associated with high food losses. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that contribution to market creation will stem from better integrating an underserved part of the country into global value chains by setting up storage and processing facilities close to the producers and demonstrating the business rationale for enhancing this type of physical infrastructure in the north of Nigeria to counter existing bottlenecks for sector development.
additionality: IFC is supporting Robust in its value-added trading and processing operations at origin in Nigeria. On financial additionality, IFC is providing long term financing in Nigeria at tenors that are otherwise not available to private sector companies and mobilize other lenders to provide financing on comparable terms. IFC's non-financial additionality centers around strengthening Robust's operations in a challenging sector where market risks are high, doing so by aligning their corporate governance, E&S and risk management with best international practices.

project_description: The proposed investment is up to a €165 million financing package to subsidiaries of the Omnium des Industries et de la Promotion Group (OIP or the Group), a leading cement producer in Morocco and West Africa, to finance (i) a greenfield integrated cement plant in Pout, Senegal; (ii) the addition of cement grinding capacity to an existing grinding station in Dio Gare, Mali; (iii) the addition of cement grinding capacity to an existing grinding station in Tema, Ghana (together, the “Project”). The Project will be implemented through Ciments de l'Afrique (CIMAF), the Group’s sub-Saharan African subsidiaries, in each of Senegal, Mali and Ghana. The Project will expand clinker and cement capacity in West Africa to meet the growing demand for building materials across the subregion and to improve CIMAF’s competitiveness. The IDA19 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) may support this Project in Mali as described in the Blended Finance Section.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsor is Mr. Anas Sefrioui, a Moroccan businessman with interests in the real estate and cement industries. Mr. Sefrioui owns 100% of OIP (a holding company incorporated in Morocco), 100% of CIMA Holdings (a holding company incorporated in Luxemburg), and 100% of the CIMAF subsidiaries. The Project will be implemented by CIMAF Senegal, CIMAF Mali and CIMAF Ghana respectively. CIMAF Senegal and CIMAF Ghana are owned 70% by OIP and 30% by CIMA Holding, while CIMAF Mali is owned 90% by OIP and 10% by CIMA Holding.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at €250 million. The proposed investment is an up to €165 million financing package, consisting of up to €92.5 million in A-loans for IFC’s own account and up to €82.5 million in B1 and/or parallel loans. IDA PSW BFF may provide an up to €7.5 million senior loan to support the project in Mali as described in the Blended Finance Section.
location_description: The Project will be located (i) in the Pout Sud region in Senegal, 25km east of Dakar, for CIMAF Senegal; (ii) on the current site of its existing cement grinding station in Dio Gare, Mali, 35 km from Bamako, for CIMAF Mali; and (iii) on the current site of its existing cement grinding station in Tema, Ghana, a major port area 30km outside Accra, for CIMAF Ghana.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcomes are economy-wide benefits and employee skills development. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to promote market competitiveness in Senegal via innovation and improved efficiency.
additionality: IFC's involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide scarce financing to the Group that is not otherwise readily available in the respective local markets of Senegal, Mali and Ghana. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will provide advice to the Group on how to raise the standards of the Company's cement operations in Ghana, Mali and Senegal in terms of corporate governance, EHS and E&S risk management in line with WBG requirements.

project_description: Established in 1920, in Morocco, and transformed into a société anonyme in 2008, OCP SA (“OCP” or the “Company,” https://www.ocpgroup.ma/ ) is the world’s leading producer and exporter of phosphate products. OCP is the largest company (c. 21,000 employees) and largest exporter (17.3% of the country’s exports in 2019) in Morocco. OCP has fertilizer processing platforms at Safi and Jorf Lasfar in Morocco. OCP is looking to increase its presence in Africa and thus established, OCP Africa SA (“OCP Africa”, https://www.ocpafrica.com/en/home ) in 2016, a subsidiary dedicated to growing the business in Sub-saharan Africa (SSA) with the main objectives of producing fertilizer near main agribusiness markets, invest in logistics and distribution, and provide support and training to farmers. The proposed investment is to finance the Company and its subsidiaries’ (the “Group”) facilities and agri-ecosystem development program in Senegal, Cote d’Ivoire, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya and Tanzania (the “Project”):
sponsor_shareholders: OCP S.A is 94.12% owned by the Moroccan State. The remaining interests are held by Infra Maroc Capital (2.98%), Prev Invest SA (1.10%), Société d'Aménagement et de Développement Vert (0.88%), SOCINVEST (0.82%) and Banque Centrale Populaire S.A. (0.10%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated project cost is US$145.5 million, of which IFC will be financing up to US$100.0 million via an A Loan.
location_description: OCP is headquartered in Casablanca, Morocco. The IFC Loan proceeds will be used in OCP Africa subsidiaries facilities located in Nigeria, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, and Tanzania.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is driven largely by stakeholder effects, particularly for farmers and distributors, namely: (i) increased agricultural productivity and farmer returns due to customized products and extension/agronomy services (ii) improved logistics for better distribution of agricultural inputs in SSA, particularly West Africa. Beyond the project level, IFC expects the investment to promote mostly small-holding farmers' integration into domestic and regional value chains.
additionality: Through the proposed investment and the parallel advisory service package, IFC will help a leading fertilizer player grow into a solutions provider in its industry for the benefits of mostly smallholder farmers in SSA. IFC's additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial, the latter coming in three forms: financing structure, providing knowledge, innovation and capacity building; risk mitigation; and standard setting.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of (i) an A Loan of up to US$30 million with a tenor of up to 3 years including one-year grace; and (ii) a B Loan of at least US$120 million with a tenor of 3 years including 1-year grace. The IFC loan will be backed by a 25% First Loss Guarantee from the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP-PSW), to rebalance the risk-return profile of the transaction for IFC. ETG is a vertically integrated agricultural supply chain manager involved in the origination, procurement, warehousing, logistics of multiple agricultural commodities and processing of consumer products. It is active in over 26 African countries, as well as in India, China and South East Asia and has additional trading, merchandising and/or treasury desks in Europe, the Americas and the Middle East. The financing will help ETG mitigate the impacts from COVID-19 across its supply chain which have adversely impacted its operations. The proposed investment will provide much needed liquidity to support the uninterrupted production and distribution of food commodities globally during this trying period. This project is linked to ETG Term Facility - https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/43692/etg-term-facility
sponsor_shareholders: Ultimate beneficial owners of ETG together controlling 55.6% are Mr. Mahesh Patel (Chairman), Mr. Ketan Patel (CEO) and Bisa Trust represented by the Joint-CEO, Birju Patel. Other key shareholders are Mitsui & Co. via its African arm MIT African Management Limited (31.9%) and Pembani Remgro of South Africa (8.8%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated project cost is US$150 million. IFC will support the Project with an investment of up to US$30 million in the form of an unsecured loan. In addition, the project is expected to be supported by the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP PSW) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
location_description: The funds are expected to be utilized mainly in Sub Saharan Africa to finance ETG’s trading flows in agri commodities including fertilizer, cashews, pulses among others.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is that, at a time of unprecedented crisis as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, the proposed investment will help food flow globally and allow developing markets to maintain jobs and exports. Further, ETG will ensure the availability of liquidity for its distributors and farmers through its procurement activities. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the financing will improve market resilience by maintaining procurement of agricultural commodities across ETG's supply chains and by building the capacity of suppliers and of the Group to withstand shocks and stresses related to COVID-19.
additionality: IFC's additionality is driven largely by its countercyclical role during crises, including IFC's experience with rapid crisis response efforts; programs aimed at investing both large-scale and transactional liquidity and capital for trade finance and working capital in emerging markets; ability to support clients to address liquidity constraints in response to COVID19 and to provide critical goods, equipment, and supplies; its ability to help clients redirect supply chains; and its support to continued employment in countries of operation.

project_description: Shanghai Fosun Pharmaceutical (Group) Co. Ltd., (“Fosun Pharma”, or the “Company”) is a leading manufacturer of pharmaceutical products and medical devices in China. The Company’s business spans across the healthcare value chain from research & development, pharmaceutical manufacturing, medical devices and diagnosis, to healthcare services, pharmaceutical distribution and retail. Fosun Pharma has been listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange since 1998 and Hong Kong Stock Exchange since 2012. The proposed IFC investment will primarily support Fosun Pharma’s manufacturing and distribution of COVID-19 related medical products, including the COVID-19 vaccine co-developed by Pfizer / BioNTech and COVID-19 testing kits and in China (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is Fosun International Limited (“Fosun International”), which owns 36.6% of the Company while 63.4% is held by public shareholders.
