total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated to be up to US$420 million. IFC’s proposed investment is a straight senior loan of up to US$200 million with a tenor of up to seven years.
location_description: Fosun Pharma is headquartered in Shanghai, China. The Project involves capital expenditures associated with expansion of cold-chain warehousing and distribution networks across China.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level effect is the broadened access to COVID-19 vaccine. Beyond the project, it is anticipated that the investment will enhance the resilience of healthcare supply chains in emerging markets.
additionality: IFC's Additionality in this Project comes in three forms: (i) long-term financing which matches the needs of project life cycle and capital structure; (ii) provision of advice as the Company expand geographical coverage, especially for its distribution of COVID-19 related products; and (iii) sharing of best practices in Environmental and Social (E&S) aspects.

sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: The proposed investment consists of up to EUR37 million senior loan package to Uni Confort Maroc – Dolidol SA (“UCM”, “Dolidol” or the “Company”), a leading manufacturer and distributor of polyurethane (PU) foam and bedding products. The Company was established in Morocco in 1972 by Berrada Sounni Family and expanded its geographical footprint in Cote d’Ivoire in 2014. Dolidol has a 45-years track record and is a trusted and quality provider of bedding products with internationally recognized accreditations (i.e., ISO 45001, ISO 9001, IATF 16949). As of December 31, 2020, Dolidol employs 1,000 people and has a logistic platform (17,000 sqm) and 150 trucks. It sells its products through a network of 1,100 distributors, 50 owned stores and 10 distribution facilities. Dolidol’s investment plans include (i) an acquisition in Nigeria, (ii) a greenfield plastic recycling capex in Morocco and (iii) installation of solar panels (1.25MW) on the Company’s industrial facilities in Morocco (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Dolidol’s main shareholders are Palmeraie Industries (63%), Palmeraie Holding (14%) and Development Partners International (DPI) Private Equity (23%). Palmeraie Industries and Palmeraie Holding are owned by Berrada Sounni Family members including Saad Berrada Sounni (33%), Hicham Berrada Sounni (33%), Nabila Berrada Sounni (17%) and Hanaa Berrada Sounni (17%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The cost of the Project is estimated at EUR42 million which IFC will support with a EUR37 million senior loan financing package comprised of up to EUR25 million A loan and up to EUR12 million parallel loan. Within the scope of the Project, IFC’s financing will be directly used to support Dolidol’s expansion in Nigeria and capital expenditures in Morocco.
location_description: The Project will be located in Dar Bouazza Industrial Park in Casablanca, Morocco.
development_impact: Project impact Economy-wide: The Project's contribution to value addition and both direct and indirect employment will be estimated using IFC's sector multipliers. The Project is expected to create between 200 and 250 jobs. Stakeholders (employee skills): The Project will support the continuous development of technical skills and the development of industry-relevant skills and adoption of superior production techniques, which will lead to an improvement of the human capital in these countries. Environment: The Project includes several climate related components, including installation of solar panels on the Company's facility in Morocco as well as plastic recycling through Dolicen, its new subsidiary. Market impact Competitiveness: The Project is expected to have meaningful impact in market-level dimension of competitiveness (i.e. through demonstration and replication effects, as other players are considering investing in the automotive sector in Morocco). It will also promote the competitiveness of other related manufacturing sectors (e.g. automotive) which use the Company's output as their intermediary products. The plastic recycling plant (Dolicen) is a commercial approach to manufacturing that can be replicated by other players in Morocco. Installing solar panels may also set a beneficial environmental precedent in the market.
additionality: Financial additionality: IFC's proposed 7-year tenor with a 2-year grace period is longer than those currently available in the local market. This long-term financing will enable the Company to both grow and weather any downturns in the industry or countries of development. Moreover, this Project will attract financing from other lenders. In addition, COVID-19 has led to operating difficulties globally, including in Morocco and Nigeria. IFC funding will help support the sponsor during a difficult time globally. Commercial banks and other lenders may be significantly less willing to provide funding at this time. Non-financial additionality: IFC will support the Company to raise its standards in terms of corporate governance and E&S practices (energy efficiency, recycling). Finally, IFC's investment will provide political and regulatory risk mitigation to the Company.

project_description: Integrated Diagnostics Holding Plc. (IDH or the Company) is a leading diagnostic service provider in the Middle East and Africa (MEA) region offering pathology and radiology services in Egypt, Jordan, Sudan and Nigeria. The Company has a 40-year track record and is a trusted and quality provider of diagnostics services with internationally recognized accreditations (ISO, CAP and JCI). IDH offers over 2,000 diagnostic tests under 7 key brands with strong reputation in underserved markets. As of September 30, 2020, IDH has a network of 471 branches and employs over 5,500 employees across its geographic footprint. IDH is a Jersey registered public limited company listed on the London Stock Exchange (LSE) since May 2015. IDHs investment plans include expansion plans in Egypt and new acquisitions and greenfield investments in other emerging markets as well as achieving a dual listing of its shares on the Egyptian Stock Exchange (EGX) (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The main shareholders of IDH are Hena Holdings (25.5 percent) and Actis Private Equity (21 percent) while the remaining 53.5 percent is free float in LSE. Hena Holdings is jointly owned by Dr. Hend El Sherbini (CEO of IDH) and Dr. Moamena Kamel (mother of Dr. El Sherbini).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is in discussions with IDH to potentially extend an up to US$45 million A loan to finance IDH’s general corporate purposes including CAPEX and investments.
location_description: The headquarters of IDH and majority of its operations are located in Egypt, in addition to regional operations in Jordan, Nigeria and Sudan.
development_impact: The proposed Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good, based on an AIMM score of 43. On an unadjusted basis (i.e., without likelihood factor), the full potential AIMM score could reach 64. The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is the benefit to patients from the provision of high-quality healthcare. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment has the potential to promote greater inclusiveness in Egypt's labor market through demonstration and capacity-building channels.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the proposed Project is financial and non-financial. Financial additionality is in the form of financing structure with the provision of cross-border, long-term funding that will enable the Company to undertake its multi-country investment plan. IFC's financing will also support the Company's dual listing on EGX which is expected to enhance the share liquidity. Non-financial additionality is provided through: (i) standard-setting in gender diversity with IFC support for IDH to pursue the EDGE Gender Equality Certification; and (ii) standard-setting in health quality with support for IDH through implementation of the IFC healthcare quality advisory.

project_description: Lexo Energy Kenya Limited and Lexo Energy Tanzania Limited (“Lexo”) are expanding and improving the efficiency of their network of service stations in Kenya and Tanzania between 2021 and 2022.
sponsor_shareholders: Lexo is sponsored by Peter and Robert Erich with the backing of AtlasInvest.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Project Cost is approximately $21.5 million, of which IFC will be financing up to $11.2 million via an A Loan.
location_description: Kenya and Tanzania
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are (i) economywide effect, through value addition and job creation; and (ii) stakeholder effects through access to a broader mix of services available at service stations.
additionality: IFC is to provide (ii) long-term financing through one facility to be used in both Kenya and Tanzania; (ii) technical support for greening initiatives; and (iii) environmental, health and social best practices.

project_description: The proposed investment comprises of a convertible C Loan of up to US$5 million and an IDA Private Sector Window (PSW) Loan of up to US$2 million to HMH Rainbow Ltd. (“HMH Rainbow” or the “Company”), the leading producer of fresh and frozen chicken in Uganda. The investment supports the Company’s US$12 million capacity expansion program comprising of: (i) construction of temperature-controlled broiler houses; (ii) improvement of abattoir operations including the installation of a spin chiller; and (iii) establishment of grain silos and bulk feed-dispatch systems (together, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: HMH Rainbow is a joint venture between Alykhan Hudani (66.5% shareholding), a Ugandan businessman, and Rainbow Farms Investments Proprietary Limited (33.5% shareholding), a wholly owned subsidiary of RCL Foods Ltd., a listed South African food manufacturer
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is expected to be approximately US$12 million. The proposed investment is a convertible C Loan of up to US$5 million and an IDA PSW Loan of up to US$2 million.
location_description: The proposed investment will support the Company’s capacity expansion comprising of: (i) construction of temperature-controlled broiler houses 50kms north Kampala, Uganda; (ii) improvement of abattoir operations including the installation of a spin chiller in the facility in Buwazi, Semuto, Uganda; and (iii) establishment of grain silos and bulk feed-dispatch systems in the facility in Buwazi, Semuto, Uganda.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcome is expanding the operations of the leading poultry producer in Uganda with positive economy-wide impacts. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that contribution to market creation will be through strengthening the competitiveness of the poultry sector in Uganda through adoption of processing efficiencies and quality control measures that will contribute to greater formalization of the sector. The Project will also contribute to marketing efficiency of the corn and soybean markets by reducing transaction costs, imposing standards, and reducing seasonal price variation by adding storage capacity and purchasing grain and oilseeds at harvest time.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in three forms: (i) financial additionality: IFC would provide HMH Rainbow with the structure and patient capital that is well-matched to the Project needs and is not available in the local market; (iii) standard setting: IFC will assist the Company in bringing its operations in line with international standards; and (iii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC will provide in-depth advice through its Industry Specialists, leveraging knowledge gathered from IFC's global poultry experience. In addition, IFC Advisory Services will help build capacity on the food safety practices, financial management and resource use efficiency of the Company's operations.

project_description: Agrofertil S.A. (“Agrofertil” or the “Company”) is a crop input distributor and agronomic services provider, headquartered in Ciudad del Este, Paraguay. Founded in 1993, Agrofertil has been an IFC client since 2011. The Company assists farmers, cooperatives and small distributors by providing technical support, agricultural inputs and preharvest financing. The proposed investment will be an “A” loan facility of up to US$100 million to be made available through five one-year commitments of up to US$20 million each. The proposed project is to support the operations of Agrofertil and enhance its capacity to provide farmers with pre-harvest financing and technical advice (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is fully owned by the Sarabia family which has more than 30 years of experience in the Paraguayan agribusiness sector. Its president and founder, Jose Marcos Sarabia, has a 53.5% shareholding stake.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of an up to US$20 million A Loan, renewable each year, for a total of five years.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Ciudad del Este, Paraguay, and operates 25 distribution centers and 24 silos.
development_impact: Given the repeat nature of the transaction, the specific contribution from this facility toward market creation may be marginal. Nonetheless, project-level outcome is preserving farmer livelihoods by supporting their access to pre-harvest financing, purchase of inputs, and continued delivery of grain and oilseeds to export markets (global food security).
additionality: IFC will have strong financial additionality by contributing to diversifying the Company's domestic sources of financing, which are typically volatile. IFC provides non-financial additionality through the introduction of additional E&S improvements.

project_description: The proposed investment is a US$25.0 million A Loan (“the IFC Loan”) to a Kenyan subsidiary of Grit Real Estate Income Group Limited (“the Group”, “the Guarantor”, “GREIG”), a Mauritius-based listed (London Stock Exchange (LSE), Premium Segment, and Stock Exchange of Mauritius (SEM)) real estate investment company with REIT type characteristics building a diversified portfolio of income generating properties across Africa. GREIG will use the IFC Loan to finance a sale-lease back transaction, which comprises: i) the acquisition of an industrial facility (“the Existing Facility”) with vacant land in Nairobi, Kenya from its current owner with the immediate lease back of the existing premises to Orbit Products Africa Limited (“OPAL”); and ii) the refurbishment of the Existing Facility as well as construction of new premises on the vacant land (“the Additional Facility”), which will be similarly occupied by OPAL on a long term lease upon successful completion (“the Project”). OPAL is an established regional manufacturer of popular personal care and home care products for multi-national clients in East Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: Stellar Warehousing and Logistics Limited is the Kenyan full subsidiary of GREIG who will serve as the Project Sponsor and the borrower of the IFC Loan. GREIG is listed on the Premium Main Market segment of the LSE and on the Official Market of the SEM.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated project cost is US$52.6 million (inclusive of VAT), of which IFC will be financing up to US$25.0 million via an A Loan.
location_description: The Project is located in the Mlolongo District, North West of the Athi River District of Machakos County, a well-established industrial area in Nairobi.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are i) environmental effects, through reduction in energy and water uses; and ii) economywide effects through value addition and job creation. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will facilitate the integration of the Kenyan real-estate market into regional and global financial markets through demonstration effects for REIT and REIT-type vehicles.
additionality: Financial Additionality - Financing structure: IFC will provide a long-term loan with a grace period, which is not readily available for the Group in the local market. The IFC Loan will improve the Group's debt profile and enhance its access to outside complementary capital, thus reducing its vulnerability to domestic financial and banking shocks. Moreover, with the COVID-19 pandemic, funding for large projects is not readily available as local banks become more risk averse. Non-Financial Additionality - Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will provide technical knowledge and advice on green building standards as well as support to EDGE-certify the Project. IFC's green building specialist will provide guidance to GREIG on the process related to green building certification.

project_description: Founded in 1996, Viveo (“the Group”, CM Hospitalar S.A.) is a leader in the manufacturing and distribution of disposables materials and medicines in Brazil. Viveo brings together the expertise of 10 specialized companies, offering a broad portfolio of more than 10,000 products, services and solutions in each link of the health sector chain, from manufacturing to delivery to the patient. Viveo is a key player addressing the challenges resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil.
sponsor_shareholders: Viveo is majority owned by two funds managed by DNA Capital Consultoria Ltda. (“DNA Capital”), which has vast experience in the health sector with investments in more than 20 companies in the health sector. In addition, Carlos Mafra (founder) and Consolação Goulart Terra have minority stakes.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing an A Loan of up to US$30 million to partially finance the capital expenditures in Viveo’s plants, which includes the acquisition of new machines and productivity improvements, as well as working capital needs, which will strengthen the Group’s response to COVID-19 and contribute to Viveo’s expansion plans.
location_description: Investments will be made in Viveo’s facilities located both in São Paulo, Minas Gerais and Santa Catarina states, Brazil.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is the improved delivery of medical products and the quality of the supply chain. This will strengthen service provision by healthcare facilities throughout the country, including in frontier regions. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that its financing could support greater market resilience as service capacity to treat COVID-19 increases.
additionality: IFC is providing long term financing to Viveo, which is not so readily available in the market. In addition, IFC is working with the Group to help them improve their Environmental and Social standards, and will benefit from IFC's sectoral knowledge and expertise developed through engaging with the sector's top players.

project_description: The proposed equity financing is for Medgenome Inc. (“Medgenome” or the “Company”), India’s leading genetic diagnostics, research and data licensing player. Founded in 2013, MedGenome is a genomics and clinical data driven diagnostics and research company with a focus on next generation sequencing (NGS). It is leading genetic diagnostics player in India with a footprint across South Asia and is set to expand its operations into other geographies. Company is headquartered in Foster City, California and has a state-of-the-art, College of American Pathology (CAP) certified lab and research center in Bangalore, India.
sponsor_shareholders: MedGenome was founded by Sam Santosh, a serial entrepreneur along with Co-founder, Mahesh Pratapneni The Company’s key shareholders include: (i) The founders (Sam Santhosh and Mahesh Pratapneni) and management team; (ii) Sequoia Capital (Sequoia Capital India Investments IV); (iii) Sofina (Sofina Partners S.A.); (iv) LeapFrog (Future Genomic Holdings Limited); and other early and growth stage venture capital funds and angel investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Company is in the process of raising US$31 million of preferred equity. IFC is proposing a preferred equity investment of up to US$16.5 million in MedGenome. IFC’s investment will support the expansion of Medgenome’s diagnostic business in India and other emerging markets and growth of its research business.
location_description: Medgenome Inc. is registered in Delaware, USA and has an Indian subsidiary with office in Bangalore, India. It currently provides research services to clients in USA and genetic diagnostics tests in India
development_impact: Expected development impact includes: (i) Access to genetic diagnostic services and targeted medication (ii) Market creation by significantly deepening the genomic segment via demonstration and replication, and capacity building channels.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists in the provision of patient capital and IFC's ability to continue to support future funding needs, particularly during the tough times brought on by the Covid-19 pandemic. Non-financial additionality involves knowledge, innovation and capacity building, provided by leveraging insights from previous investments, and connecting the Company with prospective clients.

project_description: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Limited (“Glenmark” or “the Company”) is a global research-led pharmaceutical company with presence across generics, specialty, and OTC business with global presence in over 80 countries. Glenmark’s key therapy focus areas are respiratory, dermatology and oncology. IFC committed an unsecured A loan of US$40 million to Glenmark on February 12, 2021 through an allocation under the IFC COVID-19 response facility to fund the Company's ongoing capital expenditure program in India and proposed refinancing of foreign currency debt maturities (“Project”). In June 2016, IFC had invested in convertible debt of US$75 million in Glenmark to finance the Company’s expansion project at the time, which has now been completed. The Project (2021 investment) is linked to Glenmark (#38371, 2016 investment): https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/38371/glenmark
sponsor_shareholders: Glenmark is a publicly listed company. The promoter Mr. Glenn Saldanha and the promoter group directly/ indirectly holds 46.6 percent of the shareholding and the remaining 53.4 percent is held by public institutional and non-institutional investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: A Loan of US$40 million under IFC’s COVID-19 response facility to support the Project.
location_description: The Company has 16 manufacturing facilities globally, of which 12 are in India. Glenmark’s formulation facilities are located in Indore, Aurangabad, Baddi, Sikkim, Goa, Nalagarh and Nashik and API facilities are located in Ankleshwar, Dahej, Kurkumbh &Mohol.
additionality: Additionality: IFC provides countercyclical financial additionality. The loan will help Glenmark bridge the funding gap to align with its long-term project cycle and respond to the market demand. Development Impact: The Project ensures continued supply of drugs across emerging markets for chronic ailments, sustains employment and promotes resilience in domestic market by introducing drugs targeted at COVID19.

project_description: African Hotel Development Luxembourg SAS (“Onomo” or the “Company”) is a pan African mid-scale business hotel owner and/or operator of 21 hotels in Africa, under the brand Onomo. To fill the gap in the provision of region wide midscale branded hotels that meet international standards, the Company aims to upgrade and expand in capacity and geographically through (i) the extension and renovation of its existing hotel in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, (ii) the financing of the recently completed refurbishment of its existing hotel located in Dakar, Senegal, (iii) the refurbishment of its existing hotel in Bamako, Mali, and (iv) the development of 2 greenfield hotels in Yaoundé, Cameroon and Djibouti City, Djibouti; and (iv) the refinancing of existing debt (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Onomo is a private company owned by Batipart International S.A, CDC Group Plc and Credit Mutuel Capital.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be up to EUR70.2 million. IFC proposes an A-Loan investment of up to EUR20.9 million to support the Project. In addition, IFC as implementing entity of the International Development Association Private Sector Window-Blended Finance Facility is expected to provide up to US$18.5 million in the form of a concessional subordinated loan (“blended concessional finance co-investment”). The remaining balance will be provided by the Company shareholders in the form of equity and shareholders’ loans.
location_description: The Project locations include the Company’s hotels located in Senegal/Dakar, Mali/Bamako, Côte d’Ivoire/Abidjan and the land plots for the construction of the new hotels in Cameroon/Yaoundé and Djibouti City/Djibouti.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project to increase employment, as well as demand for goods and services from the relevant Project companies' suppliers. It is also expected that the Project will promote the resilience of the tourism sector by preserving availability and quality of services provided by a pan-African player and improve the local offering of quality hotels for regional business travelers.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC will support a regional mid-scale business hotel owner and/or operator improve the local offering of quality hotels for regional business travelers. IFC's additionality in this Project comes in two forms: (i) provision of longer-term financing than Onomo is typically able to secure, and (ii) further progress with regard to implementation of E&S management systems and EDGE.

project_description: Liquid Telecommunications Holdings Limited (Liquid, LTH or the “Company”) is the leading pan-African provider of wholesale voice, wholesale data and internet protocol (IP) services. The company invited IFC to: (i) participate in its new bond offering to up to US$100 million (the Bond), and (ii) provide up to US$75 million (ZAR equivalent) of an IFC A Loan (Term Loan), to fully refinance the company’s existing Eurobond and revolving credit facilities (the “Project”). The Bond was subscribed to during February 2021 at the LTH level, with the Term Loan (at the Liquid Telecommunications South Africa level) to follow in the coming months. Liquid Telecommunications South Africa (or “LTSA”) is a subsidiary of LTH. The investment aims at freeing up Liquids current debt stock to unlock more free cash flow for capital expansion plans across Africa over the next few years. Such expansion includes furthering Liquids fiber network and digital footprint of services across markets including DRC, Angola, South Sudan, Nigeria and such other markets as deemed appropriate from time to time. The funding would allow for the necessary capex expansion plans to be funded over the next few years and contribute to Liquid remaining active and competitive in the Pan-African markets they operate in. This project is linked to https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/44798/liquid-telecom-bond
sponsor_shareholders: LTH is a privately owned company which was established in 2004 as an independent telecommunications provider of international, voice, internet and data transmission using fiber and satellite technologies. The company is ultimately owned by shareholders including Royal Bafokeng Nation, CDC Group, Gateway Partners, the Masiyiwa Family, and the Rudnick Family. Liquid operates its own fiber optic and wireless networks in South Africa, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Uganda, Botswana, DRC, Zambia, South Sudan and Zimbabwe, with further commercial presence in Nigeria, Mauritius, United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom. The Company also has a point of presence in Mozambique. Liquid has also built Africa’s largest independent fiber network, approaching 73,000 km, and operates state-of-the-art data centers in Johannesburg, Cape Town and Nairobi, with a combined potential 19,000 square meters of rack space and 80 MW of power. The scope of services offered by Liquid’s operations varies from country to country; however, its main focus is provisioning mobile operators, carriers, enterprise, media and content companies and retail customers with high-speed, reliable connectivity, hosting and co-location and digital services.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Term Loan amount is expected to be c.US$220mn. The proposed IFC investment is for an up to US$75 million investment in the Term Loan, for IFC's own account.
location_description: LTSA is the South African subsidiary of LTH. LTH is a Pan-African company with operational locations across Africa.
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase the capacity of broadband networks across several countries in Africa, potentially resulting in increased access to quality broadband internet for individuals and businesses. Beyond the Project, this investment will contribute to maintaining the competitiveness of the markets for broadband internet across Africa by providing access to shared broadband infrastructure to all retail operators under open access and a nondiscriminatory basis.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists of providing longer tenor debt to support the expansion of the Company in countries with limited availability of credit, especially as the result of economic shocks induced by COVID-19. Non-financial additionality involves non-commercial risk mitigation by providing comfort to other investors to support the Company.

company_name: IZMIR SU VE KANALIZASYON IDARESI GENEL MUDURLUGU
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an IFC A Loan of up to US$34 million, equivalent in local currency, to the Izmir Water and Sewerage Administration (“IZSU”), fully guaranteed by the Izmir Metropolitan Municipality (“Izmir Municipality” or the “City”), to ensure sustained access and quality of services to IZSU’s one million customers and support the City’s long-term water and wastewater infrastructure resilience.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1987, IZSU is the public water utility of the City of Izmir providing water and wastewater services to ~1 million subscribers. IZSU is 100% owned by the Izmir Municipality. IFC provided EUR 28 million A loan in 2013 to IZSU Wastewater project, #32078, and EUR 11.25 million A Loan in 2015 to IZSU Sewerage project, #36080. The City is the third largest of the country’s metropolitan areas, serving a population of nearly 4.4 million inhabitants. IZSU has a good credit profile and a self-sustaining business model, operated by an experienced administration that has been able to maintain a prudent financial management and adequate liquidity. The General Manager of IZSU, Mrs. Aysel OZKAN, was appointed in May 2020 following the retirement of Mr. Raif CANBEK. The Board of Directors of IZSU is composed of Mr. Mustafa Tunc SOYER, the Mayor and Chairman of the Board, Mrs. Ayse Suzan GOK, Mrs. Tulay YILMAZ, and Mrs. Serpil BARAN.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project combines several high impact water and wastewater infrastructure investments, including water-supply network rehabilitation projects, rainwater collection network and sewerage separation projects, and a potable water treatment plant, with a total investment cost of TL 236.1 million. The proposed IFC financing is up to local currency equivalent (TL) of USD 34 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The investment plan includes 8 different water and wastewater infrastructure investments in various districts of the city Izmir in Turkey. Respective locations are Urla, Mordogan, Kemalpasa, Bornova, Foca, Gultepe, and Odemis districts of Izmir.
development_impact: The most significant project level outcomes are increased access and quality of water supply and wastewater services in Izmir. Beyond the Project, at the market level, IFC will contribute to improve water resilience by demonstrating low-cost, innovative and scaleable solutions to support conservation in water stressed areas of Turkey.
additionality: [8:11 PM] Ozan Beser IFC additionality is both, financial and non-financial. Through the proposed investment, IFC is supporting IZSU, a long-standing client to access local currency finance, following policy dialogue that facilitated the development of local currency borrowing. Local currency at terms offered by IFC is not easily available for municipal water and sanitation utilities in Turkey and will support the development of key drinking water treatment, water supply and wastewater infrastructure projects in Izmir, the third largest metropolitan municipality of the country. IFC will also build IZSU capacity to test low-cost solutions to improve water conservation and bill payment compliance. IFC will also support IZSU to improve capacity and practices to manage E&S risks and mitigate the environmental footprint of associated facilities, in line with IFC PS.
Company Name: IZMIR SU VE KANALIZASYON IDARESI GENEL MUDURLUGU

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to Euros 50 million (the IFC Loan) (or an equivalent amount in Romanian leu) to Profi Rom Food S.R.L. ('Profi' or 'the Company'), the largest food retailer in Romania based on the number of stores and the third largest based on revenue, owned by Mid Europa Partners ('MEP' or 'the Sponsor'), a private equity firm focused on Central and Eastern Europe. The financing would allow the Company to (i) further expand its reach in the country by opening new stores; and (ii) refinance its existing debt. The investment will address some of the country's developmental challenges by increasing access to quality and affordable goods across the country and providing better access to modern retail in rural areas of Romania.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsor is Mid Europa Partners ('MEP'), a leading private equity firm with a focus on Central and Eastern Europe. Since its establishment in 1999, MEP raised and managed funds for a total of Euros 5.3 billion. To date, Mid Europa has completed 43 investments across 18 countries, including landmark transactions and notable financings in the region. In 2017, MEP acquired 100 percent of shares in Profits. At the time of acquisition, it was the largest retail deal in the country's history.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at EUR 485 million, with a proposed IFC investment as a direct lender of up to EUR 50 million.
location_description: Throughout Romania.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Satisfactory. The most significant expected Project-level outcome is derived from stakeholder effects through improved access to high quality food products by customers, especially in the rural areas of Romania. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Project will promote greater market competition in secondary cities and rural areas through demonstration and replication channel.
additionality: Financial additionality: IFC will provide long-term financing in local currency, bringing additional financing capacity to the Company than what it currently receives from the local market. Non-financial additionality includes knowledge, innovation and capacity building as IFC will provide advice on how to improve the energy efficiency of its stores and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. It also includes standard setting as IFC's involvement will help the Company elevate its existing environmental and social standards in order to comply with IFC's performance standards.

project_description: IFC proposed investment consists of an A/B/MCPP Loan of up to US$180 million to Agropecuaria Maggi Ltda (“Agropecuaria”), the farming company of Amaggi Group (“Amaggi” or “the Group”), a leading producer, merchandiser, crusher and exporter of grains in Brazil. The financing will support Amaggi’s three-year investment plan comprising (i) conversion of existing corn farmland into cotton production across three farms in Mato Grosso; (ii) expansion of cotton ginning capacity; (iii) investments in logistics assets for the cotton expansion and agricultural inputs for use in the cotton field areas; and (iv) crop protection/treatment inputs for productivity improvements in existing cotton fields (“the Project”.)
sponsor_shareholders: Amaggi was created in 1977 in the state of Mato Grosso by the Maggi Family and started its activities as a farming company. Since then, the Group’s operations evolved and its business model currently involves farming, sale of agricultural inputs, grain procurement including pre-financing farmers, grains processing and commercialization of grains through a series of elevators and integrated logistics and export facilities. The Group is also engaged in the production of energy through small hydro plants. The Group is 100% owned by the Maggi family since its foundation.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The investment plan is estimated in US$180 million, which will be financed by the proposed IFC investment.
location_description: Investments will be made in Amaggi’s farms located in the Mato Grosso state, Brazil.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is expanding production of sustainable cotton to meet growing consumer demand, while reducing the environmental footprint through precision agriculture methods.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC's proposed investment will provide Amaggi with longer tenors not readily available in Brazil for this nature of investment program. Mobilization: IFC will mobilize financing from commercial banks, improving Amaggi's debt profile. IFC's Standard Setting: IFC will support Amaggi in aligning its E&S practices with best international practices.

company_name: PROCESADORA NACIONAL DE ALIMENTOS C.A. PRONACA
project_description: The proposed investment consists of an up to US$50 million A Loan to Procesadora Nacional de Alimentos C.A. Pronaca (Pronaca or the Company). The proceeds of the A Loan will be used to support the Company’s investment program during 2020-2022 (the Project). Pronaca’s investment program focuses on improving efficiency and capacity expansions at its feed mills, pork farms, and pork and poultry processing facilities.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is owned by the Bakker and Gerritsen families of Ecuador and the Gutierrez and Bosch families of Guatemala
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of an up to US$50 million A Loan.
location_description: The Company’s production facilities and farms are located across ten provinces in Ecuador.
development_impact: Economy-wide Impact: The planned expansion will have a positive impact through value addition. Market Impact: The Project is expected to contribute to broader sector competitiveness by supporting a leading player.
additionality: Financial Structure: IFC will provide long-term tenors at a time when there are limited alternatives from commercial banks. Standard Setting: IFC will support the Company in adopting best environmental and social standards. Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will support Pronaca in the implementation of energy efficiency projects at some of its farms and processing facilities.
Company Name: PROCESADORA NACIONAL DE ALIMENTOS C.A. PRONACA

project_description: Liquid Telecommunications Holdings Limited (Liquid or the “Company”) is the leading pan-African provider of wholesale voice, wholesale data and internet protocol (IP) services. The company invited IFC to: (i) participate in its new bond offering to up to US$100 million (the Bond), and (ii) provide up to US$75 million (ZAR equivalent) of an IFC A Loan (Term Loan), to fully refinance the company’s existing Eurobond and revolving credit facilities (the “Project”). The Bond was subscribed to during February 2021, with the Term Loan to follow in the coming months. Such expansion includes furthering Liquids fiber network and digital footprint of services across markets including DRC, Angola, South Sudan, Nigeria and such other markets as deemed appropriate from time to time. The Bond raise allows for the necessary capex expansion plans to be funded over the next few years and contribute to Liquid remaining active and competitive in the Pan-African markets they operate in.

The company is ultimately owned by shareholders including Royal Bafokeng Nation, CDC Group, Gateway Partners, the Masiyiwa Family, and the Rudnick Family. Liquid operates its own fiber optic and wireless networks in South Africa, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Uganda, Botswana, DRC, Zambia, South Sudan and Zimbabwe, with further commercial presence in Nigeria, Mauritius, United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom. The Company also has a point of presence in Mozambique. The scope of services offered by Liquid’s operations varies from country to country; however, its main focus is provisioning mobile operators, carriers, enterprise, media and content companies and retail customers with high-speed, reliable connectivity, hosting and co-location and digital services.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Bond issuance was US$620mn. The IFC investment was for a US$100 million investment in the Bond, for IFC's own account.
location_description: LTH is a Pan-African company with operational locations across Africa.
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase the capacity of broadband networks across several countries in Africa, potentially resulting in increased access to quality broadband internet for individuals and businesses. Beyond the Project, this investment will contribute to maintaining the competitiveness of the markets for broadband internet across Africa by providing access to shared broadband infrastructure to all retail operators under open access and a nondiscriminatory basis.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial. Financial additionality consists of providing longer tenor debt to support the expansion of the Company in countries with limited availability of credit, especially as the result of economic shocks induced by COVID-19. Non-financial additionality involves non-commercial risk mitigation by providing comfort to other investors to support the Company.

project_description: Indorama Eleme Petrochemicals Limited (IEPL) is an integrated petrochemical company with a liquids cracker and downstream polyethylene (PE) and polypropylene (PP) production, located in Port Harcourt Nigeria. IEPL is the largest producer of polyolefins in West Africa, and the 2nd largest in Sub Saharan Africa. The proposed investment is for up to US$64 million in “A Loan” and up to US$9 million concessional senior loan from IFC as implementing entity of the IDA PSW Blended Finance Facility (BFF) to IEPL, to finance the debottlenecking (DBN) of its olefins and polyolefins plant, including installation of a new furnace that will expand production capacity, and two Heat Recovery Steam Generators (HRSG) to recover energy and improve steam reliability, with significant efficiency upgrades that will reduce gas consumption, increase energy efficiency and reduce CO2 emissions, at the existing Eleme Petrochemicals site in Port-Harcourt, Nigeria.
sponsor_shareholders: IEPL is owned by Indorama Corporation (Indorama) 65%, Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) 10%, Rivers State Government 10%, Host Communities 7.5%, the Nigerian Federal Government 5%, and Employees 2.5%. Indorama is one of the world’s largest producer of polyester and the fastest growing global petrochemical producer with operations across 35 countries in Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas and over 37,000 personnel. Indorama is wholly controlled and beneficially held by Mr. S. P. Lohia and his family, through the holding company, Indorama Corporation registered in Singapore.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is US$80m comprising (i) an A Loan of US$64 million for IFC’s own account; and (ii) US$9 million concessional senior loan from IFC as implementing entity of the IDA PSW Blended Finance Facility (BFF).
location_description: The Project will be implemented at the existing Eleme Petrochemicals site in Port-Harcourt, Rivers State, Nigeria.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are: (i) the economywide effects via value addition; ii) the environmental effects from savings in the consumption of fossil fuels and GHG emissions reduction. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates the potential to promote market sustainability through a demonstration effect.
additionality: IFC's expected role and additionally includes (i) providing long-term financing, not available in the local market; (ii) mobilizing funding from Blended Finance; and (iii) improving Company's standards on health and safety and community engagement.

project_description: Hamza Textiles Limited (the “Company” or “HTL”) provides dyeing and finishing services for fabrics that are utilized in the manufacturing of Ready-Made Garments (“RMG”) by its sister concerns. Finishing facilities include activities such as stenting, compacting, continuous tumbler drying, continuous washing, brushing, continuous bleaching, shearing, all over fabrics coating etc.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsors are Mr. Abdul Wahed, Mr. Mohammed Abdul Jabbar, Mr. Mohammed Abdur Rahim and Mr. Mohammed Abdul Quader (together, the “Sponsors”). The shareholding structure for the Company is as follows - Mr. Abdul Wahed (16.12%), Mr. Mohammed Abdul Jabbar (25%), Mr. Mohammed Abdur Rahim (19.44%), Mr. Mohammed Abdul Quader (21.11%) and immediate family members (18.33%). The Sponsors and immediate family members, directly or indirectly, hold 100% stake in all Group companies.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at ~US$44 million and is proposed to be financed with long-term debt totalling US$26.8 million (of which ~US$4 million equivalent will be provided by Mutual Trust Bank Limited) with the balance US$17.1 through equity, in the form of cash and land. Proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to US$11.35 million with a tenor of eight years including a two-year grace period and a US$11.35 million loan from the IDA PSW Blended Finance Facility (“BFF”) as described in the Blended Finance section.
location_description: The Project is in Nayapara, Kashimpur, Gazipur, Bangladesh.
development_impact: Economy-wide effects: The Project will support the Group to increase process and product complexity, and strengthen its vertical integration, by modernizing the fabric production facilities which in turn will improve profitability and quality of products. In addition, the Project will enable the Company to reduce its lead time to end apparel retailers. Employment Growth: The Project has a strong employment effects and will create 930 additional direct jobs and hundreds of jobs in the value chain. Beyond the large numbers of jobs created, there will also be significant upskilling and training of workers. Competitiveness: This Project, and IFC's sectoral focus in the RMG sector in Bangladesh is expected to contribute to preserving Bangladesh's competitiveness as a global player in the textile and apparel market. Resilience: IFC expects the Project will demonstrate to the other players the necessary investments required to be agile and resilient considering possible future shocks in the market. The Company plans to use the financing to implement agile manufacturing through process modernization and better technology
additionality: (i) IFC will provide financial additionality through a US$ loan with a tenor of 8 years, including 2 years of grace period. The Company requires the long tenor loan to have necessary financial flexibility as to implement a more advanced manufacturing technology and investments in resource efficiencies. (ii) IFC is expected to provide concessional financing which will make the financing affordable for the client.

project_description: Copeval is a Chilean agricultural inputs distributor reaching more than 37,000 farmers through its 24 stores and distribution centers, strategically distributed across the country’s agricultural regions. The proposed investment consists of a subscription of securitized senior notes for up to US$25 million in Chilean Peso equivalent to finance Copeval’s working capital and secure liquidity in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic. UPDATE RELATED TO ADDITIONAL INVESTMENT UNDER COVID-19 RESPONSE FACILITY: E&S Performance and COVID-19 related Impacts : The company’s E&S performance was satisfactory at appraisal and was found to be satisfactory after the last site supervision visit (SSV) in July 2018. This performance is aligned with GIIP and is materially compliant with applicable at-approval requirements under the active investment. This follow-on investment, under the COVID-19 response facility, does not result in any new material E&S risks. The company’s management of existing E&S risks and impacts other than those described in the ESRS disclosed per above on 03/22/2013 continues. Copeval has successfully completed all corrective actions outlined in the 2013 environmental and social plan (ESAP) in 2019. Copeval has enhanced its OHS management practices and performance, including improvement of Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) over the past 2 year from 35.15 to 11.45 injuries per million hours worked (reference US 2013 value for the sector is 9.5) and that is stopped distributing WHO Class Ia and Ib products and achieved the final disposal of its remaining stocks. Copeval has also undertaken a retrenchment process for approximately 9% of its workforce over the past 2 years due to a business restructuring process, which has been implemented according to PS2 requirements. The virtual appraisal completed by IFC did not identify any new material E&S risks and impacts due to COVID-19 that cannot mitigated under existing ESRS and ESAP. Scope of IFC’s Appraisal : IFC’s E&S virtual appraisal covered the review of latest information provided by Copeval on its EHS/HR management practices regarding the environment, occupational health and safety (OHS), human resources based on a detailed E&S questionnaire as well as virtual meetings and interviews. Document review included, among others: updated management programs and procedures, external OHS management system audits, certifications to international management systems (e.g. ISO 9001 and OHSAS 18001). The review also took into account Copeval’s E&S performance since the SSV, undertaken in July 2019. After COVID-19 related travel restrictions are lifted, IFC will visit the client, as part of the regular portfolio monitoring activities. Response to COVID-19 Pandemic: Copeval created a Contingency Committee for identifying and implementing measure to reduce risks associated with COVID-19. These measures resulted from a risk assessment exercise of their operations. Workers belonging to high-risk groups (i.e. 65 years and older, workers with chronic diseases) have been requested to stay at home while receiving their full salaries. All workers are screened at the start of their shift and asked to stay home if they have any of the described symptoms. There has not been layoff, and the company does not expect them in the near future. Administrative staff has the option to work remotely and the company has developed new protocols and procedures to minimize risks for exposure to workers, such as: daily cleaning and disinfection, facility access protocols, personal protective equipment, and social distance. Management communicates on a regular basis with all its employees via the available internal channels (i.e. intranet, e-mail) and external channels. Copeval’s existing HR/OHS policies and measures as well as the COVID-19 measures ensure ongoing compliance with IFC. PS2: Labor and Working Conditions and PS4: Community Health Safety and Security. As a condition of this follow-on investment, Copeval will ensure ongoing compliance with IFC Performance Standards – especially provisions under PS2 and PS4.
sponsor_shareholders: Copeval is a publicly listed company in the Santiago Stock Exchange, with three families (Martino, Bozzo and Ariztia) holding a ~54% shareholding interest, IFC a 16.8% shareholding interest and the balance atomized among several investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$25 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of a subscription of securitized senior notes for up to US$25 million in CLP equivalent to allow the Company to secure the liquidity needed to run its operations in the midst of the COVID-19 crisis.
location_description: Copeval S.A. is headquartered in San Fernando, Chile. The Company has 24 branches, two distribution centers, and two regional warehouses located throughout the major agricultural regions of Chile.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is to protect the livelihoods of many small and medium farmers operating in rural (including frontier) regions of Chile that are currently at risk during the pandemic, and to stabilize their income through the continued operations of their leading inputs distributor. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that the success of its financing may promote, thanks to its demonstration effect, greater market resilience by broadening the availability and access to financial products and services that enable viable players to withstand shocks or stresses.
additionality: IFC has primarily financial additionality in this project, by affording the client an opportunity to prop up its working capital, under stress due to the tightening credit conditions that result from the COVID19 crisis. More in particular, IFC funding will provide the client with an innovative financing structure that adds value by improving its creditworthiness, and that is not available in the market at a reasonable cost. This will be the subscription of senior notes for up to US$25 million in local currency that will be structured through a new securitization of the Company's receivables under the recent Chilean Securitizations Law. On the non-financial side, additionality will entail continuing to foster knowledge, innovation and capacity development in a Company which has long been a strategic partner of IFC's in Chile, and which has made outstanding use of the skills and experience of the Board representatives that IFC has made available over the years.

country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: The project consists of an equity investment for a minority stake in ProducePay (“PP”, or the “Company”), a commerce enablement platform focused on the produce market. The Company’s services are primarily targeted to LAC-based farmers who export fresh fruit and vegetables to the US. IFC is proposing US$8 million in equity preferred financing to ProducePay to support its operations and expansion.
sponsor_shareholders: Produce Pay Inc. is a privately owned company headquartered in Los Angeles, CA. Current major shareholders include Pablo Borquez (CEO & Founder), CoVenture (New York-based venture capital firm) and Anterra Capital (a global agri-tech venture capital firm). Prospective investors in the current funding round (in addition to IFC) include the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is proposing to invest US$8 million in an up to US$35 million Series C equity funding round.
location_description: Latin America and the Caribbean (“LAC”) / United States.
development_impact: 1) Increased Access to Financing for Farmers: IFC expects that the Project will increase access to non-collateralized financing for produce farmers, primarily from Mexico but also from other LAC countries for export to North America. 2) Contribution to Market Creation - Integration: IFC expects that the Project will contribute to an increased integration of LAC agribusinesses to the U.S. market, as it contributes to the growth of an innovative business model fostering flexible working capital solutions for produce farmers to finance pre-harvest investments - not only in Mexico, Peru, Chile, but also in more underserved countries in Central America (e.g. Guatemala, Costa Rica).
additionality: 1) Risk Mitigation, Trusted Partnership: IFC brings about a unique capacity to PP, as it possesses a combination of expertise in Fintech and agri-business areas. With its experience in agri-financing in emerging markets, IFC's due diligence and participation in developing PP's expansion strategy will provide comfort to prospective investors with respect to the validity of PP's business model and strategy. 2) Standard-setting: IFC will help PP implement an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) to equip the company with the technical capacity to identify, manage and mitigate E&S risks and impacts derived from its activities.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: Founded in 2003, GreenFeed Vietnam Corporation (“GreenFeed” or “the Company”) is primarily an animal and aqua feed producer, with integrated operations across the pork value chain, from feed production, pig breeding and commercial pig farming to pig slaughtering and pork processing. The Company’s operations are mainly in Vietnam, but it also has feed production operations in Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar. GreenFeed is currently the 5th largest feed producer in Vietnam and is among the largest locally built integrated players. GreenFeed’s strong competitive advantages lie in its integrated operations, which allows the Company to supply traceable and safe pork to consumers and offer comprehensive feed and farm solutions to its farm customers; and also in its world-class pig breeding program, which translates to higher efficiency for its commercial pig farms. The proposed IFC financing will support the expansion of GreenFeed’s commercial pig farming capacity and some maintenance of GreenFeed’s feed mills in Vietnam (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: GreenFeed’s major shareholders are Oriental Ford Holding and Quang Dung Trading Co. Ltd.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$180 million which would be funded by: (i) VND1,000 billion (approximately equivalent to US$43 million) IFC Bond; (ii) US$75 million bank borrowings and (iii) US$62 million equity and/or internal cash generation.
location_description: The Project location is in Vietnam.
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Good. The Project is assessed as part of the overarching programmatic intervention ("ASF Recovery Asia") to respond to the impacts of the African Swine Fever (ASF) on the regional pork industry. The most significant, expected Project-level outcome resulting from this expansion is the impact on consumers from the provision of safe pork at the time of severe supply shortage as well as implementation of advanced biosecurity procedures at the new farms. At the market level, the Project, alongside other planned investment and advisory interventions, is expected to promote market resilience through improvement of biosecurity and disease management, both by supporting industry consolidation and disseminating best practices among smaller players.
additionality: Financing structure: The proposed investment consists of a VND1,000 billion (approximately equivalent to US$43 million) bond with maturity of up to 7 years. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC is exploring opportunities to provide technical expertise and facilitate knowledge sharing on: (i) antibiotic use policy; (ii) disease biosecurity practices; (iii) food safety; and (iv) animal welfare. Standard setting: IFC will help enhance the Company's sustainability by developing a comprehensive E&S Action Plan. Its implementation will strengthen the Company's E&S practices and procedures in its newly built hog farms and in doing so raise the level of compliance to that of IFC's Performance Standards.

company_name: NOBEL ILAC SANAYII VE TICARET A.S.
project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of a senior loan to Nobel Ilac Sanayii ve Ticaret A.S. (“Nobel” or the “Company”) in form of an A Loan up to EUR10 million or its USD or TRY equivalent. The IFC loan fits into IFC’s crisis response for Covid-19 financing and will reduce Nobel’s working capital pressure triggered by the effects of Covid-19. That way, Nobel will uninterruptedly carry out its ongoing capex program in the areas of injectables and bio-technology. Nobel is a Turkish generic pharmaceuticals company that produces, markets, distributes and sells products domestically and exports across Europe and Central Asia. Its product portfolio is spread across chronic, acute and consumer health therapeutic areas.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is part of a vertically integrated group of pharmaceuticals manufacturing, sales and marketing companies. The Company is wholly owned by Mr. Hasan Ulusoy, a veteran Turkish pharmaceutical industrialist, through other companies.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering an A Loan at an amount of up to EUR10 million for IFC’s own account. The permanent working capital requirements of the Company are estimated to have increased following the Covid-19. This liquidity need will be financed by the IFC loan and Company’s internal cash generation.
location_description: The project location is in Turkey. Nobel is headquartered in Istanbul while its other premises are located in Duzce and Gebze.
development_impact: Access to Pharmaceuticals: IFC will support Nobel to continue supplying high quality medication to around 50 countries. Nobel's sales are largely in Europe and Central Asia with a focus on countries such as Turkey, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kosovo. Job Preservation: IFC will support job preservation during this unprecedent time at Nobel, which has more than 1,500 employees in Turkey. Resilience: IFC will promote resilience of the Turkish pharmaceuticals market through supporting a leading local drug maker during a pandemic. With Covid-19, the market is under significant strain as service providers face depleted supplies. IFC's support to Nobel will contribute towards strengthening the local supply chain.
additionality: Financial Additionality: IFC is providing long-term financing that is limited in Turkey. IFC will also play a pivotal counter-cyclical role in supporting a local drug maker in Turkey. Turkey had experienced capital outflows even before the pandemic due to its volatile macroeconomic situation and the situation worsened following the Covid-19 outbreak due to increased uncertainties globally. Non-Financial Additionality: Nobel is expected to continue benefiting from IFC's knowledge about the pharmaceuticals industry and environmental & social matters as it expands its product portfolio with the ongoing investments in new areas.
Company Name: NOBEL ILAC SANAYII VE TICARET A.S.

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: Brandix Lanka Limited (“BLL” or the “Group”) is an apparel manufacturer headquartered out of Sri Lanka and manufactures apparel primarily across four categories: Activewear, Casualwear, Intimate wear and Sleep & Loungewear. The Group employs 60,400 and has 28 manufacturing facilities across 5 countries, namely, Sri Lanka, India, Bangladesh, Cambodia and Haiti. Brandix Apparel Limited (“BAL”) is a wholly owned subsidiary of BLL and houses the manufacturing operations in Sri Lanka. The Project consists of financing the medium and long-term working capital requirements and capital expenditure of BAL’s existing operations in Sri Lanka.
sponsor_shareholders: BAL is 100% owned by BLL, which in turn is 100% owned by Phoenix Ventures Limited, in which Messrs Mohamed Haji Omar, Mohamed Aslam Omar, Mohamed Ashroff Omar and Feroz Omar hold beneficial interest.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a US$ 50 million loan from IFC’s own account to BAL and BLL, which will be the co-borrowers for the loan. The investment will be used to fund working capital as well as capital expenditure in process efficiency initiatives and renewable energy projects in Sri Lanka.
location_description: IFC funds will be utilized for working capital and capital expenditure for BAL’s existing operations in Sri Lanka.
development_impact: At the project level, it is expected to support the Group sustain its operations to counter the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic whilst preserving jobs in Sri Lanka. The Project will also ensure continued production of high value added items and foreign exchange earnings to support the Sri Lankan economy. At the market level, the Project will help to protect exports growth and promote resilience whilst limiting disruptions along the domestic and global supply chain.
additionality: IFC's additionality stems mainly from its countercyclical role during crises which in this instance comprises IFC's long-standing experience with rapid crisis response efforts, liquidity for working capital, its ability to support real sector clients to address liquidity constraints in response to COVID-19. IFC will provide a long term loan to the Group which will serve as working capital funding to allow the operating subsidiaries to retain employment, generate export revenues and continue as going concerns. IFC is also expected to continue its support to the Company through its Advisory services in Gender, given 85% of the Company's workforce are women. IFC's assistance will also be instrumental in helping the Company mitigate the effects of COVID-19 on its employees.

project_description: IFC will support Kasada Hospitality Fund LP (Kasada) by providing loan financing for its first phase capital deployment, which targets the establishment of a portfolio of up to 20 hotels (estimated 4,000 hotel keys) requiring a total investment (debt and equity) of approximately US$400 million. Kasada’s own capital deployment and the related IFC loans will be structured as discrete sub-projects, each of which will be progressively reviewed by IFC and will be subject to standardized investment criteria. The first such sub-project is Project Ayaba (Ayaba) and subsequent sub-projects are expected to align with Ayaba in terms of the proposed financial arrangements. Project Ayaba comprises Kasada’s acquisition of 8 existing Accor-managed hotels (run under the Pullman, Novotel and Ibis brands) in Abidjan, Cote d’Ivoire (4 hotels); Dakar, Senegal (3 hotels) and Douala, Cameroon (1 hotel); operating liquidity injections to ensure the functioning of the hotels in the COVID-19 pandemic environment; and capital expenditure to refurbish/improve the properties and to achieve higher operating efficiencies.
sponsor_shareholders: Kasada Hospitality Fund LP (Kasada) held it first close with equity commitments over US$500 million. It is a Sub-Saharan Africa hospitality sector-focused, private equity fund, with two limited partners: the Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), the sovereign wealth fund of the State of Qatar and Accor, Europe’s largest hotel management company. Kasada is the first large-sized, professionally sponsored and managed hospitality investment platform in Sub-Saharan Africa. Over the next 3 years, Kasada plans to build a high-quality portfolio of hotels in Sub-Saharan Africa.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Kasada’s first phase capital deployment is expected to require investment of approximately, US$400 million which IFC will support with an up to US$160 million-equivalent senior loan package, comprising IFC A loans and debt mobilization. The cost of the Ayaba sub-project is estimated at €159 million, which IFC will support with a €65 million senior loan package comprising €32.5 million A loan and €32.5 million parallel loan.
location_description: Abidjan, Cote d’Ivoire; Dakar, Senegal; Douala, Cameroon
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcome is to provide hotels in distress due to impact of the COV-19 pandemic, and acquired in the previaling environment from a liquidity-constrained non-strategic investor, with additional liquidity and operational support to facilitate necessary restructuring and recapitalization leading to successful turnarounds, and consequently job preservation in the hospitality sector and its supply chain. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater sector integration by making financing more accessible to hotels in Sub-Saharan Africa, including those in distressed situations, via support for the first large-scale, professionally managed equity fund focused on hospitality, which plans to build a significant portfolio of hotels in SSA.
additionality: Financial Structuring - IFC's additionality is driven largely by its countercyclical role during crises. IFC will provide a long-term loan with adequate grace period to accommodate protracted recovery, which is not readily available in the local market. IFC's long-term financial commitment will allow Kasada to implement its plan of building a strong and resilient hotel portfolio across SSA, in an uncertain context due to the pandemic and political/security risks in the region. Resource Mobilization - IFC will mobilize debt funding from another lender, further helping to complete the financial requirements of the project. Climate impact - IFC will provide (i) green building advice to the client to achieve EDGE standards. Standard-setting - IFC will provide environmental, social and life and fire safety guidance to ensure the project achieves compliance with PS.

project_description: Bel Ga Myanmar Limited (“Bel Ga MM” or the “Company”) is an existing IFC client that is engaged in the poultry breeding business in Myanmar with a significant market share in Myanmar. IFC loan will support the expansion of Bel Ga MM’s existing hatchery facility and sustain the Company’s operations through the COVID-19 market downturn. The proposed financing as detailed below is based on the thesis of (i) committed and financially strong Sponsors; (ii) a well secured loan with Sponsor’s support arrangements; and (iii) IFC to play an important countercyclical financial support to mitigate the COVID-19 impact. This project follows IFC's initial US$7.5 million investment in Bel Ga Myanmar in 2017 (#38236): https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/38236/bel-ga-myanmar
sponsor_shareholders: Bel Ga MM is a 49:51 joint venture company owned by De Heus Animal Nutrition B.V. (“DHAN”) and Belgabroed N.V. (“Belgabroed”, and collectively with DHAN, the “Sponsors”). DHAN is the world’s 11th largest producer of animal feed based in the Netherlands, and currently holds an estimated 10% share of animal feed market in Myanmar. Belgabroed operates the largest hatchery in Belgium.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$7 million and will be funded with an IFC A Loan of US$4 million under the Real Sector Crisis Response Envelope of the IFC Fast Track COVID-19 Facility, and capital injection from the Sponsors of at least US$3 million. In addition, the Project is supported by IDA PSW Blended Finance Facility (BFF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
location_description: Myanmar.
development_impact: By sustaining the Company's operations, the project helps to accelerate the 4-party business model that will insulate farmers from short-term price fluctuations during uncertain times. At the market level, the project helps to create a stable market by providing commercial farmers with the necessary fixed inputs, technical support and a fixed offtake at the end of the production cycle.
additionality: IFC provides countercyclical financial additionality. Currently, term loans are not readily available in the market, particularly as the Company is suffering from (i) declining operating cashflow due to COVID-19 impact on demand, and (ii) further strain on working capital resources during the construction and startup of additional parent stock farm houses.

project_description: EthioChicken Group (“EC” or the “Group”) is the leading producer of day-old-chick (“DOC”) and poultry feed in Ethiopia, focusing on selling these poultry input products to rural farmers. IFC’s funding will be used to implement part of the Group’s 5-year program (the “Project”). Particularly, use of IFC’s funds will be (i) capacity expansion that requires construction of two new breeding farms (60K bird capacity each) and one new hatchery facility; (ii) working capital for purchase of parent stock birds; and (iii) partial refinancing of an existing long-term loan.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group consists of (i) three operating companies in Ethiopia: AGP Poultry PLC, Mekelle Farms PLC and Andasa Poultry PLC; and (ii) two holding companies in Mauritius: Agflow Ventures and Agflow Poultry, which in turn are majority owned by (a) Founders’ investment vehicle company Flow Equity (60.4%), and (b) Arabica Investment (39.6%), a private equity fund. For IFC loan, the three operating companies will be Co-Borrowers and the two holding companies will be Guarantors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project Cost is expected to be c. USD 16.2 million. IFC is looking to provide an own account A Loan of up to USD 10 million in Ethiopian Birr (“ETB”) subject to an approval from National Bank of Ethiopia. If the approval cannot be obtained, USD Loan will be provided instead. Both options will include support from Blended Finance, as described in the Blended Finance Section. The remainder of the financing will be funded by equity.
location_description: As of FY20, the Group has eight breeding farms, four hatcheries, and two feedmill facilities across the main population and agricultural areas of Ethiopia. As part of the Project, the two new breeding farms will be built in SNNPR region and Amhara region, while the new hatchery will be built in SNNPR region.
development_impact: Project level impact: (i) Benefits for rural consumers through better access to affordable poultry products in a market where access to protein and micronutrients is limited; (ii) Expansion in income opportunities for the poultry agents; and (iii) Improvement in skills and capacity building for female farmers to improve their sales and profitability (with the support of IFC's advisory work). Market level impact: Promotion of the inclusiveness of the formal poultry market by expanding the use of the appropriate breed and business model that is tailored to the needs of the Base of the Pyramid (BOP) farmers and consumers throughout Sub-Saharan Africa through demonstration and replication, potentially laying the foundation for the adoption of contract farming/outgrower models in the longer term.
additionality: 1. Financial Additionality: Financing Structure: a) A facility with USD disbursement and local currency repayment is currently not available in Ethiopia; b) IFC is proposing an 8-year loan, including a 3-year grace period to allow sufficient time for to ramp up. Such long-tenor financing with the grace period is not readily available in Ethiopia. 2. Non-Financial Additionality: a) Standard Setting: IFC will assist the Group to develop Environmental Health and Safety (EHS), and social practices in line with international standards. b) Knowledge sharing and capacity building: The Group is working with IFC Advisory team for professionalizing its distribution system and enhancing participation of women in this line of work.

project_description: Dodla Dairy Limited (“Dodla” or the “Company”) is a leading dairy company based in Southern India with products across the entire milk value chain ranging from fresh milk to value added dairy products. The Company offers wide range of products comprising of fresh milk, curd, ice cream, butter, ghee, paneer, flavored milk, etc. The Company also has overseas operations in Uganda and Kenya, where it manufactures liquid milk, flavoured yoghurt, Ghee, Paneer, and Cheese under the brand name Dairy Top. This project is linked to Dodla Dairy (#42009): https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/42009/dodla IFC committed INR 1,000 million (approximately US$15 million) to Dodla on February 02, 2021 by way of subscription to equity shares of the Company to support the general capital expenditure and working capital requirements of the Company. The investment has been committed from two projects, INR 500 million committed from project #44940, and an approximately equivalent amount from project #42009.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is promoted by Mr. Sunil Reddy (the “Sponsor”), Mr. Sesha Reddy and the Dodla Family Trust. Mr Sunil Reddy belongs to a reputed family from Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh. The family has historically had strong linkages with local farmers. The Sponsor has more than two decades of experience in the industry. The Sponsor, his family and entities associated with the Sponsor have a 68.51% shareholding in the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment is up to USD equivalent of INR 1,000 million investment in the form of subscription to equity shares of the Company, out of which INR 500 million is being committed from project #44940, and an approximately equivalent amount out of project #42009.
location_description: The Project will be located at Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
additionality: IFC is providing countercyclical financial additionality by protecting the Company's long term capex plans to boost its processing capacity of dairy value-added products The AIMM score is 53. The project supports the operations of dairy farmers and consumer access to quality dairy products. The project will also move the dairy sector toward a more efficient and resilient structure.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is up to the IDR equivalent of US$50 million senior loan facility to support the development of approximately 8,000 affordable housing units on 4 sites, expected to be located in the Greater Jakarta and Java area.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1953, PT Gunung Sewu Kencana (GSK) is an Indonesian diversified business conglomerate employing 17,000 people with FY2019 revenue of US$1.2billion, and operations in the food, insurance, property, manufacturing and other emerging businesses. PT Farpoint Realty Indonesia (FRI) is the property arm of GSK, established in 2006 to focus on development and management of residential, commercial, hospitality and retail properties in Jakarta and across Indonesia. Based on the market demand in the affordable housing space, FRI started its first affordable housing project in 2018 and plans to expand this further around the country. The IFC loan will be used by FRI and its subsidiary PR Investasi Semesta Indonesia (ISI) which develops FRI’s affordable housing sub-projects. Both FRI (Borrower 1) and ISI (Borrower 2) are 100% owned by GSK (Sponsor)
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the Project is estimated not to exceed approximately US$364 million and will be funded by a senior loan of up to US$50 million from IFC’s own account.
