location_description: The Project is located across four sites in Greater Jakarta and Java area, namely Samanea Hill, Parung Panjang, Batu Malang and Cikeas (or other alternative acceptable sites to IFC.
development_impact: IFC's financing will increase the supply of quality affordable housing in Indonesia, especially in the Greater Jakarta and Java area, and mainly for the growing population of young families and millennials aspiring to acquire their first assets. IFC anticipates that the Project will enhance physical connectivity of the project sites to the nearby big city such as Jakarta city center, attracting residential population that will generate critical mass to help transform the areas. Furthermore, the Project is expected to have a demonstration effect on the sustainable green building aspect for affordable housing projects.
additionality: IFC will play a countercyclical role in providing and mobilizing long-term financing at the time when the local financial market is being affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The proposed financing will have a tenor that is not commonly available in the commercial bank market for this type of project and will enable Farpoint to pursue affordable housing development with a financially sustainable scale. In addition, Farpoint is expected to leverage IFC's knowledge and expertise in Environmental and Social (E&S) management as well as in the green building certification.

project_description: The IFC investment package is a four-year loan to the United Exports Limited (“United Exports” or the “Company”) amounting up to €3 million. The loan is shared equally (€1.5 million each) among IFC and Nederlandse Financierings-Maatschappij voor Ontwikkelingslanden N.V. (“FMO”). The loan will help United Exports to cope with the immediate challenges of the global COVID-19 crisis and continue implementing its long-term growth plan. Established in 2002 in the Republic of South Africa, United Exports is involved in blueberries farming and trading. The Company sources blueberries from farms in South Africa and Zambia that it owns partially or entirely as well as from a number of licenses growers located in the Southern Africa region. United Exports focuses on the production, grading, packing, cooling, shipping, marketing and selling of its premium proprietary blueberry varieties; its proprietary brand is the OZblu® brand. This project is linked to https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/40468/mbiza-blueberries
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Roger and Sharon Horak, South African born, now Australian nationals living in Australia, are the founders and ultimate owners of the Company. The OZblu varieties were developed and are owned in Australia together with the Australian breeder.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, together with FMO committed a €3 million financing package to the Company. The financing package will help the Company continue to invest in maintenance capex to protect employees and product quality, as well as execute on the growth plan. The funds could be also used for: (i) implementing the necessary processes for the safety of its workers; (ii) providing technical advice and assistance to its farmers; and (iii) obtaining a source of liquidity in case working capital requirement increases.
location_description: The Company manages its farms that are located in the Western Cape, Gauteng and Limpopo provinces in South Africa as well as in Zambia.
additionality: Development Impact: By sustaining the Company's operations, the facility will help suppliers and employees. By limiting supply disruptions, the Project will promote resilience in the export-oriented blueberry market. Additionality: IFC will provide countercyclical financial additionality. The terms of the loan are not available in the market, particularly as working capital needs were exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. The IFC loan is expected to help weather the period of uncertainty and support the completion of ongoing investments.

project_description: This project is proposed under the Global Trade Supplier Finance program (“GTSF” or the “Program”) approved by the IFC Board on September 21, 2010 (Original Project #28723). Under GTSF, IFC provides short-term financing to suppliers (“Suppliers”) in emerging markets selling to large companies (“Buyers”) on open account terms. Under this project, IFC will provide financing to Barry Callebaut AG for suppliers of sugar, soy lecithin and dairy based in different emerging market countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, Barry Callebaut is the world's leading manufacturer of high-quality chocolate and cocoa products with 62 factories worldwide selling its products to 140 countries. Barry Callebaut is publicly traded in the SIX Swiss Exchange, with institutional investors holding a majority of its shares and the balance held by Jacobs Holding.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project (“the Project”) is expected to be US$30 million for the supply of sugar, soy lecithin and dairy from Barry Callebaut’s suppliers.
location_description: Several countries in Latin America and Asia including Mexico, Brazil, Colombia and Thailand.
additionality: IFC's additionality includes: (i) offering a financing structure that aims to reduce both, financing and E&S risks and (ii) supporting Barry Callebaut to further improve its standards in sustainable sourcing practices. Expected Development Impact of the Project The key development impacts of the Project includes: (i) improved access to finance for Barry Callebaut suppliers in emerging markets; (ii) a measurable improvement in the E&S performance of Barry Callebaut suppliers; and (iii) demonstration effect for local and international financial institutions to offer Supplier Finance products in emerging markets and for international buyers to utilize this instrument and align their commercial and sustainability objectives.

project_description: Puravankara Limited (“Puravankara” or the “Group”) is one of the leading housing developers in Southern India, whose business is largely focused on southern and western India. The Group is primarily focused on residential real estate operating under two brands: “Puravankara” for luxury and higher-income housing and “Provident” for affordable housing. The proposed investment for an amount aggregating up to INR 5,560 million (approximately US$76 million) - by IFC for up to INR 3,160 million (approximately US$43 million) and by IFC Emerging Asia Fund, LP (EAF) for up to INR2,400 million (approximately US$33 million) would be made in one or more Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) set up by the Group, for the development of three or four housing projects under the Provident brand, including the identified projects in Kochi and Bengaluru (collectively the Project). The Project entails the development of approximately 4,000 housing units over the next five to seven years under the two identified projects, in planned and green urban spaces in micro markets with shortage of reasonably priced good quality housing units.
sponsor_shareholders: Puravankara was founded in 1975 by Ravi Puravankara (who is the Chairman) and is currently led by his son Ashish Puravankara as Managing Director, both of whom are a part of the sponsor family. With a track record of over 45 years, as of Sep 30, 2020, the Group has completed 71 projects since inception and delivered 40.9 million square feet across both brands with over 100,000 customers and is a reputed player in key south Indian markets, including Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad and Kochi, as well as more recently in Pune and other cities in west India. With experience of over a decade under the Provident brand, the Group has built over 10 million square feet and delivered over 9,000 homes catering to the affordable and mass market housing sector. The Group currently has 22.9 million square feet under development, and a land bank with a development potential of over 65 million square feet. Puravankara is listed on the Indian stock exchanges. The sponsor family holds 75% of the equity shares of Puravankara, and the balance 25% is held by other institutional and individual (public) investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC and EAF would invest a total sum of up to INR 5,560 million or approximately US$76.0 million in one or more SPVs set up by the Group. Out of this, IFC’s investment would be up to INR 3,160 million (approximately US$43 million) and EAF’s investment would be up to INR2,400 million (approximately US$33 million).
location_description: The Project is expected to be located across various cities in India, but the two identified projects are located in Edappally, Kochi and Devanahalli, Bengaluru.
development_impact: 1) The Project will increase supply of high-quality housing units at reasonable prices and contribute towards bridging the housing gap in India. Majority of the housing projects being developed as part of the Project are expected to be Affordable Housing (as defined in the Harmonized Master List of Infrastructure sub-sectors issued by India's Ministry of Finance). 2) Growing economic activity and creating jobs is essential, especially to minimize the economic consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic. The Project will create direct and indirect jobs resulting from the construction of housing units. 3) Incremental demonstration effect by strengthening operations of a successful market player in a fragmented, inefficient market.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC's involvement is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will provide a critical countercyclical financial solution to the Group through long term financing that fits the projects' profiles. This is not easily available locally, especially in the current economic environment which is further exacerbated as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will provide Green Building advisory to the Group in order to obtain EDGE certification for the Kochi project proposed to be funded by IFC and EAF as well as for another project being developed by the Group in Bengaluru. In addition, IFC would help the Group expand its engagement going forward to identify other portfolio and future projects for the EDGE certification.

project_description: CHO Group, (“CHO” or the “Company”), was established in 1996 and is a leading olive oil producer in Tunisia. The Company’s facilities are mainly located in the region of Sfax, Tunisia, and its destination markets span over 40 countries worldwide. CHO retains a workforce of 750 employees. The proposed Project would help CHO liberate cash for its permanent working capital needs, and support its capex needs over the next 3 years.
sponsor_shareholders: CHO was created in 1996 by three entrepreneurs, Mr. Abdelaziz Makhloufi, Mr. Moncef Rekik, and Mr. Abderazzak Tounsi. The original founders own directly or indirectly about 93 percent of shares. The remaining is held by SICAR Invest.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at EUR53.1 million. The proposed IFC debt commitment is up to EUR30 million, of which up to EUR10 million for IFC’s own account and up to EUR20 million through mobilization.
location_description: Sfax, Tunisia.
development_impact: CHO's overall goals through this Project are its contribution to preserving linkages with farmers, maintaining jobs, and domestic value addition. The Project's contribution to market resilience will be through building capacity along the supply chain, demonstrating improved business practices to other sector players, and enabling positive spillovers across the sector by maintaining operations during a tumultuous economic period.
additionality: Financial additionality through long-term tenor and currency. Non-financial additionality through potential engagements by IFC's Advisory Services.

project_description: Parag Milk Foods Limited (‘Parag’ or ‘the Company’), established in 1992, is one of India’s largest dairy companies, catering to major cities in the country with a strong presence in Western and Southern India. It has a milk processing capacity of upto 3,500,000 litres per day (“LPD”) - 2,000,000 LPD at Manchar, Maharashtra, 1,400,000 LPD at Palamner, Andhra Pradesh and 100,000 LPD at Sonipat, Haryana. The Company has a well-diversified product portfolio ranging from liquid milk to value added products like UHT milk, cheese, butter, ghee (clarified butter), paneer (cottage cheese), yoghurt, curd, lassi, flavored milk, dairy whitener and milk powder, sold under the brands ‘GO’, ‘Gowardhan’, ‘Top Up’, ‘Avvtar’ and ‘Pride of Cows’, with value added products being > 65% of sales. This project is linked to Parag Dairy (#33134): https://disclosures.ifc.org/#/projectDetail/SII/33134 IFC committed INR 2.3 billion (approximately US$31 million) to Parag on December 17, 2020 in the form of non-convertible debentures to support the Company’s working capital needs and long term capex plans.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company’s main Sponsor is Mr. Devendra Shah, who together with his family owns 46 percent of Parag’s shares. 29 percent of the company is held by institutional shareholders. The balance 25 percent is held by public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment under RSE COVID-19 facility aims to provide Parag with sufficient additional liquidity in support of its working capital needs and its long term expansion plans.
location_description: IFC’s proceeds will be utilized towards the milk processing plants at two locations – Manchar in Maharashtra, and Palamner in Andhra Pradesh.
additionality: Additionality: IFC's funding package will help Parag meet the increased working capital needs to enable milk procurement from farmers and capital expansion to implement their envisaged capex plans to cater to the market demand. Development Impact: The AIMM score is 53. The project supports the operations of dairy farmers and distributors / retailers. By limiting supply disruptions, the project promotes resilience and advances formalization of the dairy market.

project_description: The proposed investment is to support JV LLC Nyva Pereyaslavschyny (“Nyva” or the “Company”), the second largest industrial pork producer in Ukraine, by providing a long-term corporate loan to finance the Company’s 2021-2023 capital expansion program. Established in 1998 in the Kyiv region, Nyva now operates 11 pig farms and has 23,000 ha of agricultural land under management. In 2019, the Company produced over 40,000 tons of pork. The implementation of the Project will allow Nyva to expand its pig breeding operations.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Oleksandr Mostipan, founder and Chairman of the Board, is the ultimate beneficiary of the Company and owns 99% of the shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$27 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$20 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The expansion project is located in a rural area of the Kyiv region in Ukraine.
development_impact: Construction of new farms will improve consumer access to quality pork at the time when the industry is facing serious biosecurity risks.
additionality: The long tenor of the IFC financing matches the long-term nature of the Project. Additionally, IFC will continue sharing its industry expertise and best practices on biosecurity, related to the mitigation of ASF. The Company will receive IFC's advice on implementation of the international standards for livestock production as well as independent verification against a credible international standard.

project_description: Open Connect Limited (“OCL” or the “Company”) is the leading provider of carrier services to telecom operators in Malawi. Having recently been unbundled from Malawi Telecommunications Limited (“MTL”) and privatized through a competitive tender process, OCL now requires debt funding to complement equity investments from its new investors, for its capital expenditure program for the next two years. Specifically, IFC’s funding will be used to (i) deploy fiber for providing fiber to the Business, Home and Tower (“FTTx”) services within Malawi, (ii) build a Tier III data centre, (iii) acquire international internet capacity for domestic distribution, and (iv) fund working capital (the “Project”). IFC’s investment promotes infrastructure sharing under wholesale open-access principles and enables OCL to remain active and competitive in the Malawian telecom market.
sponsor_shareholders: Pan-African Infrastructure Development Fund II (PAIDF II), a fund managed by Harith General Partners, was the preferred bidder for the acquisition of a 60% stake as part of a competitive tender process organized by Ernst and Young. Other shareholders of OCL are the Press Corporation Limited (22%), Old Mutual Malawi (15%), the Malawian Government (2%), NICO Holdings (1%) and Investments Alliance (0.2%). Since the acquisition by PAIDF II, the Company has benefited from significant capital injection for network upgrades and fiber deployment as well as increased company efficiencies and quality of services provided by the Company. OCL owns and operates the largest fiber network in the country, nearing 3,800 km, which covers all four regions of Malawi. Since the country is landlocked, the network connects internationally via Mozambique and Tanzania, with a direct connection to two submarine cables – SEACOM and EASSy Cable. The Company provides lit and dark fiber services to Mobile Network Operators, Internet Service Provider and terrestrial TV broadcasters in Malawi. With the new financing package, the Company intends to move facilitate the creation of wholesale services for the consumer market as well as for businesses and telecom towers requiring fiber connectivity. The Company will also run Malawi’s first independent Tier III data center in Malawi, which will be purpose-built for infrastructure sharing. Further, to reduce the cost of broadband in Malawi, the Company will acquire international wholesale capacity for distribution in Malawi.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project Cost is expected to be US$ 31 million. IFC is looking to provide an own account A Loan of up to USD 10 million in Malawian Kwacha (“MWK”). The financing package will include support from the IDA19 IFC-MIGA Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (“IDA-PSW LCF”) and Blended Finance Facility (“IDA-PSW BFF”) as described below. The remainder of the financing will be funded by equity.
location_description: OCL is a Malawian Based company with operational locations across the country.
development_impact: The Project is expected to increase access to digital connectivity for end-users in Malawi by deploying fiber for increased access and improved service quality and indirectly by increasing the capacity of the broadband network. This will be further enhanced by the construction of the first Tier III data center in Malawi, which will result in increased availability of data storage capacity in the country, with the potential to enhance productivity growth for businesses and increase access to digital services for individuals. Beyond the Project, the investment will contribute to creating a competitive market for digital connectivity in the country and create a market for cloud computing.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this Project is primarily financial. It consists of providing longer tenor debt to support the Company's expansion plan in Malawi, a low-income IDA country with limited availability of capital under similar terms, especially in the context of the financial shocks induced by the COVID-19 pandemic. The local currency tranche also allows for a natural hedge to the Company, which has most of its revenues in local MWK, whilst the USD tranche matches with OCL's foreign-denominated capital expenditure requirements. IFC's role as a countercyclical investor in a time of the COVID-19 pandemic is ensuring that the Company can continue expanding its service offerings and remaining competitive in a fast-changing sector.

project_description: The Project is a funded risk participation for up to EUR 15 million by IFC in a EUR 40 million one-year secured pre-export facility provided by Societe Generale to finance the purchase of seed cotton and provide working capital to Societe Burkinabe des Fibres et Textiles (SOFITEX), a cotton company in Burkina Faso (the “Obligor”).
sponsor_shareholders: Societe Generale is one of the leading European financial services groups. Based on a diversified and integrated banking model, the Group combines financial strength and proven expertise in innovation with a strategy of sustainable growth. Committed to the positive transformations of the world’s societies and economies, Societe Generale and its teams seek to build, day after day, together with its clients, a better and sustainable future through responsible and innovative financial solutions. Active in the real economy for over 150 years, with a solid position in Europe and connected to the rest of the world, Societe Generale has over 138,000 members of staff in 62 countries and supports on a daily basis 29 million individual clients, businesses and institutional investors around the world by offering a wide range of advisory services and tailored financial solutions. The Group is built on three complementary core businesses: French Retail Banking which encompasses the Societe Generale, Crédit du Nord and Boursorama brands. Each offers a full range of financial services with omnichannel products at the cutting edge of digital innovation; International Retail Banking, Insurance and Financial Services to Corporates, with networks in Africa, Russia, Central and Eastern Europe and specialised businesses that are leaders in their markets; Global Banking and Investor Solutions, which offers recognised expertise, key international locations and integrated solutions. Societe Generale is included in the principal socially responsible investment indices: DJSI (World and Europe), FTSE4Good (Global and Europe), Euronext Vigeo (World, Europe and Eurozone), four of the STOXX ESG Leaders indices, and the MSCI Low Carbon Leaders Index.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project will be in a total amount of EUR 40 million. Societe Generale will retain up to EUR 25 million while IFC will retain EUR up to 15 million.
location_description: Societe Generale is headquartered in Paris, France. The underlying project is the financing of cotton produced and exported out of Burkina Faso.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is continued access to markets and finance for over 32,889 farmers and increases in productivity for 1,557 farmers. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates the investment will increase integration and resilience in the cotton sector in Burkina Faso, a low income/IDA country, through capacity building and demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC's additionality will come in two forms (i) standard-setting with regards to reducing / eliminating child labor; and (ii) non-commercial risk mitigation, including trusted partnerships with a commercial bank, especially since this project will follow previous engagements of IFC in the cotton sector in Burkina Faso.

project_description: MiCare Sdn Bhd (“MiCare” or the “Company”) is a leading healthcare third-party administrator (TPA) in Southeast Asia that administers and processes medical claims on behalf of insurance companies and self-insured corporate clients according to the insurance policies and employee benefit plans they offer. MiCare is headquartered in Malaysia and also has operations in Thailand and the Philippines. MiCare is expanding its operations to other countries in Southeast Asia. IFC will provide financing for MiCare’s expansion, particularly for (i) the potential acquisition of TPA providers and greenfield expansion in developing countries in Southeast Asia such as Indonesia and Vietnam; and (ii) capital expenditures and IT infrastructure development in existing countries of operation and target markets for expansion (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Zuellig Pharma Specialty Solutions Holdings Pte Ltd (“Zuellig Pharma” or the “Sponsor”) acquired MiCare in 2013. Zuellig Pharma has a 95 percent shareholding in the Company, while Moses Hee, the founder and CEO of MiCare, has retained the remaining 5 percent shareholding. Zuellig Pharma is one of the largest healthcare services groups in Asia. The core focus of the Sponsor’s business strategy is to make healthcare more accessible across the region. Zuellig Pharma provides world-class distribution, digital and commercial services to support the growing healthcare needs in the region. Established nearly a hundred years ago in 1922, Zuellig Pharma employs over 12,000 staff, works with over 500 clients, including the top 20 pharmaceutical companies in the world, and serves over 250,000 medical facilities across 13 markets in Asia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The value of the capital expansion for the Project is estimated at US$100 million, which will be funded by an equity investment from IFC, co-investment by another strategic equity investor, bank debt and internal cash generation of the Company. IFC’s proposed investment in the Company comprises an equity investment of up to US$30 million in the common shares of a newly established holding company (“NewCo”), which will own 100 percent of MiCare Sdn Bhd.
location_description: The Project will cover MiCare’s expansion into developing countries in Southeast Asia such as Indonesia and Vietnam, as well as capital expenditures in its existing countries of operation such as the Philippines and Thailand.
development_impact: At the Project level, expected outcomes include the provision of large-scale, cost-efficient, value-added medical administration services that ultimately contribute to managing healthcare costs and improving health outcomes. This will be achieved through introducing process improvements and leveraging the use of MiCare's proprietary digital tools in new markets. At the market level, IFC anticipates that the Project will enhance competitiveness in the sector through industry consolidation and replication by competitors of improvements and innovations introduced by MiCare.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC will support a leading TPA in its regional expansion, as it looks to replicate its successful business model and promote improved access and affordability of quality healthcare across Southeast Asia. IFC's additionality in this Project comes in the form of: (i) long-term financing that aims to mitigate execution and financial risk of MiCare's expansion strategy; (ii) industry linkages and knowledge sharing through WBG's and IFC's expertise and global network of healthcare clients; (iii) corporate governance improvements with the appointment of a nominee director by IFC and the establishment of an audit committee.

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: MAS Holdings (Private) Limited (“MAS” or the “Group”) manages a portfolio of businesses and has operated in the realm of apparel and textile manufacturing for over 30 years. It is also the largest apparel and textile manufacturer in South Asia. The organization is headquartered in Sri Lanka with 61 manufacturing facilities placed across 16 countries, with design locations placed in key style centers across the globe and over 93,000 people involved in its operation. Today, the Group manages a more diverse portfolio of businesses across IT, brands, wearable technology, Femtech, medical apparel, start-ups and fabric parks worldwide. MAS Capital (Private) Limited (“MCAP” or the “Company”) is a wholly owned subsidiary of MAS and the holding company of the Group’s apparel pillar. The Project consists of financing the medium- and long-term working capital requirements, capital expenditure and general corporate purposes of MCAP’s existing operations in Sri Lanka.
sponsor_shareholders: MCAP is 100% owned by MAS Holdings (Private) Limited, in which, Messrs Mahesh Amalean, Sharad Amalean and Ajay Amalean hold beneficial interest.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFCs investment would be used for working capital, capital expenditure and general corporate uses of the Company. The proposed IFC investment is a US$50 million A loan for IFC’s own account, of which US$30 million will be committed initially and US$20 million to be committed within one year on a need basis.
location_description: IFC funds will be utilized for working capital requirements capex and general corporate purposes for the Borrower’s existing operations in Sri Lanka.
development_impact: At the project level it is expected to support MCAP sustain its operations to counter the impact of the COVID19 pandemic whilst preserving jobs in Sri Lanka. The Project will also ensure continued production of high value added items and foreign exchange earnings to support the Sri Lankan economy. At the market level, the Project will help to protect exports growth and promote resilience whilst limiting disruptions along the domestic and global supply chain.
additionality: IFC’s additionality stems mainly from its countercyclical role during crises which in this instance comprises IFC’s long-standing experience with rapid crisis response efforts, liquidity for working capital, its ability to support real sector clients to address liquidity constraints in response to COVID-19. IFC will provide a long term loan to MCAP which will serve as working capital funding to allow the operating subsidiaries to retain employment, generate export revenues and continue as going concerns. IFC is also expected to continue its support to the Company through its Advisory services in Gender, given 71% of the Company’s workforce are women. IFC’s assistance will also be instrumental in helping the Company mitigate the effects of COVID-19 on its employees.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: The project comprises long-term working capital funding, and necessary equipment maintenance and upgrades, to help to mitigate the impact of the COVID pandemic on Kioo Limited, a glass container manufacturing business based in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. This project is linked to https://disclosures.ifc.org/#/projectDetail/SII/38664
sponsor_shareholders: Kioo is wholly owned by African Developments Limited, an associate of the Madhvani Group - based in Uganda for over 100 years and who are one of the leading business groups in East Africa with interests in Uganda, Rwanda, Tanzania, Middle East, and India across agribusiness, power, insurance, real estate, tourism, and other sectors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at approximately US$12.2 million. The IFC investment will comprise an A loan of up to US$10 million.
location_description: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
development_impact: By supporting Kioo to sustain operations, IFC positions the private sector in Tanzania to contribute to economic recovery and improved market resilience in the regional beverages supply chain in which Kioo participates. Development outcome indicators to be tracked for the duration of the IFC investment: employment (number of direct jobs); production volume; purchases from domestic suppliers; number of countries supplied.
additionality: IFC's additionality is driven largely by IFC's countercyclical role during the COVID-19 crisis. The loan terms are not available in the local market, particularly as long-term liquidity needs were exacerbated by COVID-19. The loan will reduce dependence on short-term debt and help support the Company's investments in machinery upgrades and replacement.

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: This project is proposed under IFC’s Global Trade Supplier Finance program (“GTSF” or the “Program”) approved by the IFC Board on September 21, 2010 (Original Project #28723). Under GTSF, IFC provides short-term financing to suppliers (“Suppliers”) in emerging markets selling to large companies (“Buyers”) on open account terms. Under this project, IFC will provide financing to Under Armour Inc (“Under Armour” or “the Company”) for Suppliers based in Latin America & Caribbean region and other emerging market countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Under Armour is a leading global designer and seller of branded footwear, apparel, equipment and accessories. The company was started in 1996, went public on the NASDAQ and in December 2008 transferred to New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”). Institutional investors constitute the majority shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project (‘the Project”) within the GTSF facility is expected to be US$5 million for the supply of apparel from Under Armour’s suppliers.
location_description: GTSF-approved countries, including Honduras, El Salvador, Jordan and other emerging market countries.

project_description: Grupo Xcaret S.A.P.I. de C.V. (Xcaret or the Group) is a group of companies focused on tourism in the Rivera Maya (Mexico). Founded in 1985, its first eco-archaeological park opened in 1990 and since then, the Group has steadily grown to become the largest tourism group in this area of Mexico with several parks, guided tours, and hospitality. In December 2017, the Group opened its first hotel (Hotel Xcaret Mexico) with 900 rooms, reaching high occupancy rates in its first year of operations. The tourism sector is one of the most seriously impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic as countries placed travel bans and lockdown periods to contain the spread of the virus. In Mexico, the state of Quintana Roo, home of Cancun and the Riviera Maya, is the most affected region due to the importance of tourism. From March to May 2020, all hotels and parks were closed, which has significantly impacted Xcaret Group’s liquidity. The Group is looking for US$100mn financing to mitigate the financial impact from the COVID-19 crisis (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Xcaret is currently owned by its founding families: Quintana family owns 70%, and the Constandse family owned 30%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$100 million financial package comprised by a US$75 million A Loan for IFC’s own account and a US$25 B Loan / Parallel Loan.
location_description: Mexico
development_impact: Grupo Xcaret has been a prominent tourism operator in Cancun/Riviera Maya. IFC's financing will provide the needed additional liquidity to ensure that Xcaret can sustain the ongoing situation, support the reopening of parks and complete the construction of Hotel Xcaret Arte. IFC's financing will help to (i) preserve thousands of jobs and support future recruitment; (ii) finance the additional expenses needed for reopening; and (iii) maintain Xcaret's significant local value-chain.
additionality: - Financing Structure: the COVID-19 pandemic has negatively impacted financing to the tourism sector, especially regarding longer tenors. Through the Project, IFC will be providing seven-year loan that can be used for working capital or liquidity needs in the upcoming months. - Resource Mobilization: IFC will help mobilize a total of US$25 million in syndicated loans or parallel loans in order to mitigate the financial impact from the COVID-19 crisis. IFC's relationships with commercial banks and international financial institutions around the world will help attract additional financing for the Company that otherwise would not be available in the current situation.

project_description: Rupshi Flour Mills Limited (“Rupshi” or “the Company”) is a greenfield flour refining plant with a capacity of 5,000 MT per day in City Economic Zone in Rupshi, 30km south of Dhaka, Bangladesh (“the Project”). Once operational, the Company will produce Atta, Maida, and Semolina flours primarily targeting the domestic market. The Company is a member of City Group, an established conglomerate consisting of leading food processing and packaged product companies in Bangladesh. City Group is promoted by Mr. Fazlur Rahman, with his wife Mrs. Hamida Rahman and his children Mr. Hasan Rahman, Ms. Shampa Rahman, Ms.Farzana Rahman, and Ms. Razia Sultana Deepa (together “the Sponsors”). IFC is proposing to provide a senior secured A Loan of up to EUR 14 million of up to 8 years’ tenor; and an additional BDT 500 million in local currency denominated loan for a tenor of up to 6 years to support the Project. The balance of the project cost will be funded by Export Credit Agency (“ECA”) backed financing, local currency financing, and the Sponsor’s equity contribution.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Fazlur Rahman founded City Group in 1973. City Group is a conglomerate based in Bangladesh, consisting of leading food processing and packaged product companies amongst its various other businesses. City Group entities are owned by Mr. Rahman, Mrs. Rahman, and their grown-up children Mr. Md. Hasan, Ms. Shampa Rahman, Ms. Farzana Rahman, and Ms. Razia Sultana Deepa. Together, Mr. Rahman, Mrs. Rahman, and their son Mr. Md. Hasan owns 100% of Rupshi Flour Mills (as of October 31, 2020).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be ~US$171 million and is proposed to be funded 70% by debt of ~US$120 million and 30% by the Sponsor’s equity contribution of ~US$50 million. The debt is proposed to be a mix of foreign currency and local currency debt. The proposed IFC investment is a secured A Loan of ~EUR 14 million and ~BDT 500 million with a tenor of up to eight years including a two-year grace period. This investment is expected to be utilized for capital expenditure to be incurred for the Project (including on plant & machinery, other equipment, building and other construction costs).
location_description: The Project is located in in City Economic Zone in Rupshi, 30km south of Dhaka, Bangladesh. City Economic Zone is on 78 acres of land at the bank of river Shitalakshya.
development_impact: Food Security: The Project will contribute to improving Bangladesh's food security by supporting improved food safety standards and provide an alternative to the major staple, at competitive prices. The Project will support an increased production of flour that will meet growing domestic demand and partially replace informal mills with hygienic flour of superior quality. Employment and broader value creation: Through this investment, the Group will be able to expand its flour milling operations, and will create an estimated 250 direct jobs at Rupshi's facilities, accompanied by further indirect and induced jobs throughout the value chain. Market creation: The Project will aid the formalization of the milling sector by increasing the size of the formal market and the expected partial displacement of the informal mills will promote better quality standards in the industry.
additionality: Long Tenor Financing: IFC is proposing a long-term loan with eight years maturity, including two years of grace period. IFC's proposed financing will meet the gap between the Project's machinery cost and foreign currency financing by ECA. In absence of IFC financing, the Company will have to finance the mentioned gap through local currency from commercial banks with shorter tenor (~5 years), which could have an adverse impact on the Project. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC's global experience in agribusiness sector, and with milling projects in particular, will assist the company with it strengthening its business by properly mitigating the risks, improving operational efficiencies, and making longer-term strategic decisions. IFC also has several advisory offerings that might be appropriate for the Company, including flourfortification, work related to food safety and reduction of wastage during processing. Standard Setting: IFC can assist in identifying and closing any gaps in the ESG performance of the Company. Through ESAP and other associated measures prescribed by IFC, the Company will make improvements which will help demonstrate best practices for the sector.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan financing package to Sao Martinho S.A. (Sao Martinho or the Company). Founded in the 1930’s by the Ometto family, Sao Martinho is a sugar, ethanol and renewable energy producer in Brazil. Sao Martinho currently operates three sugar mills in the state of Sao Paulo and one distillery in the state of Goias.
sponsor_shareholders: Sao Martinho is listed in Brazilian stock exchange B3 under the Novo Mercado segment. The Company’s majority shareholders and sponsors are the Ometto family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of a US$90 million A loan financing package to Sao Martinho, including a Green Loan tranche. The proceeds of the IFC loan will be used by Sao Martinho to carry out its investment program including (i) an expansion of bagasse-based cogeneration capacity, including the installation of a new boiler that will improve electricity to sugar cane ratios and (ii) sugarcane re-planting and crop treatment capex.
location_description: São Martinho is headquartered in the city of Pradópolis, state of Sao Paulo, where it operates the Sao Martinho sugar and ethanol mill. The Company also operates two other mills in the State of Sao Paulo and one distillery in the state of Goias.
development_impact: The project contributes to climate change mitigation by promoting the increase of renewable energy sales and supporting the production of biofuels. In addition, by supporting the ongoing capital requirements to maintain and replant sugarcane, the project contributes to keep the overall health of the industry.
additionality: IFC is providing long-term financing including a green loan tranche. IFC is playing a countercyclical role, as long-term debt financing has been limited in Brazil. IFC will support Sao Martinho's liquidity and enable critical capex for the sugar & ethanol industry. In addition, IFC will contribute to strengthening the Company's Environmental and Social practices through the adoption of IFC's Performance Standards.

project_description: Grupo Monte Rosa S.A. (“Monte Rosa” or the “Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of Pantaleon Sugar Holdings Company Ltd. (“PSH”), is a sugar and energy producer located in Nicaragua’s Pacific Northwest, with capacity to process 16,000 tons of sugar cane per day. The proposed financing consists of a US$15 million revolving credit facility renewable yearly for up to 4 years and a US$10 million long-term A-Loan for Monte Rosa. The proceeds of the short-term revolving credit facility will support the Company’s working capital needs, while the long-term investment will fund the purchase of machinery (tractors, seeding and harvesting equipment) to assist Monte Rosa on enhancing the efficiency of its operations.
sponsor_shareholders: Pantaleon is an agribusiness group founded in Guatemala in 1849, dedicated to the processing of sugarcane for the production of sugar, molasses, ethanol and energy. Along its operations in Mexico, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Brazil, Pantaleon Group employs over 20 thousand people and has a total combined daily milling capacity of 80 thousand tons of sugarcane.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total financing amounts to US$25 million, which will be funded through a US$15 million short-term revolving credit facility with commitment of up to 4-years and a US$10 million A-Loan.
location_description: Investments will be made in Nicaragua’s Pacific Northwest.
development_impact: The Project will play an important role in supporting the Company's operations in an uncertain macroeconomic environment. The investment is safeguarding production as well as further improving operational practices. At the market level, IFC will support a sugar producer and exporter that will help strengthen the country's standing in the global market through the continuing adoption of IFC's Performance Standards and contribute to setting world class standards across the industry in Nicaragua.
additionality: Financial Additionality: IFC will have a strong financial additionality in this transaction by playing a countercyclical role in a context of high political uncertainty in Nicaragua. Although the Group could raise debt at the corporate level, financing in Nicaragua is being curtailed due to the current political environment and the resulting domestic financial crisis. In this context, IFC will be providing short-term financing to ensure the Company has access to working capital financing as well as long-term financing required to finance the acquisition of equipment at terms and tenors not available domestically. Non-Financial Additionality: Over the last decade IFC has supported most of the sugar players in Nicaragua to improve their competitiveness, making a sector that is a key contributor to economic development and a vital source of exports more resilient. Also, as a result of IFC's engagement with these companies, they have improved their environmental and social practices, including the development of procedures on prevention, education, and mitigation of the Chronic Kidney Disease ("CKD") (see the Risk & Issues section). Through this project, IFC will continue to support a former client in aligning its operations with IFC's Performance Standards (PS) and therefore contribute to setting world-class standards across the industry in the country.

project_description: The Project entails the design, construction, operation and maintenance of an energy-efficient mixed-use IT park located in an underdeveloped area of the city center of Iasi, a frontier and convergence European regional city in the North-Eastern part of Romania (“Project”). The Project will be divided into two phases: Phase I: development of the “Campus” property, a 6-storey office building with a Gross Leasable Area (GLA) of c.60,000 square meters; and Phase II: development of the “Tower” property, a high-rise office building with a planned GLA of c.46,000 square meters. On the ground floor, both properties will house restaurants and convenience retail operations.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor of the Project is Iulius Holding SRL, a privately held, vertically integrated Romanian developer and operator of mixed-use real estate with 16 income-producing properties comprised of large retail schemes and Grade A offices. Iulius Holding SRL is wholly owned by Mr. Iulian Dascalu, a successful and experienced Romanian real estate developer, originally from Iasi. The borrower of the Phase 1 property will be Palas Campus SRL, an Iasi-based special purpose vehicle (“SPV”), owned 50% by the Sponsor and 50% by Mr. Dascalu. A similar SPV will be established for Phase II, but this has not yet happened as this phase is c.12 months behind Phase I. Both SPVs (the “Companies”) will directly own and operate their respective properties.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at €231.9 million for the construction and development of the Phase I and Phase II properties, of which 40 percent (€92.8 million) would be funded with equity provided by the Sponsor and 60 percent (€139.1 million) with debt . The Phase I development is expected to precede the Phase II development. For Phase I, the Project involves a 10.5 year senior loan of up to €28.2 million from IFC’s own account, and, a 10.5 year senior syndicated loan of up to €23.8 million , and a 10.5 year senior loan of up to €20.3 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-lending Portfolio Program (MCPP). For Phase II, the Project involves a 10.5 year senior loan of up to €27.1 million from IFC’s own account,, and a 10.5 year senior syndicated loan of up to €20.3 million, and a 10.5 year senior loan of up to €19.5 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-lending Portfolio Program (MCPP).
location_description: Iasi, Romania
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is derived from stakeholder effects through improved access to high quality Grade A office buildings. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Project will promote greater market integration through the development of a new business center, which will provide more economic opportunities to the local population.
additionality: IFC's involvement in the Project is expected to bring both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC's financial additionality is driven by the mobilization of 3rd party loan funds from outside Romania and the "green" characterization of the loans. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will help build the capacity of Iulius Holding SRL and of the Companies in areas of environmental and social performance and governance, as well as to help the Companies to certify their properties using EDGE standards.

project_description: Established in 2014, Twiga Foods (“Twiga” or the “Company”) is a distributor of fresh fruits & vegetables and fast-moving consumer goods in Kenya. Through its unified digital platform and robust logistics network, the company efficiently connects farmers and retail vendors to increase the availability, affordability and accessibility of food. The company is an existing IFC Disruptive Technologies and Venture Capital group portfolio client (#41195). IFC is also currently offering advisory services to Twiga on food safety, agronomy, soil & water, and agri-finance through the Africa Food Safety Program (AS project #601759). IFC is proposing to invest, through unfunded Risk Sharing Facilities (“RSFs”) with tier 1 commercial banks in Kenya, up to KES1.6 billion (US$15 million equivalent) for an aggregate portfolio of loans up to KES3.2 billion (US$30 million equivalent) to support the development of up to 300 irrigated medium-scale (>15ha) contract farmers (the “Program”). Complementing seasonal supply from Twiga’s existing ~19,500 smallholder supply base, the irrigated medium farms are expected to add stable year-round volume which would contribute to better food availability, affordability and quality in the markets Twiga serve. The RSFs will be scaled up in phases and the first phase will be implemented with KCB Bank Kenya Limited (“KCB Kenya”). The Program will also be potentially supported with blended finance through the Global SME Finance Facility (“GSMEF”) and the Women Entrepreneurs Finance Initiative (“We-Fi”) to de-risk the project and incentivize the Company to achieve significant growth in lending to medium scale farmers which are Small and Medium Enterprises (“SMEs”) including women SMEs (“WSMEs”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Twiga Foods Limited, whose shareholders are co-founders Peter Njonjo and Grant Brooke, as well as institutional investors including the IFC Venture Capital Group, Goldman Sachs, Stichting DOB Equity, ON Mauritius, Wamda MENA Ventures I C.V, Alpha Mundi, Blue Haven Global LLC, 1776 Seed Investors LP, 1776 Bananas LP, TLcom Capital Partners, Creadev International, SKC2PCC, Tide Africa Fund, Project Hand Purpose Trust, Biscuit LLC, Musha Investments LLC, Adolf H. Lundin Charitable Foundation, AHL Growth Fund LP, GLQ Holdings (UK) Limited, SocialAlpha Investment Fund (SAIF) SICAV-SIF – Bastion and other minority investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an unfunded risk sharing facility of up to up to KES1.6 billion (US$15 million equivalent) for an aggregate portfolio of loans up to KES3.2 billion (US$30 million equivalent).
location_description: The farms that will be financed through the RSFs will be located in various counties across six sourcing regions, namely Central Highlands, Mt. Kenya, Eastern, North Rift, Nyanza/Western and the Coastal regions throughout Kenya.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a senior loan to Jalles Machado S.A. (“Jalles”, “Jalles Machado” or the “Company”), composed of (i) an A Loan of up to US$20 million or the BRL equivalent, and (ii) a B Loan of up to US$7.5 million. The Company is playing an important role in the COVID-19 response in the state of Goias, ensuring a continuous supply of sanitizing products in this frontier region.
sponsor_shareholders: The Otavio Lage family, which has over 80 years of experience in the agribusiness sector, has a 51.7% shareholding interest in the Company. The balance is owned primarily by other four local families.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an up to US$27.5 million A/B Loan to Jalles. The proceeds of the loan will support an increase in production of sanitizing products, as well as support the Company’s working capital requirements.
location_description: Goianésia, Goiás, Brazil
development_impact: By sustaining the Company's operations, the project helps consumers have continued access to hand sanitizer and ensures continuity of employment opportunities in a frontier region. By limiting supply disruptions, the project promotes resilience in the sugar and ethanol sector.
additionality: IFC is providing long-term financing and resource mobilization. IFC is playing a countercyclical role following the COVID-19 outbreak, as long-term debt financing has been limited in Brazil. IFC will mobilize financing from a commercial bank. IFC will support Jalles' liquidity and enable capex expansion for a critical hygiene product.

project_description: Founded in 1967, Sunshine Holdings PLC (“Sunshine”, “SUN”, or the “Sponsor”) is a listed Sri Lankan conglomerate with a market capitalization of US$45.5 million. Sunshine operates in the sectors of healthcare, consumer goods, agribusiness and renewable energy.
sponsor_shareholders: SUN is listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange with a market capitalization of US$45.5 million as at October 12, 2020. SUN’s majority shareholder is G. Sathasivam and his family. SBI Ven Holdings Pte Ltd has a minority stake in the company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$14.7 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US $7 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Daintee has 2 primary manufacturing sites and 4 other locations for warehousing and packaging in the Ratmalana industrial zone; While the solar rooftop projects will be located in various cities in Sri Lanka.
development_impact: At the Project-level, it is expected to: (i) displace tons of CO2 annually; (ii) help meet Sri Lanka's growing electricity demand through a cost-competitive energy solution. At the Market-level, it is expected to (iii) increase competitiveness in the FMCG sector by promoting diversification, and (iv) demonstrate a scheme to scale-up rooftop solar capacity in the renewable energy sector.
additionality: IFC's Additionality includes: (i) providing longer-term debt financing not readily available in the domestic market and better aligned with the company's expansion plans; (ii) sharing knowledge and expertise in strengthening technical and project development functions in the solar sector and facilitate the adoption of higher international food safety standards.; and (iii) standard setting where IFC will help benchmark the Company's environmental and social practices and corporate governance structures to international standards.

project_description: Founded in 1965 in the Negev desert in Israel, Netafim Ltd (“Netafim”) is a global player in the micro irrigation systems (“MIS”) sector. Clients value Netafim’s team of 200 agronomists deployed globally that provide expertise in all crop types and growing conditions. The proposed investment consists of a loan up to INR1,520 million (approximately US$20 million) to Netafim Irrigation India Private Ltd (“Netafim India” or “the Company”), guaranteed by Netafim, to support the (i) working capital needs of Netafim India arising from the COVID-19 crisis, and (ii) CAPEX needs to maintain local production capacity (the “Project”). IFC is also considering mobilizing a financing package of up to INR4,178 million (approximately US$55 million) with commercial banks and /or development finance institutions (the “Parallel Loans”) for the same purpose.
sponsor_shareholders: Netafim India’s parent company, Netafim Ltd, is 80% owned by Orbia (formerly Mexichem) and 20% owned by Kibbutzim Hatzerim (also the founder of Netafim). One of Netafim’s key factories is also located within Kibbutz Hatzerim. Orbia, founded in 1953, is a Mexican company involved in several industries, including building and infrastructure, data communications, irrigation, chemicals, and more. Orbia focuses on insuring food security, reducing water scarcity, reinventing the future of cities and homes, connecting communities to data infrastructure, and expanding access to health and wellness with advanced materials.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Netafim India is facing delays in receivables caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, which has led to higher working capital requirements. Netafim India requires US$75 million of financing for the coming years to support its working capital needs, cover the financing needs of new community irrigation projects, and execute capital expenditure investments to maintain its production facilities. The proposed US$75 million long-term financing will be in the form of Non-Convertible Debentures.
location_description: Funds will be disbursed to Netafim India to cover its financing needs throughout the country, with the largest use of proceeds being in the states of Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, and Chhattisgarh.
development_impact: The expected Project-level outcome is its contribution to generating better yields for the local farmers and strengthening their resilience to climate stocks. The Project in India may have larger benefit given the potential for creating impact at scale using the community irrigation model. The Project will also contribute to sustainability by promoting water used efficiency in agriculture in several water stressed regions.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC is providing the Company the financing flexibility at the country level that is not easily available. The long-term working capital finance will support the company during these taxing times of COVID-19 pandemic. Knowledge sharing: IFC will leverage its advisory capabilities to support the Company's expansion and maximize the impacts of irrigation.

project_description: The proposed investment is by way of (a) subscription to unlisted, secured non-convertible debentures (NCDs) up to INR1,100 million (equivalent to US$14.6 million) issued by Ramkrishna Forgings Limited (“RKFL” or the “Company”), and (b) at IFC’s option, subscription to NCDs and/or an equity/quasi equity instrument, aggregating up to INR400 million (equivalent to US$5.3 million), issued by the Company (the “Project”). The Project will finance the Company’s long-term working capital requirements, maintenance capex and other general corporate purposes at its existing facilities in India and provide a much-needed liquidity during the COVID-19 crisis, which will enable a swift recovery once operations ramp up. RKFL, an existing IFC client, was established in 1981 and is one of the leading forged component manufacturers in India supplying to major manufacturers of commercial vehicles and to the railway sectors. The Company operates six manufacturing plants in the states of Jharkhand and West Bengal.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange since 2004. As of June 30, 2020, Mahabir Jalan (the chairman of RKFL), Naresh Jalan (a son of the chairman and the Managing Director of RKFL), and their family (“the Sponsors”) collectively own 4.85% of the Company. 17.42% and 23.20% of the stake are held by Eastern Credit Capital Private Limited and Riddhi Portfolio Private Limited respectively, asset management companies over which the Sponsors and the key management personnel of the Company are able to exercise significant influence. The rest of the stake (54.52%) is held by the public shareholders, including IFC which owns 2.40% of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is by way of (a) subscription to unlisted, secured NCDs up to INR1,100 million (equivalent to US$14.6 million) issued by RKFL, and (b) at IFC’s option, subscription to NCDs and/or an equity/quasi equity instrument, aggregating up to INR400 million (equivalent to US$5.3 million), issued by the Company.
location_description: Since the IFC financing would partly finance the Company’s long-term working capital needs, the project location would include all the plants of the Company. RKFL Headquarter: 23, Circus Avenue., Kolkata-700017 West Bengal, India Other locations: Plant I : Plot No. M-6, Phase-VI, Gamaria, Jamshedpur-832 108, Jharkhand Plant II: 7/40, Duffer Street, Liluah, Howrah-711 204, West Bengal Plant III & IV: Plot No. M-15, 16 and NS-26, Phase VII, Adityapur Industrial Area, Jamshedpur-832109, Jharkhand Plant V: Baliguma, Kolabira, Saraikela, Kharsawan-833220, Jharkhand Plant VII: Plot No. 1988, Plant-VII, Mouza Dugni, Block-Saraikela, P.O. Dugni, Saraikela, Kharsawan, Jharkhand-833220
development_impact: Stakeholder effects: IFC's financing will sustain the Company's ability to maintain operations and be in a better position to deliver goods and services to the commercial vehicles and railways segments during the recovery period as the crisis abates. IFC's financing will also help to preserve more than 1,700 direct jobs as well as indirect jobs across the supply chain during crisis. Resilience: The proposed investment promotes the resilience of the Company through supporting the sustainability of domestic manufacturing of forging components at competitive prices, supplying the essential products to the economy-critical industries such as commercial vehicles and railways.
additionality: IFC's additionality stems mainly from its countercyclical role during crises which in this instance comprises IFC's long-standing experience with rapid crisis response efforts, liquidity for working capital, its ability to support real sector clients to address liquidity constraints in response to COVID-19 and to provide critical goods, equipment and supplies, its ability to help clients re-direct supply chains and its support to continued employment in countries of operations.

company_name: SOUTH AFRICAN STUDENT ACCOMMODATION IMPACT INVESTMENTS (PTY) LIMITED
project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a ZAR150million equity investment in Momentum Student Accommodation Impact Fund Proprietary Limited (‘The Company” or “MSAIF”), an open-ended investment company developing and operating affordable, purpose-built student accommodation (“PBSA”) in South Africa (SA). MSAIF is registered as a private limited liability company and is managed by Eris Property Group, a leading property developer and real estate fund manager in SA. MSAIF’s business model is to provide serviced safe, secure, affordable purpose-built student accommodation that is located close to Public- universities and/or Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET’s) (which will be marketed under the “Rise Living” brand). MSAIF has developed one asset named “Units on Park” in Hatfield Pretoria; a 998 bed development. Concurrently, MSAIF is pursuing a pipeline of additional development and investment opportunities and expects to grow to 10/12-asset portfolio over the next 5 years. The proposed IFC financing package is to support MSAIF’s growth plans. It is anticipated that, MSAIF will reach an optimal size for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) and listing as a Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT)on a major stock exchange within the next 5-7 years.
sponsor_shareholders: Eris Property Group (“Eris”) is an integrated property and service operation in South Africa which provides commercial property development and management services in South Africa and across Sub-Saharan Africa. Eris is majority owned by MMI Holdings, SA’s third-largest long-term insurer (total assets of ZAR503b (US$33.3b); market cap of ZAR27.6b (US$1.8b)) as at July 2020.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: MSAIF has a total committed capital target size of ZAR2.0billion, of which IFC’s proposed investment is up to ZAR150million in equity, not to exceed 20% of total committed capital.
location_description: South Africa; MSAIF’s mandate is to invest exclusively in purpose-built student accommodation in South Africa.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level impact is increased access to high quality student accommodation in the underserved South African student housing market. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote sector competitiveness by encouraging private expansion into the student accommodation market via demonstration effects.
additionality: IFC will provide early stage equity and patient capital that will be necessary for MSAIF to develop greenfield PBSA assets which is critical to bridging the supply -demand gap in South Africa's student accommodation sector and positioning the MSAIF vehicle for a listing in the future. IFC participation as anchor investor will send positive signals to institutional investors, providing proof of concept and comfort in the standards of the underlying assets, for the ongoing capital raise and ultimately at the pre-listing and listing stage. Furthermore, IFC will also engage with MSAIF to ensure that the buildings developed achieve high green building standards.
Company Name: SOUTH AFRICAN STUDENT ACCOMMODATION IMPACT INVESTMENTS (PTY) LIMITED

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a US$75 million financing package to Hayel Saeed Anam (HSA or the Sponsor) Group’s food processing operations in Yemen (HSA Foods). The funds will be used to finance the permanent working capital needs of HSA Foods which is producing necessity foods such as flour, sugar and dairy products for local consumption.
sponsor_shareholders: HSA Foods is comprised of six Yemeni companies which shall be co-borrowers of the financing: i) National Dairy and Food Company Taiz; ii) National Dairy and Food Company Hodaida; iii) Yemen Company for Sugar Refining; iv) Yemen Company for Flour Mills and Silos Aden; v) Yemen Company for Flour Mills and Silos Al Hodaida; and vi) Al Hodaida Flour Mills Co. Limited. The co-borrowers are majority owned by the Hayel Saeed Anam family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment in HSA Foods is a loan in an aggregate amount of up to US$75 million, consisting of: (i) an A Loan of up to US$75 million for IFC’s own account; and (ii) a B1 Loan of up to US$20 million from potential participants; the proposed investment of US$75 million to be supported by a concessional unfunded first loss guarantee provided by IFC acting as implementing entity of the IDA PSW BFF.
location_description: The Project is in various regions namely Taiz, Aden and Al Hodaida, in Yemen.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is the increased supply of staple goods in a country experiencing internal strife and high levels of food insecurity. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates its investment will improve market resilience by increasing food production, which builds capacity to withstand shocks and stresses related to COVID-19.
additionality: The proposed IFC loan has both financial and non-financial additionality. IFC will be providing financing for HSA Food's food processing operations in Yemen amid a challenging economic environment due to the ongoing conflict and impact of COVID-19. In addition, IFC will contribute to strengthening the company's Environmental and Social practices in the food sector through the adoption of IFC's Performance Standards. IFC will also contribute to knowledge sharing and capacity building through the planned advisory work in the areas of gender and wastewater management.

project_description: Indospace Logistics Parks III LP (the “fund” or “ILP III”) a US$580 million 2018 vintage fund for developing logistics and industrial parks across India. The Fund invests in warehousing and industrial property assets in India through various special purpose vehicles (“SPVs”). The proposed IFC investment is a senior secured loan of up to INR 5,500 million (equivalent to US$75 million) to select SPVs of the fund which will develop and operate warehousing and industrial properties in India.
sponsor_shareholders: The SPVs are indirectly owned by Indospace Logistics Parks III LP, a Singapore limited partnership which is managed by Indospace Capital Asia Pte Limited (“Indospace” or the “Fund Manager”).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment will in the form of straight senior loans of up to INR 5,500 million (approx. US$75 million) to various SPVs that own and operate the industrial and warehousing properties.
location_description: The Industrial and warehousing parks will be located across India.
development_impact: (i) Economy-wide effects: By accelerating construction and development of parks as the Indian economy emerges from the COVID-19 crisis, the financing will enable preservation of thousands of jobs in construction of properties and ancillary / indirect jobs which would otherwise be lost. (ii) Contribution to Market Creation: a. Competitiveness: IFC anticipates that the Project will provide a significant positive step forward to the Indian warehousing and industrial property market, which is in its evolutionary phase and now going through a severe slowdown due to Covid-19. If the Fund is successful in developing and offering its properties in time for companies to set up operations, it will help demonstrate a path of recovery for the sector, relying on private investment and demonstrate to other players to replicate the Company's modern, efficient, and lower cost characteristics. b. Resilience: The Project will contribute to the resilience of real sector markets, through enabling business infrastructure that will ensure continued supply of goods and services at affordable prices and limiting disruptions along supply chains thereby mitigating the effects of the economic downturn.
additionality: IFC will play a countercyclical role by providing long-term finance enabling the Fund to continue investing in its business and prepare itself for accelerated demand in the medium-to-long term. The long tenor is also designed to provide a financial cushion as the parks emerge from the slowdown; allowing the Fund flexibility to capitalize on opportunities and manage market risks. Post-investment, IFC will continue to help the Project with EDGE certification.

project_description: Guangxi Yangxiang Co., Ltd (“Yangxiang” or the “Company”) was established in 1998 in Guigang city, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China. Its main businesses are the breeding and farming of pigs, and pig farm services. Yangxiang is among the top pig companies in China. Headquartered in Guangxi, Yangxiang has presence in Hebei, Henan, Hunan and Liaoning provinces -- all are frontier provinces in China. The Project is to expand pig breeding and farming capacity and its ancillary facilities in Guangxi. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to CNY560 million (approximately US$80 million equivalent).
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. YANG Xiang is the founder and controlling shareholder of the Company. Mr. Yang directly and indirectly owns 42.56% percent of the Company. The other shareholders are the employee-owned funds, 46 individual shareholders, Continental Feed, and 2 university funds.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be approximately US$264 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to CNY560 million (approximately US$80 million equivalent) to the Company.
location_description: Guigang, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region
development_impact: The Project is assessed as part of IFC's overarching programmatic intervention (ASF Asia Recovery Program) to respond to the impacts of the ASF on the regional pork industry. The most significant, expected Project-level outcome resulting from this expansion is the impact on consumers from the provision of safe pork at the time of severe supply shortage as well as implementation of advanced biosecurity procedures at the new farms. The Project will also strengthen the operations of smaller farmers by disseminating best industry practices through the Company's out-grower scheme. At the market level, the Project, alongside other planned investment and advisory interventions, is expected to promote market resilience through improvement of biosecurity and disease management, both by supporting industry consolidation and disseminating best practices among smaller players.
additionality: 1. Financing structure: The private companies have limited access to long-term loans in the local market. IFC's long-term loan is much needed by the Company to improve its debt maturity profile and mitigate sector cyclicality in major expansions; 2. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC will organize workshops to bring the Company's successful experience and innovations in ASF prevention and recovery to other industry players in Aisa, and support the Company's continuous efforts in obtaining higher standards in animal welfare and responsible use of antibiotics to make demonstration effects in the industry. 3. Stamp of approval: the Company is endeavoring to a domestic public listing. IFC's investment indicates a stamp of approval on the Company to the capital market.

company_name: INDORAMA VENTURES GLOBAL SERVICES COMPANY LIMITED
project_description: The proposed investment is for up to US$150 million equivalent in “A Loan” and mobilization of up to US$150 million equivalent in “Parallel loans” to Indorama Ventures Global Services Limited (“IVGS” or the “Company”). IVGS, incorporated in Thailand is a subsidiary of Indorama Ventures Public Company Limited (“IVL” or the “Group”), is one of the world’s leading petrochemicals producers, with a global manufacturing footprint across Africa, Asia Pacific, Europe and Americas. The company’s portfolio comprises Integrated PET, Olefins, Fibers, Packaging and Specialty Chemicals. IVL is a leading global producer of resins with integrated operations in the polyethylene terephthalate (“PET”) value chain.
sponsor_shareholders: IVL is a global intermediate petrochemical producer and one of the largest vertically integrated polyester value chain producers in the world, serving global brands in diversified end-use markets including food, beverages, mobility, personal care and health care. IVL is headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand, and geographically diversified with over 110 operating sites in 33 countries across five continents and employs over 24,000 employees. IVL is a publicly listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand. The Lohia Family (SP Lohia and his brother Aloke Lohia), are the largest shareholders of IVL with a 64.75% holding while the balance 35.25% of the shares are held by institutional and retail shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$300 million and will be funded with an IFC A Loan of up to US$150 million, and up to US$150 million in parallel loans.
location_description: The expansion of recycled PET capacity and other sustainability projects will be implemented across IVL’s existing and planned manufacturing facilities in Thailand, Philippines, Indonesia, India, and Brazil.
development_impact: Economywide effects: The Project will restore the lost economic value of valuable PET resources through a circular economy of PET waste and create employment. Stakeholder effects: The Project will increase PET recycling capacity in targeted emerging markets to meet the growing demand for recycling PET in food and beverage applications. Environmental effects: The Project is expected to divert PET waste from land and marine environment through recycling. The Project is also expected to reduce Greenhouse Gas (GHG) intensity through replacing virgin PET with recycled PET, and implementation of other sustainability projects such resource efficiency and renewable energy. Sustainability: The Project will promote a circular economy for PET bottles and catalyze the changes in the market by demonstrating innovative business models and best practices, and through capacity building.
additionality: This will be the first IFC investment to support recycled PET projects in diverse countries across Asia and Latin America to address growing marine and environmental pollution. A portion of the proposed investment will be IFC's first "Blue Loan" in the real sector. IFC will also mobilize significant additional funding from other development finance institutions. IVL will leverage IFC's ongoing work on plastics circularity in Asia and incorporate best practices in renewable energy and resource efficiency for their operations to further reduce operating costs and address climate impacts.
Company Name: INDORAMA VENTURES GLOBAL SERVICES COMPANY LIMITED

project_description: The Project is a 700 tons per day (TPD) brownfield expansion of its chlor-alkali plant at Bharuch (Gujarat, India), along with a 500 TPD flaker plant and a 120 megawatt captive power plant ('The Project”). The Project is expected to cost approximately US$143 million. IFC’s proposed investment of up to INR 3 billion (~US$ 40 million) in DCM Shriram Limited (“DCM” or “the Company) would be used to fund the chlor-alkali plant expansion and flaker plant (costing US$89 million) along with long term working capital and routine capex. The captive power plant will be funded through the company’s internal cash flows.
sponsor_shareholders: DCM is a company listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in India with revenues of approximately US$ 1.03 billion and Net Profit of approximately US$ 95 million for the financial year ended March 31, 2020. The Company had a market capitalization of approximately US$660 million as of July 7, 2020. The Sponsors, led by Mr. Ajay S Shriram, Mr. Vikram S Shriram and Mr. Ajit S Shriram. collectively control approximately 66% of the shares in DCM Shriram and the rest of the shareholding is widely held by institutional and other public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost approximately US$143 million. IFCs investment would be used to fund the chlor-alkali plant expansion and flaker plant costing $89 million, along with long term working capital and routine capex. IFC plans to provide a Senior Loan of up to INR 3 billion (approximately US$40 million) denominated in INR in the form of a Non-Convertible Debentures (NCD). The proposed investment fits into IFC’s crisis response for COVID financing and would help fill the Company’s cash flow gaps and provide for timely completion of the Project.
location_description: This project is located at Bharuch, Gujarat in India
development_impact: (i)Employment: IFC's financing will also help to add approx. 100 permanent skilled jobs and 250 temporary jobs and preserve 800 temporary jobs during construction, as a result of the expansion. (ii) Supply chain: The expansion will ensure the availability of caustic soda at competitive prices, and key raw materials to downstream industries such as aluminum, paper, detergents, agro-chemicals, and pharmaceuticals.
