(iii) Resilience: IFCs investment is intended to promote the resilience of real sector markets, by ensuring continued supply of goods and services in sectors affected by reduced demand, price reductions and exchange rate volatility thereby mitigating the effects of the economic downturn. The chemicals sector, an important sector in India is already exposed to the effects of severe supply chain disruptions and slowing economic growth
additionality: (a)Financial additionality: (i)The Company will benefit from IFC's long tenor offering (10-year tenor) which is useful for companies such as DCM Shriram that operate in a largely cyclical business. (ii) IFC will play a countercyclical role providing liquidity to bridge any funding gap triggered by the effects of COVID-19 (b) IFC participation help to incorporate and maintain global best practices in Environment & Social (E&S) impacts during and post expansion.

project_description: The proposed investment is an A loan of up to US$10 million to ETC Group (“ETG” or the “Company”) incorporated in Mauritius. ETG is a vertically integrated agricultural supply chain manager involved in the origination, procurement, warehousing, logistics of multiple agricultural commodities and processing of consumer products. It is active in over 26 African countries, as well as in India, China and South East Asia and has additional trading, merchandising and/or treasury desks in Europe, the Americas and the Middle East. The investment will support ETG’s long term incremental working capital needs mainly in Sub Saharan Africa which will be complemented by an advisory services program to enhance the productivity and efficiency of ETG’s supply chains (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Ultimate beneficial owners of ETG together controlling 55.6% are Mr. Mahesh Patel (Chairman), Mr. Ketan Patel (CEO) and Bisa Trust represented by the Joint-CEO, Birju Patel. Other key shareholders are Mitsui & Co. via its African arm MIT African Management Limited (31.9%) and Pembani Remgro of South Africa (8.8%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated project cost is US$115 million. IFC will support the Project with an investment of up to US$10 million in the form of an unsecured loan.
location_description: The funds are expected to be utilized mainly in Sub Saharan Africa to finance ETG’s trading flows in agri commodities including fertilizer, cashews, pulses among others.
development_impact: IFC expects the Project will help strengthen financial and value-chain integration, provide working capital financing for smallholder farmers as a result of ETG's procurement activities; and bring about price discovery in the market place.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in two forms: i) financing structure through funding not readily available in SSA; and ii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building through advisory services which seeks to reach a significant number of smallholder farmers in its key SSA countries.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is up to US$120 million loan facility to support the development of two logistic property facilities, consisting of: a single-storey warehouse – to be developed and owned by PT LOGOS Indonesia Deltamas One (“Borrower 1”) and located in Cikarang of West Java, Indonesia (“Sub- Project 1”); and two 3-storey ramp-up warehouses – to be developed and owned by PT LOGOS Indonesia Prime One (“Borrower 2”) and located in Cibitung of West Java, Indonesia (“Sub-Project 2” and together with Sub-Project 1, the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 2010, LOGOS Property Group Ltd (“LOGOS”) is one of Asia Pacific’s leading logistics property groups with operations across Australia, China, Singapore, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, Vietnam, India and New Zealand. LOGOS Indonesia Logistics Venture L.P. (“Sponsor”) is a platform established by LOGOS under its Southeast Asian arm to develop and own high quality, modern warehouses in Indonesia. The Sponsor has approximately US$280 million committed capital from its limited partners, namely, LILV Sponsor Investment Pte. Ltd. (subsidiary of LOGOS), Canada Pension Plan Investment Board and Ivanhoé Cambridge, the real estate subsidiary of Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec. Both Borrower 1 and Borrower 2 are 100% owned by the Sponsor.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the Project is estimated not to exceed approximately US$286 million. The proposed IFC senior loan facility will be allocated between Sub-Project 1 and Sub-Project 2 in proportion to estimated cost for undertaking Sub-Project 1 and Sub-Project 2, respectively. The loan facility will comprise (i) an A loan of up to US$73 million for IFC’s own account, and (ii) a Trust Loan of up to US$ 47 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program.
location_description: The Project is located in Cikarang and Cibitung of West Java, Indonesia.
development_impact: The most significant Project-level outcome is its effect on customers who will benefit from modern and high-quality warehouses that will help support their business expansion and growth in Indonesia. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater competitiveness in Indonesia's warehousing sector by introducing new concept of modern warehouses catalyzing other developers to raise their standards and improving efficiency.
additionality: IFC will play a countercyclical role in providing and mobilizing long-term financing at the time when the local financial market is being affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The proposed financing will have a tenor of up to 10 years that is not currently available in the commercial bank market for such a Project. In addition, LOGOS is expected to leverage IFC's knowledge of business conditions in Indonesia and in the region as well as advice on green building certification.

company_name: COCAL COMERCIO INDUSTRIA CANAA ACUCAR E ALCOOL LTDA
project_description: The proposed investment consists of a senior loan of up to US$70 million composed by an A loan of up to US$40 million and a B loan of up to US$30 million, to support Grupo Cocal’s (“Cocal” or the “Group”) investment plan for the next two years. Cocal is a leading sugar, ethanol and renewable energy producer in Brazil, with two mills located in the Sao Paulo state. The investment will support (i) the construction of a biogas producing plant, (ii) sugarcane replanting and (iii) upgrades to increase operating and energy efficiency (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1980, the Group owns two mills with a combined installed capacity to crush up to 9 million tons of sugarcane per year while employing 4,900 people. Cocal is a member of the sugar and ethanol cooperative and trader, Copersucar, which commercializes 100% of its sugar and ethanol production. In addition, the Group sells energy directly to the grid. The Group is 100% owned by the Garms family since its foundation.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The investment plan is estimated in US$92 million, for which IFC will provide an A Loan of up to US$40 million and mobilize a B Loan of up to US$30 million. The remaining portion is expected to be financed through internal cash generation.
location_description: Investments will be made in the Presidente Prudente region, in the Sao Paulo state, in Brazil.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcomes are its positive environmental effects from increased ethanol and biogas production as well as renewable energy sales. The positive effects of the project on local economy and the environment are somewhat dampened by the effective subsidy on ethanol as compared to gasoline that implies an economic loss to consumers. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that the investment has the potential to improve the agricultural practices at the sector level and contribute to further strengthening its competitiveness.
additionality: Long-term financing in local currency: IFC will provide the Company with tenors currently very scarce in the current macroeconomic scenario. Mobilization: IFC's financing package also includes a B Loan. The B lender will be able to provide a longer tenor because of IFC's participation. IFC Standard Setting: IFC will support Cocal in aligning its E&S practices with best international practices.
Company Name: COCAL COMERCIO INDUSTRIA CANAA ACUCAR E ALCOOL LTDA

project_description: IFC’s proposed investment is a green loan of Thai Baht (“THB”) 4,500 million (equivalent of US$137 million) to Asset World Corp Public Company Limited (“AWC” or the “Company’). The IFC green loan, expected to be compliant with the International Capital Market Association (ICMA) Green Bond Principles, will be used toward energy efficiency measures in the refurbishment of four hotels, the greenfield development of two new hotels in key tourism destinations of Thailand including Bangkok, Hua Hin, Koh Samui and Chiang Mai and working capital to support the gradual re-opening of hotels following Covid-19-related shutdowns. AWC is the key real estate and hospitality arm of Thai Charoen Company (TCC) Group (the “Group”). AWC is the largest hospitality operator in Thailand by number of rooms and has a growing and diverse portfolio of assets in hospitality and lifestyle destinations, retail and commercial workspaces, with ten retail centers and four office buildings.
sponsor_shareholders: AWC is listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand and is a subsidiary of the Thai Charoen Company (TCC) Group (the “Group”), one of the largest conglomerates in Thailand. The Sponsors of TCC, Khun Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi and his wife Khunying Wanna Sirivadhanabhakdi founded the Group in 1976, its core business at the time in beverages, and what is now Thai Beverage PCL. The Group has since expanded into real estate, retail, insurance and agriculture, and has a large asset base and diversified interests in Thailand, Singapore and the Mekong region.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is estimated at US$282 million. IFC’s proposed investment to the Company consists of IFC A Loan of up to THB 4,500 million (equivalent of US$137 million), to be disbursed in THB.
location_description: The refurbishments and new construction activities comprising the Project will be located in key tourism hubs throughout Thailand including Bangkok, Hua Hin, Koh Samui and Chiang Mai.
development_impact: 1) Job Creation: In terms of local employment, IFC expects the Project to create several direct jobs for the two new hotels such as receptionists, cleaners, security, restaurant workers as well as the indirect jobs in the hotel's supply chain and related linkages such as taxi companies and tour guides. It is expected that [XX%] will be female employment. 2) Domestic suppliers: The Project will also include refurbishments of old hotels, improving the quality of buildings and service offerings, which is in line with the Thai Ministry of Sports and Tourism and the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT)'s objective of shifting Thailand's offering from "mass-market, quantity" to "high-value, quality". Local suppliers of goods and services will benefit from greater demand for higher volume and from demand for better quality products and services that allow for greater value added. Close to 100% of AWC suppliers are domestic. 3) Effect on employees: On average, 60 hours of training will be provided to a hotel employee. The training is given all staff, even hourly employees, and includes essential skill and knowledge areas such as culinary, rooms operation and purchasing, as well as other discipline-specific skills in finance, HR, IT, loss prevention, marketing and sales. In addition, most of the international hotel brands which AWC use are committed to developing people. Managerial staff participate in management training programs. . By upskilling its employees, AWC will contribute to the mobility of these employees who can progress to higher level jobs in the same company or move to other companies in the services sector. 4) Effect on sourcing: Thailand's hotel supply chain is made up of many small and medium size enterprises (SMEs) including small manufacturing companies and smallholder farmers linked to the hotel food and beverage and procurement value chain. AWC estimates that it procures around 30% from local SMEs including give examples. AWC has worked with local suppliers to improve the quality to meet the standards of the renown global hotel operators such as Marriott, Le Meridien, Hilton and Sheraton.
additionality: 1) Long-Term Financing: IFC's loan tenor of up to 7 years will be much longer than what the Company has obtained before (up to 3 years). IFC's financing will also be the first unsecured loan for the Company. IFC's longer tenor loan and unsecured nature of the loan will pave the way for longer tenor, unsecured loans and bonds in the coming years. 2) Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building: IFC will help AWC build internal capacity with regard to green building and obtain EDGE certification for at least 5 hotels (to be confirmed). This includes AWC staff trained on GB certification process and IFC Climate Business team helping with the IFC Toolkit on Disclosure and Transparency (IFCDT). 3) Insurance: IFC has made a number of recommendations to help AWC's insurance management and improve its insurance coverages. To this end, the Company has invited IFC's insurance specialist to make a presentation to the Operations Committee in order to ensure its coverage is comprehensive and competitive.

project_description: Blue Nile Rolling Mills Ltd. (“BNRM”, “ the Company”) is a locally-owned, leading steel manufacturer in Kenya. The Company will develop Kenya’s first galvanization iron (“GI”) wire manufacturing plant in Thika, Kenya, with a capacity of 26,580 metric tonnes per annum (the “Project”). GI wire is the raw material for the steel wire products that are currently growing in demand in Kenya and East Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Kotni Rama Shankar Rao (Vice Chairman and Managing Director of BNRM), Kotni Holdings (Mr. Rao's personal company), and his two sons hold a majority stake of BNRM, with the balance held by independent individuals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated project cost is US$14.1 million, of which IFC will be financing US$8.0 million via an A Loan.
location_description: The Project will be located in Thika, an industrial town in Kenya and where the Company currently resides.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes are: (i) employee skills and know-how development from the introduction of the first galvanized wire plant in Kenya, (ii) customer benefits via improved quality galvanized wire available at quicker supplier terms, and, (iii) economy-wide and employment effects with import substitution of imported galvanized wire, creation of 53 new direct jobs for the Project, and estimated creation of 310 indirect and induced jobs in the Company's value chain. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will have a strong effect on sector competitiveness and on the integration of the manufacturing sector in Kenya through the building of manufacturing capabilities and enhancing economic complexity.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing Structure - IFC is proposing a US Dollar financing for a tenor beyond what is generally available in the market at reasonable terms and critical to the capital-intensive nature of the steel sector. Non-Financial Additionality: Standard Setting - IFC will assist the Company to develop Environmental Health and Safety (EHS), and social practices in line with international standards. Furthermore, the Company has already engaged IFC for Corporate Governance Advisory.

project_description: Agrofertil is highly dependent on access to working capital facilities to finance the sale of inputs to farmers. Given the COVID-19 outbreak, there is a risk that local banks in Paraguay reduce their financing to the real sector by decreasing financing lines to remain liquid in a volatile context with potential increase of NPLs.
sponsor_shareholders: Agrofertil SA is a Paraguay based private company fully owned by the Sarabia family, whose members have more than 20 years of experience in the agribusiness sector in Paraguay .
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at $10 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of a one-year up to $10 million A Loan to allow the Company to advance inputs to its network of farmers.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Ciudad del Este, Paraguay. The Company has 20 regional distribution centers located near the major crop regions of Paraguay.
development_impact: By supporting its clients' capacity to sustain operations during this acute shock, IFC best positions the private sector to support the economic recovery process, shortening the time it will take for the most vulnerable to return to their traditional income-earning opportunities.
additionality: Through this project, IFC will be enhancing Agrofertil's capacity to provide pre-harvest financing to farmers and will contribute to the further development of agriculture sector, a key pillar of Paraguay's economy. Additionality of the RSE COVID facility is driven largely by rapid crisis response efforts including: (i) large scale investments and working capital solutions in emerging markets, (ii) ability to support real sector clients to address liquidity constraints in response to COVID-19, and (iii) provide critical supplies to help clients re-direct supply chains and its support to continued employment in countries of operation.

project_description: Ford Otomotiv Sanayi A.S. (“Otosan” or the “Company”) is a leading Turkish automotive manufacturer and exporter of commercial and passenger vehicles. The proposed IFC investment is up to EUR equivalent of US$150 million to partially fund Otosan’s capex program during the period of 2020-2024 including the launch of new commercial vehicle models, capacity expansion and other climate related investments such as (i) production of electric and hybrid cars; (ii) efficiency; and (iii) modernization and automation (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Currently, 18% of the Company's shares is publicly listed in Borsa Istanbul, while the remaining 82% is owned jointly by Koc Holding A.S. and Ford Deutschland Holding GmbH (wholly owned subsidiary of Ford Motor Company). Mainly engaged in five sectors namely, energy, automotive, consumer durables, and finance, Koc Holding is the leading industrial conglomerate of Turkey. Koc Holding is majority owned by the Koc family of Turkey and the remaining shares (c. 26%) of Koc Holding are publicly listed. Ford is a US based car manufacturer, engaged in manufacturing, marketing and maintenance of Ford and Lincoln branded cars.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is yet to be finalized based on the Company’s investment program. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to EUR equivalent of US$150 million.
location_description: The Project is located in Kocaeli, Turkey.
development_impact: The Project's expected development includes: (i) economywide and employment effects; (ii) skills/know-how development via increased technical jobs and skills development, and (iii) promotion of sector integration via product and process innovation and increasing manufacturing complexity.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality includes its counter-cyclical role through provision of long-term financing and diversification of the Company's funding base.

company_name: PROMOTORA DE VIVIENDAS INTEGRALES, S.A. DE C.V.
project_description: Founded in 2001, Vinte Viviendas Integrales, S.A.B. de C.V. (“Vinte” or the “Company”) is a listed homebuilder focused on low-to middle-income housing in Mexico. Vinte’s operations include land acquisition, urbanization, design and development planning, construction, and sale of homes. Vinte differentiates from other housing developers by offering functional and attractively designed homes, community infrastructure not easily available in this segment, and good location within or very close to urban centers. It has built more than 43,000 homes under an innovative housing model of living in communities. Vinte is one of few developers in Mexico that was able to grow even during economic downturns such as the 2008-2009 global crisis and the 2012-2013 Mexican housing crisis. Vinte is a holding company that consolidates six operating subsidiaries: (i) Promotora de Viviendas Integrales, S.A. de C.V. engaged in land purchase, development and commercialization; (ii) Urbanizaciones Inmobiliarias del Centro, S.A. de C.V. focused on architectonic and urban design, as well as on land purchase, development and commercialization; (iii) Edificaciones e Ingenieria del Centro, S.A. de C.V. engaged in urbanization and construction activities; (iv) Conectividad para el Habitat, S.A. de C.V. engaged in engaged in the distribution of computers, internet, and related services; (v) Vinte Administracion, Diseño y Consultoria, S.A. de C.V. focused on home sales; and (vi) Comercializadora de Equipamientos y Mobiliarios para la Vivienda, S.A. de C.V. engaged in the sale of home equipment such as floors, closets, furniture and solar panels. The purpose of the project is to alleviate Vinte’s cash needs for 2020-2021 to cope with expected home sales decline due to the COVID-19 crisis and enable Vinte to continue with the construction once the stay-at-home order is lifted (the “Project”). This Project will address a long-standing housing shortage in Mexico by providing good quality affordable housing in rapidly urbanizing areas of the country. ADDITIONAL INVESTMENT UNDER THE COVID-19 RESPONSE FACILITY: IFC has committed MXN 300 million to Vinte on June 29, 2021. The investment is in the form of a revolving A-loan to be funded and disbursed in Mexican Pesos for the purposes of supporting the Company to alleviate its long-term liquidity access for the next months should the economic recovery take longer than expected and to resume investments in new developments to capitalize on potential market opportunities. This follow-on investment will continue to address a long-standing housing gap in Mexico by providing good quality affordable housing. UPDATE RELATED TO ADDITIONAL INVESTMENT UNDER COVID-19 RESPONSE FACILITY: E&S Performance and COVID-19 related Impacts: - The company’s E&S performance was satisfactory at appraisal and was determined to be satisfactory following the last site supervision visit (SSV) in April 2019. This performance is aligned with good international industry practices (GIIP) and is materially compliant with the applicable at-approval requirements under the current active investment. This follow-on investment, under the COVID-19 response facility, does not result in any new material E&S risks. The company’s management of existing E&S risks and impacts as defined in the Environmental and Social Review Summary (ESRS) as disclosed for the existing investment on 07/14/2020 continues. - Vinte has made progress in completing several corrective actions as defined in the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP) in 2020, and completion is of all associated actions is expected by December 2021. Vinte has enhanced management of environmental programs by standardizing the approach across all developments and has strengthened and standardized its emergency response plan for developments. Since March of 2020, Vinte did not reduce its construction workforce as an investment to be able to return to operations as soon as the construction activity was declared essential, which happened in June 2020. The virtual appraisal completed by IFC did not identify any new material E&S risks and impacts due to COVID-19 that cannot mitigated under existing ESRS and ESAP. Scope of IFC’s Appraisal: - IFC’s E&S virtual appraisal included a review of latest information provided by Vinte associated with environmental health and safety (EHS) and human resource (HR) management practices including OHS based on a detailed E&S questionnaire as well as virtual meetings and interviews. Document review included, among others: updated EHS management programs and procedures, COVID-19 response plan and related information as provided in response to a questionnaire. The review also considered Vinte’s E&S performance since the previous virtual appraisal undertaken in July 2020. After COVID-19 related travel restrictions are lifted, IFC will visit the client, as part of the regular portfolio monitoring activities. Response to COVID-19 Pandemic: - Vinte undertook a risk assessment exercise of its operations to identify and implement measures to reduce risks associated with COVID-19, while also ensuring compliance with local requirements related to the pandemic. \ The company has focused its efforts on information campaigns and trainings to ensure employees are aware of the risks and measures to prevent infections aimed for both office and construction staff alike. There has been no retrenchments and the company does not expect such in the near future. Administrative staff have the option to work remotely and the company has developed new protocols and procedures to minimize risks of exposure to workers, such as: daily cleaning and disinfection, facility access protocols, wearing of personal protective equipment and social distancing. Management communicates on a regular basis with all its employees via the available internal channels (i.e. intranet, e-mail) and external channels. Vinte’s existing HR/OHS policies and measures as well as the COVID-19 specific measures ensure ongoing compliance with IFC. PS2: Labor and Working Conditions and PS4: Community Health Safety and Security. As a condition of this follow-on investment, Vinte will ensure ongoing compliance with IFC Performance Standards – especially provisions under PS2 and PS4.
sponsor_shareholders: Vinte is listed in Mexico’s Stock Exchange. The major shareholders are the Company’s founders (Mexican nationals): Sergio Leal (23.6%), Carlos Cadena (20.7%), Rene Mungarro (11.9%), Antonio Zuñiga (5.5%), and Jose Soto (3.7%). Vinte’s equity is also owned by institutional investors such as PROPARCO (6.9%), and IDB Invest (0.8%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$20 million corporate A Loan from IFC’s own account.
location_description: Mexico
development_impact: IFC will position Vinte to support the economic recovery process, shortening the time it will take for the most vulnerable to return to their traditional income-earning opportunities. Project level impact: - Stakeholder effects: By providing a $20m A loan IFC will alleviate Vinte's cash needs for the next 18 months should the COVID-19 crisis extend beyond 2020 while allowing the company to maintain its existing credit standing and keep its workforce as well as ready to continue with the construction once the stay-at-home order is lifted. The project outcome will be realized through the effects on employees of Vinte who will stay on the Company's payroll, the effects on suppliers through continued demand once construction can resume, and the effects on customers as more housing supplies a high-quality developer like Vinte will be available, narrowing the supply-demand gap and generating equity value to homeowners. - Economy-wide effects: This Project will create over 1,400 direct jobs both during construction and operation of the housing communities. The Project will increase demand for construction and building materials in Mexico. Once construction is completed, housing units will stimulate the use of local supplies of goods and services, supporting maintenance, retailing and wholesaling operations. Contribution to Market Creation: - Resilience: The Project will contribute to the resilience by limiting disruptions along supply chains and ensuring continued supply of goods and services in the sectors affected by reduced demand, price reductions and FX volatility thereby mitigating the effects of the economic downturn. - Competitiveness: The first implementation of ASHA and READ tools will contribute to more socially sustainable housing projects in Mexico and LAC through demonstration and replication, as well as contribute to more competitive market by reducing the information asymmetry between home developers and banks on the sustainability and value of homes.
additionality: - Financing Structure: IFC's additionality is driven largely by our countercyclical role during crises. IFC will support a long-term client by providing working capital to continue employment during the downturn. At the time when customers' ability to pay are constrained and there are disruptions in operations due to COVID-19, IFC will provide corporate loan with four to five years tenor that is currently not available to local homebuilding companies in Mexico. - Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: Through IFC's "Affordable and Socially Sustainable Housing Application" (ASHA), and the "Real Estate Assessment of Developers" (READ) advisory tools, IFC will help Vinte to (i) evaluate and measure the social impact of its developments; and (ii) communicate to the investment community, in particular high-impact funds outside of Mexico, the social impact on communities in an objective manner, to potentially bring-in additional capital.
Company Name: PROMOTORA DE VIVIENDAS INTEGRALES, S.A. DE C.V.

sector: Fruit and Vegetable Preservation or Processing (Canning, Freezing, Drying, Jams, etc.)
project_description: Founded in 2012, Apeel Sciences is a Santa Barbara, California-based company that has developed a plant-derived coating that helps fresh produce growers, suppliers, and retailers maintain produce quality and extend shelf life, which minimize food waste across the produce value chain.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded by James Rogers, PhD (currently serves as CEO), with support from his co-founders: Jenny Du, PhD (currently serves as VP of Operations) and Louis Perez (currently serves as VP of Technology). Existing investors include GIC, Viking Global, Upfront Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, and Tao Capital.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to provide an equity investment of up to $15M in the Company.
location_description: Apeel Sciences is headquartered in California, US with operations in Mexico, Spain, Peru and The Netherlands. Apeel is working with IFC’s Advisory Service team to focus on expanding its supply customers not only in Mexico and Peru, but also in additional emerging markets including South Africa, Kenya, Vietnam, Costa Rica, Chile and Uganda.
development_impact: IFC anticipates that the Project would result in increased exports of fruits and vegetables and GHG emission avoidance, achieved by deploying at scale an edible plant-derived coating that extends the shelf-life of fruits and vegetables, thereby reducing food losses. Furthermore, the Project has the potential to strengthen the integration of local suppliers, especially from Mexico, into the international, and potentially local, fruits and vegetables value chains.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this project is primarily non-financial and consists of providing knowledge, innovation and capacity building, including through the development of a comprehensive Advisory Service project alongside the proposed investment. While recognizing the strength of the company and its investors, IFC's patient capital can act to incentivize the Company to enter emerging markets where the availability of venture capital is limited.

sector: Man-Made Fibers (Including Nylon, Polyester, Rayon, etc.)
project_description: Unimetco Holding (“Unimetco” or the “Company”), a Lebanese incorporated holding company, is the largest independent manufacturer and system house for polyurethane and adhesives used in construction, footwear, appliances and furniture sectors in Middle East and North Africa region. The Company operates manufacturing facilities in the UAE, Egypt and Italy and distribution centers in Turkey, Algeria, and Jordan. Unimetco is undertaking an investment plan to expand and establish i) polyester reactors and rigid capacity in Egypt and UAE, ii) system houses in Algeria and Nigeria, and iii) a packaging adhesives plant in Turkey. This investment plan, along with the associated permanent working capital requirement, constitutes the “Project”.
sponsor_shareholders: Unimetco is a joint stock company where shares are 100% owned by Dr. Ihsan Baalbaki collectively with his wife and three sons. Unimetco is the chemicals arm of the Baalbaki Group (the “Group”), a multi-sector Lebanon based business group with diversified operations in manufacturing (machinery and chemicals), real estate and financial services located across Middle East, Africa, Central Asia and Europe.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost to implement the Project is estimated at US$40 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to US$25m A loan for IFC’s own account to finance Unimetco’s expansions in Egypt, Algeria, Nigeria, and Turkey, in addition to the financing of the Company’s permanent working capital needs.
location_description: The expansion projects will be located in Egypt, Algeria, Nigeria, and Turkey.
development_impact: 1- Employment Creation: The Project is estimated to create 120 direct jobs Emerging Markets. Furthermore, over 4,000 indirect and induced jobs along the value chain are expected to be created. 2- Value Chain Creation: Unimetco intends to source its raw materials locally / regionally based on availability. Increasing import substitution is expected to boost local production in appliances, adhesives and footwear sectors. 3- SME Creation: The expansion plan is expected to contribute to SMEs' growth under transportation, logistics and other services. 4- Climate Change Impact: The Project will mitigate climate impact through (i) use of PET scrap in its production, and (ii) production of insulation products promoting overall energy efficiency. 5- Fiscal Benefits: The Project will lead to positive fiscal impacts on host countries through taxes paid and support in foreign trade balance from decreased imports and increased exports.
additionality: 1- Long-term Financing: Cross-border financing with comparable terms to the proposed IFC loan is not readily available in the region. IFC's loan will enable the Company to proceed timely with its expansion and to remain financially sustainable. 2- Political Risk Mitigation: Given the Group's limited exposure to Turkey, Algeria and Nigeria, IFC's support can help mitigate potential political risks associated with entering new countries. The Company may also explore political risk insurance with MIGA for the riskier markets. 3- Long-term Partnership: The engagement is viewed as the beginning of a potential long-term strategic partnership between IFC and the Company and collaboration in future projects and markets across the Middle East, Africa and Europe. 4- Environmental and Social (E&S) Performance: IFC's E&S expertise will ensure that the Company's operations and expansions are based on the highest relevant E&S standards. 5- Climate Change: The Group expressed interest in collaborating with IFC to support their SME clients in phasing out 141B blowing agents (reaction that depletes the ozone layer) from their facilities in line with the Montreal Protocol. These SME's are not eligible to obtain commercial financing and require around US$200-400k of credit lines to undertake this investment.

project_description: JV LLC “Nyva Pereyaslavshchyny” (Nyva or the Company), based in Ukraine, is a vertically integrated pork producer with crop cultivation and processing, pig farming, slaughtering and meat processing operations. The Company is the second largest market player in the Ukrainian industrial pork market. The proposed investment is part of the IFC’s COVID-19 response Real Sector Crisis Envelope and consists of a senior secured A loan of up to US$20 million (the “IFC Loan”). Due to COVID-19-related uncertainties in the supply chain of raw materials, Nyva is significantly increasing its raw material inventory in order to avoid any production disruptions. The IFC Loan will be used to fund the Company’s working capital needs.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Oleksandr Mostipan is the founder and the controlling shareholder of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The IFC A loan of up to US$20 million will be used to fund the Company’s working capital needs.
location_description: The project is located in a rural area of the Kyiv region in Ukraine.
development_impact: The Project has an AIMM rating of Good, based on an AIMM score of 53. Project Outcomes: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is contribution to the domestic food security and better consumer outcomes by increasing production of safely produced meat. Contribution to Market Creation: The Project will promote sector resilience by limiting disruptions along the pork supply chain.
additionality: IFC’s key additionality to the Project is providing critical financial support in a time of COVID-19 crisis when other sources of liquidity have dried up.

project_description: IFC is providing support to a number of MCS businesses that have been negatively impacted by the Covid-19 pandemic and associated economic disruption. This includes funds for (i) recapitalizing MCS’ hospital subsidiary Intermed, (ii) working capital and liquidity support to MCS’ property and construction businesses, (iii) long term strategic digital investments and (iv) maintenance capital expenditure in MCS’ fast moving consumer goods (FMCG) and information and communication technology (ICT) subsidiaries. Once complete, the IFC financing will enable MCS to restructure its financial liabilities so that the average maturity of its debt repayments will be significantly extended.
sponsor_shareholders: MCS Group is one of the largest diversified business groups in Mongolia operating in (i) packaging and distribution of Coca-Cola products; (ii) distribution of non-food fast-moving consumer goods, including Procter and Gamble products and food products from international brands such as Nestle and Pringles; (iii) mobile telecommunications; (iv) civil engineering; (v) healthcare, (vi) information technologies, and (vii) real estate development. MCS also owns a 31% share in Mongolian Mining Corporation which is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. MCS was founded in 1993 by two brothers, Mr Odjargal Jambaljamts and Mr Od Jambaljamts. The founders own 84% of the company, and the remaining shares are owned by existing and former senior management. MCS Group has been a client of IFC since 2008.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to US$130 million to the MCS Group of companies to provide additional liquidity to sustain operations and allow the group to maintain its investment program through the CV-19 crisis period.
location_description: Various locations across Mongolia.
development_impact: The Covid-19 pandemic and the various quarantine restrictions imposed by the government (including restricting border access, limiting mineral exports which are key to Mongolia's export earnings) has negatively impacted several of MCS' business lines. These include (i) a drop in patient volumes at Intermed Hospital (ii) reduction in consumer spending impacting the FMCG divisions (iii) rental payment deferral requests from tenants at the group's commercial and residential properties; and (iv) suspension or postponement of some construction projects due to curfews, travel/border restrictions. The proposed loan will support MCS's capacity to sustain operations and employment during the downturn and expedite post-crisis recovery. In addition, the loan will have a positive effect on (i) employees of the highly affected businesses; and (ii) customers (tenants) through deferring payments, rent relief, and improving working capital terms. All IFC projects that are designed to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic share the same development thesis: By supporting its clients' capacity to sustain operations during this acute shock, IFC best positions the private sector to support the economic recovery process, shortening the time it will take for the most vulnerable to return to their traditional income-earning opportunities.
additionality: IFC's Additionality includes: (i) Countercyclical investment, which will enable the provision of critical goods and supplies when investors are lacking confidence and customers' ability to pay is constrained; and (ii) long-term financing which is unavailable in Mongolia to help MCS support businesses that are highly vulnerable as a result of the pandemic.

project_description: John Keells Holdings PLC (JKH) is one of the largest listed companies on the Colombo Stock Exchange, with business interests primarily in Transportation, Consumer Foods, Retail, Leisure, Property and Financial Services. JKH was incorporated as a public limited liability company in 1979 and obtained a listing on the Colombo Stock Exchange in 1986. Having issued Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) which were listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange, JKH became the first Sri Lankan company to be listed overseas. JKH is a full member of the World Economic Forum and a Participant member of the UN Global Compact. The Holding Company of the Group, John Keells Holdings PLC, is based at Colombo and has offices and businesses located across Sri Lanka and the Maldives. The Project, which is sponsored by JKH, consists of (i) the expansion of its supermarket chain, (ii) the completion//refurbishment/expansion of hotel properties in Sri Lanka and the Maldives, and (iii) general corporate uses associated with JKH’s retail and leisure businesses.
sponsor_shareholders: JKH has over 70 subsidiaries of which eight subsidiaries, namely Asian Hotels and Properties PLC, Ceylon Cold Stores PLC, Keells Food Products PLC, John Keells PLC, John Keells Hotels PLC, Tea Smallholder Factories PLC (management control), Trans Asia Hotels PLC and Union Assurance PLC, are also listed on the Colombo stock exchange. JKH has a broad shareholding, of which 99.2 % is free float.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a debt financing package of up to US$175 million to JKH and consists of (i) an A loan of up to US$125 million for IFC’s account; and (ii) a Trust Loan of up to US$50 million from IFC acting in its capacity as the implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program.
location_description: JKH is headquartered in Colombo. The Project involves capital expenditures associated with (i) new retail stores throughout Sri Lanka, (ii) completion and refurbishment of hotels in Sri Lanka and the Maldives, and (iii) expansion on an asset light model in leisure opportunities in Sri Lanka and Maldives.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is the economy-wide effects from direct and indirect job creation as well as skill development training programs the Company provides to its employees, farmers and other suppliers. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater competitiveness by expanding modern retail in Sri Lanka especially in secondary provinces, which will stimulate increased competition, improved labor force, and better industry practices.
additionality: IFC will provide long-term financing that will allow the Company to complete the expansion plan with a tenor that is not easily available in the market. IFC will play a key role in mobilizing additional financing to help the Company complete its expansion plan. In addition, IFC will play a countercyclical role in improving investor confidence by sending a positive signal to the market overall and help the Company to continue to grow in this difficult economic environment.

project_description: IFC is seeking to make an equity co-investment of up to US$15 million in Reve alongside Australis Partners. Reve Group is a leading Latin American retail and consumer foodservice company operating in Colombia, Panama and Chile. Proceeds will be used to fund working capital requirements of Reve’s operations and its continued expansion during 2020 and part of 2021
sponsor_shareholders: Reve Group is engaged in the retail and consumer foodservice segments in Colombia, Panama and Chile and employs over 13,200 people. Reve’s main shareholders include (a) financial investors: private equity funds Altra Investments and Australis Partners, and IFC through a co-investment with Australis Partners, and (b) founding shareholders, such as Michel Olmi, a Chilean national, who also serves as Chairman and CEO of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Company is seeking to raise approximately US$35 million. IFC is proposing to participate with an equity co-investment of up to US$15.0 million from IFC’s own account.
location_description: Colombia
development_impact: IFC's Real Sector COVID-19 Facility is intended to promote the resilience of real sector markets, by ensuring continued supply of goods and services at affordable prices and limiting disruptions along supply chains thereby mitigating the effects of the economic downturn. All IFC projects under the COVID-19 Facility share the same development thesis: By supporting its clients' capacity to sustain operations during this acute shock, IFC best positions the private sector to support the economic recovery process, shortening the time it will take for the most vulnerable to return to their traditional income-earning opportunities. The Project will strengthen the Reve Group ability to meet surging demand of low-priced essential goods, to ensure continued access to supply, and to resume expansion when the situation improves.
additionality: IFC's additionality is driven largely by our countercyclical role during crises. The IFC's Real Sector COVID-19 Facility component contributes successful experience with rapid crisis response efforts, its set of programs aimed at investing both large scale and transactional liquidity and capital for trade finance and working capital in emerging markets, its ability to support real sector clients to address liquidity constraints in response to COVID-19 and to provide critical goods, equipment and supplies, its ability to help clients re-direct supply chains and its support to continued employment in countries of operation. IFC's financing will be used to fund working capital requirements of Reve Group, and continuing its expansion plans during 2020 and part of 2021.

project_description: Shangri-La Asia Limited (“SLA” or the “Sponsor”) is a leading owner and operator of hotels and resorts in Asia. SLA and its subsidiaries (together the “Group”) own and/or manage 101 hotels in over 20 countries. Tourism is one of the hardest hit sectors by the COVID-19 pandemic, and there have been severe business disruptions to the operations of the Group’s hotel properties as a result. The proposed investment will be to Shangri-La Asia Treasury Limited (“SLT” or the “Company”), in order to support the Group’s existing operations in Fiji, Maldives, Mongolia and Sri Lanka during this challenging time (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a wholly-owned subsidiary of SLA which is responsible for the treasury operation of SLA and its subsidiaries. SLA is a public company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project’s cost is estimated to be in excess of US$150 million, and IFC is considering the provision of an A loan of up to US$145 million to support the Project.
location_description: The Project includes the Group’s hotels and resorts located in Fiji, Maldives, Mongolia and Sri Lanka.
development_impact: At the Project level, the Project is expected to: (i) sustain the relevant project companies' ability to maintain employment of staff; and (ii) sustain demand for goods and services from the relevant project companies' suppliers so that the project companies and their suppliers could maintain their operations in the current situation. At the Market level, the Project is expected to: (i) promote the resilience of tourism sector by preserving the availability and quality of goods and services provided by a large regional player; and (ii) preserve the sector's ability to support the economic recovery effort as conditions normalize.
additionality: IFC's Additionality includes: (i) long-term financing which is not readily available, especially in the current environment where other investors' appetite is significantly weakened amid a volatile market; and (ii) standard-setting with regard to implementation of E&S management systems.

project_description: SeeTree Systems Limited (“SeeTree”, or “Company”) is an Israel based high-tech company that provides analytics services to growers of permanent crops. The Company was founded in 2017 and is headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel with customers currently across California (USA), Brazil and South Africa, and pilots in Argentina and Indonesia. The proposed investment will support the Company’s expansion plans.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded by Israel Talpaz (currently serves as CEO), Barak Hachamov (currently serves as Chairman) and Guy Morgenstern (currently serves as CTO). Existing investors include Canaan Partners Israel, The Founder’s Kitchen, Hanaco Ventures and iAngels Technologies LP.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to provide an equity investment of up to US$8mm in the company.
location_description: SeeTree is headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel with operations across California, Brazil, South Africa
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level Outcomes are derived from improved productivity of permanent crops in SeeTree's markets of operations such as Brazil, USA, Argentina, Indonesia etc achieved by deploying at scale AI technologies that measure the health of individual trees, thereby significantly increasing the percentage of healthy trees. Maintaining healthy trees is critical for productivity growth in the permanent crop sector. New technologies like AI can help improve productivity through automated analysis of large-scale permanent crop farms to measure the health of each tree individually, allow growers to understand the productivity of their trees and other parameters like expected fruit size and correlated these factors to farming practice. Potential productivity improvement can result in higher income as the outcomes of the data analytics allows growers to prepare the right marketing strategy based on size and volume of products. From this investment, the main sources of expected Market Creation outcomes are derived from the potential to maintain the competitiveness of the permanent crop sector, which is generally developed, by stimulating further adoption of precision agriculture technologies via demonstration and replication channels. The Company's technology also has the potential to trigger market changes such as the development of the spoke-and-hub farming model if implemented in lower-middle or low-income countries. It may also increase the traceability of fruits, particularly to deal with issues of rejections when crossing borders.
additionality: IFC's Additionally in this project is both financial and non-financial. Financial Additionality consists of the provision of patient capital. Non-financial Additionality comes in the form of knowledge, innovation and capacity building, through the introduction of agribusiness companies to the Company for partnership. Financial Additionality: - Own Account Equity: IFC will invest US$8 million in SeeTree's equity fundraise. Despite a relatively high availability of venture capital in the countries where SeeTree currently operates and intends to expand into, there is limited availability of patient capital available to companies working on precision agricultural technologies. A patient investor such as the IFC will enable the Company to take a long-term approach to scale up and reach a larger number of growers. - Assisting with key industry relationships: The Company will benefit from access to IFC's deep relationships in the VC market when it pursues future funding rounds. Non-Financial Additionality - Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: As the Company expands into a variety of permanent crops, IFC can help the Company leverage IFC relationships and investments in the agribusiness sector across all emerging markets and can share knowledge and lessons learned. - Best practices: IFC will support the Company in implementing best practices in corporate governance and environmental and social management.

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: The EUR 50 million investment program during 2019-2021 targets to; i) to increase existing production capacities in Tunisia and Morocco and invest in more sophisticated technology, processes and machinery to manufacture higher value added products; and ii) cater to increasing presence of Original Equipment Manufacturers in Morocco and Tunisia as a result of shifting automotive production from Europe to these countries;
sponsor_shareholders: One Tech Holding (“OTH” or the “Company”), headquartered in Tunisia and majority owned by Sellami family, is the major provider of custom solutions for industrial cables (“IC”), mechatronics and telecom in the MENA region, catering to predominantly international customers across different industries including automotive, industrial machinery, power and construction sectors. With 7 production sites, the Company’s sites span over Tunisia and Morocco
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: ~Euro 50 million
location_description: Tangier (Morocco) and Bizerte and Grombalia (Tunisia)
development_impact: Employment creation: OTH will be protecting over 4,500 its existing jobs and will increase permanent employment within its expansion plans by 2022. Moreover, OTH has a formal training center for its employees. As OTH is enhancing technological content of its products, it will engage more university graduates, which is in line with the WBG strategy for Tunisia. In some functions, women represent a significant majority of employees, and created impact on women's employment and training is in line with the WB gender strategy. Enhancing competitiveness of a key export player: the Project will support a medium size company set up a platform to undertake future expansion, thereby improving its competitiveness. The Project will help OTH integrate upstream, which will boost its exports with downstream impact on the value chain. Technology Transfer: the acquisition will allow transfer of know-how and skills and benefit operations by integrating new processes. Contribution to economic growth: export forex earning will help to boost manufacturing sector development in the Maghreb region.
additionality: Long-term financing : Cross-boarder financing required for expansion in Morocco and acquisition in Europe is not readily available for a Tunisian company. The IFC loan will enable the Company to proceed timely with its expansion and to remain financially stable. Environmental and social (E&S) performance: IFC will continue working with the Company to ensure adherence to the IFC performance standards and strengthening its environmental management systems, consider engagement with advisory services (eg, energy efficiency) IFC will continue efforts towards implementing good corporate governance practices in historically family-run company. IFC will support the Company's expansion abroad and its aim to vertically integrate and move higher in the value chain, through an acquisition of an R&D platform.

project_description: JK Paper Limited (“JKPL” or the “Company”) is a leading Indian producer of office papers, packaging boards, printing and writing papers, and specialty papers, and is publicly listed on both the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India. In 2018, IFC disbursed US$44.7 million in the form of an INR denominated A loan to the Company to help improve its productivity and refinance its existing debt. The proposed IFC investment would fund (i) the incremental working capital needs due to the impact of COVID-19; and (ii) any potential shortfall in cash flow generation for planned and future capital expenditures (together, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a part of the JK Organisation group of companies that is run by the Singhania family of India (the Sponsors or the Promoter Group). The Singhania family has a legacy of over 130 years and runs the well-respected JK Organisation which was established in 1888. The Promoter Group together own 48.9% of the Company, while the public own 51.1%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The incremental working capital needs and shortfall in cash flow generation to fund planned and future capital expenditures are expected to aggregate to approximately US$35 million, which would be financed by the IFC investment. The IFC investment is in the form of secured non-convertible debentures (“NCDs”) of up to INR2.6 billion (US$35 million equivalent).
location_description: The Project locations are at the Company's two plants: (i) JK Paper Mills, also called Unit JKPM and located at P.O. Jaykaypur, 765 017, Rayagada, Odisha, and (ii) Central Pulp Mills, also called Unit CPM and located at P.O. Central Pulp Mills, 394 660, Fort Songadh, District Tapi, Gujarat.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project level outcome is stakeholder effects (employees and customers) Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that its financing will promote greater market resilience via market enabling channels.
additionality: IFC's additionality is driven largely by our countercyclical role during crises. The Real Sector Crisis Envelope component contributes successful experience with rapid crisis response efforts, its set of programs aimed at investing both large scale and transactional liquidity and capital for trade finance and working capital in emerging markets, its ability to support real sector clients to address liquidity constraints in response to COVID 19 and to provide critical goods, equipment and supplies, its ability to help clients re direct supply chains and its support to continued employment in countries of operation.

project_description: The group of companies known as PRAN Group (“PRAN” or the “Group”) was established in 1981 and is the leading branded food and beverage group and the largest agro-processor in Bangladesh. The Group is a well-known household brand in Bangladesh, and produces more than 400 food products in at least 10 major categories including juices and drinks, snacks, dairy, spices, confectionary and frozen foods. PRAN exports to 134 countries around the world. The project is to support long-term working capital financing as well as financing of additional capital expenditures for wafer and aseptic lines, as well as maintenance capital expenditures at PRAN entity Mymensingh Agro Limited (“MAL” or the “Company”) for a total project cost of approximately US$56.8 million (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsors and shareholders of the Project companies consist of the family members of the late PRAN Group founder Major General Amjad Khan Chowdhury, including his wife Ms. Sabiha Amjad, his son Mr. Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, and his daughter Ms. Uzma Chowdhury (collectively, the Sponsors).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is expected to be approximately US$56.8 million. IFC proposes to provide debt financing comprising of an A Loan of US$25 million to MAL.
location_description: Malgaon, Kailgonj, Gazipur, Bangladesh.
development_impact: By supporting MAL's capacity to sustain operations during this COVID pandemic, IFC helps position the private sector to support the economic recovery process, shortening the time it will take for the most vulnerable to return to their traditional income-earning opportunities. The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is helping the Company maintain its operations thus preserving employment levels and economic activity throughout the value chain, especially through sourcing relationships with local farmers. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that contribution to market creation will be through enhancing the sector's resilience to withstand the impacts of the crisis.
additionality: Financing Structure: PRAN values IFC's ability to provide longer term working capital funding of six years (including two years of grace period), which is essential to support the Project, as only short term lines are available for working capital loans from local banks. For a working capital-intensive business such as PRAN, this is a strong additionality. Standard setting: IFC will continue supporting PRAN in enhancing its Environmental and Social practices. With regard to MAL operations in particular, the key new elements of the ESAP accompanying this Project focus on improving the Occupational Health and Safety standards, implementing steps to prevent sexual harassment, and putting into place measures to reduce water consumption.

company_name: ENGEE PET MANUFACTURING COMPANY NIGERIA LIMITED
project_description: Engee PET Manufacturing Company Nigeria Limited (“Engee” or “the Company”) seeks IFC’s financing for the construction of a Continuous Polymerization (“CP”) plant in Ogun State, Nigeria, with a nameplate capacity of 150,000 metric tons per annuum (mtpa) as backward integration to an existing Solid State Polymerization (“SSP”) plant (the “Project”). The addition of the CP plant will enable the Company to backward integrate by manufacturing PET using basic petrochemicals which will increase manufacturing value addition in Nigeria. The CP line will also deepen the circular economy in Nigeria through the production of recycled PET (rPET) to improve the recovery of waste plastics in the country. The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA Private Sector Window (PSW) Blended Finance Facility (BFF).
sponsor_shareholders: The borrower Engee was incorporated in 2014 with major shareholders being Dellano Holdings Limited (99%) and Jotna Nigeria Limited (1%) which is consequently 100% owned by a non-operating holding company, Jotna International Investments Limited (“Jotna Group” and the “Sponsor”), whose ultimate beneficiary is Mr. Mahinder Naraindas Vaswani (100%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is estimated to have a total cost of approximately US$74 million. The proposed IFC investment includes up to US$24 million A Loan for IFC’s own account. IFC’s own account financing represents 19% of the total investment cost including the existing SSP line.
location_description: The Project will be set up at the Company’s existing manufacturing site in Igbesa Village, Ogun State, Nigeria.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are: (i) economywide effects via local production and the development of the recycled plastics supply chain in Nigeria, and (ii) environmental effects through introducing recycled plastics into its business model. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its engagement with the Company will significantly deepen the recycled PET business in Nigeria, thereby increasing product and process complexity in the manufacturing sector in Nigeria with opportunities to further integrate into other value chains.
additionality: Financial Additionality: Financing Structure: To support the Project, IFC is proposing an 8-year loan, including a 3-year grace period to allow sufficient time for ramp up after a significant expansion. Non-Financial Additionality: Standard-Setting: Through the Project, the Company will benefit from IFC's expertise on EH&S best practices as well as introduce international best practice standards to the client as it implements its plastics recycling program in Nigeria. Knowledge Innovation and Capacity Building: IFC will also provide Engee with Advisory Services support to implement a plastics waste recycling programme specifically for bottle-grade PET supply chain development. The Advisory Services is planned under the MAS Global Climate Platform, a multi-client project with close coordination with the Company.
Company Name: ENGEE PET MANUFACTURING COMPANY NIGERIA LIMITED

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a EUR10 million senior loan to Boudjebel S.A. VACPA, a Tunisian date processor and exporter in Tunisia (“VACPA” or the “Company”) to be committed in two tranches. IFC’s first tranche will finance much needed working capital to support Company’s operations during the COVID-19 crisis and the second tranche will be used to (i) establish a production unit for date juice concentrate and (ii) upgrade its existing processing unit and (iii) upgrade supply chain improvement program (PASA), (the “Project”). Founded in 1983 by Mr. Mohsen Boujbel (the “Sponsor”), VACPA processes the collection, packaging and export of organic and conventional dates. VACPA is the largest date exporter in Tunisia, with 10% market share in volume and 12% market share in total value as of FY19. With over 1,600 employees and an access over 1,000 farmers, the Company serves c.100 clients globally across N. America, Western and Central Europe and South-East Asia. VACPA has been the first Tunisian agribusiness company to be certified ISO 9001 (Quality Management) in 1998 and also holds several international certifications in food and environment safety including IFS, BRC, ISO 22000 (Food Safety Management), ISO 14001 (Environmental Management) and Global GAP.
sponsor_shareholders: Company is 100% owned by Boujbel Family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC financing amounts to EUR10 million. Within the scope of the Project, IFC’s financing will be directly used to support VACPA’s capital expenditures and working capital needs in Tunisia.
location_description: The Project is located in Beni Khalled, Nabeul Governorate, as well as Kebili and Tozeur regions in Tunisia.
development_impact: The project has an AIMM rating of Good. The most significant, expected project-level outcome is reduction in the volume of water used to irrigate a hectare of date palms and an increase in the number of smallholder farmers that receive offtake contracts, pre-harvest financing, and training. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates its investment will increase integration in the date-based supply chain in the Middle East and North Africa, via demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in two forms: i) financing structure through funding not readily available in Tunisia; and ii) potentially, knowledge, innovation and capacity building through advisory services.

project_description: The project is to finance the development of cotton farm clusters covering a total area of approximately 50,000 hectares in two regions of Uzbekistan and engaging with local farmers through contract farming, in approximately 22,000 hectares (the “Project”) by FE “Indorama Agro” LLC (the “Company”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Indorama Group (“Indorama” or the “Sponsor”). The Company will introduce to the country modern technologies of cotton production and supply the Sponsor’s local textile plant, FE “Indorama Kokand Textile” JSC, with a stable amount of machine picked cotton fibre for its raw materials. The Project will address some of the country’s systemic developmental challenges by eliminating the use of forced labor in Indorama’s local value chain and significantly increase production efficiency at Project farms, thus enhancing the sustainability of Uzbekistan’s cotton sector. The Project will also allow Indorama to strengthen its cotton supply chain in Uzbekistan through backward integration into cotton production, therefore addressing the risks of cotton availability, quality and supply chain reputational risk.
sponsor_shareholders: Indorama Holdings B.V. currently owns 100% of the Company. Indorama Holdings B.V. is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Indorama Corporation Pte. Ltd., domiciled in Singapore (“IRC”). IRC is the holding company of Indorama Group, one of Asia’s leading industrial conglomerates with wide interests in petrochemicals, fertilizers and related downstream businesses. IRC is wholly-owned for the benefit of Mr. S.P. Lohia and his family. Indorama Group was established in 1975 in Indonesia. It is the West Africa’s largest producer of petrochemicals, including olefins, polyolefins, phosphoric acid, phosphate fertilizers, ammonia, and urea, and one of the world’s largest producers of synthetic disposable gloves. Together with its associate, Indorama Ventures Public Company Limited, domiciled in Thailand, Indorama Group is the world’s largest producer of polyester and the leading producer of polyester feedstock (PX, PTA, and MEG) and man-made fibres. Its manufacturing activities are spread across 136 sites in 37 countries with a total manufacturing capacity of almost 24.5 million tons a year and annual sales value of over US$15 billion.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$285 million, including US$185 million in capital expenditures and US$60-100 million in working capital. The proposed IFC investment is a US$60 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project farmland is located in Qashqadaryo and Sirdaryo regions of Uzbekistan.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have a positive development impact, contributing to market creation and generating economy-wide and employment effects. The Project will ensure transitioning to mechanized harvesting that would both increase efficiencies and eliminate the risk of forced labor. The Project will also source cotton from local contract-farmers, helping them integrate into a modernized value chain on commercial terms and reduce off-take uncertainties on both sides. The Project's ginning and warehousing operations will contribute to reducing post-harvest losses and facilitating domestic value addition in the context of broader sector reform and create estimated 700 non-farm new jobs. In addition, the Project will create 1,000 farm jobs.
additionality: Financial additionality: Through the Project, IFC will provide an amount and tenor that is otherwise not available in Uzbekistan from private financing sources. Non-financial additionality: (i) IFC's involvement in the Project is expected to contribute to the development of the Company's environmental, health and safety practices, in line with the World Bank Group requirements; and (ii) with the assistance of the IFC Advisory Project, Indorama will demonstrate the viability of Uzbek cotton production within a sustainable supply chain, cleared of any forced labor.

project_description: The proposed investment is to support JSC “Concern Galnaftogaz” (“GNG” or the “Company”), an independent distributor of transportation fuels based in western Ukraine, by providing a long-term corporate loan to finance the Company’s 2020-2022 capex and working capital needs (the “Project”). GNG is Ukraine’s largest company in retail distribution of transportation fuels in terms of sales volume and third largest by number of filling stations. As of December 2019, the Company owned and operated 357 OKKO-branded filling stations. In 2019, GNG sold 849 thousand tons of petroleum products (incl. LPG) in the retail segment, generating total EBITDA of US$151 million on US$1.6 billion of revenues. The Project includes the following components: (i) working capital to develop GNG’s Farmer-Supply Program (FSP) and other agricultural related permanent working capital, (ii) improvements in GNGs logistics infrastructure; and (iii) growth and improvement capex fuel stations network, including the installation of electric charging stations.
sponsor_shareholders: GNG Retail Public Limited is the holding company of GNG and owns about 90% of shares of the Company. Mr. Vitaliy Antonov, a reputable Ukrainian businessman, is the founder and the ultimate beneficiary of the group. European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (“EBRD”) owns a minority stake in GNG Retail Public Limited.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$135 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$35 million equivalent A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Lviv, Ukraine. Its network of stations is nationwide.
development_impact: The Project-level impact of the new investment is expected to have economy-wide effects by generating jobs and economic linkages to other sectors. In addition, it will also have stakeholder effects by providing better access to finance for end customers (farmers). At the market level, the project has the potential to promote competitiveness as the Company can have a strong demonstration effect in the market for other competitors to replicate its high efficiency operations.
additionality: Financial additionality: (i) a loan with a grace period and tenor not readily available in the local market; and (ii) mobilization. Non-financial additionality: (i) E&S Standard Setting: IFC will help to improve further the E&S Risk Management systems; (ii) IFC Crop Receipts Program: IFC will support the implementation of the IFC's advisory Crop Receipts program by a private sector IFC client.

company_name: CARRIERES ET CHAUX DU MALI SA
project_description: The proposed project is an investment of up to €8.92 million equivalent in XOF in the form of a 9-year senior loan to Carriere et Chaux du Mali SA (“CCM” or the “Company”), aiming at supporting CCM’s permanent working capital needs and critical new equipment upgrades to ramp up capacity utilization. CCM is the first modern and large-scale lime and limestone producer in Mali providing an alternative to lime products imported mainly from Europe, for mining and agricultural markets. The project includes support from the International Development Association’s Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA-PSW LCF) and Blended Finance Facility (IDA-PSW BFF) as described below.
sponsor_shareholders: Dr Madani Diallo is the main shareholder with 30.2% of CCM’s shares. A Malian national, Dr Diallo is a professional geochemist with over 30 years of experience in mineral exploration in Africa. He is considered as one of the ‘founding fathers’ of the mining industry in Mali and has held senior leadership positions in major mining companies including serving as BHP’s Exploration Manager for Africa. James Henderson is the co-founder of CCM with Dr Diallo. He owns 13.8% of CCM’s shares. An Australian national, he has worked in emerging markets for more than 25 years and has expertise in the area of corporate strategy. He holds strong business relationships throughout Oceania, Europe, and North America, and has been a director of several publicly listed companies. Investissement & Partenaire Afrique Entrepreneurs (IPAE), which owns 12.5% of CCM’s shares, is a French impact investing group fully dedicated to Sub-Saharan Africa with more than fifteen years of experience in SME financing.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at approximately €17.6 million. IFC is proposing to participate with a senior loan of up to €4.46 million in XOF equivalent on its own account and with a concessional loan of up to €4.46 million in XOF equivalent as implementing entity of the IDA-PSW BFF (“blended concessional finance co-investment”).
location_description: The investments will be made in Karaga, Kayes region, where CCM’s plant and quarry are located
development_impact: Consumers of agricultural lime, employee skills development and economy-wide benefits are the most significant expected project-level outcomes. In addition, the investment could promote market competitiveness in both the agricultural and mining industry in Mali which depends heavily on imported lime products.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in the form of: (i) financing beyond what is available in the market, (ii) standard setting for the Company regarding E&S, Corporate Governance and Energy Efficiency; and (iii) knowledge and support to develop the agriculture lime market in West Africa. IFC's additionality stems from the integrated package of investment and advisory services.
Company Name: CARRIERES ET CHAUX DU MALI SA

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to CNY1 billion (approximately US$150 million equivalent) to six operating subsidiaries of Muyuan Foods Co., Ltd. (“Muyuan” or the “Company”) to help finance the construction of 10 new pig farms that are primarily in frontier regions of China (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1992 and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange since 2014, Muyuan is an integrated live-hog producer in China, with annual sales of 10.25 million commercial hogs, breeders and piglets in 2019.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be approximately US$300 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to CNY1 billion (approximately US$150 million equivalent) to six operating subsidiaries of Muyuan: (i) Sheqi Muyuan Farming Co., Ltd.; (ii) Heilongjiang Lindian Muyuan Farming Co., Ltd.; (iii) Inner Mongolia Horqin Left Wing Central Banner Muyuan Modern Farming Co., Ltd.; (iv) Luyi Muyuan Farming Co., Ltd.; (v) Anhui Fengtai Muyuan Farming Co., Ltd.; and (vi) Shanxi Xiaxian Muyuan Farming Co., Ltd.
location_description: The Project is located in Anhui, Henan, Heilongjiang, Inner Mongolia and Shanxi Provinces of China.
development_impact: At the project level, IFC anticipates that the Project will generate positive impact on consumers from the provision of safe pork at the time of severe supply shortage as well as implementation of advanced biosecurity procedures at the new pig farms. At the market level, IFC anticipates that the Project will help promote market resilience through improvement of biosecurity and disease management, both by supporting industry consolidation and disseminating best practices among smaller players.
additionality: IFC's additionality in this Project centers around provision of long-term local currency financing to a long-standing strategic client on terms that are otherwise not available in the local market, during the current COVID-19 outbreak and a challenging time for the Chinese pig industry hit by serious outbreak of ASF. In addition, IFC will support the Company in increasing sustainable production in line with best market practices with regard to biosecurity, use of antibiotics, and animal welfare.

project_description: The proposed investment entails a 3-year financing package, including IFC A loan of up to RMB350 million (US$50 million equivalent) and syndication of up to US$30 million or equivalent, to Simple Credit Micro-Lending Co., Ltd. (“Simple Credit”, or the “Company”), a microfinance company holding internet lending license (“Internet MCC”) in China. The proposed IFC financing aims to support Simple Credit to grow its digital agriculture lending (“Digital Agri-lending”) business primarily in frontier regions of China and to promote access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises (“MSMEs”) along the agriculture supply chain.
