sponsor_shareholders: Simple Credit is 90% owned by Martin Lee (Lee Ka-Shing) and 10% owned by Joseph Tse (Tse Lap Bun). Martin Lee is a co-Chairman of Henderson Land Development Co. Ltd. (“HLD”, a Hong Kong listed property developer with market capitalization of US$23.8 billion). Joseph Tse is a partner at Tiang & Partners, an independent Hong Kong law firm associated with PwC Legal international Pte Ltd. Before joining Tiang & Partners, he was the Chief Partner of Allen & Overy in the Greater China region with specialization in banking and finance.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is an up to US$80 million financing package to Simple Credit, consisting of IFC A loan of up to US$50 million; and syndicated portion of up to US$30 million or equivalent.
location_description: Simple Credit is headquartered in Chongqing, China. The loan proceeds of the proposed investment will mainly be used to support the Company’s digital agri-lending program primarily in frontier regions across the country.
development_impact: Project Outcomes: Improve access to finance for MSMEs along the agriculture supply chain. The proceed of the financing will increase access to finance for the unbanked and underbanked MSMEs along the agriculture supply chain with innovative digital solution by increasing the number of Simple Credit's micro digital agri-loan from 590 by the end of 2019 to 6,094 by the end of 2023, and volume of outstanding loan portfolio from US$4.8 million by the end of 2019 to US$132 million by the end of 2023. Contribution to Market Creation: Inclusiveness: The Project will represent IFC's systematic efforts of using digital solution to promote financial inclusion in China and IFC's continued efforts to develop the agriculture and rural areas in China.
additionality: IFC provides both financial and non-financial additionality. Financial additionality includes provision of medium term local currency funding to the client, which is also the first medium term funding obtained by the Company from external sources, and the mobilization of local currency funding. Non-financial additionality includes knowledge sharing and capacity building through an ongoing advisory service engagement, which plays a critical role to help Simple Credit expand its lending activities to the agriculture sector. The advisory project aims to strengthen the digital agri-lending capacity of the Company by assisting it to develop a digital agriculture credit scoring model and agriculture benchmark database.

project_description: Naivas International Limited (“Naivas” or “the Company”) is one of Kenya’s leading supermarket chains, with over 60 stores nationwide and established over 30 years ago, by the Mukuha family. The supermarket chain offers a broad range of products that mainly include fast-moving consumer goods (FMCGs), clothing, furniture, electronics amongst others.
sponsor_shareholders: Naivas is majority owned by the Mukuha family who as part of this transaction will dispose part of their shareholding to a special purpose vehicle owned by IFC, Amethis and other co-investors. The Mukuha family will remain in the business as the main shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC seeks to make an equity investment alongside Amethis which will result in a minority stake, in the Company.
location_description: Various towns and cities in Kenya.
development_impact: The Project is expected to generate direct and indirect job creation and an increase in purchases from domestic suppliers as a result of the store expansion.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC is expected to help the Company optimize business operations and further strengthen its corporate governance structures. IFC will provide a food safety advisory program that will ensure that the Company complies with the Global Good Agriculture Practice (GGAP) that is more stringent than local standards. IFC will also help the Company improve environmental and social (E&S) standards across its operations.

company_name: RIDER IRON AND STEEL GHANA LIMITED
sector: Other Steel Products (Including Wire, Metal Sheets etc.)
project_description: The Project is the construction of a greenfield steel manufacturing plant in Kumasi area, Ghana, with a nameplate capacity of 300,000 metric tons (MT) per annum, by Rider Iron and Steel Ghana Limited (“The Company” or “RSK”). The Project on completion will be the 2nd steel plant to be constructed by the Sponsor in Ghana, primarily to promote import substitution of steel into Ghana.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is 100% owned by a non-operating holding company, Rider Green Industries Inc., domiciled in Seychelles, whose ultimate beneficiaries are Mr. Ghassan Muhsen Moh‘d Wathaifi (90%) and Mr. Walid Alalami (10%), both Jordanian nationals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$24 million (m). The proposed investment is a US$12m IFC A Loan with up to 9 years tenor including ~2.5 years of grace period.
location_description: Odumase, Kumasi Region, Ghana.
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are: (i) Economy wide effects, and in particular, related to the formal income generating opportunities that the Project will create for individuals and micro enterprises engaged in scrap collection activities in RSK's supply chain; (ii) Environmental effects: It will contribute to the abatement of pollution and emission of greenhouse gases, due to greater use of steel scrap in the production process as opposed to primary steel production from iron ore. The local steel production supported by the Project will lead to the elimination of up to 240,000 tons of steel imports, resulting in an annual emissions reduction of 331,900 tons of CO2e. The market impact includes: (iii) Market Integration- Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Project will have a moderate effect on the integration of manufacturing sector in Ghana via the building of economic complexity. As the first steel manufacturing plant in Kumasi, RSK is expected to stimulate competition and pave the way for improving the efficiency and increasing the productivity of the steel sub sector in Ghana.
additionality: IFC's Additionality include: (i) financial additionality for the provision of US Dollar financing for a tenor beyond what is generally available in the market at reasonable terms, and critical to the capital-intensive steel sector. Non-financial Additionality include: (i) Standard Setting: IFC will provide Technical, EH&S expertise to improve overall E&S performance as well as introduce international best practice to the Project; and (ii) IFC's involvement in the Project will help the Company to continue to focus on adopting energy efficient techniques and serve as an example to the Ghanaian steel industry.
Company Name: RIDER IRON AND STEEL GHANA LIMITED

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a ZAR1.2 billion (US$80 million) equity and convertible debt package to finance the development and acquisition of properties for Growthpoint Healthcare Property Holdings Ltd (“GHPH”), South Africa’s first healthcare Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT). Established in 2016, GHPH was founded by Growthpoint Properties Limited (Growthpoint or the Sponsor), South Africa’s largest REIT. GHPH is an unlisted REIT specialized in building a portfolio of income producing healthcare property assets in South Africa and these include hospitals, clinics, diagnostics centers, laboratories and other healthcare related real estate. GHPH will build its portfolio through: (a) acquiring existing properties; and (b) developing new properties (new developments will comprise up to 30% of GHPH’s target portfolio). GHPH already holds five assets with the aggregate value of ZAR2.5 billion (US$174 million), four of which are hospitals and one a medical chamber – small office suites for doctors. Growthpoint is developing a fifth hospital for GHPH called Pretoria Head and Neck hospital, a specialized hospital focused on the head and neck, spinal and vascular surgery. It is expected to be completed in 2020. Concurrently, GHPH is pursuing a pipeline of additional investment opportunities and expects to grow to ZAR5 billion worth of assets over the next three years. The proposed IFC financing package is to support GHPH’s growth plans.
sponsor_shareholders: GHPH is majority-owned by Growthpoint and the balance of equity stake is owned by South African institutional investors. Founded in 1987, Growthpoint is South Africa’s largest REIT, listed on the JSE with a market capitalization of ZAR33billion (US$2. billion) as at March 18th, 2020. Growthpoint owns and manages a diversified property portfolio valued at ZAR136.5 billion (US$8.2 billion) as at December 31, 2019. The portfolio of 502 properties is also diversified across geography and sub-sectors, that is retail, office and industrial properties. Growthpoint’s portfolio comprised of the following: a) South Africa: (i) 436 directly owned properties in South Africa; (ii) a 50 percent interest in the V&A Waterfront, an iconic mixed-use development in Cape Town, South Africa; and (iii) a majority stake interest in GHPH. b) Australia: 58 properties through Growthpoint’s 66 percent investment in Growthpoint Properties Australia Limited listed at the Australia Stock Exchange. c) Eastern Europe: a 29.8 percent interest in Globalworth Real Estate Investment Limited (GWI), which owns 60 properties in Poland and Romania valued at approximately EUR3 billion d) Sub-Saharan Africa (ex-South Africa): a 20.3% percent interest in Growthpoint Investec African Properties Fund (GIAP), which now owns 8 properties.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC financing package consists of: (i) a US$20 million equivalent equity investment in GHPH; and (ii) a US$60 million convertible C loan to Growthpoint. The C-loan investment shall be lent to Growthpoint for on-lending to GHPH. Upon the completion of the initial ramp-up phase of GHPH, which is expected to take 2-3 years, IFC will have the option to convert the C-loan or any portion of it into common equity in GHPH.
location_description: GHPH’s mandate is to invest exclusively in healthcare real estates in South Africa.
development_impact: The expected project-level outcome is increased availability of high-quality healthcare services through increased access to finance for hospital providers in South Africa. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will increase competitiveness of the private healthcare sector by removing barriers to entry for new operators via the introduction of new asset class.
additionality: IFC will provide scarce equity and quasi-equity financing to an unlisted healthcare REIT that otherwise is not readily available in the local market. IFC's investment will support GHPH's ongoing capital raise and play a catalytic role by sending a strong signal to the investment community affirming the viability of the new healthcare asset class in South Africa. IFC's participation in the healthcare REIT could be important for the success of the planned listing of GHPH on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. Furthermore, IFC will provide advice of how GHPH can reach higher green building standard.

project_description: IFC as implementing entity of the IDA Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) is expected to support IFC with two unfunded guarantee products of up to US$400 million under Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP - https://disclosures.ifc.org/#/projectDetail/SPI/23898): (i) pooled first loss (FL) of up to US$150 million and (ii) revolving limit enhancement (LE) of US$250 million that is expected to help GTFP leverage at least US$1 billion in trade finance in IDA PSW eligible countries. The indicative size of each component may change depending on market needs. Without the support under the IDA PSW, IFC will not be able to provide the necessary trade finance in IDA PSW countries given the high risk inherent in booking trade finance transactions in these countries, in particular with a focus on fragile and conflict-affected states that are expected to be severely impacted by COVID-19. IDA PSW support will benefit the real sector importers and exporters that the local banks serve. The level of concessionality (i.e. subsidy) to be provided under the IDA PSW support is estimated to be approximately 3% as a percentage of the expected US$1 billion incremental trade activity in IDA PSW eligible countries.. This estimate is based on the difference between (i) a “reference price” (either a market price if available; the price calculated using IFC’s pricing model, which comprises three main elements: risk, cost and profit; or a negotiated price) and (ii) the “concessional price” being charged for the IDA PSW FL coverage. LE is being provided by IDA PSW on the same terms as IFC and, thus, without price concessionality. Further details and historical information on estimated subsidy levels in IFC’s blended finance portfolio can be found at: www.ifc.org/blendedfinance . As is the case with all of IFC’s blended concessional finance co-investments, this project has been assessed against the Enhanced Blended Concessional Finance Principles for DFI Private Sector Operations adopted by IFC and more than 20 other DFIs in 2017. Further information on these Enhanced Principles and IFC’s blended finance approach and governance can also be found at: www.ifc.org/blendedfinance . The aim to launch this facility is to assist the local banks in surviving the current market situation and bridging the financing gap. It is expected that, over time, with proper scale, IFC and other DFIs/ FIs would be able to support similar facilities/ FIs, potentially without/ with lower FL. To support this increase in trade volumes at this most critical time, IFC is open to engaging with other partner banks on similar structures, including when relevant with the support of blended concessional finance.
sponsor_shareholders: The proposal does not have a single company and/or sponsor, but rather, is expected to support more than 2,000 real sector participants (exporters/importers) as the sponsors. This proposal will rely on GTFP’s existing and new obligors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC as implementing entity of the IDA Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) is expected to support IFC with two unfunded guarantee products of up to US$400 million under Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP): (i) pooled first loss (FL) of up to US$150 million and (ii) revolving limit enhancement (LE) of US$250 million that is expected to help GTFP leverage at least US$1 billion in trade finance in IDA PSW eligible countries. The indicative size of each component may change depending on market needs.
location_description: IDA PSW eligible countries
development_impact: The project builds on GTFP's global platform, increasing access to trade finance to emerging markets. The Project will provide increased access to trade finance to the Issuing Bank's customers, including both corporates and SMEs. On the market side, the project will further connect the Issuing Bank's cross border connections, increasing the country's integration through both financial and real sector channels. It will help to link more traders to other countries and connect the country's financial markets more deeply.
additionality: 1. A non-financial source of additionality includes GTFP's catalytic role as a trusted facilitator among cross border correspondent banks. GTFP's guarantee structure helps to reduce key elements of confirmation risk for banks that provide this essential service for trade finance. 2. The Project taps GTFP's global financial institution network for trade finance, which, along with IFC's trade finance due diligence expertise, increasing the probability of new cross border relationship formation for the Issuing Bank. 3. IFC provides comfort to the Confirming Banks by mitigating non-commercial non-environmental and social risks, such as country, regulatory, project, or political risks, while adhering to IFC's principle of political neutrality. 4. The Project is expected to help the Issuing Bank strengthen its trade finance operations. In addition, the Issuing Bank will benefit from IFC's technical expertise in redesigning its trade solutions and marketing materials.

company_name: EGYPTIAN CENTRES FOR REAL ESTATE DEVELOPMENT SAE
project_description: The proposed investment consists of a US$135 million in A Loan, of which $45 million is to finance the retail property business of Egyptian Center for Real Estate Development, SAE, Egypt (“ECRED” or “the Company”) owned by AlHokair Family (“Sponsors”). In addition, the investment will also consist of a US$90 million loan to Saudi FAS Holding Company, KSA (Saudi FAS) to refinance its existing capital contribution in ECRED for existing operations in Egypt. Saudi FAS is also fully owned by the Sponsors. The financing will support ECRED’s business expansion by partly funding retail and commercial projects in newly developed areas of Cairo and secondary cities in Egypt.
sponsor_shareholders: The AlHokair is one of the leading groups in KSA focusing mainly on retail and retail property sectors owned Sponsors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC financing amount to USD$135 million. Within the scope of the Project, IFC’s financing will be directly used to support Company’s capital expenditures and working capital needs.
location_description: Projects are located or will be located in Giza, Cairo, Gharbia and Dakhalia Governorates in Egypt.
development_impact: - Employees - A significant number of direct and indirect jobs will be created once all shopping malls of ECRED are completed. - Customers: company supports the growth of local retail brands that has a positive impact on the economy - Women Employment: modern malls provide opportunities for women to enter the workforce by providing a safe and structured environment. - Integration: Malls in secondary cities and new areas will provide more economic opportunities to the local population.
additionality: Financial Additionality: - Resource Mobilization: IFC will mobilize funds for the project. Non-Financial Additionality: -Standard Setting: IFC engaged with ECRED pre-appraisal to determine that environment, health and safety is now integrated into the new management framework. This provides the company with the necessary capacity to comply with IFC's E&S standards. -Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: green building standards with EDGE certification, sharing knowledge and best practices to enhance corporate governance; providing support to train staff on existing anti-sexual harassment policy.
Company Name: EGYPTIAN CENTRES FOR REAL ESTATE DEVELOPMENT SAE

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a US$500 million A/ B/ MCPP Loan to LD Celulose S.A. (“LDC” or the “Company”). The investment will help finance the construction of a greenfield dissolving wood pulp (“DWP”) plant in Minas Gerais, Brazil with capacity to produce 500,000 tons per annum and generate 144 MW of electricity (the “Project”). The Company will also manage approximately 70,000 ha of eucalyptus plantations on land leased from third parties.
sponsor_shareholders: LDC is a 51/49 joint-venture between Lenzing AG (“Lenzing”) and Duratex S.A (“Duratex”). Headquartered in Austria, Lenzing is a global producer of wood-based cellulose fibers. Headquartered in Brazil, Duratex is a producer of industrialized wood panels, metal fittings and ceramic tiles.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is estimated to cost US$1.8 billion, to be financed with long-term debt and equity. The proposed IFC investment consists of an up to US$200 million A Loan, an up to US$50 million MCPP Loan and an up to US$250 million B Loan.
location_description: The DWP plant will be constructed near the municipalities of Araguari and Indianopolis, in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
development_impact: (i) Economy-wide impact: The Project is expected to make a substantial contribution to employment generation in the frontier state of Minas Gerais and to value addition through the multiplier effects. The Project is estimated to generate a total of nearly 7,000 jobs (including direct, indirect, and induced jobs).The Project's overall value addition is estimated at US$512 million, including direct, indirect, and induced effects along the Project's supply chain as a result of the joint venture. (ii) Environmental and social impact: The proposed Project will achieve its objectives in environmentally and socially mindful manner by planting on degraded lands, adopting Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) standards in managing its plantations, and utilizing biomass for its energy needs. The Project consists of a set of activities that are expected to produce pulp with the lowest CO2 emissions. An increase in natural wood-based pulp production has also broader environmental benefits since the impacts of wood-based textile fibers on the environment are more limited than that of oil-based fibers. Unlike synthetic fibers, wood-based fibers do not shed microplastics into the water when washed and lend themselves more easily to recycling. (iii) Contribution to market creation: The establishment of DWP production in Brazil through the joint venture between Lenzing and Duratex could result in increasing the complexity of Brazil's manufacturing base by facilitating the development of higher value added segments of the textile industry.
additionality: The proposed investment has financial additionality in the form of mobilization under IFC's preferred creditor umbrella for the participating lenders. Non-financial additionality is related to standard setting through the dissemination of best environmental and social ("E&S") and corporate governance ("CG") standards.

project_description: The group of companies known as the Suguna Group consolidated under the holding company Suguna Holdings Private Limited (“SHPL” or the “Group” or “Suguna”) was initially established in 1984 and is one of the leading poultry integrators in India with operations covering all areas of the poultry sector. Suguna’s fully integrated operations cover broiler and layer farming, hatcheries, feed mills, and processing plants across 20 Indian states and one union territory, and have an overseas presence in Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and Kenya. The main operating company under SHPL is Suguna Foods Private Limited (SFPL) in India, which generates over 97% of the Group’s revenues. Suguna is planning (i) a capacity expansion consisting of the construction of poultry infrastructure including potentially a hatchery, processing plant, poultry environment-controlled shed, premix plant, and related poultry assets, as well as incremental working capital financing, through a US$42.9 million investment at SFPL in India to further expand its operations in northern and eastern India, primarily in Uttar Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal; and (ii) the construction of feed mills, breeders, and hatcheries in Bangladesh and Kenya through a US$15.9 million investment in Suguna Food and Feeds Bangladesh Pvt. Ltd. (“SFFBPL”) in Bangladesh and a US$8.4 million investment in Suguna Poultry (Kenya) Limited (“SPKL”) in Kenya in order to capitalize on the growing economy and expanding poultry sector in both countries, for a total overall investment across India, Bangladesh, and Kenya of US$67.2 million (the “Project”)
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsors and shareholders of the Project companies consist of the founders Mr. Bangarusamy Soundararajan, the Chairman of Suguna, as well as his younger brother Mr. Ganapathypalayam Bangarusamy Sundararajan, the Managing Director of Suguna, and their family members (collectively, the Sponsors).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is expected to be approximately US$67.2 million. The proposed investment (the “Project”) includes the following: (a) An IFC A loan comprising of (i) a US$ A Loan of up to US$15 million and (ii) an INR denominated Non-Convertible Debentures (“NCDs”) of up to INR1,800 million (approximately US$25 million equivalent) to SFPL in India; (b) An IFC A loan of US$10 million to SFFBL in Bangladesh; and (c) IFC A loan of US$4 million to SPKL in Kenya.
location_description: SHPL headquarters is located at 1020, Avinashi Road, II floor, Above AUDI Showroom, Coimbatore 641018 India. The Project is expected to be carried out at the following locations: SFPL: Suguna Foods Private Limited, Plot No - 19,20 & 21, Jayamangal Industrial Area, Khurda - Tahasil, Dist - Khordha, Odisha – 752101, India Suguna Foods Private Limited, Plot No. - A - 13 & A - 14, Panagarh industrial Park, Panagarh,Dist - Burdwan, West Bengal – 713148, India Suguna Foods Private Limited, Plot No. - 201, 202, 203, 205 & 206, MK Road, Deotala Village, Gazole PS, Malda Dt, West Bengal -732124, India Suguna Foods Private Limited, Plot No. - LR / 1355, 1356, 1363, Ratanpur, Onda, Bankura - Dist West Bengal – 722152, India Gorakhpur Industrial Development Authority, Plot No. F-6, 15 GIDA, Jidiyan, Thasil, Sahajanwa, Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh – 273209, India SFFBPL: Breeder Farm: Suguna Paitapukur Project, Bamlahal, Paitapukur, Dag RS 1101, 1123, 1125, 1127 & 1125, Post Office Chobbishnogor, 6000, Thana/Upazilla Godagari, Rajshahi, Bangladesh Breeder Farm: Suguna Narayanpur Project, Narayanpur, Uchadanga Narayanpur, Dag RS 394, 1119, 1120, 1122, 1123, 1124, 1125, 1126 JL: 61, Post Office Kharikulla Narayanpurrman, 6311, Thana/Upazilla Tanore, Rajshahi, Bangladesh Feedmill: Mirzapur, Mirzapur under 5 No. Mirzapur Union (Ward-07), Dag 371, 372, 373, 369, 378, 354, 359, 361, 360, 358, 351, 352, 353, 347, 348, 382, 384, 385, 386, 415, 381, 362, 379, 380, 383, Post Office Mirzapur, 5840, Thana/Upazilla Sherpur, Bogra, Bangladesh SPKL: Breeder Land: Plot L.R. No. Kjd/Ildamat/9448, Off Namanga Road, Kajiado, Kajiado County, Kenya Feedmill Land: Plot L.R. No. 7240/480, Near Shell Petrol Station, Thika Garissa Road, Thika, Kiambu County, Kenya Interim Feedmill at Thika: NEW OSHWAL DISTRIBUTORS LIMITED, Go Down Numbers 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9, On Title Number: Thika Municipality Block 13/318, Thika, Kiambu Country, Kenya
development_impact: 1. Greater farmer incomes: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is the impact on the incomes of poultry farmers who participate in Suguna's outgrower (contract farming) model or use the Group's inputs for independent poultry production. 2. Increased consumer access to affordable and high quality food products: Depending on how the final product composition evolves as a result of the Project to what is currently available in the market, consumers may benefit from increased access to high-quality, affordable poultry products. 3. Market creation: At the market level, the Project is expected to contribute to integrating farmers into the poultry value chain by transferring its experience and business model to Bangladesh and advancing the sophistication of contract farming in this underdeveloped market through demonstration and replication.
additionality: 1. Financial additionality: The Group is growing into a global poultry player by expanding beyond its current operations in India. To help the Group achieve its growth targets, the group needs to undertake increased capital expenditure, both domestically within India and in the countries to where it hopes to expand. The proposed Project entails the provision of long-term funding in these various geographies, thus giving the group some amount of flexibility in capital allocation. 2. Non-financial additionality: a) Standard setting: Through this Project, the Group is expected to adopt and implement appropriate standards in labor management, production, as well as supply chains and raw material procurement, particularly on food safety standards. The implementation of IFC Performance Standards including food safety standards across the group's target market will help to instill best practices in one of the organized leaders in the broiler market in India as they look to expand into newer markets such as Bangladesh and Kenya; and b) knowledge, innovation, and capacity building: IFC is able to provide the Group with global industry knowledge in poultry, food processing and agribusiness and help to facilitate the exchange of ideas with other IFC clients, thus enhancing Suguna's overall operational know-how and knowledge of the latest technological advances.

project_description: The proposed Project with Absa Bank Limited (“Absa” or the “Bank”) is an up to US$140 million equivalent in South African Rands (ZAR) working capital support to eligible suppliers of a large manufacturing company (the “Company”).
sponsor_shareholders: Absa is a leading Pan-African financial services group offering banking, insurance and financial products and services to individuals, corporates and small and medium enterprises clients. Headquartered in Johannesburg, south Africa, it is the third largest commercial bank in South Africa with operations in Botswana, Ghana, Kenya, Mauritius, Mozambique, Uganda, Tanzania, Seychelles, and Zambia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is up to US$140 million equivalent in ZAR of which IFC’s proposed unfunded risk participation is up to US$70 million equivalent in ZAR.
location_description: The Bank and the Company are headquartered in Johannesburg, South Africa. All eligible suppliers are domestic South African companies, of which the majority are micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSME).
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are the stakeholder effects - increased access to financing for suppliers engaged in the Company's supply chain. IFC also anticipates that the Project will have a strong effect on the integration of the manufacturing sector in South Africa via enhancing connectivity of suppliers into the domestic value chain.
additionality: IFC's additionality includes increased availability of funding to MSMEs at affordable terms.

project_description: IFC is providing a loan to Adeco Agropecuaria S.A., Pilaga S.A, and L3N S.A. (jointly referred to as “Adeco” or the “Company”). Adeco is currently investing in the expansion of its dairy production capacity as well as in further downstream dairy integration in Argentina. The company has requested IFC to extend an A/MCPP Loan of up to US$100 MM to finance: (i) the expansion of its milk production facilities (two new free-stalls in the Santa Fe Province); (ii) the acquisition of two milk processing facilities and brands from local cooperative SanCor, located in the cities of Morteros and Chivilcoy; and (iii) upgrade investments in the acquired facilities.
sponsor_shareholders: Adeco is owned by Adecoagro S.A, a diversified agribusiness group listed in the New York Stock Exchange which produces sugar, ethanol and energy in Brazil and grains, rice and dairy in Argentina and Uruguay.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project costs is estimated at US$112 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of a long-term loan of up to US$100 million, including a Green Loan tranche of approximately US$17.8 million, and consisting of an approximately US$57 million A-loan for IFC’s own account and an approximately US$43 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP).
location_description: Adeco is headquartered in the city of Buenos Aires. The dairy operations are located in Santa Fe province (dairy free-stalls), in Cordoba province (Morteros dairy processing facility) and Buenos Aires province (Chivilcoy dairy processing facility).
development_impact: The Project will help preserve and improve rural livelihoods. The investment will restore reliable off-take to the dairy farmers who were previously supplying the Chivilcoy and Morteros processing plants and grow its farmer reach further. The Project is estimated to create 250 direct jobs and approximately 3,500 indirect jobs through value chain linkages. The Project will also have positive environmental impacts through intensification of dairy production and climate smart elements of the investment program. The Project is expected to contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of Argentina's dairy sector by helping to shift the sector toward a more intensive and more sustainable production model.
additionality: Financial Additionality: IFC will be providing financing for the Company's Argentine operations in a challenging economic environment and at a time when alternative funding is limited. Part of IFC's financing will be in the form of a Green Loan, introducing the Company to an innovative financing solution. Non-Financial Additionality: IFC will contribute to strengthening the Company's environmental and social practices in the dairy sector through the adoption of IFC's Performance Standards. IFC will also contribute to knowledge sharing and capacity building through the planned advisory work in the areas of energy efficiency and sustainability improvements.

sector: Municipal Finance - Transport and Roads [Project only]
project_description: The Project seeks to provide long term financing to a municipal enterprise of the City of Lviv, Lvivelektrotrans (LET), which shall be used for (i) the acquisition of trolleybuses with in-motion charging batteries, and (ii) the rehabilitation of catenary lines.
sponsor_shareholders: The Borrower will be the municipal company Lvivelektrotrans (LET), and the loan will be fully guaranteed by the City of Lviv.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is EUR 32 million including rolling stock acquisition and catenary line refurbishment. IFC investment is composed of an A loan to Lvivelektrotrans (LET), for up to 19 million Euros (or Euro equivalent), which may be disbursed in EUR or UAH. The Project is also expected to be supported by a 13 million Euro senior loan from IFC as implementing entity of the Clean Technology Fund (“CTF”).
location_description: The Project is located in the City of Lviv, Ukraine.
development_impact: The main project outcome is improved user access and quality of Lviv's public transport system. The project will also address barriers to improve access of women to a safe public transport. The new efficient trolleybuses fleet, combined with renovations on catenary lines and route optimization, will contribute reduce CO2 emissions of Lviv's urban transport. At the market level, the project will open access of municipal infrastructure to local currency debt capital markets and enhance transport system wide resilience.
additionality: Financial additionality - financing structure: Long-term and non-sovereign guaranteed financing, which is not available to sub-national entities from commercial banks in Ukraine, at terms offered by IFC. Sub-sovereign entities in Ukraine, like Lviv and LET, are constrained in accessing finance from commercial banks, despite the recent fiscal decentralization reforms enabling greater fiscal autonomy and the ability to borrow. Non-financial additionality - Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC will leverage its broad experience in the urban transport sector and provide advisory services to i) build LET's capacity to reduce risks associated with the selection and implementation of the trolleybuses with in-motion charging batteries, ii) developing a long term deployment plan for the trolleybus fleet with phased implementation and clear objectives; and iii) improve financial sustainability of Lviv's public transportation system and LET, and iv) implement reporting and grievance mechanisms aimed at reducing GBV in public transport.

project_description: Warehouses de Pauw NV (WDP or the Company), a listed Belgian Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT), has requested IFC to provide a long-term loan to support the building of around 1 million square meters of semi-industrial and logistics property throughout various cities in Romania (the Project) over the next few years through its subsidiary, WDP Romania. With the aim to build a €1 billion portfolio in Romania by 2023, the Company’s goal is to have its Romania portfolio become 20 percent of its overall asset portfolio.
sponsor_shareholders: WDP is a listed Belgian Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) that develops, owns, acquires and manages logistics, warehouses and class A semi-industrial property. It has a portfolio of assets covering, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Luxembourg and Romania.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is around €600 million and entails capital expenditures of the Company over the next 2 years. IFC proposed to provide an A Loan of up to US$110 million, an MCPP Loan of up to US$50 million, and a B Loan of up to US$110 million €-equivalent to partially finance this investment plan.
location_description: Project assets will be built throughout the country, including Bucharest, Timisoara, Cluj, Brazi, Oarja, Sibiu, and Paulesti.
development_impact: The proposed investment is expected to have limited environmental and social impacts which will be sitespecific with none anticipated to be significant. Further, the impacts can be avoided or mitigated by adhering to recognized performance standards, procedures, guidelines and design criteria as described in the followingsections. Thus, this is a Category B project in accordance with IFC’s Policy on Environmental and Social Sustainability. Key environmental and social issues applicable for this investment are: design and construction of buildings in accordance with national construction codes and standards, particularly related to seismic resistance and life and fire safety; effective implementation of the environmental, occupational health and safety management plans during construction; energy efficiency and other resources consumption during buildings operation.

project_description: Engro Polymer & Chemicals Limited (“EPCL” or the “Company”) is the only fully integrated chlor-vinyl chemical complex in Pakistan. It is involved in manufacturing, marketing and distribution of poly-vinyl chloride (PVC) and chlor-vinyl allied products, including vinyl chloride monomer, caustic coda, hypochloric acid and sodium hypochlorite. The Company is undertaking implementation of a Hydrogen Peroxide plant and a few efficiency projects and has invited IFC to consider supporting its investment program.
sponsor_shareholders: Largest shareholders of EPCL are Engro Corporation (56.2%) and Mitsubishi Corporation (11.0%). Engro Corporation (“ECorp” or the “Sponsor”) is one of Pakistan’s largest and professionally managed conglomerates with business interests in fertilizers, foods, chemical storage & handling, trading, energy and petrochemicals. ECorp’s main shareholder is Dawood Hercules Corporation, which is owned by Dawood family and associated companies. ECorp is listed on Pakistan Stock Exchange. The remaining shareholding is distributed among various institutions and general public.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at around US$40 million. The proposed IFC investment includes an A loan for up to US$15 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Project will be located near Port Qasim in Karachi, Pakistan.
development_impact: Implementation of the Project is expected to increase local availability of Hydrogen Peroxide (H202) in the Country. Customers will benefit from shorter delivery time and lower inventory costs. The Project is also expected to maintain the Company's competitiveness through value addition. The proposed investment qualifies as a climate change mitigation project and is expected to achieve some reductions in annual GHG emissions. In addition, the Project will create jobs and enable transfer of technical and managerial know-how. IFC anticipates that the Project will lead to increased competitiveness of the PVC and base chemicals sector, which will support the growth of the main users of these products such as the textile, building and construction sector.
additionality: The financing will provide the Company with access to critical long-term funding in an environment where such funding is scarce. IFC will also assist the Company in improving resource efficiencies and establishing adequate E&S policies to ensure full compliance of the Project with IFC performance standards.

project_description: The Project is a funded risk participation for up to EUR 10 million by IFC in a EUR 45million one-year offshore secured pre-export facility provided by Societe Generale to finance the purchase of seed cotton and provide working capital to a cotton company in Burkina Faso.
sponsor_shareholders: Societe Generale is one of the leading European financial services groups. Based on a diversified and integrated banking model, the Group combines financial strength and proven expertise in innovation with a strategy of sustainable growth, aiming to be the trusted partner for its clients committed to the positive transformations of society and the economy. Active in the real economy for over 150 years, with a solid position in Europe and connected to the rest of the world, Societe Generale has over 149,000 members of staff in 67 countries and supports daily 31 million individual clients, businesses and institutional investors around the world by offering a wide range of advisory services and tailored financial solutions. The group is built on three complementary core businesses: French Retail Banking, which encompasses the Societe Generale, Credit du Nord and Boursorama brands. Each offers a full range of financial services with omnichannel products at the cutting edge of digital innovation; International Retail Banking, Insurance and Financial services to Corporates, with networks in Africa, Russia, Central and Eastern Europe and specialized businesses that are leaders in their markets; Global Banking and Investor Solutions, which offers recognized expertise, key international locations and integrated solutions. Societe Generale is included in the principal socially responsible investment indices: DJSI (World and Europe), FTSE4Good (Global and Europe), Euronext Vigeo (World, Europe and Eurozone), four of the STOXX ESG Leaders indices, and the MSCI Low Carbon Leaders Index.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project will be in a total amount up to EUR 45 million. Societe Generale will retain EUR 25 million while IFC will retain EUR up to 10 million.
location_description: Societe Generale is headquartered in Paris, France. The underlying project is the financing cotton produced and exported out of Burkina Faso.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is continued access to markets and finance for over 32,889 farmers and increases in productivity for 1,557 farmers. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates the investment will increase integration and resilience in the cotton sector in Burkina Faso, a low income/IDA country, through capacity building and demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC's additionality will come in three forms (i) knowledge, innovation and capacity building through advisory services to smallholder farmers; (ii) standard-setting with regards to reducing / eliminating child labor; and (iii) non-commercial risk mitigation, including trusted partnerships with a commercial bank, especially since this project will follow previous engagements of IFC in the cotton sector in Burkina Faso.

project_description: ND Refineries Limited (NDRE) is a mini-refinery located in Ogbele, Rivers State, Nigeria. The project entails the financing of the capacity expansion, infrastructure, and environmental improvement investments of NDRE (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Niger Delta Exploration & Production PLC (NDEP), which is a leading independent public liability company (PLC) in Nigeria, with integrated assets in both the upstream and downstream oil &gas. NDRE, a wholly owned subsidiary of NDEP, is involved only in refining (downstream) activities.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Project cost will be approximately US$ 140 million. IFC will provide US$35 million A-loan and mobilize US$15 million MCPP loan to NDRE to finance the Project.
location_description: The Project will be developed on NDRE’s existing facilities in Ogbele, Port Harcourt, Nigeria.
development_impact: The Project's expected development impact includes (i) reduction of Nigeria's current account deficit by reducing import of petroleum products (ii) creating direct and indirect jobs in Rivers State Nigeria (iii) improving competitiveness and quality standards in Nigerian refining sector by supporting the expansion of a private player (iv) creating a demonstration impact by showing the viability of modular refineries in countries where there are significant crude-oil reserves such as Nigeria.
additionality: IFC's expected role and additionality includes (i) providing longer term financing beyond what is available in the Nigerian market (ii) providing support to enhance corporate governance practices of NDRE and NDEP.

project_description: Headquartered in Mumbai, India, ETC Agro Processing (I) Private Limited (“ETC India” or the “Company”) is amongst the top largest pulses processor in the world and trader of pulses in India, with a current processing capacity of 500,000 MT. The Company is now expanding its operations in India, with a strategic focus on the higher yield and less volatile processing segment and by embarking on an asset-light model for future expansion. The Company requires long-term working capital (the “Project”) to support this expansion. The Project would finance ~30% of the Company’s working capital requirements over the next three years.
sponsor_shareholders: ETC India is a wholly owned subsidiary of ETC Group Ltd (“ETG” or the “Group”), a strategic client of MAS Agribusiness with investments in Africa and India. ETG is one of the largest and fastest growing integrated agricultural conglomerates in sub-Saharan Africa, importing and exporting soft commodities to and from 48 countries across Africa, Asia and America. It owns and manages a vertically integrated agriculture supply chain enabling two-way trade flows by selling fertilizer, agrochemicals, farming implements and agronomic services through their supply pipelines to the farmers and procuring agriculture produce from them. ETC Group is controlled by Mahesh Patel, Ketan Patel and Birju Patel, who were born in Africa and are based in Tanzania, London and South Africa. In addition, other private equity investors such as Mitsui & Co and Pembani Remgro Infrastructure Fund own minority stake in ETC Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the Project is approximately US$77 million, out of which IFC plans to provide a loan of up to INR 1,600 million (approximately US$22.5 million) denominated in INR in the form of a Non-Convertible Debenture (NCD).
location_description: The Project would support ramp-up of the Company’s operations across its (i) own processing capacities in Kolkata in West Bengal, Vasad in Gujarat and Khopoli in Maharashtra and (ii) third party processing units across India.
development_impact: 1. Impact on Consumers: The Project will contribute to addressing India's challenges with both food security and safety as well as diet diversity. The Project contributes to increased production of calorie rich, nutritious, and safe pulses at affordable price. Further, the Project would also have a meaningful impact on low income consumers since several of the states where ETC is planning its expansion are Low Income States (LIS), namely Assam, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Chhattisgarh. 2. Impact on Farmers: The Project will result in increased purchases of pulses from a significant number of farmers. ETC India combines global sourcing with various domestic channels (including traders, local mandis, and government tenders with NAFED) to procure the necessary raw materials. The use of inland third party processors (including in Rajasthan, UP, and MP) is expected to facilitate local sourcing from surrounding producer states. 3. Market creation: At the market level, the Project is expected to contribute to improving the competitiveness of third party processors by raising their processing efficiencies and E&S practices and building their overall capacity to serve broader processing needs in the market.
additionality: 1. Financing structure: The proposed Project entails the provision of long-term working capital to ETC India to support the Company's growth as it adapts to its new business strategy. IFC's investment would be in the amount of INR 1,600 mn (US$ 22.5 mn) in the form of INR-denominated non-convertible debentures. 2. Non - financial additionality: IFC will help enhance the Company's sustainability by developing an ESAP to match its changing business model. In particular, IFC will work with the Company to address the risks arising from engagement with third party processors by strengthening their environmental, factory, and labor compliance, implementing labor welfare measures, including OHS and life and fire safety. IFC will also help strengthen transport service agreements to help mitigate E&S risks and define a corrective action plan for ETC to mitigate workplace risks at its own facilities.

sector: Pottery, Ceramic, and Plumbing Fixtures (Including Kitchenware)
project_description: IFC will provide a financial package (consisting of both debt and equity) to Brightstar Investment Limited (Brightstar or the Company) or its direct parent company (yet to incorporated), to finance its capital expenditure program to (i) expand an existing ceramic tiles manufacturing plant in Ghana and (ii) construct/finalize completion of five greenfield ceramic tiles manufacturing plants – one each in Senegal, Cameroon, Mozambique, Zambia and Democratic Republic of Congo.
sponsor_shareholders: Keda is a China base ceramics machinery producer. Sunda is an Africa-focused manufacturing and trading company, headquartered in China.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated cost of the Project is US$323million. IFC is considering providing a total financing package of up to US$192.7m including debt and equity.
location_description: The facilities will be built in the below locations: Ghana Factory: In Shama District. Senegal Factory: Near Dakar. Cameroon Factory: Near Douala. DRC Factory: Near Maluku Bonded Zone. Mozambique Factory: Near Maputo Beluluane Industrial Park. Zambia: In multi-functional economic zone in the southern Lusaka
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level outcomes are economy-wide and employment effects, and skills development. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Project will have a strong effect in integration via increasing manufacturing complexity; and of integration in the regional manufacturing sector by linking various production hubs across the sub-Saharan Africa region to Sunda's extensive distribution and dealership network in the region.
additionality: Financing structure: IFC will provide a long tenor loan, which is not readily available to Brightstar in the local markets. Standard setting: Through the proposed investment, IFC aims: a) to help the Company achieve higher corporate governance standards; and b) to share its E&S expertise with the Company to help develop Brightstar's environmental, health, safety and social practices in line with World Bank Group requirements.

project_description: The proposed investment is a US$30 million equivalent A-loan to Xiang Nian Foods Co. Ltd. (“XN”, or the “Company”), an existing portfolio client of IFC. Headquartered in Nanyang, Henan Province, XN is a manufacturer of dried wheat noodles. With the support from IFC’s financing, XN successfully established the Phase I of a new dried noodle factory in Zhenping county, Henan Province. The proposed IFC’s investment is critical in meeting the remaining capital expenditure and working capital needs for this new factory.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company’s shareholding was 67.5% controlled by Mr. Sun Jungeng and his family (collectively, the “Sponsors”). Mr. Sun Jungeng is the Chairman, CEO and founder of the Company. With a major in food engineering, he steered the Company from a small noodle workshop to a regional leader with well established brands. Mr. Sun Jungeng is a reputable, well-recognized professional and a Vice Chairman of the Food Safety Association of Henan province.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$60 million and IFC is invited to provide a long-term loan of US$30 million.
location_description: Zhenping County, Henan Province, People’s Republic of China
development_impact: Project-level development impact: (i) create more job opportunity; (ii) reach more farmers for supply of wheat; and (iii) provide high quality food for consumers. Market-level (i) promote inclusive development in frontier regions of China; and (ii) promote integration of supply chain.
additionality: (i) provide long-term local-currency financing which is not readily available in local market; (ii) promote higher Environmental & Social standards; and (iii) Global industry knowledge sharing.

project_description: IFC is considering to provide financing of up to US$24 million to support the expansion of Zalar Agri, a producer of high-value fruits and nuts in Morocco. Zalar operates 16 orchards with a total land area of 1,372 hectares and planted area of 741 hectares as of 2018.
sponsor_shareholders: Zalar Agri is owned by the Chaouni family, and its main shareholders are Mr. Farouk Chaouni, Mr. Fouad Chaouni Benabdallah, and Mr. Ali Berbich.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$24 million which IFC proposes to finance with a C loan of up to US$12 million and a syndicated loan of up to US$12 million.
location_description: The orchards are in various areas of Morocco, including in the region of Agadir, Casablanca, Errachidia, Fes, Kenitra, and Taroundant.
development_impact: Project outcomes: The Company will increase direct and seasonal workers by 400 mostly in rural regions of Morocco. Today, 40% of Zalar Agri's workers are women. Moreover, at the holding level, 35% of the Company's top management is composed of women. In addition, Zalar Agri expects up to 1,600 indirect jobs would be created among sub-contractors and suppliers. Contribution to Market Creation: Through the Project, IFC expects the Moroccan date sector to be better integrated into global value chains, through demonstration and replication effects, as Zalar Agri extends the product range by relaunching the production of premium variety dates (Medjoul).
additionality: Financial Additionality: IFC will be providing an innovative financial product to Zalar Agri. Moreover, IFC will be mobilizing up to US$12 million through the B-Loan program. Non-Financial Additionality: IFC will bring to the Company potential advisory services support in the areas of gender and linkages with farmers. The Company expressed its interest in potentially developing together with IFC share-value program with its raw material suppliers.

project_description: Founded in 1998, Globaltronics for Electronics SAE ('Gtronics' or the 'Company' - http://www.gtronics.com/ ), a leading fully integrated Egyptian manufacturer of electricity management solutions, specializes in the development and manufacture of power meters including smart digital meters, prepaid meters and provides smart grid solutions in addition to Meter Management Systems (MMS). IFC is considering a USD10m preferred equity investment in Globaltronics. The proposed investment will be used to (i) finance increased working capital for the greater expected sales and inventory of the Government of Egypt's mechanical meter replacement cycle; (ii) finance Globaltronics' overseas expansion plans, including in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (“KSA”) and Eastern Europe; and (iii) finance additional R&D and enhance the tendering department to be able to effectively compete in several African and Middle Eastern countries and meet their technical requirements, in addition to developing new products (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The company was founded by Dr. Hany Assal (“the Sponsor”), a veteran investor with more than 35 years’ of experience establishing and managing successful information and communications technology (“ICT”) and manufacturing ventures in Egypt and the Middle East. Dr. Assal and his family fully own the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at USD15m, of which IFC will provide USD10m in the form of preferred shares. The remainder will be financed through internal cash generation.
location_description: The Company has 2 factories in 6th of October City in Greater Cairo, and is also building a plant in Modon Industrial City near Madinah in KSA.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have (a) economy-wide effects through (i) increased production of digital electricity meters and linkages to domestically available inputs, and (ii) increased direct, indirect and induced jobs; and (b) stakeholder impacts through improved electricity distribution networks, more efficient energy demand management, and decrease of network losses. Beyond the Project, IFC also anticipates that as one of the largest and most sophisticated digital meter manufacturing plants in the country, the Project will have a strong effect on the integration of the manufacturing sector in Egypt via the building of economic complexity.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the Project will comprise of (i) financial additionality, related to IFC's own account equity; (ii) non-financial additionality in terms of knowledge transfer and capacity building; and (iii) standard setting in terms of corporate governance expertise.

project_description: Established in 2000, Luna Export Slaughterhouse PLC is one of the leading export abattoirs in Ethiopia. The company currently exports livestock carcasses and meat to the U.A.E. and Saudi Arabia. The abattoir is FSSC 22000, ISO 9001:2015 and Halal certified. The fresh produce distribution business line also distributes fresh fruits, vegetables and meat in Addis Ababa through shops owned by the Company. The Project represents Luna Slaughterhouse PLC’s backward integration into feed crop farming and animal fattening by establishing a modern livestock farm and securing quality livestock on a long-term sustainable basis (“the Project”). The Project is expected to improve access to markets for approximately 7,000 small scale producers (pastoralists and agro pastoralists). Through the Project, these small-scale producers will benefit from improved breeding, feeding, animal health support and water access for their animals. IFC expects the Project to increase integration of the Ethiopian meat export sector, domestically and internationally, through replication and demonstration effects. Domestically, the Company would be the first semi-intensive goat farm in Ethiopia. The backward integration from meat export into livestock production is expected to achieve better fattening and conditioning leading to higher meat yield and income. If successful, players in Ethiopia could replicate the model, thereby transforming goat cultivation and export in Ethiopia. Internationally, the Project will assist the Company with repositioning of imported Ethiopian goat meat in the Gulf market by improving product quality and introducing complete traceability.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is Mr. Tesfalidet Hagos Gebru, the founder and general manager of Luna. Mr. Hagos and his family own 100% of Luna Export Slaughterhouse PLC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated project cost is US$ 9.8 million. The proposed investment is an own account A loan of up to US$ 5 million equivalent in Ethiopian Birr (“ETB”) in the form of senior secured loan. The proposed ETB loan will be provided under the signed Framework Agreement between IFC and the National Bank of Ethiopia. The remaining project cost of US$ 4.8 million will be funded by internally generated cashflow.
location_description: The project area is located in the arid Weyto valley in Weyto (Berhale) town inhabited by agro-pastoralists communities. The semi-intensive feedlot (c. 300ha for corn silage and Calliandra species) is located in Enchete Kebele, Bene Tsemay District/Woreda, South Omo Zone. The project will occupy a total of 500ha.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is an increase in access to export markets for 5,000 smallholder farmers in northern Ethiopia. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates the investment will increase integration in the supply chain, through demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in three forms: (i) financing structure through long-term funding; (ii) knowledge, innovation and capacity-building via IFC Advisory Services; and (iii) standard-setting related to more rigorous health, safety, animal welfare, and traceability standards.

project_description: The proposed investment is a senior secured corporate loan to Viva Fresh sh.p.k (the “Company” or “Viva Fresh”) that will be used to fund the Company’s medium-term retail expansion plan. Founded in 2002, the Company is the largest food and non-food physical retailer in the Republic of Kosovo having a diversified portfolio of fast-moving consumer goods, fresh foods, fashion, footwear, and home goods categories. At the end of September 2019, the store network operating under the Viva Fresh Store banner comprised 63 units, of which one in Skopje, Republic of North Macedonia.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is fully owned by Mr. Xhevdet Rexhepi.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at €12.3 million and will be financed by a mix of debt and internal cash-flows. The proposed IFC investment is an 8-year €5 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Republic of Kosovo.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have a positive development impact, the most significant expected Project-level impact is derived from: (i) economy-wide, employment and supply chain development effects through the expansion of the Company retail network and; (ii) stakeholder effects through improve access of local lower and middle-income consumers to a more affordable and diverse selection of high-quality food products. Beyond the Project, IFC investment will help companies along the supply chain in the Republic of Kosovo to integrate into domestic supply chain.
additionality: With the proposed Project, IFC provides financial additionality through the provision of long-term financing that is not readily available in the market and non-financial additionality through standard setting. Financial Additionality: IFC will provide a long-term local-currency loan that will have a longer grace period than available from local banks. The loan will improve the Company's debt profile and enhance its access to outside complementary capital, thus reducing its domestic-bank dependence, which will make the Company less vulnerable to financial and domestic banking shocks. Moreover, IFC's long term financial commitment in local currency will allow the Company to continue with the expansion strategy amid an elevated political risk in the country, which negatively impacts the supply of credit. Non-financial Additionality: IFC will support the Company to (a) enhance its E&S practices and develop an E&S management system; and (b) improve its corporate governance and reporting standards. Additionally, IFC will provide technical knowledge and advice on green building standards and work with Viva Fresh to introduce EDGE green-building certification system in Kosovo. Moreover, IFC will share its global industry knowledge and experience to help Viva Fresh become even more resilient and innovative.

company_name: JSC INDORAMA KOKAND FERTILIZERS AND CHEMICALS
project_description: The project is to finance the privatization and modernization of JSC Kokand Superphosphate Plant, renamed post privatization to JSC Indorama Kokand Fertilizers and Chemicals (“IKF” or the “Company”), an outdated phosphate fertilizer plant located in Uzbekistan (the “Project”). The Company was acquired in 2019 by Indorama Holdings B.V., domiciled in the Netherlands, through direct negotiations with the Government of Uzbekistan. The Project will enable ICP to establish its first fertilizer production facility in Uzbekistan, which has natural feedstock to produce a wide range of fertilizers.
sponsor_shareholders: Indorama Holdings B.V. currently owns 95.54% of the Company. The balance belongs mainly to current and former Company employees. Indorama Holdings B.V. is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Indorama Corporation Pte. Ltd., domiciled in Singapore (“IRC”). IRC is the holding company of Indorama Group, one of Asia’s leading industrial conglomerates with wide interests in petrochemicals, fertilizers and related downstream businesses. IRC is wholly-owned for the benefit of Mr. S.P. Lohia and his family. Indorama Group was established in 1975 in Indonesia. It is the largest West Africa’s producer of petrochemicals, including olefins, polyolefins, phosphoric acid, phosphate fertilizers, ammonia, and urea, and one of the world’s largest producers of synthetic disposable gloves. Together with its associate, Indorama Ventures Public Company Limited, domiciled in Thailand, Indorama Group is the world’s largest producer of polyester and the leading producer of polyester feedstock (PX, PTA, and MEG) and man-made fibers. Its manufacturing activities are spread across 124 sites in 35 countries with a total sales volume of almost 21 million tons a year and annual sales value of over US$15 billion.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$45 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$10 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: IKF is located in the city of Kokand in the Fergana Region in eastern Uzbekistan.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have a positive development impact, contributing to market creation and generating economy-wide and employment effects. As the first majority privately-owned phosphorus fertilizer plant in the country, IKF is expected to stimulate competition and pave the way for further privatizations of state-owned chemical companies. The Project will also contribute to improving the efficiency and increasing the productivity of the manufacturing sector in Uzbekistan.
additionality: Financial additionality: IFC can provide an amount and tenor that is otherwise not available from private financing sources. Non-financial additionality: Standard Setting - IFC E&S expertise will ensure that the Project is implemented in an environmentally and socially responsible and sustainable way.
Company Name: JSC INDORAMA KOKAND FERTILIZERS AND CHEMICALS

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a €3.5 million A-loan from IFC for its own account. In addition, IFC as implementing entity of the Private Sector Window of the International Development Association (IDA PSW) is expected to provide a €3.5 million IDA PSW-loan (“blended concessional finance co-investment”) to support Société Africaine d’Ingrédients S.A. (SAF Ingredients or the Company), a French-Senegalese joint venture, in the development of a €18 million greenfield onion dehydration plant and 760-hectare nucleus farm near St Louis in Senegal. The A loan and the IDA PSW loan would be for capital expenditures and permanent working capital. The project entails decommissioning an existing onion dehydration plant (newly built in 2003 and closed in 2014) near Dijon, in France, and SAF Ingredients purchasing it for relocation to St. Louis. As the sponsor of the project, Dijon Céréales (a French agricultural cooperative) will manage the transfer of the plant with the technical support of Biaugeaud (a French engineering company), setting up the nucleus farm, and operating the plant in Senegal (the “Project”). This would be the first industrial-scale dehydration plant of its kind (no direct exposure of onions to the heat source) located in West and Central Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: The main sponsors are Dijon Céréales (a French agricultural cooperative) and Biaugeaud (a French engineering company). Other shareholders include some Senegalese nationals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is €18 million. IFC would provide €3.5 million A Loan for its own account and €3.5 million IDA PSW Loan from IFC acting as the implementing entity of IDA PSW..
location_description: The Project is located in the Gandiolais region in the Senegal River Valley, approximately 20 km from St. Louis and 275 km from Dakar in Senegal.
development_impact: Stakeholders - suppliers (commercial farmers & smallholder farmers). IFC expects the Project will increase market access for onion farmers and help raise their productivity. Economy-wide impacts - IFC expects the project will create 70 permanent and 20 temporary jobs at the factory and 50 direct and 200 seasonal jobs at the nucleus farm. In addition, the Project will build specialized skills regarding quality, food safety and maintenance in large, commercial and professionally-run, food processing operations, and raise standards by formalizing and structuring the onion supply chain with offtake contracts, price guarantees, and quality requirements.
additionality: Financial structure: the proposed IFC financing is for a long term loan. Resource mobilization: IFC is working closely with another development finance institution to provide financing to SAF Ingredients. Standard-setting: IFC would assist to put in place a corporate governance structure in line with global best practices. In addition, the dehydration plant would meet FSSC 22000, which would serve as a benchmark for the food processing sector in Senegal.

project_description: Maharashtra Hybrid Seed Company Ltd (“Mahyco India” or the “Sponsor”) is one of India’s leading seed producers and was the first to introduce hybrid seeds for millets, wheat, sorgrum, maize and sunflower and the first to commercialize insect tolerant cotton in India. Mahyco India’s subsidiary, Mahyco International Pte Ltd (“Mahyco International” or the “Company”) incorporated in Singapore, is the holding company for the Sponsor’s international operations and owns operating entities that sell cotton seeds in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and rice seeds in Vietnam and Bangladesh. The Company seeks to invest US$26 million to expand its cotton business in SSA and to expand its rice and eggplant business in Asia (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Mahyco International is fully owned by Mahyco India. Mahyco India was founded in 1964 by World Food Prize Laureate, late Dr. BR Barwale and is one of India’s largest seed companies. It is headquartered in Mumbai with a field research stations at Jalna, Maharashtra, India. It focuses on research, development and commercialization of a variety of seeds in India with a focus on producing quality seeds that ultimately improve farmer income.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the Project is estimated at US$26 million. IFC proposes to support the Project with US$20 million in funding, comprising of a US$10 million equity investment from IFC’s own account and a US$10 million equity investment in its capacity as Implementing Entity of the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP). The balance is proposed to be funded through internal accruals.
location_description: The Project compromises funding the technology costs, working capital needs, pre-commercialization costs and capex in several countries in SSA including Nigeria, Malawi, Kenya, Zambia, Tanzania and Burkina Faso and in Asia (including Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines, Laos and Cambodia).
development_impact: 1. Farmer Incomes: The Project is expected to improve farmer incomes in SSA through job creation for seedproducing contract farmers, most of whom are smallholders. Farmers in SSA will also benefit from betterquality planting material, which has the potential to significantly increase cotton yields in small holder farmsand reduce losses due to pest attacks, thus increasing farmer income. The Project is also expected to limithealth risks for cotton farmers as the use of insect tolerant seeds reduces the need for pesticides. 2. Food Security: The Company's high quality rice seeds are expected to result in 30-50% yield improvementsfor rice, a critical component of South-East Asian diets thus improving food security and benefiting end consumers.
additionality: 1. Access to Long Term Funding: IFC will support the Company by providing flexible, long-term funding. The Project requires regulatory approvals, farmer education, development of strong distribution networks andcritically, farmer adaptation, and therefore has a long gestation period and requires patient capital. 2. Knowledge sharing and capacity building: IFC will be able to share its extensive global experience in the agribusiness sectors as well as regional experience in SSA with the Company, particularly in capacity building to improve small holder productivity.

project_description: The Project consists of a greenfield development of a 100 percent retail facility in East Legon, a fast-growing suburb of Accra, Ghana (the “Project”). The Project is aimed at providing an A-Grade modern shopping centre, leisure and corporate business environment offering visitors the concept of a one-stop shopping experience. The Project will be owned A&C Development Company Limited (“A&C Development” or the “Company”).
sponsor_shareholders: The project will be owned by A&C Development Company Limited, a real estate development group in Ghana and owner of A&C Square Mall (‘A&C Mall’), a mixed-use mall with retail and office space. The shareholders of A&C Development are Mr. Andrew Asamoah (50 percent ownership), his wife Mrs. Cecilia Asamoah (10 percent ownership) and their four children; Mr. Frederick Asamoah (10 percent ownership), Mr. Edmund Asamoah (10 percent ownership), Ms. Vivian Asamoah (10 percent ownership) and Mr. Andrew Asamoah (10 percent ownership) (together, the “Sponsors”).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$6.9 million (including US$0.3 million of interest during the construction and pre-operating phase) and will be funded with a combination of equity from the Sponsor, and debt. IFC will provide a Senior Loan (A-Loan) of up to US$3 million. The proposed IFC financing will be structured as a senior secured loan and will have a tenor of up to 6 years (inclusive of a 2-year grace period on principal repayments).
location_description: The Project is being built on Jungle Road in East Legon, a fast-growing suburb of Accra, Ghana.
development_impact: The Project is expected to provide modern retail space that will be built around the concept of home improvement that currently does not exist in Ghana as well as to reduce the prices of and to provide more options for building materials and home improvement supplies. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater competitiveness by exhibiting the demand for this new type of retail store to other international retailers to expand into Ghana or into other African countries where there is currently no or limited supply of home improvement goods.
additionality: In terms of financial additionality, IFC will provide a longer-term loan to the Company that is critical for the construction of the mall expansion. Provided the current weakness of Ghanaian property market, similar term loans are not readily available from local banks. In terms of non-financial additionality, IFC will continue to work with the Company to improve corporate governance standards. IFC will also assist the Company to obtain the EDGE certification for its green building. Lastly, IFC will provide advisory service to improve food safety standards of the food and beverage outlets within the mall.

company_name: INDORAMA ELEME FERTILIZER AND CHEMICALS FZE
project_description: The Indorama Group (“Indorama” or the “Sponsor”) a long-standing IFC client in several countries, is one of the world’s fastest growing groups in the petrochemical and fibres business, with global business presence in 35 countries in Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas and more than 37,000 employees. In August 2006, Indorama International Finance Plc, UK (“Indorama International”) purchased a 75% equity stake in what was formerly known as Eleme Petrochemicals Company Limited (now known as Indorama Eleme Petrochemicals Limited – “IEPL”) under the Nigerian federal government’s privatization plan, to which IFC had acted as advisor. IFC also invested in Indorama to implement a turnaround program for Eleme’s olefins, polyethylene and polypropylene plants (IFC Project # 24802). In June 2016, Indorama successfully commissioned a 1.4 million metric tons per annum (MMtpa) urea fertilizer facility (including a captive ammonia facility) in Nigeria under its Indorama Eleme Fertilizer & Chemicals Limited (“IEFCL” or the “Company”) subsidiary, with investment from IFC’s own account, IFC-mobilized parallel lenders and other commercial lenders (IFC Project #30967). In March 2016 IFC made an additional investment in IEFCL to support construction of a jetty in the nearby Onne port for the export of fertilizer (IFC Project #38096). Having successfully commissioned the Line I Ammonia Urea fertilizer facility, Indorama also approved the construction of Line II, the second ammonia / urea fertilizer line, to expand the current capacity to 2.8 MMtpa; IFC provided a loan to this project as well (Project # 40420). Line II is currently under construction and is expected to be operational by 3rd quarter of 2021. IFC is considering a further investment in IEFCL of up to US$35 million (“MM”) for its own account and up to US$115MM in parallel loans to be mobilized from commercial banks and other DFIs, for construction of a feed conditioning unit (“FCU”), an add-on gas processing facility to Line II with capacity of 160 MM standard cubic feet per day (the “Project”). The FCU will recover carbon dioxide in the gas and shall also separate heavier by-products. This will ensure the supply of gas having consistent composition to Line II, and the heavier by-product will help increase polymer production in IEPL . The Project will essentially replicate, at a larger size, the recently completed FCU unit, located next to the IFC-supported Eleme Fertilizer I urea plant (project #30967) and used for the recovery of heavier by-products from feedstock supplied by a gas supplier. The first FCU, which was completed in 2018, was installed as part of the construction of Line I and is operating satisfactorily. FCU II will be located next to the existing FCU; the two units will share several facilities including the control room and flare systems. The Project is expected to be started up in April 2022, about a year after expected Line II start-up.
sponsor_shareholders: The Indorama Group is a long standing IFC client having its headquarters in Singapore. Since IFC’s first investment, it has grown into a global business entity with over US$16.7 billion in revenues.
