Indorama is the world’s largest producer of polyester and PET resins as well as one of the fastest growing global petrochemical producers with a presence in 35 countries. The group’s existing fertilizer plant in Nigeria is the world largest single stream Urea Fertilizer plant with a capacity to produce 2,300 tons of Ammonia per day and 4,000 tons of granulated urea per day.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$170 million and will be funded with an IFC A Loan of up to US$35 million, and up to US$115 million in B Loan syndication and parallel loans and US$ 20 million through Shareholder’s Loan/ Retained Earnings.
location_description: Port Harcourt, Nigeria
development_impact: The Project will promote (i) Economic diversification in Nigeria by increasing supply of raw materials converted to higher value products; (ii) Direct and indirect employment; (iii) Environmental impact through savings in feed usage and the reduction in CO2/GHG emissions; (iv) Integration of smaller downstream companies in the value chain, and possible development of additional plastic processors in Nigeria with the increase in polymer product availability.
additionality: IFC will (i) provide long-term financing for a tenor beyond what is generally available in the market, and critical in the capital-intensive petrochemicals sector; (ii) mobilize significant additional funding from other development finance institutions and commercial banks; (iii) continue to support a strategic client as it invests and grows in Sub-Saharan Africa; and (iv) provide IFC's in-house technical, insurance, and EH&S expertise.
Company Name: INDORAMA ELEME FERTILIZER AND CHEMICALS FZE

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A/B/MCPP loan financing package to Klabin S.A. (Klabin or the Company), an integrated Brazilian pulp and paper producer, to support the expansion of its paper producing capacity in Parana state.
sponsor_shareholders: Klabin's controlling shareholders are the Klabin and Lafer families. Together they hold more than 50% of the voting shares. Klabin has over 100 years in the pulp and paper industry and counts with an experienced board of directors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an up to US$390 million A/B/MCPP loan financing package composed of an up to USD120 million A Loan, up to USD220 million B Loan and up to USD50 million MCPP. The proceeds will be used to fund the expansion of the Company's kraftliner capacity (the Project).
location_description: The Project will be developed in the city of Ortigueira, state of Parana, Brazil.
development_impact: Economy-wide impact: The investment will support the increase in competitiveness of an integrated player in pulp and paper in Brazil, a sector that is a significant driver of economic growth in the country. The investment will promote the growth of economic activity and domestic value addition. It will create significant direct employment in the region, which will be complemented by positive indirect effect along the value chain. Environmental impacts: IFC's investment in Klabin will contribute to climate change mitigation as part of the financing will be allocated for co-generation, installation of a gasification plant, and wastewater treatment facilities. Market sustainability: The investment will facilitate broader sustainability improvements in the pulp and paper sector by demonstrating innovative practices, promoting the use of best available technology with respect to pollution controls, maintaining and expanding the use of key certifications.
additionality: - Long term financing: IFC is providing financing for its own account at longer tenors than is otherwise available in the market; - E&S standards: IFC will support the Company in the adoption of best practice E&S guidelines in line with IFC E&S Performance Standards; - Mobilization: IFC will be mobilizing long-term finance from commercial banks and MCPP, on conditions only possible as a result of the multilateral's preferred creditor status.

project_description: The proposed investment is an unfunded risk participation of USD 25 million in an uncommitted trade finance facility, made available and arranged by ING Belgique, Bruxelles, succursale de Lancy/Genève (ING) for ETG Agri Inputs FZE (ETG) (the “Facility”), an entity of the ETG group. Its purpose is to support ETG's imports, storage and sales of fertilizers.
sponsor_shareholders: ING: ING Group is the largest Dutch financial institution in terms of assets and 26th globally. With over 54,000 employees, ING operates in more than 40 countries globally, serving 38.4 million customers. The bank’s ratings are A+ / Aa3 / AA- with stable outlook. ETG: established in 1967 in Kenya, the ETG is a vertically integrated agricultural supply chain manager involved in the origination, procurement, warehousing, transport, agriculture processing and consumer products. It is active in over 25 African countries, as well as in India, China and South East Asia. It has additional trading and merchandising desks in Europe, the Americas and the Middle East. ETG employs more than 7,000 people globally. The major shareholders are the Sponsors, Ketan Patel, Mahesh Patel and Pradip Patel family trust and institutional investors Pembani Remgro (South Africa) and Mitsui & Co Ltd of Japan.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total amount of the Facility is estimated at USD 50 million, with a proposed IFC participation of up to USD 25 million.
location_description: Sub-Saharan Africa
development_impact: The renewed facility is expected to continue having the following development impacts: (i) support of commodity trade finance for importers/exporters in emerging markets; (ii) increased access to trade finance for critical commodities, especially in the agro-commodity sector in emerging market; and (ii) improved market integration by facilitating intra-regional and south-south trade for commodities and enhancing connectivity of real sector firms into value chains.
additionality: IFC's risk participation will help provide short-term liquidity to agri supply chain across Africa. IFC's support would continue encouraging greater activity in IDA countries and support smaller traders and processors.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: NSG UK Enterprises Limited (“NSG UK”, “Pilkington”, the “Borrower” or “the Company”), a leading global glass producer has invited IFC to consider providing up to US$80 million corporate loan to finance its investments in Argentina. Vidrieria Argentina S.A. (“VASA”), 51% owned by NSG UK and 49% by Saint-Gobain Cristalerias S.L. (Spain), will build a new float glass line with an anticipated initial production of 225,000 tons per annum (“tpa”) (“the Project”) on the Exaltation de la Cruz industrial site located 70 kilometers north-west of Buenos Aires.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1918 and headquartered in Tokyo, Nippon Sheet Glass Co. Ltd. (“NSG Group”) is a well-diversified global manufacturer of glass and glazing products for the automotive, architectural and technical glass markets. NSG Group ranks among the global top 3 producers in each of its global core markets, with strong presence in automotive applications. With manufacturing operations in about 30 countries and sales in over 100 countries, it employs approximately 27,000 people worldwide. NSG Group is listed on the Tokyo stock exchange. NSG UK Enterprises (“NSG UK” or the “Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of Nippon Sheet Glass Co., manufactures architectural and automotive glass products. With more than 150 years in business, the Company has 18 float glass lines, 16 automotive glass plants, and large downstream glass operations in over 20 countries throughout America, Europe and Asia. Saint-Gobain, NSG UK’s JV partner in VASA, is a European and worldwide leader in flat glass, high-performance materials, and construction products.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposed investment consists of a US$80 million A Loan to fund the Company’s US$222 million investment program in Argentina.
location_description: The Project will be located in an industrial site in Cardales, approximately 70 kilometers north-west of Buenos Aires.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have a positive development impact by (i) increasing access to high quality, affordable float glass for SMEs operating in the construction sector in Argentina and neighboring countries, which is likely to result in improved competitiveness and growth of local SMEs; (ii) contributing directly to Argentina's balance of trade by replacing imports with local competitive production by a leading local company; (iii) creating a large number of direct and indirect new jobs; and (iv) training and developing the skills of the newly recruited staff.
additionality: IFC expected additionality stems from its ability to engage strategically with the Company by offering: (i) long-term financing not readily available to the Company, suitable to the capital intensity and cyclicality of the industry and the payback period of the Project; (ii) non-commercial risk mitigation, since IFC's support has a signalling effect to other investors that the target country and sector are open to financially viable investments despite the high-risk perception; and (iii) long-term partnership, as IFC's long-term partnership with Pilkington has facilitated entry into emerging markets and in this case, expansion of its operations in a high-risk country.

company_name: MIDDLE EAST GLASS MANUFACTURING COMPANY S.A.E
sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: The IFC project under consideration will refinance Middle East Glass Manufacturing Company’s (“MEG” or “the Group”) existing long-term loans, denominated in both EGP and US$, and the ongoing capital expenditures program, including three major furnace rebuilds, resource efficiency improvements and the operational streamlining of the cullet processing operation (the “Project”). In addition to IFC funds of US$100 million, the Group will contribute up to US$26 million from internal cash generation, bringing total Project costs to US$126 million. The uses of funds are as follows: US$67 million for the refinancing and US$59 million for capex.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group is listed in the Egypt Stock exchange since 2002. The majority shareholder with 51.4% is MENA Glass Holding, a Cayman based investment vehicle for Mr. Abdulgalil Besher. He hails from a prominent Yemeni merchant family and is currently the sole owner of MENA Glass Holding. Gulf Capital has a shareholding of 35.9% in the business through two of its investment funds (MTM Packaging 1 &2). Gulf Capital is one of the largest alternative investment firms in the Middle East, managing US$4 billion across ten funds and investment vehicles.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering a proposed IFC financing of US$100 million in total including the following: (i) IFC A loan of US$30 million; (ii) IFC Trust fund loans of up to US$45 million, comprising of a US$22.5 million MCPP HKMA Loan and an additional US$22.5 million MCPP SAFE Loan; and (iii) B Loan/Parallel loan of up to US$25 million.
location_description: Investments under the Project will be made in the Group’s three operational facilities in Egypt: (i) MEG plant, situated in Nasr city, constructed in 1983, with one furnace totaling 84,963 tons per annum capacity for flint and green color, (ii) MEG Sadat, in Sadat city, constructed in 2007 and acquired by MEG in 2014, with two furnaces totaling 71,158 tons per annum capacity, for flint and amber color; and (iii) MGMG plant, situated in Moustord, constructed in 1968 and acquired by MEG in 2016 with three furnaces totaling 105,093 tons per annum in capacity for flint, green and amber color.
development_impact: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are: (i) economic diversification and economy-wide effects, (ii) resource efficiency via more efficient production processes, and (iii) regional customers benefits through improved access to more affordable, good quality glass bottle products and suppliers through capacity building. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Project will have a strong effect in the competitiveness of the regional glass market mainly across North and East Africa, which is facing competition from global players, by improving efficiency and quality standards, and introducing product diversity.
additionality: Financial additionality: IFC's role is evidenced by the prevailing terms that the Company has in the Egyptian market, which carry tenors two to five years shorter than the nine-year tenor that IFC will be providing to the Company. This tenor is in line with the Company's strategy of extending the average life of its financial debt to allow the Company to operate more sustainably. Additionally, IFC's mobilization will help bring additional long-term capital of up to US$70 million to the Company. This will be under IFC's syndications program including B1 or Parallel Loans and MCPP. Proposed nine-year maturity is not readily available in the market by commercial lenders. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC has been providing environmental and social expertise to ensure the Project's implementation and operation at par with the IFC Performance Standards and internationally accepted technical standards. This will enhance MEG's Environmental and Social practices. The IFC Resource efficiency team is also working with the client on potential energy and water savings through the implementation of an advisory project focusing on implementing several changes in its process to save energy and increase cullet use.
Company Name: MIDDLE EAST GLASS MANUFACTURING COMPANY S.A.E

project_description: The Project is to expand the extrusion technology based aquafeed capacity of Shenzhen Alpha Feed Group Company Limited (Alpha, or the Company) in China and Vietnam. The Project will help accelerate the aquaculture industry upgrades, in which IFC will invest up to US$60 million equivalent.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Pingchuan Wang, the Chairman, and Mr. Chuipeng Gu are the two founders and collectively own 75.09% in Alpha. The remaining shares are held by individuals through Alpha Management, a management holding entity.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is estimated to cost US$143 million in total, of which up to US$60 million will be funded by IFC, through an A Loan and an equity investment.
location_description: (i) Guangdong, Jiangxi and Hubei provinces of China, and (ii) Vietnam
development_impact: (i) Through the Project, the Company will reach and support the growth of about 80,000 additional aqua farmers. Most of them would be switching from other feed providers whose quality of feed or of technical support does not match Alpha's. While all input providers focus on extension work to build customer loyalty, Alpha's differentiating factor is the type of technical support provided that takes a more enterprise level approach focusing more on-farm profitability and sustainability. (ii) The Project is categorized as climate adaptation. Climate change related higher temperatures increase the risk from eutrophication that impacts water quality. The extruded feed, due to its characteristic of better water stability and consequent lower losses within the water system, reduces such risks. Additionally, better feed conversion ratio (FCR) supports lower impacts on water quality and addresses higher fish metabolism that is related to temperatures.
additionality: (i) Financing Structure: The proposed investment consists of a 6-year senior loan and an equity to Alpha to support its capacity expansion. The IFC loan will be the Company's first long-term loan, help it mitigate the refinancing risk and allowing flexibility in disbursement currency (can be USD or RMB) to accommodate purchases of raw materials and the international expansion. IFC as a shareholder signals a stamp of approval and can further enhance the Company's practices in corporate governance. (ii) Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: The Company is looking to benefit from IFC's strong regional network and sectoral expertise in animal feed and aquafeed, both on a standalone basis and as part of the integrated animal protein operations. (iii) Standard Setting: IFC is also supporting the Company in improving the sustainability of its operations, particularly through implementation of ESAP with regard to sustainable management of fish meal/oil supply chain.

project_description: The proposed project involves the second renewal of the existing syndicated funded risk sharing facility with Standard Chartered Bank (the “Bank” or “SCB”) for a trade finance facility of US$250 million to support ETC Group (“ETG”) agri commodity trader’s import of fertilizers in Sub-Saharan Africa and export of cash and food grains, storage. IFC’s investment amount will be up to US$10 million. The Project will support the import, storage and sales of fertilizers in SSA countries such as Benin, Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Ivory Coast, and export of agri commodities. Commodities financed by the project are bought from mostly smallholder farmers in SSA and sold to wholesalers, cooperatives, NGOs and governments in various IDA countries and into the international market. This project is linked to GWFP ETG SCB III https://disclosures.ifc.org/#/projectDetail/SII/42889
sponsor_shareholders: Standard Chartered Bank: Headquartered in London, Standard Chartered is a leading international banking group, with more than 86,000 employees, representing 130 nationalities and a 160-year history in some of the world’s most dynamic markets. It is one of the world's most international banks, with over 1,000 branches, offices and outlets in 60 countries across the globe. The group earns around 90% of its income and profits in Asia, Africa and the Middle East across Corporate, Institutional and Retail banking. As of December 31, 2018, Standard Chartered had total assets of US$ 689 billion, and total equity of US$50.4 billion. Standard Chartered PLC is listed on the London and Hong Kong Stock Exchanges as well as the Bombay and National Stock Exchanges in India and ranks among the top 30 companies in the FTSE-100 by market capitalization. As at 31 December 2018, Temasek Holdings (Private) Limited is the only shareholder that has an interest of more than 10 per cent (15.77%) in the Company’s issued ordinary share capital carrying a right to vote at any general meeting. The bank’s long-term ratings are A / A1 / A+ with stable outlook. ETG: established in 1967 in Kenya, the ETG is a vertically integrated agricultural supply chain manager
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost will be up to US$250 million with IFC’s investment of up to US$10 million in the form of a funded participation.
location_description: Standard Chartered is headquartered in London, United Kingdom, and has offices in 60 countries. The Bank’s Trade Risk Distribution is managed out of its Singapore hub. The proposed project will involve trade transactions mainly in east, south and west Africa.
development_impact: The renewed facility is expected to continue having the following development impacts: (i) support of commodity trade finance for importers/exporters in emerging markets; (ii) increased access to trade finance for critical commodities, especially in the agro-commodity sector in emerging market; and (ii) improved market integration by facilitating intra-regional and south-south trade for commodities and enhancing connectivity of real sector firms into value chains
additionality: IFC's risk participation will help provide short-term liquidity to agri supply chain across Africa. IFC's support would continue encouraging greater activity in IDA countries and support smaller traders and processors.

project_description: The proposed investment is an A Loan of up to US$11 million to Grainpulse Limited (Grainpulse or the Company) in Uganda. The Company engages in coffee and grain supply chain management, human and animal nutrition, and is also the pioneer in local fertilizer blending in the country. The investment will support the Company’s ongoing US$17.6 million expansion program which will be complemented by an advisory services program to support smallholder farmers, agro-input dealers and retailers in the country (the Project). The Project may be supported by IFC as the implementing entity of the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is an existing joint venture between Savannah Commodities Company Limited (56% shareholding) and K+S AG (44%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is an A Loan of up to US$11 million to Grainpulse.
location_description: The proposed investment will finance the Company’s working capital and capital expenditure for the expansion of (i) fertilizer blending and warehouse facilities in Mukono; (ii) grain, flour and animal feed milling facilities in Mukono; (iii) rural grain collection centers; and (iv) coffee facilities in Kampala, Uganda.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is an increase in the supply and delivery of quality crop-specific fertilizer for smallholder farmers in Uganda. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that its investment will increase competitiveness in the country's fertilizer sector by changing the market structure through demonstration and replication effects, capacity building and skill development.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in two forms: (i) financing structure through funding not readily available in Uganda; and (ii) knowledge, innovation and capacity building. Grainpulse chose to work with IFC because of the size and tenor of the IFC facility and IFC's support to develop extension services for smallholder farmers.

project_description: Future Consumer Limited (FCL or the Company) is an integrated food and Home & Personal Care (HPC) company that markets a portfolio of brands. These brands are backed by a network of agricultural commodities sourcing centers and manufacturing facilities across India. FCL is publicly listed on Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE). The Company plans to raise capital for (i) investment in development and expansion of manufacturing and processing operations for food and HPC products; (ii) expansion of its rural distribution network; (iii) working capital requirements; and (iv) meet upcoming debt repayments (Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The founder of Future Group (comprising various entities in retail and associated businesses including FCL, Future Retail Limited, Future Lifestyle Fashions Limited and others), Mr. Kishore Biyani and his various intermediate investment entities (Sponsor), control 46.3 percent of FCL. Other key institutional investors include Arisaig Partners Asia (Pte) Ltd (7 percent ownership), Verlinvest S.A. (7.3 percent ownership), and Proterra Investment Partners (7.6 percent ownership).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project Cost is about INR 3.5 billion. IFC is to invest up to INR 2,100 million in FCL in the form of Compulsorily Convertible Debentures (CCDs) to partly finance the Project. Another key investor in the Project is Verlinvest S.A., which will invest up to INR 700 million and the Sponsor will contribute INR 700 million.
location_description: The Project will be carried in various parts of India. All facilities in the Project are existing facilities including the Company’s state-of-the-art integrated food park at Tumkur Region, Karnataka.
development_impact: Stakeholders Impact: IFC expects that the Project, through the introduction of new products and an increase in production, will increase the procurement of food produce sourced from local farmers, thus increasing farmer incomes. The penetration of FCL's wholesale centers in rural areas combined with its retail management platform will benefit small retailers through the introduction of technology and infrastructure. IFC also expects long-term benefits for end-consumers in terms of safer and higher-quality food products and lower product prices. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater market competitiveness via demonstration and replication.
additionality: (i) IFC's own account equity will provide FCL with patient capital required for its profitable growth in a competitive sector. (ii) IFC's potential advisory services will help FCL implement best practices to enhance food safety.

IFC’s investment amount will be up to US$40 million. The Project will support the purchase, storage and sales of agri commodities and fertilizers in SSA countries such as Malawi, Benin, Kenya, Tanzania, etc. Commodities financed by the project are bought from mostly smallholder farmers in SSA and sold to wholesalers, cooperatives, NGOs and governments in various IDA countries and into the international market.

total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost will be up to US$80million with IFC’s investment of up to US$40 million in the form of a funded participation.

company_name: COOPERATIVA NACIONAL DE PRODUCTORES DE LECHE
project_description: Cooperativa Nacional de Productores de Leche (“Conaprole”) is Uruguay’s leading dairy producer and one of the lowest cost producers in the world. Conaprole has eight production plants in which they produce a wide range of dairy products including liquid milk, milk powder, yogurt, cheese, butter, ice cream, and milk by-products, both for the local and export market. The Project consists on: i) expansion of milk powder capacity at its Villa Rodriguez plant to produce more value-added products; ii) revamp the plants’ waste water treatment plants; and iii) replace the existing boiler system with a more efficient one.
sponsor_shareholders: Conaprole is a Uruguayan cooperative established in 1936 and owned by about 1,900 dairy farmers
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$110 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$60 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Villa Rodriguez (Plant #8) is located in the Department of San Jose, about 100 km west of Montevideo.
development_impact: Farmers Reached: The Project will result in a 16% additional milk intake capacity for Conaprole, which would translate into large production volumes of raw milk for the cooperative members. The production of high value-added products such as infant formula will allow Conaprole to generate better returns for its membership base. Environmental outcomes: Conaprole has a few areas of improvement on the E&S front (ammonia safety, occupational safety and health, waste water treatment). IFC's continued engagement together with the Cooperative's strong commitment will contribute to the adoption of best industry practices.
additionality: Standard Setting and Best Practices: The proposed Project would allow IFC to continue to provide E&S assistance and advice. Conaprole has made significant progress on the E&S front, and IFC's involvement will help Conaprole achieve full compliance with Performance Standards. Long Term Partnership: IFC is a key relationship for Conaprole as it can provide longer tenors than available in the market, as well as, support on enhancing E&S practices.
Company Name: COOPERATIVA NACIONAL DE PRODUCTORES DE LECHE

project_description: The Project is to provide an export pre-financing facility to BIOVANILLA SARLU (“Biovanilla”) for the purchasing and processing of vanilla beans for exports to international offtakers.
sponsor_shareholders: Biovanilla is a company founded in 2017 and owned by Mr. Eric Sinikely Patine. Biovanilla has developed a diversified network of offtakers and is an important player in in the vanilla sector in the Sava region.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, acting for its own account and in its capacity as implementing entity of the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP), is considering investing up to $15.75m in a 3-year short-term export pre-financing facility with annual clean up.
location_description: Biovanilla facilities are located in Sambava and Ambanja in the Diana region, North of Madagascar.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have a GOOD development impact - At the Project level: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is the growth in the exporter's sourcing network, combined with an increase in producer vanilla yields and certification. - At the Market level: IFC anticipates its investment in the Malagasy vanilla supply chain, coupled with the activities of IFC Advisory, will encourage systemic changes to the vanilla market in the country by increasing sustainability, through replication and demonstration effects and building capacity and skills.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in three forms: (i) Financing structure: The proposed pre-export facility is not readily available in Madagascar. This financing structure will build the exporter's bankability track record which is expected to lead to improved access to finance. (ii) Standard-setting: IFC is supporting standard-setting in the vanilla value chain in Madagascar by assisting the Exporters to develop internal audit systems to assess, monitor, and mitigate potential risks and impacts of child labor and deforestation in its supply chains, in line with IFC E&S Performance Standards. (iii) Knowledge, innovation and capacity-building: IFC Advisory Services is supporting the exporter to increase the production and quality of certified and traceable vanilla.

project_description: The Project is to provide an export pre-financing facility to Ramanandraibe Exportation (“Ramex”) for the purchasing and processing of vanilla beans for exports to international offtakers.
sponsor_shareholders: Ramex was founded in 1973 and is part of the Ramanandraibe Group, itself established in 1927. It is one of the country’s historical and major vanilla exporters.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, acting for its own account and in its capacity as implementing entity of the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP), is considering investing up to $10.5m in a 3-year short-term export pre-financing facility with annual clean up.
location_description: Ramex facilities are located in six cities: Sambava, Antalaha, Ambanja, Andapa, Maroantsetra, Mananara Nord, but all conditioning and packing is done in two centers: Antalaha or Sambava in the SAVA Region, north-eastern Madagascar.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have a GOOD development impact - At the Project level: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is the growth in the exporter's sourcing network, combined with an increase in producer vanilla yields and certification. - At the Market level: IFC anticipates its investment in the Malagasy vanilla supply chain, coupled with the activities of IFC Advisory, will encourage systemic changes to the vanilla market in the country by increasing sustainability, through replication and demonstration effects and building capacity and skills.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in three forms: (i) Financing structure: The proposed pre-export facility is not readily available in Madagascar. This financing structure will build the exporter's bankability track record which is expected to lead to improved access to finance. (ii) Standard-setting: IFC is supporting standard-setting in the vanilla value chain in Madagascar by assisting the exporter to develop internal audit systems to assess, monitor, and mitigate potential risks and impacts of child labor and deforestation in its supply chains, in line with IFC E&S Performance Standards. (iii) Knowledge, innovation and capacity-building: IFC Advisory Services is supporting the exporter to increase the production and quality of certified and traceable vanilla.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a financing package of up to €2.5 million to Mali Shi SA (“Mali Shi” or the “Company”), a greenfield shea nuts processing company headquartered in Bamako, Mali. Mali Shi will produce shea butter for export market. The Company will employ over 83 people will collect shea nuts from more than 120,000 women collectors in Mali. The project consists of an investment plan to (i) construct a greenfield shea nuts processing plant in Mali, with an installed capacity of 30,000 tons of shea nuts, (ii) the construction of shea nuts storage warehouses; (iii) the purchase of logistical equipment; and (iii) a working capital line (the “Project”). The Project will also be supported by the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (“GAFSP”), a multilateral mechanism launched by the G20 with the purpose of scaling-up support to help less developed countries alleviate poverty and improve food security, a program implemented by IFC.
sponsor_shareholders: OMNIUM MALI, which owns 58.5% of the Company’s shareholding, is a leading industrial player in Mali, producing batteries, since 1996. OMNIUM MALI is a subsidiary of OMNIUM INVEST, an investment vehicle established in Mali, set up by Karim Ghammache, its founder and 90% owner, to own all of his shares in different companies. SOATAF, which owns 6.5% of the Company’s shareholding, is a Malian company specialized in the export of several commodities including shea nuts, sesame, arabic gum and peanuts. SOATAF’s main sponsor is Mr Modibo Tala, one of the biggest shea traders in Mali, who has developed a collection network of 25,000 women. ECODEV VENTURE, which owns 35% of the Company’s shareholding, is an investment trust owned by Endeavor mining, a medium-size mining company, established to invest in projects which can provide significant sustainable positive impact in area close to their mining operation in Mali, Burkina Faso and Cote d’Ivoire.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at approximately €5.8 million. IFC is proposing to participate with an A Loan of up to €1.25 million on its own account and a GAFSP Loan of up to €1.25 million in its capacity as the implementing entity of GAFSP.
location_description: The investments will be made in the district of Bamako, where the Mali Shi’s plant will be built.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is the increased income for ~120,000 new and existing shea nuts collectors in Mali, primarily women. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates the investment will increase competitiveness in Mali's shea nuts sector through demonstration and replication effects, and capacity building and skills.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in three forms: (i) financing beyond what is available in the market, (ii) standard setting for the Company and sector regarding E&S, and (iii) knowledge, capacity building and innovation related to shea nuts cooperatives, food safety and energy efficiency. IFC's additionality stems from the integrated package of investment and advisory services.

company_name: DEEPAK FERTILISERS AND PETROCHEMICALS CORPORATION LIMITED
project_description: Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corporation Limited and its subsidiaries (“DFPCL”, or the “Company”) is an industrial chemicals and fertilizers company engaged in manufacturing and trading of Iso-propyl alcohol (IPA), Nitric Acid, Methanol, Technical Ammonium Nitrate (TAN), compound fertilizers and other chemicals. Smartchem Technologies Limited (“STL”) is a 100% subsidiary of DFPCL. Deepak also plans to expand its ammonia production capacity through Performance Chemiserve Private Limited (“PCPL”), a subsidiary of STL.
sponsor_shareholders: S.C. Mehta and family with related entities (51.2%). The Company is publicly listed and the balance is held by financial institutional investors and general public.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated to be around US$160 million. IFC’s investment package of up to US$60 million will be used to finance the IPA project in DFPCL, and N2O abatement facilities and maintenance capital expenditures and working capital requirements of STL’s fertilizer business.
location_description: DFPCL’s manufacturing sites in Taloja, Maharashtra and Panipat, Haryana. These facilities / expansions under the project will be developed inside DFPCL’s existing plants.
development_impact: Access: The Project will help the Company ramp up the production and distribution of specialty fertilizers in India. The Project will also allow Deepak to increase its IPA production capacity in India by 100,000 MTPA. Climate Change and Resource Efficiency: This Project is expected to contribute to climate change mitigation by net reduction of GHG emissions. This will be achieved by installing N2O catalyst conversion devices at all existing Nitric Acid manufacturing processes at Taloja. Competitiveness: IFC's engagement will likely contribute to increase competitiveness in the fertilizer sector as the Company works on innovation and expanding the product offering in the market.
additionality: Innovative Financing Structure and Instruments: IFC will finance through a mix of quasi-equity instruments. Standard setting: IFC will assist the Company with a greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction plan, including the establishment of the N2O catalyst conversion devices and formulate and implement an Environmental and Social action plan (ESAP). Knowledge, expertise and innovation: Leveraging IFC's global knowledge and networks, and the value of IFC's region and industry-specific insights, will the help the Company its growth and expansion plans.
Company Name: DEEPAK FERTILISERS AND PETROCHEMICALS CORPORATION LIMITED

project_description: The proposed project involves IFC investing debt of up to US$ 30 million, and equity in US$ equivalent of up to INR 542 million in Mahansaria Tyres Private Limited (“MTPL” or the “Company”). The proposed investment will support the Company in setting up a greenfield off-highway tyre (OHT) manufacturing facility in India (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: MTPL is owned by Ashok Mahansaria, Yogesh Mahansaria and Yogesh Investments Private Limited (YAIPL), erstwhile sponsors of Balkrishna Industries and Alliance Tyre Group, with over 25 years’ experience in the OHT segment. The Company will manufacture off-highway tyres primarily for use in agriculture and construction industry globally.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Cost for phase 1 which will involve setting up 40,000 MT capacity (Phase 1) is ~US$ 107 million. This will be funded by debt of up to US$ 54 million, of which IFC will invest up to US$ 30 million in the form of an A Loan, mobilize up to US$ 24 million in the form of a Parallel Loan, and invest up to INR 542 million as equity in the Company.
location_description: The Project will be located in Panoli district in Gujarat, India
development_impact: Economywide and employment effects: a) Exports and value addition: The Company estimates exports to account for 70-80 percent of sales and contribute to India's forex earnings. The Project will support value-addition in the domestic rubber product industry b) Employment: The Project is expected to create significant direct local employment by creating 1,500 additional jobs in phase 1 alone. Stakeholders Impact c) Access to affordable customized agriculture tires to improve mechanization in agriculture and thereby, productivity. Customized tire products (OHT) lead to better traction, lower downtime and result in an increase in higher productivity. The Project will increase availability of value brand products (defined as the brands that are able to offer a quality competitive product at a lower price), which are more affordable than the regular customized tires. d) Expanding outreach to more farmers and low-income states (LIS) with better extension services: The Company plans to onboard and extend attractive credit terms to distributors and wholesalers, who are mostly SMEs, to further market the product and enhance awareness of the use of customized tires to farmers. e) Better productivity through investments in modern machineries and training; The Company aims to set their level of productivity to be higher than the India industry average and more aligned with the industrial benchmark in Europe and North America, through improvement in machineries and training. Market Outcomes: f) Competitiveness: Increased penetration of value brand OHT in India: Penetration of OHT in India is still relatively lower compared to developed markets such as EU and North America and other emerging markets outside. The Indian OHT market is less mechanized and more price sensitive due to low farm incomes and as a result the product range in Indian markets is not as specialized as in the EU and North America, where more application specific solutions are available. IFC anticipates more investments in this sector will happen, increasing the degree of customization and product range available, thus resulting in an increased penetration of OHT in India. g) Integration by way of increased participation by Indian OHT tire players in the global market: The size of OHT segment globally is still relatively small compared to the entire tires industry at ~10% of total tire industry. At present, value brands hold around approximately 30% of the global market share, with Indian players holding half of this market share. Indian players such as the Company have the advantage to produce more of value brand segment of OHT tires, given conversion costs in India are lower than in any other manufacturing bases. This Project will demonstrate the competitiveness of Indian players in the global market and increase the overall share of Indian value brands.
additionality: a) IFC will be providing an USD corporate loan with tenor of 10 years including a sufficient grace period of 4 years, which is relatively longer than what is readily available in the market. b) IFC will mobilize parallel loan of up to USD 24 million on similar terms. This gives the Company access to a different fundraising channel from institutional financiers and develop a more diversified investor base c) IFC's investment will provide validation of a greenfield business plan and the growth prospect of the sector. This will send a positive signaling effect to other investors on the soundness of the Project and help attract investors for the current and future financing stages d) Standard setting through provision of expertise in environmental and social standards which could also have a demonstration effect on the overall sector.

project_description: Apetit (or “the Company”) is a leading meat trader and processor in Kosovo providing industrials and consumers with frozen meat, fresh meat cuts, and, cured meat products such as sujuk and prosciutto. Apetit seeks to grow and modernize its operations. To do so, the Company is planning to (i) establish a large and modern slaughterhouse, which will comply with EU regulations on food safety, (ii) integrate upstream by setting up a cattle farm, which will partly replace Apetit’s imports, and, (iii) powering all its facilities (the slaughterhouse, the farm and the meat processing plant) with solar panels.
sponsor_shareholders: Apetit is owned by the Ferizi family: Destan Ferizi and his five sons, Avni Ferizi, Sami Ferizi, Remzi Ferizi, Fehmi Ferizi and Gani Ferizi. The family has been operating in the meat business in Kosovo since 1947.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is €8.1 million out of which IFC will fund €2.5 million or 31%.
location_description: Apetit’s facilities are located in Milloshev, 15km away from Pristina.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcome is the provision of safe meat and associated products to the domestic consumers and expanded income opportunities for the local farmers. In addition, the Project will contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of Kosovo's meat processing sector by showcasing modern production practices and international food safety standards, which would be disseminated though demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC additionality in this Project stems from its ability to provide long-term funding that is not always available in the market as well as extensive technical support and capacity building for the Company in the areas of food safety, financial management, and corporate governance.

company_name: KENYA TEA DEVELOPMENT AGENCY HOLDINGS LTD
project_description: The proposed investment is an A Loan of up to US$10 million to Kenya Tea Development Agency Holdings Ltd (KTDA). The A Loan will support the expansion strategy of KTDA in logistics business and finances a US$17.7 million greenfield inland container depot (ICD) project that comprises of 6.7 acres of container stacking yard, 0.9 acres of covered warehouses, and auxiliary facilities in Nairobi (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: KTDA, an existing IFC client, is the largest tea business in East Africa. The Group emerged from the privatization of the Kenya Tea Development Authority in 2000. KTDA services over 610,000 smallholder tea farmers, who are suppliers as well as shareholders of 54 separate tea companies owning a total of 69 tea factories. Smallholder farmers under the auspices of the Group account for over 60 percent of national tea production.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$17.7 million. The proposed investment is an A Loan of up to US$10 million to KTDA.
location_description: The ICD is located in a commercial area in Embakasi in Nairobi, adjacent to the ICD owned by Kenya Ports Authority (KPA).
development_impact: The Project develops cargo freight logistics infrastructure in the city of Nairobi, which improves capacity and affordability of services. At the market level, the Project contributes to improving integration of the logistics networks centered around the Port of Mombasa and the new standard gauge railway (SGR) line linking Mombasa to Nairobi, by improving the Port's hinterland footprint and connectivity.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the Project comes in two forms: (i) financing structure through funding terms not readily available in Kenya; and (ii) non-commercial risk mitigation, including trusted partnerships. IFC will also leverage its technical expertise in logistics to provide advice on the Group's business strategy.
Company Name: KENYA TEA DEVELOPMENT AGENCY HOLDINGS LTD

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: Pasabahçe Egypt Glass Manufacturing S.A.E. (the “Company” or “Pasabahce Egypt”) is a glassware company incorporated in Egypt following the acquisition of a local glassware manufacturer in 2017. The proposed IFC investment is up to US$30 million to support (i) the renovation and upgrade of existing plant and furnace including a cold repair and (ii) working capital and refinancing needs of the plant. (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are Sise ve Cam Fabrikalari A.S. (“Sisecam Group”) and Pasabahce Cam Sanayii ve Ticaret A.S. (“Pasabahce”). Pasabahce Egypt is indirectly owned by Pasabahce through its subsidiaries Pasabahce Investment B.V. (93%), Nude Design Investment B.V. (5%), Istanbul Investment B.V. (1%) and Nude Glass Investment B.V. (1%). Pasabahce Investment B.V. is entirely owned by Pasabahce and was established as the platform company for Pasabahce’s overseas operations and hence, owns 100% stake in other minority shareholders of Pasabahce Egypt as listed above. Pasabahce is a leading Turkish glassware producer, jointly owned by Sisecam (84.6%), European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (“EBRD”) (14.9%) and Islamic Development Bank (0.5%). Engaged in the production and distribution of flat glass, tableware, glass containers, glass fiber and associated products worldwide, Sisecam is Turkey’s leading glass manufacturer and a prominent player in the global glass industry. Sisecam is 75% owned by Turkiye Is Bankasi and its related entities and the rest of the shares are publicly traded on Istanbul Stock Exchange with a total market capitalization of c. US$2.2 billion as of April 8, 2019.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is expected to be US$50 million and the proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to US$30 million which will be provided in two tranches. The Loans will be used to finance the upgrade investments and shorter-term working capital needs of Pasabahce Egypt.
location_description: The Project is located in the industrial zone of 6th of October City, 45km southwest of Cairo, Egypt.
development_impact: Employment Creation and Skill Transfer: The Project is expected to create more than 300 direct jobs and 100 indirect jobs in Egypt. The Project will also enable skill development of the local workforce through Pasabahce's transfer of its global know-how and labor standards. Increased Economic Returns: The Project will promote Egypt's export activities and foreign exchange generation through increased production levels and export-oriented sales. Improved overall standards: The Project is expected to have a positive impact on the environment given improved energy and cost efficiency as well as cleaner production that is envisaged from renovation investments. The Project will also contribute to the improvement of existing production thanks to Pasabahce's transfer and implementation of modern production methods which is expected to result in higher value-added products.
additionality: Long-term Financing: The proposed IFC investment will enable Pasabahce Egypt to address its longer-term funding need in an environment where long-term financing is scarce. E&S Support & Energy Efficiency: IFC will share E&S best practices & help the Company improve its energy efficiency policies.

project_description: Engro Vopak Terminal Ltd. (“EVTL”, or “the Company”) owns and operates the largest terminal and storage facility for bulk liquid chemicals and Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) in Pakistan. It is involved in the handling and storage of Para-Xylene, Acetic Acid, Ethylene Di Chloride (EDC), Vinyl Chloride Monomer, Ethylene, Mono Ethylene Glycol, Phosphoric Acid and LPG. The proposed investment will support the Company to: i) expand LPG storage capacity by 6,000 tons; ii) expand EDC handling facility; iii) undertake 3-year terminal rehabilitation program and; iv) install solar panels (The “Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Engro Corporation Limited (“ECorp” or the “JV Partner”) and Royal Vopak N.V. (“Vopak” or the “JV Partner”) of Netherlands are the joint venture partners each holding 50% shareholding in the Company. ECorp is one of Pakistan’s largest and professionally managed conglomerates with business interests in fertilizers, foods, chemical storage & handling, trading, energy and petrochemicals. Its main shareholder is Dawood Hercules Corporation, which is owned by Dawood family and associated companies. ECorp is listed on Pakistan Stock Exchange. The remaining shareholding is distributed among various institutions and general public. Vopak is engaged in the storage and handling of oil products, liquid chemicals, gases, bio fuels and vegetable oils through 69 terminals in 25 countries. It is listed on the Amsterdam stock exchange. Vopak’s main shareholder, HAL Trust is also listed on Amsterdam Stock Exchange and is majority owned by Van der Vorm family. The remaining shareholding of Vopak and Hal Trust is distributed among various institutions and general public.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$40 million and IFC will provide an” A” Loan of up to US$40 million to fund the project.
location_description: The Project will be located in Pakistan.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have the following development impacts: a) Environmental sustainability - the Project is expected to support energy transition in Pakistan towards cleaner fuels by increasing access to reliable supply of LPG, which has low indoor health hazards and greenhouse gas emissions relative to alternative conventional fuels like firewood, kerosene or charcoal. The Proposed Project will allow the Company to implement 3-year terminal rehabilitation capex program covering some high priority scheduled maintenance and terminal rehabilitation that is essential for its continued safe and efficient operations. b) Stakeholders Effects: The Project will have economy-wide effects by substantially alleviating current deficit of LPG in Pakistan and improving access to cleaner fuels for rural households, as well as automotive sector consumers. Extension of LPG capacity will also provide additional business opportunities for thousands of Small and Medium Enterprises operating in the downstream LPG distribution business, such as LPG cylinder distributors, fueling stations and others. c) Market creation: The Project will result in systemic changes to the existing LPG market in Pakistan through implementation of infrastructure to import, store and market larger quantities of LPG which is expected to substantially increase the local availability of LPG.
additionality: The financing will provide the Company with access to critical long-term funding in an environment where such funding is scarce. IFC will also advise the Company on designing and implementing investments aimed at improving efficiency of the terminal and reducing its energy consumption and emissions.

project_description: Project is to construct and operate a resort hotel, which includes a multi-purpose venue, located in the rural outskirts of Lusaka. The hotel will be an upscale 249-room greenfield development operating under the Protea Hotels by Marriot brand while the multi-purpose venue will have capacity for up to 2,500 persons.
sponsor_shareholders: The project Sponsor and Shareholder is Union Gold Zambia Ltd (UGZ or the Sponsor), a repeat client of IFC. UGZ through its majority owned subsidiary Protea Hotel Zambia (PHZ) is the largest hospitality provider in Zambia. They have successfully executed eight Protea greenfield hotel projects across Zambia, with a total of 612 rooms. The Sponsor also owns a construction company, Velos Enterprise Ltd, which was the EPC for all PHZ greenfield projects.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is US$29.6 million. IFC’s proposed investment is up to US$9.0 million of debt in the form of an A-Loan.
location_description: Project will be located in the Kasisi area, Chongwe district, Lusaka, Zambia.
development_impact: The most significant development impact is on stakeholders, with local employees and suppliers benefitting from training, employment and growth opportunities. The Project will promote enhanced competitiveness in the tourism/hospitality sector by introducing a new concept in the country that combines a hotel and a large multi-purpose venue. It will also open a new segment in Zambia's tourism industry, contributing to the desired economic diversification from mineral raw materials.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment provides both financial and non-financial additionality. The critical type of financial additionality is the financing structure proposed, this includes the provision of longer-term capital. Whereas, the non-financial additionality includes the: (i) provision of advisory services, including food safety programs and community development initiatives; (ii) industry expertise and advice, and (iii) standard setting, particularly related to corporate governance, green building and E&S.

project_description: The proposed investment would support 3B Group of Hotels (“3B” or “the Company”), one of Rwanda’s leading ecotourism groups, to expand its network of mid-tier lodging in Rwanda with investment in: (i) the completion of a 30-room Akagera Safari Camp in the Lakes District in the Eastern Province of Rwanda, (ii) the acquisition, refurbishment and putting into operation of the Nobilis Hotel, a 61-room hotel in Kigali and (iii) the introduction of a modern management information system (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The 3B Group consists of five separate companies, each 50-50% owned by Mr. Paul Muvunyi and his wife Mrs. Yvonne Impundu, a family of Rwandan entrepreneurs.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is US$13.6mn. IFC is proposed to provide a loan package of up to US$7.7 million to support the Project. The package will comprise: (i) a senior IFC A loan of up to US$3.0 million and (ii) a parallel loan from a development financing institution of up to US$3 million. In addition, IFC acting as Implementing Entity of IDA18 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility will provide a US$1.7 million concessional subordinated loan to help create quality jobs in Rwanda’s ecotourism sector of the underdeveloped eastern region.
location_description: Kigali, Rwanda and Kayonza District, Eastern Province, Rwanda
development_impact: - Jobs: The expansion will create new direct jobs as well as temporary jobs during its construction period, and a support a number of indirect jobs through its supply chain. Direct employees will benefit from training, contributing to the upskilling of the country's workforce, as the Project is expected to hire low skilled, low income local employees, and train them to gain basic skill sets. -Local Linkages and Community Engagement: 3B is committed to developing local communities and expects to source as much as possible through local suppliers, to train its suppliers to help them reach required quality standards. Some of the activities organized by 3B during its circuits (e.g. paid visits to local villages and bringing tourists to local markets and cooperatives) will create additional business opportunities for local entrepreneurs. Also, 3B is expecting to continue its community engagement programs with generous donations, support to the vulnerable and the promotion of football among the local youth. -Tax Benefits: The Project will result in fiscal benefits through increased tax generation.
additionality: Financial Additionality: IFC will provide and mobilize a loan package of the tenor and repayment profile that are not readily available for the Group in Rwanda. This will enable 3B to proceed timely with its expansion, as well as to ensure a stable financial performance of the Group. Non-Financial Additionality: - Corporate Governance (CG) Improvement Plan: IFC's CG team has performed a review of the Group's governance practices and proposed a comprehensive CG improvement plan; - Financial Advisory: IFC's Financial Advisory team has performed a review of the Group's financial management function and has prepared a proposal for a comprehensive intervention with the goal to structure, formalize and professionalize the function. The intervention will catalyze the strengthening of 3B's financial management team, the adoption an appropriate MIS, and the appropriate financial reporting, including the introduction of the practice of preparing audited IFRS-based financial statements; - E&S: IFC's E&S expertise will ensure that the Project be implemented based on the highest relevant E&S standards through time-bound requirements of the agreed ESAP; - Insurance: will help the Group in the structuring and adoption of an effective insurance policy. - Green Building: A preliminary review of the technical drawing of a building housing an individual guest room at Akagera by the green building consultant suggests that there is energy savings potential for energy savings improvements. IFC will engage with 3B to pursue the realization of this potential. The engagements described above translate into strong support for the Group in its transition from an informally-managed company to a professionally-run business.

project_description: AMRU Rice Cambodia Ltd. (“AMRU” or the “Company”) is a leading rice processor and exporter in Cambodia. Its products include fragrant jasmine, organic and brown rice, sourced from rice millers and producers across the country. AMRU is expanding its business volume and, with the help of IFC, seeks to increase its working capital funding and refinance short-term debt which was used to finance the construction of the Company’s rice mill in Kampong Thom province (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: AMRU is majority-owned by its CEO Saran Song, a respected entrepreneur in Cambodia’s rice sector. Mr. Song started the business in 2011. Other shareholders include members of Mr. Song’s family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$13.5mn. IFC proposes to support the Project with up to US$10.0 million in funding, comprising an up to US$5.0 million A-loan from IFC’s own account and an up to US$5.0 million loan in its capacity as Implementing Entity of the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP). Other funds have been availed in the form of equity investments from the shareholders and the Company’s internal cash generation.
location_description: The Company’s milling and processing facilities are located in Phnom Penh as well as Battambang and Kampong Thom provinces. The working capital funding will help the Company to source raw materials in the country’s rice growing regions, including Battambang, Kampong Thom, Preah Vihear, Kampong Cham, Kampong Chhnang, Kampong Speu and Takeo provinces.
development_impact: At the Project level, expected outcomes include increased offtake of rice from smallholder farmers, improved farmer incomes and strengthened farmer resilience to market volatility and contribution to disseminating best sustainability practices (resource-efficient, climate smart, incl. provisions for addressing forced/child labor and biodiversity risks in the supply chain). At market level, IFC anticipates that the Project will enhance the competitiveness and sustainability of the sector by showcasing the benefits and modalities of contract farming as well as the superior financial business outcomes of focusing on more niche product lines, such as organic or SRP rice.
additionality: Financial additionality: provision of long-term financing, which is difficult to raise in the market for SMEs like AMRU, to support a stable balance sheet. Standard setting: IFC will support the Company in bringing it E&S practices in lines with national requirements and best international standards. The key gaps that have been identified are the focus of the ESAP and potential associated advisory interventions. Knowledge, innovation, and capacity building through rendered Advisory Services (implementation of SRP standards, strengthen supply chain and food safety management).

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a financing package equivalent to US$5 million to Caribbean Bottling Company (“CBC” or the “Company”), a bottling company headquartered in Croix Des Bouquets, Haiti. CBC is one of the leading manufacturers and distributors of (i) water and related products, (ii) juice beverages under the brand “Frooty”, and (iii) iced tea under the brand “Brizz”. The Company employs over 400 people and commercializes its products through a well-established distribution network. The project consists of investments to expand the Company’s bottling and warehousing capacity and incremental working capital needs. The Project will also be supported by the IDA18 IFC-MIGA Private Sector Window (IDA PSW), created by the Word Bank Group to catalyze private sector investment in IDA countries, with a focus on fragile and conflict affected states, such as Haiti.
sponsor_shareholders: The Barrau family, Jacques Villejoint and Jean Phillippe Dufort own an aggregate shareholding interest of 73% in the Company, with the balance being owned by minority shareholders
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at approximately US$15 million. IFC is proposing to participate with an A Loan of up to US$2.5 million from IFC’s own account and with an IDA PSW Loan of up to US$2.5 million from IFC acting as implementing entity of IDA PSW.
location_description: The investments will be made in CBC’s plant in Croix Des Bouquets (Port Au Prince province, Haiti).
development_impact: (i) Project level impact is expected to derive from economy-wide effects through the creation of direct and indirect jobs, environmental and resource efficiency through improved practices in the production process, and access to safe drinking water to a wider population in rural areas. (ii) anticipated Market level impact includes building up the local manufacturing base by aiming to source more inputs locally, initiatives to reduce plastic waste, and demonstration effect by investing in a country despite its various challenges.
additionality: IFC's core financial additionality in the Project derives from fixed long term financing not readily available in the market. IFC's core non-financial additionality will stem from Environmental and Social standard setting.

project_description: Westfalia Fruto Mozambique (WFM) is a commercial scale-avocado farm that was established in 2014 with the development of a 250-ha avocado orchard and packing house near the vicinity of Chimoio, a city in central Mozambique. It has operated successfully since its inception and as provided access to export markets for litchi farmers in the Manica province. WFM is considering acquisition of land and development of an avocado and litchi farm in the Catandica area of Manica Province in Mozambique. The Project will involve acquisition of 958 ha Pegache Farm for the development of 100 ha of avocado orchards. The Project will also support local small farmers and emerging commercial growers through provision of training and technical assistance. The Project will be supported by the IDA18 IFC-MIGA Private Sector Window (IDA PSW), created by the World Bank Group to catalyse private sector investment in IDA countries, with a focus on fragile and conflict affected states.
sponsor_shareholders: WFM is indirectly 75% owned by Westfalia Fruits and 25% by AgDevCo (together the Sponsors). Westfalia Fruits is a wholly owned subsidiary of Hans Merensky Holdings Proprietary Limited (HMH) and is a leading multinational supplier of fresh subtropical fruit. HMH is a South African-based vertically-integrated, natural resource-based Company which was created in 1949 and owns two main businesses: (i) the fruit business (Westfalia) and (ii) the timber business (Merensky or Merensky Timbers). HMH's operations are spread across Sub-Saharan Africa, South America and Europe. HMH Group shareholding is as follows: The Hans Merensky Foundation - 40%, the Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) - 30%, IFC - 20%, and, three Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (BBBEE) organizations: Vuka Forestry Holdings (4%), Women Investment Portfolio Holdings (WIPHOLD) (3%), and, HMH Employee Share Ownership Plan (3.0%) owning the outstanding 10%. AgDevCo is a social impact investor and project developer working in the African agriculture sector. The proposal would represent a repeat investment with WFM and a fourth investment with the company’s parent, HMH. Details on previous investments with HMH are as follows: An equity investment aimed to support timber processing efficiency in South Africa and fruit plantation development in South Africa and Latin America https://disclosures.ifc.org/#/projectDetail/SPI/31557 The establishment of an avocado plantation in Manica Province of Mozambique: https://disclosures.ifc.org/#/projectDetail/SII/34183 A project aimed to strength the company’s supply chain in Latin America: https://disclosures.ifc.org/#/projectDetail/SII/40091
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed Project is estimated to cost USD 7.5m and will be financed with 50% debt and 50% equity. IFC and IDA PSW are jointly considering financing part of the debt package with a loan of up to USD 2.8 million to finance the Project consisting of: i) IFC A Loan of up to USD 1.4 million; and ii) IDA PSW Loan of up to USD 1.4 million from IFC acting as Implementing Entity of IDA PSW. AgDevCo will provide balance of the debt package in the form of a loan of USD 0.9 million. The remaining 50% will be financed through equity from Westfalia Fruit and AgDevCo in the proportion of 75% and 25%, respectively.
location_description: Pegache Farm is located on the outskirts of Catandica, in the Barue District of Manica Province in Mozambique. The farm is located on the northern side of Catandica Town, at the eastern base of the Cerro Choa Mountain.
development_impact: Project Outcomes: IFC expects the Project will i) create ~300 direct jobs during the first phase, (ii) further expand procurement from 50+ local farmers, who have formed an association and are eager to expand, and (iii) benefit local farmers from better output and more varieties given Westfalia's expertise in cultivar and seed development. Market Creation: i) Competitiveness: IFC expects the Project will increase competitiveness in the horticulture sector in the Catandica area of Mozambique, through demonstration and replication effects, ii) Integration: IFC expects that upon completion, the Project would expand fruit production in Mozambique to such a degree that it would justify the business case for a larger packing facility, which would increase integration along the supply chain, retain more value domestically, and create additional jobs.
additionality: IFC's financial additionality to the Project includes i) Financing structure: IFC will provide a loan with an 11-year tenor including a 4-year grace period, which is not available in Mozambique. Lack of access to finance is a serious constraint for private sector development in the country. IFC's non-financial additionality includes: i) Knowledge, Innovation, and Capacity Building or Non-commercial risk mitigation, including trusted partnerships. IFC's country teams in Africa and South America have provided country knowledge to Westfalia as it explored growth opportunities in these markets.

project_description: This project is proposed under the Global Trade Supplier Finance program (“GTSF” or the “Program”) approved by the IFC Board on September 21, 2010 (Original Project #28723). Under GTSF, IFC provides short-term financing to suppliers (“Suppliers”) in emerging markets selling to large companies (“Buyers”) on open account terms. Under this project, IFC will provide financing to McCormick & Company (“McCormick” the “Company”) for suppliers based in different emerging market countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1889 and headquartered in Sparks, Maryland, McCormick & Company is a manufacturer, marketer, and distributor of spices, seasonings, flavorings, and other specialty food products for the consumer and industrial markets. McCormick is publicly traded in NYSE and institutional investors hold majority of its shares
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project (‘the Project”) within the GTSF facility is expected to be US$30 million for the supply of spices from McCormick’s suppliers.
location_description: GTSF-approved countries, including Vietnam, Indonesia, Brazil, and Madagascar.

project_description: Pan American Energy, S.L. is a leading integrated energy company with upstream and downstream operations engaged primarily in the exploration, development and production of crude oil and natural gas, the refining of crude oil and the distribution and marketing of refined products. Pan American Energy, S.L. Argentina Branch (“PAE” or the “Company”) is completing a project at its Campana Refinery in Argentina to increase the production of refined products, produce higher value and cleaner burning fuels, and reduce refinery air emissions (the “Project”). PAE requires financing (i) to for the Company’s investment program to finalize the construction and commissioning of the Project and (ii) increased working capital needs.
sponsor_shareholders: PAE is a company owned 50/50 by BP plc and BC Energy Investments Corp. (“BC”). BC itself is 50% indirectly owned each by Bridas Energy Holdings Ltd. and China National Offshore Oil Corporation Ltd.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project amounts to US$400 million. IFC will provide up to US$100 million A Loan for its own account and up to US$300 million of mobilization loans.
location_description: The Project refers to the Campana Refinery, which has easy access to roadways and waterways. It is located in a designated industrial area of the city of Campana, Argentina The address is: Av. Ing. Emilo Mitre 574 – B2804ABA Campana, Buenos Aires Province, ARGENTINA
development_impact: The Project is expected to (i) create value addition for Argentina by increasing supply of refined products in keeping up with the expected growth in demand, (ii) reduce emissions and lower sulfur dioxide levels, (iii) provide employment opportunities with direct and indirect job creation, and (iv) continue incorporating IFC's EH&S Performance Standards tools to set best practices for the sector.
additionality: i) Resource Mobilization: IFC aims to raise significant financing by bringing in international banks under its B Loan umbrella; (ii) long term tenors, not readily available in Argentina; (iii) Standard-Setting/EH&S Expertise: IFC's involvement will help ensure that the investments meet best-in-class EH&S protocols.

project_description: DCM Shriram Limited (“DCM” or the “Company”) is one of India’s leading business conglomerates with its main business lines as follows: (i) Agribusiness (fertilizer, seeds, sugar and trading of agri inputs); and (ii) Chloro-Vinyl (caustic soda, chlorine & polyvinyl chloride (PVC)). The proposed transaction is an A-Loan of US$35 million by IFC to support (a) a brownfield expansion of its existing sugar plant at Hariawan (located in Hardoi district in Uttar Pradesh) by an incremental 5000 tons of cane per day (TCD); (b) an installation of a 30 MW cogeneration power plant using bagasse as fuel in Hariawan; and (c) an expansion of its distillery capacity in Ajbapur.
sponsor_shareholders: DCM Shriram Limited is a publicly listed company on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in India with revenues of approximately US$ 1.06 billion and Net Profit of approximately US$ 104 million for the financial year ended March 31, 2018. The Company had a market capitalization of approximately US$ 866 million as of February 22, 2019. The Sponsors, led by Mr. Ajay S Shriram, Mr. Vikram S Shriram and Mr. Ajit S Shriram. collectively control approximately 66% of the shares in DCM Shriram and the rest of the shareholding is widely held by institutional and other public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at INR6,031 million (US$86.1 million) for its expansion of the sugar plant, co-generation power plant in Hariawan and the distillery unit in Ajbapur in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A-loan of US$35 million by way of an external commercial borrowing (ECB).
location_description: This project is located at Hariawan and Ajbapur, Uttar Pradesh in India.
development_impact: a. Investment in Priority Region in India: The Company would be investing in Uttar Pradesh, one of the key low-income states in India. This would help channel further private sector investment into the state. b. Farmer Productivity Gains: the client will seek to (i) improve farmer income through purchase of higher quantity of cane and (ii) create small scale / micro entrepreneurs who can facilitate productivity gains for the farmers c. Jobs: create about 150 additional jobs through the project. d. Demonstration effect: The Project will further demonstrate best practices and cleaner production norms in the Indian sugar industry.
additionality: Financial additionality: Access to long term finance: The Project would benefit from IFC's long tenor offering (11 year) which is very useful for companies such as DCM Shriram which operates in largely cyclical businesses Non-financial additionality: (a) Knowledge and innovation: Company can benefit from IFC's knowledge and insights gained through its investments across the world, especially in Brazil which is the world's largest sugar producer.

sector: Other Vegetable Oil Crops (Coconut, Rapeseed, Peanut, Sunflower, etc.)
project_description: Comercializadora de Mani S.A. (“Comasa” or the “Company”) is a Nicaraguan company engaged in the processing and commercialization of peanuts, mainly for the export markets. With 30 years of experience in the sector, Comasa has become the largest peanut company in Nicaragua. The project consists of providing an A Loan of up to US$15 million and mobilizing a B Loan of up to US$50 million to Comasa to allow the Company to finance the working capital required to purchase, process and export peanuts (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is majority owned by Mr. Mauricio Jose Zacarias Batres, Mr. Juan Alvaro Munguia Alvarez and the Zavala Navarro family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment will consist of an up to $65 million one-year loan facility (the “Facility”) with up to four renewable tranches comprised by: i) an IFC A Loan of up to US$15 million; ii) B Loan of up to US$50 million.
location_description: The Company has administrative offices in Managua and Chinandega and 4 peanut processing plants, in Posoltega, Sempro, Manicasa and Central.
development_impact: The project is being undertaken during a period of constrained financing in the country. Therefore, the Project will enable Comasa to preserve the existing level of production and exports, providing an access to market to peanut farmers. By maintaining production at its existing levels, the Project will help preserve jobs through a countercyclical intervention.
additionality: IFC's additionality is expected to be threefold: i) the proposed Facility will provide Comasa funds in a scenario of scare financing for the entire peanut supply chain and the private sector more broadly, ii) the 5-year nature of the Facility will mitigate Comasa's refinancing risk, and iii) IFC's umbrella will allow for the mobilization of funds from commercial banks and other multilateral institutions.

company_name: MARTUR SUNGER VE KOLTUK TESISLERI TICARET VE SANAYI ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Established in Bursa, Turkey in 1985, Martur Sunger ve Koltuk Tesisleri Tic. Ve San. A.S. (“Martur” or the “Company”) together with its subsidiaries engage in design and manufacturing of seats as well as other interior parts for passenger cars and light commercial vehicles. The Company has production facilities in Turkey, Romania, Russia, Algeria, Poland and is in the process of expanding into Morocco. The project entails financing of Martur’s expansion investment program in Romania, Morocco and Algeria (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsor is Ustunberk Holding A.S. (“Ustunberk Holding” or the “Sponsor”) which owns Martur’s majority shareholding. Ustunberk Holding’s main area of focus is automotive parts industry through Martur and its subsidiaries. Ustunberk Holding is established in Turkey and is privately owned by Ustunberk Family. Martur’s current shareholding structure is as follows: 83% by Ustunberk Holding, 5.4% by IFC and 11.6% by Ustunberk Family, Ustunberk Holding companies and management.
