total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is up to EUR71.5 million. IFC considers providing a EUR45 million of financing package in the form A and C Loans to finance the Project.
location_description: The proposed IFC investment is planned to be utilized in the Company’s facilities in Romania, Morocco and Algeria.
development_impact: The Project's expected development impact includes (i) increased employment and skills development, (ii) value addition and supply chain linkages in Romania, Morocco and Algeria, and (iii) increased stakeholder benefits (i.e. customer benefits via better access to wider variety of components and parts; supplier benefits via additional domestic purchases). Beyond the project, IFC anticipates the investment will help increase the competitiveness in the auto-parts industry in Romania, Morocco and Algeria.
additionality: IFC's expected role and additionally includes (i) providing long-term financing, (ii) contribution to the improvement of the Company's E&S practices; and (iii) non-commercial risk mitigation through an established partnership.
Company Name: MARTUR SUNGER VE KOLTUK TESISLERI TICARET VE SANAYI ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: Phu My Hung Development Corporation (“PMH” or the “Company”) is a Vietnamese property developer with its flagship development of Phu My Hung township in the outskirts of Ho Chi Minh City (“HCMC”). The Company is looking to expand through the development of (i) a new master-planned ecological township in Hoa Binh, as well as (ii) residential projects in HCMC targeted at the local population (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is 70% owned and controlled by Phu My Hung Asia Holdings (the Sponsor), a foreign investor in Vietnam since 1990s. The remaining 30% is ultimately owned by the government of Ho Chi Minh City.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated to be US$150 million. IFC has been invited to provide a VND-denominated bond of up to US$75 million equivalent.
location_description: The Project is located in HCMC and Hua Binh.
development_impact: 1. Job creation: The Project will create direct and indirect jobs through the development of the townships and purchases from local suppliers during and after construction. 2. Improved quality of life: PMH's developments create integrated and environmentally sustainable townships in Vietnam, which in addition to housing also includes commercial areas, public facilities, hospitals, schools and sports facilities. 3. Increase access to housing: The Project is expected to supply more than 5,000 housing units within the next 5-7 years.
additionality: 1. Financing Structure: IFC will provide VND long term fixed rate funding which is not readily available in the market since local banks mostly offer floating rate financing at short or medium term only. 2. Standard Setting on E&S best practices and Green Buildings (GB): IFC will be able to provide the Company with E&S best practices and GB/EDGE certification and assist in achieving those certifications. This Project could also be used to pilot the new EDGE Urban Communities tool, which can be used to better design their mixed-used buildings.

project_description: Soufflet is a French family-owned agri-food group of international scope with a presence in 19 countries. It operates in the barley, wheat and rice and pulses sectors and advises and provides support for wine growers. The group is the leading family-owned direct buyer of cereals in Europe, and also operates in the international cereal markets through its subsidiary Soufflet Négoce. In the barley sector, it is one of the world’s top malt producers, with a presence in Europe, Asia, and South America. In wheat, it is one of Europe’s leading millers and an expert in developing tailor-made ingredients. The Group also develops and manufactures enzymes and yeasts and is a significant player in the bakery food industry in France and Portugal, and is also active in the fast food sector. The Soufflet Group invests in research and innovation to enhance the value of agricultural resources. Proposed investment consists of a EUR 20 million financing to Soufflet Malting Ethiopia PLC (“Soufflet Ethiopia” or the “Company”), a 100% subsidiary of Soufflet. The project will directly support the Group’s strategy in Africa to build and operate a malting facility in Ethiopia with a total output capacity of 110K tpa (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Groupe Soufflet is a French family owned agri food group
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC financing amounts to EUR 20 million. Within the scope of the Project, IFC’s financing will be directly used to support Soufflet Ethiopia’s capital expenditures and working capital needs in Ethiopia.
location_description: The Project will be located in Bole Lemi II Industrial Park in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
development_impact: The project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) score of Good to Excellent. The most significant, expected project-level outcome is an increase in access to markets and support to increase productivity for more than 20,000 barley farmers. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates the investment will increase integration in the malt barley supply chain, through capacity building and demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in two forms: (i) equity financing from IFC and GAFSP; (ii) frameworks. The Company selected to work with IFC because of its long-term and strategic partnership, IFC's in-country expertise, and IFC's support to establish local sourcing of commercially available malt barley.

project_description: Edita, a publicly listed company on Egypt and London stock exchanges, is a market leading branded bakery products company in Egypt. It produces and sells packaged cakes, croissants, rusks (baked bread snacks), wafers and candies in Egypt and exports to 16 countries. Edita’s investment plan includes (a) expansion into Morocco through a JV with a Moroccan partner to establish a production facility in Morocco, (b) capital expenditures in Egypt, (c) refinancing a portion of Edita’s existing debt, and (d) acquisitions in Egypt and other countries.
sponsor_shareholders: The shareholders include the Quantum Investment BV (42%), Kingsway Fund (15%) which is a UK based investment fund, Exoder Limited (13%) which is fully owned by Chipita, and free float (31%). Mr. Hani Berzi is the founder of Edita and serves as its Chairman and Managing Director.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a loan of up to US$30 million for IFC’s own account to finance Edita’s investment plan.
location_description: Edita’s headquarters is in Sixth of October City in Giza governorate. Three out of Edita’s five production facilities are located in Sixth of October City, one is located in Tenth of Ramadan City in Sharqia governorate, and one in Beni Suef governorate. Edita’s planned production facility in Morocco will be located in Casablanca.
development_impact: IFC's investment will help in: (a) sustaining and creating new jobs in Egypt and Morocco (Edita's future growth will create 400 direct jobs per year in Egypt alone, totaling 2,000 over the next five years); and (b) increasing integration of Egypt's processed foods sector, through capacity building and skills, as Edita will continue to support and develop local suppliers of raw materials, and these suppliers will supply other players in Egypt's processed foods sector.
additionality: Through this investment, IFC will (a) provide a long-term loan with flexible features that will help Edita strengthen its balance sheet, and (b) help Edita in its expansion plans by capitalizing on IFC's sectoral and regional experience.

company_name: SHANDONG HEKANGYUAN POULTRY BREEDING INC LTD
project_description: The Project is for the Company to expand its duck breeding capacity in Jilin, Inner Mongolia and rural Shandong in the next 3 years.
sponsor_shareholders: Two founders and management team own 47.47% through Jinan Hezhou Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. Jiangxi Yonglian Agriculture Holdings Co., Ltd owns 38.85%, IFC owns 13.68%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated total cost is US$48 million. IFC will invest an A Loan of up to US$10 million equivalent.
location_description: Jilin, Inner Mongolia and Shandong, China
development_impact: On the project level, the major impact is food safety and farmer income increase. On the market level, the impact relates to potential to strengthen competitiveness and integration in the domestic duck sector through demonstration of higher hygiene, resource efficiency and food safety standards to other market participants.
additionality: IFC may provide long-term financing in local currency, mobilize new equity, as well as advise on industry knowledge and corporate governance.
Company Name: SHANDONG HEKANGYUAN POULTRY BREEDING INC LTD

project_description: SignatureGlobal (India) Private Limited (“Signature” or the “Company”) is a leading real estate company in India developing only affordable housing projects. The Company started its operations for development of affordable housing projects in 2014. With its units priced in the range of US$22,000-42,000, Signature has launched 11 projects, totaling approximately 11,000 units and 7.5 million square feet (of saleable area), since inception. Signature is one of the pioneers of affordable housing policy in the state of Haryana, delivering the first project under the Haryana state affordable housing policy recently. The proposed project involves IFC investing INR equivalent of approximately up to US$30 million in the form of equity/ quasi-equity instrument in Signature. The project proceeds would be used to acquire land as well as fund for construction and working capital requirements for the proposed affordable housing projects in the National Capital Region includingGurgaon, Haryana (the “Project”). The Project comprises of approximately 8,000 residential units with a total saleable area of approximately 5 million square feet and is mostly targeted at low to middle income population.
sponsor_shareholders: 76 percent of the equity shares of the Company are currently held by Mr. Pradeep Aggarwal, Mr. Ravi Aggarwal, Mr. Lalit Aggarwal, Mr. Devender Aggarwal, related Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)) and their family members (collectively the sponsors ) while the balance 24 percent is held by other individual investors. The sponsors have demonstrated their ability to spot a business opportunity and build a focused business at scale in their previous stint at SMC Group, where they were occupying key managerial positions. SMC Group is a diversified financial services company engaged in broking, trading, investment banking, wealth management, research, distribution of financial products and depository and clearing services.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost for which IFC investment of up to US$30 million equivalent will be used, is estimated at approximately US$100 million.
location_description: The proposed projects would be primarily located in the National Capital Region (including Gurgaon, Haryana).
development_impact: Accessibility (for consumers): The Project will increase the supply of affordable housing by approximately 8,000 units, across the National Capital Region, at a price point where good quality housing is severely lacking. Affordability (for consumers): Signature's housing units are typically priced substantially lower than the other units in conventional projects in the micro market. Inclusiveness: The Project will provide access to better health and social infrastructure (like schools, hospitals) while also improving safety, security and quality of living for its customers, the majority of whom belong to incomes below US$15,000.
additionality: Financing structure. IFC will provide $30 million equity / quasi-equity to Signature, to enable the Company to mobilize significant capital to fund its future plans and achieve scale while preserving headroom in the cash flows. EDGE certification: IFC will provide its global expertise in Green Buildings for the Company to obtain EDGE certification for all its units, which will improve resource efficiencies of affordable housing in Gurgaon. Corporate Governance: As part of this Project, IFC will help Signature to implement a Corporate Governance Action Plan (CGAP) focused on adoption of best practices in the field of corporate governance.

project_description: In 2012, a digital health platform called HealthkartPlus was started as a division within BLPL (Bright Lifecare Private Limited). In 2015, this was de-merged and transferred to 1MG Technologies Private Limited (1mg or the Company). 1mg was incorporated in April 2015 with Prashant Tandon and Gaurav Agarwal as founders. It currently operates as an online marketplace for: (i) sale and purchase of pharmaceutical products (comprising over-the-counter (OTC) drugs and prescription drugs), wellness products and fast-moving consumer goods by various third party pharmacies and manufacturers.; (ii) diagnostic services being offered by various third party diagnostic centers; and (iii) online medical consultancy services/ second opinion being offered by third party independent doctors using the domain name www.1mg.com , an internet based portal and “1MG” a mobile application. It is the largest digital healthcare platform in India ( https://www.1mg.com/aboutUs ). 1mg acquired LFS Healthcare Private Limited (“Droplet”) and Delhi Mediart Private Limited (“DMPL”) (wholly-owned subsidiaries of 1mg) in FY18 which is engaged in the business of providing home collection solutions for diagnostic services and wholesale trading of pharmaceuticals, healthcare and personal-care products respectively. The Company is raising finance to support its continued growth.
sponsor_shareholders: 1mg was founded by Mr. Prashant Tandon and Mr. Gaurav Agarwal who now serve as its Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chief Technology Officer (CTO) respectively. The lead investors are Maverick Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Corisol Holdings AG, HBM Investments and Omidyar Network.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes an equity investment as part of US$70 million fund raise.
location_description: 1mg has its registered office in New Delhi, India
development_impact: The expected development impact of the project includes i) increased access to affordable and safe medicines, ii) integrated approach to chronic diseases, online consultations and diagnostic services, iii) increased efficiency and productivity for hospitals and retail pharmacies, and iv) improving nationwide connectivity between patients and suppliers of medicines
additionality: IFC's expected additionality includes: i) provision of long term early stage equity financing ii) bringing deep expertise in scaling tech startups and its networks in India's traditional heath sector and iii) IFC's global pharmaceutical and health service knowledge and best practices.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an up to US$25 million senior A loan to Société Nouvelle de Commerce S.A. (SONOCO or the Group), a leading Guinean diversified family business group. The funds will be mainly used to finance the investment program of the Group that includes: (i) additional wheat storage facility to be located at the port of Conakry; (ii) the revamping of an existing seasoning cubes processing unit previously owned by the Nestlé group; (iii) the construction and operation of a greenfield soft drink plant; and (iv) general capital expenditures for its wheat milling operation (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor, founder, majority shareholder and CEO of SONOCO is Mr. El Hadj Saliou Diallo, a successful 58-year old Guinean entrepreneur with a diversified portfolio of activities. Mr. Diallo started his career in the 1980s selling fresh bread from traditional bakeries, later moving on to petty trade, then flour imports before diversifying into other consumer products, spurring the growth of SONOCO into a leading Guinean business group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide up to US$25 million in the form of a senior A loan to partially finance the investment program of SONOCO.
location_description: The Project will include investment components located at the Port of Conakry and in the industrial zone of Conakry (Commune de Ratomba).
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcomes are (i) increased efficiency of the Port of Conakry; (ii) less traffic congestion at the exit of the Port and on the main road through Conakry; (iii) increased access to iron fortified bouillon cubes; and (iv) economy-wide effects associated with the growth of Guinea's nascent industrial sector.
additionality: IFC's additionality comes in two forms: (i) financing structure, given long-term funding is not available in Guinea; and (ii) standard-setting related to corporate governance and capacity building for its network of small bakeries distributors.

project_description: Netafim Ltd. (“Netafim” or the “Company”) is a global leader in technology-advanced smart irrigation solutions. The Company was founded in 1965 in the Negev desert in Israel. By trying to grow crops in desert soil, Netafim created the world’s first commercial dripper in 1966. Today Netafim has become the largest micro irrigation systems (“MIS”) provider globally.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is currently owned by Mexichem SAB de CV (“Mexichem”), a publicly traded company headquartered in Mexico. Mexichem owns an 80% stake while the remaining 20% stake is held by a kibbutz (communal settlement in Israel) entity called Hatzerim. Hazterim is one of the initial founders of the Company and Netafim’s main plant is still located at the kibbutz.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is a loan of up to $90 million to Netafim. The financing package would be comprised of an A Loan of up to $40 million, a B1 Loan mobilized under IFC’s standard B Loan program of up to $30 million, and a Trust Loan of up to $20 million provided under the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (“MCPP”).
location_description: Disbursements will be directed to the holding company in Israel to fund working capital needs in Africa and to Netafim´s subsidiaries in China and Turkey.
development_impact: The expected Project-level outcome is its contribution to generating better yields for the local farmers and strengthening their resilience to climate shocks. The Project will also contribute to sustainability by promoting water used efficiency in agriculture in several water stressed regions.
additionality: Financing Structure: IFC is providing the Company the financing flexibility at the corporate and country level that is otherwise not available. Mobilization: IFC will mobilize MCPP funds from the HKMA and a B1 Loan. Knowledge-sharing: IFC will leverage its advisory capabilities to support the Company's expansion and maximize the impacts of irrigation.

project_description: The proposed project involves IFC investing debt in an INR equivalent of approximately US$ 15 million in Dodla Dairy Limited (“Dodla” or the “Company”). The proposed investment will support Dodla to: (a) expand and upgrade its existing manufacturing infrastructure by purchasing new equipment for select processing plants; (b) fund its working capital needs; and (c) for general corporate purposes including marketing and brand building (the “Project”). Update February 2021: IFC committed INR 1,000 million (approximately US$15 million) to Dodla on February 02, 2021 by way of subscription to equity shares of the Company to support the general capital expenditure and working capital requirements of the Company.. The investment has been committed from two projects, INR 500 million committed from project #42009, and an approximately equivalent amount from project #44940.
sponsor_shareholders: Dodla Dairy was incorporated in 1995 and has an average procurement of 1.02 million litres of raw milk per day as of December 31, 2020 with a presence in the southern region of India. The Company’s operations in India are primarily across the five Indian states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra. . The Company also has overseas operations in Kenya and Uganda. It engages in the procurement, production, distribution and marketing of milk and milk products, comprising milk, ghee, curd, butter, paneer (cottage cheese), flavoured milk, ice cream, milk sweets among others. The Company is promoted by Mr. Sunil Reddy (the “Sponsor”), Mr. Sesha Reddy and the Dodla Family Trust. Mr Sunil Reddy belongs to a reputed family from Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh. The family has historically had strong linkages with local farmers. The Sponsor has more than two decades of experience in the industry. The Sponsor, his family and entities associated with the Sponsor have a 68.51% shareholding in the Company
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$71 million and IFC’s proposed investment is up to INR equivalent of US$15 million investment in the form of an A Loan in the Company. Update February 2021: IFC invested INR 1,000 million (approximately US$ 15 million) in the form of subscription to equity shares in the Company, out of which INR 500 million is being committed from project #42009, and an approximately equivalent amount out of project #44940.
location_description: The Project will be located at Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka in India.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have the following development impacts: a) Farmers: The Project is expected to improve access to a reliable off-take market for a significant number of smallholder farmers while increasing their productivity and supporting their shift toward greater commercialization. b) Employees: The Company's expansion is expected to create over 2,500 jobs directly and potentially twice as many jobs would be created along with the value chain, contributing to skill building and non-farm employment. A high share of employment created in the dairy sector tends to be at the bottom of pyramid (BOP). c) Consumers: IFC anticipates that the Project will contribute both to improving the food safety and food security through expanding access to quality affordable dairy products.
additionality: a) IFC's own account debt will improve the Company's practices in the areas of environmental and social standards as well as insurance. b) Knowledge, innovation and capacity building through sharing IFC's global expertise in the dairy sector, technical advice on best operating practices, and improvement of food safety standards. c) Standard setting through provision of expertise in environmental and social standards which could also have a demonstration effect on the overall sector.

project_description: BIM Land Joint Stock Company (BIM Land or the Company) is a leading tourism property developer in Vietnam. The Company builds, sells and/or operates properties that cater to both domestic and international tourists’ needs including hotels, residences and retail space. BIM Land’s projects are all located in tourism areas such as Ha Long city in Quang Ninh province or the Phu Quoc island in Kien Giang province. Recently, the Company has expanded into neighboring Laos, where it is replicating its successful tourism property development model in Vientiane. IFC is providing debt financing to the Company to support the Project which consists of: (i) the Intercontinental resort in Ha Long bay, Vietnam, comprising of a hotel and residences; (ii) the Citadines apartments and a water park in Phu Quoc island, Vietnam; and (iii) the Holiday Inn in Vientiane, Laos, comprising of a hotel, office and retail spaces.
sponsor_shareholders: BIM Group was founded by Mr. Viet Quoc Doan (the Sponsor). Mr. Doan started his first businesses in Poland where he and his wife were studying for their PhD at Warsaw Politechnic, before returning to Vietnam in 1994 to form BIM Group and subsequently BIM Land. The Company is wholly owned by the Sponsor and his direct family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is estimated to be US$202.8 million. IFC has been invited to provide a senior loan of up to US$57.2 million for IFC’s own account; and mobilize a senior loan of up to US$42.8 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP).
location_description: The Project is located in Quang Ninh and Kien Giang provinces, Vietnam, and Vientiane, Laos.
development_impact: 1. Tourism development: By developing critical tourism infrastructures, the Project will (i) enable tourists extend their stay in Ha Long; (ii) stimulate the development of a new international tourism destination in Phu Quoc island; and (iii) upgrade the supply of international standard accommodation in Vientiane. 2. Job creation and local linkages: The Project is expected to create a number of skilled job opportunities, including a significant proportion of female jobs, and stimulate demand for locally-sourced materials, services and labor which are mostly provided by local small and medium enterprises. 3. Environmental and Social (E&S) standard setting: The Project is expected to exhibit high level of E&S compliance in areas such as waste treatment and land acquisition, which is expected to have a strong demonstration effect to other property developments in the same area.
additionality: 1. Long-term financing and resource mobilization: IFC will provide a long-term debt financing package to the Company which suits the Project's cash flow profile. Such long-term financing is not readily available in Vietnam. 2. Resource mobilization: IFC will mobilize additional long-term financing for the Project, through the provision of a senior loan from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the MCPP. 3. Environmental & Social (E&S) best practices and green building: IFC will share international E&S best practices with the Company to enhance its E&S standards. In addition, the Project is expected to comply with IFC's Green Building standards.

sector: Garment and Apparel (Without Fabric , Excluding Footwear)
project_description: Epyllion Knit Wear Limited (the “Company” or “EKWL”), an existing IFC Advisory Services client and one of Bangladesh’s integrated knitted apparels manufacturers and exporters, has approached IFC to finance the expansion of its Ready-Made Garments (“RMG”) cutting and sewing operations (the “Project”). The Project involves setting up a greenfield factory in Narayanganj, which will comprise 50 sewing lines, washing facilities, and embellishment capabilities. The proposed Project will increase Epyllion’s cutting and sewing capacity by 25 million pieces per year from current capacity of 16 million to post project capacity of 41 million pieces per year, which will be fully exported to major global retailers.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsors are Mr. Reaz Uddin Al-Mamoon, Mr. Md Junaid Abu Salay Musa and Mrs. Kishwar Jahan, who are the shareholders of Epyllion Knitwears Limited. The shareholding structure is as follows - Mr. Reaz Uddin Al-Mamoon (45.8%), Mr. Md Junaid Abu Salay Musa (31.7%) and Mrs. Kishwar Jahan (22.5%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$34.7 million and is proposed to be financed with a debt: equity ratio of 42:58 as follows: long-term debt of US$14.44 million and equity of US$20.20 million. Proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to US$14.44 million with a tenor of eight years including a two-year grace period.
location_description: The Project is located in Narayanganj, around 25 kilometres south of Dhaka. The Project is accessible by road.
development_impact: Stakeholder's impacts: i. Employment Growth: The Project will create 5,900 additional jobs, mostly for women. ii. Employee skills/know-how: The Project is going to attract skilled recruits and further develop their skill sets through various training program required by the new technologies and product range, and thus adding to the skilled workers base in Bangladesh. iii. Effect on emissions and waste generation: EKWL's new factory will be a LEED certified green factory. Market impact: i. Contribution to Market Creation: The project, along with IFC's advisory services engagements in Bangladesh, has the potential to promote greater market sustainability and intergration in the RMG sector in Bangladesh. ii. Impact on market emissions and waste generation: The project, along with IFC's advisory services engagements in Bangladesh, will help foster adoptioin of environmental and social sustainability principles by firms and consumers across the sector through direct capacity building channels and demonstration effects as a result of EKWL's success. iii. Increasing manufacturing complexity: The Project is expected to upgrade the company to a more value adding level, involving advanced products, innovative product development, automated production technology and up-grading of professional skills of the personnel. It could potentially be the model that other factories will follow as Bangladesh is climbing up to higher value garment products.
additionality: i. Provide long-term foreign exchange financing which would otherwise be difficult to secure in the current market scenario to support a local player to expand its core business. ii. Continue to integrate EKWL into various RMG/Textile-focused IFC advisory programs such as the Buyer's Forum and Better Works programs, which are geared towards improving compliance, competitiveness, energy efficiency, and labor welfare at firm and industry levels. iii. Assist EKWL to formulate and implement E&S action plan to expand social/labor management systems for inclusion of environmental, occupational, health and safety (OHS) guidelines and enhance OHS management systems.

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: Camel Group Co., Ltd. (“Camel Group”) is a publicly listed company that engages in the production, distribution and recycling of auto starter batteries. The proposed IFC investment will support Camel Group’s capacity expansion for its lead-acid battery recycling operation in frontier regions of China (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Liu Guoben is the controlling shareholder and Chairman of the Board of Camel Group (the “Sponsor”). He owns 48% of Camel Group. Mr. Liu Changlai, the CEO, and Miss. Tan Weiping, a relative of the Chairman, own 3.4% and 1.3% of Camel Group respectively. The three of them are shareholders acting in concert. Other senior managers collectively owns 4.3% of Camel Group and the remaining shares are public float.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be approximately US$116 million. IFC’s proposed investment is a senior, secured A loan of up to US$36 million and a MCPP loan of up to US$45 million.
location_description: The Project is expected to be located in Anhui Province, Jiangxi Province and Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region of People’s Republic of China.
development_impact: Environment: The Project will increase the volume of recycled lead and neutralization for discharge in an environmentally safe way i.e. reduce soil and water contamination. This Project will make sure additional lead are processed and neutralized before discharge to the environment. Economy-wide effects: The Project will help to create circular economy by establishing the recycling and reusing waste in the value chain since scrap plastic and secondary lead alloys can be used for new battery production and other lead products. The circular, more integrated design of lead acid battery manufacturing and recycling offers a more cost-effective way to produce batteries and create and help to formalize employment in the recycling value chain. Employees: The upgrading of the two existing facilities will make sure the employees therein benefit from more modern, safer equipment, and strengthened workplace control against excessive lead/acid exposure therefore reduce the occupational safety/health risks. Sustainability: The Project is expected to foster adoption of higher E&S standards driven by better technology and processes across the different players in the value chain in China and thus promote Sustainability principles in the market through its demonstration effects. Integration: The project will demonstrate that it is a natural fit for battery manufacturers like Camel which requires large quantity of lead and has easy access to used batteries to integrate recycling business into their value chain. The project will also contribute to expand China's economic complexity through increased process and supply chain complexities.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality in the Project stems from its ability to provide long-term loans to support Camel Group's recycling business, which features a long payback period and slim margins. Moreover, IFC's E&S standards will help the Company adopt the best international industry practices and facilitate sustainable development in the lead-acid battery industry, which has significant potential E&S risks that require strong safeguards and controls. Financing Structure: IFC will be providing an USD corporate loan with tenor relatively longer than what is readily available in the market. Lead-acid battery recycling business features a long payback period with slim gross margins. The Company wants to be prudent in its financing mix and seeks long term capital to fund the Project. Resource Mobilization: IFC also mobilizes MCPP capital with the same tenor that can meet the client's needs at reasonable cost. Standard Setting: Lead-acid battery production and recycling is an industry in which there are significant E&S risks and require strong safeguards and controls in the process. One of IFC's significant additionalities is to help the Company to improve its lead dust control and related occupational health and safety management. Knowledge, Innovation and Capacity Building: Camel Group is keen to establish relationships with partners like IFC that can share their knowledge, experience and networks from investing in the emerging markets. The client is also keen to leverage on IFC's networks and values its ability to forge relationships with potential partners and clients.

project_description: The Project is a funded risk participation for up to EUR 28.5 million by IFC in a EUR 65 million one-year offshore secured pre-export facility provided by Societe Generale (“SG”) to finance the purchase of seed cotton and provide working capital to a cotton company in Burkina Faso.
sponsor_shareholders: Societe Generale is one of the leading European financial services groups. Based on a diversified and integrated banking model, the Group combines financial strength and proven expertise in innovation with a strategy of sustainable growth, aiming to be the trusted partner for its clients, committed to the positive transformations of society and the economy. Active in the real economy for over 150 years, with a solid position in Europe and connected to the rest of the world, Societe Generale has over 147,000 members of staff in 67 countries and supports on a daily basis 31 million individual clients, businesses and institutional investors around the world by offering a wide range of advisory services and tailored financial solutions. The Group is built on three complementary core businesses: French Retail Banking, which encompasses the Societe Generale, Crédit du Nord and Boursorama brands. Each offers a full range of financial services with omnichannel products at the cutting edge of digital innovation; International Retail Banking, Insurance and Financial Services to Corporates, with networks in Africa, Russia, Central and Eastern Europe and specialised businesses that are leaders in their markets; Global Banking and Investor Solutions, which offers recognised expertise, key international locations and integrated solutions. Societe Generale is included in the principal socially responsible investment indices: DJSI (World and Europe), FTSE4Good (Global and Europe), Euronext Vigeo (World, Europe and Eurozone), four of the STOXX ESG Leaders indices, and the MSCI Low Carbon Leaders Index.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project will be in a total amount up to EUR 65 million. SG and IFC will retain each EUR 28.5 million.
location_description: Societe Generale is headquartered in Paris, France. The underlying project is financing cotton produced and exported out of Burkina Faso.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is continued access to markets and finance for over 273,000 farmers and increases in productivity for 1,000 farmers. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates the investment will increase integration and resilience in the cotton sector in Burkina Faso, a low-income/IDA country, through capacity building and demonstration and replication effects.
additionality: IFC's additionality will come in three forms: (i) knowledge, innovation and capacity building through Advisory Services; (ii) standard-setting with regards to child labor; and (iii) non-commercial risk mitigation, including trusted partnerships with a commercial bank, especially since this project will follow previous engagements of IFC in the cotton sector in Burkina Faso.

sector: Tour Operators (i.e., Arranging and Assembling Tours)
project_description: Aqua Expeditions Pte. Ltd. (“Aqua” or the “Company”) operates soft-adventure environmentally sustainable cruises in exotic and emerging destinations. Presently the Company operates in the Cambodian Mekong and Peruvian Amazon. The Company is considering an expansion in Indonesia.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded by Francesco Lorenzo Galli Zugaro (CEO) and Fred Brown. The company is owned by Mr. Galli Zugaro, his father in law, Fred Brown and Bison Capital, a US-based investor.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost of the Indonesia expansion is US$12.5 million. The proposed transaction is an A Loan of up to US$10 million.
location_description: Indonesia
development_impact: Skilled employment: The Company offers extensive training to its employees to deliver a customized local experience. High-quality training facilitates knowledge transfer and improves career prospects. Local linkages: The Aqua Expedition boat will be based full time in Indonesia. The project will have strong linkages with local SMEs in remote locations. Market creation: The Company will introduce a new product to a market which currently does not have offerings of that quality. The marketing linkages with international broadcaster and magazines will put this new emerging destination on the map, and contribute to the development of the destination in a sustainable way.
additionality: LT financing: IFC will provide LT capital for the Project complementing new equity funding. A loan at suggested terms is not generally available from other financial institutions for this type of investment. E&S: The Client is supportive of introducing best practices. In addition, while Indonesia ranks well for its natural and cultural tourism resources, the country is ranked among the lowest for environmental sustainability in tourism and is seeking ways to improve it.

project_description: Established in 1995, Nafoods Group Joint Stock Company (Nafoods or the Company) is a small but niche fruit manufacturer and exporter in Vietnam with a leading position in passion fruits. The Company is currently engaged in four business lines: fruit concentrate and puree, individually quick frozen (IQF) fruit products, passion fruit seedlings and more recently, fresh fruits. The Company is operating 2 manufacturing facilities in central and southern Vietnam with a total annual capacity of 12,000 tons of concentrate/puree and 7,900 tons of IQF. It also produces passion fruit seedlings in an area of 6 hectares (ha) in a mountainous area of Nghe An, central Vietnam. For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2017, the Company posted net revenues of US$22.9 million, EBITDA of US$4.2 million and net profit of US$2.9 million. Nafoods is approaching IFC for support to fund the construction of the second phase of the Long An factory; development of a passion fruit liquid extraction workshop and a packing house in Central Highland; R&D expenses for development of citrus seedlings, implementation of technology for supply chain management and permanent working capital (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Nafoods is a publicly listed company on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange. The Company is 24.3% held by its founding Chairman, Mr. Nguyen Manh Hung, 52.7% by his relatives and associates, 5.3% by Endurance Capital Vietnam Limited, a boutique investment fund domiciled in British Virgin Islands. The remaining shareholding of 17.7% is public float. Mr. Nguyen Manh Hung was born in 1968 in Ha Tinh province, Vietnam. He established a beverage manufacturing company in 1995 which became Nafoods in 1995 and has been the Chairman and CEO of Nafoods since then.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$28.2 million which would be funded by (i) an up to US$8 million VND denominated corporate bond which is convertible into common shares of the Company; (ii) internally generated cash, and (iii) equity/ bank borrowings.
location_description: The project locations are Nghe An province, Long An province and Central Highland in Vietnam
development_impact: Farmer reach: The Project is expected to increase the number of farmers who supply raw materials or are employed at the Company's own land by about 11,500. Much of the Company's operations are located in economically depressed or unproductive areas. Because Nafoods is planning to provide its suppliers with high quality seedlings from own nurseries and guidance on the planting density in exchange for off-take of the crop, the yields can improve from Vietnam average of 15-30MT/ ha to 45-50 MT/ ha. Jobs creation and linkages: The Project is expected to create 150 full time equivalent new jobs which represents an above average impact compared to other agribusiness investments of similar size. Market creation: By supporting Nafoods, IFC is helping to strengthen the image of Vietnam as a reliable global supplier of passion fruit concentrate. In particular, the work planned by the Project to help rationalize the supply chain will also be beneficial to the broader sector. The resulting efficiencies are expected to both facilitate competition and put a pressure on less efficient smaller players (encouraging consolidation) and promote better practices throughout the value chain. Specifically, other passion fruit producers are expected to improve their traceability and food safety practices to match the efforts being undertaken by Nafoods.
additionality: Financial Additionality: IFC can provide long-term patient capital with a long grace period, as well as a diversification in borrowing sources since all other loans are from local banks. Non Financial Additionalities: - IFC's strong network within the agribusiness sector: IFC can introduce potential business partners to Nafoods and help the Company expand its customer base internationally. Furthermore, Nafoods highly values IFC's expertise in the fresh fruit business and would like to have an IFC representative on the board of directors who can advise the Company, especially on the expansion into the fresh fruit business. - Environmental & Social (E&S): Implementing E&S recommendations will allow the Company to operate at higher E&S standards. As part of the appraisal, per IFC's advice, the Company has undertaken a third party social assessment on its land holdings to identify gaps between the Company's current practices and IFC's Standards. - IFC Advisory Services & Collaboration Across WBG: The Company may benefit from collaboration with the World Bank/ FCI Vietnam Agribusiness Competitiveness Project. In addition, IFC would provide Nafoods with technical supports in various areas including food safety and corporate governance which would help build a sustainable and effective business and strengthen the Company's supply chain.

company_name: RESPONSABILITY ACCESS TO CLEAN POWER FUND S.A., SICAV-SIF
project_description: Access to Clean Power Fund (“ACPF” or the “Fund”) is a US$150mn fund (in the process of being raised), which will extend debt financing to companies providing renewable energy and energy efficiency solutions in the retail and off-grid Pay-As-You-Go (PAYGO) sector, and in the commercial and industrial sector, both part of the Distributed Generation (“DG”) market. ACPF is the scale-up of the Energy Access Fund (“EAF”), into which IFC invested in 2015.
sponsor_shareholders: ACPF will have multiple shareholders, including IFC, and will be managed by responsAbility (the “Fund manager”). Founded in 2003 in Zurich, responsAbility is an asset manager with US$3 billion under management across 15 funds in 10 offices globally. responsAbility’s funds provide financing predominantly to non-listed firms in emerging markets across energy, finance and agriculture sectors while responsAbility’s investees help to meet the basic energy needs of mainly the lower income households as well as SMEs. responsAbility is owned by Swiss financial institutions and its employees.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed US$45 million quasi-equity investment, as part of the US$150 million Fund raise, is comprised of: (i) US$30 million for IFC's own account; and (iii) US$15 million from IFC acting as implementing entity of Clean Technology Fund Dedicated Private Sector Programs III.
location_description: ACPF will focus on financing companies in Sub-Saharan Africa, and Asia.
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is increased access to energy by un(der)served households and SMEs with unreliable access to affordable energy, and increased access to financing for manufacturers and distributors of DG. The Project is expected to target predominantly lower income segments and will contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the Project will enhance financial integration and inclusiveness through the demonstration and market enabling channels.
additionality: The debt and mezzanine financing required by small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and other companies offering distributed energy solutions is often difficult to access in local markets in Sub-Saharan Africa and Asia. IFC's expected additionality in this Project is both financial and non-financial: (i) the financing structure; (ii) resource mobilization; and (iii) the sharing of global knowledge and international best practices.
Company Name: RESPONSABILITY ACCESS TO CLEAN POWER FUND S.A., SICAV-SIF

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of a $15 million loan to Reforestadora de Sinu S.A. Sucursal Colombia (Sinu or the Company) to establish about 5,700 ha of eucalyptus plantations and maintain farms already planted in the Antioquia and Cordoba departments of Colombia (the Project). The Company started pilot tree plantings in 2013. In its first five years of planting, Sinu established roughly 4,800 ha plantations and conservation areas clustered in a region of sparsely populated and degraded pasturelands. Sinu aims to reach a total planted area of 10,500 ha by 2021, managing the plantations on a 7-year harvest cycle in conformity with the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) Principles and Criteria and is committed to meeting IFC’s Performance Standards.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was established in 2010 as a long-term investment by members of the Solari Donaggio family of Chile.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: US$ 15 million senior loan with a grace period and principal amortization aligned to meet the deferred operating cash flow profile of plantation forestry.
location_description: The plantations are distributed across an area of roughly 25km radius of San Pedro de Uraba, straddling Antioquia and Cordoba departments.
development_impact: Environmental and/or Social (E&S): IFC anticipates the Project will generate several important positive impacts on the environment. - GHG emissions: This sustainable forest management Project will implement carbon sequestration activities that result in significant GHG emission reductions at an average of 155,000 tons CO2eq per year (negative net emissions) and zero gross GHG emissions. - Climate Resilience: As part of its operations and with IFC's support, the Project will contribute toward strengthening climate resilience in the area. This entails employing techniques such as the use of meteorological information, identification of drought and wind-resistant planting material, silviculture to improve moisture retention, and further enhancing Sinu's fire management practices. - Sustainable Land Management: The Project will make a contribution toward sustainable land management in an area characterized by extensive agriculture, land degradation from cattle ranching. Stakeholder impact: IFC anticipates that the Project will strongly contribute to the development of employment and economic activity in the area, improving resilience and stability in a post-conflict region which can be considered a frontier. Formal employment opportunities are scarce and large companies are absent in the area, apart from Sinu which represents the only formal employment option outside subsistence agriculture. The development of competitive agriculture and agribusiness sector is central to Colombia's overall efforts to diversify its economy.
additionality: Financing Structure: The proposed Project requires longer tenors than those available in the market and which are especially important for forestry. Standard Setting: The proposed investment will enable IFC to facilitate the adoption of appropriate E&S practices by the Company. Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: IFC has a role to play in sharing its extensive global knowledge in the forestry sector and helping the Company access export markets in due course. Knowledge Dissemination:IFC's global expertise from similar projects in other parts of the world provides benchmarks to help Sinu assess operating standards, and performance expectations.

company_name: JERONIMO MARTINS COLOMBIA S A S
project_description: Jeronimo Martins, SGPS, SA (“the Group”), one of the largest European food retailers, has requested IFC to provide a long-term loan to partially finance the next two year’s investment plan of its subsidiary, Ara Tiendas (“Ara”) in Colombia. Ara is a chain of neighbourhood food retail stores, having started its operations in 2013 in Colombia. Over the next couple of years its expansion plan includes both the opening of new stores and distribution centres that will provide logistic support to the stores (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Jeronimo Martins SGPS SA is a Portugal-based group engaged mainly in the food retail business. The Group focuses on distribution and sale of food and other consumer good products, employing more than 100,000 people across 3 countries – Portugal, Poland and since 2013, Colombia – with an annual revenue of € 16.2 billion and an EBITDA margin of 5.7%, as of FY17. The Group owns a portfolio of brands in these countries, including Biedronka and Hebe in Poland; Pingo Doce and Recheio in Portugal and Ara Tiendas in Colombia. The Group is listed in the Lisbon stock exchange (PSI-20) since 1989 and is controlled by a family holding – Sociedade Francisco Manuel dos Santos, SGPS, SE – that owns 56.1% of the share capital.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The next two years of investment in Colombia is estimated between €500-600 million. IFC proposes to provide an A loan of up to US$93 million in local currency to partially finance this investment plan.
location_description: Investments under the Project can be made in small and large cities throughout Colombia.
development_impact: 1) Job creation: The Project will create job opportunities, including in frontier regions, for local communities and women. 2) Development of frontier regions: The Project will finance the expansion of proximity discount stores in the local neighborhoods across the country, including frontier regions. 3) Boost formality and tax generation: The shops will contribute to boost formality and tax generation. 4) Impact on customers: The Project will provide quality products at very competitive price, thus helping in improving the living standards for the local population. The Project targets to reach the vast majority of the national population and will focus primarily on low- and middle-income groups. 5) Support of SMEs: The Project will strengthen the SME suppliers and the local supply chain, a vast majority of the products sold in the shops being sourced and produced locally.
additionality: 1) De-risking: It is Jeronimo Martins first investment in Colombia, so IFC's strong knowledge and presence in Colombia are valuable. 2) Long maturity in local currency: Local currency lending with long tenor to finance ramping up operations. 3) IFC global footprint: Industry expertise and knowledge sharing in the retail sector.
Company Name: JERONIMO MARTINS COLOMBIA S A S

sector: Pottery, Ceramic, and Plumbing Fixtures (Including Kitchenware)
project_description: Ferrum S.A. de Cerámica y Metalurgia (“Ferrum” or the “Company”), founded more than 100 years ago, is Argentina’s largest producer of ceramic sanitary ware. Ferrum sells mostly toilets, sinks, stands, bidets, and urinals which are produced in its two plants in Avellaneda and Pilar (Buenos Aires Province). Ferrum employs over 1,500 people and commercializes its product through a well-established distribution network. The project consists of investments to be done at the two major plants for the next two years, regarding new equipment and upgrades.
sponsor_shareholders: Ferrum is controlled by FV S.A. (an IFC client) and Sydney Inversora. The remaining (12%) is publicly listed in the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at approximately US$20 million. IFC is proposing to participate with an A Loan of US$16 million (IFC’s own account).
location_description: The investments will be made in Ferrum’s plants in Pilar and Avellaneda (Buenos Aires Province, Argentina).
development_impact: The most significant expected Project-level impact is derived from: (i) economy-wide effects through expansion of local manufacturing capacity and improved productivity; (ii) environmental and resource efficiency via more efficient production processes.
additionality: Long term financing: IFC will be providing Ferrum long-term financing with tenors that cannot be matched by easily matched by the local market. Stamp of Approval: IFC's long-term commitment to support Ferrum's expansion plans is expected to send a positive signal to the market and provide comfort to current and potential investors on the quality and sustainability of the Company.

company_name: S.A. SAN MIGUEL A.G.I.C.I. Y F.
project_description: The proposed investment consists on a $60 mm A/B long-term loan to San Miguel to be used in Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and South Africa for (i) short and medium-term debt refinancing; (ii) the financing of the 2018-2020 capex program; and (iii) permanent working capital. The total project cost is $152.5 mm
sponsor_shareholders: The Otero Monsegur and Miguens Bemberg families conform San Miguel’s controlling group, with an aggregate 53% shareholding interest and 83% of voting rights. The ANSES (Argentine public pension fund) has 26% economic interest and the remainder floats in the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is $152.5 mm comprised of: 2018-2020 CAPEX for $90.5 mm, which includes: (i) Argentina: relocation of packing plant and offices, improvements in plantations, and miscellaneous investments, (ii) Uruguay: development of new lemon plantations and the construction of a new industrial plant, (iii) Peru: miscellaneous investments in packinghouse and plantations, and (iv) South Africa: miscellaneous investments in packinghouse and plantations. Debt Refinancing: for a total of $25 mm Permanent working capital financing for $37 mm IFC investment will consist of a long-term loan of up to $60 mm, with a portion syndicated among B Lenders. The rest will be financed with a Parallel Loan for a similar amount and A/B loan structure, with the remaining financed through internal cash generation
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Buenos Aires, Argentina, with field operations in Tucuman province (Argentina), Uruguay, South Africa and Peru.
development_impact: The most significant, expected Project-level outcomes vary by country: in Argentina, these represent employment preservation in a frontier region and generation of foreign revenues during a macroeconomic crisis; in Uruguay, they relate to expansion of high-value agriculture accompanied by job creation and export growth; in Peru, they focus on significant yield improvements that enhance sector competitiveness and reduce environmental impacts of production. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater global market integration for Uruguay's citrus sector.
additionality: (i) Longer Tenors: As it takes approx. 7-8 years for a citrus tree to provide fruit of acceptable export quality and ~2 years for grapes, the proposed Project requires longer tenors than those available in the market. Currently, only IFC and other multilaterals can reach the proposed tenors in Argentina. (ii) Resource Mobilization / Introducing new relationships: Total mobilization will amount to $65 mm including a B and Parallel B loan to be funded by Rabobank ($45 mm) and the remaining ($20 mm) to be mobilized by Rabobank and IFC as Joint Lead Arrangers to other financial institutions to be defined. IFC share of total mobilization will be $32.5 mm. (iii) Standard setting and best practices: The proposed Project would allow IFC to continue to provide E&S assistance and advice with regards to Tucuman and Uruguay operations. Since the new scope of the Project is also reaching South Africa and Peru, it will allow to spread the application of best practices and IFC's Performance Standards in those locations which had not been reviewed in previous transactions.
Company Name: S.A. SAN MIGUEL A.G.I.C.I. Y F.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan in local currency to Metro Wholesale Myanmar Limited (‘MWML’ or the ‘Company’) , to support the Company in launching its wholesale trade operations in Myanmar (the ‘Project’). MWML is the local subsidiary of Metro AG, Germany (‘Metro’ or the ‘Sponsor’ ) , a leading global retailer specializing in cash & carry food retail and holding 85% stake in the Company. Yoma Strategic Holdings Ltd., (‘Yoma’) a Myanmar based conglomerate listed in Singapore and also an existing IFC client is a minority shareholder i n the Company holding 15% stake.
sponsor_shareholders: Metro headquartered in Dü sseldorf , Germany, operates more than 750 wholesale stores in 27 co untries across Europe and Asia under its brands ‘METRO’ and ‘MAKRO’. Metro offers a broad range of food and other consumer good products which is geared to commercial customers, particularly to hotel and restaurant owners, catering firms, small stores , as w ell as other service providers. Metro also runs a retail hypermarket operation in Germany under the brand name ‘Real’ with b oth store-based business and online stores . ? Metro is listed in the Frankfurt stock exchange and has a significant free float of a bit less than 50%, which is held by public and institutional investors. ? IFC already has an existing relationship with Metro through its Global Fo od safety advisory program where in it has provided training and other capacity building support to SME suppliers of Metro in markets like Ukraine, Russia and Kazakhstan .
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project, which is estimated to cost US$40 million, consists mainly of a central warehouse in Yangon and future satellite warehouses and cross-docking platforms across Myanmar. It is proposed an IFC loan of approximately US$ 25 million to fund the Project .
location_description: MWML, which was incorporated in 2017, is headquartered in Yangon with its central warehouse currently under construction at the Thilawa Special Economic Zone near Yangon. It plans to also have satellite warehouses and cross docking platforms in other cities.
development_impact: Stakeholder impact: The Company will source around 50% of its products locally, largely from SMEs. thereby creating a large and reliable source of demand for those suppliers, broadening their market, and give other smaller suppliers a chance to develop and become competitive. These suppliers will also work with small and marginal farmers across the country to help promote modern practices like contract farming, smart input use and post-harvest management thereby increasing their productivity and enabling them to sell their produce at remunerative prices. The Company will improve the local distribution and logistics infrastructure; and introduce higher standards and efficient delivery practices for its clients. This is expected to result in lower prices of quality products for end consumers. The Project is expected to create more than 200 jobs during operations as well as many indirect jobs in the services sector. MWML will contribute to sector formalization and increased tax revenues for the government through transparent tax collection practices. Market impact: By investing in training, and implementation of international standards for local suppliers and service providers, the Company will contribute to better integrating them in domestic and possibly regional markets. This can help positively impact the local agriculture sector.
additionality: Local currency solution: IFC will provide long term local currency financing that is not readily available in the market and will support the Company's anticipated gradual ramp-up of its activities while matching the currency of its revenues. Advisory for local suppliers: IFC will seek to replicate its past experience of successfully working with Metro on food safety advisory by providing training to MWML's local suppliers, including farmers, specifically for meat, fruits and vegetables and help upgrade the quality, safety and traceability of their products.

project_description: Disclaimer: This SII is prepared and distributed in advance of CLN’s Board of Directors’ consideration of the proposed transaction. This document should not be construed as presuming the outcome of CLN’s Board of Directors’ decision and is not in any way a commitment by CLN. Project Description: The IFC proposes to provide an up to EUR€50 million loan to support CLN Group’s expansion plans in South Africa. CLN is a leading automotive stamping part manufacturer based in Italy and a repeat IFC client. It has 7 existing plants in South Africa and is looking to expand its production to serve new vehicles produced by automotive manufactures. It produces and assembles steel and aluminum automotive structural parts and skin panels .
sponsor_shareholders: CLN Group: Founded in 1949, CLN is an Italian company that operates in three business segments: Steel Metal Stamping (“MA”), Steel Wheel Manufacturing (“MW”) and Steel Service Centers (“SSC”). CLN is the preferred steel stamping and wheel supplier of many OEMs. CLN is owned 65% by Magnetto-Perris Family, 25% by Arcelor Mittal, and 10% by Marubeni-Itoshu . ]
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total proposed project amounts up to EUR€100 million, including project and maintenance capital expenditures and working capital in South Africa. The proposed project will be financed through a package of up to EUR€100 million from IFC’s own account and other parallel loans, including IFC acting in capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (“MCPP”).
location_description: The proposed Project is located in South Africa, where CLN, through its subsidiaries, have plants across Rosslyn, East London, and Port Elizabeth.
development_impact: The most significant project-level outcome is (i) increased value addition resulting from greater localization, which will improve customer access to a more reliable supply of good quality automotive components and parts built to the highest standards, (ii) a continuing focus on proactive career development opportunities that provide increased participation of women in more technical roles. Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote sector integration via value addition in the local economy, introduction of new processes products, and skills upgrading which will contribute to increasing value chain integration.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC aims to support an existing client to further expand capacity in line with the industry's growth. By providing this financing package, IFC seeks to promote localization, increasing manufacturing complexity, and the strengthening of the competitiveness of the local supply chain for an automotive parts producer in the South African market. IFC provides financial additionality through a longer tenor (7 years) and resource mobilization. IFC's non-financial additionality includes continued support to maintain environmental and safety (E&S) best practices as it implements the next stage of its growth plans in South Africa.

project_description: The project involves a debt financing package to PT Trans Corpora (“Trans Corp” or “the Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of CT Corp, which is one of Indonesia’s largest conglomerates and engaged in various sectors including tourism, leisure, retail, property, financial services, transportation and media. Trans Corp has three subsidiaries – Trans Lifestyle, Trans Entertainment and Trans Media. Trans Lifestyle has additional subsidiaries key of which is Trans Retail that has a central focus on retail activities and, to a lesser extent, property development and hotels. IFC’s investment will be used to (a) expand the retail and tourism (hotels) and related property components and for general corporate purposes corresponding to these activities, and (b) strengthen the Company’s balance sheet through lengthening of the maturities of some of its debt.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company derives its revenues mainly from its retail operations but also from hotels, shopping malls, theme parks and media businesses. Trans Retail - its retail subsidiary and one of the largest Indonesian retailers – is currently operating 110 hypermarkets and supermarkets in 51 cities across the country (some of which under the French Carrefour brand) as well as distribution centres. The Company is further expanding its footprint by opening new modern stores in more cities in under-served regions, thereby meeting the needs of the fast-growing middle class. At the same time, it will expand its wholesale services for small store owners and increase its purchases of local products from many small and medium sized (“SME”) farmers and suppliers located in these regions. The Company is also investing in new hotels to cater primarily to local and regional tourists. The Project Sponsor is Mr. Chairul Tanjung who, along with his family, wholly own CT Corp , the parent . Mr. Tanjung , who founded the group in 1987, is a well-known Indonesian business man.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is estimated at US$275 million. IFC is assisting the Company to arrange the entire debt of US$275 million being raised for the Project. IFC’s proposed investment will comprise (a) an A loan of up to US$75 million for its own account; and (b) a mobilization of (i) a trust loan of up to US$106.25 million from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority / SAFE through the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program ( together called the “Trust Loans” ) ; and (ii) B loans of up to US$125 million from commercial lenders. The final amounts of the A Loan, Trust Loans and B Loans will be determined among all lenders and the Company so that the aggregate loan amount does not exceed US$275 million.
location_description: The Project will be located across several cities in Indonesia, including many less developed tier II and tier III cities.
development_impact: By expanding access to modern retail, tourism and leisure infrastructure in the country's less developed regions, the Project will (i) promote food affordability and safety, (ii) support SMEs along the retail value chain, (iii) improve job quality, increase wages and other associated benefits as well as female participation in the workforce, (iv) improve energy efficiency, especially in new buildings, through green building certification; (v) increase tax revenues for the government and (vi) enhance social and economic benefits from the development of integrated sustainable communities in under-served regions.
additionality: IFC's role will include (i) provision of long term financing and mobilization - in the form of A and Trust Loans, which will have longer maturities more suited for the Project operations and associated cash flows, (ii) acting as a catalyst to complete the required debt finance, (iii) providing its seal of approval which is expected to support the Company's plans of listing its retail subsidiary in the future, and (iv) enhancing the Project's environmental, social, health and safety standards through the application of best practices in areas such as energy and waste management, food safety, life and fire safety as well as energy efficiency of buildings.

project_description: Capria Fund LLC, a Delaware series limited liability company (the “Fund”), is targeting a US$100 million fund to make (i) investments into fund management companies in emerging markets; (ii) commitments into emerging market investment funds as a limited partner; and (iii) direct investments into the entrepreneur-led local businesses invested into by selected fund managers. The project will be additionally supported by the Blended Finance Facility of the IDA18 IFC-MIGA Private Sector Window (PSW), created by the Word Bank Group to catalyze private sector investment in IDA countries, with a focus on fragile and conflict-affected states.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by Capria Manager LLC, a Washington State limited liability company that contracts with Capria Ventures LLC, a global impact investment firm founded in 2012 to develop scaled and profitable risk capital funds in emerging markets. The Capria team is led by Dave Richards, Will Poole, Daniel Kranzler, and Jack Knellinger.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes an equity investment of up to US$8 million, not to exceed 20% of total committed capital. IFC , acting as Implementing Entity of the IDA PSW BFF , will co-invest up to US$5 million in equity alongside IFC, not to exceed 20% of the Fund’s total capital commitments.
location_description: The Fund will be a series limited liability company registered in Delaware, managed from Seattle, Washington; Nairobi, Kenya; and Bangalore, India; and plans to invest capital in Sub-Saharan Africa, South/South-East Asia and Latin America.
additionality: IFC's support as an investor in the Fund is expected to (i) play a catalytic role as a DFI investor to help the Fund achieve first close and critical mass; and (ii) mobilize resources, with IFC's commitment expected to enable the Fund to get closer to its target size, thereby increasing the Fund's ability to positively impact businesses and fund managers in the target regions. Expected development impact includes (i) support for new and existing local fund management teams that will activate sufficient capital and related expertise to enable promising entrepreneurs and small businesses to have access to finance; (ii) job creation and economic growth through financing SMEs, which are a growth driver in the target geographies, with Capria Fund's fund managers helping address the financing gap faced by small and growing businesses; and (iii) operational and financial improvements, implementation of best-practice corporate governance and ESG improvements of local businesses.

project_description: The proposed project involves IFC investing equity in an INR equivalent of approximately US$ 23 million in Srinivasa Farms Private Limited (“Srinivasa” or the “Company”). The proposed investment will support Srinivasa to: (a) expand its existing layer, broiler and breeding operations by setting up additional farms and hatcheries; (b) expand its feed mills and add soya refineries; (c) setup a food park; and (d) setup chicken and egg processing businesses (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Srinivasa operates an integrated layer and broiler breeding business in India and is headquartered in Hyderabad, Telangana (TS). The Company has presence in soya, feed, layer and broiler breeding and contract farming. The Chairman of Srinivasa, Mr. Jagapati Rao Chitturi started Srinivasa in 1965 and has over five decades of experience across all facets of the poultry industry. The Company is now managed by his son Mr. Suresh Chitturi. The family collectively owns 80.04% of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$83 million and IFC’s proposed investment is up to INR equivalent of US$23 million investment in the form of straight equity / compulsorily convertible preference shares / compulsorily convertible debentures in the Company.
development_impact: The project is expected to have the following development impacts: a) Farmers: A greater number of contract farmers engaged in broiler production will benefit from stable access to key inputs and expertise as well as reliable off-take, which help improve and stabilize their incomes. The layer farmers will benefit from access to quality inputs (DOCs and feed) which should have a positive impact on profitability of their operations. Smallholder producers of maize and soybeans will gain improved access to market as the company increases its feed production. b) Employees: The Company's expansion will create over 5,000 jobs directly and ensure working conditions that are in line with IFC Performance Standards, which will constitute an improvement over prevalent industry practices. Potentially twice as many jobs would be created along with the value chain, contributing to skill building and non-farm employment. A high share of employment created in the poultry sector tends to be at the bottom of pyramid (BOP). c) Consumers: The consumers will benefit from increased access to quality processed poultry products that meet food safety standards in a market that is largely dominated by open air sales.
additionality: IFC has the following additionality: a) IFC's own account equity will strengthen the financial soundness, creditworthiness and governance of the client, enabling access to a wider pool of financiers in the longer term. b) Knowledge, innovation and capacity building through sharing IFC's global expertise in the poultry sector, technical advice on best operating practices, and improvement of food safety standards. c) Standard setting through provision of expertise in environmental and social standards and corporate governance which will help the Company in its next phase of growth.

project_description: The objective of the proposed investment of up to US$40 million for Chenggang Biotech Group Co., Ltd. (Chenguang” or the “Company”) is to support the Company’s permanent working capital needs to increase production. Chenguang is a leading producer of natural, plant-based food extracts and additives in China. The Company currently sources raw materials from Xinjiang, China and Andhra Pradesh, India, and is looking to expand its sourcing footprint to Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Lu Qingguo, Chairman, Founder and General Manager, is the largest shareholder of Chenguang with a shareholding of 18.58%. He is an executive council member of the China Food Additives and Ingredients Association. He has over 20 years of industry experience in the natural extracts space. Chairman Lu Qingguo owns 18.58% of Chenguang and his wife, Ms. Li Yuezhai (board member of the Company) holds 4.17%. 13 senior management team members own 5.35%. The remaining shares are owned by public investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is around US$30-40 million and IFC investment is an up to US$40 million equivalent, 6-year, senior, secured CNY loan.
location_description: Handan, Hebei Province, China
development_impact: Development Impact: - To consumers, the Project is expected to deliver high quality natural ingredients at a larger scale, which will in turn be used in various consumer goods, such as healthcare products, processed foods, cosmetics etc. - To employees, the Project can create new knowledge of production technologies and train staff to fill gaps in the current job market that is facing a shortage of highly skilled talents in food manufacturing and safety monitoring. - To suppliers and distributors, the Project will engage various actors, domestic and global, in the value chain for products and services. It will also help improve the quality standards of food exporters in China. Market Impact: By supporting a global provider of natural pigments and extracts that generates 30+% of revenue through exports, IFC hopes to raise the quality and competitiveness of natural ingredients that are used broadly in industrial value chains, to increase visibility of Chinese companies with sophisticated technologies, to promote South-South investment between China and India.
additionality: Currently, all of the Company's debts are short-term. By providing long term local currency financing that is not readily available for most privately sector companies in China, IFC helps strengthen Chenguang's capital structure, putting the Company in a more prudent financial position.

project_description: IFC, acting for its own account and in its capacity as implementing entity of the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP), is considering to invest a minimum of US$ 3 million alongside other investors including TLCom who will invest up to US$ 4 million in the Company. Launched in 2014, Twiga is a fast growing, mobile-based B2B m-commerce platform using technology to enhance supply chains by more effectively and rapidly consolidating highly fragmented supply and demand. Starting with the large target addressable mass-market Fresh Food and Vegetable (“FFV”) segment, Twiga more efficiently matches supply and demand between small-scale vendors and small-scale farmers. By cutting out multiple layers of middlemen, Twiga eliminates wastage and inefficiencies in the FFV value chain, ultimately resulting in lower food prices for mass market end-consumers. Twiga offers stable, transparent prices and guaranteed offtake for farmers and convenience and reliability for small-scale vendors, e.g. street sellers and kiosks through the platform. Twiga started off with bananas, but has since grown to include other produce such as mangoes, potatoes, onions, tomatoes and cabbages and plans to onboard more products in the near future.
