sponsor_shareholders: Twiga’s sponsors are Peter Njonjo (Co-founder and Chairman) and Grant Brooke (Co-founder and CEO). Other key shareholders in the Company include: DOB Equity, Omidyar Network, Wamda Capital, 1776 Seed Investors, Alpha Mundi and Blue Haven Initiative.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, acting for its own account and in its capacity as implementing entity of the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Foo d Security Program (GAFSP), is considering to invest a minimum of US $ 3 million alongsid e other investors , including TLCom who will invest up to US$ 4 million in the Company.
location_description: Kenya.
development_impact: This Project will result in positive outcomes for key stakeholders in the agricultural supply chain (farmers and vendors) and the environment at large. - Smallholder farmers: The Project will (i) increase access to markets through guaranteed off-take (ii) increase prices (iii) increase efficiency through transparent pricing, swift digital payments and technical assistance, which will result in increased productivity - Small Scale Vendors: The Project will (i) increase access to supply (ii) improve quality of produce (iii) improve productivity, which will result in increased vendor incomes - Reduce Post-Harvest Food Loss: The Project's post-harvest food loss rate is expected to be 5%, significantly lower than the 30% in the traditional market. The Project will also result in improved market outcomes by increasing competition in the sector through innovative channels which compel industry players to improve on quality and pricing of produce in order to compete. The Project will enhance integration of different stakeholders in the agricultural value chain working towards increasing farmer productivity. In addition, the Project could increase access to new services (e.g. credit) by reducing informality and demonstrating that farmers can be reached in a commercially sustainable way through technology
additionality: IFC will provide the following financial and non-financial additionality: 1. Financial Additionality: IFC will provide early stage funding to help scale the business from its startup phase 2. Non-Financial Additionality: IFC will provide knowledge, innovation and help build capacity in the Company as it positions itself for growth. This will be achieved through: - Advisory projects with the Food Safety team to develop Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) that will increase farmer yields - Exchange of experiences from other last mile delivery and e-commerce players that IFC has invested in which can provide lessons to the Company from these investments - IFC's Infrastructure Team can help with infrastructure and logistics efficiencies once the Company reaches scale

project_description: Camlin Fine Sciences Limited (“Camlin” or “the Company”) is inter alia engaged in research, development, manufacturing, and marketing of specialty chemicals and blends, which are used in a wide array of food, feed, animal and pet nutrition, fragrance, pharmaceutical and industrial products.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor, Ashish Dandekar along with his family and related entities own s 22.3 4 percent equity shares in the Company . Ashish Dandekar has over 30 years of experience in the fine chemicals and pharmaceuticals industry and has been instrumental in the growth of the Company since setting up the anti-oxidants plant in Tarapur in 1984 (prior to demerger from erstwhile Camlin Limited) . The Company is publicly listed on Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE). While t he institutional investors own 21.82 percent , the Directors and relatives (other than sponsors) own 7. 84 per cent. The balance 4 8 percent is held by other public shareholders (as on March 31, 2018) .
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC prop oses an investment of up to US$ 30 million to part finance this capital expenditure plan through a combination of debt and quasi-equity instruments.
location_description: The project is proposed to be located in in Dahej SEZ in the state of Gujarat, India.
development_impact: a) Improved Access: The Project will ensure availability of diphenols and produce a range of their derivatives, such as antioxidants, performance chemicals and aroma chemicals which are used in food products, supplements, animal feed, pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals. The demand for anti-oxidants is growing due to the centralized mass production of food and feed, ageing population, change in lifestyles, and increasing consciousness of health among the end consumers. The Project will help address the shortage of diphenols which hinders the growth of the sectors that heavily rely on the derivatives. b) Lower Prices: The cost of production of diphenols at the Dahej facility is expected to be lower than the cost at existing diphenols plant in Italy. IFC expects some of the cost savings to translate into lower price for the customers. c) Employment: The Project will create high skilled jobs and allow for skills upgrading of the local employees through training and technology transfer from the facility in Italy to the Dahej plant. d) Environmental Effects: The new plant in Dahej will have higher efficiency in terms of waste management, greenhouse gas emissions, energy consumption and other operational efficiencies as compared to Camlin's existing plant in Italy. e) Competitiveness: The Project will help Camlin innovate new product formulations that improve the quality of specialty chemicals and make the manufacturing process more cost effective, more customized to meet local needs, and environmentally friendly.
additionality: a) Financing Structure: IFC will provide a mix of long-term foreign currency senior debt and a quasi-equity instrument. This kind of structure is not easily available from local banks at reasonable terms, especially without adequate fixed asset security cover. b) Environmental and Social Standards: IFC will assist Camlin formulate and implement an E&S action plan, and introduce social/labor management systems, which are enhanced to correspond with recognized and accepted best practices in this sector. c) Knowledge and Innovation: IFC will share its global knowledge and expertise in the specialty chemicals space as well as facilitate relationships with IFC's global agribusiness clients who are potential clients of Camlin.

project_description: DrBridge Holdings Ltd. ("Vezeeta" or "the Company") is creating a digital healthcare platform for the Middle East and North Africa ("MENA"), focusing on booking and medical apps for private doctors and patients. Launched in Egypt in 2012, Vezeeta salso operates in Jordan and plans to soon expand to Saudi Arabia and the broader MENA region. The Company is transforming the way patients and doctors schedule appointments and manage health outcomes in MENA. The two main product offerings are: (1) a consumer-facing web app and mobile app where users can find doctors by neighborhood, specialty, insurance and ratings to book an appointment; and (2) Clinic management software and premium mobile apps for doctors, which enable them to manage appointments and patient data as well as to communicate with patients.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Amir Barsoum, the CEO and co-founder of Vezeeta. Amir was formerly at McKinsey and then went on to become the Head of Strategy for the MENA region at AstraZeneca, a global biopharmaceutical company. The primary shareholders include the two co-founders (Amir Barsoum and Ahmed Badr) , Technology Development Fund II , Badia Impact Fund , Vostok New Ventures, and BECO Capital.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment in Vezeeta is an equity investment of up to US$ 1 million.
location_description: Vezeeta is headquartered in Cairo, Egypt and has operations in both Egypt and Jordan.
development_impact: - Improved access to quality care by lowering the transaction costs of finding relevant doctors and specialists. Through Vezeeta, patients are able to search for doctors based specialty, location, gender, etc. This is particularly relevant for patients who would otherwise struggle to find doctors to meet their needs, such as female patients who prefer female doctors (+20% of the doctors on the Vezeeta are female) and rural patients seeking medical care (represent 19% of the bookings). - Increased transparency and accountability through doctor details and rating system, which in turn improves health outcomes and patient welfare. - Enhanced connectivity within the broader healthcare system through roll-out of new and future products including pharma detailing, doctor-to-doctor referrals, lab integration, etc.
additionality: - Stamp of Approval: IFC's support is expected to enhance Vezeeta's profile and credibility in a nascent sector, providing comfort for future co-investors, regulators, and operating partners. - IFC's global industry expertise and client network: IFC will support Vezeeta in its expansion goals by leveraging our knowledge and relationships across the healthcare space globally and in MENA in particular. - Institution building: IFC will promote best practices in insurance, corporate governance, and E&S, which are critical for a growth stage company.

project_description: Financing to support Novare Africa Property Fund II (“NAPF” or the “Sponsor”) to acquire, upgrade and expand the Twin Palms Mall , a 7, 500 sqm GLA one-level strip mall, by 4 ,500sqm GLA in Salama Park, Lusaka , Zambia (the Project) . The project will be implemented through a local SPV and will be anchored by established South African supermarket chain s . The Twin Palms Mall (39410), is a pipeline split project of Great North Mall (38397).
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is NAPF II, a US$351 million real estate fund focused on commercial property development in Sub-Saharan Africa. NAPF II achieved final close in June 2016. Novare Fund Manager Limited (Mauritius) is the fund manager and Novare Equity Partners (PTY) Limited (South Africa) is the sub-advisor (jointly " Novare ").
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US $2 4 . 5 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$ 6 . 8 million A loan for IFC's own account.
location_description: The Project will be located in Salama Park, Lusaka, Zambia.
development_impact: The Projects will contribute to economic growth and urban development through: (i) Jobs: direct and indirect employment opportunities for local communities during the construction and operations including jobs created or maintained throughout the supply chain (SMEs). Construction workers learn advanced construction methods and safety standards from a high-quality South African developer. (ii) Consumers: access to higher quality goods for the low-to-middle income and base of pyramid population in an underserved area (i.e. through supermarket anchors with higher food quality/safety standards that are currently unavailable in the immediate area). (iii) Green building: Novare has indicated a willingness to adopt EDGE where possible within its development pipeline.
additionality: (i) Long-term Partner: IFC seeks to develop a strategic relationship with Novare to support its development pipeline in multiple African countries with long-tenor debt, which is often not available; (ii) Ensure that NAPF II maintains corporate governance, environmental, social, health and safety structures at international standards; (iii) Green Building / Energy efficiency advice: help the NAPF II identify opportunities for energy efficiency and gain EDGE certification.

sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: Time Technoplast Limited (TTL or the Company) is India’s largest manufacturer of polymer-based industrial packaging (IP) products (e.g. plastic drums, tanks, pails, pallets, Intermediate Bulk Containers). It also produces high-density polyethylene (HDPE) pipes, technical and lifestyle products, composite gas cylinders and cross-laminated (MOX) films. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to INR2,600 million (approximately US$40 million) to fund the Company’s capital expenditure in India.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company has 4 co-founders / sponsors – Mr. Anil Jain (Managing Director) , Mr. Bharat Vageria, Mr. Raghupathy Thyagarajan and Mr. Naveen Jain.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment is a senior INR denominated loan of up to INR2,600 million (approximately US$40 million) will be used to fund the Company’s capital expenditure in India .
location_description: The project locations will be at the Company’s existing manufacturing facilities in India, including Daman, Silvassa, Baddi, Panoli and others.
development_impact: The expected development impact for the project is the following: (i) Improved customer access to more packaging and other value-added products: (ii) Positive environmental effects due to recycling of polymer; and (iii) Positive economywide effects due to creation of additional direct and indirect jobs.
additionality: Financial Additionality - Financing beyond what is available: IFC's loan with its longer tenor and sufficient grace period will provide greater cushion for business cycles especially as the Company is pursuing multiple growth initiatives. Non Financial Additionality - IFC's experience and global network: IFC has a large global network and experience in emerging markets. It can help the Company improve environment and safety standards in a competitive market.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an IFC investment package of €30 million ($36 million equivalent) loan to Mbiza Trading (“Mbiza” or the “Company”) to support its expansion of blueberry farms and related infrastructure in the Republic of South Africa. Mbiza is a Mauritian trading and holding company that focuses on the production and marketing of blueberries under its proprietary “OZblu” brand. Established in 2014, Mbiza has quickly expanded to currently manage its own farm (either wholly or partially owned) in South Africa and Zambia while sourcing from out growers. The OZblu brand has garnered strong attention from its customers in Europe with their new varieties of blueberries. These varieties, driven by its fine combination of firmness or crunch (measured technically by way of Durofel) which provides better shelf life, and sweeter blueberries (measured technically by way Brix (symbol °Bx), i.e. fruit sugars) means a superior eating experience for the end consumer. The OZblu varieties are also more flavourful, have very good bloom and larger in size.
sponsor_shareholders: Mbiza is a wholly-owned subsidiary of United Exports (“UE” or the “Sponsor”), an Australian horticulture trading company founded in 2002 by Mr. Roger Horak.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, together with its syndication banks will provide a €30 million long-term financing package to support the Company’s expansion plan in South Africa.
location_description: The Company manages its farms that are located in the Western Cape, Gauteng and Limpopo provinces in South Africa as well as in Zambia.
development_impact: At the project level, the IFC investment will create new jobs, train potential future employees and out growers, and ensure land is managed sustainability as blueberry production expands. IFC expects the proposed transaction will create more than 200 new permanent jobs and 2,000 new seasonal jobs in South Africa. The farmland expansion will include drip-irrigation to ensure water efficiency, fertigation, soil analysis and variable speed pumps to ensure efficiency of energy demand. The Government will benefit from this project through an increase in taxes, foreign exchange revenues and job creation. On a more broader market level, Mbiza's successful penetration in the global blueberry market will showcase South Africa's emergence as a new production center of blueberries in the Southern Hemisphere and create a new export industry for the country. The development of this new industry will not only create large-scale employment in the rural areas of South Africa but also contribute to the diversification of exportable fruit agri-production sites in the country (away from the Cape area where agriculture production sites are concentrated).
additionality: (a) Financing: long-term quasi equity for agribusiness which is not available at the same terms in the local market; (b) Mobilization and structuring: IFC will mobilize up to 20 million euros to complete the financing package and lead structuring negotiations; and (c) Advisory Services: the Company is currently a family-owned business and IFC corporate governance advisory team will provide necessary advise for a path towards formalizing the governance framework of the Company.

project_description: Engro Polymer & Chemicals Limited (“EPCL” or the “Company”) is the only fully integrated chlor-vinyl chemical complex in Pakistan. It is involved in manufacturing, marketing and distribution of poly-vinyl chloride (PVC) and chlor-vinyl allied products, including vinyl chloride monomer, caustic coda, hydrochloric acid and sodium hypochlorite. The Company is undertaking capacity and productivity enhancement plan and has invited IFC to consider supporting its investment program.
sponsor_shareholders: Largest shareholders of EPCL are Engro Corporation (56.19%) and Mitsubishi Corporation (10.24%). Engro Corporation (“ECorp” or the “Sponsor”) is one of Pakistan’s largest and professionally managed conglomerates with business interests in fertilizers, foods, chemical storage & handling, trading, energy and petrochemicals. ECorp’s main shareholder is Dawood Hercules Corporation. ECorp is listed on Pakistan Stock Exchange. The remaining shareholding is distributed among various institutions and general public.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at around US$92.3 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan for IFC’s own account for up to US$35 million.
location_description: Project will be located near Port Qasim in Karachi, Pakistan, within the current EPCL facility.
development_impact: Implementation of the Project is expected to improve availability and affordability of high quality PVC resin and caustic flakes, strengthen competitiveness of local industries that consume these products, such as construction, housing, agriculture, and others, create jobs and enable transfer of technical and managerial know-how.
additionality: The financing will provide the Company with access to critical foreign currency funding in an environment where such funding is scarce. IFC will also assist the Company in establishing adequate E&S policies and ensure full compliance of the Project with IFC performance standards.

project_description: The proposed investment is up to US$8 million senior secured loan, comprised of up to US$4 million each from IFC and the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (“GAFSP”), to Global Tea & Commodities Ltd. and five of its subsidiaries: namely, Global Tea & Commodities (Kenya) Ltd., Gold Crown Foods (EPZ) Limited, Gold Crown Beverages (Kenya) Ltd., Global Tea & Commodities (Malawi) Ltd., and Sable Farming Company Ltd. (together “Global Tea” or the “Group”). Global Tea is an agribusiness group with macadamia and coffee plantations in Malawi, as well as tea sourcing business and tea packing facilities in Kenya. The proposed IFC/GAFSP investment will support the Group’s capacity expansion in Malawi and Kenya.
sponsor_shareholders: Global Tea is majority (86%) owned by the founder Mr. Nadeem Ahmed and his family who started the Group in the United Kingdom in 1992.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project involves up to US$8 million senior secured loan, consisting of up to US$4 million from IFC’s own account and up to US$4 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for GAFSP.
location_description: Global Tea’s macadamia and coffee plantations are located in Ngapani, Chilape, and Mapanga in Malawi, and tea packing facilities are in Mombasa, Kenya. The Group plans to plant additional 600 hectares of macadamia across Ngapani and Mapanga plantations, and replant 300 hectares of the existing 600 hectares coffee across Ngapani, Chipale and Mapanga plantations in Malawi. Global Tea’s existing tea packing facilities in Kenya are near Port of Mombasa. The Project involves the relocation and expansion of the factories within Mombasa, Kenya.
development_impact: (i) Contribution to the development of Kenyan and Malawi agri-business industry by supporting a leading agribusiness player that conducts processing and value addition in local Kenya and Malawi markets for export to international markets, (ii) Employment generation and smallholder development in Kenya/Malawi. In addition, the sourcing arrangements with smallholder farmers are likely to improve access to inputs, training and markets for these producers, including through potential support from IFC advisory; (iii) Export earnings for Malawi and Kenya (tea, coffee and macadamia) will provide value sources of foreign exchange for both countries, (iv) Support climate smart agricultural practices - the project will assist the company to switch to renewable power for its Ngapani plantation in Malawi that is expected to reduce costs and carbon footprint.
additionality: (i) Financial structuring: The proposed blended finance package would help the Group align the maturity of its assets and liabilities and manage cash flow constraints during the long gestation period of the plantations. (ii) Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: renewable energy solutions: IFC Advisory Services will support the Group in assessing and implementing renewable energy solutions, with a focus on the solar PV facilities at the Group's plantations and processing facilities in Malawi. (iii) Knowledge, innovation and capacity building: farmer linkages: IFC Advisory Service will work with the Group on traceability and good agricultural practices (GAPs) to support the Group's smallholder coffee project in Malawi with GAFSP's funding support.

project_description: PT. Surya Semesta Internusa (SSIA) is an Indonesian conglomerate with core businesses interests in real estate, construction services and hotels. SSIA is looking to expand through the development of a new 2,000 ha industrial estate in Subang in several phases .
sponsor_shareholders: SSIA has been l isted on the Indonesia Stock Exchange since 1997. Approximately 69% of the shares of SSIA are held by public . T he control of SSIA is under PT. Arman Investment Utama , which hold s around 8 % of the shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost to develop Phase 1 of the Subang estate is estimated at US$262 million. IFC has been invited to provide a USD-denominated debt financing package of up to US$100 million comprising an A Loan and mobilization through the Managed Co- Lending Portfolio Program (“MCPP”).
location_description: The Subang site is located 100km east of Jakarta.
development_impact: 1. Business efficiencies and linkages: The modern, high-quality infrastructure that SSIA will develop will result in improved efficiencies and reduced operational costs for occupants and their supply chain partners. 2. Elevating standards: SSIA will demonstrate that industrial estates can be developed on both a sustainable and commercially viable basis. The Project is expected to servce as a catalyst for other firms to make improvements in areas such as labor conditions, safety, efficient use of resources and environmental sustainability. 3. Job creation: The Project will create direct and indicrect jobs and the development of new factories and facilities of associated occupants.
additionality: 1. Long-term financing and mobilization: IFC will provide a loan with long tenor and grace period that can match the cash generation profile of the Company. IFC will also utilize its mobilization platform (MCPP) to close the financing gap for this Project. 2. Environmental and social standard setting: SSIA intends the new development to be a green industrial estate. With IFC's support, the Company will seek to implement IFC's EDGE standards in the Project. There is also an opportunity for SSIA to use EDGE for its hotels and other property operations. 3. Industry knowledge: The Company will benefit from IFC's sectoral expertise and global client network. As a major conglomerate involved in hotels, commercial property and other sectors strategically in-line with IFC's industry groups, there are opportunities for IFC to provide knowledge, network and potential financing beyond the Project in future.

project_description: Olam International is a leading agri-business operating across the value chain in 66 countries, supplying various products across 18 platforms to more than 22,000 customers worldwide. From a direct sourcing and processing presence in most major producing countries encompassing Asia-Pacific, SSA, North, Central & South America, Olam has built a global leadership position in many of its businesses. Headquartered in Singapore and listed on the SGX-ST on February 11, 2005, Olam currently ranks among the top 30 largest primary listed companies in Singapore in terms of market capitalization . It differentiates itself by focusing on niche commodities and businesses, buying from growers and village-level agents at the farm gate, and providing value-added solutions and services to customers (e.g., traceability guarantees). The proposed transaction is an agricultural supply chain financing to Olam to promote inclusive and sustainable agricultural value chains in SSA, East Asia, and the Pacific. With the proposed financing IFC will support Olam’s efforts to create markets for smallholder farmers in IDA countries, most of whom are unbanked or disconnected from financial systems.
sponsor_shareholders: Olam is listed on Singapore Stock Exchange, and Temasek Holdings, the Singapore sovereign wealth fund (53.6 %) and Mitsubishi Corporation (Japan) (17. 4 %) are the main shareholders. Olam’s management team has a 6.5% ownership in the company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Proposed IFC A loan of up to $120M is an unsecured, corporate loan to Olam to finance Olam’s increasing procurement activities on farmer financing/market access in certain FCS/IDA countries in Africa, Southeast Asia and the Pacific.
location_description: The proposed loan will support Olam’s supply chain financing for sourcing of crops primarily grown by smallholder farmers in several countries, including FCS/IDA Timor Leste, PNG, and Uganda, which represents a shared strategic priority for both IFC and Olam, as well as Vietnam and Indonesia.
development_impact: The key project impacts will be centered around the nearly 40,000 smallholder farmers supplying Olam who will benefit from reliable access to market, as well as finance and extension services, with positive implications on yield enhancement, optimal inputs usage and increased income. The farmers may also participate in the Olam Livelihood Charter, the relevant certifications, and Olam's digital farmer platform, to obtain better prices for products meeting certification requirements and also to ensure the sustainability of the supply chains. Olam's work with farmers also has the potential to generate more extensive market impacts by influencing the way other traders and integrators manage similar issues of competitiveness and sustainability.
additionality: (i) Continuation of strategic partnership with Olam to support its investments in the supply chains; (ii) Advisory services to improve the quality, sustainability and/or productivity of smallholder farmers; (iii) Supporting the Company to remain best-in-class in terms of its E&S standards in sustainable sourcing practices and transparency in supply chain management.

project_description: The proposed investment is to support Agrofusion Group (the “Company”), the largest tomato paste and industrial tomato producer in Ukraine, by providing a long-term corporate loan to finance the Company’s 2018-2019 expansion and debt refinancing program (the “Project”) . Established in 2007, Agrofusion is the largest vertically integrated tomato paste producer in Ukraine . The Company works with the global FMCG companies, export s 70% of its production to 35 countries. The Company’s operational assets include: (i) three tomato paste plants with total processing capacity of approximately 75 0,000 metric tons of tomatoes per season; (ii) two seedling green-houses; and (iii) approximately 2 5 , 000 hectares of irrigated leased land in Mykolayiv and Kherson regions of Ukraine . The implementation of the Project will allow the Company to expand its product portfolio and increase export volumes .
sponsor_shareholders: Agrofusion Group is wholly-owned by the Sypko family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$30 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$17 million equivalent A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Company conducts its operations in Mykolayiv and Kherson regions of Ukraine.
development_impact: The Company is an important provider of jobs in the rural area of Mykolayiv, where it has also supported a broader hub of economic activity. The project-level impact of the new investment is fairly modest as it focuses on incremental value addition rather than production base expansion. At the market level, the project has the potential to promote market competitiveness and integration. The innovative investment may attract replication from other market players, improving sector competitiveness as it diversifies its product offering and focuses on value addition.
additionality: (i) Financial additionality: IFC is providing significant long-term financing which is scarcely available to Ukrainian corporates. IFC support in implementing a long-term expansion program is essential for the Company's strategy. (ii) Non-financial additionality: In the past projects, IFC has helped the Company with the improvement of its corporate governance practices. With the support of IFC in the proposed investment, the Company will finalize ownership succession plan.

project_description: Malia Invest S.A.L . (‘Malia Invest’ or ‘Company’), a company incorporated in Beirut, Lebanon, is planning to develop a greenfield, multi-functional entertainment center of 16,685 sqm being constructed in Sulaymaniyah, Iraq (‘Project’).
sponsor_shareholders: Malia Invest is a wholly owned company of Malia Holding (‘ Sponsor’ or ‘Malia’ or ‘Group’) . A repeat client of IFC, Malia Invest is active in the hospitality sector in Iraq, owning two hotels in Erbil, Iraq and the proposed Project in Sulaymaniyah, Iraq. Malia Holding , established in 1986 in Beirut, Lebanon, is a diversified conglomerate in Lebanon covering 8 business streams including Industries, FMCG Manufacturing and Distribution, Pharmaceuticals, Technology & Management Solutions, Fashion, Engineering & Contracting, and Hospitality and Real Estate encompassing 27 companies.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is US$26.5 mn, where US$17.5 mn (66% of total Project cost) will be equity contribution by the Group . IFC is proposed to extend an A loan of up to US$9 mn to the Company to support the Project.
location_description: Sulaymaniyah, Iraq
development_impact: The proposed IFC investment in Magma Square is expected to result in the following benefits: (i) improvements in the urban infrastructure surrounding the commercial center; (ii) better consumer choices in view that the clustering of competitors facilitates price/offer comparisons and improves consumers' knowledge, resulting in higher quality goods available at lower prices for the customer; (iii) improvements in the quality of goods sold, especially food and fresh produce; (iv) increase in standards for hygiene and safety in product handling and storage; (v) increase in business for and improvements in practices and standards of local product suppliers, especially food and fresh products that filter through to other retail formats; and (vi) creation of more than 1,000 direct and indirect jobs during the construction and operational stage. In addition, as in many other malls, the proposed Project is expected to attract other developments to the area, creating a demonstration effect and contributing to the overall community development.
additionality: (i) Supporting the development of a one of the first multi-functional shopping malls in Sulaymaniyah which introduces modern shopping experience; (ii) Providing long-term financing to the Company that would otherwise be difficult to mobilize from local banks and, by doing so, help Magma Square mobilize additional capital. IFC's expertise will be used to help structure the investment and its presence will provide comfort to the other investors; (iii) Supporting a strong Sponsor in its first investment in the retail sector in Iraq, which could be mutually beneficial in kick-starting future beneficial projects for the country. This Project is also in keeping with IFC's role of being a pioneer, proactively engaging in FCS markets.

project_description: Agrotec S.A. (“Agrotec” or “the Company”) is one of Paraguay’s leading crop input distributor and agronomy services company operating since 1990. Agrotec offers a “one-stop shop” to more than 800 client farmers, providing seeds, fertilizers, agrochemicals, technical support, storage and logistic services, pre-harvest financing, as well as commercialization of the grains of its farmer client base. The Company’s strategy is to develop strong relationships with farmers providing integral agronomic services from sowing planning and advice, through the provision of seeds, nutrition integration and crop protection. Agrotec operates 13 Regional Distribution Centers (“RDCs”) , including its headquarters in Ciudad del Este . They are located near the major crop regions of Paraguay to guarantee a rapid delivery of inputs and efficient customer service to its clients. The Project consists of providing Agrotec an up to $ 20 million one year loan facility (the “Facility”) with up to four renewable tranches, and a long term facility of up to US$ 5 million to support the working capital needs of the Company.
sponsor_shareholders: Agrotec is owned by the Z anchet family through two holding companies: Agrihold Investment Ltd. and Agrihold Management Corp (“Agrihold” or the “Group”), which centralizes the Group’s business and operations in Paraguay, Uruguay, and Brazil.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at $25 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an up to $ 20 million A Loan renewable for up to 4 years, and a 5-year A Loan of up to US$ 5 million, both for IFC’s own account , to finance working capital needs of the Company.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Ciudad Del Este, Paraguay. The Company has 13 Regional Distribution Centers located near the major crop regions of Paraguay
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is improved access to key inputs for farmers leading to better yields and incomes. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that the project has the potential to promote greater market competitiveness and sustainability via demonstration and replication channels
additionality: (i) Long-term financing: This is the first time IFC will provide a 5-year long-term loan to Agrotec. (ii) Conservation of Biodiversity: Agrotec will develop an internal procedure to verify that new clients and existing clients' expansions would not provide repayment with crops sourced in areas where has been recent conversion of natural habitats

company_name: LATAM LOGISTIC COL PROPCO COTA 1 S A S
project_description: The proposed project entails a n approximately US$ 30 m illion COP equivalent (COP 77.5 b illio n ) A-Loan and a Parallel Loan of an equivalent amount coordinated by IFC to support LatAm Logistics Pro perties (LLP or the Sponsor) in the development of Phase I and II of its first class-A logistic warehousing park in Bogota (the Project). The warehousing park has a total potential of 252,000 sq uare meters (sq m ) (240,000 sqm of warehousing space and 12,000 sqm of office area mezzanine level), on a plot of 567,300 sqm, and will be developed in 3 phases. The Project entails the construction of approximately 160,000 sqm (including office space and restrooms for employees). The plot is located on the Calle 80 ( Tenjo Municipality), which is one of the most important new logistics clusters in Bogota. The p roject will expand the supply of scarce efficient class-A wareho using space to support the growth of retailers, e- tailers , consumer goods companies , third-party logistic op erators and manufacturing companies. This new class-A warehousing space will result in increased efficiency for tenants’ supply chains and introducing international green build ing practices through obtaining IFC’s EDGE certification.
sponsor_shareholders: LLP is dedicated to developing and operating logistic warehouse facilities for rent in the underserved markets of Costa Rica, Peru, Colombia and Panama. LLP aims at developing approximately 700,000 sqm of logistics Class A warehouses with modern specifications, providing significant efficiency improvements to multinational, regional and local retailers and logistic operators in the region . It has developments underway in Costa Rica and Peru, where it has already built 99 ,000 sqm and let 84 ,000 sqm to multinational, regional and local companies. LLP was founded in 2013 by Mike Fangman, CEO and shareholder, who has 1 5 years of institutional logistics property experience in Latin America. In June 2015, Jaguar Real Estate Partne rs LP (the “Fund” or “JREP1”), a New York based RE private equity fund managed by Jaguar Growth Asset Management LLC (“Jaguar”), became the majority shareholder of LLP . Jaguar executives have deep experience in RE in emerging markets, especially in Latin America. Through the Fund, Jaguar provides capital as well as global RE experience adding value throughout various life stages of projects.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project has a total cost of approximately US$ 123 million COP equivalent (COP 317 billion) , out of which approximately US$30 million COP equivalent (COP 77.5 billion) will be financed with an A Loan, and a Parallel Loan of an equivalent amount coordinated by IFC and the remaining with equity from the Sponsor.
location_description: The site is located approximately 20 kilometres away from downtown Bogota, with 800 meters frontage and direct access to Calle 80 (the Bogota-Medellin highway), one of the most strategic locations for logistic operations in Bogota.
development_impact: Project-level Impacts (i) Increased Availability of logistics infrastructure and reduced supply chain costs for businesses - The Project will add ~160,000 sqms of Class A+ storage and distribution capacity (252,000 if total park is considered) to support the efficient development of the supply chains of manufacturers, retailers/e-tailers and associated third-party logistics providers. Class A+ warehousing parks involve large, modern, flexible and well-located buildings and service infrastructure, conceived to optimize distribution configurations and facilitate scale, throughput and consolidation of inventories and transportation. They offer increased availability of docking ports with levelers for all types of trucks, matched with ample maneuvering yards for large vehicles; the buildings have 12 meters of higher ceilings, increased floor load capacity, long and column free span areas, which together significantly increase the number of pallet positions per unit of GLA when compared to existing Class A, B and C. Common services such as security, maintenance, shared cafeterias and training centers, result in further benefits for tenants. Such advantages of Class A+ structures provide tangible benefits to the typical LLP tenants, retailers/e-tailers, manufacturers and 3PLs. Some examples are:- Scalable Class A+ warehouses allow retailers to consolidate all stocks (which typically have been in multiple sites) into a single larger and more efficient warehouse, reducing total warehousing stocks.- Similarly, the retailers' suppliers (generally manufacturers) can simplify their distributions into larger and more frequent deliveries to one central location, instead of small and numerous deliveries to multiple locations (stores and multiple distribution centers), reducing their stocks and better optimizing manufacturing set-ups.- Such broad retail-manufacturing supply-chain reconfigurations, are estimated to result in material savings equivalent to up to 1.0-2.0% of retailers' revenues. (ii) Economy-wide effects - The Project will foster the creation of direct jobs during both the construction and operation of properties. During construction, the Project will support approximately 600 direct jobs. Further, approximately 1,200 direct and indirect jobs will be created during the operational phase. The Project will support a significant number of indirect jobs through the supply chains, including the sourcing construction inputs and related services during the development phase and the sourcing of products and services to be sold within completed properties. (iii) Positive Environmental Impact: LLP has committed to achieve EDGE certification, which results in at least 20% savings in energy, water and in materials consumption compared with benchmarks for equivalent buildings. Market-level Impacts (i) Competitiveness: The Project will provide a positive impact in the local warehousing and industrial property market. As of today, Class A warehousing parks in Colombia stand at 450,000 sqm -or 4% of total existing supply. In addition, the Project will be the first of Class A+ quality. Given its modern, efficient, and lower cost characteristics, it is expected that LLP will set high industry standards and demonstrate the economic viability of a further refined business model. (ii) Sustainability: Currently, the penetration of modern and energy-efficient industrial warehouses in Colombia is negligible. The buildings built under the Project will achieve global best practice in energy efficiency standards and, will be the first Green Building certified warehousing properties in the country.
additionality: (i) Financial Additionality (Financing Structure and Resource Mobilization): IFC's role as a lender is to provide direct financing in local currency matching the Project's cashflows and help structure parallel funding for the Project. (ii) Non-Financial Additionality (Standard Setting): IFC will continue to provide technical knowledge and advice to support LLP in enhancing its E&S practice and ensuring that the Project meets IFC's E&S standards. In particular, IFC will assist LLP to obtain the EDGE green building certification. LLP has committed to obtain EDGE certification on all of its existing and new developments, including the Project. The Company has been using EDGE certification as differentiating factor to attract companies both from a carbon footprint and lower operation costs perspectives.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A / B/ Trust loan financing package to Pandurata Alimentos Ltda ("Bauducco" or "the Company"). Bauducco , founded in 1952 , is one of the leading baked products companies in Brazil , producing panettones , toasts, cookies , wafer biscuits and other baked products . The Company produces baked products under 3 complementary brands (Bauducco, Visconti and Tommy) to target the entire spectrum of Brazilian consumers. Bauducco is currently carrying out an investment program of about US$ 70 million over the next 2 years consisting of (i) expansion of its plant in Extrema , (ii) civil construction to expand its Guarulhos plant; and (iii ) associated working capital needs .
sponsor_shareholders: Bauducco is a private family-owned company and was founded in 1952 by the Bauducco family. The shareholders of the Company are Pandurata Participações Ltda. and Bedece Comércio e Participações Ltda. Pandurata Participações Ltda. shareholders are Mr. Massimo Bauducco, Mr. Carlo Andrea Bauducco and Silvana Bauducco. Bedece Comércio e Participações Ltda. shareholders are Mr. Luigi Bauducco, Mrs. Carla Bauducco, Mr. Massimo Bauducco, Mr. Carlo Andrea Bauducco and Silvana Bauducco.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at about US$70 million, and IFC investment consists of an A Loan, a B Loan and a Trust Loan.
location_description: Bauducco headquarters are located in Guarulhos, state of Sao Paulo. development_impact: The Project is expected to have a positive development impact by i) supporting a competitive player in the baked products industry and ii) creating new jobs, with a significant portion of these for women. project_description: The proposed investment consists of: (i) a €13 m illion senior A loan; and (ii) an €11 m illion parallel loan mobilized by IFC. The loans will be made to Gaselia Industries Group, a n existing IFC client and one of the largest beverage and packaging groups in West Africa . The funds will be mainly used to finance (i) the expansion of the Group’s producti on capacities in Côte d’Ivoire and Mali, and (ii) its greenfield soft drink project in Guinea .
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor and majority shareholder of Gase lia is Mr. Madiou Simpara, a 58-year old Malian businessperson with a diversified portfolio of activities. Mr. Simpara started out in the 1980s as a trader of automobile spare parts before expanding into importation and distribution of other products (textiles, hydrocarbons and home appliances), commercial real estate and into the b everage sector in 2002 with Gase lia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide up to €13 million in the form of a senior A loan and mobilize an additional €11 million to partially finance the approximately €3 5 mi llion investment program of Gase lia .
location_description: Gaselia’s investment plan will cover three countries: Côte d’Ivoire (in Abidjan and in Bonoua), Mali (in the Bamako area) and Guinea (in the Conakry area).
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is the downstream linkages with base of the pyramid retailers, the employment created, and the environmental impact in Mali and Cote d'Ivoire. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that this investment has the potential to promote greater sustainability and inclusiveness via demonstration and replication channels.

project_description: The proposed loan of up to EUR 10 million, to Société Sénégalaise Agro-Industrielle (“Sosagrin”) and Industrie des Boissons du Sénégal (“IBS”) (together with Sosagrin the “Borrowers”), is to support the Borrowers’ investment program, and includes: (i) acquiring a new greenfield site and building new production and warehouse facilities; (ii) expanding production capacity; (iii) implementing a packaging recycling program; and (iv) working capital requirements.
sponsor_shareholders: Sosagrin and IBS are primarily owned and managed by the El Sahili family (the “Sponsors”). The founder, Mr. Kassim El Sahili, is joined by his two sons, Mr. Rouda El Sahili and Mr. Mohamed El Sahili in managing the businesses.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at EUR12.7 million. IFC’s proposed financing is an A loan of up to EUR6.0 million for IFC’s own account and a syndicated loan of up to EUR4 million.
location_description: The 27,000-sq. meter new project site is in Diamniadio, Senegal.
development_impact: The project impacts are centered around: - Sustainability, especially through Sosagrin's envisioned glass recycling program. - Employment, whereby the Project is expected to create 100-200 new direct jobs. - The Companies stakeholders, namely their (i) distributors/buyers through increased sales volumes, and (ii) local suppliers through increased purchases. Moreover, the proposed investment has the potential to generate market impacts by encouraging systemic changes to existing markets that deliver development impact by increasing sustainability in Senegal, through demonstration and replication channels.
additionality: - Provide long-term funding including through syndication. - Provide IFC global industry knowledge. - Advisory Services to improve the Borrowers' waste and water management, health & safety procedures and food traceability systems.

project_description: Omera Petroleum Ltd. (“Omera” or “the company”) is the second largest liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) player in Bangladesh, with a throughput capacity of 12 0,000 metric ton per annum (MTPA). The company has its main import storage terminal in Mongla, and three satellite storage / bottling stations in Ghorashal (Central region), Bogra (Northern region) and Chittagong (Southern region), respectively. Omera has a fleet of one river barge, road tankers, and contract distributors’ cylinder trucks to transport LPG from central terminal to satellite stations, and to customers. All storage terminals and filling stations are located along the rivers / main roads and inside industrial areas.
sponsor_shareholders: MJL Bangladesh Limited ("MJL") holds 62.5% stake in the company, followed by BB Energy with 25% and FMO with 12.5%. MJL, a joint venture company between state owned Jamuna Oil Company and EC Securities Limited (a subsidiary of the East Coast Group), is the leading lubricant manufacturing company in Bangladesh with about 31% market share.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost over the next 2 years is estimated to be around US$60 million including capital expenditures for cylinders, barges, storage tanks, trucks and filling machinery. IFC proposes an investment of up to US$20 million to partially finance this capital expenditure.
location_description: Omera has its main import terminal in Mongla. OPL has established three other satellite filling and bottling stations at Ghorashal (Central region), Bogra (Northern region) and Chittagong (Southern region). The proposed IFC financing will support Omera's operations through these regions.
development_impact: 1. Stakeholders Effects: a) Customers effects: Currently, about 90% of natural gas in Bangladesh is used to generate electricity, with demand from both domestic household and industrial segments expected to grow substantially. However, there is a daily shortage of natural gas of approximately 1,000 million cubic feet (mmcft/day) which might cause major disruptions to the economic activities if remain unaddressed. Due to the shortage of natural gas, LPG is even more needed now especially by the domestic households as natural gas is increasingly diverted for industrial and power sector use. The Project will help minimize the shortage gap and address the lack of storage facilities that have become the bottleneck in the distribution chain by increasing the storage capacity at various stages in the value chain. The other bottleneck is in the downstream logistic services, where certain locations are hard to reach or that the transport lead time is long, both due to the constraints in the transportation infrastructure. The Project will help smoothen the distribution of LPG to the end users by constructing capacity barges, cylinder carrying barges, and upgrading the LPG road tankers fleet. This will direct and indirectly increase the reliability of supply by shortening the delivery time and lowering the transportation costs, and to ensure end customers will have access to LPG when they need them. b) Distributors effects: OPL has established a strong distribution channel with more than 200 distributors across the country. OPL is now present in more than 22,000 retail points in the country, and has presence in all the administrative sub-districts of Bangladesh. The project will increase economic activity of these distributors and retailers, most of them MSMEs, due to the higher volume of LPGs and number of cylinders being distributed to the end users. By 2020, additional 2.1 million cylinders will have been distributed to the market and by 2018, additional 3,000 retailers will have been added to the distribution network. 2. Contribution to Market Creation: a) Resilience: The project will help create a more resilient energy system through promotion of supply diversification, by helping a private sector player such as OPL deliver LPG to the market. The Project also supports the Government of Bangladesh's policy to dedicate the natural gas production to power generation and industrial consumption, which are currently facing erratic and short supplies. Allocating more natural gas to power generation and fulfil the demand of the household segment with LPG will not only create a more resilient energy system but also lead to better manufacturing productivity and thus generate greater economic value from scarce natural gas resources. b) Sustainability: This project will support the promotion of LPG which has low greenhouse gas emission characteristics when compared to for example, conventional cooking fuels such as firewood, kerosene and charcoal. Usage of these conventional cooking fuels have reduced drastically in rural Bangladesh, but represent still around 75% of the consumption of cooking fuels, so there is a big potential for LPG to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Inefficient cooking emits greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane, and aerosols such as black carbon. Better access to LPG in rural areas of Bangladesh through new distribution networks will provide a cleaner and efficient fuel than biomass, reducing overall emissions and thereby improving overall health of the local population. Unlike firewood and charcoal, LPG is easy and instantaneous to light, easy to control so that the required rate of heating can be obtained. LPG does not produce any smoke or soot therefore in overall is more environmentally friendly and sustainable compared to conventional cooking fuels.
additionality: 1) Global knowledge and international best practices: IFC will share its global knowledge in the fuels and fuel distribution (including LPG) industry, and advise the company to help strengthen the Company's business strategy and practices. 2) E&S improvement: IFC's E&S team shall work with the Company to identify the opportunities to reduce the environmental impact and ensure that the best safety and social practices are followed.

sector: Fruit and Vegetable Preservation or Processing (Canning, Freezing, Drying, Jams, etc.)
project_description: The group of companies known as PRAN Group (“PRAN” or the “Group”) was established in 1981 and is the leading branded food and beverage group and the largest agro-processor in Bangladesh. The Group is a well-known household brand in Bangladesh, and produces more than 400 food products in at least 10 major categories including juices and drinks, snacks, dairy, spices, confectionary and frozen foods. PRAN exports to 134 countries around the world. PRAN is planning (i) a capacity expansion of several of its existing food products (fruit juices, biscuits, noodles, and spices) through a US$65 million capital expenditure investment at P RAN A gro B usiness L imited (PABL) as well as (ii) a refinancing of short term working capital facilities at PRAN Agro Limited (PAL) and Natore Agro Limited (N AL ) of BDT1,600 million (up to US$20 million) for a total project cost of approximately US$85 million (the “Project”). The capacity expansion will be undertaken at PABL, an entity of the PRAN Group , at two sites in Natore and Rajshahi. The expansion will include the following components: (i) setting up an aseptic pulping facility in Rajshahi for increasing fruit-based beverage capacity; (ii) increasing production capacity of spice products; (iii) expansion of noodle-making capacity and backward integration into flour milling; (iv) developing a distribution channel of 1,500 distributors; (v) modernizing existing operations.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsors and shareholders of the Project companies consist of the family members of the late PRAN Group founder Major General Amjad Khan Chowdhury, including his wife Ms. Sabiha Amjad, his son Mr. Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, and his daughter Ms. Uzma Chowdhury (collectively, the Sponsors).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is expected to be approximately US$85 million. IFC proposes to provide debt financing comprising of an A Loan of US$30 million to PABL , as well as local currency working capital facilities tota ling BDT1,600 mm (up to US$20 million ) to PAL and NAL .
location_description: PABL site in Natore: Chandpur, Pirgonj, Natore Sadar, Natore, Bangladesh. PABL site in Rajshahi: Vill: Amanotpur, P/O: Pirijpur (6290), 6 Matikata Union Porishad, (Ward No. 3), P/S: Godagari, Dist: Rajshahi, Bangladesh. PAL: Tabaria Union, Hat Singradaha, Ekdala, Natore, Bangladesh. NAL: Tabaria Union, Hat Singradaha, Ekdala, Natore, Bangladesh.
development_impact: (1) Greater farmer reach: The project is expected to help PRAN increase its farmer network by procuring raw materials from an incremental 10,000 farmers, thus contributing to market creation for these farmers. (2) Increased job creation and MSME improvement: The project is expected to create approximately 650 incremental direct jobs and 4,000 indirect jobs, including sizeable female employment (around 60% of PRAN's workforce is female). In addition, the project is expected to create additional indirect employment in micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) along the value chain. (3) Setting food safety standards and local demonstration effect: By increasing the availability of hygienically-packaged food, the project would help to set higher standards on food safety in the country for other players, including a large base of farmers. (4) Extension services: The project is expected to support climate smart agriculture through implementation of good agricultural practices (GAP) for incremental farmers in its supply chain for key crops such as mango, tomatoes, turmeric and cassava.
additionality: (1) Access to long term finance: With IFC's long term, appropriately structured capital and local currency funding, PRAN Group would be able to further expand without incurring excessive liquidity risks, better match its investment payback period, and create more stability in its financing. (2) Continued Advisory support on food safety: This project and investment will benefit from continued IFC Advisory work in the form of Stage 2 of the IFC Food Safety Advisory Support which would entail farm level advisory targeting 12,000 farmers who supply to PRAN Group. (3) Environmental and social (E&S) standards setting: Through this Project, the Company is expected to continue to adopt and implement appropriate standards in labor management, production, as well as supply chains and raw material procurement, particularly on food safety standards. (4) Industry knowledge and support: IFC is able to provide PRAN with global industry knowledge in food processing and agribusiness and help to facilitate the exchange of ideas with other IFC clients, thus enhancing the PRAN Group's overall operational know-how and knowledge of the latest technological advances.

project_description: Craftsman Automation Private Limited (“Craftsman” or “the Company”) is a diversified engineering company, with vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities, primarily catering to the (i) automotive and (ii) industrial and engineering segments . Craftsman offer s comprehensive end to end solutions including design and process and design engineering services and manufacturing services including non-ferrous, foundry, heat treatment, fabrication, machining and assembly . The proposed Project is for capacity augmentation and modernization of the existing facilities through purchase of new machinery and for the expansion of the C ompany’s facilities.
sponsor_shareholders: S. Ravi is the Project Sponsor and majority shareholder of Craftsman with 52.83% shareholding. The other major shareholders are the private equity investors IFC and Standard Chartered Private Equity through its investment arm Marina III Singapore Pte Ltd. who in aggregate hold 29.56% .
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: I FC will invest up to US$30 .7 million as a loan to part finance the Project.
location_description: Craftsman is headquartered in Coimbatore, India and has manufacturing facilities in Coimbatore, Pune, Sriperumbudur (near Chennai), Bangalore, Faridabad, Jamshedpur and Pithampur. The Project expenditure will be incurred across all the manufacturing facilities of the Company.
development_impact: (i) Employment creation and knowledge transfer: The Project will create additional high skill jobs as it expands its operations. The Project will also create additional employment along the supply chain as it increases purchases and variety of its raw materials. (ii) Impact on customers: Customers will benefit from the increase in capacity which will provide a consistent and reliable supply of quality auto component parts, meet the increasing requirements of components as they expand their volumes. (iii) Impact on suppliers: Craftsman will impact the suppliers through the increase in its business with the existing local suppliers through additional purchases and a broader range of purchases of components. (iv) Increase in taxes: The Project is expected to contribute to the domestic economy through increased tax revenues
additionality: (i) Long Term Debt Funding: IFC will provide long term debt funding with sufficient grace period, to finance the Company's expansion. (ii) Long term partnership: IFC was the first external equity investor in Craftsman in 2010. IFC has played an important role in making the Company IPO ready and continue to provide industry and technical expertise as it expands. (iii) Environment and Social Standard Setting: IFC will provide continued support to maintain E&S best practices and getting the Company IPO-ready

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A/B loan financing package to Usina Açucareira S. Manoel S.A. ("Sao Ma n o el " or "the Company"). Established in the 19 49 and owned by the Dinucci family, Sao Manoel is one of the most competitive Brazilian sugar and ethanol producers. The Company operates one sugar mill in the state of Sao Paulo with a total capacity to process 4 .3 mill ion tons of sugarcane annually.
sponsor_shareholders: Sao Manoel’s majority shareholders and sponsors are the Dinucci family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an up to US$42 million A/B loan financing package composed of approximately BRL75 million A Loan tranche 1, c. US$2 million A Loan tranche 2, c.US$9 million B Loan and c.US$8 million internal cash generation. The proceeds will be used for the renewal and expansion of sugarcane plantations, investments in machinery and equipment, incorporation of energy-efficient technologies and social programs .
location_description: Sao Manoel is headquartered in the city of Sao Manuel, state of Sao Paulo, where the Company operates one mill, and where the investment will be directed.
development_impact: - Stakeholders: The investment will contribute to creating skilled jobs and increasing female employment. - Private Sector Development: The investment will support the continued expansion of a competitive domestic player in the sugar and ethanol industry, one of the most important sectors in the Brazilian economy. - Payments to Government: The Brazilian agribusiness sector is highly competitive globally and is key to the economy in terms of its capacity to raise Government revenues. This investment will allow the Company to expand its operations and will contribute to the growth of the Brazilian economy. - Climate Change: IFC's investment in Sao Manoel will contribute to climate change mitigation by promoting the use of renewable fuel in a country with expanding demand. - Sustainability: The investment will contribute to disseminating the adoption of solid agricultural practices, as by promoting the use of innovative technologies São Manoel reports high productivity levels compared to the industry average.
additionality: IFC brings both financial and non-financial additionality to the proposed transaction. The financial additionality stems from provision of long-term financing and mobilization. Non-financial additionality is related to the adoption of IFC’s Environmental and Social (E&S) standards, and potential advisory support in case the Company decides to expand its co-generation facility in the future.

project_description: Sanctum Inle Resort (the “Project”) is a 5-star hotel with 97 rooms in Inle Lake, Myanmar, owned and operated by Sanctum Inle Resort Co., Ltd. (the “Company”). The Project started operating in April 2016 and currently needs a long-term funding to optimize its balance sheet.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is privately owned by Ms. Su Su Tin (90%) and her husband, Mr. U Than Too Kyaw (10%). Ms. Su Su Tin is a local entrepreneur in Myanmar who founded and managed a number of successful businesses in Tourism, Hospitality and Retail industries, including Exo Travel Myanmar, Annam Myanmar Group Co., Ltd . She is an active member in various local tourism associations and committees. The Company has a service agreement in place with Apple Tree Group (Singapore) to receive hotel management services.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Th e final Project cost totaled approximately US$20 million and was completed in early 2016. The Project was financed by a mix of bank loans, investor loans and equity. The proposed investment is an A loan of up to US$6.0 million for IFC's own account.
development_impact: i. Job creation: The Project is creating over 130 direct jobs at the Project, majority of which are for the local community. ii. Capacity Building: The Project is being operated at high international standards (currently ranked number 1 on TripAdvisor among hotels in the area) and through training of employees, it is facilitating knowledge transfer and improving services standards. iii. Benefits to the local economy and supply linkages: The Project will help create demand for locally-sourced materials, services, and labor. The Project is expected to support SMEs, including a wide range of goods and service providers, such as produce farmers, food processors, transportation companies, restaurateurs, and arts and crafts manufacturers. iv. Increase in domestic revenues and foreign exchange: The Project is expected to contribute to the domestic economy through increased tax revenues and in particular, foreign exchange inflow as a large majority of the Project's revenues is expected to be in foreign currency.
additionality: i. Long-term Financing: IFC will provide long-term capital for the Project that will replace the short-term loans and will optimize the balance sheet of the Company. ii. Industry Expertise: The Sponsors have been involved in the tourism sector in Mekong for many years and is keen on deepening its industry knowledge and reach, and is hence courting investors that can bring value-add beyond the monetary resources, such as IFC. IFC's industry specialist has previously provided much insight on this and other projects, which the Sponsors have availed of. iii. E&S: IFC will share E&S best practices with the Sponsors and ensure that the Project complies with IFC's Performance Standards and sustainability standards.

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: Esquire Knit Composite Limited (the “Company” or “EKCL”), an existing IFC AS client and one of Bangladesh’s integrated knitted apparels manufacturer and exporter, has approached IFC to finance the expansion of its ready made garments (“RMG”) cutting and sewing operations (the “Project”). The Project involves setting up a new cutting and sewing factory in Bhaluka , Mymensingh, Bangladesh. The new facility, to be housed in a green building, will comprise 102 sewing lines, seamless garment knitting, molded bra cup technology and automatic cutting and sewing for production of active wear and lingerie. The proposed Project will increase EKCL’s cutting and sewing capacity by 31.8 million pieces per year, which will be fully exported to major global retailers.
sponsor_shareholders: Esquire Knit Composite Limited, incorporated in 2000, is directly or indirectly 100% owned by Mr. Mofazzal Hossain and his family members (the “Sponsors”). The shareholding structure of EKCL is: Mr. Md. Mofazzal Hossain (28.8%), Mr. Md Ehsanul Habib (15.03%), Mr. Md. Muddasar Hossain and Mr. Arifur Rahman (each 7.93%) and Mrs. Peara Begum (3.68%). Three other corporate entities (owned by the Sponsors) have shareholding as well – Esquire Dyeing Industries Limited (29.58%), Esquire Accessories Limited (1.21%) and Esquire Electronic Limited (5.85%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost of US$35.2 million. IFC will invest up to US$22.0 million as A loan. Equity of US$13.2 million would be fresh equity injection by the Sponsors.
location_description: Bhaluka , Mymensingh, Bangladesh.
development_impact: Stakeholder's impacts: i. Employment growth: The Project will create 5,500 additional jobs, mostly for women. Additionally, the number of temporary workers required for the construction at its peak is 300. ii. Employee skills/know-how: The Project is going to attract skilled recruits and further develop their skill sets through various training program required by the new technologies and product range, and thus adding to the skilled workers base in Bangladesh. iii. Effect on emissions and waste generation: EKCL's new factory will be a LEED certified green factory. Supported by IFC's Advisory Program Partnership for Cleaner Textile (PaCT), the factory will focus on water, wastewater, and chemicals conservation and energy efficiency. Market impact: i. Contribution to Market Creation: The Project, along with IFC's advisory services engagements in Bangladesh, has the potential to promote greater market sustainability and integration in the RMG sector in Bangladesh. ii. Impact on market emissions and waste generation: The project, along with IFC's advisory services engagements in Bangladesh, will help foster adoption of environmental and social sustainability principles by firms and consumers across the sector through direct capacity building channels and demonstration effects as a result of EKCL's success. iii. Increasing manufacturing complexity: The Project is expected to upgrade the company to a more value adding level, involving advanced products, innovative product development, automated production technology and up-grading of professional skills of the personnel. It could potentially be the model that other factories will follow as Bangladesh is climbing up to higher value garment products.
additionality: i. Provide long-term foreign exchange financing which would otherwise be difficult to secure in the current market scenario to support a local player to expand its core business. ii. Continue to integrate EKCL into various RMG/Textile-focused IFC advisory programs such as the Buyers' Forum and Better Works programs, which are geared towards improving compliance, competitiveness, energy efficiency, and labor welfare at firm and industry levels. iii. Assist EKCL to formulate and implement E&S action plan to expand social/labor management systems for inclusion of environmental, occupational, health and safety (OHS) guidelines and enhance OHS management systems.

project_description: The Project will increase National Cement Company Ltd.’s (NCCL) clinker nominal capacity from 1.1 m illion tons per annum ( mtpa ) to 2. 9 mtpa and cement grinding capacity from 2.1 ( m tpa ) to 3.0 mtpa in Kenya and will introduce 0.8 mtpa new cement capacity through its sister company, National Cement Company Uganda Ltd (NCCL Uganda).
sponsor_shareholders: Project sponsor is Mr. Narendra Raval, founder of NCCL and 85% shareholder together with his family. The balance is owned 7.5% by IFC and 7.5% by IFC African, Latin American and Caribbean Fund LP .
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated cost of the Project is approximately $ 200 million , of which $162 million is for NCCL in Kenya and $38 million is for NCCL Uganda . IFC is considering providing towards the financing plan an A Loan of $25 million and arrange a B Loan and/or parallel loans, including with its Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program ( MCPP), of up to $65 million. NCCL in Kenya and its sister company, NCCL Uganda, are the co-borrowers for the financing. IFC is also considering an equity investment of up to $7 million of which approximately $4 million in NCCL in Kenya and $3 million in NCCL Uganda.
development_impact: The Project (i) reduces cement prices to end-customers; (ii) promotes market competitiveness via the introduction of efficient processes; (iii) benefit those small and medium enterprises engaged in transporting the company's raw materials and products in their own trucks and providing maintenance and general services to the company; (iv) significantly increases the domestic business with local suppliers in both countries; (v) supports the domestic value addition to abundantly available natural resources (i.e. pozzolana, limestone and gypsum) in Kenya and Uganda; (vi) creates 496 new direct jobs (323 in Kenya and 173 Uganda), and support an additional 39,000 indirect and induced jobs in Kenya and 29,700 in Uganda through forward linkages; (vii) generates a positive and strong Life-of-Project Economic Return on Invested Capital; and (viii) achieves a positive environmental effect with CO2 emissions per ton of cement produced expected to be 10% lower thanks to the use of more efficient technology.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality for the project is significant - both in financial and non-financial terms, through the provision of: (i) long-term financing in a region where it is not readily available; (ii) mobilization of $65 million from other financial institutions for the development of the project; (iii) corporate governance advisory service program; (iv) environmental and social expertise for cumulative impact analysis, land acquisition, energy efficiency, health and safety, mitigation plans, public disclosure, and community development; and (v) strategic partnership for south-south investments along with technical expertise and global industry knowledge.

project_description: Lagos State is one of the 36 States of the Federal State of Nigeria, and is divided into 20 Local Government Areas. Among the latter, 16 of them form Metropolitan Lagos. Metropolitan Lagos is one of the world's largest cities with a population estimated at approximately 17 million. The population is highly mobile and largely reliant upon public transport; however, the lack of an organized public transport network has led to inefficiencies in its provision and a low level of service to those who use it. Existing public transport has been widely described as chaotic, inefficient, expensive, low quality and dangerous both in terms of road traffic accidents and personal safety. The proposed project involves a strategic engagement with Lagos State to support the development of two Quality Bus Corridors (QBC) (the Project). The development of the two QBC's will cost approximately US$50 million. IFC's proposed investment will be an A loan of the Nigerian naira (NGN) equivalent of up to US$50 million.The QBC's are part of the Lagos State Transport Master Plan Project (LSTMPP), an ambitious city-wide reform of the public transportation services in Lagos, which was developed in part with financing from the World Bank,and, some of which is being implemented by the Lagos Metropolitan Transport Authority (LAMATA). LAMATA is the transport planning, implementing, regulating and franchising authority of the Lagos State Government. The two originally identified for IFC financing in 2018 were Command Abule Egba(6 km) and Ile Ile Ile Epo (4.3 km), both along existing road networks. The project activities will include road infrastructure improvement, rehabilitation of pedestrian walkways to improve walking conditions and accessibility to public transport services, rehabilitation of drainage, improvements of road junctions, provision of dedicated lanes for public transportation buses and construction of a new bus terminal for each QBC (a hub passenger pick up and drop off) and installation of a number of additional bus stops (laybys)/ flags at each QBC. Buses will be sheltered, maintained and refueled at a bus depot. The SII for this transaction were updated to reflect that in 2024, the intended use of IFC proceeds changed to financing two different QBC packages (comprising four corridors). The four corridors are Ojuelegba – Idi Araba – Ilasamaja (3.5 km); Anthony – Oshodi (2 km); and Oshodi – Onipanu (4.1 km) (packaged together as QBC package 1); and Iyana Ipaja – Ayobo (9.3 km) (QBC package 2). The project activities remain the same as those of the original QBCs. There is a combined population of around 292,000 persons within a radius of 400 meters around these two corridors and about 10,400 passengers pass through them per hour during peak hours. Considering 75% of this passenger traffic is with public transportation, developing these QBC's will help reduce travel times and improve road safety. The project will support improved access to jobs and services, while achieving environmental objectives of reducing air pollution and carbon emissions. Pre-feasibility studies for both the QBCs were completed in 2021. Detailed project design and relevant environmental and social studies, including a project specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP), have been completed by the end of 2024. The construction works will begin in early 2025 and are expected to be completed by the end of 2026.
sponsor_shareholders: Lagos is the largest city in Sub-Saharan Africa with an estimated population of 22 million. With a total area of 3,577 square kilometre, of which 22% is wetlands, Lagos has a population density of about 6,000 persons per square kilometer. This makes Lagos the most densely populated area per square kilometer in Nigeria. Lagos is the economic and financial center of Nigeria, generating approximately 30% of Nigeria’s GDP and 50% of the non-oil GDP. Even though most commercial and financial institutions are headquartered in Lagos, Lagos State’s economy is well diversified, covering key sectors like manufacturing, construction, agriculture and transportation.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The development of the two QBC’s will cost approximately US$50 million. IFC’s proposed investment will be an A loan of the NGN equivalent of up to US$50 million. The project is expected to be supported by the IDA-19 Private Sector Window (PSW) Local Currency Facility (LCF), as described in the Blended Finance section.
location_description: Lagos State, Nigeria
development_impact: The Project will support the support the rehabilitation of 2 Quality Bus Corridors ("QBC") located in the low-income areas of Lagos, providing passengers with more reliable and efficient public transportation, thereby reducing commute times and accidents along the corridors.
