Through more efficient and environmentally friendly transportation into the Lagos metropolis, the Project will contribute to a reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and environmental pollution. The Project is also expected to create local job opportunities during construction and provide training for long-term operations phase positions. The improved connectivity is expected to benefit the local community and support social inclusion by facilitating access to job opportunities and key social and business services. At the Market level, the Project will complement World Bank support for the Lagos Strategic Transport Master Plan Project, which is developed with technical and financial assistance from the World Bank. It will contribute to improving physical and economic integration and social and environmental sustainability.
additionality: (1) Long tenured local currency financing: IFC's 10-year loan will provide long-tenured local currency financing to the State, which is better suited for long-lived infrastructure projects. (2) Diversification of State's funding sources and reduction of FX risks: Historically, Lagos State has secured short term NGN loans from Nigerian commercial banks, and long term foreign currency loans from multilateral agencies - the World Bank and French Development Agency, AfD. IFC's proposed loan will provide a new source of long-term local currency financing to the State, which better matches the tenors of the State's infrastructure investments than loans from commercial banks, while reducing the State's FX risks; (3) WBG technical and E&S expertise in implementing the IFC-selected projects: IFC will assist Lagos State in implementing technical leading practice and IFC's Performance Standards for the selected projects, which should serve as an example to the rest of the State's ministries, departments and agencies, and ultimately to other subnational entities in Nigeria.

project_description: Globalworth Real Estate Investments Limited (“GREIL”, or together with its subsidiaries, the “Group”) is an integrated commercial property developer and manager in Romania and Poland. The Group focuses on Class A office space, premium logistics/light-industrial properties in the CEE region, either standing or through low-risk developments. The office sector has been going through challenging times since the onset of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. The uncertainty caused by the COVID-19 pandemic has had an impact on demand for office space in the second half of 2020, which has persisted in 2021. Market conditions are expected to remain uncertain in 2022 as several companies keep reassessing their occupational plans (extensions, expansions, relocations, release of spaces etc.), both due to the lasting effects of the pandemic as well as due to the recent outbreak of the war in Ukraine. The proposed investment is part of IFC’s COVID-19 response Real Sector Crisis Envelope and is aimed to support GREIL mitigate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on its operations in Romania (the “Second Project”). This is IFC’s second financing to the Group. In March 2018, IFC has subscribed a €50 million (approximately US$55 million) in a €550 million (approximately US$600 million) 7-year, senior, unsecured, Eurobond issued by GREIL. This is IFC’s second financing to the Group. In March 2018, IFC has subscribed €50 million in a 7-year senior unsecured Eurobond issue launched by GREIL under its €1.5 billion Euro Medium Term Notes program. The notes issued under the program are listed on the Irish Stock Exchange and the Bucharest Stock Exchange (the “First Project”). UPDATE RELATED TO ADDITIONAL INVESTMENT UNDER COVID-19 RESPONSE FACILITY: E&S Performance The company’s E&S performance continues to be satisfactory and aligned with good practices, which is materially compliant with applicable at-approval requirements under the active investment. The Project does not result in any new material E&S risks. GREIL’s management of existing E&S risks and impacts continues as described in the Environmental and Social Review Summary disclosed on April 2, 2018. Scope of IFC’s Appraisal IFC’s E&S due diligence for this follow-on investment, comprised meetings with the GREIL’s senior management and HR teams via video conferencing to understand the impact of COVID-19 pandemic on the company’s operations - particularly on its workforce and have updates on the company’s business operations, strategy, E&S performance. Also, IFC relied on the findings of recently virtual supervision visit completed in February 2022, which included meetings with the client’s teams responsible for human resources, environmental, health and safety (EHS) and overall management, review of EHS documentation, as well as virtual walk-through of the Globalworth Square office building in Bucharest, Romania. Response to COVID-19 Pandemic To manage COVID-19 pandemic impacts on its business operations, GREIL developed an appropriate mitigation strategy, a series of procedures and COVID-19 infection prevention and response plan, as well as assigned a dedicated COVID-19 management team to ensure business continuity and implementation of preventive measures at their operational buildings and development sites. GREIL had implemented COVID-19 response measures in line with the national legislation and good practices, made adequate arrangements to support and retain its direct and third-party employees, and provided help to fight the spread of the coronavirus in the community. Mitigation Measures / ESAP No further corrective measures in the form of the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP) has been developed for the Project. Refer to the completed E &S Action Plan in the ESRS of the previous project on the SPI (publishing) site: https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/41142/grei-bond
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 2013, GREIL is incorporated in Guernsey and listed on the AIM of the London Stock Exchange. GREIL is the indirect parent of all property-owning companies of the group in Romania and Poland and based on information made available to GREIL as of December 31, 2021, its shareholders include: Zakiano Enterprises Ltd (60.6%), Growthpoint Properties Ltd (29.4%) and Oak Hill Advisors (5.3%). The remaining 4.7% of GREIL’s shares are traded freely on the stock exchange, with no single shareholder holding more than 3%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The First Project was part of a bond issuance that was sized at €550 million with a 3.000% coupon. The proceeds where earmarked for general corporate purposes including acquisitions and new property developments, as well as to refinance existing debt. GREIL will use an amount at least equal to the proceeds of IFC’s investment in the bond exclusively for real estate property developments in Romania. The Second Project entails a senior, unsecured, 6-year, green loan of €85 million to Globalworth Holdings Cyprus Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of GREIL, for IFC’s own account (the “IFC Green Loan”). The IFC Green Loan will be used to finance or refinance commercial property projects in Romania that meet the eligibility criteria under GREIL’s Green Loan Framework.
location_description: Romania
development_impact: The Second Project will maintain access to high-quality commercial property in Romania, support the construction of projects under development, and contribute to future expansion as the sector recovers. Additionally, the Second Project helps the sector withstand shocks by supporting a systemically important player sustain its operations and continue with its expansion plan.
additionality: Expected Role & Additionality of the First Project: (i) IFC will provide long-term financing that will help GREI spread its debt service obligation over a longer horizon and better match the economic life of its commercial property portfolio; (ii) IFC will provide technical knowledge and advice to GREI on IFCs EDGE green building standard and will facilitate the environmental certification of a material part of its portfolio eligible for such certifications; and (iii) IFC will support the Company to enhance its environmental and social (E and S) practices. Expected Role & Additionality of the Second Project: (i) IFC's additionality is driven largely by its countercyclical role during crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. (ii) IFC's financing will provide critical access to liquidity to the Group, which will be used to maintain and prepare the office buildings for post-pandemic reopening, to sustain purchases of goods and services for ongoing developments in the logistics space, as well as to stay ahead of the curve and unlock developments in the office sector when demand picks up

company_name: INDORAMA ELEME FERTILIZER AND CHEMICALS FZE
project_description: The Project involves the expansion of an existing fertilizer facility located in Port Harcourt, Nigeria. The Project will double the capacity of the existing plant from 1.4 million tons per annum to 2.8 million tons per annum and is owned by Indorama Eleme Fertilizer & Chemicals Limited ("IEFCL" or the "Company"), a long time repeat IFC client. The Project is expected to cost US$1.1 billion and will be funded with an IFC A Loan of up to US$120 million, a MCCP loan of US$50 million, and up to US$830 million in B Loan syndication and parallel loans along with US$100 million equity subscription by the shareholders.
sponsor_shareholders: The Indorama Group is a long standing IFC client based in Indonesia. Since IFC’s first investment, it has grown into a global business entity with over US$10.5 billion in revenues. Indorama is the world’s largest producer of polyester and PET resins as well as one of the fastest growing global petrochemical producers with a presence in 29 countries. The group’s existing fertilizer plant in Nigeria is the world largest single stream Urea Fertilizer plant with a capacity to produce 2,300 tons of Ammonia per day and 4,000 tons of granulated urea per day.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost US$1.1 billion and will be funded with an IFC A Loan of up to US$120 million, a MCCP loan of US$50 million, and up to US$830 million in B Loan syndication and parallel loans.
location_description: Port Harcourt, Nigeria
development_impact: The Project will promote (i)economic diversification in Nigeria; (ii)direct and indirect employment; (iii)strong environmental sustainability by redirecting polluting wasted flared gas to productive use and introduce best in class energy and resource efficient technology; (iv)improvement in accessibility and supply of quality fertilizer to farmers; and (v)building of value chain linkages by supporting the local government to integrate smaller local NPK manufacturers into the domestic value chain.
additionality: IFC's participation will (i) provide long-term financing beyond what is generally available in the market, which is key in this sector; (ii) mobilize large amounts from other developmental financial institutions and commercial banks; (iii) continue support to a strategic client as it expands in Sub-Saharan Africa; and (iv) provide IFC's in-house technical, insurance, and EH&S expertise.
Company Name: INDORAMA ELEME FERTILIZER AND CHEMICALS FZE

project_description: The greenfield project entails the development of the first modern feedlot and abattoir in Southern Madagascar. The project aims to be a catalyst in assisting the Madagascar livestock industry to grow and reach its full export potential.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project is sponsored by Mr. Danilhoussen Ismael and his son Mr. Shahim Ismael (together the Sponsors). Mr. Ismael is a successful businessman in Madagascar who started as a trader and importer / distributor of spare parts/ paints. He moved thereafter to the manufacturing of plastics when he created Société Malgache de Transformation de Plastiques (SMTP). Together with his son Shahim Ismael, he now owns the SMTP Group, a leading conglomerate of about 20 companies involved in industrial plastics, bakery, poultry, animal feed, real estate, automobile dealership.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$15.3 million. The proposed IFC investment is a C loan for IFC’s own account of US$3.5 million and a C loan of US$3.5 million for GAFSP’s account.
location_description: Project is located in Fort-Dauphin, in a remote part of Southern Madagascar, one of the poorest regions of the country
development_impact: The Project has an Anticipated Impact Measurement and Monitoring (AIMM) rating of Excellent. The most significant, expected project-level outcome is improved access to market for herders and smallholder farmers, increased employment, and more economic activity in one of the poorest regions of Madagascar. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that this investment has the potential to promote greater integration and market competitiveness via the creation of a new market for meat exports and animal feed, linked to global value chains.
additionality: IFC additionality will stem from financial and non-financial sources. On the former, IFC's long-term, quasi equity funding is not available in the market and will enable the Companies to proceed with the investment. On the latter, IFC Advisory Services (AS) has worked with the Companies to make this investment viable. Through IFC AS, IFC will add value to the Companies by setting standards for the meat industry and providing knowledge and innovation in the form of technical and industry expertise, support for business strategy and operations, and supplier development.

project_description: Egyptian Fertilizers Company ( “ EFC ”, or the “Company”) is the largest private sector granular urea producer in Egypt. The proposed IFC’s investment is up to US$100mln to refinance EFC’s existing debt and support its maintenance capex and working capital needs (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is OCI N . V ., a global producer and distributor of natural gas-based fertilizers and industrial chemicals , l isted on Euronext in Amsterdam . EFC is wholly owned by OCI N.V.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC’s investment is up to US$100mln to refinance EFC’s existing debt and support its maintenance capex and working capital needs .
development_impact: IFC's investment will help to: (i) support growth in the agriculture sector through granular urea production; (ii) sustain employment and economic returns, EFC provides significant employment in the area; and (iii) support foreign currency generation through exports.
additionality: Through this investment, IFC will provide support to an existing client with good business prospects and export capacity by providing longer tenors that is scarce in the market.

project_description: NEPI Rockcastle plc (“NEPI Rockcastle”) is an internally managed commercial property investor and developer that owns a portfolio of regionally dominant shopping centers spread across nine countries, including Romania, Poland and Hungary. In the countries where NEPI Rockcastle operates, the retail activity was disrupted by restrictions introduced to prevent the spread of Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. The proposed investment is part of IFC’s COVID-19 response Real Sector Crisis Envelope and is aimed to support NEPI Rockcastle mitigate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on its operations in Romania (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: NEPI Rockcastle is incorporated in the Isle of Man and listed on the Main Board of the JSE and on Euronext Amsterdam (share code NRP). T he ownership of NEPI Rockcastle’s shares, as at the latest practicable date prior to the publication of the present Summary of Investment Information, in so far as it is known to NEPI Rockcastle, is as follows: (i) Fortress Income Fund 24.2%; (ii) Resilient Property Income Fund 13.0%; (iii) Public Investment Corporation 8.6%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project entails an EUR 73,521,134.49 senior, unsecured, 7-year, Green loan to NE Property B.V. for IFC’s own account. The proceeds of the Green loan will be utilized to finance or refinance, in whole or in part, projects in Romania that meet the Eligibility Criteria, as defined and listed in the Use of Proceeds section of NEPI Rockcastle’s “Green Finance Framework” dated June 2020, available at https://nepirockcastle.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/NEPI-Rockcastle-Green-Finance-Framework_Final.pdf .
location_description: The project is located in Romania.
additionality: I- Provide long-term financing and hence, extend the average maturity of the group's borrowings; - NEPI Rockcastle will benefit from IFC's advice on improvements in resource efficiency in construction and operations of its investment properties; and - IFC will share with NEPI Rockcastle international best practices in E&S management, and work on constant improvement of E&S standards.

project_description: Jain Irrigation Systems Limited (“JISL” or the “Company”) is one of India’s largest integrated agribusiness players, with operations in Micro Irrigation Systems (MIS), plastic pipes and sheets, dehydrated vegetables, processed fruits and other smaller businesses including tissue culture, agri-tech solutions and green energy. It is headquartered in Jalgaon in the western Indian state of Maharashtra. JISL is India’s leader in Micro Irrigation Systems and the second largest globally; it is also the largest manufacturer of plastic pipes in India. The Company had revenues of approximately US$ 1 billion for the last financial year (FY) ended March 31, 2017 and had a market capitalization of approximately US$ 930 million as of February 2, 2018.
sponsor_shareholders: JISL is listed on the National Stock Exchange and the Bombay Stock Exchange in India. The sponsors, the Jain family, currently own approximately 28.5% of the Company’s equity shares as of December 31, 2017. The Jain family has been involved in agriculture and plastics businesses since 1960s. Institutional investors own approximately 43.1% and the rest of the shareholding is held by other public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost over the next 12 months is estimated to be approximately US$ 50 million including capital expenditure for expansion of the Company’s operations in MIS, plastic pipes, tissue culture, and solar products in India and funding future growth IFC proposes an investment of up to US$ 40 million equivalent in INR denominated debt to part finance this capital expenditure in JISL.
location_description: JISL and its subsidiaries operate production facilities for MIS, plastic pipes, plastic sheets, tissue culture dehydrated vegetables and processed fruits in Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Rajasthan of India and has also invested in other subsidiaries overseas including the United States, UK, Turkey, and Israel. The proposed IFC financing will support JISL’s operations in India.
development_impact: 1) Raising farmer incomes: the adoption of MIS and better farming techniques is expected to reduce risk from weather, lower cost of farm inputs such as fertilizers and energy, and also increase yields. This will improve farmer income and have a direct impact on poverty reduction for those at the bottom of the pyramid. The Company also contracts with farmers to buy output for its food processing business. 2) Improved water management: India has 18% of the world's population and only 4% of the fresh water resources, and per capita availability is projected to keep declining. MIS improves water efficiency from the average 30-40% in India to 80-85%. This will lead to improved water management and a smaller environmental footprint caused by agricultural growth. 3) Improved infrastructure: The Company manufactures pipes used for water supply, sewage, waste management supporting the GoI's "Swachh Bharat" (Clean India) Mission. They will also be integral in the creation of Smart Cities.
additionality: 1) Long term partnership: The Company values the long-term relationship and shared values for development impact. 2) Long tenor capital: In an industry subject to variations in profitability due to weather patterns and fluctuations in productivity, IFC would provide long term capital which is not easily available. 3) Stamp of Approval: Raffirm faith in the Company management since redemption of previous instalment.

project_description: The proposed investment is to support JV LLC Nyva Pereyaslavschyny (“Nyva” or the “Company”), a large industrial pig and grain producer in Ukraine, by providing a long-term corporate loan to finance the Company’s 2018-2019 capital expansion program. Established in 1998 in the Kyiv region , the Company is Ukraine’s top-5 industrial pork producer. Nyva operates 9 pig farms and has 23,000 ha of agricultural land under management. In 201 7 , the Company produced over 2 8 0,000 of live pigs. The implementation of the Project will allow Nyva to expand its pig breeding operations and increase the meat processing capacity.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Oleksandr Mostipan, the founder and Chairman of the Board, is the ultimate beneficiary of the Group and owns 99% of the shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$35 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$12.5 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The expansion project is located in a rural area of the Kyiv region in Ukraine.
development_impact: The proposed investment is expected to benefit consumers, employees, and local community. The retailers, and ultimately the end consumers, will benefit from increased volumes of pork, produced in line with best international practices with regard to quality and food safety standards. In addition, IFC anticipates that the project will contribute to job creation in rural areas where employment opportunities are scarce, and will support the local community.
additionality: (i) Financial additionality: IFC is providing financing with longer tenors that are otherwise available in the market (commercial banks offer tenors of up to 3 years on comparable terms). (ii) Non-financial additionality: (a) Further improvements in E&S standards: A new ESAP will be implemented as part of the proposed investment. (b) Industry expertise, including on animal welfare practices: IFC will share industry expertise, drawing in its extensive global experience in this sector and continue to advise the company of best practices with regard to animal welfare.

project_description: The proposed investment is to support Astarta (“the Company”), a leading primary agriculture producer in Ukraine, by providing a long-term corporate loan to finance the Company’s 2017-2019 capital expansion program. This program aims at improving resource efficiency through the implementation of Best Available Technique standards at the Company’s factories, and at developing the farming and trading of grains and oilseeds through the financing of farming equipment and storage. Established in 1993, Astarta farms 246,600 hectares of land spread across Ukraine, operates nine processing plants and 200,000 tons of storage capacity and owns 30,000 cows. In 2016, it produced 910,000 tons of grains and oilseeds, 505,000 tons of sugar, 106,000 liters of milk and crushed 197,00 tons of soybeans into feed meal and oil. The implementation of the Project will allow Astarta to reduce its waste, fresh water consumption, gas usage and CO2 emissions and provide for additional saving on costs of sugar production and storage.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Victor Ivanchyk, the founder and the CEO of Astarta, owns 36% of the interest in the Company. The second major shareholder is Fairfax, a Canadian insurance broker, owning 28% of the Company. The rest is a free-float on WSE.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide corporate long-term financing to the Company in the form of an up to US$30 million A Loan.
location_description: Astarta’s HQ is located in Kiev, Ukraine. Astarta’s sugar factories, farms and storage are located in Ukraine’s rural areas, in the regions of Poltava, Kharkiv, Vinnitsa, and, Khmelnitskiy .
development_impact: The most significant, expected project-level outcomes are the benefits to farmers and the positive environmental effects of the planned Best Available Techniques (BAT) investments. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that the investment has the potential to promote market integration through improved competition and market enabling investments. The project will have the following impact: (i) Environmental and/or social benefits - IFC anticipates that, alongside improved operational efficiencies and lower costs of production, the project will have a significant positive effect on the environment. The BAT investment program financed by the project entails reductions in both water and energy use at Astarta's sugar plants. The project will also finance more modern and efficient machinery and equipment for the agriculture operations, enabling the Company to cultivate the land in a more sustainable manner. (ii) Benefits for the Consumers - IFC anticipates that, given the Company's focus on staple crops and its export orientation, the project will have a strong contribution on food security. IFC expects the increase in production of grains and oilseeds to translate into food availability for about 500,000 additional people. (iii) Benefits for the Farmers - IFC anticipates that the project will reach additional farmers through purchases of larger volumes of grains and oilseeds from third parties, investments in new storage capacities for third-party use, and new employment in agricultural operations at Astarta's own farms. IFC expects the construction of new storage facilities to address a significant infrastructure bottleneck for Ukraine's primary producers, enabling sales at more opportune times, expanding choices of who to sell to, and reducing port-harvest losses by up to 3,500 MT per year. IFC expects that these in turn will generate better incomes and more streamlined trading relationships.
additionality: IFC's additionality in the proposed transaction stems primarily from its contribution to shaping the Company's sustainability practices and mitigating the country risks through consistent high-level support to a long-standing client in a country that is susceptible to periods of economic and political instability. In particular: (i) Standard Setting with support to improvements of Environmental & Social standards: Since IFC's first investment in 2012, the Company has steadily improved its E&S performance as evidenced by (a) the Company's compliance with IFC's several the Environmental and Social Action plans; (b) the Implementation of energy efficiency measures at the sugar plants with the BAT program 2012-2016, and now, the BAT program 2017-2022; and; (c) the award of several E&S certifications to the Company including ISO9001/14001/500001, OHSAS 18001, and, FSSC 22000. As a result of this project, two four new plants (Kobeljatsky, Yareskivsky ZhdanivskyNovoorzhytskiy, and, Novoivanivskiy) will be certified ISO 14001OHSAS 18001 (E&S Management) and ISO22000 (food safety) while Globino, now equipped with its waste water treatment plant, will be certified ISO50001 (energy management). (ii) Non-Financial risk mitigation by minimizing the risk of political intervention and the impact of the political crisis. Indeed, IFC stayed during the political and economic crisis which affected Ukraine and continued to support the Company with two liquidity loans (in 2015 and 2016) commercial funding was not available.

project_description: The project consists of an IFC equity investment of up to US$5 million in Smartpaddle Technology Private Limited (“Bizongo” or the “Company”), a Mumbai based company that operates as a B2B technology platform providing one-stop-shop packaging solutions to medium and large companies. The Company curates, on-boards and provides access to SME packaging material manufacturers across India. The end-to end platform allows for strong customer and supplier stickiness and unlocks efficiencies in the supply chain.
sponsor_shareholders: Bizongo was founded by Aniket Deb (CEO, ex-Opera Solutions), Sachin Agrawal (COO, ex-Gravitas) and Ankit Tomar (CTO, ex-Microsoft). The Company’s investors also include leading venture capital investors such as Accel Partners and IDG Ventures.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes an equity investment of up to US$5 million as part of the Company’s fundraising round with additional capital being provided by existing investors and new investor.
location_description: Bizongo has its registered office in Mumbai, India. It has warehouses in three cities – Mumbai, Bangalore and New Delhi through which it services customers across the country.
development_impact: A. Project Impact A.1. Stakeholder Impact A.1.1. Increase in number of SME suppliers reached: Bizongo has more than 2500 registered SMEs, allowing smaller offline players to integrate better into the market. A.1.2. Increased capacity utilization of SME suppliers by providing access to larger customers: Many SMEs in this sector lack professional expertise to market and distribute products, leading to low (less than 50%) capacity utilization. Bizongo is able to provide incremental demand and process knowhow which has led some suppliers to increase capacity utilization, significantly improving efficiency. A.1.3. Improved financial sustainability of the SME suppliers through shorter working capital cycles: Suppliers are better able to manage their business financially due to shorter working capital cycles - since they no longer need to approach buyers individually - which leads to lower working capital needs and better inventory and time management. Customer acquisition costs are also decreased. A.2. Economic Impact A.2.1. Improved Employment: Bizongo currently gives jobs to ~110 employees directly (of which women are ~30%). Increased order volumes for suppliers could also lead to more employment within the SME packaging sector. B. Market Impact B.1. Improve efficiency and innovation by aggregating a highly fragmented industry: Bizongo contributes to market creation by consolidating and tech-enabling the packaging sector, which is currently fragmented and largely unorganized, with more than 30k registered packaging companies, out of which 85% are MSMEs. The platform supports innovation and efficiency by improving quality, developing new designs, standardizing existing designs and improving the efficiency of suppliers to make them more competitive. B.2. Promoting the digital economy by increasing SME integration into ecommerce: SME B2B ecommerce in India is still underdeveloped. Bringing SMEs into the digital economy improves market linkages, strengthens the value chain and promotes financial inclusion (as digital invoices can prove credit worthiness to banks). This project also signals IFC's confidence in the financial viability of the broader B2B eCommerce space.
additionality: 1. Financial Additionality 1.1. Early stage equity finance: IFC can play a counter-cyclical role in the ongoing tough fund raising environment in India for early-stage companies, especially for companies looking for Series B stage funding. 2. Non-Financial Additionality 2.1. Knowledge sharing: IFC will share Indian and global sector learnings and expertise from existing investments in the B2B eCommerce space (Moglix, Power2SME) and other related sectors. 2.2. Best practices: IFC will support the company in implementing best practices in corporate governance and environmental and social management through the appointment of a Director to the Board. Through adoption of the IFC Performance Standards, the Company will be able to further improve its operating standards 2.3. Assisting with key industry relationships: The Company will benefit from access to IFC's deep relationships in the Indian VC market when it pursues future funding rounds.

sponsor_shareholders: IndoSpace Capital Asia Pte. Limited (“Singapore Manager”), a Singapore private limited company will act as the fund manager to the Fund. The Singapore Manager will appoint IndoSpace Capital Advisors Private Limited, a company incorporated under the Indian Companies Act, 1956 in India (the “Indian Sub-Advisor” or “IndoSpace”), to be a non-discretionary investment advisor. The Fund’s sponsor is IndoSpace Capital Management (Cayman) Limited (“Sponsor”), which is jointly owned and controlled by Everstone Capital and Realterm.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund is seeking to raise US$500 million in capital commitments. IFC proposes an equity investment of up to US$25 million (not to exceed 20% of total commitments) in the Fund. IFC’s Asset Management Company (“IFC AMC”) is also considering a parallel investment.
location_description: The Fund, a Singapore limited partnership, will focus on investing directly or indirectly, through Indian subsidiaries, to own and operate industrial and warehousing parks across locations in India. The Fund’s India Sub-Advisor is based out of India.
development_impact: Supply of high quality industrial and warehousing property assets in India's core industrial areas is very limited with demand far exceeding supply and resulting in lost opportunities for industrial growth and job creation. The Project will bring in a significant new supply of industrial and warehousing infrastructure for rent in locations across the country, including low income states in India. The modern high quality industrial and warehousing parks developed by the Project will reduce operating costs and improve efficiency in the entire supply chains of manufacturing companies and logistics operators, which will trickle down to lower cost of goods and services. It will also enhance ease of doing business in India, thereby attracting valuable foreign investment and anchoring manufacturing growth. The Project will foster the creation of direct jobs during both the construction and operation of properties. The project will also support a significant number of indirect jobs through the supply chain. The Project assets, once developed, will constitute an attractive pool of matured, institutional-quality property assets that are expected to be aggregated into a portfolio. This portfolio of matured assets as it evolved will become a significant private or public REIT-platform, thus contributing to debottlenecking the evolution of this still embryonic property-based financial market in India. Lastly, the warehouses under the Project are expected to be certified IFC EDGE compliant with potentially at least 20 percent savings in energy, water and materials consumption compared with benchmarks for equivalent buildings.
additionality: IFC is uniquely positioned to provide as well as mobilize capital for IndoSpace's largest property fund so far. IFC's participation will also result in the Project meeting EDGE Green Building standards, promoting resource efficiency and positive environmental impact, which would otherwise not have occurred.

project_description: In 1985, Mr Krisdianto Lesmana and his wife, Mrs Ida Surjati Djaja Mukti established a traditional snack company serving the local market in Indonesia. In 2003, this home industry business was transformed to PT Kaldu Sari Nabati Indonesia (“Nabati” or the “Company”), a producer of wafers, biscuits, snacks and confectioneries under two principle brands: Richeese and Richoco. The Company owns three plants in Indonesia in the cities of Cicalengka, Rancaekek and Majalengka, all located in West Java. The proposed investment is an up to US$100 million loan package comprising up to US$ 40 million A loan, up to US$ 30 million B Loan and up to US$ 30 million MCPP Loan to Nabati to support the expansion of its wafers, biscuits and snacks factory in Majalengka (the “Project”). The Project is expected to cost US$133 million of which US$33 million is from internally generated cash.
sponsor_shareholders: Nabati was founded in 1985 by Mr Krisdianto Lesmana and his wife, Mrs Ida Surjati Djaja Mukti (the “Founders”). The Company is part of the Nabati Group which consists of several lines of business: (i) Food manufacturing; (ii) Quick service restaurants; (iii) Domestic sales and distribution; (iv) International sales and distribution; (v) Property and building management services. The Founders in 2005 passed the leadership baton to their eldest son, Mr Erwin Lesmana. Their other sons, Mr Ernest and Ericksanders Lesmana, and daughter, Mrs Elisa Lesmana, are also holding key management positions. Nabati is wholly owned by the Founders’ family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$133 million. IFC´s investment consists of an A Loan of up to US$40 million, a B loan of up to US$30 million and an MCPP loan of up to US$ 30 million.
location_description: The Project will be located in Majalengka, West Java, Indonesia.
development_impact: - The development impact of the proposed project will be assessed using the AIMM framework. Project-level impacts are expected through employment creation both during the construction and operation phases as well as through economic activities along the value chain, especially at the downstream end with Nabati's extensive sales force and distributors. - The Project will also increase tax revenues in Majalengka, a frontier region in Indonesia where the minimum salary is US$150 per month vs. US$ 200 in the closest largest city (Bandung) or US$ 250 in Jakarta. The Project will also improve incomes of the SMEs which supply materials to Nabati. - The Project is also expected to contribute to food security for bottom of the pyramid consumers. The new facilities to be funded by IFC will produce low market pricing products which are fortified with vitamins A, B1, B2, B6 and B12 (currently ~80% of Nabati's products are fortified).
additionality: - IFC is considered an ideal partner given its reputation, environmental & social standards, long term local presence and network around the world. - IFC is able to provide debt with a 7 year tenor, 2 years longer than what the market is offering. IFC helps mobilize long term capital which meets the Company's financing needs and matches the maturities of assets and liabilities, improving the balance sheet structure. - IFC will assist Nabati in upgrading its practices to meet IFC's Performance Standards. This would not only help Nabati to build a sustainable operation but also encourage other companies to adopt international best practices as consumers give each day more value to E&S friendly products. - During the appraisal, IFC has advised the Company to strengthen its corporate governance by establishing a functioning board of commissioners and an effective audit committee. IFC Advisory Services ("AS") will help Nabati to establish corporate governance best practices that will allow the Company to continue expanding and prepare for an eventual IPO. - From an energy efficiency perspective, IFC Energy and Water Advisory team is conducting a back of the envelope assessment of waste heat to power options. The improved efficiency through modernization and potential investments in waste heat recovery will produce significant reductions in Green House Gas Emissions. Nabati is looking forward to hearing IFC's proposal.

project_description: Morris Holdings Limited (“Morris” or the “Company”) is a publicly listed company and a global leader in the upholstered sofa industry. With a market capitalization of approximately US$200 million and 2016 sales of approximately US$141.5 million, the Company is the second largest upholstered sofa manufacturer in China in terms of export value to the U.S. Morris integrates the functions of design, research and development, manufacturing, online and off line sales, and after sales services. The proposed IFC investment will support Morris’ capacity expansion program for i) additional production facilities and working capital in both Cambodia and China in order to address production bottlenecks and growing demand and ii) refinancing of short term debt (together, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Morris is 75% owned by Morris Capital Limited, a British Virgin Islands-incorporated holding company which is owned 85% by the Mr. ZOU Gebing (the “Sponsor”) and 15% by his wife Ms. WU Xiangfei. The other 25% of Morris is owned by public shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be approximately US$103.5 million. IFC’s proposed investment is a convertible loan of up to HK$200 million (approximately US$26 million equivalent).
location_description: The Project is expected to be located in 500 Youquan Road, Haining, Zhejiang 314400, People’s Republic of China and in 212km National Road No. 4, Prey Nob District, Sihanoukville, Cambodia.
development_impact: South-South Investment and Higher Operational Efficiencies: - Cambodia: The Project entails the transfer of knowledge and technical expertise as well as foreign direct investment from China to Cambodia, developing a stronger South-South value chain in the forestry and wood products sector. As a supplier to demanding U.S. and Canadian markets with stringent industry standards, Morris is well-placed to disseminate these practices to less developed countries. The adoption of best industry practices is expected to strengthen technological capacity and bring process improvements to the furniture industry in Cambodia, improving competitiveness at a larger scale than what is currently prevalent in the country. - China: In addition, the China component of the Project will help the Company achieve even greater economies of scale in China, leading to more competitive products for domestic consumption as well as export markets. The planned expansion in China is expected to increase the Company's production by 30%. Employment Generation and Standards Setting: - Cambodia: The transfer of export-quality furniture manufacturing knowledge and technology from China to Cambodia will go hand in hand with creating jobs in Cambodia and improving the skill base of the local labor force, thus raising overall productivity in the sector. The Project is expected to help create viable long term skilled and semi-skilled direct labor opportunities for approximately 800 people at the Cambodian operating facility as well as additional employment along the supply chain. The Project is also expected to help the Company pursue an ethical work program and contribute to improved labor conditions in Cambodia though the application of IFC's Performance Standards. - China: A sizeable number of direct jobs will also be created in China as a result of the Project. The Company's operations are fairly labor-intensive and the new facilities will require about 2,200 new employees. Over the longer term, the number of jobs and their skills level may evolve if the Company undertakes the recommended automatization which would improve resource use efficiencies. The Project has the potential to generate market level impacts by supporting the development of the nascent furniture industry in Cambodia and helping to integrate the country into more diversified global value chains. In particular: - Cambodian industrial production is characterized by a narrow base, low level of technological sophistication, low value addition, and high concentration in only a few sectors (notably textiles and footwear, which represent approximately 80% of merchandise exports). Against this backdrop, a Chinese company diversifying its manufacturing base to Cambodia would help a country which is eager to both move up the manufacturing value chain as well as diversify over-reliance on textiles and garments. To help the country's manufacturing sector, Cambodian authorities have established the new Industrial Development Policy (IDP) 2015-2015, which provides a roadmap to boost investment and broaden the manufacturing base. - The proposed Project would build a new production facility in Sihanoukville Special Economic Zone (SSEZ) in line with IDP's vision. By undertaking a phased approach that starts with textile-based production (sofa covers) the Company is utilizing Cambodia's existing comparative advantages but is planning to invest in training and skill-building necessary to transition to furniture manufacturing and assembly. A successful outcome of the project is expected to demonstrate to international investors that Cambodia is a viable place of origin for high quality furniture and potentially attract new players. Furthermore, the Project is expected to have a positive impact on the local economy by upgrading the domestic manufacturing industry, diversifying exports, and integrating the country into new global value chains, thus strengthening its resilience to economic shocks.
additionality: 1) Access To Long Term Finance: The Company relies on short term loans and equity to fund its operations. The Company's balance sheet is currently not big enough to attract many commercial lenders, and thus the IFC long term financing is expected to act as a catalyst to bring in other potential investors. In addition, IFC's C Loan will be the first convertible debt for the Company and represent a new instrument in the Company's capital structure. With IFC's long term, appropriately structured capital, Morris would be able to further expand without incurring excessive liquidity risks, better match the investment payback period, and create more stability in its financing. 2) Environmental and Social (E&S) Standards Setting: Through this Project, the Company is expected to adopt and implement appropriate standards in labor management, production, as well as supply chains and raw material procurement, particularly those between China and Cambodia, thus enhancing traceability and sustainable resource use. 3) Local Presence in Cambodia: Morris is new to operating in Cambodia, while IFC has a long presence in the country and could help introduce the Company to local financial institutions and other potential business partners. 4) Credibility and Positive Signaling: Some firms in China, especially those listed overseas, including in Hong Kong, have recently been accused of improper financial disclosures and governance issues. IFC's support to Morris may send a positive signal to the market about its operations and enhance its credibility with potential partners.

project_description: The proposed loan of US$2.5 million (the “IFC Loan”) is a corporate facility to be provided to Tajero (the “Company”) for financing its working capital needs.
sponsor_shareholders: Tajero is 100% owned by Mr. Abdurakhmon Gaibullozoda, a reputable Tajikistani entrepreneur. The Company specializes in the distribution of foods including meats, oils, juices and confectionary. It also represents over 30 international brands with national coverage of ~80% of Tajikistan’s retail points of sales.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is ~US$7 mn, the working capital needs for FY18. IFC has been invited to provide an A loan package of US$2.5 mn, and the balance will be funded by sponsor loan (US$3.0 mn) and internal cash generation (US$1.6 mn).
location_description: Dushanbe, Tajikistan.
development_impact: The Project will have strong development impact through: i) improvement of consumer access and value through better access to a more diverse selection, quality, affordability of food products, and better consumer prices due to economies of scale; ii) development of food distribution sector as the expansion will help increase the number of suppliers, build additional sales channels, and contribute to improvement in efficiency and operating standards throughout the supply chain; iii) import substitution: through improving and increasing its distribution capability, the Group will have an increased ability to distribute its rapidly developing dairy production capacity for the local market. This would decrease sales of imported, hard currency denominated goods providing a less costly, locally produced alternatives in a country which depends for 80% on imported food items.
additionality: By providing much needed financing IFC will support the long-term relationship with the leading retailer in the country, which is likely to expand in the future both in the retail and manufacturing sectors.

project_description: The Carlyle Group (“Carlyle”) has invited IFC to participate with an equity investment in a dedicated warehouse investment platform Roma Holding Company Limited (the “Platform”). The Platform will develop, build and operate between 10 and 15 warehouses in various cities across China. The warehouses will be built to modern efficient designs incorporating the latest green building technology, and leased to third parties such as retail and logistics operators.
sponsor_shareholders: As of September 30, 2017, the Carlyle Group is a global alternative asset manager with US$174 billion of assets under management (“AUM”) across 116 funds and 190 fund of funds vehicles. In emerging markets, Carlyle manages 8 private equity fund families with total AUM of US$14 billion.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC has been invited to provide up to USD30 million of equity capital to support the Project. The IFC Asset Management Company is also considering a co-investment.
location_description: The warehouses will be located in various cities across China.
development_impact: Expected development impact includes: (i) Linkages: Modern, high-quality warehouses support improved efficiencies and reduced operational costs for local businesses and supply chains. (ii) Standards: Other industry players will be encouraged to raise standards by increased competition. The Project is expected to serve as a catalyst for other firms to make improvements in areas such as labor conditions, safety, efficient use of resources and environmental sustainability.
additionality: (i) Industry knowledge: IFC has experience of this emerging sub-sector globally, and knowledge of sector trends/evolution are being shared with the Carlyle team. (ii) Green buildings: IFC green buildings expertise is being shared to reduce the environmental footprint in terms of resource consumption.

project_description: Vinavil Egypt for Chemicals S.A.E. (“Vinavil Egypt” or “the Company” ( http://www.vinavil.com/eg/ ) is a leading manufacturer of industrial chemicals used in paints, adhesives and other special materials for construction industry. The Company is part of the “Mapei Group”, (“Mapei Group” or the “Group”) - a vertically-integrated Group manufacturing of emulsion, and polymer additives for concrete and end-user construction specialty for building, the Group includes marketing and sales companies operating in more than 50 countries worldwide. Vinavil’s investment plan is to expand production line inside its existing production hall.
sponsor_shareholders: Mapei S.p.A. (“Mapei”, or “the Sponsor”) is a private company and the 4th largest global construction specialty chemicals producer. Mapei was founded in 1937 with its corporate headquarters in Milan, Italy. Mapei wholly-owns the Project company Vinavil Egypt
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is US$15 million. IFC will be providing US$15 million Straight Senior Loan
location_description: The plant is located in the Attaqa Industrial Area Suez Region, Arab Republic of Egypt
development_impact: Development impact TBD with IFC's AIMM framework. Project Level - Stakeholders: local builders increased access to quality adhesives, sealants and concrete additives for efficient/lasting construction. - Value addition/employment/economic returns TBD with newly-developed sector multipliers. - Environmental impacts/climate change mitigation: 70% of R&D is for eco-sustainable products with 5-10% in CO2 emissions/energy savings. Market Level demonstration impact TBD for resilience/sustainability of specialty materials.
additionality: IFC's role and additionality in the proposed investment is expected to include: Additionality - Strategic partnership: In complex political/business environments, as Egypt, Mapei expects IFC to help with associated risks. - L/T EGP funds to hedge FX risk for WC/capex needs -70% of sales in EGPs. - Diversified funding: IFC funds complement those of commercial banks.

project_description: Rikweda Fruit Process Company (Rikweda, the Project or the Company) is a 15,000 ton per annum (tpa) raisin processing plant in Kabul, Afghanistan. The Project cost is estimated at US$9.0 million of which US$6 million is financed by the Sponsors' equity. IFC has been invited to extend a revolving working capital facility of up to US$2.5 million renewable on an annual basis for five years. IFC will also extend a C Loan of up to US$0.5 million in exchange for advisory services to support Rikweda’s growth.
sponsor_shareholders: Project Sponsor and Major Shareholders of Project Company Pending
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is estimated to cost US$9.0 million. The Sponsors will invest up to US$6 million through the Company's equity while IFC will contribute up to US$2.5 million as a working capital facility (A Loan), and US$0.5 million as a C Loan in exchange for IFC Advisory Services. IFC’s A Loan will benefit from a first-loss guarantee (FLG) up to 50% of IFC’s exposure provided by the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP).
location_description: Rikweda, headquartered in Kabul, has a raisin processing plant in Istalif, 30 km north of Kabul. It is strategically located in Afghanistan’s raisins producing region of Shamali.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have the following development impact: (i) providing farmers with sustainable access to markets; (ii) expected employment creation of 60 direct jobs and a number of indirect jobs across the value chain; (iii) building farmers' capacity through advisory services to support extension services and improve farming practices; (iv) promoting women's role through support to female producers; (v) promoting food safety through IFC's technical assistance services; and (vi) support climate smart agriculture through the construction of a modern processing plant designed to reduce heat waste and increase water efficiency savings.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality stems from its ability to provide: (i) financing not readily available in the country and at affordable rates; (ii) advisory services and environmental and social best practices; and (iii) stamp of approval as IFC's involvement is expected to raise the Project's profile and possibly facilitate future financing from local banks.

country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: IFC is considering providing an unsecured A and B/Parallel loan financing package of up to US$150m to CIE Automotive S.A. (“CIE” or together with its subsidiaries the “Group”) to finance 2017-2019 capital expenditure for its expansion plans in Mexico (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: CIE is a global Tier 2 automotive components and sub-assemblies supplier, headquartered in Bilbao, Spain, with 98 production sites located across 17 countries. The Group has two business units: i) CIE Automotive which is focused on the design and manufacturing of components and sub-assemblies supplies for the automotive sector and represents approximately 78% of revenues and, ii) Dominion which provides services to the telecommunications, transport, healthcare, utilities, renewable energy and government sectors and represents approximately 22% of revenues. The Group trades in the Madrid, Bilbao and Bombay stock exchanges; market capitalization as of October 13, 2017 of €3.1bn (price: €24.15, 52-week low: €16.26, 52-week high: €24.45) in the Madrid Stock Exchange. CIE is mainly owned by Acek Desarrollo y Gestion Industrial (formerly Corporación Gestamp) which has a direct and indirect participation of 20.9%, Mahindra & Mahindra which directly and indirectly owns 12.4%, Antonio Maria Pradera who directly and indirectly owns 10%, the Egaña Family (founding shareholders) with 9.6% indirect participation and Addvalia Capital S.A. and Alantra Asset Management S.A. with a 5% participation each. The remaining is owned by other public shareholders.?
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: CIE’s 2017-2019 investment plan for Mexico has a total cost of US$234 million, out of which up to US$75 million will be financed with the IFC A Loan, up to US$125 million from B/Parallel Lenders the rest being financed from internal cash generation.
location_description: The project is being implemented in the states of Mexico, Guanajuato, Puebla and Coahuila, where OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers have confirmed to invest in expanding their production capacity .
development_impact: - Supply Chain: Strengthening the competitiveness of one of a leading automotive parts and components producers and its supply chain in the Mexico, will result in corresponding impacts on technical upgrading of its local supply chain, production volumes and economy-wide linkages. - Sustainable employment: The Project will generate 899 skilled direct jobs across the CIE's 9 manufacturing plants in the country in addition to several indirect jobs in the Group's suppliers who will also be increasing capacity and upgrading skills to meet the higher volume requirements. - Customers: End consumers, predominantly OEMs and Tier 1 companies operating in Mexico, will benefit from better access to a reliable source of good quality locally produced components and parts for their operations, which ultimately helps with sustaining the competitiveness of the automotive cluster in the country which will depend less on imported parts. - Market: Stronger integration of local suppliers into the domestic and global value chains through the improvement of standards and capacity.
additionality: - Diversification of funding, longer tenor and US$ funds: IFC will help CIE diversify its source of funds, further increase the maturity of its financial debt and provide US$ currency to better match the cash flow from the NAFTA region. - Establishing a strategic long-term partnership: CIE values IFC's global presence, risk mitigation and expertise in the sector. This investment could be followed by further collaboration in other developing countries.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: The proposed project involves a combination of: (i) IFC investing equity in an INR equivalent of approximately US$23 million in one or more Special Purpose Vehicles (“SPVs”) promoted by Ashiana Housing Limited (“Ashiana” or the “Company” or the “Sponsor”) set up for the development of affordable / mid-income housing and senior living projects in India; (ii) A senior loan of an INR equivalent of US$18 million to Ashiana Housing Limited for general corporate purposes.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1979 by late Om Prakash Gupta, Ashiana Housing is promoted by three brothers, Vishal Gupta, Ankur Gupta and Varun Gupta. Ashiana is listed on the Bombay and National Stock Exchanges in India. Ashiana is a leading real estate company in India developing affordable / mid-income housing including senior living. Focused on the middle-income segment, Ashiana has constructed 42 projects since inception, constructing over 20 million sq.ft. and over 10,000 units. As on 31 March, 2017, the Company is present in multiple city-clusters across India with over 2.4 million sqft of existing projects and a pipeline of over 8 million sqft of future projects. Ashiana is one of the pioneers of the senior living having launched its first senior living project in Bhiwadi in 2005. Subsequently, Ashiana launched four more senior living projects in Bhiwadi, Jaipur, Lavasa and Chennai.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost for which IFC's equity investment of US$23 million will be used is estimated at about US$267 million. IFC's debt investment will be used for general corporate purposes.
location_description: The project is expected to be located across various cities in India, but primarily in Jaipur (Rajasthan), Pune (Maharashtra) and Chennai (Tamil Nadu).
development_impact: 1. Stakeholder Impact: Access to affordable / mid-income housing for customers in the Low-Income State (LIS) of Rajasthan and in Tier II cities in India; Access to senior living houses for senior citizens Project to provide 5,000-6,000 units over the next 5-7 years; development of 200 to 250 units for the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) and lower Low Income Group (LIG) segments in the LIS of Rajasthan. 2. Value-added and employment impact: Creation of ~1,800 jobs direct jobs through the Project, a large number of which are expected in the LIS of Rajasthan; jobs will be created in construction, marketing, and sales amongst other verticals; Creation of a number of indirect jobs through supply linkages. 3. Environment Impact and Sustainability: All projects will be executed under the IFC Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies (EDGE) or Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) certification; 100% of the Project will contribute towards climate change. 4. Competitiveness: Lean operations across verticals to provide demonstration effect to the market; 5. Inclusiveness: Project to develop 5,000-6,000 units in the underserved affordable / mid-income housing segment;
additionality: 1. Long-term financing: Long term capital is not readily available to the real estate sector. IFC's equity investment is a structured 8-year equity investment, which would provide patient capital with a tenor that matches the Project's life. 2. Demonstration effect: IFC is one of very few financiers to the affordable/mid-income housing sector. IFC's continued support of the sector, through the provision of long-term capital at reasonable terms is critical for the further development of and investor confidence in the sector. 3. Environmental & social: IFC's Green Building Specialists will work with the Company to identify opportunities to reduce its environmental impact during the construction process and to reduce the energy consumption and waste generation of the units built.

project_description: IFC will provide a five-year loan of up to US$ 35 million to Westfalia Fruit International Limited (“WFIL”), a wholly owned subsidiary of South Africa-based Hans Merensky Holdings (Pty) Limited. The loan will be used to strengthen WFIL’s supply chain network in the Latin America region. The project is expected to transfer fruit farming, ripening, storage, distributing knowledge and skills to farmers in Chile, Mexico and Colombia. IFC investment will support acquisition of a local fruit exporting company in Chile and development of a Nursery in Colombia. The IFC investment will allow a leading South African fruit exporter to strengthen its position as a leading international supplier of avocados and enhance capacity to supply avocados year-round.
sponsor_shareholders: Westfalia is a leading multinational supplier of fresh subtropical fruit and related processed products to international markets. It is part of the HMH Group, with an annual revenue of US $700 million and net income of ~US $37 million. Westfalia grows, sources, ripens, packs, and distributes sustainably grown avocados year-round. Westfalia’s vertically-integrated supply chain enables it to market quality fruit from across the globe. HMH is a South African-based vertically-integrated, natural resource-based Company which was created in 1949 by the late Dr. Hans Merensky (a biologist and philanthropist). It has two main businesses, namely: (i) the fruit business ("Westfalia") and (ii) the timber business ("Merensky" or "Merensky Timbers"). HMH's operations are spread in Sub-Saharan Africa, South America and Europe. Group shareholding is as follows: The Hans Merensky Foundation - 40.02%, the Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) - 29.7%, IFC - 20%, and, three Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (BBBEE) organizations: Vuka Forestry Holdings (4.03%), Women Investment Portfolio Holdings (WIPHOLD) (3.30%), and, HMH Employee Share Ownership Plan (2.95%) owning the outstanding 9.9%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Westfalia is planning to raise US $140 million through a syndicated five-year facility to acquire an avocado food grower in Chile, establish a Nursery in Colombia, develop supply chain infrastructure in Mexico, and expand marketing operations in North America and Europe. The investment in Part I countries (Europe and USA) is critical in supporting further production in Part II countries. IFC is providing a loan of up to US$ 35 million, as part of a broader $165 million syndicated facility.
location_description: Major portion of the financing will be used in Chile, Colombia, and Mexico to strengthen avocado supply chain from these markets,
development_impact: IFC anticipates the project will affect a significant number of avocado farmers in Colombia, Chile, Peru, and Mexico, who will benefit from better access to inputs such as avocado cultivars from newly-established or expanded nurseries. The project will also create ~730 new direct jobs in Colombia (nursery and orchards), Chile (nursery and logistics), and Peru (orchards) . In addition, the project is expected to have meaningful impact across a range of market-level dimension, including competitiveness, inclusiveness, and sustainability. The proposed investment will make the South African avocado industry more globally competitive and enhance the country reputation's as a hub for sector expertise and on avocados.
additionality: Through this proposed investment IFC will (a) support an existing South African client make a South-South investment into South Africa (b) strengthen the long term partnership with HMH in their expansion (c) work with HMH to improve smallholder engagement in Colombia and Peru and (d) help bridge the environmental and social practices between HMH and the new company.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an up to US$300 million syndicated pre-export finance facility to support Vicentin S.A.I.C.’s working capital needs from exports of oilseed oil and sub-products (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Vicentin SAIC (“Vicentin” or the “Company”) is an Argentine family-owned company incorporated in 1929 and one of the ten largest exporters in Argentina. With a crushing capacity of 29,500 tons/day, it is among the five major oilseed crushers in country. The company operates several oilseeds crushing plants, a refinery, biodiesel plants and a port.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC investment will consist of a long-term loan for up to US$300 million, including the rescheduling of existing IFC A/B Loan outstanding amounts and new financing. A portion will be syndicated among B lenders.
location_description: The P roject area is Santa Fe Province, in Argentina.
development_impact: - Stakeholders' impacts: i) benefits to soybean and sunflower farmers who will secure a reliable access to market, and ii) benefits to the end consumers who benefit from improved food security as a result of larger volumes of oilseeds (+900,000 metric tons) and their derivatives brought to market; - Support the Competitiveness of an Export-Oriented Sector in Argentina: as Argentina slowly reengages with the global capital markets, IFC's support to Vicentin should send positive signal to other investors about the strong prospects and solid fundaments of the oilseeds sector in Argentina, which is globally competitive and relevant in the international markets; - Environmental and Social Standards: IFC investment is expected to further enhance Vicentin's E&S performance in a number of areas by setting performance indicators and targets.
additionality: - Longer Tenor Financing: Long-term financing that is not readily available locally at adequate terms. The proposed investment has a tenor of up to 7 years for pre-export financing, which is currently unavailable in Argentina for this type of pre-export financing structures; - Resource Mobilization: IFC's umbrella has been critical to mobilize additional funding from B lenders. IFC's participation in this Project will mobilize about 7.6 times the amount of IFC investment on its own account in participations from commercial lenders; - Long Term Partnership: The proposed investment represents IFC's sixth transaction with Vicentin, enabling a domestic family-owned company to successfully compete with multinationals that usually have access to competitive financial terms on a global basis; - Improvement in Environmental and Social Standards: IFC's participation in the Project will continue strengthening the Company's Environmental and Social Standards, particularly in relation to Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) and waste water treatment.

project_description: Productos Naturales de la Sabana SA Alqueria (“Alqueria” or the “Company”) is the third-largest dairy company in Colombia. The Company processes milk and its derivatives into a wide range of diversified dairy products. Alqueria is seeking financing to strengthen its capital structure and support its expansion program for 2017- 2021. IFC would provide US$20m in equity ,
sponsor_shareholders: Alqueria is owned by the following: (i) Cavelier Family: The largest shareholder of Alqueria, with 93.8% of the shares of the Company; (ii) IFC: holds 4.4% of the Company trough convertible preferred shares; and (iii) Alianza Fiduciaria: owns 1.8% of Alqueria’s in the form of convertible preferred shares, represented by Humberto Polania, former main shareholder of Freskaleche, a dairy company acquired by Alqueria in 2015 .
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The funds will strengthen Alqueria’s capital structure to support its expansion program for 2017- 2021 that expects to: (i) Consolidate the identified synergies with Freskaleche in the Santander Region in distribution, raw milk access, transport, administration, and branding strengths; (ii) Reach a higher market penetration in the Atlantic and Pacific Coasts via increased commercial / marketing efforts; (iii) Increase its share in the yogurt segment by the recent acquisition of DASA; (iv) Develop new value added products, such as different kind of yogurts, 100% fruit based juices, almond beverages, whey products and others; and (v) Ally with strategic third parties in the distribution of juices. Alqueria has a vast distribution network of +160,000 points of sale.
location_description: Alqueria is headquartered in Cajica, Cundinamarca. The Company has production facilities in several regions across Colombia.
development_impact: Farmer reach & Rural Development: By investing in Alqueria IFC will be supporting 13,000 farmers, most of them in rural areas where poverty levels are higher than in urban areas. Supporting rural development through income generating opportunities is key for the GoC post-conflict agenda. In addition, as a consequence of the project the Company will increase its sourcing of fresh milk benefitting thousand of small farmers in frontier regions of Colombia such as the Orinoquia and costal regions. Forward linkages development: Alqueria distributes its products through a vast network of distributors, including 160,000 mom & pop shops across the Colombian geography. These shops will benefit by an increased products offer such as fruit juices, yogurt, almond beverages, whey and eventually cheese. Food security: Alqueria is the third largest dairy producer in Colombia. The Company processes up to1.2 million Liters of fresh milk per day and produces up to 32 MT of several different products ranging from whole milk to dairy value-added products such as yogurt, flavored milk, whey-based products, in addition the Company produces other drinks such as orange juice and almond based beverages. Alqueria's products reach a great percentage of the Colombian population daily, including infants, children, adults and the elderly. Food safety: Alqueria produces with the highest standards of quality. All of its products comply with public and private food safety standards. Alqueria's most important dairy plants have been awarded with the Chicago based certification of Quality Check'd. The latter is awarded only to those dairy companies that produce with the highest environmental, social and food safety practices.
additionality: Branding: IFC's presence as a shareholder will allow the Company to access new sources of financing, including strategic institutional investors who are actively looking for potential acquisitions in the dairy sector. Equity financing: While the Company enjoys easy access to debt financing this is not the case of equity, since there are no sources of equity financing in Colombia, except for some Investment Funds that target SMEs rather than large companies. The IFC equity contribution will strengthen the Company's capital structure by reducing existing expensive debt, at the same time will support the Company's expansion in the next 5 years. Corporate Governance: By having a seat in the Board, IFC will have the opportunity to support the implementation of good CG practices, so far the Company has been managed mainly by Mr. Carlos Enrique Cavelier but he has expressed his desire for a further professionalization of the Management and the Board.

sector: Paper Packaging Products (Including Boxes, Cartons, etc.)
project_description: The proposed loan of up to EUR 9 million to Polykrome SA (the “Company”) is to support the Company’s investment program, and includes: (i) relocating Polykrome’s existing production facility to a new industrial site; (ii) purchasing additional machinery to expand its product offering; and (iii) working capital requirements (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Polykrome’s main shareholders include Mr. Walid Attieh, Mr. Karim Attieh, and Mr. Hassan Fares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at EUR10.5 million. IFC’s proposed financing is an A loan of up to EUR5.0 million for IFC’s own account and a syndicated loan of up to EUR4.0 million.
location_description: Polykrome is located in Dakar, Senegal, and will be relocating its production facilities to Sebikotane, 45 km from Dakar.
development_impact: The project impacts are centered around: - Improving the company's operational practices and production efficiencies. - Building up the domestic manufacturing sector in Senegal. In addition, the proposed investment has the potential to generate market impacts by stimulating competitiveness of the domestic manufacturing industry and promoting sustainability by obtaining the first Green Building Certification with IFC's support.
additionality: - Provide industry expertise and knowledge sharing - Provide suitable long term funding needed to support the expansion - Provide guidance on Environmental, Social and Health and Safety standards

project_description: Founded and headquartered in Guangdong since 1998, Guangdong Haid Group Co., Ltd (“Haid”) is one of China’s leading animal and aqua feed producers, with sales of US$4 billion and a market capitalization of US$3.7 billion. The Project is to expand Haid’s overseas aqua feed operations in the developing countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Haid, the Sponsor, is a public company listed on China's Shenzhen Stock Exchange (ticker: 002311.SZ). The general public owns 42% in Haid. The remaining shares are owned by Guangzhou Haihao Investment Co. Mr. XUE Hua, the Chairman, owns 22.88% in Haid through this investment entity.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is estimated to cost US$103 million. The IFC proposed investment consists of an A Loan of up to US$50 million.
location_description: Vietnam, India and potentially other developing countries
development_impact: (i) Spur Regional Economic Growth through a South-South Investment: Haid's cross-border investments in Vietnam, India and potentially other emerging markets will help to stimulate regional integration, job creation, and economic development through upstream and downstream linkages. (ii) Improve Farmer Incomes: Aqua feed and fingerlings supplied by Haid to independent shrimp and fish farmers have been shown to generate better feed conversion ratios than those from other suppliers. The use of these inputs and the accompanying technical services from Haid will enhance the supply chain efficiencies and lower inputs costs for farmers, thus contributing to improved farmer incomes. (iii) Support Climate Change Agenda: The Project will also contribute to the development of Climate Smart Agriculture and climate change adaptation through better efficiencies, reduced waste, and lower fish and shrimp mortality. These all jointly result in a smaller environmental footprint of aquaculture and higher water quality in the ponds, which is especially relevant in markets experiencing a strain on the environment. (iv) Food Safety: Haid will adopt best food safety practices in the new markets, in line with its current operations that are subject to several Quality Assurance systems (such as ISO22000, BAP, Global GAP and HACCP). These certifications not only mitigate risks but give the Company a competitive advantage.
additionality: (i) Long Term Financing: IFC is providing a long-term loan that is not readily available in the markets into which Haid is expanding. With a tenor of 7 years, this will be the longest term financing obtained by Haid so far. (ii) Springboard to Emerging Markets: Haid will leverage IFC's rich investment experience and country presence in new markets to mitigate its entry risk.

project_description: IFC is considering to provide an A Loan of up to EUR10 million to part-finance the investment plan of Subati Group (“Subati” or the “Company”) aimed at expanding and diversifying its high quality rose exports. Subati is undertaking a three-year Project (2016-2018) of US$19.5 million in Kenya comprised of (i) upgrade of existing 80ha rose farms; (ii) development of 15ha new rose farm; and (iii) scale up of fresh herb farm to 40ha with a cold storage facility, water treatment plant, and solar panels.
sponsor_shareholders: Subati, founded in 2007, is a family-run grower and exporter of roses with three production farms based in Kenya. The Company grows ca. 120 different varieties of high-end “spray” and “single head roses” and fully supplies its production (55 million stems a year) to the direct market (wholesalers and florist chains; no supply to flower auction markets). Subati is fully owned by the Chandaria and Patel families.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is US$19.5mn for 2016-2018. IFC investment is up to EUR10 million of straight senior A Loan.
location_description: Kenya (Naivasha, Subukia, Kibwezi)
development_impact: Project Impacts - Stakeholder Impact: In order to support the employees and their communities, which predominantly rely on subsistence agriculture, Subati provides housing and access roads to link its workers to the farms and cold storage facilities. - Direct employment: Greenhouse production and subsequent preparation of flowers for export are very labor intensive operations, requiring 2,000 employees currently and increasing by about 700 as a result of the project. - Value added, and return to the economy: Better operational efficiencies, climate smart solutions and expansion of both rose and herb farms will help the company to diversify into different crops and enhance the company's competitiveness.
