The expansion of sustainable flower production and the development of the new export-oriented herb sector will contribute to broader private sector competitiveness in Kenya, help to diversify the economy, and generate valuable foreign currency revenues. - Environmental & social impact: Given the environmental and social sensitivities related to flower production in Kenya, especially in the area of Lake Naivasha, the bar for the sustainability of any new investments is very high. IFC anticipates the project will be developed in line with best international practices, especially with regard to water management to maximize resource use efficiency. A new water treatment plant will be financed by the project at the herb farm. The project will contribute to the climate change agenda by financing solar panels and a cold storage facility for herbs, reducing GHG emissions and crop losses. Market Impact - The project has the potential to enable the development of herb markets in Kenya by further confirming the country's competitiveness in this space and the natural complementarities with the flower production.
additionality: (1) Knowledge and innovation - The Project represents a unique opportunity to leverage IFC's expertise to improve the Company's operation: (i) Technical expertise, global knowledge of the industry and markets as well as lessons learned from other horticulture projects; (ii) Climate smart production: value added from IFC's energy & resource team as the Company plans to improve energy efficiency (2) Standard setting - IFC will collaborate with the Company to mitigate any deficiencies in these areas: (i) Water management and (ii) Food safety (3) Financial risk mitigation - IFC will provide a long-term financing at an affordable rate in a country where long-term financing is scarce and expensive.

company_name: Suzhou Jiahe Foods Industry Co., Ltd.
project_description: Suzhou Jiahe Foods Industry Co Ltd. (“Jiahe” or the “Company”) is China’s leading manufacturer of non-dairy creamer (NDC) – a key ingredient in packaged beverages, fresh bakery products and processed food. The Company is planning to invest to: (i) upgrade its NDC production lines for capacity expansion; (ii) construct a new R&D center; (iii) set up a beverage mixture production line; (iv) build a freeze-dry coffee facility and (iii) add a modern warehouse (together, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is 100% owned by Mr. Liu, together with his wife (Ms. Tang Zhengqing) and sister-in-law (Ms. Tang Zhengming).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a US$25 million equity investment in Jiahe. The total project cost is estimated at US$82 million.
location_description: Jiahe is located in Suzhou, Jiangsu province.
development_impact: 1. Access to quality food ingredient: By supporting a quality-focused NDC producer, IFC will help Jiahe to set an example for the rest of the sector, and raise the country's overall food safety standards; consumers will benefit from having access to safe and affordable alternative to milk in processed food and beverages. 2. Direct Job creation: The Project is expected to create about 250 direct jobs. The use of quality ingredients by hundreds of SMEs (bakeries and other food companies) will help strengthen their operations and market position.
additionality: 1.Stamp of Approval: IFC's engagement as the first external investor in the Company in the run-up to IPO will provide comfort to new investors. 2.Support in South-South expansion: IFC will be a valuable partner to Jiahe as it embarks on its international expansion. IFC is well-positioned to help build relationships and share its global expertise and sector knowledge by connecting Jiahe to IFC's clients in coffee production in Vietnam and Columbia, coconut processing in the Philippines, etc.
Company Name: Suzhou Jiahe Foods Industry Co., Ltd.

project_description: Almarai Company (Almarai or the Company), headquartered in Riyadh and founded in 1977, is one of the region’s leading food and beverage companies. The proposed loan will fund Almarai’s contributions to support the expansions of its joint-venture operation in Egypt which includes setting up of a new juice factory and expansion of its existing dairy facilities (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Almarai is listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange since 2005. The current biggest shareholders of Almarai are Savola Group at 36.5 percent and HH Prince Sultan bin Mohammed bin Saud Al Kabeer at 23.7 percent. About 36.3 percent of the Company’s shares are freely floated as of March 30, 2017.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The investment program is expected to be financed by IFC, local debt and internal cash generations from the operations in Egypt. The proposed investment is up to $150 million in the form of an A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project site will be in Egypt in Beheira Governorate as Almarai plans to strengthen its existing operational base in the country.
development_impact: The main development impacts of the Project in Egypt include: (i) creating direct and indirect employment; (ii) supporting a large number of small and medium enterprises along the primary supply chain; and (iii) enhancing food safety given Almarai's focus on product quality.
additionality: IFC's investment will help (i) address the long-term funding needs otherwise not widely available; (ii) share best practice E&S standards to enhance sustainability and energy efficiency in production in Egypt; and (iii) build a long-term partnership with Almarai for potential investments in frontier markets across the Middle East and North Africa region.

project_description: The proposed Project consists of providing an IFC A Loan of up to EUR60 million and a parallel loan of up to EUR45 million, mobilized by IFC, to support the expansion of Hyprop Investments Limited (South Africa) and PDI Investments Limited (Mauritius), into Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) following their acquisition of three operating shopping malls in Belgrade, Serbia; Podgorica, Montenegro; and Skopje, FYR Macedonia. The proposed investments shall be used to refinance existing debt of the mall entities and therefore provide a more sustainable capital structure, and to finance the upgrade and/or expansion of the malls. The malls are each owned by locally incorporated private companies that are 100% subsidiaries of Hystead Limited, UK ("Hystead" or the "Company”).
sponsor_shareholders: Hystead is a UK based asset management company which is jointly owned by Hyprop Investments Limited ("Hyprop") (60%) and PDI Investment Holdings ("PDI") (40%) and established for their expansion/diversification into CEE. Hyprop Investments Limited is a leading South African REIT specialized in shopping centres and listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange with a market capitalization of EUR 1.8 billion. PDI Investments Limited is a Mauritius-registered investment company, which is majority owned by Louis Norval, an independent non-executive director of Hyprop.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the Project is EUR327.9 million. IFC is proposing to provide an A Loan of up to EUR60 million and mobilize a Parallel Loan of up to EUR45 million through the managed co-lending portfolio program (“MCPP”).
location_description: The Project assets (shopping malls) are in (i) Belgrade, Serbia, (ii) Podgorica, Montenegro and (iii) Skopje, FYR Macedonia.
development_impact: - Improved overall standards and setting standards: The Project is also contributing to the overall improvement of quality standards in Serbia, Montenegro and Macedonia, through meeting IFC's E&S standards, including an international life and fire safety (LFS) standard and is expected to demonstrate and transfer knowledge on best practices to other operators in each market. - Green building certification: The malls will adopt international green building standards, which is expected to contribute to improvements in water and energy efficiency for the facilities in Serbia, Montenegro and Macedonia. - Skills Transfer: The Company will implement a training program through its management team, building on its existing operations and training program in South Africa, and by setting up cooperation with local educational institutions to support their newly developing CEE operations.
additionality: - Mobilization and co-investment support: IFC's role as a lender to the Borrowers is providing and mobilizing funding and following this, in the near future, will help Hystead be better able to mobilize additional funding from the capital market from investors in or outside CEE. - Sustainability practices: i. Green buildings: IFC is providing technical knowledge and advice to the Borrowers on cost efficient improvements that will lead to the malls achieving green building standards. ii. Environmental & Social aspects: IFC is providing technical knowledge and advice to support the Borrowers towards enhancing their E&S practices and ensuring that the Project meets IFC's E&S standards.

project_description: The proposed project involves IFC investing an INR equivalent of approximately US$50 million in a combination of instruments in one or more Special Purpose Vehicles (“SPV”) promoted by Mahindra Lifespace Developers Limited (“MLDL” or the “Company” or the “Sponsor”) set up for the development of three industrial clusters (ICs) around established industrial areas in Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: MLDL is a part of the Mahindra Group. The Group's operations span across 10 sectors with presence in 100+ countries. MLDL is listed on the Bombay and National Stock Exchanges in India with Mahindra & Mahindra having approximately 51% shareholding (as of March 2017). Established in 1994, MLDL is a leading real estate development company in India. The Company operates in three diversified business verticals: (i) residential developments; (ii) affordable housing; and (iii) large-format integrated cities and industrial clusters. The Company is present in multiple city-clusters across India. MLDL has a footprint of over 1.31 million sq.m. (14.06 million sq. ft.) of completed projects and 0.81 million sq. m. (8.7 million sq. ft.) ongoing and forthcoming residential projects. MLDL also pioneered the concept of integrated cities in India with their Mahindra World City developments in Chennai and Jaipur. These developments span over 4,000 acres and house over 130 reputed global and Indian companies and serve to drive economic growth and community development. MLDL is a one of the leaders in sustainable urbanization and was ranked 28th amongst the ‘Top 100 companies in Asia' in the 2016 Channel News Asia Sustainability ranking.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$210 million, of which IFC will invest an INR equivalent of US$50 million in a combination of instruments, with an equal investment from MLDL in a combination of instruments and assets.
location_description: The Project is to be located in the states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra.
development_impact: The proposed project is expected to generate strong development impact along several channels. Part of the area to be developed is located in the low income state of Rajasthan, impacting the development of a region in need. In the other two states, the project is located in areas that have potential for greater large-scale industrial infrastructure creation. a) Development of quality industrial infrastructure: (i) For small and medium businesses: The project is expected to increase availability of critical industrial infrastructure, directly benefitting small and mid-sized businesses that do not have the resources to set it up themselves. (ii) For large businesses: By providing a plug-and-play ecosystem, the Project is expected to reduce the time for companies to go-to-market and enable them to instead focus on core business operations. b) Demonstration effect: Private industrial parks are a relatively new asset class in India, and the project is expected to generate a positive demonstration effect and promote the development of such spaces in the country. c) Exporting capacity: The Project is expected to expand India's exporting capacity through the development of a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in Rajasthan; d) Employment: The Project is expected to contribute significantly to job creation. During the construction phase, the Project is expected to generate temporary jobs in the construction sector, and a significant number of indirect jobs in suppliers' industries for construction materials. The project is expected to also create permanent jobs in the form of outsourced labor for services such as housekeeping, security, landscaping, maintenance, etc. during the ICs operations, as well as jobs through the businesses using the space developed in the IC. e) Community development: The Project is also expected to positively impact local communities and seek to promote inclusive development through various activities such as vocational skill training, self-help groups for women etc.
additionality: IFC's primary additionality is the provision of long-term capital for the development of industrial parks in India. With IFC's investment, MLDL can leverage its investment to develop a larger area than it would be able to on its own. Further, once the Project is underway, there is potential to mobilize capital from a larger set of long-term investors to scale up the business and thereby accelerate growth in these regions. IFC has collaborated with MLDL on carbon pricing and on green residential development. The Project would be the next step in IFC's strategic partnership with the Sponsor for climate change. In continuation with this engagement, IFC will explore working with MLDL along with the occupants of these industrial parks for the adoption of renewable energy under its Eco-Assist program.

company_name: GUANGXI FENGLIN WOOD INDUSTRY GROUP CO., LTD.
sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: Guangxi Fenglin Wood Industry Group Co., Ltd. (“Fenglin” or the “Company”), an IFC existing client, is planning to decommission an existing medium-density fiberboard (MDF) plant and construct a new particle board plant in Nanning, Guangxi (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Fenglin was listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (Stock Code: 601996) on September 29, 2011. It is headquartered in Nanning, and has operations in Guangxi and Guangdong Provinces. The Project Sponsor is Mr. Yichuan Liu, the founder and the key shareholder of the Company. The Company is 47.9% owned by Fenglin International Limited, with the rest by small shareholders and public.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated to be around US$80 million including capital expenditure and working capital requirements. The proposed IFC investment is up to US$40 million in A Loan. The remaining will be funded by internally generated cash from operations.
location_description: The Project will be located at Nanning, Guangxi Autonomous Region, a frontier region in China.
development_impact: (1) Private sector development: Continued investments from IFC in successful and scalable companies like Fenglin contribute to the development and consolidation of fragmented forestry and wood panel industries in China, particularly in Guangxi Province, a frontier region where the local economy depends heavily on the industry. Fenglin would continue adopting good practices and high standards for its business practices, such as implementing a laser measuring system for scrap woods delivered to its gate, which allows a more objective and prompt way to compensate its suppliers; introducing higher value-added and innovative products to the market using its in-house R&D work; and adopting international standards and systems in its operations, thereby setting a demonstration effect for the industry as a whole. (2) Farmers' reach and local economy: The Project would procure at least around 363,000 tons of scrap wood per year directly and indirectly from local forestry farmers in Guangxi Province. This helps to stimulate economic activity among local forestry households, create additional income for them and directly improve their livelihoods. In addition, the Project will procure about 90% more chemicals, such as formaldehyde and urea from local SME suppliers, providing them with more business opportunities. (3) Environmental impact: The Project would help to raise the industry environmental standards in China through the use of advanced technologies for particle board production including a new air emission system. The new plant would have capability to produce boards with formaldehyde free adhesive on a large scale and continuous basis when the market demands such products, which is currently rare in the industry in China. The Project would also help productively utilize scrap wood that would otherwise be burnt for cooking, thus reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The Project is a sustainable solution to resolving the issues of diminishing wood supply and scrap wood waste, and creates a positive impact on the local forestry industry. The Company's commitment to the highest national and international environmental standards sets an example for the industry.
additionality: (1) Long-term partnership: IFC has been a consistent supporter of Fenglin through two rounds of investments in the past 12 years. IFC will continue to support a competitive and standard-setting client investing in a frontier region in China. (2) Long-term financing: IFC would provide long-term funding in USD that is not readily available to Fenglin and matches with the needs of the Project to improve the Company's production facilities. (3) Global knowledge: IFC can provide assistance to the Company in exploring overseas and/or South-South expansion opportunities in the next stage of the Company's growth by introducing other clients in such markets.
Company Name: GUANGXI FENGLIN WOOD INDUSTRY GROUP CO., LTD.

project_description: Founded in 2013, Chaldal is the leading online grocery supplier in Bangladesh. The Company is raising finance to support its continued growth .
sponsor_shareholders: Chaldal was founded in 2013 by Waseem Alim, Tejas Viswanath and Zia Ashraf. It has raised two rounds of seed financing from angel investors and early stage VC funds.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes an equity investment of US$2-3 million as part of a US$4-6 million Series A round .
location_description: Chaldal has its registered office in Dhaka. It currently has 5 warehouses spread around the city.
development_impact: The expected development impact of the project includes: i) demonstrating the viability of venture investing in Bangladesh, which is expected to have a catalytic effect on the broader venture ecosystem in Bangladesh ii) contributing to the company's financial sustainability and growth iii) job creation in warehousing and logistics.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality includes: i) provision of long term early stage equity financing which is not available locally; ii) facilitating the participation of co-investors who take comfort in IFC's experience in similar investments globally.

project_description: Wadi Holdings Company (SAE) and its subsidiaries (“Wadi” or the “Company”) is a leading vertically integrated agri-food group in Egypt with operations in poultry (broiler day old parents, broiler and layer day old chicks), poultry feed (including soy bean crushing), food (olives, olive oil, and other packaged foods), and food retail and logistics (including port operations). Established in Egypt in 1984 with a small-scale poultry operation, Wadi today operates 12 subsidiaries with ten brands over three distinct sectors: Dawagen (poultry), Sina'at (industries) and Mazareh (farms). Fifty Four Holding is a Lebanese holding company that was established to be the raw materials trading arm for Wadi, and to eventually hold all of Wadi’s offshore operations. It has an identical ownership structure to that of Wadi. IFC’s investment is a corporate A loan in the amount of USD22 million to Wadi and Fifty Four Holding. The proposed Project consists of (i) the establishment of new poultry grandparent and parent breeder sites in Toushka in southern Egypt, to increase capacity in line with Wadi’s growing poultry market position in Egypt, and to improve bio-security measures for the flocks. Wadi will also relocate its existing farms to the new farms in Toushka; (ii) expanding Wadi’s growers’ hypermarket concept and relocating Wadi’s food processing plant from Sadat City to a new, larger plant in KM54 on the Cairo-Alexandria Desert Road; (iii) refinancing some of Wadi’s short term local-currency debt; and (iv) restructuring the corporate organization of Wadi and Fifty Four Holding, and clearing some of the inter-company debt.
sponsor_shareholders: Wadi is majority-owned by members of the Freiji and Nasrallah families (89%, which are also the project sponsors) while the remaining 11% is owned by institutional shareholders, namely the Horus Food and Agribusiness Fund, and the EuroMena Fund.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$31 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to US$22 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The poultry grandparent and parent project will be located in Toushka, in the south of Egypt, on a total land area of 4,800 acres (undeveloped desert land). The Wadi food complex in KM54 is on land already owned and developed by Wadi, and where Wadi’s current grandparent farms, olive orchards and olive oil press are located.
development_impact: IFC's investment is expected to: - Support a local producer to expand its exports which will contribute positively to generation of foreign currency in Egypt. Wadi currently exports fruits, vegetables, packaged foods and cell pads (industrial cooling solutions), and has recently starting exporting large animal feed, mainly to Jordan and GCC countries. Furthermore, Wadi produces soy bean meal and mono-calcium phosphate (MCP) locally, which would otherwise need to be imported (Wadi is the only producer of MCP in Egypt). - Increase farmer and SME reach. The Company purchases olives, vegetables, and other agricultural products from more than 70 local farms. Wadi also currently reaches more than 1,500 small farmers through sales of its day-old chicks and poultry feed. As it enters new product markets, Wadi will grow its reach to additional farmers and value chains, increasing its economic reach through distributors and suppliers. - Create direct and indirect jobs, by making the Company's funding sources more sustainable. Wadi currently has more than 3,000 employees.
additionality: - Long term USD financing: IFC will support a long-standing client to restructure its balance sheet and make the company more sustainable. The proposed loan will support Wadi's permanent working capital needs with long term, USD-denominated financing at reasonable interest rates, which is not currently available in Egypt. - Technical assistance support: IFC is currently in early discussions with Wadi on potential energy and water efficiency technical assistance intervention. - Long-term partnership: This investment, the fourth with Wadi, will strengthen an existing relationship with a leading and reputable regional agribusiness company. The investment will allow IFC to help with the Company's current and future corporate initiatives, such as validating its corporate governance practices and facilitating access for Wadi to raise capital through a planned IPO in the medium term.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment includes an A loan up to US$100 million (to be disbursed either in TRY or US$) to Turkiye Petrol Rafinerileri A.S. (“Tupras” or the “Company”), an existing oil refining company, for the financing of (i) the Company's research and development expenditure during 2017-2019 period, (ii) the new sulphur recovery units (the "SRUs") to be constructed in Izmit, Izmir and Kirikkale refineries, and (iii) the capacity increase of the continuous catalyst regeneration (the "CCR") platformer in Izmir refinery (the "Project").
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsor is Tupras, a local oil refining company, with 28.1 million tons annual crude oil processing capacity and four refineries (Izmit, Izmir, Kirikkale and Batman) located in Turkey. Tupras is currently the sole operational refining company in the country. Tupras was a state owned enterprise and was privatized in 2006. Currently, 49% of the Company's shares is publicly listed, while the remaining 51% is owned by Enerji Yatirimlari A.S., which is a Koc Holding A.S entity. Koc Holding A.S. is the largest conglomerate in Turkey and operates in four core business sectors: energy, automotive, consumer durables and finance.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is expected to be US$278 million. The Project will be financed by a combination of (i)IFC A loan up to US$100 million (to be disbursed either in TRY or US$) and; (ii) internal cash generation or other external financing.
location_description: The Project sites include the Company's existing refineries in Izmit, Izmir and Kirikkale. All the refineries are located in industrial areas.
development_impact: The expected development impact of the Project includes (i) supporting energy security of the country, (ii) improving the Company's resource efficiency, (iii) supporting the Company's R&D activities and, (iv) contributing to the enhancement of the Company's financial performance and sustainability
additionality: IFC's expected additionality includes (i) providing a long-term dual currency funding to Tupras in a volatile market environment, and (ii) helping Tupras improve its E&S practices.

project_description: As part of its strategic focus on mobilizing third party capital for infrastructure investment in emerging markets, IFC is proposing to support the development of an infrastructure debt platform (the “vehicle”) that will invest in senior loans in infrastructure projects alongside IFC. IFC will provide support to the vehicle in the form of an unfunded portfolio guarantee, which will enable third party investors to consider this asset class. In addition to providing the unfunded portfolio guarantee, IFC will contract with the vehicle to provide co-investments using IFC’s Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP). Under MCPP IFC creates loan portfolios for third party investors based on pre-agreed eligibility criteria. All investments made by the vehicle will be in IFC originated senior loans on the same terms and conditions as with IFC’s investment for its own account. All underlying loans will need to meet IFC’s own internal standards and IFC will be required to seek independent Board approval for each loan following its standard approval process. It is only upon IFC’s commitment for its own account that a portion of the loans would then be allocated to the vehicle.
sponsor_shareholders: IFC is currently contemplating providing an unfunded portfolio guarantee to the vehicle which it is contemplated will fund itself through issue of debt securities to certain insurance companies in the AXA group. The vehicle will become an MCPP investor and as such all investment origination and supervision will be conducted by IFC under the Managed Co-lending Portfolio Program.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: An IFC Unfunded Portfolio Guarantee of up to $50m is being contemplated with the intention of mobilizing up to $500m of private sector third party capital, in addition to IFC’s investments for its own account alongside the vehicle. The transaction will contribute to the demonstration model of debt mobilization vehicles participating in IFC’s MCPP program that will allow for further replication of the MCPP model and further mobilization from institutional investors. IFC’s investment will be structured as an unfunded portfolio guarantee to the investor in the vehicle.
location_description: The vehicle will be formed under the law of one of IFC member countries, and compliant with IFC’s policies on investing in third party vehicles.
development_impact: 1. Given that the vehicle will co - invest with IFC (on the same terms and conditions) the proposed investment will support private sector development by increasing access to long term debt capital for infrastructure projects across emerging markets from an asset pool (i.e. institutional investors located in OECD countries) that has yet to venture in significant scale into infrastructure investments in emerging markets. 2. Under MCPP investors approve funding in projects much earlier than traditional co-lenders, providing IFC's clients with greater certainty of finance and reducing their transaction costs during the project development phase, allowing for a faster process to financial close. 3. The vehicle is directly leveraging IFC's own economic capital allowing IFC to participate in larger transactions.
additionality: 1. Standard setting: The vehicle is being specifically designed to facilitate institutional investor participation into emerging market infrastructure lending creating a model that can be replicated to significantly scale mobilization from investors such as insurance companies. 2. Sustainable Investment: Under MCPP IFC originates and assesses each individual loan. As such IFC is able to support good social and environmental performance through the application of its performance standards.

sector: Fruit and Vegetable Preservation or Processing (Canning, Freezing, Drying, Jams, etc.)
project_description: The proposed investment consists of a Eur6.5 million senior secured loan to Centre d’Etude et de Développement Industriel et Agricole du Mali SA (“Cediam” or the “Company”), a multi-fruit processing company, operating in Yanfolila (southern Mali), established in 2011 and operating since 2012. Cediam sources mangoes from 2,000 smallholders for export as fresh mangoes as well as to produce mango concentrate and puree packed in drums and exported mainly to Europe and the Middle East, via Montecarlofruit, a Montecarlo-based company specialized in the distribution of fruits as well as products such as puree, concentrates and juices. The proposed financing may also be made available under the private sector window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (“GAFSP”), a multilateral mechanism launched by the G20 with the purpose of scaling-up support to help less developed countries alleviate poverty and improve food security, a program implemented by IFC. The investment will help support the company’s expansion plan, which entails: (i) development of a 234 ha land parcel, under acquisition in the Yanfolila region, to produce its own mangoes, tomatoes and passion fruit; (ii) expansion of the storage warehouse at the existing processing facility in Yanfolila and construction of a fresh mango sorting and packing platform; (iii) acquisition of vehicles to expand the transportation fleet; and (iv) installation of a pouch-filling line for tomato concentrate targeting Mali and neighboring countries. This investment would help support Cediam’s vertical integration and diversification projects, aimed at securing fruit supply as well as diversifying its business through products that would ensure year-round operation of the company’s existing processing facility rather than limiting operations to mango processing only for 4 months of the year (April to July). As part of a future expansion project, Cediam plans to install a fruit juice production line using the company’s mango puree. However, this does not fall within the scope of IFC’s proposed investment.
sponsor_shareholders: Cediam is majority owned by Roberto Ballabeni, through its holding company SCI MCF-SMS Group. M. Ballabeni is an Italian investor who has more than 20 years of experience in the food sector and owns other companies in the food distribution sector in Europe such as SMS SAM (specialized in the sale of fresh Italian food products to large supermarket chains in France and to other European players). The second largest shareholder is Diadie Sankare, who is a well-known Malian entrepreneur, owning and managing several companies in West Africa including SAER, a major human resources company active in the West Africa Region. The remaining shares are owned by Andrea Soave, CEO of Cediam who has more than 20 years of experience as Project Manager.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, with GAFSP support, will provide a Eur6.5 million financing package in the form of a senior secured loan to partially finance the Eur13 million Cediam’s investment program.
location_description: Cediam’s project is located in the Sikasso region, southern Mali. Cediam’s processing plant is located in the commune of Wassoulou Ballé (Yanfolila circle) and the 235 ha plantation is located in the commune of Faragouaran (Bougouni circle, 15 km east of CEDIAM’s already existing processing plant). The proposed plantation site is located between the village of Mafèlè (5 km to the north), the hamlet of Soulawoulé Fara (800 meters to the north), the village of Sanakoroba (3 km to the east) and the village of Djièguènina (3 km to the south).
development_impact: The project will (i) increase income of farmers involved in mango production by linking them to market and improving support services, (ii) help the creation of additional employment, (iii) contribute to the industrialization of Mali, which has one of the lowest industrialization rate in the Africa sub-region.
additionality: (i) provide long term financing that is not currently available in this fragile country environment; (ii) have a catalytic role and build confidence for foreign investors; (iii) guide the Company to enhance its E&S practices to improve long term sustainability and to achieve compliance with IFC performance standards; (iv) bring IDA support to address external constraints hampering the development of the mango sector.

project_description: The proposed investment in Yapi Merkezi Holding A.S. (“Yapi Merkezi,” “YMH,” the "Company," or the “Borrower”) consists of an IFC A Loan of up to US$75 million and an IFC B Loan or Parallel Loan of up to US$25 million for a working capital loan to the Borrower (the “Revolving Credit Facility,” “RCF,” or the “Facility”). The Facility will be in the form of a US$50 million Dollar tranche and a US$50 million-equivalent Euro tranche. The RCF will be used towards the working capital needs of YMH’s 99.9%-owned subsidiary, Yapi Merkezi Construction and Industry Inc (“YMI”). YMI is one of the leading construction companies in Turkey operating in rail-systems. YMI also has interests in concession businesses including Eurasia Tunnel, and Dardanelles Bridge projects. The Facility will support YMI as YMI expands its construction activity in Africa, the Middle East, and Turkey (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsor is Yapi Merkezi, which is privately owned by the Arioglu, Anadol and Aykar families. The construction and concession businesses are the main business lines of the Company. YMI is one of the leading construction companies in the field of transportation specializing in constructing rail systems including tunnels and bridges. YMI has operations in eight different countries including Ethiopia, Tanzania and Turkey .
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is expected to be US$100 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$75 million A Loan for IFC’s own account and US$25 million of IFC B Loan or a Parallel Loan.
location_description: The proposed investment is planned to be used for working capital purposes for the existing projects in Algeria, Ethiopia, Morocco, Saudi Arabia , Tanzania, Turkey and new business opportunities.
development_impact: The expected development impact of the Project includes (i) help improve infrastructure, especially those of the rail-based transport networks in Middle East, Sub-Saharan Africa and North Africa and Turkey, (ii) create substantial employment opportunities since construction sector is one of the largest employment generators through contractors and sub-contractors, (iii) stimulate industries in the supply chain including building materials and logistics.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality includes (i) providing a tailor-made working capital facility, the tenor and amount of which are not readily available in most of the markets, in which YMH is active; and (ii) support to a successful construction company to expand simultaneously into African and Middle Eastern markets by supporting the client's financing needs, and providing local market know-how.

company_name: Operadora y Procesadora de Productos Marinos Omarsa S.A.
project_description: The project will expand and upgrade operations of Operadora and Procesadora de Productos Marinos, Omarsa S.A. ("Omarsa" or "the Company"), one of the leading integrated shrimp producers and processors in Ecuador. The Project involves the construction and development of the "Las Brisas" plant in the locality of Duran, in the Guayas province in Ecuador.
sponsor_shareholders: Omarsa's majority shareholders and Project sponsors are the Vanoni family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Total Project cost is estimated at US$13 million. The proposed financing is a US$8m A loan for IFC's own account.
location_description: All Omarsa's operations are located in the Guayas province in Ecuador. The processing facility is located in Duran whereas the three farm facilities are located in Guayaquil.
development_impact: Export-oriented sector development. The Project will contribute to the development of a competitive export oriented sector with extensive linkages throughout the value chain that is key for Ecuador's economy. Private sector development. IFC's funding will support further professionalization of a family-owned business as it grows into one of the sector's regional leaders. Job creation. Omarsa currently employs about 2,950 people. The expansion will create significant direct and indirect employment opportunities. Access to health. As a result of the Project, more families will have access to health support provided by the Company. Tax generation. The Project will increase tax generation for the government.
additionality: Stamp of approval. IFC's involvement will enhance the profile of a medium-sized family owned company and allow it to further capitalize on its recent first Aquaculture Stewardship Council-certified shrimp company status. Long-term financing. IFC will provide tailer-made long-term financing that is not readily available locally in competitive terms. E&S standards setting. IFC will support Omarsa to further improve its environmental and social standards
Company Name: Operadora y Procesadora de Productos Marinos Omarsa S.A.

project_description: The proposed project (“Aanandi: Riverview”) is the construction completion of a seven-storey residential building located in Vientiane, Lao PDR. The property is located approximately six kilometers from the main town center within close proximity to many of the embassy buildings, set back one street from the Mekong River. The building will house 76 units covering a gross floor area of approximately 6,500 m 2 . Construction of the building is expected to be completed by the end of 2019 with the developer also managing the rental operations, targeted to commence at the start of 2020.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project’s sponsor is Aanandi Group Pte. Ltd, a newly established property development company formed by bringing together the skills of the lead sponsor Sue Ma (12% shareholder), Leslie Glosby (18% shareholder), Thuan Teh (20% shareholder) and Andrew Su (5% shareholder). Sue Ma’s mother, Chou Ma (45% shareholder) is a financial investor into the group. The group’s operating shareholders have construction management, architectural, project management and hospitality expertise over a period of more than 20 years each.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is expected to be US$6.6 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$2.0 million A loan for IFC's own account.
location_description: The greenfield project will be located approximately six kilometers south of the town center of Vientiane, on a vacant 2,600 square meter plot of land. The site is an urban area, with many suburban houses surrounding.
development_impact: (i) Increased quality housing supply to accommodate the business community: this will also counter the impact of rapid urbanization. The project will directly address the need for residential and business infrastructure given the increasing urbanization in the Vientiane area. (ii) Promotion of gender equality: Through the support of a female, ethnic-Lao, lead sponsor returning to her country of birth. (iii) Job creation and upskilling: The project is expected to create jobs both during the construction of the development sites and also post-completion, for the operation of rental management and building maintenance. With a nascent construction development skill set among local developers, this project has capacity to impart significant international standard construction expertise to local construction contractors. (iv) Local linkages: During construction, the project will increase demand for locally sourced labor and building materials in the country and promote inclusive growth through increased SME linkages. (v) Community development: The apartment block built by the project will contribute to urban infrastructure development and surrounding community development. (vi) Demonstration effect: signaling to foreign investors IFC's conviction for investment prospects in Laos, facilitating business accommodation, and encouraging participation in similar projects by local entrepreneurs. (vii) Knowledge transfer: upskilling the local construction workforce through knowledge transfer from an internationally experienced construction and development team.
additionality: (i) Provision of long-term financing: Long-term financing is not available for developers in Laos. IFC will provide a long term debt facility with repayment structure to match the cash flow profile of the project. It is noted that the company has ambitions for larger projects down the line in other regions of Laos, for which they will require further IFC expertise. (ii) Sector expertise: IFC will bring sector knowledge to improve construction and operational standards, provide market strategy and project management expertise. (iii) Environmental & Social and Insurance: IFC will provide guidance to improve and ensure insurance and environmental and social standards are in line with international best practices, including potentially attaining IFC EDGE Green Building certification. This may also extend to the remainder of the pipeline projects.

project_description: “KazFoodProducts” LLP (KFP or the Company), established in 1998, is one of the leading Kazakh food processing companies, operating in grain milling and confectionary sectors. The project aims to support KFP growth through: (i) vertical integration and product diversification in milling and deep processing of wheat (production of gluten, starch, animal feed and fructose syrup), and (ii) expansion of the confectionary business (the “Project”) Update related to additional investment under the COVID-19 response facility (#45257): IFC will provide an A loan of up to US$15 million equivalent in Kazakh Tenge (KZT) to KFP as an allocation under the IFC’s COVID-19 response facility. The IFC Loan will be used for expansion of KFP’s operations and its working capital needs.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is controlled and majority owned by Mr. Yerlan Baimuratov and Balapanov family, each with 43.5%, and Mr. Alikhan Talgatbek with 5%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$55 million. The proposed IFC investment is a loan of up to US$25 million.
location_description: The Project is to be implemented by three subsidiary companies of KazFoodProducts: JSC “Bayan Sulu”, located in Kostanai, JSC “Asia AgroFood”, located in Chemolgan, Almaty region, and LLP “BioOperations”, located in Tainsha village, North Kazakhstan region. All of the abovementioned companies are domiciled in Kazakhstan.
development_impact: - Economic diversification: The Project will contribute to the country's strategic objective of economic diversification, through development of agribusiness sector, where Kazakhstan has significant potential. - Employment creation: The Project will contribute to job creation, including in frontier regions of Kazakhstan, where there are higher poverty rates and limited employment opportunities. - Food security via continuing exports of flour to grain deficit countries of Central Asia (including Tajikistan and Afghanistan). - Domestic value addition: By supporting domestic processing of agricultural commodities into gluten, starch, fructose and packaged food products, the project promotes local value addition, stronger downstream linkages with SMEs, and acquisition of new skills by the local labor force.
additionality: - Provision of long-term financing to support the Company's growth. - IFC will help the Company improve its corporate governance practices. - IFC will provide guidance to the Company to implement international standards in its environmental and social practices.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A/B loan financing package to Jalles Machado S.A. (“Jalles Machado” or the “Company”). Founded in 1980 in the state of Goias, Jalles Machado operates two mills with combined annual crushing capacity of 4.6 million tons of sugarcane and co-generation capacity of 88 MW.
sponsor_shareholders: Jalles Machado is controlled by Grupo Otavio Lage (the “Sponsor”), a company with over 70 years in the agribusiness sector, through its subsidiaries Veracruz Agropecuária Ltda and Planagri S.A., that together have a 50.9% ownership in the Company. The remaining 49.1% is owned primarily by four local families.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of an up to US$54 million A/B loan financing package composed of a US$34 million A Loan and an up to US$20 million B Loan to Jalles Machado. The proceeds of the A/B loan will be used by the Company to carry out its investment program for the 2017/2018 and 2018/2019 harvests. The investment program consists of sugarcane planting capex, expansion of the irrigation system and the implementation of a white sugar processing factory at the Otavio Lage mill.
location_description: Jalles Machado is headquartered in Goianesia, state of Goias, where it operates its two mills.
development_impact: (i) Support the expansion of a globally competitive sector: The investment will support the development of Brazil's sugar and ethanol industry, one of the most important sectors in the Brazilian economy, by helping one of the leading companies to improve efficiencies and upgrade its operations. (ii) Promote climate change mitigation: The project will support climate change mitigation by increasing efficient production of biofuels. Hydrous ethanol made from sugarcane is the most competitive CO2 alternative to gasoline and one of the "greenest" fuels. (iii) Strengthen a frontier region: The Company's operations are located in Goianesia, part of the Cerrado region, where the project will be undertaken. By expanding the company's activities, the project will create about a 100 new jobs and contribute to government revenues in a region that is highly dependent on the agricultural sector for income generation but has lagged behind national averages in terms of development indicators. (iv) Contribute to government revenues: The Brazilian agribusiness sector is highly competitive globally and is key to the economy in terms of its capacity to raise government revenues. This investment will allow the Company to expand its operations and will contribute to the growth of the Brazilian economy.
additionality: (i) Long-term Financing: IFC's involvement will provide the Company with the necessary financing for its capital expenditures which is not otherwise available in the market on comparable terms. (ii) Mobilization: IFC will mobilize additional long-term capital from a commercial bank through the B-Loan program, expanding the Company's access to finance further. (iii) Environmental and Social Standards: By introducing the Performance Standards on Social and Environmental Sustainability, IFC will help Jalles Machado further improve its sustainability practices. (iv) Corporate Governance: IFC will help Jalles Machado strengthen its Corporate Governance policies and practices by implementing the Corporate Governance Improvement Plan.

project_description: IFC together with Google Inc, Convergence Partners and Mitsui & Co., Ltd. (“Mitsui”) start a partnership in CSquared, a broadband infrastructure company focused on building wholesale, carrier-neutral open-access fibre optic networks in Sub-Saharan Africa (the “Project”). The Project will initially involve the development and expansion of the existing operations initiated by Google in Uganda, Ghana. CSquared will then serve as a platform to expand into new markets with additional investments in the Sub-Saharan Africa region in the future. The Project targets to provide key sector players in these markets, such as mobile operators or internet service providers, with access to an essential shared communication infrastructure that would enable them to improve broadband connectivity as well as the quality of services and their affordability. CSquared has operations in Uganda, Ghana and Liberia and is considering new markets, including Togo. To support CSquared expansion into Togo, the Project is expected to be supported by the IDA19 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (PSW BFF), and to support CSquared expansion in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Liberia, the Project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project will be developed as a partnership among IFC, Google Inc., Mitsui & Co., Ltd and Convergence Partners Communication Infrastructure Fund (together the Partners) in the project company to be established for this purpose CSQUARED LINK HOLDINGS (MAURITIUS) LIMITED (the Company or CSquared).CSquared will operate as an independent private company headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya Google is a leading US-based international information technology company founded in 1998. Google's mission is to organize the world's information and make it universally accessible and useful. Through products and platforms like Search, Maps, Gmail, Android, Google Play, Chrome and YouTube, Google plays a meaningful role in the daily lives of billions of people and has become one of the most widely-known companies in the world. Google is a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., which is publicly listed on NASDAQ. Convergence Partners is a Pan-African ICT focused private equity player, delivering enhanced investment returns while underpinning Continental development. Convergence Partners has a proven track record of developing new investment opportunities as well as actively adding value to investments across the lifecycle of ICT assets. As impact investors, Convergence Partners brings its skills, experience and capital to accelerate ICT infrastructure development on the Continent, focusing on initiatives that increase availability of communications, broadband services and new technology offerings to the people of Africa. For more information, visit http://www.convergencepartners.com/ Mitsui is one of the most diversified and comprehensive trading, investment and service enterprises in the world, with 137 offices in 65 countries as of April 2017. Utilizing its global operating locations, network and information resources, it is multilaterally pursuing business that ranges from product sales, worldwide logistics and financing, through to the development of major international infrastructure and other projects in the following fields: Iron & Steel Products, Mineral & Metal Resources, Infrastructure Projects, Integrated Transportation Systems, Chemicals, Energy, Food & Retail Management, Healthcare & Service, Consumer Business, IT &; Communication Business, Corporate Development Business. Mitsui is actively taking on challenges for global business innovation around the world. For more information, visit http://www.mitsui.com/jp/en.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project will initially involve the development and expansion of the existing operations initiated by Google in Uganda, Ghana. During this initial phase, the initial total project cost is estimated at US$66 million, and IFC will provide an initial equity investment of US$15 million CSquared will then serve as a platform to expand into new markets with additional investments in the Sub-Saharan Africa region in the future. Blended Finance IFC as implementing entity of the IDA19 PSW BFF is expected to provide USD 5 million in the form of warrants (“Blended Concessional Finance Co-investment”) convertible into equity. The Blended Concessional Finance Co-investment supports CSquared expansion in Togo and is needed to rebalance the risk-reward for the company’s shareholders who, in light of the high risk of the investment, would not be able to proceed with the expansion in Togo without the Blended Concessional Finance Co-investment. The level of concessionality (i.e., “subsidy”) provided by the Blended Concessional Finance Co-investment is expected to be in the range of 9%-15% of the total Togo project cost of US$23.6 million. This estimate is based on the difference between (i) a “reference rate” (either a market price if available or the price calculated using IFC’s base case projections and (ii) the “concessional rate” being charged by the Blended Concessional Finance Co-investment. In addition, IFC as implementing entity of the IDA20 PSW BFF is expected to provide up to USD5.0 million in the form of equity (“second Blended Concessional Finance Co-investment”). The second Blended Concessional Finance Co-investment is needed to complete CSquared’s funding plan to expand in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Liberia. As the IDA20 PSW BFF investment will be made on the same terms as those of the Company’s common shareholders, no pricing concessionality (i.e., “subsidy”) is provided by the second Blended Concessional Finance Co-investment. Further details and historical information on estimated subsidy levels in IFC’s blended finance portfolio can be found at: www.ifc.org/blendedfinance. As is the case with all of IFC’s blended concessional finance co-investments, this project has been assessed against the Enhanced Blended Concessional Finance Principles for DFI Private Sector Operations adopted by IFC and more than 20 other DFIs in 2017. Further information on these Enhanced Principles and IFC’s blended finance approach and governance can also be found at: www.ifc.org/blendedfinance.
location_description: The Project will initially involve the development of the existing operations in Uganda (mainly in Kampala), Ghana (mainly in Accra). Additionally, the Project has developed operations in Liberia (mainly in Monrovia) and is currently considering expansion in new markets in Africa. CSquared's headquarter will be in Nairobi, Kenya. Additional markets in Sub-Saharan Africa are expected to be determined based on further review and approval by the Partners.
development_impact: (i) Access to Broadband: The Project addresses the growing demand for fiber networks critically needed to support the expansion of broadband services. (ii) Shared infrastructure: As telecom operators are under pressure to expand their networks and improve their level/quality of service, a company like CSquared will be well positioned to provide high quality infrastructure services more efficiently. (iii) Promote economic growth: Improved broadband connectivity directly and indirectly benefits virtually every sector of the economy, creates jobs, fosters innovation and entrepreneurship, promotes social and financial inclusion and improves transparency and efficiency. Broadband access is also expected to help small and medium enterprises to better market their good and services, both locally and internationally.
additionality: (i) Stamp of approval: IFC's brand and global reputation of a vigilant development investor will provide visibility to the Project, while endorsing its commercial viability, particularly, in more challenging markets. (ii) Sector Knowledge & Financial Expertise: The Project Partners will rely on IFC's knowledge of emerging market telecom sector, successful track record of investing in challenging environments as well as innovative financial structuring. (iii) Harmonization of Policy and Regulation: IFC will be able to deploy the expertise of WBG ICT Practice to address potential issues related to regulatory frameworks and telecom sector reform.

project_description: Kaufland, a chain of hypermarkets with primary focus on food retail, is continuing its store expansion across Romania and Bulgaria and plans to open new Kaufland stores in Moldova (the “Project”). The Schwarz Group, owner of Kaufland and one of the leading European food retailers , has requested IFC to provide a long-term loan to partially finance the next two year’s investment plan of Kaufland in Romania, Bulgaria and Moldova (the “Target Countries”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Schwarz Group (the “Group”) ranks among the top five food retail companies globally. Headquartered in Germany, the Group is a privately-held company. The Group is involved in food retail through two brands: Lidl and Kaufland. The Group has presence in basically all western European countries as well as in Central and Eastern Europe. The project companies are Kaufland Romania SCS and Kaufland Bulgaria EOOD & Co. KD, which are wholly owned by the Schwarz Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The next two years of investment in the Target Countries is estimated at €400 million. IFC is proposed to provide an A loan of up to €180 million to partially finance this investment plan.
location_description: Investments under the Project can be made in small and large cities throughout Romania, Bulgaria and Moldova.
development_impact: - Affordable goods: Modern retail distribution introduces efficiencies which enables low pricing at high quality standards. The share of modern retail in food in Romania and Bulgaria is about half that of developed countries and even lower in Moldova. Expansion of organized retail in the Target Countries will promote access to affordable and high quality food products for low to middle income households. - Food safety: Modern retail formats contribute to food safety by improving supply chain efficiencies and reducing food wastage. Local procurements will encourage local producers to apply best practices in their production and operations, thus ensuring quality and safety. - Employment generation: The Project is expected to generate significant direct employment in the new stores, indirect employment in the supply chain as well as temporary employment during construction. Typically, women constitute more than 50% of the direct employment in retail stores. - Green buildings: New stores expansion through the Project is expected to have energy efficiency features and showcase green building best practices, which will potentially have a demonstrational effect on local building standards.
additionality: - Energy efficiency and EDGE certification: Schwarz was very appreciative of IFC's collaboration in energy efficiency which led to EDGE certification of 52 Kaufland stores in Bulgaria in 2015. IFC is expected to extend its work with the client to help Schwarz reach higher standards on energy savings, have Green buildings, and EDGE certify its stores in one or more of the Target Countries; - Food safety advisory: IFC has already provided training to farmers in the Kaufland supply chain in Bulgaria through its food safety program. Schwarz recognizes the improvements this will bring to the quality, reliability and safety of its product assortment. The Group is interested in designing a comprehensive program addressing the Group's challenges within its supply chain. IFC will advocate further capacity building programs to promote sustainable supply chain development in the Target Countries.

company_name: AMERRA LATIN AMERICA FINANCE ONSHORE, LLC
country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: AMERRA Capital Management, LLC, (AMERRA) is an investment manager, focused on providing customized agriculture-focused and commodity-based finance solutions to producers, processors, distributors and traders, mainly in the Americas. AMERRA has over US$1.8 billion in assets under management across several funds and accounts managed for single institutional investors. In 2012 and in 2014, IFC approved two medium-term loans to support an AMERRA-managed fund totaling US$60 million which has since been repaid as loans in the debt portfolio began maturing. IFC is currently considering providing two further loans totaling up to US$100 million to help AMERRA in support of its newly launched AMERRA Agri Fund III, L.P. (Onshore III) and AMERRA Agri Offshore Fund III, L.P. (Offshore III), increasing the capital they have to lend (the Project). The two funds will have similar portfolios and the distinction is that Onshore fund is open to most U.S. institutional investors whereas the Offshore Fund is available to non-US institutional investors and tax exempt U.S. investors.
sponsor_shareholders: AMERRA is a partnership which is 50% owned by Craig Tashjian, Nancy Obler and Pat Morabito as its principals. The balance is held by M.D. Sass-Macquarie Financial Strategies, L.P. (25%) and Macquarie Group Limited (25%). The principals had long and successful careers in banking before AMERRA. M.D. Sass-Macquarie Financial Strategies, L.P. is a joint venture focused on investing in alternative strategies private equity fund managers and is equally owned by M.D. Sass and Macquarie Group Limited (Macquarie). M.D. Sass was founded in 1972 and is a well-established investment management firm based in New York City. Macquarie is based in Australia and is a diversified financial group providing clients with asset management and finance, banking, advisory and risk and capital solutions across debt, equity and commodities (ASX:MQG).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project entails IFC making up to US$100 million of credit available for up to four and one-half years to support Onshore III and Offshore III.
location_description: AMERRA is based in New York City and its funds invest throughout the Americas, especially in Mexico, Central and South America. More than 80% of AMERRA’s clients have been based in Brazil, Mexico, Ecuador, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Haiti, or buy agricultural commodities from those countries and elsewhere in Latin America and the Caribbean.
development_impact: i) Contribution to food security: The Project will provides liquidity to the food supply chain, ensuring agribusiness companies (and the farmers linked to them) have the funding need to produce efficiently, contributing to food security. Many AMERRA clients are low cost producers of exported food commodities, contributing to making staple foods as inexpensive as possible. ii) Despite their contribution to food supply and rural livelihood, smaller and medium-sized agribusiness companies (and the farmers that supply them) have historically had insufficient access to finance from private sector sources, in particular finance that extends for more than one crop season. The unfavorable supply-to-demand dynamics for financing to this segment continues to deteriorate as commercial banks who had been operating in some parts of the supply chain continue to retreat from it to meet capital requirements. The Project supports the launch of the next generation of closed-end funds from a firm whose business model has successfully intermediated capital from institutional investors in North America that have not historically not invested significantly in these agribusiness segments in the emerging markets.
additionality: i) Stamp of Approval: Appetite of investors in developed countries to take credit exposure in emerging markets has not been consistently strong in recent times. IFC support for AMERRA through a period of fluctuating investor appetite is a useful expression of confidence in AMERRA's expertise in originating, structuring and servicing a specialized emerging markets loan portfolio in light of IFC's own experience of investing in emerging markets over sixty years, during which IFC has become the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. ii) Addressing financing gap in agribusiness: Agribusiness sectors do not enjoy good access to finance and financing that extends beyond a single growing season is especially limited for smaller and medium-sized companies. Through the Project, IFC is supporting a financier to the sector and bolstering its ability to provide rare, 4-year and longer tenors. iii) Improved E&S evaluation systems: AMERRA developed a formal Environmental & Social Management System (ESMS) after IFC started working with the firm in 2012 to provide a systematic means to screen for environmental and social risks. IFC will continue to support AMERRA as it strengthens the implementation of its ESMS, which has downstream benefits of also incentivizing and disseminating better E&S practices among its clients in the agricultural commodity supply chain.
Company Name: AMERRA LATIN AMERICA FINANCE ONSHORE, LLC
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: JK Paper Limited ("JKPL" or the "Company"), an existing IFC client, is a leading Indian producer of office papers, packaging boards, printing and writing papers, and specialty papers, and is publicly listed on both the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India. IFC’s investment aims to help the Company improve its productivity and restructure its balance sheet, in the process preparing the Company to capitalize on growth opportunities expected to be available in the sector in the short to medium term. The proposed project consists of (i) capacity and efficiency improvement capital expenditures at the two existing plants and (ii) refinancing of existing debt (together, the "Project").
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is part of the JK Organisation group of companies that is run by the Singhania family of India (the "Sponsors" or the "Promoter Group"). The Singhania family has a legacy of over 125 years and runs the well-respected JK Organisation which was established in 1888. The Promoter Group together own 54.99% of the Company, while the public own 45.01%
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at approximately US$100 million. The proposed IFC investment is in the form of secured non-convertible debentures (“NCDs”) of up to INR3.35 billion (US$50 million equivalent).
location_description: JK Paper's headquarters are located at Nehru House, 4 Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, New Delhi, 110002. The Project locations are at the Company's two plants: (i) JK Paper Mills, also called Unit JKPM and located at P.O. Jaykaypur, 765 017, Rayagada, Odisha, and (ii) Central Pulp Mills, also called Unit CPM and located at P.O. Central Pulp Mills, 394 660, Fort Songadh, District Tapi, Gujarat.
development_impact: 1. Strengthening Domestic Capacity: IFC's investment will help to consolidate and strengthen India's domestic capacity in the sector and enhance manufacturing capabilities, thus improving its competitiveness against imports. 2. Climate Change Mitigation: The Project will support the Company's efforts to make its plants more energy efficient by reducing the usage of water and coal. In addition, the Project supports a company that now plants more trees than it consumes, consequently helping to mitigate climate change and making JK Paper a net green company. The Project will thus help set the benchmarks in a sector where environmental footprint is a major issue. 3. Supporting Rural Incomes: The Company's strong farm forestry program that was bolstered by IFC's previous Advisory initiative completed in 2014 continues to enhance productivity, provide regular offtake, and hence improve the income stream of local farmers. The Company currently works directly with more than 20,000 farmers. IFC will explore possible re-engagement on the Advisory Services front in order to widen and further add to the impact already achieved through the earlier advisory project.
additionality: 1. Access To Long Term Finance: IFC has had a long relationship with JK Paper and has been a partner of the Company since we first invested in 2006. Securing IFC financing is critical for the Company in undertaking more long term strategic business investments and to grow market share. JK Paper is expected to benefit from the long tenor offered, grace period, and local currency funding, which is in line with the long gestation period and required currency of the proposed Project. 2. Technical Expertise and Sharing of Best Practices: JK Paper values IFC's global footprint, knowledge, network, and practical experiences in vetting and implementing projects, as reflected in IFC's ability to support pulp and paper projects worldwide. This is particularly relevant for the Company as it enters high growth specialty segments such as tissue paper and as it seeks opportunities to continue to expand its business internationally outside of India. 3. Continued Environmental and Social Standards Setting: IFC's investment in the Project will continue to reinforce the benefits of using sustainable best practices. The Company will also benefit from the implementation of the latest 2012 version of IFC's E&S Performance Standards, which contain updated criteria compared with the previous IFC Safeguard Policies that JK Paper was subject to in 2006 during the time of IFC's first investment in the Company.

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: IFC is considering providing an A loan of up to US$3 million to partially support Hansae Co. Ltd., a South Korean garment manufacturer in setting up its first manufacturing operating in Haiti. Hansae currently exports approximately 300 million pieces of clothing per year from 11 production facilities in 5 countries: Nicaragua, Guatemala, Indonesia, Myanmar and Vietnam. Phase 1 of the Haiti project entails the establishing of a cutting and sewing plant of up to 44 production lines in the Sonapi (Societe Nationale des Parcs Industriels) industrial park in Port-au-Prince.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Hansae Co. Ltd, a South Korean-based publicly traded apparel manufacturing company focused on the production of shirts, knits, women’s suits and casual apparel. Hansae was established in 1982 and is headquartered in Seoul. Hansae Co is owned 31% by minority or public shareholders, 14% by the CEO Dong Nyeong Kim and family, 42% by Hansae Yes 24 Holdings (owned 64% by Mr. Kim and family), 11% by the National Pension Service and 2% by various Hansae senior employees.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Hansae's investment plan in Haiti amounts to US$30 million, out of which US$13.5 million is allocated to the project or phase I of the investment plan . IFC is financing phase I with an A loan of up to US$3 million .
location_description: The project will be located in Sonapi's Parc Industriel Metropolitan (PIM), in Port-au-Prince, Haiti. PIM is located in the vicinity of the international airport. Sonapi is a government-owned institution responsible for the development and administration of industrial parks.
development_impact: - Job creation and employee skills development. The Project will create up to 2,600 new jobs, most of which will be for women, the majority of whom are uneducated and have limited earning opportunities. - Contribution to economic growth. The textile and apparel sector is one of the sectors where Haiti currently has a strong competitive advantage. The Project will thus contribute to economic growth in Haiti. It will generate significant foreign currency cash flows given its export focus, helping Haiti reduce its trade deficit. - Demonstration effect. The project will demonstrate to other foreign investors that despite various challenges, Haiti remains an attractive investment location for textile and apparel operations.
additionality: - Providing financing for projects in challenging investment environments. - E&S Standards: The Project will set a high standard for E&S practices by following IFC's E&S requirements.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an IFC equity co-investment of up to $15 million with Helios Investors III, LP (“Helios”) to support the formation of one of Africa’s largest Fast Moving Consumer Goods (“FMCG”) businesses (“GBfoods Africa” or the “Company”) through a joint venture with GBfoods S.A. The Company has acquired assets from different African companies including leading brands such as Jumbo (bouillon), Gino and Pomo (tomato paste), and Jago (milk powder and mayonnaise), as well as Bama (mayonnaise) distribution rights for Africa. This combination will result in a leading pan-African culinary products business with presence in over 30 African countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Helios Investment Partners (the “Sponsor”) is an Africa-focused private investment firm established in 2004, led and managed by a predominantly African team and based in London, Lagos and Nairobi. Helios’ portfolio companies operate in more than 30 countries in all regions of the continent. Helios has a track record of investing in businesses that span from start-ups to established companies. The Sponsor manages funds totalling c. $3 billion including three generalist funds in which IFC invested: Helios Investors LP, a 2006 vintage fund (Project# 25580); Helios Investors II, LP, a 2009 vintage fund (Project# 27876); and Helios Investors III, LP, a 2014 vintage (Project# 34569).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide an equity investment of up to $15 million alongside HIP.
location_description: The combined business will operate across Sub-Saharan Africa, with a presence in over 30 African countries.
development_impact: 1) Increase in processing activity and value addition across the value chain: Consumer product companies in emerging markets are contributing to development across the value chain, by modernizing manufacturing and logistics services through increased processing activities; 2) Large-scale employment: The Company, on a combined basis, employs approximately 600 full-time employees and, with the projected organic growth, the Company will be substantially increasing this number by 2021; 3) Highly diversified reach: outside of the Company's core markets, the Company reaches to markets including Democratic Republic of Congo, Djibouti, DRC, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Liberia, Mali and Somalia, among others. The Company intends to disseminate high quality food products at affordable prices to these states; 4) GBfoods' innovative pipeline of convenience products adds value to the African consumer by saving both money and cooking time versus the alternative of buying individual ingredients; 5) Promoting South / South investment: the proposed integration of brands and assets will form a unique business that encourages other local and multinational FMCG players to pursue investment opportunities across Sub-Saharan Africa; 6) Local farmers' linkage: the long-term backward integration plan is anticipated to reach local farmers across its supply chain.
additionality: 1) Long-term funding: provide long-term equity financing not easily available in the Pan African market; 2) Local sourcing advisory services: one of the strategic pillars for the Company is to integrate backwards to minimize supply volatility, thus the local sourcing supported by IFC's advisory services will be a unique value add; 3) Local sourcing investment: Post completion of the 100-day plan, the Company intends to expeditiously implement a backward integration investment program in select markets. IFC is uniquely positioned to support the investment program; 4) Stamp of approval: With an eventual public listing of the Company's shares on the public stock market, adding IFC as a direct investor adds unparalleled weight to the investor bench; and 5) Environmental & Social: A review by IFC's E&S appraisal adds prestige and improvements to the Company's credentials and facilitates discussions with socially-minded investors.

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: The proposed transaction is an A loan in Ananta Apparels Limited (AAL or the Company). AAL is setting up a washing plant (the Project) in its readymade garments factory located at Adamjee Export Processing Zone of Bangladesh. IFC will invest up to US$6 million in long term debt. The proceeds of the IFC loan will be used to fund the machinery of the washing plant.
sponsor_shareholders: AAL, incorporated on 1992, is owned by Mr. Sharif Zahir (43.09% shareholding) and Mr. Asif Zahir (29.40% shareholding), Mrs. Qamrun Nahar (6.84% shareholding), Mr. Ishtiaq Alam (5.13% shareholding), Brummer & Partners (13.75% shareholding) and IFC (1.79%). AAL is one of the fast growing ready-made-garments manufacturers and exporters focusing mainly on jeans, trousers, suits etc. The Company employs over 17,000 workers and exports to leading global brands.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost of US$10 million. IFC will invest up to US$6 million as A loan.
location_description: The proceeds of the IFC investment will be used to fund the washing plant in Adamjee Export Processing Zone of Bangladesh.
development_impact: - Enable backward integration and allow efficiency gains: The Project will allow backward linkage support to AAL, helping to increase efficiency through cost and time savings, and helping to access orders with higher value addition. - Addressing climate change: The Project will include use of efficient water consumption, heat absorption and other techniques to improve energy and resource usage efficiency, which will have a demonstration effect on addressing climate change issues in the RMG industry of Bangladesh. - Employment creation: The Project will help create 1,369 direct jobs upon being commissioned.
additionality: - Industry knowledge: The Project would benefit from IFC's industry expertise and experience to improve overall project viability - Environmental and Social Standard Setting: The Project would benefit from IFC's environmental, health & safety and social standards.

project_description: The project consists of an IFC equity investment of up to US$10 million in Power2SME (or the “Company”), a Delhi-NCR based company that functions as a 'buying club' for Small and Medium Enterprises (“SMEs”) helping them benefit from economies of scale as a result of volume purchases and buying power across a large network of manufacturers.
