In addition to giving buying power to SMEs, Power2SME provides access to finance by helping its customers obtain working capital financing, more efficiently and at better terms through its network of empaneled banks and Non-Banking Financial Companies (“NBFCs”).
sponsor_shareholders: Power2SME was founded by Narayan Ramaswamy, Debrata Majumdar, and Snehashish Bhattacharjee. The Company’s investors also include leading private equity and venture capital investors such as Accel Partners, Inventus Capital Partners, Kalaari Capital, and Mr. Nandan Nikelani.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes an equity investment of up to US$10 million as part of the Company’s fundraising round with additional capital being provided by existing and other new investors.
location_description: Power2SME has its registered office in Delhi and is headquartered in Gurgaon, India. It has operations in 14 states throughout the country.
development_impact: 1. Enabling SMEs to gain pricing advantages: Poor infrastructure and inadequate market linkages are among the key factors that have constrained the growth of the SME sector in India. The Company's key offering enables SMEs in the manufacturing sector to procure raw materials / inputs in a transparent manner while benefiting from better pricing of such items due to demand aggregation. 2. Enabling SMEs gain access to affordable financing: Lack of adequate and timely access to finance by SMEs is another key challenge to an SME's growth. Financial institutions too have limited on ground presence / access to data needed to profile credit servicing capabilities of SMEs. The Company's online demand aggregation platform enables it to capture unique data points on SME customers which allow superior credit profiling that an external lender can comfortably rely on and provide attractive financing terms. 3. Increase in SMEs reached: The Company has more than 50,000+ registered SMEs on its platform. 2000+ SMEs have transacted on the platform so far. Post launch of GST in India, the Company will be able to operate pan India. As a result, the number of transacting SMEs is expected to grow more than 10x by CY21. 4. Increase in employment by enabling SMEs to grow: According to 2015 estimates of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises ("MSME"), Govt. of India, the MSME sector generates around 100 million jobs through over 46 million MSMEs across the country each year. The Company's mission is aligned towards improving the financial health of MSMEs which will in turn result in additional job creation.
additionality: 1. Knowledge sharing: IFC will share its extensive India and global experience pertaining to the SME sector, industry knowledge and expertise gained from investments across various emerging markets. 2. Assisting with key industry relationships: The Company is keen to engage with IFC's banking and NBFC portfolio in India which would be relevant for the Company's SME financing platform. 3. Long term investor: The Company values IFC's suite of financial products and ability to continue to support future funding needs, as it continues to grow. 4. Best practices: IFC will provide inputs on environmental and social best practices and on corporate governance. Through adoption of the IFC Performance Standards, IFC will enable the Company to further improve its environmental, social and operating standards.

company_name: LATAM LOGISTIC PER PROPCO LURIN I S.R.L.
project_description: IFC is considering providing an A loan and B Loan financing package of up to US$28 million to support LatAm Logistic Properties LLC. (“LLP” or the “Sponsor”), a Latin American commercial real estate (“RE”) investment and development company, in developing its first logistic warehouse park in Peru. Phase I of LLP’s development plans in Peru entails the development of 65,578 square meters of warehouse space (the “Project”), distrusted among 3 buildings which will be located in Lurin, Lima. The Project will be the first true master planned logistics park in the market designed to international standards and focused towards third-party logistic operators, consumer goods companies and retailers that demand more efficient and less costly spaces.
sponsor_shareholders: LLP is dedicated to developing and operating logistic warehouse facilities for rent in the underserved markets of Costa Rica, Peru, Colombia and Panama. LLP aims at developing approximately 700,000 square meters of logistics Class A warehouses with modern specifications, providing significant efficiency improvements to multinational, regional and local retailers and logistic operators in the region. LLP was founded in 2013 by Mike Fangman, CEO and shareholder, who has 15 years of institutional logistics property experience in Latin America. In June 2015, Jaguar Real Estate Partners I LP (the “Fund” or “JREP1”), a New York based RE private equity fund managed by Jaguar Growth Asset Management LLC (“Jaguar”), became the majority shareholder of LLP. Jaguar executives have deep experience in RE in emerging markets, especially in Latin America. Through the Fund, Jaguar provides capital as well as global RE experience adding value throughout various life stages of projects.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project has a total cost of US$52.7 million, out of which US$14 million will be financed with an A Loan, US$14 million with a B Loan and the remaining with equity from the Sponsor. Construction of the first building began during 1Q2017 and it is expected to be completed by 1Q2018
location_description: The Project is located in the Lurin district in the department of Lima, which has experienced significant growth in logistics operations given the proximity to the city of Lima.
development_impact: - Infrastructure development: LLP will help address the existing shortages of quality industrial and logistics property infrastructure in Lima, where there is no supply of efficient, Class-A buildings to service multinationals and local equivalents; - Business efficiencies and linkages: The modern, high-quality infrastructure developed by LLP will result in improved efficiencies and reduced operational costs for local businesses and supply chains. Class A developments can be significantly more efficient with lower operating costs than existing properties in these markets, given some of their characteristics. These include: higher ceilings, increased floor load capacity, column-free span areas, intensive docking ports with levelers for all types of trucks, and ample maneuvering yards for large vehicles. LLP estimates that in Lima the improved cost efficiency of its properties with respect to those of its competitors is at least 100% vs Class C properties and between 30% to 40% for the best Class B properties; - Economic growth, job creation and supply chain development: The Project will drive the creation of direct jobs during both construction and operations, also supporting a significant number of indirect jobs through the supply chains of its tenants. The sourcing of construction inputs and related services during the subsequent development phases will foster the development of local SMEs and support local suppliers; and - Improved standards: LLP is also strengthening its ESG practices contributing to the overall improvement of quality standards in Peru, including E&S and life and fire safety standards as well as in terms of building construction methods and energy efficiency features.
additionality: - Institutional backing, mobilization and co-investment support: IFC's role as a lender to LLP is providing and mobilizing funding to the Project as well as helping fund and mobilize additional funding in the future from other lenders to its new developments in or outside Peru; - E&S: IFC is providing technical knowledge and advice to support LLP in enhancing its E&S practices and ensuring that the Project meets IFC's E&S standards; and - Green buildings: IFC has been providing technical knowledge and advice to LLP on IFC's EDGE green building standard.
Company Name: LATAM LOGISTIC PER PROPCO LURIN I S.R.L.

project_description: The proposed investment is to support Nibulon (“the Company”), one of the largest Ukrainian grain and oilseeds originators and exporters, by strengthening its capital base and financing the Company’s expansion. The implementation of the Company’s expansion program will increase the trading volume by approximately 40% over 5 years.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Oleksiy Vadaturskyy, the founder and the CEO of the Company, owns 80% of the shares. The remaining 20% are owned by his son, Andriy Vadaturskyy, who is currently not involved in the Company’s operations and has transferred voting rights related to his ownership share in the Company to Mr. Oleksiy Vadaturskyy.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is up to US$90 million, including A and B Loans.
location_description: Nibulon's key operating assets are located in Ukraine. The Company farms 82,000 hectares of land, operates second largest network of inland silos and river terminals and a modern seaport terminal, located in Mykolaiv, in the Black Sea region of Ukraine. Nibulon mainly exports corn, wheat and barley to more than 20 global destinations. Nibulon's annual trading volume reaches 4.5 million metric tons.
development_impact: The Project is expected to: Enhance food security: IFC's investment will contribute to strengthening food security by expanding the Company's grain traded volumes from 4.5 in 2016 to 7.0 million tons by 2021 and increasing food availability by 40%. Strengthen Ukraine's infrastructure: Nibulon will continue supporting the development of Ukraine's grain and oilseeds sector by creating access to storage and reducing crop losses. The Company's ongoing investment in Ukraine's river transport helps to revitalize the country's commercial navigation and provides cost efficient and more environmentally friendly alternatives to rail and truck transport. Facilitate the access to market: Through its wide origination network, Nibulon annually procures grains from up to 4,700 farmers. As a result, these farmers benefit from a reliable marketing channel and from access to Nibulon's storage, conditioning and transportation infrastructure.
additionality: IFC's expected additionality includes: (i) Countercyclical long-term financing; (ii) Corporate Governance advice; and (iii) Demonstration effect.

project_description: Bayerische Motoren Werke Aktiengesellschaft (“BMW AG” or together with its subsidiaries, the “BMW”) has invited IFC to provide up to US$150 million financing equivalent in South African Rand (ZAR) for the upgrade of its existing automotive assembly plant to produce the new BMW X3 model in South Africa (the “Project”), for global markets including Europe, Africa and Asia. The IFC financing would be a long-term loan in local currency and would be extended to BMW (South Africa) (Pty) Ltd, Pretoria (“BMW SA”). BMW SA is incorporated in South Africa (“SA”) and engages in the manufacturing, importing, exporting and distribution of motor vehicles, parts and accessories. The Project will be undertaken at BMW SA's existing assembly plant in Rosslyn (the “Rosslyn Plant”), which was taken over by BMW in 1973 as BMW's first overseas plant out of Germany. Currently the plant produces the BMW 3 Series with about 2,800 direct employees and about 12,000 indirect employees engaged by suppliers. The IFC investment will be used to support the establishment of a new BMW X3 production facility, increase the plant efficiency and upskill employees. The investment will support technological transition of the plant from producing steel body vehicles to vehicle bodies built partially from aluminum with significant impacts to the supply chain.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor: Bayerische Motoren Werke Aktiengesellschaft (BMW AG), based in Munich, Germany, is the parent company of the BMW Group. The general business purpose of the Corporation is the development, production and sale of engines, engine-equipped vehicles, related accessories and products of the machinery and metalworking industry as well as the rendering of services related to the aforementioned items. The BMW Group operates on a global scale and is represented in more than 150 countries worldwide. The Company: BMW SA is a wholly-owned subsidiary of BMW AG.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$319 million. The proposed IFC investment of US$150 million is an A loan.
location_description: The Project is located in the existing Rosslyn Plant of BMW SA, South Africa. The Rosslyn Plant is located in a dedicated industrial zone specializing in automotive industries with no residential community in the vicinity of the site.
development_impact: 1. Support the development of the SA automotive industry; 2. Introduce new products and processes, and increase the competitiveness of the SA automotive sector; 3. Maintain/sustain direct employment and generate indirect employment opportunities; 4. Support the local economy through export diversification; 5. Support the development of local suppliers; 6. Increased local value added.
additionality: 1.Global knowledge and expertise: Support BMW's supply chain with Advisory and Investment services to increase the rate of localization, improve the competitiveness, and efficiency of local suppliers; 2.Global partnership with BMW: IFC's global presence, stamp of approval and support on supply chain, climate change and urban mobility; 3.Long-term financing: Long term local currency funding to match cash flow cycle and diversify BMW South Africa's funding.

project_description: Cibrafertil - Companhia Brasileira de Fertilizantes (“Cibrafértil” or the “Company”), is a family investment business that produces, imports and distributes fertilizers in Brazil. Cibrafértil is the 5th largest fertilizer company in the country (~4% of market share) and operates 8 production, blending and storage facilities with capacity of 1.7 million tons of fertilizer. Cibrafértil employs around 450 people. Cibrafértil was founded in 1994 by a local group and acquired by the Vashisht family in 2012. Main Shareholder is Paribara (99.99%), controlled by the Vashisht family (Neha Vashisht (30%), Niti Vashisht (30%), Ashu Vashisht (20%) and Naresh Vashisht (20%) - the “Family”), citizens of the United States. The Family has a long history of successful investments, with Omimex Group in the United States and fertilizers in Latin America with Grupo Abocol.
sponsor_shareholders: Main Shareholders are members of the Vashisht family (Neha Vashisht, Niti Vashisht, Ashu Vashisht and Naresh Vashisht).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Cibrafertil is in a period of operational growth after acquiring Agro Industrial São Luiz´s (fertilizer division) that tripled its capacity in the past year. The majority of its capital expenditures are dedicated to acquiring new fertilizer blending units to gain scale in strategic regions, upgrading existing facilities to increase the output and working capital. Project Costs for 2017 - 2019 (“Project Cost”) is estimated at US$80.0 million (BRL253.4 million) comprised as follows: (i) upgrading the existing SSP manufacturing facility at Camaçari (US$3.4 million), Bahia; (ii) upgrading other existing blending facilities in Bahia, Goiás, Paranaguá, São Francisco do Sul, and Mato Grosso (US$25.0 million); and (iii) acquiring new blending assets (US$37.9 million), (iv) working capital (US$13.7 million), together the “Project”. The investments defined in the Project will be financed through an IFC Loan of up to US$40 million, local bank loans and internal cash generation.
location_description: The Company’s headquarter is in Salvador (Bahia) and it has a manufacturing plant of Single Superphosphate (SSP) with 270,000 ton/year production capacity in Camaçari (Bahia). Cibrafértil has also fertilizer blending and distribution centers in Candeias and Luiz Eduardo Magalhães, located in Bahia State, São Francisco do Sul, located in Santa Catarina State, Paranaguá located in Parana State, Sorriso, located in Mato Grosso State and Cristalina, located in Goiás State.
development_impact: 1. Strengthening food security: improved availability and cost of high quality fertilizers will help local farmers in Brazil to boost productivity and increase agricultural production. 2. Frontier Regions: Supporting a second tier market leader with operations in frontier regions of Brazil: Cibrafertil is headquartered and has 5 out of 8 plants in Brazil's much needed frontier regions of Brazil (state of Bahia, Goias and Mato Grosso). 3. Job creation: Cibrafertil currently employs around 450 people in Brazil. Implementation of the Project will help Cibrafertil to generate additional 150 jobs. 4. Transfer of technology and know-how: the Project will enable transfer of technical and managerial know-how in the fertilizer manufacturing and distribution sectors, strengthening competitiveness of local famers and contributing to sector growth.
additionality: 1. Long term Financier: IFC will help Cibrafertil to increase the average maturity of its debt while Cibrafertil continues to build up relationship with local banks. 2. Long Term Relationship and Strategic Partnership: The Company is keen on maintaining the long-term partnership with IFC as it recognizes IFC's ability to provide financing long term financing especially in markets subject to economic crisis cycles. 3. Climate change mitigation: IFC Loan will support the Company in the efforts to improving energy efficiency and agriculture yields. 4. Utilization of best international E&S practices: By introducing and ensuring full compliance with best international E&S standards, IFC's participation will bring best international practices to second tier players in this the sector in Brazil, thus raising awareness of sustainability practices and global standards.

project_description: Established in 1998, Xiang Nian (XN) is a manufacturer specialized in the research, development and production of dried noodles. Upon completion of the Project, XN’s total production capacity would increase from 100,000 tons to 200,000 tons of dry noodles per annum.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Mr. Sun Jungeng. Mr. Sun is the Chairman, CEO and founder of Xiang Nian. With a major in food engineering, he started his noodle business in 1998 as a small workshop. Over the last 20 years, Mr. Sun had developed XN into a regional leading branded noodle producer. Given his achievement in leading XN, Mr. Sun has been awarded the title “top 20 entrepreneur in Agribusiness of 2015” by China Central Television. He also serves as the Chairman of Nanyang Food Association.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a US$10 million equity investment in XN. The total project cost is estimated at US$47 million which includes a) acquisition of land; b) construction of building; c) construction of a flour mill; d) installation of noodle production line equipment and utilities.
location_description: XN is located in the city of Nanyang, Henan province, a frontier region in China where almost half of the population is engaged in agricultural activities.
development_impact: Access to staple food: Xiang Nian provides sustainable supply of affordable staple food to China's rural populations in inland provinces. Dried noodles are considered healthier alternatives to instant noodles, while Xiang Nian's dried noodle products are especially preferred due to their higher nutritional content and no addition of chemical additives. Direct Job creation: Xiang Nian currently has 770 employees; with the planned capex, the number is expected to grow to 1,000 by 2022.
additionality: Stamp of Approval: The transaction is an important step towards Xiang Nian' IPO on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange over the next few years. Adding IFC as one of the early stage investors is a critical exercise to ensure the Company can have a blue chip name on its investor bench; E&S: IFC will help Xiang Nian to design and implement an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) to identify and manage potential environmental and social risks in its operations.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: The Project comprises the planned investment program of Kioo Limited in its existing production facility in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Kioo is a leading glass container producer in East Africa and the sole producer in Tanzania. The key components of the Project include general upgrades and enhancement to plant and machinery and the addition of transportation equipment. Equipment suppliers for the Project are among the best in their respective fields globally. IFC plans to support the Project by providing senior debt.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company: Kioo Limited is the largest glass packaging manufacturer in East Africa, in operation for over 50 years, and located in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Kioo produces both flint and colored glass and sells to its domestic market, where it has dominant market share, as well as to export markets in Eastern, Central, Southern Africa, and the Indian Ocean Islands. Its customers include leading beverages multinationals. The Shareholders: Kioo is wholly owned by African Developments Limited, a fully owned associate company of the Madhvani group of Uganda. The Madhvani family have been based in Uganda for over 100 years and are one of the largest indigenous business groups in East Africa with holdings in Uganda, Rwanda, Tanzania, Middle East, and India across agribusiness, power, insurance, real estate, tourism, and other sectors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at approximately US$35 million. The proposed IFC investment will comprise an A loan of up to US$21 million.
location_description: The Project site is in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
development_impact: 1. The Project will support the development of a competitive manufacturing sub-sector capable of generating exports. 2. Stimulate economic activity in Tanzania: The IFC loan will be directed to finance a capital investment program, involving upgrading of the glass container manufacturing plant. Increased and more efficient production will not only stimulate the beverages sector by providing local customized packaging solutions but also boost the intermediate industries in its value chain and vice versa. The multiplier effect of this process will generate greater economic activity, increase economic complexity and competiveness thus providing momentum for Tanzania to continue to progress along in its development path. 3. Increased availability of high quality glass containers in East, Central and Southern Africa as well as Indian Ocean islands. 4. Transfer of technology and best practices to the Tanzanian glass manufacturing sector since the project includes investment in plant and technological upgrades. 5. Increase of foreign currency earnings for Tanzania, as Kioo generates the majority of its revenues, both exports and domestic sales, denominated in US Dollars. 6. Job creation: the direct employment creation in addition to the over 600 people currently employed by the company; the jobs also generate strong skills transfers.
additionality: 1. Long-term financing: The Project requires long-term US$ financing which is not readily available in Tanzania, during the construction phase and on an ongoing basis for importation of certain raw materials. Given this situation, IFC has a crucial role in ensuring that the financing for the Project is available and it is completed on schedule. 2. Provision of Environmental and Social (E&S) expertise: IFC financing will directly support investments in energy efficiency improvements. IFC will also promote best practices in E&S and Energy Efficiency. 3. Provision of technical and sector expertise: Sharing of global industry expertise and best practices on production techniques and sales/marketing strategies with the client.

company_name: KINGENTA ECOLOGICAL ENGINEERING GROUP CO LTD
project_description: Kingenta Ecological Engineering Group Co., Ltd. (“Kingenta” or the “Sponsor”), a leading compound and specialty fertilizer producer and supplier in China, has invited IFC to jointly fund a green-field project in China. A new company will be established to undertake the project, which plans to establish and operate several individual projects in China (jointly called the “Project”), including Crop Production Service Centers (“CPS Projects”) in rural farming areas and new production plants (“Upgrade Projects”) to upgrade local conventional fertilizer output into compound and specialty fertilizers. The development of the Project is expected to be implemented over 3 years.
sponsor_shareholders: Kingenta, established in 1998, is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in China with a market capitalization of about US$3.4 billion in February 2017 . Its diversified product profile, including compound fertilizers (CF), slow/controlled release fertilizers (SCRF), nitro-compound fertilizers (NCF), water-soluble fertilizers (WSF) and bio-fertilizers etc, can serve food crops, cash crops and horticulture. Kingenta is controlled by its founder and Chairman Lianbu WAN, who holds a direct stake of about 18.3% and an additional 39.1% via his controlling over Linyi Kingenta Investment Holding Ltd. Other minority shareholders are mainly financial investors who buy and sell its stocks in the secondary market. The Project Company will be incorporated in China with Kingenta directly owning about 40%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at about US$1 billion. IFC has been asked to consider providing a total financing of up to US$205mn, comprised of both equity and debt. The debt is expected to consist of IFC A loan of up to US$ 100 million and a syndication and mobilization portion of up to US$105 million.
location_description: The project is expected to be registed in Shandong Province with operations in various provinces across China. The CPS projects will be located in the rural farming area in China while the Upgrade projects will sit next to conventional fertilizer producers.
development_impact: Food Security: The Project will improve the accessibility and affordability of high-efficiency fertilizer products for millions of Chinese farmer families. Kingenta's specialty products can sustainably improve crop yield and generate improved food security and higher incomes for farmers. Environmental and Climate Benefits: The Project will reduce the use of conventional nitrogen and phosphate fertilizer in China. Higher efficiency in nutrient delivery will result in less fertilizer being applied, leading to improved productivity, less soil contamination and less pollution to the waterways and the atmosphere. Higher Farmer Productivity: Shortage of labor in many farming families is an impediment to better farming business and higher incomes in China. The skilled labor service provided by the Project will result in improved farmer productivity. Job Creation and SME Development: The Project will create about 10,000 direct jobs and a large number of indirect jobs in China. The Project provides also opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises to be involved in transportation and distribution of agricultural inputs.
additionality: Global Experience and Expertise: Kingenta is expanding its footprint globally and sees IFC as an important partner for its expansion into overseas emerging markets. Long Term Financing: IFC's long-term financing supports the need of the Project to construct and roll out a large number of individual projects in China. Mobilization: Besides IFC's own equity and A loan, IFC will work on mobilizing a large amount of funding to support the Project. Environmental and Social Practices: The Project contains more than a hundred individual programs across China with material Environmental & Social work. The Project will foster the utilization of high-standard environmental and social practices in China.
Company Name: KINGENTA ECOLOGICAL ENGINEERING GROUP CO LTD

project_description: Shwe Taung Cement Company Limited (“STC” or the “Company”) is part of the Shwe Taung Group (‘STG’ or the ‘Group’) of Myanmar. The Group has presence across diverse businesses including real estate, construction, retail and financial services. STG expanded into the cement business in 2010 by setting up STC, to meet the rapidly growing demand of concrete and cement in Myanmar. STC is an integrated cement manufacturer with current clinker manufacturing capacity of 1,500 tons per day (”TPD”) and cement grinding capacity of 2,800 TPD. The Company distributes its cement all over Myanmar under the brand name “Apache Portland Cement (“Apache”)”. Through its wholly owned subsidiary, Shwe Taung Mining (“STM”), STC has mining concessions providing captive sources for limestone and coal. High Tech Concrete Company Limited (‘HTC’), a subsidiary of STC, is one of the leading manufacturers of Ready Mix Concrete (‘RMC’) in Myanmar. HTC has been in been in business for more than two decades and has a network of batching plants across the country. The Project envisages brownfield expansion of STC’s cement plant at Pyi Nyaung Village, Thazi through expansion of clinker capacity to 5,500 tpd and cement grinding capacity to 7,200 tpd. The Project also involves construction of a Waste Heat Recovery System (‘WHRS’) and improvement in emission control systems.
sponsor_shareholders: STC is a closely held entity with majority stake held by family of Mr. Aik Htun, and his son Mr. Aung Zaw Naing (‘the Sponsors’). STG was founded in 1990 by Mr. Htun and the Group has been present in the building material business for more than two decades.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$110 million. The proposed IFC investment in STC comprises of investment in common equity for up to US$15 million and providing an A Loan of up to US$20 million. IFC is also looking to mobilize upto US$20 million through syndication of Parallel Loans and upto US$20 million investment in common equity from IFC AMC Emerging Asia Fund (“EAF”). The balance portion of the Project cost will be financed through internal accruals, fresh equity infusion from Sponsors and other loans.
location_description: STC’s cement plant is located in the Thazi District, Mandalay region of Myanmar, 330 miles from Yangon.
development_impact: 1. Private sector development in a FCS: IFC's proposed investment will contribute to private sector development and support increase in economic activity in Myanmar, an IDA and FCS country. 2. Increase local supply of cement: The Project will support Government of Myanmar's initiative of reducing import dependency, preserving foreign exchange and providing access to affordable construction materials by increasing the role of private sector in cement manufacturing. Improved supply of cement in turn, will provide a boost to the development of key sectors like infrastructure, housing etc. 3. Employment generation and local economic activities: The Project is expected to create about 200-300 new direct jobs and about 500-700 indirect jobs. Besides, the Project will also create more than 1000 temporary jobs during the construction period. The Project will also create new business opportunities in the local economy due to increased demand for ancillary services. In particular, it will benefit those small and medium enterprises engaged in providing logistic, maintenance and general services to the Company. In addition, the communities close to the plant sites will benefit by the way of induced job creation effects as they will provide local services and supplies to the plant and its employees. 4. Demonstration effect: IFC's investment in the sector will send a positive signal to other investors considering investments in the country and attract future capital flow into the sector. IFC's involvement with the client will also help showcase E&S best practices, resource efficiency and cleaner production norms alongside serving as a catalyst for other firms to raise their standards such areas.
additionality: 1. Long term financing: STC requires long term capital commensurate with the project requirements and the intrinsic cyclicality of the cement sector. The proposed IFC investment and mobilizations will bridge this gap and provide the necessary financing to the Company. 2. E&S Management: Association with IFC will help STC to upgrade its environmental, health, and safety (EHS) standards by improving its environment & social management system. This in turn should enhance the group's reputation by reducing the risk of adverse impacts on issues like local community relationship, clean production and help in its delivery of corporate social responsibility. 3. Global sector expertise: In its next phase of growth, STC is looking to be competitive with international cement producers and create a long term sustainable business model. IFC's global knowledge of the cement and construction material sector is likely to benefit the company in their endeavor. 4. Corporate Governance standard setting: IFC is also advising STG on improving its corporate governance standards. IFC's Corporate Governance unit is engaged with the client to conduct diagnostic assessment of existing corporate governance structure, develop a corporate governance roadmap and provide support in implementing such roadmap.

project_description: Renova S.A. ("Renova" or the "Company”) owns a soybean crushing and port facility in Timbues, Santa Fe, with a crushing capacity of 20,000 tons/day. The Company also owns a biodiesel facility in San Lorenzo with a processing capacity of 480,000 tons/year. The proposed project will support the construction of a third soybean crushing line with capacity of 10,000 ton/day, a new grain port with loading capacity of 4,000 tons/hour and a barges port with a capacity of 9,000 ton/day, among others (the "Project").
sponsor_shareholders: Renova is a joint venture between Vicentin S.A.I.C. (“Vicentin”) and Oleaginosa Moreno Hermanos S.A.C.I.F.I. Y A. (“OMHSA”), a wholly owned subsidiary of Glencore Agriculture Ltd. (“Glencore Agri”). Vicentin, a family-owned business, was incorporated in 1929 and has been in the soybean crushing business since 1979. It is one of the largest soybean processors in Argentina, owning 3 other facilities and a port terminal in the Great Rosario Area, and two other biofuel plants in northern Santa Fe. OHMSA operates 2 multi-seed crushing plants, 1 vegetable oil refinery, 2 storage facilities and 2 ports, among others. Glencore Agri is owned by Glencore Plc (49.99%), Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (39.99%) and British Columbia Investment Management Corp. (9.99%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$434 million. Proposed IFC investment will consist of a long-term loan of up to US$75 million for its own account, and the mobilization of parallel and B loans.
location_description: Timbues, Santa Fe, Argentina.
development_impact: The Project's main development impacts include: -Supporting growth and operations of a competitive domestic player in the oilseed crushing industry, one of the most important sectors in the Argentine economy, with positive impacts through the entire supply chain. -Enhancing port infrastructure in Argentina, one of the key drivers to improve logistics and competitiveness of the soybean supply chain. -Reaching up to 8,500 additional soybean and grain farmers who are expected to benefit from improved market access through the Company. Sourcing from farmers is being carried out by the Sponsors through the commodity exchange and the services of aggregators.
additionality: -Financial Additionality: IFC's involvement will mobilize significant financial support from other multilaterals and commercial banks, in a context where financing to local companies is very scarce. -Long-term partnership: Continuing to support Vicentin, a longstanding IFC's client.

sector: Other Miscellaneous Fabricated Metal Products (Including Non-Wood Housing Products, Tanks, Cutlery, Kitchen Utensils and Handtools, etc.)
project_description: F.V. S.A. (“FV” or “the Company”) is Argentina's leading producer of brass and metal fixtures for bathrooms and kitchens. FV is a second-tier family-owned and managed company focused on the production of a variety of fixtures such as faucets, showers, taps, spouts, siphons, and other bathroom accessories. The project consists of: (i) the acquisition of an Argentine manufacturer of other related products to FV's business ; and (ii) follow up investments in FV’s existing production facilities for capacity expansion (i.e. a new building and machinery).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded in 1921 in Argentina by Franz Viegener and is still privately held by the Viegener family (the Sponsor).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$40 million. IFC will provide an A Loan for up to US$25 million to partly finance the Company's investment plan.
location_description: All the investments related to the Project will be made in the Province of Buenos Aires, Argentina.
development_impact: Unlock the value of a player to be acquired in a related sector. Through the acquisition FV will: (i) give new products entry to more diverse markets in Latin America (ii) spread its operating efficiency and customer service culture; and (iii) disseminate good management practices and E&S Standards. Reinforce the competitiveness of an existing IFC client: FV is a market leader in Argentina and in other latin american countries. Through the acquisition and the planned investments for the existing plant, FV will be more competitive and its product offering will be more sophisticated.
additionality: Long term financing: Long-term funding is critical to FV's pursuit of its growth objectives. Financing under the terms and conditions offered by IFC is not readily available in Argentina. Long-term partnership: The Company perceives IFC as a strategic long-term partner. IFC has supported FV in three different transactions since 1998.

project_description: The proposed transaction is an A loan in Bengal Hotel and Resorts Limited (BHRL or the Company). BHRL has undertaken to develop a greenfield, 350 room business hotel property (the Project) in Dhaka, Bangladesh, to be operated by Swissotel Management GMBH (the Operator) under its Swissotel brand. IFC will invest up to US$18 million in long term debt and will mobilize up to US$18 million as parallel loan from another multilateral. The proceeds of the IFC loan will be used to fund the construction of the hotel.
sponsor_shareholders: BHRL, incorporated on April 2013, is 100% owned by the owners of Bengal Group. Shareholding structure of BHRL is: Mr. Humayun Kabir (16%), Mr. Jashim Uddin (17%), Mr. Morshed Alam (20%) and other family members. Established in 1969, Bengal Group is a family owned business house in Bangladesh. The Group now comprises of six companies with business interests in plastics, garments accessories, media, food & agro, flexible packaging and a media company. Each company is a separate legal entity and the Group does not have a holding structure.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost of US$75 million. IFC will invest up to US$18 million as A loan and would mobilize another US$18 million from a development finance institution (DFI).
location_description: The proceeds of the IFC investment will be used to fund the construction of the hotel in Gulshan-Tejgaon link road in Dhaka.
development_impact: - Improvement of business infrastructure: The Project will improve the supply of business infrastructure, which is important in driving growth in the export sector (primarily garmenting) and other economic activities in Bangladesh. - Employment creation and knowledge transfer: The Project will create approx. 400 new direct jobs (including several female jobs), as well as temporary jobs during construction. It will also promote knowledge transfer to local staff through training in all areas of hotel operations. - Indirect job creation and local supply chain linkages: As in all hotel projects, a significant number of indirect jobs are expected to be created. The Project will generate incremental business and indirect jobs for domestic Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the value chain, construction supply and services during implementation including transportation, F&B suppliers and other service providers. - Increase in domestic revenues and foreign exchange: The Project is expected to contribute to the domestic economy through increased tax revenues and foreign exchange earnings from overseas travelers.
additionality: - Long Term Debt Funding: IFC will provide long term debt funding with sufficient grace period, which is critical for financing hotel projects with long development and implementation period, which is currently not available in Bangladesh. - Mobilization: Mobilize an additional US$18 million through a parallel loan. - Industry Knowledge: The Project Sponsors will benefit from IFC's hospitality industry expertise and experience to improve overall Project viability. - Environment and Social Standard Setting: IFC will assist BHRL to formulate and implement E&S action plan, and introduce social/labor management systems, which will be beneficial for the Project.

project_description: IFC is considering to provide financing of up to EUR4.5 million to support the modernization of Societe Industrielle Agro-Alimentaire (the "Company" or “SIAGRO”), a Senegal-based beverage producer (primarily mineral water, juice drinks and UHT milk)(“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: SIAGRO main shareholders include Mr. Mohamed Fares, Mr. Muhyedine Fares, Mr. Hassan Fares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at EUR5.6 million. IFC’s proposed financing is an A loan of up to EUR3.0 million for IFC’s own account and an A loan of up to EUR1.5 million in its capacity as Implementing Entity of the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (“GAFSP”) .
location_description: SIAGRO is located near the village of Kirene, Senegal in the sub-prefecture of Thies.
development_impact: - Increased availability of good quality and affordable beverages. - Support to rural livelihoods through development of local fruit & milk value chains. - Direct and Indirect job creation. - SIAGRO distributes milks to schools in Dakar, Senegal, thereby promoting nutrition and learning. - Increased tax revenues.
additionality: - Provide long term funding to support modernization program. - Provide IFC Advisory Services to develop local sourcing. - Provide guidance on the implementation of IFC's Environmental and Social Perfomance Standards, and the World Bank Group Environmental, Health and Safety General and Specific Guidelines.

project_description: Financing to support Novare Africa Property Fund II (“NAPF” or the “Sponsor”) in) the US$27.0 million greenfield development of Great North Mall (the Project), a single-level, 9,844 sqm GLA covered shopping mall in Great North Area, Lusaka, Zambia. The Project will be implemented through a local SPV and will be anchored by an established South African supermarket chain.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Novare Africa Property Fund II (\"NAPF\" II or the \"Sponsor\"), a US$351 million real estate fund focused on commercial property development in Sub-Saharan Africa. NAPF II achieved final close in June 2016. Novare Fund Manager Limited (Mauritius) is the fund manager and Novare Equity Partners (PTY) Limited (South Africa) is the sub-advisor (jointly \"Novare\").
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US $27.0 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$4.5 million A loan for IFC's own account and a syndication of US$4.5 million from a parallel lender.
location_description: The Project will be located on a greenfield site in the Great North Area of Lusaka, Zambia. The site is located on a busy highway about 8 km north of the CBD in an area of mainly low and low to middle income housing.
development_impact: The Projects will contribute to economic growth and urban development through: (i) Jobs: direct and indirect employment opportunities for local communities during the construction and operations including jobs created or maintained throughout the supply chain (SMEs). Construction workers learn advanced construction methods and safety standards from a high-quality South African developer. (ii) Consumers: access to higher quality goods for the low-to-middle income and base of pyramid population in an underserved area (i.e. through supermarket anchors with higher food quality/safety standards than are currently available in the immediate area). (iii) Green building: Novare has indicated a willingness to adopt EDGE where possible within its development pipeline.
additionality: (i) Long-term Partner: IFC seeks to develop a strategic relationship with Novare to support its development pipeline in multiple African countries with long-tenor debt, which is often not available; (ii) Ensure that NAPF II maintains corporate governance, environmental, social, health and safety structures at international standards; (iii) Green Building / Energy efficiency advice: help the NAPF II identify opportunities for energy efficiency and gain EDGE certification.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A/B loan financing package to Sao Martinho S.A. ("Sao Martinho" or "the Company"). Founded in the 1930’s by the Ometto family, Sao Martinho is currently the fourth largest sugarcane processor in Brazil with 20 million tons of cane crushed in 2015/2016 crop season. Sao Martinho currently operates three sugar mills in the state of Sao Paulo and one mill in the state of Goias with a total capacity to process 24 million tons of sugarcane annually.
sponsor_shareholders: Sao Martinho is listed in the Sao Paulo stock exchange under the Novo Mercado segment, the segment with highest corporate governance standards. The Company’s controlling shareholder with 52% ownership is the Ometto family and the remaining is free-float. The Ometto family has been involved in the agribusiness sector for over 100 years and the board of directors (mostly composed by members of the family) has an active role in setting the Company’s strategy.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment consists of a US$90 million A/B loan financing package composed of a US$60 million A Loan and a US$30 million B Loan to Sao Martinho. The proceeds of the A/B loan will be used by São Martinho to carry out its investment program for the crop 2017 / 2018 consisting of sugarcane planting capex; expansion of Santa Cruz mill; operational improvements in existing units; agricultural automation and financing of working capital needs.
location_description: Sao Martinho is headquartered in the city of Pradopolis, state of Sao Paulo, where it operates the Sao Martinho mill, the world’s largest single-site sugar and ethanol mill. The Company also operates other two mills in the State of Sao Paulo and one mill in the State of Goias.
development_impact: - Private Sector Development: The investment will support the growth of a competitive domestic player in the sugar and ethanol industry, one of the most important sectors in the Brazilian economy. - Payments to Government: The Brazilian agribusiness sector is highly competitive globally and is key to the economy in terms of its capacity to raise Government revenues. This investment will allow the Company to expand its operations and will contribute to the growth of Brazilian economy. - Supply-chain linkages: The Company has extensive linkages especially upstream with about 30% of sugarcane sourced from third-parties and about 150,000 ha of leased land. - Climate Change: IFC's investment in Sao Martinho will contribute to climate change mitigation by promoting the use of renewable energy.
additionality: - Long-Term Financing: IFC's involvement will provide the Company with the necessary financing for its capital expenditures, in a context where long-term financing to local companies is scarce; - Mobilization: IFC will mobilize most needed long-term capital from a commercial bank through the B-loan program, as well as to provide the mitigation that the bank is looking for; - Environmental and Social Standards: IFC, by introducing the Performance Standards on Social & Environmental Sustainability, can help Sao Martinho to further improve its sustainability practices.

project_description: Headquartered in Mumbai, India, ETC Agro Processing (India) Private Limited (“ETC Agro” or the “Company”), along with its associate entity ETG Agro Private Limited, are engaged in pulses processing and trading, wheat flour milling and biscuit manufacturing. The Company is in the process of setting up a new pulses processing facility of 300,000 MTPA in Kolkata, West Bengal, which, once completed, will be one of the largest pulses processing plants in the world, handling processing of yellow peas, lentils, green gram and black gram (the “Project”). The Project will allow the Company and its associate entity to expand their existing pulses processing capacity in India to about 475,000 MTPA to provide high-quality processed pulses to the Indian market; pulses are a key source of protein and an integral part of the diet of the Indian population.
sponsor_shareholders: ETC Agro is a 60% subsidiary of ETC Group (“ETC Group” or the “Group”), an important IFC client in Africa. ETC Group is a vertically integrated agricultural supply chain manager involved in origination, procurement, warehousing, transport, trading, agriculture processing and consumer products. The Group and its subsidiaries are active in 35 countries across Africa, Asia and America; in addition, the Group has trading desks in Europe, the Americas and the Middle East. ETC Group has its registered office at Port Louis, Mauritius. ETC Group is controlled by Mahesh Patel, Ketan Patel and Birju Patel, who were born in Africa and are based in Tanzania. In addition, other private equity investors such as Standard Chartered Private Equity and Pembani Remgro Infrastructure Fund own minority stakes in ETC Group. Mr. Vijay Doshi and his family hold the remaining 40% equity shares in ETC Agro. Mr. Doshi is the Chairman and Managing Director of ETC Agro and has about 40 years of experience in the pulses industry.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the Project, including working capital for processing and trading, is approximately US$98 million, out of which IFC plans to provide a Senior debt of up to INR 2,010 million (approximately US$30 million) denominated in INR in the form of a Non-Convertible Debenture (NCD).
location_description: The Project is located on a leased site at the port of Kolkata, in the Low Income State of West Bengal in India.
development_impact: 1. Food and Nutrition Security: As a result of the Project, the Company's increased pulses processing capacity will contribute to food and nutrition security in India, as it will help reduce the gap between actual and WHO recommended levels of protein intake, while following international food safety standards. 2. Domestic Manufacturing Capacity Building and Job Creation: In supporting the building of one of the largest pulses processing facilities in the world, the IFC investment supports the expansion of domestic processing of pulses (instead of importing "processed" pulses), providing an impetus to Government of India initiatives of 'Make in India' and 'Skill India'. This will generate incremental jobs and income, government revenues and widen the tax base as well as support economic growth. 3. Northeastern States: The funding will be used entirely towards setting up a processing facility in West Bengal, one of the lower income states in India.
additionality: 1. Preferred Partner with a range of offerings: IFC can be a long term partner of the ETC Group in expanding the Group's businesses in other emerging markets outside Sub-Sahara Africa. The proposed investment will strengthen IFC's existing relationship with the client and highlight IFC's ability to present diverse product offering of IFC to the ETC Group. 2. Environmental & Social Standards: Implementation of IFC's Environmental & Social policy standards to the Company's expanded processing base in India will instill best practices in one of the largest pulses processing companies in India. 3. South-South Partnership: The investment will help an Africa-based Group expand its investment and production in India and provide further impetus to trading of essential agricultural commodities both within Asia (Myanmar, India) as well as between Asia and Africa.

project_description: The Project, sponsored by Immer Group (the “Group” or the “Sponsor”), of approximately Euro 60 million is to expand and modernize the Group’s operating capacities as well as strengthen its balance sheet through re-profiling of its debt portfolio.
sponsor_shareholders: Immer Group, a leading supplier of flexible plastic packaging for consumer goods, is a 100% family owned business with facilities in Kiyv, Ukraine and Ventspils, Latvia. The Group’s primary company, Kiyv-based OSJC Ukrplastic, was established in 1932. The Group is presently owned by Irina Mirochnik and her three daughters.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is approximately Euro 60 mln. The IFC investment is expected to consist of an IFC loan for its own account of up to Euro 20 mln and an IFC syndicated or mobilized financing of up to Euro 20 mln.
location_description: The Project will be undertaken by the Group’s facilities in Kiyv, Ukraine and Ventspils, Latvia.
development_impact: 1) Supporting local producer: Immer Group is one of the largest producers in the manufacturing sector in Ukraine, supporting viable economic activity and preserving jobs during these difficult times in Ukraine 2) Demonstration effect: some of the IFC's financing will be directed towards completion of energy and cost efficient investments, launched before the crisis. The Project will serve as a strong example to other companies in Ukraine and encourage them to reduce their cost by investing in energy efficient technologies. 3) Employment preservation: IFC financing will help sustain operations and, hence, preserve jobs for the Company's employees as well as for its people/ businesses in the supply chain. 4) Food security and resource efficiency: improvement of agriculture yields thanks to locally produced, affordable mulch and silage films helping to save on watering, seeds and cattle food 5) Support of the weakened economy of a conflict affected country.
additionality: 1) Longer Tenor: IFC is providing long-debt in the environment where such debt is scarce. IFC will allow the Group to replace the existing financing that includes a bullet repayment due in 2017 with longer-term funds and eliminate refinancing risk. Furthermore, it will allow the Group to focus on completing its strategic investment aiming at increasing its competitiveness. 2) Long-Term partnership: IFC will establish a new partnership with one of the most stable companies in Ukraine. 3) Catalytic effect: By making long-term investment in the Group during this critical time, IFC will provide comfort to its existing lenders and ensure that the financial plan is completed on terms suitable for the Group's operations. 4) The Group would benefit from IFC industrial expertise to be guided towards better, leaner manufacturing practices and offset difficult market conditions by improving its reactiveness and competitiveness. IFC would be able to propose to the Group to benefit from its Industrial Supply Chain Efficiency Advisory Services to support it in this direction.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: NSG UK Enterprises (“NSG UK” or the “Company”) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Nippon Sheet Glass Co. Ltd (“NSG Group”). Formerly Pilkington, the Company was acquired by NSG Group in 2006. It still uses the Pilkington brand in its operations. IFC is considering to provide an up to US$100 million equivalent A-loan to partially finance the Company’s US$200 million investment program in Eastern Europe and South America for financial year 2017.
sponsor_shareholders: NSG UK is involved in manufacturing of architectural and automotive glass products and its operations span across Europe and South America as well as in USA and India. In FY16, (period ending March 31, 2016), the Company recorded annual revenues of £2.3 billion, and total assets of £4.05 billion. Headquartered in Tokyo, Nippon Sheet Glass Co. Ltd. (“NSG Group”) is a well-diversified global manufacturer of glass and glazing products for the automotive, architectural and technical glass markets. The company is listed on the Tokyo stock exchange and has market capitalization of JPY 78.7 billion (US$ 675 million equivalent) as of January 6, 2017. In FY16 (period ending March 31, 2016), NSG Group recorded annual revenues of JPY629 billion (US$5.1 billion equivalent). As of September 30, 2016, NSG Group had total assets of JPY709 billion (US$6.1 billion equivalent).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to provide an A loan of up to US$100 million equivalent to partially fund the Company’s FY16-18 investment program amounting to US$450 million.
location_description: IFC loan is expected to be utilized for: - Partial financing of the Company’s FY16-18 investments in its subsidiaries in Poland; - Funding research & development (R&D) expenses geared towards improving energy efficiency of the manufacturing processes and to produce more climate friendly products. This R&D is primarily performed in the United Kingdom, whereas new products and processes are rolled out across all of the NSG UK operations in emerging and developed markets; and - Refinancing of high priced local debt in the Company’s Brazilian operations to improve the financial structure and help sustain these operations in the current depressed automotive market situation.
development_impact: - Stimulate economic activity in emerging markets: As of FY16, the Company generates about 24% of its revenues and about 11% of its operating profit (excluding overheads) in emerging markets. The IFC loan will be directed to finance recent and ongoing capital expenditures in architectural and automotive glass production in emerging markets, likely Poland and Brazil. Increased production will not only stimulate the construction and automotive sectors but also boost the intermediate industries in its supply chain. The multiplier effect of this process will generate greater economic activity, increase economic complexity and competiveness thus providing a momentum for emerging markets to progress along in their development path. - Industrial Competitiveness, Productivity and Jobs: The Project will introduce new energy efficient technology to the Company's operations, helping address the urgent need for cold repairs and equipment upgrades which is required every 18 to 20 years to stay competitive in the glass manufacturing sector. This type of investment is necessary to improving productivity and competitiveness and maintaining the current job levels. Specifically for NSG UK Poland: (i) since the 1990s, the Company has continuously been adding jobs to the Polish economy, starting with about 300 in the early years and having more than 3,500 today. The new investment will create more than 200 additional jobs (many of them highly skilled) of which at least 25% are expected to be women employees. (ii) The greater impact however is in the job preservation. The cold repair is needed to keep the float line running. Without this investment, the float operations cannot sustain the level of existing jobs. (iii) In the downstream investment, the service centers are expected to be extended to under developed regions of Poland, thus creating employment opportunities in such areas. (iv) NSG UK Poland operations include European Shared Service Center for NSG Group employing 160 highly qualified jobs, of which 95% are occupied by female employees. At a time when these investments are needed, IFC can support the Company in maintaining these critical jobs along the supply chain, while at the same time promoting innovation and know-how transfer. For example, the Project will also include R&D investments primarily undertaken in the Company's R&D facilities in the UK, however, geared towards improvements in the manufacturing process in emerging markets (Poland and Brazil) with the view to make them more efficient and for the development of innovative energy efficient product - Demonstration effect: Responsible environmental and social behavior of a global player in emerging markets has a demonstration impact which fosters adoption of industry best practices of sustainable growth by local market players. - Climate change benefits: Glass products can play an important role in energy conservation and generation. NSG UK is committed to developing innovative products that help address climate change. The Company has sustainability targets to improve its own energy usage as well as make a positive environmental contribution through its products.
additionality: - Financial additionality: The average maturity of the proposed IFC loan is longer than the existing commercial bank debt of the Company. IFC's longer term debt is more adapted to the capital intensity of the investment and cyclicality of the glass industry. Longer term financing will help the Company achieve a more optimal financial structure. - Diversify bank exposure: IFC financing will help diversify the Company's bank exposure. - E&S Standards: IFC will build on its successful past collaboration with the Company in the sphere of environmental and social practices and, where appropriate, will support the Company's performance in this area to continue achieving excellence in sustainable operations.

project_description: National Fisheries Developments Limited (NFD or the “Company”), based in Noro in Solomon Islands’ Western Province, is Solomon Islands’ only domestic purse seine tuna fishing operation. NFD's owned fleet of seven fishing vessels (five purse seiners and two pole-and-line boats) operates in Solomon Islands' archipelagic waters and exclusive economic zone (EEZ). The proposed Project involves the purchase of an additional purse seine fishing vessel, increasing NFD's purse seine tonnage capacity by more than 50%.
sponsor_shareholders: NFD is wholly-owned (100%) by Tri Marine International (Pte.) Limited (“PTE”), an affiliate of Tri Marine (“Tri Marine” or the “Group”), which consists of a group of 43 privately-held entities that together comprise one of the largest global tuna supply companies in the world.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is expected to be approximately US$25 million for which IFC, with GAFSP support, will provide US$10 million in long-term debt funding.
location_description: The Project will be located at NFD's existing facilities in Noro, Solomon Islands.
development_impact: (i) Contribute to the sustainability of the Pacific tuna fishery in general, through compliance with IFC's principles for engagement in the Pacific tuna industry as well as improved fisheries management through mutually reinforcing World Bank and IFC Investment Services and Advisory Services projects.\r(ii) Improve the flow of benefits from the fishing industry to the local economy by substantially increasing the amount of tuna that is processed onshore, thereby retaining greater value add domestically.\r(iii) Contribute to domestic food security.\r(iv) Generate additional jobs for local fishermen as well as in the broader fisheries and fish processing supply chain.\r(v) Increase tax and other revenues to the Solomon Islands government.
additionality: (i) Provision of financing where it is not readily available. Without IFC, it is unlikely the Company would be able to complete the debt refinancing portion of the Project within the required timeframe, at a reasonable interest rate; (ii) Improved environmental and social outcomes. IFC will work with NFD to ensure compliance with IFC's Performance Standards on environmental and social sustainability, including improved working conditions; (iii) IFC / World Bank coordination and commitment, and IFC Advisory Services / Investment Services approach. The WBG's combined offering of technical assistance to government, potential advisory services for the fisheries sector and for NFD, and IFC investment support come together to strengthen the fishery sector, the Project and the Company. Potential work around voluntary wild catch standards (MSC) also strengthen sustainability aspects and provide reputational risk mitigation for the Project, the Sponsors and IFC.

project_description: Established in 1998, Pan Group (“PAN” or the “Group”) is an existing IFC investee in Vietnam and a publicly listed group of agribusiness companies aiming to benefit from the fast growing and fragmented agricultural and food sectors in Vietnam. PAN currently controls the leading distributor and producer of crop seeds named National Seed Corporation (“NSC), a new flower and farming venture Pan-Saladbowl JSC (“Pan-Saladbowl”), an integrated pangasius and clam processor in the Mekong Delta named Ben Tre Aquaproduct Import and Export JSC (“ABT”), and an important cashew processor named Long An Food Processing Export JSC (“LAF”) in addition to its 43.7% interest in a leading confectionary producer Bibica Corporation (“BBC”). PAN established two holding intermediary subsidiaries Pan Farm JSC (“Pan Farm” or the “Company”), which holds the shares of NSC and Pan-Saladbowl, and Pan Food JSC, which holds the shares of ABT, LAF and BBC. The purpose of the Project is to support the Company’s expansion plan in the agriculture and food sectors.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group is 11.84% owned by the founder chairman Mr. Nguyen Duy Hung, a reputable Vietnamese businessman and his relatives and 20.1% by Saigon Securities Inc. and its associates, a leading securities company in Vietnam which was also founded by Mr. Hung. Other board members and management holds 1.82% of the Group. Key institutional shareholders include The Asia Entrepreneur Legacy fund (TAEL - 20.67%), a private equity fund based in Singapore; Mutual Fund Elite (8.75%), a Finland domiciled mutual equity fund licensed under the EU regulations and focusing on small to medium capitalized companies in Vietnam and China; The Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (GIC - 4.88%), a sovereign wealth fund established by the Singaporean government in 1981; and Orix (2.46%), a Japanese integrated financial services group. IFC is holding 4.81% of PAN. Pan Farm is a 99.99% subsidiary of PAN.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at VND 643 billion (approximately US$28 million). The proposed IFC investment is up to VND 230 billion (approximately US$10 million) in common shares of the Company.
location_description: There are multiple locations related to the Project in the north, the center and the south of Vietnam.
development_impact: Benefits to farmers: NSC provides high quality seeds and technical advice to a large number of farmers across the country, which would lead to increased production yield, better output quality and reduced farming losses, hence helping to improve farmers' livelihood. In addition, Pan-Saladbowl plans to establish a contract farming model in Lam Dong province which would directly benefit farmers. Food security: the financing will contribute to the global food security through supporting the growth of leading seed companies and production of vegetables and fruits which is an importance part of daily human diet. Standard setting: Pan Farm is keen to adopt international best practices especially in the food safety area, which would have significant demonstration effect on the overall agriculture industry in the country.
additionality: Long term financing and partnership: The proposed investment will be a repeat transaction with the Group. IFC will provide growth equity capital which is not readily available in Vietnam in the agriculture sector. Global industry expertise: IFC has extensive global experience within agribusiness, which in particular could benefit the Group, as it seeks to expand its business overseas. Advisory services: IFC Food Safety Advisory has already completed a food safety assessment on the Group and is discussing a plan to support the Group and its subsidiaries including Pan Farm with implementation of food safety standards.

project_description: The IFC financing will fund the investment program undertaken by Grivalia Properties REIC that includes green building upgrades, refurbishments of the existing portfolio as well as investments (acquisitions, developments) in a number of sectors including logistics and retail throughout Greece.
sponsor_shareholders: Grivalia Properties REIC is the leading real estate investment company (REIC) in Greece, focusing on the office/retail/logistics and industrial sectors in highly commercial areas. It manages approximately EUR 850 million, including a portfolio of 92 assets, the majority located in Greece, two commercial properties in Serbia and three in Romania. Grivalia has the following main shareholders: Fairfax Financial Holding Ltd, with 41.5% Eurobank Ergasias S.A., with 20.3%, Wellington Management Company LP, with 11.2%, Brandes Investment Partners L.P with 5,0% and Fidelity Management and Research LLC with 4.99%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering an A loan of EUR 50 million to support Grivalia’s ongoing investment program.
location_description: Investments under the Project can be made throughout Greece.
development_impact: Energy efficiency and Green Buildings: Grivalia is implementing best practices on energy efficiency improvements and green technology. Supporting business-enabling infrastructure: The project relates to improvements of existing office and commercial buildings in Athens, contributing towards the improvement of existing business infrastructure, much needed given the limited investment taking place since the beginning of the crisis. Increased employment and linkages: The project will create employment opportunities, during construction and renovation works as well as increase demand for materials and services in the construction sector, one of the worst hit sectors during the Greek crisis, contributing towards IFC's goal to support crisis-hit sectors and reduce unemployment. Tax revenues: The project will generate tax revenue for the government through property and other taxes applicable for real estate investment companies.
additionality: Strong partnership potential: The client is one of the largest real estate players in the Greek market, actively participating and bidding for a number of privatization projects in property, tourism and logistics, all key sectors for Greece. Long term financing: IFC is offering long term financing which is difficult to obtain otherwise in the current market environment. Energy efficiency best practices: IFC will support the client in its efforts to modernize its current portfolio of office buildings to the highest energy efficiency standards, offering expertise in different ways to achieve it as well as in the area of certification through the EDGE tool when available in Greece. Furthermore, the client is committed to the certification of a portion of its portfolio to Green Building standards.

company_name: Norson Holding, S. de R.L. de C.V.
project_description: Norson Holdings, S. de R.L. de C.V. (Norson or the Company), an existing IFC client, is one of the largest integrated pork producers and processors in Mexico. Norson is a good portfolio client with a key global strategic partner (Smithfield) which plays an active role in the Company’s operations. The project will expand and upgrade operations of Norson. The project includes (i) expanding Norson's production capacity, (ii) developing the required new farms for capacity expansion and adapting some of the existing facilities, (iii) increasing slaughtering capacity at the processing plant, (iv) increasing its feed mill capacity; and (v) installing plastic liners at the waste lagoons.
sponsor_shareholders: Norson is a joint-venture between Grupo Mazon and Smithfield Foods Inc. Grupo Mazon is a Mexican business group based in Hermosillo, Sonora. Smithfield Foods, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of WH group, is the world's largest pork producer and processor headquartered in Virginia. WH Group is a publicly traded company in the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, with operations in the production of meat products and related businesses such as logistics, packaging, materials, etc.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$69.8 million, which consists primarily of investments in farms, slaughtering and processing equipment, waste lagoons, and working capital. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A Loan of up to US$15 million equivalent on IFC's own account. Out of this cost estimate, Norson is seeking to outsource the construction of some of the farms through leasing contracts, which could potentially reduce the investment amount.
location_description: The project's capital investments will be made at Norson's production facilities located in the state of Sonora, Mexico, primarily in and around the city of Hermosillo. All project sites have the necessary utilities, road access, and permits.
development_impact: (i) Reorganizing and increasing the Company's production system and debottlenecking pig production to improve biosecurity, animal welfare, management of sanitary conditions, and labor efficiency. (ii) Increasing land productivity. The lands for developing the new farms are currently sub utilized or not developed. The new facilities will be a sustainable and financially sound way to procure a correct use of natural resources. (iii) Employment generation primarily in rural areas and for women (currently 44% of its total workforce). (iv) Increasing the availability of pork meat and value added products in the local and international markets.
additionality: (i) Long-term financing. IFC will provide a tailor-made long term product which suits the Company's needs. (ii) Resource efficiency. IFC will provide support to the Company in identifying resource efficiency improvement opportunities focused primarily on energy and water, and in the use of renewable energy. (iii) E&S standards. IFC will keep supporting Norson in the improvement of environmental and social standards.
Company Name: Norson Holding, S. de R.L. de C.V.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an IFC C loan of €20 million to Bounty Brands (“Bounty” or the “Company”), a South African fast moving consumer goods (FMCG) platform. Bounty operates three divisions: food, personal care, and home care, and owns a wide portfolio of leading brands that are being sold in over 40 countries globally. The IFC loan will support the Company’s acquisition activities and geographical expansion over the next few years in preparation for an upcoming IPO (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Bounty is a South African privately held company that is owned 100% by Coast2Coast and its affiliates (“C2C”), a South African based investment group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide a convertible loan of up to €20 million to support the Company’s acquisition activities.
location_description: The Company is looking to acquire food and personal and home care manufacturers in Central and Eastern Europe as well as in South Africa.
development_impact: 1) Pan-African Expansion of Direct Marketing: Bounty owns two companies that carry out a direct marketing business model, engaging 20,000 members, 95% of which are female. The direct marketing network is a highly effective avenue to create SME entrepreneurs and disposable income in emerging markets. The Project will allow the Company to double its network, leading to knowledge and technology transfer and contributing to inclusive economic growth. 2) Pan-African Expansion of SME Distributors: The Company will be working with SME distributors to expand its Pan-African network into Botswana, Mozambique, Zambia and Kenya. 3) Mass employment: Bounty employs approximately 1,800 full-time employees. The Company is expected to increase its total number of employees to 3,000 in the next 12 months via organic and inorganic growth. 4) Global capital market: The Company is targeting a listing on the LSE and the JSE and will be the eighth such company to do so outside of the mining, property and financial sectors, setting a further precedent on the potential of African companies in the global capital markets.
additionality: 1) Stamp of approval: Adding IFC as one of the early stage investors is critical to the Company to ensure it can have a blue chip investor as an anchor in preparation for its listing. 2) Corporate Governance: As the Company prepares for its IPO, IFC's Corporate Governance Advisory Service may add value, ensuring that the Company has the necessary requirements to become a publicly listed entity. 3) The transaction will be the second transaction with C2C in 2016 and will be a cornerstone in forging a long-term partnership with C2C, a successful investment platform managed by two businessmen in South Africa. 4) A review by IFC's E&S appraisal adds prestige and improvements to Bounty's credentials and facilitates discussions with socially-minded investors. In addition, the proposed transaction is intended to transfer IFC's experience and knowledge base to the private sector, which will be utilized for future transaction opportunities

project_description: IFC is investing up to US$50 million in an investment consortium which is acquiring a controlling stake in Grupo Los Grobo LLC (“GLG” or “the Group”), a diversified agribusiness company operating in Argentina and involved in: (i) the manufacturing of crop-protection inputs, (ii) agri-inputs distribution, (iii) grain origination, storage and logistics services, (iv) farming, and (v) milling. The use of proceeds will be to refinance debt and gain working capital fire power in order to be ready to capture expected growth opportunities in the Argentine agribusiness sector and acquire the shareholding stakes of some minority shareholders.
sponsor_shareholders: The main sponsors are: (i) Victoria Capital Partners (VCP), a private equity management firm focused on PE investments in South America which is leading the investment consortium, and (ii) members of the Grobocopatel family. The investment consortium is comprised of IFC, Victoria South American Partners II LP (a fund managed by VCP), and other VCP co-investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at about US$230 million. The proposed IFC Investment is a US$50 million equity investment for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Grupo Los Grobo is headquartered in the City of Carlos Casares, in the Province of Buenos Aires, and has over 20 agri-inputs points of sales and grain storage facilities throughout the country. GLG’s crop protection manufacturing facility is located in the City of Zarate, in the Province of Buenos Aires.
