The first phase aims to test the Company’s forestry model by developing up to 40,000 ha of sustainably managed eucalyptus plantations and establishing its operational base in the country in 2014-2016 (“Project”). IFC is working closely with the Company to provide advisory support at this critical early stage of the Project. The second commercial phase of the Project will comprise the establishment of commercial scale eucalyptus plantations, roll out of agriculture partnerships and construction of a 1.5 million ton pulp mill and a biomass power generation plant by 2023. The government has awarded the Company the land use rights to 356,000 hectares of land, roughly two-thirds of which will be used for forestry activities. Among the development priorities of the Project is improving conditions for agriculture on the remaining land and creating well-functioning agribusiness supply chains to link smallholders with markets. As such, the Project is positioned to become the first integrated eucalyptus plantations, agriculture, pulp and energy project in Mozambique. The objective of the proposed IFC investment is to support the development of this transformational opportunity to help create an inclusive agro-forestry project in Mozambique.
sponsor_shareholders: Incorporated in Mozambique in 2009, the Company is a fully owned subsidiary of Portucel Soporcel Group (“Portucel”), the leading European manufacturer of printing and writing paper and Europe''s leading manufacturer, and one of the largest producers in the world, of bleached eucalyptus kraft pulp. Portucel also produces wood biomass-based energy for internal consumption and for sale to the grid, a model it intends to follow in Mozambique. The group exports pulp and paper to 120 countries. Portucel is listed as Portucel S.A on the Euronext Lisbon and is controlled by Semapa group. It is headquartered in Setubal, Portugal, and has 2,258 employees. Portucel is a recognized leader of sustainability in Portugal and Europe, with 120,000 ha of FSC and PEFC certified eucalyptus plantations under management. With 55 years of experience in pulp and paper sector and a strong financial performance trend, the group has extensive sector expertise and a strong consumer market position.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated total project cost of US$125 million will be funded with equity from Portucel and IFC. IFC will invest up to US$25 million in the common shares of the Company, representing roughly 20% of the Company’s total share capital.
location_description: The Project will be rolled out in two provinces of Mozambique, Zambezia (Ile and Namarrói districts) and Manica (Manica, Mossurize, Sussundenga, Báruè and Gondola districts). The locations were selected on the basis of soil and climate conditions, to ensure adequate levels of productivity, and potential to provide adequate logistic solutions for access to pulp mill and ports, and followed an open and transparent concession process. The Company is headquartered in Maputo.
development_impact: Portucel''s investment in the under-developed rural regions of Mozambique lays the foundation for a far greater and expansive development of the regions and of industry over the next 12 years. While mega-projects in the mining and energy production sectors in Mozambique may be limited in their ability to impact employment creation and productivity spillovers, the Project will create rural jobs and have a significant multiplier effect, thus broadening the economic base of the country. - Employment: generating at least 2,000 direct and indirect rural jobs during the first phase and up to 6,500 additional jobs once the second phase has been fully implemented; - Smallholder Farmers'' Benefits: reaching over 150,000 rural poor, and with complementary public investment by IFC and the World Bank in agriculture and agribusiness development, improving livelihoods for 23,000 farmer households; - MSME Development Catalyst: promoting development of an estimated 100 MSMEs as suppliers of goods and services to the company, including through training and outgrower component imbedded in the Company''s business model; - Infrastructure Development: developing several types of infrastructure, including secondary and forest roads, and - during the second phase - a port, that will encourage economic integration; - Training and Demonstration: encouraging knowledge transfer by providing trainings to local employees, supporting forestry programs in Universities and integrating agriculture extension services to local farmers in the Company''s business model; - Increasing Country''s Competitiveness through Economic Diversification: Despite the Government''s targets, Mozambique''s forest products sector potential remains unrealized. Successful implementation will encourage additional investment and stimulate forest products sector development, and provide the much-needed diversification to the local economy and additional source of forex earnings to the budget.
additionality: - Environmental and Social Standards: Through its emerging market experience in sustainable forestry projects and its participation in large-scale plantation and pulp and paper investments globally, IFC is well placed to assist Portucel with advice on environmental and social sustainability, including development of a comprehensive ESIA and an Environmental and Social action plan to mitigate the potential negative and enhance the positive impacts of the Project. - Catalytic Role: As one of the largest agribusiness investors on the continent, IFC will play a key role - as a shareholder in the Project company - in promoting agriculture development in the areas of the Project influence. IFC will seek to invest in commercial agriculture projects with substantial out-grower and demonstration components. In addition to catalysing private sector activity through direct investment, IFC will work closely with IBRD and development partners to (i) take advantage of and enhance their ongoing activities in the sector in Mozambique and (ii) develop new joint World Bank Group interventions in agribusiness and forestry, such as in the area of smallholder commercialization. - Advisory Support: IFC is already implementing a custom-tailored advisory project, which will help the Company to develop and operationalize a comprehensive land access policy and design a multi-year stakeholder engagement and community development strategy. The objective of the community development programs would be to empower local communities, smallholder farmers, and small and medium enterprises to take maximum advantage of the economic opportunities created by the Project and to improve livelihoods. - Risk Mitigation: IFC participation will provide comfort and political risk mitigation to Portucel as they embark on this substantial and expansive multi-year project in an unfamiliar market vulnerable to political uncertainty

project_description: The Project is to provide an A Loan of up to US$40 million and an MCPP Loan of up to US$20 million to support the capital expenditure and working capital needs of New Hope Singapore Holdings (Private) Ltd. (New Hope Singapore or the Company) for its expansion in Southeast Asia (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: New Hope Singapore is the holding company for New Hope’s agribusiness in Southern and Southeast Asia (SSEA). It currently has operations in eight countries and is involved in feed production and poultry operations. The Project Sponsor is New Hope Liuhe Co., Ltd. (China) (NH Liuhe). NH Liuhe is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (Stock Code: 000876.SZ). The Company is wholly owned by NH Liuhe.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated to be US$450 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$40 million A Loan for IFC’s own account and a US$20m MCPP Loan.
location_description: The Project will be located in several selected SSEA countries including: Indonesia, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam, Philippines, Nepal and India.
development_impact: The development impact of the Project is expected to include (i) improved food security through increased efficiency in the supply chain, (ii) increased reach to farmers, mainly small independent players, in regions where the economy relies heavily on agriculture, (iii) support of competitive economic activity in IDA countries, (iv) South-South known-how transfer in animal protein, (v) direct and indirect job creation, and (vi) increased tax revenues.
additionality: IFC''s expected role and additionally includes: (i) Long-term Partnership: continued support to a competitive IFC client investing South-South in IDA in a systemically strategic sector, (ii) Longer Tenors: IFC''s long-term loan will enable the Company to better match its funding with the payback period of the Project and maintain a solid financial structure while increasing the size and scope of its operations, (iii) Global Knowledge: through the provision of multi-country financing, IFC is sharing international best practices and providing global comparators and benchmarks to New Hope Singapore, including advise on environmental and insurance matters.

project_description: Established in 1994 by Mr. Kairat Mazhibayev and Mr.Erken Koshkinbayev, RG Brands LLP (RG Brands or the “Company”) is a leading branded consumer products company in Kazakhstan. It produces and distributes the following products: (i) fruit juice and water; (ii) UHT milk; (iii) packaged tea and potato chips and (iv) PepsiCo and Pepsi-Lipton International franchised products. The proposed corporate loan will be utilized for partial refinancing of the Company’s bank debt, working capital financing and capital expenditures (collectively, the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project''s Sponsors are Mr. Mazhibayev and Mr. Koshkinbayev (the “Sponsors”), reputable Kazakh businessmen. Mr. Mazhibaev owns a 61.5% stake of the Company, Mr. Koshkinbaev owns a 35.5% stake and the remaining 3% is owned by the management of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at around $ 45 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $30 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Headquartered in Almaty, RG Brands has three operating facilities: Almaty, Almaty region (Aksengir) and one facility located in Kostanay, a city in northern Kazakhstan.
development_impact: The Project will have following development impact: (i) Creating and preserving direct and indirect jobs; (ii) Supporting food security and availability; (iii) Strengthening linkages with dairy farmers; (iv) Increasing tax payments for the Government.
additionality: IFC expected role and additionality will include: (i) Long-term partnership: RG Brands aims to grow internationally and values IFC as a long-term partner; (ii) Advisory services: IFC will explore areas of the advisory support to the Company, particularly related to the energy efficiency and supply chain linkages; (iii) Standard-setting in Environmental & Social issues: IFC''s expertise in Environmental & Social areas will provide additional value to the Company.

project_description: The project is the development of commercial real estate properties which will include office, retail and warehouse space in the Minsk region of Belarus (the Project). The Project sponsor is the Belarusian construction company - A-100. The Project implementing and operating company is Eterika ALC.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Eterika ALC a leading Belarusian construction company focused on developing commercial property and affordable housing projects in Belarus. The Company owns and operates a portfolio of mixed-use property assets. Eterika is 95% owned by the Company’s founder Mr. Alexander Tsenter. The balance (5%) is owned by Ms. Nadezhda Matveenok. Mr. Tsenter is a well-established businessman who also owns A-100, the leading chain of gas stations in the country.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$74 million. IFC''s participation is sought to provide an A loan of up to US$20 million.
location_description: The greenfield project will be located in the Minsk region of Belarus.
development_impact: - Improving business infrastructure- the stock of quality commercial real-estate in Belarus remains limited and the project will reduce the existing demand-supply gap. - Demonstration effect: by supporting a local private provider IFC will contribute to the development of real estate sector and raise its attractiveness to private investors; - Employment Generation: The Project will create significant number of new direct positions. Temporary employment will also be provided to local labor during the design and construction phase. Commercial real estate projects will also support indirect employment with a multiplier effect along the supply chain. - Increased tax revenues- the Project will lead to increased tax revenues to local and federal authorities. - IS-AS cooperation- the Client is interested to work with IFC''s Green Building Specialist to explore opportunities for energy efficiency. In parallel A-100 is considering engaging IFC''s Corporate Governance team as it recognizes the need to strengthen CG as it evolves from a closely held family business into a holding.
additionality: - Provision of long-term financing- Not available in the local markets, long-term financing from IFC will enable the Client to proceed timely with the Project and moderately leverage the business; - Risk mitigation- IFC knowledge of the retail sector is important in assessing the feasibility of this Project. IFC''s financial structuring expertise will ensure that the Project is bankable and the risks are properly mitigated. - Environment and social standard setting- IFC will advise the Company on the necessary actions that will facilitate the Company''s compliance with IFC E&S guidelines and international best practice.

project_description: Kaymu Eurasia is an Online Marketplace that enables businesses and consumers to offer their goods for sale online and end customers to research, compare prices and purchase online. This venture was initiated by Rocket Internet GmbH (“RI”), a global online venture builder. Kaymu Eurasia has identified IFC as a potential strategic partner in its endeavor to significantly expand its e-commerce footprint in Eastern Europe and Central Asia and has invited IFC to provide equity capital to support its growth (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Rocket Internet (“Sponsor” or “RI”), one of world’s most successful global online venture builders, was started in 2005 by entrepreneurs Alexander, Marc and Oliver Samwer. RI has incubated more than 100 fast growing online companies all over the world since inception and is currently located in more than 25 international branch offices on all 5 continents. RI’s portfolio companies are present in more than 40 countries and generate more than US$2.5 billion in revenues.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is comprised of an up to €10 million equity investment in Kaymu Eurasia.
location_description: The Project will support the development of Kaymu’s operations in Eastern Europe and Central Asia.
development_impact: The Project''s expected development impacts include: (i) job creation in the areas of marketing and IT services and indirectly through supply chains, logistics, and other supporting services; (ii) transfer of technology by replicating proven internet business concepts in emerging markets with the goal of turning its ventures into local/regional market leading companies in the online retail space; and (iii) benefit to consumers in frontier regions and secondary cities through more choices, lower prices and convenient service with home delivery.
additionality: IFC additionality will manifest itself through (i) the strategic long-term partnership IFC can build by playing a catalytic role, particularly in the regions where equity capital funds are less readily available in particular in IDA countries (ii) political/country risk mitigation in the more difficult environments; (iii) the stamp of approval IFC can provide at time of exit.

project_description: Usina Delta S.A. (“Delta” or the “Company”), is a sugar and ethanol company, based in Minas Gerais, Brazil, that operates three mills with a combined sugarcane crushing capacity of 10.5 million tons. In the season ended in March 2013, the Company produces about 500,000 tons of very high polarity sugar, about 230,000 tons of crystal sugar, about 250,000 m3 of ethanol (sold mainly for use as fuel to substitute petroleum derivatives for motor vehicles) and about 330 MWh of electricity per year through bagasse-fueled co-generation, most of which is sold to outside parties. The proposed IFC Loan entails providing a tranched corporate facility of US$ 80 million with final loan maturities expected to be between 7 and 9 years. This facility is composed of a senior loan of US$ 40 million from IFC''s own account, a syndicated loan of US$ 20 million, and US$20 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program. The Loan is part of a financing package for Delta’s 3-year capital improvement program. During this period Delta’s investments include cogeneration capacity expansion, industrial upgrades as well as sugarcane replanting and treatment (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Delta started operations in October 2012 as a spin-off of Usina Caete S.A. (“Caete”), a player in the sugar and ethanol industry since 1965. Caete was founded by Mr. Carlos Lyra in the state of Alagoas (the Northeast of Brazil). Robert Lyra is Carlos Lyra’s son and he is the owner of the Company. Mr. Robert Lyra has more than 36 years of experience in the sugar and ethanol business.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total investment program is estimated at BRL 510 million and comprises planting and maintaining cane, acquisition of agri-machinery, construction of new co-generation facility, and investment in industrial and storage facilities.
location_description: Delta Group currently has three mills located in a geographically concentrated cluster in the “Triângulo Mineiro” region of southwestern Minais Gerais state. The location is strategic as it is surrounded by cane planting areas and has good access to roads and railroads to reach either Sao Paulo (ethanol) or Santos Port (sugar exports).
development_impact: The most relevant development impacts are expected to be on climate change mitigation and on assisting communities in frontier regions. The effect on climate change mitigation will come from the co-generation investment, which will be enough to power a city with 180,000 people, thereby promoting the use of renewable energy in a country with expanding demand. The frontier region supported by the investment is Cerrado region. The Project will foster economic development in the Cerrado by increasing agricultural production and creating jobs in areas which are highly dependent on the agricultural sector for income generation.
additionality: The long-term funding provided by IFC is not readily available in the local market, and is needed to support the Company''s investment program. IFC''s role will also be to promote its E&S standards though Delta''s social programs (health and education, among others) to the local community and support the Company in the adoption of best environmental practices by applying IFC performance standards. IFC will also provide its expertise to help the Company to develop better corporate governance and build a succession plan.

project_description: Cargills Foods Company (Private) Limited (“CFPL” / “Company”) plans to raise upto US$20 million from IFC through a primary purchase of shares of CFPL. In addition to capitalizing the Company, the proceeds are expected to be partly utilized to fund the expansion of the Company’s retail business and partly utilized for pay down of debt by CFPL.
sponsor_shareholders: CFPL is a wholly owned subsidiary of CCPLC, a listed company on the Colombo Stock Exchange with a market capitalization of US$258 million as of July 24, 2014. CT Holdings PLC owns 70% of CCPLC and the total percentage of shares held by public per the March 2014 Annual Report is 20.48%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Company’s total project cost is approximately US$75 million for the period FY14-FY16. In addition to capitalizing the Company, the funds would be used for (i) expansion of the Company’s retail stores during this 3 year period and ii) deleveraging the Company by pay down of debt. IFC will be investing upto US$20 million in common shares of CFPL.
location_description: The stores are located in various parts of Sri Lanka with a majority of the stores expected to be in areas outside the western province.
development_impact: - Maintain and create jobs in the growing retail sector: The Group''s retail business currently employs 5,300 employees and the Project is expected to create significant jobs as the Company increases capacity. Majority of the workforce is expected to be employed from the local communities thereby contributing to community development. - Improvement in the quality of life and fostering inclusive growth: The Project will contribute towards bringing better quality food products at low prices to post conflict areas in Sri Lanka thereby fostering better life quality and inclusive growth across socio-economic strata. - Development of local supply chains: The Project would increase the number of and volumes from local suppliers, provide additional sales channels for local producers and importers and effectively contribute towards strengthening the retail eco-system relating to efficiencies and operating standards. - Increase in farmer reach: The Company procures fresh produce from 8,000 farmers across the country on a daily basis at a fixed price leading to predictable demand and pricing for farmers. The Project is expected to increase its reach to farmers through increased demand for end products.
additionality: - Long term capital provider: IFC will provide the Company long term equity capital in a market that is witnessing dearth of long term debt and equity financing. - Equity mobilization through Stamp of Approval: The proposed IFC investment will serve as an IFC Stamp of Approval to the Company''s operations, growth potential and Sri Lanka as an investment destination. It will play a catalytic role in raising further equity from other institutional investors. - Sector knowledge sharing: IFC will share its knowledge of global retail operational best practices with the Company as it implements the Project and improves efficiencies in its existing operations.

project_description: Nidera is a global trader of agricultural commodities (including oilseeds, grains and biofuels) and a producer of seeds and crop protection products with operations in 18 major exporting and importing countries; distribution to over 60 countries. Nidera is seeking to launch the second phase of an expansion plan (started in 2009) to continue to grow its grain/oilseeds origination and infrastructure platform in Latin America (Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay), Eastern Europe (Russia, Kazakhstan, and Romania) and North America (U.S.) and thus seeking a capital increase to fund its plans. COFCO Corporation (“COFCO”), through its subsidiary, has entered into an agreement with Nidera to subscribe primary shares to support the above expansion plan and also acquire secondary shares from existing shareholders, which would result in COFCO getting 51% shareholding in Nidera. IFC is invited to co-invest with COFCO, HOPU Fund and other investors into Nidera.
sponsor_shareholders: Nidera has been privately owned by different shareholder groups. Post COFCO acquisition, the existing shareholders will have 49% shareholding collectively. COFCO is a state-owned enterprise headquartered in Beijing. It is a leading agribusiness company, and food supplier and services company in China, with revenues of US$31 billion (in 2013) and with several listed subsidiaries. COFCO is a new client for IFC. HOPU Fund is a private equity fund with investments in public and private assets and companies. COFCO, HOPU Fund, IFC and other investors will collectively have 51% shareholding after closing of the COFCO investment in Nidera.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: COFCO, through its subsidiary, entered into an agreement with Nidera and its shareholders to own a 51% shareholding in Nidera including subscription to primary shares and acquisition of secondary shares from existing family shareholders. The propose IFC investment is up to US$ 60 million equity with effective indirect minority shareholding in Nidera through a holding company jointly held by COFCO, HOPU and other international investor(s).
location_description: Nidera is headquartered in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, and has operations in 18 countries spanning South America, North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, including Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, Netherlands, Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Romania, China, India, U.S. and Australia.
development_impact: - The new global agri trading platform will improve efficiencies of global food supply chains with expected synergies and economies of scales and scopes, and increase competition and efficiency of the global agri trading landscape dominated by large global agri traders. - Contribute to food security: Part of the investment will be fresh capital to support agri logistics and infrastructure projects in Brazil, Eastern Europe and US, providing farmers better access to market and farm inputs (seeds), and leading to more supply of agri commodities. -Employment generation in multiple developing countries under the Project.
additionality: - Industry Expertise & Local Presence: IFC''s global industry knowledge and local presence add value to the new platform. - Improvement of E&S best practices: IFC will assist the new integrated platform with further development and implementation of E&S management system and monitor progress in establishing best E&S practice along its supply chains. - Sustainable South-South investments: IFC will support COFCO for sustainable overseas investments in global food supply chains, enhancing E&S and economic impacts and setting examples for sustainable Chinese overseas investments. - IFC participation helps strengthen corporate governance and will benefit the post-acquisition company with stamp of approval in the marketplace.

project_description: The Project involves providing a long term loan of up to US$25 million to JV LLC Nyva Pereyaslavschyny (“Nyva” or the “Company”), a large industrial pig and grain producer in Ukraine, to support the Company’s expansion plans in Ukraine and refinance its medium term debt.
sponsor_shareholders: Nyva is one of the leading vertically integrated pig producers in Ukraine, operating 7 pig production complexes and farming 22,000 ha of land. Nyva is owned by Mr. Oleksandr Mostipan, a Ukrainian businessman.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$75 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$25 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The expansion project is located in a rural area of the Kyiv region in Ukraine.
development_impact: The proposed investment will support a leading pork producer with significant linkages to the economy of rural areas. Its expansion will help to create business opportunities for local MSMEs, as well as generate employment in processing facilities and in the controlled retail network, with a significant portion of positions likely to be held by women. Debt refinancing will help the Company strengthen its balance sheet in the expectation of possible economic shocks.
additionality: (i) Long term financing: Provide long-term financing otherwise not available at reasonable commercial terms during a time of economic instability. IFC's long term loan would help smoothen the Company's debt servicing during an expansion phase; (ii) Global expertise: Share global experience in livestock production through coordinated investment and advisory services. (iii) Strategic Advice: IFC would promote corporate governance and reporting standards through informal and formal support. This is particularly important to the Company through its next phase of development.

project_description: Noble Agri is Noble Group’s fully-owned subsidiary in agribusiness, with origination, processing and distribution of grains and oilseeds, sugar and ethanol, and other soft commodities (cotton, cocoa, coffee) trading. It is a global agriculture commodities company operating through 60 offices around the world, including Brazil, China, Argentina, Eastern Europe, India and South Africa. In April 2014, COFCO Corporation (“COFCO”), the leading agribusiness group in China, through its subsidiary entered into agreement with Noble Group to buy 51% shareholding in Noble Agri through secondary purchase, and create a joint-venture trading platforms to capitalize on potential synergies across the supply chain with COFCO. IFC is invited to co-invest with COFCO, HOPU Fund and other investors into Noble Agri.
sponsor_shareholders: Noble Group is a leading global supply chain manager of agricultural and energy products, metals and minerals. Noble Group was founded by Mr. Richard Samuel Elman in 1986 and listed on the Singapore Exchange Limited in March 1997. It has headquarters in Hong Kong. Noble Group’s major shareholders include Noble holding Ltd (deemed interest by Mr. Richard Elman) of 20.8% stake and China Investment Corporation (14%). IFC currently has a US$23 million exposure (loan) to Noble Argentina. COFCO is a state-owned enterprise headquartered in Beijing. It is a leading agribusiness company, and food supplier and services company in China, with annual revenues of US$31 billion and with several listed subsidiaries. COFCO is a new IFC client. HOPU Fund is a private equity fund with investments in public and private assets and companies. COFCO, HOPU Fund, IFC and other investors will collectively have 51% shareholding after closing of the COFCO investment in Noble Agri.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total consideration of COFCO’s secondary purchase of 51% shareholding in Noble Agri is estimated at approximately US$1.5 billion. The propose IFC investment is up to US$80 million equity with indirect minority shareholding in Noble Agri through a holding company jointly held by COFCO, HOPU Fund and other international investors.
location_description: Noble Agri is headquartered in Hong Kong, and has with over 60 offices covering South America, Africa, Europe, India, Asia, and Australia.
development_impact: - The new global agri trading platform will improve efficiencies of global food supply chains with expected synergies and economies of scales and scopes, and increase competition and efficiency of the global agri trading landscape dominated by large global agri traders. - Contribute to food security - The COFCO acquisition will enable Noble Agri to access capital support for its investment program on agri logistics and infrastructure, providing farmers better access to market and farm inputs and leading to more supply of agri commodities. - Turnaround of under utilized assets of Noble Agri. - Employment generation in multiple developing countries under Noble Agri''s investment program supported by COFCO partnership.
additionality: - Industry Expertise & Local Presence: IFC''s global industry knowledge and local presence add value to the new platform. - Improvement of E&S best practices: IFC will assist the new integrated platform with further development and implementation of E&S management system and monitor progress in establishing best E&S practice along its supply chains. - Sustainable South-South investments: IFC will support COFCO for sustainable overseas investments in global food supply chains, enhancing E&S and economic impacts and setting examples for sustainable Chinese overseas investments. - IFC participation helps strengthen corporate governance and will benefit the post-acquisition company with stamp of approval in the marketplace.

project_description: The project consists of a 3-year Risk Sharing Facility (RSF) for a portfolio of up to ETB 300M (approx. USD 15.2M) working capital loans to coffee farmer cooperatives, originated and serviced by NIB Bank in cooperation with Technoserve (TNS). The loan will enable the farmer cooperatives to buy “cherry” coffee to process into “washed” coffee. Under the RSF, IFC will assume [60]% of the credit risk on the portfolio, up to a maximum IFC exposure of ETB 180M (approx. USD 9M). The remainder would be covered by Nib Bank.
sponsor_shareholders: TechnoServe is a reputable international NGO with 40 years of experience in rural economic development. It operates in 30 countries across Africa, Latin America and Asia and is active in agricultural sectors including coffee, horticulture, dairy, tea, cocoa and cashew. Technoserve is funded by various public and private donors including the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, USAID, and Rockefeller Foundation. NIB is a licensed commercial bank in Ethiopia with interest in expanding its agribusiness portfolio especially to small farmers producing coffee, Ethiopia’s main export commodity. It is the 4th largest private sector bank in the country by size of equity, and it currently operates 86 branches across Ethiopia. IFC’s exposure will be to farmer cooperatives most of which are legally incorporated in Ethiopia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total size of the financing program or maximum portfolio balance will be of ETB 300M. IFC’s participation will be in the form of a Risk Sharing Facility with a maximum risk amount of ETB 180M (60% of the overall portfolio).
location_description: The Project targets coffee farmers in rural areas of Ethiopia, especially Jimma and Limmu. Processing of the “cherry” coffee would take place in wet mills located in these rural areas. After processing, the “washed” parchment coffee will be transported to warehouses of the Coffee Service Providers (“CSP”) in Addis Ababa, for dry milling and packaging for exports as “washed” green bean coffee.
development_impact: The Project is expected to continue to have the following development impact: (i) Strengthen the competitiveness of the Ethiopian coffee sector; (ii) Support economic livelihoods in the Ethiopian coffee supply chains, particularly small farmers and household labor; (iii) Develop a commercially sustainable model of long-term and short-term financing for the Ethiopian coffee supply chain, with potential for expansion to other countries/sectors dominated by small scale suppliers; (iv) Establish the credit worthiness of selected cooperatives; Indicators to be tracked include: Farmers Reached, MSMEs Reached, Employment and Female Employment, Number of wet mills financed, and Volume of coffee processed annually by financed cooperatives.
additionality: Local currency financing: IFC provides a credit enhancement structure that allows coffee farmer cooperatives to access local currency working capital financing that is not otherwise available to them. Long-term partnerships: IFC build long term partnership with Nib Bank that encourages the bank and potentially new banks to support the coffee sector in Ethiopia. Stamp of Approval: IFC provides a stamp of approval that attracts other investors to take the risk of financing farmer cooperatives in Ethiopia for coffee and other crops. Financial structuring and Advisory Services: IFC advises Nib Bank and other participating banks on how to structure innovative and creative facilities to finance smallholder farmers and mitigate risks. IFC Access to Finance provides capacity building support to the participating banks alongside the IFC investment. Environmental and social standards/implementation: IFC introduces best practices in environmental risk management to the farmer cooperatives.

project_description: IFC is considering a $60 million investment to be allocated to Smithfield Romania (“SFR” or the “Company”) and its subsidiaries, Smithfield Ferme (“Ferme”) and Smithfield Prod (“Prod”). SFR, a wholly owned subsidiary of Smithfield Foods, is the largest hog producer and fresh pork processor in Romania, producing about 1 million pigs in 2013. SFR, which sells its fresh pork meat and semi processed pork meat under the Comtim brand, controls about 54 farms and a modern pork meat processing plant. SFR’s operations are fully integrated from hog production to meat processing. IFC’s funds will go towards the restructuring of SFR’s loans to facilitate long-term financing, optimize its capital structure, and support SFR’s growth plans to expand its farms and processing facilities in Romania.
sponsor_shareholders: SFR is wholly owned by Smithfield Foods, a global food company with operations in 13 countries through wholly-owned subsidiaries and joined ventures. Headquartered in Smithfield, Virginia, US, the company produces more than 50 brands of pork, beef and turkey products and more than 200 gourmet foods. Smithfield Foods is the world’s largest producer and processor of pork.. In 2013, Smithfield Foods was bought by Shuanghui (now named WH Group), a Chinese meat processing company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC financing will be directed to support the Company’s long term investment needs and optimizing its capital structure. IFC is considering an investment of up to $60 million which will be structured as a corporate finance facility.
location_description: Both Ferme and Prod are headquartered in the city of Timisoara, with facilities in various locations primarily in the Timis and Arad counties in Romania.
development_impact: The proposed investment is expected to have the following developmental impacts: (1) Demonstration effect: IFC will support an efficient producer with solid track record to expand high international standards of livestock production and animal welfare practices to other pork producers; (2) Increased reach to farmers through the Company''s planned addition of contracted farms, critical in a country where the economy relies on agriculture; (3) Improved food safety through implementation of highest food safety and E&S standards; and (4) Job creation and increased tax income for the government as a result of growth of operations and enhanced profitability.
additionality: IFC''s role in this investment is expected to have a strong additionality through: (1) IFC will be supporting a competitive and standard-setting client by strengthening the Sponsor''s operations in Romania and helping the company achieve its future growth plan and further improve its cost competitiveness; (2) IFC will provide long term, local currency debt which is not readily available in the market; (3) IFC will help the Company to mobilize additional debt financing with local banks in a challenging financing environment; and (4) IFC will leverage its agribusiness and structuring experience in developing the Project with selected local banks.

sector: Soap and Cleaning Compound (Soap, Detergent, etc.)
project_description: IFC is proposing an equity investment in a proposed Joint Venture Project (“Project”) to set-up a soap manufacturing operation in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The proposed Project initially involves importing palm oil based soap noodles produced by Musim Mas Group (“MM” or the “Group”) in Indonesia, value adding and packaging these soap noodles into soap bars in the proposed plant, to be sold in the Ethiopian market, with the possibility of exporting to neighboring countries.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project will be led by Musim Mas Group (“MM” or the “Group”). MM is a fully integrated palm oil corporation with operations spanning the entire palm oil value chain from upstream palm oil plantations to midstream and downstream operations such as kernel crushing, refining and manufacturing of specialty fats, biodiesel, oleochemicals, soap, palm wax and fine chemicals. MM operates globally and has its corporate headquarters are in Singapore. MM is fully owned by the Karim family who are the founders of the Group. A new Joint Venture Project Company (“JV Co”) to be incorporated in Ethiopia and will be sponsored by MM and its local partner; Luxury and Popular Trading Plc. (an Ethiopian general trading and distributing company), with MM owning the larger stake. Another minority shareholder may be brought on board. IFC proposes to take a minority (<20%) equity stake in the JV Co.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$7.5 million. The proposed IFC equity investment in the JV Co is c.US$1.2M on IFC’s account.
location_description: The Project will be located in Oromiya State, Duukam Industrial Zone, Ethiopia.
development_impact: 1. Add value to the Ethiopia economy by moving from import model to local soap production operation which provides direct and indirect employment to the local community and contributes to the government revenue 2. Bring FDI into Ethiopia, thereby encouraging other foreign investments to the country 3. Transfer of knowledge and know-how on soap-making 4. Introduction of international standards in corporate governance including financial management 5. Foster increased competition and quality in the Ethiopian soap industry through the addition of high-quality soap production facilities in Ethiopia
additionality: 1. IFC additionality includes the following a) political risk mitigation; b) honest broker role between the client and the local partners; c) local market knowledge; and d) access to local financial markets through existing relationships with financial intermediaries 2. This is the client''s first investment in Africa - if this works out and the client expands across Africa, IFC can leverage our presence and market knowledge across the continent 3. IFC can add value by helping Musim Mas Group expand in other IDA countries outside Africa

sector: Computer & Electronic Products(Computers & Peripherals, Communications Equip., Elec. Watches & Similar Elec. Products. Integrated Circuits & the application of Miniturization Technologies characterize this sector.)
project_description: IFC is considering to invest up to US$20 million convertible loan (“C Loan”) in Hollysys Automation Technologies Limited (“Hollysys” or the “Company”). The proceeds will be used to strengthen the Company’s capital structure.
sponsor_shareholders: Hollysys is a leading provider of automation and control technologies and products in China and increasingly, Southeast Asia and the Middle East. Founded in 1993 and headquartered in Beijing, the Company is listed in NASDAQ and has over 3,500 employees. Mr. Changli WANG, the founder and the largest shareholder of Hollysys, is holding 16.37% of the Company as of August 30th, 2013.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a US$20 million C Loan which will be used to strengthen the Company’ s capital structure.
location_description: Beijing, China
development_impact: 1) Industry upgrade for better productivity and quality: The successful implementation of the Project will help China to upgrade its industry for better quality products with increased productivity by adopting more automation systems in the production process., helping address increasing wage costs. 2) Access to better infrastructure: The Project will increase assess to better infrastructure, namely high speed rail (HSR), at lower cost for the mass population. 3) Employment generation: The Project is expected to create employment opportunities both direct and indirect employment along the value chain. 4) Energy saving and environment protection: The project will also promote energy saving and environment protection in China as automation systems will help to increase energy utilization and reduce emissions.
additionality: 1) Help a medium sized company to grow: The Project will help IFC to establish long-term partnership with Hollysys which has the potential and ambition to grow from a medium sized company into a leading global player in the field of automation. 2) Stamp of Approval: IFC''s investment in the Company will provide a "Stamp of Approval" from an internationally recognized institution and help Hollysys develop overseas market. Given IFC''s global knowledge and extensive networks, IFC can help the Company to expand its overseas business and collaborate with the Company on potential South-South transactions going forward 3) Environmental and Social Good Practices: IFC will provide guidance on setting and implementing standards for E&S practices.

company_name: Guangxi Fenglin Wood Industry Group Co., Ltd.
sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: The Project is to provide a $30m A Loan RMB equivalent to support Guangxi Fenglin Wood Industry Group Co., Ltd. (“Fenglin” or the “Company”), an IFC existing client, to support certain expenditure associated with its medium-density fiberboard (MDF) operation in Mingyang, Guangxi and its particle board operation in Huizhou, Guangdong.
sponsor_shareholders: Fenglin was listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (Stock Code: 601996) on September 29, 2011. It is headquartered in Nanning, and has operations in Guangxi and Guangdong Provinces. The Project Sponsor is Mr. Yichuan Liu, the founder and the biggest shareholder of the Company. The current shareholding structure of the Company is: (i) Fenglin International Limited. 53.94%; (ii) IFC 2.92%; (iii) Nanning Fengcheng Investment Management Co. 4.22%; and (iv) Public float 38.92%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated to be US$79 million. The proposed IFC investment is a RMB equivalent of US$30 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project will be located at Nanning, Guangxi Autonomous Region, a frontier region in China, and Huizhou, Guangdong Province.
development_impact: 1. Sustainable natural resources management: As Fenglin invested in upstream forestry operations, it is committed to adopting best practices and standards in forestry operations. Part of its plantations were already FSC-certified, and it is committing to adopt Controlled Wood Certification for the rest of its plantation. This will be a significant development impact in Fenglin''s wood supply chain. Fenglin is also producing some of its panels at the FSC-certified standard, which is expected to have an important demonstration effect in the wood product sector in China. 2. Job creation in frontier region It is expected that Fenglin will create more than 200 direct jobs (based on the projected ramp up size of the plant) and additional indirect jobs in MSMEs through the support services to its plants. These jobs will benefit local livelihoods in a poor area of an interior province. 3. Local wood sourcing Fenglin had a total production capacity of 500,000m3 in 2012. In 2013, it has established Mingyang Plant (200,000m3) and has acquired Huizhou plant (200,000m3), and has arrived with a total production capacity of 850,000m3. It is expected that Fenglin will double its local wood sourcing to about 1.28 million tons from the farmers when the two new plants ramp up. 4. Sustainable products Fenglin''s products have received CARB certification (California Air Resources Board) and have reached China''s national standard of E0/E1, both are the highest standards for toxic control from formaldehyde. It is expected that the Project will help Fenglin promote the sustainable, lower emission panel products to the market.
additionality: 1. Support a low cost, high quality and environmentally-friendly panel producer IFC will continue to support the sustainable growth of a strong player in China''s wood panel industry. Fenglin is a disciplined company focusing on product quality and resource efficiency. IFC''s support will help strengthen the Company''s position as a possible consolidator in the industry . 2. Frontier region investment and catalytic role Although Guangxi Province has been growing in the past 10 years, it is still one of the poorest provinces in southern China and local investment activities are still limited compared with other regions. IFC''s investment in the Project would demonstrate investors'' confidence in the Company''s growth in Guangxi, and enhance its visibility for its expected secondary issue in the capital market. 3. Industry expertise IFC''s wide ranging experience in forestry, plantations and wood products investment will be a valuable resource for the Company as it continues to grow. IFC industry specialist has strongly encouraged the Company to formulate a long-term wood supply strategy, which will strength the Company''s long term competitiveness in the market. 4. Long-term financing and capital market development IFC will provide long-term local currency debt financing that suits the cash flow cycle of the Project. To provide the local currency financing, IFC will utilize the new RMB product approved by the People''s Bank of China, promoting the development of onshore-offshore RMB capital market. 5. Environmental & social best practice IFC will continue to help Fenglin improve its capacity in environment and social management systems as well as sustainable natural resource management. IFC will continue to provide guidance and technical support to Fenglin to further improve its wood sourcing and panel manufacturing.
Company Name: Guangxi Fenglin Wood Industry Group Co., Ltd.

project_description: IFC is considering a potential investment consisting of debt and/or equity in Ballarpur International Graphic Paper Holdings (BIGPH), a company incorporated in the Netherlands. BIGPH owns subsidiaries which are leading pulp and paper manufacturers in India and Malaysia. BIGPH is a step-down subsidiary of Ballarpur Industries Limited (“BILT” or the “Company” and BILT together with its subsidiaries referred to as the “Group”), which is head quartered in India and is an IFC investee company (# 10066 in 2000) and (# 20798 in 2003). Part of the investment proceeds may be directed to Sabah Forest Industries (SFI), whose operations are located in Sabah state of Malaysia.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group is a US$4.0 billion revenue conglomerate, with business interests in diverse areas. In addition to BILT, other flagship companies include (i) Crompton Greaves Limited, India''s largest power equipment company, (ii) Avantha Power and Infrastructure Limited (APIL), a thermal power generation company, (iii) Salient Business Solutions, niche business process solution provider, in areas such as finance, health care, financial services, human resource and knowledge process outsourcing and (iv) Solaris ChemTech Industries Limited (SCIL), India''s largest manufacturer of bromine and bromine chemicals. As per its audited financial statements dated June 30, 2013, BIGPH is a subsidiary of Ballarpur International Holdings B.V. Amsterdam (“BIH”) which holds 79.2% . BIH is 100% held by BILT. The balance shareholding is with Lathe Investments (11.7%) and Avantha International Assets BV (9.1%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost has been estimated at US$472 million. The proposed IFC investment comprises a combination of an equity investment of up to US$100 million, A Loan of up to US$50 million and a B Loan/Parallel Loan/ of up to US$100 million.
location_description: Ballarpur International Graphic Paper Holdings B.V., Paasheuvelweg 16, 1105 BH Amsterdam Zuidoost, The Netherlands (Please refer to Environment and Social Review Summary for details)
development_impact: 1. The Company will support rural households by sourcing wood from several thousand farmers, including marginal ones. In its existing locations, the Company helps farmers use more modern farming techniques to improve yield and provides an incentive to farms to meet quality standards. 2. IFC has shared with the Company some of the best available technology and practices to increase the efficiency of the forestry operations. Throughout the investment, IFC will support the Company''s efforts to implement the changes and improve its operations. 3. The Project will implement and obtain FSC or a similar certification of sustainable forest and land management that conserves biodiversity, soil and water resources and safeguards the health and ecological functions of ecosystems, and lead to a strong demonstration effect. 4. The pulp & paper industry in India remains fragmented. BILT is one of two high grade product (coated paper) producers in the country, and much of the demand is imported. Supporting the Company through restructuring will thus contribute to the overall modernization of the industry.
additionality: 1. IFC is one of the few financial partners with strong expertise in forestry sector. IFC has shared and will continue sharing concrete action steps to enhance productivity and reduce the wood procurement costs at Sabah. 2. IFC will help the Company develop a robust E&S management system covering forestry and mills and hence improve its environmental and social practices. 3. The IFC investment will send a strong signal of confidence in the Company and the paper industry in South Asia. IFC will allow the Company access to new sources of long term funding, including through mobilization of parallel loans..

project_description: Al Safi Danone for Dairy Production and Distribution LLC. (the “Company” or “ASDI”) is an establishment that was formed for the production, marketing and sales of processed dairy products in Iraq. The Company constructed a new factory with an initial production capacity of circa 59,000 tons of dairy products per annum. The “Project” entails the construction of ASDI’s dairy plant, including the installation of multiple filling lines, and completion of other capital expenditures to make the Company fully operational. The Project will be funded by a combination of the Sponsors’ equity and IFC long-term financing. The main purpose of the Project is to partially replace the importation of processed dairy products from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (“KSA”) to Iraq through the Company’s local production. ASDI will initially offer the following three dairy product categories to the Iraqi consumers: (i) Drinkable yoghurt; (ii) Spoonable yoghurt; and (iii) UHT milk (by way of distribution of imports).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Company was established by Al Safi Danone Limited Liability Company (“ASD”), Al Faisaliah Group Holding, a Joint Stock Company, (“AFG”), and Al Yasra General Trading Limited Liability Company (“Al Yasra”), (together the “Project Shareholders”). Al Safi Danone LLC, incorporated under the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, is a Joint Venture of: (i) Danone Corporation, a leading global dairy producer with operations in 140 countries and 95 years of experience if the dairy and broader food industry, and (ii) Al Faisaliah Group Holding JSC, a major diversified enterprise based in Saudi Arabia and operating across the Middle East. AFG has diversified investments across several industries. Al Yasra General Trading Limited LLC is engaged in the import and distribution of foodstuffs, while conducting retail operations and real estate investments across the region . Al Yasra is majority owned by Al Yasra International Food Group Company, headquartered in Kuwait.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at approximately US$54 million. The proposed IFC investment is an US$18 million A Loan, that will be structured as a Shariah-compliant sale-and-lease-back product, “Ijara”.
location_description: ASDI‘s manufacturing facility, as well as its Iraqi headquarters is located in the city of Erbil, which is located within the borders of the Kurdistan Regional Governorate (“KRG”) in Northern Iraq. The Company’s products will be distributed across all of Iraq.
development_impact: (i) Import Substitution of basic food & beverage sector products in Iraq will contribute towards the growth of the non-oil sectors in the country, and reduce the reliance on imported dairy products. (ii) Creation of direct and indirect jobs: the biggest impact would be at the distributor level where Al Yasra currently employs 380 workers dedicated to distribution of Al Safi Danone products in Iraq. This number is expected to grow by an additional 450 distribution staff within 5 years. In addition, the ASDI operation will employ 71 FTEs (39 of which are local) at inception, with 15 more positions to be filled by FYE''2015. (iii) Technology and Knowhow Transfer: The Company is importing the latest dairy processing and packaging equipment, while training Iraqi nationals on the job to international standards. (iv) Food Safety: The Project will increase the abundance of high quality dairy products, which are packaged according to international industry practices, at affordable prices. This should benefit end-customers, as well as setting the bar for other producers to emulate such quality standards.
additionality: IFC''s involvement in the proposed Project will support capital mobility into a fragile and conflict-effected country. IFC will provide the following unique contributions to the Project: (i) Comfort on non-commercial issues: IFC''s presence in the Project adds a factor of comfort and stability for the Sponsors as long-term investors in Iraq ; (ii) Potential for IFC Advisory Services engagement: IFC and the Sponsors will assess the possibility to improve food safety and handling standards along the distribution chain by IFC''s cooperation with Al Yasra in the near term; while evaluating the potential for IFC to provide advisory work on the Company''s potential integration of a dairy farming component to the Project in the longer term.

project_description: The proposed investment to Africa Improved Foods (Holding) B.V. and Excellent African Foods Limited will finance the construction of a processing plant to produce fortified blended food in Rwanda. The plant will sell to institutional clients as well as local and international markets. The plants will source raw material from local farmers, therefore providing additional income opportunities to rural communities in these countries. The proposed financing package will be supported by the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (“GAFSP”). GAFSP funding plays a catalytic role to create opportunity to support innovative private sector investments and deliver a level of additionality and impact beyond what is possible through IFC’s regular operations.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Royal DSM, a nutrition company. A minority shareholding by the Government of Rwanda is anticipated for Excellent African Foods Limited.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$66 million out of which IFC, with GAFSP support, will provide up to US$26 million in equity and debt investments. A portion of IFC investment may be syndicated among parallel and/or B lenders.
location_description: The Project area is Kigali, Rwanda.
development_impact: 1)More than 700,000 children will get access to fortified blended food annually, supporting the prevention and treatment of malnutrition among vulnerable populations. 2)Additional income opportunities for farmers that supply raw material to the plants (12,000 farmers in Rwanda). 3)Increased access to high-quality nutritional products among African urban and rural populations. 4)Support to agri-manufacturing and related value chains in Africa. 5)Introduction of higher food safety standards in Rwanda for complimentary foods industry for older infants and young children (above 6 months). 6)Large-scale employment (more than 200 full-time employees).
additionality: 1) Investment by IFC provides stamp of approval to the Project, thus leveraging financial support from private investors and other financiers. 2) IFC will assist Sponsors in the development of its supply chain through access to finance and technical assistance to local farmers that supply raw material to the plants. 3) IFC will leverage IBRD''s knowledge and expertise in the region in support of the plants'' supply chains.

project_description: Established in 2011, Kvarlis Baga Ltd (the “Company”) is one of the largest Georgian dairy farms. The Proposed IFC loan will be will be utilized for: (i) to increase dairy farms existing capacity from 116 milking cows to 350 milking cow; and (ii) working capital requirement (collectively the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor of the Project is Mr. Lasha Papashvili, a reputable Georgian businessman. Mr. Papashvili is 100% shareholder of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$ 8 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$2 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Kvarlis Baga has its headquarter and main operational facilities in Kvareli, a small city located in the Kakheti region (150 kilometers east of Tbilisi, the capital city). IFC’s investment will be made in Kvareli as well.
development_impact: The proposed Project has significant development impact including the following: - direct and indirect job creation and preservation in regions where job opportunities are scarce; - supporting food security in an IDA country; - increased tax payments (generating additional amount of taxes to be paid to the State).
additionality: IFC''s additionality includes following: - Long-term financing, which is not readily available for agribusiness sector in Georgia; - Standard-setting in Environmental & Social issues; and - Advisory Services: IFC''s food safety advisory team is exploring areas of cooperation with the Company.

project_description: Groupe Soufflet (Soufflet or the Group) is a mid-size, vertically-integrated, global agribusiness group whose main activities include the procurement, primary processing and trading of grains - primarily wheat and barley. With presence in 16 countries, the Group is a leading agricultural input distributor, grain originator, grain exporter and wheat miller in its home-base of France as well as a global market leader in malting. The project entails support to the Group’s strategy in Europe and Central Asia (ECA) to (i) increase in-kind pre-financing to farmers and grow its non-barley business; (ii) decrease foreign exchange risk by increasing local currency funding; and (iii) maintain a buffer to absorb the impact of grain price volatility on the Group’s working capital needs (the Project). The Project will directly support the Group’s working capital needs in Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Romania, Serbia and Poland (collectively, the Project Countries).
sponsor_shareholders: Established in France in 1900, Soufflet is privately-owned by the Soufflet family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be €200 million which corresponds to the peak working capital need of the Group in ECA. The proposed IFC financing amounts to €60 million-equivalent in the form of a multi-country working capital loan.
location_description: The IFC financing will be directly used to support Soufflet’s working capital needs in the six Project Countries.
development_impact: The development impact of the Project is expected to include: (i) Small-holders reach as the IFC financing will be channeled by Soufflet throughout the agricultural supply chain; (ii) Improved food security through increased productivity; (iii) Private sector development in challenging business environments.
additionality: IFC''s expected role and additionality include: (i) Local currency financing; (ii) Global presence & knowledge; (iii) Sharing of E&S best practices; and (iv) Long-term partnership with Soufflet.

project_description: wEstablished in 1962, Tbilvino (the “Company” or “Tbilvino”) is one of the largest Georgian wine-makers and exporters, concentrating exclusively on wine production and procuring grapes from more than 1,000 Georgian farmers, located in the Kakheti region of Georgia. The Proposed IFC loan will be will be utilized for: (i) development of the Company’s own vineyards in the Kakheti region of Georgia; (ii) permanent working capital requirement; and (iii) additional capital expenditures (collectively the “Project”)
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsors are Mr. Zurab Margvelashvi and Mr. George Margvelashvili, who are Georgian citizens. The Sponsors own 100% of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$ 6.8 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$2.0 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Headquartered in Tbilisi, Tbilvino has its main operational facilities in Tbilisi, the capital city, and in Kvareli, a city located in the Kakheti region. The investment will be mostly made in the Kakheti region of Georgia, which is one of the main grape growing regions in Georgia and located 150 kilometers east of Tbilisi.
development_impact: The Company significantly exceeded Development Impact Indicators set for the IFC''s firts loan in 2011. The proposed new project will have significant development impact, including following: -Promotion of the formal private sector abiding by rules and regulations; -Direct and indirect employment creation in rural areas of Georgia, where the job opportunities are scarce; -Generation of additional amounts of taxes paid; -Linkage to the farmers: in 2010, the Company had 300 Georgian farmers suppliers, however, today it procures grapes from more than 1,000 farmers, which is expected to grow even further even after development of own vineyards as the Company grows fast.
additionality: -Long-term financing, which is scarcely available for the agricultural sector in Georgia; -Advisory Services: IFC''s resources efficiency advisory team will explore areas for advisory support, especially for the irrigation part of the project; -Standard-setting in Environmental and Social Issues: Tbilvino will benefit from the implementation of IFC''s environmental and social performance standards for the development of vineyards.

project_description: SAMHI Hotels Private Limited (“SAMHI” or the “Company”), incorporated in 2010, is the flagship holding and operating company of the SAMHI group, which comprises of joint ventures and subsidiaries. (the “Group”). The Group is involved in the development and ownership of a portfolio of hotels across India including in economy and midscale segments. SAMHI’s hotel properties are operated by major global hotel operators like Accor, Marriott, Hyatt and Starwood under their brand names. SAMHI has also entered into 2 joint ventures with international hotel operators Marriott and Accor. SAMHI JV Business Hotels Private Limited (“SAMHI JV”) (held 67% by SAMHI and 33% by Marriott through Luxury Singapore Holding Company Pte. Ltd.) is mainly focused on development of midscale brand “Fairfield” across India along with other Marriott owned brands. Barque Hotels Private Limited (“Barque”) (held 60% by SAMHI and 40% by Accor through AAPC Singapore Pte. Ltd.) is an SPV currently developing a portfolio of 17 low-budget economy hotels (4 already operational) with planned room inventory of around 2000 across various cities in India. All the properties under Barque are managed and operated by Accor under its global “Formule1” brand (F1). SAMHI is currently implementing its growth plan, through the development of a portfolio of 27 hotels (7 operational, 17 under development, 3 more acquisitions in pipeline, comprising around 4000 rooms). The financial closure for debt and equity component for this identified portfolio is mostly complete. The Group is also exploring opportunities to add approximately 10 more assets (around 1500 rooms) to the portfolio. These assets would primarily be in the midscale segment but some could be developed or acquired in economy/budget segment. This may encompass the development of roughly 5 new greenfield hotels, and may also include acquisition and/or rebranding of roughly 5 brownfield properties. However, the exact mix will be determined depending on the opportunities opening up to the Group going forward.
sponsor_shareholders: SAMHI is a closely held private limited company incorporated in 2010, under the provisions of Indian law. The two largest shareholders of SAMHI are: Blue Chandra Pte Ltd (a company registered in Singapore, a subsidiary of Equity International Fund V) (“EI”) and GTI Capital Alpha Private Limited (a company registered in Mauritius) (“GTI”), with combined equity shareholding of approximately 95% (EI ~70% and GTI ~ 25%). EI is a fund manager specializing in real estate and real estate related investments in global markets. EI is led by Mr. Sam Zell, a globally acclaimed investor. Ira Chaplik, Senior Advisor and Vijay Jayaraman, Senior Vice President of EI sit on the board of SAMHI and manage EI’s investment in SAMHI. GTI is an India focused long term investment vehicle backed by prominent industry figures from India and overseas and managed by Mr.Gaurav Dalmia (Managing Director, OCL India, an existing IFC investment client) and Mr. Madhav Dhar (formerly, co-founder of Traxis Partners and Head of Morgan Stanley – Asset Management, Emerging Market Group). The Group is managed by a professional team led by Mr. Ashish Jakhanwala, a veteran of the Indian hotel industry who has previously worked with companies such as Accor India JV and PKF International. Mr. Ashish Jakhanwala, Mr. Manav Thadani (co-founder) and their relatives, friends and associates have a combined current equity shareholding of approximately 5%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to partially finance the next phase of the Group’s growth plans. The total Project cost is estimated at US$84 million. The estimated equity investment in the Project would be US$38 million with balance US$46 million to be funded through debt. The proposed IFC equity investment in the Company would be upto US$21 million.
location_description: SAMHI intends to develop/acquire hotel assets across India including in Tier I and Tier II centres
development_impact: 1) Job creation: On successful completion the Project is estimated to create direct jobs of more than 2000, with female job creation of more than 400 across the planned properties in India. Additionally, the Project will create indirect jobs, both during construction and operations, including construction activities, facilities management and maintenance, security, transport, logistics, food and beverage supply, etc. 2) Affordable hotels: SAMHI group would be amongst the few internationally branded and professionally managed hotel companies in India focusing on budget travelers. This is likely to make domestic business travel more affordable by increasing supply of competitive hotels in budget segment. 3) Boost investment in Low Income States (LIS): SAMHI has a pan-India footprint with strong pipeline spread across LIS. The Group has already made investments in LIS of Uttar Pradesh (Greater Noida) and West Bengal (Kolkata) and plans to invest more in these regions. 4) Local supply chain linkages: The Project will create business opportunities along the value chain, both during construction and operations, for small and medium enterprises engaged in transportation, distribution, maintenance and general services to the hotel.
additionality: 1) Provide long-term funding in sluggish market conditions to support an institutionally owned hotel platform in otherwise closely owned Indian hotel industry. 2) Expand Green Edge footprint across India through the Company''s hotel chain which could have a positive demonstration effect on other players. 3) IFC will assist the Group to formulate and implement E&S action plan to introduce social/labor management systems for inclusion of E&S and OHS guidelines and enhance OHS management systems. 4) Re-inforce the stamp of approval for the Company as an internationally recognized investor and act as a catalyst for the Company''s future IPO/capital raising plans.

country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: AMERRA Capital Management, LLC, (“AMERRA”) is an investment fund manager, focused on providing customized agriculture-focused and commodity-based finance solutions to producers, processors, distributors and traders, mainly in the Americas. AMERRA has about US$800 million in assets under management across several funds and accounts managed for single institutional investors. IFC approved a US$ 50 million loan to support AMERRA in 2012, which has since then has been fully deployed in AMERRA’s operations. IFC is currently considering providing a new loan of about US$ 10 million to help AMERRA extend its reach to new clients and to countries where it has historically not been as active. In 2013, AMERRA started making additions to its team which is supporting an increase in its lending operations in Paraguay and Uruguay. Between 2009-2014, AMERRA has been deploying capital raised largely from US institutional investors with a small but focused team led by its principals, who have decades of commodity finance experience. AMERRA has proven a good complement to the banking sector in terms of providing finance solutions to clients in the agribusiness value chain where assessment of lending risks is specialized and where client needs often require shorter response times than banks are able to provide. The proposed project entails IFC extending about US$ 10 million as a medium-term loan to help fund a part of the portfolio of AMERRA Agri Fund II, L.P. (“Agri Fund II”), increasing the capital it will have to lend (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: AMERRA is a partnership which is 50% owned by Craig Tashjian and Nancy Obler (its two founding principals) along with Pat Morabito (its Chief Operating and Risk Officer). The balance is held by M.D. Sass-Macquarie Financial Strategies, L.P. (25%) and Macquarie Group Limited (25%). The founding principals and COO had long and successful careers in banking before AMERRA. M.D. Sass-Macquarie Financial Strategies, L.P. is a joint venture focused on investing in alternative strategies private equity fund managers and is equally owned by M.D. Sass and Macquarie Group Limited. M.D. Sass was founded in 1972 and is a well-established investment management firm. Today, the M.D. Sass organization has approximately US$6 billion in assets under management and employs over 70 people. Macquarie Group Limited (Macquarie) is a global provider of banking, financial, advisory, investment and funds management services. Founded in 1969, Macquarie employs more than 13,000 people in over 28 countries. Macquarie has approximately US$396 billion of assets under management and is listed in Australia (ASX:MQG).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project entails making US$ 10 million of credit available to leverage the funds Agri Fund II has available as it broadens its geographic reach in southern South America, most recently in Paraguay and Uruguay. The IFC investment is expected to be to a sub-fund of Agri Fund II, which is also the entity that received the first IFC loan mentioned above.
location_description: AMERRA is based in New York City and invests throughout the Americas, especially in Mexico, Central and South America. More than 80% of AMERRA’s clients have been based in Brazil, Mexico, Ecuador, Guatemala and Nicaragua, or buy agricultural commodities from those countries or elsewhere in Latin America and the Caribbean.
development_impact: The Project will support liquidity in the food supply chain and help ensure agribusiness companies (and the farmers linked to them) can continue to maximize production in scenarios of high commodity prices, which would make a contribution to food security. Many AMERRA clients are low cost producers of food staples. Despite their contribution to food supply and rural livelihoods, smaller and medium-sized agribusiness companies (and the farmers that supply them) have historically had insufficient access to finance from private sector sources, in particular finance that extends for more than one crop season. The supply-to-demand dynamics for financing of the agricultural sector continue to show insufficient supply from the established financial sector and commercial banks that had been financing some parts of the supply chain but continue to be under pressure to strengthen their capital ratios, which limits their activity in the sector. The IFC Project supports the expansion of an innovative firm whose business model includes providing financing into this segment by intermediating capital from an institutional investor segment in developed countries that has not historically invested significantly in these agribusiness segments from the emerging markets.
additionality: IFC is helping AMERRA implement and refine an Environmental & Social Management System (ESMS) to identify and manage potential environmental and social risks. The system will include the following. (i) Initial screening for every transaction, and an environmental and social (E&S) due-diligence for long-term finance transactions; (ii) When applicable, the preparation of a plan to mitigate E&S risks or strengthen client E&S practices; and, (iii), monitoring and enforcement of the plan. Improved E&S evaluations systems make AMERRA among the few finance firms in its and related financing niches with a formal ESMS, which in turn disseminate better E&S practices among its clients in the agricultural commodity supply chain. Agribusiness sectors generally do not enjoy good access to finance and financing that extends beyond a given crop year is especially limited for smaller and medium-sized companies. By providing a medium-term loan, IFC is enabling a financial intermediary that serves the sector to sustainably provide longer tenor finance to its clients (more than half of AMERRA''s portfolio has a tenor greater than 1 year). IFC''s support for the Project represents an important diversification of funding sources for AMERRA and may have a demonstration effect to help catalyze the mobilization of additional debt from new sources for this financial intermediary and others in similar niches.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

sector: Garment and Apparel (Without Fabric , Excluding Footwear)
project_description: Founded in 1986, Grupo M is a vertically integrated apparel manufacturer in the DR producing knits and woven products to the highly competitive US market. Grupo M (DR) and its subsidiary CODEVI (Haiti) are an integrated operation with 7500 workers in Haiti and 500 workers in the DR and remain one of the largest garments manufacturing operation in the Caribbean/Central American region, supplying major US brand name companies including Liz Clairborne, Polo, Levis, Hanes and Calvin Klein. The main production site is at Caribbean Industrial Park (CIP), in Santiago City. Their Haitian operation, the CODEVI complex, a duty-free zone in Ouanaminthe, on the border with DR, is operating successfully and has grown its Haitian payroll from 300 in 2006 to more than 7,000 employees by mid-2013, making it currently the largest employer in Haiti. CODEVI is engaging in an expansion program which consists of the construction of a new facility destined to its wovens line; and (ii) the acquisition of specialized machinery.
sponsor_shareholders: Fernando Capellan a well-respected Dominican entrepreneur is the founder of Grupo M. He and other family members are the controlling shareholders who, together with other senior management officials, hold 82% of the outstanding share capital.
