Other shareholders include Grupo popular and other members of the business community. Grupo M fully owns CODEVI.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Project cost is estimated at US$20 million and will be financed by an IFC A Loan of up to US$10 million and with internal cash generation.
location_description: Grupo M’s main production facilities are located in two industrial zones developed by the group in Santiago, Dominican Republic. The Haiti Project is located on the northern border of the Dominican Republic and the Republic of Haiti on the outskirts of the towns of Ouanaminthe (Republic of Haiti, population 56,000 ) and Dajabon (Dominican Republic).
development_impact: The project will have a strong development impact. At full development, over a two year implementation period, the expansion project would generate 4,000 additional skilled jobs. CODEVI''s payroll, higher than the minimum wage, is the only source of stable livelihood for the 7,000 workers and their dependents, whose number is now estimated at approximately 60,000 in the town of Ouanaminthe and its surroundings. It is estimated that another 30,000 people live in Ouanaminthe, deriving their livelihood from indirect jobs associated with CODEVI''s operations. Furthermore, CODEVI''s payroll is made up of approximately 50% women who are amongst the most vulnerable segments of Haitian society. The project will therefore provide a social safety net to the current workers and their dependents. This investment is also expected to send a positive signal on the creditworthiness of private sector investment in Haiti and on the potential of the textile sector in the country. This project will contribute to the creation of new growth pole built entirely on the private sector initiative. The IFC approach in this investment is also driven by a focus on delivering impact on the ground to the community that has agglomerated around the jobs generated by CODEVI. To ensure delivery, IFC has also systematically identified upfront partners (with and through Ashoka and other NGOs) to identify and respond to community needs with technologies and businesses to deliver BOP goods and services. A pilot project managed by Ashoka with CODEVI''s support has already reduced the cost of basic goods and services to the workers and families, thus boosting disposable income and tangibly reducing poverty levels.
additionality: Even though CODEVI is a well -established operation with a long track record of delivery to highly demanding clients, commercial banks are reluctant to provide long-term financing to Haitian-based operations and limit their involvement to trade finance at high spreads. IFC has been, and remains, the only source of long term financing which is crucial to CODEVI''s ability to undertake capital intensive projects such as the construction of industrial buildings and related infrastructure. Consolidation of CODEVI''s performance through continued IFC support (and potential partners) can only enhance the prospects of Haiti as an attractive garment manufacturing destination, as CODEVI continues to grow, with a skilled and motivated labor force. IFC will also help the Company to improve its Environmental and Social practices.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: In 1999 Sisecam Sanayi A.S. (“Sisecam”) acquired a 76% interest in JSC Ksani Mina (“Ksani”), leading manufacturer of glass containers for food and beverages, as part of the Georgian Government''s privatization program. With the financial support of IFC and EBRD, Ksani undertook an expansion and modernization program to take advantage of the growing regional demand. The current expansion program in 2014 is expected to cost US$25 million and will be used to support: (i) installation of a new furnace to increase capacity from 30 thousand tonnes/year (tpa) of glass, to 60 thousand tpa; (ii) improvements in energy and resource efficiency; (iii) improvements in Ksani’s operational efficiency through renovation and equipment upgrades; and (iv) long-term working capital financing.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Sise ve Cam Fabrikalari A.S. (“Sisecam”) and Anadolu Cam Sanayii A.S. (“Anadolu Cam”), both listed on Istanbul Stock Exchange (“ISE” or”BIST”). Ksani is fully owned by the Anadolu Cam, the glass packaging arm of Sisecam. Sisecam is a leading Turkish producer of flat glass, tableware, glass containers, glass fibers and associated products worldwide. Sisecam owns 80% of Anadolu Cam’s shares directly and indirectly, the rest of the shares being publicly traded.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$25 million. The project will be financed by US$10 million A Loan for IFC’s own account, and US$7.5 million syndicated B Loan.
location_description: The project is for the expansion of Ksani’s existing plant located in the village of Ksani, 40 kilometers from Tbilisi, Georgia.
development_impact: IFC''s investment in Georgia continues to be a large employer and a successful example of privatization and foreign direct investment in Georgia
additionality: Through this investment, IFC will provide support to an existing client in a South-South investment with good fundamental business prospects and export capacity. IFC''s investment will enable the company (i) to help expand its capacity and growth, increasing its competitiveness (ii) to take advantage of the expected growth in the regional glass-packaging market, (iii) to encourage resource and energy efficiency investments. The investment will also help sustain employment.

project_description: Bidco Oil Refineries Limited (“BORL”, “Bidco” or the “Company”) is one of East Africa’s leading fast moving consumer goods (“FMCG”) company which generates revenues from the sale of edible oils, cooking fats, soaps, detergents, animal feeds and baking powder. Bidco is constructing new facilities to expand its production capacity in FMCG products.
sponsor_shareholders: Bidco, a Kenyan private limited liability company, is a family business owned by father and founder Bhimji Shah (33.3%), and sons Tarun Shah (33.3%) and Vimal Shah (33.3%). Company chairman and founder Mr. Bhimji Shah originally set up Bidco as a garment manufacturing company in 1970. Following the liberalization of the textile industry in Kenya in the 80’s, Bidco shifted from garment manufacturing to soap manufacturing. By 1991, the Company had begun manufacturing and marketing edible oils and fats, in addition to soaps and detergents. The Company has since expanded through organic growth and through the acquisition of leading consumer brands from Unilever and Unga Group Ltd.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $46 million. The proposed IFC investment will consist of a corporate A Loan investment of up to $23 million on IFC’s account and a syndicated B Loan investment of up to $13.5 million.
location_description: The Project will be implemented and located on Plot Nos. 4953/1511 and Plot 29, Section 370, situated in Thika Municipality, Kiambu County, Kenya. The site has good access to major transport routes.
development_impact: 1) Farmers Reached: The Project will reach over 20,000 smallholder farmers supplying into Bidco''s supply chain. 2) Support of basic hygiene needs: The Project will increase the supply of affordable quality detergent, which is a basic hygiene need and helps prevent diseases. 3) Private sector development: through support of local suppliers of inputs and general suppliers. 4) Serving the BOP: Bidco has a rich history of providing benefits to the lower income, Bottom of the Pyramid ("BOP") segment of the East African market by delivering quality products at affordable prices.
additionality: 1) Water and Resource Efficiency: IFC will provide support to Bidco on water and resource efficiency. 2) Standard Setting: IFC will help the Company in implementing best practice environmental, social, health and safety standards. 3) Knowledge and Innovation: Bidco will leverage IFC''s global experience in Fast Moving Consumer Goods projects to facilitate access to brand positioning expertise. 4) Risk Mitigation: IFC is providing long term financing structured to match the requirements of the project, particularly the need for 7-year tenor which is not readily available in the Kenyan market. 5) Advisory Services: IFC will engage with the Company to explore opportunities for Advisory Services to support smallholder farmers in its supply chain and overall supply chain development.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a senior secured US$10.0 million loan in Malawi Mangoes (Mauritius) Limited. (“Malawi Mangoes”). Malawi Mangoes was established in 2009 with processing operations based in the Salima District of Malawi. Malawi Mangoes produces and markets mango and banana not from concentrate (“NFC”) fruit puree and fresh fruits primarily for export markets in Africa, the Middle East and Europe via its wholly-owned Malawian subsidiary, MM Operations Limited. The proposed financing package will be supported by the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (“GAFSP”). GAFSP funding plays a catalytic role to create opportunity to support innovative private sector investments and deliver a level of additionality and impact beyond what is possible through IFC’s regular operations. Malawi Mangoes presently owns two farms with total land at 426 hectares as well as a multi-fruit processing facility built and commissioned in December 2013 with currently installed capacity of 31 metric tons of NFC production per day. Malawi Mangoes is seeking to transition into its next stage of growth by adding production capacity. The plan is focused on realizing the potential of its existing mango and banana farms and its 4,000 outgrowers and expanding its primary production at the proposed Nyu Nyu Farm and processing capacity.
sponsor_shareholders: Malawi Mangoes is majority owned by BXR Group, an international private investment group based in Amsterdam. BXR Group has a 17 year track record across multiple sectors including natural resources, real estate, transport, education, healthcare and agriculture, where BXR Agro has been established to create efficient operations of scale through the introduction of modern farming techniques, land development and soil correction in a way which is sustainable and sensitive to the needs of local communities. Malawi Mangoes is one of four current investments in BXR Agro’s growing portfolio. The second largest shareholder is Mr. Stewart Newton a well-known fund manager and philanthropist and he is the Chairman of Veritas Investment Management LLP. The remaining shares are owned by other individual shareholders and management.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, with GAFSP support, will provide a US$10 million financing package in the form of a senior secured loan.
location_description: Malawi Mangoes’ main operation is located in the Salima District of Malawi, which consists of two farms (Matumba – 126ha and Dzuwa- 300ha) totalling 426 hectares of land and a state-of-the-art fruit processing plant. A new proposed farm, Nyu Nyu, estimated at 1500-2000 hectares, is also planned in the Salima District.
development_impact: 1) Expected to reach at least an incremental 2,000 small scale mango farmers over the next five years, thereby improving sustainable income streams along these value chains. 2) Penetration of modern farming practices and sustainable land use in farming communities in Malawi. 3) Development of improved natural resource management techniques, especially water resource efficiency through promotion of drip irrigation. 4) Contribution to wider regional development in terms of jobs, infrastructure, education, health and other socio-economic parameters.
additionality: 1) IFC''s investment provides the needed long-term capital to an early stage business to enhance production volumes, diversify product offerings and reinforce the capital structure. 2) IFC''s technical expertise, global knowledge of the industry and markets as well as lessons learned from other integrated fresh juice / concentrate producers will be valuable resource. The team will also tap into the World Bank''s experience in funding the development of mango value chains in West Africa (Mali, Burkina Faso, Senegal and Ghana). 3) The team will work to mobilize GAFSP funding and other developmental financial institutions to further reinforce the capital structure of Malawi Mangoes. 4) IFC''s investment will provide a "stamp of approval" for other private sector investors to provide working capital and other funding where necessary to Malawi Mangoes.

project_description: Establish a greenfield 750 tons capacity per day wheat mill in the South African port city of Durban, to serve primarily the KwaZulu-Natal province and export to neighboring countries including Mozambique. Bakhresa has decided to establish a wheat mill in South Africa at a cost of US$80 million and has invited IFC to provide senior debt of US$25 million. The IFC’s participation is up to US$25 million A Loan to Bakhresa South Africa (Pty) Ltd which will be used to fund a greenfield project in Bakhresa South Africa operations.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Bakhresa a leading industrial group headquartered in Dar es Salaam and whose core business is wheat milling in countries such as Tanzania, Mozambique, Uganda, Rwanda and Malawi. Previous projects with IFC include financing milling activities in Mozambique (#29475&#27398), Rwanda (#633443%#29477), and Malawi (#27399). Bakhresa Group has a ~5,000 tons per day (tpd) milling capacity which requires yearly purchases of over a million tons of wheat. The shareholders of project company are members of the Bakhresa family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: As part of the US$80 million wheat mill project in South Africa, IFC’s participation is up to US$25 million A Loan to Bakhresa South Africa (Pty) Ltd.
location_description: Bakhresa has bought a disused flour mill in Umbilo a prime location which is 3.7 km from the main discharge terminal at the Durban Port in KwaZulu-Natal province in South Africa. Bakhresa will entirely refurbish the mill with a 750 tpd state-of-the-art Buhler complete wheat milling line. The bulk grain handling equipment is fully operational as the silos had been rented out to third parties until recently. The storage capacity in silos is 30,000 MT in 70 separate silo bins with loading capacity ranging from 150 to 250 t/h. The premises are strategically located near the main grain bulk discharge terminals: Durban Bulk Services (DBS) terminal (currently under improvement, will have a draft of 11.3 meters allowing Panamax sizes (up to 50,000 MT vessels), 7,000 MT a day discharge rate. South Africa Bulk Terminals MW5 terminal with 9.6 min (vessel would first upload at DBS and then possibly shift to this other terminal). Rennies Bulk Terminal (up to 14,000 MT / day discharge rate). Agriport 6-7,000 MT / day discharge.
development_impact: (i) Employment Generation: The project will generate permanent jobs for local communities in Durban, South Africa. Also during the construction of the mill, temporary positions will be created in the region. The creation of additional indirect jobs throughout the value chain is expected. (ii) SME supply chain development: Agro allied businesses in the value chain such as local SME''s that provide goods and services to the mill, (transportation, packaging materials, ingredients, distribution, general services) or buyers from the mill (wholesalers, retailers, bakeries, animal feed manufactures) will benefit from the development of a flour mill plant in Durban, South Africa. (iii) Food security: Improved food security in South Africa and neigboring countries, where wheat products are a staple diet. (iv) Fiscal benefits: Increased tax revenues.
additionality: (i) Long-term partnership: IFC has supported Bakhresa''s expansion in East and Central Africa over the years. Bakhresa is expanding in Southern Africa and is looking to IFC for continued support. The proposed IFC loan to Bakhresa will enable the group to successfully enter the South African market. (ii) Global expertise: IFC''s global knowledge of industry and best practice in agribusiness will help Bakhresa''s entry in South Africa. (iii) Environmental, safety and social standards: IFC will work with the Company to enhance its environmental, safety and social standards. (iv) Stamp of approval: IFC''s investment will bring a high level of comfort to other financiers which rely on IFC''s sector expertise.

company_name: IHS FUND II SA COLLECTOR, LP
project_description: The Project consists of investing in “IHS Fund II”, a ZAR2.4 billion (~US$300 million equivalent) affordable housing fund (the “Fund”) that will provide equity for the development of affordable housing projects primarily in South Africa and selectively in Sub-Saharan African countries (the “Project” ). The Fund will be managed by International Housing Solutions (IHS), through its main investment management team based in South Africa, International Housing Solutions South Africa (“IHS-SA”). This will be the second IHS fund to focus on affordable housing in South Africa, after the “South Africa Workforce Housing Fund I”, a R1.9 billion (~US$240 million) 10-year fund that was closed in 2008. IHS is one of the most important equity investors in the South African housing space. The target market will be lower-and-middle income houses priced between ZAR250,000 and ZAR800,000 (i.e. approx US$30,000 to US$100,000).The fund will focus on the following types of projects – (i) New Builds – Develop new single-family and multifamily housing, as well as related commercial real estate (ii) Conversions – Rehabilitation of existing real estate to multifamily housing (iii) Acquisition, Rental, and Sale – Transactions in single family and multifamily housing. The IFC participation in this Fund will be an investment of up to US$25 million, but not to exceed 20% of total fund size. . In addition, an up to US$10 million concessional investment from the Global Environment Facility, through the IFC Earth Fund Platform, would support the Fund making investments in green housing projects in South Africa. The Fund will seek to deliver equity type returns with a target IRR of 20%+, net of fund cost, fees and carry. By the time the Fund matures, it is expected that safe and affordable housing would have been provided to over 20,000 families.
sponsor_shareholders: International Housing Solutions limited is a company owned by the following: MMA Financial International, LLC (MMA Int?), an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Municipal Mortgage & Equity, LLC called “MuniMae” (a U.S. real estate finance company) (82.2%); Cathal Conaty, its founder and Managing Partner (13.2%); and two other investors, Ronan King and Frank Gormley (4.6%). MuniMae, the largest shareholder, is a diverse real estate financial company specializing in tax-exempt bonds issued by state and local government authorities in the United States and secured by affordably multi-family housing projects.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The IFC participation in this project will be an equity investment of up to US$25 million, but will not exceed 20% of the total fund size. In addition, an up to US$10 million concessional investment from the Global Environment Facility, through the IFC Earth Fund Platform, would support the Fund making investments in green housing projects in South Africa. The fund will seek to deliver equity type returns with a target IRR of 20%+, net of fund cost, fees and carry. The projected final size of the Fund is US$300million to US$400 million, to be denominated in local currency (i.e. South African Rands), and is expected to be raised over at least two closings
location_description: The Fund will invest in real estate projects located in South Africa and Sub-Sahara Africa. It will make equity investments focusing on development of affordable housing in urban areas and large cosmopolitan cities. About 85% of the fund’s capital will be invested in South Africa and 15% in five other African countries – Botswana, Ghana, Namibia, Mauritius, and Zambia.
development_impact: The Fund will have the following development impacts: 1. Economic development: The Fund will help address the short supply of quality affordable housing and will increase the quality of life for the lower-middle income population in Sub Saharan Africa. The spillover effects will include the provision of urban infrastructure through the development of housing communities where families can live, work and play. The Fund is expected to deliver well over 20,000 housing units over the next 10 years 2. Demonstration Effect: Successful implementation of the fund will stimulate other industry stakeholders to replicate this model in other countries. IFC's early involvement in this fund provides support for a successful close. IHS is also demonstrating that low-to-middle income housing in South Africa is a viable asset-class 3. Private Sector Infrastructure Development: The fund will contribute to urban infrastructure development and surrounding community development, such as roads, electricity, water access and sanitation and will mobilize government investment on supporting infrastructure 4. Job creation: The Fund will foster, through its investee companies, the creation of direct and indirect jobs during construction of the residential properties, and also during property maintenance. The Fund is expected to create over 15,000 construction jobs over its lifetime 5. Linkages: The Fund will increase the demand for construction and building materials in the target markets and will stimulate the use of local goods and services.
additionality: IFC's additionality will manifest itself in the following areas: 1. IFC Global housing sector expertise: The IFC will provide general insights to the Fund management on how best to assess the best investment opportunities in the affordable housing sector as it expands into other countries outside South Africa 2. E&S Expertise: The IFC will support IHS in the areas of Environmental and Social Standards and best practices for the Fund. 3. Fostering a Long Term Partnership: Providing the Fund with financing support will help IFC establish long term business relations with a key partner in Africa, through which IFC can participate in a sector where it has a clear role. 4. IFC's Stamp of Approval: The IFC's participation in this transaction will send a strong signal and endorsement of low cost housing as a viable asset class.
Company Name: IHS FUND II SA COLLECTOR, LP

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: MAS Capital (Pvt) Ltd is a vertically integrated intimate-wear and active-wear manufacturing group headquartered out of Sri Lanka. The group’s operations span the entire value chain of the manufacturing process from fabric, elastic, lace and accessories to the final product. The proposed project is new investment for capacity expansions, sustainability projects and product development at MAS Capital (Pvt) Ltd, MAS Active (Pvt) Ltd, Trischel (Pvt) Ltd and Textprint Lanka (Pvt) Ltd (collectively the “Co-borrowers”) and their subsidiaries.
sponsor_shareholders: MAS Active (Pvt) Ltd, Trischel (Pvt) Ltd and Textprint Lanka (Pvt) Ltd are wholly owned subsidiaries of MAS Capital (Pvt) Ltd. MAS Capital (Pvt) Ltd is a wholly owned subsidiary of MAS Holdings (Pvt) Ltd which is the ultimate holding company of the MAS group. MAS Holdings is privately held company owned by the Amalean family Mr. M. Amalean, Mr. S. Amalean and Mr. A. Amalean. The Group started out in 1986 and has since grown to become an international operation with 34 manufacturing plants in Sri Lanka, 9 plants overseas (including India and Bangladesh), and 3 international design offices. MAS group is Sri Lanka’s largest export apparel manufacturer and largest private sector employer with a workforce of 66,000+.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at US$35 million and the proposed IFC investment is up to US$27 million, A-loan for IFC’s own account to the co-borrowers.
location_description: The project will be carried out in the Co-borrower’s plants and premises located in the Western Province of Sri Lanka.
development_impact: 1. Increased forex earnings: The project will help increase forex earnings of the apparel industry and improve the currently the country''s Balance of Payments. 2. Job creation: The project will lead to increased employment opportunities, and in particular, female employment, in Sri Lanka. 3. Demonstration Effect: The project will support one of Sri Lanka''s premium apparel sector players in terms of E&S compliance, OHS standards, and energy efficiency thereby setting the industry benchmark.
additionality: 1. Provide long-term FX financing to support a leading conglomerate to expand its core business. IFC''s investment would enable the Group to access a longer tenor and grace period than is available in the local market. 2. Form a strategic partnership and provide continued financing support to the client for the expansion of it operations both locally and internationally. 3. Provide global industry insights from IFC''s experience in the sector.

project_description: Agrotec S.A. (“Agrotec” or “the Company”) is one of Paraguay’s leading crop input distributor and agronomy services company operating since 1990. Agrotec offers a “one-stop shop” to more than 800 client farmers, providing seeds, fertilizers, agrochemicals, technical support, storage and logistic services, pre-harvest financing, as well as commercialization of the grains of its farmer client base. The Company’s strategy is to develop strong relationships with farmers providing integral agronomic services from sowing planning and advice, through the provision of seeds, nutrition integration and crop protection. Agrotec operates 11 Regional Distribution Centers (“RDCs”) including its HQ in Ciudad del Este located near the major crop regions of Paraguay to guarantee a rapid delivery of inputs and efficient customer service to its clients. The Project consists of providing Agrotec an up to $15 million one year loan facility (the “Facility”) with up to four renewable tranches, and a long term facility up to US$10 million to support the working capital needs of the Company.
sponsor_shareholders: Agrotec is owned by local Sponsors through two holding companies: Agrihold Investment Ltd. and Agrihold Management Corp (“Agrihold” or the “Group”), which centralizes the Group’s business and operations in Paraguay, Uruguay, and Brazil.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at $25 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an up to $15 million A Loan renewable for up to 4 years, and an A Loan of up to US$10 million, both for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Ciudad Del Este, Paraguay. The Company has 11 Regional Distribution Centers located near the major crop regions of Paraguay.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have a significant development impact by - Reaching farmers operating in rural frontier regions - Supporting the dissemination of agricultural and inputs handling best practices to farmers - Generating tax income for the Government - Additional employment following the growth of the Company - Demonstration effect of supporting a sustainable operation in Paraguay
additionality: Through this project, IFC will be enhancing Agrotec''s capacity to provide pre-harvest financing to farmers and will contribute to the further development of agriculture sector, a key pillar of Paraguay''s economy.

project_description: The Project involves providing a long term corporate loan facility of up to US$250 million to Myronivsky Hliboproduct (“MHP” or the “Company”), the largest integrated poultry producer in Ukraine, to support the Company’s expansion plans in Ukraine and refinance its Eurobond maturity falling due in 2015.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is MHP, a leading vertically integrated poultry producer in Ukraine. In 2013 the Company produced 472,800 tons of chicken meat and harvested around 2 million tons of crops. The total land bank at the end of 2013 reached 360,000 hectares, including 320,000 hectares in Ukraine and 40,000 hectares in the Russian Federation. MHP is 66% owned by WTI Trading Limited, with 34% of the shares listed on the London Stock Exchange. WTI Trading Limited is owned by Mr. Yuriy Kosyuk, a local entrepreneur, who graduated from the Ukrainian Food Institute in 1991 and established MHP in 1998. Prior to launching his poultry business, Mr. Kosyuk was involved in various business activities, including grain and retail trading, food processing.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$250 million. IFC investment will include: (i) up to US$100 million A Loan from its own account; (ii) US$75 million from IFC acting in its capacity as implementing entity for the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program; and (iii) up to US$75 million B Loan.
location_description: The expansion project linked to the IFC loan is located in a rural area of the Vinnytsia region in Ukraine.
development_impact: The Project will help facilitate its continued growth in a high potential sector to Ukraine''s economy and strengthen the debt servicing capacity of a leading agribusiness group. Key development impacts of the Project include the following: (i) Support food security: MHP''s overall volumes are expected to increase as a result of the Project and contribute to improved food security in Ukraine and beyond by efficiently converting grain to meat through supporting a leading and efficient poultry producer; (ii) Provide demonstration effect: By supporting MHP, a socially responsible and efficient producer with solid track record, IFC''s investment, which includes a B Loan, will encourage foreign and local investors to invest in Ukraine''s economy in crisis times; (iii) Support job preservation and creation: The Group currently employs 30,000 staff, including 11,400 women. Direct employment is expected to increase as a result of the Project; and (iv) Support inclusiveness: The Company supports a network of 2,600 SMEs, a franchise network of small shops selling MHP branded poultry. Significant number of these SMEs operate in rural locations often underserved in terms of basic food retail reach.
additionality: IFC''s additionality is as follows: (i) Crisis response: In light of the fluid economic situation in Ukraine, the local and regional banking sector has cut liquidity in the domestic market. IFC''s Loans will provide long-term funds otherwise not available locally at commercially acceptable rates; (ii) Mobilization of Capital: through the proposed B amd MCPP Loans, IFC will seek to attract additional financing from international lenders to help broadening the Company''s long term base; (iii) Long-Term Partnership: MHP has relied on IFC as a long term partner through its various phases of growth and will continue doing so in order to support its future expansion strategy.

project_description: IFC is considering investing an “A” loan of up to US$18 million to finance the US$ 53 million project of Terra S.P.R.L. (“Terra”) and African Milling Company Congo S.P.R.L. (“AMCC”), an integrated maize farming and milling operation in Katanga, a province in Southern Democratic Republic of Congo (“DRC”). The Project consists mainly of: Expansion of Terra’s maize farm from current 1,500ha to approximately 5,000ha by 2017; Greenfield construction of AMCC maize mill with 336 ton-per-day capacity. The project sponsors have financed almost all needed capital expenditures and the mill is almost completed. The mill is expected to be commissioned in mid-2014; and, Working capital for Terra and AMCC operations (e.g. farming inputs for Terra; and external purchase of maize grain for the milling at AMCC).
sponsor_shareholders: Passiflora Limited is an 80% shareholder of Terra and 75% shareholder of AMCC. Passiflora is owned by the Chug, Dhrolia and Rai families, represented by Chaitanya Chug, Rahim Dhrolia and Jaswant Rai, respectively. The Chug and Dhrolia Families have interests in mining/ manufacturing/ trading/ agro processing, mainly in Katanga and East Africa. The Chug and Dhrolia Families founded Terra & AMCC. Mr. Rahim Dhrolia is Managing Director of Terra and AMCC, and has been the driving force behind the Project. The Rai Family participated as a new shareholder in November 2013. RAI Family owns the RAI Group, a Kenyan agribusiness group with sugar/forestry/manufacturing activities. Mr. Daniel Piraino is 20% shareholder of Terra and 25% shareholder of AMCC. Mr. Piraino is a United States citizen who owns a truck-parts and aviation spare-parts importation business in the DRC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost (capital expenditures, pre-operative expenses, working capital and contingency) is estimated at US$53 million. IFC’s proposed financing is an “A” loan of up to US$18 million.
location_description: The project site of Terra is located approximately 90 km east of Lubumbashi and 80 km south of Kundelungu National Park in the vicinity of the N5 road (Route Kasenga) to the south in the surrounding area of the Lubanda Village, Kasenga territory, Haut-Katanga District in Katanga Province of DRC. The farming concession consists of two blocks: Lubanda Block (5,000 hectares) and Katofio Block (5,000 hectares). The project site of AMCC is located on Route Kinsevere 5457, Katanga Province, Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of Congo.
development_impact: - The project will reduce import dependence of Katanga on maize flour which is a staple food in the province. Imports are costly due to high logistic costs and can be unreliable due to policies in exporting countries. The project is for the development of local maize production at competitive costs and its processing in state of the art maize flour mill. - Local production will promote competition with imports and contribute to improved food security for local populations. - The project will demonstrate the potential to develop primary farming and food manufacturing activities to diversify the local economy from its reliance on mining. - The project will create jobs at various levels of skills thus offering an entry point into formal employment for a significant number of job-seekers. Today, Terra has 38 local full-time employees and approximately 100 contract labors. Terra will have about 80 local full-time employees at project completion. In addition, it will have about 500 contract labors for land clearing. AMCC today has 34 local full-time employees and approximately 100 contract labors for the construction. At the project completion, it will have about 100 local full-time employees and about 60 contract labors. - The project is expected to improve the company''s ability to increase its CSR projects, where Terra already assists the local community with various infrastructure, including access to clean water (boreholes) and lighting (solar street lights).
additionality: - Stamp of approval and vote of confidence on agribusiness in a post-conflict country. - Promoting environmental and social best practices, and advising the Company on sustainable community engagement. - Long-term funding (8-year tenor with 3-year grace period) not easily available in DRC.

project_description: AuchanSuper (“Auchan”), the supermarket arm of Groupe Auchan S.A. from France, a leading global food retailer and IFC strategic client, is planning to significantly expand its retail network in emerging markets over the next three years. The proposed transaction is a €250m debt and equity facility to finance (i) Auchan’s supermarket expansion in Russia, (ii) expansion in Vietnam, a new market and (iv) opening or expanding retail operations in countries in Eastern Europe, Asia, and Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is Groupe Auchan SA, the 4th largest retailer in France with a 9.2% market share and the 10th world’s largest food retailer in terms of revenue. Groupe Auchan operates 774 hypermarkets and 817 supermarkets in 15 countries, with 302.525 employees. The Group has 4 complementary business lines: (i) hypermarkets, (ii) supermarkets, (iii) commercial real estate (Immochan), and (iv) consumer banking activities (Banque Accord). Groupe Auchan SA is a privately-held company with two main groups of shareholders: 88.1% owned by the Mulliez family (“Association Familiale Mulliez” or “AFM”), and 11.9% owned by employees.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is a €250m facility to finance the retail expansion of AuchanSuper in emerging markets and developing countries over the period 2014-2016, for an estimated project cost of €600 million. The facility will be used to provide debt and possibly equity to the country operations of Auchan to finance existing or new country operations (the sub-projects) in countries in Eastern Europe, Asia, or Africa. The first two sub-projects are (i) the expansion of the supermarket operations of Auchan in Russia and (ii) the opening of supermarket operations in Vietnam.
location_description: The first two subprojects are located in Russia and Vietnam. The future subprojects will be located in countries to be identified in due time, in Eastern Europe, Asia and Africa.
development_impact: i) Affordable goods for lower to middle-income households: consumers will benefit from increased access to better quality and variety of products at lower prices. Auchan''s target is explicitly the lower bracket of the middle income class in urban areas. ii) Employment generation: Auchan''s projects will create significant local direct employment (with a significant portion of female employment) and in addition also indirect employment in the retail value chain. Typically a retail store creates approximately three full time positions for every 100 square meters of building area. iii) Expansion in second-tier cities and frontier regions: Auchan''s expansion will not only target large cities but also second-tier cities in frontier regions of countries such as Russia. iv) Best practice transfer: Auchan''s projects are expected to (a) facilitate the transfer of modern retail and management techniques, which allow lowering food prices without compromising the food quality, to the targeted regions and (b) enhance the efficiency of the supply chain in the countries and promote efficient logistic system. v) Impact on Food Safety: The expansion of modern food retail formats will contribute to food safety by improving supply chain efficiencies, and reducing food waste. The procurement of products locally sourced will generate backward linkages and encourage local producers to process according to best operating standards in terms of safety and quality.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment will have the following additionality features: i) Accompanying a global retailer in difficult markets: Auchan values IFC''s country knowledge, country risk appetite and knowledge of the global retail market ii) Provision of long-term financing from debt to equity in local or hard currency: Long-term financing is not easily available in Auchan''s targeted countries and IFC capability to match the profile and the currency of the Project''s cash flows is valued by the Group. Furthermore IFC is able to provide both loan products and equity for Auchan''s development. iii) Standard setting: IFC will ensure that the Project is implemented based on best practice environmental, social, health and safety standards.

project_description: IFC, Natixis and other commercial lenders are jointly establishing a trade finance facility of up to US$ 450 million to finance year 2014 importation of refined oil products in Ethiopia. The facility will provide Independent Petroleum Group Limited (“IPG”) with a short term structured trade finance facility to maintain the supply of oil products to Ethiopia over one year. This facility will help securing fuel supply to the second most populated country in Sub-Saharan Africa and one of the fastest growing economies in Africa. A steady supply of fuel through reliable channels is critical to ensure a better pricing, and therefore control inflation. Of the total facility amount, IFC’s funded and unfunded exposure will be up to US$ 150 million in a form of direct parallel lending. IFC has financed the year 2013 importation of refined oil products in Ethiopia through a risk participation facility with BNP Paribas (IFC project number 32846)
sponsor_shareholders: The project Sponsor is Independent Petroleum Group Limited Bahamas (“IPG Limited”), which is a 100% subsidiary of Independent Petroleum Group S.A.K (“IPG SAK”), a well-established independent company incorporated in 1976, based in Kuwait City and listed on the Kuwait Stock Exchange since 1995. IPG Limited is active in petroleum products trading and related investments and currently has over 100 employees. Since 1990, IPG Limited has remained the trading arm of IPG SAK and is active in the Middle East, East Africa, Singapore, Mediterranean and Black Sea area. IPG Limited’s obligations are guaranteed by the holding Company IPG SAK.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total amount of the facility is estimated at up to US$ 450 million, with proposed unfunded and funded IFC investment of up to US$ 150 million. Natixis is leading the facility with an estimated exposure up to US$ 150 million for its own account and plans to mobilize up to US$150 million from commercial banks.
location_description: Djibouti and Addis, Ethiopia
development_impact: The proposed investment will have significant development impacts as follows: (a) Maintain the availability of trade finance in Ethiopia. The Project is expected to finance about US$ 1 billion of imports of oil products to Ethiopia over a year. This will ensure stability in supply of energy products into an IDA economy. (b) Ensuring availability of energy products is critical for retail and industrial consumption, power and transportation sectors. (c) Support to Private Sector - The facility will indirectly support the business activities of private marketing and distribution companies in the downstream oil sector.
additionality: With this sizeable Facility, IFC will fill an existing funding gap and therefore assure stability in the financing of oil flows into the second most populated country in Sub-Saharan Africa, thus covering more than 50% of the country''s energy needs. Due to the continuous constraints on banks traditionally active in the trade finance space, including European banks, the proposed facility will allow continued importation of energy products into Ethiopia. Without this facility, major sectors and economic agents in transportation, agriculture, industrial and commercial entities and households would be negatively impacted, hurting economic activity.

project_description: PT Ciputra Residence (CR) is a 99.99% subsidiary of PT Ciputra Development Tbk in Indonesia. CR focuses on the construction of new neighborhoods with a focus on low-rise houses. In order to expand its business, CR is planning to issue bonds to fund parts of its future growth. The proceeds will be used to build low-rise homes and ancillary commercial facilities. The proposed project is to assist CR with credit enhancement for its upcoming bond issuance.
sponsor_shareholders: PT Ciputra Development Tbk is one of the largest property developers in Indonesia and is a publicly listed company on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. The company was incorporated in 1981 as a family owned business and was listed in 1994. Current shareholding structure is 61% held by the public and 39% held by Dr. Ir. Ciputra and family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: CR targets to raise up to IDR500bn in a bond issuance and IFC proposes to provide credit enhancement through a partial credit guarantee with an expected amount of up to IDR100bn.
location_description: PT Ciputra Residence is headquartered in Greater Jakarta and has property development projects in Java and Sumatra. The proceeds from the bond issuance are expected to finance new and existing projects in Java, Kalimantan and Sumatra.
development_impact: Capital markets development: IFC''s partial credit guarantee product will provide credit enhancement and assist companies such as CR to raise debt funds with institutional investors in the public market and thereby diversify their sources of funding. Reducing housing deficit: The housing deficit in Indonesia is estimated to be high and IFC''s support to CR will contribute to increase in supply. Sustainable urbanization: CR''s focus is on new neigbourhood developments and the use of the proceeds will include new neihbourhoods in frontier regions. Developments outside Jakarta are expected to support the development of new hubs of economic activity and promote living in cities in frontier regions. Job creation: The Project will provide direct and indirect jobs to local businesses.
additionality: IFC''s AAA credit enhancement: IFC''s strong credit enhancement will be needed to reach the targeted institutional investor base, given current investment regulation or internal investment guidelines of institutional investors. Without IFC''s credit enhancement, the company would most likely not be able to reach the targeted institutional investors. Long term funding: Given CR''s primary focus on new neighbourhood developments, which has a long term nature, the company needs long term funding for its operations. IFC''s partial credit guarantee will enable the company to raise long term debt. Improving E&S Standards: IFC''s involvement will assist to increase E&S best practice and standards for CR, which is expected to have a positive impact on the Ciputra Group.

project_description: IFC is considering an investment in partnership with CITIC Construction Co., Limited (“CITICC”) to establish a greenfield holding company (the “Platform”) to facilitate the development of affordable housing projects in Sub-Saharan Africa (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is CITICC, a subsidiary of the CITIC Group which was established in 1979 and is a large scale transnational conglomerate comprising a broad range of industries in both the financial and non-financial sectors. The CITIC Group is a wholly owned state enterprise of the Government of China. IFC and CITICC plan to hold 20 percent and 80 percent shareholding respectively in the Platform.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC and CITICC will invest a total of US$ 300 million as a combination of equity and shareholder loans to set up the Platform. In addition to the above, IFC and CITICC propose to mobilise another US$ 300 million in a debt facility to provide debt funding directly at the individual project level.
location_description: The Platform is a strategic pan-African initiative which will invest in countries across Sub-Saharan Africa.
development_impact: The Project will have the following development impacts: (i) Increase affordable housing supply thereby contributing to the alleviation of the current housing deficit in Sub-Saharan Africa; (ii) Create thousands of both direct and indirect jobs during construction and the operating phase of the housing communities; (iii) Transform the affordable housing sector by demonstrating the viability and affordability of this sector whilst maintaining IFC''s environmental and social standards; (iv) Enhance local supply linkages through sourcing from local suppliers and creating critical mass of market demand to justify local manufacturing capacity build-up; and (v) Contribute to more sustainable urbanization through providing much needed urban infrastructure in good quality and at fair cost.
additionality: IFC will have significant additionality in this Project as follows: (i) Mobilize equity and debt financing both at the Platform level and at the Sub-project level as well as providing financial structuring expertise; (ii) Serve to align key stakeholders'' interests including local governments, investors, local banks and local developers and ensure compliance with key environmental and social (E&S) standards; (iii) Support the creation of mortgage take-out facilities through collaborating with local financial institutions which will provide critical access to finance for potential home buyers and therefore mitigate the risk for developers; (iv) Bring in E&S best practices and Green Buildings knowhow to help set the standards in terms of environmental management and resource efficiency; and (v) Ensure the adoption of sound international standard corporate governance practices by the Platform particularly through the structuring of the venture and participating on the Board.

project_description: Lucid Colloids Limited (“LCL” or the “Company”) plans to raise up to US$30 million from IFC through a combination of equity and long term debt. This is a corporate financing with proceeds expected to be utilized to fund the Company’s growth plans and working capital requirements.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr Uday Merchant (the Sponsor) and his family directly or indirectly own 100% of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Company plans to increase the production capacity and undertake backward integration. The Company also plans to set up research facilities. These projects are in various stages of development and implementation.
location_description: The Company is implementing the projects at locations in Gujarat and Rajasthan including at its existing manufacturing facilities in Jodhpur, Rajasthan.
development_impact: The Project will involve supporting a Company with significant operations in Rajasthan, a low income state, thereby increasing employment and economic opportunities in this frontier region. The Project will also result in increased sourcing of guar from farmers in the arid / semi-arid regions of this low income state, it will improve their access to global markets and enable better price realizations. The investment will also enhance the global competitiveness of a mid-sized export-oriented player and will help increase the value addition within India.
additionality: IFC will support the Company in its expansion plans by providing long-term capital. The Company is keen on capitalizing on IFC''s knowledge base on corporate governance. The Company would also benefit from IFC''s Environmental and Social Performance Standards.

project_description: The US$255million Project involves the construction and operation of a greenfield cement manufacturing, limestone quarry, and associated facilities in the Bas Congo province of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Key Components of the Project include: (i) cement plant (annual production capacity 1.2 mtpa); (ii) Limestone quarry; (iii) overburden storage facility; (iv) 220 KV power line (6 km long) to an existing substation; (v) employee accommodation camps (for 300 personnel); (vi) waste management facility; (vii) access and haul roads; (viii) railway connection to the national rail network; (ix) auxiliary facilities (water management infrastructure, package sewage treatment plant, etc.)
sponsor_shareholders: Nyumba Ya Akiba SARL (“NYA” or the “Company”), is a 50:50 joint venture between Lucky Cement of Pakistan and Groupe Rawji of DRC (together, the “Sponsors”). Lucky Cement Limited (“LCL”) is Pakistan’s largest manufacturer and exporter of cement, with a total production capacity of 7.7 mtpa and 19 percent market share. Lucky Cement’s growth strategy is focused on expanding its footprint to other developing countries and to becoming a top tier global cement producer. It has recently completed a 0.87 mtpa grinding facility in Iraq (operations started in January 2014). Lucky Cement is part of the Yunus Brothers Group, one of the largest conglomerates in Pakistan, and is publicly listed on the London Stock Exchange as well as the Karachi, Lahore, and Islamabad Stock Exchanges of Pakistan. Groupe Rawji is one of the largest conglomerates in DRC and has operated in the country for over 100 years. The Group has business activities across financial services, real estate, manufacturing, and distribution. Rawbank, an existing IFC client, is the largest company within Groupe Rawji.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$255million Project involves the construction and operation of a greenfield cement manufacturing, limestone quarry, and associated facilities in the Bas Congo province of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan amount of upto $30 million to partially finance the Project.
location_description: The Project is located in Songololo, Bas-Congo province, DRC, 100km east of Matadi port and 250km west of Kinshasa.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have the following development impact: (i) access to reliable supply of cement and the creation of a competitive domestic market, (ii) support housing and infrastructure development in the DRC, (iii) job creation & technology transfer, and (iv) contribution to economic growth and SME activity.
additionality: IFC’s expected additionality stems from its ability to provide and support: long-term financing in an IDA and a fragile and conflict-affected country, (ii) demonstration effect and setting the standard for other companies to consider investing in the DRC, (iii) South-South investment by supporting the investment from one IDA country (Pakistan) to another IDA country (DRC).

project_description: The project involves the construction of a greenfield integrated cement plant of 1.25 million tons per annum (Mtpa) capacity to supply cement locally.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsors are PPC Ltd of South Africa, the largest cement producer in Southern Africa, and Barnet Group SPRL of DRC. PPC is a public company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, while Barnet Group is a private company owned by Mr. Jean Saidi Bamanisa and his family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$280 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to US$56 million. In addition, IFC may consider an equity investment of up to US$11.2 million.
location_description: The Project is located in Bas-Congo province about 19 km from Kimpese town and about 240 km west of Kinshasa. The project lies about 8 km off the main highway from Kinshasa to the Atlantic coast.
development_impact: 1. Support to industrial, social and infrastructure development: the project will expand local production of cement, reduce dependency on imports and save foreign exchange. Ultimately, the project will help reduce cement prices and support the development of the housing and infrastructure sectors. 2. Local supply chain development: the project will create new SME business opportunities due to increased demand for the supply of raw materials, transportation and distribution services. 3. Job creation: The project will create about 270 jobs for locals and many more indirect jobs in the value chain. 4. South-south investment: IFC will be supporting a South African corporate investing up north in Sub-Saharan Africa.
additionality: 1.Long term financing: IFC will provide appropriate long-term funding in equity and debt of US$64.8 million to help complete the financial plan. Such long-term financing is not readily available in DRC,a fragile and post-conflict country. 2. Resource Mobilization: IFC will mobilize an additional US$27 million long-term debt to help complet the financing plan. 3. EHS Support: IFC is playing an important role providing guidance in EIA preparation, and in meeting IFC Performance Standards.

project_description: Probiotech Industries Private Limited (“PBIL” or the “Company”) is one of the first organised sector poultry feed manufacturers in Nepal. Currently, key products are animal feed, de-oiled cake and crude edible oil. Company is now undertaking capital expenditure for forward integration into the production of soya flour and nuggets and refined edible oil. PBIL is also streamlining its ownership and improving its balance sheet structure. IFC and the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP) are looking to support the Company with this project. GAFSP is a multilateral mechanism launched by the G20 with the purpose of scaling-up support to help less developed countries alleviate poverty and improve food security, and IFC is the implementation entity of the Private Sector Window
sponsor_shareholders: PBIL is a closely held private limited company incorporated in 1999. The majority shareholding (72%) is held by Mr. JP Agrawal, his son Mr. Anand Bagaria and Nimbus Holdings. Mr. Virendra Shah and Mr. Ashok Kumar Bahety, business associates of the Agrawal family each hold 14% shares in PBIL.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost including the balance sheet restructuring, is estimated to be up to US$ 8.0 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of equity of upto US$1.9 million along with a GAFSP investment of equity of upto US$1.9 million.
location_description: The project is located at Birgunj in Nepal, close to the Company’s existing operations.
development_impact: (i)Food security: Since feed represents over eighty per cent (80%) of live broiler production costs, improvement in feed quality and feed mill production efficiencies, as envisaged by the project would help in reducing cost of production of broiler making it more affordable to the end-consumer through achieving economies of scale. (ii)Supply chain efficiency and income generation for small growers:On successful completion, the project is likely to help increase the efficiency of the food supply chain leading to improved productivity at the farm-gate level thereby translating into higher income for the growers (iii)Employment creation:The proposed project once completed is expected to help create both direct and indirect employment opportunity for people both at the plant and farm level
additionality: (i)Providing flexible financing and patient capital to support a small balance sheet (ii)IFC, with its equity participation and advisory programs, will help the company in enhancing its corporate governance standards. (iii)IFC''s equity partnership will also incorporate best practices in environmental, health & safety and social standards in the Company through implementation of the ESAP (iv)Global sector expertise and leveraging existing relationships for company''s growth

project_description: Yoma Strategic Holdings Ltd. (“Yoma”) together with First Myanmar Investment Co., Ltd (“FMI”) will develop a mixed-use complex on a 10-acre site surrounding the 136 year-old building of the former headquarter of the British Burma Railway Company (the BBR Building) in downtown Yangon, Myanmar. The Project consists of the development of two office towers, a business hotel and a serviced apartment building, a branded residential building, a retail podium, car park, public spaces and underlying infrastructure. The redevelopment of the BBR Building will be undertaken separately to house a Peninsula branded hotel and is not part of the Project.
sponsor_shareholders: Meeyatha International Hotel Limited or another company to be established (the “Company”), both Myanmar-incorporated companies, would undertake the Project. At the commencement of the Project, the Company is expected to be wholly owned by the Project Sponsors together with other investors participating in the Project Yoma and FMI will together be the Project Sponsors, with Yoma being the principal Project Sponsor. Yoma, a leading conglomerate in Myanmar with predominant business interests in real estate, is listed on the Singapore Stock Exchange since 2006. FMI is a Myanmar public company, with a diverse local shareholder base owning approximately 30 percent of its share capital.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Based on the latest design and a quantity surveyor report, the total Project cost is estimated to range from US$515 million to US$540 million. IFC is considering the provision of a financing package of up to US$75 million, consisting of both debt and equity, and mobilizing a parallel financing package of a similar amount.
location_description: The Project site is located on Bogyoke Aung San Road, Pabedan Township, in central Yangon.
development_impact: (i) Construction of critical business infrastructure: The Project will add much-needed supply of international standard office, retail and hospitality infrastructure to Yangon. International standard business infrastructure such as these are of critical importance in attracting foreign investments in the country. (ii) Improvement of service standards: The Project will significantly improve the standards of office, retail and accommodation facilities and services available to travelers and the business community. (iii) Employment creation and knowledge transfer: The Project will create a significant number of direct and indirect employment opportunities for the local community both during construction and operational phases. It will also promote the transfer of service and management expertise and knowledge to the local staff. (iv) Benefits to the local economy and local linkages: The Project will help create demand for locally-sourced materials, services, and labor both during the construction and operation stages. The Project is expected to generate additional sales for local small and medium enterprises, including a wide range of goods and service providers. (v) Increase in tax revenues and foreign exchange: The Project is expected to contribute to the domestic economy through increased tax revenues and foreign exchange inflow, particularly as it is expected that a significant portion of the users (office, retail and apartment lessees and hotel guests) will be foreign nationals and that a significant amount of Project revenues is expected to be paid in foreign currency. (vi) Private sector development: The presence of this large scale development in Yangon will send a positive signal about investing in Myanmar, particularly to foreign investors.
additionality: IFC''s additionality includes: (i) provision of long-term foreign currency financing that is particularly suited for large capital intensive project; (ii) structuring and mobilizing financing from another leading financial institution for the Project; and (iii) sending a positive signal to foreign investors interested in operating in Myanmar, a country that is currently in a transition mode and needs foreign investment to accelerate its development.

project_description: Westfalia Fruto Mocambique Ltda (“WM” or the “Company”), a local subsidiary of Westfalia Limited, the leading South African avocado producer, plans to establish a 200 hectare avocado farm near the city of Chimoio in Central Mozambique (the "Project"). The Company will also build a packhouse to handle own production and that of the local fruit growers (avocados, litchis, mangoes) for the export market. WM will support local small farmers and emerging commercial growers in improving their fruit production through provision of training and technical assistance; and ensuring their access to markets through Westfalia''s established networks.
sponsor_shareholders: Westfalia Fruto Mocambique Ltda will be majority-owned (75%) by Hans Merensky Holdings (“HMH”), a South African fruit producer, exporter, trader and distributor known under its Westfalia trademark, also involved in timber production and processing under the Merensky brand. HMH is South Africa’s largest avocado producer and exporter, and Europe’s largest avocado importer. HMH is an IFC investee company since December 2012. AgDevco will be a minority shareholder (25%) in WM. AgDevCo is a social impact investor and agribusiness project developer with a strong presence in Central Mozambique, across 17 ongoing projects. AgDevCo will provide debt and equity funding and use its experience in small agribusiness development in Mozambique to support the Company in engaging with local farmers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$10.5 million. IFC''s proposed investment comprises a senior A Loan to the Company of up to EUR 3.1 million (US$ 4.1 million equivalent). A portion of the A Loan may be mobilized through the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP). GAFSP portion would finance the construction of the packhouse with capacity sufficient to handle fruit from the neighboring smallholder farmers, giving them access to market through Westfalia''s establish marketing and trading networks.
location_description: The project will be located in the rural area near Zembe, Gondola District, Manica Province of central Mozambique. The company is in the process of acquiring land use rights to an existing 318ha farm located 37km out of Chimoio, capital of the province of Manica. Company''s office will be located in Chimoio.
development_impact: (a) Employment creation: The farm will employ 40 permanent workers while during the harvest period (2 months), it will require 400 additional casual workers. (b) Market access and shared prosperity: WM will provide access to market and fair pricing to hundreds of litchi, mango and avocado growers in Central Mozambique and Zimbabwe (neighbouring Chipinge growing region). (c) Knowledge transfer: WM will provide access to training, inputs and appropriate planting material to smallholders and emerging commercial farmers. (d) SME supply chain development: WM will hire local contractors (logistics, earth moving, equipment & chemicals suppliers and the like). (e) Community Development benefits: WM will set up social infrastructures (local clinic, roads¦) and will partner with local NGOs to improve the well-being of the community. (f) Replicability/Demonstration effect: WM sees a lot of potential for expansion in Mozambique and in the medium term in Zimbabwe. WM also hopes to attract other South African avocado and fruit growers by demonstrating Manica''s suitability for agriculture investments.
additionality: (a) Political and country risk mitigation: IFC''s role is strong in light of the recent instability in the country. IFC will provide country specific advice and notional political risk mitigation. (b) Strategic partnership to strengthen Westfalia''s leadership: Westfalia has requested IFC''s support for its first venture as a primary producer in Sub-Saharan Africa. (c) Long-term financing: IFC is providing a long-term loan, not available on the local market, with a long grace period to accommodate the challenges of an avocado greenfield production and of operating conditions in Mozambique. (d) Community engagement and outgrower scheme support: IFC will provide support via the involvement of GAFSP and of IFC''s technical assistance and advisory programs.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an IFC senior loan of Euro 50 million to Mapei SpA to finance its capital investment program in emerging markets, including facilities in Turkey, Mexico, Egypt, Panama, India, Russian Federation and other emerging countries (the “Project”). The Mapei Group producers and develops adhesives, sealants, waterproofing agents, concrete additives and other specialty chemicals for the construction industry.
sponsor_shareholders: Mapei is a private company owned largely by the Squinzi family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is around Euro 63 million. The proposed IFC loan is Euro 50 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Turkey, Mexico, Egypt, Panama, India, Russian Federation and other emerging countries.
development_impact: The Project is expected to enable transfer of technical and managerial know-how in the specialty chemicals sector, create around 500 jobs and improve competitiveness of local construction industries.
additionality: Knowledge and strong presence in the emerging countries. Diversifying funding sources for Mapei, particularly with longer term tenors for emerging markets investments.

company_name: RC RONESANS INSAAT TAAHHUT ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Renaissance Group is a diversified conglomerate with activities mainly in construction and real estate businesses. IFC is planning to provide a corporate revolving facility of up to US$[50-70] mln to support the working capital (WC) needs of RC Rönesans İnşaat Taahhüt A.Ş. (RCI, or the “Borrower”) and direct and indirect subsidiaries in Turkmenistan, Russia and Turkey between 2014-2017. RCI specializes in design and construction of shopping centers, offices, hotels, mixed-use facilities, heavy industry plants, infrastructure facilities and civil engineering and enjoys a ranking of 64th on the ENR Top 100 International Contractors list.
sponsor_shareholders: All the Renaissance Group companies are consolidated under Renaissance Holding A.S. (“RHOL”, the “Sponsor” or the “Guarantor”) which is 95 % owned by Erman Ilicak, 2.5 % Bahar Ilicak, 2,5 % Ipek Ilicak. The Group operates in Turkey, Russia and various other developing countries in the CIS and MENA regions. RHOL which also owns 100% of RCI is an Ankara-based diversified conglomerate with activities in construction, real estate, energy and expanding into healthcare PPP projects. Renaissance Group was first established in 1993 by civil engineer Erman Ilicak.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Borrower and its direct and indirect subsidiaries have a 3 year WC funding need- mainly to bridge the gap between progress payments and cost of production in the Russia, Turkey and Turkmenistan. The team is proposing to provide RCI and its direct and indirect subsidiaries with a short term revolving facility of US$[50-70] mln, to finance the WC requirements.
location_description: The proposed IFC investment will be a corporate loan and there will be no particular project location. Nevertheless, the Borrower is headquartered in Ankara, while subsidiaries are located in Russia (e.g., St Petersburg, Moscow), Turkey and Turkmenistan.
development_impact: 1. Employment preservation and creation; 2. SME support, by channeling funds to subcontractors through RCI; 3. Payment of taxes (directly from RCI and indirectly from subcontractors);
additionality: The proposed Project is a sound opportunity for IFC to play an important role in its supporting infrastructure development in emerging markets, helping the debottlenecking of key needs for overall economic growth. The Project also represents a way for IFC to make a difference in supporting an important regional EPC company to cope with the additional demand in Russia, turkmenistan on a South-South basis.
Company Name: RC RONESANS INSAAT TAAHHUT ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: Established in 1992, Nam Long Investment Corporation (the “Company”), is one of the leading residential real estate developers in southern Vietnam. The Company operates two key lines of business: (i) affordable housing that targets low to mid income and first time home buyers and (ii) development of townships which comprises mid-high end apartments and townhouses. The Company is seeking to raise up to VND 459 billion (approximately US$21.6 million) to finance the expansion of its affordable housing business which includes but not limited to the following developments: North Saigon EHome 4, Bridge View EHome 5, Golfview EHome 6, and Greenhill EHome 7 (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are: Mr. Nguyen Xuan Quang (the Chairman/ CEO), Mr. Tran Thanh Phong (the Vice-chairman), and Ms. Nguyen Thi Bich Ngoc (the Chairman’s wife) who collectively own 33.6% of the Company’s common shares. The project sub-sponsors are: Ms. Ngo Thi Ngoc Lieu and Nam Khang Investment Corporation who collectively own 14.6% of the Company’s common shares. Other major shareholders of the Company include: (i) ASPL V6 Limited (16.3% shareholding): a US$50 million fund managed by Ireka, a Malaysia based real estate developer; (ii) Nam Viet Ltd. (9.1% shareholding): a 100% owned subsidiary of Goldman Sachs Asset Management; and (iii) Vietnam Azalea Fund Limited (6.7% shareholding): managed by Mekong Capital, a PE fund focusing on the Vietnam market.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$97.6 million. IFC is considering to invest up to VND 158.94 billion (approximately US$7.5 million) in common shares of the Company to fund the expansion of the Company’s affordable housing business.
location_description: Nam Long is headquartered in Ho Chi Minh City, southern Vietnam. The proposed Project comprises of 5 affordable housing developments located in Ho Chi Minh City and Binh Duong, a second tier province next to Ho Chi Minh city.
development_impact: Access to quality and affordable housing: The project will add a significant number of affordable housing units in Vietnam, an IDA country; improve living standards of the lower income population by giving them access to quality and affordable housing. Infrastructure development: affordable/low income housing is currently under-supplied in Vietnam. Governmental support for the sector has been fairly weak and the Project will help improve the infrastructure for the low to middle income earners. Being a pioneer in developing affordable housing in Vietnam Nam Long will encourage other investors to serve the mid-low income population. Employment creation and SME linkages: The Project will help create significant number of direct and indirect employment opportunities for the local communities as well as demand for locally sourced materials, services and labour both during and after construction phase; hence benefit the local community and SMEs. Inclusiveness: Some EHome projects will be built in the suburb areas of Ho Chi Minh city or second tier cities; hence promote inclusive economic growth.
additionality: Long term financing: IFC''s debt financing will be structured with sufficient tenor and grace period that suit the Project''s cashflow. Such financing is not readily available, especially in the current period of macro austerity and credit tightening. In addition, IFC will provide long term capital to the Company in the form of equity. Sector expertise: IFC will share its experience in affordable housing in other emerging markets with the Company. In addition, IFC will share international best practices in property development, particularly during appraisal. Environmental and social best practices: IFC with share with the Company international best practices in E&S management and will work with the Company to improve its standards especially on land acquisition. IFC will also explore energy efficiency opportunities with the Company, for example on green building.

project_description: The Project consists of the construction and operation of a greenfield 210-key, 11-storey business hotel in Addis Ababa (Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia). Upon completion, the Project will be branded “Crowne Plaza” hotel under a full management contract with International Hotels Group (IHG). The purpose of this investment is to help to address the shortage of hotel rooms of international standards in the capital city Addis-Ababa.
sponsor_shareholders: IFC is considering an investment in Tsemex Global Enterprise Plc. (“Tsemex” or the “Company”) and its subsidiary, Tsemex Hotels and Business Plc., both organized and existing in the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. Tsemex is a family business (majority) owned by Mr. Rezene Ayalew, and his children. Mr. Ayalew is a successful local business man.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$37.7 million. IFC''s proposed investment is in the aggregate amount of up to nineteen million United States Dollars (US$19,000,000) comprising loan amounts for the accounts of IFC and, if applicable, participant or parallel banks.
location_description: The Project will be located in the fast-growing Liteda area in Addis Ababa.
development_impact: - Provision of modern business infrastructure: As only 3 hotels carry an international brand in Addis Ababa, the Project will increase the availability of hotel rooms of international standards and stimulate competition in the hospitality industry, particularly in the branded segment. -Migration of best practice: The Project will benefit from (i) the transfer by IHG of its extensive global hotel management expertise to the locally recruited staff through training and development; and (b) IFC''s support in implementing international E&S and health & safety standards. -Employment creation: The investment will create significant local direct employment for about 315 people, including approximately 20 percent of female employees, and indirect employment in the supply value chain. - Benefits to local suppliers: The Project will provide business opportunities to the local suppliers during and after project implementation, particularly in the areas of food & beverages supply and the provision of services (for example, transportation, security services). - Increased tax revenues: The Project will generate tax revenue to the Government of Ethiopia
additionality: -Financial structuring: IFC has supported the Company in developing a financial structure for the Project that adequately mitigates the implementation and operational risks. - Long-term financing: IFC will provide the Project with a loan carrying a tenor that is not available locally or regionally other than through development finance institutions. - Capital mobilization: On a best effort basis, IFC will help to raise additional debt financing for the Project. - Standard setting: IFC will advise the Company on sustainable business and E&S practices specific to the property development and hospitality business. -Global industry expertise/knowledge sharing: IFC will avail to the Project its experience in financing hotel projects particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa.

project_description: The project involves an investment by IFC of up to US$ 4.5 million debt and up to US$ 3.5 million straight equity in Boulos Food and Beverage Limited (“ BFB” or the “Company”), a greenfield company being established for the production of fruit juices, milk products and tomato paste in Nigeria. IFC’s investment will support the procurement and installation of plant and machinery, procurement of delivery trucks, working capital financing and refinancing of existing debt (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: BFB is a private company established in Nigeria and owned by the Mr. Boulos Boulos (50%) and Mrs. Hind Boulos (50%). Mr. Boulos Boulos and the Boulos family have been involved in businesses in Nigeria for over 60 years with interests in automotive assembly through Bel Enterprises Limited, waste paper recycling through Bel Papyrus Limited and paper conversion through Bel Impex Limited.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$30 million. The proposed IFC investment will consist of an A Loan of up to US$ 4.5 million for IFC’s own account and straight equity of up to US$ 3.5 million. IFC’s investment will be alongside Asset and Resource Management Company Private Equity LLP (“ARMPE”, or the “Fund’), a Nigerian private equity firm focused on investments in Nigeria’s fast moving consumer goods sector. ARMPE has proposed to invest up to US$ 6 million in straight equity.
