location_description: The Company’s plant and main warehouse will be located at Antonio Village, Km 9, Ibadan-Lagos Expressway in Ibadan, with a distribution hub to be located in Lagos.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have the following impacts: (i) Adoption of new packaging technology with improved food safety benefits. (ii) Direct and indirect employment with the creation of 446 jobs, of which approximately 139 will be to women. (iii) MSME development through development of wholesalers, retailers, distributors. (iv) Tax revenues accruing to Government.
additionality: IFC''s additionality in the Project will include: (i) Provision of competitive long-term financing including equity financing with tenors commensurate with the Project. (ii) Long-term partnership as the Compnay views IFC as a strategic partner for current and future projects. (iii) Enhancement of corporate governance practices within the Company. (iv) IFC will ensure the Company adheres to high standards for food safety, and environmental, health and safety practices.

project_description: Century Sunshine Group Holdings Limited (CS or the Company) is a public company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (Ticker: 0509). Founded in 2000, CS’s businesses include ecological fertilizers and magnesium alloys, with main manufacturing facilities located in Donghai, Jiangsu province and Baishan, Jilin province respectively. CS is currently considering the following expansion plan by 2016 (the Project): (1) increasing the production capacity of its fertilizer manufacturing facility from 300,000 tons to 750,000 tons at the Donghai site; and (2) increasing the production capacity of its magnesium (Mg) manufacturing facility from 16,000 tons to 75,000 tons at the Baishan site.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Chi Wen Fu is the Founder, Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and majority shareholder (42.39% shareholding) of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost is estimated to be $174 million and the proposed IFC investment includes an A Loan of up to $25 million and straight equity of up to $15 million.
location_description: At the Donghai site, CS owns an open-pit serpentine mine. The fertilizer plant is adjacent to the mine with sulfuric/phosphoric acid manufacturing facilities. The main products are compound fertilizer (NPK or Si-Mg-NPK) and organic fertilizer which use agriculture wastes as raw materials. Si-Mg is from serpentine mine. At the Baishan site, CS owns an open-pit dolomite mine and dolomite is used as the raw material for Mg alloy. The Mg smelting and refining plant is 15 km from the mine.
development_impact: - Improve food security: CS supplies fertilizers to farmers in 14 provinces and 2 autonomous regions in China, of which ten are classified as frontier regions by the International Development Association (IDA). The fertilizers help enhance the yield of the farmland and hence address food security issues in China. - Promote the applications of an environmentally-friendly material: Weight reduction is the most cost effective means to reduce fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions from the transportation sector. Generally, it has been estimated that for every 10 percent of weight eliminated from a vehicle''s total weight, fuel economy improves by 7 percent. Magnesium alloy is one of the lightest structural materials used in automobiles -- 75 percent lighter than steel and 33 percent lighter than aluminum. The Chinese government encourages the development and application of high-performance magnesium alloys, as stated in its twelfth 5-year plan. - Employment creation and local linkages: The Project is expected to create approximately 1,000 new job opportunities, of which 600 are in Jilin, a frontier province. The Project is also expected to spur the growth of local supply of goods and services, such as machinery, raw materials, and transportation services.
additionality: Long-term partnership: IFC will support an existing client to further expand its manufacturing capacity in new high value added products. Technical/ Industry/ Global Knowledge: IFC has invested in similar sectors around the world and built in-depth knowledge. CS values IFC''s insights and lessons learned. Particularly, the Company is looking forward to IFC''s sharing of knowledge and expertise on optimizing the use of by-products, operational benchmarking and industry connections. Expertise in Environment and Social Standards: IFC can help CS improve its capacity in areas of environment and social management. Stamp of Approval: IFC''s participation can send a positive signal to the market of IFC''s support for CS to be a first mover in commercializing specialty magnesium alloys, which is mentioned as the 21st century new material in the twelfth 5-year plan of the Chinese government. This will help CS enhance its image and brand.

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: Through this project, IFC is looking to support the expansion plan of The Willbes Haitian S.A (“the Company”), the Haiti-based subsidiary of a leading South-Korean ready-made apparel producer. The Willbes Haitian S.A. currently was established in 2001 and operates out of the Haitian State owned SONAPI industrial park in Port-au-Prince assembling apparel product, employing approximately 1,740 workers, mostly uneducated women. The Project would create around an additional 1,000 jobs. IFC proposes will support the Company’s investment program which includes the expansion of its existing sewing facility. This expansion will help the Company and Haitian workers benefit from the opportunity presented by the HELP Act which grants Haitian apparel duty-free entry to the United States and allows apparel factories flexible use of third-country materials in production (expiring 2020).
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is The Willbes & Co. Ltd (“Willbes” or the “Sponsor”), a Korean company founded in 1973 that operates as a manufacturer of apparel products. It is listed on the Korean Stock Exchange. The Sponsor provides textile products including knit wears, woven wears, swim wears, sweaters and microfiber products; these are produced at factories in Korea (1973), Dominican Republic (1989), Honduras (1991), China (1994), Haiti (2001), Cambodia (2007) and Indonesia (2008). All of these subsidiaries, except The Willbes Haitian S.A., are 100% owned by The Willbes & Co Ltd. The Willbes Haitian S.A. is owned by The Willbes Dominicana Inc. (80%) and The Willbes & Co Ltd (20%). Key customers include Target, Gap and Wal-Mart. The Willbes & Co Ltd is also engaged in the following other sectors: education services and real estate rentals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$ 12 million. The IFC financing would be in the form of a US$ 4 million corporate loan to The Willbes Haitian S.A. IFC is also mobilizing an equivalent parallel loan from Inter American Development Bank (IDB). The remaining US$ 4 million has been contributed by parent company The Willbes Dominicana Inc. since 2011.
location_description: The expansion project will occur in the SONAPI Industrial Park, located less than 2 miles from the Port-au-Prince International Airport and less than 5 miles from the Port of Port-au-Prince. The SONAPI park is Haitian Government owned and offers industrial facilities to a wide range of manufacturing companies.
development_impact: The Project also has a solid Development Impact which includes: 1) Higher employment: this project will increase employment opportunities particularly for women; 2) Higher exports: the project will increase the inflows of foreign exchange into the country and fuel economic growth; 3 3) Improvement of Environmental & Social practices: the project will set a high standard for E&S practices by following IFC''s E&S requirements.
additionality: IFC will play a significant role through: 1) Long Term Financing: IFC''s loan will provide long-term financing that is currently unavailable; 2) Sending a strong Signal: IFC''s investment will send a strong signal to the private sector, thereby boosting new investors'' confidence in Haiti; and 3) Resources mobilization: IFC will arrange an additional financing required for the project.

project_description: The project involves first the expansion of the Athi River grinding plant of National Cement Company Limited (“NCCL”), in order to have an installed nominal cement grinding capacity of 1.7 million tons per annum (Mtpa) of Portland cement. It is located at Athi River, c.40 km south of Nairobi, Kenya’s capital. Secondly, a new clinker production line will be built at Merueshi, c.160 km south of Nairobi, near the Nairobi-Mombasa highway. The nominal capacity of the kiln is expected to be 3,300 tons per day (tpd) or 1.1Mtpa, assuming a maximum 330 days of annual operation.
sponsor_shareholders: NCCL is a stand-alone company which forms part of the Devki group of companies (“Devki” or the “Group”) which comprises five Kenya-based entities operating in the steel, cement and services sectors and two companies based in the Democratic Republic of Congo producing steel and copper. Devki was established in 1986 by Mr. Narendra Rameshchandra Raval, EBS, as a steel and trading company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$188 million. IFC is considering an investment for its own account, including debt and equity, of up to US$74 million. In addition, IFC would mobilize up to US$22 million through a B loan.
location_description: The grinding plant (first phase of expansion) is located at Athi River, 40 km south of Nairobi, Kenya’s capital, while the new clinker production line (second phase of expansion) will be built at Merueshi, c.160 km south of Nairobi, near the Nairobi-Mombasa highway.
development_impact: Employment generation: - the project will create direct and indirect employment; - the project will provide skilled and unskilled jobs during the construction phase; - the project will create temporary jobs during construction; - the project is expected to add permanent jobs at the NCCL facilities; and - the project will create a large number of indirect jobs in the transportation and delivery sectors. Increased local supply chain and consumption of local goods and services: - the project will create new business opportunities in the local economy due to increased demand for the supply of raw materials and delivery services. In particular, it will benefit those small and medium enterprises engaged in transporting the company''s raw materials and products in their own trucks and providing maintenance and general services to the company; and - the communities close to the plant will benefit as they will provide local services and supplies to the plant and its employees. Other benefits to local communities: - the local communities will benefit from the company''s corporate social responsibility initiatives including the development of community infrastructure and the establishment of a scholarship fund. Environmental and social performance: - by complying with IFC''s performance standards and the World Bank Group''s environmental, health and safety (EHS) standards, the company will achieve higher environmental and social standards, which should increase its reputation, reduce the risk of adverse impacts on local communities, and increase the credibility of the private sector with respect to corporate social responsibility. Private sector development: - the success of the project will send a positive signal to other investors considering investments in Kenya; and - the project is expected to set environmental and social standards that can be replicated by other cement producers.
additionality: Long-term partnership: - the company is keen to develop a strong relationship with IFC as it values IFC''s long-term financing, which is suited to the capital intensity and cyclicality of the cement industry, to support projects in emerging markets; - the company believes that IFC''s decision to support the company''s project after IFC''s comprehensive review of the project''s technical, environmental and social aspects would demonstrate IFC''s confidence in the viability of the project; and - the company would like IFC, based on its global cement sector knowledge and expertise, to advise the company on all aspects of the investment from construction and implementation to operational matters to ensure the project''s successful implementation and operation across economic cycles. Environmental and social standards/implementation and various advisory services: - the company is seeking to integrate sustainable development into its business strategies and operations and it seeks strong financial performance with an equally strong commitment to social and environmental responsibility. In this context, the company believes that IFC can play a significant role in helping the company achieve these goals and would appreciate IFC''s stamp of approval; - IFC, unlike commercial lenders, has global expertise and cement industry knowledge to provide the company with guidance on setting and implementing higher standards. IFC will work with the company to identify resource efficiency opportunities; and - IFC can provide the company with various advisory services in areas such as environmental and social (E&S) management systems capacity-building, corporate social responsibility initiatives and corporate governance enhancement.

project_description: IFC is considering to provide financing of up to EUR5 million to support the expansion of Societe Industrielle Agro-Alimentaire (the "Company" or “SIAGRO”), a Senegal-based beverage producer (mineral water, nectar juice and UHT milk)("the Project").
sponsor_shareholders: SIAGRO main shareholders include by Mr. Mohamed Fares, Mr. Muhyedine Fares, Mr. Hassan Fares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at EUR10 million. IFC’s proposed financing is an A loan of up to EUR5 million.
location_description: SIAGRO is located near the village of Kirene, Senegal in the sub-prefecture of Thies.
development_impact: Â· Increased availability of affordable quality beverage products for consumers in West Africa. Â· Increased tax revenue. Â· Creation of a regional beverage champion. Â· Demonstration effect for potential new entrants in the beverage sector in the region. Â· Kirene is distributing its milk to schools thereby promoting nutrition and learning. Â· Increase stable revenue for farmers in Senegal providing fresh milk to Kirene.
additionality: - Provide long term financing to support expansion. - Supporting import substitution.

project_description: IFC is investing in ZincOx Resources PLC (ZincOx or the Company), a recent entrant in the zinc recycling sector with an innovative technology, to help it finance pre-operating and research and development expenditures related to potential zinc recycling projects in Turkey, Thailand and Russia.
sponsor_shareholders: ZincOx is quoted on the London Stock Exchange’s Alternative Investment Market (AIM). About 65% of the Company’s shares are held by institutional investors, many of which are major international companies. The balance is held by the management and private investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is about US$10 million. The overall proposed IFC''s investment is up to US$8 million with an immediate investment of US$4 million. The Project is financing pre-operating expenditures to develop potential projects in Turkey, Thailand and Russia.
development_impact: - Positive Climate Change Impact: The investment will support recovery of resources and creation of valuable raw materials from hazardous waste. - -Furthermore, unlike the traditional method of zinc recovery, the ZincOx process is energy efficient, environmentaly friendly and has a higher recovery rate, with no resudual waste. - Management of waste: EAFD recovery reduces amount of poisonous waste going to landfills, which is a significant benefit, given a major environmental hazard landfills present for health of population. - Job Creation and know-how transfer: Introduction of waste processing on a commercial scale in multiple countries will result on direct and non-direct employment opportunities. The expansion of the innovative technology will help promote a concept of viable commercial resource-saving and environmentally friendly business model.
additionality: - Strategic Partnership in the Climate Change Space: IFC''s initial support of ZincOx will facilitate the development of long-term partnership with the Company, supporting its expansion plans in emerging countries. As ZincOx needs new capital to finance expansion of its operations, IFC''s support in funding the upcoming projects in Thailand, Turkey and Russia is vital for implementation of its expansion plans. Subsequently, IFC will be able to follow up with financing of individual projects'' main capex with debt/equity as the projects come to fruition. - Catalytic Role: IFC''s engagement with ZincOx in early stages of projects development would be positively viewed by the market and can catalyze further support for the technology and the business model. - IFC has the technical expertise to understand the new technology to help the industry reshape its recycling of hazardous materials, while other institutions may not have this capacity nor appetite for such novelty.

project_description: Marina Market was created in November 1989. As of today, the company operates 4 supermarkets with a warehouse facility in Burkina Faso (Marina Market Burkina Faso), a supermarket and retail/office building in Ghana (Marina Market Ghana), and a supermarket in Niger (Marina Market Niger). The Project entails: (i) the modernization and expansion of the main supermarket, Centre Ville by building and equipping two additional floors of 2,250 sq.m in total on the current supermarket site. The new floors accommodate non-food items on the first floor and a food court on the last one; (ii) the construction of two other buildings of 1,050 sq.m., at the centralized purchasing warehouse; and (iii) the expansion of the Bobo Dioulasso supermarket by 900 sq.m, as well as, the acquisition of some equipment.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsors are Fadi Restom, Georges Restom, and Fares Restom. The Sponsors are private regional players, and well established in Niger, BurkinaFaso, and Ghana. The project company is equally owned by the three Sponsors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be EUR 2.75 million. IFC proposed investment is EUR 800,000 in the form of an A Loan.
location_description: The Project will be located in Ouagadougou as well as Bobo Dioulasso, both of which cities are in Burkina Faso Expected Developmental Impact of the Project: The Project will contribute to the modernization of the retail and service industries through the introduction of business infrastructure in a country where there is lack of such facilities. The success of the Marina Market Burkina project will help develop local skills in modern retailing and support the development of malls by demonstrating their commercial viability. Projects like the Marina Market retail center in Burkina Faso is aimed at facilitating the private sector initiative in increasing the stock of prime retail properties in Ouagadougou as a way of enhancing economic growth. The Project will also create local jobs during the operational stage in a country where the unemployment rate is high. In addition, it will have a direct impact on consumers that will benefit from improved retail services, better consumer choices and higher quality of goods sold.
additionality: - By entering into markets currently not supported by FDI, IFC will play a catalyst role. Burkina has attracted relatively low levels of FDI which reflects the obstacles to of investing in a land locked country with resultingly high production costs. Total inflows of Burkina represents 10% of FDI inflows into Cote d''Ivoire and 14% of those into Ghana. - IFC has been engaging with the Sponsors for the past five years. Through IFC''s informal advice and introduction to external consultants, they have been able to set up a bankable project and develop an adequate financing plan that leading local commercial banks have been encouraged to support financially today. - To ensure a sustainable growth of Marina Market business, one critical area would be to raise the level of management sophistication of the companies. Following IFC''s recommendations, the companies'' financials are getting now audited. The Sponsors are also setting in place a capable management team for the activities expansion. -IFC will help provide a steadier flow of long-term financing and an opportunity for Marina Market to expand and diversify its operations. The loans will be on an 6-year basis. Since inception, none of the Marina Market companies has been able to secure loans with such terms in Burkina as they are not available in those markets.

company_name: SHANDONG HEKANGYUAN POULTRY BREEDING INC LTD
project_description: Shandong Hekangyuan Poultry Breeding Company Ltd. (“Hekangyuan - HKY” or the “Company”) was established in December 2010. Currently, HKY operates through twenty one active subsidiaries, organized across three main business segments, including: 1) The duck breeding division has 8 subsidiaries, located in Shandong, Hebei and Jiangsu provinces. Both grandparent stock (GP) and parent stock (PS) ducks are bred, with existing capacity of around 80 million PS day-old ducklings (DODs) per annum; 2) The broiler breeding division has 3 subsidiaries, located in Shandong and Hebei provinces with capacity of around 38 million PS day-old chicken (DOCs) per annum; 3) Commercial growing poultry (duck and broiler) division, operated by 10 subsidiaries in Shandong with production capacity per annum of 4 million broilers birds and 10 million ducks. About 90% of the farming is contracted to independent farms. Post the expansion, HKY can be the top 2 duck company and the top 5 broiler company by 2016, with total breeding capacity of 189 million DODs and 90 million DOCs, and locations in Shandong, Jiangsu and Hebei provinces (the “Project”). The construction of the Project has already commenced and it is expected to be completed over the next 18-24 months.
sponsor_shareholders: The founders (Mr. MENG Qingli and Mr. WANG Sheng) and the management team collectively hold 55% of the Company. Jiangxi Zhengbang Farming Co., Ltd holds 40% ownership. The remaining 5% is held by Shanghai Hejun Investment Consulting Co., Ltd.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project’s total cost is estimated to be US$51.7 million equivalent, including $34.6 million for equipment, building & construction including a 10% contingency, and $17.1 million for working capital.
location_description: The Project Locations are in Shandong and Hebei provinces.
development_impact: Farmers Reached: Currently, about 1,000 rural households are working with the Company as contract farmers for commercial ducks and broilers farming. The Project will increase the number by another 500 rural households. Food Safety: The Chinese poultry sector is still characterized by poor hygiene standards, inadequate bio-security, and over-use of antibiotics. By investing in Hekangyuan, IFC is supporting a company with a focus on efficiency and food safety and then enhancing its image in the market and setting an example for other similar companies in the industry. Supply Chain Efficiency- the Company is dedicated to the improvement of poultry breeding operation. Its development means the increased supply of high-quality day old ducks and chicks to commercial duck/broiler operations, which enhances the whole supply chain efficiency (better FCR/lower mortality, etc).
additionality: Long-term partnership: Hekangyuan is keen to attract financing from credible and knowledgeable partners such as IFC who have a long-term investment horizon and can add value to the operations through industry knowledge and enable the Company to implement a properly designed strategic plan. Global perspective and Deep Industry knowledge: IFC has invested in the poultry sector around the world and built up in-depth knowledge. Hekangyuan values IFC's insights and lessons learned. Particularly, The Company is looking forward to IFC's sharing of knowledge and expertise on food safety, disease management, and operational control. Credibility and positioning: IFC's participation, particularly as an equity investor, can help Hekangyuan enhance its image and brand in the market. Specifically, the on-going issues with food safety in the poultry sector (high antibiotic levels in chicken) have created a negative impact on the poultry growers. IFC's signaling through its diligence and investment can help bolster the Company's image with customers as a quality supplier with a focus on disease management and food safety. The Company is also aiming at an IPO in domestic market in next 3-4 years and expects the signaling from IFC's direct investment will enhance its reputation with investors and other partners.
Company Name: SHANDONG HEKANGYUAN POULTRY BREEDING INC LTD

project_description: The proposed investment is to assist Industrial Milk Company (the “Company” or “IMC”), a large-scale primary agricultural producer operating in Central and Northern Ukraine, in expanding the scope of its agricultural operations. The proposed 4-year investment program involves: (i) expansion of agricultural land to 185,000 hectares by 2015, (ii) expansion of storage capacity to 554 thousand tones, (iii) further modernization and purchase of supporting farm machinery and infrastructure, and (iv) increase in working capital.
sponsor_shareholders: IMC is majority-owned (76.5%) by Alexander Petrov, a Ukrainian businessman. In April 2011, IMC did an IPO on WSE floating a 23.5% equity stake
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$237 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to US$50 million. The balance of the project will be financed with internal cash generation and local bank financing.
location_description: IMC is headquartered in Kyiv, Ukraine. The Project will support the Company’s operation in Chernigiv, Sumy and Poltava regions of Ukraine.
development_impact: The proposed investment will: (i) support a viable economic activity and help secure employment in frontier rural areas of Chernigiv, Sumy and Poltava regions; (ii) contribute to food security by increasing production of grains and oil crops; and (iii) contribute to private sector development through promotion of best practice in farming.
additionality: Through a strategic engagement with the Company, IFC is well positioned to: 1. Finance significant part of of the Company''s funding needs at the time when long term financing from local sources is scarce; 2. Establish long term partnership with the Company with the ability to support further expansion; 3. Share its global expertise in primary production through coordinated investment and advisory operations.

sector: Other Textile Products (Including Industrial and Medical Products)
project_description: Flexituff India Limited (“FIL” or the “Company”) plans to raise US$16 million from IFC through a combination of straight equity and Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds (“FCCBs”). This is a corporate financing with proceeds expected to be utilized to fund the Company’s growth plans and towards working capital requirements.
sponsor_shareholders: The promoter group collectively owns 30.6% of the Company. Apart from them, Clearwater Capital owns 9.7% and TPG Growth Fund owns 5.3% of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Company plans to increase the production capacity of geo-textiles, FIBC and drippers at its existing facilities. The Company also plans, in future, to set up FIBC finishing facilities in Brazil and South Africa. These projects are in various stages of development and implementation.
location_description: The Company is implementing brownfield expansions at its existing manufacturing facilities in Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh and Kashipur, Uttarakhand. The Company also plans to set up FIBC finishing operations in Brazil and South Africa.
development_impact: The Project is expected to enhance employment generation and downward SME linkages in frontier regions in India, including a low income state. It will also increase the availability of the various products manufactured by the Company which contribute towards safe packaging and delivery of food and pharmaceuticals and support to infrastructure.
additionality: IFC will support the Company in its expansion plans by providing long-term capital. The Company is keen on capitalizing IFC''s presence and experience in the geographies it intends to establish operations in. The Company would also benefit from IFC''s Environmental and Social Performance Standards.

company_name: Stora Enso Pulp And Paper Asia AB
project_description: The Project is to build plantation-based integrated board and pulp mills at Beihai city in Guangxi, southern China. The mill will initially include a 450,000 tons per year state-of-the-art paperboard machine and pulp capacity of 900,000 tons per year, including necessary energy plant and auxiliary facilities. The project will be implemented in two phases, with the first phase of investment being the state-of-the-art paperboard machine and an integrated bleached chemical thermo mechanical pulp (BCTMP) mill. Following the completion of the first phase the second investment phase will comprise a kraft pulp production line. The board and pulp mills will be integrated with wood supply from self-managed eucalyptus plantations. The project currently operates 90,000 hectares of land and will continue to develop its plantation base until the conclusion of Phase II, with a possibility for expansion through further land leasing. The Project will serve the fast-growing market for liquid packaging board and other premium consumer board grades. The Project is subject to regulatory approvals, the signing of final documentation and other customary conditions precedent. Construction at the industrial site will commence when the mentioned preconditions have been fulfilled, which is expected to occur latest in the beginning of 2014. Production of board is estimated to start early 2016. Stora Enso Pulp & Paper Asia AB (the “Company”), an existing holding company domiciled in Sweden, will implement the Project through three subsidiaries: two sino-foreign joint venture companies with 85% ownership by the Company and 15% ownership by Guangxi Forestry Group Co. Ltd., a state-owned company under the Guangxi provincial government; the third is the existing Guangxi Stora Enso Forestry Co., Ltd., to be reincorporated as a sino-foreign joint venture company with 95% ownership by the Company and 5% ownership by Beihai Forestry Investment & Development Company Ltd., a state-owned company under Beihai city government.
sponsor_shareholders: Stora Enso Oyj (“Stora Enso”) is the Sponsor of the Project. It is a long-established global international pulp & paper company listed in Stockholm and Helsinki. Its business segments include biomaterials, paper, packaging, and wood products.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at EUR1.6 billion, excluding working capital and other pre-operation expenditures. The proposed IFC investment includes an A loan of USD equivalent of up to EUR65 million for IFC’s own account, a B loan of USD equivalent of up to EUR360 million, and equity of up to RMB357 million.
location_description: The mill site of the Project is a greenfield site within the Tieshangang Port Industrial Park, 40 kilometers east of Beihai City, Guangxi, China. The site is two kilometers from the port and has existing access to roads and future access to railway. The plantations of the Project locate at four regions (Beihai, Nanning, Qinlian, Yulin) in south Guangxi. All plantations are in rural areas.
development_impact: - Contribute to the development of Guangxi, an underdeveloped region in China, by creating jobs, improving plantation productivity and processing wood raw material wood into high-value products. - Mitigate climate change through carbon sequestration - Contribute to continuous modernization of pulp & paper industry in China. - Introduction of safe and productive harvesting and silvicultural operations in China - Promote sustainable forest management. - Provide linkage to farmers by supplying high-yield seedlings, plantation establishment knowledge, renting land and sourcing various products and services from farmers. - Contribute to food safety through full product traceability and supply of high quality liquid food packaging materials.
additionality: - Contribute to the implementation of best practices in environmental & social areas through a solid environmental and social action plan and proactive cooperation with the Sponsor in the implementation and supervision. - Share IFC''s knowledge and experience in the country. - Provide risk capital as an equity investor. - Provide longer tenor financing with an extended grace period, which commercial banks cannot provide but is needed given capital intensive nature of the Project. - Mobilize B loans.
Company Name: Stora Enso Pulp And Paper Asia AB

company_name: TIRYAKI AGRO GIDA SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: As an agricultural commodity trade and supply chain manager since early 80’s, Tiryaki Agro Gida Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (the “Company” or “Tiryaki”) is engaged in sourcing, processing and storage of both conventional and organic agricultural products with a storage capacity of more than 500,000 tons. The proposed project involves refinancing of the existing working capital facility of and to finance incremental working capital needs required for the Company’s growth in operations at an estimated cost of US$330 million (the ‘Project’). The Project will ensure Tiryaki’s continued access to working capital funding which is critical for the Company’s growth.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsors are ultimately Tiryaki Family as they fully own the majority shareholder of the Company (Tiryaki Holding A.S., representing 71% of share capital of the Company) in addition to their individual shares corresponding less than 1% of the Company’s share capital in aggregate. Remaining shareholders of Tiryaki are (i) Gulf Investors Agro S.A.R.L., a Luxembourg based company established by Investcorp, a Bahrain-listed private equity fund, to utilize part of Gulf Opportunity Fund I launched in 2008 (23%) and (ii) European Bank of Reconstruction and Development, a multilateral development bank (5.5%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$330 million consisting of refinancing the existing working capital loan facility (US$230 million) and financing the potential incremental working capital needs of the Company (US$100 million). IFC considers providing an A loan of up to US$40 million for its own account.
location_description: The proposed IFC investment will be a corporate loan and there will be no particular project location. Nevertheless, the Company is headquartered in Istanbul while its processing and storage facilities are located in Turkey (e.g., Gaziantep, Balikesir, Corum, Mersin and Trabzon) and Jordan. The Company has two sales offices in Dubai/UAE & China.
development_impact: - Supply Chain Linkages & Access to Farmers: Tiryaki sources directly from more than 2,850 farmers (all of whom are MSMEs) in Turkey, providing them seeds and pre-financing in the process excluding 30-40 wholesalers who have supply linkages with individual farmers. - Supporting a Regional Player: The Project will improve competitiveness of the Company as well as underline its market position in Turkey which has substantional room for competition. - Job Preservation and Tax Revenues for the Governments: Given that agribusiness is a strategic sector for Turkey, accounting for 25% of employment, the Project will help the sector to preserve the job while increasing tax revenues to the Government on the back of improved supply chain linkages as well as sound operations of the Company.
additionality: - Access to Liquidity & Long-term Partnership: IFC will provide the most crucial component for the growth of the trading business by enhancing Tiryaki''s access to liqudity. Furthermore, IFC will also improve the Company''s access to a developmental financial institution which has the ability to offer various products from straight debt to equity by fostering the relationship with this existing IFC client. - Stamp of Approval: Having IFC in the Company''s capital structure as a financier will strengthen Tiryaki''s ability to raise financing by signaling the sound performance of the Company. It can further provide comfort to the client at a potential initial public offering in the medium- to long-term. - Global Networking and Know-How Sharing: Tiryaki is growing internationally and IFC''s global experience and network in agribusiness sector could continue to create additional value to the Company in this respect in addition to increasing its know-how to further penetrate highly fragmented domestic market. - Environmetal and Social (E&S) Standard Setting: E&S management is becoming more critical for agribusiness companies, particularly in international markets where there is room for the Company to further increase its presence. IFC can continue to play a key role in developing Tiryaki''s E&S management systems strengthening its competitive position domestically and internationally.
Company Name: TIRYAKI AGRO GIDA SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: Shangri-La Asia Limited (“Shangri-La”) is undertaking the following developments in Yangon, Myanmar: (i) construction and refurbishment of the existing 485-room Traders Hotel in downtown Yangon; and (ii) development of the 240-room Shangri-La branded service apartments on a 15-acre site near the Kandawgyi Lake (together, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Shangri-La Asia Limited (“Shangri-La”), headquartered in Hong Kong, is a leading owner and operator of deluxe hotels and resorts primarily in Asia. Shangri-La is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Kuok (Singapore) Limited is an investment holding company based in Singapore and Kerry Holdings Limited is an investment company based in Hong Kong. Shangri-La, Kuok (Singapore) Limited and Kerry Holdings Limited and their subsidiaries together own the entire share capital of the Project companies.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is expected to be US$241 million and IFC is considering the provision of a debt financing package of up to US$80 million.
location_description: The Project will take place at the existing Traders Hotel in downtown Yangon and a 15-acre site near the Kandawgyi Lake.
development_impact: (i) Construction of critical business infrastructure: The Project will add much-needed supply of international standard hospitality infrastructure to Yangon. International standard business infrastructure such as these are of critical importance in driving foreign investments in the country. (ii) Improvement of hotel service standards: The Project will improve the standards of accommodation facilities and services available to travelers and the business community. While Shangri-La''s extensive training and high operating standards will assure guests of a high-quality product, it will also encourage broad improvements in the standards of existing hotels. (iii) Employment creation and knowledge transfer: The Project will create a significant number of direct and indirect employment opportunities for the local community both during construction and operational phases. It will also promote the transfer of hotel management expertise and knowledge to the local staff. (iv) Benefits to the local economy and local linkages: The Project will help create demand for locally-sourced materials, services, and labor both during the construction and operation stages. The Project is expected to generate additional sales for local small and medium enterprises, including a wide range of goods and service providers. (v) Increase in tax revenues and foreign exchange: The Project is expected to contribute to the domestic economy through increased tax revenues and foreign exchange inflow, particularly as it is expected that a significant portion of the users (hotel guests and apartment lessees) will be foreign nationals and that the majority of Project revenues will be paid in foreign currency. (vi) Private sector development: The presence of these large scale developments in Yangon will send a positive signal about Myanmar, particularly to other foreign investors who are considering investments in the country.
additionality: IFC''s additionality includes: (i) provision of long-term foreign currency financing that suits the Project''s cashflow cycle; (ii) supporting a long-term IFC client in an IDA country; and (iii) sending a positive message to potential foriegn investors interested in operating in Myanmar, a country that is currently in a transition mode and needs foreign investment for its growth.

company_name: The Palestine Growth Capital Fund C.V.
project_description: The Palestine Growth Capital Fund (the "Fund") is a Palestine dedicated SME private equity fund, seeking minority and controlling positions in high-growth SMEs.
sponsor_shareholders: The project is co-sponsored by The Abraaj Group ("Abraaj”) and Palestine Investment Fund ("PIF"). PIF was established in 2003 as a publicly owned investment company which aims to build a strong economy by developing strategic projects in vital sectors, such as SMEs, real estate, energy, telecommunications and finance. Abraaj is an alternative asset management group which invests in Asia, MENA, Turkey and Central Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America. The regional and the country teams have experience in private equity as well as operational and industry background and experience in adding value through active ownership and change management. The country team in Ramallah will be supported by a Dubai-based Abraaj regional team who will provide assistance in transaction sourcing and execution, due diligence on potential investments, management assistance at investee companies and strategic advice.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund is targeting a size of US$ 35.8 million. It is proposed that IFC will invest up US$ 3 million in the Fund.
location_description: The Fund is a limited partnership under Dutch law. The Fund will make investments in Palestine.
development_impact: 1) Job creation: SMEs are the major sources of employment in West Bank and Gaza. Through the Fund's investment in SMEs, much needed growth capital will be injected into the system to foster employment creation. 2) Access to finance: The Fund will provide long term risk capital, which is very difficult for the local SMEs to obtain. 3) Introducing new sources of finance: Establishment of funds in the region introduces additional and complementary sources of financing to the financial markets which are largely dominated by banks. 4) Promoting sustainable growth: The Fund will play an active role in strengthening the SME's governance and transparency. Through hands-on involvement, operating efficiencies of the portfolio companies will be improved, thus promoting growth and sustainability.
additionality: 1) Support for a first time team in frontier markets: IFC will provide support for a management team targeting SMEs in Palestine for the first time, in a conflict affected frontier market. 2) Restoring investor confidence: IFC's participation will enhance investor confidence to channel more stable institutional capital flows to a conflict-affected country that typically has difficulty attracting equity investors. This is a much needed role for post-crisis MENA countries. 3) Environmental and social: IFC will advocate the implementation of E&S standards and continue its stewardship in that area.
Company Name: The Palestine Growth Capital Fund C.V.

project_description: The project involves providing an annual revolving working capital facility to Mriya, a leading Ukrainian primary agricultural producer with a proven track record of growing wheat, barley, sugar beet, rapeseed, potatoes, and other crops. The working capital facility will provide financing for inputs needed for agricultural production to produce agricultural commodities for sale to local clients and international traders. In addition to the working capital facility, the project includes a three year loan to help Mriya improve its waste management and realize energy efficiencies.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is the Guta family (the “Sponsors”), who founded Mriya in 1992 and control it till this day. The head of the Guta family, Ivan Guta, a well-respected Ukrainian businessman, and his wife, Klaudia Guta, Ivan and Klaudia Guta established Mriya, after having worked for eight years at a state farm. In 2002, Andriy and Mykola Guta, the sons of the founders, joined the family business after completing their education in Ukraine and abroad. Following a private placement on the Entry Standard of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2008, the Sponsors collectively own 80% of Mriya’s Cyprus-based holding company that fully controls all of Mriya’s Ukraine-based operating companies, with the remaining owned by institutional investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment is a US$60 million corporate facility which will be used to finance procurement of agricultural inputs to produce grains and other crops. Additionally, IFC will issue new three-year US$5 million A loan to improve Mriya’s energy efficiencies and waste management.
location_description: The project is located in the Ternopil, Ivano-Frankivsk, Chernivtsi, Lviv and Khmelnitsky regions, which are among the poorest, primarily agricultural, regions of Ukraine.
development_impact: IFC''s financing will contribute to the development of a large-scale modern farming operation which will improve land productivity and have a demonstration impact on other neighboring farms. Mriya''s land and operations are located in Western Ukraine in the Ternopil, Ivano-Frankivsk, Lviv, Chernivtsi and Khmelnitsky regions. These four regions are amongst the poorest regions in the country. Development impact of the project will be as follows: Employment: Mriya''s investment program and the additional permanent and seasonal employment positions created by Mriya will make a significant contribution to the emergence of economic opportunities for the population in the regions that Mriya operates in. In addition to creating new jobs, Mriya is setting new employment standards in the region by providing benefits to its farm workers such food and housing. Environmental and Social Standards: As part of the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP), Mriya will implement an ESMS to further enhance its environmental and social management. Private Sector Development: Mriya sells its products to a diversified base of final customers and traders. Among them, there currently are about 50 MSME distributors of mainly potatoes and corn, for final sales on the domestic market and 110 trasporters to deliver the grains and crops to the port for export.
additionality: Source of financing: The IFC facility will allow Mriya to secure part of its large and growing financing needs at the time when available local financing is scarce; Long-term partnership: Mriya has made a strategic decision to build relationships with steady and long-term financiers such as IFC and EBRD that have extensive emerging markets experience and will stay the course alongside their partners; By partnering with IFC, the Company will be able to enhance its risk profile. Mriya is expected to benefit from its on-going relationship with IFC during a future listing on a major stock exchange.

company_name: CENTRAL AMERICAN MEZZANINE INFRASTRUCTURE FUND II LP
project_description: The Central American Mezzanine Infrastructure Fund II LP (“CAMIF II” or the “Fund”) is a follow-on fund to the existing CAMIF fund (“Fund I”), in which IFC is currently an investor. Like Fund I, CAMIF II is a 12 year mezzanine Fund that will invest in operating and new (brownfield and greenfield) medium-sized companies/projects in infrastructure and related sectors in Central America, the Caribbean, Mexico and Colombia. The Fund will make subordinated long-term US dollar loans, with current coupon and equity participation features as well as straight equity investments. The Fund will be managed by a subsidiary of LAP Latin American Partners LLC (“LAP”). A first closing of US$80-150M is expected in November 2013 and a second closing reaching the target amount of $250M is expected up to one year later.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment in the Fund is up to US$30 Million for IFC’s account split between Subordinated Debt and Equity (not to exceed 25% of total fund committed capital or 20% of total Equity portion).
location_description: The Fund is a regional infrastructure fund covering Central America and the Caribbean. The Fund may invest in the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Panama, Suriname, and Trinidad and Tobago, as well as in Colombia and Mexico.
development_impact: Reduce Infrastructure Bottlenecks: Fund will provide capital for infrastructure projects which will contribute to the competitiveness of the target region and will help eliminate critical infrastructure bottlenecks that limit growth and job creation. Economic and Private Sector Development: Fund will provide quasi-equity and equity capital to help promote growth and job creation in local communities. Demonstration Effects: Fund will strengthen investees from a financial and governance perspective and help them scale up their operations, thus making them more attractive targets for further investment. This will help to demonstrate the business case for private infrastructure projects and encourage more private investors to enter the sector in the target region.
additionality: Mobilization: IFC would be supporting a capable investment team and helping it to attract other DFIs and private investors in the Fund. This follow-on fund would probably be raised without IFC participation but most likely with a smaller size and more unbalanced liability structure. Collaboration in the Financing of Projects: IFC and CAMIF II can collaborate in co-financing of infrastructure projects. IFC can provide expertise (such as industry, environmental and social and product) and resources to improve the Fund's efficiency and help them continue building industry and country knowledge and incorporate best practices. Knowledge Transfer: By participating in the Fund's Advisory Committee, IFC would contribute to the implementation of CAMIF's investment strategy, by providing industry and country knowledge and advice on international best practices. AML Best Practices: Like Fund I, CAMIF II will implement a comprehensive Anti-Money Laundering and Combatting the Financing of Terrorism Policy, which will be based on IFC's latest standards. IFC's involvement in the Fund will promote implementation of these standards not only at the Fund and its investors' level, but also at the investee company level. E&S Best Practices: The inclusion of IFC's E&S sustainability standards and the monitoring of compliance by IFC will improve project quality in a manner not contributed by any other investor. IFC's presence will assist the fund managers to insist on and obtain compliance both when negotiating projects and once projects are in portfolio.
Company Name: CENTRAL AMERICAN MEZZANINE INFRASTRUCTURE FUND II LP

project_description: Muyuan Foodstuff Co., Ltd. (“Muyuan Foodstuff”) is a pig breeder and hog producer located in China. IFC’s proposed loan investment of $20M will primarily support the development of a Project of the Company with annual production capacity of 400,000 hogs. Upon completion, this Project would expand further the Company’s hog production.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Qin Yinglin is the Chairman of Muyuan and the Sponsor of the Project. Mr. Qin has about 20 years of experience in pig farming and is well regarded in the Chinese pig farming industry. He is responsible for the overall business strategy and development of the Company. Mr. Qin owns 48.8% of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be RMB460 million (approx. US$75 million equivalent). IFC is considering to provide a senior debt to the Project Company in an amount of up to US$20 million on its own account.
location_description: The Project is located in Zhongxiang County, Hubei Province, China.
development_impact: Employment: The Company''s operations are located in western Henan Province - a frontier region in China. It provides stable employment opportunities for around 1200 staff, including 400 female employees. Farmers reached: Currently, about 24,000 rural households supply the Company with raw materials such as corn, barley and silage. SMEs reached: The Company sells its breeds to about 1,200 rural pig farms for further fattening for sale to market. Food Safety: The Chinese hog sector is still very fragmented, leading to poor hygiene standards, inadequate bio-security, poor nutrition, and over-use of antibiotics. By creating a larger enterprise with greater focus on efficiency and food safety, the Company supports the improvement of breeding techniques, quality standards as well as the production efficiency of the industry. Renewable energy/waste management practices: The Company''s on-going project to collect and treat the waste from farms to generate electricity for the farms contributes to reducing GHG emissions. Frontier region development: The Project will help the development of Hubei, a frontier province ranking 13th in China in terms of GDP per capita.
additionality: Long-term partner: the Company is keen to attract financing from credible/knowledgeable partners such as IFC who have a long-term investment horizon and can add value to the operations through our industry knowledge and enable the Company implement a properly designed strategic plan. Credibility and Positioning: The Company is preparing for an IPO in domestic market in 2012-13 and expects the signaling from IFC''s direct investment will enhance its reputation with investors and other partners. Adoption of Best-Practice Operational Standards: By supporting the deployment of environmentally friendly, energy-efficient pig farms yielding quality pigs, the Company can have a positive, visible demonstration effect for improving the operational management standards in the Chinese pig industry. Helping the Expansion to New Province: With IFC''s continous support, the Company has been able to maintain sustainable growth and now is moving from its home province, Henan, to new province, Hubei. Animal welfare: The Company is the first company in China to implement animal welfare practices. These high standards and best practices would also apply to the increased hog production under the Project.

project_description: Private Enterprise Company Nadezhda (“Nadezhda”) is based in eastern Ukraine and is a wholesale and retail distributor of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), gasoline, and diesel fuel. The purpose of the project is to support the expansion of Nadezhda through a) increasing the number of retail stations, which would sell traditional fuels as well as LPG, and b) managing working capital risks by partially replacing short-term loans with long-term debt.
sponsor_shareholders: Nadezhda is a private, Ukrainian company that has been in operation for more than twenty years. The ultimate controlling party of Nadezhda is Mr. Victor Batrachenko.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$ 22 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$ 10 million A loan and a US$ 10 million C loan. The remainder of the financing will come from internal cash generation of Nadezhda.
location_description: Nadezhda is headquartered in Poltava, Ukraine. Its wholesale operations are present in all regions of Ukraine, and its retail sites are concentrated in certain regions including Poltava, Sumy, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhya, Crimea, and Uzhhorod. This project will support Nadezhda’s further retail expansion in the regions that are in or adjacent to the regions where it operates today.
development_impact: -Development of Ukraine''s infrastructure based on modern and safe standards. -Supporting the expansion of the distribution infrastructure for liquified petroleum gas, which is a "cleaner" fuel. -Employment creation / preservation: The investment is expected to create 238 new, permanent jobs.
additionality: -Provision of risk capital and long-term funds. -Guidance on environmental and social aspects of the project. -Financial advice on improving the Company''s debt repayment profile.

company_name: THIEN MINH TRAVEL JOINT STOCK COMPANY
sector: Tour Operators (i.e., Arranging and Assembling Tours)
project_description: Thien Minh Group (“TMG” or “Company”) is one of the largest private sector integrated tour and hotel operator companies in Vietnam. In 2010, IFC made its first investment of US$12 million in a convertible loan to fund part of the Company‘s acquisition costs of the Victoria hotel chain in Vietnam. TMG is undertaking a long term strategic plan to expand both the tour and the hotel business by: (i) developing a branded three star hotel chain across major cities in Vietnam; (ii) scaling up the four-star Victoria hotel chain to major cities and tourist destinations in Vietnam; and (iii) diversifying its tour product portfolio by adding additional services. The proposed project is to provide equity financing to TMG to fund its new projects.
sponsor_shareholders: TMG was established in 1994 by Mr. Tran Trong Kien (CEO & Chairman) and his family. Since 2004, the Company has been expanding the tour operations business as well as diversifying into other aspects of the travel business such as hotel operations and management. The Company is 52% owned by Mr. Tran Trong Kien and 48% owned by Vietnam Investments Group (VIG), a private equity fund.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be US$43.4 million. The proposed IFC investment is US$14 million in equity. IFC has been invited also to convert US$3.5 million of the existing convertible loan into equity.
location_description: There are multiple locations related to the Project in the North, the Centre and the South of Vietnam.
development_impact: Demonstration effect: The Project will have a significant demonstration effect by establishing viability of green buildings in Vietnam. TMG is committed to having a number of its projects meet IFC''s Green Building Standards, thereby demonstrating that it is possible to adopt energy and water conservation measures in the hotel sector. Improve tourism infrastructure: The use of proceeds will primarily be used for the development of three and four star hotels, which will increase much needed supply for hotel rooms in this category, thereby increasing private sector lead improvements in the tourist infrastructure. Employment creation and local linkage: The Project will create a number of direct and indirect jobs, as well as demand for locally sourced materials, services and labour, for the local economy. Foreign exchange and tax generation: The Project is expected to contribute to the domestic economy through increased tax revenues and foreign exchange inflow, as a significant of TMG''s hotel guests are foreign nationals.
additionality: Long term capital mobilization: IFC will provide long term financing in the form of equity, which is not readily available in Vietnam. The company has secured debt financing, but needs growth equity to ensure an appropriate capital structure for expansion. Industry expertise and global knowledge: IFC has extensive global experience within the hotel industry, which in particular could benefit TMG, as the company seeks to expand this part of the business. Environmental & social standards: IFC will continue to assist the Company achieve international best practice for its acquired/constructed hotels.
Company Name: THIEN MINH TRAVEL JOINT STOCK COMPANY

project_description: The IFC proposes an equity investment of EUR20 million in MA South Africa, a subsidiary of the CLN Group, to support its expansion plans in the country. CLN is a leading automotive stamping part manufacturer based in Italy and a repeat IFC client. It has 8 existing plants in South Africa and is looking to expand its production to serve new local automotive manufacturers. It produces and assembles steel and aluminum automotive structural parts and skin panels.
sponsor_shareholders: CLN Group: Founded in 1949, CLN is an Italian company that operates in three business segments: Steel Service Centers (“SSC”), Steel Wheel Manufacturing (“MW”), and Steel Metal Stamping (“MA”). CLN is the preferred steel stamping and wheel supplier of many OEMs. CLN is owned 65% by Magnetto-Perris Family, 25% by Arcelor Mittal, and 10% by Marubini-Itoshu.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total proposed project amount is EUR55m including project and maintenance Capex and working capital. IFC funds will be for the purpose of Capex and refinancing of short-term bridge loans. The envisioned finance plan includes IFC equity financing, inter-company loans, and senior financing from local banks.
location_description: The Projected is located in South Africa, where CLN, through its subsidiaries, have plants across Rosslyn, East London, Durban, and Port Elizabeth.
development_impact: - Job Creation: The Project will create and sustain a total of 250 positions of direct employment, with nearly half of the jobs located in Eastern Cape, a frontier region and South Africa poorest province. - Support Auto Sector Development & Localization: By helping CLN achieve greater scale in South Africa to serve more OEM clients, the Project is contributing to the localization efforts of the automotive sector development goals in South Africa. - Training: The Company provided training to 450 employees in 2013, and will continue to provide annual internal and external training that contribute to skill and career development.
additionality: - Global partnership: IFC is supporting CLN Group in its growth in emerging markets. Having invested in PMC Serbia, IFC is looking to continue the partnership with CLN by investing in South Africa - Long-term financing and Counter-cyclical role: Italian banks are still under pressure to de-leverage their balance sheet. Although liquidity is back, long-term lending is not readily available. IFC will support CLN''s long-term financing needs in a time of financial uncertainty and in a higher risk region

company_name: TURKIYE SISE VE CAM FABRIKALARI ANONIM SIRKETI
sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: Turkiye Sise ve Cam Fabrikalari A.S. (“Sisecam”), the leading Turkish glass manufacturer and a longtime IFC client, launched a US$500 million Eurobond to be used for refinancing maturing debt obligations and to help fund Sisecam’s capital expenditures program in 2013 – 2014. Sisecam invited IFC to participate in the issue for up to US$40 million to strengthen its credibility and ensure a successful placement among international investors. Update related to additional investment under the COVID-19 response facility: IFC will provide an A loan up to US$75 million or its equivalent in Euro (the “IFC Loan”) to Turkiye Sise ve Cam Fabrikalari A.S. (“Sisecam” or “Sisecam Group”) as an allocation under the IFC’s COVID-19 response facility. The IFC Loan will be used for Sisecam Group’s flat glass, glass packaging and glassware operations in developing countries, and will help Sisecam Group implement its capital expenditure program which was partially delayed due to COVID-19 and finance its working capital needs.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1935, Sisecam Group is Turkey’s leading glass manufacturer and a prominent player in the global glass industry. Sisecam Group controls more than 50 affiliated companies along four main business divisions, namely flat glass, glass packaging, chemicals, and glassware. Sisecam is c. 57% owned by Turkiye Is Bankasi A.S. and its related entities and the rest of the shares are publicly traded on Borsa Istanbul with a total market capitalization of c. US$2.8 billion as of June 24, 2021.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project Cost is expected to be EUR285 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to Euro equivalent of US$75 million.
location_description: Sisecam’s headquarters and majority of its operations are located in Turkey while Sisecam Group has production facilities in 13 countries, most of which are in the EMENA region.
development_impact: The main development benefits of the proposed investment derive from supporting Sisecam''s US$1.5 billion capital expenditures program in 2013 - 2014. Sisecam is one of the main industrial groups in Turkey and in the region. It has a proven track record as a successful long-term investor, generating employment and fiscal revenues, and transferring industrial know-how to many countries in which it established its presence. This investment program will generate significant development impact for the countries in which Sisecam will invest and is critically important as it comes at a time when FDI in the region has slowed down, many investors remain on the sidelines and there is an increased need to generate stable employment opportunities, particularly in the manufacturing industry. Sisecam has issued a Eurobond which has been internationally rated (BB+ by S&P and Ba1 by Moody''s, the bond has the same rating as Sisecam Corporate rating). The transaction has a strong demonstration impact for other Turkish companies which are considering accessing the international bond markets, an important step in reducing the country''s dependence on short-term flows and mobilizing the large amounts of long-term capital needed to sustain its development. At the company level, the Eurobond issue will help Sisecam achieve larger economies of scale and broader geographical diversification, enhancing Sisecam''s competitive market position in the global glass industry. Update related to additional investment under the COVID-19 response facility: The Project will (i) contribute to the post-COVID-19 recovery especially through increased economic activity, and also (ii) promote resilience by contributing to supply chain continuity across various key industries (e.g., automotive, construction, food & beverages) in which Sisecam Group’s products are utilized.
additionality: IFC, as a partner of more than 40 years, has financed Sisecam in Turkey and other countries during its international expansion. IFC's participation in Sisecam's debut Eurobond bond issuance as an anchor investor will be important as this Eurobond is expected to help (i) pave the way for future bond issues; (ii) raise long-term unsecured 7-year debt with a non-amortizing bullet structure that will lengthen the average maturity of the Company's debt stock; (iii) support the Group's South-South expansion program in the wake of the global financial crisis and while investment flows in the ECA region remain subdued; and (iv) develop a corporate environmental, health, and safety system (EHSS). Update related to additional investment under the COVID-19 response facility: IFC's expected additionality includes its counter-cyclical role through provision of long-term financing and diversification of Sisecam's funding base.
Company Name: TURKIYE SISE VE CAM FABRIKALARI ANONIM SIRKETI

company_name: Acuagranjas dos Lagos, S.A. de C.V.
project_description: The proposed investment consists of a senior secured loan of US$10 million to Acuagranjas Dos Lagos (“ADL”) to finance its capital expenditures for the development of additional production infrastructure at Lake Malpaso, installation of additional processing lines at its existing processing facility and other related investments. ADL was established in 2007 in Chiapas province of Mexico as the third and newest operation of the Regal Springs Group (“RSG”), the world’s largest vertically integrated producer and marketer of tilapia products. The project is a key element of RSG’s strategic objectives to: i) maintain its global leadership in a growing industry by reaching 150,000 MT of total biomass production and ii) step-up its presence in key premium markets of the Americas and Europe.
sponsor_shareholders: ADL is indirectly owned by Aquafinca Saint Peter Fish, S.A., one of the key operating companies of RSG based in Honduras. RSG was founded by Mr. Rudolf Lamprecht in Indonesia in 1989. Mr. Lamprecht is the majority shareholder and sponsor of all the group companies within RSG.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide a US$10 million senior secured loan to finance ADL’s US$24 million capital expenditure program.
location_description: All ADL operations are located in Chiapas province of Mexico. The processing facility is located in the Ostuacan municipality whereas Lake Malpaso is located in Mezcalapa municipality.
development_impact: 1) Job creation: Chiapas province is one of the poorest provinces in Mexico with limited supply of full-time employment opportunities. To date, the Company has created approximately 1,000 jobs and will generate at least 1,000 additional direct jobs. 2) Outreach: about 40 local fishermen from the local communities have seen their income and skills significantly improved as the Company assisted them in developing their own fish farms with annual production of up to 40 MT per annum for the larger farmers. Over 300 additional local fishermen will benefit from similar arrangements in Lake Malpaso. 3) Health and education infrastructure: as a result of the Project, more families will have access to health and education support provided by the Company.
additionality: 1) Long-term financing that is not readily available locally in competitive terms. 2) IFC''s advice on corporate governance best practices and internal control systems as the family-owned Group is reinforcing its corporate structure to support its global expansion. 3) IFC''s involvement in this project is expected to be the first step of a long-term partnership with the Group to support its expansion into other emerging markets.
Company Name: Acuagranjas dos Lagos, S.A. de C.V.

project_description: Chipita Turkey (the “Company”) is the newly created subsidiary of Chipita S.A., a leading international company in the production and marketing of flour-based snacks and chocolate confectioneries, headquartered in Athens, Greece. The Company is undertaking a greenfield project for the production of croissants in Turkey. The croissant manufacturing plant, currently at the last stages of construction, will operate with two production lines, with a total capacity of 410 pieces of packaged products per minute producing two types of croissants: cocoa cream and vanilla cream croissants, under the global ‘7-Days’ brand. With the construction of the plant expected to be completed in October 2013, the Company will proceed with the equipment installation during the last quarter of 2013, aiming to start production in the first quarter of 2014 and launch the product in the second quarter of 2014.
sponsor_shareholders: Chipita S.A. a leading international company in the production and marketing of flour-based snacks and chocolate confectioneries operates globally through its own plants in Greece, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland and Russia and through joint ventures in Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Mexico. In addition, the Group has its own distribution companies in the Czech Republic, Germany, Hungary, Slovakia, Serbia and Ukraine. The Group exports its products in a number of other countries, including Australia, Central Asia and Western Europe. Chipita S.A. is 100% by UFIB Cyprus which is majority owned by the Olayan Group and Mr. Spyros Theodoropoulos that control over 80% of the shares. A Greek private equity fund, Greek Banks and individuals hold the remaining shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at EUR 21.5 million. The proposed IFC A loan of EUR 10.75 million for IFC’s own account will finance the project in addition to a EUR 10.75 million equity contribution of the Sponsor Chipita S.A. (the “Group’).
location_description: Chipita Turkey plant will be constructed in Gebze Plastic Manufacturers Organized Industrial Zone (hereafter referred to as “OIZ”) which is located on the TEM Motorway at a distance of 50 km from Izmit, 36 km from Istanbul and 36 km from the Center of Gebze Provincial District. The plant will be constructed as a 2-floor facility with a total land plot of 12000 m2.
development_impact: - Job creation: The Company will create 172 positions of direct employment. In addition, it would help third-party service and product suppliers increase their employment. - Increased tax revenues: The project is expected to generate EUR 6.7 million corporate taxes over the first 7 years of operations. In addition, it will generate other forms of tax revenues for the Government (e.g. VAT payments and social security contributions for employees). - Foreign direct investment: Although FDI figures are relatively high in Turkey, it takes mostly the form of acquisitions/privatization, and investments in green-field production plants are relatively low.
additionality: - Crisis response: IFC is engaging with a Greece-based Company at a time when financing conditions are challenging due to the ongoing sovereign debt crisis. - Long term financing: Longer tenors are not easily available in the current market environment and Chipita needs long-term financing for its green-field project. - Strategic partnership: This financing will be the first step in building a relationship between Chipita and IFC. Chipita operates in several emerging markets and IFC could play in the future a bigger role in their expansion to a number of markets through large scale financings. - Local market network: Chipita is new to Turkey, and IFC''s presence and know-how of the local market is likely to benefit the Company. - E&S standard setting: Chipita will benefit from IFC''s E&S due diligence and standards for its green-field project in a new market.

company_name: CIMKO CIMENTO VE BETON SANAYI TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Cimko Cimento ve Beton Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (“Cimko”, the”Company”) is an existing IFC client which produces cement and ready mixed concrete. The Company has two cement plants in Kahramanmaras, and Adiyaman; and various ready mix concrete plants in the Southern-Anatolian region of Turkey. The project includes efficiency improvement investments, addition of three new Ready mixed concrete plants to its existing facilities, and working capital needs of the Company. This is a brownfield-investment. The purpose of the project is to make Cimko more efficient and cost-competitive.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is owned by Sanko Holding A.S. and Cementerie Aldo Barbetti (“Barbetti”) with shareholdings of 70% and 30% respectively. The Sanko Group, which started out as a textile company, is a 109-year old Turkish diversified conglomerate comprising 51 companies which operate in 12 sectors. Sanko Holding is privately-held. Headquartered in Gubbio, Italy; Barbetti operates in the cement industry for more than 50 years. Barbetti is privately-held. Barbetti acquired its stake in Cimko in 2007.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be US$96 million. IFC will invest an A loan of up to US$40 million from its own account and mobilize a B loan of up to US$25 million (or its Euro equivalent).
location_description: Investments will be performed in the existing Kahramanmaras, Adiyaman plants of the Company. Three new ready mix concrete plants will be built in the same region.
development_impact: Benefits to the employees: The IFC investment will increase the competitiveness of Cimko and preserve employment in Southeast Anatolia, least developed region in Turkey. Increased exports: By improving its competitiveness, the Company is expected to export more of its products regionally. Energy efficiency: Investment program, which is designed to improve energy efficiency, will enable the Company to have sizeable energy savings.
additionality: -Industry Expertise: IFC will be sharing benchmarks and industry best-practices with the client. -Monitoring E&S practices during the expansion phase: IFC''s involvement will add value as IFC''s E&S standards will be implemented during the investment program. - Mobilization: IFC helps mobilize another lender to provide long term funding for the investment program.
Company Name: CIMKO CIMENTO VE BETON SANAYI TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

company_name: ACTIS JABI LAKE MALL DEVELOPMENT COMPANY LIMITED
project_description: Actis Africa Real Estate Fund 2 LP (“AR2” or the “Sponsor”), an existing IFC client, is a closed-end private equity fund dedicated to investments in real estate companies and projects in East, West and Southern Africa, excluding South Africa. The Sponsor is undertaking a greenfield development of a shopping mall of international standard in Jabi Lake, Abuja, Nigeria (“the Project”). The Project will help to alleviate the supply gap of high quality retail space in Abuja. At completion the Project is expected to provide approximately 31,000 square meters of business infrastructure. Duval Properties Limited (“Duval”), as local partners, will co-sponsor the project by contributing land for the development; and AR2 will be the majority owner of the Project.
sponsor_shareholders: AR2 is fund managed and controlled by Actis LLP (“Actis”), a leading private equity investor in emerging markets that invests exclusively in Africa, Asia and Latin America. It has developed the first, internationally specified, purpose-built mall in Nigeria and Ghana. Actis was formed in 2004 as a spinout of CDC Group Plc. (“CDC”), a developmental institution sponsored by the UK government, which is also a limited partner in AR2, and until May 2012, was 60% owned by its senior management and 40% owned by the UK government. In May 2012, Actis purchased the UK government''s remaining 40% shareholding. AR2 had its first closing on May 24, 2011, with IFC committing US$25 million to the fund. In September 2012, AR2 reached final close of US$268.4 million from 21 limited partners. AR2 is a follow-up to Actis Africa Real Estate Fund 1, Actis’ first dedicated private equity real estate fund for Sub Saharan Africa which closed in 2006 at US$154 million and is almost fully invested. Duval is wholly owned by Mr Hakeem Belo-Osagie and Dr (Mrs) Myma Belo-Osagie. Mr Hakeem Belo-Osagie is a businessman who has interests in several businesses, particularly in the energy, finance and telecommunications sectors. Dr Myma Bello-Osagie is a seasoned lawyer that currently serves as managing partner of Udo Udoma & Belo-Osagie, one of the leading law firms in Nigeria.
