total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at approximately US$130.2 million, which AR2 proposes to finance with a combination of equity and debt. Of this amount, IFC has proposed to directly invest up to US$11.1 million in equity into an investment vehicle (majority owned by AR2 alongside other prospective co-investors that may commit to the Project) that will have direct and indirect majority ownership and control of the Project.
location_description: The Project will be located on 5 hectares of land along Jabi Lake water front at Jabi, Federal Capital Territory, Abuja. The Project forms part of an overall master plan for the development of 35 hectares site for hospitality, residential and commercial properties.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have the following impacts: - Provision of critical business infrastructure that is currently significantly undersupplied in Africa''s second largest market and most populous nation. - Provision of a growth platform for local SMEs (manufacturers and wholesalers) in the retail value chain (owners of stores within mall) to gain access to customers and increase their sales. - Improvement of food security as a result of increased distribution outlets for local farmers leading to increased demand for local products (fresh produce in particular, but also locally processed foods). - Improvement in hygiene, health and safety standards in the food retail sector. - Serve as a catalyst for urban development in the area around the new mall. Development of better aesthetic environments and strong demonstration effect in improving commercial property standards across Nigeria. - Creation of direct and indirect employment during construction and operations. - Generation of tax revenues for the government. - Transfer of operational and environmental & social best practices, both during construction and operations
additionality: - IFC''s central role and additionality in the proposed project will be provision of scarce equity capital to ensure a bankable structure for a development with a high expected development impact. - IFC''s involvement will ensure that the Project is implemented based on international best practice in environmental, social and corporate governance areas. - The Project will benefit from IFC''s sector knowledge and expertise in retail property development.
Company Name: ACTIS JABI LAKE MALL DEVELOPMENT COMPANY LIMITED

project_description: Public Joint Stock Company “Concern Galnaftogaz” is based in western Ukraine and operates the second largest petrol filling station network in Ukraine by volume under the “OKKO” brand. Galnaftogaz’s petrol filling stations are built in a format common in western Europe, comply with up-to-date technical and environmental specifications, and offer various related products and services such as convenience stores and restaurants. The purpose of the project is to support the expansion of Galnaftogaz through a) expanding the number of petrol filling stations, convenience stores, and liquefied petroleum gas modules, b) investing in infrastructure upgrades and measurement / control systems, and c) managing working capital risks by partially replacing short-term loans with long-term debt.
sponsor_shareholders: Galnaftogaz’s parent company is Financial and Investment Energy Holding Establishment, a Liechtenstein-based company that holds interests in Galnaftogaz as well as in companies active in various other sectors in Ukraine including agribusiness, construction and insurance. The ultimate controlling party of the Sponsor is Mr. Vitaliy Antonov.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US $ 220 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US $15 million A loan for IFC’s own account and a US $85 million syndicated B loan. The remainder of the financing will come from internal cash generation of Galnaftogaz and from European Bank for Reconstruction and Development A and B loans.
location_description: Galnaftogaz is headquartered in Lviv, Ukraine, and its petrol filling stations are present in all regions of Ukraine, with a particularly strong presence in western and central Ukraine. This project will support Galnaftogaz’s further expansion in all regions of Ukraine and will have a particular emphasis on expansion in the southern region.
development_impact: -Development of Ukraine''s infrastructure based on modern and safe standards. -Access to high-quality petroleum products and services. -Employment creation / preservation: The investment is expected to create 380 to 480 new, permanent jobs. -Development of local suppliers: Convenience stores, automotive services and fast-food help local economies because such services at stations are primarily locally supplied. -Support of cleaner fuel types: GNG offers liquified petroleum gas (LPG) in many of its filling stations, and the new stations will also offer this cleaner fuel alternative.
additionality: -Mobilization of a significant amount of long-term debt with a high B loan to A loan ratio. -As a result long term partnership between IFC and Galnaftogaz, IFC is uniquely positioned to support the company on its business strategy as well as on its environmental and social improvement efforts.

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: Borets International Limited (“Borets” or the “Company”) is one of the leading ESP (“Electronic Submersible Pump”) manufacturers globally and market leader in Russia. The Company designs and manufactures pumps, motors and cable used in artificial lift systems and provides a full range of related services, including installation, maintenance and repair, leveraging its extensive research and development, manufacturing and service infrastructure. The Company has 3 manufacturing operations in the USA, Canada and Slovakia, and 6 in Russia. A further manufacturing facility is currently being constructed in Russia, Stariy Oskol. The Company also has 18 servicing facilities, 6 in Russia and remaining sales and servicing centers are in the USA, Canada, Venezuela, Congo, Colombia, Serbia, Oman, Brasil, Indonesia, Egypt. Proposed project is to finance long-term corporate funding needs of the Company including (i) working capital and capital expenditure needs of the Company in relation to its international expansion, (ii) refinancing existing IFC and EBRD loans, and (iii) acquisition of shares in Borets.
sponsor_shareholders: 61.5% shareholding in Borets is owned by Tangent Fund Limited (“Tangent”), a Cayman Islands fund, while the remaining 38.5 % is held by Weatherford, one of the largest products and services provider for oil and natural gas production. Borets is a privately held company with operations in more than 10 countries. Tangent is privately-held while Weatherford is publicly-listed.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Project cost is estimated to be US$736 million. IFC considers providing an A loan or making a bond investment of up to US$50 million for its own account, mobilize a B loan of up to US$130 million and making an equity investment of up to US$21 million.
location_description: This is a corporate loan and there is no particular project location. The Company has various plants, service centers, and offices inside and outside of Russian Federation.
development_impact: 1. South South investment: The project will support international expansion efforts of Borets which includes other emerging markets 2. Development of new technologies: The project will help Borets develop new and more efficient technolgies. 3. Increased tax revenues for the government: The project will lead to higher revenues and profitability which will translate into a higher tax revenues for the government.
additionality: 1-Support the sucess of Eurobond issuance: Having IFC as an anchor investor may increase the probability of success for Borets. 2-Mobilization: IFC may help the Company with mobilizing funds from international lenders.

project_description: ASA (“the Company” or “the Group”) is a vertically integrated chicken and port meat producer that currently produces hatching eggs, day-old chicks, pork and chicken meat and industrialized products for sale in the domestic market. The Group operates 2 slaughterhouse facilities in the Federal District, 1 in the state of Goias and two in the State of Tocantins, out of which one is currently not operating. In the aftermath of the 2008 crisis, Banco da Amazonia (a strong regional player) cut financing lines for the integrated farmers in the State which caused lack of sufficient broiler supply to justify operating the plant and required the Group to interrupt operations in 2010. Banco da Amazonia resumed financing the outgrowers at the end of 2011. The Project will involve providing the Company with financing to (i) invest in animal capex in order to increase day-old chicks production to support increase of broilers supply for processing in its existing slaughterhouse facilities; (ii) resume operations in its currently closed facility in Tocantins, thus increasing total processing capacity by more than 50%; (iii) provide sufficient working capital related to the investments; and (iv) refinance existing short term debt to improve liquidity.
sponsor_shareholders: ASA is a family owned Brazilian group comprised by three operating companies, consolidated under a holding company named Asa Participações e Administração Ltda, which is fully owned by the Amorim family (Aroldo Silva Amorim Filho, the current CEO, and Myriam Pinto de Amorim, his mother). Asa Alimentos is the main operating company of the group and fully controlled by the Amorim family; Asa Norte is controlled by the holding (51%), with the remainder being directly held by Aroldo Silva Amorim Filho (15%) and other partners as follows: José Luis Aborihan Gonçalves (30%), Sérgio Costa Araújo (2%) and Paulo Roberto Galleti (2%); while Frango Norte is a 50/50% JV of the Amorim family with two local partners: José dos Santos Carneiro (25%) and João Batista Carneiro (25%). The Company was founded in 1967 with Mr. Aroldo Silva Amorim, father of the Group’s current CEO, initially focused on the production of hatching eggs and day-old chicks in the Center West region of Brazil. Currently the Company is a leading regional player with brand leadership in the Center West and North regions of the country. There are currently two members of the Amorim family with a management role in the Company: Aroldo Silva Amorim Filho, CEO, and his sister, Katia Pinto de Amorim, director responsible for the HR and IT functions. The rest of the management team is composed by professionals with experience in the protein and food sector.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project will involve providing an A-Loan of up to BRL 30 million and an up to US$ 6.8 million equivalent C-Loan (with income participation features), denominated in Brazilian Reais (or approximately BRL 15 million) to assist with ASA’s corporate needs. The Group has a total investment plan of around US$ 76 million over the next 6 years consisting of expansion capex for both its facilities located in DF/GO regions as well as in Tocantins State.
location_description: ASA’s headquarters are located in Brasilia, DF (Federal District) in Midwest region of Brazil. The Group’s facilities are spread out in the Federal District (Recanto das Emas, Paranoá, Samambaia, Santa Maria, Gama, Sobradinho, Brazilândia, Planaltina, and São Sebastião), Sates of Goias (Formosa, Nova Veneza, Luiziânia), State of Tocantins (in Paraiso do Tocantins, Araguaína, Tocantinópolis, and Aguiarnópolis cities) and São Paulo State (Ajapi). The slaughterhouse currently stopped and subject to the project mentioned herein is located in the city of Aguiarnópolis in Tocantins State.
development_impact: The project will allow ASA to increase production of poultry and pork meat thus contributing to (i) employment generation in Tocantins, a frontier region; (ii) rural development as the Company will need to expand its current network of integrated small farmers who breed chicken and pork under contracts with ASA, which provides them with a stable source of income and (iii) the sustainable worldwide increase in food supply, being Brazil well-positioned to support this increase due to the country''s competitive advantages as a low-cost producer of protein.
additionality: (i) IFC''s investment will improve liquidity and support the expansion of an efficient poultry and pork producer in Brazil, providing a stamp of approval that will facilitate the Company''s access to other long term funds and (ii) IFC global industry and E&S expertise will assist the Company in the implementation of high environmental and social standards, thus contributing to a positive demonstration effect for the sector.

company_name: PUERTAS FINAS DE MADERA MONTEALBAN, S.A. DE C.V.
project_description: The project will expand operations of Holding Montealban SA de CV ( “Puertas Finas” or the “Company”), a leading company in the production of doors, contract woodwork and plywood in Mexico. The project includes: (i) implementing its 2012-2016 capital expenditures program; (ii) satisfying working capital needs; and (iii) refinancing of existing debt. Puertas Finas’ capital expenditures program aims at the modernization, expansion and energy efficient improvements of its existing operations. The Company has production facilities in various parts of Mexico and its headquarters are located in Oaxaca.
sponsor_shareholders: Puertas Finas is a private Mexican business group fully owned by the Borgio family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$ 31 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an approximately US$ 13 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project’s capital investments will be made at Puertas Finas’ production facilities located in the states of Oaxaca and Guerrero, Mexico, primarily in and around the urban area of Oaxaca. Both project sites have the necessary utilities, road access and permits.
development_impact: (i) The project will contribute to the development of two frontier regions in Mexico: Oaxaca and Guerrero, where economic stimulators are scarce and very much needed. (ii) Creation of both direct and indirect jobs, especially in Oaxaca where a new production line will be established. (iii) Promotion of sustainable forestry practices as Puertas Finas, provides technical and logistical support to the communities from where it supplies part of its pine wood. (iv) The Company is expected to continue improving its environmental performance, thus reducing its overall environmental footprint. (v) Company''s improvements in energy efficiency of its existing operations.
additionality: (i) Long-term financing: IFC will provide tailor-made long term financing which is not available in the local market. (ii) Long-term partnership with IFC: The company considers IFC''s continuous support as a comparative advantage and provides the needed stamp of approval to enable its access to markets and financing with other institutions. (iii) IFC''s technical advisory: The Resource Efficiency team is in the process of evaluating energy efficiency and cleaner production solutions that are expected to benefit the company as well as the environment. (iv) E&S standards: IFC''s continuous support will support Puertas Finas in the further improvement of environmental and social standards.
Company Name: PUERTAS FINAS DE MADERA MONTEALBAN, S.A. DE C.V.

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: Headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, Fluidic Energy (“Fluidic” or “the Company”) is an early stage provider of energy storage systems with significant operations in Indonesia. Founded in 2007, the Company supplies zinc-air batteries to support critical loads and backup power applications worldwide. The Company’s products are capable of covering ultra-long outages at the lowest cost, and include remote site management, multi-year performance warranties and innovative financing terms. Additionally, Fluidic’s solutions offer customers significant operating and capital savings making it a viable alternative to the backup incumbent: diesel generators and lead-acid batteries. The Company’s proposed investment plan is focused on the scale up of production in Indonesia, the acceleration of its commercial rollout in the emerging markets and continued research and development.
sponsor_shareholders: Fluidic is a privately held company incorporated in the United States and founded by current members of the management team. The Company has had previous rounds of financing and is majority owned by institutional investors that are global private investment firms including Madrone Partners and TN2 Capital Ventures.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Fluidic is seeking to raise up to $45 million through a Series C equity round of financing. The proceeds of the financing are to be used to support the scale-up of its commercial activities. The Company’s main end markets are the emerging markets. The proposed IFC investment is up to US $10 million in equity. Co-investors include current shareholders, Madrone Partners and TN2 Capital Ventures.
location_description: The Company is a US incorporated entity with headquarters in Scottsdale, Arizona. The Company also operates manufacturing, storage, and a simulated site testing facility in Indonesia.
development_impact: 1. Decrease operating cost of telecoms to facilitate mobile network coverage expansion in remote areas; 2. Contribute to climate change mitigation by reduced diesel consumption and carbon emissions; 3. Generate local jobs at the hubs and satellites established by Fluidic as well as jobs created during installation in remote areas; 4. Promote investment in IDA countries; and 5. Demonstration effect: an investment in Fluidic further enables the Green Power for Mobile initiative, a joint initiative between IFC and GSMA, which aims to replace diesel consumption in the mobile telecom sector in developing countries and especially in Sub Saharan Africa.
additionality: 1. Demonstration Effect: IFC''s investment in Fluidic will provide the Company with a vital "stamp of approval" which will help the Company complete its equity raise, implement its business plan and attract private capital to the energy storage market where investments are critical for the development of a cleaner economy; 2. IFC Network and Expertise: the Company will benefit from IFC''s global expertise and network in the telecom and renewable energy / energy efficiency industries. Additionally, Fluidic will be better able to access IFC portfolio companies, including mobile operators and tower companies in its target markets; 3. Knowledge sharing: Fluidic is keen to benefit from the IFC''s experiences in the IFC / GSMA joint initiative of green power for telecoms in developing countries; and 4. Financial Expertise: IFC may assist the Company in tailoring financial solutions as part of its managed services sales in many of its target markets.

project_description: The proposed investment would support Kuibyshevazot Open Joint Stock Company (KuAz) in implementation of its 2013-2016 capital expenditures program. The program is expected to result in production capacity expansion, streamlining of operations, improvement of cost-competitiveness, energy savings and reduction of greenhouse gases emissions.
sponsor_shareholders: Located in Togliatti, Samara region, KuAz is the leading Russian manufacturer of caprolactam (the raw material for synthetic fibers, engineering plastics, automotive and other downstream products) and one of the top ten Russian producers of nitrogenous fertilizers. KuAz is an existing IFC client. The Company is majority owned by its management and employees.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The investment program is around US$610 million comprising of expansion of production capacities and streamlining of operations (the Project). The proposed IFC investment package is an up to US$100 million A loan for IFC’s own account and an up to US$75 million B loan mobilized from participating banks.
location_description: Project investments will be implemented in Togliatti, Samara region, Russian Federation.
development_impact: Investments to be financed under the proposed project will help KuAz implement its 2013-2016 capital expenditures program, which would result in expansion of production capacities, streamlining of operations, energy efficiency improvements and reduction of greenhouse gases emissions. The project is expected to create around 150 additional jobs at the Company.
additionality: 1. Strategic Partnership: Kuaz has been an IFC''s Client since 2003 2. Long-term Financing: IFC will support Kuaz through the provision of long term funds to fit its capital investment needs. 3. Mobilization of Funds: IFC will mobilize financing from international banks and thus help the Company to expand its future access to the financial markets. 4. Technical Expertise: IFC will help Kuaz evaluate production optimization and resource efficiency improvements for its modernization and expansion projects. 5. Environmental and Social (E&S) Expertise: IFC will ensure E&S good practice in accordance with IFC Performance Standards and will continue to provide ongoing E&S advice to the Company.

project_description: Zalagh Holding SA (“Zalagh” or the “Company”) is a vertically-integrated industrial poultry producer in Morocco, present across the entire poultry meat value chain: grain trading/import, animal feed production, day-old-chick/poult production, broiler production, poultry slaughtering, and meat processing. To help meet Morocco’s fast-growing demand for chicken protein, Zalagh has defined a three-year expansion plan comprised of: (i) the expansion of feedmill capacity for ruminants and poultry, (ii) the set-up of additional chicken and turkey rearing and laying farms and hatchery capacity for day-old-chick/poult production, and (iii) the set-up of additional turkey broiler farms (the “Project”). The Project will increase Zalagh’s ability to support a greater number of farmers with its supply of day-old-chick/poult and animal-feed, which in turn will increase the supply of affordable meat protein in Morocco where population growth and rising incomes per capita have led to robust increase in protein demand.
sponsor_shareholders: Zalagh’s main shareholders (the Sponsors) are the Chaouni family from Morocco.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is mainly financed via IFC’s equity investment of up to US$24 million, and via local bank loans.
location_description: The Project will be located throughout the main poultry production regions of the country, across the key Casablanca - Fès corridor.
development_impact: Development impact includes: (1) Employment generation, including gender: Zalagh plays a critical role in the generation of employment in Morocco particularly, in rural areas. The current 1,718 positions (of which 390 female employees) comprise a wide range of skill levels, from entry level positions to highly-skilled engineering, veterinary and managerial positions. All employees have access to dedicated training opportunities that allow them to strengthen their skills and develop within the organization. Zalagh''s expansion is expected to increase employment to around 1,900 by 2017, which will provide direct employment opportunities, particularly to the skilled youth who suffer from relatively higher levels and longer durations of unemployment in Morocco. (2) Non-farm MSME linkages: as part of its operations, the Company also maintains relationships with a network of service MSMEs providing personnel, security, safety, transportation, recycling and waste disposal services, thus extending the employment reach of the Company well beyond its direct employees. (3) Economic opportunities in rural areas: as one of the leading providers of animal feed and poultry products in the country, Zalagh supports the economic activity of about 3,845 registered poultry farmers, including some contract outgrowers, and a large number of dairy and cattle farmers. Zalagh provides a range of services to its clients that include regular visits by its sales force, technical assistance, benchmarking of performance against standards, etc.
additionality: Through the proposed investment, IFC will support an emerging leader in the Moroccan agribusiness sector by providing an equity infusion that will: (i) provide a stamp of approval to the capital markets, reinforcing Zalagh Holding''s image in the market; and (ii) lower the Company''s leverage and enhance its capital structure, thereby establishing a solid base for continued growth.

project_description: The project described under this summary of investment information document is related to project 33609 which was publically disclosed on June 17 2013 under its former name “Rocket Internet”. The previous summary of investment information for Rocket Internet described IFC’s proposed investment into two companies: Dafiti Latam GmbH & Co. Beteiligungs KG (“Dafiti”) operating in Latin America and Lamoda GmbH (“Lamoda”) operating in Russia and Kazakhstan. The following summary relates to IFC’s potential investment in Lamoda only. The proposed investment in Dafiti is now covered in an update to the summary for project 33609. Bigfoot GmbH (“BF”) has launched, through subsidiaries, online retailing ventures in South America, the Commonwealth of Independent States and Asia (India). BF was initiated by Rocket Internet GmbH (“RI”), a global online venture builder. BF has identified IFC as a potential strategic partner in its endeavor to significantly expand its e-commerce footprint in emerging markets and has invited IFC to provide equity capital to support the growth of Lamoda, its subsidiary operating in Russia and Kazakhstan, as well as possibly expanding into other former CIS countries (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: BF, a new IFC client, is currently inter alia held by RI and several other investors including investment vehicles of Kinnevik AB, Tengelmann and Summit Partners. IFC is considering investing in Lamoda, an online retailing venture incubated and supported by BF operating in Russia and Kazakhstan, as well as possibly expanding into other former CIS countries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is comprised of an up to €10 million equity investment in Lamoda.
location_description: The Project will support the operations of Lamoda in the Russian Federation Kazakhstan, as well as possibly into other former CIS countries.
development_impact: The Project''s expected development impacts include: (i) job creation in the areas of logistics, warehousing as well as IT services and marketing and indirectly through supply chains and other supporting services; (ii) transfer of technology by replicating proven internet business concepts in emerging markets with the goal of turning its ventures into local/regional market leading companies in the online retail space; and (iii) benefit to consumers in frontier regions and secondary cities through more choices, lower priced goods and convenient service with home delivery.
additionality: IFC additionality will manifest itself through (i) political/country risk mitigation in the more difficult environments; (ii) the stamp of approval IFC can provide at time of exit; (iii) the strategic long-term partnership IFC can build by playing a catalytic role, particularly in the regions where equity capital funds are less readily available (iv) provision of E&S advice in the supply chains.

company_name: Dafiti Latam GmbH & Co. Beteiligungs KG
country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: This is an update to the summary of investment information document for project 33609 which was publically disclosed on June 17 2013 under its former name “Rocket Internet”. The previous summary of investment information for Rocket Internet described IFC’s proposed investment into two companies: Dafiti Latam GmbH & Co. Beteiligungs KG (“Dafiti”) operating in Latin America and Lamoda GmbH (“Lamoda”) operating in Russia and Kazakhstan. The following summary relates to IFC’s potential investment into Dafiti only. The proposed investment in Lamoda is now covered in a separate summary for project 34026. Bigfoot GmbH (“BF”) has launched, through subsidiaries, online retailing ventures in South America, the Commonwealth of Independent States and Asia (India). BF was initiated by Rocket Internet GmbH (“RI”), a global online venture builder. BF has identified IFC as a potential strategic partner in its endeavor to significantly expand its e-commerce footprint in emerging markets and has invited IFC to provide equity capital to support the growth of Dafiti, its subsidiary operating in Latin America (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: BF, a new IFC client, is currently inter alia held by RI and several other investors including investment vehicles of Kinnevik AB, Tengelmann and Summit Partners. IFC is considering investing in Dafiti, an online retailing venture incubated and supported by BF operating in Latin America.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is comprised of an up to €15 million equity investment in Dafiti.
location_description: The Project will support the operations of Dafiti in Latin America.
development_impact: The Project''s expected development impacts include: (i) job creation in the areas of logistics, warehousing as well as IT services and marketing and indirectly through supply chains and other supporting services; (ii) transfer of technology by replicating proven internet business concepts in emerging markets with the goal of turning its ventures into local/regional market leading companies in the online retail space; and (iii) benefit to consumers in frontier regions and secondary cities through more choices, lower priced goods and convenient service with home delivery.
additionality: IFC additionality will manifest itself through (i) political/country risk mitigation in the more difficult environments; (ii) the stamp of approval IFC can provide at time of exit; (iii) the strategic long-term partnership IFC can build by playing a catalytic role, particularly in the regions where equity capital funds are less readily available (iv) provision of E&S advice in the supply chains.
Company Name: Dafiti Latam GmbH & Co. Beteiligungs KG
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: The proposed investment consists of an $8 million financing package to Pearl Dairy Farms Limited (“Pearl Dairy” or the “Company”), a Ugandan milk processor. The proposed financing package will be supported by the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (“GAFSP”). GAFSP funding plays a catalytic role to create opportunity to support innovative private sector investments and deliver a level of additionality and impact beyond what is possible through IFC’s regular operations. The financing package will support Pearl Dairy in establishing a greenfield powdered milk processing plant in the Mbarara District of Uganda with a handling capacity of 240,000 liters of milk per day. The project will source raw milk from smallholder farmers in the surrounding region and will support the development of milk collection centers to further strengthen the dairy value chain. The Project is in the final stages of construction phase and its commissioning is expected by the second half of 2013. The construction has been financed by sponsor equity, shareholder loans as well as bank loans from Stanbic Uganda.
sponsor_shareholders: Pearl Dairy, based in Uganda, is a part of the Midcom Group of companies operating throughout sub-Saharan Africa, whose primary business operations include distribution of Nokia mobile phones and accessories, education, and real estate. The Company is jointly owned by the family trusts of the two key sponsors, Mr. Bhasker Kotecha & Family (50.5%) and Mr. Anand Kapoor & Family (49.5%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $15 million. IFC, with GAFSP support, will provide a US$8 million senior loan.
location_description: The Project will be implemented and located on a 15 acre plot in Mbarara, Uganda. The registered address of the Company is: Plot 29B Acacia Avenue, Kololo, P O Box 7420, Kampala, Uganda. The factory address is: Plot 100, Folio 2, LRV 4045 Kashari Block, Nyakinengo Parish, Biharwe Sub-Country Mbarara District, Uganda.

project_description: BHG – Brazilian Hospitality Group S.A. (BHG or the Company) is the third largest player in the Brazilian hospitality industry; it is listed in the Novo Mercado section of the BM&F Bovespa stock exchange (Novo Mercado) with a market capitalization of approximately US$450 million. The current hotel portfolio includes 8,513 rooms distributed in 48 properties, of which 23 are fully or partly owned and 25 are managed for third parties. The Company intends to continue growing complementing its acquisitions and management segments with the implementation of greenfield, energy efficient hotels under a dedicated investment fund, Fundo de Investimento e Participação em Hotelaria (the FIP). BHG’s 2013-2015 investment program (the Project) includes: the execution of new acquisitions; the construction and operation of a number of three-star, energy efficient greenfield hotels under the FIP; the entering into new management contracts totaling; and the implementation of refurbishments on a number of recently acquired hotels. The Project will expand BHG’s portfolio of rooms and provide exposure to a number of cities where the Company is not present.
sponsor_shareholders: BHG is 44.6 percent controlled by GP Investments (GPI or the Sponsor), the largest private equity firm in Brazil, which has a track record of investing approximately US$4 billion in 49 companies so far. GPI is listed in Novo Mercado and created BHG in 2008. All other shareholders in BHG are financial investors holding minority stakes below 8.5%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at approximately US$585 million. To finance the Project, the Company intends to raise US$250 million equivalent in a follow-on public share issue at Novo Mercado, which is expected to be executed during April 2013 (the Follow On). IFC will become an investor in the intended Follow On with an up to US$25 million equivalent equity investment for its own account.
location_description: BHG is headquartered in the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil and currently has 46 hotels across the country. Investment will be made along throughout Brazil.
development_impact: - Increasing the supply of competitive price-value business rooms/hotels in first, second and third-tier cities with consistent international quality and safety standards; this should encourage increased tourism, business and MICE travel; - Supporting the economic development of frontier regions of Brazil since a portion of the Project will take place in the Midwest, North and Northeast regions of Brazil, thus helping develop key business-enabling infrastructure in these priority areas; - Creating both direct and indirect jobs as well as providing training and promotion opportunities; the Project is expected to create and 2,500 new direct jobs in the operation stage (and over 4,500 direct jobs during the construction phases), with approximately 45% being for women; indirect jobs along the supply chain are also expected to be significant, including in food supply, transportation, security and other needed services; - Providing management and staff with comprehensive training opportunities, primarily through BHG''s own training center in SÃ£o Paulo and through additional training centers planned in Rio de Janeiro and BelÃ©m; BHG will also continue its social program for convicted criminals by continue offering them in-house training and, in some cases, jobs to support their re-integration into society. - Contributing to the development of the local economy by enhancing upstream and downstream supply linkages with SME vendors serving the needs of both the hotel and guests; in addition, the Project will increase tax revenues and tourist''s spending would help support a wide range of local economic activities; - Adopting sustainable green-building design and construction, ensuring higher levels of energy efficiency; the upcoming new properties would meet IFC''s EDGE Green Building standard; Improved environmental and social performance as BHG''s portfolio of hotels would conform to the World Bank Group''s environmental and social standards, including with regards to life and fire safety; and - Providing a demonstration effect to other potential investors.
additionality: - Anchor Investor and Stamp of Approval: IFC''s provision of long-term equity financing is expected to enhance BHG''s profile and credibility, hence providing comfort to third-party investors for the Company''s Follow On; - Green Building Expertise: IFC has provided the Company with guidance and support in analyzing its energy consumption and identifying areas for improvement on the Company''s proposed design for the first FIP greenfield hotel, which will effectively be used for all of the Company''s greenfield properties as a standardized template; through this exercise, the IFC team has determined that BHG''s new greenfield properties could be eligible for IFC''s EDGE Green Building certification, which would enhance the properties'' marketability and value; and - Environmental and Social Standards: IFC will provide guidance in the implementation of the World Bank''s standards in environmental and social practices, including life and fire safety.

project_description: The proposed investment consists of a preferred equity investment of US$6 million in africaJUICE B.V. (“aJ BV”). aJ BV was established in 2007 as a holding company which owns an 81% stake in africaJUICE Tibila Share Company (“aJ TSC”), the first Faitrtrade certified tropical fruit juice producer (mainly passion fruit, mango and papaya) in sub-Saharan Africa and based in the Upper Awash region of Ethiopia. The proposed financing package will be supported by the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (“GAFSP”). GAFSP funding plays a catalytic role to create opportunity to support innovative private sector investments and deliver a level of additionality and impact beyond what is possible through IFC’s regular operations. aJ TSC owns a 1,600 hectare farm as well as a EU compliant multi-fruit processing facility built in 2010. Over 1,400 tonnes of juice products have been exported to date, mostly to Europe. aJ TSC is seeking to transition into its next stage of growth by adding production volumes and product diversity. The plan is focused on realizing the passion fruit potential of its existing farm and its outgrowers and on diversifying its product base with the development of three new strategic crops (pomegranate, acerola and lemon) as well as expanding its processing capacity. The outgrower program will be expanded to incorporate 1,000-2,000 ha of smallholder passion fruit farmers.
sponsor_shareholders: Approximately 55% of aJ BV is primarily owned by the four founding members of the business and their family members via two asset management vehicles. The remaining 45% is owned by Agri-Vie Agribusiness Investment Fund, a South African private equity fund and an investee company of IFC. aJ BV owns 81% of aJ TSC, while the remainder is held by Privatization & Public Enterprises Supervising Authority (14%), an Ethiopian governmental entity and Fair & Sustainable Participations B.V., a Dutch limited liability company holding equity on behalf of the local community.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC, with GAFSP support, will provide a US$6 million financing package in the form of preferred equity.
location_description: aJ TSC’s primary operation is located in the Upper Awash region in Ethiopia, which consists of three farms (Degaga, Membere Hiwot and Tefiste Genet) totaling over 1,600 hectares of land. The fruit processing plant is located in Membere Hiwot.
development_impact: 1) Expected to reach at least an incremental 1,000 small scale passion fruit farmers over the next seven years. 2) Significant improvements in local food security. 3) Penetration of fair trade / modern farming practices to the wider producer base in Ethiopia. 4) Development of improved natural resource management techniques, especially water utilization. 5) Contribution to wider regional development in terms of jobs, infrastructure, education, health and other socio-economic parameters.
additionality: 1) IFC''s investment provides the needed long-term capital to an early stage business to enhance production volumes, diversify product offerings and reinforce the capital structure. 2) IFC''s technical expertise, global knowledge of the industry and markets as well as lessons learned from other integrated fresh juice / concentrate producers will be valuable resources to aJ TSC. 3) The team will work to mobilize GAFSP funding to further reinforce the capital structure of aJ TSC. 4) IFC''s investment will provide a "stamp of approval" for other private sector investors and DFIs to participate in the Project.

company_name: IFC Financial Institutions Growth Fund, LP
project_description: As part of IFC''s strategic focus on supporting the financial sector in emerging markets, IFC is proposing to invest in a to-be-established investment vehicle (the "IFC Global Financial Institutions Fund") that will mobilize additional capital for co-investments in financial institutions operating in emerging markets.
sponsor_shareholders: IFC proposes to invest in the IFC Global Financial Institutions Fund. Large global institutional investors are expected to invest alongside IFC. The IFC Global Financial Institutions Fund will be managed by IFC Asset Management Company, LLC ("AMC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of IFC. AMC mobilizes and manages third party funds for investment in developing and frontier markets. It was created in 2009 to expand the supply of long-term capital to these markets by accessing IFC''s global reach, investment approach and standards.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC''s investment will be 20% of total commitments made to the IFC Global Financial Institutions Fund subject to an overall cap of $200 million. The target fund size is US$1 billion.
location_description: The IFC Global Financial Institutions Fund will be formed under the laws of one of the IFC member countries, to be determined upon completion of due diligence.
development_impact: 1. Given that the fund will co-invest in IFC investments, it will support private sector development by increasing access to growth capital for SMEs in Emerging Markets. 2. The fund will further enhance and expand IFC''s development impact by leveraging IFC''s economic capital so that IFC can make more investments and thus expand its developmental reach. 3. The fund will also allow IFC to participate in larger ticket transactions which IFC would otherwise not be able to finance from its own balance sheet.
additionality: 1. Standard setting: In addition to financial resources, IFC brings in sustainability and governance advice. This has enabled investee companies to raised operating standards, improve risk mitigation, and generate value. 2. Long-term relationships: As a long-term partner IFC brings to its investee companies a network of global knowledge, technical expertise and best practice. 3. South-South mobilization: Successful establishment of this Fund could potentially mobilize funding from middle income emerging markets to developing emerging markets.
Company Name: IFC Financial Institutions Growth Fund, LP

project_description: The proposed investment consists of investment of up to €8 million to Velocity Dairy Plc (“VD”) through Velocity Africa Holding B.V. in support of its investment in a greenfield dairy operation in Ethiopia. VD was established in 2010 by Velocity Africa Holding BV to carry out this investment. The proposed investment will finance the construction of a modern dairy processing plant with a daily capacity of up to 70,000 liters, related infrastructure work, and the procurement of factory machinery and equipment. VD intends to produce dairy products and fruit juices to be marketed primarily in the local market. The proposed financing package will be supported by the Private Sector Window of the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (“GAFSP”). GAFSP funding plays a catalytic role to create opportunity to support innovative private sector investments and deliver a level of additionality and impact beyond what is possible through IFC’s regular operations.
sponsor_shareholders: Approximately 100% of the shares of VD are held by Velocity Africa Holding B.V., a holding company established by Velocity Capital Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is of approximately €45million out of which IFC, with GAFSP support, will provide up to €8million.
location_description: The project area is located in the Oromiya National Regional State in Ethiopia.
development_impact: 1) Additional and steady income for 5,000+ dairy farmers in the Oromiya region of Ethiopia. 2) Positive incentives for farmers to invest in their livestock and increase their yields. 3) Introduction of healthy, safe dairy products and a resulting increased food safety. 4) Large-scale employment (250+ full-time employees) as well as further jobs in the adjacent business areas. 5) Increased competition in the Ethiopian dairy industry. 6) Economic development of a sector of pivotal importance to rural and urban economic development.
additionality: 1) Investment by IFC provides stamp of approval to the Company / Sponsor and facilitates the sourcing of a debt package from the Development Bank of Ethiopia. 2) IFC''s technical expertise, global knowledge of the industry and markets as well as lessons learned from other integrated dairy projects are valuable resource to the Company. 3) IFC will assist VD in the adoption of best E&S standards across its operations by applying IFC''s performance standards.

project_description: DBL Group (“DBL” or the “Group”), an existing IFC Advisory Services client and one of Bangladesh’s largest and most reputed integrated knitted apparels manufacturers and exporters, has approached IFC to finance its knitted fabric, yarn and sewing thread dyeing expansion project (the “Project”) undertaken by the Group company Color City Limited (“Color City”, the “Company” or the “Borrower”). The proposed greenfield Project, with a targeted operational date of June 2014, will increase DBL’s dyeing capacity by 22 metric tons (“MT”) for knitted fabrics and 12MT for knitted dyed yarn (including 3MT for sewing thread). The proposed Project is Phase II of Color City’s expansion plan. Phase I, currently under implementation with DEG financing and expected to go online in January 2014, will increase DBL’s knitted fabric dyeing capacity by 28 MT. After implementation of both phases, Color City will have total dyeing and finishing capacity of 62MT and is expected to operate at 75% capacity utilization in the first year to fully cater to the Group’s forward-linked ready-made garment (“RMG”) units’ requirements.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsors are the Directors of the DBL Group, Mr. Abdul Wahed (Chairman), Mr. Mohammed Abdul Jabbar (Managing Director), Mr. Mohammed Abdur Rahim (Director) and Mr. Mohammed Abdul Quader (Director). Color City Limited, is owned by four DBL Group companies as follows: Jinnat Apparels Ltd. – 25%; Flamingo Fashions Ltd. – 25%; Hamza Textiles Ltd. – 25%; and Jinnat Fashions Ltd. – 25%. DBL Group, a reputable local business group in Bangladesh, is a privately-held, vertically integrated knitted garment (T-shirt products) manufacturing and exporting conglomerate comprising 14 companies. The Group’s operations cover the entire value chain of the knitted garment manufacturing process from yarn spinning and knitting to dyeing, sewing and packaging. DBL’s main buyers include H&M, Wal-Mart, Puma, C&A, Espirit and G-Star, with the Group being H&M’s only Platinum Supplier in Bangladesh for knitted products.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$35 million and is proposed to be financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of 60:40 as follows: long-term debt of US$21.0 million and shareholders’ equity (in the form of paid-up capital and subordinated loans from shareholder companies) of US$14million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to US$10.5 million with a tenor of seven years including a two-year grace period. IFC will attempt to raise an additional US$10.5 million in parallel loans from another multilateral or development financial institution.
location_description: The Project is located in Sadarganj, Kashimpur in the industrial belt of Gazipur, Bangladesh where DBL Group’s existing dyeing and finishing plants are located. The Project is accessible by road.
development_impact: 1. Job creation: The Project will create 850 new direct jobs, as well as temporary jobs during construction. Since dyeing and finishing is physical labor-intensive process, most of the employees will be male. However, being the first state-of-art dyeing facility of the country, the Company will diversify local workers'' skill-set and trigger learning curve on textiles dyeing operation. Moreover, the factory will adhere to international occupational, health and safety standards, thereby, offering better environment to improve workers'' quality of life. 2. Technology transfer: DBL intends to adopt global best practices in terms of lean manufacturing concepts, factory efficiency, worker productivity and energy efficiency, which will set an important example for and potentially elevate productivity and efficiency standards of the overall industry. 3. Boost local competitiveness: The Project is expected to boost Bangladesh''s knit apparel industry competitiveness by enhancing local dyeing and finishing capacity, which will enable DBL and other similar Groups to move towards higher value products. 4. Benefit to the government: The Project will generate tax revenues for the Government of Bangladesh.
additionality: 1. Provide long-term FX financing otherwise difficult to secure in the current market environment to support a leading conglomerate to expand its core business. 2. Through the proposed investment, IFC will integrate DBL into various textile/RMG-focused IFC advisory programs such as the ongoing environmental assessment of factories, effluent treatment plant study, Cleaner Production program, Buyer''s Forum and the planned Water Resource Efficiency and Better Works programs, which are geared towards improving compliance, competitiveness, energy efficiency, and labor welfare at the firm and industry levels . 3. Along with its own funding, IFC expects to mobilize an additional US$11 million through a Parallel loan from other DFIs. 4. Assist the Group to formulate and implement E&S action plan to expand social/labor management system for inclusion of environmental, occupational, health and safety (OHS) guidelines and enhance OHS management systems.

project_description: The Project involves the construction of a 175 room full service four star Marriott hotel in Port-au-Prince (PaP), Haiti by Turgeau Developments S.A. The hotel will include a ballroom, meeting facilities, a full service restaurant, a swimming pool, and a fitness center –among others.
sponsor_shareholders: The project will be developed by Turgeau Developments S.A, an entity incorporated in Haiti and indirectly owned by Digicel Limited, which is the project Sponsor.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project Cost is estimated at US$57.2 million. Of this amount, US$13.25 million will be financed by an IFC A Loan, and US$13.25 million by FMO, with the remainder funded by Sponsor’s equity.
location_description: The project will be located in Turgeau, a district of Port-au-Prince, the capital city of Haiti.
development_impact: The Project''s development impact is expected to include: - Development of business infrastructure of international standard in Port au Prince. - Creation of a significant number of jobs during the construction and operational phase. - Generation of downstream and upstream local supply linkages with the rest of the economy. - Increase of direct tax revenues by the government. - Improved environmental and social performance, including demonstration of solar water heating.
additionality: IFC''s additionality in the project is as follows: (i) long-term financing in Haiti, which cannot be obtained in the local market; (ii) mobilization; (iii) assisting the client in identifying and addressing potential areas of improvement on social and environmental aspects; and (iv) providing best practice guidance, validating the business plan.

company_name: ELIF PLASTIK AMBALAJ SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: The Project, sponsored by Elif Plastik Ambalaj ve Ticaret A.S. (”Elif Plastik”), of approximately US$64 million is to construct and operate a new packaging facility in the industrial area in Cairo, Egypt, and to provide funding for general corporate purposes, mostly working capital, for Elif Plastik main operating facility in Istanbul, Turkey.
sponsor_shareholders: Elif Plastik, a global supplier of flexible plastic packaging solutions for consumer goods, is a family owned company with production facilities in Istanbul, Turkey. It was formed in 1972 and is presently owned by the Salargil family of Turkey.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at US$64 million. The IFC investment consists of a loan of up to US$35.5 million.
location_description: Elif Plastik is located in Istanbul, Turkey. The new packaging facility, Elif Global Packaging S.A.E. (“Elif”) is located in the industrial area of Cairo, Egypt.
development_impact: -The project will: - Create 300 direct employment at the production facility and an additional 200-300 indirect jobs in Egypt, plus several hundred temporary jobs tied to the construction period. - Generate fiscal benefits through increased taxes. - Support Egyptian economy in foreign trade balance in terms of both decreased import and increased export. - Procure from local suppliers and support them. - Bring manufacturing management and technical know-how to Egypt and leverage sectors it serves. - Will help to provide timely delivery to the customers and develop the industry in Egypt. - Will have the capability to manufacture from recycled materials
additionality: - Provision of long-term funding. - South- South Investment: The project fits with IFC''s Turkey country strategy of supporting Turkish companies'' south-south investments as it supports a relativelly small Turkish company with its first investment outside of Turkey. - Potential IFC long-term partnership with Sponsor in other parts of the world going forward. Company plans to expand to Asian and Latin American markets in the future. - Demonstration effect at a time when investors are reluctant to invest in Egypt due to political uncertainty.
Company Name: ELIF PLASTIK AMBALAJ SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: The Project consists of providing up to US $1.5 million A Loan to Tetri Qudi LLC (“Tetri Qudi” or the “Company”). Tetri Qudi is the leading Georgian producer of fresh mushroom. The Company was established in 2010 and currently produces two types of mushroom: Champignon (Agaricus) and Oyster (Pleurotus). The proposed investment entails providing a corporate loan to Tetri Qudi, to be utilized for financing of the Company’s capital expenditures in 2013 and for additional working capital requirements to support the Company’s growth.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors and the shareholders of Tetri Qudi are: i) Mr.Areg Azoyan, citizen of Armenia. Currently, Mr. Azoyan holds 50% stake of the Company; ii) Mr. Temur Ketiladze, citizen of Georgia, he holds 25% stake of Tetri Qudi and iii) Mr.Tornike Tugushi, citizen of Georgia, holds 25% stake of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of US $1.5 million for IFC’s own account with 7 years maturity, including 2 years grace period.
location_description: Tetri Qudi’s headquarter and the production facilities are located in Georgia at the following address: Rustavi highway 17, Gardabani District, Georgia.
development_impact: The proposed Project has significant development impact including the following: - Supporting development of agribusiness sector: The Project will expand the Company`s operations in agribusiness, improve its competitiveness, and will support import substitution of mushroom products in Georgia. - Job creation: Direct and indirect job creation and preservation outside Tbilisi, the capital of Georgia, where the job opportunities are scarce. - Food Security: The Project will support food security in an IDA country. - Increased tax payments: Generating additional amount of taxes to be paid to the State. - Supply chain linkages: Growth of the Company will require increased level of economic activity with farmers, distributors and retailers.
additionality: -Long-term financing: IFC will provide long-term funding to Tetri Qudi for supporting the Company''s expansion and modernization of the fixed assets. -Standard-setting in Environmental & Social (E&S) issues: IFC would help the Company to improve its capacity in E&S management with the introduction of the policies which goes beyond the local regulation. -Advisory Services: IFC will also explore areas of advisory support to the Company, such as food safety and corporate governance. -South-South Investment: IFC will be supporting successful Armenian company expanding its operations in Georgia.

project_description: Parag Milk Foods Pvt. Ltd. (‘Parag’ or ‘the Company’), established in 1992, is one of India’s largest private dairy companies, catering to major cities in the country with a strong presence in Western and Southern India. It has a milk processing capacity of upto 2,000,000 litres per day (“LPD”) - 1,200,000 LPD at Manchar, Maharashtra and another 800,000 LPD at Palamner, Andhra Pradesh. The Company has a well diversified product portfolio ranging from liquid milk to value added products like UHT milk, cheese, butter, ghee (clarified butter), paneer (cottage cheese), yoghurt, curd, lassi, flavored milk, dairy whitener and milk powder, sold under the brands ‘GO’, ‘Gowardhan’ and ‘Top Up’, with value added products being > 60% of sales. For its next phase of growth, the Company plans to continue with its strategy of shifting to value added products which offer better margins, especially Whey (de-mineralised whey powder), Cheese and UHT milk. Also, the Company plans to strengthen its current operations through plant automation and expanding its procurement and distribution networks.
sponsor_shareholders: Parag was established in 1992 by Mr. Devendra Shah who is the main sponsor and the Chairman of the Group. Mr. Shah has over 25 years of experience in the field of dairy and allied activities. His two brothers, Mr. Pritam Shah (Managing Director) and Mr. Parag Shah (Director) are also co-sponsors in the Company and responsible for its day to day operations. The Company is privately held, with all local sponsors. Currently, the three promoters and their family own ~58% of Parag. Private equity funds, IDFC and Motilal Oswal own ~21% and ~12% respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$32.7 million, of which US$13.9 million or 42% has already been funded through an equity investment by IDFC in September 2012. IFC proposes to invest up to US$17 million in the project.
location_description: The Company currently has milk processing plants at two locations – Manchar in Maharashtra, Western part of India and Palamner in Andhra Pradesh, Southern part of India - both sites located in rural areas. The project involves setting up the following at the existing Company sites – i) a Whey plant in Manchar, ii) UHT milk plant in Palamner, iii) plant automation in Manchar and Palamner, and iv) chilling centers at both Manchar and Palamner.
development_impact: Improvement in food safety standards & technology: In India majority of the milk & milk products have very poor traceability till farm level. Also contamination and adulteration of milk is common owing to significant supply-demand gap and lack of extensive cold chain network. An organized sector player like Parag will help improve food safety standards. Also, Parag is ahead in technology as compared to other players in the Indian dairy sector. Enhanced supply chain linkage with farmers and food suppliers: Parag currently collects milk from ~60,000 farmers directly or through third parties and is focusing on growing the procurement network by setting up more chilling centers and bulk coolers. This increased demand of milk will lead to increase in number of farmers in the supply chain. It will also support other input suppliers to the industry including feed and veterinarian suppliers. Development of medium and small enterprises: Parag distributes its products through 60+ super-stockists, 1,000+ distributors and over 120,000 retail outlets thus having a far reaching impact on supporting medium and small enterprises across the country. Improved incomes in rural and peri-urban areas: The project will create direct and indirect employment and result in other development benefits such as linkages with local suppliers, as also seen in our previous project with Pran Dairy, Bangladesh. Also, Parag sells cows from its own dairy farm to the local population after the cow has its 5th / 6th lactation. These are superior breed cows with yields better than those reared locally and will hence help improve rural incomes. Supporting growth/guiding the critical Indian dairy industry: Expecting a shortfall in supply and to improve yields, NDDB expects a gradual increase in the share of the organized sector to 60% from the current share of 30%. IFC investment will help this medium sized dairy Company to expand rapidly and develop best practices to increase yield that would be disseminated down to farmers who form a critical link in Company''s supply chain.
additionality: E&S related guidance: Parag''s operations show poor housekeeping, multiple issues related to management systems, human resources policy, air emissions, effluents, farm manure management, resource efficiency. IFC will be able to guide the Company on several aspects, as it embarks on the process of newly professionalizing and developing management system based approaches to quality and energy management, which will then be expanded to environmental and safety management. Global Knowledge: IFC can share global knowledge with the Company on a continuous basis. Productivity of Indian cattle is between 800 and 1,000 litres of milk per animal per year as compared to between 7,000 and 8,000 liters per year for the best varieties around the world. IFC, leveraging its relationship with companies around the world, can help the Company with international best practices. Access to financing matching investment profile: Parag''s proposed project expansion is large and will benefit from the flexibility of a long-term financing with appropriate grace period that is not easily available in the local market for companies of medium size. Business advisory & work with targeted farmers to extend coverage: Parag currently collects milk from ~60,000 farmers directly or through third parties. IFC would be able to guide the client on appropriate business strategy, environmental and food safety standards which are necessary for sustainable growth of the enterprise. In view of the scale of expansion the option of providing training through the ''Business Edge'' product would also be offered to the client. IFC''s proposed study along with Gates Foundation on the diary sector focusing on (a) smallholder dairy farm productivity; (b) smallholder dairy farmer awareness and practice of food safety and (c) Water use-efficiency and GHG emission reduction from smallholder dairy farms, will potentially be very useful for the client.

project_description: Kaiima Bio Agritech Ltd. (“Kaiima” or the “Company”) is an Israel-based company that has developed an innovative non-GMO technology platform to breed crops with dramatically improved productivity and resource use efficiencies. Kaiima’s enhanced breeding technologies allow for rapidly breeding plants that have high yield potential and are adapted to specific climate conditions. Kaiima is currently engaged in projects to commercialize key high-impact food and industrial crops. Kaiima has three business lines – (i) high impact food crops, such as wheat, corn, and rice; (ii) industrial crops; and (iii) vegetable seeds including tomatoes, cucumbers, and peppers. The Company’s proposed investment plan will be used to support the scale-up of its R&D and commercial activities globally, including developing countries such as China, Kazakhstan and Mexico.
sponsor_shareholders: Kaiima is a private firm founded in 2006 by members of the current management team. The Company has had previous rounds of financing and is majority owned by institutional investors that are global venture capital firms including Draper Fisher Jurvetson, DFJ Tamir Fishman Ventures, and Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Kaiima is seeking to raise up to $50 M through a Series C equity round of financing. The proceeds of the financing are to be used to support the scale-up of its R&D and commercial activities. The Company’s end markets are primarily in emerging markets where food security is a prime developmental challenge. The proposed IFC investment in Kaiima is up to US$20 million in equity (the “Project”).
location_description: Kaiima is headquartered in Israel and the Project locations have not yet been determined.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have significant development impact by (i) increasing agricultural yields which will result in increased land use efficiency; (ii) developing seed alternatives that are adapted to climate extremes in emerging markets; (iii) creating a non-GMO product that requires fewer regulatory hurdles and thus can benefit smaller markets, including smallholder farmers in IDA countries; (iv) promoting the development of sustainable industrial oils and thereby reduce GHG emissions.
additionality: IFC''s Role & Additionality in the Project include (i) early stage equity & mobilization; (ii) introducing client to new markets; (iii) E&S and corporate governance.

company_name: NEOGAS DO BRASIL GAS NATURAL COMPRIMIDO S.A.
project_description: NEOgas do Brazil (“NEOgas” or “the Company”) is a leading provider of off-pipeline natural gas solutions in Latin America. The Company is utilizing its own proprietary equipment design and technology and operates in Brazil, Peru, Mexico and Colombia where it supplies CNG by trailers in remote areas that are not serviced by the existing gas pipelines. The Company is seeking financing to fund its capital expenditure program that includes acquisition of additional new equipment to support growth in the markets where it currently operates.
sponsor_shareholders: NEOgas is majority-owned (76%) by a fund sponsored by Global Environment Fund (“GEF”), a private equity fund manager based in Washington, D.C. focused on investing in companies improving the natural environment. Minority shareholders include CleanTech, a private equity fund managed by Emerging Energy and Environment (“EEE”), a Stamford, CT based private equity fund manager focused on clean energy investments in Latin America (8%); NPR Group, a Rio de Janeiro-based partnership for investments in energy businesses (8%); and Purbeck do Brasil & Adoble, investment vehicles for the original company founders (6%) represented by Antonio de Azevedo, currently Director for Brazil and Operations and members of his family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is around US$100 million. IFC is considering an investment up to US$40 million in the Company to involve a combination of a C Loan and potential straight equity investment through a warrant. The balance of the Project will be financed with internal cash generation and senior bank loans.
location_description: The Project will be implemented at various locations in Brazil, Colombia, Mexico and Peru.
development_impact: Climate change mitigation: NEOgas'' primary business is the distribution of natural gas to areas where it is otherwise unavailable, resulting in the displacement of competing fuels such as fuel oil, gasoline and diesel, which are more polluting and with a much higher carbon impact per energy unit. Improved competitiveness of local companies located in frontier areas that are not serviced by the existing gas pipelines: NEOgas provides off-pipeline natural gas solutions to vehicular and industrial customers utilizing a proprietary technology that reduces capital and operational expenses to its customers: the average annual energy cost savings for industrial customers range from 40-60% depending on the location. Job creation: expansion of NEOgas operations will create quality employment opportunities in Peru, Brazil, Mexico and Colombia. Private sector development: the proposed Project will promote private sector participation in the regional natural gas distribution sector that is dominated by state owned companies in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.
additionality: IFC will play a major role by providing a much needed quasi equity and equity capital to ensure overall sustainability of the Company''s growth. NEOgas is a rapidly growing company and is using its net cash inflows to fund expansion and acquisition of new equipment. IFC investment will allow for acceleration of this growth and provide additional capital base to support further long-term debt. IFC''s participation will also help diversify sources of funding and provide comfort to other potential investors. IFC would also help the Company to develop comprehensive environmental and social assessment documentation and insure compliance of the Company''s operations with IFC''s Performance Standards.
Company Name: NEOGAS DO BRASIL GAS NATURAL COMPRIMIDO S.A.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: Sisecam Soda Lukavac d.o.o. (“SSL”) is involved in the production of light and heavy (dense) soda and other products based on soda ash. SSL was created from the transfer of soda ash production assets from a loss making state owned soda ash producer. IFC provided €39 million (approximately US$50 million) of financing to SSL in two successive investments in 2007 and 2010 for its acquisition and post-privatization investments to turnaround its operations. Total outstanding IFC loan is US$31 million equivalent. The proposed expansion project is expected to cost US$65 million and will comprise (i) a capacity increase from 365 thousand tons/year (tpa) to 500 thousand tpa leading to economies of scale; (ii) improvements in energy and resource efficiency and reduction in energy costs; (iii) improvements in SSL’s operational efficiency through renovation and equipment upgrades and additional infrastructure; (iv) a waste management project to improve emissions and waste water treatment and (iv) some permanent working capital financing to SSL.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Sise ve Cam Fabrikalari A.S. (“Sisecam”) and Soda Sanayii A.S. (“Soda Sanayii”), both listed on Istanbul Stock Exchange (“ISE”). SSL is 89% owned by the Soda Sanayii, with the remainder of the Company being state owned. Sisecam is a leading Turkish producer of flat glass, tableware, glass containers, glass fibers and associated products worldwide. Sisecam owns 61% of the Soda Sanayii’s shares directly and 18% through Anadolu Cam Sanayii A.S., its glass packing arm.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at US$65 million that will mostly comprise capacity expansion, efficiency and environmental improvements. The project will allow SSL to sustain its operations while further increasing production capacity. The proposed investment is to provide a senior loan of up to $30 million from IFC (for its own account) and up to $10 million from IFC as implementing entity of the Canada Climate Change Program (CCCP).
location_description: The project is located in the Tuzla Canton of the Federation Bosnia Herzegovina on the outskirts of the city of Lukavac (140 km north of the capital Sarajevo and 14 km west of Tuzla).
development_impact: IFC''s investment in SSL continues to have a strong demonstration effect as SSL has become an example of a successful privatization and foreign direct investment in Bosnia and Herzegovina, an IDA country. The new project will help enhance SSL''s turnaround and competitiveness through economies of scale and improvements in energy and resource efficiency. SSL is one of the largest employers in the Tuzla area (approximately 550 people) and generates significant employment at the local brine and limestone mines.
additionality: IFC''s investment will enable SSL to help enhance the turnaround of its operations and increase its competitiveness. IFC will also invest in waste management and clean production that will increase energy and resource efficiency and result in further energy savings and environmental improvements.

project_description: The proposed project will support an investment by Property Development Company CJSC (“Prodeco”) for the construction of a ~23,000sqm Class A, 9 storey “energy efficient green office complex” in central Yerevan. The project is a greenfield that will contribute a modern, green building to the existing business infrastructure of the country, providing an important model for future energy efficient construction projects in the country. The office complex will be constructed on a total land area of 2,850 sqm on V. Sargsyan street, with the main façade of the existing building remaining intact in the new construction. The property developer, Prodeco, owned 100% by Ameria Group, was established in 2007 and specializes in real estate development.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Ameria Group Ltd, a private holding company incorporated in Cyprus, where Mr Ruben Vardanyan and Mr Noubar Afeyan are ultimate beneficial shareholders. The main company of the Group is Ameriabank CJSC (“Ameriabank”) which is the 2nd largest bank in Armenia and an existing IFC client.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at USD 38.6 million, with construction expected to be completed within 2 years. The proposed IFC investment will be a loan of up to USD10 million, complemented by a loan from the proceeds of Canada Climate Change Program, a donor-funded facility for climate change friendly projects administered by the IFC, and a USD 10 million loan provided by a parallel lender. The Sponsor is contributing equity of USD18.6 million.
location_description: Project site is located in central Yerevan, within 100m from the main Republic Square of Yerevan, Armenia. The land location has large amount of pedestrian and land traffic being situated in one of the central streets of the city. Currently there are existing buildings in the site location, which will be demolished during the construction of the new building. Exact address for the site is as follows: Bd. 2, V.Sargsyan 4, Yerevan 0010 Republic of Armenia http://www.prodeco.am
development_impact: 1) Elevation of commercial real estate standards-throughout the country through development of a Class A office building; 2) Development of high quality business infrastructure in Armenia; 3) Direct and indirect employment of service jobs; possibility for further linkages; 4) Tax revenues will accrue to the government; 5) Implementation of green building standards and sound E&S policies as per IFC requirements
additionality: By supporting an existing IFC Sponsor, IFC has a strong role in infrastructure development taking place in an IDA country that will help create the necessary business infrastructure to support further growth. IFC''s additionality includes: (i) Provision of long-term financing, along with another IFI; (ii) Improvement of the Company''s capital structure; (iii) Access to IFC''s green building expertise in project development; (iv) Enhancement of corporate governance within the Company;

project_description: The proposed project involves the renewal of the existing Master Risk Participation Agreement (“MRPA”) with Standard Chartered Bank(“SCB”) for a trade facility of US$150 million for the issuance of Letters of Credit (“LC”) to a Ghanaian bulk distribution company (“BDC”) for the importation of petroleum products into Ghana for another 3 years starting from June 2013. The BDC under consideration is Chase Petroleum Ghana Limited (“Chase”). Of the total facility amount, IFC’s exposure will be up to US$75 million through the risk sharing arrangement, whereby, IFC will effectively share the underlying credit risk of the BDC with SCB.
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in London, Standard Chartered Bank has over 1,700 branches and outlets located in over 70 countries and has operated for over 150 years in some of the world''s most dynamic markets. The group earns around 90 per cent of its income and profits in Asia, Africa and the Middle East, from its wholesale and consumer banking businesses. Its income and profits have more than doubled over the last five years primarily as a result of organic growth. It is among the top three global banks for trade. Standard Chartered Bank is committed to building a sustainable business over the long term and is holds high standards of corporate governance, social responsibility, environmental protection and employee diversity. It employs around 70,000 people, nearly half of whom are women. The group''s employees are of 125 nationalities, of which about 70 are represented in the senior management. Standard Chartered Bank is listed on both London and Hong Kong stock exchanges. Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s rating for SCB are A2 and A+, respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s exposure will be up to $75 million through a risk sharing arrangement, whereby, IFC will effectively share the underlying credit risk of Chase with SCB.
location_description: Standard Chartered Bank is headquartered in London, United Kingdom and operates in over 70 countries. The project involves providing structured trade finance to Chase which imports and supplies petroleum products in bulk to the Ghana’s retailers.
development_impact: (i) Alleviation of Fuel Shortages and Meeting Demand Growth: IFC will support the largest fuel importer who is contributing to alleviation of fuel shortages. Given the empirical evidence of a high correlation between energy consumption and GDP growth and a direct relationship between the absence of adequate energy and many poverty indicators, the project has significant economic importance for the country.
