(ii) Deepening Ghanaian Financial Markets: The project supplements the facilities offered by local banks and IFC''s GTFP program through providing additional cost effective trade finance solutions in Ghana. (iii) Private Sector Development: The facility is supporting Ghanaian private sector companies in a recently deregulated and growing sector.
additionality: (i) Stamp of Approval: The IFC facility will continue to serve as stamp of approval to Chase and the industry and helping to mobilize financing to support the fuel sector. (ii) Financing Gap: Supporting the African private sector in a market environment where deleveraging to meet regulatory capital requirements constrains the risk appetite of international banks. (iii) Environmental and Social Expertise: For the existing facility IFC has worked succesfully with a BDC and a bank that are committed maintaining strong environmrntal and social practices.

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: The project consists of the establishment of a greenfield aluminum rod and conductor manufacturing plant to be located in Boane district of Mozambique.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor is Midal Cable limited of Bahrain, a private company jointly owned by Al Zayani Investments and Saudi Cable Company. Midal has been manufacturing aluminum rod and conductors for the past 36 years.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at US$50 million for capital costs plus US$35 million working capital costs. The proposed IFC investment is a US$25 million A loan and US$7 million equity for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project will be located in Baluluane Industrial Park adjacent to Mozal aluminum smelter in Boane district of Mozambique.
development_impact: 1. Job creation: The Project will create 220 direct permanent jobs for Mozambican nationals and more indirect jobs in the local supply chain. 2. Local value addition to a local product: The project will be the first local downstream manufacturing to add value to a part of Mozambique''s aluminum production at Mozal, which will facilitate development of further local downstream manufacturing using output from the project, and also increase export revenues for the country. 3. Knowledge transfer: The project will allow the transfer to Mozambique of technical and management know-how of aluminum rod and conductor manufacturing and expand the knowledge base of manufacturing in general.
additionality: 1. Appropriate long-term finance: IFC will provide appropriate long-term financing required by the project, which is not readily available in Mozambique due to low capital base of local banks. 2. Mobilization: IFC''s presence will facilitate the raising of additional long-term financing needed by the project. 3. Risk mitigation: IFC''s presence will help mitigate project risks and provide comfort to the sponsor and other stakeholders. 4. IFC''s global knowlegde and industry expertise: IFC will use its global knowledge and industry expertise to help strucutre the project and ensure its long-term sustainability. 5. Support EHS standards: IFC will support the company and ensure it prepares an adequate Environmental Impact Assesment and constructs the project to meet internataional Environmental Health and Safety best standards.

project_description: Although the origins of Bekto Precisa d.o.o. (Bekto Precisa or the Company) stem from Bekto Internacional d.o.o. which was established as one of the first privately owned companies in the Former Yugoslavia, about 35 years ago, the Company was founded as a family business in 2005 right after the sale of Bekto Internacional d.o.o. to EMKA Beschlagteile GmbH & Co (Emka) in 2004 where Emka is still the largest customer of the Company operating eight factories across Europe and China with annual turnover of €220 million. Bekto Precisa has specialized in technical know-how and up-to-date technology in the production of highly sophisticated tools and non-ferrous metals, as well as metal-plastic combinations. The Company is export-oriented and mainly supplies three industries, which in the importance of the turnover generation are automotive, electrical, and ski industries. Formed with 10 employees, the Company successfully managed to grow into one of the leading companies in the Southern Europe offering turn-key production solutions covering design, engineering, precision tool making and molding, plus additional fitting and assembly services of sophisticated plastic and metal injection molding units by employing more than 350 employees currently. The Company plans to (i) execute an expansion investment in 2013-2015 to strengthen its competitiveness and to accept multi-tool and larger tool orders for heavier and complex plastic parts, (ii) refinance and restructure its existing debt to optimize the number of relationship banks as well as (iii) improve its corporate governance practices (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Bekto Precisa is a private company, fully owned by Mrs. Rasema Bekto while the strategic decisions at the Company are taken by her husband, Mr. Redzo Bekto (the founder of the Bekto Precisa) and her daughter Mrs. Enisa Bekto (the general manager of the Company) and (all together referred to as the Bekto Family). Although the Company doesn’t have any subsidiaries, the related companies, due to having the same beneficial owners, are: (i) Hella Bekto Industries d.o.o. in Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) which is a joint venture with German HELLA KGaA Hueck & Co. to produce efficient street lighting fixtures), (ii) Ebi d.o.o. in BiH (a holding company owned by Mrs. Enisa Bekto and Mr. Bekto which holds the shareholding of Bekto Family at Hella Bekto Industries d.o.o.; and (iii) Marbe Handels GmbH in Austria (a customer relationship management company owned by Mrs. Rasema Bekto, her daughter and son-in-law to transact with the Western European clients.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a €8 million A Loan for IFC’s own account where the total project cost is estimated at €12 million in 2013-2015.
location_description: Bekto Precisa’s headquarters and operations are based in Gorazde, a city in BiH located 100 km east of Sarajevo and 20 km from the Serbian border. Gorazde is in the eastern part of the country which is known for its low level of development and was badly affected by the war in the 90’s. However, it has since succeeded in developing an engineering hub primarily focused on the automotive sector. Current population of the city is estimated at 30,000 and Bekto Precisa is one of the leading employers in this remote town, promoting high skilled labor.
development_impact: - On top of existing labor force of the Company, Bekto Precisa is expected to create additional direct skilled jobs until 2014 in a country where official unemployment rate is around 45%, - Moreover, the multiplier effect is estimated at 3x for indirect jobs in small-medium enterprises focused on factory & machine maintenance and small mechanical workshops located mainly in Gorazde, a small remote mountain town, supporting local MSMEs, - On the back of increased sales & production capacity of the Company as well as export-oriented production & sales will boost the hard-currency flow to BiH with a certain positive impact on BiH''s current account deficit and tax revenues; and - Finally, given that Bekto Precisa mainly sources its main processing material and services domestically, which corresponds more than 50% of total annual expenses of the Company, the Project will have a direct positive local supply chain impact.
additionality: - Long-term Financing: The proposed long-term IFC financing will help Bekto Precisa to grow/modernize by (i) funding its capital expenditure program to improve its competitiveness by broadening its products'' dimensions; and (ii) restructuring its debt through extending the maturity which is not ready available in the market at favorable rates to enhance the Company''s financial flexibility, - Corporate Governance Advice: IFC is expected to accelerate the Company''s transformation from a family-owned business to a more institutionalized firm, - Global Sector Expertise & Knowledge: IFC will share its global sector expertise and knowledge that will help improve the Company''s lean manufacturing programs, fine-tune its long-term strategic vision to grow beyond traditional customer base; and - Standard-Setting: IFC will help the Company improve its E&S practices to exceed local regulatory requirement and be a pioneer in the country.

project_description: IFC is considering an up to US$120 million loan facility to Olam International Limited (“Olam” or the “Borrower”), a global supply chain management group headquartered in Singapore and listed on the Singapore Stock Exchange (SGX: Olam). The proceeds of the loan provided by IFC shall be used for: (a) partial refinancing of existing financial debt of Olam’s subsidiaries in respect of Approved Projects pre-agreed between Olam and IFC; and (b) financing permanent working capital and capital expenditure requirements in respect of Approved Projects. Approved Projects are projects of Olam’s subsidiaries that are pre-agreed between Olam and IFC in the Loan Agreement. Currently, approved projects are expected to consist of the following: India – Hemarus Industries Limited - Sugar and Cogeneration Facility Acquisition and Upgrade India – SVI Spices Processing Facility Upgrade Nigeria – Crown Flour Mill Factory Expansion Nigeria – Greenfield Cashew Nut Processing Plant Nigeria – Greenfield Sesame Hulling Unit - Relocation of Existing Facilities and Upgrade
sponsor_shareholders: Olam’s key shareholders are: KC Group (20.2%); Temasek Holdings (24.0%). Management holds approximately 9.5%, and the remaining shares are held by a number of institutional investors globally.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is an up to US$120 million A Loan for IFC’s own account to Olam for use to finance a pre-approved list of projects.
location_description: The current list of approved projects are located in the following sites: India – Hemarus Industries Limited - Sugar and Cogeneration Facility Acquisition and Upgrade: Rajkoli, Kolhapur- 416508, Maharashtra, India India – SVI Spices Processing Facility Upgrade: 9/102, Resurvey No V/178, Varikoli PO, Puthencruz, Ernalulam 682308, India Nigeria – Crown Flour Mill Factory Expansion: (i) Gate No.2, Behind Berth No.1, Tin Can Island Port, Apapa, Lagos, Nigeria; (ii) Warri: New Port Complex, Warri, Delta State, Nigeria Nigeria – Greenfield Cashew Nut Processing Plant: Km 3, Afon Road, Near Ganmo Power Station, Ogbondoroko Illorin, Kwara State Nigeria – Greenfield Sesame Hulling Unit Relocation of Existing Facilities and Upgrade: Flowergate Scheme, Extension, along Lagos/Ibadan Expressway, Ibido Village, Sagamu Local Government Area, Ogun state of Nigeria
development_impact: The proposed investment covers a range of corporate projects in various geographies and subsectors. The development impact of each project will be assessed on its particular merits as regards: (i) financial viability; (ii) economic viability; (iii) E&S performance; and (iv) private sector development. Most of these projects, however, are likely to contribute to one or more of the following: - Food sufficiency, especially in the host countries - Farm productivity improvement, technology transfer and demonstration impact - Farmers'' incomes. According to its Annual Report, Olam has relationships with about 200,000 producers, a number that will increase as part of this investment, including in some post-conflict countries in Africa - Employment generation. The projects contribute to the creation of formal, non-farming jobs in rural areas where most of the world''s poor live - Support to local MSMEs that provide goods and services or participate in the marketing of Olam''s products.
additionality: IFC''s expected additionality is seen to materialize through a wide spectrum of contributions that include: (i) support to adhere to best practices and transparency on supply chain management; (ii) stamp of approval to its efforts to improve food security and the livelihoods of small farmers especially in Sub-Saharan Africa; (iii) political risk mitigation, particularly in the challenging countries and sometimes difficult political environments Olam operates in; (iv) counter-cyclical role providing growth funds to Olam in a tightened financing environment; (v) advisory services support to Olam''s efforts to improve competitiveness of its suppliers.

project_description: Malia Invest (Holding) sal (“Malia Invest” or “the Company”), a Lebanese company focused on developing projects in Iraq, is proposing to set up a multi-use branded extended stay greenfield commercial property project comprising of 20 floors in Erbil, Iraq (the “Project”). The property will be managed by Rotana Hotel Management Corporation, an independent and internationally reputable hospitality management company. The Project will consist of (i) 154 –keys serviced apartments. (ii) two floors of serviced offices space ; (iv) an all day dining restaurant, roof top bar and gym; and (vi) a 100 parking spaces. The Company has obtained an investment license and has leased a plot of land with a total surface of 2,300 square meter (“sqm”) and total built‐up area of the project is 23,665 sqm. Malia Invest currently owns the 201 keys five stars hotel in Erbil (called the “Erbil Rotana”) located close the project site, and has been in operation since 2010. The Project is being set up by the Company with a view to capture an increasing demand for service apartments in the growing city of Erbil, where a large number of businesses are setting up their presence.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project will be owned by Tower Line for Touristic Investments Limited, an Iraqi company, 100% owned by Towerline (Holding) sal, a Lebanese company which in turn is held by Malia Invest. Malia Invest is 100% owned by Malia Holding sal (the “Sponsor”), a well diversified Lebanese company with operations in Lebanon, Syria and Iraq. Its key activities include manufacturing, marketing and distribution of cosmetics, fragrances, pharmaceuticals, insecticides, detergents, and consumer products, as well as in real estate development and construction, electromechanical contracting, system integration, and information technology businesses. The Sponsor is owned by Mr Jacques Sarraf, and three of his immediate family members.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost for the Project is estimated to be US$42.9 million (the “Project Cost”) including civil construction, furniture and fixtures, and initial working capital. The Project Cost is expected to be financed by 51% equity, balance 49% debt, which includes IFC loan of up to US$14 million and US$7 million from other lenders/financiers.
location_description: The Project is being built on the leased land on the new 100 Avenue in the Erbil City of Kurdistan, Iraq. This land was owned by the Erbil Municipality and was subsequently transferred to the Board of Investment (“BOI”), Government of Kurdistan. With the development of Erbil as a key city of Kurdistan, the land has now become central and a prime location. The Company has indicated that no resettlement or expropriation was necessary to secure this land. All necessary permits have been obtained, including construction permit, Ministry of Environment approvals, BOI licenses, Municipality approvals.
development_impact: The Project will foster the development of business infrastructure in Erbil through (i) providing much needed business infrastructure to the employees of development institutions, diplomats, government workers, NGOs, investors, as well as many private companies that are involved in rebuilding Iraq that frequently use Erbil as their home base during their stay and work in other parts of Iraq; (ii) benefiting the municipal city planning by providing infrastructure for business development such as conference rooms and business centers; (iii) creating outsourcing opportunities, (iv) creating employment (around 110 employees); and (v) extensive hotel training that will be provided by Rotana prior to and during operations, which is expected to enhance the overall service quality standards for the hospitality industry in the region.
additionality: IFC will play catalytic role in facilitating further private investment into a conflict affected country. IFC''s involvement will have a strong demonstration effect by supporting the private sector foreign investments in the country, with all of the related challenges, and laying critical groundwork for future private investments in hotels and other sectors. Moreover, IFC will provide (i) political coverage, (ii) global sector knowledge and expertise, (iii) appropriate financing conditions for the proposed investment and (iv) guidance to the Company to implement environmental and social best practices.

project_description: The proposed project comprises a greenfield development of a 280-room 5-star hotel in Conakry, Guinea (the “Project”). The Project is implemented by the Guinea-incorporated Palma Guinée S.A. (“Palma Guinea”). Fully owned by the Topaz Group of companies, Palma Guinea has been incorporated specifically to develop and own the Project hotel, which will be operated by Starwood Hotels & Resorts Worldwide, Inc., under the Sheraton brand. The purpose of the Project is to reduce imbalance between supply and demand for quality hotel accommodations in Conakry. At present, Guinea’s capital has no 5-star hotels. This gap in the hospitality market has been hindering travel to Conakry and slowing down the city’s development into an important national and regional business destination. The Project hotel is expected to help change this situation and to become an important part of Conakry’s business infrastructure.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is the Topaz group of companies (“Topaz”). Topaz is an international group fully controlled by the Vaswanis, a family of prominent entrepreneurs. The main business of the group main business is international wholesale trade of a variety of goods of everyday consumption. In addition, the Group produces plastic extrusion products in Guinea being one of the country’s few manufacturers. Present in Guinea for approximately 25 years, the Group strived through periods of instability and has grown into Guinea’s most important foreign investor in Guinea outside the mining sector.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$61 million. The proposed IFC investment is a secured senior loan package of up to US$26 million to Palma Guinea. The loan package is expected to comprise: (i) an A loan for IFC’s own account of up to US$15 million and (ii) a syndicated B loan of up to US$11 million.
location_description: The Project hotel will be located on a seafront greenfield site in Kipe, a district of Conakry, Guinea’s capital. The site of the future hotel is adjacent to residential and business areas and has a convenient access to the city’s major transport arteries.
development_impact: Business infrastructure development/Opening of Conakry as a travel destination: The Project will support the development of a high-standard hotel, which will help Guinea''s capital city address growing demand for quality hotel accommodation driven by increasing business travel and the emerging conference activities sector. Furthermore, the availability of a high-quality hotel is expected to become a driver for more travel (both business and conference) to Conakry in its own right, contributing to the development of the city into a regional center. Best practice transfer: The Project is expected to support transfer of best international business practices to Guinea, especially in such areas as (i) real estate development; (ii) hotel management; (iii) management of environmental, social life and fire safety issues; (iv) business ethics, transparency and integrity in dealing with employees, business partners, authorities and other stakeholders. Employment generation: The investment will create significant local direct employment of about 400 and indirect employment in the supply value chain. Linkages to the local economy: The Project hotel will seek to establish linkages with the local economy, specifically in such areas, as the supply of food products and the procurement of services (e.g. transportation). Encouragement of investment activity in Guinea/Demonstration effect: The Project will have a demonstration effect by encouraging other international and regional players to pursue investment opportunities in Guinea as this IDA post-conflict country works to improve the business climate, facilitate greater foreign direct investment inflows and diversify its economy from the natural resource-based sectors.
additionality: Provision of long-term financing/Mobilization: IFC will provide and mobilize a loan package of the size, tenor and repayment profile that are not readily available in the region. This will enable Topaz to proceed timely with its investment project, as well as to ensure a stable financial performance of the Project hotel during the operational stage. In addition, IFC''s knowledge of the tourism sector is important in assessing the feasibility and structuring this investment. and will help ensure that the related risks are properly mitigated. Environmental and social (E&S) performance: IFC''s E&S expertise will ensure that the Project is implemented based on the highest relevant E&S standards. In addition, IFC has been providing to the Sponsor with advice in the energy efficiency/ green building areas. South-South investment: IFC''s investment will support a South-South expansion of a successful business group originating from and focused on emerging market countries in Guinea, a post-conflict IDA country.

project_description: Rubliovskiy (“Rubliovskiy” or the “Client”) is planning to open 21 new stores and acquire 4 existing stores with a combined trade area of over 30 thousand square meters (“sqm”) in 2012-2014. Rubliovskiy is the leading wholesaler and 5th largest food retailer in Belarus. The client owns and operates a chain of 45 stores and 9 warehouses throughout Belarus. The expansion contemplated by Rubliovskiy will allow it to expand on its success to-date by tapping into significantly underserved regional markets, expand its market share in Minsk and strengthen its overall competitive position.
sponsor_shareholders: Rubliovskiy was established in 1993 as a wholesale Company. The Group opened the first Rublyovskiy supermarket in 2003 in Minsk and has been adding several stores to its chain every year since then. The business is owned by its three founders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$74 million. IFC has been requested to provide a loan of up to US$20 million for its own account.
location_description: Rubliovskiy is headquartered in Minsk. The company has 45 retail stores and provides logistics and distribution services using its own warehouse nearby Minsk and 9 leased warehouses throughout Belarus.
development_impact: Benefits to consumers: By enhancing its retail chain, the Group will be able to provide access to a more diverse selection of high-quality, affordable products than most Belarusian consumers currently have access to. Stronger bargaining positions vis-a-vis suppliers, economies of scale achieved through geographical expansion, as well as improved inventory management, will allow for cost savings, which eventually can be passed on to the end customer; Supply chain development: The Group''s expansion will (i) increase the number of its local suppliers, (ii) provide additional sales channels for local producers and importers, as well as (iii) contribute to improvements in efficiency and operating standards throughout the supply chain. Employment generation: The Project will provide additional direct employment for approximately 2,500 people 80% of whom are expected to be women. Five of the Project stores will be greenfield construction projects, so temporary jobs will be created during the construction phase. In addition, indirect employment will be created in the retail value chain. Best practice transfer: The Project is expected to facilitate the transfer of modern retail techniques to Belarusian regions and to enhance the efficiency of the supply chain in the country. The Project will also create a standard for employee training and development across the country. Demonstration effect: The Project will have a demonstration effect by encouraging other companies in the region, as well as Western investors, to pursue investment opportunities in Belarus as the country tries to improve its business climate and facilitate greater inflows of foreign direct investment. In addition, the Project will have a demonstration effect for private sector activity in general by showing the capacity of a private sector company to meet effectively and professionally the needs of the population in a predominantly state-dominated economy.
additionality: Provision of long-term financing: Not available in the local markets, long-term financing from IFC will enable the Group to proceed timely with the Project and to remain financially stable in the post-crisis environment. Also, in 2012/2013 Belorusian government significantly restricted local companies from taking hard currency loans, while the local currency loans interest rates go as high as 40-50% per annum. In this environment IFC''s reasonably priced hard currency loan would provide the Company with a more suitable type of funding. Risk Mitigation: IFC''s knowledge of the retail sector is important in assessing the feasibility of this project. IFC''s financial structuring expertise will ensure that this project is bankable and that its risks are properly mitigated. IFC''s Global Expertise: Rublyovsky highly values IFC''s global retail sector expertise. RTL and IFC have been working together productively on a wide range of issues. The Group values suggestions made by IFC to-date, such as the introduction of fresh fruit supply chain program, IFC''s recommendation to refocus on expansion of the retail business rather than on growing distribution; IFC''s inputs in developing the distribution center etc. RTL''s shareholders frequently invite IFC to participate in internal meetings and in meetings of the board of directors. IFC''s cooperation with Rublyovsky is likely to deepen in the context of the new deal. Environmental and social ("E&S") supervision in March 2010 identified that Rubliovskiy had a very impactful program underway to enhance energy efficiency in its cooling systems. IFC''s participation in the Project will ensure that cooling system upgrading is part of the refurbishment of the existing stores, as well as an element of the design of the new stores, included in the scope of the Project.

project_description: SolTuna Limited (“SolTuna” or the “Company”) is Solomon Islands’ sole tuna loining and canning processor based in Noro, Western Province. The Company commenced operations in 1973 as Solomon Taiyo Limited, a 100% pole and line tuna fishing operation. Since then it has grown to become exclusively a tuna processing operation comprising a cannery, loining and cold storage facility. The Project is to support the expansion and upgrade of SolTuna’s tuna processing plant and increase capacity from 90 metric tonnes per day currently to 150 metric tonnes per day.
sponsor_shareholders: SolTuna is majority-owned and controlled (51.5%) by Tri-Oceanic Overseas Holdings, LLC (“TOOH”), an affiliate of Tri Marine (“Tri Marine” or the “Group”), which consists of a group of 41 privately-held entities that together, comprise one of the largest global tuna supply companies in the world. The other shareholders of the Company are Solomon Islands National Provident Fund (31.4%), Investment Corporation of Solomon Islands Limited (9.3%) and Provincial Executive of the Western Province (7.8%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is expected to be approximately US$31.0 million. IFC is considering an A loan for IFC’s own account totaling up to US$10.0 million.
location_description: The Project will be located at SolTuna’s existing plant in Noro, Solomon Islands.
development_impact: (i) Capturing more value in-country. IFC''s support is expected to substantially increase the amount of tuna that is processed onshore in Solomon Islands, thereby helping the country retain greater value-add from its own tuna resources and thus further benefitting the local economy. (ii) Domestic food security. IFC''s involvement in the Project is expected to help contribute to domestic food security. (iii) Job creation. The Project is expected to help create additional jobs and skills training in the broader fisheries and fish processing supply chain. (iv) Generation of tax revenues. The Project is expected to generate additional tax revenues for the Solomon Islands government.
additionality: (i) Provision of long-term foreign currency financing. Without IFC, it is unlikely that SolTuna will be able to raise financing to complete the Project within the timeframe required and increase the Company''s processing capacity, thereby affecting the Company''s growth potential. (ii) Stamp of approval. Having IFC as an investor in the Company may increase its credibility with other regional banks who have traditionally been reluctant to participate in the agribusiness and fisheries sector. (iii) Enhanced environmental and social standards. IFC''s work with SolTuna and the Sponsor to ensure consistent outcomes with IFC''s Performance Standards on E&S Sustainability and the draft "principles of engagement" for tuna-related projects in the Pacific is expected to strengthen the Project''s E&S sustainability as well as provide reputational risk mitigation. (iv) IFC/World Bank coordination and IFC Advisory Services / Investment Services approach. The World Bank Group''s combined offering of technical assistance to government, IC/C3P/SBA advisory services for the sector and for SolTuna, and IFC investment support all come together to strengthen the sector, the Project and the Company. Potential work around standards also strengthen sustainability aspects and provide reputational risk mitigation for the Project, the Sponsor, and IFC.

sector: Fruit and Vegetable Preservation or Processing (Canning, Freezing, Drying, Jams, etc.)
project_description: The Project consists of providing up to US $2.5 million A Loan to CJSC Euroterm (“Euroterm” or the “Company”). Euroterm is the leading Armenian producer of fruit juice, concentrate and preserved food. In addition, the Company provides heating system installation services. The Company has recently expanded its capacity in fruit concentrate and tomato paste processing. Euroterm has already financed the expansion with short- term loans as a bridge financing. The proposed investment entails providing a corporate loan to Euroterm, to be utilized for refinancing part of its existing debt and for additional working capital requirements to support the Company’s growth. .
sponsor_shareholders: The main sponsor of the project is Mr.Edward Ghazaryan, a former heating engineer. He founded the Company in 1998. Currently, Mr Ghazaryan holds 95.23% of the Company’s stake and his wife Ms. Ripsime Kaukchyan has 4.77% ownership.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of US $2.5 million for IFC’s own account with 7 years maturity, including 2 years grace period.
location_description: Euroterm is headquartered in Yerevan, Armenia and has two production plants across the country. The existing production facility is located next to the major highway at the address: 5 A. Kochinyan Street, Yerevan and the new production plant is located in Armavir region of Armenia, close to the farmers supplying fruits and vegetables to the Company.
development_impact: The proposed Project has significant development impact including the following: (i) Support of the development of Armenian agriculture, a sector which is the largest employer in Armenia; (ii) It would also help promote export-oriented manufacturing, generating hard currency revenues; (iii) Job creation; (iv) Linkage to the farmers: as a result of expanded production, the Company is expected to increase the number of farmers supplying agricultural products from app. 570 to around 740. The project would have significant positive trickle down effects on farmers who can increase their sales and revenues by supplying agricultural products to Euroterm
additionality: (i) IFC will provide long-term funding to Euroterm for supporting the Company''s expansion and modernization of fixed assets; (ii) Without IFC participation the Company''s funding strategy will be confined to use of short and medium-term financing and will be less sustainable; (iii) IFC''s Food Safety Advisory Program: IFC''s Food Safety Advisory team is helping Euroterm to implement HACCP system. According to the plan, implementation should be completed by the end of 2013; (iv) IFC will also explore areas of other advisory support, such as Corporate Governance Advisory Services.

project_description: The proposed Project with Minerva S.A. (“Minerva” or “the Company”), the third largest meat processor in Brazil, will support the implementation of a regional expansion program and address the environmental and social impacts of cattle ranching in Brazil. The proposed investment consists of an A-Loan and/or Equity investment. The Company is undertaking an investment plan over the next four years to: (i) expand the processing and slaughtering operations in South America, more specifically in Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay; (ii) potentially develop a slaughtering plant in Colombia; (iii) construct, acquire and/or lease six distribution centers across Brazil; and (iv) expand the processing capacity of the Minerva Dawn Farms plant in Brazil (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Minerva is one of the largest meatpackers in Brazil with a slaughter capacity of 11,480 heads / day and the second largest beef exporter with 22% market share on Brazilian beef exports. The Company was founded by the Vilela de Queiroz family, active in the beef industry with cattle ranching and transportation since the 1950’s. Minerva was founded in 1992 in the city of Barretos, State of São Paulo and currently operates eleven slaughtering and deboning plants located across 6 Brazilian states (Sao Paulo, Mato Grosso do Sul, Minas Gerais, Goias, Tocantins and Rondonia), as well as two plants in Paraguay and one in Uruguay. It owns and operates Minerva Dawn Farms, a multiprotein processing plant. Minerva is also the largest exporter of live cattle in Brazil. Minerva is a public company with shares listed at the “Novo Mercado” at BOVESPA since 2007. In 2011, they launched ADR Level 1 traded at the NYSE. Free float ownership accounts for 65% and the remaining 35% stake is held by VDQ Holding, fully owned by the Vilela de Queiroz family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: To support the implementation of the investment program, IFC is considering providing up to US$85 million through an A Loan and/or Equity investment.
location_description: The Project entails investments in plants in Brazil (Mato Grosso), Paraguay, Uruguay and potentially in Colombia. Minerva also plans to construct, acquire and/or lease six distribution centers in Brazil, most of them in the North and Northeastern region. In addition, Minerva will expand Minerva Dawn Farms operations located in the city of Barretos, state of São Paulo, Brazil.
development_impact: (i) E&S Standards: The Project will support the implementation of an environmental and social action plan to address the environmental impacts of the cattle industry in Brazil, Colombia, Paraguay and Uruguay which if successful will result in an important demonstration effect in the sector. Minerva will put together a pilot project (with IFC's support) to enhance its traceability programs. If successful, this involvement will be a paradigm change in the region. (ii) Farmers (Ranchers) Reached: Minerva is one of the largest cattle producers, and one of the largest buyers in the region. It currently purchases approximately 1.7 million head of cattle per year from 9,000 ranchers, but with this expansion (especially into new foreign markets), Minerva expects to increase its rancher supply base by around 30%. (iii) Employment: Minerva employs approximately 10,000 full time staff. The expansion will create significant employment opportunities, expected to exceed 4,000 additional jobs in total, especially in rural areas that need non-farm economic opportunities. (iv) South-South Investment: The Project will also support the further South-South expansion of one of the most efficient companies in the sector and support the improvement of the institutional environment in Colombia and Paraguay.
additionality: (i) Sector-wide E&S Standards Setting: IFC is uniquely positioned to support Minerva in the implementation of high environmental and social standards in its supply chain. IFC has prepared and discussed a detailed E&S plan with the Company highlighting the gaps and what is needed for them to be addressed. (ii) Improve communication with stakeholders: Although Minerva is ahead of its peers in sustainability issues, it never sold it as a differential and had historically had a very low profile and reactive approach. IFC is supporting the Company in setting up a communication and civil society organizations engagement plan; (iii) Stamp of Approval: Minerva seeks IFC's stamp of approval, as it is convinced it will differentiate it from the other meatpackers operating in Brazil. (iv) Advisory Services: By supporting Minerva in establishing a pilot traceability program, IFC will help the Company to stay ahead of the curve, fully access the potential of the Hilton Beef Quota and prepare for a discussion that is expected to come. (v) South-South investments: IFC will support the company in its South-South investment plan which involves investing into riskier markets where long-term investors are reluctant to support.

project_description: Compañia Agropecuaria Copeval S.A. (“Copeval” or the “Company”) is Chile’s leading agricultural input distributor, reaching more than 30,000 farmers through its 27 branches across the country. The Company offers pre-harvest financing for the acquisition of agricultural inputs as well as up to 3-year financing for the acquisition of agricultural machinery and irrigation equipment. The Company is expanding its operations and expects to reach a total of around 30 stores by the end of 2013 throughout Chile’s main agricultural regions. The Company will also continue to expand its services and distribution of inputs to farmers and agricultural SMEs (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Copeval was established in 1956 as a cooperative and since 2003 it turned into a listed company in the Santiago Stock Exchange. Its major share holders are: Gonzalo Martino Gonzalez (23%), Ariztia Group (22%) and Hernan Bozzo (17%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Copeval’s expansion will significantly increase its operational funding needs. IFC will provide a financing facility of up to US$70 million, including a securitized bond to finance increased permanent working capital needs and support Copeval’s growth efforts and further geographical reach within Chile.
location_description: The company is headquartered in San Fernando, Chilean VI region. The Company currently has 27 stores spread all throughout Chile’s agricultural main areas which comprises from the III to the X region.
development_impact: Copeval is having a significant developmental impact by efficiently providing pre-harvest financing to farmers operating in rural areas (including recently developed agricultural regions) making a significant contribution to Chile''s rural economic development as well as to global food security. Copeval currently reaches more than 30,000 farmers through its network of stores strategically located across all Chile''s agricultural regions. Copeval''s main impacts include: (i) providing farmers with training, advisory, certifications services and technical support; and (ii) contributing to rural economic development through linkages with agricultural MSMEs, farmers, and local rural communities in the surrounding rural frontier regions where the Company operates. Copeval currently sponsors different programs that provide support to small producers, including programs for enhancing the productivity and quality of suppliers, assistance in the implementation of quality certifications, advice in feasibility studies for the implementation of irrigation services, supporting entrepreneurship and encouraging the integration of small producers to the agro-industrial chain. The training services include sessions for agricultural good practices, pesticides handling, treatment of plagues and diseases, operation and maintenance of irrigation systems and agricultural machinery. During 2012, Copeval provided assistance to about 3,900 farmers from the region of Coquimbo to Los Lagos.
additionality: IFC''s role and additionality in Copeval will be materialized thorugh: i) Providing strructured long term financing in local currency at longer terms than usually available in the local market; ii) IFC will supervise Copeval''s compliance with Environmental & Social best practices and Standards; and iii) Long term partnership to support the growth potential of a locally owned agribusienss input distribution and agricultural services provider with extensive farmers reach.

company_name: CVENTURES PRIMUS FUNDO MUTUO DE INVESTIMENTO EM EMPRESAS EMERGENTES INOVADORAS
project_description: The project consists of BRL$15 million in equity investment, not to exceed 20% of the total commitments in Cventures Primus Fund (the “Fund”), a Brazilian early stage venture fund focused on cleantech, life sciences, IT and telecom, and digital media/education technology. The Fund’s expected size is BRL$80 million. The intent is to have a maximum of 12-16 companies, initially receiving BRL$3-4 million per company with follow-on investments as growth targets are met. Key focus regions are the three southern states (Parana, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul) of Brazil where many of the research institutes, incubators and universities exist as part of a venture/seed ecosystem. The Fund will be managed by CRP Companhia de Participações (“CRP”) with Cventures Innovative Enterprises and Holdings (“Cventures”) acting as a special advisor assisting pipeline development, deal execution, portfolio monitoring and exits.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund is sponsored by CRP as the General Partner and Cventures as the special consultant/advisor. Fund management duties will be shared between the two organizations. This arrangement combines a source of deal flow and early stage tech-based companies incubation (Cventures) with proven early stage investment execution, growth and exit experience (CRP). Further, the link to CRP leverages CRP’s existing investment monitoring practices. Formed in 1981, CRP is Brazil’s oldest and most established venture capital firm and operates from Porto Alegre, Brazil. CRP has raised eight funds totaling $320 million (BRL$460 million) and has invested in 68 companies, of which 43 have been exited. Cventures brings over 25 years of experience in supporting tech-based companies, developing innovation and entrepreneurship projects, accelerating innovative technologies and helping more than 70 companies to succeed. Cventures was founded by CERTI, a research foundation in Brazil that was originally the technology transfer center for the University of Santa Catarina, but today has grown to include specialized research, incubation centers and science parks in Brazil. The team currently consists of five key persons that bring complementary skills: Clovis Meurer, Jose Eduardo Fiates, Dalton Schmitt Jr., Felipe Marcondes de Mattos and Gabriela de Salles. While this is the first time the two entities will work together as a fund management operation, CRP and Cventures personnel have worked together in the past. Carry and management fees will be split between Cventures and CRP to reflect the expected time and resource commitment of each entity. Following the first closing, Cventures will recruit an additional staff to be located in the Cventures Florianopolis office.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost and size of the Fund is expected to be BRL$80 million. The proposed IFC investment is an equity commitment of BRL$15 million, not to exceed 20% of total fund equity commitments.
location_description: Domiciled as a Brazilian on-shore structure, the Fund will be governed by Brazilian CVM Rule 209 as a Mutual Investment Fund in Emerging Companies. The Fund will pursue investments across Brazil, but expected to focus on innovative opportunities in southern regions of Brazil. Both CRP and Cventures are local teams and have strong deal sourcing capability and networks across Brazil. CRP is headquartered in Porto Alegre while Cventures is based in Florianopolis, Brazil.
development_impact: (i) Private sector development: The Fund will provide equity capital to help promote growth and improve revenue and profitability of the Fund's SME investees, and help support the venture capital industry in Brazil. (ii) Economic sustainability: demonstrated through the Fund's ability to help its investees grow sustainably and generate employment growth faster than the national average. Cventures Ecosystem today has created thousands of jobs, a significant number of which are skilled jobs; (iii) Financial success: evidenced by the Fund's investment return (net IRR). (iv) Narrowing the gap of funding for early-stage companies: Despite the existence of innovative technologies, well established research centers/incubators and young companies in Brazil, there exists a gap in funding for early-stage companies in Brazil. There are limited venture investors for IT/telecom and internet in Brazil, and beyond that sector there is a dearth of venture capital funds. Demonstrating that investments in early-stage companies in cleantech, biotech, education tech/digital media sectors is profitable should lead to increased inflow of much needed private capital for these sectors in Brazil. (v) Reduction of CO2 and other GHGs: The Fund is expected to invest a portion of its investments in clean technology companies, thus contributing to a reduction in carbon emissions.
additionality: IFC's participation in the Fund and its governance committees will create the following additionalities: -- Catalytic role: as a multi-sector early stage venture fund, the Fund may have difficulties raising sufficient capital. IFC's investment will enable the Fund to achieve its target size. More generally, an IFC investment in a venture/early stage fund in Brazil will catalyze more international limited partners to investigate opportunities for venture/early stage investments in Brazil. -- Provide unique IFC resources and experience: IFC's global experience and regional presence creates specific advantages: (i) governance leadership --Cventures seeks IFC's leadership with market standard practices for investment and advisory committees, which is key in Brazil where investment committees have LP presence; (ii) additional financing source --IFC's presence as a potential co-investment partner will be critical for new investees as well as when the investees grow and need access to additional growth funding; and (iii) regional and technical expertise --IFC's deep and broad experience in the Fund's sectors and target markets will help refine the Fund Manager's outlook, which is particularly important in a first time fund manager. -- E&S best practice guidance: IFC will require and guide the Fund Manager in developing a robust E&S management system. -- Stamp of approval for future fund raising: With IFC's investment, the Cventures team will have a stronger platform to raise international LP capital on this Fund or future funds.
Company Name: CVENTURES PRIMUS FUNDO MUTUO DE INVESTIMENTO EM EMPRESAS EMERGENTES INOVADORAS

project_description: Consorcio Naviero Nicaraguense SA (“Navinic” or the “Company”) owns the smallest of four sugar mills in Nicaragua (Montelimar mill), with a milling capacity of 2,300 tons of sugar cane per day (“tcd”). The project involves an increase in the Company’s sugar annual production from 33kton to 67kton and includes: i) the acquisition of 1,628 ha of land to increase own planted area to 5,262 ha, ii) investment in irrigation and other infrastructure in the field, iii) increasing milling capacity to 4,100 tcd, iv) acquiring additional harvesting and transportation equipment and v) funding incremental working capital needs (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Navinic’s majority shareholders and Project sponsors are the Fernandez Holmann and Morales families.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at US$38 million. The proposed financing is a US$15 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Company and Project are located in San Rafael del Sur, 62 Km away from Managua, Nicaragua.
development_impact: - Support Nicaragua''s economic growth and employment generation, in particular in poor rural areas, by increasing exports of locally sourced product. - The Company will support vulnerable families in the process of titling their land. - The Project will contribute to financial transparency since the Company will hire an auditing firm satisfactory to IFC. - The Project will increase employment in the rural area of an IDA country by an estimated 1,300 new jobs.
additionality: IFC''s participation will provide clear expected additionality given (i) the extensive guidance by the IFC environmental and social team in the preparation of the Company''s E&S documents and plans to enhance its practices, including those linked to land tenure issues, (ii) the enhancement of the Company''s finance and reporting functions, (iii) the potential mitigation of political and regulatory risks and (iv) IFC''s regional and global expertise in the sugar industry.

project_description: Faber Industrie S.p.A.(Faber) of Italy, a leader in the production of seamless steel and composite cylinders for the storage of high-pressure gases, has established Chalybs Cylinders Ltd. to build a plant in the Eastern Seaboard Industrial Estate, to manufacture seamless gas cylinders (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1972, Faber has grown to become the leader in the production of seamless steel and composite gas cylinders for medical and industrial applications (oxygen, nitrogen, and hydrogen tanks), leisure (scuba diving), and compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles. Faber is known for its high quality standards and capability to comply with the most stringent specifications. Faber has four plants located in Italy with a production capacity of one million cylinders per year.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at EUR50 million. IFC has been requested to provide a loan of up to EUR20 million for its own account.
location_description: The Project is located in the Eastern Seaboard Industrial Estate, Thailand.
development_impact: Technology transfer: As a leading producer of seamless cylinders for the storage of high-pressure gases, Faber uses state-of-the-art technologies and efficient processes, which will be installed in Thailand. Local staff will be trained to a new, highly competitive standard in manufacturing processes and management. While most gas tanks are made with welded cylinders, Faber produces seamless cylinders using precision technology that empties out a steel profile into a shell and seals it into a tank shape. Faber has developed its own safety control processes. Climate change: Compared with traditional vehicles, compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles provide for reductions in carbon monoxide emissions of 90% to 97%, and in carbon dioxide emissions of about 20%. Other environmental benefits: Combustion of natural gas rather than gasoline in vehicles results in reduced emissions of toxic and carcinogenic compounds and virtually eliminates particulate emissions. Import substitution/improved access to CNG vehicles: Currently automotive plants in Thailand import high-quality, seamless cylinder parts that are not locally available. The Project''s production will lead to import substitution and contribute to the country''s economic growth. Improved access to CNG vehicles will translate into higher incomes for micro, small and medium enterprises and taxi operators, based on lower operating cost of CNG vehicles, which will contribute to inclusive growth. Job creation: The Project is expected to create direct and indirect jobs in Thailand.
additionality: Risk mitigation/long-term partnership: The Project is one of the first significant investments in emerging markets for Faber, a family-owned company. Faber expects to benefit from IFC''s experience in Thailand, and, more broadly, in emerging markets. IFC is well-positioned to support Faber globally as it expands into other emerging markets. Counter cyclical role: The availability of long-term financing for mid-size European companies, especially for greenfield projects in the emerging markets, is constrained due to the crisis in Europe, and pending new capitalization rules for banks. Demonstration effect: The Project will demonstrate a strong momentum and growth potential of the CNG vehicle market. The Project will also promote the recovery from the flood in Thailand and send a positive signal to the market. Facilitate technological transfer: IFC is to help Faber transfer innovative technology new to middle income countries to help them keep up with global value chains.

company_name: PROCESADORA NACIONAL DE ALIMENTOS C.A. PRONACA
project_description: The proposed project entails providing a corporate facility to finance the expansion of Procesadora Nacional de Alimentos C.A. – PRONACA (“Pronaca” or the “Company”), a vertically integrated poultry and pork processor and one of Ecuador’s leading agro-industrial companies. The Company initiated its operations in 1958 and today it produces and commercializes meats (poultry, pork, and turkey), value added foods, rice and eggs, as well as animal feed and pet foods. The proposed facility will help the Company finance its growth both domestically and abroad.
sponsor_shareholders: Pronaca is a private company, owned by the Klein (41%), Bakker (41%), Ribadeneira (9%), and Gerritsen (8%) families, along with some other individual local investors (1%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is a corporate facility, which entails providing an A loan for IFC’s own account of up to US$70 million to finance Pronaca’s expansion in Ecuador and abroad.
location_description: The Company’s poultry processing plants are located in Quito, Bucay and Valle Hermoso. The Company also has a pork processing facility in Valle Hermoso, next to its poultry processing plant in Santo Domingo de los Colorados. Pronaca’s distribution facilities are located in or around Ecuador’s main urban centers, primarily Guayaquil and Quito. The Company’s feed mills are located in Puembo, Durán, and Quevedo. All the above facilities are located on or have good access to the main road. Farms and hatcheries are located in semi-rural areas for bio-security reasons. Pork and broiler farms are located near Santo Domingo de los Colorados. Additional broiler farms are located near Bucay and in the outskirts of Quito.
development_impact: (i) Farmers reach: Pronaca supports the activities of about 3,000 farmers. As an input to its operations, Pronaca buys about 40 percent of the country''s corn production. It also works together with the Government under an initiative called "Inclusive Business Program", a program that supports small farmers in increasing land productivity by providing technical assistance and financing for the purchase of certified seeds and inputs. It also ensures the purchase of their products (guaranteed volume and prices) via purchase agreements (849 farmers under this program). (ii) MSME development: Currently, Pronaca purchases about US$340 million from domestic suppliers, out of which over 90 percent are considered MSMEs. In addition, the Company supplies over 65,000 small retailers across the country with its products, thus supporting a vast supply chain, which is mostly composed of MSMEs. (iii) Downstream reach: Pronaca serves over 75,000 clients across the country directly and indirectly, through 43 exclusive distributors. By supporting Pronaca''s growth, the Project will generate business downstream. (iv) E&S best practices: Pronaca places high value on conducting its business in a sustainable manner and follows IFC''s best practices in E&S matters, being an example to the sector players in Ecuador.
additionality: (i) Long-term funding is not easily available in Ecuador and local private sector companies struggle to access financing on competitive terms. IFC''s proposed 8-year corporate facility will provide highly valuable support to Pronaca at times of constrained liquidity and volatile global conditions. (ii) Long-term Partnership: IFC has worked with Pronaca since 2004, establishing a very productive relationship, which has helped the Company grow and improve on various fronts, including operational excellence (efficiencies of its livestock and feed operations), Environmental and Social ("E&S") practices and focus on the supply chain. (iii) Environmental and Social Standards: IFC continues to support Pronaca''s efforts to further improve its environmental and social standards. IFC and Pronaca have been working closely since 2004 on a number of initiatives that go beyond environmental compliance to provide sustainable value to the Company''s business and a more cost-efficient use of resources.
Company Name: PROCESADORA NACIONAL DE ALIMENTOS C.A. PRONACA

project_description: PT Panca Amara Utama (“PAU” or the ”Company”) is a private limited company that plans to set up a 2,000 metric tonnes per day greenfield ammonia production plant (the “Project”). The gas will be sourced from the Senoro-Toili gas fields in Central Sulawesi province of Indonesia. Key associated infrastructure for this project includes a pipeline to transport the gas to the plant and a jetty to supply the ammonia to buyers.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is 60% owned by PT Surya Esa Perkasa Tbk. (“SEP”), a company that is listed on the Indonesian stock exchange. Mr. Theodore Rachmat, Mr. Garibaldi Thohir and Mr. Vinod Laroya (through their shareholding in SEP) and SEP are the key Sponsors of this Project.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost has been estimated to be US$750 million and will be financed by up to US$500 million of senior debt and US$250 million of equity. IFC is expected to invest up to US$125 million in the form of debt and equity, to finance part of the Project. In addition to the above investment, IFC plans to mobilize up to US$400 million of senior debt from other banks.
location_description: The Project is located at Jl. Poros Sulawesi, Uso Village, Batui District, Banggai, Central Sulawesi 94762, in Sulawesi island of Indonesia. It is approximately 40 km away from the nearest airport which is at Luwuk – the Capital of Banggai Regency.
development_impact: 1) Enhancement of food security: The project will introduce a new supplier of a critical nutrient that is essential for improving farm productivity. This is expected to improve the supply in the regional ammonia market and therefore directly and/or indirectly help address the increasing challenges of affordable and sufficient food supply. 2) Local Value Addition and Creation of Export Revenues: The proposed project would contribute towards value addition taking place within Indonesia and create significant export revenues for Indonesia. 3) Job Creation and Community Development: The Project will create quality employment opportunities in the Central Sulawesi province of Indonesia. The Project is expected to create about 350 direct jobs during operation and 2,000 indirect jobs. Indirect jobs are expected to arise from opportunities created for local contractors engaged in regular maintenance and repair activities for the Project, transportation, food supply and other activities associated with the Project. In addition, the Company will provide social infrastructure and professional training to its personnel. 4) SME Development Impact: Chemical and petrochemical projects typically create a large number of downstream jobs and entrepreneurial opportunities in segments such as trading, logistics and transportation. The proposed Project is expected to have a significant multiplier effect through the creation and growth of supporting SME businesses.
additionality: 1) Long Term Financing: Ammonia plants are capital intensive and the sector is cyclical and therefore needs appropriately structured long-term financing to be sustainable. IFC will provide funding with tenors longer than those currently available in the local market. 2) Mobilization: In addition to a direct investment, IFC will syndicate about US$400 million for the Project. IFC''s participation will attract and provide comfort to other investors at a time when other global and local banks have reduced lending due to the continuing shortage of long term liquidity in foreign currency. 3) Sharing Industry Knowledge: IFC has extensive global experience in project finance of large complex green-field plants in the chemical sector. IFC will share this experience/ expertise with the Company; in particular ways to manage risks related to Project execution. IFC will also share this knowledge and expertise with the syndicate banks, which is expected to give them additional comfort on the Project structure. 4) Environment and Social (E&S) Guidance: IFC would help the Company to: (i) develop its environmental and social management systems and capacity; (ii) address the Project''s substantial E&S challenges due to its size and complexity; (iii) develop comprehensive E &S assessment documentation and ensure compliance of the project with IFC''s Performance Standards and (iv) share IFC''s global experience/best practices dealing with community related issues.

project_description: Axzon (the “Company” or “Group”) is a leading pig farming and meat processing group in Poland and Ukraine. The Group currently has more than 30 pig production farms in Northwestern Poland and around 10 in Western Ukraine, a slaughtering and meat processing facility in Poland and a smaller specialty slaughtering facility in Denmark. The Group also operates 8 biogas plants in Poland, and one in Ukraine as well as 10.000 hectares of farming land in Ukraine and 13.000 hectares of farming land in Poland. The proposed project is to expand the Company’s operations in Ukraine (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsor is Polen Invest A/S, a 99.76% shareholder of Axzon. Polen Invest A/S is a Danish holding company owned by 90 individual Danish pig farmers and their families.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at EUR133 million. IFC is considering an investment up to EUR54 million in the combination of an A Loan and equity. The balance of the Project will be financed with parallel loans and internal cash generation.
location_description: Axzon’s operations are located in the Ivano-Frankivsk region of western Ukraine. The Project would support the Group’s operations in the region and expand the Group’s operations across Ukraine.
development_impact: The development impact of the Project is expected to (i) support an efficient producer with a solid track record to expand EU standards of livestock production, showcase biogas plants, energy efficiency, clean production, and animal welfare to new farms in Ukraine; (ii) contribute to the modernization of the under-developed pork sector in Ukraine; (iii) support frontier regions in Ukraine by developing creating jobs in rural areas, and contributing to local community; and (iv) contribute to regional and global food security by expanding primary production of crops and animal proteins.
additionality: IFC is uniquely able to (i) provide stamp of approval that could enhance the Company''s value and future marketability; (ii) provide long term financing otherwise not available in Ukraine; (iii) share IFC''s global and regional livestock investment experience with the Company; (iv) help improve corporate governance, corporate social responsibility and E&S management and enforcement systems; and (v) offer needed risk capital to strengthen the Company''s equity base.

project_description: Country Bird Holdings Limited (CBH) is an agricultural group comprising (i) integrated poultry and stock feed operations in South Africa trading as Supreme Poultry and Nutri Feeds; (ii) poultry breeding, broiler and stock feed operations in the southern African region trading as Ross Africa and Master Farmer; and (iii) South African retail and distribution operations trading as Long Iron Meats, Supreme Distributors and Ama Chick Chick. CBH currently operates in Botswana, the DRC, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe. The Project entails: (i) increasing DOC production in Zambia & Botswana; (ii) expansion of the Zambia feedmill capacity; (iii) increase broiler meat processing capacity in South Africa; and (iv) construct soya bean deactivation plants at two of its feedmills.
sponsor_shareholders: CBH was established in 2003 and listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in 2007. Currently, the Company’s market capitalization is approximately US$90.1 million. The major shareholder is Synapp International Limited (“Synapp”), a family owned investment company led by Kevin James, an executive director with the Company. The family holds 81.9% shareholding. CBH currently has over 900 minority shareholders including institutional and individual shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$42.4 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$25m convertible loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: CBH has existing operations in Lusaka, Zambia; Gaborone & Francistown in Botswana; and in the North West Province of South Africa. The proposed projects will be based on its owned facilities at these operations.
development_impact: The project''s expected development impact includes: (i) higher efficiency, quality and best practise bio-security standards transfer by a leading regional poultry player in the region; (ii) SME development through increased outgrowers and distributor network; (iii) supply chain development through investments in agro allied businesses; (iv) creation of additional direct and indirect jobs; (v) improved food security in the investment countries; and (vi) increased tax revenues to Governments
additionality: IFC additionality will encompass: (i) IFC''s technical expertise, global knowledge of the industry and markets, as well as lessons learned from other integrated poultry projects are a valuable resource to the Company; (ii) IFC will further support the Company''s long-term regional project scope with tailor-made financing mix of debt & equity; (iii) IFC will assist CBH with resource efficiency management program

project_description: The project (the Project) involves the clinker production capacity expansion of UltraTech Cement Limited (UltraTech or the Company) at its integrated cement plant in Chhattisgarh, a low-income state in the eastern part of India and the investments for the necessary infrastructure to support the expansion. The Project is a key component of the Company’s cement capacity expansion strategy in the eastern part of India.
sponsor_shareholders: UltraTech is a part of Aditya Birla Group (ABG) – one of India’s largest and most reputable conglomerates and a long-standing client of IFC in Egypt, India, Thailand and Indonesia. ABG operates in 33 countries with more than 133,000 employees worldwide. The group has diversified business interests in viscose staple fiber, metals, cement, viscose filament yarn, branded apparel, carbon black, chemicals, fertilizers, insulators, financial services, telecom, BPO and IT services. Grasim Industries Limited of the Aditya Birla Group has a 60.3% stake in UltraTech. UltraTech, a listed company, has 12 integrated cement manufacturing plants, 15 grinding units, 5 bulk terminals and more than 100 ready mix concrete plants, spanning India, UAE, Bahrain, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka with 52 million tons per annum (Mtpa) capacity.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$297 million. IFC has been requested to provide a loan of up to US$100 million for its own account.
location_description: The integrated plant is located near Rawan village, Tehsil Sigma in Chhattisgarh.
development_impact: Employment generation: The Project will create direct and indirect employment in Chhattisgarh. The Project will provide skilled and unskilled jobs during the construction phase. In addition, the Project will create a large number of indirect jobs in the transportation and delivery sectors. Increased local supply chain and consumption of local goods and services: The Project will create new business opportunities in the local economy due to increased demand for the supply of raw materials and provision of transportation and delivery services Other benefits to local communities: The Company has established health and medical facilities in India to benefit about 200,000 people and manages schools in India where more than 6,500 students attend. The local communities will benefit from the Company''s corporate social responsibility initiatives. Positive climate change impact: As a member of the Cement Sustainability Initiative (CSI) of the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD), a global association of about 200 companies dealing exclusively with business and sustainable development, UltraTech is committed to sustainable development. Its investment in energy efficient initiatives has resulted in specific heat consumption in its clinker production being one of the lowest. The Company has taken the lead in the cement sector in India to co-process industrial and agricultural wastes as fossil fuel substitutes in its plants. The Company is among the early proponents of waste heat recovery and alternative fuel usage in cement operations in India. The Project includes a waste heat recovery system, which will reduce energy usage. Higher level of environmental and social performance: By complying with IFC''s performance standards and the World Bank Group''s environmental, health, and safety (EHS) guidelines, UltraTech will achieve higher environmental and social standards, which should increase its reputation, reduce the risk of adverse impacts on local communities, and increase the credibility of the private sector with respect to corporate social responsibility. Private sector development: The success of the Project will send a positive signal to other investors considering investments in Chhattisgarh, a low-income state where foreign direct investment (FDI) is limited. The Project is expected to set environmental and social standards that can be replicated by other cement producers. Increase in domestic revenues: The Project is expected to contribute to the domestic economy through increased tax revenues.
additionality: Long-term partnership: UltraTech is keen to develop a strong relationship with IFC as the Company has begun implementing its overseas expansion strategy. The Company wants to select IFC as its long-term strategic partner as it values IFC''s long-term financing, which is suited to the capital intensity and cyclicality of the cement industry, to support projects in emerging markets, including fragile and conflict-affected countries. Environmental and social standards/implementation and various advisory services: As a member of the Cement Sustainability Initiative (CSI), a voluntary CEO-led global program initiated by leading cement companies in 1999, and operating under the auspices of the WBCSD, UltraTech has integrated sustainable development into its business strategies and operations, as it seeks strong financial performance with an equally strong commitment to social and environmental responsibility. The Company has co-chaired CSI''s Low Carbon Technology Roadmap for Indian Cement Industry, a carbon emissions reduction initiative in India, supported by IFC. The Company is among the early proponents of waste heat recovery and alternative fuel usage in cement operations in India. In this context, UltraTech''s management wants to further reduce its carbon footprint and to adopt best practice standards for environmental and social aspects while the Company already has high standards. The management believes that IFC can play a significant role in helping the Company achieve these goals. IFC has already begun working with UltraTech to identify resource efficiency opportunities for the Company to further reduce its carbon footprint. In addition, IFC is exploring the possibility of providing UltraTech with various advisory services in such areas as alternative fuel usage as well as corporate social responsibility initiatives.

project_description: The Project consists of providing an up to US$13M revolving loan facility for the development of mostly affordable housing projects in Georgia sponsored by SB Real Estate (“SBRE”, the “Company” or the “Borrower”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bank of Georgia (“BoG” or the “Bank”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Borrower: SB Real Estate is a wholly owned subsidiary of BoG. The Company business model is to develop residential projects for outright sale. Current project portfolio comprise mainly of a mix of affordable housing units, middle income units and commercial real estate. SBRE already implemented its first affordable housing project on Chubinashvili Street, Tbilisi, Georgia and the second project is currently under construction in Tamarashvili Street. The Sponsor: BoG is 100% ultimate shareholder of SBRE. It was established in 1994 in Georgia. BoG is the largest among 19 Georgian banks in terms of total assets, equity and net income. The Bank is the only Georgian bank with a premium listing on the London Stock Exchange (“LSE”) through the UK incorporated Holding Company. Its rating from agencies: ‘BB-/B’ from Standard & Poor’s, ‘B1/NP’ (FC) & ‘Ba3/NP’ (LC) from Moody’s and ‘BB-/B’ from Fitch Ratings.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The US$13M Corporate loan will be in the form of a revolving facility designed to meet the working capital requirements of the Company. The IFC investment will be complemented by a co-investment from the Canada Climate Change Program (CCCP) where IFC acts as implementing entity for CCCP to support climate change friendly projects.
location_description: The Project will involve the construction during the life of the IFC Corporate Loan of new affordable housing projects across the city of Tbilisi, Georgia.
development_impact: Development Impact include: (i) addressing the housing deficit; (ii) Job creation; (iii) enhanced local supply linkages; (iv) community development; (v) support an emerging company with excellent sponsorship and management team; (vi) demonstration effect to mobilize more funding into this much needed sector.
additionality: (i) Standard Setting in energy efficiency and environmental management; (ii) transfer of experience in affordable housing: (iii) appropriate financial structure; with a revolving line,: (iv) complementing governmental efforts to promote the development of new low- to-middle income housing units;

project_description: Jiangxi Tianren Ecology Co., Ltd (“TianRen” or the “Company”) is one of the leading fungus based pesticides producer in China, located in the south of Jiangxi Province. TianRen has been engaging in the research and development, production, sales and technical service for a variety of fungal pesticides products since 2002. Beauveria bassiana (“Bb”) and Metarhizium anisopliae (“Ma”) are the major products of Tianren. Currently TianRen has an annual capacity of 1,800 tons Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API ) and is working on expanding its fungal pesticides capacity by another 1,800 tons per annum (“tpa”) to build up a larger supply base and strengthen its service capacity both in the air and on the land during 2012 – 2014 (the “project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company and its Shareholding Structure: TianRen was founded by Mr. Liang Xiaowen in 2002. Currently the controlling shareholder of TianRen is Mr. Liang Xiaowen and its key management. The remaining shares are mainly held by Blue Ridge China and its affiliated funds; China Science and Merchants Capital Management Limited (CSM) and its affiliated funds; Kleiner Perkins Caufield Byers China Partners, L. P. (KPCB) and its affiliated funds; and Shanghai Saijie Investment Partnership.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is about US$60 million. IFC is considering providing up to US$28.5 million financing.
location_description: The Project is located in the center of a 1,270 ha industrial park in JiAn, Jianxi Province and there are no communities nearby. The Project expansion will be located within the Company’s existing property.
development_impact: i) Crop protection and strengthen supply: IFC''s finance to the Project is expected to help securing supply of bio-pesticides to agricultural users with consideration on environment and health; ii) Forest protection: IFC''s support is expected to help the Company to supply more products and provide needed spray service for forest protection; iii) Job creation in frontier region in China: The Project will create more than a hundred of new job position in JiAn, Jiangxi Province, a frontier region in China.
additionality: i) Global knowledge: IFC''s global knowledge in related areas will help TianRen to gain global vision and valuable insights on the industry. ii) E&S standard: IFC can contribute to TianRen''s operation and management with its advanced environmental and social standard. iii) A variety of financial menus: IFC provides a broad range of financing products including equity and debt to support the Project.

project_description: As one the largest piglet feed companies in China, Anyou (China) Research of Animal Nutrition Company Limited (“Anyou” or the “Company”) plans to build more animal feed facilities in China to meet its expanding market demand.
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Taicang City, Jiangsu province, Anyou has operations in more than 20 provinces across China. The Project Sponsor is Mr. HUNG Ping, the founder and Chairman of the Company. The current shareholding structure of the Company is: (i)Mr. HUNG Ping 73%; (ii) Mr. CHEN Zuobang 21%; (iii) Mr. SU Wufeng 6%;
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated to be US$83.6 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$35 million financing package including debt and equity investment for IFC’s own account.
