location_description: The Project will be located at Sichuan, Hebei, Henan, Jilin, Liaoning, Hunan, Shaanxi, Shandong and Jiangsu Province.
development_impact: The Project is expected to: (i) support the sustainable economic development and reach more than 25,000 MSMEs in the frontier regions in China; (ii) create more than 500 direct jobs and improve local livelihoods in rural/frontier Chinese provinces; and (iii) have a strong demonstration effect in Chinese animal raising sector
additionality: 1. Long-term partnership. IFC can provide the long term debt financing to support the Company''s animal feed operation and its expansion strategy. 2. Risk mitigate: IFC''s equity financing can play important stamp of approval role and strengthen capital market confidence in the Company''s initiative in expanding its animal feed operation. 3. Standard setting: IFC will continue to help Anyou to improve its capacity in environment and social management systems. 4. Global sector knowledge: IFC can keep introducing international recognized standards and provide technical support for the Company to further improve its animal value chain development.

company_name: Norson Holding, S. de R.L. de C.V.
project_description: The project will expand and upgrade pork growing operations of Norson Holdings S. de R.L. de C.V. (“Norson” or the “Company”), one of the leading integrated pork producers and processors in Mexico. The project includes: (i) modernizing Norson’s swine farms; (ii) increasing nursery capacity; (iii) expanding cold storage capacity; (iv) increasing slaughter, processing and value added capacity; (v) continue with the implementation of its sustainability program, including installing plastic liners and covers in the existing waste lagoons for methane capture; and (vi) refinancing of the existing debt.
sponsor_shareholders: Norson is a joint-venture between Grupo Mazon and Smithfield Foods Inc. Grupo Mazon is a Mexican business group based in Hermosillo, Sonora. It has interests in industrial parks, retail, tourism, agribusiness, housing and cable television. Smithfield Foods Inc. is the world’s largest pork producer and processor headquartered in Virginia. Smithfield runs facilities in 26 states of the United States and has operations in China, France, Mexico, Poland, Romania, Spain and the United Kingdom.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$180 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an approximately US$40 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project’s capital investments will be made at Norson’s production facilities located in the state of Sonora, Mexico, primarily in and around the city of Hermosillo. All project sites have the necessary utilities, road access and permits.
development_impact: (i) Streamlining and debottlenecking of pork production which will improve biosecurity, animal welfare and result in improved efficiency. (ii) The project will contribute to the reduction GHG emissions through the installation of methane capture and combustion equipment. (iii) Norson currently employs about 2,000 people with a high level of female employment. The expansion will create significant direct and indirect employment opportunities, especially in rural areas that need non-farm economic opportunities.
additionality: (i) Long-term financing: IFC will provide tailor-made long term financing which is not available in the local market as banks are reluctant to provide long-term funds to pork growing operations. (ii) Stamp of approval: IFC''s involvement is expected to provide the stamp of approval required by the Company to access local sources of financing in the future. (iii) IFC''s technical advisory. IFC''s advisory services team in energy efficiency/cleaner production is expected to engage with the Company to evaluate opportunities in: (a)methane capture and combustion into energy generation; and (b) heat recovery from refrigeration process; and (c) solar energy. (iv) E&S standards setting: IFC will support Norson in the improvement of environmental and social standards in its supply chain.
Company Name: Norson Holding, S. de R.L. de C.V.

project_description: Project Description: Muyuan Foodstuff Co., Ltd. (“Muyuan Foodstuff”) is a pig breeder and hog producer located in China. IFC’s proposed loan investment of $20M will primarily support the development of a Project of the Company to allow for annual production of 300,000 hogs. Upon completion, this Project would expand further Muyuan Foodstuff’s hog production.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is privately held.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be RMB300 million (approx. US$48 million equivalent). IFC is considering to provide a senior debt to Wolong Muyuan Breeding Co., Ltd. (“Wolong Muyuan”, a subsidiary of Muyuan Foodstuff) in an amount of up to US$20 million on its own account.
location_description: The Project is located in Wolong County, Henan Province, China.
development_impact: mployment: The Company''s operations are located in Province - a frontier region in China. It provides stable employment opportunities for thousands, including female employees. Farmers reached: Currently, a significant number of rural households supply the Company with raw materials such as corn, barley and silage. SMEs reached: Company sells its breeds to rural pig farms for further fattening for sale to market. Food Safety: The Chinese hog sector is still very fragmented, leading to poor hygiene standards, inadequate bio-security, poor nutrition, and over-use of antibiotics. By creating a larger enterprise with greater focus on efficiency and food safety, the Company supports the improvement of breeding techniques, quality standards as well as the production efficiency of the industry.
additionality: Long-term partner: Muyuan Foodstuff is keen to attract financing from credible/knowledgeable partners such as IFC who have a long-term investment horizon and can add value to the operations through our industry knowledge and enable the Company implement a properly designed strategic plan. Credibility and Positioning: Muyuan Foodstuff expects the signaling from IFC''s direct investment will enhance its reputation with investors and other partners. Adoption of Best-Practice Operational Standards: By supporting the deployment of environmentally friendly, energy-efficient pig farms yielding quality pigs, Muyuan Foodstuff can have a positive, visible demonstration effect for improving the operational management standards in the Chinese pig industry.

sector: Soap and Cleaning Compound (Soap, Detergent, etc.)
project_description: The proposed investment is to support the Wings Group of Nigeria (“Wings” or the “Group”) with the development of a greenfield detergent manufacturing facility in Nigeria (“the Project”). In addition, the Group is also planning to develop a greenfield food manufacturing facility (“Food Facility”) in Nigeria. Both the Project and the Food Facility will be owned majority by the Wings Groups. The Wings Group is headquartered in Indonesia where it has various operations and the Group commissioned its first powder detergent facility in Nigeria in September 2007. This facility is located at Igbessa in the OPIC Industrial Estate situated in Ogun State some 40 kilometers from central Lagos. The Project is being constructed on an adjacent 3.6 hectare site and is expected to be commissioned in August 2013. The Group is still in the preliminary stages of designing the Food Facility with limited information on the project currently available. However, Wings has extensive experience in such operations in Indonesia and is assessing various possible locations for this facility.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor and majority shareholder is the Wings Group. The Wings Group is a privately held Company, owned by two Indonesian families, Katuari and Sutanto. The Group is one of IFC’s key strategic clients in East Asia Pacific Region. IFC has provided financing for the consumer products, agribusiness and chemical investments of the Wings Group, with over 7 investments since 1997.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost for the Project and the Food Facility US$59.8 million of which the proposed IFC investment is through an A Loan of US $29.9 million.
location_description: The detergent project will be located at Igbessa, Ogun State about 40 kilometers out of Nigeria’s commercial capital – Lagos. The Food Facility project will be located at site to be identified in Nigeria.
development_impact: Expected development impacts are (i) increasing the supply of quality and affordable detergents in Nigeria, (ii) enhancing food safety and quality standards, (iii) transfer of skills, knowledge and industry best practices from an established group into Nigeria and (iv) creation of 1200 new jobs in Nigeria.
additionality: IFC Role and Additionality are (i) supporting South-South investments by financing the Company''s foray into Nigeria, (ii) providing continued support to a long standing IFC client and (iii) advice on environmental, health and safety aspects.

project_description: The Wings Group (or the “Sponsor”) is undertaking a US$176 million project (i) to expand its beverage product lines under PT Tirta Alam Segar (PT TAS), (ii) to expand fruit flavored beverage in plastic cups under PT Murni Alam Segar (PT MAS), (iii) to commission a greenfield coffee mix production under PT Harum Alam Segar (PT HAS), and (iv) to increase the capacity of existing detergent business under PT Sayap Mas Utama (PT SMU).
sponsor_shareholders: The Wings Group is a privately held Company, owned by two Indonesian families, Katuari and Sutanto. The Group is one of IFC’s key strategic clients in East Asia Pacific Region. IFC has provided financing for the consumer products, agribusiness and chemical investments of the Wings Group, with over 7 investments since 1997.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$176 million. The proposed IFC financing is a loan package of up to US$88 million: US$44 million A Loan on its own account and US$44 million of syndicated B loan.
location_description: PT Tirta Alam Segar is located in Jakarta, Indonesia. PT Murni Alam Segar is located in Surabaya, Indonesia. PT Harum Alam Segar is located in Surabaya, Indonesia. PT Sayap Mas Utama is located in Jakarta, Indonesia.
development_impact: Expected development impacts are (i) demonstration effect of the Wings Group''s strong attention to food safety and quality standards to other producers, (ii) providing quality products to people at the Bottom of Pyramid (BoP), (iii) increased value addition in the local economy through the coffee project and (iv) higher reach to MSME through Wings'' extensive distribution network (iv) creation of additional 2,100 jobs.
additionality: IFC Role and Additionality are (i) providing continued support to a long standing IFC client in its reach to consumers at the BoP, (ii) mobilizing capital for the expansion in Indonesia through the proposed B loan, (iii) standard-setting through requirement and recommendation to use one of the big-four audit firms and certification on food safety, and (iv) providing IFC''s support to the Wings Group south-south project in Nigeria as the proposed IFC financing for the Indonesian project is being considered as a combined financing with another project in Nigeria with the Wings Group (Project# 32209).

project_description: As part of IFC’s Critical Commodities Finance Program Phase II (“CCFP II”), IFC is proposing the following project: 1) an expansion of the funded risk-sharing facility (“CCFP SocGen”, Project No. 34955) with Société Générale SA (“SocGen”or “the Bank”); 2) an extension of the maturity of the facility from March 2014 to January 2015. The US$150 million increase would supplement IFC’s existing US$250 million investment in the facility, bringing up IFC’s total participation up to US$400 million in SocGen’s trade and commodity finance portfolio of the critical agriculture and energy commodities/inputs. CCFP program is a public-private partnership (“PPP”) initiative that is part of IFC’s multi-faceted rapid global financial crisis response. It is aiming at mitigating disruptions in two critical commodity value chains: (i) exports and imports of agricultural commodities and inputs globally; and (ii) imports of energy products into IDA or IDA- blend countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1864, Société Générale (the “Bank”) is one of the largest banks in France and in the Eurozone. Its three main divisions are Retail Banking & Specialized Financial Services, Corporate and Investment Banking and Global Investment Management & Services. The Bank is currently rated A by S&P, A2 by Moody''s and A+ by Fitch.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: As part of IFC’s Critical Commodities Finance Program Phase II, IFC’s funding to the Bank will be up to $150 million for a trade portfolio of up to $300 million, aimed at supporting both agricultural commodities/inputs globally and exports/imports of crude oil and refined oil products in and out of emerging countries, primarily IDA countries.
location_description: SocGen is headquartered in Paris, France.
development_impact: The CCFP-Bank facility is expected to have the following specific development impacts: - Increase Liquidity: The Facility will ensure continuing and additional funding to the major agricultural and energy sectors in Emerging Countries, especially in Africa and IDA countries. This Facility will contribute to the Bank maintaining its level of business in commodity finance. Among other things, the Facility will enable traders to purchase from and finance agricultural producers, the mainstay of most economies in Africa, and ensure food security and income for the public at large, but especially to farmers. - Strong Demonstration Effect by catalyzing other IFIs to Support Agri and Energy Finance: By supporting commodity backed finance and outreach in partnerships with banks, the facility will have a significant demonstration impact on other banks, especially local /regional banks to participate in funding the agricultural and energy sectors. This would ultimately help increase access to finance for critical economic sectors. - A steady supply of critically needed refined oil products through regular channels will keep prices in check, remove parallel market incentives, improve affordability for the vulnerable poor and contribute to sustaining local economic activities.
additionality: The IFC Facility will provide additional dollar liquidity for a pre-agreed period to the Bank. This extra funding source will allow the Bank to apply it to its business plan in regards to the funding of critical commodities as targeted by the CCFP, particularly in Africa, where the Bank is one of the foremost players.

project_description: Value and Budget Housing Corporation (“VBHC” or the “Company”) is headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India. The Company was incorporated in 2008, with a focus on building affordable and entry level housing in India. VBHC has projects under various stages of development and construction across Bengaluru, Chennai (state of Tamil Nadu) and Mumbai (state of Maharashtra). Further, the Company is in various stages of identification and procurement of land for developing affordable housing in the states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh (the “Project”). VBHC is in the process of raising capital from IFC for part-financing the development of the above affordable housing projects.
sponsor_shareholders: VBHC was established in 2008 by Mr. Jaithirth Rao and Mr. P.S.Jayakumar with the aim of providing affordable homes coupled with buyer friendly practices and strong governance. Together, Mr. Rao and Mr. Jayakumar hold about 34% of VBHC’s equity stake. Mr. Jaithirth Rao has over 20 years experience in the banking industry. In the past, he served Citibank, and its parent Citicorp Incorporated, United States of America, in various capacities across Asia, Europe, South and North America. He was Country Manager for India at Citibank. He developed the consumer business of Citibank in India, Middle East, Eastern Europe and the United Kingdom. He was head of Citibank''s Global Technology Development Division and Global Electronic Cards Division. He co-founded Mphasis in 1998 - a software company based out of California - which was later bought over by EDS, a division of HP. Mr. P.S. Jayakumar has about 24 years experience in the banking industry. He worked with Citibank and held several senior management positions. He was the head of Citibank’s retail banking division in India. The other investors in VBHC are Housing Development Finance Corporation Limited (HDFC), First Carlyle Growth IX (a fund managed by The Carlyle Group), and India Financial Inclusion Fund (a fund managed by Caspian Advisors Private Limited).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at over US$24 million and IFC proposes to invest equity to part finance the Project.
location_description: VBHC is headquartered at HM Strafford House, #29/4, 3rd Floor, 7th Cross, Vasanthnagar Extension, Off Millers Road, Bengaluru 560052, Karnataka, India. The Project will be undertaken in the states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.
development_impact: This investment will have the following development impact: (a) provide essential residential infrastructure to support the ongoing rapid urbanization in India, resulting in improved sanitation and health conditions; (b) demonstration effect for attracting private capital to the affordable housing sector in India; and (c) demonstration effect with regard to use of construction technology to shorten delivery times as well as eco-friendly practices. Compared to conventional constructions, the Project is expected to use 35% less water and meet IFC''s green building standards that results in at least a 20% lower energy consumption.
additionality: (1) This investment in the Company lends IFC''s stamp of approval to VBHC for the governance practices adopted by Company. (2) This investment will make available long term equity capital which is not readily available for the the affordable housing segment in particular, thereby providing financial flexibility to VBHC. (3) VBHC will benefit through access to expertise across IFC''s network in Latin America and other markets where IFC has financed such affordable housing projects. (4) This investment will provide access to IFC''s knowledge base in the field of green buildings/construction as the Company plans to adopt green building practices in the design of its projects.

company_name: EARLYBIRD DIGITAL EAST FUND 2012 SCA SICAR
project_description: Earlybird Digital East Fund 2012 SCA SICAR (“EDEF” or “the Fund”) is a venture capital fund dedicated to investing in early stage technology companies originating primarily in Turkey, Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, Romania, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Czech Republic and opportunistically in Former Yugoslav Republics, Southern/Eastern Mediterranean and Baltics. EDEF intends to invest in the next generation of leading companies in a number of industry sectors, with a focus on technology-enabled scalable services; web applications and online services; digital media; financial services; e-commerce, communication and mobile technologies and services; scalable IT services; IT components and green technology.
sponsor_shareholders: The Founder Partner of the Fund is Earlybird Digital East GmbH & Co. KG. The Fund will be managed by Earlybird Luxembourg Management SA. The Fund’s Advisory Team, combining strong operational and entrepreneurial experience, will be formed of four partners (Mr. Cem Sertoglu, Mr. Dan Lupu, Mr. Evren Ucok and Mr. Roland Manger), and one venture partner (Mr. Ali Kutay).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposal is for IFC to make an equity investment of up to US$25 million in the Fund, not exceeding 20% of total commitments
location_description: The Fund will be formed as a Luxembourg SICAR limited partnership and will have a local management team based in Istanbul, Turkey.
development_impact: (i) Support for SMEs: IFC experience has shown that small to midcap companies can achieve higher job creation rates than large cap companies. IFC would support job creation in Turkey and the broader region as the Fund's strategy is in line with IFC's development impact goals (ii) Demonstration effect: Support for a new fund concept (early-stage TMT VC fund) raising funds in a difficult environment (iii) Support local entrepreneurship and private sector development: Support growth and innovation in the high-growth technology/media/telecom sectors. The Fund's ability to identify best practices and superior management skills in its invested companies and subsequently disseminate them across the portfolio may lead to increased competitiveness and sustainability
additionality: (i) Catalytic Role: Earlybird is raising funds in a difficult environment due to the economic crisis, the lack of a mature ITC market, and the absence of a consistent track record of exits in the region. In addition, IFC's participation can mobilize other investors to join the Fund. (ii) Access to long-term early-stage venture capital is limited in Turkey and in the region. The gap is currently filled by small pool of angel investors who have limited capacity for follow-on investments, limited management skills and a smaller network with which to support the investee companies' growth. (iii) Environment & Social: IFC Environmental & Social standards will be applied to all of the Fund's portfolio companies. It is also the first time the General Partner's ("GP") is working with DFIs, so IFC would likely have a significant impact in enhancing the GP's ESG capabilities. (iv) Additional financing through co-financing: IFC can assist the investee companies by providing co-investment/debt financing to help complete their financial and business plans.
Company Name: EARLYBIRD DIGITAL EAST FUND 2012 SCA SICAR

sector: Garment and Apparel (Without Fabric , Excluding Footwear)
project_description: Founded in 1992, Ananta Apparels Limited (“AAL” or the “Company”) is one of the leading apparel exporters of Bangladesh (top 10 position among woven product manufacturers). The Company specializes in denim products with monthly production capacity of 1.8 million woven bottoms across three factories comprising 850,000 square feet and employing about 13,000 workers. AAL recently re-structured into a group holding company with five manufacturing subsidiaries: Ananta Casualwear Limited (99% shareholding), Ananta Denim Technology Limited (99%), Ananta Fashion Limited (99%), DNV Clothing Limited (75%), and Universal Menswear Limited (51%; a joint-venture company with Romanian suit manufacturer Time Trade International). Major customers include top retail brands such as H&M, GAP and Bestseller Group. AAL has undertaken an expansion plan to be developed in two phases: Phase I, costing approximately US$24.4 million, will primarily involve the relocation of its existing casual woven bottoms factory to a new custom built facility in Kanchpur, south of Dhaka thereby replacing its original factory in downtown Dhaka (the “Project”). The Project is brownfield in nature. The second phase (Phase II), which would involve further capacity expansion, will be undertaken at a future date once Phase I is fully implemented and operational.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Sharif Zahir, Managing Director of AAL , owns 47% of the Company while his younger brother, Mr. Asif Zahir, owns 30%. Their mother Mrs. Qamrun Nahar, with 9% shareholding, is the Chairperson of AAL. Frontier Fund (“FPE”), a Bangladesh-focused IFC-portfolio private equity fund managed by Swedish hedge fund Brummer and Partners, owns the remaining 14% of AAL.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated to be US$24.4 million. IFC will provide a financing package for up to US$8 million.
location_description: The Project will be located in AAL’s existing facility in Noyabari, Kanchpur, south of Dhaka, Bangladesh. AAL’s head office is located in House 20, Road 99, Gulshan 2, Dhaka 1212, Bangladesh.
development_impact: - Job Creation: Approximately 1,500 new jobs expected over both Phases I and II. - Technology Transfer: AAL intends to adopt global best practices in terms of lean manufacturing concepts, factory efficiency, worker productivity and energy efficiency standards of the overall industry. - Local Supply Chain Linkages: The Project will generate incremental business for MSMEs in the value chain, including accessory and package suppliers, service providers and logistics support. - Benefits to the Government: The Project will generate tax revenues, which is expected to contribute to Bangladesh''s Annual Development Program budget, enabling the Government to execute a greater number of developmental activities. - Demonstration Effect: The Project will support a Company that has committed to adopting best practices in corporate governance, E&S compliance, labor standards, and energy efficiency in Bangladesh''s RMG industry.
additionality: - Provide longer tenor foreign currency financing, otherwise difficult to secure in Bangladesh, to support a strategic, private equity portfolio client expand its core business. - Integrate the Company into various textile/RMG-focused IFC advisory programs such as environmental assessment of 250 factories, effluent treatment plant study, Cleaner Production program across 12 pilot factories, Buyer''s Forum and the planned Water Resource Efficiency and Better Works programs, which are geared towards improving compliance, competitiveness, energy efficiency, and labor welfare at the firm and industry levels (more on slides 11-12). - Resource mobilization from other DFIs (FMO is already on board).

sector: Household Appliances (Including Refrigerators, Laundry Machine, Dishwashers, etc.)
project_description: The Project involves financing the ongoing capital expenditure of Butterfly Marketing Limited (“BML” or “the Company”) to facilitate its backward integration into the assembly/manufacturing of some of its key imported white goods. The Company is in the process of setting up two manufacturing plants, Butterfly Industries Limited (“BIL”) and Butterfly Manufacturing Company Limited (“BMCL”) in an effort to manufacture its products locally, thereby giving it better competitiveness. The Project Company is BML, which is setting up the two manufacturing plants. It is one of the leading consumer electronics/white goods retailers in Bangladesh.
sponsor_shareholders: BML currently has 23 shareholders, representing 11 groups of friends and family. The Sponsor, Mr. M.A. Mannan, who set up the Company in 1987, is also the chairman of the Company. The Chairman and his immediate family manage the business and own 35% of the shares, while an additional 20.5% stake is held by his extended family and close friends - thus the Sponsor Group exercises control over approximately 55.5% of the shareholding.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment from IFC is a financing package of up to US$ 42 million consisting of an A loan, a B/parallel loan and an equity purchase. The A and B/parallel loans would be used to part-finance capital expenditure towards setting up the manufacturing plants while the equity investment would help the company streamline its share holding structure to support its future growth and expansion plans.
location_description: The Company’s head office is located in Motijheel, Dhaka, Bangladesh. The two manufacturing plants will be located adjacent to each other in the industrial area of Bhaluka, near Dhaka.
development_impact: The Project is expected to: (i) Job creation: BML''s various projects are expected to create 90 jobs during the construction stage of the plants and 367 permanent jobs in the factories post-construction. The company will be creating 200 new dealerships across the country in the next three years to expand its distribution network, which will create additional indirect jobs; (ii) Technology transfer: BML will be leveraging the technical expertise of LG and Hisense to set up its manufacturing plants, adopting manufacturing best practices, which is expected to improve the overall quality of BML and, in due course, of other companies in the industry; (iii) Diversify Bangladesh''s export basket: BML plans to export Hisense (and possibly other branded) products once operations have stabilized. This would help Bangladesh diversify its export basket and improve the country''s over dependence on the textile sector; (iv) Increase domestic consumption: By selling branded household appliances at lower prices, BML will make these aspirational goods affordable to a much larger section of the country''s population, promoting domestic consumption; and (v) Reduce trade deficit: BML''s backward integration will help reduce Bangladesh''s total import bill and will lead to foreign currency savings, which will help shore up the country''s foreign exchange reserves.
additionality: (i) Industry: IFC''s industry expertise in retail and manufacturing have yielded a set of recommendations, which have already been incorporated into the Company''s future plans. Very much welcomed and valued by the Company, IFC will seek to add value through its expertise going forward as a long-term partner; (ii) Demonstration effect: IFC''s equity investment will positively influence the perception of Bangladesh''s undeveloped manufacturing sector, potentially encouraging more investments that could improve the overall scale and competitiveness of the sector; (iii) Corporate governance expertise: Through the proposed investment, IFC/FPE will be able to appoint two to three independent directors to the board of the Company between themselves, which will help promote adoption of corporate governance best practices and increased financial transparency and accountability. IFC is also exploring an engagement of the Corporate Governance Advisory team with the Company; and (iv) Long-term financing: Through the provision of A and B loans, IFC will provide long-term financing to facilitate the growth of the Company, that is not currently available in the local market.

company_name: GLOBAL HEALTH INVESTMENT FUND I, LLC
project_description: The project being proposed is a US$10mm equity investment in a mezzanine fund, the Global Health Investment Fund, LLC (“GHIF” or the “Fund”), sponsored by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. GHIF is seeking to raise approximately US$100mm for the purpose of improving global health. The Fund would support the development of drugs, vaccines, preventatives, diagnostics and other related technologies aimed at infectious diseases that cause significant morbidity and mortality in developing countries (e.g. neglected infectious diseases), as well as those that provide solutions for maternal, neonatal and child-health challenges.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by the Global Health Investment Corporation, a Delaware non profit non stick corporation, which has mandated LHGP Asset Management LLP, the affiliate of Lion’s Head Global Partners LLP, as the designated Investment Manager.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposal is for IFC to make an equity investment of up to US$10 million in the Fund, which aims to total US$100 million.
location_description: The Fund will invest in multiple companies and/or Product Development Partnerships (PDPs) who are advancing the development of promising health products and technologies for diseases that disproportionately affect developing countries.
development_impact: Given the Fund's focus on the late stage in the development of many of the drugs, vaccines and diagnostics in the pipeline, it is reasonable to expect a large development impact on several fronts: (i) possible replication of the business model and scale-up of the flow of additional funding into late stage development of drugs for neglected diseases; (ii) millions of patients, and especially those in vulnerable population (children and pregnant women) will benefit from the drugs that will be commercialized through this vehicle; (iii) by demonstrating the commercial viability of the proposed funding structure, this could prove to be an important catalyst for the development of drugs that otherwise would not be developed; and (iv) demonstration effect to other charitable foundations that their money could be multiplied and effects of their charitable giving amplified through this funding mechanism, which is expected to bring positive financial return to investors.
additionality: (i) By participating in the first close, IFC's presence signals the confidence in a novel funding model for the development of drugs targeting neglected diseases and the poorest in the emerging markets; (ii) IFC's will endeavor to make its emerging markets experience and expertise available to the Fund; and (iii) The recipients of mezzanine funding may be beneficiaries of IFC's direct co-funding in certain cases, which could further expedite the commercialization of these drugs.
Company Name: GLOBAL HEALTH INVESTMENT FUND I, LLC

project_description: The project is to assist Myronivsky Hliboproduct (“MHP” or the “Company”), a vertically integrated and the leading poultry producer in Ukraine, expand its production capacity. In line with its strategy of vertical integration, the Company plans to strengthen its grain growing segment by cultivating up to an additional 120,000 ha of land.
sponsor_shareholders: The project is sponsored by MHP. Mr. Yuriy Kosyuk, a local entrepreneur, who owns 100% of WTI Trading Ltd, which in turns owns approximately 66% of MHP. A remaining 34% is floated on the London Stock Exchange. Mr. Kosyuk graduated from the Ukrainian Food Institute in 1991 and established MHP in 1998. Prior to launching his poultry business, Mr. Kosyuk was involved in various business activities, including grain and retail trading, food processing.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is to provide an A Loan into the Project of up to US$50 million from its own account for working capital financing.
location_description: The main location of the project is in rural area of Vinnytsia region in Ukraine.
development_impact: The investment program will help MHP expand its domestic and export sales. The proposed Loan will support the Company''s working capital requirements for the successful implementation of MHP''s growth plans, which will have a significant impact on the local economy. Benefits include: - SMEs: MHP supports a network of 2,600 SMEs, a franchise network of small shops selling MHP branded poultry, which will significantly increase with the implementation of the Vinnytsia project. Significant number of these SMEs operate in rural locations often underserved in terms of basic food retail reach. - Employment: The Company currently employs 24,800, including 9,000 females. As a result of the investment program, employment will increase by an additional 8,000 workers. - Food security: MHP''s competitive cost structure will help the company provide competitively priced chicken in Ukraine as well as in importing countries in Africa, Middle East and Asia, thereby contributing to food security in those regions.
additionality: (i) Long-term partnership with IFC which would facilitate its growth through continued advice while facilitating the renewal of its bond in 2015; (ii) IFC''s political and country risk cover in the context of political and economic volatility would encourage MHP to proceed with its investment plans; (iv) IFC''s advisory services in resource efficiency and IFC''s assistance in certification of MHP farms to Global Good Agricultural Practice would set the standard for more environmentally friendly farming operations in Ukraine.

project_description: The project consists of the development of a 1.5 million ton per annum (mtpa) greenfield pulp production facility, with associated forest plantations, infrastructure and logistics, near Ortigueira, Brazil. The plant will produce a mix of hardwood and softwood pulp, which will serve the domestic and export markets.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Klabin S.A., Brazil’s largest producer, exporter and recycler and exporter of paper. Klabin S.A. is publicly listed on the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange, and has two levels of shareholding: (i) common shares (accounting for 35% of total shares, and with voting power): 60% of these are held by the founding Klabin and Lafer families; and (ii) preferred shares (accounting for 65% of the shareholding, but with no voting rights): 43% of these are held by free float investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be up to US$3.5BN (including the cost of associated forests), and IFC’s investment is expected to be in the form of an equity investment of up to US$100MM.
location_description: The project will be located in a Greenfield site near the town of Ortigueira, near Klabin S.A.’s existing paper mill in Telemaco Borba in southern Parana.
development_impact: 1. Employment: The project is expected to employ over 5,000 workers during construction, and following the start of operations, is expected to employ around 1,000 employees in the pulp mill and forestry operations. Along with Klabin''s existing paper mill in nearby Monte Alegre, the project will be the largest employer in this part of the state. 2. Taxes: The project is expected to pay over US$50MM annually in taxes, once it reaches steady state. Under a scheme that was developed through Klabin''s initiative, in conjunction with local governments, the tax receipts will be shared with the neighboring municipalities, all of which are among the poorest municipalities in Parana. 3. Carbon Sequestration: The project will include a forestry base of 106,500 ha, which will be under FSC certification. 4. Renewable Energy: The project includes a biomass-based co-generation plant with a capacity of 260MW. 5. Import Substitution: The project will be the first fluff producer in Brazil, and one of the few softwood producers in the country. By replacing imports that currently meet demand for these products, the Project will enable domestic proeduction in these segments in Brazil.
additionality: 1. Anchor Investor: IFC would play the role of an early investor, which would help Klabin to raise more external equity financing for the project. 2. Environmental and Social Considerations: IFC''s involvement will help Klabin incorporate environmental and social best practices, learned through IFC''s involvement in landmark investments in the sector in Latin America and Asia. 3. Corporate Governance: IFC is working with Klabin to incorporate best practices in the Board structure of the project.

project_description: OCL India Limited (“OCL” or the “Company”) is an existing IFC client and a leading cement producer in eastern India with a capacity of 3.8 million tons per annum (MTPA). The Company started manufacturing cement in 1952. OCL also manufactures refractories. OCL proposes to setup a 1.35 million tons per annum (MTPA) greenfield cement grinding unit at Medinipur, West Bengal (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: OCL is a part of the Dalmia Group and is publicly traded on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange. Dalmia Cement (Bharat) Limited, the flagship company of the Dalmia Group, is the largest shareholder in OCL with a 45% stake & the Dalmia family collectively controls 70% in OCL. The remaining 30% is owned by the general public and institutional investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The investment cost for the Project is estimated at US$102 million and IFC is evaluating an A-Loan of US$40 million to part finance the project. The balance funding requirement will be met through rupee debt and internal accruals.
location_description: The Project will be located at village Kulapachuria, Salboni sub-division, District Medinipur, West Bengal. The proposed site is located at approximately 1 km distance from National Highway 60 and 20 km from National Highway 6. As a part of developing ‘Godapaisal Industrial Park’ the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation has acquired and leased 154.43 acres of land for the Project to OCL as the anchor investor.
development_impact: - The Project will lead to the creation of 150 direct and 120 sub-contracted jobs upon Project implementation. It will also create 10-15 managerial jobs & ~500 construction jobs during its peak construction. - The Project would produce Portland slag cement, which due to its low clinker-cement ratio would result in savings of 84,000 tons of annual CO2 emissions. - The project will contribute an estimated US$7 million per annum of tax revenues to the exchequer.
additionality: IFC will play a significant role in the Project by: (i) Providing a long term finance, well suited to project & difficult to obtain under current market conditions for mid-sized companies. ; (ii) Partnering with an existing client in a difficult frontier market, (iii) Offering IFC''s Advisory Services to strengthen the clients'' supply linkages, (iv) Enhancing the Project''s technical, environmental and social review and practices and ensuring compliance with IFC Performance Standards and reduce the Project''s carbon footprint.

company_name: SHANDONG CHANGLIN DEUTZ-FAHR MACHINERY CO., LTD.
project_description: IFC proposes to provide a loan up to Euro 10 million (approx. US$13 million) to support Shandong Changlin Deutz-Fahr Machinery Co., Ltd. (“Changlin-SDF”) to build a greenfield plant in Shandong province to manufacture four-wheel tractors in China. Changlin-SDF is a joint venture established by Same Deutz-Fahr Group SpA (“SDF”), an Italian agri-machinery manufacturer and Shandong Changlin Machinery Group Co., Ltd (“Changlin Group”), a Chinese machinery manufacturer in July 2011.
sponsor_shareholders: SDF was founded in Treviglio, Italy, in 1927 by Francesco Cassani, and is currently owned by his family. SDF is an integrated manufacturer of tractors, combine harvesters, specialist harvesters, diesel engines and farm machinery. Currently SDF’s production is based in four plants in Europe (Italy, Germany, France and Croatia), one in India, and one in Russia. Changlin Group was founded in June 1993 by Mr. Zhang Yihua and employees of the group. Its main products are agricultural machinery, construction machinery, single cylinder diesel engines, hydraulic systems, machining parts and foundry products. Each of SDF and Changlin Group owns 50% of Changlin-SDF.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at RMB340 million (approx. US$54 million). The proposed IFC investment is a Euro 10 million (approx. US$13 million) A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project is located in Linyi City, Shandong Province, China. The site for the Project is in a peri-urban / agricultural / industrial area with a well developed infrastructure in place.
development_impact: (i) Food security. The Project will have significant contribution to efficient use of farm land and higher productivity through supply of four wheel tractors that offer higher technology and horsepower by manufacturing close to 200,000 tractors and reaching that many farmers during the life of the IFC loan. (ii) Development of downstream food industry. Higher crop output resulting from large scale farming with four-wheel tractors will help develop downstream industries such as food processing and packaging. (iii) Inclusive business. The Project will help the development of SMEs along the value chain, including the dealers/distributors, suppliers, logistics and service providers. A significant portion of these SMEs, especially the distributors, are based in frontier regions and rural areas. (iv) Job creation. The Project is expected to create more 700 direct jobs in its facilities, as well as significant level of indirect jobs along the value chain and downstream industries.
additionality: (i) Long-term Financing. IFC offers longer term loan and grace period to the greenfield project, This allows the company to have more flexibility in managing its cash flow especially in case of longer than expected ramp up period. Such long-term financing is not accessible from local banks in China. (ii) Stamp of approval/catalyst role. IFC''s investment in the Project is expected to provide comfort to other lenders and improve the Company''s ability to access long term financing. (iii) E&S advice. As the project is in implementation stage, IFC could provide timely advice for the Company to establish best E&S practices, as well as input on efficient use of energy and water.
Company Name: SHANDONG CHANGLIN DEUTZ-FAHR MACHINERY CO., LTD.

country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: AMERRA Capital Management, LLC, (AMERRA) is an investment fund manager, focused on providing customized agriculture-focused and commodity-based finance solutions throughout the Americas to producers, processors, distributors and traders. AMERRA has about US$600 million in assets under management across five funds and accounts. After successful deployment of investor capital through several funds during 2009-2012, AMERRA is in the process of raising additional equity for the AMERRA Agri Fund II, LP (AMERRA Fund II) which will provide a broader range of finance solutions to its existing and new clients, especially longer loan maturities than it has not been able to provide up until now. The proposed project entails IFC making about US$50 million of credit available to AMERRA Fund II for up to 5 years, leveraging the capital it will have to lend (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: AMERRA is a partnership which is 50% owned by Craig Tashjian and Nancy Obler (its two founding principals) along with Pat Morabito (its Chief Operating and Risk Officer). The balance is held by M.D. Sass-Macquarie Financial Strategies, L.P. (25%) and Macquarie Group Limited (25%). The founding principals and COO had long and successful careers in banking before AMERRA. M.D. Sass-Macquarie Financial Strategies, L.P. is a joint venture focused on investing in alternative strategies private equity fund managers and is equally owned by M.D. Sass and Macquarie Group Limited. M.D. Sass was founded in 1972 and is a well-established investment management firm. Today, the M.D. Sass organization has approximately US$8 billion in assets under management and employs over 100 people. Macquarie Group Limited (Macquarie) is a global provider of banking, financial, advisory, investment and funds management services. Founded in 1969, Macquarie employs more than 15,000 people in over 28 countries. Macquarie has approximately US$340 billion of assets under management and is listed in Australia (ASX:MQG).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project entails making up to US$50 million of credit available to extend and leverage the funds AMERRA Fund II has available. The IFC investment is expected to be made in support of a sub-fund of AMERRA Agri Fund II, LP, which when it has deployed all of its resources to finance its clients, would consist of US$50 million lent directly from (or guaranteed by IFC) and at least US$150 million funded by equity for a total portfolio of US$200 million or more.
location_description: AMERRA is based in New York City and invests throughout the Americas, especially in Mexico, Central and South America. More than 80% of AMERRA’s clients have been based in Brazil, Mexico, Ecuador, Guatemala and Nicaragua, or buy agricultural commodities from those countries or elsewhere in Latin America and the Caribbean.
development_impact: Despite their contribution to food supply and rural livelihoods, smaller and medium-sized agribusiness companies (and the farmers that supply them) have historically had insufficient access to finance from private sector sources, in particular finance that extends for more than one crop season. Recently, the unfavorable supply-to-demand dynamics for financing to this segment has deteriorated as working capital needs have risen across the agribusiness supply chain with higher commodity prices at a time when the commercial banks who had been operating in some parts of the supply chain have come under increasing pressure to strengthen their capital ratios. The IFC project supports the expansion of an innovative firm whose business model includes providing financing into this segment by intermediating capital from an institutional investor segment in developed countries that has not historically invested significantly in these agribusiness segments from the emerging markets.
additionality: (A) IFC is helping Amerra design and implement an Environmental & Social Management System (ESMS) to identify and manage potential environmental and Social risks. The system will include the following. (i) an initial screening for every transaction, and an environmetnal and social (E&S) due-diligence for long-term finance transactions. (ii) When applicable, the preparation of a plan to mitigate E&S risks or strengthen client E&S practices. And (iii), monitoring and enforcement of the plan. Improved E&S evaluations systems are expected to make Amerra: (i) among the few finance firms in its and related financing niches with a formal ESMS, which in turn (ii) helps disseminate better E&S practices among its clients in the agricultural commodity supply chain. (B) Agribusiness sectors generally do not enjoy good access to finance and financing that extends beyond a given crop year is especially limited for smaller and medium-sized companies. Through this project, IFC is supporting a financial intermediary serving the sector as it moves toward providing longer tenor finance to its clients (earlier up to about 3 years, now up to 5 years). (C) Although Amerra is proving its business model works, its role in intermediating funding from institutional investors to medium-sized agribusiness companies in emerging market countries and companies that purchase commodities from emerging market countries has not tapped all the funding that such intermediaries could efficiently deploy given unmet finance needs of medium-sized agribusiness companies. IFC''s support for the Project represents an important diversification of funding sources and may have a demonstration effect to help catalyze the mobilization of funding from new sources for this financial intermediary and others in similar niches.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

sector: Other Vegetable Oil Crops (Coconut, Rapeseed, Peanut, Sunflower, etc.)
project_description: IFC is considering an investment up to US$75 million in Euro equivalent in Victoria Group a.d. (“Victoria”, or the “Group”). Victoria is a leading agro industrial group in Serbia with a primary focus on processing of soybean and sunflower oilseeds and grain trading. The Group employs over 1,800 people. IFC’s loan proceeds will be used to finance the Group’s permanent working capital financing needs and restructure the Group’s debt financing towards a longer term, more stable structure that is suitable for the nature of the Group’s operations. The long-term facility will be used partially to provide input financing to farmers needed to produce oilseeds for processing on the Group’s plants. Thereby, IFC’s investment is expected to strengthen the support to farmers and increase the sustainability of the Group’s operations.
sponsor_shareholders: Victoria’s shareholders consist of: (a) three Serbian businessmen (who are also the founders of the business) Mr. Zoran Mitoric, Mr. Milija Babovic and Mr. Stanko Popovic (22.5% each); (b) EBRD (21.4% share) and, (c) Apsara Limited (11%), a Cyprus domiciled holding company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s financing will be directed to support the Group’s permanent working capital needs and replacing existing shorter term debt financing. IFC is considering an A loan investment up to €60 million for IFC’s own account which will structured as a corporate finance facility.
location_description: The Group is headquartered in Belgrade, Serbia. IFC’s investment would support the Group’s agriculture-related operations concentrated in the northern Serbian province of Vojvodina. The Group owns and operates two oilseed processing plants in Becej and Sid; a fertilizers production facility and a port at Backa Palanka.
development_impact: The development impact of the Project is expected to include: (i) Strengthening of agribusiness linkages and support to farmers: given the strong linkages of Victoria Group with farmers, provision of longer term permanent working capital will help ensure stable access of pre-harvest financing to farmers; (ii) Job preservation: the Group employs about 1,800 people across its operation and collaborates with about 400 partners which in turn supply the Group from over 25,000 farmers; (iii) Increase tax revenues: IFC''s investment will contribute to the growth of government revenues from taxation; and (iv) Addressing food security concerns: IFC''s investment will contribute to food security and in meeting the challenges of increasing demand and food crisis.
additionality: IFC''s expected additionality includes: (i) Crisis response and countercyclical support: In light of the fluid economic situation in Serbia in the context of the Eurozone crisis, the local banking sector has cut liquidity on the domestic market. Through the Project, IFC is stepping up its presence on the local market, helping to restore confidence and increase investment in Serbia; (ii) Provision of long-term financing: Provide long-term financing otherwise not readily available on the market; and (iii) Diversified funding base: At a time of financial strain for local banks, IFC is starting its relationship with Victoria, a new partner which will benefit from a further diversified funding-base as a result of IFC''s presence.

project_description: Atlantic Grupa d.d. (the “Atlantic” or the “Group”), headquartered in Zagreb, Croatia, is a multinational company whose activities include the production, sale and distribution of fast moving consumer goods throughout the Balkans, Russia and Western Europe. The Group is a leading producer of food and personal care products as well as a leading distributor of consumer goods in South-Eastern Europe. The Group also owns a private chain of pharmacies in Croatia. The Project entails the refinancing of Group debt, including debt of its Serbian and Croatian subsidiaries, and is aimed at supporting the Group’s balance sheet restructuring.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1991, Atlantic is a well-established regional leader in South-Eastern Europe and a leading producer of coffee, sweet and salted snacks, sports and functional food, savory spreads, beverages, baby food and personal care products. As of June 30, 2012, the Group’s shareholders were as follows: Emil Tedeschi (50.2%); Raiffeisen OMF (9.6%); European Bank for reconstruction and Development (8.5%); DEG (8.5%); Lada Tedeschi Fiorio (5.8%); Management (1.1%); with the remaining 16.3% publically traded on the Zagreb stock exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project is estimated at €300 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A-Loan of up to €55 million for IFC’s own account. The balance of the project funding is to be provided by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development as well as other commercial lenders.
location_description: Atlantic Group is headquartered in: Miramarska 23, 10000, Zagreb, Croatia The Group operates through 17 production sites producing various food products, beverages and personal care products. Site locations include: Serbia – 4 facilities: 2 in Belgrade, 1 in Smederevska Palanka and 1 in Ljubovija; Slovenia - 4 facilities: 2 in Izola, and 1 Rogaška and Mirna; Bosnia & Herzegovina - 2 facilities: Glavičice, Hadžići; Macedonia - 1 facility in Skopje; Germany - 1 facility in Bleckede; Croatia - 5 facilities: 2 in Zagreb and Rakitje and 1 in Apatovec.
development_impact: The development impact of the project is expected to include: (i) support to a Croatian company in its south-south investments in the region, including in Serbia, thus helping a new regional player in its expansion and regional integration; (ii) through appropriate financial support, further improve the business sustainability of an important regional employer and agri-processing company involved in value-added production in a sector important to the region and particularly to the Serbian economy; (iii) generate tax revenues.
additionality: IFC is well positioned to assist the Group with long-term financing to help ensure its growth and strengthen its regional base. IFC''s expected additionality includes: (i) provision of financing at reasonable rates and longer tenors appropriate for the type of investment and not otherwise available in the country; (ii) strengthening of the Group''s balance sheet by consolidating its debt and extending the maturity of it loans post-acquisition of another regional player; (iii) diversifying the Group''s funding base; (iv) providing expertise in energy efficiency and cleaner production investments expected in the coffee and beverage production.

project_description: Groupe Auchan (“Auchan” or the “Group”), one of the largest European food retailers, is expanding its operations in Ukraine, where it opened its first hypermarket in 2008 and currently operates ten stores. The Group has requested IFC to provide a long-term loan to its Ukrainian subsidiaries to partially finance a hypermarket in Odessa, as well as new hypermarkets and shopping centers in other cities (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Groupe Auchan SA (“Auchan” or the “Group) is a privately–owned company that started operations in food retail in 1961 in the North of France. Today, Auchan is one of the largest food retailers in the world with a strong footprint in Western Europe, and fast growing operations in emerging markets in Central and Eastern Europe and Asia. Auchan’s main food retail format is the hypermarkets format through which the Group applies a discount strategy focusing on offering the lowest prices on a large assortment of products in the markets in which it operates. Immochan, Auchan’s commercial property arm, develops and operates shopping centers and galleries located in or adjacent to the Auchan hypermarkets. The project companies are all Ukrainian subsidiaries majority owned and controlled by the Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a US$75million A loan for IFC’s own account to Auchan’s subsidiaries in Ukraine.
location_description: The Project will involve the construction and operation of hypermarket(s) and shopping center(s), the first one being a hypermarket located in Odessa.
development_impact: The Project''s development impact will include: i) Benefit to low and middle-income consumers: The Project will contribute to increase access by low and middle-income households to quality foods, vegetables and goods at affordable prices as Auchan''s historical value proposition is being a food retail price-leader; ii) Food supply chain development: The Project will help improve food quality and safety standards throughout the agribusiness value chain iii) Employment creation: The Project will generate a significant number of direct jobs during construction and operation. Furthermore, the Project will also generate a significant number of indirect jobs through retail supply chains and related services companies; iv) Improvement in green building standards: The Project will contribute to set higher local green-building standards in the country which could have a strong demonstration effect in terms of local climate change mitigation.
additionality: IFC Additionality will manifest itself in the following areas: i) Risk mitigation: IFC will provide country and retail sector knowledge and long-term debt financing, which is not readily available in Ukraine, in light uncertain financial markets conditions in Europe; ii) Standard setting: IFC will ensure that the Project is implemented based on best practice environmental, social, health and safety standards. iii) Advisory services: IFC will engage with Auchan to explore opportunities for Advisory Services to contribute, through its Food Safety Program, to improving food quality and safety standards throughout Auchan''s agribusiness value chain.

project_description: The proposed investment is to support Agrofusion Group (the “Company”), the largest tomato paste and industrial tomato producer in Ukraine, by strengthening its capital base through refinancing existing short term debt and financing incremental permanent working capital. Established in 2007, Agrofusion is the largest vertically integrated tomato paste producer in Ukraine, marketing its products mainly to large FMCG companies in Ukraine, Russia, other CIS countries, and to a lesser extent Western European markets. The Company’s operational assets include: (i) two tomato paste plants with total processing capacity of approximately 300,000 metric tons of tomatoes per season (6,000 tons of tomatoes a day); (ii) two seedling green-houses; and (iii) 12,000 hectares of irrigated leased land in Mykolayiv and Kherson regions as well as modern farming equipment.
sponsor_shareholders: Agrofusion Group is wholly-owned by the Sypko family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide corporate financing to the Company in the form of an up to US$20 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Agrofusion is headquartered in Mykolayiv, Ukraine. The Company conducts modern farming operations on 12,000 hectares of leased land in Mykolayiv and Kherson regions.
development_impact: The proposed investment intended to support the Company''s current capital structure will: (i) help a leading Ukrainian tomato paste producer to scale up its export revenues and increase inflow of the foreign currency; (ii) support a viable economic activity and help secure employment in frontier rural area of Kherson region; and (iii) have a demonstration effect on other vegetable producers in Ukraine through promotion of sustainable agricultural practices.
additionality: Through a strategic engagement with the Company, IFC is well positioned to: 1. Support the Company''s capital base by providing longer tenors and stable working capital financing 2. Establish long term partnership with the Company with the ability to support further expansion 3. Share its global expertise in primary production and processing

project_description: LLC “Okkoskhidinvest” (“Okkoskhidinvest”, or the “Company”) is a joint venture between PJSC “Concern Galnaftogaz” (“Galnaftogaz” or “GNG”) and ADM Capital (“ADM”) with the objective to build/purchase and operate a network of gas filling stations in four eastern regions of Ukraine, where GNG had little presence in the past. The stations will operate under Galnaftogaz’ proprietary OKKO brand and will comply with up-to-date environmental and technical specifications. The format for OKKO stations is designed to maximize services offered to clients and, in addition to selling petroleum products, sell snacks, fast food, and other automotive-related services (car wash, car repair etc). Today, the Company has 21 operating stations The Project is to build/purchase and operate high-volume OKKO gas filling stations and the associated increase in working capital to bring the total network of the Company’s stations to 80 stations (the “Project”). The total Project cost is estimated at US$165 million.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are Galnaftogaz and ADM Capital. Galnaftogaz is a leading Ukrainian petroleum retail company based in western Ukraine that operates 350 gas filling stations in Western, Central, and Southern Ukraine. GNG is a private company. The single largest shareholder of GNG is Vitaliy Antonov, its founder. ADM Capital is an emerging markets investment fund established in the wake of the 1997 Asian financial crisis with $1.6 billion in assets under management. ADM’s investment in the Company was done via its latest fund raised in 2010 (“ADM CEECAT”) which focuses on small and mid-sized companies in the Black Sea Region.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $165 million. The Company has requested financing of $85m from IFC to build and restore 80 fuel stations in Eastern Ukraine. IFC’s proposed investment consists of a $15 million A Loan, a $55 million B Loan, and a $15 million subordinated C Loan.
location_description: The gas filling stations under this Project will be located in four regions in Eastern Ukraine: Luhansk, Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, and Zaporizhia. Some of the stations will be acquired from third parties and rebranded while others will be newly constructed. The stations will be in both rural and urban areas and will be built next to main transportation routes.
development_impact: - Development of Ukraine''s infrastructure according to modern and safe standards and introduction of higher service standards in the region through GNG''s OKKO filling stations and convenience stores - Provision of reliably cleaner high-quality fuels to Ukrainian automotive consumers - Employment generation/preservation - Linkages to local suppliers: the JV''s station''s convenience stores, automotive services and fast-food restaurants will provide opportunities for local suppliers who supply the goods sold
additionality: - Provision of risk capital and long-term funds - Mobilization of a significant amount of long-term debt - IFC has a long-term partnership with both GNG and ADM, and can leverage that relationship to provide relevant assistance to the JV in terms of business strategy, in E&S issues, and in times of need. - With its corporate governance expertise, IFC is in a unique position to assist GNG and ADM in their collaborative efforts as JV partners.

company_name: KENYA TEA DEVELOPMENT AGENCY HOLDINGS LTD
project_description: Kenya Tea Development Agency (Holdings) Ltd (“KTDA” or the “Company”) is a holding company which generates revenues from its operating subsidiaries which are involved in tea warehousing, tea sales to export and domestic markets, and various services provided to the 65 factories. KTDA is constructing a new state-of-the-art 200,000 square feet warehouse complex to replace 50% of its current warehousing space which is leased from 3rd parties.
sponsor_shareholders: KTDA, a public limited liability Kenyan holding company, is wholly owned by 54 Tea Companies ("TCs") which own 65 tea factories. As of December 31, 2011, there were 562,000 smallholder tea farmers who are individual shareholders in the 54 TCs. Individual farmers'' shareholding in their respective TCs is commensurate to the volume of their green leaf tea deliveries. Each TC owns between 1-2% of KTDA. KTDA emerged from the privatization of the Kenya Tea Development Authority in 2000. The Kenya Tea Development Authority was established in 1964 as a government parastatal charged with promoting and fostering the development of tea for the small-scale tea growers primarily through providing factory management services.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $24 million. The proposed IFC investment will consist of a corporate A Loan investment of up to $12 million on IFC’s account.
location_description: The Project will be implemented and located on Plot # 2423, Section V Mainland North, situated west of Mombasa Municipality (Miritini), Mombasa, Kenya. The site has good access to major transport routes.
development_impact: 1) Farmers Reached: The project will reach tea farmers and further strengthen KTDA which serves as a good model for smallholder supported enterprises. 2) Support a key export sector which benefits the Kenyan economy.
additionality: 1) Standard Setting: IFC will assist to implement best practice environmental, social, health and safety standards. 2) Knowledge and Innovation: KTDA can benefit from IFC''s global experience on many warehousing projects as well as green building expertise. 3) Advisory Services: IFC will engage with KTDA to explore opportunities for Advisory Services to support smallholder farmers in its supply chain
Company Name: KENYA TEA DEVELOPMENT AGENCY HOLDINGS LTD

project_description: The proposed project consists of a revolving secured short term trade facility, with a significant funding mobilization factor, to support key private sector operators (the international energy trader and domestic oil marketing companies) in their access to finance the import, purchase and marketing of refined fuel products in Mauritania. The proposed project would lend in parallel along with Societe Generale, DFIs and other commercial lenders to BB Energy- the successful bidder under Government of Mauritania’s oil import tender arrangement. BB Energy, an international trading company domiciled in the United Arab Emirates, has been awarded a 2-year contract to supply refined oil products to Mauritania for 2012-2014. The funding will be used by BB Energy to finance: (i) purchase of oil products imported into Mauritania and related storage expenses; (ii) as well as related receivables against local oil product marketing companies, and major domestic industrial entities which are consumers of refined fuel products.
sponsor_shareholders: BB Energy (Gulf) DMCC, domiciled in the United Arab Emirates, is part of the BB Energy Group of companies (the “Group). The Group is mainly active in the oil trading business for crude oil, refined petroleum products and bitumen. It is ultimately controlled by members of the Bassatne family. Established in 1969, BB Energy Group is well represented through trading and services companies in London, Singapore, Dubai, Beirut and Athens with over 200 employees. The Group trades around 7-10 million metric tons of crude oil and petroleum products annually.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The facility size will be up to $500 million two year arrangement to finance the importation of refined energy products into Mauritania. Out of the total $500 million facility, IFC and Société Générale are each considering an exposure of up to $150 million for their respective accounts and both institutions together plan to mobilize up to $200 million from commercial banks and DFIs.
location_description: Nouakchott and Nouadhibou, Mauritania
development_impact: The proposed investment will have significant development impacts as follows: (a) Maintain the availability of trade finance for trade businesses in Mauritania. The Project is expected to finance in excess of US$1.5 billion of energy commodity trade flows to Mauritania over two years by providing much needed liquidity. This will protect an IDA economy against the risk of energy shortages, the risk of being cut off from suppliers as commercial banks have reduced their emerging market exposure. (b) Ensuring availability of energy products in the local economy, critical for consumption, power and other energy needs. A steady supply of critically needed fuel through regular channels will keep prices in check, remove parallel market incentives, and improve affordability particularly for the vulnerable poor and is necessary to sustain economic activities. (c) SME Development - By supporting the private sector companies in the country''s downstream oil sector, the project will provide business opportunities to local private companies involved in transportation, distribution, and retail of refined oil products
additionality: (a) With the help of IFC, Mauritania can access commercial and official sources of funding to finance the import of refined energy products essential for the working of its economy, covering the country''s entire energy needs over the next two years. Due to the continuous constraints on banks traditionally active in the trade finance space, including European banks, and the increased cost of US funding, the proposed facility will allow continued importation of energy products into Mauritania. Without this facility, all sectors and economic agents, such as power generation, transportation, agriculture, industrial and commercial entities and households will be negatively impacted, hurting economic activity. There is also a risk that the current successful tendering and private sector involvement would stop, forcing the State to get again involved in the trade of fuel products, use scarce foreign exchange reserves for energy rather than food imports, and potentially resorting to barter trade if state financing were not available. This will be a setback to Mauritania''s reform program of private sector development and devolving the importation and marketing of energy to private companies. (b) IFC''s presence enables the mobilization of financial resources from other development financial institutions and also commercial lenders. In the current market environment, Mauritanian risk is hard to finance, notwithstanding the security structure from pledged oil and confirmed L/Cs from international banks, and currently importers have difficulty accessing discounting facility of commercial banks, an arrangement needed to finance their trading operations.

project_description: Softlogic Holdings Plc (‘Softlogic’ or the ‘Company’), is a Sri Lankan conglomerate with existing operations across retail, information and communication technology, healthcare and financial services sectors. The proposed project by Softlogic involves an investment of up to US$67.7 million over the next three years to (a) expand its network of retail stores from about 124 to up to 280 as well as increase its geographical reach to smaller cities; and (b) to rebuild and expand an acquired hotel to a total of 166 keys (the ‘Project’). The Project will be implemented through subsidiaries of Softlogic.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1991, Softlogic has been publicly listed company on the Colombo Stock Exchange since July 2011. Its largest shareholder is Mr.Ashok Pathirage who holds 43.4% of the shareholding. Other significant shareholders include Mr. H.K.Kaimal (8.3% shareholding), Mr. R.J.Perera (7.8% shareholding) and Mr.H.U.Gunawardena (7.3% shareholding).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$67.7 million. The proposed IFC investment of up to US$30 million (or equivalent in local currency) will include A Loan(s) for IFC’s own account and equity/quasi equity in Softlogic and/or its subsidiaries. The proceeds of IFC’s financing will be used to partially fund the planned expansions in retail and tourism sectors.
location_description: Softlogic is headquartered in Colombo, Sri Lanka and has operations across the country. The hotel project will be located in Bentota. Softlogic has planned its retail expansion across several cities and towns in Sri Lanka. The proposed IFC investment for the retail expansion will be deployed at several locations in Sri Lanka.
development_impact: (i) Job creation: The project is expected to generate 930 direct jobs, with a significant part of the workforce drawn from the local community. In addition, the project will also generate indirect employment related to the supply chain of the tourism sector. (ii) Best practices in hotel management: The hotel is expected to be managed by a global hotel chain and will bring best practices in the sector to Sri Lanka. (iii) Increase access to high quality consumer products: The project will increase the number and geographical reach of retail products for Sri Lankan consumers and also make the products available to lower income segment of the population in smaller cities.
additionality: (i) Provide long-term tailored capital to support Softlogic''s growth in the tourism and retail sectors in Sri Lanka. The tenors provided by IFC are not readily available in Sri Lanka. (ii) IFC will share its experience and expertise in the tourism and retail sectors which is expected to contribute to an improved capital structure, efficiency of operations and risk management, especially in the hotel sector which is new to the Company. (iii) Forge a long term strategic partnership which will be leverage to support Softlogic''s broader growth plans across the other sectors as well. (iv) IFC''s investment will function as a stamp of approval for the Company which is expected to help the Company attract other potential debt and equity investors.

sector: Man-Made Fibers (Including Nylon, Polyester, Rayon, etc.)
project_description: SRF Limited (“SRF”), a producer of bi-axially-oriented polyethylene terephthalate (“BOPET”) in India, and a market leader in Nylon 6 tire cord as well as belting fabrics, proposes to set up a facility for the production of BOPET packaging films in Thailand (the “Plant”). The Plant having a capacity of 28,500 tonnes per annum will be set-up in the SRF’s subsidiary SRF Industries (Thailand) Ltd (“SRFIT”). The project is expected to cost around US$71 million including working capital requirements , of which IFC is considering financing up to US$ 45 mm. The balance will be financed by SRF contribution and loans through local banks.
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Gurgaon, India- SRF is a large company with three main businesses: 1) Technical Textiles (Nylon and polyester tire cord fabric, and belting fabrics); 2) Chemicals (Refrigerant gases, Chloromethanes, fluorospecialities); and 3) Packaging Films. It is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) in India. 50% of the company is held by the Bharat Ram family, while 50% is owned by the general public including Foreign Institutional Investors, Mutual Funds, Banks and DFIs. SRFIT is a wholly-owned subsidiary of SRF.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be about US$71 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$ 45 million A loan for IFC’s own account. The balance will be funded as equity or sponsor loans by SRF, as well as loans from local banks.
location_description: SRFIT has purchased 22 acres [54 Rai] land at the Hemaraj Eastern Seaboard Industrial Estate (HESIE) approximately 30 kilometers from the Laem Chabang deep-sea container port and Sri Racha city and approx 110 kilometers from Bangkok. The company has received approval from IEAT (Industrial Estate Authority of Thailand), covering various environmental and land clearances. Utilities and road infrastructure is part of the facilities available at the estate.
development_impact: (i) Improving Local Supply Chain: Local procurement of about US$10 million is expected during construction. During operational phase, business for local supply chain will increase. (ii) Job creation: The Project is expected to create about 300 direct jobs and 1500 indirect jobs in ancillary units and supply chain. In addition, there will be temporary jobs created during construction phase and during life of the project. (iii) Food Security: The Project supports the expansion of the food packaging industry, thereby reducing food spoilage and enhancing availability of processed foods. (iv) Enhanced Financial Sustainability through Product Diversification: The BOPET plant expands the company''s product base in Thailand (currently producing Nylon 6 tire cord), thus providing an additional revenue source, and access to new markets and customers.
