(v) Demonstration Effect of a South-South Investment: The project will facilitate a South-South investment and its success could encourage other Indian companies to expand in emerging markets.
additionality: (i) Global Knowledge: IFC''s global presence and expertise enables IFC to offer the Sponsor advice and comfort, as SRF expands its footprint overseas. (ii) Long-term Partnership Opportunities: This project will be a part of IFC''s endeavor to establish a long-term partnership with SRF. IFC is currently looking at another investment with SRF in South Africa, where IFC is requested to provide US$40 million dollar denominated loan. (iii) The project is large in relation to the size of the Company along with gradual ramp up, hence requiring longer tenor financing which is not easily available in the local market. IFC''s ability to offer long-term dollar denominated loans are important for the financing of a project of this nature. (iv) Environmental and Social Good Practice: IFC''s support of the Project will ensure E&S good practice in accordance with IFC''s Performance Standards.

project_description: Ramkrishna Forgings Limited (“RKFL” or the “Company”) is headquartered in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, and its manufacturing units are located in Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, India. Founded in November 1981, RKFL manufactures forged and machined Transmission and axle components for medium and heavy commercial vehicles, and is currently one of the market leaders in this space in India. In order to increase its market share in a growing domestic market, and improve its operating efficiency, RKFL has undertaken an expansion program in Jamshedpur requiring a capital expenditure of approximately US$97 million. The greenfield expansion program will include a new Front Axle Beam manufacturing line, with machinery imported from Germany, and will be installed near the Company’s existing plant in Jamshedpur.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Mahabir Prasad Jalan, the current Chairman, of RKFL, founded the Company in 1981, and has been actively associated with the Company since its inception. He is a Mechanical Engineer from Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani and has more than 20 years experience in this industry. Mr. Jalan has worked with Orient Paper Mills Limited, Spinning Accessories Limited, Shalimar Wires Limited and Calicut Engineering Works Limited. His first entrepreneurship was as Managing Partner of Tribeni Steel Forgings in the year 1974. His son Mr. Naresh Jalan, Managing Director of RKFL is actively involved in running the business with his core strength being in marketing and finance. The Company listed in April 2004. It is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange. Collectively, Messrs. Jalan and other family members own approximately 52.7% of RKFL, Mutual funds and FIIs own around 21.4%, and the balance 25.9% is owned by the Indian public.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$97 million. IFC proposes to invest upto US$20 million to finance the Project.
location_description: RKFL is headquartered at Ramkrishna Chambers, 72, Shakespeare Sarani, Kolkata - 700017, West Bengal, India. The Project will be undertaken at either of the two available sites identified at either at land being leased from Adityapur Industrial Development Authority or 25 acre land purchased on willing buyer-willing seller basis located at Bholadih, Dist. Seraikella, Kharsawan.
development_impact: This investment will have a strong development impact in the form of (a) direct employment generation for about 390 people in the state of Jharkhand and (b) enhance global competitiveness and capabilities of the Company as it embarks on its journey to become a player of scale in the auto-components sector.
additionality: (1) IFC''s proposed long term finance provides necessary flexibility to the Company in the current economic environment. It will also help support the Company''s access to long term funds. (2) IFC''s investment will also help the Company strengthen its environmental, health and safety and social standards as it moves forward on its path to become a large player in the auto-components sector.

company_name: KIPAS KAGIT SANAYI ISLETMELERI ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Kipas Kagit A.S, a subsidiary of the Kipas Group, is embarking on a new project to set up a recycled fiber based greenfield corrugated paper and cardboard facility, with a capacity of 450,000- 480,000 tons per annum (tpa) in Kahramanmaras, Turkey. Through its corrugated cardboard investment, Kipas intends to take advantage of the growth of the packaging industry in Turkey, in particular in the South and Eastern parts of the country.
sponsor_shareholders: The Kipas Group (the ‘Sponsor’ or ‘Kipas’) is a well-known business group in Kahramanmaras, Turkey with operations in textiles, cement, energy, agribusiness and education with an estimated total turnover of USD 750 million. Kipas was set up in the mid-1980s by the Oksuz (58% shareholding) and Gumuser (42% shareholding) families, which have since maintained a strong partnership, enhanced by the formation of Kipas Holding A.S. in 1985. The Group employs approximately 6,000 people and is the largest tax payer in Kahramanmaras. Kipas has several companies ranking in the top 500 and the subsequent 500 corporations in Turkey, including Kipas Mensucat AS, Kipas Denim A.S. and KCS K.Maras Cimento A.S.. With demand for corrugated paper and cardboard in Turkey rising steadily, Kipas Group has decided to diversify into corrugated cardboard production. Kipas has formed a new company, Kipas Kagit A.S. (or the ‘Company’), which will be the operating entity for the project. Kipas Kagit is owned by various Kipas Group companies as follows: Kipas K.Maras Iplik Pamuk Tic.A.S.(35%), Erdem Tekstil Tic.A.S (30%), Kipas Mensucat Isletmeleri A.S. (15%), Kipas Holding A.S. (10%), KCS K.Maras Cimento A.S. (10%). Erdem Tekstil is a joint venture between Kipas and the Buyukerzurumlu family, also from Kahramanmaras.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the project is estimated at around EUR260 million, which is expected to be financed by a EUR38 million loan for IFC’s own account and an estimated EUR123 million of export credit agency and other loans. The rest of the financing will be contributed by the Sponsors.
location_description: Kipas Kagit, the Kipas Group subsidiary undertaking the project, is located in Kahramanmaras, Turkey. The rest of Kipas Group is also located in the same area in Kahramanmaras.
development_impact: The project will create additional employment through 300 additional jobs in Kipas and indirectly in related fields, notably waste paper collection in a frontier region of Turkey. The project will increase the use of recycled paper and in turn improve the domestic waste paper recovery rate, especially in a frontier area. Moreover, the project will result in the production of high quality cardboard through the use of the most recent technology in the industry that will help substitute for imports. Kipas Kagit will also supply corrugators in the food packaging container business that contribute to improved efficiency in food distribution and ultimately lower costs, thereby helping with food security.The project will also be integrated with an on-site co-generation plant. It is expected that the waste ash from the co-generation plant will be used in the cement operations of Kipas.
additionality: By providing long-term financing for a sizeable project at a difficult time in global markets, IFC will be assisting in the growth of the corrugated paper industry and the development of a competitive business group in a frontier region of Turkey. Kipas could also benefit from IFC''s industry expertise as it diversifies into a new sector and IFC''s environmental and social (E&S) guidelines and performance standards, which encourage more robust E&S assessment and management system and best practice to achieve higher resource efficiency.
Company Name: KIPAS KAGIT SANAYI ISLETMELERI ANONIM SIRKETI

sector: Man-Made Fibers (Including Nylon, Polyester, Rayon, etc.)
project_description: SRF Limited (“SRF”), a large Indian producer of packaging films, is setting up a greenfield 26,000 ton per annum (“TPA”) bi-axially oriented polypropylene (“BOPP”) and 5,700 TPA metallizer plant in Durban, South Africa, to produce packaging films catering to various industries including food production and distribution, at a cost of about US$67 million (“Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in India, SRF is a large company with three main businesses: 1) Technical Textiles (Nylon and polyester tire cord fabric, belting coated and laminated fabrics); 2) Chemicals (Refrigerant gases, Chloromethanes, fluorospecialities); and 3) Packaging Films. It is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) in India. 50% of the company is held by the Bharat Ram family, while 50% is owned by the general public including Foreign Institutional Investors, Mutual Funds, Banks and DFIs.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be about US$67 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$40 million A loan for IFC’s own account. The balance will be funded as equity or sponsor loans by SRF, as well as other long term & short-term loans.
location_description: The company has is in the process of acquiring approximately 70,000 sq. meters of land just outside Durban. The land is suitably zoned, and the process is underway to obtain utilities.
development_impact: (i) Import substitution: Currently, South Africa imports around 20,000 TPA BOPP plain films. The BOPP films produced by this Project will lead to import substitution and eventually facilitate the growth of the local economy. (ii) Job creation: The Project is expected to create more than 200 new jobs during construction and operation. Furthermore, additional jobs will be created through auxiliary services, through the life of the Project. (iii) Environmental and social best practice: A successful implementation of IFC''s Environmental & Social (E&S) standards will serve as an example which other chemical companies might emulate. (iv) Knowledge transfer: SRF''s experience in India and IFC''s technical advice will allow the Sponsor to transfer knowledge of efficient plant management and operations to Africa.
additionality: (i) Demonstration effect of a South-South investment: The Project will facilitate a South-South investment and its success could encourage other Indian companies expand overseas and in Africa in particular. (ii) Long-term foreign currency loan: SRF values IFC''s ability to offer long-term US$ financing, which is not available from local banks. (iii) Long-term partnership opportunities: The success of this Project could lead to other mutual investment opportunities as the Sponsor further expands overseas.

project_description: The greenfield project is to construct a steel fabrication plant in the state of Gujarat, near the city of Vadodara with an annual capacity of 25,000 tons. The plant will manufacture in roughly equal quantity steel structures for transmission & distribution (T&D) projects and metallic support structures for the cylindrical parabolic solar collectors (CPC) and heliostats in concentrated solar power (CSP) projects that will be developed globally, including in India and neighboring countries.
sponsor_shareholders: Inabensa Bharat Private Limited (Inabensa Bharat) is a 100% owned subsidiary of Abengoa S.A. (the Sponsor), a Spanish infrastructure conglomerate operating since 1941, and one of the top global players focusing on technology and engineering solutions for sustainable development. The group has 5 core businesses: Solar, Bio-energy, Environmental, IT and Engineering & Construction
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at 1,002 million Indian Rupee (approximately US$20 million). The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to US$14 million from IFC’s own account.
location_description: The site is 165 Kms from the city of Gandhinagar and 45 Kms from the Vadodara Rail station and 30 Kms from Godhra rail junction.
development_impact: Inabensa Bharat''s operations will support the construction of solar energy plants globally by providing a necessary component in the form of the solar panel structure, thereby encouraging the use of clean energy and reducing CO2 emissions through the implementation of clean energy plants. In addition, Inabensa Bharat will support improvements in the infrastructure supply chain through the increased manufacture and sale of transmission towers across Asia, the Middle East and Sub-Saharan Africa to meet growing demand. As a result of increased focus on transmission capability in India, energy access is expected to improve. Finally, the project will support job creation in India, both during the expansion and operation of the facility, a key objective for the Indian government.
additionality: IFC will support Inabensa Bharat through the provision of long term finance to support development of a greenfield manufacturing plant in India and the acquisition of technology and equipment to improve its delivery of components along the renewable energy and infrastructure supply chains in India and other countries in Asia, Africa and the Middle East. This expansion will enable Inabensa Bharat to establish a stronger presence in India, allowing it to bid for and win turnkey projects in India with companies such as Power Grid. The India plant will also be able to supply solar steel structures to Abengoa''s solar projects globally. IFC will provide technical support to Inabensa Baharat to ensure compliance with IFC''s Environmental & Social Performance Standards. IFC''s support of a subsidiary of Abengoa SA, a leading global player in the area of sustainable energy, will reinforce IFC''s long term strategic partnership with Abengoa SA, supporting the group''s growth plans in emerging markets both in the manufacturing space as well as the downstream implementation of clean energy. While Abengoa is a large group with good banking relationships, Abengoa is relatively highly leveraged and growing in areas IFC would like to encourage and support. As such, the Group will continue to require long-term funding sources in Emerging Markets, providing an opportunity for further collaboration between IFC and Abengoa in the future.

project_description: The Vino Zupa AD project includes a corporate loan of up to EUR 12.5 million for capital investments, including additional bottling and fruit concentrate capacity and investment in the energy block (EUR 3 million); (ii) E&S wastewater treatment improvements to bring the Company into compliance in accordance with IFC Performance Standards and applicable World Bank Group’s Environmental, Health and Safety Guidelines and EU standards (EUR 1.5 million); (iii) re-financing a portion of its existing short / medium term debt facilities (with up to 2 year maturities) on a longer term basis (EUR 6 million); and (iv) provision of additional, permanent working capital (EUR 2 million) (the “Project”). The Project will enhance the Company’s E&S standards and overall performance, reduce funding risk and strengthen the Company’s liquidity position. During appraisal, IFC has also explored possible AS work with regard to supply chain linkages, inclusive business opportunities and sustainable business practices.
sponsor_shareholders: Originally established in 1956, Vino Zupa was privatized in 2002 through an auction and listed on the Belgrade Stock Exchange (ticker VINZ). Following a successful turnaround post privatization, the Company has exhibited strong growth with production per annum increasing from 2 million liters to over 90 million liters in 2010. In the process, EUR 53 million was invested in new equipment and upgrades in order to add new capacity and improve efficiencies, remove production bottlenecks, and settle prior obligations to workers and third parties. The Company is majority owned by Mr. Radimir Sljivic (58%), a Serbian businessman who acquired his stake during privatization with the remaining shares owned by management (12%), several funds and other small shareholders (collectively 30%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project consists of a corporate loan of up to EUR 12.5 million in the form of IFC A loan to be used for capital investments, including additional bottling and fruit concentrate capacity and investment in the energy block (EUR 3 million); (ii) E&S wastewater treatment improvements to bring the Company into compliance in accordance with IFC Performance Standards and applicable World Bank Group’s Environmental, Health and Safety Guidelines and EU standards (EUR 1.5 million); (iii) re-financing a portion of its existing short / medium term debt facilities (with up to 2 year maturities) on a longer term basis (EUR 6 million); and (iv) provision of additional, permanent working capital (EUR 2 million).
location_description: Vino Zupa is located in Alexandrovac, Serbia and Povardarie AD is located in Negotino, FYR Macedonia.
development_impact: The development impact of the project is expected to include: (i) strengthening of agribusiness linkages and indirect support to farmers; (ii) support of a Company based in a frontier region in southern Serbia, one of the least developed areas in the country; (iii) support of an agriculture company involved in value added production and exports in a sector important to the Serbian economy; and (iv) job preservation in a severely underdeveloped region where a substantial portion of the local population depend on the Company for the livelihoods.
additionality: FC is well positioned to assist the Company with long term financing for capital expenditure, to help reduce refinancing risk and to strengthen its balance sheet. Expected IFC additionality includes: (i) Longer tenors: provision of long term financing at reasonable rates suitable to the Company''s needs which is otherwise not readily available in the market; (ii) Financing in a crisis: provision of permanent working capital, reducing refinancing risk; and (iii) Environmental and social standards/implementation: provision of financing and expertise in environmental, health and safety standards by assisting the Company in bringing its wastewater filters into compliance with IFC Performance Standards and EU norms.

sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: Jain Irrigation Systems Ltd. (JISL or the Company) is India’s largest provider of micro-irrigation systems (MIS). In addition to MIS, the Company is also a leading producer of plastic sheets and pipes, agro processed products, tissue culture and green energy. Its headquarters are located in Jalgaon in the western Indian state of Maharashtra. IFC is considering financing part of its capital expenditure project with the total cost of about US$257 million.
sponsor_shareholders: JISL is listed on the National Stock Exchange of India and the Bombay Stock Exchange. The sponsor, the Jain family from Jalgaon, currently owns about 31% of the Company’s shares as of June 30, 2012. The Jain family has been involved in agriculture and plastics businesses since 1960s.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost over the next two years is estimated to be around US$ 257 million including: capital expenditure for expansion of the Company’s production of MIS, food processing, plastic pipes, tissue culture, and solar products in India; capital expenditure for expansion of a MIS plant and working capital requirement for the Company’s operation in Turkey and other region; reduction of short term loans and refinancing of an existing loan. IFC proposes an investment of up to US$ 60 million and mobilization of up to US$ 65 million to part finance this capital expenditure plan.
location_description: JISL operates production facilities for MIS, plastic pipes, plastic sheets, dehydrated vegetables and processed fruits in Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Rajasthan of India and has also invested in companies overseas, such as the United States, UK, Turkey, and Israel. The proposed IFC financing will support JISL’s operations in India as well as its plant in Adana, Turkey and other region.
development_impact: Raising farmer incomes: The adoption of MIS is expected to result in reduced risk from weather, lower cost of farm inputs and an increase in farm yields due to better utilization of inputs. This is expected to improve farmer income and have a direct impact on poverty reduction. Improved water management: India has 16% of the world''s population and only 4% of the water resources. MIS improves water use efficiency from the average 30-40% in India to 80-85%, leading to improved water management resulting in more sustainable growth for the country. Supporting the development of a modern food processing industry: A very low proportion of fruit and vegetable produce is currently processed in India and growth in processed foods is likely to be constrained by lack of a reliable supply chain. JISL is expected to play a key role in not only supplying some of the inputs but in setting the benchmark for other players that enter the market. Employment: Additional employment is expected in India.
additionality: IFC''s role and additionality include: - Continuing financing the growth of a leading local MIS company which promotes the use of more efficient and water-saving agricultural practices in India; - Providing a financing package as JISL''s long term partner with a range of different products (loan, equity/quasi-equity, mobilization) that are not easily available locally; - Supporting the Company''s expansion in overseas market such as Turkey; and - Mobilizing funds from other international financial institutions for the Project.

project_description: SAME DEUTZ FAHR Zetelice d.o.o. is a producer of combine harvesters, located in Zupanja, Croatia. It was privatized in 2005 when it was acquired by the Italian producer of agricultural machinery, SAME DEUTZ FAHR Group SpA (SDF). Since the acquisition, SDF revamped the Company’s operations by modernizing its machinery and operations, consolidating SDF’s European harvest combine production on its site, introducing new products, and making it one of SDF’s main logistics centers. The project consists of introduced leading edge harvesting technology into the Croatian company and gearing it to become a major exporter and distribution center for Europe and the CIS.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor, SAME DEUTZ FAHR GROUP SpA. (SDF), was founded in Treviglio, Italy, in 1927. SDF is an integrated manufacturer of tractors, combine harvesters, specialist harvesters, diesel engines and farm machinery. Its products are marketed under the brands SAME, DEUTZ-FAHR, LAMBORGHINI, HÜRLIMANN and GRÉGOIRE. SDF currently employs approximately 2,800 staff. SDF combines decentralized production activities with a sales and service network providing extensive coverage of all key markets. Sales, after-sales service and parts distribution are handled by 14 subsidiaries, 120 importers, and 3,000 dealers located in all parts of the world. Based on higher demand growth in the emerging markets, SDF is increasing its presence in these markets.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at Euro25 million and the proposed IFC investment is Euro15 million C loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project is located at the existing site in Industririjska 5, 32270, Županja, Croatia.
development_impact: 1. Contribution to food security. Based on competitive cost structure, quality, efficient distribution network and service, the projects are expected to increase the availability of tractors and harvest combines in their regions. This, in turn, should help improve the agricultural productivity and thus output, and contribute to food security. 2. Contribution to rural development: Increased mechanization of the agriculture in the region is expected to lead to higher farmer income as well as development of small businesses that provide spare parts and maintenance/ repair services for the agricultural machinery. 3. Job preservation in a frontier region. By supporting the continuation of the Croatian Company''s post-privatization restructuring, IFC''s investment is expected to ensure the preservation of at least 300 jobs at the plant, and help increase indirect employment in the supply chain and distribution network of the SDF group in the region through the Company''s growth.
additionality: 1. Counter cyclical role. Current market conditions in Europe magnifies IFC''s countercyclical role as most of the European banks, especially the Italian banks that are active in eastern Europe, have been limiting their exposure to emerging markets due to funding and capital constraints. In this regard, IFC would be supporting a second tier European company within the context of IFC response to the European crisis. 2. Longer term flexible financing structure. The proposed loan structures fits well with the needs of SDF, which is not available from other sources especially during the current market conditions. In the context of the evolving European crisis, access to long term finance has been limited especially for second tier European companies.

project_description: SAME DEUTZ FAHR INDIA Ltd has been for more than a decade an integrated producer of 35/70-horse power tractors and tractor engines for local markets and for exports. To keep up with increasing demand, the company is undertaking a project to increase its tractor production, aligning itself with European methods and standards, and restructure its balance sheet to sustain long-term growth.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is SAME DEUTZ FAHR GROUP SpA. (SDF), founded in Treviglio, Italy, in 1927. SDF is an integrated manufacturer of tractors, combine harvesters, specialist harvesters, diesel engines and farm machinery. Its products are marketed under the brands SAME, DEUTZ-FAHR, LAMBORGHINI, HÜRLIMANN and GRÉGOIRE. SDF currently employs approximately 2,800 staff. SDF combines decentralized production activities with a sales and service network providing extensive coverage of all key markets. Sales, after-sales service and parts distribution are handled by 14 subsidiaries, 120 importers, and 3,000 dealers located in all parts of the world. Based on higher demand growth in the emerging markets, SDF is increasing its presence in these markets.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at Euro38 million and the proposed IFC investment is Euro15 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project site is in the SIPCOT Industrial Complex in Ranipet-Vellore, Tamil Nadu, India.
development_impact: 1. Contribution to food security. Based on competitive cost structure, quality, efficient distribution network and service, the projects are expected to increase the availability of tractors and harvest combines in their regions. This, in turn, should help improve the agricultural productivity and thus output, and contribute to food security. 2. Contribution to rural development. Increased mechanization of the agriculture in the region is expected to lead to higher farmer income as well as development of small businesses that provide spare parts and maintenance repair services for the agricultural machinery. 3. Job preservation in an IDA-blend country.
additionality: 1. Counter cyclical role. Current market conditions in Europe magnifies IFC''s countercyclical role as most of the European banks, especially the Italian banks, have been limiting their exposure to emerging markets due to funding and capital constraints. In this regard, IFC would be supporting a second tier European company within the context of IFC response to the European crisis. 2. Longer term flexible financing structure. The proposed loan structures fits well with the needs of SDF, which is not available from other sources especially during the current market conditions. In the context of the evolving European crisis, access to long term finance has been limited especially for second tier European companies. 3. Catalyst role in access to local financing. IFC''s investment in SDF''s Indian subsidiary is expected to play a catalyst role in broadening its relationships with Indian financial institutions for the financing of its distribution network and retail customers. SDF India is currently searching for a bank to help finance its dealers and IFC can help play a role in this effort.

project_description: Ngon Coffee Company Limited, Vietnam (“NCL”) was established in 2009 as an instant coffee manufacturer in the Dak Lak province of Vietnam. NCL has recently completed the construction of a greenfield instant coffee manufacturing facility with a processing capacity of 10,000 MTPA. It now plans to add ancillary equipment and utilities at the facility and also secure financing for its working capital requirements.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is CCL Products (India) Limited (“CCL”), an instant / soluble coffee processor in India set up in 1995. NCL is a wholly owned subsidiary of Jayanti Pte Limited, Singapore, which in turn is a wholly owned subsidiary of CCL. CCL exports instant coffee to second tier brands and private labels in over 58 countries. It has a plant with processing capacity of 15,000 metric tons per annum (“MTPA”) in Andhra Pradesh, India and a granulation-cum-packaging plant with a capacity of 3,000 MTPA in Switzerland. CCL is promoted by Mr. Challa Rajendra Prasad, who together with his family, holds a 35.25% stake in CCL. The remaining stake is held by foreign collaborators (13.4%), institutional investors (15.91%) and other public shareholders (35.43%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost including the greenfield plant which is already completed, the proposed expansion and working capital requirements, is estimated at US$50 million. IFC proposes an A loan of up to US$20 million for its own account.
location_description: The project is located in the Cu Kuin Industrial Complex, Dak Lak Province, Vietnam
development_impact: Economic value addition and employment generation in Vietnam Expansion of a mid-scale Indian company in Vietnam will have a demonstration effect for other Indian companies considering similar avenues for growth. Positive environmental impact: Ngon Coffee recycles solid waste generated during the production of instant coffee to be used as biomass fuel, thus conserving scarce fossil fuel and reducing environmental pollution
additionality: Long term partner: With presence in both India and Vietnam, IFC can act as a long term partner as NCL establishes itself in a new geography / market. Expertise: NCL can leverage IFC''s knowledge, experience and relationships in the industry. Further, there is a potential to help the company improve environment, safety and quality standards.

project_description: The IFC investment will support Vegpro Ghana (“VGL” or the “Project”), a Ghanaian company associated with Vegpro Kenya Limited (“VKL” or the “Company”), Kenya’s largest vegetable producer, processor and exporter. The Project consists of: (1) setting up of a 1,070 hectares (ha) commercial farm to produce vegetables on land leased from the Government of Ghana on a 50-year renewable lease; (2) development of 768 ha equipped with 12 Centre Pivot Irrigation Systems each covering 64 ha; (3) procurement of farm equipment and refrigerated vehicles and (4) construction of a bespoke pack house on the farm for packing and processing vegetables for export to UK and EU markets.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is Vegpro Kenya Limited while the major shareholders are James Cartwright and Bharat Patel who each own 50 percent of VGL. Bharat Patel co-founded Vegpro Kenya Limited in 1979 and is the Managing Director of VKL. James Cartwright is the Business Development Director of VKL and has over 36 years of experience in horticulture; joined VKL in 1995.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is $14 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $7 million secured A loan to VGL to support the Project.
location_description: VGL is located at Kpong in the South of Ghana, approximately 86 km from Accra. The site is in Torgome (Sokope) in the North Tongu District in the Volta Region of the Republic of Ghana.
development_impact: The proposed Project will help a) create employment for up to 1500 people; b) develop the horticulture industry in Ghana; c) develop a network of suppliers of goods and services (inputs, transportation, maintenance; equipment, etc) which has industry-wide benefits; d) provide access to export market for 200 smallholder farmers which should improve their incomes and e) contribute to food security through the production of maize for the local market and increased incomes of employees and smallholders.
additionality: IFC will provide: (i) funds at a longer tenor and grace period than generally available in the market which is critical for this Greenfield project; (ii) the company with political risk mitigation in its South-South investment; (iii) advisory capacity building to small farmers as needed and (iv) assist Vegpro to implement environmental and social standards that will form a benchmark for projects in the horticulture sector in Ghana. Vegpro is also keen to work with IFC ti improve Corporate Governance and to establish a more efficient corporate structure.

project_description: This SII was disclosed in November 10, 2009 under Titan Egypt, Project #27022, which was approved by IFC Board in December 2009. In October 2010, prior to IFC disbursement, an internal product change was done via the system, and as a result of this internal system split, a new project identification and number (Alexandria Development Limited, ADL, Project #30274) were generated. Based on operational procedures, there was no need for a new disclosure at that time, given that the change of to the project identification and number were only due to an internal product change, and the original entities involved, the requirements and the project scope remained unchanged. Titan Group, an existing IFC client and Greece’s leading private cement company, is seeking to expand its cooperation with IFC in its Egyptian operations which consist of two entities: Beni Suef Cement Company (“BSCC”) and Alexandria Portland Cement Company (“APCC”), (together, the ”Company”). BSCC and APCC have a combined production capacity of 3.5 million tons per annum (“mtpa”) and are engaged in an investment program to add a second integrated cement production line of 1.5 mtpa in BSCC, and various debottlenecking investments in both plants (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Titan Cement Company S.A. (“Titan” or the “Sponsor”) is an independent cement and building materials producer with over 100 years of industry experience. Based in Greece, Titan Group has a presence in 12 countries half of which are in emerging markets, owning 12 cement plants. Titan is listed on the Athens Stock Exchange and is a core member of the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. In 2008 Titan Group sold over 17.2 m. tones of cement and cementitious materials, 5.4 m.m3 of ready mix concrete, 18.6 m. tones of aggregates and various other building materials like concrete blocks, dry mortars etc.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost of Beni Suef’s second line and debottlenecking at both plants is estimated at around EUR180 million (the “Project”). IFC is considering a potential investment in Titan Egypt.
location_description: Titan’s Egyptian operations consist of: Beni Suef Cement Company (“BSCC”), established in 1993 and located about 120 km south of Cairo. BSCC has access to abundant raw materials which are in close proximity to the plant. BSCC has a current capacity of 1.5 mtpa which is expected to reach 3.0 mtpa once the new line is completed; and Alexandria Portland Cement Company (“APCC”), established in 1948 and rehabilitated in 2000. It is located 5 km from the Mediterranean Sea and has a current cement capacity of 2 mtpa. APCC is listed on the Egyptian Stock Exchange (“ESE”).
development_impact: Key development impacts of the Project in the local economy include the following: support to the construction and infrastructure sectors: the Project will provide new capacity to a growing market characterized by a pressing need in low income housing as well as numerous construction projects, eg new communities (New Cairo, Emaar projects), colleges (AUC etc), financial and other campuses (Smart city for telecom etc); benefit to consumers: consumers are expected to benefit from increased local availability of cement; employment retention and generation: the Project will help retain current employment as well as generate new employment in the local community, both temporarily during the construction phase as well as permanently during operations; and environment and social standards: the Project and the Company are expected to achieve higher environmental and social performance, therefore minimizing impact on the local communities.

company_name: INDORAMA ELEME FERTILIZER AND CHEMICALS FZE
project_description: The Project (‘Eleme Fertilizer’) consists of the construction of a nitrogenous Fertilizer Complex at the existing Eleme Petrochemicals site in Port-Harcourt, Nigeria. The project will include an Ammonia plant, a Urea production plant, supporting boundary infrastructure, and an 84km gas pipeline from the gas supplier’s facilities. Total plant capacity will be 2,300 metric tons per day (MTPD) of ammonia, and 4,000 MTPD of granulated urea. A new port terminal will also be constructed at the nearby Onne Port to support the fertilizer complex; however the port is not being financed by the IFC. With exception of the external natural gas facilities, all main associated off sites and utilities necessary to make the fertilizer plant self-supporting are already in existence at the Eleme Petrochemicals Complex. At completion, Eleme Fertilizer will supply the domestic fertilizer market in Nigeria, and also export directly into the international urea market. The plant is expected to be completed and commence operations by early 2016. The IFC plans to support the project by providing senior debt, mobilizing 3rd party funding, and potentially making an equity investment.
sponsor_shareholders: The project company is Indorama Eleme Fertilizer & Chemicals Limited (IEFCL), which is owned 51% by Indorama Eleme Petrochemicals Limited (or ‘Eleme Petrochemicals’), and 49% by the Indorama Group. Eleme Petrochemicals is the largest producer of polyolefins in West Africa, and the 2nd largest in Africa. It is owned by the Indorama Group 65%, Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) 10%, Rivers State Government 10%, Host Communities 7.5%, the Nigerian Federal Government 5%, and Employees 2.5%. Indorama Group is a leading manufacturer of petrochemicals and associated downstream products shipped to over 100 countries across the globe. Indorama employs over 21,600 personnel, and has 40 manufacturing sites in 20 countries. Indorama is wholly controlled and beneficially held by Mr. S. P. Lohia and his family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fertilizer complex will cost US$1.2 billion. Details of the proposed investment are as follows (i) An ‘A-loan’ of US$150m for IFC’s own account (ii) A mobilization tranche of US$150m comprising of an IFC B-loan and parallel loans (under IFC’s Master Corporation Agreement - MCA) , and (iii) a potential equity investment
location_description: The Fertilizer complex will be located within the existing Eleme Petrochemicals premises, which is one of the major large scale industrial units in the oil belt of Port-Harcourt, Rivers State, in the South-Southern region of Nigeria. Eleme Petrochemicals complex is currently self- sufficient in offsite, utility, storage, administration, safety, and commercial activities. The complex site covers a fully developed, and secured area of c.361 hectares. The new fertilizer plant will require about c.38 hectares.
development_impact: The expected development benefits from the project are: (i) Food Security: Contribution to the development of the agricultural sector and unlocking its potential, thereby reducing Nigeria''s dependence on imports. The project will increase fertilizer production which promotes intensive agricultural production, and will improve crop yields. (ii) Economic Diversification: Increased value addition to a natural resource in Nigeria (i.e. natural gas), and advancement of the downstream chemicals sector. The project supports regional fertilizer capacity in Sub-Saharan Africa, which is a growing market heavily reliant on imports. (iii) Employment: Creation of significant direct and indirect employment opportunities. (iv) SME Development: Removal of obstacles that prevent farmers with small land holds from efficiently optimizing their crop yields and maximizing their incomes. (v) Current Account Impact: Foreign exchange savings by import substitution. (vi) Demonstration Effect: The project is expected to have a positive signal for other foreign investors on the government''s commitment for economic diversification and agricultural transformation project
Company Name: INDORAMA ELEME FERTILIZER AND CHEMICALS FZE

project_description: Hans Merensky Holdings Proprietary Limited (“HMH” or the “Company’) is a South African vertically integrated natural resource company with over 60 years operating history in the forestry and sub-tropical fruit industries. The Company is the largest grower and exporter of avocados out of Africa, and a leading player in South Africa’s timber industry through its timber plantations and sawmilling operations. HMH is embarking on a capital expenditure program that will expand and upgrade its timber processing capacity and increase the production of avocados in existing markets as well as new markets.
sponsor_shareholders: HMH’s majority shareholder is the Hans Merensky Foundation (“HM Foundation”) with a 50.1% shareholding. The HM Foundation’s primary mandate is to promote science by driving the Company’s research and development strategies. The second largest shareholder with 37% shareholding is Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa Limited, a government-owned development finance institution whose objectives include the development of the South Africa’s industrial capacity and implementing the Country’s industrial policy. The other shareholders are Vuka (5.1%), WIPHOLD (4.1%) and an HMH Employee Share Option Plan (3.7%) which are Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (“BBBEE”) shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project is estimated at ZAR 1.043 billion. IFC is contemplating a minority equity investment of up to 20%, which will contribute to financing the Company’s capital expenditure over a five year development period. The balance of the project funding is to be provided by other commercial lenders as well as internally generated funds.
location_description: HMH is headquartered at 9 Eton Road, Parktown, Johannesburg, South Africa. The Group’s site locations include: Limpopo province (South Africa) – 10 700 ha of Eucalyptus plantations, 1 timber processing facility, 1 321 ha of avocado orchards with a packhouse, processing plants for avocado puree, dried mango, fruit juice, avocado oil and avocado ripening; Mpumalanga (South Africa) - 5 800 ha of mainly hard wood timber plantations; Kwa-Zulu Natal (South Africa) – 40 700 ha of Pine plantations, 2 timber processing facility, 286 ha of avocado orchards with a packhouse and 1 processing plant for avocado oil; Eastern Cape (South Africa) – 17 000 ha of Pine plantations and1 timber processing facility; Western Cape (South Africa) – 1 avocado ripening facility; Kent (United Kingdom) – avocado and exotic fruits ripening and distribution facilities; Rungis Zone Euro Delta (France) – avocado and exotic fruits ripening and distribution facilities; Maasdijk (Holland) - avocado and exotic fruits distribution facilities; Peru – 120 ha of existing and 390 ha of proposed avocado orchards through a joint venture; Columbia – 1 proposed avocado packhouse; and Mexico – 100 ha proposed avocado orchard.
development_impact: The development impact of the project is expected to include: Employment creation: The Company has about 4,300 employees. The expansion of its operations and market position in South Africa and South America is expected to lead to the creation of more jobs. Rural Development: The project will make significant contribution to the development of rural communities in South Africa. Women Inclusion: The project will enhance inclusion as a significant number of the Company''s business units employ largely women. Increased tax and export revenue for government.

project_description: The MCS Group of companies (“MCS Group” or the “Sponsor”), IFC’s repeat client and one of Mongolia’s leading business groups active in (i) distributing fast-moving consumer goods; (ii) beverage manufacturing; (ii) mobile communications and information technologies; (iii) civil engineering and infrastructure development, (iv) mining, as well as in a number of other industry sectors, is expanding the scale of its property development operations, which are currently focused on a large-scale affordable housing development in Ulaanbaatar (“UB”). MCS Group’s property-focused subsidiary MCS Properties Holdings Ltd (BVI) (“MCS Property”, “MCSP” or the “Company”) has requested a long-term IFC loan of up to US$60 million, which will be used (i) to complete the Company’s affordable housing development “Shine Ger” in UB; (ii) to build an affordable housing residential complex in the vicinity of the Ukhaa Khudag (“UHG”) mine site, 500 kilometers to the south of UB, as well as (iii) to develop an office tower, which will be an important contribution to the Mongolian capital business infrastructure, and a school building in UB (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Founded by prominent Mongolian businessmen, Mr Odjargal Jambaljamts and Mr Od Jambaljamts, in 1993, MCS Group is currently 74% owned by the founders, while the remaining shares belong to the Sponsor’s senior management. MCS Group first became IFC’s client in 2008. Since then, the Group has significantly strengthened its positions in the role as Mongolia’s (i) sole distributor of Procter & Gamble products; (ii) largest manufacturer and distributor of soft drinks and beer under licenses from Coca Cola and Asia Pacific Brewery; as well as (iii) the country’s 2nd-largest operator of a mobile communications network “Unitel” and became a strong player in many other businesses. The proposed repeat IFC investment in the MCS Group subsidiary MCSP is expected to help the Sponsor emerge as a leader in Mongolia’s property development sector. MCS Property is a fully-owned subsidiary of the Sponsor specifically incorporated to consolidate the Group’s expertise in construction management, property development and property management. It has successfully participated in a number of residential, commercial and industrial developments, mainly related to other businesses of the MCS Group. Currently, the Company is in the process of scaling up its market presence, with the completion of a 1,642-unit affordable housing development “Shine Ger” to become MCS Group’s first hallmark project in the property development industry.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an MCS Group-guaranteed A loan of up to US$60 million to the Company to finance part of the cost of the Project, which is currently estimated at US$123 million. The remainder of the Project will be financed with proceeds from pre-sales of apartments and shareholder loans from the Sponsor.
location_description: The office tower included in the Project will be built in the central areas of UB. The Shine Ger affordable housing development is being constructed on the outskirts of UB, approximately 50 kilometers from the central part of the city. In addition, the Project includes affordable housing in the vicinity of the UHG mine site, 500 kilometers to the south of UB. All the Project sites have adequate access to all the necessary infrastructure.
development_impact: (i) The Company''s activities are focused on improving UB''s urban infrastructure. As such, they have a direct and immediate development impact with respect to improvements in living standards and inefficiency of doing business in Mongolia''s capital. In particular, the Company''s pipeline of properties scheduled for completion in the near future includes socially important developments, such as 1,617 affordable housing units in an innovative and replicable "Shine Ger" project with the goal to make home ownership affordable for young professional families; (ii) MCSP is an important source of indirect employment with 4,782 indirect employees (e.g. contractors); (iii) Through increased purchasing local materials and services, the expansion of MCSP activities will strengthen the Company''s linkages to the local economy; (iv) MCSP is committed to bringing international property development standards and best practices to a country where the quality of construction needs to be drastically improved; (v) The MCS Tower included in the Project will contribute to the development of the UB business infrastructure that lacks quality office buildings at this point in time.

project_description: The Project will support LLC Astarta-Kyiv (the “Company” or “Astarta”), a leading primary agriculture producer in Ukraine with 240,000 ha of land under cultivation. Astarta’s principal activities include (i) production of sugar beet and sugar processing, and (ii) production of other crops including wheat, barley, corn, sunflower, and soya. The Company owns and operates 8 sugar plants across 7 business units and 4 operational regions in Ukraine. IFC''s financing will support one of the leading grain and sugar producers in Ukraine. IFC financing will support the (i) construction of a 700 tpd soybean crushing facility to process locally grown soybeans into meal for the local market and oil, potentially for export, (ii) construction of a biogas facility, (iii) expansion of agricultural land, (iv) purchase of supporting farm machinery, storage and dairy infrastructure to increase production volumes of crops and (iv) further modernization of sugar production and storage capacity. IFC''s financing will also support a viable economic activity and create new jobs in some of the poorest frontier rural regions of Ukraine (Vinnytsya, Khmelnytsky, among others).
sponsor_shareholders: 36.99% of Astarta is owned by Viktor Ivanchyk and 25.99% by Valery Korotkov, with the remaining 37.02% floated on the Warsaw Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide corporate financing to the Company in the form of an up to US$50 million long-term loan to support Astarta’s on-going modular investment program aimed at providing value addition and diversification to its main business units. The IFC long-term loan will partly finance the Company’s FY2012-2013 capex program of approximately US$175 million. The remaining portion of the capex will be financed from long term loans from other financial institutions and internal cash generation.
location_description: Astarta is headquartered in Kiev, Ukraine. The company conducts modern farming operations on 240,000 ha of leased land in over four regions across Ukraine: Khmelnytsky, Vinnytsya, Poltova, and Kharkiv.
development_impact: The project is to support the growth and diversification of one of the leading farm enterprises in Ukraine, engaged in the production of crops, sugar and milk. The corporate investment program will include in particular: (i) a cost reduction program for sugar production; (ii) a biogas capture component that will both reduce GHG emissions and improve energy efficiency in processing; and, (iii) a soybean processing project that will add value to the local production of soybeans while serving the needs of the fast developing livestock and poultry sector. This program will contribute to the growth of the Ukrainian economy, to global food security by increasing production of key crops exported from Ukraine, while supporting direct and indirect employment in rural areas where alternative job opportunities remain scarce.

project_description: As one the largest wood flooring companies in China, China Flooring Holding Company limited (“Nature” or the “Company”) plans to engage more in the upstream forestry plantation business in China to meet its expanding fiber needs in a sustainable manner. IFC financing will support acquisition and development of forestry plantation assets in China to support its wood flooring business.
sponsor_shareholders: Nature is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange since May 2011. The Project Sponsor is Mr. Se Hok Pan, the founder and Chairman of the Company. The current shareholding structure of the Company is: (i) IFC 7.2%; (ii) Mr. Se Hok Pan and his family 48.6%; (iii) Morgan Stanley Private Equity Asia (“MSPEA”) 17.9%, and (iv) Public Float 26.3%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: As the Company grows it seeks to develop plantation resources which it can control and which hedge against future wood price increases. Specifically, Nature is seeking for a potential acquisition plantation forests in the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region of China (“the Project”). At the time of this disclosure, the consideration of the Project by the Company is at early stage and there is no certainty of completion. The Company has not signed any letter of intention or any legally binding agreement for the Project. IFC is proposing a US$40m financing package to support the development of forest resources business of the Company, including the Project.
location_description: The project will be located at rural areas of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region of China, where there are existing forestry plantation operations and basic infrastructure, such as forestry roads.
development_impact: The Project is expected to: (i) support the sustainable economic development and natural resources management in the frontier region; (ii) create more than 200 direct jobs (based on the projected plantation size achieved) and improve local livelihoods in rural/frontier Chinese provinces; and (iii) have a strong demonstration effect for China forestry sector to support legal and certified forestry operations.

sector: Miscellaneous and Industrial Ores (Including Magnesite, Fluorite, Sulfur, Soda Ash, Clays, Gypsum, Lime, Peat, Boron, Diatomite, Feldspar, etc.)
project_description: The Project consists of Calidra’s investment plan in Mexico and South America to be implemented over the 2012-2014 period, geared primarily towards: (i) equipment purchases for the modernization of existing plants and acquisitions/JVs within Mexico, (ii) construction of one-two production sites in Peru and (iii) construction of one-two production sites in Colombia together with Cementos Argos (joint venture partner with Calidra).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Grupo Calida (“Calidra” or the “Company”). Calidra was founded in 1908 and is the leading producer of lime and limestone related products in Mexico. The Company is privately owned by two major shareholders (shareholder groups), Riefkohl family members (55%) and Graymont (Canadian lime producer) (45%). Graymont is a family owned company focused on high calcium and dolomitic lime, value added lime based products such as specialty hydrates and precipitated calcium carbonates, and in the aggregate and pulverized stone business. Graymont is the third largest lime producer in the world.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$188.2 million. The proposed financial plan includes a combination of US$98.2 million internal cash generation and US$90 million debt from IFC and a/the commercial bank(s) under the IFC B Loan. IFC will provide an up to US$50 million A Loan for its own account and mobilize an up to US$40 million B loan from a/the commercial bank(s).
location_description: The Project’s capital investments will be deployed throughout Grupo Calidra’s production plants in Mexico and in one to two locations, either greenfield or existing, in each country Peru and Colombia.
development_impact: The following summary development impacts are expected to be achieved: maintaining profitability, achieving cost-energy efficiency, using alternative fuels and raising environmental, health and safety standards.

company_name: MODERN KARTON SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
sector: Paper Packaging Products (Including Boxes, Cartons, etc.)
project_description: Modern Karton Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (Modern Karton or the Company), an existing IFC client since 1998, is engaged in manufacturing of cardboard (i.e., testliner, white-top testliner and fluting) from waste paper and straw pulp since 1998. Being the domestic leader in corrugated paper business, the Company is the flagship company of Eren Group in paper and packaging business with its operating facilities that have 600,000 tons per annum production capacity. This major player in the corrugated paper and cardboard industry in Europe and Middle East is seeking to expand its cooperation with IFC in establishing a waste water recovery system with 15,600 m3/day treatment capacity utilizing ultra filtration and reverse osmosis technologies (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Eren Group is a diversified industrial group with operations in the paper, energy, cement, textiles and retail sectors through more than 20 companies. It is ultimately owned by Eren Family. The main vehicle of Eren Family to manage and control its various investments in Eren Group companies is Eren Holding A.S.. Eren Holding’s consolidated revenues in 2011 were at US$1.3 billion on total assets of over US$2.0 billion. This privately owned local holding company controls Modern Karton through its 93% shareholding while remaining minority stake is owned by individual member of Eren Family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated cost of the Project is US$11 million and IFC is considering to provide up to US$8 million loan to Modern Karton from the cleaner production lending facility as a cleaner production loan.
location_description: The project site will be adjacent to the Company’s existing premises in Corlu/Tekirdag (Turkey), 100 km west of Istanbul. The site is in an industrial zone and has good access to land transportation by being next to the highway.
development_impact: - Resource Efficiency: Thanks to the environmental and climate friendly benefits of the Project, at optimum capacity after implementation Modern Karton will be able to consume less fresh water and discharge less waste water per paper produced compared to the current levels. - Demonstration Effect: The Project is likely to have strong demonstration and replication potential thanks to being a pioneering investment in the sector.
Company Name: MODERN KARTON SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: The proposed investment would support Kuibyshevazot Open Joint Stock Company (KuAz) in implementation of its energy efficiency and cleaner production program. The program is expected to result in significant energy savings and reduction of greenhouse gases emissions.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Kuibyshevazot Open Joint Stock Company, existing IFC client. Located in Togliatti, Samara region, KuAz is the leading Russian manufacturer of caprolactam (the raw material for synthetic fibers, engineering plastics, automotive and other downstream products) and one of the top Russian producers of nitrogenous fertilizers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at around US$54 million. The proposed IFC investment is a senior loan of up to US$10.0 million.
location_description: Project investments will be implemented in Togliatti, Samara region, Russian Federation.
development_impact: Investment to be financed under the proposed project will help KuAz implement its energy efficiency and clean production program, and ultimately achieve reduction of greenhouse gases emissions and reduction in energy consumption.

project_description: The Project consists of an up to R500mn (~$65mn) funded risk participations in Standard Chartered Bank South Africa (“SCB” or the “Bank”) financing facilities to the Farmsecure group of companies (“Farmsecure” or the “Group”), for the provision of pre-harvest working capital to contracted farmers in grains and livestocks and own production in fruits. The facilities also cover other working capital needs of the Group. Among others, the financing facility will be used for input financing (e.g. seeds, fertilizer, agrochemicals), purchase of weaner calves/lambs for rearing and payment of insurance premiums and other marketing expenses.
sponsor_shareholders: Farmsecure is an active participant and specialized agribusiness service and input provider operating in South Africa. Its core business is development and optimization of farming enterprises through its contracting and farmer partnership schemes which include the provision of services for the mitigation of climatic risk (through insurance) and price risk (through hedging). Farmsecure also provides farmers with technical advice and crop marketing. Farmsecure''s main business segments are: (i) grain production, (ii) livestock, (iii) own fruit production and fruit exports, (iv) distribution of fertilizers, and (v) provision of technical services. Farmescure is owned by four shareholders: (i) The Jerogene Trust, a trust related to the Yazbek founder family (40,95%), (ii) The Trio Farms Trust, a trust related to the three founder executives: Schalk Lubbe, Johnny Maass, and Erick de Klerk (20,25%), (iii) the Sameer Group (28,8%), a major Kenya based conglomerate with interests in agriculture, banking, construction and IT sectors controlled by Mr. Naushad Merali; and (iv) Deutsche Investitions- und Entwicklungsgesellschaft mbH (DEG), a subsidiary of the German promotional bank KfW a German investment and development company focusing on investments in emerging markets (10%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC funded risk participation in SCB’s financing is capped at R500 mn. IFC’s maximum participation would not exceed 50% of SCB’s total facilities to Farmsecure. The IFC participation will have tenor of one year and be renewable up to two times.
location_description: Farmsecure is headquartered in Cape Town (South Africa) and its operations are well spread across South Africa, with fertilizer business throughout the Southern Africa. The IFC risk participation concerns the South Africa operations only.
development_impact: Farmsecure is having a significant developmental impact by promoting a more productive and sustainable agri-business model in South Africa. The Project is expected in turn to make a significant contribution to South Africa''s rural economic development, as well as to global food security by increasing access to sustainable and profitable farming structures for farmers. This means that Farmsecure''s focus includes the empowerment of farmers with scientific farming skills, agricultural knowledge and technologies, and hands-on support to assist farmers in fulfilling their maximum potential both in terms of yield and revenues, positioning the Company ahead of the field in the region''s agricultural development. Farmsecure works on a commercial farming basis with a long term goal to further develop small scale farming supported by the infrastructure of sustainable commercial farming.

company_name: FALCON HOUSE PARTNERS INDONESIA FUND I, LP
project_description: Falcon House Partners Indonesia Fund I, L.P. (FHP I or the Fund), a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership, is a private equity fund seeking US$200 million in capital commitments to invest in middle-market growth-oriented companies formed and operated in Indonesia.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by Falcon House Capital Management Ltd. (the Manager) who has offices in Indonesia and Singapore. The Fund is the first private equity fund managed by the Manager who currently comprises of Mr. Glenn Yusuf, Mr. Samir Soota and Mr. Brian O’Connor.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to make an equity investment of up to US$25 million in the Fund, not to exceed 20% of the total commitments of the Fund.
location_description: The Fund will invest primarily in mid-market companies in Indonesia.
development_impact: The Fund would help private sector development through supporting growth and operational improvement of its portfolio companies. The Project would support private equity investments in Indonesia, helping develop the financial markets in the country.
Company Name: FALCON HOUSE PARTNERS INDONESIA FUND I, LP

project_description: Alliance Tire Group (ATG or the Company) manufactures off-highway tires that are used in agricultural, forestry, construction and earth-moving equipment. ATG has a 48,000 tonnes per annum (tpa) plant in India in a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) near Tirunelveli, India that is in the process of being expanded to 61,000 tpa and 35,000 tpa plant near Hadera, Israel. The Company plans to expand its Indian operations via: (i) the construction of a greenfield plant with a capacity of 50,000 tpa in Jhagadia Kharchi Extension in Gujarat; (ii) a further expansion of 29,000 tpa in Tirunelveli; and (iii) the installation of a cogeneration plant at Tirunelveli (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: ATG was established in 2007 and is a privately held company. ATG acquired Alliance Tire Company Israel (Alliance Israel) in 2007 and commenced the construction of its first Indian manufacturing facility in 2008. ATG is promoted by private equity firm Warburg Pincus, which has a majority stake in the Company and Mr. Ashok Mahansaria and his son, Mr. Yogesh Mahansaria.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at US$160 million. IFC proposes a financial investment of up to US$65 million for its own account and will try to mobilize additional funds to finance a part of the expansion.
location_description: The greenfield facility will be located near Jhagadia in Gujarat, India, in close proximity to the port of Hazira. The Project also involves the brownfield expansion of the Company’s facility in Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu.
development_impact: 1. Technology transfer and enhancing India''s competitiveness: Innovation and technological ability are critical to the development of off-highway tires, a high-value niche segment of the global tire industry. The Project will increase the competitiveness of the Indian OHT manufacturing sector as a result of shared R & D and technology between ATC India and its associate companies, Alliance Tire Company Ltd., Israel and Alliance Tire Americas Inc., USA. 2. Employment generation: The Project will create direct employment for about 850 people. ATG is committed to developing and strengthening its employees'' technical expertise and engineers from each of its Israel and India facilities are often sent to the other location to conduct training. In addition, the Project will create temporary employment during its construction phase. 3. Agricultural productivity: Almost 60% of ATG''s sales are to the agriculture equipment sector, where increasing productivity is critical to meet increasing food demand. ATG invests significant resources in its research and development and conducts extensive testing to ensure its tires are designed to increase the productivity of the equipment on which they are used.

project_description: The Trans-Oil group of companies (“T-O”), a leading integrated agro-industrial group focused on grain origination trading and oilseed crushing in Moldova, is seeking financing to support (i) its capital expenditure program, including capacity expansion, energy efficiency investments and environmental upgrades; (ii) its acquisition of five additional elevators and an 87% stake in Moldova’s leading oilseed processor, Floarea Soarelui (“FS”, and together with T-O, the “Group”); and (iii) refinancing of short term debt to strengthen its capital structure (collectively, the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Group is owned and controlled by Mr. Vaja Jhashi, a Georgian and US citizen (the “Sponsor”) with extensive experience in trading in the region.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is US$110 million. IFC is considering an investment up to US$70 million in the Group to involve a combination of A, B and C Loans. The balance of the Project will be financed with equity from the Sponsor, and internal cash generation.
location_description: The Group is headquartered in Chisinau, Moldova. The Project would support the Group’s operations across Moldova. To date, the Group has operations in Belti, 137 km north of Chisinau); Giurgiulesti port, located on the southern tip of Moldova; Ciadir Lunga, located in the rural south of Moldova in addition to commodity silos located across Moldova.
development_impact: The expected development impact includes the following: (i) improve efficiencies of under-performing acquisition assets; (ii) support the competitiveness of a leading Group operating in a key sector to Moldova''s economy; (iii) realize benefits to local farmers in the form of integrating farmers with higher value added domestic and international markets and increased access to finance for farmers; (iv) encourage local and regional companies to consider investments in Moldova by demonstrating a successful test case; and (v) job preservation and increased tax revenues.

company_name: COOPERATIVA NACIONAL DE PRODUCTORES DE LECHE
project_description: Cooperativa Nacional de Productores de Leche (“Conaprole”) is Uruguay’s leading dairy producer and one of the lowest cost producers in the world. Conaprole has eight production plants that produce a wide range of dairy products including liquid milk, milk powder, yogurt, cheese, butter, ice cream, and milk by-products. Conaprole exports 55% of production, mainly in the form of milk powder. The Project entails capacity expansion at two production plants. At the Villa Rodriguez plant (“VR” or “Plant 8”), the existing powdered milk capacity of one 6 tons/hour spray drier with associated evaporator will be progressively expanded by the addition of a second evaporator, then a second spray drier and finally a third evaporator, to develop capacity to produce 12 tons /hour of whole or skim milk powder, with supporting investment in milk reception and processing and in utility systems. At the Montevideo plant (“CIM”), the Project will expand production capacity for ice cream, desserts and yoghurt production, again with supporting investment in factory infrastructure. The Project will increase raw milk reception from farmers by about one third.
sponsor_shareholders: Conaprole is a Uruguayan cooperative established in 1936 and owned by about 1,500 dairy farmers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$90 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$30 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The new powder milk plant will be constructed at Conaprole’s existing plant located in Villa Rodriguez (Plant #8), Department of San Jose, about 100 km west of Montevideo. In addition, Conaprole will invest in the upgrade of its value added lines in Centro Industrial Montevideo (CIM), located in the city of Montevideo.
development_impact: - Raw milk production is the primary source of income for over 2,000 farmers, especially in the frontier region of Rivera. The additional capacity will increase raw milk purchase from farmers, improve their livelihood, and contribute to the devevelopment of rural communities. - IFC''s Advisory Services project provides technical assistance to small and medium farmers to help them improve productivity and profitability. - IFC''s investments help increase Conaprole''s commitment to sustainable production and social responsibility. - The new plant will create additional jobs (both direct and indirect). - The Project will enable Conaprole, Uruguay''s largest exporter, to increase the export of milk powder and contribute to the country''s export revenue.
Company Name: COOPERATIVA NACIONAL DE PRODUCTORES DE LECHE

project_description: The proposed transaction involves a credit enhancement facility to a local bank, which is expected to be in the form of an unfunded partial credit guarantee. IFC will support (a) the PNG Kina 9 million (approximately US$4.25 million equivalent) renewable annual working capital need for Kongo Coffee Limited to purchase parchment from local coffee growers and (b) the PNG Kina 6 million (approximately US$ 2.84 million equivalent) long term facility for capacity enhancements, overall technology improvements along with processing capacity expansion. IFC will provide an unfunded partial credit guarantee to a local bank, which may result if called upon in a potential direct exposure to Kongo Coffee Limited. It is expected that the level of guarantee will gradually decrease over time. Kongo Coffee Limited is the only coffee processing company based in PNG Highlands. It operates out of its existing processing facilities in Chuave, Chimbu province.
sponsor_shareholders: Kongo Coffee Limited, a privately held company incorporated under the laws of Papua New Guinea, established in 1990. The company is owned by Jerry and Lilly Kapka.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project involves an annual revolving working capital facility of PNG Kina 10.0 million (US$4.73 million equivalent) and a long term loan of PNG Kina 6.0 million (US$2.84 million equivalent) which will be funded by a local bank. IFC will provide an unfunded partial credit guarantee which will gradually decrease over time.
location_description: The investment will be located at Portion 1004C, Milinch Goroka, Fourmil Karimui, Wawi Coffee Mill, Okuk Highway, Chuave, Simbu Province, Papua New Guinea
development_impact: 1. Income generation for small holder coffee growers: Expanded processing capacity will generate increased demand and therefore income for growers. Growers will have access to a local, price competitive coffee buyer who has capacity to demonstrate a consistent buying pattern, thereby promoting security of income. 2. Job creation and upskilling: Additional employees will be required as processing volumes increase, many of which are roles undertaken by women. New machinery and technology will provide the opportunity for the local labour force to develop of new skills. 3. Small holder sustainability: The investment is expected to impact up to 500 coffee growers. This may assist in encouraging younger people to continue participating in local businesses, thereby contributing to industry sustainability. 4. Rural development: approximately 100, 000 people in the Chimbu region are heavily reliant on the coffee industry. Growth of KCL''s business will create additional downstream business opportunities for MSMEs including buyers and other related businesses. 5. Improved financial management and corporate governance: IFC''s involvement will provide an opportunity to improve internal systems and broaden management capacity 6. Skills training for growers: opportunity for IFC technical assistance such as enabling business training and accreditation courses.

project_description: The project is the development of Equatoria Tower a12 storey commercial property with total built up area of 7,704 m² in Juba, the financial and commercial hub of Central Equatoria State and capital of South Sudan. The Project company is UAP Properties Limited ("UAPL" or the "Company") located in Juba, South Sudan and the Equatoria Tower is the first project that it is undertaking.
sponsor_shareholders: UAPL is a privately owned company with the shareholders being UAP Insurance Sudan Ltd - 70% equity stake and Central Equatoria Investment Corporation (CEIC) - 30% equity stake. UAP Insurance Sudan Ltd is a wholly owned subsidiary of UAP Holdings Ltd one of the leading insurance and financial services companies in East Africa. CEIC is the investment arm of the Central Equatoria State (CES).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$17.9 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$5 million convertible C Loan (Quasi Equity).
location_description: The Project site is located on plot A 16-22 and plot B 16-22, in Hai Neem, area of the Hai Malakal neighborhood, in the centre of Juba’s central business district, South Sudan.
development_impact: The proposed project will help (a) create business infrastructure that will improve the investment climate of South Sudan; (b) address a severe demand-supply imbalance in commercial real estate sector of South Sudan; (c) create of a minimum of 100 jobs directly and indirectly; (d) provide a demonstration effect where IFC''s involvement in the Project could act as a catalyst to encourage other financial institutions partner with good regional companies to invest in South Sudan; and (e) promote South-South investments through providing finance to a regional group (UAP Holdings) to enable it expand its business regionally.

company_name: SUPER FILM AMBALAJ SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: The “Project” is related to the investment programs of Sanko Holding’s two subsidiaries. Superfilm is a manufacturer of packaging film, while Sanko Tekstil is a vertically-integrated textile operation. The Project includes proposed investment by Superfilm in new production lines which will increase capacity and expand its product mix, and by Sanko Tekstil which will increase the production capacity in Gaziantep and Corlu facilities.
sponsor_shareholders: Sanko Holding is the main shareholder of Sanko Tekstil and Superfilm. Based in Gaziantep, Sanko Holding is a major conglomerate of Turkey with operations in energy, cement, textile, packaging, heavy industrial machines, hospital, yacht manufacturing, white-goods, financial sector, IT, education, water bottling.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Project cost is composed of Superfilm and Sanko Tekstil’s investments and associated working capital needs. The project cost is estimated to be US$156 million. IFC will provide an A loan up to US$70 million to finance the project.
location_description: Sanko Tekstil and Superfilm investments will be made in existing Gaziantep plants of the respective Companies located in Gaziantep Industrialized Zone and Corlu plant of Sanko Tekstil located outside of Tekirdag.
development_impact: 1)Preservation of employment in frontier region of the country: Combined Superfilm and Sanko Tekstil have around 6,000 employees most of which work in the frontier regions of Turkey. The increased capacity at Superfilm and Sanko Tekstil will enable the Borrowers to be more competitive and retain the existing work-force. 2)Exports: Superfilm and Sanko Tekstil are exporters. The investments will enable them to improve their standings in the export markets and help increase export activity and hard currency inflows into Turkey. 3)Environmental Benefits: New machines will be more energy-efficient which will increase overall energy efficiency of Superfilm and Sanko Tekstil.
