Company Name: SUPER FILM AMBALAJ SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: SinoGreen Fund L.P., (“SinoGreen” or the “Fund”), a Cayman Island exempted limited partnership, is an eight-year private equity fund seeking to raise $150 million to invest in the cleantech sector in China. The Fund will invest in early- and growth- stage companies focusing on renewable energy, energy efficiency, cleaner transportation, non-energy related climate change mitigation technologies and other technologies that have direct contribution to climate change mitigation and adaptation.
sponsor_shareholders: SinoGreen will be managed by GRC Managers Limited (“GRC” or the “Fund Manager”), a management company under the China-focused venture capital private equity investment firm Grand River Capital Management Co., Ltd. GRC was established in 2005 by a team whom previously worked and invested together in the venture capital and private equity fields focused on the hi-tech and clean technology sectors in Silicon Valley and Greater China. The Manager has sponsored two venture capital and private equity funds namely Grand River Investment Company Limited (“GRC I”) and GRC II Corporation (“GRC II”), both were structured as a three-year fund with an optional two-year extension. The management team is led by Dr. Eric Wang and Mr. Benjamin Jen.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC proposes to make an equity investment of up to $20 million in the Fund, not to exceed 20% of the total commitments of the Fund.
location_description: The Fund will invest in companies focusing on China.
development_impact: IFC''s investment in the Fund is expected to have the following quantifiable development impact: (i) Reduction of GHGs through adoption of clean technologies and more environmentally sustainable practices: indicated by potential reduction of CO2 emissions directly and indirectly by the Fund''s investees; (ii) Private sector development: indicated by improved revenue and profitability of the Fund''s investees; (iii) Economic sustainability: demonstrated through the Fund''s ability to help its investees grow sustainably and generate employment growth faster than the national average; (iv) Financial success: evidenced by the Fund''s investment return (net IRR) and the Manager''s ability to raise successor fund.

project_description: MK Group d.o.o. (the “MK Group”, or the “Group”), a leading vertically-integrated agro-industrial conglomerate with vast the majority of its operations in Serbia, has embarked on a €87 million investment plan which comprises: (i) the acquisition of Carnex AD Meat Industry (“Carnex”), the Serbian brand leader in processed meat products; (ii) the upgrade and expansion of Carnex’s vertically-integrated operations; (iii) the expansion and modernization of the Group’s primary agriculture operations; and, (iv) permanent working capital to support the growth of the Group''s operations (the “Project”). The Project will enable the Group to further diversify and expand its operations vertically and horizontally in sectors where it already operates as well as adjacent industries, namely livestock and meat production. Thereby, the Project is expected to increase the size, strength and sustainability of MK Group’s operations.
sponsor_shareholders: Based in Belgrade and Novi Sad but with operations across Serbia and Ukraine, the MK Group is involved in (i) agricultural crop production; (ii) sugar production; (iii) storage, transportation and trading of agricultural commodities, and (iv) other miscellaneous activities. Established in 1983, the MK Group is a privately-owned company and a market leader in all of its key lines of business. Miodrag Kostic, the founder and driving force of the MK Group, is the beneficial owner of 100% of the shares in MK Group, together with certain close relatives.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at €87 million. IFC’s support to the Project entails a €45 million A-Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: With offices in Belgrade and Novi Sad, the Project funds will support MK Group’s agriculture-related operations which are concentrated in the northern Serbian province of Vojvodina. Carnex’s operations are located in the municipality of Vrbas, also in the Vojvodina province. The Vojvodina province is home to Serbia’s most fertile land and most of its economy revolves around agribusiness activities.
development_impact: The development impact of the Project is expected to include: (i) Operational turnaround and efficiency improvements at Carnex, a large employer and former regional leader; (ii) Support to an agricultural company involved in value-added production in a sector important to Serbia''s economy; (iii) Extend the MK Goup''s reach to farmers and imporve agricultural infrastructure; (iv) demonstration effect by encouraging other companies to invest in the region; and (vi) increased tax revenues.

company_name: COMPAGNIE HOTELIERE DE LA LAGUNE SA
project_description: The proposed project consists on the construction of a 180-key 4-star hotel in Abidjan, Cote d’Ivoire, as part of the expansion plan of the Groupe Azalai Hotels S.A (“Azalai” or the “Group”), a Mali-based holding company operating 7 business hotels in 4 IDA countries in West Africa.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project company is Compagnie Hôtelière de la Lagune (“CHL” or the “Borrower”) owning and managing the Abidjan operations of Azalai. CHL is a 60%-owned subsidiary of the Azalai Hotels S.A. (“Azalai”, the “Group” or the “Holding”). The 40% remaining belong to SIFCOM group operating in Cote d’Ivoire. Azalai is headquartered in Bamako and is 70.91%-owned by Mr. Mossadeck Bally and 21.87% by his family. Mossadeck Bally has been partnering with IFC since 1994 when he entered into the tourism industry. He is a Malian national with an MBA from San Francisco (CA).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Project cost is estimated at EUR22.7 million. The proposed IFC investment is a EUR6 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project’s site is located in Marcory, a busy commercial and business area of Abidjan, the capital city of Ivory Coast, on the major highway to the airport.
development_impact: - South-South investment; - Job creation and skills development; - Benefits to the local economy through both downstream and upstream local supply linkages; - Government revenues through tax collection; and - Environmental and Social standards improvement including life & fire safety and green building components.
Company Name: COMPAGNIE HOTELIERE DE LA LAGUNE SA

company_name: Urbi Desarrollos Urbanos, S.A.B. de C.V.
project_description: Urbi Desarollos Urbanos SAB de CV (“Urbi” or the “Company”) has requested IFC to support its Low Income Housing (“LIH”) construction and development efforts and in particular the macro projects, through an investment of up to US$50mm either in US$ or equivalent Mexican Pesos (the “Project”). IFC is also considering providing a US$20 million loan from the Canada Climate Change Program to support eligible ‘green building’ projects in addition to mobilizing up to US$35mm equivalent in local currency through syndication.
sponsor_shareholders: Within the Mexican context, Urbi is one of the largest, most established and profitable homebuilders (despite having lowest prices in the sector), with presence in 39 cities and municipalities, including the main metropolitan areas. Urbi’s innovative approach has resulted in it being a pioneer in initiatives targeted to positively impact segments of the population that were not benefiting from access to government programs and consequently housing. Through this, Urbi has been ahead of the curve, having the first mover advantage by tapping new segments of the market, which has strengthened its credibility, brand as well as market positioning. During over 30 years of operations, Urbi has built more than 400,000 housing units. Some of Urbi’s initiatives, that support and differentiate its operations, include: (i) UrbiNet, a sophisticated information technology platform, (ii) UrbiNova, Company’s proprietary construction technology, and (iii) Alternativa Urbi, a unique program in the industry to attend the non-traditional population segments (low-income workers, non-wage earners, and those not affiliated to the housing agencies). Through the City Licensee Manager (CLM) program, the company has managed to rapidly diversify into new Mexican geographies with lower working capital requirements, almost doubling its geographic coverage in three years. These tools have allowed the Company to increase its operating efficiencies and obtain profitable growth. Furthermore, Urbi was the first company to develop a Sustainable Integral Urban Development project (“DUIS”) in Mexico. These macro projects are comprehensively planned areas of development that contribute toward improving the quality of life of the residents and the territorial organization of the states and municipalities. The Company is in the process of developing additional DUIS projects, which would continue putting it on the front line of innovation. In addition to the housing development business line, URBI also has a housing-related line of business, which includes commercial land sales, Urbi’s Casa Capital Program and housing equipment and services. Urbi has been listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange since May 2004 with a market capitalization of US$1.3bn as of 1/16/2012. 54.5% of the shares is public and traded on the exchange. ~40% of the shares belong to the Pérez Román brothers (co-founders and members of the current management team). Company’s credit rating in Mexican market is Moody A3 and Fitch A- as well as an S&P B+ in the international bond market.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: An investment of up to US$50mm either in US$ or equivalent Mexican Pesos (the “Project”) is intended to be made in Urbi in the form of a senior secured corporate loan (the “IFC A Loan”). In addition, IFC would pursue a mobilization (the “Mobilization” or the “IFC B Loan”) which would result in an increase of the funding to Urbi’s environmentally sustainable affordable housing projects by another US$35mm equivalent in local currency. IFC is also considering providing a US$20 million loan from the Canada Climate Change Program to support eligible ‘green building’ projects.
location_description: Not relevant given the corporate loan nature of the investment.
development_impact: The Project''s strong development impact includes: (i) job creation; (ii) addressing the housing deficit; (iii) integrated and sustainable urban developments; (iv) transfer of knowledge and best practices on green building in Mexico, and E&S sustainability; and (v) contribution to equitable economic growth and community development.
Company Name: Urbi Desarrollos Urbanos, S.A.B. de C.V.

project_description: The proposed Project is with the Alutech group of companies (“the Company”, “Alutech” or “the Group”), the only producer of roller shutters accessories, sectional doors and aluminum extruded products in Belarus and the IFC good-standing client since 2010. Alutech was founded in 1996. It operates four manufacturing enterprises (Alutech, AluminTechno, Alutech Industrial Doors Systems and Alstrong) in Minsk, Belarus, and one in Kyiv, Ukraine, as well as over 20 trading companies and local warehouses in Belarus, Ukraine, Russia, and Czech Republic (jointly referred to as the Group). The implementation of the Project would allow Alutech to further reduce its production cost, strengthen its leading market position and penetrate new geographic markets, predominantly in the growing former CIS region and European Union through the expansion of its production capacities for sectional doors and aluminum profiles.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group is owned by several individuals, all are citizen of the Republic of Belarus.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The investment program is around €90 million comprising of expansion of production capacities and streamlining of operations (the Project). The IFC investment package is expected to include the IFC A loan of up to €25 million and a parallel loan of up to €20 million.
location_description: The Project will be implemented on Alutech’s main production site in the Republic of Belarus – within the Free Economic Zone (FEZ) near Minsk.
development_impact: The Project will further increase the supply of high quality extruded aluminum products and panels, which are important components for the construction industry, and are used in infrastructure, housing amd industrial real estate developments across the region. The Project will help Alutech grow its share in the regional market, substituting imports and providing adequate quality products at competitive price. It will also help the Company to increase its exports to the European markets. Key development impacts to the local economy include employment generation and benefits to the consumers. The Project has a significant demonstrational effect.

project_description: Zambeef Products plc (“Zambeef” or the “Company”), established in 1994 and with headquarters based in Lusaka, Zambia, is one of the largest agri-business groups in Zambia and the region, involved in the production, processing, distribution and retailing of beef, chicken, pork and dairy products among others. The Project entails supporting Zambeef’s investment program in: (a) expansion of its poultry, pork, dairy and edible oils production; (b) expand its feed milling plant; (c) expanding its irrigation land at Mpongwe farms; (d) upgrading of existing and roll out of new retail outlets, among others
sponsor_shareholders: Zambeef is a publicly listed company on Lusaka Stock Exchange in Zambia with a current market capitalization of US$140 million. The shareholders include local and international fund managers, pension funds and individuals including the founders, Carl Irwin and Francis Grogan, who collectively hold 3.2%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a US$30 million A Loan to support the Company’s US$52m capital expenditure program.
location_description: Zambeef has various farms and properties in Zambia from where it operates its cropping, animal husbandry, processing and retailing. The proposed projects will be based on its owned facilities in Zambia.
development_impact: The project''s expected development impact includes: (i) Development of a sustainable and reliable food supply chain; (ii) Facilitate the growth of a successful regional integrated agribusiness player; (iii) Better capacity utilization of industrial facilities by relieving constraints on the supply of soya and wheat at the Company''s plants; (iv) Intensification of crop production due to additional irrigation; (v) Increased employment opportunities across the group

project_description: Persianas Group (the “Company” or “Persianas”) is the developer of the first, internationally specified, purpose-built mall (The Palms Shopping Mall) in Nigeria. The Company’s existing portfolio comprises the Palms Shopping Mall and Polo Park Mall in Lagos and Enugu State respectively which are in operation and two other malls in Kwara and Oyo States that are under development. The Company’s vision is to develop and list Nigeria’s first investment grade real estate portfolio. The Nigerian real estate sector is expected to produce high growth in the medium term driven by the recovering economy, and other high growth sectors of commerce, construction, telecommunications, and a recovery in the financial services sector. This is expected to lead to demand for real estate product in all sectors in an environment where there is a dearth of quality stock of real estate and the market is undersupplied. To address Nigeria’s vastly underserved commercial property, Persianas is undertaking a restructuring and expansion of its operations which involves the: i) building and development of new retail and mixed used centres; ii) establishment and development of a professional asset management company; and iii) restructuring of the Company’s balance sheet (“The Project”). At completion, the new Project is expected to provide at least approximately 140,000 square meters of business infrastructure.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Adetayo Amusan is the primary sponsor/ promoter of the Project. He currently serves as executive chairman of Persianas Limited (Mauritius), Persianas Properties Limited (PPL), Persianas Investment Limited (PIL) and all other related mall development subsidiaries which will eventually come under one holding company – The Persianas Group. PPL (a.k.a the Palms Mall) is the premier asset in the Group and it is wholly owned by the founder, Mr Adetayo Amusan, while PIL is owned by himself and his wife, Mrs Ayodeji Amusan. The Company has entered into joint venture with a number of state governments for the development of retail and commercial real estate. These state governments own between five to thirty percent shareholding in the respective joint venture company. Mr Amusan also holds majority ownership in the Group’s asset management company, Africa Real Estate Investment and Asset Management Company Limited (ARIA), while the remaining shareholding is held by Mr. Michael Williams – the group’s chief investment officer.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at approximately US$400 million and will be financed with a combination of debt and equity. Of this amount IFC and IFC African, Latin American and Caribbean Fund, LP (“ALAC”) have proposed to invest up to US$74 million in equity and IFC providing an additional financing of US$50 million A-Loan.
location_description: The Project will be implemented in different states within Nigeria. Some project sites have been identified and are in various stages of development and operation. These include: Lagos Sate: The Project will be located on approximately 69,000 square meters of land at the Oniru Chieftaincy Family Private Layout, Victoria Island Annex, Lekki-Pennisula, Eti-Osa Local Government Area. Oyo State: The Project will be located on approximately 77,210 square meters of land along M.K.O Abiola Road, Ibadan in Ibadan South West Local Government Area of Oyo State. Enugu State: The Project is located on approximately 83,000 square meters of land at Polo Park grounds in GRA, Enugu, along the Abakaliki Expressway, Enugu State. Kwara State: The Project will be located on approximately 32,240 square meters of land at Fate Road/ Alhaji Tunde Mohammed Road, by Nigeria Television Authority Station, Ilorin, Kwara State. Persianas expects to develop additional mall projects during the lifetime of IFC’s proposed investment, and may also acquire existing buildings for redevelopment and subsequent letting.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have the following impacts: i) Improvement of food security - rollout of modern food retailing as planned anchor for every development. ii) Direct and indirect employment - retail and service jobs; possibility for linkages. iii) Tax revenues will accrue to the government. iv) Development of critical business infrastructure in Africa''s second largest market, and most populous nation. v) Elevation of commercial real estate standards - throughout the country. vi) Better aesthetic environment, particularly states outside Lagos undergoing redevelopment.

company_name: SOCIETE IVOIRIENNE DE PRODUCTION ANIMALE SA
project_description: IFC is considering to invest up to €7 million to support the expansion of La Societe Ivoirienne de Productions Animales (“SIPRA or the “Company”), a leading poultry operator based in Cote d’Ivoire. SIPRA has vertically integrated operations established in three key business units, namely 1) Ivoire Poussins, which encompass parent stock farms and hatchery for production of one day-old chick, and commercial farming facilities composed of 4 egg laying farms, and 34 broiler chickens farms, including 9 under SIPRA’s management and 25 contracted farms; 2) Ivograin, a feed mill unit. Ivograin is also selling its products through a network of 22 retail outlets throughout Ivory Coast; and, 3) CoqIvoire, a slaughtering unit and 43 retailing outlets for chicken and eggs. IFC’s financing will be used for SIPRA’s €22 million expansion project (the “Project”) over the next 3 years. The Project includes: (i) expand broiler production to 8 million birds p.a.; (ii) expand egg production to 70 million eggs p.a. (from current 20 million eggs); (iii) increase poultry & egg retail outlets to 80 (from current 43); (iv) debottlenecking of feedmill to increase capacity; and (v) others (working capital, etc.).
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Jean-Marie Ackah, the president of SIPRA, owns 78% of SIPRA. Rest of the ownership is held by the Company’s employees (2%), BICICI (subsidiary of BNP Paribas in Cote d’Ivoire) (10%), and COLINA (an insurance company) (10%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at €22 million. IFC’s proposed financing is equity and loan of up to €7 million.
location_description: SIPRA’s facilities are located in the greater Abidjan area. Ivoire Poussin’s facilities are situated in Bingerville (isolated from communities, for biosafety reasons), slaughtering unit is in Abobo (surrounded by commercial and residential areas), and Ivograin’s feed mill plant in Yopougon (an industrial area).
development_impact: (i) Contribution to the Development of the Ivoirian Poultry Industry: IFC investment will support the Company''s efforts to promote higher efficiency, quality, and best practice biosecurity standards. These best practices would spread throughout the country, and contribute to development of Ivorian poultry industry. (ii) Benefit to the supply chain: SIPRA operates in a post conflict country with significant linkages to farmers and MSMEs. SIPRA works with 25 poultry outgrower farms. Also, SIPRA sources maize locally reaching small farmers, and sells its feed and day-old chicks to poultry meat and egg farmers. The Company indirectly contribute the growth of small service-oriented businesses (transporters, restaurants, etc.). (iii) Employment creation: The Company has 523 full-time employees and 217 temporary workers. The Project is estimated to create approximately 200 additional jobs. (iv) Increased Tax Revenue For Government. (v) Demonstration effect: IFC investment in Cote d''Ivoire will raise confidence of other investors.
Company Name: SOCIETE IVOIRIENNE DE PRODUCTION ANIMALE SA

company_name: CONVERGENCE PARTNERS COMMUNICATIONS INFRASTRUCTURE FUND LLC
project_description: The Project consists of an IFC’s equity commitment of up to US$45 million in Convergence Partners Communications Infrastructure Fund LLC, an up to US$500 million investment vehicle, which is being raised and will be managed by Convergence Partners Management Limited (“Convergence Partners”), a South Africa based investment management firm. The Fund’s strategy is to invest in the opportunities presented by current underdeveloped state of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) infrastructure in Africa. In IFC’s experience, funding is often not the only requirement for successful ICT infrastructure investments. Other critical components include project conceptualization, design, development and implementation. Over the past few years, Convergence Partners have demonstrated the capacity, knowledge and skills, as well as proven investment track that position the firm to successfully capitalize on the opportunities in Africa ICT infrastructure sector.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 2006, Convergence Partners is an investment management and advisory firm focused on the ICT sector in emerging markets, with a principal focus on Africa. Since inception, the firm’s investment and research activities have been covering the full spectrum of industry sectors, across various phases of the investment cycle, including early stage/venture capital, expansion capital, private equity and project equity. In the recent years, Convergence Partners have been closely involved in the development phase of new communication infrastructure projects, bringing critical bandwidth to the African market and serving rapidly evolving communication needs of African businesses and consumers. The management team comprises professionals with a solid track record of sourcing, structuring and managing investments in the ICT sector. The team has an on-the-ground presence and over the years has developed relationships with key business players and regulators in the region. All senior partners are significant shareholders in the business. The team is led by Andile Ngcaba, Chairman, Brandon Doyle, Chief Executive Officer, Idan Segal, Chief Investment Officer, and Stefan Ferreira, Chief Financial Officer.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment will consist of an equity commitment of up to US$45 million in Convergence Partners Communications Infrastructure Fund LLC. Total IFC’s exposure to the Fund will not exceed 15% of the Fund’s total final commitments.
location_description: The Fund Manager is based in South Africa. The Fund will make investments in ICT infrastructure companies across Africa region.
development_impact: - Further Development of ICT Sector in Sub-Saharan Africa: Based on substantial expertise in ICT sectors and hands-on, value added approach to investees, the Fund Manager will continue to proactively source investment opportunities with significant socio-economic and developmental impact. - Provision of Critical Funding and Expertise to Emerging Market Companies: The Fund will address critical funding needs by emerging market companies that due to their business stage or scale might face capital access constraints. The Fund''s investments will support entrepreneurship, innovative business models and technologies, and generate employment. The Fund Manager will provide operational, technical and managerial advice to its investees. - Development of Africa Private Equity Sector: The importance of private equity for development of emerging market private sector, nurturing entrepreneurship and supporting business innovation is well recognized, and IFC''s commitment to the Fund will serve as a vote of confidence for Africa''s growing private equity industry.
Company Name: CONVERGENCE PARTNERS COMMUNICATIONS INFRASTRUCTURE FUND LLC

company_name: NILE KORDSA COMPANY FOR INDUSTRIAL FABRICS S.A.E.
sector: Other Textile Products (Including Industrial and Medical Products)
project_description: The proposed modernization Project entails the replacement of obsolete equipment with more efficient machinery at Nile Kordsa Company for Industrial Fabrics S.A.E (the “Company”). Based in 10th of Ramadan City, Area No. 7, Industrial Zone B1 Egypt, the Company is a joint venture between Kordsa Global Endustriyel Iplik ve Kord Bezi Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (“Kordsa” or the “Group”) and the Egyptian Partners focusing on tire cord fabric processing. The Project will increase the Company’s production capacity and enable it to expand its product offering.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1973 and headquartered in Istanbul, Kordsa is a world leading producer of nylon and polyester yarns, cord and industrial fabric mainly used in automotive tires, rubber parts, and transmission and conveyor belts. Kordsa has 11 manufacturing plants located in 9 countries and is an existing IFC client. The Group is majority-owned (91.1%) by the one of the largest conglomerates in Turkey, Haci Omer Sabanci Holding A.S (“Sabanci Holding”), and 8.9% of its shares are listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange. Meanwhile, the Company is a 51/49 joint venture between the Group and the Egyptian Partners. Mr. Hossam Mohammed Lasheen is the Chairman of the Company and the largest single shareholder in the Egyptian Partners.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$11 million. The proposed IFC investment entails an A-Loan for IFC’s own account of US$11 million.
location_description: The Company’s operations are located in the Tenth of Ramadan City, Area No. 7, Industrial Zone B1 Egypt, about 60 km north of Cairo.
development_impact: -Employment preservation: through capacity increase and efficiency gains, the Project helps to maintain and further create employment at the Company -Continued know-how and technology transfers: given the Group''s focus on product innovation and its ability to meet stringent quality standards, the Project is expected to result in continued technology and know-how transfer through the expansion of the Company''s operations into PET.
Company Name: NILE KORDSA COMPANY FOR INDUSTRIAL FABRICS S.A.E.

project_description: The Project consists on the development of approx. 5-10 Low Income Housing (LIH) projects in Colombia. Triada S.A.S (Triada or the Company) will be responsible for developing all housing projects under this investment.
sponsor_shareholders: Triada Is a Tier II Colombian family owned company. T riada will be in charge of developing and managing all housing projects under this investment. Promotora 3 Is a family owned company that owns 35% of Triada. Promotora 3 is the Sponsor of this investment.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is estimated at $100 mm. The proposed IFC Investment is up to $10 mm mezzanine financing for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The development of the subprojects will take place in Colombia with focus in Bogota and Cali. Sites for each subproject are still to be determined.
development_impact: (i) Address housing deficit: Colombia''s current deficit stands at 1.3 mm units that grows at 140,000 units per year. The Project will contribute to address the increasing deficit by supporting the development of 5 to 10 projects in a five period; (ii) Address shortage in housing supply: Colombian homebuilders face constraints in obtaining medium- to long-term financing, especially equity to finance land acquisition. This issue constraints the ability for homebuilders to develop larger projects and is one of the main reasons why the number of housing units built every year is not enough to address the increasing deficit. The Project will help Triada to develop larger scale projects; (iii) Alignment with Government''s priority: Housing is one of the strategic pillars of the government. President Santos is setting up the framework and designing the incentives to increase the stock of new units by 250,000 per year. The Project will be aligned with the government''s strategic priorities for the period 2012-2014 and will benefit of the incentives that the government will make available to foster housing supply.

project_description: Tonicorp is one of the largest agribusiness companies in Ecuador. Through its subsidiary Industrias Lacteas Toni SA (“ILT”), Toni is the leading dairy company in Ecuador. The Group processes milk purchased from +2,400 farmers into a wide range of dairy products (UHT milk, flavored milk, cream, butter, cheese and yogurt) and produces bottled water, energy drinks and fruit beverages from concentrate under the licensed ‘Tampico’ brand. In all product categories Toni commands between 50-70% market share. The Group also owns Plasticos Ecuatorianos SA (“Plasticos”), a packaging plant that supplies the dairy business and sells to 3rd parties, and Dipor SA (“Dipor”), which distributes all of ILT’s products. With a production capacity of ~200,000 liters of milk/day, Toni operates a plant located in an industrial area of Guayaquil. This plant, originally designed in the early 1970s to produce 7,000 MT/year of yogurt, is currently producing +30,000 MTs. Although the Group has managed to grow its capacity over time in order to keep up with increasing demand, the plant is currently cramped, having reached a point where there is no more space to grow, or changes to the layout would derived in loss of efficiencies. Therefore, ILT is currently planning to move the plant to a new site (the “Project”). This will allow increasing production capacity, generating efficiencies through better layout, newer equipment and improving E&S management.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1978 by Mr. Francisco Alarcon, Toni is mainly owned by the Alarcon family: Mr. Francisco Alarcon Alcivar (58.3%), Ms. Barbara Alarcon Alcivar (20.9%), Mr. Jaime Patricio Alarcon (4.7%), Ms. Maria del Carmen Alarcon (3.6%), and Ms. Maria Gloria Alarcon Alcivar (1.5%). The rest is floating in the Quito stock exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost over the 2011-2014 period is estimated at US$60 million. IFC is considering providing the Company with a US$30 million A-Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: ILT’s existing plant is located in an industrial area of Guayaquil, Ecuador. The new plant will be built in a new site in the Guayaquil area as well.
development_impact: IFC will be supporting the continued growth of one of Ecuador''s leading agribusiness companies in terms of employment and linkages through the value chain and one of the most important staple food producers in the country. The Project will contribute to improve Toni''s competititveness in the production and commercialization of dairy products, and help the Company extend its reach toward the interior of Ecuador. Toni has a strong base of the pyramid focus as it services more than 90,000 small shops, and sources milk from approximately 2,300 small and medium-size farmers, most of them located in rural frontier regions where employment opportunities are scarce. Its activities therefore have a considerable reach in the local economy and impact on livelihood of local population. There are specific developmental impacts associated with the Project, which are summarized below: Product Safety: consumption of raw milk is still very popular in Ecuador, in particular in the interior of the country. This is considered a health hazard as the product does not meet minimum health and safety standards. On the contrary, Toni''s products conform with high quality and safety standards, and therefore reduce public health risks for consumers. Toni''s growth strategy in the interior of Ecuador will displace consumption of raw milk with high quality and safe products. Employment: Toni''s improved performance and increased production capacity will result in higher employment opportunities at the plant, and in rural areas througout the country. Farmers linkages: Toni sources milk from direct and indirect farmers througout the country. As a consequence of the Project, Toni will further develop milk production and tehrefore enhance and stabilize farmers'' income and increase hired employment on dairy farms.

project_description: The proposed project is a risk sharing facility (“RSF”) with CREDIT AGRICOLE BANK (the “Bank”), a 99.9955%-owned Ukrainian subsidiary of Credit Agricole S.A, on portfolio of receivables generated by Bayer in connection with sales of crop-protection products to private sector farmers in Ukraine. The RSF will cover a portfolio of seasonal receivables (with maturities less than 1 year) with a total portfolio amount of up to US$35 million equivalent in local currency. IFC will share 50% of credit losses in the portfolio with the Bank up to a maximum IFC exposure of up to US$17.5 million equivalent in the local currency. IFC will enter into agreement with Bayer in order to complement the risk sharing arrangement with the Bank. CREDIT AGRICOLE BANK is a medium-size universal bank ranked ?32 in the Ukrainian banking system with ca. US$800 million of total assets and total equity of approximately US$100 million. It serves around 400,000 clients via its network of 200 branches and outlets covering all regions of Ukraine. CREDIT AGRICOLE BANK is universal bank with specific focus on the agricultural sector. The Bank has defined agriculture as priority sector for their operations in Ukraine. Its exposure to agri-sector reached US$157 million and constituted 26% of the Bank’s loan portfolio as of mid-2011. The proposed project will be IFC’s second engagement with Bayer Ltd, main supplier of plant protection products in Ukraine with revenues of approx. US$150 million. The Company’s clients are mainly represented by small and medium size farmers.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project is cosponsored by CREDIT AGRICOLE BANK and Bayer Ltd. CREDIT AGRICOLE BANK is 99,9955%-owned by Credit Agricole S.A. France (“CA”), one of the largest financial banks in Europe in terms of income from retail business. CA is represented in more than 70 countries serving 54 million customers worldwide. The Group’s long-term ratings are: A+ Stable Outlook (Fitch); Aa3 Negative Outlook (Moodys); A Stable Outlook (S&P). In Ukraine, CA has two subsidiaries: (i) CA, and (ii) a corporate investment bank, CIB Credit Agricole, in operation 18 years. CA plans to strengthen its position at the Ukrainian market through consolidation of the two subsidiaries in 2012-2013. After consolidation, the bank would have US$1.3 billion in total assets and be ranked ?21 in Ukraine. Bayer Ltd. is a Ukrainian entity wholly owned by Bayer AG, a Germany-based pharmaceuticals, polymers and agrochemicals conglomerate with sales of approximately €35 billion and EBITDA of approximately of €6.3 billion in 2010. The group’s structure consists of three divisions: (i) Bayer Healthcare, (ii) Bayer CropScience, and (iii) Bayer MateriaScience. Bayer CropScience, with revenues of approximately €6.8 billion in 2010, manufactures herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, seed treatment and seeds.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $17.5 million for IFC’s own account, to be provided as a risk sharing facility on the portfolio of up to $35 million of receivables generated by Bayer Ltd. to its existing and new farmer clients. The CAB will provide a guarantee to farmers which will allow them to buy on credit from Bayer.
location_description: Bayer and the Bank are headquartered in the capital of Ukraine, Kyiv. Credit Agricole Bank operates around 200 outlets located in big cities, provincial and district centers across Ukraine. Bayer Ltd. covers the entire territory of Ukraine via the chain of local distributors.
development_impact: IFC involvement through this transaction is expected to have a strong development impact, through: (i) increased and improved access to financial services for agricultural SME's and farmers; (ii) improved productivity through the provision of certified, top quality crop protection products and know-how to SME farmers; (iii) improvement of Bayer's and farmers' integrated pest and disease management (IPM/IDM) approach, coordinated use of pest and environmental information along with available pest control methods, including cultural practices, biological, genetic and, as a last resort, chemical means to prevent unacceptable levels of pest damage.

project_description: Merec Industries Lda (Merec) was established in 1998 and is today the largest wheat miller in Mozambique. IFC provided partial guarantees for the establishment of the company’s first mill in 2000 and for the acquisition of a second mill in 2003 followed up by a US$7 million loan in 2008 to finance the establishment pasta plant in FY2008 The proposed project would allow Merec group to expand and optimise their operations through the establishment of: a new wheat mill in the north of the country in Nacala; and a port based discharge and storage facility at the port of Maputo.
sponsor_shareholders: Merec’s main sponsor is Mhamud Charania, CEO of the company. Mr. Charania is a mechanical engineer with specialization in manufacturing with over 15 years of experience in trading, manufacturing and leasing. Mr. Charania founded Africom Lda in 1995, which is now Mozambique’s leading distributor of soft commodities and Merec Industries Lda in 1998 which he grew to be the largest wheat miller in Mozambique in less than 10 years. Merec is a 100% family owned company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated to be $58 million consisting of: (i) pasta production plants; (ii) milling expansion; (iii) storage capacity expansion; and (iv) working capital. The proposed project consists of a corporate facility of up to $25 million that will be used to finance Merec’s expansion project.
location_description: Merec’s operations are located in Maputo, Machava and Beira with the new project in Nacala. The expansion projects will take place on Merec owned and leased properties. The project sites have good access to road network.
development_impact: (i) Strengthening the wheat procurement logistics and improving the group''s production infrastructure; (ii) Employment creation; (iii) SME development as the company''s new projects would entail increased demand for locally produced maize and increased business for retailers; (iv) Increase domestic food production in Mozambique; (v) import substitution which will save the country foreign currency outflows; and (iv) Increased tax revenues to government

project_description: Titan Cement Company S.A. (“Titan Group”, the “Group” or the “Sponsor”), an existing IFC client and Greece’s leading private cement company, is seeking to expand its cooperation with IFC by inviting IFC to invest in its Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia (FYROM), Kosovo, and Serbia operations. These operations mainly consist of three entities: Cementara Kosjeric (TCK), Cementarnica Usje (TCU), and SharrCem (TSC) (together, the “Companies”) that have a combined production capacity of about 3.5 million tons per annum (mtpa) and are engaged in an investment program which also includes environmental improvements and various debottlenecking investments in all plants (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Titan Group is an independent cement and building materials producer with over 100 years of industry experience. Based in Greece, Titan Group owns 14 cement plants in 9 countries, with half of these plants being in emerging markets. Titan is listed on the Athens Stock Exchange and is a core member of the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. In 2011, Titan Group sold 15.3 m. tons of cement and cementitious materials and had revenues of EUR1.1 billion and EBITDA of EUR243 million.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering a potential investment in the company which will consolidate the Group’s operations in FYROM, Kosovo and Serbia, in the form of a minority equity stake. Total Project cost is estimated to be EUR 75 million for the period 2011-2016.
location_description: The Project sites are located at three different plants: TCK, TCU and TSC. TCK – Titan Cementara Kosjeric D.O.O. is located around 130 km South-East of Belgrade and has an annual production capacity of about 800,000 tpa of cement. TCU – Titan Cementarnica Usje A.D. is located in Skopje and has an annual production capacity of about 1.7 mtpa of cement. TSC-SharrCem SH.PK is located in Hani Elezit, Kosovo and has an annual production capacity of about 1.0 mtpa of cement.
development_impact: (i) Contributing to further improving infrastructure development and strengthening the capacity of the construction sector and related activities, a key growth and local sustainability area for the Balkans in the long-term (ii) Supporting employment and enabling entrepreneurial opportunities through increased operational efficiencies at energy consumption, resource utilization, etc. (iii) Contributing and safeguarding income to the Governments through taxes as a result of the plants'' operations and continuous performance improvement (iv) Supporting and strengthening local SMEs by promoting sub-contracting at local level and investing in their continuous performance improvement

project_description: CLN Group, and Proma Group, two Italian automotive suppliers (the “Sponsors”) have decided to jointly invest in Serbia in a Greenfield metal stamping factory (the “Project”). The Project will be located in Grosnica, a supplier park dedicated to FIAT’s new plant in Kragujevac. FIAT current production capacity in Kraguievac is 20,000 car/year and is expecting to grow to 140,000 car/year by 2013 and potentially 300,000 car/year by 2015. The Project will produce for FIAT, seat structure, safety component and system, suspension and car jacks, with manufacturing processes including press, assembly and painting. The plant is expected to create 367 skilled jobs.
sponsor_shareholders: Simest: Società Italiana per le Imprese all’Estero (“Simest”) is a financial institution which provides financial instruments and services to support Italian companies in foreign markets. Simest is owned by the Italian Ministry for Economic Development, whose participation includes leading Italian banks and Confindustria, which is the General Confederation of Italian Industry. Simest will participate as a minority equity holder in the Project. CLN: Founded in 1949, CLN is an Italian company which operates in three business segments: Steel Service Centers (“SSC”), Steel Wheel Manufacturing, and Steel Metal Stamping (“MA”). CLN is the preferred steel stamping and wheel supplier of many OEMs. CLN is 65% owned by Perris-Magnetto family and 35% by Arcelor Mittal. In 2011, CLN’s consolidated expected revenue is EUR1.8 billion, with an EBITDA of EUR169 million and total assets of EUR 1.5 billion. The Automotive division, MA, is CLN’s most profitable division and will directly invest in Project. Proma: Proma SpA, the operating holding of Proma Group, is the legal entity investing in the JV. Founded in 1980 with its first plant specialized in steel cold stamping, Proma Group is controlled by the Pino Family, and is a long standing metal stamping part manufacturer, part of FIAT supplier’s group. It has 9 plants in Italy, one in Morocco, Poland, Spain and France. It employs globally 1,750 staff. Proma is the leader in the car seat frame area, stamping and metal assemblies for the vehicles of the main European car-makers. Proma Group offer to its customer (automotive) a complete service, consisting of product Engineering, industrialization, production, assistance and logistic.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is EUR 37 million. It will be financed by Senior Debt, equity and shareholder loans. The sponsors will inject in equity plus quasi equity an amount of approximately EUR 15 million (paid in cash) representing 40% of the Project cost. IFC’s is contemplating providing a loan of up to EUR 20 million.
location_description: The project is a greenfield, located in Grosnica, a supplier park less than a kilometer from FIAT’s plant in Kragujevac, Serbia.
development_impact: Sustainable employment creation - The Project is expected to create at least 367 skilled jobs in Sumadija District, a frontier region of Serbia. Support FDI in Serbia - Channeling foreign direct investment is a priority for Serbia. The project will contribute to balancing Serbia''s large current account deficit. Support export oriented industry - the project will sell its product to FIAT assembly plant in Kragujevac, which will export 90% of the production. Technology transfer - MA and Proma are FIAT trusted suppliers and have state-of-the-art technologies and efficient processes. Local staff will be trained to new, highly competitive standards.

project_description: Proteak Uno S.A.P.I.B de C.V. (“Proteak” or the “Company”) is a mid-sized publicly traded Mexican company engaged in the sustainable management of teak plantations. The proposed Project consists of the Company’s expansion plan, which includes the financing of the recent acquisitions of teak plantations in Central America and Colombia; as well as the establishment of new teak plantations in Mexico.
sponsor_shareholders: As of December 31, 2011, Proteak had 4,408 ha planted with teak trees located in the Mexican states of Jalisco, Nayarit, Tabasco and Chiapas. The Company has also acquired 1,956 ha of established plantations in Colombia and Costa Rica as well as in Mexico to improve its inventories profile by adding older plantations to its portfolio. The Company established 1,000 ha of new plantations in 2011 and plans to continue adding an average of 1,000 ha/year over the next few years.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost amounts US$ 113.6 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of a US$ 15 million A Loan and a US$ 15 million B Loan.
location_description: Proteak is based in Mexico and has subsidiaries in Costa Rica and Colombia. The expansion of the Company includes rural areas in Costa Rica, Colombia, and Mexico among other countries in Latin America.
development_impact: Climate change mitigation: IFC financing will support the Company in establishing teak plantations and supporting the growth of the existing planted area, which will directly result in a significant carbon sequestration. Moreover, since land reserves and land to be acquired comprise mainly ranch lands that have been degraded due to over-grazing of livestock, the Project will have a considerable impact on soil regeneration. Employment generation: The Project is expected to create direct and indirect employment (number of jobs to be created and wage levels) and contribute to poverty reduction in remote rural areas. Strong demonstration effect: Successful implementation of the Project will demonstrate the long term viability of sustainable forestry projects in regions with favorable weather and soil conditions for forestry, and degraded land available. Frontier regions: The Project involves direct investment and job creation in remote rural areas of Costa Rica and Colombia, and frontier regions in Mexico such as the states of Nayarit, Tabasco and Chiapas.

project_description: The A&C Square is an existing one-stop mixed-use concept consisting of a shopping mall, a fuel station, fitness centre, two multi-purpose office buildings, a pool area and a children’s play ground. The mixed-use development has an ongoing expansion program. IFC has been approached to provide a loan that will be used to fast track the completion of the expansion program comprising the construction of an additional office block and the refurbishment of the existing retail area (the “Project”) in Accra, Ghana.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project will be owned 100% by A&C Development Company Limited (“A&C Development” or the “Company”) which is a privately held real estate development company based in Accra, Ghana. A & C Development is a family owned business with Andrew Asamoah owning 50% of its shares and the remaining 50% split equally among Cecelia Asamoah his wife his four children-Frederick Asamoah, Edmund Asamoah, Vivian Asamoah, and Andrew Asamoah Jr. (the “Sponsors”). Mr. Andrew Asamoah is a retired international civil servant who worked for the United Nations for over 30 years as a staff of the World Health Organization in a variety of senior positions.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be approximately $10.8 million. The proposed investment is approximately $ 4.35 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project location is the urban residential area of East Legon in Accra, Ghana at the existing A&C Square mixed-use development.
development_impact: i) Development of necessary business infrastructure: The Project will alleviate the country''s critical lack of class A office space and it will improve retail services to meet the country''s growing population; ii) Job creation: The new office building will create new direct and indirect employment both during the permanent stage and during construction; iii) Benefit to local suppliers: Local procurement of construction supplies, food and services throughout construction; and iv) Skills transfer: there will be the transfer of skill and expertise in the construction and renovation of the mall and office building to the local workers

project_description: The Project (“Continental Automotive Thailand Ltd”) is a green field manufacturing facility in Thailand, with a production capacity of 500,000 high pressure pumps and 2,500,000 injectors per year. These pumps and injectors are used in Continental’s high-precision Piezo common rail systems, which in turn are used in its diesel-based Powertrain engine systems. Continental sells the complete system, which consists of the Piezo injector, the pump, the fuel rail, and the engine control unit, to Original Equipment Manufacturers. Diesel engines consume about 30% less fuel than gasoline engines do. Further, Piezo technology produces fuel savings of up to 5% relative to other diesel engines, reduces particulate and nitrogen emissions and makes engines quieter without any loss of performance. These components fulfill EURO 6 emission standards which will apply in Europe from 2014 onwards. The Project aims at supplying injectors for passenger with diesel engines. The Project is an important step taken by the Sponsor to expand its manufacturing base in Asia in order to support the growth of its clients’ fuel efficient vehicle sales in the region.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Continental AG, a worldwide automotive supplier of a broad range of electronic systems and components, tires and non-tire rubber products, founded and headquartered in Germany. Continental AG generated revenues of about €26 billion in 2010 and has approximately 164,000 employees across 45 countries globally. Continental AG indirectly holds 99% of the shares of the Continental Automotive (Thailand) Co., Ltd (the “Company”). In compliance with Thai law, which requires a minimum of three shareholders, the remaining 1% is held by three individuals, all employees of Continental Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be about €180 million, to be funded via €87 million in equity from the Sponsor, €13 million in intercompany loans, a €10 million working capital loan and the proposed IFC investment. The proposed IFC investment consists of a €35 million A loan for IFC’s own account and a €35 million B loan syndicated facility.
location_description: The Project is located at the following address: 7/259, Moo 6, Amata City Industrial Estate, T. Mabyangporn, A. Pluakdaeng, Rayong, 21140, Thailand. The facility is strategically located 27 kilometers from Laem Chabang Deep Sea Port and 114 kilometers from Bangkok.
development_impact: 1. Climate change: The Project involves the manufacturing of high pressure pumps, a key component of the Piezo common rail system. Continental is a pioneer of diesel technology and is the market leader for Piezo Common Rail Technology, which will promote adherence to EURO 6 emission standards, which will be mandatory from 2014. This new technology will lower carbon dioxide emissions by over 15% relative to regional standards, and by 5% relative to world-class standards. Assuming that half of the CO2 savings are attributable to the injection system , the Industry Specialist calculates CO2 emissions reduction of 17 g/km per vehicle attributable to the use of the Piezo common rail technology. With an annual mileage of 30,000 km, a lifetime of 10 years per vehicle and a production of 145,030 vehicles in 2011, total estimated CO2 savings is 739,650 tons in 2011. 2. Technology transfer and enhancing Thailand's competitiveness: The Project will increase the competitiveness of the Thai automotive sector through the transfer of best practices and managerial and technological know-how. Innovation and high-tech manufacturing processes will support Thailand's transition to a developed country status. Historically, the development of the auto sector, including the export of high-value components, has played a significant role in the economic transformation, as exemplified by Japan, Korea and Taiwan. 3. Generation of highly skilled labor: The Project will generate approximately 780 jobs. Continental is committed to developing and strengthening its employees' technical expertise. All newly recruited engineers from Thailand attend a one year training program at its headquarters in Germany. 4. Support of local suppliers: This Project will require local suppliers to improve their quality and will generate around EUR40 million of local purchases annually by 2014. We estimate that over 1,000 employment opportunities could also be created within the local supply chain. Continental is situated close to its supply base and provides regular inputs to improve quality through internal audits and supplier evaluation.

project_description: IFC is considering a loan of up to $30 million to Armajaro Trading Group Limited (“ATGL” or “Armajaro”). ATGL is an intermediary holding company and owns 100% of Armajaro Trading Limited (“ATL”), which was founded in 1998 and is an integrated supply chain manager of soft commodities including cocoa, coffee and, more recently, sugar. ATL aims to be partner of choice in the Agri-commodity supply chain. The proposed investment will scale up ATL’s upcountry sourcing capabilities in the origin countries, improve its funding flexibility, strengthen its balance sheet and assist more farmers achieve sustainable farming practices.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is ATGL. It was incorporated in England in 2010 as an intermediary holding company to own 100% of ATL, which was founded in 1998. Armajaro Holdings Limited (“AHL”) is the group holding company. The majority of AHL’s equity is owned by Mr. Anthony Ward (51%) and Mr. Richard Gower (44%). Both persons are co-founders and directors of AHL. The rest of the shares (5%) are owned by the staff and widow of the deceased former Chairman.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering a corporate loan up to $30 million. The proposed investment will scale up ATL’s upcountry sourcing capabilities in the origin countries, improve its funding flexibility, strengthen its balance sheet and assist more farmers to achieve sustainable farming practices. In addition, the IFC African, Latin American and Caribbean Fund, managed by the IFC Asset Management Company, is also considering a $25 million corporate loan to ATL.
location_description: The investment is a corporate facility supporting the company’s financing needs in its key commodity origins across Sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia and Central America. The use of the funds is restricted to Part 2 country operations in IFC member countries.
development_impact: The project''s development impact includes direct benefits to rural populations in many developing countries in Africa and Asia and a demonstration impact on sustainability and traceability initiatives. Some key impacts will be: 1) increased number of farmers reached/trained, 2) improved E&S practices in the traceable portion of the supply chain 3) improved farmers'' income through certification, training and improved access to market.

project_description: Pran Group (“Pran” or the ‘Company’) is seeking IFC’s assistance to finance the expansion of its food processing operations. The proposed expansion project has been incorporated as a new private limited company, Natore Agro Limited. Pran is a diversified group involved in the production and sale of a wide product range covering beverages, snacks, culinary products, confectionery, dairy products, rice and tea. The Project (“Pran Natore Agro”) consists of an investment of approximately $25 million for the expansion of Pran’s food processing and manufacturing capacity with the goal of introducing new packaged food and spice/condiment products to the Company’s product line for both local and export markets.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsors are Mr. Amjad Khan Chowdhury, Mrs. Sabiha Amjad, Mr. Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, and Ms. Uzma Chowdhury who control the seven Pran Group companies engaged in the food processing sector: AMCL Ltd., PRAN Agro Ltd., PRAN Foods Ltd., Bango Agro PRAN Ltd., PRAN Beverage Ltd., PRAN Dairy Ltd., and PRAN Natore Agro Ltd. All of these companies are fully privately-owned, with the exception of AMCL, which is listed in the Dhaka Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $25 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A Loan of up to $15 million.
location_description: The project will support the expansion of Pran’s existing food and confectionary lines in Natore in northern Bangladesh.
development_impact: Agriculture accounts for 21% of Bangladesh's GDP, whereby 55% of the country's population derives its income from the sector. Private sector involvement will ensure continued growth in income-generating agriculture activities, particularly by integrating small farmers into formal supply chain linkages such as those that Pran's operations have established. In addition to creating over 1,200 new jobs, the proposed Project will positively impact the livelihood of several thousand farmers and their communities by ensuring consistent demand and fair pricing for their produce. Further, Pran's unparalleled distribution network will enable the Company to reach under-served, impoverished communities and provide them with affordable, essential food products of high quality.

project_description: Laxmi Organic Industries Ltd (LOIL or the Company) is an Indian company producing specialty chemicals used in diverse end-user industries. The Company is undertaking an expansion (the “Project”), comprising brown field expansion of ethyl acetate (ETAC) and diketene derivatives (DD) products capacities, a coal fired co-generation facility and a greenfield facility to produce acetic anhydride.
sponsor_shareholders: LOIL is an unlisted company and the promoter family holds 100% of its share capital. The Company was promoted by Mr. Vasudev Goenka and is currently being managed by his sons, Mr. Ravi Goenka and Mr. Rajiv Goenka.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated Project cost is approximately US$43.6 million and IFC is proposing a financial investment to fund a part of the expansion. The balance will be funded from other financing institutions and internal accruals of the Company
location_description: The project site is Mahad, Maharashtra, India, where the Company’s existing plant is located.
development_impact: - IFC''s proposed investment will help LOIL become a leader in adopting latest practices to ensure clean production. This is significant, especially in an industry where most medium-scale chemical manufacturers tend to follow polluting processes with minimal investment in waste effluent handling. LOIL has designed a zero discharge ETP for additional effluents generated from expansion projects where processed effluent will be used as feed water. - The proposed investment in a thermal co-generation power plant will provide the most efficient â€˜Energy and Product Integration'' solution between steam intensive ETAC plant and power intensive DD plant. - LOIL is in the process of carrying out R&D for cost effective thermal solar panels which has potential to integrate with co-generation unit in DD plant. This pioneer design will mitigate LOIL''s reliance on fossil fuels and reduce its greenhouse gas footprint. - The proposed expansion is expected to create nearly 70 jobs over the next two years and result in other indirect development benefits such as linkages with local suppliers, upgrade of existing infrastructure, and indirect employment creation through auxiliary businesses in the region and during construction phase. - Considering that 70% of India''s current requirement for DD products is being imported, the proposed investment will facilitate self sufficiency and conserve foreign exchange.

project_description: The project is to support Grupo Canopus (“Canopus” or the “Company”), to expand its focus on low-income housing developments under the Minha Casa Minha Vida or any follow on governmental program. Canopus, one of the largest real estate developers and construction companies in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil, has invited IFC and the IFC African, Latin American and Caribbean Fund, LP, managed by IFC Asset Management Company LLC (ALAC Fund) to make an equity investment to support its corporate capital expenditure plan for the expansion of its footprint in the affordable housing segment specially in the 0 to 10 minimum wages segment (including underdeveloped regions such as Brazilian North and Northeast), as well as the consolidation of its current position in the mid-high income and commercial segments (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in Belo Horizonte and with a focus on the medium/high income residential and commercial buildings segments and most recently on the low income housing segment through its wholly owned subsidiary Emcasa, Canopus is an integrated homebuilder involved in acquisition of land, planning, development and construction of residential and commercial buildings as well as sales. The Company enjoys of more than 40 years of expertise in the real estate industry, mainly in the Southeast region of Brazil, but has been currently expanding its footprint in other underdeveloped regions such as the Brazilian North and Northeast. The Company was created in 1971 by Mr. Adgar Mattos, a reputable and well-known entrepreneur. Since 1992, CANOPUS has been controlled by the second generation of the Mattos Family, represented by Mr. Lucas Mattos and Mr. Tulio Mattos (50% stake each).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will provide an equity investment in the newly created company Canopus Holding S.A. for an amount to be determined. In addition, the ALAC Fund is also considering a similar investment in Canopus Holding S.A.
location_description: Housing and commercial projects will be developed in various states of Brazil, including frontier regions such as the Brazilian North and Northeast.
development_impact: The stability of the Brazilian macro economy during the last seven years coupled with the Government’s agenda to prioritize the housing sector in a countercyclical effort, have boosted the demand for lower- and middle-income housing. The proposed Project will support a reputable domestic housing company to undertake its growth plan in response to increasing demand for quality and affordable entry level lower-income houses in Brazil, thereby helping to reduce the current housing deficit in the country – particularly among lower-income families. Consumers will benefit from the expanded supply of residential units, while such housing developments will contribute to urban infrastructure development and community development around them, such as roads, electricity, hospitals, recreation areas, and so forth, thus also improving living standard of the population in the surrounding area. Finally, in addition to promote significant job creation, the Project will also enhance local supply linkages through increased demand for construction and building materials in the country. Once construction is completed, the housing units will stimulate the use of local supplies of goods and services, supporting maintenance, retailing and wholesale operations. In addition, local employment will be generated during and after construction.

project_description: Vonpar Alimentos S.A. (“Vonpar Alimentos” or the “Company”) has an investment program for 2011-2013 to the relocation and expansion of its chocolate manufacturing plant, to be located in the city of Arroio do Meio, Brazil and the expansion and modernization of the Company’s dairy and candy businesses.
sponsor_shareholders: Vonpar Alimento’s controlling interest is owned by Vonpar S.A., the Vontobel family’s holding company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment in the project is a $50 million A Loan.
location_description: Arroio do Meio, State of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
development_impact: IFC's investment in Vonpar will have a direct and significant impact in the region's development: (i) The company works together with about 1,133 farmers that produce milk for Vonpar, and Vonpar provides technical assistance to the farmers it sources raw milk from, with dedicated staff, and will support the farmers in improving the quality of milk in light of the new milk safety regulations that are expected to come to effect in 2012; and (ii) although the production staffing needs will decline in the new chocolate factory due to increased automation and efficiencies gained from co-locating the candy and chocolate plants, increased employment is expected in the transportation, sales and promotion staff as sales of the company continue to increase.

project_description: The Project (“CPLF-Mryia”) involves providing a long-term financing to Mriya Agro Holding Public Limited (“Mriya” or the “Company”), a leading Ukrainian primary agricultural producer with a proven track record of growing wheat, barley, sugar beet, rapeseed, potatoes, and other crops. The long-term loan will provide financing to improve the operational processes and resource efficiencies at the sugar plant companies.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is the Guta family (the “Sponsors”), who founded Mriya in 1992 and control it to this day. The head of the Guta family, Ivan Guta, a well-respected Ukrainian businessman, and his wife, Klaudia Guta established Mriya on 50 hectares of land (124 acres) after having worked for 8 years at a state farm. In 2002, Andriy and Mykola Guta, the sons of the founders, joined the family business after completing their higher education in Ukraine and abroad. Following a private placement on the Entry Standard of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2008, the Sponsors collectively own 80% of Mriya’s Cyprus-based holding company that fully controls all of Mriya’s Ukraine-based operating companies, with the remaining 20% owned by over 20 institutional investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is $12.5 million, a portion of which will be financed using IFC’s Cleaner Production Loan Facility (“CPLF”). Mriya will use the funds to implement IFC’s cleaner production team recommendations at four out of six sugar plant companies to bring about a reduction in energy consumption, water use and CO2 emissions. IFC investment will consist of a five-year senior loan of up to US$ 5 million.
location_description: The Project will allow Mriya to improve process efficiencies at the four sugar plants located in Ternopil region, within a 50-km radius of its HQ in Vasylkivtsi. Ternopil region is one of the poorest, primarily agricultural regions of Ukraine.
development_impact: IFC''s financing will support resource and energy efficiency improvements at the sugar plants. The implementation of the project will achieve significant reductions in energy consumption, water use and CO2 emissions. As a result, Mriya will realize direct economic benefits and enhance its competitiveness.

project_description: Etileno XXI (the “Project”) consists of the development, construction and commercial operation of a petrochemical complex in Mexico, composed of one cracker facility to produce ethylene from ethane, integrated to three polyethylene plants with an aggregate nominal capacity of 1,050,000 tons per year. Etileno XXI, which is located in Nachital de Lazaro Cardenas a frontier region of Coatzacoalcos, represents the largest investment in Mexico’s petrochemical sector in the last 20 years. Access to competitively priced feedstock will make the Project one of the most competitive in the Americas. The Project seeks to serve the Mexican polyethylene market, which is rapidly growing and currently being supplied in part by imports.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsors are Braskem S.A. (“Braskem”) and Grupo Idesa S.A. de C.V. (“Idesa”). Braskem and Idesa have established a joint venture company, Braskem Idesa, S.A.P.I. (the “Company”), to house the Project. Braskem and Idesa will hold shareholding interests of up to 65% and up to 35%, respectively, in the Company. Braskem is a listed Brazilian company and leading thermoplastic resin producer in the Americas. Idesa is a privately owned Mexican petrochemical company dedicated to the production and distribution of a variety of petrochemical products.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at $4.3 billion. The proposed IFC investment consists of a loan of up to $300 million for IFC’s own account and the mobilization of a B Loan.
location_description: The Project will be located in Nanchital de Lazaro Cardenas, in the state of Veracruz.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have a significant development impact by (i) adding value to a natural resource which would otherwise be used as natural gas, (ii) creating forward linkages that would develop the downstream industry, (iii) improving the position of Mexican downstream converters, such as savings on inventory, reduced foreign exchange exposure, local access to a PE supplier that could provide services and new solutions, (v) providing inclusive growth for an economically underdeveloped southern region of Mexico, (iv) creating employment and training opportunities.

project_description: Based in Dushanbe, the Tajero Group of Companies (“the Group”) is composed of three related but separate companies: Tajero LLC, Tajero-Sugd and Amal Industry. It is the leading nationwide importer and distributor of food and beverages with exclusive contracts from 16 International Fast Moving Consumer Goods (“FMCG“) companies. Tajero distribution currently covers 70% of sales points in Tajikistan. Tajero is exposed to volatility in global prices as a distributor of imported food, which makes up 80% of food in Tajikistan. Increasing food prices coupled with currency depreciation have limited Tajero’s ability to further expand the operation, particularly as access to affordable capital has diminished in Tajikistan. To sustain stable volumes and further grow the business, Tajero seeks more affordable sources of financing and has approached IFC to reduce refinancing risks. Tajero has approached IFC for a 3-year working capital line to refinance a current loan and reduce financing costs (the “Project”). This would be IFC's second investment with Tajero.
sponsor_shareholders: The three Tajero group companies are all owned 100% by Mr. Abdurakhmon Gaibullozoda, the Project Sponsor. Mr. Gaibullozoda started in sales at a local grocery in Dushanbe in 1992, which he purchased in 1995. Since then, Mr. Gaibullozoda transformed this business into the largest FMCG distributor in Tajikistan for perishable and non-perishable products with suppliers from Ukraine, Russia, Kazakhstan, the US and Brazil. IFC has an existing outstanding loan of $1.3 million loan to Amiri LLC, a chocolate confectionary company in Tajikistan, 100% owned by the Sponsor.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $2.9 million. The proposed investment is an IFC A working capital facility of up to $1.7 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Company is located in the Rudaki district of Dushanbe, Tajikistan. The site used to be an old storage facility which Mr. Gaibullozoda purchased in 2005 and fully renovated into modern storage and production complex including a 1,000 sq.m. modern refrigerated warehouse and a 2,300 sq.m. dry warehouse. Throughout Tajikistan, Tajero owns and leases warehouse facilities of approximately 7,360 sq. m in total including warehouses of 1,850 sq. m. for frozen products and refrigerated warehouses of 1,160 sq. m.
development_impact: Through this Project, IFC will be supporting a local sponsor that has built a distribution business in a challenging environment. The project will have strong development impact: i) in the business community where Tajero will serve as an example of the benefits to be gained through improved transparency and corporate governance; ii) for consumers, as the affordable financing that Tajero will obtain from IFC will help mitigate the price increases it is passing on to its customers, which are also as a result of global food price increases; and iii) for investors and exporters to the region, as IFC's involvement with Tajero adds comfort in identifying potential partners in Tajikistan, a country with few foreign investors outside the resource sectors and microfinance.

company_name: TIRYAKI AGRO GIDA SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: IFC considers an investment up to $50 million A Loan to Tiryaki Agro Foods (“Tiryaki” or the “Company”), which is an integrated supply chain manager with activities in sourcing, logistics, processing, storage and marketing of agricultural products (the “Project”). The Company is headquartered in Istanbul, has a substantial presence in Turkey by operating plants across the country, including processing facilities in the southeast Turkish city of Gaziantep, and has international trade presence. Tiryaki is a family owned private company which is engaged in sourcing, processing, storage and trading of conventional and organic grains (wheat, barley and corn), Pulses (lentils, chickpeas, peas, beans, rice and bulgur), Oil seeds (sunflower, sesame, kanola and soybean) and Nuts (pistachio, almonds, walnut and peanuts) across Europe, Africa, the Middle East, CIS countries, Indian subcontinent and America.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is privately owned. The main shareholders are Tiryaki Holding A.S. with 80% shareholding and Gulf Investors Agro S.A.R.L., a fund managed by Investcorp from Manama, Bahrain , with 20% shareholding. Established in 1965 by the Tiryakioglu family and headquartered in Istanbul, the company has successfully expanded to become an integrated supply chain manager sourcing from over 15 different countries with storage and processing facilities in Turkey and exporting to more than 40 countries. Tiryakioglu family has only been focused on Tiryaki and does not have ownership in other businesses.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC considers an A loan up to $50 million to finance working capital needs of the Company.
location_description: IFC consider providing a corporate loan to finance working capital needs of the Company. IFC’s investment is not therefore earmarked for any particular plant. The Company has two operational plants in Turkey in the cities of Gaziantep and Bandirma. Third plant in Mersin is currently at the construction stage. The Company also has three storage facilities located in Gaziantep, Trabzon, Mersin.
development_impact: -Supply Chain Linkages and Access to Farmers: Tiryaki sources directly from 40 farmers in Turkey through contract farming arrangements, providing them seeds and pre-financing in the process. In addition, the Company works with third-party logistics and service companies. The Project will increase the impact of the Company on SMEs along its supply chain. -Job Creation and Increased Tax Revenues for the Government: Profitable growth of Tiryaki''s business would create new jobs and increase the tax revenues to the Government. -Supporting a Regional Player: The Project will strengthen the Company`s market position, which has substantial room for consolidation, and improve its competitiveness in agribusiness sector regionally.
Company Name: TIRYAKI AGRO GIDA SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: Agricover Credit (the “Project”) would involve a senior loan of up to €12.5 million to Agricover Credit IFN S.A. (the “Company”) for on-lending to qualified small and medium sized farmers in Romania. The proceeds of the sub-loans would be used to finance working capital expenses, equipment and machinery purchases by farmers. The Company is the financing arm within the Agricover Group and is the only financial institution in Romania aimed exclusively at agriculture financing.
