sponsor_shareholders: Agricover (“Agricover” or the “Group”) is an integrated agricultural group whose main operations include: (i) grain sourcing, trading and logistics services; (ii) distribution of agricultural inputs to farmers; (iii) provision of financing to farmers; (iv) fuel distribution to agriculture; and (v) trading of meat and livestock. It is the 3rd largest grain trader in Romania and has the 2nd largest logistics network across the country with 32 silos for a total storage capacity of 700,000 tons. The Company’s shareholders are Agricover S.A. (87%) and Agricover S.R.L. (13%) while the ultimate majority owner of the Group is Mr. Jabbar Kanani.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The financing will be comprised of a senior loan of up to €12,500,000 from IFC’s own funds.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Bucharest, Romania. Investments can be made throughout the country.
development_impact: This project generates multiple developmental impacts: (i) Increases Access to Finance for Farmers: Romanian farmers would be able to access to long-term debt to finance their investments in agriculture sector, resulting in higher productivity and economic growth. (ii) Job Creation and Increased Tax Income for the Government: With IFC financing, the Company will be able to grow its business, creating new jobs and resulting in higher revenues and taxable income. (iii) Support to a Domestic Agriculture Group: The Project will strengthen the Company''s and the Sponsor''s market position and improve its competitiveness in agriculture sector.

project_description: Desarrollo Agricola del Paraguay S.A. (“DAP” or the “Company”) is one of the leading farming companies in Paraguay. IFC started its relationship with DAP in 2009 with a short term facility followed by an equity investment to support its operations. DAP currently owns more than 26,000 hectares and leases another 8,000 hectares in Paraguay to cultivate soybean, corn and sunflower with a social-inclusive and sustainable approach. It outsources farming operations to local specialized service providers such as seeding, fertilizing, harvesting, storage, and transportation operators. Desarrollo Agricola del Paraguay LT Financing (the “Project”) consists of providing a corporate long term facility to DAP for the financing of permanent working capital needs to sustain its farming activities in Paraguay.
sponsor_shareholders: DAP is a private Paraguayan Company owned by (i) Paraguayan and Argentine investors (39.1%), (ii) The Rohatyn Group (15.2%), (iii) Berkley International (26.1%), (iv) JP Morgan (10.6%), and IFC (9.1%). The Company is owned by its shareholders through two holding companies: Mercosur Agro Frontiers Fund LLC (MAFF) and NFD Agro Limited (NFD).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project consists of financing permanent working capital needs to sustain the Company’s farming activities in Paraguay. The proposed IFC investment is an up to $8 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Asunción, Paraguay and its farms are mainly located in rural areas in the States of the San Pedro and Concepcion of Paraguay.
development_impact: DAP is having a significant developmental impact by supporting a more productive farming business model in Paraguay, which is expected in turn to make significant contribution to Paraguay''s rural economic development as well as to global food security. DAP''s main impacts include: (i) DAP''s innovative approach to establish trust-based relationships with the local peasant communities. DAP''s initiatives help rural families to improve their farming practices, triggering a virtuous circle of development. (ii) DAP is partnering with leading NGOs and local community organizations to develop outreach programs for rural farmers to improve their access to new markets by (a) capacity building on good agricultural practices, (b) advise on product diversification (e.g. organic products), and (c) improve access to roads and logistic services. (iii) DAP has contributed to the development of a new class of agricultural service companies and SMEs agri-contractors in frontier rural areas that provide various services and inputs to the Company. DAP supports indirect employment for 850 persons working for more than 44 SMEs agri-contractors, which DAP promotes through trainings, workshops, and social activities. (iv) DAP contributes to food security by promoting soil conservation agriculture expertise (no-till farming), sustainable pest management (IPM) and world-class farm technology and management, increasing the yields and sustainability of owned and leased farms.

project_description: Lidl, a chain of discount grocery stores owned by the Schwarz Group (the “Group” or the “Company”) is implementing a long-term expansion plan in Romania by opening new Lidl discount stores (“Lidl Romania” or the “Project”). The Group, one of the largest European food retail discounters, has requested IFC to provide a long-term loan to its Romanian subsidiaries to partially finance the Project.
sponsor_shareholders: The Schwarz Group is a private company based in Germany. It is involved in discount food retail through two brands: Lidl (discount supermarket format) and Kaufland (discounting hypermarket format). It is one of the largest and fastest growing European discount retailers and has good presence in many western European countries as well as in Central and Eastern Europe. The project companies are Lidl Romania S.C.S., Lidl Discount S.R.L. and Lidl Immobiliare Romania Management S.C.S., which are all wholly owned by the Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a €50 million A loan for IFC’s own account to the Group.
location_description: The Project will involve the construction of new distribution centers and new discount stores located mainly in frontier regions and secondary and tertiary cities of Romania (e.g., Oltenita, Giurgiu, Slatina, Sighetu, etc.).
development_impact: Improvement in green building standards: As one of the few global retailers in the food discount stores segment in Romania, the Sponsor will, through the Project, contribute to the improvement of local green building standards by applying the highest level of energy efficiency measures, in line with the ones prevalent in its home market of Germany; which would help the new Lidl stores exceed IFC''s Green Building standard Food Supply chain development: Schwarz''s expansion will (i) increase the number of its local suppliers, (ii) provide additional sales channels for local fresh and dry food producers in Romania, and (iii) contribute to improvements in food security and availability, as well as in efficiency and operating standards throughout the supply chain. Benefits to low income consumers: By expanding the modern discount format in frontier regions and secondary and tertiary cities of Romania, Schwarz will be able to improve access of local low income customers to a more affordable diverse selection of high-quality food products. Employment generation: The Project will create significant local direct employment (mostly women who represent more than 60% of Lidl employees), and indirect employment in the retail value chain.

project_description: Matco Rice Processing (PVT) Ltd. (the “Company”) is a private-family owned limited company engaged in rice processing and export business. The Company has three rice processing plants, two in Karachi (Matco 1 & Matco 2) and one in Sadhoke. Rice is procured from Punjab and Sindh provinces and stored in warehouses in Karachi and Lahore. The production activity in Karachi comprises mainly of re-processing include polishing, length grading, color sorting, and packing lines of 5 and 25 tons per hour (tph) capacity respectively whereas Sadhoke has paddy drying, storage and milling processing line of 10 tph capacity. The project is to construct a modern rice paddy drying, husking and parboiling plant at Sadhoke, Punjab and storage capacity in Sadhoke (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project sponsor is the Ghori family (“Sponsors”) which own 100% of Matco Rice Processing. The Sponsors are a well established family which has over 45 years of experience in basmati rice business. Mr. Jawed Ali Ghori, is Matco’s Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director. Mr. Ghori has led Matco through various phases which included the construction and operation of Pakistan''s largest rice processing plant with the capacity of 25 MT/hour. Four additional members of the Ghori family play front-line roles in Matco as sponsors and managers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is $17.8 million investment program. IFC is considering an equity investment up to $5 million in the Company.
location_description: The Project is located at Sadhoke, a village of Gujranwala, Punjab of Pakistan. As a result of the Project, the Company will procure paddy directly from farmers and paddy trader which is expected to reduce supply bottlenecks and translate into additional margin opportunities for Matco.
development_impact: The expected development impact includes the following: (i) Employment: The Project will generate 300 new rural jobs and about 200 seasonal employees in Punjab in 2 years; (ii) Farmers reach: The Project will create additional backward linkages which are expected to generate benefits to approximately 1,500 farmers in the region; (iii) Improved agri-infrastructure: The Project will increase automatic drying capacity by 45,000 MT and automated silo capacity by 30,000 MT thus improving food storage in the Punjab region and reducing losses and bottlenecks; and (iv) Better quality product: The company will expand the production of its high quality branded rice products in Pakistan.

project_description: The proposed Project is an expansion of a greenfield plant in Egypt producing chemicals, primarily for export to large, international companies that manufacture home & personal care products in MENA, Europe & the Americas. A majority of Galaxy Egypt’s sales will go to multinationals, many of which are currently supplied from the Sponsor’s existing operations in India.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Galaxy Surfactants Limited (“Galaxy” or the “Company”), an Indian unlisted public company founded in 1986 that produces chemicals used by manufacturers of home & personal care (“H&PC”) products including shampoos, toothpastes, liquid soaps etc. It is a prominent & established supplier in the Indian market & exports to over 90 countries. Growth is expected in the BRIC and other developing countries as improved standards of living provide opportunity for increased demand for H&PC products. Galaxy’s top customers include multinational producers of home and personal care products. The Company''s promoters and promoter group collectively have approximately 76% of the equity shares in Galaxy.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be about $41 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $8 million A Loan, thus bringing the total IFC investment to $20 million.
location_description: The Project is located in the Suez Public Free Zone, an industrial area near the Red Sea, approximately 150 kilometers from Port Said, Egypt.
development_impact: (i) Setting up environment friendly world class facilities compliant with International Regulatory Standards. (ii) Employment Generation: The original project is expected to create nearly 110 jobs (including direct and indirect employment) with an additional 10 from the expansion. Additional training opportunities for about 30 local engineers. (iii) IFC''s investment in the Company will have a significant number of direct and indirect development benefits such as linkages with local suppliers, upgrade of existing infrastructure, indirect employment creation through auxiliary businesses in the region.

project_description: The Greenfield project involves the construction and operation of a 3 star hotel in Takoradi Ghana (the “Project”) by Alliance Estates Limited (the “Sponsor”). The hotel will be branded as a Protea Select managed by Protea International. Facilities will include 132 rooms and suites, a restaurant and bar, meeting space for 130 people, a workout room and 78 parking spaces.
sponsor_shareholders: Capital Alliance Property Investment Company (“CAPIC”) – CAPIC is $165 million real estate private equity Fund sponsored by African Capital Alliance (“ACA”). ACA is an independent firm formed in 1997 to promote private sector invests in Africa. ACA is headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria and is an existing IFC client. CAPIC holds a 49% equity stake in the Project. The Mohinani Group of Companies (“MG”). MG was established in 1966 in Ghana. It is a private diversified family owned group with interests in packaging product manufacturing, distribution of electronics, property, chemicals trading and recently, quick service restaurants. MG has over 3,000 staff globally, with operations in Ghana, Nigeria and Hong Kong. It also has a presence in East Africa, South Africa and India. In 2010 it achieved a global turnover of $347 million, and held assets of $198 million. The group has won many local and international awards for CSR, quality and market leadership. The group holds a 51% equity stake in the Project.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is $21.8 million The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of $5.45 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project is located in Takoradi, Ghana. The Project site is on a 8,134 sqm site in a low density residential area in central Takoradi with good road access to the airport, beach and other attractions. Approval has been obtained from the relevant authorities to demolish part of the existing buildings on the site.
development_impact: (i) Absorb the unmet demand for quality hotel of international standards in a major business district of Takoradi. (ii) Standards: Improve hotel standards in the 3 star segment. (iii) Skill transfer: Encourage the transfer of skills and expertise in hotel management to the local workforce. (iv) South-South Investment: support a South/South investment in CAF region. (v) Employment: Direct and indirect employment for locals during construction and operations. (vi) Revenues: Government revenue source through tax collection. (vii) Local supplies: local procurement of construction supplies, food and services throughout construction and operations.

project_description: As part of IFC’s strategic focus on addressing adverse climate change across the emerging markets, IFC is proposing to invest in a to-be-established investment vehicle (“Climate Catalyst Fund”) that will mobilize additional capital for co-investment alongside IFC in private equity funds (“Climate Funds”) focused on low-carbon and climate-friendly projects and companies globally across the emerging markets. The objective of the Climate Catalyst Fund is to stimulate the development of Climate Funds and climate friendly projects and companies which are expected to play a key role in accelerating the growth of investment in renewable energy and other low-carbon solutions.
sponsor_shareholders: IFC will seed the Climate Catalyst Fund. Large global institutional investors are expected to invest alongside IFC. The Climate Catalyst Fund will be managed by IFC Asset Management Company, LLC (“AMC”), a wholly owned subsidiary of IFC. AMC mobilizes and manages third party funds for investment in developing and frontier markets. It was created in 2009 to expand the supply of long-term capital to these markets by accessing IFC’s global reach, investment approach and standards.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC''s investment will be 20% of total commitments made to the Climate Catalyst Fund subject to an overall cap of $75 million.
location_description: The domicile of the Climate Catalyst Fund will be determined upon completion of due diligence.
development_impact: The project is expected to deliver strong development impact by: (i) stimulating the development of Climate Funds and climate friendly projects and companies which are expected to play a key role in accelerating the growth of investment in renewable energy and other low-carbon solutions; (ii) mobilizing the additional capital needed to help fill the investment gap caused by the reluctance of institutional investors to invest in Climate Funds and climate friendly projects; (iii) reducing GHG emission and creating other positive environmental impacts; (iv) promoting the robust, inclusive economic growth needed to improve the lives of people impacted by adverse climate change; (v) transferring technology, best practices (including IFC Performance Standards) and innovative business models; and (vi) raising awareness of the commercial attractiveness of investing in low-carbon and climate-friendly projects and companies, and helping institutional investors to learn about these sectors in emerging markets.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: Located in Chisinau, Moldova, Glass Container Prim S.A. (“GC Prim” or the “Company”) is an early-stage flint glass investment, which was established as the sister company of the leading Moldovan glass packaging producer, Glass Container Company (“GCC”). While GCC specializes in the production of colored glass packaging products, in light of the historical demand observed by the GCC management for flint (i.e. transparent) glass packaging products, and due to increased customer focus on quality, two of GCC’s largest shareholders decided to launch a new investment in the high-quality flint glass segment under a new legal entity, that became GC Prim. Construction process of GC Prim was finalized in May 2010, when GC Prim opened the new glass plant with a total capacity of 65,000 tones of finished goods per annum (rough equivalent of 130 million bottles). At this juncture, during the ramp-up stage of operations, additional financial resources are needed for GC Prim in order to strengthen the capital structure of the Company, to refinance part of its existing loans, to provide working capital and to fund capital expenditure requirements of the Company (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Horizon Capital (“HC”) is a private equity fund manager with over $600 million under management, focusing on mid-cap businesses in Ukraine, Belarus and Moldova. Western NIS Enterprise Fund (“WNISEF”) is a $150 million fund managed by HC and funded by the United States government via the United States Agency for International Development (“USAID”). WNISEF has a successful track record of 15 years of investments in the region. The WNISEF fund currently holds a 90% ownership stake in GC Prim, with the remaining 10% split between Mr. Oleg Baban (GC Prim’s CEO) and Moldova-Agroindbank (“MAIB”). MAIB is the leading commercial bank in Moldova. It offers a wide range of banking services with a nationwide presence and has a history of over 20 years on the local market. MAIB''s network included 69 branches and 22 representative offices at the end of 2010, having a national market share of 19.8% by total assets, 21.4% by total loans and 19.2% by total deposits. MAIB provides services to corporates, SMEs and retail customers; corporate lending represented 58% of loans as of end-2009. MAIB also owns 100% of MAIB Leasing (leading leasing company on the market) and has 8 minority participations in companies active in sugar / leather processing, glass production, agriculture.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project Cost is estimated at $29.3 million and involves the recapitalization of GC Prim’s capital structure through the combination of partial refinancing of the Company''s existing indebtedness and a partial debt-to-equity swap by WNISEF and MAIB, as well as the provision of additional funds for capital expenditures and working capital needs of the Company. The proposed IFC financing entails a total of $13 million investment, which would be comprised of a senior secured A Loan and a C Loan with income participation component, both facilities having an 8-year tenor. Total financing amount is expected to be shared evenly by IFC with a parallel lender, which is being mobilized by IFC.
location_description: GC Prim’s production facility is located in Chisinau, Republic of Moldova. With a brand new melting furnace (supplied by Techglass, Poland) and two Emhart (Sweden) production lines put in operation in May 2010, GC Prim’s high quality flint glass production complements the range of bottles and jars produced by GCC in its production facility, which is located at the same industrial campus.
development_impact: By providing financial support to GC Prim, IFC directly supports: - the retention of jobs for local staff in an IDA country with limited alternative employment prospects; - a sustainable local glass packaging industry player to continue its operations in a financially sustainable manner, that would also have positive effect on the beverage production sector in Moldova; - the competitiveness of a successful exporter in an IDA country. Furthermore, by facilitating the partial reduction of the outstanding MAIB loan by proposed USD 5 million, IFC would enable MAIB to: - comply with the recently tightened single-client exposure limitations of the Central Bank of Moldova; - free-up additional capital to be redeployed domestically to a broader base of borrowers, including many SMEs.

company_name: JIANGXI JINYUAN AGRICULTURE DEVELOPMENT CO., LTD.
project_description: With a growing customer preference for credible organic foods, larger and branded organic food companies are expected to further strengthen their market position. Jiangxi JinYuan Agriculture Development Co., Ltd (“JinYuan” or the “Company”) is planning to build an organic food processing facility in Tonggu county in Jiangxi Province (the “Project”), a neighboring county to Wanzai where the Company’s existing facility is located, to expand its capacity. The Project is estimated to cost about $54 million.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 2004, JinYuan is now a leading processor and exporter of organic fruits and vegetables. Its major shareholders include Wanzai County Kangmei, SAIF Partners and DT Capital. Currently the Wanzai County Kangmei owns about 61% of the Company, while SAIF Partners and DT Capital total owning rest about 38%. Mr. Chen Gengsheng, aged 48, is the Executive Chairman of the Board. Mr. Chen received PhD in law from Beijing University in China. Inspired by the provincial government’s ambition to promote organic industry in Wanzai and Tonggu area and recognizing the opportunity in organic foods, Mr. Chen established JinYuan in 2004.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at about $54mm. The proposed IFC investment is up to $20 million, including equity and debt.
location_description: Both the Wanzai and the proposed Tonggu facilities are located in peri-urban settings. The Wanzai facility is located in the county economic development park with a number of residential houses nearby, and the proposed Tonggu facility will be located close to a local village.
development_impact: 1.Rural growth and Employment: The Project supports a organic food company in the frontier region in China. The Company will have impact and rural reach by procuring from additional households, employing additional rural workers, and create business opportunities for MSMEs. 2. Sustainability and Standards: By investing in JinYuan, IFC will be supporting a Company with a keen desire to contribute to the sustainable rural development and adopt higher food safety/quality standards. 3. Demonstration Effect: The success of the Project is expected to have strong demonstration effect in the organic food industry in China and sets a good example for peers to improve their operational standards.
Company Name: JIANGXI JINYUAN AGRICULTURE DEVELOPMENT CO., LTD.

sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: Cosmo Films Limited (“Cosmo” or the “Company”) is an Indian manufacturer of bi-axially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) and thermal films. BOPP films are used in packaging materials in the textile and food industry, sticky tape, labels of mineral water and soft drink bottles, the lamination of book covers, etc while thermal laminating films are used to laminate books, posters, calendars, etc. The proposed project involves the expansion of its manufacturing capacity in Shendra Special Economic Zone in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, by a 40,000 tonnes per annum line (the “Project”). Initially, Cosmo had proposed expansion of its manufacturing facility in Vadodara by 40,000 tonnes per annum line as well as the setting up of a facility in another developing nation. However, those plans have been subsequently changed.
sponsor_shareholders: Cosmo is India’s second largest manufacturer and exporter of BOPP films with its facilities in Aurangabad, Maharashtra and Vadodara, Gujarat. Incorporated in 1976, Cosmo is listed on both, the Bombay and the National Stock Exchanges, and has a market capitalization of roughly $14 million.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be about $43 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $10 million A loan for IFC’s own account. The balance will be funded through other loans and internal accruals.
location_description: The expansion of the Indian operations will be located within Shendra Special Economic Zone in Aurangabad, Maharastra, India.
development_impact: Employment opportunities - The Project is expected to create up to 300 new employment opportunities. Efficient technology usage – The Project will employ technology that improves the conversion ratio (input raw material to film output) thereby reducing wastage in the environment and contributing to a cleaner environment.

project_description: The proposed project consists of the renovation and rebranding of the former 3-star 106 keys Novotel hotel in Bujumbura, Burundi into a 4-star 138-room “Doubletree by Hilton” hotel (the “Project”or the “hotel”or “Hilton Bujumbura”). The hotel will be the first international, upscale brand operating in Burundi and will address the lack of adequate accommodation facilities in Bujumbura.
sponsor_shareholders: Opulent (B) Ltd (the “Company”), the Burundi-based project company, ownes the Hotel and will operate it under a franchise agreement with the Hilton Group. The Company is equally owned by Mr. Ayaz Ali Jivraj and Mr. Bashir Nathoo (together the “Sponsors”). Mr. Ayaz Ali Jivray has a sound experience in hospitality management coupled with property development and construction. He has an Honors Degree in Building Legislation and technology and an MBA from the Manchester Business School in England. Mr. Bashir Nathoo has a BSc. in Electronics and a MSc. in Computer Sciences at the University College London. Mr. Nathoo has been in the hospitality industry for over 20 years. The Sponsors have successfully developed two Double Tree by Hilton hotels in Tanzania, respectively in Dar Es Salaam and Zanzibar.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $21.8 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan of up to $5.5 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project is located in the heart of the business district of the capital city of Burundi.
development_impact: The Project will: (i) address the supply-demand gap for business hotels of international standards, providing key business infrastructure as the Country emerges from a post-conflict status; and (ii) raise the country hotel standards by supporting the establishment of a 4-star internationally managed hotel in the country.

project_description: Established in 1962, Tbilvino (the “Company” or “Tbilvino”) is one of the largest Georgian wine-makers and exporters, concentrates exclusively on wine production and procures grapes from more than 300 Georgian farmers, located in Kakheti Region of Georgia. The Proposed IFC loan will be will be utilized for: (i) construction of primary facilities for grape collecting and crushing, in Kvareli region of Georgia; (ii) working capital requirement and (iii) additional capital expenditures to increase capacity of wine holding refrigeration tanks (collectively the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsors are Mr. Zurab Margvelashvi and Mr. George Margvelashvili, Georgian citizens. The Sponsors own 100% of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at $3 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $1.5 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Headquartered in Tbilisi, Tbilvino also has its main operational facilities in Tbilisi. The investment will be made in Kvareli region, about 150 kilometers from Tbilisi (east of Georgia). Kvareli is one of the main grape growing regions in Georgia and new facilities will be located close to the farmers, who are the main suppliers of Tbilvino.
development_impact: The project will have following development impact: i) Promotion of formal private sector abiding by rules, regulations and obligations; ii) Creation and preservation of direct and indirect employment in rural areas of Georgia, where the job opportunities are scarce; iii) Linkage to farmers - IFC''s support will ensure the sustainability and growth of income for more than 300 Georgian farmers; iv) Improvement of product quality and food safety management systems, compared to uncontrolled producers; v) Contribution to the recovery of Georgia''s wine sector, helping to increase the Country''s export potential; vi) Generating additional amount of taxes paid by the Company to the Government.

project_description: PROGIMMO S. A (“Progimmo” or the “Company”), a local property developer in Burundi, intends to build and manage a modern office/commercial building in Bujumbura (the “Project”). The Project will consist of two three story structures with about 7,000 m2 and adequate parking. The design of the building will conform to international life, fire and safety standards.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor is Mr. Edouard Hicintuka, a 58 year old Burundian businessman and property developer. He incorporated PROGIMMO in June 2005 to develop and manage commercial properties in Burundi.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project cost is estimated at $ 8.3 million. The proposed IFC investment is expected to consist of an “A” loan of up to $ 1.5 million and a “C” loan of up to $ 2.0 million on IFC’s account.
location_description: The Project will be located on a 8,250 m2 plot of land in a new neighborhood off Avenue du Large in Bujumbura. The plot is close to Lake Tanganyika, about 2 km from the city centre, and is easily accessible to major roads.
development_impact: - Contribute to filling the gap between supply and demand for quality office space in Bujumbura and provide much needed property infrastructure which is necessary to attract and retain investment in this post conflict country; - Private sector development, an important engine for growth, in a post-conflict country; - Introduce new building standards to the market; - Have a demonstration effect on other local companies to pursue similar commercial property development projects; - Create opportunity for linkages and benefit to other sectors of the economy, from suppliers to tenants who will benefit from additional quality office space; - Create employment (direct and indirect) for about 200 people during construction and about 100 post-construction; - Increase in government revenues through taxes paid.

project_description: IFC is considering to invest up to EUR11 million to support the expansion of Patisen, a food processing and distribution company in Senegal. Patisen’s main activity includes the production and distribution of bouillon cubes and chocolate and peanut spreads. IFC’s financing will be used to expand Patisen’s production capacity to serve domestic and export markets, to build a new factory and warehouse facilities, support product diversification, and for working capital needs.
sponsor_shareholders: Patisen, based in Dakar, Senegal, was founded in 1981 by Mr. Youssef Omais, a Senegalese national, who owns and manages the business.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at EUR23 million. IFC’s proposed financing is up to EUR11 million.
location_description: Patisen’s existing facilities whose production capacity is being expanded are located in industrial zones of Dakar, Senegal. The new facility is expected to be built near Ndiass, Senegal, in proximity to a new highway and airport that are under construction.
development_impact: - Increase supply of food production domestically, thereby benefiting local consumers. - Support transformation of a local company into a regional champion. - Employment creation: The Company has 250 full-time employees and 1,000 temporary employees. The Project will create additional jobs. - SME development: The Company assists small wholesalers with a professional Patisen sales force to distribute its products to consumers, thereby transferring marketing know-how and sustainability of local SME wholesalers.

project_description: IFC is considering providing a $50 million long term subordinated debt facility to ECOM Agroindustrial Corp. Ltd (“Ecom” or the “Company”), which would support Ecom’s internal financing needs to maintain and grow its business (e.g. risk management systems, sustainability initiatives, provision of services to farmers). Ecom is active in sourcing from Latin America, Africa and Asia, and the proposed project will support Ecom’s global efforts to continue to source from smallholders and assist smallholders adopt Voluntary Commodities Standards and, as such, improve their overall Environmental and Social performance.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Ecom, a commodity trading company incorporated in Switzerland, with operations primarily in agricultural commodities such as coffee, cotton and cocoa and to a lesser extent grain and other agricultural products, and raising pork. Ecom operates as a fully integrated commodity originator, processor and merchandiser, providing primary processing, logistics and risk management services, and selling to branded product manufacturers covering the United States, Central and South America, Europe, Asia and Africa. Ecom was founded in Barcelona, Spain in 1849 by the Esteve Family, which still owns 94% of the Company with the balance held by the senior management. Ecom is a long-standing client of IFC, with one completed investment (fully repaid), and two ongoing investments. Ecom is also an Advisory client of IFC, with several ongoing initiatives and one successfully completed project.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a $50 million convertible C Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The investment is a corporate facility, improving the Company’s current capital structure and supporting their financing needs across Latin America, Africa and Asia. The use of funds is restricted to Part 2 country operations in IFC member countries.
development_impact: The project will create significant benefits to the communities where Ecom operates in terms of employment, business opportunities for small farmers and promotion of sustainable business practices. IFC quasi equity financing and the Advisory Services programs will, directly and indirectly, enable Ecom to expand its sustainability programs which will generate the following development impacts: - Improved E&S practices at the farm level and improved traceability and certification of cocoa and coffee; - Demonstration effect: other physical merchants attracted to Better Cotton Initiative; - Increased farmers' income through training, improved access to market and improved farm productivity. - Improved access to finance for farmers and ability to implement capex at the farm level with-multi-year payback periods where Ecom extends supplier advances

sector: Paper Packaging Products (Including Boxes, Cartons, etc.)
project_description: Altyn Ajydar (AA) is a leading producer of corrugated packaging in the Kyrgyz Republic and a long-term IFC client with sales of $5.4 million in 2010. AA’s management has currently identified strong demand for packaging in Kazakhstan in line with the growth potential of the agribusiness, food processing, appliances and consumer goods sectors. AA now wishes to expand its production and sales to neighboring Kazakhstan closer to its main market and clients. Through this investment, IFC will be able to: (i) provide longer term financing that is currently unavailable in the local market in sufficient amounts; (ii) support the expansion of an existing viable client in an IDA country to larger markets in Kazakhstan in the wake of the global financial crisis and economic contraction in the Kyrgyz Republic; and (iii) continue working with AA on implementing improved safety, labor, health, and environmental practices as well as provide advice on corporate governance in both Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan.
sponsor_shareholders: The majority of shares (53%) of Altyn Ajydar (“AA”) are owned by Mr. Pavel Terekhov, President, and the rest of the shares are owned by his family members (the “Sponsors”). IFC provided financing of $0.3 million to AA in 1999 for the modernization and expansion of its existing cardboard packaging facility and $1.4 million in 2005 to set up a new corrugated packaging line with a capacity of 10 million square meters near Bishkek. In 2008, IFC committed a third loan of $1.6 million to finance the production of alucobond panels and insulated glass window units, which was partially disbursed and the remainder was cancelled in 2010 due to declining demand for building materials during the global economic slowdown. IFC projects were implemented successfully, as AA improved its operating performance, increasing its sales from $1.6 million in 2003 to $5.4 million in 2010, by more than 3 times. AA is currently the leader in the corrugated packaging industry in the local Kyrgyz market. AA now wishes to expand its production to neighboring Kazakhstan in order to be closer to its main market and clients. Production in Kazakhstan will be undertaken by Intermultiservices (“IMS”), AA’s wholly-owned subsidiary in Kazakhstan.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the new project is estimated at around $4.5 million, which will be financed by an estimated contribution from the Sponsors and AA of $2.25 million and a senior IFC loan of $2.25 million for IFC’s own account to finance the AA’s corrugated packaging production in Kazakhstan.
location_description: The project is located in facilities owned by the IMS in Alma-Aty, Kazakhstan with suitable road, power, water and security infrastructure.
development_impact: The proposed project will help AA expand into Kazakhstan and improve its competitiveness with the production of multi-layer packaging products through the use a new and more efficient corrugated packaging line in a location that is closer to its client base in Kazakhstan. Moreover, the project will have a demonstration effect for other SMEs, as AA has been a successful company in the region. Besides improving the company’s competitiveness, the investment is expected to result in an estimated additional employment of 100 workers in Kazakhstan.

project_description: The proposed investment of up to $40 million would support Alpha (the Company), a subsidiary of Corporacion GEO S.A.B. de C.V. (Geo or the Sponsor), in the expansion of its prefabricated construction business for affordable housing in Mexico. With this investment, Alpha expects to achieve the capacity to build 40,000 - 45,000 houses per year. Alpha has an innovative process that will allow GEO to build all the pieces of a house in a production facility and assemble them on site using modern European technology. Alpha production facilities include a factory in Tijuana which started production in 2010 and other three factories (Zumpango, Monterrey and Jalisco) that are in the process of being built.
sponsor_shareholders: Alpha is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Corporacion GEO S.A.B. de C.V (Geo or Sponsor), a leading housing developer in Mexico and one of the largest in Latin America. Geo is a fully integrated and highly diversified homebuilder engaged in all aspects of design, development, construction, marketing, sales and delivery of houses mainly in the low-income segment. The Sponsor was founded in 1973 and is now present in 57 cities and 18 states, selling more than half a million homes since its inception. GEO is listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange with a market capitalization of approximately $1.4 billion as of May 13, 2011.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $150-200 million. IFC is planning to invest up to $40 million in equity or quasi-equity.
location_description: The project will be implemented in Mexico supporting plants in Tijuana, Zumpango, Jalisco, Monterrey, and an additional plant to be determined as well as mobile plants throughout Mexico.
development_impact: The development impacts of the project include: (i) increase of housing supply for low income households - this project is expected to contribute to the alleviation of the current housing deficit in Mexico, increasing the supply of affordable entry level housing by 40,000 houses a year; (ii) GEO plans to leverage part of the efficiency gains by providing a larger house (more square meters) to its clients at the same low entry price (approximately US$15,000); (iii) enhanced supply linkages - the project will increase demand for construction and building materials in the country; (iv) job creation - the new facilities are expected to create 1,500 new jobs in 2011 and additional jobs in line with the Company's growth in the future; (v) demonstration effect - the project will lead the way to improve private sector development in this segment of the housing market; (vi) Green Building- the technology adopted by ALPHA will reduce the environmental impact building materials by saving of more than 70% of the traditional waste generation and reduction of the energy use in the construction process by 18%. The prefabrication will also allow for higher levels of insulation and integration of water and energy efficient technology in the homes. The client is interested to work with IFC's Green Building Specialist to explore these opportunities.

project_description: IFC is considering a $350 million investment to be allocated to Orascom Construction Industries (“OCI”) and its wholly owned subsidiary, the Egyptian Fertilizers Company (“EFC”). OCI is one of the largest construction and fertilizers groups in the Middle East and Africa region and is present in over 25 countries across the world. In its present form OCI acts as a holding and operating company. Collectively, the Group’s companies (fertilizers and construction) employ more than 86,000 people. OCI, post disposal of the cement business to Lafarge at the end of 2007, became a leading global nitrogen fertilizer producer and distributor through acquisition of existing players and investment in Greenfiled projects. EFC, which was acquired by OCI in 2008, manufactures granulated Urea with a total production capacity of 1.3 million tons per annum. The majority of EFC’s output is targeted for export. OCI’s overall production and distribution capacity is expected to reach 7.45 mtpa by 2012. IFC funds will go to support OCI’s growth plans for the fertilizers and construction operations as well as restructure the Group’s debt financing towards a longer term, more stable structure that is suitable for the nature of the Group’s operations.
sponsor_shareholders: OCI is the largest company listed on Egypt Stock Exchange (EGX), with GDRs listed on the London Stock Exchange and ADRs listed on the US Over-the-Counter (OTC) market. OCI’s current capitalization is US$8.5 billion (based on May 15th share price). OCI’s major shareholder is the Sawiris family with a 54.3% stake in the company (“the Sponsor”). Other shareholders with significant stakes include Abraaj Capital (6.2%) and Lazard (5.0%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC financing will be directed to support the Group’s long term investment needs and replacing existing shorter term debt financing, previously raised in to partially fund the acquisition costs related to the Group’s fertilizers assets. IFC is considering a total investment package of up to $350 million which will structured as corporate finance facilities.
location_description: OCI is headquartered in Cairo, Egypt. The construction operations span most of Egypt, a number of countries in MENA including Algeria, UAE, Saudi Arabia and Qatar OCI construction Group also operates in Europe and the United States. For fertilizers, OCI plants are located in Egypt, Algeria and the Netherlands. The Group also includes fertilizers distribution channels in Western Europe, Dubai, Brazil and the United States. EFC is located in the Suez Industrial Development Company, in Ain Sokhna, Suez Governorate on the Red Sea in Egypt.
development_impact: The proposed investment is expected to have the following development impacts: (1) revenue generation to the Egyptian government as both OCI and EFC through tax payments by OCI and EFC; (ii) contributing foreign currency income to the country through export revenues and dividends received from investments outside of Egypt; (iii) job creation, directly through a number of planned capacity expansions in the fertilizers sector, and indirectly through sub contracting parts of the construction works in many on the Group''s projects; and (iv) contribution to food security through increased availability of fertilizers to support supply growth in primary agriculture.

company_name: S.A. SAN MIGUEL A.G.I.C.I. y F.
project_description: San Miguel runs a capital intensive business as citrus trees take an average of 5-7 years to reach maturity. The proposed 6-year A loan (US$5 million) & B loan (US$20 million) would allow San Miguel to maintain an adequate balance sheet structure by replacing loans due in the coming 2 years with longer maturities.
sponsor_shareholders: S.A. San Miguel A.G.I.C.I.y.F (“San Miguel”) is a world leader in citrus production and exports, with US$207 million consolidated revenues, 1,200 permanent staff and 5,500 seasonal workers, and operations in Argentina, Uruguay and South Africa. In 2009, San Miguel produced 250,000 MT of lemon on its own 5,500 Ha of plantations, exported over 73,000 MT of fresh citrus to Europe and Asia, and processed 275,000 MT of lemons to produce concentrated frozen lemon juice, essential oil and dry peel.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed investment is for a US$5 million A loan for IFC’s own account and US$20 million B loan.
location_description: San Miguel owns and operates several plantations in the Tucuman, a region in the northern part of Argentina where the climatic conditions and the quality of the soils is ideal for citrus growing. The company’s packing and processing plants are located in San Miguel de Tucuman and Famaillá respectively.
development_impact: The project would help to: (i) improve the debt structure of the Company by replacing financial debt maturing in the next two years with long term debt; (ii) assist the Company to continue its investment program in a frontier region in Argentina (province of Tucuman); (iii) support the final completion of an innovative waste water treatment designed to adress the specific and difficult effluent issue faced by San Miguel; (iv) provide economic benefits for Tucuman, a frontier region, and benefit local farmers, workers and affiliated enterprises; (v) maintain the financial flexibility of San Miguel in order to continue its South-South investments in Uruguay and South Africa.
Company Name: S.A. SAN MIGUEL A.G.I.C.I. y F.

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: Founded in 1691 in Japan, Sumitomo Forestry Co, Ltd. (“SFC” or the “Sponsor”) is one of the most experienced companies in sustainable forest and plantation management, wood products and wood-based housing sectors. SFC is planning to invest in a USD 93 million project to establish a greenfield particleboard plant with an annual capacity of 250,000 m3 near Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (the “Project”). The Project will increase Vietnam’s particleboard production capacity, responding to the growth outlook of Vietnam’s furniture and wood processing sector and current limited particleboard production capacity available in Vietnam.
sponsor_shareholders: The new particleboard plant will be owned and operated by Vina Eco Board Co., Ltd. (“VECO” or the “Company”). VECO was established in May 2010 by SFC and Sumitomo Forestry (Singapore) Ltd., SFC’s wholly owned subsidiary in Singapore. Incorporated in 1947, SFC is a publicly listed company on the first section of Tokyo Stock Exchange and Osaka Securities Exchange. SFC’s shares are widely held by institutional investors, financial institutions as well as individual investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be approximately USD93 million, and SFC plans to finance the Project with 50% in long term debt and 50% in equity. The proposed IFC investment is an equity investment of up to USD9 million for up to 20% of VECO’s share capital.
location_description: The Project site is at the Phu An Thanh Industrial Park, Long An Province, about 30 km west of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
development_impact: (i) Climate Change Mitigation: Through the Project, IFC will support positive climate change impact linked to sourcing of waste wood and use of bio-mass based power plant. (ii) Employment: The Project will generate about 200 jobs at the Project site and also indirect employment through linkages to farmers who will supply part of the wood raw materials to the Project. In the future, the Company is considering supporting farmers in sustainable plantation by working with local government agencies and research institutes and providing advice and seedlings. (iii) Development of Local Industry: The Project will support the development of local wood processing industry by establishing the first particleboard facility in Vietnam. From construction phase to operational stage, SFC will bring in its first class expertise and quality management system, which is expected to have demonstration effect to the local industry.

project_description: Paradeep Phosphates Limited (PPL or the Company) is a going concern engaged in the production of approximately 1.2 million metric tons per annum (MTPA) of fertilizers, including di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) ) and other complex phosphatic fertilizers representing a combination of multiple nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, potash, and sulphur. PPL also produces intermediary products like phosphoric acid and sulphuric acid, which are its critical raw materials. The plant, located in the port town of Paradeep in the district of Jagatsinghpur in Orissa, has an installed capacity of 720,000 MTPA of DAP, making PPL one of the largest integrated complex-fertilizer plants in India, with a strong market presence, especially in Orissa, and in the neighboring states of West Bengal, Jharkhand, Chattisgarh, eastern Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh. PPL has been operating at over 100% capacity since 2003, and has now undertaken a three-year expansion plan requiring a capital expenditure of approximately $120 million to increase its current production capacity of di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) and nitrogen, phosphorus and potash NPK fertilizers by ~25% to 1.5 million MTPA to meet India’s growing demand for fertilizers (the “Project”). The Project entails the addition of incremental capacity as well as improvements to plant efficiency by improving raw material consumption, the material handling system, product quality and environmental standards.
sponsor_shareholders: PPL is majority owned by Zuari Industries Limited (ZIL), a K.K. Birla Group company, and Maroc Phosphore, SA, a Moroccan state-owned 100% subsidiary of Office Cherifien Des Phosphates (OCP). Government of India (GoI) holds residual shares post-privatizetion. ZIL: Zuari Industries Ltd, initially incorporated as Zuari Agro Chemicals Ltd. in 1967, is a member of the US$2.5 billion K.K. Birla Group, one of India’s most well-respected business houses. Started as a partnership with the US Steel Corporation, the company now has four manufacturing facilities in Goa, which provide the neighboring markets with urea, DAP and NPK fertilizers. ZIL has now diversified into several other areas, including cement, hybrid seeds, engineering consultancy, financial services and oil tanking. ZIL is publicly listed and has a market capitalization of over US$400 million. OCP: OCP was founded in 1920 and is based in Casablanca, Morocco. The OCP Group engages in mining, processing, exporting, and marketing phosphates. The company produces phosphate rock, phosphate derivatives, such as basic and purified phosphoric acid and phosphatic fertilizers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be up to $120 million. The proposed IFC is investment is an A Loan of up to $50 million. The loan shall be utilized for capacity expansion and other allied CAPEX programme.
location_description: PPL is headquartered at Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Marg, Bhubaneshwar 751 001, Orissa. Orissa. The Project will be undertaken in PPL’s existing plant located at PPL Township, Paradeep 754 145, District: Jagatsinghpur, Orissa.
development_impact: The Project is expected to: (i) increase the domestic capacity of DAP and other complex phosphatic fertilizers, and contribute to the growth of the agricultural sector in India; (ii) assist the Company in upgrading its environmental and operating performance to achieve international standards; (iii) help lower PPL's production costs which would benefit the farmers; (iv) help mitigate the impact of climate change since the energy released during the sulphuric acid oxidation process will be used to power a significant part of the plant's operations; (v) create a number of direct and indirect job opportunities for local communities, including temporary employment to local labor during the construction phase of the Project assets.

project_description: Artha Capital S de RL de DV (“Artha” or the “Sponsor”) a Mexican real estate fund, focused on the development of affordable housing, retail, industrial and tourism projects in Mexico. Artha finances land and infrastructure investments consisting of the acquisition and development of land, the implementation of planned and sustainable urban projects and the implementation of basis infrastructure and sale of land for the purposes of housing, tourism, industrial and commercial development. The Company completed the raising of $200 million and has already built up a solid project pipeline. In its efforts to diversify its portfolio and complete the execution of its targeted projects Artha has invited IFC to invest up to $25 million equivalent in Mexican pesos in equity to finance the individual sub-projects. It is estimated that Artha will raise additional financing of $75 million.
sponsor_shareholders: Artha was founded by Mr. Carlos Gutierrez and Mr. German Ahumada who have a track record of over 16 years of experience in the real estate, infrastructure and financial markets. Artha’s Board and Investment Committee includes members such as Citigroup, BBVA, Bancomer and Banobras-Fonadin (Government Development Bank) as well as independent board members from Cushman & Wakefield and SOFTEC (Real Estate Market Research and Consulting firm in Mexico).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $250-300 million. IFC is planning to invest up to $25 million equivalent in Mexican pesos in equity alongside Artha and potentially other investors into an investment vehicle, which will then invest directly into individual sub-projects.
location_description: The investment vehicle through which IFC will invest will be set up in Mexico and will make investments into individual sub-projects throughout the country.
development_impact: The development impact of this project includes: (i) housing supply - alleviate the current housing shortage in Mexico; ii) community development - development of states and municipalities facilitating the efficient provision of municipal services; (iii) economic growth - contribution to the economic growth in the regions where investments will be made as a result of public private participation; and (iv) job creation - the project will create job opportunities both during construction and operation of the communities; (v) enhanced local supply linkages - increase demand for construction and building materials in the country.

sector: Other Steel Products (Including Wire, Metal Sheets etc.)
project_description: The project of approximately $120 million is to support operations of Scholz A.G. Germany (“Group” or the “Sponsor”) in Croatia, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, FYR Macedonia, Romania, Montenegro and Albania (referred to as the “Balkan” countries or the “Region”) over the next 4 years. The investment will finance modernization and working capital needs of the Group in the Region.
sponsor_shareholders: Scholz Group, headquartered in Essingen, Germany, is one of the leading metal waste management and recycling player in Europe and in the Balkan countries with developing presence in Asia, Central America, Middle East and North Africa.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project cost is estimated at $120 million. The IFC investment will consist of a loan of up to $60 million in Euro equivalent.
location_description: The Project will be focused (but may not be limited to) on the Group subsidiaries’ plants in Croatia, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania and Romania.
development_impact: An important aspect of this investment lies in the climate change element related to recovery of resources and creation of scrap as a raw material for steel making out of metal waste. Production of steel out of scrap significantly reduces CO2 emission and lowers energy and water consumption as compared to the traditional method. In addition to the environmental impact, metal waste management is vital for growth and sustainability of the Balkan economies, many of which are struggling with high unemployment and with management metal waste. The Group''s operations and the Project address both issues by providing direct and indirect employment for collecting the waste metal and cleaning up the areas from the waste An important aspect of this investment lies in the climate change element related to recovery of resources and creation of scrap as a raw material for steel making out of metal waste. Production of steel out of scrap significantly reduces CO2 emission and lowers energy and water consumption as compared to the traditional method. In addition to the environmental impact, metal waste management is vital for growth and sustainability of the Balkan economies, many of which are struggling with high unemployment and with management metal waste. The Group’s operations and the Project address both issues by providing direct and indirect employment for collecting the waste metal and cleaning up the areas from the waste

project_description: Fawaz Abdulaziz Al Hokair & Co. (“ALH Retail” or “the Company”), Saudi Arabia’s leader in the apparel retail franchise sector, is implementing a program to expand its domestic operations, as well as to grow its international presence, which currently spans Egypt, Jordan, Kazakhstan and the UAE. The proposed expansion program comprises the increase in the number of stores operated by the Company from approximately 1,028 to approximately 1,780 over a 3-year period, and includes store openings in new countries of operations, such as Azerbaijan and Georgia.
sponsor_shareholders: ALH Retail, is part of Fawaz Alhokair Group (the “Group”), a diversified corporation with core businesses in retail, real estate and entertainment, mainly across Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (“KSA”). Established in 1989, the Group is controlled by the Al Hokair family, one of the most prominent business families in Saudi Arabia. ALH Retail owns franchising rights to more than 80 established global apparel and other consumer brands (women’s wear, menswear, children’s wear, footwear, intimate wear and accessories), which it sells throughout its extensive network of mainly leased stores across the KSA and other countries, including emerging markets, such as Egypt, Jordan and Kazakhstan. The Company holds a market leader position in its business in the KSA. Thirty percent of ALH Retail is a publicly traded at Tadawul, the KSA stock exchange. The remaining 70% of the Company’s shares directly and indirectly (through the Group) are controlled by the founding family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment comprises a corporate package of long-term loans to ALH Retail and its majority-owned subsidiaries in emerging market countries of operations for a combined amount of up to $75 million.
location_description: ALH Retail’s new leased stores to be opened as part of the Company’s corporate expansion program and to be financed with proceeds of IFC’s loans will be located in modern malls with good access to transportation routes and other necessary infrastructure in cities throughout the Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan and Georgia.
development_impact: Consumer Benefits: the expansion of the Company’s retail chain in the Central and Eastern Europe, as well as in the Middle East and North Africa regions, will enable ALH Retail to provide for its customers better access to a more diverse selection of high-quality, affordable apparel. This will be especially important for consumers in such countries as Azerbaijan and Georgia where modern apparel retail sector is still nascent. Stronger bargaining positions vis-a-vis suppliers, economies of scale achieved through geographical expansion, as well as improved inventory management are expected to result in cost savings, which eventually can be passed on to the end customer; Employment Generation: the expansion of the Company’s operations will create 1,000 permanent jobs. In addition, ALH Retail’s large-scale expansion will involve numerous leasehold improvements, which will generate temporary employment; Life and Fire Safety (“LFS”) Improvements: As a condition of the IFC investment, ALH Retail will commit to implement an improved LFS Action plan; Supporting IFC's reach in frontier regions and south-to-south investments: establishing a long term partnership with an important local player in its expansion plans to surrounding developing countries;

project_description: Idavang A/S (“the Company”, previously named “Danish Lithuanian Holding A/S”) is a Danish holding company that has pig and crop farms in Russia and pig farms in Lithuanian. The Project, located in Russia, is to: (i) build a green field pig farm in Pskov region; (ii) develop another pig farm in northwest region; (iii) complete the expansion of the pig farm in Leningrad region; and (iv) develop crop farms in Pskov and Leningrad regions. The total project cost is about EUR86.5 million. The Project is implemented in 2009-2014 and will increase production capacity by 6,450 sows and 185,000 finishers
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are the ultimate shareholders of the Company: Ole B. Hansen (50%), Carsten Thomsen (33%) and Claus Baltsersen (17%), all Danish farmers. The shareholders hold their shares through their respective private holding companies: Tofthøj Agro A/S in Denmark, Asket A/S in Denmark, and Sommerset Holding Limited in Cyprus.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at EUR86.5 million and the proposed IFC’s investment is straight equity of up to EUR16.8 million.
location_description: The Project will be implemented in Pskov and Leningrad regions in Russia. All land is farm land located in rural areas.
development_impact: - Support Russia's under-developed pork sector to modernize, achieve self-sufficiency & international competiveness. - Support an efficient producer with solid track record to expand efficient production in Russia, introduce high European standards of livestock production, showcase clean production (CP) and energy efficiency (EE) to other pork producers. - Support the frontier Pskov region (per capita GDP about 60% below national average) to revitalize waste land, develop competitive pig and crop production, create jobs in remote rural area, contribute to local community. The Project will help alleviate insufficient domestic pig production, substitute imports, increase fresh meat supply (vs. frozen imported meat), and pass cost savings to consumers. The Project will rehabilitate the crop land that has not been cultivated for 15-20 year and create jobs in the rural area with high level of unemployment. As pork production remains highly supported by the Government (interest subsidized loans, tax benefits, import tariffs), additional domestic production will also result in losses for the Government and local tax payers, which is expected to be compensated by increased corporate tax payment, benefits to employees, local economy and communities. Overall, the medium to long term developmental impact can be expected as: (i) Russia has excellent long term fundamentals for pig production (feed availability, climate, large tracts of land for waste disposal); (ii) current production costs in the country are not globally competitive but can be improved with better technology and livestock management standards introduced by efficient producers; and (iii) the country is a net importer and may be able to compete on an import parity basis.

sector: Other Miscellaneous Fabricated Metal Products (Including Non-Wood Housing Products, Tanks, Cutlery, Kitchen Utensils and Handtools, etc.)
project_description: Founded in 1921, FV S.A. (“FV” or the “Company”) is a second-tier family-owned and managed company and Argentina's leading producer of brass and metal fixtures for baths and kitchens. FV is well known to IFC, in 1998 IFC approved a $16 million financial package to FV, in 1999 IFC committed a $9 million financing package to FV Ecuacobre, and more recently in 2008, IFC committed another project with FV for up to $20.0 million. FV will embark in an investment program of about $20 million for the next two to three years, that would mainly comprise: (i) permanent working capital to maintain a well supplied wide portfolio of products to attend an exigent demand on a timely basis; (ii) improve operational efficiencies, including savings on a better use of energy resources; and (iii) completion of the environmental upgrades suggested by the IFC’s action plan.
sponsor_shareholders: FV is privately owned by the Viegener family. Four brothers, descendants of the founder, control through holding Companies 70.7% of the shares of the Company. The balance is held by other members of the extended family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: FV will embark in an Investment Program of about $20 million for the next two to three years. The proposed IFC Investment will comprise a corporate financing of up to $10 million to support the Company’s strategic plan.
location_description: FV is headquartered in an 8,000m2 facility in Florida, Buenos Aires, and has a production plant in a 60,000m2 site in Villa Rosa, Municipality of Pilar, Buenos Aires province.
development_impact: - Expansion of Argentine Export Base: FV's ability to continue developing its export base is dependent on the required permanent working capital needs to sustain an adequate and diversified level of stock to supply different markets abroad. The wide portfolio of products require FV to allocate larger amount of resources in order to better attend each market it supplies and enhance its competitive position abroad. - Creation of Consumer Surplus: FV's cost optimization and energy efficiency improvements is expected to eventually translate into more competitive prices to end users, primarily within the construction sector. More competitive prices for building materials will benefit the housing sector.

project_description: Food Concepts (“FC” or the “Company”) is a leading Quick Service Restaurants (QSR) and bakery operator based in Nigeria. QSR is branded as “Chicken Republic” with 60 outlets in Nigeria, 9 of which are franchised, and three in Accra, Ghana. FC also operates 10 bakeries, branded as “Butterfield”. The IFC investment would support capital expenditures and working capital over a 4 year period to develop approximately 40 additional QSR outlets; expand bakery capacity by approximately 100%, and make a further investment into poultry backward integration in Nigeria (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: Food Concepts was founded in 1999 by Mr. Deji Akinyanju, and commenced operations in 2001. It is a public company (though not listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange) whose shareholders are Food Concepts International Limited or FCIL (63.7%), Employee Share Trust (1.9%) and other shareholders (34.4%). In turn, FCIL’s main shareholders include Chief Dele Fajemirokun, Mr. Deji Akinyanju, Akinyanju Family, Mr. Sola Alabi, Mr. Jerry Chukwueke and Asaris Limited.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated to be $86 million consisted of: (i) QSR expansion; (ii) Bakery expansion; (iii) Setting up a poultry farm; and (iv) working capital. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan for IFC’s own account of up to $ 10 million, and equity of up to $ 10 million, to be used for QSR and bakery expansion.
location_description: Chicken Republic outlets are located in following cities: Lagos; Abuja; Port Harcourt; Zaira; Kaduna; Owerri; Ibadan; Warri; Benin; Calabar; Enugu; and Ilorin. Butterfield bakeries are located in following cities: Lagos; Abuja; Port Harcourt; Abeokuta; Ilorin; Benin; Kaduna; and Ibadan. Free Range Farms Limited (FRF) is being established on a 250 hectares of land in the Abeokuta Agricultural Zone (AAZ), Ogun State. All sites have good access to major transport routes.
development_impact: The Project's expected development impact includes (i) employment generation; (ii) gender promotion (QSR sector employs a high proportion of women); (iii) demonstration effect to the QSR/poultry market in West Africa; (iv) MSME reach; (v) develop efficient poultry industry in Nigeria; and (vi) introduction of best practice poultry using a technical partner with a proven track record.

company_name: KONCERN FARMAKOM M.B. DOO - U STECAJU
sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: Farmakom is one of the largest exporters in Serbia. Since 2006, the group has invested over EUR140 million in its operations in order to add capacity and improve productivity and environmental standards. The IFC project involves both an investment component and a corporate governance advisory component. The investment component seeks to (i) provide much needed financing to a leading private sector group in Serbia to restructure its debt, (ii) fund some capital investments, and (iii) finance additional working capital requirements in line with the projected growth in 2011-13 to increase utilization of completed investments.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1992, Farmakom is a diversified private group wholly owned by Mr. Miroslav Bogicevic, a Serbian citizen. Farmakom grew rapidly over the past five years by investing and successfully turning around all acquired companies through privatization.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at EUR166 million for the period covering 2011-2013. The project includes a corporate capital expenditure plan including maintenance capital investments, working capital financing, and the refinancing of the short-term debt in order to restructure the balance sheet. The project is proposed to be financed partially by an A Loan of EUR40 million for IFC’s own account in addition to up to EUR60 million in parallel loans from local banks in Serbia.
location_description: The Group is a regional player in the Balkans organized in three business lines (manufacturing, agribusiness and mining) with eight operating companies in Serbia in addition to the parent, Farmakom MB in Sabac. The operating companies of the Group are Fabrika Akumulatora Sombor, AD Mlekara Sabac, Zajaca Loznica, Pozega, IK Guca, PIK Debrc 7th July, Lece and Suva Ruda.
development_impact: The Group will - have access to liquidity in order to support its expansion in export markets generating hard currency for the country, - strengthen existing linkages with local suppliers, - provide value-added products & services to customer improving their living standards; and - additional tax revenues to the local Government by increased operations.
Company Name: KONCERN FARMAKOM M.B. DOO - U STECAJU

project_description: The project involves providing a three-year renewable working capital facility to Mriya, a leading Ukrainian primary agricultural producer with a proven track record of growing wheat, barley, sugar beet, rapeseed, potatoes, and other crops. The three-year facility will provide financing of inputs needed for agricultural production to produce agricultural commodities for sale to local clients and international traders.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is the Huta family (the “Sponsors”), who founded Mriya in 1992 and control it till this day. The head of the Huta family, Ivan Huta, a well-respected Ukrainian businessman, and his wife, Klaudia Huta, Ivan and Klaudia Huta established Mriya on 50 hectares of land, after having worked for eight years at a state farm. In 2002, Andriy and Mykola Huta, the sons of the founders, joined the family business after completing their education in Ukraine and abroad. Following a private placement on the Entry Standard of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2008, the Sponsors collectively own 80% of Mriya’s Cyprus-based holding company that fully controls all of Mriya’s Ukraine-based operating companies, with the remaining 20% owned by over 20 institutional investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is $90 million. The Project will encompass financing of agricultural commodities grown by Mriya as well as the purchasing of seeds, fertilizers, CPPs, fuel and other costs related to work in progress.
location_description: The project will allow Mriya to expand its farming operations and grain storage infrastructure in the Ternopil, Ivano-Frankivsk, Chernivtsi and Khmelnitsky regions, which are among the poorest, primarily agricultural, regions of Ukraine.
development_impact: IFC''s financing will contribute to the development of a large-scale modern farming operation which will improve land productivity and have a demonstration impact on other neighboring farms. Mriya''s land and operations are located in Western Ukraine in the Ternopil, Ivano-Frankivsk, Chernivtsi and Khmelnitsky regions. These four regions are amongst the poorest regions in the country. Development impact of the project will be as follows: Employment: Mriya has approximately 1,002 permanent employees and 623 seasonal employees. The project is expected to increase permanent employment to about 1700 and seasonal employment to about 900. In the western Ukraine where Mriya operates, employment opportunities are scarce. In addition to creating new jobs, Mriya is setting new employment standards in the region by providing benefits to its farm workers such food and housing. Environmental and Social Standards: As part of the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP), Mriya will implement an ESMS to provide a structured framework to identify and act on environmental and social risks and opportunities in the management of its agricultural operations as well as down-stream in the agricultural value chain, in the operations of the Sponsor-owned affiliated sugar beet processing plants. Private Sector Development: Mriya sells its products to a well diversified base of final customers and traders. Among them, there currently are about 55 MSME distributors of mainly potatoes, buckwheat, and corn, for final sales on the domestic market. On the purchasing side, Mriya relies on about 27 MSME suppliers, in addition to several large key ones, for deliveries of fertilizers, plant protection chemicals, and spare parts.

project_description: Formerly Dunlop Tyres South Africa Ltd, Apollo Tyres South Africa (Pty) Ltd has two manufacturing plants in South Africa, Durban and Ladysmith producing car, light truck, truck and bus, and of-the-road tires. The project is the expansion of the company’s car and light truck tire production capacity at it Ladysmith plant by about 30% to 13,000 tires per day.
sponsor_shareholders: The company is wholly owned by Apollo Tyres Ltd of India. The Company was acquired in 2006. Apollo Tyres is a leading Indian tire company and is listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd., Bombay Stock Exchange Limited and Cochin Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at R228 million ($31.4 million). The proposed IFC investment is a R75 million ($10.4 million) A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The company is headquartered in Durban. The project site is at the company’s plant in Ladysmith approximately 450 km south east of Johannesburg.
development_impact: The project will allow the company to increase domestic tire supply, maintaining the competitive market dynamics, with benefits to consumers, and to increase exports, earning the country an additional foreign exchange. The project will provide increased tax revenues to government.

project_description: Dunar, headquartered in Karnal, India is in the business of procurement, processing and supply of basmati rice. The Company owns two production facilities in Karnal, Haryana (modernized in 1996) and Amritsar, Punjab (commissioned in March 2010). The processing capacity of Karnal facility is 26 tons per hour (tph), while that for Amritsar facility is 24 tph. Dunar plans to invest in the expansion of its production capacity in Karnal from 26 tph to 50 tph during the next two years. It will also invest in additional silo capacity of 60,000 metric ton and rice husk-based power generation capacity of 3 MW in Karnal and a new rice husk-based power plant of 2 MW in Amritsar (in addition to the existing 1 MW capacity).
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Surender Gupta is Dunar’s Managing Director and son of the founder Late Shri. Duli Chand Agarwal, who founded the Company in 1979. Mr. Gupta has been actively involved in the basmati rice industry for over two decades. Mrs. Kanta Gupta, the sister-in-law of Mr. Gupta, is also involved in making strategic decisions as a board member. Mr. Surender Gupta with his wife and children and Mrs. Kanta Gupta own 63% and 28% of Dunar, respectively. The remaining minority shares are owned by Mr. Gupta’s mother and Dunar’s management.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Project cost of about US$140 million includes capital expenditure for the expansion as well as additional working capital requirement associated with increased sales.
