The Company plans to raise up to US$30 million in equity and fund the remaining project cost by internal cashflow and working capital debt. IFC is proposing to invest up to US$30 million in total with combination of equity (up to 20% of the Company’s share capital) and A loan. A private equity fund is proposing to invest about US$10 million in equity as a co-investor to the IFC investment.
location_description: The Company owns two production facilities in Karnal, Haryana and Amritsar, Punjab where the Project will take place.
development_impact: (i) This Project is expected to generate new rural employment of 34 permanent and about 100 seasonal employees in Haryana and Punjab in three years. (ii) This Project is likely to create additional backward linkages with farmers as it is expected to increase procurement of basmati rice paddies from about 230,000 mt to 440,000 mt in three years, via "mandis" (markets) from farmers in various states. (iii) This Project is likely to create forward linkages with SME distributors as well. (iv) This Project will provide climate change benefits by adding 5 MW husk power generation capacity.

project_description: Guangxi Hwagain Group Co., Ltd (“Hwagain” or the “Company”) plans to expand its tissue production capacity in Jiangxi Province (the “Project”). The proposed Project consists of a new pulp mill and two tissue paper production lines. Ultimately, the Company aims to become a regional tissue paper leader in China.
sponsor_shareholders: Hwagain is now a medium-sized, integrated bamboo and scrap wood based pulp and paper producer. In 2008, Hwagain diversified into tissue papers. The Company plans to shift its focus from printing and writing papers to tissues, and significantly build up its tissue production. Mr. Ning Jun, aged 50, is the Chairman of Hwagain and the Sponsor for the Project. He is responsible for the strategic planning and overall management of the Company. Mr. Ning has more than 15 years experience in pulp and paper, and is well regarded in the local business community as a competent, credible entrepreneur. Under his leadership, the Company evolved from a small sugar plant into an integrated pulp and paper producer with good reputation in southern China.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the Project is estimated at$245 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $15-25 million equity investment.
location_description: The Proposed Project will be implemented by Hwagain in Ganzhou City of Jiangxi Province, China. The Production facility is located in an industrial park developed by the local government.
development_impact: (1) Rural growth and employment: The Project supports the expansion of a successful pulp and paper company in the frontier regions of China. The Company procures bamboo from around 6,000 rural households in frontier Guangxi and Jiangxi regions. As a result of its expansion, the Company will have a significant impact and extensive rural reach by procuring from additional 6,000 rural households, and creating business opportunities for MSMEs, such as traders of bamboo, truck owners, distributors, etc. (2) Sustainability: Pulp and paper sector is reported to account for a significant portion of water pollution in China and the sector places a huge demand for global wood resources. IFC will be supporting a Company with a keen desire to contribute to sustainable development by: (a) contributing to proper management of forest (bamboo) resources; (b) efficient manufacturing, and (c) adopting and ensuring workplace safety and pollution control.

project_description: SLV was established in Santa Cruz, Bolivia for the purpose of constructing and operating a state-of-the-art mill to produce hardwood tropical rotary veneer, plywood and its byproducts, mostly for exports. Investments started in 2005. The plant was built within a 18 ha free-trade industry zone and includes a modern sawmill, veneer lathe and dryer. The Company currently has a total annual capacity to process 120,000 mt of logs/year, being one of the largest operations of its kind in Latin America. The purpose of the project is to support SLV to consolidate its operation and business model by: (i) improving plant efficiencies through diversified product mix and higher log recovery rates; (ii) increasing reliability and consistency of log supply; (iii) funding incremental working capital; and (iv) refinancing exiting short-term debt with local banks.
sponsor_shareholders: Today, on a fully diluted basis, SLV is owned by Ospraie (New York based private equity fund) with 57%; Fernando Campero with 29% (the “Sponsor”); SLV management with 6.0%; and other local investors with 8.0% (no individual shareholder owning more than 5.0% of the shares).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is estimated at $8.5 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to $6 million C loan for IFC’s own account
location_description: SLV is located in the duty free zone of Warnes, Santa Cruz, Bolivia.
development_impact: IFC involvement with the Company is expected to have a strong development impact in the economy by: i) supporting the development of an export oriented sector with deep roots in the economy and with extensive linkages throughout the value chain; ii) creating additional direct and indirect employment while helping to preserve 140 existing jobs; iii) improving living standards and climate change by promoting sustainable management of natural tropical forest through certification.

project_description: The proposed investment will support the expansion of Galnaftogaz (“GNG” or “the Company”) - an independent distributor of petroleum products in Ukraine. GNG has financing requirements of $210 million over the next two years (“the Project”) for the following activities: - $150 million for expansion of its gas station network. GNG plans build/reconstruct around 75 high-volume gas filling stations and finance the associated working capital. The stations will be built according to the highest EHS standards and will have energy efficiency elements. $15 million of the investment will be used to purchase energy efficient heating systems, insulation, lighting and electric controls, pumps and more fuel efficient tanker trucks. Most of the planned stations will be in central and eastern Ukraine because GNG would like to increase its presence outside of its home region (western Ukraine). The Project is expected to create at least 480-500 new jobs (newly created stations) and preserve another 380-400 jobs (purchased/reconstructed stations), for a total of at least 860 jobs. - $60 million to refinance mezzanine debt at GNG’s holding level.
sponsor_shareholders: Galnaftogaz is an existing IFC client and based in western Ukraine. It operates mainly in the retail segment, through 307 gas filling stations, of which 281 are operated under the proprietary “OKKO” brand. OKKO branded stations have a modern layout and up-to-date technical, safety and environmental specifications. The stations offer high-quality petroleum products and various related products and services (shops, fast food, auto repair). Consistent quality of products helps to attract and retain loyal customers to OKKO stations because Ukraine does not yet have a strict minimum quality of fuels (e.g. EURO-4 or above) and often other distributors sell fuels of low standards and lack proper quality controls. The Company is the third largest petroleum distribution company in Ukraine by number of stations and the second largest by volume. In 2010 the Company achieved revenues of $1,092 million and retail sales of 787 thousand tons. For the same period, the Company generated $82 million EBITDA and $39 million Net Income on assets of $714 million. GNG Retail Public Limited is the holding company of GNG and owns about 64% of shares of the Company. Mr. Vitaliy Antonov, a reputable Ukrainian businessman, is the founder and the ultimate beneficiary of the group. European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (“EBRD”) owns about 10.3% and its stake will increase to about 19% after upcoming equity subscription which is the part of the financing required for the Project.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at about $210 million, while IFC’s proposed investment is a financing package of $80 million, consisting of an A loan of up to $15 million and a C loan of up to $20 million both for IFC’s own account, and a syndicated B loan of up to $45 million for the account of participant banks. EBRD is considering matching IFC investment in identical amounts.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Lviv, Ukraine. Its network of stations is nationwide, and expansions for this project will be concentrated mostly on central Ukraine, with an emphasis on fuel stations in urban areas and near highways.
development_impact: - Development of Ukraine's infrastructure based on modern and safe standards. - Access to high-quality petroleum products and services - Employment creation/preservation. GNG employs 4,700 people (only 2,000 in 2004). The proposed investment is expected to create about 900 permanent jobs and 250 thousand man hours of construction jobs - Development of local suppliers. Convenience stores, automotive services and fast-food help local economies because such services at stations are primarily locally supplied.

project_description: Pran Group (“Pran” or “the Group”) has requested IFC’s assistance to finance the expansion of its dairy operations, which are run under Pran Dairy Ltd (“PDL”), one of the Group companies. Pran is a diversified group involved in the production and sale of a wide product range covering beverages, snacks, culinary products, confectionery, dairy products, rice and tea. The proposed project consists of an investment of approximately $15 million for an expansion in PDL’s processing and procurement capacity and related working capital needs (“the Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsors are Mr. Amjad Khan Chowdhury, Mrs. Sabiha Amjad, and Mr. Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, who control the six Pran Group companies engaged in the food processing sector: AMCL Ltd., PRAN Agro Ltd., PRAN Foods Ltd., Bango Agro PRAN Ltd., PRAN Beverage Ltd., and PDL. All of these companies are fully privately-owned, with the exception of AMCL, which is listed in the Dhaka Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $15 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A Loan of up to $7 million.
location_description: The project will support the expansion of PDL’s existing milk and juice processing facilities in Ghorashal, Bangladesh, and its milk procurement activities in Natore in northern Bangladesh.
development_impact: The agriculture sector in Bangladesh accounts for 21% of its GDP, and 55% of its population is dependent on agriculture, including 20% in dairy activities. The local dairy sector is undergoing a slow transformation from unorganized to organized channels. Within the organized sector, there are a very limited number of private sector players. The Project will support the continued expansion into the dairy sector by one of the largest agribusiness companies in Bangladesh. Pran's extensive distribution reach in Bangladesh will enable it to reach to under-served populations while bringing in improved efficiencies in the sector. The proposed Project will also have a transformative impact on the supply chain for dairy products. Pran currently works with 17,000 farmers on the dairy business. As part of this Project, PRAN will set up 60 new dairy hubs over a course of ten years, which will enable it to increase its reach to 90,000 additional farmers. The hubs will support smallholder dairies by providing entire package of logistic support including, veterinary care, animal husbandry, dairy housing, feed, breed improvement and training.

sector: Man-Made Fibers (Including Nylon, Polyester, Rayon, etc.)
project_description: PT South Pacific Viscose (SPV or the Company), an IFC client and one of the leading producers of viscose staple fiber (VSF), is undertaking a capital expenditure program (the Project) which includes: (i) a new VSF production line together with additional utilities and auxiliaries and associated infrastructure; (ii) a wet gas sulphuric acid plant (WSA) for sulphur recovery and regeneration of sulphuric acid required in the VSF production process; (iii) incremental working capital; and (iv) regular refurbishment capital expenditure.
sponsor_shareholders: SPV was established in 1978 near Purwakarta, 120 kilometers east of Jakarta, and began commercial production in 1983.SPV is an internationally competitive producer of high-quality VSF. SPV is about 90.6% (directly and indirectly) owned by Lenzing, the second-largest viscose manufacturer in the world. SPV’s minority shareholders are P.T. Pura Golden Lion and an Indonesian individual.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is expected to cost $192 million. IFC is considering an A loan of up to $30 million and a B loan of up to $110 million.
location_description: The Project is being undertaken at the Company’s existing site in Purwakarta, Indonesia.
development_impact: Sustainable development of the textiles industry: The Project supports the development of additional fiber capacities based on renewable raw material - dissolving grade wood pulp. Arguably, viscose has a lower impact on the environment compared with cotton (due to lower usage of land and water per unit of fiber) and petrochemical-based synthetic fibers (considering the bio-degradable properties of viscose and lower usage of fossil-based sources). Job creation: The Project is expected to create 270 new job opportunities for the local economy. In addition, the Project will support the long-term growth of the Indonesian textiles sector through increased domestic production of VSF at internationally competitive quality and costs. This, in turn, will ensure the retention and growth of employment across the textiles value chain in Indonesia, textiles being one of the country's key sectors in terms of employment and foreign exchange earnings.

project_description: Market Shopping Center Limited (“MSC” or the “Company”) is a newly created Rwandese real estate company undertaking the development of a $37 million greenfield mixed-use commercial property (the “Complex”) in the Central Business District (CBD) of Kigali, Rwanda (the “Project”). The Complex with a gross leasable area (GLA) of 29,383 m2 would be the first purpose mixed-used commercial complex with first class facilities to offer a combination of retail, accommodation, food, entertainment and office space in Kigali. The Company is seeking an IFC financing package of up to $13 million to support the development of the Project.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is owned by three shareholders: Mr. Bertin Makuza, the main sponsor, owns 90% of the Company, Ms. Irene Makuza and Ms. Francine Umuraza (who are both relatives of Mr. Makuza) together own the remaining 10% of MSC. Mr. Makuza is a seasoned and well respected local entrepreneur who has been in private business in Rwanda for over 40 years and owns several successful enterprises covering a wide range of business lines.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $37 million of which IFC is proposing to provide up to $13 million consisting of an up to $10 million A loan and up to $3 million of equity.
location_description: The project is located in the Nyarugenge Hill, a prime area of Kigali’s CBD, on a site that used to house a state-owned post office building.
development_impact: The project is expected to have the following development impacts: Provision of Business Infrastructure Services: The project will add 29,383 square meters of quality real estate infrastructure to Kigali and support the implementation of the Kigali City Master Plan; Employment: The project will create a minimum of 100 jobs during construction and further 15-20 jobs post construction. The project will also create indirect jobs through supply chains; Demonstration Effect: IFC’s involvement in the project will act as a catalyst to encourage other financial institutions to partner with strong and reputable local sponsors on similar projects in the country; Energy Efficiency: The property design includes energy efficient components like solar powered extractor fans, heat reflective glass etc that when implemented will have a demonstration effect as one of the few true energy efficient buildings in Kigali.

project_description: Shangri-La Ulaanbaatar Hotel LLC (the Company or Shangri-La Ulaanbaatar Hotel) is a joint venture between IFC’s existing clients: (i) Shangri-La Asia Limited (Shangri-La or the Sponsor); and (ii) MCS Holding LLC (MCS). The project is to develop and operate a 280-room, 5-star hotel in the city of Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia (the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The Company will be 75% beneficially owned by Shangri-La and 25% owned by MCS. Shangri-La, headquartered in Hong Kong, is a leading owner and operator of deluxe hotels and resorts primarily in Asia. Shangri-La is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Incorporated in Ulaanbaatar in 1993, MCS is one of the leading private enterprises in Mongolia with subsidiaries operating in various business sectors, including: (i) energy and infrastructure; (ii) general manufacturing and services; (iii) information and communications; (iv) property development; and (v) food and beverages.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $123 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to $50 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The hotel will be part of an office, retail and hotel complex located on the east side of the Sukhe-Bahor Square, between the City Theatre and Peace Avenue, in the centre of Ulaanbaatar.
development_impact: The Project's expected development impact includes the following: (i) Increased supply of hotel services: The Project will help meet the growing demand for hotel accommodation in the presently under-served 5-star hotel sector in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. (ii) Employment creation: The Project will create a significant number of direct and indirect job opportunities for the local communities. (iii) Benefits to the local economy and local linkages: The Project will help create demand for locally sourced materials, service, and labor, both during the construction and operation stages . The Project is expected to support small- and medium-sized enterprises, including a wide range of goods and service providers. (iv) Increase in domestic revenue and foreign exchange: The Project is expected to contribute to the domestic economy through increased tax revenues and foreign exchange inflow. (v) Private sector development: The presence of the Shangri-La Hotel in Ulaanbaatar will send a positive signal to other foreign investors who are considering investments in Mongolia where there is limited private sector activity. The Project is also expected to have an impact on the upgrade and development of retail and travel-related infrastructure in the city of Ulaanbaatar.

company_name: CONSTRUCCIONES METALICAS MEXICANAS COMEMSA S.A. DE C.V.
project_description: Construcciones Metalicas Mexicanas Comemsa SA de CV, a subsidiary of Abengoa SA and engaged in the design and manufacturing of galvanized steel structures, is implementing an expansion of its existing plant in Apaseo el Grande, Guanajuato, Mexico to satisfy increased demand for solar panel structures and transmission towers in the region. Production capacity is expected to increase from 30,000 tpa to 50,000 tpa as a result of the expansion project which will result in the addition of several production lines and an additional galvanization plant.
sponsor_shareholders: Comemsa is owned by Abengoa Mexico SA de CV, Servicios Auxiliares de Administracion SA de CV (a service company) and Eucomsa SA. Eucomsa is a global leader in the design and engineering of transmission and solar structures, and is owned by Abeinsa and Abengoa Solar. Abengoa Solar is a global leader in the application and development of solar technologies, as well as in the promotion and operation of solar energy plants. Abeinsa Ingenieria y Construcción Industrial SA, the flagship company of Abengoa SA and global leader in the EPC industry.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $40 million. IFC will provide a $24 million A loan for IFC’s own account to cover the expansion plan and refinance $4 million of existing debt.
location_description: Comemsa is located in the industrial area of Apaseo el Grande, Guanajuato, a few kilometers away from the nearest residential area and close to the local railway line for transportation of raw material and finished products.
development_impact: Key development impacts of the project include: Supporting the construction of solar energy plants globally by providing a necessary component to the solar panel structure and encouraging the use of clean energy, thus reducing CO2 emissions through the implementation of clean energy plants. Improving the infrastructure supply chain through the increased manufacture and sale of transmission towers across Latin America and in the USA to meet growing demand. As a result of increased focus on transmission capability in Mexico and Central American, energy access is expected to improve. Supporting job creation in Mexico, a key objective for the Mexican government, both during the expansion and operation of the manufacturing facility.
Company Name: CONSTRUCCIONES METALICAS MEXICANAS COMEMSA S.A. DE C.V.

project_description: Moorhouse Properties Limited (“MPL” or “the Company”) is embarking on a $37.4 million expansion Project which involves the (i) construction of two 3- star hotels and two 2-star hotels to be implemented respectively by its operating companies A. M. Hotels Limited (“AMHL”) and MP Budget Limited (“MP Budget”); (ii) setting up of its corporate office and (iii) refinancing of debt (the “Project”). The main purpose of the Project is to meet demand in the middle and budget segments of the Nigerian hotel market by developing an easily-recognizable international brand (Ïbis”) and an indigenous value brand (Travelhouse) of international standard. MPL’s expansion model is centered on offering to business and leisure travelers, comfortable and moderately priced lodging facilities in markets where such products are presently not available. The emphasis is on providing room quality with less public area, food and beverage outlets than a full service.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsors are two Nigerian entrepreneurs, Koye Edu (50%) and Gbolly Balogun (50%). Mr. Edu, a lawyer specializing in commercial and intellectual property matters, worked for Irving & Bonnar (an ex-IFC local counsel) in association with Bentley Edu & Co. for ten years before starting his own firm, Jackson, Etti & Edu, in 1996 with two other partners. Mr. Balogun is an entrepreneur and property developer/manager with a good track record. The Sponsors started MPL in 1996 with a primary focus in property development and asset management.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at $37.4 million. The proposed IFC investment is $7.5 million senior loan in AMHL for IFC’s own account and $7.4 million equity in MPL for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The AMHL hotels will be located in Lagos and Ibadan cities of Nigeria. The proposed sites for Lagos and Ibadan are greenfield locations, close to business establishments and major roads. The Travel house budget hotels will be located in and around Lagos city.
development_impact: The proposed Project will (i) bridge the supply gap for high quality under-served hotel markets in major business cities in Nigeria which is presently met with sub-standard accommodation and guest houses, (ii) contribute to the improvement of the business infrastructure of the country, (iii) create significant job opportunities to the local people and linkages with other sectors of the local economy many of which are SMEs, both during Project implementation and ongoing operations, such as small contractors, building material suppliers, agricultural and food processing, textiles manufacturers, etc, (iv) encourage improvements in the standards of existing hotels and transfer of hotel management expertise and training of the local staff, and (v) the Project has the potential to provide a demonstration effect and kick off the development of a mid and budget market hotel segment in Nigeria. It is also important to note that international chains assure guests of an established product and service quality; often encourage broad improvements in the standards of existing hotels; and provide staff with compensation usually above local norms.

project_description: The proposed IFC project entails providing a risk sharing facility (“RSF”) in partnership with Raiffeisen Bank Aval (“Aval” or the “Bank”) of up to $70 million on the portfolio of receivables generated by Bayer Ltd. Ukraine (“Bayer Ltd” or the “Company”) on the sale of crop protection products to existing and new farmer-clients. The Bank will provide a guarantee to farmers which will allow them to buy on credit from Bayer. An RSF will be signed with Aval on a portfolio of up to U$140 million equivalent with an IFC exposure of up to $70 million, under which IFC will share with the Bank 50% of principal losses on a portfolio of guaranteed Promissory Notes and guarantees to farmer- clients. IFC will have a first-loss counter-guarantee from the Company. Aval is a universal commercial bank ranked number four in Ukraine by total assets as of December 31, 2010, and offering a full range of banking services to all kinds of customers – from big corporate to individuals. The Bank has a well established network of branches with around 930 outlets present in all regions. Aval deals with agri-businesses and has strong agri-finance record in the country. Since October 2005, close to 96% of the Bank’s equity has been owned by Raiffeisen International Bank Holding AG (since October 2010 - Raiffeisen Bank International or “RBI”), a fully consolidated subsidiary of Raiffeisen Zentralbank Österreich AG (“RZB”). The remaining stock (ca. 4%) is traded at the local stock exchange. Raiffeisen International has been a long-standing IFC client since 1987, and Aval has benefitted from three investments in the recent past: two subordinated loans in total amount of $70 million, a senior loan of $15 million, and a GTFP line of $30 million. Bayer Ltd., a Ukrainian entity fully owned by Bayer AG, is a main input supplier of crop protection products (mainly pesticides, herbicides and fungicides) in Ukraine with revenues of about US$100 million per year. The Company’s clients are mainly represented by small and medium farmers. Bayer Ltd. operates under the CropScience division of Bayer AG.
sponsor_shareholders: The Bank’s Parent company – RBI – is one of the leading corporate and investment banks in Austria and in Central and Eastern Europe (“CEE”). In CEE RBI operates an extensive network of subsidiary banks, leasing companies and a range of other specialized financial service providers in 17 markets. 56,000 employees service about 15 million customers through around 3,000 business outlets in the region. RZB owns about 78.5% of RBI common stock; the balance is free-float, listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange. Founded in 1927, RZB is the central institution of the Austrian Raiffeisen Banking Group (RBG) and acts as group centre for the entire RZB Group, including RBI. Bayer AG is Germany-based pharmaceuticals, polymers and agrochemicals conglomerate with sales of about €31 billion and EBITDA of about €6 billion in 2009. The group’s structure consists of three divisions: Bayer Healthcare, Bayer CropScience and Bayer MateriaScience. Bayer CropScience manufactures herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, seed treatment and seeds.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $70 million at IFC own account, to be provided as a risk sharing facility on the portfolio of up to $140 million of receivables generated by Bayer Ltd. to existing and new farmer-clients. The Bank will provide a guarantee to farmers which will allow them to buy on credit from Bayer. IFC will share with the Bank 50% of principal losses on a portfolio of guaranteed Promissory Notes and guarantees to farmer clients. IFC will benefit from a first-loss counter-guarantee by the Company.
location_description: Bayer and the Bank are headquartered in the capital of Ukraine, Kyiv. Aval operates around 930 outlets located in big cities, provincial and community centers and villages across Ukraine. Bayer Ltd. covers the entire territory of Ukraine via the chain of local distributors.
development_impact: IFC development impact in this investment will be measured according to the following indicators: i) increased and improved access to financial services for agricultural SME''s and farmers; ii) support agri-customers and one of the leading sectors of the Ukrainian economy through an innovative financial product; iii) demonstration effect to the local market that should encourage local banks to serve this crucial yet largely underserved sector; iv) improvement of Bayer''s and farmers'' integrated pest and disease management (IPM/IDM) approach, coordinated use of pest and environmental information along with available pest control methods, including cultural practices, biological, genetic and, as a last resort, chemical means to prevent unacceptable levels of pest damage.

company_name: TAMEK GIDA VE KONSANTRE SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Established in 1955 by Mr. Mehmet Melih Sipahioglu, Tamek Gida ve Konsantre Sanayii ve Ticaret A.S. (Tamek or the Company) concentrates on two main areas: (i) fruit juice and concentrates; and (ii) processed food, including tomato and pepper pastes, ketchup, mayonnaise, canned and stewed products, ready dishes, pickles, jams and marmalades. The proposed corporate loan will be utilized for refinancing part of the Company’s existing short-term debt, working capital requirement and additional/maintenance capital expenditures (collectively the Project).
sponsor_shareholders: Tamek Holding A.S. (the Sponsor or the Holding), headquartered in Istanbul, has the controlling shareholding in Tamek and holds 95% of the Company’s capital. The Sponsor is owned by Sipahioglu and Sengor Families, and the remaining 5% of the Company is held by individual members of both families.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a long-term local currency financing of up to TRY25 million for the Project.
location_description: Headquartered in Istanbul, Tamek has three operating facilities in Marmara and Aegean Regions (i.e. one facility in Bursa – Karacabey, one in Manisa – Salihli and one in Balikesir – Kiziksa) in addition to one warehouse (i.e. in Bursa – Nilufer) in the Marmara Region.
development_impact: The Project will have following development impact: - Increased Competition: The Project will strengthen Company's position in the market as well as improve its competitiveness, which in turn will promote the competition in the fast growing fruit juice and branded processed food sectors. - Local Supply Chain Linkages & Farmers Reached: The Company works with various distributors throughout Turkey and applies contracted farming for various raw materials. So, with the Project the Company would be able to (i) collaborate more with its distributors to increase efficiencies, (ii) support more individual farmers; and (iii) further extend its local supply chain coverage thanks to improved operational and financial performance at corporate level. - Job Preservation & Increased Tax Revenues: With the Project, the Company will be able to retain its existing labor force while improved financial performance would lead to higher revenues/profitability resulting in returns to the society in form of taxes.
Company Name: TAMEK GIDA VE KONSANTRE SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: Agrofertil (or the “Company”), founded in 1993, is one of Paraguay’s leading crop input distributor and agronomic services companies. The Company assists farmers, cooperatives and small distributors providing technical support, agricultural inputs and pre-harvest financing. The project consists of providing a working capital facility to Agrofertil to support the pre-harvest financing needs of its network of clients (the “Project”). The Project will increase access to working capital finance for farmers in Paraguay, who will also benefit from Agrofertil’s commercialization services and technical expertise. The Project consists of providing Agrofertil a one- year loan facility (the “Facility”) with up to five renewable tranches and composed of an A-Loan of up to $15 million and a B-Loan of up to $10 million, subject to market appetite.
sponsor_shareholders: Agrofertil is fully owned by the Sarabia family, whose members have more than 15 years of experience in the agribusiness sector in Paraguay.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at $25 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A-Loan of up to $15 million for IFC’s own account and a B- Loan of up to $10 million, subject to market appetite.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Ciudad del Este, Paraguay. The Company has 9 regional distribution centers located near the major crop regions of Paraguay.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have a significant development impact by (i) reaching farmers operating in frontier regions (likely to include a significant share in BOP), (ii) supporting the dissemination of agricultural best practices and inputs to farmers, (iii) generating tax income for the Government, and (iv) employment.

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: The project involves an IFC investment in two subsidiaries of OAO Energomera Concern (“Energomera Group”): namely OAO Monocrystal (“Monocrystal”), and ZAO Energomera (“Energomera”). Energomera develops and produces a wide range of electronic metering technologies and equipment. Monocrystal produces (i) synthetic sapphires - the key material for substrate used in the production of light-emitting diodes (“LEDs”), and (ii) special materials (namely aluminum photovoltaic paste) used in the production of solar cells.
sponsor_shareholders: Energomera Group is a Russian Group. Neither the Group nor its subsidiaries are publicly traded at this stage. The Group has 16 years of operating history. Mr. Vladimir Polyakov, is the main shareholder of the Group and its subsidiaries, with 93.4% shareholding.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Proposed corporate loans to Energomera and Monocrystal include senior loans up to $20 million (or its Ruble equivalent) to Energomera for refinancing its short-term loans; and up to of $15 million to Monocrystal to support the growth of Company’s operations in 2011 and refinance its short term loans.
location_description: Energomera has two main plants located in Nevinomissk and Stavropol. Monocrystal has also two plants located in Stavropol and Belgorod region. Both Companies have their headquarters in Stavropol. Investments for Monocrystal shall be mainly performed in the existing facility located in Stavropol.
development_impact: i.The project is expected to contribute to the energy savings in Russia through wider use of metering, especially new generation meters, and lead to reduced GHG emissions in the longer term. Monocrystal's increased production will support further reduction in GHG emissions through the use of LED lighting and employment of solar cells in electricity generation. ii.Employment preservation: IFC's investment will support one of the largest employers in Stavropol. Moreover, Energomera is a high-technology employer in a region where employment opportunities are generally limited to agriculture jobs. Currently the Company employs approximately 4 500 people of which 2 300 are female. iii. Monocrystal is an export oriented company which brings foreign currency denominated revenues to Russia.

project_description: The goal of the Project is to facilitate investments into energy efficient renovations of residential multi-family buildings in Russia and avoid CO2 emissions by creating an effective legal and institutional platform to support Russian home owner associations and housing management companies in getting access to finance for the purpose of improving energy efficiency of the country's existing housing stock. This five-year, advisory services Project will take on a programmatic approach and will focus on the following key objectives: Develop regulatory and legal environment addressing key legal and regulatory issues, in particular (i) the framework for energy efficiency in residential buildings and (ii) legislation enabling local home owner associations and management companies to access finance for the purpose of improving energy efficiency in multifamily buildings. Develop and market financially-viable residential energy efficient products by working with pilot Russian banks. Increase capacity and awareness about residential energy efficiency among key market stakeholders. The Project will be implemented jointly by IFC and EBRD, and will allow both entities to closely coordinate all sector work, leverage resources, and achieve greater impact by joining efforts. By partnering with EBRD, IFC further enhances its additionality as EBRD’s involvement will provide additional investments in energy efficiency in the Russian residential sector and will allow each agency to capitalize on its strengths in addressing sector barriers.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project will support a number of different sponsors. These will be identified and disclosed under individual investment agreements.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is co-financed by the Finnish Ministry of Employment and the Economy, the Finnish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, and by the Global Environemtal Facility (GEF). This SPI covers only the GEF co-financing piece of $4.7 million, which, in turn, consists of two components: (1) an advisory component of $1.3 million and (2) an investment component of $3.4 million indented to be channeled through a risk-sharing vehicle that the Project will be developing jointly with the IFC Investment department. The amount of IFC invesment is to be determinted but notionally is anticipated to be $50 million over a five-year period. These investments will be made through financial institutions for further on-lending to finance energy efficient renovations of multi-family buildings in Russia.
location_description: All work will be carried out in the Russian Federation with both Russian and international stakeholders, sponsors, and financial institutions. All anticipated future investments will be to clients with projects in the Russian Federation.
development_impact: Successful implementation of the Project is expected to lead to avoidance of approximately 2.5 million tonnes of CO2 over the lifetime of the investments enabled by this Project (see next section).

sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: Vitafoam Nigeria Plc (“the Sponsor”) is a foam and related products company established 48 years ago in Lagos Nigeria. Vitafoam Nigeria Plc services hotels, academic institutions and private entities with its varied products such as flexible reconstituted and rigid foam products and non flammable contact adhesive. The project involves the establishment of a subsidiary of Vitafoam Nigeria Plc known as Vitafoam Sierra Leone limited and involves the construction and operation of a foam manufacturing company in Hastings, Sierra Leone.
sponsor_shareholders: Vitafoam Sierra Leone Limited will be 99% owned by Vitafoam Nigeria Plc, a publically traded company on the Nigerian Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be approximately $5.0 million. The proposed investment is approximately $2 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project will be located on a greenfield site in Hastings, a suburb of Freetown, Sierra Leone. Access to the site is available from routes coming from Freetown.
development_impact: Increased private sector development especially since there is no foam manufacturing plant in Sierra Leone. Transfer of technology to a new market. Reduction in Imports and increased local production. Increased government revenue. Job creation.

project_description: The Project involves providing a multi-country A-Loan of up to €60 million - including IFC current exposure - to Soufflet’s Eastern Europe and Central Asia operations. The Project will mainly support Soufflet in Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, while a small portion of the facility (up to €10 million) will also be used for Soufflet’s operations in Serbia and Romania. It will support Soufflet’s strategy to increase its presence and grow in ECA. Soufflet will use the proceeds of the IFC Loan to: (i) originate wheat, barley and other cereals; (ii) increase in-kind prefinancing to farmers and procurement of alternative grains and oilseeds; (iii) process grain into malt; and, (iv) support trading operations. The Loan will be committed as a 4-year A-Loan with a revolver feature, to match working capital cycles. In 2009/2010, Soufflet originated almost half a million metric tons (mt) of grain in these five countries, where the Company owns 4 silos. Soufflet also owns and operates 5 malting plants in the region that sold 377,000 mt of malt in 2009/2010. With a stabilized source of funds, Soufflet is expected to increase its origination volumes. This would in turn help the Company scale up its presence in the region, develop its input supply and farmers prefinancing, and diversify its procurement of grain beyond malting barley, which would ensure a better capacity utilization of its silos. This additional financing will also provide a buffer against the volatility of grain prices.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in France in 1900, Soufflet is a mid-size global agribusiness group whose activities include grain procurement, primary processing (wheat and corn milling, malting) and grain trading. The group, privately owned by the Soufflet family, is active in 12 countries of Western and Eastern Europe. Soufflet maintains control over its supply chain by providing farmers with seeds and fertilizers in some European countries. The farmers subsequently sell their crop to Soufflet, who then stores and sells to commercial and industrial end-users of wheat, barley, oilseeds, and other agricultural commodities. The group is also a major flour miller in Europe and among the largest global malt producers.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will be providing an up to €60 million working capital loan to Soufflet’s agriculture, processing, and trading subsidiaries in Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Romania, and Serbia.
location_description: Russia: St-Petersburg and Griazy. Ukraine: Slavuta, Jashkov, Kiev, Carolina, Gorodok. Kazakhstan: Tekeli. Romania: Buzau. Serbia: Backa Palancka.
development_impact: Project is to secure the working capital needs of a large regional player in the grain/oilseed/malt sector in five countries in a challenging economic context. The Project supports the long term strategic commitment of Soufflet to the region, where it expects to expand its activities in in-kind prefinancing of farmers (in the form of inputs), procurement of grains and oilseeds, storage and logistic services, malt processing and international trading. - SMEs, farmers, and employment. The Project will also carry significant benefits for Soufflet’s partners. In particular, employment and number of farmers reached are expected to grow. Most farms in the region are fairly large and provide substantial employment in rural areas. In addition, Soufflet’s activities also support many MSMEs (e.g. independent elevators, importers of inputs, transportation companies, security, catering, cleaning, maintenance, etc), which further reinforces the Company’s direct impact on the local economy. - Upgrading of storage/logistics infrastructure. Soufflet has acquired and developed 210,000mt of grain storage capacity in the five countries. These facilities were usually poorly maintained, inefficient because of bottlenecks at various stages of loading and unloading, and were not operated at standards of safety applied to the Company’s facilities in other countries. The Company has engaged into a multiyear improvement program that frees usable capacity, eliminates bottlenecks and upgrades the standards of operation to internationally accepted levels. This will in turn improve the quality of services to local farmers and local residents. This also provides a benchmark for the operation of competing elevators in the region. - Building more competitive markets. Storage and drying capacity in inland elevators remains limited relative to the current production levels, which provides better negotiating power to elevator operators. Soufflet’s expansion of its presence and higher standards of operation will provide valuable competition in this underserved market. - Agricultural productivity improvements. Soufflet has a staff of agronomists whose primary mission was to ensure adequate agronomic practices for the production of high quality malting barley. As the Company expands its procurement towards other grains and oilseeds, this expertise is being redeployed to ensure that a package of inputs, prefinancing, agronomic advice, storage and marketing services is available to local farmers to improve productivity and strengthen their partnership with Soufflet. - Strengthening rural economic development. Soufflet’s operations generate significant economic opportunities for rural communities in terms of employment as well as linkages to MSMEs.

company_name: ACTIS AFRICA REAL ESTATE FUND 2 LP
project_description: The proposed project involves a $25 million equity investment in Actis Africa Real Estate Fund 2 LP (“AARE 2” or the “Fund”) managed by Actis LLP (“Actis” or the “Sponsor”), a leading private equity investor in emerging markets. AARE 2, a limited partnership organized under the laws of the United Kingdom, is a projected $250 million, 10-year closed-end private equity fund dedicated to investments in real estate companies and projects in Sub-Saharan Africa. AARE 2 is a follow-up to Actis Africa Real Estate Fund 1, the Sponsor’s first dedicated private equity real estate fund for sub-Saharan Africa, closed in 2006 at $154 million and almost fully invested.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor and manager of the Fund is Actis, an emerging markets private equity firm founded in July 2004 when it spun out from CDC Group Plc (“CDC”, formerly Commonwealth Development Corporation). Actis is active in Africa, China, Latin America, South Asia and South-East Asia and has close to 60 years of experience investing in emerging markets through its CDC history. As of December 31, 2009, Actis had $4.8 billion worth of assets under management, 69 portfolio companies employing more than 87,000 people. 117 limited partners have invested in Actis-led funds.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is a proposed equity commitment of up to $25 million in AARE 2, not to exceed 20% of total capital commitments. The projected final size of the Fund is $250 million to be raised over at least two closings.
location_description: The Fund will invest in real estate companies and/or projects located mainly in Western and Eastern Africa. The Fund will make equity investments ranging from $15 to 40 million per company focusing on development stage real estate projects and/or selective acquisition and repositioning of assets, in property segments with strong economic drivers and clear supply shortages (primarily class A retail / leisure, class A office and affordable residential).
development_impact: The Fund will have the following development impacts: i) contribution to filling the gap between supply and demand for quality commercial real estate and providing increased access to quality business infrastructure critical for economic growth in key markets of Sub-Saharan Africa; ii) improvement of business infrastructure standards through the introduction and the implementation of best practices in terms of environmental and life and safety standards in key markets of Sub-Saharan Africa; iii) development of quality retail infrastructure in Sub-Saharan Africa thus improving access to quality products and services for the consumers; iv) creation of direct and indirect jobs both during construction and operation of the commercial properties in the target markets, and v) benefits to other sectors of the economy such as in the supply chain.
Company Name: ACTIS AFRICA REAL ESTATE FUND 2 LP

project_description: The Greenfield project consist of developing: (i) a 259-key 5-star hotel to be managed by Mövenpick; (ii) 9,000m2 of Class A office space (with gross lettable area 5,500m2); and (iii) 1,260m2 of retail space (with gross lettable area 900m2) in Accra, the capital of Ghana (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Project company is KHI Ghana Limited, a 100% owned subsidiary of Kingdom Hotels Investments (KHI). KHI is as a global player in the hospitality and leisure business with operations mainly in Asia, Middle East/North Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa and has over 27 properties (5000+ rooms) under management in 18 countries. KHI is owned by Prince Alwaleed bin Talal bin Abdul Aziz Alsaud (Prince Walid) of Saudi Arabia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $103 million. The proposed IFC’s investment is a $20 million A loan for IFC’s own account, a $20 million B loan, and a $6 million C loan.
location_description: The development is located along Independence Avenue, on one of Accra’s major thoroughfares and within Accra’s central business district on the site of the former Hotel Ambassador. Besides being centrally located, the hotel is about 15 minutes from the international airport, Kotoka International. The site is located close to a number of government buildings and offices.
development_impact: (i) Develop infrastructure: The project will add to the country's critical lack of business infrastructure. (ii) Job creation: The hotel and associated development will create new direct and indirect employment. (iii) Benefits to local suppliers: The hotel is expected to source almost all of their food and non-food purchases locally, thereby providing increased business opportunities to a wide range of local suppliers and sub-contractors, most of whom are SMEs. Going forward, KHI Ghana's operations are expected to offer a significant revenue source to these SMEs, thereby enhancing their competitiveness and growth.

project_description: Based in Pernik, Bulgaria, Stomana Industry S.A. (“Stomana”, or the “Company”) is a leading steel manufacturer in Southern Europe. The Company has been present in the Balkan and international markets for more than 50 years, and produces a wide range of products, including reinforcing steel, heavy plates, merchant bars, special steels, special profiles and sections. In June 2001, Sidenor S.A. of Greece, acquired the Company from the Bulgarian State, and assumed responsibility for the overall operation. The transition to the private sector, which constituted a turning point in the company's history, involved a major investment plan aiming at the modernization of the production facilities and the overall restructuring of the company. The proposed project entails the strengthening of the Company’s balance sheet by providing a long-term loan to more closely match the long-term nature of the Company’s productive assets, as well as the support of Stomana’s recent capital investments into machinery and equipment, including a recent purchase of a new electric arc furnace.
sponsor_shareholders: Stomana is owned 100% by Sidenor Steel Products Manufacturing S.A. (“Sidenor”, or the “Sponsor”). Established in 1962 in Thessaloniki, Greece, Sidenor is part of the Viohalco Group of Greece. Sidenor has been publicly traded on the Athens Stock Exchange since 1997, and is engaged in the production, manufacturing and sales of steel products through its subsidiaries. Sidenor, together with its subsidiaries, employs a total of circa 3,000 people, and is the largest Greek steel producer with a leading position in Greece and the Balkans. The main areas of activity of Sidenor include steel mini-mill operations (in Greece, Bulgaria and FYR Macedonia), pipe manufacturing, downstream operations, and sales & distribution of reinforcing bars, merchant bars, wire mesh, steel plates and steel pipes.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The overall project cost is expected to be approximately €70 million. The proposed IFC involvement in the project entails an investment of up to €25 million into Stomana comprising a C-Loan of up to €18.75 million and up to €6.25 million of A Loan, both facilities being on IFC’s own account.
location_description: Stomana’s steel mini-mill is located in Pernik, Bulgaria, approximately 20 kilometers to the south-west of Sofia. The total surface of the land owned by Stomana is approximately 300 hectares including a total covered and used surface of 28.5 hectares including: a scrap-yard, a steelmaking facility, two long products rolling mills, a flat products mill, a grinding balls plant, a cold finishing plant, and a concrete reinforcing mesh and steel cages plant. All of the above mentioned facilities are actively operating.
development_impact: - Countercyclical Support: The proposed transaction would provide durable financial support to a significant employer, exporter and tax payer in Bulgaria by supporting Stomana's efforts in the aftermath of the worst financial year in recent history for most steel-makers. - Environmental and Financial Benefits: Part of the proposed IFC financing is aimed for the capital investments of Stomana. The investment into the new Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) would bring forth better utilization of electric and natural gas consumption of Stomana. This would create both environmental and financial benefits as soon as the new technology is installed and implemented.

sector: Metal Can and Other Metal Container (Including Aluminum Beverage Cans)
project_description: Headquartered in the city of Sao Paulo, Latapack-Ball Embalagens Ltda (“Latapack” or the “Company”) is an established Brazilian manufacturer of aluminum beverage cans. Founded in 1995, Latapack is Brazil’s third-largest producer of aluminum cans, mainly for Brazilian brewing companies, with a 18% domestic market share. The Company has three production facilities: (i) a can body plant in Jacareí, São Paulo State; (ii) another can body plant in Três Rios, Rio de Janeiro State, and (iii) a can end plant in Simões Filho in the State of Bahia. Latapack is undertaking an Investment Program consisted of the installation of a new plant at the city of Alagoinhas, in the state of Bahia to produce aluminum can bodies on 3 sizes, 12oz, 16oz and sleek. The new plant will respond to the rapidly growing market demand for aluminum cans in Brazil and especially to the country’s Northeast Region. Also, Latapack will increase its can end capacity in its Simões Filho plant to meet the additional production from Alagoinhas plant.
sponsor_shareholders: Latapack is a joint venture between (i) Ball Corporation, a US-based publicly-held international packaging sector leader, and (ii) a group of Brazilian investors. The Brazilian investors are comprised of: (a) Participações Industriais do Nordeste S.A., a publicly held company controlled by the Mariani Group, a family of prominent Brazilian entrepreneurs; and (b) Mr. Dalmo Vasconcelos, a former executive of Banco BBM.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Latapack’s 2010-2011 Investment Program totals US$132 million in capital expenditures. IFC is considering a total investment of US$80 million, being up to US$20 million for IFC’s own account, and US$60 million to be syndicated among international banks. The remaining US$52 million investment will be funded by the Company’s operating cash flow generation. On June 2011 the Company disbursed US$ 47.8MM out of the US$ 80 million approved IFC A/B Loan facility mentioned above. The Second and Final disbursement in the amount of US$ 32.2 million (being US$ 8.05 from IFC’s own account) was cancelled in June 2012 due to changes in the Brazilian legislation that made the disbursement unattractive to the Company. Such US$ 32.2 million has been refinanced with a longer tenor IFC A/B Loan facility (being US$ 8.05 from IFC’s own account) committed on May 24, 2012 and disbursed on June 6, 2012 so that Latapack is able to complete the Investment Program within the original timeframe.
location_description: The Project proceeds will be invested as follows: (i) the installation of a new plant at the city of Alagoinhas, in the state of Bahia, to produce aluminum can bodies; and (ii) can end capacity increase at the Company’s existing Simões Filho facility in the state of Bahia to meet the additional production from Alagoinhas plant.
development_impact: (i) Development and employment generation (136 direct employees) in a frontier region of Brazil (100% of the investment in the Bahia State); (ii) Increase the production and utilization of easily recyclable packaging materials; (iii) Increase of energy efficient manufacturing process, including new CDL technology; (iv) Increase of supply in an underserved market/replacement of imports; and (v) Indirect Positive Base-of-Pyramid effect.

sector: Fruit and Vegetable Preservation or Processing (Canning, Freezing, Drying, Jams, etc.)
project_description: Favorita Fruit Company (Favorita or the company), a holding company, is one of the leading banana growers and exporters in Ecuador. The company operates other wholly-owned subsidiaries whose activities include trading and shipping bananas, producing plastic bags, providing fumigation services, and importing and distributing fertilizers. It has requested IFC’s assistance in financing a corporate-wide investment program which involves: - replanting efforts to change the banana variety from Valery to Williams - redesign and modernization of equipment and machinery; and - refinancing short and medium term debt The project is aimed to: - continue reducing operating costs by increasing the banana yield per hectare; - carry out needed maintenance investments and equipment upgrades to maintain the company’s competitive position in the global market; and - strengthen Favorita’s financial structure in order to firm-up its banana/overall operations in Ecuador.
sponsor_shareholders: The project is sponsored by Favorita Fruit Co. Ltd. (Favorita), the holding company incorporated in the British Virgin Island owned and controlled by the Wong family (99% ) and IFC (1%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $21 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $10 million A loan.
location_description: The company is headquartered in Guayaquil. The proposed investment program will affect all of the banana production locations operated in the company, and the company’s dairy plant redesign and modernization.
development_impact: The Project supports the continued growth of one of Ecuador's leading agribusiness companies and a long standing IFC client. It will improve Favorita's competitiveness in the production of bananas, and ensure greater traceability and sustainability certification demanded by customers in developed markets. The Company employs over 10,000 workers (nearly 9000 agricultural) and provides commercial opportunities for over 300 business partners and 400 farmer suppliers.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment in Engro Fertilizers Limited (“Engro” or the “Company”), consists of a subordinated loan of up to $30 million to help mitigate the impact from the recent floods on their fertilizer business.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Engro Corporation Limited whose major shareholding is owned by Dawood Hercules Chemicals Limited. Dawood Hercules is a Pakistani urea manufacturer with a capacity of 445,000 tons per annum. Dawood Hercules is owned by Mr. Hussain Dawood, a prominent and well respected business figure in Pakistan and Chairman of the Board of Engro Chemicals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a corporate C loan of up to $30 million that will help Engro meet its corporate finance activities.
location_description: The Company’s fertilizer plant is located in Dharki, in the Northern Sind district, a rural area of Pakistan. The Company is currently building an additional fertilizer facility next to the existing plant site.
development_impact: The emergency loan is expected to help the Company deal with declining fertilizer sales and delays in completion of its new fertilizer plant that are due to the large scale floods in Pakistan. The facility’s objective is to smooth the operation and output and support the Company to respond quickly to the recovery in fertilizer demand once agricultural production picks up again.

project_description: The proposed project is to provide debt financing of up to €11 million to Gamesa Wind Turbines (“GWT” or the “Company”), a wind turbine assembly facility in India (the “Project”). The turbines assembled at this facility will be exported, sold domestically as well as used in local wind farms developed by the Company. Spain-based Gamesa Corporación Tecnológica S.A. (“Gamesa” or the “Sponsor”), which is one of the three largest wind turbine manufacturers globally, established GWT in late 2009 to lay the groundwork for producing wind turbines in India. The GWT facility is located in Chennai and will produce cost effective wind turbines specially suited for the Indian grid and wind conditions. GWT is also involved with conducting research on developing sites appropriate for wind farms in the region and has, to date, signed contracts in India and Sri Lanka for the installation of more than 60 MW. The facility has a capacity of 200 MW per annum and the Company has plans to scale it to over 800 MW in the coming two years through the new wind turbine assembly facility.
sponsor_shareholders: GWT is 100% owned by Gamesa, which was established on January 28, 1976 as a company specializing in robotics, microelectronics, aeronautics and the development of composite materials. Gamesa founded its wind turbine manufacturing unit, a subsidiary called Gamesa Eólica, in 1994. Since completing its first wind farm project in 1996, Gamesa has primarily focused its efforts on the development of wind power technology, culminating in its withdrawal from aeronautics services in 2006 and solar power services in 2008. Today, the Company has three business lines: (i) design, manufacturing and installation of wind generators (3,145 MW in 2009) through its subsidiary, Gamesa Eólica; (ii) promotion, construction and sale of solar and wind farms through its subsidiary, Gamesa Energia (182 MW in 2009); and (iii) energy solutions. The Company was publicly listed on the Madrid Stock Exchange in 2000 and has been included in the selective Ibex 35 rankings since 2001.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at €70 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to €11 million.
location_description: The Project is expected to be located just outside of the city of Chennai in the state of Tamilnadu. The current assembly facility is located in Red Hills, Tamilnadu.
development_impact: Job creation: The new facility is expected to create about 150 new jobs as well as additional jobs in line with the facility’s growth and expansion in the coming years; Support for the Indian wind power market: by producing low-cost turbines locally that are best suited to the country’s grid and wind conditions, the Gamesa Project will help develop and bolster the wind market in India; Technology transfer: while the Project currently envisions assembly in India, the Company aims to have a full turbine production facility set up in the long-term. This process will result in the transfer of important climate change related technology.

sector: Fruit and Vegetable Preservation or Processing (Canning, Freezing, Drying, Jams, etc.)
project_description: Frikom is a leading ice cream, frozen food and frozen pastry producer in Serbia. In 2008, the company acquired Nova Sloga, a former Serbian state-owned mineral water, fruit and vegetable producer. The proposed project is to provide long term financing for the modernization of Frikom, and for the post-privatization investments in Nova Sloga. The project includes the expansion of production capacity in frozen fruits & vegetables, ice-cream and mineral water, investments in storage and retail space, the establishment of fresh fruit and vegetable purchasing, and efficiency improvements.
sponsor_shareholders: Agrokor is a leading food and retail company in the CEE region, with over 36,000 staff, and operations in Croatia, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Macedonia, Montenegro, Slovenia and Hungary. Over the last thirty years, Agrokor has expanded from a small family business for flower and trade, into a private company generating revenues in excess of €3.6 billion, owned 91.7% by Mr. Ivica Todoric, the founder and President, and 8.3% by EBRD. Agrokor owns 95.83% of Frikom. The minority holding in Frikom is owned by the Serbian privatization fund (3.75%) and other small shareholders. Nova Sloga is 100.00% owned by Frikom.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at €40 million, which is proposed to be financed with a €40 million loan investment, of which €30 million will be an A Loan on IFC’s own account, and the remaining €10 million to be in the form of a parallel commercial loan.
location_description: Frikom’s ice-cream and cold storage plants are located in Belgrade, Serbia. Nova Sloga is located in Serbia, in the Rasina area, which is renown as a rich agricultural area with over 160,000 hectares of arable land.
development_impact: The proposed Project supports the continued regional growth of an emerging market player, and also develops a local supply chain for small fruit and vegetable farmers: - Private Sector Development: Support privatization, rehabilitation and improve the productivity of formerly state-owned assets; - Employment: Safeguard employment at Nova Sloga, including a large number in rural areas; - Farmer benefits: Strengthen the competitiveness of vegetable supply chain by providing reliable access to market and technical assistance to farmers; - SME development: companies like Frikom (and eventually Nova Sloga after its turnaround) are the local engines of supply chains, upstream supporting farmers by providing a reliable off-take of fruits and vegetables, and downstream by supplying retail and distribution networks; - Community development: the construction of a local supermarket (there is none within a 60 km radius), the local presence of an off-taker for produce with credible infrastructure on the ground, the availability of technical assistance for horticulture will support rural and community development; - Tax-payer benefit: Increase taxes paid and decrease in state support to a loss making state-owned enterprise; - Quality Management Certification: Improve E&S management and quality certification at Frikom, and support introduction of E&S management and certification process at Nova Sloga.

project_description: Karsten Farms (Pty) Limited (Karsten or the company) is the parent company of the largest table grape exporter in South Africa. In addition to grapes, Karsten produces dates, apples, melons and citrus on a total of over 1,500 hectares. The project entails providing a corporate loan to Karsten to introduce energy efficiency measures and use of renewable energy in its farming operations.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Mr. Petrus Karsten Sr., who established Karsten as a 13ha raisin farm 30 years ago. The Shareholding structure now comprises: Karsten Family Trust (51.95%); Industrial Development Corporation (36.95%); Yarona Farms Limited, a company owned by the employees of Karsten (11.06%) and Bertus Loubser (0.04%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total estimated project cost is $1.2 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan (Cleaner Production Loan) of $900,000 for IFC’s account extended through the Cleaner Production Lending Facility (“CPLF”), a $125 million facility approved by IFC’s Board in September 2009 to support Cleaner Production investments among existing IFC clients.
location_description: The project will be implemented at Karsten’s farms located in the Northern and Western Cape Provinces, South Africa.
development_impact: The proposed project will help Karsten reduce its high energy costs and its carbon emissions footprint. Karsten will pilot the use of solar panels in farm worker housing, which it can replicate on its other farms. This is in line with IFC’s stated objective of creating demonstration projects that can showcase successful cleaner production efficiencies for others in the sector.

company_name: Bioparques de Occidente, S.A. de C.V.
project_description: Bioparques de Occidente, S.A. de C.V. (Bioparques or the company), a greenhouse tomato producer is undertaking a $12.5 million investment program to add 30 hectares of hydroponic greenhouses and a packing facility to its existing greenhouses in the state of Jalisco, Mexico. The investment includes acquisition of greenhouses and irrigation equipment, infrastructure and working capital. This project is IFC’s second transaction with Bioparques and builds on a partnership begun in 2007, when IFC provided a $12 million loan to the Company.
sponsor_shareholders: The company is owned by the de la Vega family which also owns Impulsora Azucarera del Noroeste, S.A. de C.V. (Zucarmex), Mexico’s 3rd largest sugar producer representing about 10% of Mexico’s sugar production.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project is to be implemented in one phase totaling $12.5 million. The company requested IFC financing of up to $5 million, in the form of an A loan and a C Loan. The balance will be financed from cash generation.
location_description: Bioparques is located in the municipality of San Gabriel in the state of Jalisco. The expansion project will be located next to the existing site which is predominantly rural and about 140 km from the city of Guadalajara.
development_impact: The investment will support the growth of a competitive tomato producer in Mexico through: (i) Cost reduction through higher utilization of capacity and economies of scale; (ii) Higher prices thanks to the ability to serve long term contracts with US retail vendors; (iii) Assist the company in sponsoring permanent housing for its full time workers; (iv) Assist the company in continuing its institutionalization process which is expecting to be beneficial for Bioparques to access better financing and insurance terms in the future.
Company Name: Bioparques de Occidente, S.A. de C.V.

sector: Other Miscellaneous Fabricated Metal Products (Including Non-Wood Housing Products, Tanks, Cutlery, Kitchen Utensils and Handtools, etc.)
project_description: Established in 2006, Lattice Power Corporation (“Lattice” or the “Company”) is a growing Chinese manufacturer of high brightness light emitting diodes (“LEDs”) chips, which are used in efficient liquid crystal display (“LCD”) screens, notebooks, televisions, monitors and applications in the automotive sector as well as for energy efficient lighting. The Company’s proposed $100 million investment plan that will be used to support its business expansion related to the manufacturing of LED chips in China.
sponsor_shareholders: Lattice is a private firm founded by Prof. Fengyi Jiang (an expert in LED technology), Dr. Min Wang and funded by reputable private equity and venture capital funds with expertise in new technologies such as GSR Ventures, Mayfield Fund, AsiaVest, Temasek Holdings, Keytone Ventures. The Company’s other shareholders include the management team and small private investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is approximately $100 million and consists of capital expenditures related to the purchase of up to 20 MOCVD machines and build out of a new manufacturing facility. IFC’s proposed funding is yet to be determined but it is projected to be up to $20 million.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in and has its manufacturing operations in the high-tech development zone located in Nanchang, Jiangxi Province, China.
development_impact: IFC’s expected development impact resulting from a potential investment in Lattice includes: Contributing to the development of Jiangxi Province which has a much lower GDP per capita (US$2,200) compared to the average GDP per capita in China (US$3,200). Helping China address climate change challenges by financing a company that manufactures energy efficient LED technology. The success of this Project will provide the development of an important technology notably for more energy efficiency lighting, computer monitors, notebook and TV displays. Creating employment opportunities for both operational and management positions (around 1000 new employees) in a frontier region.

project_description: The proposed Project for Suu Dairy (“Suu” or the “Company”) comprises of the following components: To expand production capacity to meet the increasing demand. Currently, the production is limited by the packaging capacity; To renovate the existing machinery and building to improve productivity; To further develop raw milk supply chain by establishing 4 new milk cooling points and 2 new parlors, and upgrading 9 existing cooling points; To establish 2 additional mini processing plants in Erdenet city and Khentii – Batshireet province; To refinance the Company’s existing short-term debt ; General working capital purposes.
sponsor_shareholders: A leading Mongolian Dairy processor, Suu was founded in 1958 as a state owned company. The Company was partially privatized in 1992 and fully privatized in 2006. At present, 94% of equity stake is held by three sponsors, and remaining 6% is listed on the Mongolian Stock Exchange. Mr. Ganbaatar Dagvadorj, Chairman of Max group and Suu, started his export and import business in the early 1990s when the country shifted to an open market economy. He later expanded successfully into restaurants, manufacturing, retailing, construction and property management. These activities (except Suu) are now operating under the Max group , one of the large business groups in Mongolia (Annex 5). Mr. Ganbaatar is responsible for overseeing the general direction of all his business interests and remains actively involved in the operations of each entity. Mr. Jamyan Dagvadorj was general manager of Max Impex where he was in charge of sales and distribution. He also managed the construction of various office buildings and apartment complexes. Currently, he is a board member of Suu and holds a position as Director at Max Trade LLC. Mr. Tuvshintugs is currently a member of Suu’s Board of Directors. He joined the Suu in August 2005, and served as the CEO from March 2006 – April 2007. Altogether, three sponsors hold a 94% stake in the Company. Mr.Jamyan and Mr.Tuvshintugs are brother and brother-in-law of Mr. Ganbaatar respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total Project Cost is estimated at $8.6 million, to be funded by an IFC A Loan of up to $2 million and the balance by other financiers and internally generated funds.
location_description: The Project will be implemented Suu (Milk) Company building, Uildverchnii gudamj-37,18th khoroo, Songinokhairkhan district, Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia 211213
development_impact: (i) Expansion of raw milk procurement is expected to provide 2,500 existing and 1,500 new herders and farmers involved in milk supply chain with increased and more sustainable income; (ii) at the same time the project will provide them with more information about quality milk standards through newly established MCPs and MCU as well as new milking parlors that will offer a controlled environment for cow milking; and (iii) Self-sustainability of Mongolia for domestic milk product supply will be improved and import dependency will be reduced. Currently around 25 % of all processed dairy products are imported.

project_description: The owner of the leading FMCG distributor in Tajikistan, plans to create a new entity, Amiri LLC, to launch chocolate and confectionary production in Dushanbe. Production is planned to start by the end of December for chocolate products, targeting the middle class consumers, with nationwide distribution. Amiri will be the first modern chocolate operation in Tajikistan, competing against imported brands. The project includes investment in: (i) the renovation of existing production premises, formerly used for storage; (ii) equipment for chocolate production; and (iii) working capital. IFC funding will be used to support the purchase of modern chocolate processing equipment. The existing distribution company, Tajero, was established in 2002 and has since built strong relations with leading international companies to distribute and market FMCG products in Tajikistan. The new company, Amiri, will take advantage of the Tajero network for brand management, distribution and key shelf space to leverage Tajero’s depth of expertise and strong relationships with retail players.
sponsor_shareholders: Amiri LLC was incorporated in 2010 and is 100% owned by Mr. Abdurakhmon Gaibullozoda, a local Tajikistan entrepreneur who is also the sole owner of Tajero, one of the largest distribution operations in Tajikistan. Mr. Gaibullozoda started in sales at a local grocery in Dushanbe in 1992, which he purchased in 1995. Since then, Mr. Gaibullozoda transformed this business into the largest FMCG distributor for perishable and non-perishable products with suppliers from Ukraine, Russia, Kazakhstan, the US and Brazil.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $2.6 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to $1.3 million senior A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Amiri LLC is located in the Rudaki district of Dushanbe, Tajikistan. The site used to be an old storage facility which Mr. Gaibullozoda purchased in 2005 and fully renovated into modern storage and production complex. Part of the complex measuring 1,500 m2 is now being outfitted for chocolate production.
development_impact: Through this Project, IFC will be investing with a local sponsor that has built a strong distribution business in a challenging environment and now is looking to start its own production in a predominantly import dependent market. With IFC's involvement, Amiri is well positioned to become a model production site through support from IFC on food safety, HACCP and environmental standards, and would be able to disseminate best practices through its distribution network. The Project's main beneficiaries will be financiers, employees, owners of small stores and consumers.
