company_name: XINJIANG GOLDWIND SCIENCE TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: Goldwind Science and Technology Co., Ltd (“ Goldwind” or the “ Company”) is China’s second largest wind equipment supplier with 21% market share. The Company was founded in 1998. As of the end of 2009, Goldwind had total revenues of $1,569 million and a net income of $ 263 million. Goldwind is in the process of (i) building and upgrading manufacturing facilities, and (ii) developing new products (the “Project”). The project will result in the implementation of three new manufacturing facilities and introduction of two new products for deployment in both domestic and international markets.
sponsor_shareholders: Goldwind has been listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange since 2007. Goldwind’s shareholders include Xinjiang Wind Energy Co.Ltd (18.27%), China Water Investment Group Corporation (15.75%), China-Belgium Direct Equity Investment Fund (7.2%), management (4.35%), Public A-share holders ( 45.9%) and others ( 8.4%)
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be $ 1,100 million. IFC is considering a financing package of up to $ 50 million.
location_description: The Project is located in the 3 sites, as: New District Beijing Economic & Technological Development Area, Beijing; No. 151 Huangshan Street Economic & Technological Development Zone Phase II, Urumqi City Autonomous Region; and No.118 Tianyuan Road Jiangning Science Park Jiangning District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.
development_impact: The project will have the following positive developmental impacts: Contribution to the Sustainable Development of Wind Technology: Goldwin, as a leader in China’s wind market, has developed unique direct drive and permanent magnet generator (“DDPMG”) technology that is seen to represent the future trend of turbine development worldwide. The success of the new turbine technology can significantly help improve the economic return of wind power investment and thus sustain the healthy development of the industry, both in China and other emerging economies. Development of Frontier Regions: Goldwind, headquartered in Xinjiang, one of the most impoverished regions in China. Goldwind also has production bases in other less developing remote frontier regions like Inner Mongolia, Gansu, Shaanxi and Ningxia. Given the labor intensive nature of the business, Goldwind can create abundant job opportunities in these regions and further develop its supply chain which in turn benefits local SMEs. Goldwind has a significant impact on the local economy of West China. Role Model for Domestic Player in China’s Wind Market: Goldwind was the pioneer and leader in China’s wind market. The Company’s impressive achievement in becoming the fifth largest turbine manufacturers globally has made clearly demonstrated that newly start-up companies, originated from frontier region, can also succeed in sectors that are mostly dominated by big state owned enterprises.
Company Name: XINJIANG GOLDWIND SCIENCE TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.

company_name: Beijing ShenWu Environment & Energy Technology Co.Ltd.
project_description: The IFC investment is to support the expansion plan of Beijing Shenwu Thermal Energy Technology Co., Ltd. (“Shenwu” or the Company”) in the next 3-5 years. The specific operating entities receiving IFC funds will be Shenwu (the holding company), Hubei Shenwu and Beijing Huafu (two of Shenwu’s wholly owned subsidiaries). The use of proceeds (‘the Project’) will be to finance the Company’s expansion plan, which comprises (i) the expansion of the Company’s facilities in Beijing and Hubei; (ii) development of High Temperature Air Combustion (HTAC) applications for more industries; (iii) R&D; and (iv) marketing and business development.
sponsor_shareholders: Beijing Shenwu Thermal Energy Technology Co., Ltd. (“Shenwu” or the “Company”) is a privately held Chinese company established in 1995 in Beijing that designs, manufactures and installs high temperature air combustion (“HTAC”) equipment and system. The HTAC applications are designed to provide energy-saving and emission reduction technologies and solutions for many energy-intensive industries, which in China means they are directly or indirectly heavy consumers of fossil fuel. According to the Company, its HTAC systems improve fuel efficiency by 5-50%, depending on application, and reduce carbon emissions by up to 30%. The founder and Chairman of Shenwu is Dr. Wu Daohong, a pioneer in HTAC technology in China. Dr. Wu is the originator of HTAC or regenerative burner technology in China and holds 17 national patents related to HTAC technology. Dr. Wu currently holds 67% of the Company. The remaining 33% are held several private equity firms.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost for the Company expansion in the next 3-5 years is around $100 million. IFC is considering making an senior loan of up to $22 million.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Machikou Town, Changping district, Beijing. The Company’s office building, R&D centers and other facilities cover around 160 mu land in Zhongguancun High Tech Zone in Changpin. Shenwu also has 4 subsidiaries/JVs locate in Beijing. One subsidiary locates in Liu Kou Industry Zone, Xiantao, Hubei Province, and one locates in Nanjing, Jiangxu Province.
development_impact: (i) Support innovation and contribute to development of clean technology sector in China. (ii) Assist the government of China to achieve its energy efficiency and CO2 emmisions reduction goals. (iii) Enable cleaner production best practices in key polluting industries in China and other developing regions. (iv) Increase Employment: with the successful implementation of the Project, the Company will create additional 600 new jobs in total in the next three years. (iv) Increase Employment: with the successful implementation of the Project, the Company will create additional 50 new jobs in its Bejing headquarters and Hubei manufacturing site.
Company Name: Beijing ShenWu Environment & Energy Technology Co.Ltd.

project_description: A modernized former Soviet factory in Ust-Kamenogorsk, Kazakhstan, UKPF is an established regional poultry leader in Kazakhstan (14% of domestic production, 6% market share) serving the remote though populated northeast market, as well as Almaty and Astana and marginal export sales to Kyrgyzstan. Currently, UKPF is the sole chilled chicken meat producer in Kazakhstan. With its new processing operation and improved technical operations, UKPF can leverage on its regional strength to gain market share in other regions, and expand fresh poultry production. UKPF’s strategy is to transition the bulk of its sales from frozen whole birds to chilled products to capture higher margins, provide an alternative to frozen import options, and secure a stronger foothold in Almaty. Chilled product sales will be achieved through locating UKPF-branded counters and refrigerators in key retail spots in Almaty, Astana, Pavlodar and Ust-Kamenogorsk for the majority of sales. Supporting this effort is an already-embarked upon modernization program and improvements in the distribution system to build close relationships with leading supermarkets. The IFC Project will help UKPF (i) improve the operation’s bio-security to reduce the risk of disease; (ii) accelerate the retailing of the branded chilled production; and (iii) reduce feed costs. Advisory services will assist the Company with corporate governance, food safety and energy efficiency.
sponsor_shareholders: Serik Tolukpayev and Baurzhan Mozhaev, both Kazakhstan citizens, own 75% and 25% of UKPF respectively. They acquired UKPF from Eagle Kazakhstan Fund in 2004. The Sponsors also control Aitas Group LLC, which is the holding company of LLC Aitas Distribution, a distribution operation for multinational brands in Eastern Kazakhstan. .
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project cost is estimated at $18.6 million over the next 2 years. IFC investment will be in the form of a C loan of up to $2.0 million.
location_description: UKPF is located on 592, 820 hectares near the Molodezniy village, approximately 20 kilometers from Ust-Kamenogorsk, on the Almaty highway. UKPF was founded in 1976 as a poultry operation, and has worked in this sector for over 30 years.
development_impact: Through working with UKPF, IFC will support the development of a local market leader in the poultry sector, a high priority for the Government of Kazakhstan. Since the IFC project will address improvements in bio-security, cleaner production and energy efficiency, the Company will be able to serve as a model for other poultry and meat producers to improve their operations. The Project main beneficiaries will be financiers, grain farmers, soybean and sunflower farmers, employees, retail stores, consumers, and the nearby residents of the UKPF operation.

project_description: South Asian Petrochem Limited (“SAPL” or the “Sponsor”), India’s second largest manufacturer of Polyethylene Terephthalate (“PET”), and Egyptian Petrochemical Holding Company (“Echem”), an agency of the Government of Egypt, have set up a joint venture (“JV”) to establish a 420,000 tpa greenfield PET resin plant in the Eldorado Integrated Development and Free Zone S.A.E. which is at Sector 2 of the Southern Region of the Economic and Industrial Zone, North West of the Suez Gulf at Ain Sokhna on Egypt’s Red Sea coast (the “Project”). SAPL will hold a 70% share in the JV Egyptian Indian Polyester Company (“EIPET” or the “Company”), Echem will hold 23%, and Engineering for the Petroleum & Process Industries (“Enppi”), another Government of Egypt agency, will hold the balance (7%). The Project has an estimated cost of approximately $160 million. PET, which is produced from mono ethylene glycol (MEG) and terephthalic acid (PTA), is sold in small pellets and its major use is for the manufacture of lightweight plastic bottles for carbonated soft drinks and water.
sponsor_shareholders: SAPL operates a 200,000 tpa PET plant at Haldia in West Bengal state, India, which started operations in 2003. It is the second largest PET producer in India, marketing products under its brand name “ASPET”, with a 37% domestic market share. SAPL is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange. SAPL’s founder and major shareholder is the Dhunseri Group of Companies, promoted by the Dhanuka family, a reputable Indian business family which also owns tea businesses in Eastern India, holds a 54.5% share in SAPL while the balance is held by IFC, Indian institutions and corporate bodies (14%) and the public (22%). SAPL is in the process of merging with its holding company Dhunseri Tea & Industries LTD, awaiting statutory clearances. Post merger the Dhanuka family will hold 62% in the merged entity. Echem, apart from its role as a promoter and investor in master projects, markets a number of petrochemical products produced in Egypt. Enppi, established in 1978, provides full-integrated engineering, procurement, construction supervision and project management services for the petroleum, petrochemicals, power and other related industries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Project is estimated to cost approximately $160 million. The proposed IFC investment includes up to $35 million A Loan for IFC’s own account and about $65 million in syndicated B Loan/or Parallel Loans.
location_description: The Project will be located at the Eldorado Integrated Development and Free Zone SAE Company site, which is at Sector-2 of the Southern region of the Economic and Industrial Zone, North West of the Suez Gulf at Ain Sokhna. The site is connected by highway 100 km east of Cairo.
development_impact: (1) Demonstration Effect of a South-South Investment: The Project will be the first PET project in Egypt and North Africa as a whole, a region which has the potential to become an important region in this industry. The Project is a South-South investment and its success could help GOE attract further FDI in the country. (2) Promotion of Downstream Industry: The water and carbonated soft drinks bottling industries in Egypt, which comprise several small players, currently lack domestic sources of PET resin. This Project is expected to help these players improve the efficiency of their operations through savings in logistics costs. (3) Diversification of export earnings: The majority of Egypt's foreign currency revenues currently come from natural gas sales and tourism. The Project is expected to contribute to the diversification of Egypt's export base. (4) Employment Creation: The Project is expected to create about 450 permanent jobs and about 800 jobs during construction. In addition, it will provide indirect employment through use of local port facilities and supplies.

project_description: Founded in 1996, Alutech Group of companies (Alutech or the Group) is a leading Belarusian producer of value-added aluminum products, including roller shutter systems, sectional doors and aluminum profiles. Alutect comprises of four manufacturing enterprises and several branches and warehouses in Belarus, Russia and Ukraine. The proposed transaction is up to $30 million corporate loan to support Alutech’s strategic growth through vertical integration, cost optimization and operational efficiency.
sponsor_shareholders: Alutech is owned by several individuals, all are citizens of the Republic of Belarus and Cyprian companies.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at around $82 million. The total IFC investment is expected to be up to $30 million.
location_description: The Project will be implemented on Alutech’s production sites in the Republic of Belarus, near Minsk.
development_impact: The project will support one of the largest private companies in Belarus. Furthermore, the project will contribute to Alutech’s export prospects. It is expected to have a positive demonstrational effect for improvements in business practices, transparency and financial reporting.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: Sisecam Soda Lukavac d.o.o. (“SSL”) is involved in the production of light and heavy (dense) soda and other products based on soda ash. SSL was created from the transfer of soda ash production assets from a loss making state owned soda ash producer. IFC provided a € 24 million loan to SSL in 2007 to finance initial post-privatization investments of SSL. Total outstanding IFC loan is €20.3million. SSL is currently undertaking a €32 million revamping investments to accelerate the turnaround after privatization, together with the restructuring of short-term debt. The project is expected to (i) increase SSL’s operational efficiency through renovation and equipment upgrades that will also increase capacity, leading to economies of scale, (ii) improve environmental performance through water treatment and air emissions investments (iii) reduce energy costs and, (iv) replace some short-term debt.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Sise ve Cam Fabrikalari A.S. (“Sisecam”) and Soda Sanayii A.S. (“Soda Sanayii”), both listed on Istanbul Stock Exchange (“ISE”). SSL is 86% owned by the Soda Sanayii, with the remainder of the Company being state owned. Sisecam is a leading Turkish producer of flat glass, tableware, glass containers, glass fibers and associated products worldwide. Sisecam owns 71% of the Soda Sanayii’s shares directly and 14% through Anadolu Cam Sanayii A.S., its glass packing arm.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is estimated at €15 million comprising (i) the replacement of short-term debt and (ii) financing of ongoing investments. These investments comprise new equipment that will result in a capacity increase and allow SSL to benefit from economies of scale, reduce costs and emphasize product quality and high margin products.
location_description: The project is located in the Tuzla Canton of the Federation Bosnia Herzegovina on the outskirt of the city of Lukavac (140 km north of the capital Sarajevo and 14 km west of Tuzla).
development_impact: The investment will help enhance SSL's turnaround and increase its competitiveness through economies of scale. Once SSL returns to profitability, this will enhance tax and export revenues for the country. SSL is still one of the largest employers in the area and also generates significant employment at the local brinestone and lime mines.

project_description: The proposed investment includes support to Piaggio & C. S.p.A. (“Piaggio”, or the “Sponsor”), for its two separate projects in Vietnam and India. The project in Vietnam comprises establishment and start-up of operations of approximately 100,000 units per annum (p.a.) capacity, green-field, two-wheeler manufacturing facility in Vinh Phuc, Vietnam, targeting domestic market and regional exports. The project is being implemented by Piaggio Vietnam Company Ltd. (“PV”), which was established in 2007. The project in India includes establishment of a plant to manufacture compact and more fuel-efficient 1000cc and 1200cc diesel and turbo diesel engines for light commercial vehicles (“LCV”s) and two-wheelers, with an installed capacity of 150,000 engines p.a. The project is being implemented by Piaggio Vehicles Private Ltd. (“PVPL”) in its existing LCV plant in Baramati, Maharastra, India. PVPL was established in 1998 and the planned engine investment targets exports and the domestic market.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is Piaggio, a leading, global manufacturer and distributor of two-wheelers, and three and four-wheeler LCVs. Established in 1887, it is headquartered in Pontadera, Italy. Piaggio sells its products globally and has manufacturing plants in Italy, Spain, China, India and Vietnam, where it has started its operations recently. Piaggio is listed on the Milan stock exchange (30%). Its majority shareholder (about 54%) is IMMSI S.p.A., an Italian listed company, which in turn is controlled by Omniaholding S.p.A., a company controlled by Mr. Roberto Colaninno. The remainder of its shares are spread across private and institutional investors. The Vietnamese subsidiary, PV is directly and indirectly, 87.5% owned by Piaggio and 12.5% by Simest S.p.A., a government entity that promotes investments abroad by Italian companies. The Indian subsidiary, PVPL, is wholly owned by Piaggio.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated total cost for both projects is approximately €88 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of two separate loans; an A loan for IFC's own account of up to €15 million to PV and of up to €30 million to PVPL.
location_description: The green-field plant in Vietnam is located in Vinh Phuc province industrial zone, 45 kms north of Hanoi. The plant in India will be an expansion of PVPL’s existing location in Baramati, 160 kms southeast of Mumbai, in the state of Maharashtra.
development_impact: The projects will have a number of important development impacts as follows: (i) Improved access to economic life and mobility for individuals as well as micro/small enterprises in two IDA countries: In India, Piaggio's LCVs are sold to self-employed or micro/small business owners active in transportation of cargo and passengers and provide highly cost-effective solutions for distribution systems/logistics. In Vietnam, the project will increase competition and improve the quality of two-wheelers available to the consumers. (ii) Enhancing competitiveness of the manufacturing sector in both countries and technology transfer: Through the projects, Piaggio will transfer technological know-how and help develop technical and management skills in the automotive sector. (iii) Employment generation: The projects will benefit the local population by generating new employment, approximately 500 in Vietnam and 300 in India. In addition, significant number of indirect jobs are expected to be created along the value chain from suppliers to distribution and after sales services. (iv) Demonstration effect: Successful completion of Piaggio's projects will boost confidence in both economies and provide a demonstration effect to other foreign investors. (v) Improved energy consumption in product manufacturing and product usage: Piaggio's technology is expected to be highly efficient in terms of energy consumption in the manufacturing. In addition, the vehicles manufactured will offer better fuel-efficiency and lower green house gas emissions as compared with the competition.

sector: Other Steel Products (Including Wire, Metal Sheets etc.)
project_description: Roofings Limited (“Roofings”), the largest Uganda-based manufacturer of steel building materials, is implementing a 3-phase expansion program setting up a (i) Wire Galvanizing Plant; (ii) Hot Rolling Mill Complex and; (iii) Cold Rolling Mill Complex, all together the “Project”. The Project will be implemented over 4 years (2009-12), under the Roofings subsidiary Roofings Rolling Mills Limited (“Sponsor” or “RRM”), a Uganda-based subsidiary of Roofings. Upon Project completion, RRM is expected to produce and sell steel construction materials (such as galvanized wire, high tensile reinforcement bars, cold rolled coils, galvanized iron coils and pre-painted galvanized iron coils) for both the local and export markets.
sponsor_shareholders: Roofings is owned by Mr. Sikander Lalani (founder and Managing Director) and his immediate family. Roofings was created in 1994 and is one of the top exporters in the Great Lake Region. Roofings employs 850 people and has an installed annual capacity of 110,000 Metric Ton (MT). RRM is owned 100% by Roofings.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment consists of an A-loan of up to $25 million into RRM.
location_description: The Project will cover 30 acres in the new industrial park in Namanve situated approximately 15 kilometers from Kampala city centre. The site is close to good road links and has a working railway line running through. The industrial park in Namanve is a World Bank- sponsored project.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have a strong development impact by: (i) providing consumers with increased access to high quality steel products in a 110-million people market; (ii) contributing to the upgrade of local business practices through the introduction of modern production technology; (iii) positively impacting other sectors such as construction and low-income housing; (iv) focusing on job creation and retention; and (v) encouraging other economic operators to move into the new industrial park.

company_name: Promotora de Viviendas Integrales, S.A. de C.V.
project_description: A medium term (3-5 yr.) debt issuance of MXN 300 million (around US$23.4 million) in the domestic debt capital market by Vinte (the “Company”). Support for the issue is to be provided by IFC in the form of a partial credit guarantee. It is expected that the partial credit guarantee will raise the credit rating of the issuance. This would be the Company's first debt issuance, which it seeks to place with institutional and retail investors. The debt issuance will: 1) provide working capital support for Vinte’s growth strategy, 2) strengthen its liquidity position, and 3) secure and diversify its funding over the next few years.
sponsor_shareholders: Vinte (www.vinte.com.mx) is a Mexican local private Company and mid-sized homebuilder founded in 2001 by a group of professionals with significant experience in the design, construction and promotion of low income housing developments. The CEO, Architect Sergio Leal, together with a group of selected investors and executives with expertise in key areas within the Company have focused their strategy on developing high quality houses that allow low and mid-income families to have access to technology and to the benefits of innovation. IFC is a shareholder of the Company. Vinte Viviendas Integrales S.A.P.I. de C.V. is the holding company consolidating all of Vinte’s operations. Vinte comprises its holding co. and five operating subsidiaries: Promotora de Viviendas Integrales, engaged in the promotion of the developments; Urbanizaciones Inmobiliarias del Centro, engaged in research and development for housing, including technological, environmental and design aspects; Edificaciones e Ingenieria del Centro, engaged in urbanization, design and construction activities; Conectividad para el Habitat, engaged in the distribution of computers, internet and related services; and Vinte Administracion, Diseño y Consultoria, engaged in human resources management.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The IFC investment is expected to consist of a partial credit guarantee equivalent and up to a certain percentage of the outstanding amount (MXN 300 million or US$23.4 million) of the bond issued by Vinte.
location_description: The Company is domiciled in Mexico City and the Project will help provide funds for expansion and working capital purposes. There is no specific Project/Site location. It is expected that the housing projects funded with the debt placement will be developed in various states of Mexico.
development_impact: The increased supply of funding will help Vinte build quality and affordable entry level dwellings, and in turn benefit a large number of families in the low to middle income segments. The housing developments built by Vinte will contribute to urban infrastructure and surrounding community development, previously built by local/federal authorities and neglected for a while due to persistent government deficits.
Company Name: Promotora de Viviendas Integrales, S.A. de C.V.

project_description: The proposed project (the “Project”) is a $50 million expansion of the do-it-yourself (“DIY”) retail chain Nova Liniya (the “Company”), an existing IFC client. The Project involves the construction of five new DIY stores, one in Kyiv and four throughout regional cities in Ukraine, and will bring the total number of stores operated by the Company to nineteen. The Project will be implemented over two and a half years.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsors are Mr. Oleg Shandar, Mr. Igor Shandar, and Dragon Capital, all three of whom are shareholders in the Company. Messrs. Shandar and Shandar are the founding shareholders of the Company and are actively involved in strategic decision-making as well as in the day-to-day operations of the Company. Dragon Capital is a leading Ukrainian bank specializing in investment banking, securities trading, asset management and private equity services. Dragon Capital acquired its stake in the Company in 2002.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at $50 million. The proposed IFC loan is for $22 million and will bring IFC’s total financing to the Company to $29.5 million.
location_description: Two of the proposed five stores, one located in Sevastopol and one in Bucha, have already been constructed. The remaining three stores are tentatively planned for Kyiv, Odessa and Donetsk. All five stores are or will be located on greenfield sites and in urban areas.
development_impact: The new stores would provide the consumer with more efficient distribution channels and greater access to goods at more affordable prices, including access to products which are important for local consumption. The new stores would also help boost local production of import substituting products in Ukraine. In addition, the new stores will support local supply chains and create additional jobs. As four out of the five planned news stores are outside Kyiv, the proposed IFC investment would also support development of retail operations in more underserved markets in Ukraine.

project_description: Wadi Holdings Company (SAE) (Wadi or the company) and its thirteen subsidiaries comprise a group of Egyptian companies which, has three core business activities. The first of these consists of poultry operations. The second core activity is the planting, cultivating, harvesting and processing of olives and other vegetables and fruits. The third core activities is the production of glass, poultry feed and other industrial products. Wadi is now implementing a two-year expansion and diversification investment program, which includes: (i) setting up a soybean crushing plant in Noubaria, Egypt to support its feed mill operations; (ii) expansion of table eggs production from 70 million to 650 million eggs per annum by 2012; (iii) construction of a mono-calcium phosphate (feed ingredient) plant; (iv) construction of a plant to assemble trailers; and (v) development of a fish production project.
sponsor_shareholders: Wadi is a majority-owned by the members of Freiji and Nasrallah families (80.6%) while the 19.4% is owned by institutional shareholders namely Commercial International Investment Company (CIIC), Horus Food and Agribusiness Fund and EuroMena Fund.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated total project cost is US$90 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to US$25 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The company is headquartered in Giza of Egypt and has 13 subsidiaries in Egypt. The concerned subprojects will be located along the Cairo-Alexandria Dessert Road.
development_impact: The proposed Project encompasses several autonomous components. The primary economic benefits will be in the economic value added by the overall investment program, as well as possible synergies with the Company existing operations. The various components of the program (soybean crushing, table eggs) do not appear to benefit from excessive levels of effective protection, so that financial and economic returns are likely to be aligned. Other economic impacts will include: (i) additional taxes; (ii) additional employment; (iii) additional reach to MSMEs, and, (iv) additional reach to farmers, although most of the new projects will rely on imported agricultural raw materials of which Egypt has been a major importer. Development outcome indicators will include (i) the project FRR and ERR, (ii) employment including female employment, (iii) taxes paid, and (iv) number of farmers and MSMEs reached.

project_description: The Project involves the setting up of up to four new units in strategic locations close to Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and their subsidiaries in the commercial vehicles and tractors segment. These new units will provide machining services to the OEM’s and their subsidiaries. In addition to the new units, the Project will also involve the expansion of the Project Company’s existing facilities in India.
sponsor_shareholders: Project Company: Incorporated in 1986, Craftsman Automation Pvt. Ltd. (Craftsman, the Company) is an engineering company with a diversified business mix encompassing: (i) machining of critical parts for domestic OEMs in the commercial vehicles, tractors segment (ii) contract manufacturing of assemblies and sub assemblies for various sectors like automotive, textiles, printing machines, locomotives for both domestic and export markets, and (iii) manufacture of products such as industrial gears, hoists, marine products. Currently, the Company has three manufacturing units in Coimbatore, and four units that provide machining services at Chennai, Sriperumbudur, Pithampur and Jamshedpur. The Company has a subsidiary in the Netherlands that sells marine products and two joint ventures with: (i) Carl Stahl International Gmbh, Germany, to develop and market material handling equipment (ii) Mitsubishi for selling their laser cutting machines. Major Shareholders: Mr. Srinivasan Ravi owns 75% of the Company and serves as the Managing Director. Two other individuals, Mr. Srinivasan Murali (Mr. Ravi’s brother) owns 15% and Mr. Kaliappa Goundar Gomatheswaran, director of the Company, owns the balance 10%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The new units and expansions will be spread out over a two year period based on estimated business pipeline and the total cost would be up to $37 million. IFC’s investment will be in the form of straight equity/quasi equity investment in the Company to part finance the Project and to support the growth of the Company.
location_description: The new equipment purchased will be used at Craftsman’s existing facilities in India: Coimbatore, Chennai, and Sriperumbudur located in the state of Tamil Nadu in the southern part of India, Pithampur in the state of Madhya Pradesh in central India and Jamshedpur in the state of Jharkhand in the eastern part of India. New units will be set up in strategic locations close to the OEMs and their subsidiaries.
development_impact: (i) Supporting investment in low income states: Craftsman's investments in Jharkhand and Madhya Pradesh will result in increased employment and enhance the skill sets of local personnel. Further, IFC's investment may have a demonstration effect, encouraging other institutions to invest in these states as well; (ii) Climate change impact: The Company has set up a business that manufactures windmill gears thereby assisting the renewable energy industry; (iii) The Project will result in the creation of around 600 direct jobs and 300 indirect jobs over the next three years; and (iv) Strengthening the corporate governance of the Company through IFC’s advisory services as it prepares to access public markets for further growth.

project_description: Indian Farmers Fertilizer Cooperative Limited (“IFFCO”), India and Jordan Phosphate Mines Company PLC (“JPMC”), Jordan have formed a joint venture, Jordan India Fertilizer Company LLC (“JIFCO”) for the construction and operation of a 475,500 metric tons P2O5 per annum (“MTPA”) phosphoric acid plant in Eshidya Ma’an Governorate, Jordan (the “Project”). The bulk of the phosphoric acid will be exported to India to be used as feedstock for IFFCO’s Kandla fertilizer plant in Gujarat state. The Project will include a greenfield phosphoric acid manufacturing complex in Eshidiya and a storage tank farm in Aqaba to facilitate export of phosphoric acid via Aqaba port. Rock phosphate from JPMC’s Eshidiya mines will be used by the Project for the production of phosphoric acid.
sponsor_shareholders: JIFCO is a Jordanian Limited Liability Company with 52% of its shares held by IFFCO while JPMC holds the remaining 48%. IFFCO, the largest producer of fertilizers in India, was established in 1967 in the Cooperative Sector with majority shareholding by the Government of India (“GoI”). By 2004 GoI's equity was fully divested by subscription from the Cooperative Societies. IFFCO's entire equity is now held by over 39,000 cooperative societies and 26 marketing federations spread across the country, representing over 50 million individual farmers. IFFCO owns and operates five fertilizer plants in India with a combined annual capacity of 8.58 million tons of fertilizers, including over 4 million tons of phosphatic fertilizers. JPMC is a Jordan based company listed on the Amman Stock Exchange, established in 1953 as a public shareholding company with the objective to mine and market phosphate rock, as well as produce fertilizers and invest in related industries. JPMC operates three mines, producing phosphate rock and downstream fertilizers, and a chemicals plant at Aqaba, Jordan producing phosphoric acid, DAP, sulfuric acid and aluminum fluoride. JPMC is the largest mining and industrial employer in Jordan and is the sixth largest producer of high quality rock phosphate and the second biggest exporter worldwide.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at about $681 million. The proposed IFC investment includes up to $150 million A Loan for IFC’s own account and up to $300 million in syndicated B Loan and Parallel Loans.
location_description: The chemical complex and associated infrastructure and utilities will be located adjacent to the existing JPMC mining facility in Eshidiya, Ma’an, approximately 250 km south of Amman, and 120 km north east of Aqaba Port, from which phosphoric acid will be exported. Aqaba is connected to the Project site by road, as well as by railway which lies 30 km from the site. The nearest city, Ma’an, is about 75 km from Project site, with an estimate population of approximately 50,000, and has the second highest poverty level among Jordanian governorates.
development_impact: The expected development impact of the Project includes: (i) creating permanent employment opportunities in the Project area (estimated 440 permanent jobs) as well as temporary construction jobs (estimated 750 on average); (ii) helping increase Jordan's industrial exports by generating approximately US$2 billion in export revenues over the life of the proposed IFC investment; and (iii) linkages with national suppliers as the Project is expected to award at least US$140 million worth of contracts to local firms. In addition, the Project is assisting the largest fertilizer producer in India to meet increasing demand for fertilizer by Indian farmers, particularly in the supply of phosphate, a critical element in nutrient growth and part of the Government of India's strategy to increase its usage. As part of project supervision process, IFC will track the following indicators: (a) number of new jobs created, (b) export revenues from the Project, and (c) amount of contracts awarded to Jordanian firms.

project_description: The Program consists of a 3-year, up to $10 million revolving IFC guarantee facility for selected bank participants under a financing program to assist coffee farmer cooperatives in Ethiopia to (i) acquire wet mills for processing “cherry” coffee into “washed” parchment coffee, and (ii) meet their working capital needs. The facility will be structured as an unfunded Risk Sharing Facility (“RSF”) to be committed annually and renewable for up to two times on the selected banks’ portfolio of loans to the small farmers. For the 2010/2011 coffee season, IFC has selected Nib International Bank S.C. (“NIB”) for the Program. It may add new banks in subsequent seasons. The total size of the financing program over the 3-year period is expected to be up to $21 million to be phased as follows $8.5 million in 2010; $15 million in 2011 and $21 million in 2012. Up to 20% of the program will be for equipment loans of a 3-year maturity while the remaining 80% will be post-harvest working capital loans of up to one year. Each working capital loan will have a clean-up period.
sponsor_shareholders: IFC’s exposure will be to farmer cooperatives which are legally incorporated in Ethiopia but will be collaborating with TechnoServe and NIB for the 2010/2011 coffee season. TechnoServe, is a reputable international NGO with 40 years experience in rural economic development. It operates in 17 countries in Africa, Latin America and Asia and is active in agricultural sectors including coffee, horticulture, dairy, tea, cocoa and cashew. TechnoServe is funded by various public and private donors including the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, USAID, and Rockefeller Foundation. NIB is a licensed commercial bank in Ethiopia with interest in expanding its agribusiness portfolio especially to small farmers producing coffee, Ethiopia’s main export commodity. The bank has made remarkable growth in all areas of its operations since its establishment in 1999. At the end of March 2010, the authorized and paid up capital reached Birr 1.0 billion and 580 million respectively. Shareholders and employees number increased to 3,284 and 1,595 correspondingly. The number of full-fledged branches also reached 45. NIB has received international recognitions and won several prestigious awards including “Bank of the Year in Ethiopia” award winner for 2005 and 2008 by The Banker magazine as well as “Best Bank Award” winner in Ethiopia for 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009 and 2010 by Global Finance magazine.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total size of the financing program over the 3-year period is expected to be up to $21 million to be phased as follows $8.5 million in 2010; $15 million in 2011 and $21 million in 2012. Up to 20% of the program will be for equipment loans of a 3-year maturity while the remaining 80% will be post-harvest working capital loans of up to one year. Each working capital loan will have a clean-up period. IFC’s investment will be up to $10 million revolving guarantee facility.
location_description: The farmer cooperatives are located in the coffee growing areas of rural Ethiopia especially Jimma and Limmu. Processing of the “cherry” coffee would take place in wet mills located in these rural areas. After processing, the “washed” parchment coffee will be transported to warehouses of the Coffee Service Providers (“CSP”) in Addis Ababa, for dry milling and packaging for exports as “washed” green bean coffee.
development_impact: The Program is expected to have the following development impacts: Strengthen the competitiveness of the Ethiopian coffee sector; Support economic livelihoods in the Ethiopian coffee supply chains, particularly small farmers and household labor; Develop a commercially sustainable model of long-term and short-term financing for the Ethiopian coffee supply chain, with potential for expansion to other countries/sectors dominated by small scale suppliers; Establish the credit worthiness of selected cooperatives;

company_name: THIEN MINH TRAVEL JOINT STOCK COMPANY
project_description: Thien Minh Travel Joint Stock Company (“Thien Minh”, “Thien Minh Group” or the “Company”) is a leading Vietnamese destination management company that provides tour, hotel and transportation operations as well as travel agency services. The project is to support Thien Minh to strategically develop its hotel operations business in Vietnam, potentially through acquisition of assets of a foreign hotel group (the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The main sponsor and shareholder of Thien Minh is its Founder and Chairman Mr. TRAN Trong Kien who holds 70.8% of the Company’s shares. Mr. Tran started the Company with his family in 1994 as an inbound tour operator. The second largest shareholder of Thien Minh is Vietnam Investments Group (“VI Group’), a private equity firm headquartered in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam which holds 29.2% of Thien Minh. VI Group is an IFC portfolio private equity fund that targets investments in high growth companies in Vietnam. The fund provides Thien Minh support on strategy, financial structuring and funding and is acting as financial advisor to Thien Minh on this transaction.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at approximately $38 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $12 million C loan for IFC’s own account. Up to $3.5 million of IFC’s C loan is proposed to be convertible into common shares of the Company.
location_description: The Company’s headquarters are located in Hanoi and the Company’s existing hotel operations are located in Mai Chau and Hue City. The Foreign Group owns and operates several four-star boutique hotel-resorts in Vietnam and in Cambodia and a hotel management company.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have significant development impact as described below: i) Income and Foreign Exchange Revenue: The Project will generate benefits to the Vietnamese government including tax revenue and foreign exchange inflow, particularly as a significant portion of the hotel guests are foreign nationals and the majority of hotel revenues are paid in foreign currency. ii) Employment: The Project provides permanent employment opportunities in hotel management, of which a significant portion are to local staff including a number of female employees. iii) Staff Training/Knowledge Transfer: The Foreign Group will continue to provide hotel management training to its own local staff and will also provide cross-fertilization of knowledge transfer via staff training to other lower-tier hotel properties owned by the Thien Minh Group. iv) Purchases from Local Suppliers: The successful implementation of the Project will also ensure continued and increased local supply purchases (food and beverage, supplies and other local services rendered during hotel operations). v) Environmental and Social Management System: The Project, through IFC's support to put in place an appropriate environmental and social management system, will help to ensure implementation of proper World Bank Group life, fire and safety procedures at all of Thien Minh Group's hotel properties.
Company Name: THIEN MINH TRAVEL JOINT STOCK COMPANY

sector: Paper Packaging Products (Including Boxes, Cartons, etc.)
project_description: Magic Box is the leading producer in Kyrgyz Republic of small cardboard packages and one of the major label producers (based on offset printing) with exports to Kazakhstan and Tajikistan. Magic Box produces a variety of small size packaging and printing products for the tea, beverage, confectionary, food, detergent, and tobacco industries with an annual turnover of $3.3 million in 2009. In 2007, IFC helped the company in its first capacity expansion in cardboard packages through a $1.5 million loan. Magic Box is currently undertaking a $5.3 million investment project to (i) diversify its production base by production of flexible packaging that will serve a wider range of clients in Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan; and (ii) improve operational efficiency and expand current offset production.
sponsor_shareholders: Magic Box is owned by Mr. Muammer Akkaya, a Turkish national, with a background in media and the printing business. Mr. Akkaya also owns a printing house, Mega Media, in Kyrgyzstan. In 2004, Mr. Akkaya established Magic Box in Kyrgyzstan to diversify into cardboard packaging. Mega Media is one of the largest printing houses in KR, while Magic Box has become a leading manufacturer of small packaging in the Kazakh market.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a senior A loan in the amount of $2.5 million to help finance the Company’s $5.3 million expansion in flexible packaging and offset printing.
location_description: The project is located in the Bishkek Free Economic Zone, in Ak-Chyi village, about half an hour away from Bishkek. The Zone was created by the Government with suitable road, power, water and security infrastructure, and houses several light industrial companies. The investment will be located within the current facilities already owned by the company, with some additional space to be built.
development_impact: The investment will help increase Magic Box's product range and variety, thereby improving its competitiveness and export capacity into neighboring markets in the region, notably the larger Kazakstan market. The project will also promote import substitution in Kyrgyz Republic.

company_name: HOTELES CITY EXPRESS S.A.B. DE C.V.
project_description: Through its subsidiaries, Hoteles City Express, S.A.P.I. de C.V. (“City Express” or “the Company”) is engaged in the development and operation of business hotels for the middle and middle low income markets in Mexico. It has successfully engaged in the implementation of 47 hotels in 24 of the 31 states of Mexico. The project consists of the development of new hotels (the “Project”), which would help the Company to consolidate its leading position in the budget business hotel sector, accelerate existing growth plans and initiate its expansion outside of Mexico.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company was founded in 2002 by a management team with extensive experience in the hospitality industry. Today, City Express shareholding includes: Morgan Stanley (through MSREF SSFIII), prominent businessmen from Mexico City and Monterrey, and the management of the Company. As of March 31, 2010, the Company manages 47 hotels representing 5,214, rooms within three different brands: (i) City express (ii) City junior; and (iii) City Suites. The Company has built a strong competitive advantage by having a wider coverage throughout the country, which enables it to maintain a central reservation system, a loyalty program, alliances with airlines and travel agencies, and corporate agreements.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is an equity investment of up to $20 million to finance a portion of the 2011-2015 business expansion plan of the Company which comprises the development of approximately 50 additional new hotels. This capital increase will help the Company consolidate its leading position in the budget business hotel sector, accelerate existing growth plans and initiate its expansion outside of Mexico.
location_description: The Company’s hotels are located in commercial, services and industrial areas of various cities in Mexico. Already operating in more than 30 cities, the new hotels will be developed primarily in capitals of state, second tier cities, services, commercial and industrial areas, and close to airports. The Company will also target similar areas within its Latin America expansion initiative.
development_impact: The proposed project will have the following development impact: (i) increase in supply of competitive price-quality business hotels with consistent international quality and safety standards; (ii) creation of new employment both directly at the hotels and indirectly along the supply chain, temporary employment will also be provided to local labor during the construction phase; and (iii) the Project will generate supply linkages for local vendors serving the needs of both the hotel and its guests and will contribute to the development of the local economy.
Company Name: HOTELES CITY EXPRESS S.A.B. DE C.V.

project_description: The proposed project (“Elite Plaza”) is the construction completion of an 18-floor Class-A office building located in Yerevan, Armenia. The property is located at the core of the city center, near the main square and the Central Bank offices, with excellent access by car and public transportation. The building will accommodate approximately 25,000 m² of office, retail, conference and exhibition areas. It is expected to be available for lease by mid 2011 with the objective to attract quality long-term tenants.
sponsor_shareholders: The project’s sponsor is Elite Group CJSC; a leading property development company with operations in Armenia and Georgia. It started its operations in 2002 with focus on residential property, having developed several large scale class A and B housing projects on a build to sell basis. The project owners the three shareholders of Eltie Group: Mr. Armen Mkoyan (60%), Mr. Amatuni Tonoyan (20%), and Mr. Haykaz Bakhshetsyan (20%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $23 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $9 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The property is at Khorenatsi Street, near the main square and the Central Bank offices in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia.
development_impact: (i) Support for Investments in IDA countries: IFC will play a role to support a local company pursue its strategic objective to develop a portfolio of real estate investment projects in Armenia and Georgia, both IDA countries, by providing long-term financing that is not currently readily available in the market. (ii) Supporting Business-Enabling Infrastructure: The Project will provide the first true Class-A office commerical building in Yerevan and contribute towards meeting the demand for Class-A commercial/office space in the country. (iii)Increased Employment: The Project will create new employment, both directly and indirectly. In addition, temporary employment will be provided to local labor during the construction phase. (iv) Demonstration Effect: IFC's participation during the crisis will encourage other investors and financial institutions to also pursue other investment opportunities with viable companies in Armenia.

project_description: Atul Limited (“Atul” or the “Company”) is a leading chemicals manufacturer in Western India. The Company’s main facilities are located in the towns of Atul and Ankleshwar in the state of Gujarat. Atul has adopted a strategy to transform into a global market leader for a few select products while retaining a smaller portfolio of commodity products where the Company can sustain its low cost advantages. The proposed US$15 million corporate loan will help finance its expansion plans and efforts to diversify into new products.
sponsor_shareholders: Atul was established in 1947 as part of the Lalbhai Group of companies (the “Group”), one of India’s large business houses. The Group’s main businesses now include textiles, chemicals, engineering and finance. The Sponsors have a 41% shareholding in Atul, with the balance held by the general public (35%), financial institutions (6%) and other corporates (18%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a corporate loan of up to US$15 million on IFC’s own account that will help Atul meet its funding needs, including: capital expenditures to expand capacity for existing products; capital expenditures to diversify into new product lines
location_description: Atul Ltd. owns two manufacturing sites in Gujarat State, India: 1,250-acre Atul site and 33-acre Ankleshwar site. There are six manufacturing divisions at Atul site, which include aromatics, agrochemicals, bulk chemicals & intermediates, colors, pharmaceuticals & intermediates, and polymers. Aromatics division is located at Ankleshwar site. The Atul site is located by the Par River, which is approximately 8-km from the Arabian Sea. Majority of the Atul site is undeveloped, and Atul preserves the undeveloped part as a natural protection area, cooperating with World Wildlife Fund (WWF) – India. There are approximately 1,100 houses in Atul’s residential colony inside the Atul Site. The other nearby farming community is approximately 1.5 km from Atul site. The major land usage in the Par River basin is mango orchard. There are no endangered species in or near the Atul site. The Ankleshwar site is located inside a chemical industry park – Ankleshwar industrial estate, which is one of the largest in India and well organized.
development_impact: This investment is expected to have the following development impacts. It will help strengthen and expand the operations of a mid-tier company to enable it to become internationally competitive and help the Company’s efforts to reduce water conservation. The Company is also expected to step up its social contributions in local communities and also actively maintain and increase more than one million trees planted in its campus.

project_description: Muyuan is planning to increase its breeding and commercial hog farm capacity (the “Project”) by constructing: a commercial hog farm with 120,000 hog/year capacity and a commercial hog farm with 80,000 hogs/year capacity a 15,000 sow breeder farm, with linked commercial grow out hog farm with capacity of 300,000 hogs/year; another 15,000 sow breeder farm; and working capital needs Upon completion of the Project, Muyuan’s annual hog production capacity would increase from 0.5 million to 1 million.
sponsor_shareholders: Muyuan Foodstuff Co., Ltd, located in Neixiang, Henan province, is one of the largest hog producers in China. Founded in 1992 by Mr. Qin Yinglin, Muyuan evolved from a backyard pig farm of 22 pigs, to a large scale, farrow-to-finish hog production company with an annual production capacity of around 500,000 hogs and breeders. Muyuan owns 1 Great Grand Parent (GGP) farm, 12 breeding and growing farms, and 2 feed mills with an annual production capacity of 400,000 tons. A few more breeder and growing farms are being planned or constructed. Mr. Qin Yinglin, aged 45, is the Chairman and General Manager of Muyuan and the Sponsor of the Project. Mr. Qin has more than 17 years of experience in pig farming industry and is well regarded in the Chinese pig farming industry. He is responsible for the overall business strategy and development of the Company. In 2002, Mr. Qin served as a member of the Henan People’s Congress. Mr. Qin graduated from Henan Agriculture University with a major in animal nutrition. Currently, Mr. Qin is a visiting professor of Henan Agriculture University. He received numerous provincial and national honors and awards. Ms. Qian Yin, aged 44 , the wife of Mr. Qin and the co-founder. She is a seasoned veterinarian with extensive experience in immunization and disease control. A graduate of Zhengzhou Animal Breeding Professional Institute, she is the general manager of Neixiang Muyuan Industrial Co., Ltd.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total estimated Project cost: $ 51.3 million, which will be funded by IFC equity investment $10 million, domestic bank loan $15 million, Internal Cash generation $ 26.3 million (Muyuan has already spent $6.3million in the project).
location_description: The project will be implemented by Muyuan Foodstuff Co., Ltd in Neixiang County, Henan Province, China. Under the proposed project, four hog farms with an annual production capacity of 500,000 will constructed and put into operations.
development_impact: Corporate Development: The proposed investment will support the continued expansion of a small, private pig farming company in a frontier region to become a competitive, quality conscious national player - which will ultimately be publicly owned. The Project will benefit, as highlighted below, one of the poorest areas in Henan province (Neixiang County) which has a GDP per capita of $1150, only half the average GDP of the province. Employment: The Company will provide stable employment opportunities for around 1000 staff, including 300 female employees. The Project will create 300 new jobs, of which 100 would be for female employees. Farmers Reached: Currently, about 24,000 rural households supply raw materials directly and indirectly, through aggregators/traders, to the Company. The additional capacity will allow the Company to expand this reach further by either increased sourcing from its existing supply base and/or expanding the supply base. SMEs reached: Muyuan sells its breeder pigs to about 1,200 rural pig farms, which in turn grow the piglets to produce commercial hogs for sale. In addition, the Company uses over 100 small, rural contractors for its raw material sourcing and logistic services.

project_description: IFC and Standard Chartered Bank (“SCB”), UK are jointly considering to establish a trade finance facility of up to US$300 million to help reduce periodic acute fuel shortages in Ghana. The facility will provide private sector bulk distribution companies (“BDCs”) in Ghana access to oil import financing facilities, enabling the BDCs to import petroleum product cargoes on a regular basis, thereby helping reduce fuels shortages in Ghana. Of the total facility amount, IFC’s exposure will be up to US$150 mn through a risk sharing arrangement, whereby, IFC will effectively share the underlying credit risk of the BDCs with SCB.
sponsor_shareholders: Headquartered in London, Standard Chartered Bank has over 1,600 branches and outlets located in over 70 countries and has operated for over 150 years in some of the world's most dynamic markets. The group earns around 90 per cent of its income and profits in Asia, Africa and the Middle East, from its wholesale and consumer banking businesses. Its income and profits have more than doubled over the last five years primarily as a result of organic growth. It is among the top three global banks for trade. Standard Chartered Bank is committed to building a sustainable business over the long term and is holds high standards of corporate governance, social responsibility, environmental protection and employee diversity. It employs around 70,000 people, nearly half of whom are women. The group's employees are of 125 nationalities, of which about 70 are represented in the senior management. Standard Chartered Bank is listed on both London and Hong Kong stock exchanges. Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s rating for SCB are A2 and A+, respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s exposure will be up to $150 mn through a risk sharing arrangement, whereby, IFC will effectively share the underlying credit risk of the BDCs with SCB.
location_description: Standard Chartered Bank is headquartered in London, United Kingdom and operates in over 70 countries. The project involves providing structured trade finance to Ghana’s BDCs, which import and supply petroleum products in bulk to the country’s retailers. Most of these BDCs are headquartered in Accra, Ghana.
development_impact: The project is designed to have a development impact in terms of: Reducing Supply Interruptions: Improving access to trade finance is designed to help the BDCs import product on a regular basis, alleviating the occurrence of petroleum product shortages in Ghana; Private Sector Development: The facility is designed have a role in supporting independent private sector players.; and Supplementing Existing Facilities: The project supplements the facilities offered by local banks and IFC's GTFP program by providing additional cost effective trade financing solutions in the Ghanaian market and helping increase the overall trade finance flows to the country. IFC proposes to monitor the following key development impacts during the life of IFCâ?™s investment: - The volume of petroleum products imported in Ghana through the use of this facility - The number of BDCs using this facility - The total storage infrastructure established by the BDCs in Ghana in terms of capacity

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: WEG Industries (India) Pvt. Ltd. (WII) is constructing a greenfield plant near Hosur, Tamil Nadu State, India, to produce high voltage motors and generators. Production is expected to be ramped-up by the end of 2011 and in its initial years of operation, the plant is expected to produce an average of about 250 motors and generators per year (the Project). Sales will be largely in India, although there will also be exports from India to neighboring countries. These motors and generators are large, technologically sophisticated and are typically used in infrastructure (small, electric generation stations and water pumping stations), agriculture (irrigation), as well as mining and industry.
sponsor_shareholders: WII is fully-owned by WEG S.A. (WEG). WEG was founded in 1961 in Jaraguá do Sul, state of Santa Catarina, Brazil, where it is still headquartered. WEG engineers and manufactures capital goods, in particular it specializes in electric motors, generators, transformers and electronic and electromechanical components for industrial and other automation systems. While WEG has exported throughout the world since its earliest days, the company is in a phase of investing in production capacity outside Brazil, of which WII is an important step. In 2009, WEG reported BRL 4.2 billion in net sales (approximately US$ 2.1 billion). WEG S.A. is listed on the Sao Paulo stock exchange, whereby approximately 65% of the company’s shares are with the founders and their families (Voigt, Silva, and Werninghaus) and the balance of shares is more widely held.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at approximately US$ 95 million, of which half is attributable to production machinery, approximately one-quarter for civil works and leasehold. The balance of one-quarter is working capital, information technology, and pre-operational expenses. IFC has been asked to provide a loan of approximately US$ 25 million. While WII will have some working capital facilities from local institutions, most of the balance of the project cost is funded by WEG S.A.
location_description: The site lies within the boundaries of the SIPCOT Industrial Complex, Phase II at Hosur, where the WII is building a 33,000 m2 facility. The plant is located approximately 40 kms south of Bangaluru (Bangalore) on National Highway 7 linking Bangalore and Chennai. In addition to the site, WII has a project office in Hosur and WEG’s sales company in India maintains an office in Bangalore.
development_impact: Improved Product Availability and Quality. The Indian market is undersupplied with locally-manufactured, high voltage motors and generators that are state-of-the-art technologically. The importance of manufacturing this equipment locally derives not only from transportation cost savings but also because this equipment is built-to-order to very detailed specifications, bringing to the client benefits from the ease and accuracy of information exchange with a local manufacturing facility and improved delivery times. Infrastructure Development. Infrastructure, including power generation is a bottleneck to economic development in India. WEG will increase its capacity to sell turbines for small-scale, run-of-the-river generation projects that tend to serve areas that are off-grid. Further, another important segment which requires high voltage motors are the producers of basic infrastructure building blocks: cement and steel plants. WEG also is building on its track record in India of supplying motors for the pumping stations that make up important, government-sponsored irrigation projects. Employment. The Project will generate at least 250 direct jobs and is estimated to generate a multiple of this in the supply chain of WII and contractors for corporate and industrial services including maintenance, security, transportation providers, etc.

project_description: Lafarge’s operations in Iraq consist of a 2.5 mtpa cement plant in Bazian, Suleimanyah, and a 2.3 mtpa cement plant in Tasluja, Sulaimaniyah, leased from the Government. In addition, Lafarge is in the process of finalizing a lease agreement with the Government of Iraq to rehabilitate and operate a 1.8 mtpa cement plant near Kerbala, Iraq. The Project has three components: (i) supporting Lafarge’s expansion and growth in Iraq; (ii) refinancing a portion of Lafarge’s shareholder loans to the Bazian plant, originally made as a shareholder bridge loan in the absence of banks willing to lend directly into Iraq; and (iii) debt financing to the Kerbala plant.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project’s Sponsor is Lafarge, a leading player in the global cement industry, based in France and publicly listed in the Paris Bourse. Lafarge’s holding company for its Iraqi operations is in the process of being established. Bazian Cement Company (“BCC”), which is the project company for the Bazian plant, is owned 70% by Lafarge and 30% by Mr. Faruk Rasool, a local businessman in Iraq. Al-Rowad, which is the project company for the Kerbala plant, would be 51% owned by Lafarge, and 49% owned by MerchantBridge, an investment house focused on the Middle East region.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The IFC investment is expected to consist of: (i) an equity investment of up to US$25 million in Lafarge’s holding company for its Iraqi operations; (ii) an IFC A Loan of up to US$50 million in BCC; and (iii) an IFC A Loan of up to 25 million to Al-Ruwad, to support a rehabilitation program.with an estimated project cost of US$220 million.
location_description: The project covers two cement plants currently under the control of the project sponsor and located in Bazian and Tasluja respectively, close to Suleimanyah, Iraq. In addition, the project sponsor is in the process of finalizing a lease agreement with the Government of Iraq to rehabilitate a cement plant near Karbala, Iraq. All three plants are existing industrial operations located in rural areas with low population density and sparse vegetation.
development_impact: The development impact of the project is expected to include: (i) increased supply of cement to meet Iraq’s needs for reconstruction; (ii) substitution of imports from neighboring countries, which will help stabilize prices in the sector; (iii) modernization and standard-setting in the sector, in which Lafarge is currently the only private sector player, and all other plants are state-owned, many of which are small and in poor condition; (iv) demonstration effect on other potential foreign investors who could help bring much-needed FDI into Iraq; (v) job creation; and (vi) tax revenues for the Government of Iraq.

project_description: The Gateway Mall Project is a new US$37 million mall development comprising about 18,000 m2 gross lettable area in Lilongwe the capital city of Malawi. The mall will cater to both local and regional customers and will be anchored by major South African retailers as well as a number of key local retail players. The land was acquired from the Government of Malawi on a 99-year lease and the site is sufficiently large to include the potential for a 7,000 m2 extension of the mall and also has sufficient space for a 150 room hotel project to possibly be implemented at a later stage. Construction of the mall is earmarked to begin in May 2010 and occupation is planned for September 2011.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Malawi Property Investment Company Limited (“MPICO”). MPICO together with its main shareholder, Old Mutual Life Assurance Company (Malawi) Ltd (“Old Mutual Malawi”), will maintain a majority ownership in the Project. MPICO is the largest property company in Malawi and is the only listed property group on the Malawi Stock Exchange. It has a portfolio of 35 properties, predominantly commercial offices, but also residential, retail and industrial properties, in Lilongwe and Blantyre. MPICO is owned 55% by Old Mutual Malawi, 11.5% by Lincoln Investments and the balance is held by the public. Old Mutual Malawi is owned 100% by Old Mutual Plc which is listed on the London Stock Exchange. Old Mutual Plc has a market capitalization of about US$9 billion. The principal activity of Old Mutual Malawi is the transaction of all classes of life assurance savings and retirement funding business.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is US$37 million. IFC is considering an investment of up to US$12 million comprising of an A loan of up to US$10 million and a C loan of up to US$2 million. The balance of the funding will come from the Project Sponsors and institutional investors in Malawi and South Africa.
location_description: Gateway Mall is situated in a prime location on the western side of Lilongwe at the intersection of the new Western Bypass to be constructed and the east-west highway linking Lilongwe with Zambia’s Eastern Province.
development_impact: Key development impacts of the Project include: ???Provision of high quality retail infrastructure: Currently there is no shopping mall in Lilongwe, the capital city of Malawi. The Project will support the development of high quality retail that meets international standards. With strong international anchor tenants and a range of retailers including smaller local companies, the shopping mall will bring quality retail services closer to the community, thus minimizing costs to consumers and helping to establish a strong retail destination; ???Job Creation: The Project will create jobs both directly and indirectly during construction and operational stages; ???Enhanced local supply linkages: The Project will increase business opportunities to local suppliers of goods services; and ???Formalization of the retail sector: The Project will enhance the formalization of the retail sector in the country, which is currently mostly informal. This will help increase the tax revenue to the government.

project_description: Established in 1977, Apollo Tyres Limited (“ATL” or “Apollo”) is one of India’s leading tyre manufacturers. Apollo also has a significant global presence through its export operations and through its subsidiary companies in South Africa, Zimbabwe and in Netherlands. Apollo is setting up a greenfield tyre manufacturing facility at Oragadam (near Chennai, state of Tamil Nadu) and is implementing various capital expenditure programs at its existing facilities (together, the “Project”) at Limda (state of Gujarat).
sponsor_shareholders: Main sponsors of Apollo are Mr. Onkar Singh Kanwar (a second generation entrepreneur) and associates, who own 39% of Apollo. Apollo is publicly listed on the major stock exchanges of India and other shareholders of Apollo comprise financial institutions and mutual funds (16%), Indian public (17%), Foreign Institutional Investors and NRIs (26%) and governments (2%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$515 million. IFC is proposing a financial package of US$ 60 million comprising both an A loan on IFC’s own account and B loans syndicated from participants.
location_description: The greenfield tyre manufacturing facility is located at the State Industries Promotion Corporation of Tamil Nadu (“SIPCOT”) industrial park at Oragadam, near Chennai in the state of Tamil Nadu, India. SIPCOT is promoted by the state government of Tamil Nadu. Apollo is also implementing smaller capital expenditure programs at its existing facilities at Limda (state of Gujarat).
development_impact: The greenfield project will result in the creation of about 1,500 skilled and semi-skilled direct, permanent jobs and an additional 2,000 jobs during the construction phase. The Project will also result in establishment and development of new Small & Medium Enterprise (“SMEs”) in the supply chain.

project_description: The project is a planned expansion by Millennium Investments Ltd. (the “Company” or “Millennium”), a vertically integrated operator and owner of The Crane Resort, situated on 38 acres in St. Philip, Barbados. The business model at Millennium is to (i) construct residential units in Barbados and sell the ownership in fractions to end-users and (ii) to operate the completed rooms as a resort management company. The proposed project is to (i) continue construction at the Company’s existing site, (ii) commence construction at a site owned by the Company and (iii) to acquire new land for continued growth.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company controlled by Mr. W. Paul Doyle (“Mr. Doyle”). Mr. Doyle, a Canadian national.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC has proposed a US$20.0 million investment for its own book, which would be divided into a $10.0 million A-Loan and $10.0 million C-Loan.
location_description: The project is located in the parish of St. Philip, Barbados.
development_impact: In addition to the “demonstration effects” there are a host of quantifiable benefits to resort staff, suppliers, customers, and the destination that are associated with leveraging high quality management and facilities.

project_description: Aubaine Graphic (‘Aubaine’ or the ‘Company’) is a Chadian printing Company created in 1999. The Company located in Ndjamena, the capital city of Chad employs 51 people. The proposed project consists of the expansion of the Company through the strengthening of the existing production lines as well as the purchase of additional printing equipment for new production lines aimed at diversifying the products offering (the "Project"). The Project should help Aubaine grow and consolidate its position as a key sector player of the Chadian market.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor, Mr. Abderamane Mahamat, owns 70 percent of the Company’s shares with the balance being held by his immediate family. This dynamic businessman, founder and current Manager of Aubaine, has successfully established the Company as the leading printing company in Chad only a few years into operations.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is EUR 6.6 million. The proposed investment is a EUR 2.3 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project is located on: (i) the existing company site, measuring 2,000 square-meter surface area in downtown Ndjamena and (ii) a new site of 8,000 square-meter surface in the Farcha industrial zone which will house the new production lines. Both sites are earmarked for industrial and economic activities with availability of utilities.
development_impact: IFC investment would help support the growth of a local sponsor, increase the competition in the local printing industry and substitute imported products with locally manufactured products. The investment will highlight IFC support to private sector development, especially in Chad. The Project will also generate employment estimated at 77 positions and provide quality education material to local schools at competitive cost.

company_name: SOLIDA ADMINISTRADORA DE PORTAFOLIOS S.A. DE C.V.
project_description: Solida (or the Company) has invited IFC to participate in one of its main business operations: investments in lower-income housing projects. In this line of business, Solida provides preferred equity capital to large homebuilders in Mexico for the acquisition of land. On its own account, the Company has financed approximately 50 projects to date, equivalent to the construction of around 110,000 mostly lower-income houses. The proposed project would entail IFC co-investing up to US$50 million, or 20% of the total financing needs, through a master trust to provide preferred equity capital for individual low-income housing subprojects. Solida and possibly another investor will provide the remaining funds.
sponsor_shareholders: Solida is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Banco Mercantil del Norte (Banorte), the third largest bank in Mexico in terms of asset size. Banorte is publicly listed and has a market capitalization of around US$9.4 billion as of April 15, 2010. Established in 2001 as an investment vehicle, Solida started operations by acquiring non-performing assets for recovery. Today, the Company focuses on two areas of operation: (i) acquisition, administration and collection of portfolios of nonperforming assets; and (ii) alliances in investment projects with strong housing developers in low-income housing projects and to a lesser extent in real estate projects (mostly commercial centers).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $350 million. IFC is planning to invest $50 million in preferred equity into a master trust. The master trust will then invest directly into individual housing sub-projects.
location_description: The master trust will be set up in Mexico and will make investments into individual housing sub-projects throughout the country.
development_impact: Key development impacts of the Project include: - Increased Housing Supply for Low-Income Households: This Project is expected to alleviate the current housing deficit in Mexico, including in a few frontier states and benefit over 100,000 families in the low to middle income segments with increased supply of quality and affordable entry level housing. - Community Development: The housing developments built by the homebuilders financed by Solida and IFC will contribute to urban infrastructure development and surrounding community development. In addition, the Project helps support the urbanization efforts of local governments, as the housing projects include partial infrastructure works. - Job Creation and Financial Security: The Project will create job opportunities both during construction and operation of the housing communities.
