Increased supply of low-cost housing developed by the Company will make an impact on the lives of the low income purchasers who will improve their personal security and through payment of their mortgage build up equity (often for the first time) in a significant asset. - Enhanced Local Supply Linkages: The Project will increase demand for construction and building materials in the country. Once the construction is completed, the housing units will stimulate the use of local supplies of goods and services, supporting maintenance, retailing and wholesale operations. Moreover, the low income properties financed by the Project are often the buyers' first property title and such property rights are considered a key determinant of economic development as they promote the formal economy.
Company Name: SOLIDA ADMINISTRADORA DE PORTAFOLIOS S.A. DE C.V.

sector: Household Appliances (Including Refrigerators, Laundry Machine, Dishwashers, etc.)
project_description: The Gorenje Group is the largest household appliance manufacturer in Southeast Europe and among the top 8 manufacturers of appliances in Europe. The Project involves (a) modernization, restructuring and expansion identified under the 2010-2013 strategic plan and (b) restructuring its debt maturing in 2010-2012.
sponsor_shareholders: With 60 years of tradition, Gorenje is the largest home appliance manufacturer in Southeast Europe and exports 90% of its sales to 70 countries with a focus on Europe, from that more than half to Eastern European markets, where Gorenje brand has been highly recognized. In 2009 Vienna Brand institute valued Gorenje brand at 458 mio EUR, 85% of its sales are under its own brand names. Gorenje business activities are organized within three operating divisions: (i) Household Appliances Division (78% of sales) - this division manufactures and distributes refrigerators and deep freezers, cookers, washing machines and dryers; (ii) Home Interior Division (4% of sales) - this division manufactures and markets kitchen and bathroom furnishings, bathroom fittings and ceramic tiles; and (iii) Ecology, Energy and Services (18% of sales) - this division engages in energy trading, ecology and environment protection, trade, engineering, and catering services. Gorenje produces over 2.9 million units large home appliances of its own production in its three factories in Slovenia, Serbia and Czech Republic. Gorenje has been publicly-listed on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange since November 2000. The Group has about 21,000 shareholders. The ownership is divided as follows: (i) Slovenian state-owned pension fund , KAD (25.19%); (ii) Home Products Europe B.V (7.63%), a share swap with a strategic investor at acquisition of leading Dutch home appliance company; (iii) INGOR d.o.o.&Co.k.d.(5.66%) - management; KD Galileo (4%) – investment funds; (iv) treasury stock (0.86%), and other small shareholders consisting of banks, investors and individuals (51.98%)
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is planning on investing up to EUR 30 million in equity in Gorenje and providing EUR50 million Senior A-Loan form IFC’s own account and raising up to EUR 100 million in syndication under IFC’s B-Loan umbrella.
location_description: Gorenje’s main facilities are located in Velenje, Slovenia, Valjevo and Stara Pazova in Serbia and Mora Moravia in the Czech Republic. All of these sites are located near small towns and are the largest generators for employment in the region.
development_impact: The IFC investment will help Gorenje continue its longstanding leadership, by helping it expand, modernize, and restructure its operations following the economic crisis. The investment will result in better product competitiveness through improved energy efficiency and innovation, enhanced high end product range, improved labor productivity and job creation in South-East region. The Group’s investment program will allow the transfer of first-class production methods and manufacturing practices including the development of local industry through linkages with network of local suppliers. The capital increase associated with the Project will reduce the government's influence and strengthen market-oriented behaviors. Moreover, the IFC investment will support the Group’s growing focus on ecology and offer comprehensive waste management solution to regional clients.

sector: Other Textile Products (Including Industrial and Medical Products)
country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: Kordsa Global Endustriyel Iplik ve Kord Bezi Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (“Kordsa” or the “Sponsor”), a former IFC client, is the world’s leading producer of nylon and polyester yarns, cord and industrial fabric mainly used in automotive tires, rubber parts, and transmission and conveyor belts. Kordsa has 11 manufacturing plants located in 9 countries. The proposed investment in the South American subsidiaries of Kordsa entails providing two separate corporate loans to Kordsa Argentina S.A. (“Kordsa Argentina”) and Kordsa Brasil S.A. (“Kordsa Brasil”), to be utilized for refinancing part of their existing debt, working capital requirements and maintenance capital expenditures (collectively the “Project”).
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is established in 1973 and headquartered in Istanbul. Kordsa is majority owned (91.1%) by the one of the largest conglomerates in Turkey, Sabanci Holding, and 8.9% of its shares are listed on Istanbul Stock Exchange. Kordsa Argentina is a wholly owned subsidiary of Kordsa. Kordsa Brasil is indirectly (through wholly owned Sabanci BV, Acordis Int. BV and Dusa Spain) 94% owned by Kordsa while the remaining 6% is held mainly by two local nationals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment includes two separate loans; an A Loan of up to US$25 million to Kordsa Brasil, and an A Loan of up to US$15 million to Kordsa Argentina. There will be two loan agreements for each loan. This disclosure covers the IFC A loan to Kordsa Brasil. Prior to signing the legal documents with Kordsa Argentina, appropriate, separate, property specific public disclosures will be made for Kordsa Argentina investment.
location_description: Kordsa Brasil’s operations are located within the Camaçari industrial complex (Polo Industrial Camaçari) near the city of Salvador in the state of Bahia. Kordsa Argentina’s plant, located in Berazetegui, Argentina.
development_impact: The Project will have significant development impacts: IFC's investments in Kordsa Brasil and Kordsa Argentina will benefit the manufacturing cluster in both countries, and particularly in the case of Brazil, in a frontier region of the country, where employment opportunities are limited. Employment preservation: By strengthening the capital structure of the companies, IFC's investment will help retain jobs and assist the companies emerge from the crisis as more viable entities. Continued know-how and technology transfer: Given the Sponsor's focus on product innovation and its ability to meet stringent quality standards, the Project is expected to result in continued technology and know-how transfer to the subsidiaries in terms of manufacturing and quality processes.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

company_name: GLOBINO MEAT-PROCESSING PLANT LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY
project_description: The Project will assist the expansion of the Globino group of companies (“Globino” or the “Company”), one of the leading vertically integrated meat processing companies in Ukraine, which sells processed meats, butter and cheese under the “Globino” brand. Globino’s operation includes a modern pig farm and slaughterhouse. The Project includes: i) increasing production capacity of fresh and processed meat; ii) increasing pig farm and slaughterhouse capacity; and iii) modernizing and expanding the cheese and butter making capacity.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Alexander Kuminsky, the founder and sole owner of the Company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at approximately $100 million. The proposed IFC investment is a mixture of debt and quasi-equity for a total of up to $25 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project is located in and near the town of Globino, which is in the Poltava region of Ukraine. The region is predominantly rural, and centrally located in Ukraine. The project will be both on existing and greenfield sites.
development_impact: The project is expected to have the following development impacts: i) increased employment of approximately 600 new employees; ii) increased purchases of raw materials from local small and medium enterprises; and iii) benefit to consumers from lower prices and a higher standard of food safety.
Company Name: GLOBINO MEAT-PROCESSING PLANT LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY

project_description: Zambeef Products plc (“Zambeef” or the “Company”), established in 1994 and with headquarters based in Lusaka, Zambia, is one of the largest agri-business groups in Zambia and the region, involved in the production, processing, distribution and retailing of beef, chicken, pork and dairy products among others. The Project entails supporting Zambeef’s investment program in: Zambia – (a) expansion and upgrading of retail outlets, wholesale depots and processing plant; and (b) expansion of its piggery operations; and Nigeria – (a) establishment of an integrated livestock feedlot and processing facility; and (b) expansion of its retail outlets
sponsor_shareholders: Zambeef is a publicly listed company on Lusaka Stock Exchange in Zambia with a current market capitalization of US$134 million. The shareholders include local and international fund managers, pension funds and individuals including the founders, Carl Irwin and Francis Grogan, who collectively hold 4.7%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is (i) a US$7 million A Loan for the Zambian investment program and (ii) a US$3 million A Loan for the Nigerian project.
location_description: Zambeef has various farms and butcheries in Zambia from where it operates its cropping, animal husbandry, processing and retailing. The proposed projects will be based on its owned facilities in Zambia. In Nigeria, the Company has leased a 300ha farm from Ogun State Government, 60km north of Lagos, where the project is going to be implemented.
development_impact: (i) Creation of jobs; (ii) Increase food supply; (iii) Improvement in local farmers'' incomes through the purchase of young calves as well as technical assistance; (iv) Development of an efficient integrated meat supply chain; and (v) Improvement in quality standard of meat available to retail.

project_description: The proposed project involves a construction of a 135,000 tons per annum (“tpa”) greenfield duplex board plant (the “Project”) and seeks to utilize the imported and domestic waste paper as one of the main raw materials to produce duplex board, thereby harnessing the increasing demand for packaging materials as a result of the growing consumer goods industries in the MENA region. The proposed Project is based on acquisition, refurbishment and relocation of a good-quality second-hand machine from The Netherlands to the Project site in the Sadat city industrial zone, 60 km away from Cairo. The Project cost is estimated at approximately US$84.5 million. The Project will lead to increased recycling of paper in Egypt and is in line with the new IFC Forest Strategy, which supports investments in resource efficient manufacturing. It will create approximately 200 direct manufacturing jobs and additional employment throughout the waste paper collection supply chain. Project concept rests on the existing deficit of duplex board in the MENA region, whereas regional converters are unable to satisfy their demand for duplex board from local sources, and factors for cost-competitive duplex board manufacturing in Egypt, including availability of competitively priced gas and power, labor advantage and potential for access to extensive waste paper base, which has not yet been tapped due to lack of comprehensive waste paper collection infrastructure in Egypt. With no newly-announced capacity in the region, the Project is expected to replace imports and compete with the regional duplex board producers on quality as well as cost basis. The Project will be implemented by El Shorouk, an operating subsidiary of the National Printing Company ( “NPC”), the largest converter and printing house of consumer packages in the region with consolidated 2008 revenues of US$73.8 million, EBITDA of US$13.3 million and Net Income of US$4.1 million. For the purposes of the Project, El Shorouk will set up a new subsidiary, El Motaheda, which will be majority owned by El Shorouk.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsors of the Project are Grandview Investment Holdings and the Al-Moallem family, jointly owning 92.5% of NPC (the “Sponsors”). The balance of 7.5% is owned by the EuroMena Pack Holding SAL, Lebanese private equity fund that targets investments in MENA. Grandview Investment Holdings is an investment company established by Citadel Capital, a leading private equity firm in Middle East and North Africa regions with more than US$8.3 billion in investments across 12 countries and 14 industries. Grandview was established in May of 2005 with objective to invest in small and mid-cap industrial companies and to position them for regional growth and expansion, and is domiciled in the BVI. As of December 31, 2009, Grandview had US$160 million in assets under management. Al-Moallem Family is represented by Eng. Ibrahim Al-Moallem, Chairman and CEO of the National Printing Company, a reputable and well-known businessman, who has been active in printing and publishing in Egypt for over 40 years.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated project cost is US$84,500,000 equivalent. The proposed IFC investment package comprises an equity investment of up to US$10 million in NPC and an A loan of up to $15.5 million to El Motaheda for IFC’s own account (US$25.5 million combined), representing 30% of the Project cost.
location_description: The proposed Project site will be located in the Sadat city industrial zone, 60 km away from Cairo.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have the following key developmental impacts: Employment Generation: The Project will help create 200 direct jobs in manufacturing, and at least as many indirect jobs throughout the wastepaper collection supply chain; Waste Paper Recycling & Positive Impact on Environment: The Project will improve the paper recovery rates in Egypt, where they remain at historically low levels. An organized wastepaper collection system that will be established to provide the main raw material to the Project could have a transformational impact in this field. Import Substitution: At present, around 75% of Egypt’s duplex board is imported. The Project will lead to increased supply of the locally-produced good quality packaging products, as the Project output is destined predominantly for domestic consumption. Positive Impact on Consumer Goods Industries: Increased availability of high-quality packaging materials at competitive prices will have a positive impact on the domestic and regional consumer goods companies, helping them increase their sales, working capital management and profitability.

project_description: Agrotec S.A. (“Agrotec” or “the Company”) is one of Paraguay’s leading crop input distributor and agronomy services company operating since 1990. Agrotec offers a “one-stop shop” to more than 700 client farmers, providing seeds, fertilizers, agrochemicals, technical support, storage and logistic services, pre-harvest financing, as well as commercialization of the grains of its producer client base. The Company’s strategy is to develop strong relationships with farmers providing integral agronomic services from sowing planning and advice, through the provision of seeds, nutrition integration and crop protection. Agrotec operates 7 Regional Distribution Centers (“RDCs”) including its HQ in Ciudad del Este located near the major crop regions of Paraguay to guarantee a rapid delivery of inputs and efficient customer service to its clients. The Project consists of providing Agrotec an up to $15 million one year loan facility (the “Facility”) with up to five renewable tranches, to support the working capital needs of the Company.
sponsor_shareholders: Agrotec is owned by local Sponsors through two holding companies: Agrihold Investment Ltd. and Agrihold Management Corp (“Agrihold” or the “Group”), which centralizes the Group’s business and operations in Paraguay, Uruguay, and Brazil.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at $15 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an up to $15 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Ciudad Del Este, Paraguay. The Company has 7 Regional Distribution Centers located near the major crop regions of Paraguay.
development_impact: IFC’s involvement in this project is expected to have a strong developmental impact as it will: - Increase farmers’ access to pre-harvest financing, - Contribute to rural economic development while reaching the BOP in rural areas, - Contribute to the development of agri services and supply chain sector in Paraguay, and - Support the dissemination of agricultural best practices and inputs to farmers (Agrotec provides technical assistance to farmers to improve productivity through improving yields and profitability).

project_description: BioCarbon Group Pte. Limited (“BioCarbon”, the “Company”), registered in Singapore, has been established to invest in Avoided Deforestation (AD) projects in emerging markets. These projects will conserve forests from being converted into other forms of land-use and generate carbon credits – the sale of which will be the main source of income for the Project. BioCarbon is in the process of raising circa US$25 million of new capital. The proceeds will be used for (i) pre-development work in the identified sites for AD work; (ii) investment in concessions in Indonesia to be undertaken over the course of next 12-18 months, (iii) next two year development costs for projects in Indonesia and (iv) development of a pipeline of AD projects outside Indonesia.
sponsor_shareholders: Macquarie Capital Group Limited, a financial services firm based in Australia, currently owns 100% of the Company. At financial closing, it is expected that 4-5 investors including IFC will each own between 15-40% of the Company. The final composition of investors will be known in the next 2-3 months. BioCarbon has partnered with Fauna & Flora International (FFI), a well respected, operationally focused NGO to be the on-the ground project manager for its initial projects.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be approximately $25 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $5 million equity investment in BioCarbon.
location_description: The proposed project sites in the first phase of investments will all be located in Indonesia in the provinces of Kalimantan and Papua. BioCarbon is currently in discussions with state and private parties to acquire long term concession rights for these sites.
development_impact: Climate change mitigation and adaptation is one of the World Bank Group’s strategic priorities. IFC has identified the forest sector as one of the key pillars of its climate change mitigation strategy. The following outlines the key development impacts of the proposed transaction. The Project will directly help in climate change mitigation through avoided deforestation of mainly tropical rainforests in several countries where these forests are seriously threatened. The Project will result in intervention in sites where there is a significant threat of biodiversity loss. The Project will provide for direct benefit sharing with local communities and local governments as well as development of alternative livelihood strategies for the local communities. The Project would support one of the early private sector initiatives for conservation of forests and is likely to have a demonstration impact that could catalyze large amounts of private capital in this sector. Finally, the Project is expected to demonstrate the viability of AD projects and serve as a test case for advancing the discussions on the adoption of an international Reduced Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD) framework.

project_description: In 2003, in an attempt to replicate the success of the Maldives’ tourism industry, the Seychelles government invited Maldivian hospitality companies, including the sponsors of the Universal Enterprises Pvt Ltd (“UEPL”, or “Universal”), the Maniku family, to invest in the country (which faces similar geographical and infrastructural limitations). Consequently, the 111-room Labriz Silhouette Island Resort (“Labriz”, the “Project”) was developed and commenced operations in late 2006. Belonging to the collection of the 480 Small Luxury Hotels of the World, Labriz is positioned as an affordable luxury resort that blends elegant hospitality with the Seychelles’ tropical rainforest environment and is currently the largest five-star resort in the Seychelles. Labriz has 325 employees, 135 of which are local. In 2005, IFC committed a $30 million A loan to three companies within the UEPL group of companies in the Maldives, under IFC’s $150 million Tsunami Tourism Loan Facility. IFC’s A loan was used to partially fund: (i) the reconstruction and refurbishment of two of Universal’s properties that were damaged during the tsunami; (ii) the refinancing of certain existing overdraft facilities for recently renovated properties in anticipation of the downturn in the tourism market as a result of the tsunami; and (iii) the development of one new property.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsors are the owners of the Maldivian hospitality group, Universal. The ownership of Labriz is as follows: Universal Holdings Ltd. holds 70% of Labriz and is owned by the same shareholders as UEPL and in the same proportion. UEPL itself does not hold any equity interest in Labriz. UEPL is the flagship company of the Universal Group and was incorporated in 1978 in the Maldives by three brothers, M.U. Maniku, A.U. Maniku and I.U. Maniku who combined their existing tourism interests in four resorts into one entity. The very first resort in the Maldives was developed in 1972 by M.U. Maniku, and UEPL currently owns / has interests in seven resorts in the Maldives, making the Maniku family the first and one of the largest investors in the Maldives’ tourism industry. UEPL is privately held by the three founding members and four of their nephews. The remaining 30% of Labriz is owned by the Silhouette Island Lodge, which in turn is owned by two local investors. The Silhouette Island Lodge used to be a 22-room lodge on the island, owned and operated by the two investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost was $57.5 million. The Project was financed by loans from UEPL (which took on short-term loans), Mauritius Commercial Bank and by internal accruals. The proposed IFC investment comprises a $20 million loan to Labriz, to be co-borrowed by UEPL, as the proceeds will be used to strengthen their balance sheets while repaying the short-term borrowings incurred by UEPL during Project’s construction.
location_description: Silhouette Island is the third largest granitic island of the Seychelles. It lies approximately 20 kilometers northwest of Mahé with a land area of approximately 20km2 and a maximum altitude of approximately 750 meters. Silhouette Island is surrounded by a National Marine Park declared in October 1987. The Marine Park extends around the entirety of the Island to a distance of one kilometer from the low water mark. In addition much of the Island is soon to be declared as a National Park; however, the resort itself is located outside the National Park. The Resort is constructed on land that previously housed a 22-room hotel and land that was historically used for farming.
development_impact: Facilitating the development of the tourism industry in the Seychelles: Because of the similarities in geography and infrastructural limitations between the Maldives and the Seychelles, Universal was one of two Maldivian hospitality companies approached by the Seychelles Ministry of Tourism to help develop the Seychelles' tourism industry, which was virtually non-existent before 2006. Despite having been present in the Seychelles for less than three years, Universal has contributed significantly to the local economy by providing employment opportunities, establishing a clinic and a school, by building required infrastructure (e.g. a jetty) and by providing free transport for the island's locals to Mahé, the capital. Environmental support: IFC's biodiversity and environmental specialists, together with external consultants, are working with Labriz to ensure that the resorts' operations have minimal impact on the biodiversity of the island and the resort's surrounding environment.

company_name: SAID SALIM BAKHRESA AND COMPANY LIMITED
project_description: The Bakhresa Group, established in 1983, operates milling businesses in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda, Zanzibar and Malawi. The Group has invested in new mills and grain storage to cater for the growing demand and market opportunity for its flour in the region. The Group objective it to continue to reduce its production costs and offer affordable flour for consumption in the Eastern Africa region. In this context, the Group has indicated further interest with new expansion projects in Mozambique. Also, it would consider the purchase of additional transport equipment for its existing mill in Rwanda; and additional financing options for Tanzania (Said Salim Bakhresa & Company Ltd.) at a later stage.
sponsor_shareholders: Bakhresa’s main sponsor, Mr. Said Salim Awadh Bakhresa is founder and CEO of the Bakhresa Group of companies, a prominent Tanzanian businessman. Current responsibility and leadership for operation in Tanzania. Other mill operations and projects, including the new projects in Mozambique and Rwanda are managed by one of his son, Mr. Abubakar Said Bakhresa, as Executive Director. Other shareholders are family members.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC A-loan is a multi-facility of up to $20.5 million that will be used to finance the proposed projects in the three (3) countries mentioned above. IFC loans would be allocated as follows: (i) US$8 million for the establishment of the Nacala (Mozambique) new mill; (ii) US$2.5 million for investment in transport equipment for the Kigali (Rwanda) mill; and (iii) US$10 million standby loan for SSB Tanzania operations (Tanzania).
location_description: The projects have three (3) separate locations as described below: Nacala (Mozambique) mill would be located in Nacala industrial zone, where Bakhresa has already purchased a land, some 9 km away from the port and on the main road in/out of Nacala. Kigali (Rwanda) transport project would be located nearby the existing BGM Rwanda mill, currently under construction. The mill is located in the new Kigali Industrial Park (KIP), which is managed by Rwanda Investment Group (RIG). Bakhresa has recently finalized the land acquisition process. Dar es Salaam (Tanzania) operations.
development_impact: The proposed projects will have the following impacts: (i) local production of flour, substituting for flour imports with consequent impact on value added, service to local bakeries, employment, SME reach and contributions to government revenues through increased income taxes; (ii) Improved logistics, via rail and road.
Company Name: SAID SALIM BAKHRESA AND COMPANY LIMITED

country: Middle East, Pakistan, and Afg Region
project_description: Headquartered in Amman, Jordan, the Nuqul Group is a leading regional manufacturing group primarily involved in the production of jumbo tissue rolls and their subsequent conversion into paper-based hygienic products such as facial tissues or diapers. The proposed project mainly consists of expanding the Group’s conversion capacity in facial tissue, toilet paper, napkins and diapers in Egypt and Jordan. This Project is the continuation of Nuqul’s expansion efforts across the MENA region and will enable it to cater to the basic hygienic needs of populations in Jordan, Morocco, Egypt, Iraq, Syria, Algeria, Libya, Algeria and Tunisia. Additionally, part of the project funding may be utilized to support investments in energy and water savings as identified in the context of IFC’s Advisory Services collaboration with Nuqul.
sponsor_shareholders: Established as a trade and import company for food stuff by Mr. Elia Nuqul in 1952, the Nuqul Group began its paper converting operations in 1958. With IFC’s support through four projects since 1990, the Nuqul Group has grown from a family-run Jordanian conversion operation into a leading regional integrated manufacturing corporation focusing on hygienic paper products (facial tissues, diapers, feminine pads, table napkins, toilet rolls) with operations in 9 countries and selling its products across the Middle East region. The Nuqul Group is wholly-owned by its founder and his family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed conversion capacity expansion and potentially energy and water efficiency project represents a total consideration of approximately $67 million of which $30 million would be provided by IFC in the form a of 10-year amortizing corporate loan.
location_description: The project consists in financing the acquisition of new machinery to equip (i) a new conversion plant in an industrial area in 6 October in Egypt, close to Nuqul’s Egyptian paper mill; (ii) the extension of a conversion plant in the outstrips of Amman; and (iii) potential water and energy efficiency improvements across the Nuqul Group’s mills in Egypt and Jordan.
development_impact: Improved economic resilience: The expansion of conversion capacity in the host countries of the project (namely Egypt and Jordan), will help support the local economic environment by decreasing reliance on typically more expensive and volatile imported goods. Additionally, the manufacturing focus of the project will support diversification of the economy in the countries where the new capacity will be established. The project will also enable Nuqul to increase its internal consumption of jumbo tissue rolls and focus its sales on higher-margin finished products, thereby improving its operational performance and resilience. Spread of world-class business practices: Over the past years, Nuqul has made significant progress on the path to institutionalization notably in separating ownership and management as well as implementing world-class corporate governance and business practices. The Nuqul Group is a highly respected institution across the MENA Region and the project will enable Nuqul to spread its commendable business practices by expanding the Group’s regional reach. Benefits of regional integration: The project will facilitate increased trade linkages within the region and serve as an example to other players of the rewards available from global integration. Improved living standards for the populations: The project will create sustainable employment opportunities in countries where youth unemployment is a major issue. Domestic and efficient operations will enable the Nuqul Group to bring more affordable quality products in the market, thereby improving the local populations’ access to products catering to basic human needs. Demonstration effect: By providing long term financing in markets where these types of financing are typically not available, IFC sets a long term interest rate benchmark for commercial loans of longer tenors. This may lead to the eventual development of a long term interest rate curve in the local market and enable local lenders to provide these types of financing. Cleaner production support: The project will support the Nuqul Group’s efforts to move towards cleaner production, thereby contributing to decreasing the Group’s environmental footprint.
Country: Middle East, Pakistan, and Afg Region

project_description: Groupe Industriel Madiou Simpara SA (“GRIMAS” or the “Company”), is a producer of carbonated soft drinks, performs and caps for PET beverage bottles, and carbon dioxide for beverages. The proposed project will (i) expand its existing operations in Mali and (ii) create new operations in Cote d’Ivoire and Senegal. The purpose of the project is to increase the Company’s revenue and market, and create a leading regional beverage group.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Mr. Madiou Simpara, one of Mali’s leading entrepreneurs that has been in business for over 30 years. Among other concerns, he is chairman and CEO of GRIMAS, one of the largest privately-owned Malian industrial groups with 6 companies and over 200 employees. After project completion, GRIMAS will comprise of: Nouvelles Brasseries Bamakoises (NBB) – production of soft drinks and mineral water since 2002; Hamaya Preformes SARL (HPML) – production of preforms and caps since 2004; Santigila-Gaz – production of carbon dioxide since 2003; Hamaya Preformes Senegal (HPSN) – production of preforms and caps since 2009; Nouvelles Brasseries Cote d’Ivoire (NBCI) – production of soft drinks to commence in 2010; and, Hamaya Preformes Cote d’Ivoire (HPCI) – production of preforms and caps since 2009. Mr. Simpara is the primary shareholder of GRIMAS with 89% of the shares, while other Malian business people own the remaining 11%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at EUR 35 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan for IFC’s own account of up to EUR 14 million.
location_description: There are four different project sites: The NBB, HPML and Santigila factories are located at the existing GRIMAS factory site just outside Bamako in Mali. The site is on a major regional road, Route de Koulikoro, adjacent to the small village of Nyabakoro Droit. HPSN is a greenfield site located on Route Nationale 1, a major regional road in an industrial part of Rufisque, a well-developed town about 40 km from Dakar in Senegal. NBCI is located at an existing partially-completed factory site in Bonoua, a well-developed town about 56 km from Abidjan in Cote d’Ivoire. The site is on a major regional road and is adjacent to a mineral water bottling plant. HPCI is located in an existing factory in Zone II, a well-developed industrial area in Abidjan, Cote d’Ivoire. All sites have good access to major transport routes.
development_impact: - Industrialization and private sector development in Mali, Senegal and CI: The Project will support a local sponsor who is contributing to industrialization of the region. The success of the Project would create backward linkages with suppliers and forward linkages with local wholesalers/retailers (who sell GRIMAS' soft drinks) many of which are MSMEs. - Employment: The Project will create local employment, direct and indirect through the supply chain. - Import Substitution: Currently some of beverages/preforms/caps/gas consumed in the region are imported (especially in CI and in Senegal). The increase of local production with local brands would enable import replacement. - Government Revenues: The overall Project will contribute to public revenues through increased taxes paid by GRIMAS as well as those paid by suppliers and other downstream service providers (i.e. distributors, etc.).

project_description: The New Africa Mining Fund II (“NAMF II”) is a private equity style mining sector fund seeking to raise $100 million to $300 million for investment in equity and equity-like investments in small-to-mid-tier companies (“juniors”) that are focused on early-to-later stage exploration, mining and beneficiation activities in Africa. NAMF II will aim to make investments in which it can exercise significant influence, with the aim of delivering capital growth and sustainable return over the long term. The target commodity focus will include base metals, gold, platinum group metals, coal and potentially other bulk minerals, where the medium-to-long-term industry fundamentals are attractive.
sponsor_shareholders: NAMF II will be managed by NAMF Capital Partners (Pty) Ltd (the “Fund Manager”); a jointly-owned partnership to be formed by Decorum Capital Partners (Pty) Ltd (“DCP”) and a Black Economic Empowerment (“BEE”) partner to be identified. DCP is a proprietary South African private equity fund management company that was established by Neil Gardyne, John Taylor and Arthur Mashiatshidi to manage the first New Africa Mining Fund. Both Gardyne and Taylor are on the management team for NAMF II, although Mashiatshidi has since left and been replaced by Wayne Botha. The principals of DCP are individuals with extensive fund management, deal structuring and mining sector experience and also have a good understanding and track record of working with juniors. DCP will serve as Advisor to the Fund Manager and will accordingly deploy the investment team and apply the practices and policies of DCP. Through the involvement of a BEE partner, DCP aims to introduce Historically Disadvantaged South Africans (HDSAs) into the management team, to broaden the team, develop a succession plan and potentially achieve compliance with South Africa’s BEE Code, as it applies to private equity funds.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund Manager expects to raise $100 million to $300 million for NAMF II. IFC is considering providing up to $30 million in equity.
location_description: NAMF II will be established as two parallel investment vehicles, one offshore registered entity and another vehicle registered in South Africa. Both vehicles will be making investments in Africa with a bias toward Southern African Development Community (“SADC”) member countries.
development_impact: With the involvement of IFC and potentially other Development Finance Institutions ("DFIs"), NAMF II is expected to establish a sizeable fund with significant financial and operational capability. NAMF II will focus on junior mining companies in Africa, which are typically unable to attract institutional investment for their early exploration and pre-development work. Providing capital at this end of the extractives resources value chain fills an important gap in an important sector, whose development holds significant potential economic impact and developmental benefits for the host countries in the long term. More immediately, the Project is expected to help junior mining companies advance their projects up the value chain, through the provision of equity capital and close support from the Fund Manager, while applying environmental and social best practices and establishing long-term partnerships across the region. The following indicators will be tracked throughout the life of the fund: Achievement of first close/funds raised Net IRR Number of employees of NAMF II investees Percentage/number of NAMF II investees acquiring mining permits/completing feasibility studies Percentage/number of NAMF II investees going into mine development Number of NAMF II investees in which the Fund Manager maintains a board seat

project_description: Moderna Alimentos S.A. (“Moderna”, or the “Company”) leads the wheat flour milling market in Ecuador with 39% market share and sales of $130m in 2009. Leveraging on this strength, Moderna plans to further improve efficiency and expand value-added products (bread, pasta, social programs). Moderna is headquartered in Quito with operations in Quito, Amaguaña, Manta, Riobamba, Guayaquil, and Cayambe. The Project is for the Company to (i) upgrade wheat/flour storage & logistics; (ii) acquire the assets of Molinos La Union; (iii) start-up Millerecuador S.A. and add a pasta line; and (iv) expand bakery business.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor are the Company and its ultimate shareholders: (i) the Seaboard Corporation (25%), an international company listed and based in the US; (ii) the Continental Grain Company (25%), a private international company based in the US; (iii) the Correa family (36.6%), a local Ecuadorian family; (iv) the Lopez family (10.6%), a local Ecuadorian family; and (v) Fondo Pais Ecuador (2.8%), an investment fund in Ecuador.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $29 m. The proposed IFC investment is a $8 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Project will be implemented in the Company’s existing plants in Manta, Quito and Cayambe.
development_impact: Expected developmental impacts include: (i) support a key staple food producer in Ecuador, help to secure food supply; (ii) help with the feasibility study and implementation of a program aimed at increasing fortified food supply to poor children & women through the GAIN/IFC AS program; (iii) create new jobs by reviving a bankrupted flour & pasta company which will have a significant impact on the development of a rural area of Ecuador.Expected developmental impacts include: (i) support a key staple food producer in Ecuador, help to secure food supply; (ii) help with the feasibility study and implementation of a program aimed at increasing fortified food supply to poor children & women through the GAIN/IFC AS program; (iii) create new jobs by reviving a bankrupted flour & pasta company which will have a significant impact on the development of a rural area of Ecuador.

project_description: The project consists of the construction of a 5 million ton per annum hydro-cracking and coking facility in Mostorod, Greater Cairo, by the Egyptian Refining Company SAE (“ERC” or the “Company”) to upgrade locally available refinery atmospheric residue into lighter products, such as ultra low sulfur Euro V diesel and high octane gasoline blending component, for the domestic Egyptian market (the “Project”). The Project will also include environmental upgrades to the adjoining facilities of state-owned Cairo Oil Refining Company (“CORC”) and Petroleum Pipeline Company (“PPC”). Egyptian General Petroleum Company (“EGPC”), a Government of Egypt (“GOE”) economic authority, and owner of both CORC and PPC, will supply most of the feedstock to the Project and off-take most of its production. The Project is seen by GOE as an important import substitution project which will address the strong deficit of lighter petroleum products in the Greater Cairo region, which represents about half of the Egyptian refined products market, and Egypt’s surplus of atmospheric residue/fuel oil.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a greenfield Egyptian company incorporated in 2007 for the sole purpose of carrying out this Project. It is owned 82% by Orient Investment Properties Limited (“Orient”), 15% by EGPC and 3% by other investors. The Project’s main sponsor is Citadel Capital S.A.E. (“Citadel” or the “Sponsor”), a leading Cairo-based private equity firm founded in 2004. Citadel, together with co-investors, established Orient to invest in ERC and serve as the investment vehicle for the Sponsor’s oil refining activities in the Middle East and North Africa region. ERC is Orient’s first project. EGPC is GOE’s petroleum arm responsible for the development of Egypt’s upstream and downstream oil industry, including ensuring the supply of various refined petroleum products within Egypt. EGPC owns and operates all of Egypt’s nine existing refineries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be approximately $3.6 billion. The Project will be financed on a 64/36 debt/equity basis ($2.3 billion in debt and $1.3 billion in equity and subordinated contractor loan financing). IFC is proposing up to a $100 million equity investment in Orient, the Company’s main shareholder.
location_description: The Project is to be located on the outskirts of Cairo, on the Ismailia canal in the Mostorod District, adjacent to the existing CORC refinery. The site is in a highly populated urban area, but the Project will be located within the walls of an existing petroleum complex. The processing facilities will occupy approximately 323,000 square meters to the South of the CORC refinery.
development_impact: The Project will help optimize the domestic production and distribution of low sulfur refined products, address increasing fuel demand within the country, particularly in the Greater Cairo area, and generate savings for the GOE through the substitution of higher-cost imports. Environmental benefits will also materialize through upgrades of existing facilities and the production of ultra-low sulfur diesel. During construction and operation of the refinery the main benefits include: (i) Employment: Approximately 10,000 jobs created during construction (at peak) and 700 direct permanent jobs during operations in addition to the other services that are expected to flourish around the Project. (ii) Benefits to GOE: In addition to tax revenues, the GOE will benefit through a carried interest in the Project, a price discount on diesel produced by the Project, savings on logistics for imports, and additional revenues for CORC and other state-owned companies for services rendered to ERC. (iii) Environmental Upgrades and Benefits: ERC has agreed to implement, at its own cost, a series of environmental upgrades to the existing site, CORC and the storage facilities of the adjoining state-owned PPC. The upgrades are expected to lead to significant improvements to local air and water quality as they will involve soil decontamination, installation of low nitrogen oxide burners and of a tertiary waste water system at CORC. In addition, with the start of ERC operations, CORC will switch to using natural gas exclusively for internal energy needs, away from high sulfur fuel oil. This is expected to reduce cumulative sulfur dioxide emissions in the area surrounding ERC significantly. More broadly, potential environmental benefits of the Project will come from the supply to the GOE of ultra low sulfur diesel, which has significantly lower sulfur content than diesel currently produced in Egypt, at lower cost than alternative imports. This will therefore give GOE a low cost option to reduce the average sulfur content of locally consumed diesel and thereby the level of sulfur dioxide emissions in Egypt. (iv) Community Impacts: Community Development Centers will be established to offer a variety of community services, including employment/skills training, literacy, health and other life skills education programs and healthcare support. ERC is expecting to invest over US$5 million in community investment during the construction period. The key development indicators that are proposed to be monitored during the life of the IFC investment are: - Employment (# of jobs during construction and during operations) - Implementation of environmental upgrades to CORC/PPC and soil remediation (US Dollars spent) - Reduction in sulfur dioxide emissions in Mostorod area (% decrease from baseline) - Payments to GOE (US Dollars) - National Purchase of Goods and Services (US Dollars) - Community Development Outlays (US Dollars)

project_description: The proposed Project involves the construction of a greenfield plant in Egypt to produce chemicals, primarily for export to large, international companies that manufacture home & personal care products in MENA, Europe & the Americas. A majority of Galaxy Egypt’s sales will go to multinationals, many of which are currently supplied from the Sponsor’s existing operations in India.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project Sponsor is Galaxy Surfactants Limited (“Galaxy” or the “Company”), an Indian unlisted public company founded in 1986 that produces chemicals used by manufacturers of home & personal care (“H&PC”) products including shampoos, toothpastes, liquid soaps etc. It is a prominent & established supplier in the Indian market & exports to over 90 countries. Growth is expected in the BRIC and other developing countries as improved standards of living provide opportunity for increased demand for H&PC products. Galaxy’s top customers include multinational producers of home and personal care products. The Company’s promoters and promoter group collectively hold approximately 78% of equity shares of Galaxy.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated to be about $30 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $12MM A Loan.
location_description: The Project will be located in the Suez Public Free Zone, an industrial area near the Red Sea, approximately 125 kilometers from Port Said, Egypt.
development_impact: The Project is expected to have the following development impacts: (i) establishment of the first such state-of-the-art manufacturing facility of this type in Egypt, helping diversify the economy away from its dependence on natural resources and tourism, (ii) local employment of approximately 70 direct jobs during operations and about 1,000 labourers during construction, (iii) training opportunities for about 40-45 Egyptian locals who will be sent to India for approximately 4 months, (iv) export earnings from export of manufactured products and (v) social spending in the local community.

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: Financed by IFC, Kronospan Bulgaria produces melamine-faced particleboard (“MFC”) and oriented strand board (“OSB”) at two facilities in Bourgas and Veliko Tarnovo. In the past three years, the company made investments of EUR50 million to upgrade particleboard production and environment equipment in Bourgas, establish a warehousing and distribution center in Sofia, and to acquire and rebuild a domestic particleboard company in Veliko Tarnovo. These investments were bridge-financed by shareholder’s funds and internal cash generation and Kronospan is now looking to partially refinance them with the help of IFC. This will allow Kronospan Bulgaria to position the company for growth when the economic situation improves.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is Kronospan Holdings Ltd. (“KHL”), a holding company for the Kronospan Group's Central and Eastern European operations. Its operating subs are located in Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Serbia, Romania, Croatia and Hungary. Their principal activities are manufacturing and distribution of wood based panels. KHL is a part of the Kronospan Group. Established in 1897, the Kronospan Group is the world’s largest producer of medium density fiberboard (“MDF”), particleboard and laminated flooring, and Europe’s leading producer of OSB with combined capacity of around 16 million m3. With a high level of vertical integration and plant locations near its key markets, the Group is amongst the lowest cost producers in the industry. It operates 26 manufacturing sites across 24 countries, and employs 11,000 people world-wide. The Group has a good operating track record and a lean and flat management structure.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is EUR 50 million. The proposed IFC investment is a EUR 25 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Kronospan has particleboard, MFC and OSB production in the industrial zone of Bourgas, a particleboard and MFC facility in Veliko Tarnovo and a warehousing and distribution center in a suburb of Sofia. All sites have good access to transportation routes (auto and railway).
development_impact: Climate Change Mitigation: Climate change benefits include a corporate commitment by Kronospan to produce panel products from waste-wood chips, forest residues and pulpwood, and to stimulate growth of forests through sustainable forest management practices. Employment: The Project will help the continued operation of the plants in Bulgaria and preserve the jobs of approx. 300 people. Benefits to Local SMEs: High volume production of value added products benefits the local furniture manufacturers and construction industry through lower prices and higher product quality. Demonstration Effect: The success of the project during the ongoing financial crisis is likely to have a demonstration effect for similar investments by other global and regional companies. This will encourage FDI, boosting confidence in the economy and the environment for private sector investment.

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: Kronospan Serbia has finished construction of a particleboard plant in Lapovo to better serve the markets of Serbia and the Balkan countries. Planned plant capacity is 380,000 m3 of particleboard and 11 million m2 of melamine facing per annum. The project was financed by Kronospan and HVB, Germany. Production was to commence in Spring 2009, but the project was delayed due to difficulties with land acquisition, regulatory permissions and a decision to increase capacity to better realize economies of scale. It is expected that the full scale production will start in 2010.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is Kronospan Holdings Ltd. (“KHL”), a holding company for the Kronospan Group''s Central and Eastern European operations. Its operating subs are located in Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Serbia, Romania, Croatia and Hungary. Their principal activities are manufacturing and distribution of wood based panels. KHL is a part of the Kronospan Group. Established in 1897, the Kronospan Group is the world’s largest producer of medium density fiberboard (“MDF”), particleboard and laminated flooring, and Europe’s leading producer of OSB with combined capacity of around 14.6 million m3. With a high level of vertical integration and plant locations near its key markets, the Group is amongst the lowest cost producers in the industry. It operates 26 manufacturing sites across 24 countries, and employs 11,000 people world-wide. The Group has a good operating track record and a lean and flat management structure.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at EUR94 million. The proposed IFC investment is a EUR24 million loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project is a greenfield particleboard plant in the town of Lapovo, near the city of Kragujevac in Serbia. Lapovo is approximately 100 km from Belgrade. The site is located in a rural area, next to a major highway and has direct rail access.
development_impact: Climate Change Mitigation: Climate change benefits include a corporate commitment by Kronospan to produce panel products from waste-wood chips, forest residues and pulpwood, and to stimulate growth of forests through sustainable forest management practices. Kronospan Serbia aims to source 50% of raw material inputs from wood chips and saw dust. Employment: The Project will generate approximately 200 additional jobs in the relatively undeveloped rural area. Benefits to Local SMEs: High volume production of value added products will benefit the local furniture manufacturers and construction industry through lower prices and higher product quality. Increased Linkages: The Project is expected to increase the sourcing of raw materials and wood from local suppliers, thereby enhancing the income of the people involved in the upstream production as well as the planting and harvesting of forests. Import Substitution: Domestic wood panels’ manufacturers in Serbia are unable to meet local demand. Increased local supply of particleboard is expected to substitute imports and lower board prices in the country and contribute to the competitiveness of exports and the local downstream construction and furniture industries. Strong Demonstration Effect: The success of the project during the ongoing financial crisis is likely to have demonstration effect for similar investments by other global and regional companies. This is likely to encourage FDI, boosting confidence in the economy and the environment for private sector investment.

project_description: Ozer Konveyor Band Turizm Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (the “Sponsor”, or “Ozer Band”), a mid-sized Turkish conveyor belt manufacturer, is carrying out a modernization and expansion program for its subsidiary Newko Balkan L.L.C. (the “Borrower”) incorporated in Kosovo to improve its competitiveness and widen its product range . The Sponsor asked IFC to provide an A Loan of up to EUR 6 million to Newko Balkan (the “Project”). The Borrower, which was privatized in 2005 by the Kosovo Trust Agency (“KTA”) enjoys a 40 years experience in conveyor belt manufacturing. Similarly, the Sponsor has 34 years experience in conveyor belt manufacturing; and more than 60 years experience in the rubber industry.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is the main shareholder of Newko Balkan. Upon completion of the transfer procedures established by the KTA, the Sponsor will own 100% of the share capital of Newko Balkan. The Sponsor is a family business lead by Yusuf Ozer.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is Eur10million and IFC is considering an A Loan of up to Eur6million.
location_description: Newko Balkan has only one plant located 120km away from Pristina, the capital city of Kosovo. The site is within the city of Suhareke in an urban area.
development_impact: The proposed south-south Project is expected to: (i) transfer modern manufacturing technology from Turkey to Kosovo, which would improve efficiency and competitiveness, (ii) implement sound environmental and social best practices, (iii) improve corporate governance and financial transparency in privately held family group of companies; and (iv) provide a demonstration effect and promote foreign direct investment in Kosovo.

project_description: The project involves providing a long-term quasi-equity financing and a three-year renewable working capital facility to Mriya, the 7th largest Ukrainian primary agricultural producer with a proven track record of growing wheat, barley, sugar beet, rapeseed, potatoes, and other crops. The long-term loan will be used for a construction of three grain silos with storage capacity of 100,000 tons each, purchase of farm machinery, and acquisition of lease rights for 165,000 ha of agricultural land, while the three-year facility will be used for working capital. Mriya will use proceeds from the loans to produce wheat, corn, barley, sugar beets, rapeseed and other agricultural commodities for sale to local clients and international traders.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is the Huta family (the “Sponsors”), who founded Mriya in 1992 and control it till this day. The head of the Huta family, Ivan Huta, a well-respected Ukrainian businessman, and his wife, Klaudia Huta, Ivan and Klaudia Huta established Mriya on 50 hectares of land, after having worked for eight years at a state farm. In 2002, Andriy and Mykola Huta, the sons of the founders, joined the family business after completing their education in Ukraine and abroad. Following a private placement on the Entry Standard of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2008, the Sponsors collectively own 80% of Mriya’s Cyprus-based holding company that fully controls all of Mriya’s Ukraine-based operating companies, with the remaining 20% owned by over 20 institutional investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $213.7 million. Mriya will use proceeds from the loans to produce wheat, corn, barley, sugar beets, rapeseed and other agricultural commodities for sale to local clients and international traders. Higher working capital will allow Mriya to increase its production volumes 2-3 fold and increase land area under cultivation to 315,000 ha by 2012. IFC investment will consist of a one-year loan facility (the “Working Capital Facility”) of up to $25 million renewable twice at the end of a 365 day period for one year each time, a long-term C-Loan of up to $25 million, and warrants of up to $25 million.
location_description: The project will allow Mriya to expand its farming operations and grain storage infrastructure in the Ternopil, Ivano-Frankivsk, Chernivtsi and Khmelnitsky regions, which are among the poorest, primarily agricultural, regions of Ukraine.
development_impact: Employment: Mriya has approximately 606 permanent employees and 310 seasonal employees. The project is expected to increase permanent employment to about 800 and seasonal employment to about 500. In the western Ukraine where Mriya operates, employment opportunities are scarce. In addition to creating new jobs, Mriya is setting new employment standards in the region by providing benefits to its farm workers such food and housing. Environmental and Social Standards: As part of the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP), Mriya will implement an ESMS to provide a structured framework to identify and act on environmental and social risks and opportunities in the management of its agricultural operations as well as down-stream in the agricultural value chain, in the operations of the Sponsor-owned affiliated sugar beet processing plants. Private Sector Development: Mriya sells its products to a well diversified base of final customers and traders. Among them, there currently are about 88 MSME distributors of mainly potatoes, buckwheat, and corn, for final sales on the domestic market. On the purchasing side, Mriya relies on about 22 MSME suppliers, in addition to several large key ones, for deliveries of fertilizers, plant protection chemicals, and spare parts.

project_description: SUMMARY OF PROJECT INFORMATION Project Name Czech Republic - Plzensky Prazdroj, a.s. (PP) Modernization and expansion of PP''s two breweries located in Plzen, and financial restructuring. Region Central Europe Sector Industry Project No. 004352 Company Name Plzensky Prazdroj, a.s. Description of Location The Company comprises five breweries: two located in the City of Plzen, and one in each of the following Northwestern Bohemian cities: Karlovy Vary, Cheb, and Domazlice. The Company also has a bottling plant at Beroun, in West Bohemia. The project involves the two breweries in Plzen called Prazdroj and Gambrinus, which are located on an adjacent site to each other, in a total area of about 70 hectares. Date SPI sent to PIC April 11, 1995 Projected Board Date May 15, 1995 Description of Company and Purpose of Project The Company is a limited liability company, privatized on April 30, 1992, in the Government''s first wave of coupon privatization. It''s main activity is the production and sale of beer in the domestic and export markets. It also distributes Vodka produced by third parties and sells small amounts of malt in the export market. The project consists of the completion of the general modernization program and rationalization and upgrading of the Prazdroj and Gambrinus breweries; the completion of four distribution centers in the Czech Republic, and the refinancing of short term debt with long term loans. Technical Partner and/or Major Shareholders The Company is 100% Czech owned and is controlled by four coupon privatization investment funds. Project Cost The total estimated project cost is US$170.5 million equivalent. IFC has been asked to assist in the financing of this project by providing loans for a total of DM90 million (US$75 million equivalent). Environmental Category and Issues This is an environmental review category B project; principal issues are: air emissions, recycling and solid waste management, effluent treatment, ambient noise, fire prevention, PCB and CFC free equipment, and general employee health and safety. IFC''s Technical and Environment Department staff have reviewed these issues. The majority of the Company''s boilers are gas fueled and are having air emissions well within local requirements and World Bank Guidelines. Those operated on oil will be converted to gas as part of the project. Glass, paper and polyethylene waste from the Company are recycled. Waste oil is collected by a specialized company and domestic solid waste is land filled according to local regulations. The Company will ensure that waste water that is not supplied to municipal sewage treatment systems operating in compliance with World Bank Guidelines, will be in compliance with Czech national standards revised towards European Union Standards or World Bank guidelines by the end of 1998, either by upgrading the waste water treatment facility or by connection to an upgraded municipal system. The Company has proven that the other environmental issues mentioned above are being addressed within World Bank guidelines. The Environmental Review Summary will be available from the Public Information Center on the same date as this Summary of Project Information. For additional information contact: Corporate Relations Unit telephone: (202) 473-7711 facsimile: (202) 676-0365 Environmental documents for this project are available at http://www.ifc.org and from the World Bank InfoShop (http://www.worldbank.org/html/pic/aboutinfo.html).

project_description: Established in 2002, Universtar Science & Technology (Shenzhen) Co. Ltd. (“Universtar” or the “Company”) is a leading provider of environment monitoring equipment and services in China. Its core operations include manufacturing equipment, managing data monitoring systems and providing environmental treatment services. The Company’s clients include municipal and provincial governments as well as private sector industrial clients. The Company’s proposed US$180m investment plan spans 2010 and 2011, and will be used to support its business operations related to online monitoring equipment and services in China.
sponsor_shareholders: The Company is a private firm owned primarily by its Chairman and founder, Mr. LI Ye and another investor, Mr. YU Chung. Its other shareholders include KPCB China Fund, Fountainvest Fund, the management team and two angel investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost, which comprises the Company’s investment program over the next two years, is approximately US$180 million. IFC’s proposed funding is yet to be determined but is projected to be approximately US$20 million.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Shenzhen, China and has its main assembly and manufacturing operations in an industrial area of city. In addition, it has 8 operation subsidiaries, 18 branches and 26 operation service centers across 23 provinces across China.
development_impact: IFC's expected development impact resulting from a potential investment in Universtar includes: (i) Contribute to the development of the environment protection sector in China and assisting local governments achieve their short-and medium-term environment protection goals; (ii) Help China address key climate change challenges by financing a company that produces equipment that energy intensive industries and local governments can use to monitor their water and air emissions; and (iii) Provide a means for Chinese environment regulators to have reliable and consistent data so that it can monitor and prioritize environment performance and objectives.

project_description: Masan Group Corporation (“Masan Group” or the “Sponsor”) is the parent company of Masan Food Corporation (the “Company” or “Masan Food”). Masan Group is seeking long-term financing primarily to expand and upgrade Masan Food’s operations, as well as meet long-term working capital needs, and enter into other agribusiness ventures, either through acquisition or organic growth (the “Project”). Masan Food is a branded packaged food-and-beverage company based in and with nationwide distribution throughout Vietnam. Established in the late 1990s, the Company has established recognizable local brands for soy, instant noodles, fish and chili sauces. Headquartered in southern Ho Chi Minh City, the Company operates four production facilities and five distribution centers across Vietnam. The Company has focused on developing products with higher health and safety standards than the products currently available on the market.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsor is a holding company, listed in the Ho Chi Minh City stock exchange, which invests in growth industries, such as consumer goods, financial services, natural resources, logistics and business services. At present, the two most significant holdings of the Group are Masan Food and Technological and Commercial Joint Stock Bank (“Techcombank”), Vietnam’s third largest private sector bank and an existing IFC client.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering a corporate loan, denominated in Vietnamese Dong (VND), for IFC’s own account of up to $50 million equivalent to and warrants of up to $12.5 million equivalent in Masan Group.
location_description: Masan Food is headquartered in Ho Chi Minh City. The Company operates three main factories in Tan Binh Industrial Park (Ho Chi Minh City), Tan Dong Hiep Industrial Park (Binh Duong province) and Dai An Industrial Park (Hai Duong province). The factory in Tan Binh IP will be relocated to extended factory in Tan Dong Hiep IP within the next two years. Besides, the Company has a small factory in Phu Quoc island producing raw fish sauce.
development_impact: (i) Contribution to Employment: The Company employs over 4,000 workers, composed primarily of women. The Company’s continued expansion will ensure it maintains the current level of workers, despite the switch to automated machines. (ii) Farmer Linkages: The Company purchases over 90 million liters of raw fish sauce from approximately 400 fishermen based in Phu Quoc Island. The Company’s continued expansion of their fish sauce operations will increase their purchases to over 140 million liters annually from approximately 600 local fishermen. (iii) Consumer Benefits: The Company’s focus on providing healthy and safe products has enabled the consumer healthy and safe alternatives which did not exist before the Company entered the fish sauce, soy sauce and instant noodle markets. The Company plans to continue to introduce products which are healthier and safer than products currently available to the Vietnamese consumer. (iv) SME Linkages: The Company’s products are sold in nearly 100,000 small and medium size retailers through over 100 independent distributors. The Company’s products generate significant profits for these retailers and distributors of between 5-15%, or approximately US$10 million in 2008.

project_description: SUMMARY OF PROJECT INFORMATION (SPI) Project Name: MALI: Extension of LE RABELAIS Hotel Region: Sub-Saharan Africa Sector: Tourism (accommodation) Project No. 009672 (under Proparco Agency Line # 8938) Projected Board Date: February 18, 2000 Company Name: LE RABELAIS - GROUPE SARL Technical Partner and/or Major Shareholder : Mrs Monique DORAY was associated in this project on a 50/50 basis with Mr Sidy Mohamed KEITA for administrative reasons. Mrs DORAY holds now 100 % of the company. Project Cost Including Proposed IFC and Proparco Investment : The project cost is Euro 1,9 M equivalent and the financing plan would include a Euro 230 000 PROPARCO loan and a Euro 230 000 IFC loan. Location of Project and Description of Site : The Quizambougou residential area in Bamako, capital city of Mali. The extension would be situated on a 1,800 square metres ground next to the existing hotel. Description of Company and Purpose of Project : The first hotel created by Mrs DORAY in Bamako (LA TOURAINE RABELAIS) was financed by AFD in the end of the eighties (the loan has been prepaid). This hotel is located on a site with a lease expiring in 2009. The extension and creation of the new company LE RABELAIS GROUPE will enable the sponsor to continue its activity if the lease is not renewed. The project plans the construction of the following facilities: 29 rooms, 5 suites, one bar, several meeting rooms, a pancake restaurant for 50 guests, a gift shop, a craft workshop, a garden with swimming pool, a storage area and some outbuildings. Expected Development Impact : a 20 persons local staff will be hired. Environmental Category and Issues : This is an environmental category B project. The staff will benefit from appropriate sanitary facilities in the buildings and from social security. project_description: SUMMARY OF PROJECT INFORMATION (SPI) Project Name Colombia-ICOLLANTAS Region Latin America & Caribbean Sector Industry Project No 004608 Projected Board Date June 22, 1995 Company Name Indústria Colombiana de Llantas S.A. Technical Partner and/or Major Shareholders Corporación Financiera del Valle S.A., the second largest private finance company in Colombia owns 80.9% of Icollantas'' common shares. The Grupo Mazuera-Villegas, a major Colombian construction and real estate group owns another 15.8% of the shares outstanding. In December 1994, IFC subscribed to 2.8% of Icollantas'' common shares. The Company has license and technical assistance agreements with Uniroyal Goodrich Licensing Services, (the licensing division of Michelin S.A.). Project Cost including proposed IFC investment US$61.5 million Location of project and Description of site Headquarters in Cali, Colombia; plants in Bogota and Cali Description of Company and Purpose of Project Icollantas was founded in 1942 and merged with another Colombian tire company in 1994 to create the largest tire producer in Colombia with a 55% share of the domestic market. The Company is undertaking a US$53.5 million project to modernize and specialize its radial tire production facilities in Cali and to modernize and specialize its bias-ply tire plant in Bogota. The Company is also considering other investments/acquisitions in Latin America. A Summary of Project Information (SPI) for a proposed US$14 million IFC loan and US$5 million equity investment was filed with the PIC on November 23, 1994. Occupational health and safety issues include general worker safety, record keeping on accidents and noise protection. As a condition to IFC''s loan financing, the Company has agreed to comply with World Bank guidelines and Colombian environmental regulations. Date SPI sent to PIC May 31, 1995 For additional Information contact: Corporate Relations Unit - telephone (202) 473-7711 - facsimile: (202) 676-0365. project_description: Summary Of Project Information (SPI) RegionEurope Sector Project No010063 Projected Board DateMarch 27, 2000 Company NameIsiklar Ambalaj Technical Partner and/or Major Shareholders The project sponsor is Isiklar Holding, the core company of the Isiklar Group in Turkey. Isiklar Group is comprised of several subsidiaries active primarily in four core businesses: (i) packaging materials; (ii) building materials; (iii) construction and engineering; and (iv) services. Isiklar Holding was incorporated in Istanbul in 1974. Isiklar Holding and its subsidiaries are controlled by the Isik family (primarily three brothers) through their majority ownership (94.2%) in Isiklar Holding and also direct shareholding in certain of its subsidiaries. Ambalaj is listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange and Isiklar Holding owns nearly 78% of the enterprise. Project Cost Including proposed IFC investment The total project cost is projected to be $42 million, including $10 million debt refinancing for Isiklar Ambalaj and $32 million needed to complete the company''s Celhart project in Bulgaria. The proposed IFC investment consists of a convertible loan of up to $10 million to Isiklar Ambalaj in Turkey. The same amount will be committed by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) in parallel. Location of project and Description of site Isiklar Ambalaj owns five sack factories in Turkey (in the following cities: Bartin, Konya, Izmir, Elazig and Adana), a sack factory in Egypt and Celhart kraft pulp and paper mill in Bulgaria. Description of Company and Purpose of Project Isiklar Ambalaj is the leading Turkish manufacturer of kraft paper sacks (for use mostly in the cement industry) accounting for 65% of both total production and sales in 1998. Ambalaj is listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange and Isiklar Holding owns nearly 78% of the enterprise. The project will help ensure the continuation of a viable investment in Bulgaria (namely, the Celhart pulp and paper modernization project to which IFC has previously invested $15.4 million). Moreover, the project will help ensure the financial viability of Isiklar Ambalaj in Turkey. With this project, IFC will help ensure the continuation of a viable investment in Bulgaria. The Celhart project is an export-oriented project, and will increase Bulgaria’s net foreign earnings. Moreover, the project will ensure that Celhart retain its employees. The project includes preventive and corrective measures that will significantly improve the plant’s environmental status. IFC’s role is further augmented by the fact that the proposed investment plan will help ensure the long-term viability of Isiklar Ambalaj, which will be the biggest customer of Celhart. Environmental Category and Issues This is a category B project according to IFC''s environmental review procedure and the following environmental and occupational health and safety issues were reviewed: progress on environmental and health and safety measures in IFCs existing investment in the Celhart plant, air, water and solid waste emissions from other plants in the Group, implementation of a group-wide Environmental Management System, and fire safety and worker health and safety issues in all facilities Sack Manufacturing Plants: These will operate in compliance with World Bank Group requirements for air emissions, solid waste, wastewater, and occupational health and safety except for secondary fuel containment (absent at some facilities) and the sponsor will ensure that this is examined and corrected at all plants as required. The Izmir plant has recently received the international environmental certification - ISO 14001 and remaining plants are in the process of preparing for certification, and are training staff, identifying issues and preparing procedures. The company plans to implement ISO 14001 systems at all its facilities. Celhart Pulp and Paper Mill: The Celhart mill is located in Stamboliyski, Bulgaria. The plant is an existing IFC investment, received environmental review in 1998 and an Environmental Review Summary was prepared and disclosed at that time. An environmental action plan (EAP) was prepared to address compliance failings at that time and Celhart has made some progress in the interim in addressing these issues. However, since that time, the operation has experienced financial difficulties and the plant has been essentially shut down. As part of the appraisal for the current investment, the EAP has been reviewed and updated and the current investment will permit Celhart to resume the plant upgrading to achieve compliance with WBG requirements. Additionally Celhart has agreed to an independent fire and life safety audit, in order to assist in their planning process and to prioritize future actions in this area.
