location_description: The Fund will be formed as a Guernsey limited liability partnership. 7LCP formed as a Guernsey limited liability company and will have local teams in Athens,Greece, and in each of the target markets of the Region.

company_name: JS PRIVATE EQUITY FUND I LLC
project_description: An investment of up to $20 million in JS Private Equity I (or the Fund), which has a target size of $100 million. The fund management team will be led by Mr. Ali Siddiqui, with close supervision from Mr. Jahangir Siddiqui, a well-reputed asset manager with thirty years of asset management experience and well known to the IFC. Abamco Limited (Abamco), an asset management company, owned by the JS Group (or the Group) will invest in the Fund the equivalent of more than 20% of its total capitalization.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group is a well-diversified financial services group in Pakistan, and includes: - Jahangir Siddiqui & Co. (investments & fixed income trading); - JS Capital Markets (equity & fixed income sales and corporate finance); - JS Investment Bank (commercial lending); - Bank Islami (Islamic commercial bank); - Abamco (asset management); - JS Finance (Sharia-compliant asset management); - DCD-JS Factors (export credit protection & receivables factoring), - Network Microfinance Bank (microfinance & microleasing); - EFU Insurance Group (life, health & general insurance). The team will work to address potential conflict of interest issues and ensure that there are appropriate firewalls in the legal structure. The private equity team will consist of three partners: Ali Siddiqui, Stephen Smith and Mohammad Sajid (collectively, “the Team”). Ali Siddiqui, who will lead the Team, has seven years of private equity investment experience in Hong Kong (Crosby Capital Partners and Techpacific Capital) and Pakistan. Stephen Smith has 13 years of experience in project finance (European Capital) and private equity in Asia (Techpacific Capital). Mohammad Sajid has 13 years of experience in Pakistan in corporate finance, and has led legal negotiations of key transactions within JS Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC investment would consist of an equity investment of up to $20 million, for up to 20% of the Fund’s total capital commitments. IFC’s proposed investment amount has been chosen to fulfill IFC’s role of helping the Fund achieve a critical size and to reflect IFC’s anchor role. IFC will not be the largest investor in the Fund.
location_description: The Fund will be a Limited Liability Company domiciled in Mauritius.
Company Name: JS PRIVATE EQUITY FUND I LLC

project_description: Karsten Farms (Pty) Limited (Karsten or the company) is the parent company of the largest table grape exporter in South Africa. In addition to grapes, Karsten produces dates, apples, melons and citrus on a total of 1,527 hectares. The project entails providing a corporate loan to Karsten to support its on going investment program, which consists of replanting ageing vines and orchards, establishing berries and cherries production, establishing grape farming activities in Egypt; building a complementary logistics and marketing operation in the United Kingdom; and refinancing $1.7 million of medium term debt.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Mr. Petrus Karsten Sr., who established Karsten as a 13ha raisin farm 30 years ago. The Shareholding structure now comprises: Karsten Family Trust (51.4%); Industrial Development Corporation (36.6%); Yarona Farms Limited and Yarona Company Property Trust, two entities formed by the employees of Karsten (11.3%). The remaining shares are owned by Land Merit Trust, investment vehicle of South Africa’s state owned Land Bank and BAASA (a Black Empowerment Group).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $15 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $ 7.5 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project will be implemented in 3 geographical locations: South Africa: Karsten will expand farming operations located in the Northern Cape and Western Cape Provinces. Egypt: Karsten will enter into contracts to manage and provide packhouse and cold storage facilities in the Cairo Alexandria region. Karsten will also establish a Greenfield grape farm in Aswan. United Kingdom: Karsten will set up complementary marketing company close to London

company_name: Shanghai Aero Computer System Engineering Co., Ltd.
project_description: Shanghai Aerospace Computer System Engineering Co., Ltd (SAC or the company) is a private shareholding company, engaging in the development of a multi-media medical training system, an image processing and satellite transmission system, and distance learning platform. SAC provides a satellite platform for, and partners with, the medical universities & colleges in China and other public partners to provide long distance medical education and training to working medical staff to upgrade their medical education level and fulfill their continuing education requirements. The proposed project is an expansion of the SAC’s existing distance medical education and training services to working healthcare professionals throughout China. The project includes expansion of SAC’s satellite network, helping local partners (medical schools and hospitals) set up additional distance learning centers and continuing medical education only learning centers, setting up additional data technical support centers, and design and production of educational programs and software.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Kang Hong, the founder of SAC, is the largest shareholder and Chairman & CEO of the company. Mr. Kang is both a senior IT expert and an experienced medicine & medical education practitioner. In the 1990s Mr. Kang was part of a group of professionals that assisted the government in setting new standards for clinical medicine education programs for China’s Ministry of Education. In 2004 Mr. Kang was one of China’s invited speakers at the US-China Education Forum which is an annual event that is usually well attended by leading US and other western medical schools, universities and medical research and software groups.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $13 million. IFC’s investment in this project will be a combination of equity and an A loan for IFC’s own account with a total amount of an estimated $4.6 million.
location_description: The location of the project is in HongQiao Road, Shanghai, China.
Company Name: Shanghai Aero Computer System Engineering Co., Ltd.

project_description: Suzano Petroquimica S.A. (Suzano or the company) is one of the largest petrochemical companies in Brazil that, through its controlled company Polibrasil Resinas S.A. (Polibrasil), and its joint controlled companies, Politeno Industria e Comercio S.A. (Politeno) and Petroflex Industria e Comercio S.A. (Petroflex), produces, markets and distributes petrochemical products. The company was incorporated in 2001 as a result of a corporate reorganization that culminated in a spin-off of all petrochemical assets then held by Companhia Suzano de Papel e Celulose (a former IFC client). These companies produce three main products: polypropylene (PP), in the case of Polibrasil, polyethylene (PE), and synthetic elastomers, which are sold in both the domestic and the international markets. The company also has a controlling block of a new company, Rio Polimeros S.A. (Rio Polimeros), which is building the first petrochemical complex in Brazil that will use natural gas fractions as raw material and has integrated ethylene and polyethylene production units. The project under consideration includes the buyout of Basell''s 50% stake in Polibrasil with the aim to hold 100% ownership of the company, the announced corporate restructuring, the debottlenecking of Polibrasil’s operations and debt refinancing. The acquisition was announced on June 20, 2005 and was completed on September 1st 2005. By taking full control of Polibrasil, Suzano will become an operating company, positioned as one of Latin America’s largest thermoplastic resins producers and the largest PP producer. This acquisition enables Suzano to become a major integrated petrochemicals player, instead of an investor and holding company, positioning itself as a consolidating agent in the Brazilian petrochemical sector in the Southeast region. Suzano will also implement a corporate restructuring aimed at simplifying its group structure and turn itself into an operational company as disclosed to the market on its press release of September 1st, 2005.
sponsor_shareholders: The company is a publicly held corporation. The Feffer family holds, directly and indirectly, all the outstanding common shares and approximately 9,32% of the preferred shares through Suzano Holding S.A., some other parties related to the Feffer family hold approximately 45,62% of the preferred shares, and the remaining 45,07% is free float. Leon Feffer founded Suzano group in 1924. The Feffer family are long-time entrepreneurs in the pulp and paper market, and they initiated activities in the petrochemical sector in 1974. The members of the Feffer family who are currently on the Board of Directors are: David Feffer (48), President of the Board, his brother Daniel Feffer (45), Vice-President of the Board, and Jorge Feffer (44 - another brother), member of the Board. The three brothers are sons of Max Feffer, who was the son of Leon Feffer.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is approximately $452 million. The proposed IFC Investment is a corporate loan of $60 million for its own account and $140 million as a B loan.
location_description: The industrial complex of Polibrasil is formed by three facilities producing polypropylene resins with a combined annual production capacity of 625.0 thousand tons, located in the municipalities of Duque de Caxias, State of Rio de Janeiro, Mauá, State of São Paulo, and Camaçari, State of Bahia. Inaugurated in 1992, the Duque de Caxias facility has a production capacity of 200.0 thousand tons per year, and produces homopolymers and random copolymers using Lipp technology. The new polypropylene industrial facility located in Mauá has world-size production scale of 300.0 thousand tons per year, using the latest generation Spheripol technology licensed by Basell Polyolefins and is located in Brazil''s main consumer market. The Camaçari industrial facility in Bahia was inaugurated in 1978. This facility has an installed capacity of 125.0 thousand tons per year, and produces homopolymers and heterophasic copolymers.

project_description: The proposed project consists of the construction and operation of a grain river port terminal at Timbues (Timbues Port), located about 340 km from Buenos Aires on the lower Parana River in Santa Fe province. The project will be constructed and operated by Noble Argentina S.A. (Noble Argentina or the company). Established in 2001, Noble Argentina is a commodity trader that offers a range of highly diversified agricultural commodity products, as well as logistics and technical services. The project includes: - the acquisition of 201 hectares of land with 1,800 m of waterfront; - the construction of a truck parking area and facilities for sampling, conditioning and storage; and - the purchase of equipment. Timbues Port will have a storage capacity of 120,000 tons and will be able to accommodate a throughput of about 2.5 million tons of grain per year, consisting mainly of exports of wheat, corn and soybeans. Construction began at the end of February 2005 and the project is expected to be completed by July 2006.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is the Noble Group. Founded in 1987 and headquartered in Hong Kong, the Noble Group is a major commodity trading group. Noble Argentina is 99% owned by Stelmont Group Limited, which is wholly-owned by Noble Group Limited, the holding company of the Noble Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $51.2 million. The proposed IFC investment comprises an A Loan of $18 million, for IFC’s own account, and a syndicated B Loan of $18 million, for the account of participant banks.
location_description: The Timbues Port project will be a new grain river port located on the lower Parana River in Santa Fe province, about 35 km north of Rosario or 340 km from Buenos Aires.

project_description: Arcor S.A.I.C. (Arcor or the company) is one of the leading producers and distributors of candies, chocolates and cookies in South America. The project entails providing a corporate loan to Arcor to lengthen the maturities of its debt and to finance its capital expenditures program.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Arcor, a private locally-owned company founded in 1951. Arcor is owned by Inaral S.A., a local company owned by several local families. Arcor has grown from a local operation in the province of Córdoba into a multinational company, commercializing a well-diversified portfolio of consumer goods. Arcor and its subsidiaries are vertically integrated with industrial operations in the dairy, maize, sugar, and packaging industries, among others.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project is estimated to be at least $200 million; depending on syndication outcome. The proposed investment includes an A Loan of up to $70 million, for IFC’s own account, and a B Loan to be syndicated.
location_description: Arcor operates over 25 state-of-the-art facilities throughout Argentina producing candies, chocolates, cookies, cardboard, packaging material, sugar, flour, corn syrups, and canned foods, among other.

project_description: The project company is the Closed Stock Company Chukotka Mining and Geological Company (CMGC). Exploration and production licenses have been issued to CMGC to develop the greenfield Kupol deposit. Kupol is expected to produce 552,000 ounces of gold per annum and 5.8 million ounces of silver per annum for at least 6.5 years. The Kupol property has inferred resources estimated at approximately 4 million tons that can extend the life for up to an additional 6 years. Mining will be a combination of open pit and underground, with the underground providing a majority of the ore from the fifth year of operation onward. The mine is expected to produce an average of approximately 550,000 ounces of gold per year at an operating cash cost of $47 per ounce and a total cash cost of $88 per ounce for a minimum of 6.5 years.* * (using silver as an operating credit)
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Bema Gold Corporation (Bema), a Canadian gold exploration and mining company incorporated in 1998, with producing mines in Russia and South Africa and developing projects in Chile and Russia. Bema operates the IFC financed Julietta gold mine in Russia and is experienced in cold weather logistics. Bema also has the Petrex mine in South Africa, is a 50% owner of the Refugio Mine in Chile,and a 24% owner of Cerro Casale one of the world’s largest undeveloped gold and copper projects in Chile. Kupol with its low cost operating costs and rich deposit will be Bema’s flagship mine. Bema (through its fully owned subsidiary, Kupol Ventures Limited (a Cyprus registered company) can acquire up to 75% ownership of CMGC, with the remaining 25% to be held by the Chukotka government. Bema is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $460 million. IFC is proposing an investment of $35 million, comprising an A loan of $10 million and a C loan of $25 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Kupol is located in the Northwest part of the Anadyr foothills on the boundary between the Anadyr and Bilibino Regions in Chukotka, an autonomous Okrug (region) in northeast Russia. It is 200 kilometers east of the city of Bilibino. The remote area is presently accessible only by helicopter during the summer months and over a winter road from December until the middle of April. Kupol’s remoteness requires it to be self-sufficient, and a mining camp, power generation, and ancillary facilities will be built in addition to the mine. An airstrip is being constructed to allow year-round access by fixed-wing aircraft.

project_description: The proposed IFC financing will be used to support the corporate investment and debt restructuring program of International Shopping Center Holdings (ISCH or the company) including the construction of a new shopping mall and the expansion of an existing shopping mall in Honduras and the debt restructuring at the company’s subsidiary in Nicaragua. ISCH covers the Poma Group’s shopping mall development and operations business.
sponsor_shareholders: The Poma Group, based in El Salvador and majority owned by the Poma family, has business interests in automobile distribution, manufacturing, real estate including hotels and shopping malls.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The corporate investment program is estimated of up to $150 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of a senior loan in the amount of up to $35 million to the selected subsidiaries of the company.
location_description: The project will be located in Nicaragua and Honduras.

company_name: IAC INTERNATIONAL AUTOMOTIVE INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED
project_description: The project is the expansion of International Auto Limited (IAL or the company). IAL is one of the largest independent automotive component manufacturers in India, supplying truck, tractor and construction equipment manufacturers. The project will expand IAL’s production capacity and enable the company to meet growing domestic and export demand.
sponsor_shareholders: IAL is a family owned company established in 1975 by Mr. R. K. Behera, a first generation Indian entrepreneur. IAL consists of two main companies: International Auto limited and RSB Transmissions Limited. The Behera family own 75.3% of International Auto, Actis owns 12.5% and Ceat 12.2%. The Behera family own 89.5% of RSB Transmissions and the Industrial Development Bank of India 10.5%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $23.5 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to $10 million Rupee equivalent in convertible preference shares.
location_description: The company is headquartered in Pune and operates six plants in Jamshedpur, Pune and Dhawar. A seventh plant is under construction in Chennai. The expansion will be take place at Jamshedpur and Pune, and at the new facility in Chennai.
Company Name: IAC INTERNATIONAL AUTOMOTIVE INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED

project_description: The project consists of the acquisition and refurbishment of five hotels and lodges in Kenya that previously comprised Lonrho Hotels Kenya B.V. These are the following: - Norfolk Hotel, Nairobi (167 rooms) - Mount Kenya Safari Club (114 rooms) - Mara Safari Club (50 room tents) - Ark Safari Lodge, Aberdare (60 rooms) - Aberdare Country Club (48 rooms) Acquisition has been recently finalized for $33.4 million and refurbishment cost is estimated at $29.6 million, for a total project cost of $63.0 million. Kenya is rich in tourism assets and after suffering in the last few years mainly due to security concerns, signs of recovery are apparent. In addition to capitalizing on the upswing in demand in Kenya, the sponsors believe the project will create significant value by: - enhancing performance through stronger management; - positioning the hotels to effectively compete at the top end of the market; - leveraging off KHI and Fairmont’s international exposure; and - benefiting from KHI’s economies of scale in the Africa region.
sponsor_shareholders: The project is sponsored by Kingdom Hotel Investment Group (“KHI”), Fairmont Hotels, Inc. (“Fairmont”), and International Financial Advisors Hotels and Resorts (“IFA Hotels and Resorts”) (together, known as the “Sponsors”). KHI, chaired by Prince Alwaleed bin Talal of Saudi Arabia, is a private equity group engaged in the hospitality and leisure business mostly in the Middle East and Africa. Fairmont is one of North America's leading operator of luxury hotels and resorts with a distinctive collection. IFA Hotels and Resorts is a Kuwaiti-based tourism and real estate development company active in the Middle East, Europe and Africa. The project’s five hotel properties were acquired by a joint venture formed by KHI, IFA and Fairmont. The following summarizes the shareholders of the joint venture and their corresponding equity interest. KHI - 55% IFA Hotels and Resorts - 30% Fairmont - 15%
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $63.0 million. It includes a purchase price for the hotel properties of approximately $33 million and a refurbishment of the hotels at a cost of $25.6 million. Working capital needs and interest during construction have also been included as part of the project cost. The proposed financial plan includes equity of $33.4 million and cash generation of $4.6 million. Debt financing includes an IFC A Loan of $15 million, an IFC C Loan of US$5 million and a Fairmont loan of $5 million.
location_description: The following is a summary description of each hotel property: - The Norfolk (167 rooms) The Norfolk Hotel has been one of Nairobi's most storied gathering places since it opened in 1904 hosting notables like American President Theodore Roosevelt, Lord Baden-Powell and Baroness Karen Von Blixen-Finecke, better known as Out of Africa author Isak Dinesen. Today, this 167-room hotel 30-minutes from Jomo Kenyatta International Airport continues to provide a sophisticated respite from the bustling nearby business district and an ideal safari departure point, complete with four impressive dining venues, an outdoor heated swimming pool, a full-scale health club, a ballroom and four function rooms. Mount Kenya Safari Club (114 rooms) Located 190 kilometers (118 miles) north of Nairobi, the 115-room Mount Kenya Safari Club showcases magnificent views of neighboring Mount Kenya and a long-held reputation for secluded elegance including a variety of cottages, suites and villas. Spread over 100 acres of landscaped grounds, the property features a nine-hole golf course, heated swimming pool, horseback riding, bird walks, organized trips to game reserves, fishing as well as access to an animal orphanage. Seven restaurant and bar offerings range from casual poolside cocktails to formal dinners accompanied by music and traditional Chukka dancers. Originally the retreat of movie star and Club founder, William Holden, illustrious members have included Winston Churchill, Bing Crosby and John Wayne.. Mara Safari Club (50 room tents) The Mara Safari Club is located at the foot of the Aitong Hills, northwest of the Masai Mara Game Reserve, Kenya's most popular game reserve, on the Ol Choro Oirowua Group Ranch. This expansive lodge with dining room, lounge and pool bar is surrounded by lush gardens clustered around indigenous trees. The 50 tented accommodations include deluxe beds, en suite baths and other features of a top hotel. Guests can choose from a wide range of activities, including game drives, walking safaris, bird walks, fishing and balloon safaris over the Mara plains. A naturalist, traditional dancing and talks on Masai culture enrich this luxurious adventure. The Aberdare Country Club (48 rooms) Described as "Scotland with lions," the unique 1,300-acre setting of the Aberdare Country Club encompasses moorland, thick forests and clear mountain streams. An easy three-hour transfer from Nairobi, this 1930s country hotel was originally built on the slope of Mweiga Hill as the private farm and residence of wealthy English landowners. The hotel's 48 accommodations are in luxurious cottages with spectacular views of the Aberdare Mountains to the west, Mount Kenya to the east and the plains below. Beyond a main lodge dining room with two lounges and a well-equipped conference center, the Club offers a nine-hole golf course, swimming pool, two tennis courts, riding stables, trout fishing and a wildlife sanctuary that abounds with zebra, giraffe, gazelles and even the elusive leopard. The Ark (60 rooms) Built in 1969 to complement the Aberdare Club, The Ark is a tree-lodge set in the heart of Aberdare National Park and uniquely shaped to resemble Noah's Ark. True to its ship-like structure, it overlooks the floodlit Yasabara waterhole and contains 60 "cabins," accommodations with en suite bathrooms. In addition to a main dining room, lounge and bar, this one-of-a- kind safari lodge also features three decks of balconies and a lounge with 24-hour tea and coffee service, providing ideal vantage points for viewing game. A ground-level "bunker" takes you close to the animals for photography and cabins are fitted with buzzers to announce the arrival of the one of the "Big 5" at the forest waterhole.

company_name: ASSAN DEMIR VE SAC SANAYI ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Assan Demir ve Sac Sanayii A.S. (Assan or the company), established in 1977 and part of the family-owned Kibar Group, is the largest aluminum sheet, coil, and foil manufacturer in Turkey, and also ranks amongst the top Turkish steel galvanizing companies. The project comprises of: - restructuring of the company’s balance sheet; and - implementing a debottlenecking and modernization program, primarily at its aluminum plant. As part of the project the sponsors have also committed to improve the corporate governance of Assan. The project will significantly improve Assan’s balance sheet, enable it to focus on its operations, and consolidate and further grow on its market position.
sponsor_shareholders: The Sponsors are (i) Kibar Holding A.S.; (ii) Mr. Asim Kibar; (iii) Mr. Ali Kibar; and (iv) Mr. Ahmet Kibar. Kibar Holding A.S., founded in 1984, is the holding company of the family-owned Kibar Group. Assan, the principal company of the Kibar Group, is fully owned by the Kibar family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $125 million, of which IFC has been requested to arrange up to $60 million, including a syndicated participant bank loan of $30 million.
location_description: Assan owns an aluminum processing plant, located in Tuzla, Istanbul, and a steel galvanizing factory, located in Kartal, Istanbul. The modernization and de-bottlenecking investments envisaged in the project will be done predominantly at the aluminum plant in Tuzla, approximately 30 kilometers southeast of Istanbul.
Company Name: ASSAN DEMIR VE SAC SANAYI ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: Ethos Private Equity Fund V (Ethos V or the Fund) is a private equity fund which will make equity and equity-related investments primarily for control positions in market-leading growth businesses located in South Africa as well as in other African countries. The Fund has a target committed equity capital of up to $500 million. The Fund will be the fifth fund raised and managed by Ethos Private Equity Limited (“Ethos”) which is based in Johannesburg and has a core group of 16 professionals that have worked together since 1985. IFC intends to invest up to $25 million in Ethos V and will also consider an investment of up to $5 million in Sphere Private Equity Fund I (Sphere I) which is a related fund set up as a joint venture with Ethos V to share deals and the expertise of senior Ethos partners. Sphere I is a Rand-denominated private equity fund with target capital commitments of Rand 600 million (~$100 million) which will be managed by Sphere Holdings (Sphere). Ethos V and Sphere I are fundraising simultaneously for capital commitments in the ratio of 5:1 respectively.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor of Ethos V is Ethos Private Equity Limited (the Fund Manager or Ethos) based in Johannesburg, South Africa. The Fund Manager has been operating since 1984 and has managed four previous funds with aggregate capital commitments of Rand 2.48 billion ($487 million) which was invested in 85 investments. Sphere I will be managed by Sphere Private Equity (the “Sphere Team”), composed of a group of four young black professionals with investment banking and private equity experience who have a 24% shareholding in Ethos (under a Black Economic Empowerment shareholding restructuring). The Sphere Team has previously concluded one investment.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Ethos V has a target equity commitment of $500 million and may include an additional debt feature of $150 million in guaranteed debt from the Overseas Private Investment Corporation (OPIC). Sphere I has target capital commitments of Rand 600 million (about $100 million). IFC expects to invest up to $25 million in Ethos V, and up to $5 million in Sphere.
location_description: Both funds will operate principally in South Africa, Ethos V may invest up to 25% of capital commitments in investments that expand in other African countries.

company_name: EMERGING EUROPE CONVERGENCE FUND II, L.P.
project_description: The Emerging Europe Convergence Fund II, L.P. (EECF II, or the Fund), is a 10-year closed-end regional private equity fund formed by Mid Europa Partners LLP (MEP), with the objective to achieve superior returns through a portfolio of investments primarily in mature, cash-flow generative companies in sectors with high barriers to entry based in the markets of the new European Union members and the EU accession candidate countries (Emerging Europe, or the Region). The Fund is targeting total capital commitments of €500 million, and expects to have a first closing in late June/early July, 2005.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed through a limited liability partnership, Mid Europa Partners LLP (“MEP”), which is controlled by its three Partners: Thierry Baudon, Craig Butcher and Colin Hewett. MEP is a successor to EMP Europe Ltd, which was formed in 1999 by EMP Global (an independent private equity fund advisor, responsible for the investment of six private equity funds totalling US $5.7 billion in commitments in Africa, Asia, Latin America, Europe and the Middle East) for the purpose of advising the AIG Emerging Europe Infrastructure Fund (“EEIF”), a $550 million private equity fund focused on infrastructure projects in Central and Eastern Europe, in which IFC is an investor. Although MEP will now be operating independently of EMP Global, the two organizations will retain a close relationship. Under the management of Thierry Baudon, EMP Europe was built to its current size of 11 investment professionals and successfully operates out of three offices in Budapest, London and Warsaw. The majority of the core team has been working together since EEIF’s inception in 1999. This team of professionals’ shares over 50 years of combined private equity investment experience, 100 years of transaction experience, and 80 years of experience in the region including managerial and industrial expertise in relevant sectors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total size of the EECF fund is expected to be €500 million. IFC would be investing up to €20 million in the Fund.
location_description: The region in which EECF II is planning to invest includes both countries that recently joined the EU (Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia) and accession candidate countries (Bulgaria, Croatia, Romania). Also EECF is contemplating investing up to 20% of its capital in other countries (such as Russia and Ukraine).
Company Name: EMERGING EUROPE CONVERGENCE FUND II, L.P.

project_description: A proposed IFC investment of $20 million in Carlyle Mexico Partners, L.P. (“Carlyle Mexico”) a private equity fund with target commitments of $250 million. The Fund is sponsored by The Carlyle Group (“Carlyle”) to invest in buyout or other private equity opportunities in Mexico and in U.S. companies that have a significant Hispanic customer base or cross-border initiatives. The Fund will target medium and large companies. The Fund expects to make 5-8 investments of between $20-50 million, acquiring controlling or significant minority stakes.
sponsor_shareholders: Carlyle is a global private equity firm based in Washington, DC and with offices in 14 countries. Carlyle manages a total of $23 billion in commitments in 24 funds in the United States, Western Europe, and Asia. Carlyle Mexico General Partner, L.P., an Ontario limited partnership will be the General Partner and Fund Manager.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The target size of the Fund will be $250 million and IFC’s proposed investment is $20 million in equity up to a maximum of 19% of the total Fund size.
location_description: The Fund will be established as a limited partnership domiciled in a suitable jurisdiction and will invest in companies located principally in Mexico. The Fund Manager will manage the investments from its offices in Mexico City, and in Washington, DC.

project_description: VeriSilicon is an IC (integrated circuit) design foundry providing semiconductor chip design services and intellectual property (IP) products to fabless IC companies and Original Equipment Manufacturers worldwide, primarily in Greater China and the US. The company was founded in 2001 to serve as a bridge between China-based wafer foundries and global IC system design houses. The purpose of the project is to provide the company capital: - for research and development of new IP products, - expansion of sales and marketing efforts; and - to support the expansion of the company’s turn-key business.
sponsor_shareholders: The project company was founded by current Chairman and CEO Wayne W.-M. Dai in 2001. The company’s shareholders include many well-known Asian venture capital funds, namely WI-Harper, IDG Technology Ventures and iGlobe Partners. Please see summary shareholding percentages below: WI-Harper 20.87% IDG Tech Ventures 16.92% iGlobe Partners 16.92% Wayne W.-M. Dai 12.60% Other Employees 19.18% Other Investors 13.51% TOTAL 100.00%
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $12.0 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $1.0 million preferred equity investment.
location_description: VeriSilicion has it’s primary offices in Shanghai, with satellite sales offices in Taipei and Santa Clara, California. VeriSilicon’s offices in Shanghai are located in the Zhanghjiang Hi-Tech Park in Pudong.

company_name: MODERN KARTON SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
sector: Paper Packaging Products (Including Boxes, Cartons, etc.)
project_description: Modern Karton Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (Modern Karton), the main operating company of the Eren Group’s paper and packaging business, was established in 1974. It manufactures test liner and fluting paper using wastepaper at its factory located in Corlu, located 100 km west of Istanbul. With a 300,000 metric tons per annum capacity, Modern Karton is Turkey’s largest plant in the corrugated cardboard sector. The project consists of a $365 million expansion program of Eren Holding’s paper and packaging businesses in Corlu. The project includes: - a capacity increase of 300,000 metric tons per annum to the paper mill (i.e. installation of a new paper making machine); - an investment in their packaging and paper recycling businesses; and - an expansion of the associated cogeneration plant (for steam and power) and wastewater treatment plant.
sponsor_shareholders: The Eren Group is a diversified industrial group with operations in the paper, energy, cement, textiles and retail sectors. It is owned by the Eren family through Eren Holding, which owns and manages portfolio investments in various Eren Group companies. Eren Holding’s consolidated revenues during 2004 were $470 million on total assets $543 million. Modern Karton, the flagship company of the Group, is currently the leader in the Turkish corrugated paper industry. Eren Holding has controlling shareholding of Modern Karton (93%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $365 million. The IFC investment will consist of an A Loan of up to $40 million for its own account and a B Loan of up to $20 million.
location_description: The project will be located in Corlu,Turkey on a 10 hectare-site adjacent to the existing manufacturing facilities.
Company Name: MODERN KARTON SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: Wadi Holdings Company (SAE) (Wadi or the company) and its ten subsidiaries comprise a group of Egyptian companies which, at present, has two core business activities. The first of these consists of poultry and, in particular, the production of broiler day old parents, commercial broilers, layer chicks, hatching eggs and poultry feed. The second core activity is the planting, cultivating, harvesting and processing of olives and other vegetables and fruits. Having started operations in 1984, Wadi is now implementing a four-year expansion and diversification investment program, which will lead Wadi from a mid-tier company to one of Egypt’s and the region’s premier agribusiness groups. The investment program in implementation includes: - a modern 60 MT per hour feed mill (completed in October 2004), - a grandparent hatchery and breeder sites, - olive groves, vegetable farms and processing facilities, - contract farming with independent out-growers to raise broiler chickens, and - a joint-venture with local and foreign partners to manufacture glass containers to be used by Wadi and other glass packaging companies in Egypt and abroad.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are owner-operators who have been involved in the Middle Eastern poultry industry for over 46 years and in the Egyptian poultry industry for the past 20 years. The main project sponsors are: Messrs. Musa S. Freiji, Tony S. Freiji, Ramzi P. Nasrallah and Khalil P. Nasrallah. The investment program includes the establishment of a new glass packaging company, Wadi Glass Container (SAE), which is a joint-venture and whose shareholders are Wadi (70%), Hwa Hsia Glass Company of Taiwan, China (12%), Mr. J.J. Jow, chairman of Jochlenlee Molds & Machine Manufacturing, Inc. of Singapore (3%), and Mr. Samih Sawiris of Cairo (15%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated total project cost is $46.6 million, including working capital. The proposed IFC investment is a $15 million Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Wadi’s headquarters are located at 10 Mahager & Managem Street, Mohandessin, Cairo, Egypt. Wadi’s operating subsidiaries are located along the Cairo-Alexandria Desert Road. Those companies which are expected to use IFC’s financing are as follows: Rula Company for Land Reclamation: Location 1: KM 49 from Cairo Cairo-Alexandria Desert Road Giza, Egypt Location 2: KM 54 from Cairo Cairo-Alexandria Desert Road Giza, Egypt Location 3: KM 84 from Alexandria Cairo-Alexandria Desert Road West Noubariya Beheira, Egypt Wadi Farms: KM 49 from Cairo Cairo-Alexandria Desert Road Giza, Egypt Wadi Poultry Parents: Hatchery: Lot Number 190 Industrial Zone No. 5 Sadat City Menoufiya, Egypt Farms: KM 49 from Cairo Cairo-Alexandria Desert Road Giza, Egypt Wadi Food Industries: Location 1: KM 54 from Cairo Cairo-Alexandria Desert Road Giza, Egypt Location 2: Lot Number 7, 8/2 Industrial Zone No. 3 Sadat City Menoufiya, Egypt
additionality: IFC’s investment will support the further development of a successful private sector company in Egypt’s poultry and food sector. Drawing on its operational, technical and managerial capabilities, Wadi is expanding and diversifying its poultry and food activities and entering the complementary container glass industry. It will develop a broiler chicken production system based on contracts with outgrowers, which will be one of the first in Egypt for poultry. The investment program will create about 1,000 jobs in Egypt over the next four year period. The new glass company will employ modern glass technology provided by Hwa Hsia. Mobilizing its global agribusiness and industrial experience, IFC specialists and consultants will provide financial, technical, environmental and best management practices resources to Wadi. IFC’s loan will help Wadi achieve a more balanced debt structure. Its loan will include a long grace period to help the new agribusiness investments to become well established prior to the beginning of principal repayment. IFC will support agribusiness and food processing which are critical sectors in Egypt. These sectors benefit from Egypt’s comparative agricultural advantages, a growing economy, and proximity to export markets. IFC will provide financing and technical services which will facilitate Wadi’s transition to an international enterprise.

project_description: Vicentin is one of Argentina’s leading oilseed processors and exporters. IFC will provide financing for Vicentin to expand port storage capacity at San Lorenzo (Santa Fe province); upgrade management information systems; establish new origination and commercial offices; and extend the maturities of some debt.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Vicentin, a private local company founded in 1929. The company’s core business is oilseed crushing and exporting of its byproducts, oil and meals. Vicentin’s operations also include cotton ginning and spinning; formulation of pesticides and herbicides; and meat processing through its subsidiary Friar S.A. (“Friar”).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $120 million. The proposed investment includes an A Loan of up to $20 million and a C Loan of up $15 million, for IFC’s own account, and a B Loan of up to $50 million.
location_description: The company has the following facilities: - oilseed crushing plants and port in San Lorenzo (Santa Fe); - edible oils refinery in Avellaneda (Santa Fe); - cotton ginning plants in Avellaneda, Bandera (Santiago del Estero), El Colorado (Formosa), Gral. Pinedo (Chaco) and Villa Angela (Chaco); - herbicides and pesticides formulation plant in Reconquista (Santa Fe); and - spinning plant in Reconquista (Vicentin has also a 50% interest in a spinning facility in Brazil). Friar has facilities in Reconquista, Santa Fe City, Desvío Arijón (Santa Fe) and Carcaraña (Santa Fe).

company_name: Beijing DQY Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd.
project_description: Beijing Deqingyuan Agriculture Technology Co. Ltd (Deqingyuan or the company) is a company based in Beijing, China, that produces high quality eggs. It currently houses 500,000 layers and produces and sells 200,000 eggs per day. Its eggs received the “no harmful ingredients” certificate, the “organic food product” certificate, and the “safe agricultural food product” certificate from the government. It is the only egg product that was granted as a “national priority new product” by the Ministry of Technology, Ministry of Commerce, Ministry of Quality Inspection, and Ministry of Environment Protection. The quality of the Deqingyuan eggs is well recognized by the market. The eggs sell at a price that is substantially higher than that of the non-brand, regular eggs and the sales grow rapidly. Deqingyuan’s strategy is to quickly increase its production capacity and market share. It plans to expand the capacity of the layer sheds to house an additional 800,000 birds, which will add production capacity by 500,000 eggs per day.
sponsor_shareholders: The shareholders of the company (collectively, the Sponsors) and their shareholding percentages are: Beijing Deqingyuan Technology, 51.76%, Tianjin Baodi Agricultural Technology, 10.50%, Shanghai Yibei Management Consulting, 7.63%, and six individuals, together 30.11%. Mr. Zhong Kaimin is the major shareholder and one of the key founders of the company. Mr. Zhong holds an engineering master degree and an MBA. Between 1984 and 2001, Mr. Zhong worked for the government in Beijing. He became aware of the health, safety and environmental issues of the egg industry and saw the potential for producing high quality eggs. Mr. Zhong left the government in 2002 and devoted himself to building the company into a leading high quality egg producer in China.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is $12.6 million. The proposed IFC investment is an equity of $2.76 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project will be developed on a 32 ha site that is adjacent to the company’s existing operation and lies 100 km west of Beijing. The site comprises barren land that is owned by local government and the company (1.5 ha is owned by the company the remainder will be leased by the company on a long term basis from local government). The site is served by municipal electricity and water supply and has access to local transport infrastructure. Development of the site has not required any resettlement.
Company Name: Beijing DQY Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd.

company_name: FINANCIERA EDUCATIVA DE MEXICO, S.A. DE C.V.
project_description: The project is to support the establishment of Financiera Educativa de Mexico S.A. de C.V. (“FINEM” or “the company”), a new specialized non-bank financial institution that will be established as a “sociedad financiera de objeto limitado” (SOFOL) and focus on financing the Mexican education sector. FINEM’s core business will be to provide peso denominated term loans to eligible Mexican privately-owned schools and higher education institutions, to help fund their expansion and infrastructure modernization programs. In addition, FINEM will provide advisory services or technical assistance in a wide range of managerial or technical disciplines, to help qualifying clients reinforce the quality of their management and become more viable and competitive firms. FINEM will initially target upper-secondary and higher education institutions and gradually extend its services across all segments of the education market. The project aims to address the currently large gap between demand and supply of long-term financing for private education institutions in Mexico, and to contribute to improving the quality of infrastructure, education and management in the private education sector through investments and technical assistance.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Consorcio Pro-Desarollo S.A. de C.V.., a private Mexican company that has established business interests in the real estate, construction, agribusiness, biotechnology and security areas. Consorcio Pro-Desarollo S.A. de C.V..will also be FINEM’s majority shareholder, owing 81% of its share capital. The remaining 19% will be held by IFC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project corresponds to the initial phase of establishment of FINEM, and covers the first two years of operation, by the end of which the company’s portfolio is expected to reach $20 million equivalent. During this period, the company intends to finance high schools and universities that will primarily be located in the Mexico City metropolitan area. The second phase, which is beyond the scope of the project, will scale up the Company’s portfolio and expand its activities into other cities of Mexico. The proposed IFC investment consists of: - an equity investment for up to $680,000, which would represent approximately 19% of the company’s aggregate share capital, and - a Mexican peso denominated loan facility of up to the equivalent of $15 million. The IFC loan will finance the first two years of operations of the company.
location_description: FINEM is headquartered in Mexico City and does not plan to operate branches or local representation offices outside Mexico City at this stage.
Company Name: FINANCIERA EDUCATIVA DE MEXICO, S.A. DE C.V.

project_description: The project entails a loan facility of up to $200 million (the “Facility”) to support Raiffeisen International Bank-Holding AG (Raiffeisen International or “RI”), a holding company whose primary shareholder is Raiffeisen Zentralbank Österreich AG (“RZB”). Raiffeisen International currently holds controlling stakes in 15 banks and several other finance companies in Central, Eastern and South Eastern Europe, namely in Albania, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Poland, Romania, Russia, Serbia and Montenegro, Slovakia, Slovenia and Ukraine. RI’s assets amount to EUR 28.9 billion as of December 31, 2004, with aggregated shareholders equity of EUR 1.84 billion, which due to an initial public offering of its shares in April 2005 increased to EUR 2.39 billion.
sponsor_shareholders: The major shareholder of RI is RZB with 70% of RI’s shareholding. In April 2005, 24% of RI shares were floated on the stock exchange by selling old shares and issuing new shares. The remaining 6% of its shares are held by IFC and the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development. RZB acts as the central bank to Austria’s Raiffeisen Banking Group as well as a commercial bank and in some countries as an investment bank. With assets of EUR 67.9 billion it is currently Austria’s 3rd largest banking group. In 1987 RZB started to diversify its activities outside of Austria by creating a subsidiary in Hungary (founding Unicbank together with IFC, now called Raiffeisen Bank Rt.). Since then it has grown one of the most complete and locally focused banking networks in the Central, Eastern and South Eastern European region. RZB continues to play an important role in the economic development of the region, and in particular in the less developed markets, such as Albania, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Romania, Russia, Serbia and Montenegro (including Kosovo) and Ukraine.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project consists of a debt investment totaling up to $200 million to support Raiffeisen International and its subsidiaries.
location_description: Raiffeisen International is a Vienna based Austrian joint stock company, which holds controlling interests in a number of finance subsidiaries and banks in the countries listed above.

project_description: Ramenka (or the company), a Russian limited liability company, was founded in 1997. Operating under the name Ramstore, Ramenka conducts two major types of business operations: - retail sales of food and non-food products and - lease of retail space in the company-owned hypermarket stores to other businesses. Ramenka started its business in Moscow with one hypermarket, which opened in 1997. Now, the company operates a total of 6 hypermarkets and 32 supermarkets with a net retail area of 92,000 sqm and a net leasable area of 61,000 sqm. To respond to the booming market demand for quality retail outlets and rental space in Russia, Ramenka is planning to build two additional supermarkets with attached shopping malls located in the Moscow Region (Orekhovo-Zuyevo and Reutov) and three additional hypermarkets with attached malls in Moscow, St.Petersburg and Togliatti. The total retail area and rental area of the project stores will be 19,435 sqm and 55,700 sqm, respectively.
sponsor_shareholders: Ramenka is 50% owned by Migros Turk Ticaret Anonim Sirketi (Migros), the largest and the oldest supermarket chain in Turkey with international operations in Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Kazakhstan and Russia. 48.94% of Migros’ shares are traded at the Istanbul Stock Exchange. The remaining shares are controlled by the Koc Group, one of Turkey’s leading industrial conglomerates. The remaining 50% of the company are owned by Enka Insaat ve Sanayi Anonim Sirketi (Enka) through its European subsidiaries: - Enka Holding Investment S.A. (38.3%); and - EnTrade GmbH (11.7%). Enka is a Turkey-based international conglomerate active in construction, power, management of real estate properties and retail. Enka is active in Algeria, Azerbaijan, Croatia, Germany, Kazakhstan, Lybia, the Netherlands, Russia and Turkey. 13.1% of Enka’s shares are traded at the Istanbul stock exchange. The remaining shares are held privately.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated project cost is $119 million. IFC is considering an A loan of $40 million to the company. The financial plan also includes subordinated loans and cash generation.
location_description: The project consists of 2 supermarket/malls located in Moscow oblasts and 3 hypermarket/malls in Moscow, St. Petersburg and Togliatti. Udelny Park in St. Petersburg is going to be located on a 2.0 ha land plot. Orehokhovo-Zuyevo in Moscow oblast is located on the eastern side of the city of Moscow with a land plot of 2.0 ha. Reutov in Moscow oblast is also located on the eastern side of the city of Moscow with a land plot of 1.5 ha. Butova is located in the southern part of Moscow with a land plot of 2.9 ha. Togliatti located in Samara oblast, Southern Russia has the biggest land plot in the project with 5.2 ha.

company_name: KHAI VY CORPORATION AND DUYEN HAI CORPORATION
project_description: Khai Vy Corporation (Khai Vy) and Duyen Hai Corporation (Duyen Hai) – known collectively as KVC or the group – together produce and export outdoor and indoor furniture to the Asian, European and North American markets and employ 6,200 workers in four operating sites across Vietnam. Total export market for the group is split 70% to European market, 25% to U.S. market and 5% to Asia. The group has its main factory in Ho Chi Minh City and three others are located in Binh Dinh Province. By investing in this project, IFC will be providing longer-term financing to help a low cost Vietnamese company maintain its competitive edge while upgrading its operations, and improving environmental, social and corporate governance practices.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Doan Van Trang, the Chairman, founded the group in 1995. Prior to establishing Khai Vy, Mr. Trang worked in the local wood sector for nearly 17 years. Mr. Trang and his wife have majority ownership of the group with 90% of Khai Vy (Mr. Trang’s brother-in-law owns the remaining 10%) and 100% of Duyen Hai.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $11.5 million project, which involves predominantly the expansion of permanent working capital. A small component (12% of project cost) of the funding would be directed towards additional capital expenditure. IFC’s proposed investment is $6 million in the form of an A Loan.
location_description: KVC has four operating sites across Vietnam. The main site, Khai Vy Factory, is based in Ho Chi Minh City and the remaining three - Duyen Hai 1 Wood Processing Factory, Duyen Hai 2 Wood Processing Factory and Duyen Hai 3 Wood Processing Factory are located in Binh Dinh Province. The Binh Dinh Province is a predominantly rural and less developed province in Central Vietnam with vast forest resources.
Company Name: KHAI VY CORPORATION AND DUYEN HAI CORPORATION

project_description: Anhui Conch Cement (Conch or the company) is the largest cement manufacturer in China, and depending on the metric used, about the seventh largest cement manufacturer in the world. Conch operates 11 clinker plants with a total capacity of 36.5 million tons and 23 cement grinding mills with a total capacity of 41.5 million tons. During 2004, the company produced a total of about 32 million tons of each of cement and clinker. IFC’s proposed investment would support the company’s capital expenditure program for 2005.
sponsor_shareholders: The company was incorporated on September 1, 1997 as a joint stock limited company owned by the Anhui Provincial Government (prior to that, it was a state-owned enterprise). Conch has since had three public listings of its shares. Currently, 50.4% of the company’s shares are publicly traded on the Hong Kong and Shanghai stock exchanges. The other 49.6% of the company’s shares are owned by Anhui Conch Group Holdings Co Ltd (ACH). ACH is 51% owned by the Anhui Provincial Government and 49% owned by Conch employees.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $300 million equivalent. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to $78 million equivalent.
location_description: Conch is headquartered in Anhui Province, with a primary focus on the Yangtze River Delta region (Shanghai and the neighboring provinces). The capital expenditures for 2005 will include, among other things, building new clinker production plants in Anhui province

project_description: Paul Maitland International Inc. (PMI or the company) is a BVI registered company with three manufacturing facilities in Vietnam and is one of the largest furniture manufacturers in Southeast Asia with 9,000 employees worldwide, 8,900 of which are based in Vietnam. The company manufactures high quality European style furniture under the trade names of Theodore Alexander and Atelier De La Madeleine. The purpose of the project is to help PMI fund additional working capital which is largely driven by the introduction of a new product line and to help the company maintain its competitive advantage which stems from its superior product design capabilities, well-established customer network, high quality production, and ability to serve customers by providing full furniture packages.
sponsor_shareholders: PMI is a private company closely held by Maitland-Smith family and friends. The founder, Mr. Paul Maitland-Smith has been in the high-end furniture production business for over 50 years, most of which has been in Asia. The major shareholders of the company are Mr. Paul Maitland-Smith (31%), Sherrill Furniture company (a US-based company) with 25% shareholding and Mr. David Pemberton (17%). 28 other individuals own the rest of the shares, none of whose holding exceeds 7%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total transaction is estimated at $22 million project, which involves predominantly the expansion of permanent working capital and the refinancing of short-term debt. A small component (9% of project cost) of the funding would be directed towards the installation of an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and MIS system, the establishment of warehouses and the development of an acacia plantation. IFC’s proposed investment is $8 million in the form of an A Loan.
location_description: PMI has three sites in Vietnam including 2 manufacturing facilities, and a plant with a saw-mill, dry kiln facility and a foundry. The company also has approximately 600 hectares of acacia plantation. The IFC investment will be directed towards activities at the two manufacturing facilities in Ho Chi Minh City – - Theodore Alexander HCM Ltd. (TAHL), a 334,000 sq. feet, 4-storey manufacturing facility constructed in the principal export processing zone and - Saigon Fine Furniture (SFF) is a 430,000 sq. feet manufacturing facility situated in Linh Trung Export Processing Zone (EPZ) II.

project_description: This project applies the Credit Enhanced Lending Transaction concept (CELT”) to foster a global multi-country partnership between Societe Generale S.A. (SocGen or the Group) and IFC. Due to the new Basle II requirements, many international banks may need to allocate more capital for their emerging market exposures. A consequence is that smaller amounts of private sector capital may be allocated by the most active global banking players to the emerging markets. In addition, the Group is also restricted by its lending limits to emerging markets countries based on its country exposure limits, which are set individually for each country. The CELT structure would help global sponsors to address the issue of capital provisioning for emerging market exposures as well as existing lending limitations by managing country-specific risk and hence their country exposure restrictions. The CELT structure that is being pioneered with SocGen is an innovative product designed to promote continued private-sector financial flows at a time of impending change in the international regulatory environment. Proceeds of the IFC financing will be used in Russia and Ukraine to promote consumer finance and operational car leasing, which SocGen has targeted as amongst the most promising sectors, with a particular focus on the regions, where unmet demand for modern financial services is even greater than in the capitals of Moscow and Kyiv.
sponsor_shareholders: Societe Generale Group (SocGen) is a leading French-based banking group with important market shares in core products and operations throughout the world. SocGen is a joint-stock company listed on the Paris stock exchange. Its stock is widely held, and there is no dominant shareholder. The Group is active in emerging markets, with a Euro 14 billion loan portfolio in emerging markets. On January 6, 2005, SocGen’s market capitalization was at EUR 33.9 billion. The Group’s shareholders’ equity stood at EUR 18.6 billion as of December 31, 2004. The Group employs 92,000 employees worldwide.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project consists primarily of senior loans of up to EUR 185 million, or its equivalent in other currencies, for IFC’s own account to current and future affiliates of Societe Generale Group (SocGen affiliates) in Russia and Ukraine. The proceeds of IFC’s loans will be used to support the growth of SocGen affiliates’ consumer finance and operational car leasing activities and related investment projects.
location_description: - Societe Generale has formed a joint venture with Baring Vostok Capital Partners and is setting up a banking subsidiary specializing in consumer finance in Russia. Through the joint venture Societe Generale is present in 15 regions of Russia, and 90% of the loan book, financed exclusively from equity, is outside of Moscow. - The SocGen group (using the name “ALD” in Russia) is also a leader in operating car leasing in Western Europe, a service it intends to provide through its affiliates in the region. - Franfinance Ukraine is a start-up project to establish and provide consumer finance services throughout Ukraine using SocGen’s proven approach in other European markets. - Other affiliates of SocGen involved in providing financial services in Russia and Ukraine may participate subject to certain restrictions.

project_description: Stora Enso Oyj (Stora Enso or the sponsor), the world’s largest paper and board producer in produced tonnes and number three sawn timber producer, has approached IFC for a loan facility to finance the development of its timber plantation and related investments in China. China is the second largest and fastest growing paper market in the world, yet it is critically short of timber/fiber. China accounts for over 1/3 of the total increase in global paper capacity for the period 2001-2006, however the country’s short supply of fiber has led it to import unsustainably harvested fiber from neighbors such as Russia or the Pacific Rim. Stora Enso’s current projects in China include expanding its plantation in the Guangxi province of Southern China, which began operating in 2002 as well as a paper mill in Suzhou, which was acquired by Stora Enso in 1998. Stora Enso plans to further develop both operations, with an immediate financing need to help development of their plantation. These investment projects, combined with Stora Enso’s other possible investment projects in China comprise an estimated $125 million investment program over the next five years. Stora Enso has thus requested IFC for a flexible debt facility for to help it with its investment program financing needs.
sponsor_shareholders: Stora Enso is a publicly listed (Helsinki, Stockholm and New York), Finland-based global forest products company. It specializes in integrated paper, packaging and forest products, producing publication and fine papers, packaging boards and wood products, areas in which the Group is a global market leader. The Group has approximately 45,000 employees in more than 40 countries in five continents. It has about 16 million tonnes annual production capacity in various paper and packaging board grades and more than 7 million m3 in sawn timber. It maintains a leading global market share in most of its paper grades, namely coated (magazine) paper, graphic and specialty papers where it enjoys market leadership in Europe and North America, and also has a leading position in Europe in newsprint, office paper, consumer packaging board and forest products. On the forestry side, it has leading competence of sustainable forestry operations, including long experience of developing fast growing plantations in Southern Europe, Latin America and Asia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is $125 million. The proposed investment is a $50 million A loan for IFC’s own account and up to a $25 million B loan from syndicate lenders.
location_description: Stora Enso’s plantations are located in the Guangxi province, primarily in five counties on or near Guangxi’s coastal areas. The headquarters of Stora Enso Guangxi is located in the capital city of Guangxi province, Nanning, and its operational headquarter for the plantation operation locates in Beihai city. The plantations are located in rural locations which have primarily been used for forestry and/or agricultural plantations. Stora Enso’s paper mill is located on an industrial site in an industrial region of the city of Suzhou, some 160 kilometers west of Shanghai.

project_description: The project comprises the construction of a greenfield bleached eucalyptus kraft pulp (BEKP) mill with annual capacity of one million tons in Fray Bentos (Uruguay) by Europe’s second largest pulp producer, OY Metsa Botnia AB (Botnia, or the sponsor) from Finland. Uruguay is one of very few locations in the world where already existing plantations can supply the raw material for a new pulp mill of this scale. Wood for the mill will be procured from existing plantations owned by the sponsors and from third parties within Uruguay and Argentina.
sponsor_shareholders: The company: Botnia S.A. (or the project company) is 100% owned by entities controlled by the sponsor (with an option for the local partner to purchase up to 9% of the shareholding). The local partner, the Otegui Group, has been in the agribusiness sector since the beginning of the last century and employs approximately 600 people. Grupo Otegui started its forest products’ activities at the end of 1980s and currently owns eucalyptus plantations (FSC certified since 2001) and sawmills. The sponsor: Botnia is Europe’s second largest pulp producer and owns five pulp mills in Finland with total production capacity of 2.7 million tons per annum. Approximately 80% of Botnia’s pulp is sold to its shareholders and the rest is sold as market pulp, mainly to Europe. Botnia’s audited turnover as of end of 2004 amounted to $1.5 billion and net profit to $142 million equivalent (compared to $69 million as of end of 2003). Botnia is owned by three Finnish companies: M-Real Corporation (39%), UPM-Kymmene (47%) and Metsaliitto Cooperative (14%). M-Real is Europe''s third largest paper merchant and a leading supplier of paper, paperboard and packaging solutions. UPM is the world’s leading magazine paper, silicon paper and label producer and Europe’s leading envelope paper, industrial wrapping products and plywood producer. Metsaliitto Cooperative, the parent company of Metsaliitto Group, is an organization of Finnish forest owners with approximately 131,000 members.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is expected to be approximately $1.2 billion. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan for IFC’s own account of up to $100 million and a syndicated B loan for the account of participants of up to $100 million.
location_description: The pulp mill will be built in Fray Bentos, the capital of the Rio Negro Department. The city is located some 200 miles North-West from Montevideo and has an estimated population of 23,000. Fray Bentos is an important trade conduit as it is located on the Uruguay River and next to an international bridge that connects Uruguay to Argentina.

project_description: The project is to create a chain of 12 multi-screen cinemas in the Russian Federation under the name Cinema Park (“Cinema Park” or the “Company”). Cinema Park was established in 2002 and currently operates from its offices in Moscow.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Prof Media, the media arm of the Interros group, one of the biggest Russian private economic groups, with investments, in addition to Prof Media, in mining (Norilsk Nickel), banking (Rosbank), power machines (Silovye Mashiny) and agribusiness (Agros) among others. The Interros group is controlled by Mr. Vladimir Potanin, a Russian investor and businessman. Interros currently owns 80% of Cinema Park. The remaining 20% of Cinema Park is owned by Studio Trite, a Russian company in the film production business in Russia, controlled by Mr. Nikita Mikhailkov, a Russian film producer.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $128 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $20 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Cinema Park’s headquarters will be located in Moscow. The company operates two cinemas in Moscow and is planning to open additional cinemas in several cities in the Russian Federation, including Moscow, Saint Petersburg and other regional cities. Cinema Park will operate mainly in retail space in shopping malls and entertainment centers, as well as in free standing buildings in highly populated urban centers with good access to public transportation.
additionality: The project’s expected development impact are in the following areas : - Affordable Leisure: Providing affordable, safe and good quality entertainment and cultural options for the Russian middle class, especially for the young. In-doors entertainment is particularly important in Russia given its severe weather conditions for most part of the year. - Infrastructure: Providing infrastructure for a modernizing and fast growing media sector, with spillover effects to other sectors of the economy. In addition, cinemas help create traffic and extend hours of shopping malls, which is critical to the success of modern retail, a sector IFC is promoting. Clustering leisure facilities like stores, cinemas and restaurants makes efficient use of urban infrastructure including parking lots and access facilities or services - Environmental and Social: The project will elevate environmental and social standards in the Russian cinema sector. The company will produce a Master Fire and Life Safety Plan following international standards (German DIN or equivalent), to be designed by international expert consultants acceptable to IFC. Cinema Park’s cinemas will include special facilities for the disabled at international standards, including special hearing aids for the hearing impaired in selected cinemas. - Local Content: By creating the audiences that creates demand for investors to inject money to the production side of the chain, the Project will indirectly support the production of local films. The company plans to become an advocate of local film production by supporting the Golden Eagle Award for young local film producers. - Piracy: The project will also help counter piracy in media products by increasing the supply of affordable, legitimate products widely within the Russian Federation and supporting an industry whose development will depend on a continued battle against piracy. - Job Creation: The project is expected to create over 500 permanent jobs throughout the country. - IFC Role: Through its investment, IFC will support the development, growth and diversification of a locally-owned and successfully operated company, a role IFC has played in only a select few of its general manufacturing projects to date in Russia. IFC also has a role to play by providing long-term financing that is otherwise not available in Russia today for projects in the media/entertainment sector. IFC’s participation in the project will also lend credibility to Interros on international markets which, given Interros’ considerable contribution to Russian GDP, will have a positive effect on the Russian economy as a whole.

project_description: OAO Lukoil is Russia’s largest integrated oil company. In 1998, Lukoil acquired the Petrotel refinery from the Romanian government through a privatization process. Since then, Lukoil has expanded its downstream operations in Romania to include about 300 retail petrol stations, 60 LPG filling skids and 8 petroleum distribution centers throughout the country. Through these targeted investments, Lukoil succeeded in creating a fully-integrated business chain starting at the oil well in Russia and going all the way downstream to the pump in Romania. Apart from the Romanian fuel wholesale and fuel retail market, Lukoil’s Romanian operations also cater to the Moldavian market and other export markets through Lukoil’s international trading company, Litasco International S.A. The project involves the modernization and revamping program of S.C. Petrotel-Lukoil S.A. (Petrotel), its Romanian refinery. The project is aimed at: - providing high quality petroleum products to Romanian consumers that comply with European Euro-3 and Euro-4 standards, - improving refinery operations by increasing the output of higher value petroleum products and reduce emissions and energy consumption; and providing high quality petroleum products to Romanian consumers that comply with European Euro-3 and Euro-4 standards. This in turn will strengthen the overall long-term competitive position of Lukoil’s entire downstream network.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor and guarantor is OAO Lukoil, which accounts for roughly 19% of Russia’s crude oil production or 86.2 million mt in 2004. Throughput at Lukoil’s refineries amounted to 43.8 million mt in 2004. Lukoil's shares are publicly traded on the Russian stock exchanges (RTS, MICEX, SPICEX, SSE) and its ADRs and GDRs trade on the US over-the-counter market and exchanges in London, Berlin, Frankfurt, Munich and Stuttgart. Lukoil became the first Russian company to obtain London Stock Exchange (LSE) listing in 2002. In September 2004, the Russian Government sold its remaining 7.59% stake in Lukoil to Houston-based ConocoPhillips, who has since indicated it will increase its stake to up to 20% and become a major equity investor. Following an internal reorganization in 2000, the sponsor’s international assets were placed with Lukoil Overseas Limited B.V. for upstream operations and Lukoil International GmbH for downstream operation. Petrotel’s shares are owned by Lukoil Europe Holding B.V., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Lukoil International GmbH, (93.67%), the investment company S.I.F. Muntenia (3%), former State Property Fund - A.P.A.P.S. (2.59%) and various individuals (0.75%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Lukoil’s investments in Romania are in the range of $367 million, out of which $260 million was invested to expand the gas station network, tank farms and other distribution installations, and $107 million for the modernization of the refinery. At the outset of the project in 2003, Lukoil engaged IFC to provide long term financing. However, in the interest of expediting the refinery modernization, the sponsor provided its own bridge financing to commence project implementation. The refinery re-commenced operations in the fall 2004, and IFC’s loans will replace the sponsor bridge financing. IFC’s proposed investment will consist of a $35 million A loan and a $47 million B loan.
location_description: The Petrotel refinery is located in Ploesti, a city with 300,000 inhabitants in central Romania. The city is dominated by the Romanian oil industry, there are 4 refineries in the immediate area. Lukoil has 300 gas stations and 8 storage tank farms across the country.
additionality: The proposed project will have the following development impacts: - As part of Lukoil’s operations in Romania, Petrotel forms a crucial element of a professionally run downstream business, which can serve as benchmark for other players. - Romania’s refining sector is a legacy of the COMECON time with too many refineries at sub-optimal size. Lukoil’s investment in the downstream industry will facilitate rationalization of Romania’s refining sector, by helping to remove overcapacity and loss-making players. By streamlining the industry, the overall economics of the refining sector in Romania will be strengthened, allowing for a market-driven approach. - Together with the privatization of Petrom, which was acquired in 2004 by Austria’s OMV, the project will reduce the need for the Government of Romania’s involvement in the downstream industry. This by itself is a benefit for the entire economy as western business practices are increasingly adopted. - Lukoil’s investments in the Romanian economy will also be perceived as a showcase for a successful privatization. Not only has Lukoil honored its commitment to carry out the modernization program as part of the privatization contract, but it will keep investing in the Romanian economy through the expansion of its gas station network and other activities. - In view of Romania’s aspired EU accession, Petrotel’s modernization program allows Lukoil to supply Euro-3 and Euro-4 fuels (the latest EU fuel Specifications) to Romania, as well as bring new technology to the country’s debilitated refining sector, moving Romania’s refining industry closer to EU best practices. - Due to the modernization program, Petrotel’s air emissions have been reduced and meet IFC, EU and Romanian emissions standards, as low NOx burners are installed in boilers and heaters. - As part of the modernization program, $11 million were spent for a wide-ranging environmental improvement program as part of Lukoil’s obligation to the Government of Romania to carry out environmental clean-up work. - Lukoil has trained and will continue training its Romanian staff to improve on current working practices, as well as health and safety standards. - Petrotel has total direct employment of 1,241 staff. Moreover, Lukoil has currently 3,819 staff employed at its petrol station network and distribution facilities throughout Romania, which brings the total employment for Lukoil to 5,060. All of Lukoil’s operations will create substantial backward linkages in the country’s economy. The proposed project fits well with the World Bank Group strategy of promoting private sector development in a key sector that has been traditionally important for Romania. In addition, it is in line with IFC’s strategy of supporting the increase of foreign investment flows and investor confidence in the country. IFC’s participation in the project would enable the company to obtain adequate long-term financing at reasonable terms. In addition to providing direct financing, IFC would serve as a catalyst by mobilizing sources in Europe via a B loan syndication at a time when limited access to long-term financing is available in Romania for these type of projects. IFC has played a key role in structuring the financial plan, and evaluating environmental issues, thus reducing the project's risk profile. In view of the perceived macroeconomic and political risks of investing in Romania, IFC's participation together with Lukoil, a regional leader in oil, gas and petrochemicals, will have a significant demonstration effect in supporting foreign direct investment in Romania.

project_description: Joint Stock Company “Concern Galnaftogaz” (GNG or the company) operates one of Ukraine’s new and fastest growing network of service stations selling petroleum products and related services. It is based in Western Ukraine, which is where it has the strongest market presence. IFC’s investment will provide financing for further expansion of the company’s network to other regions in the country, which will result in a significant increase in its market share and profitability.
