sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor is Financial and Investment Energy Holding (FIEH), a Liechtenstein based company with interests in various sectors in Ukraine including energy, agriculture, construction, banking and insurance. FIEH owns directly and indirectly about 71% of the shares of GNG.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $115 million over five years. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan of up to $20 million and equity/quasi-equity of up to $5 million
location_description: The company is headquartered in Lviv, Ukraine. Its network of service stations is concentrated around Western Ukraine, however, as a part of the project, GNG has plans to spread its network throughout Ukraine.

sector: Soap and Cleaning Compound (Soap, Detergent, etc.)
project_description: The project involves an overhaul of the existing activities of NOSA through the following components: - improvement of the work flow, - upgrade of the plant safety and environment conditions, - installation of control, measurement and monitoring devices; and - the expansion of the production capacity from about 8,700 to 17,400 tpa. The company specializes in the production of laundry soap, using locally produced palm oil as the main raw material. IFC supported the company with a guarantee facility (approved in June 1998, and committed in Feb. 1999) of CFA280 million ($0.4 million) to launch the then greenfield project.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor is Mr. Samuel Noumsi (39), with 99.5% of the company's shares. Close family members (children) hold the remaining balance of the shares. NOSA is a limited partnership company (SARL) with a share capital of CFA200 million ($0.27 million). For over 10 years Mr. Noumsi was primarily involved in palm oil trading under the sole proprietor firm NOSACAM. Mr. Noumsi decided in 1997 to diversify through downstream integration, and to manufacture soap.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at ?uro2.01 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan for IFC's own account for the amount of ?uro 800.00.
location_description: The project is located on the existing company site, measuring 6,243 square-meter surface area in the Simbock district of Yaounde. The site is an uninhabited peripheral zone, earmarked for industrial activities, and with good road connections to major towns.

project_description: Bonite Bottlers Limited (BBL or the company) is a beverage bottling and distribution company located in Moshi, Tanzania. BBL holds the franchise to bottle carbonated soft drinks (CSD) for Coca Cola in several regions in northern Tanzania. BBL’s franchise regions include Arusha, Kilimanjaro and Manyara and two districts – Singida and Manyoni – in the Singida region. The Company also bottles mineral water under the Kilimanjaro Drinking Water (KDW) brand. The project is to assist BBL to expand its production capacity and acquire the latest equipment for its operations. The project involves the following components: - expanding its CSD production capacity to 36,000 bottle per hour (bph) from the present 24,000 bph on its returnable glass bottle (RGB) line; - replacing an existing PVC bottling line with a modern PET bottling line; - extending its factory complex to house the new RGB line and provide additional storage space; - acquiring additional vehicles to augment its distribution network; - acquiring a PET-preform manufacturing line and - providing incremental working capital. The total project cost is estimated at $20 million. BBL has not upgraded or replaced any machinery within its operations in the last 10 years. Now is an opportune time for BBL to replace its dated machinery with modern equipment, and increase production efficiency. The Project will enable BBL to produce a larger volume of Coca-Cola products and expand its market share through the supply of a wider range of products. The Project will also change the type of material used from PVC to PET, which is a better packaging material, is less costly and has a more aesthetic presentation. Finally, the ability to manufacture PET-preforms will significantly reduce operational cost for BBL and increase its ability to produce a wider variety of PET packaged products.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are IPP Limited and Mr. Reginald Mengi. The Reginald Mengi Family Trust owns 100% of BBL. The Trust controls the IPP group of companies which are involved in media, beverages, mining and minerals, and gemstones prospecting. IPP’s leading products/service brands include The Guardian newspaper, ITV national television station. IPP also has a strategic shareholding in the CRDB Bank and the African Media Group and is a minority shareholder in other Coca-Cola franchises through the following: - Zanzibar Bottlers; - Kwanza Bottlers; - Afri Bottlers; and - Mtwara Bottlers. Kwanza bottlers is the largest beverage bottler in Tanzania.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $20 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A-Loan of up to $10 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The expansion project will be located at BBL’s existing production plant located in Shiri Matunda in the Moshi municipality in northern Tanzania.

project_description: The Jinan Shanshui Group (SSG or the company) is the second largest cement manufacturer in China based in Jinan, Shandong. SSG has a total cement production capacity of 13.4 million tons per year and owns 12 cement facilities, all of which are located in Shandong. The company was established in 1996, and was until recently, a state-owned enterprise directly owned by the Jinan Municipal Government. Chuangzin Investment (CX) was established in 2001 as a private investment vehicle for SSG management and staff who owned 94% of CX, with the other 6% was owned by SSG itself. In October 2004, after SSG received approval to restructure and reorganize, the company began the process of privatization, whereby SSG was taken over by CX (with CX as the surviving entity), and the management and staff became the legal owners of the company. The project consists of three main components aimed at assisting SSG: - to merge with Chuangxin Investment (CX), privatize and restructure its cement operating companies; - consolidate its cement operations in its home province of Shandong through expansions and new investments; and - debt restructuring.
sponsor_shareholders: While the exact ownership percentages are yet to be finalized, the likely shareholding structure following the privatization and pre-IPO equity investment is expected to be : Morgan Stanley Private Equity Asia (MSPEA)/CDH – 35%; IFC – 7%, and Management and Staff – 58%. MSPEA is the private equity investment arm of the international financial conglomerate based in Hong Kong. CDH was established as an 8 year closed-end Cayman vehicle with a capital of about US$ 100 million with the objective of generating long-term capital appreciation through late-stage equity investments in established companies with substantial operations in China. The management and staff shareholding will include over 1,000 employees, none of whom will own more than 1% of the company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $436 million which includes the company’s ongoing capital investment program and debt restructuring. The proposed IFC investment includes a senior loan of $50 million for IFC’s own account and equity/quasi equity investment of up to $8 million.
location_description: The company is headquartered in Jinan, Province of Shandong, China. The company is expanding its existing activities in the cities of Pinyin, Rizhao, and Anqiu.

company_name: S.A. SAN MIGUEL A.G.I.C.I. y F.
sector: Fruit and Vegetable Preservation or Processing (Canning, Freezing, Drying, Jams, etc.)
project_description: San Miguel is an Argentine company that produces fresh lemons on 5,500 ha of agricultural land in the province of Tucumán, in the north of Argentina. From its own production as well as third parties’, San Miguel exports over 100,000 tons of fresh lemons, and processes more than twice this amount of fruit to produce frozen lemon juice concentrate, essential oil and dried peel. The project is to support San Miguel’s overall plantation and industrial operations, permanent working capital as well as its sophisticated industrial waste treatment system.
sponsor_shareholders: San Miguel is listed in the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange, and controlled by a group of individual shareholders. The company also has operations in sweet citrus and lemons in Uruguay, through its subsidiaries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is supporting San Miguel with a syndicated corporate loan, financing overall lemon production and processing operations with a particular focus on environmental matters and treatment of the company’s industrial waste. IFC is proposing to lend $20 million of long term debt for its own account, and to syndicate a B loan with other lenders.
location_description: San Miguel’s offices and its main fresh fruit packing facility are located in the suburbs of San Miguel de Tucumán, while its plantations are scattered in the province. San Miguel industrial processing plant is located in Famaillá, about 30km away from the town.
Company Name: S.A. SAN MIGUEL A.G.I.C.I. y F.

project_description: The Trinidad Cement Limited Group (the Sponsors, or the Group,), which has cement operations in Trinidad, Jamaica and Barbados, is the leading producer and dominant supplier of cement in the Caricom, the economic grouping of English-speaking Caribbean island nations plus Belize, Guyana and Suriname which together have a population of approximately six million. Its three main operating subsidiaries are Trinidad Cement Limited (TCL or the company), Caribbean Cement Company Limited (Carib Cement) in Jamaica and Arawak Cement Company Limited in Barbados. With combined cement production capacity of 2.3 million tons per year, the three plants produce for their domestic markets and also export to the Caricom markets, where the Group commands an 85% market share. Purpose of the project is a $133 million capital expenditure program in Carib Cement between 2005-2009 includes: - expansion of clinker manufacturing capacity by installing a new modern dry process kiln and upgrading the existing dry process kiln; - upgrading/expanding the capacity of the existing cement mills; - quarry mapping and upgrades to mobile fleet; - expansion of packing capacity; and - general improvements. The project will help Carib Cement improve the cost base of its cement plant and become a stronger regional player. Carib Cement will be better able to compete with both importers and competitors in the region. At present, the markets of Trinidad, Jamaica and Barbados are protected by tariffs on cement imported from outside the Caricom region and have high domestic prices (above $100/ton), reflecting a lack of competition in the local markets and high production costs. In anticipation of tariff reductions and increased competition from imports, the TCL Group, including Carib Cement is embarking on a strategy that focuses on improving cost competitiveness and upgrading capacity.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor, TCL Group, is incorporated under the laws of Trinidad and Tobago and its principal activity is the manufacture and sale of cement. It was established as Trinidad’s first cement company in the early 1950s in response to the invitation by the Government of Trinidad and Tobago to Rugby Portland of the UK. Until it was effectively privatized in 1990, TCL was wholly owned by Government of Trinidad and Tobago, which began divesting its shareholding in TCL on a phased basis in 1989. To facilitate the establishment of a strategic alliance, a block of shares representing a 20% interest in TCL was sold to Cemex in 1994. Shares were also offered to the general public and, in 1999, GOTT completed its divestment by selling its last remaining shareholding to Trinidad National Insurance Board (9.96%), Trinidad Unit Trust Corporation (4%), TCL Employee Share Ownership Plan - ESOP (6%), and others (0.8%). At present, the Group is Caricom’s only cement manufacturer and it is a vertically integrated operation with involvement in the pre-mixed concrete/aggregates and packaging sectors. TCL is both an operating and holding company with 16 subsidiaries (4 in Trinidad, 4 in Jamaica, 2 in Barbados, 2 in Nevis, 1 in St. Maarten, 1 in Anguilla, 1 in St. Martin and 1 in Guyana) of which 5 are wholly-owned and 11 are majority-owned joint ventures. Cement accounts for 88% of TCL’s total revenues (11% from the concrete and aggregates sector, and 1% from the packaging sector) and geographically, 42% of the Group’s revenues are derived from Jamaica, 32% from Trinidad and Tobago, 11% from Barbados and 15% from other regional markets. TCL’s shareholding is widely distributed among approximately 6,000 shareholders with Cemex being the single largest shareholder (20%). Other main shareholding groups include institutional investors (52%), Trinidad and Tobago nationals (17%) and employees (7%). TCL is listed on the three regional stock exchanges of Trinidad and Tobago, Barbados and Jamaica.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $133 million. IFC is considering an “A” Loan of up to $25 million and a “C” loan of up to $10 million to TCL. The remaining $98 million required will be funded with a combination of internally generated cash flow and parallel financing from regional financial institutions.
location_description: The project will be implemented in Carib Cement (Jamaica) which is an existing operation. Carib Cement is located near Manley Airport in Kingston with excellent access to national highways and port facilities. The limestone quarry is located in the mountain above the cement plant, and the gypsum and shale quarries are located nearby in a hilly area.

company_name: Changchun TBK SHILI Auto Parts Co., Ltd
project_description: The project consists of the construction of a new plant in Changchun, Jilin Province, in northeastern China, to produce linings for drum brakes and pads for disk brakes for commercial vehicles. The brake linings and pads to be produced by the plant will be supplied primary to First Automotive Work (FAW) group. FAW is the largest vehicle manufacturer in China with a production of around 890,000 passenger cars and commercial vehicles in 2004.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Tokyo Buhin Kogkyo Co., Ltd. (TBK). TBK, a Japanese corporation listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, is the leading manufacturer of brakes for commercial vehicles (CVs) with an approximately 70% market share in Japan. In addition, TBK is the leading producer of oil and water pumps for CVs representing about 90% and 70% of the Japanese market, respectively. The Project will be implemented through a joint venture company to be owned 60% by TBK and 40% by Changchun Shili Automobile Brake Parts Co., Ltd (CSABPC). CSABPC is a producer of brake friction materials owned 51% by Sihuan Chassis Parts Plant, and 49% by Zhejiang Shibao Holding Group Co., Ltd, a Chinese private limited liability corporation.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $11 million. The proposed IFC investment will be $4 million loan for IFC own account.
location_description: The plant will be located in the Changchun High-Technology Industries Development Area in the province of Jilin, north east part of China.
Company Name: Changchun TBK SHILI Auto Parts Co., Ltd

project_description: Yantai Changyu Group Company Limited (the Group) is a holding company controlling a 53.8% stake in Yantai Changyu Pioneer Wine Company Limited (Changyu or the company), a Shenzhen-listed company involved in the production and distribution of wine, sparkling wine, tonic wine, and brandy. The Group also has minor operations in a hotel, a tourist company and a general service company. Established in 1892, Changyu is the oldest and largest wine producer in China, with cumulative output of 80,000 tons per annum of wine products and a domestic market share of 21%. Changyu has nationwide distribution channels and a wide product range from low-end to high-end wines. Changyu currently generates more than 75% of its revenue from wine, grape cider, tonic wine and sparkling wine products and less than 25% from brandy products. The company expects to grow mainly through expanding the core wine operation, in a growing wine market in China. The Yantai City People’s Government State Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (Yantai Government) of Shandong Province currently controls 55% of the Group and intends to sell 43% of its stake to foreign investors. The shares are planned to be sold in two tranches of 33% and 10% each to two separate investors. The proceeds from the sale will accrue to the Yantai Government, which has requested IFC to consider taking a stake in the Group. The proposed IFC investment is to purchase the 10% stake in the group, representing an equity investment of about $20 million.
sponsor_shareholders: Changyu (the Company) has the following ownership structure: - Changyu Group Co. (holding) - 53.8% (non-listed “legal person shares”) - Public and institutional shareholders of “A” shares - 12.4% (listed shares) - Public and institutional shareholders of “B” shares - 33.8% (listed shares) The Group (holding) was historically 100% owned by the Yantai Government, which is privatizing the Group via a two stage process: - an EMBO (Employee and Management Buyout) of 45% of the Group, which was concluded in October 2004; and - Sale of a further 43% stake in the Group to foreign investors, in two separate tranches of 33% and 10% each. While IFC is considering investing in the 10% stake, IFC has learned that Illva Saronno, an Italian company, was selected for the 33% stake. Illva Saronno Group, a diversified group, has interests in three areas: - the production and sales of alcoholic beverages including wines and liquor; - raw materials for ice-creams bakery products, and - optical lenses. After the completion of the privatization process, the shareholding structure of the Group will be: - Yantai Government - 12% - Management and employees - 45% - Foreign investors - 43% (including two investors with 33% and 10% each)
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Yantai Government’s asking price for the shares on sale represents a 20% premium over the appraised net asset value (NAV) of RMB 1,215.72 million of the Group. The corresponding asking price for the proposed 10% shareholding is $ 17.62 million.
location_description: Changyu is headquartered in Yantai city, Shandong province of China.

company_name: ADVENT LATIN AMERICAN PRIVATE EQUITY FUND III-E LIMITED PARTNERSHIP
country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: The Latin American Private Equity Fund III, L.P (LAPEF III, or the Fund) is a closed-end regional private equity fund with a target size of $300 million formed by Advent International (Advent, or the sponsor) to achieve attractive investment returns through a portfolio of diversified investments in Latin American countries. The Fund will acquire primarily control positions in later-stage businesses and add value through active investment management, majority share ownership positions, and board and executive committee participation.
sponsor_shareholders: Advent, founded in 1984, is one of the world's largest and most experienced global private equity organizations. It operates 14 offices and 10 affiliates in 25 countries and employs over 100 investment professionals. Advent has raised over $6 billion in aggregate and invested in more than 500 companies in 35 countries in many different industries. It manages global, regional and corporate/strategic venture capital funds covering investment opportunities in both developed and emerging markets (including North America, Western Europe, Central and Eastern Europe, Asia and Latin America) and is regarded as a top-tier performer in its industry. In Latin America, Advent has been active for 10 years and invested approximately $400 million in 24 companies. It is the only pan-regional private equity firm with a direct presence in each of the markets in which it invests. The firm has wholly-owned offices staffed by local nationals in Mexico City, Sao Paulo, and Buenos Aires.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC equity investment is of up to $20 million. The fund's target size is $300 million.
location_description: The fund will be formed as a Cayman Islands limited partnership. The geographical focus of investments will be the three Latin American countries where Advent has wholly-owned offices: Mexico, Brazil, and Argentina.
Company Name: ADVENT LATIN AMERICAN PRIVATE EQUITY FUND III-E LIMITED PARTNERSHIP
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: The proposed project initiative will promote investments in energy efficient technologies in Russia. IFC will create an investment facility to provide credit lines for Russian financial institutions who will on-lend to energy efficiency and renewable energy projects. The credit lines will be supported by a partial risk guarantee, funded by the Global Environment Facility. The investment facility will operate in parallel with an extensive technical assistance program. The immediate objective of the IFC/GEF investment project is to encourage private sector financing of energy efficiency projects in Russia in three pilot regions. The ultimate impact of the proposed investment/TA project will be the improved energy efficiency (EE) and profitability of Russian companies, leading to a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. This will be accomplished by creating an awareness in Russian financial institutions that energy efficiency projects are - financially viable and - improve the risk profile of the client by reducing operating costs. The project will work with the participating financial institutions to “deepen” the Russian financial markets, making longer term capital available for investment by Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). The Technical Assistance Project will be structured around five inter-related objectives, which are to: - Establish and monitor the operation of the investment facility; - Support development of EE investment projects by participating FIs and their clients; - Improve market awareness and understanding of energy efficiency; - Strengthen capacity of emerging local energy service companies (ESCOs); and, - Provide policy and legal support to EE investment projects given the evolving legislative landscape.
sponsor_shareholders: IFC will put in place a framework financing facility that will finance credit lines with a number of different, reputable, private Russian financial institutions, who will act as sponsors of the project. The technical assistance program will be open to all Russian financial institutions and Russian private sector entities. In certain circumstances technical assistance may be available to municipal entities as long as there is a scope for private sector engagement
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s will invest initially $20million in the financing facility. The Global Environment Facility will invest $2m in a Guarantee Facility to support portfolios of sub-loans. The cost of the technical assistance program will be $6.25million funded through the Global Environment Facility, donors and using IFC’s own internal resources.
location_description: The project will be executed in the Russian Federation through project offices based in Moscow, St Petersburg and Ekaterinburg. Individual investments are expected to be made in Central Russia, the Urals and North-west Russia, however, the program may expand into other regions according to local demand.

project_description: Cosan S. A. Indústria e Comércio (Cosan, the company or Group) is the parent company of the largest integrated sugar and ethanol producer and exporter in Brazil, and one of the largest and most efficient producers in the world. Cosan reached this position by acquiring and turning around sugar mills, mostly during the last four years. Cosan operates 12 mills, 3 sugar refineries and one export terminal at the Port of Santos. All facilities are located in the State of São Paulo, in Brazil’s Center-South region, with the exception of one small sugar refinery located in the State of Santa Catarina, South region. In FY 2004, ended April 30, Cosan milled 26.1 million mt of cane, sold 2.2 million mt of sugar (of which 82% or 1.8 million mt were exported), and 946 million liters of ethanol (of which 23% or 214 million liters were exported). The proposed project, to be implemented over the FY05 to FY07 period (May 2004 to April 2006), will allow the company: - to maintain its leading position in the Brazilian sugar industry; - to respond to growing demand for fuel ethanol, particularly in the domestic market; and - to respond to increased competition in international markets by improving agricultural yields and cutting costs. More specifically, the project will allow Cosan to increase its installed milling capacity, improve sugar cane agricultural yields and further reduce costs. The project will also support Cosan’s efforts to improve monitoring and compliance of environmental and social standards.
sponsor_shareholders: The Group includes five operating companies, of which Cosan is the largest, and two land holding companies. All companies are privately held. Cosan started in 1936 with one sugar mill and in the following 67 years it grew mostly by acquiring and consolidating existing sugar mills. Cosan’s main shareholders are Indústria Açucareira São Francisco S/A., Irmãos Francheschi Administração e Participação S/A., Usina Costa Pinto S/A Açúcar e Álcool and Nova Celisa S/A. Mr. Rubens Silveira Mello controls 76% of Cosan’s voting shares through its ownership in Indústria Açucareira São Francisco S/A; Irmãos Francheschi Adminstração e Participação S/A; and Nova Celisa S/A.. Mr. Silveira Mello has over 30 years of experience in management of sugar companies and has been with Cosan for over 20 years.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $ 344.9 million and comprises the following components: - acquisition of assets to support the Group''s growth strategy; - investment in planting, modernization and maintenance of existing operations; and - additional working capital. The project will be implemented over the FY05 to FY07 period. The proposed IFC investment is a $30 million A Loan for IFC’s own account and a $20 million C Loan.
location_description: Cosan’s operations are located in the State of São Paulo, Center-South of Brazil, where all mills and agricultural operations are based, with the exception of a small sugar refinery located in the South. Brazil’s Center-South region has some of the best cane growing land in the world in terms of soil, topography and climate. As a result, this region has some of the lowest production costs in the world. This natural competitive advantage is compounded by the very large size of cane farms, efficient farming practices, long harvest season and large and efficient mills. Cosan’s headquarters are located in the city of São Paulo, capital of the State, and the management of industrial and agricultural operations is based in the city of Piracicaba, in the interior of the State.

project_description: The Tata Iron & Steel Company Limited (Tata Steel or the company) is a fully integrated steel company headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Tata Steel is a cost-competitive steel manufacturer primarily due to its captive iron ore and coal mines. The company produces hot & cold rolled products and long products at its facility in Jamshedpur (state of Jharkhand), and Mumbai (state of Maharashtra), India. In the year ended March 31, 2004, the company sold 3.96 million tonnes of steel and recorded a net income of $380 million. Tata Steel wants to become a competitive, global player with a significantly larger capacity. The company plans to - increase its production capacity from its current 5 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) to 7.4 MTPA by 2009 and to 15 MTPA by 2010 through organic growth and acquisitions in India and overseas; - move up the value chain and improve its product mix; - further improve its cost competitiveness by improving operational efficiency; and - maintain its leading position in the Indian market, where further growth is expected. To achieve these goals, the company plans to implement a $2.6 billion investment program. The investment program consists of the following: - a capacity expansion program in two phases – Phase I includes a 1 MTPA capacity expansion which is under final stage of completion, Phase II includes a 2.4 MTPA capacity expansion and modernization program - both at its operations in Jamshedpur; and - the acquisition of the steel-related businesses of NatSteel Limited (NatSteel), a Singaporean company with operations in five emerging countries in Asia, including China.
sponsor_shareholders: The Tata entities (the sponsors) currently have a 26% shareholding in the company. The rest of the shares are held by the general public (29%), private corporate entities (7%), and institutional investors - both domestic and foreign (38%). Tata Steel was established in 1907 by Mr. Jamsetji Tata, the founder of the Tata group, one of the largest and most reputable business groups in India.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Tata Steel has requested a corporate loan of up to $200 million for part financing of its investment program.
location_description: The company has a steel plant in Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, India. It has easy access to major roads and infrastructure.

project_description: Universal, the largest tourism company in the Maldives, has requested a loan of up to $25 million to finance the following: - rebuilding of 52 bungalows and a spa at the Full Moon Resort (156 rooms) damaged by the recent tsunami; - refinancing of the loan for the Huvafenfushi resort (42 rooms) that was completed in 2004; and - other corporate purposes.
sponsor_shareholders: Universal Enterprises was founded in 1972 by two brothers from the Maldives, Mohamed Umar Maniku and Ahmed Umar Maniku. Mr. Mohamed Umar Maniku was one of the hosts for the first organized tour to visit the Maldives. In 1978, the two brothers incorporated Universal Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., a Maldives based tourism company. Universal has since grown and evolved and is now the largest single resort operator in the country with ten quality resorts in eight islands and a total of more than 1000 rooms.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated cost of rebuilding, renovation and refinancing is approximately $65 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $25 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: All resorts of Universal are located on individual islands in the Republic of Maldives.

company_name: CDH CHINA CAPITAL GROWTH FUND II LP
project_description: IFC is considering an equity commitment of $18 million in the CDH China Growth Capital Fund II, L.P. (CDH II), an investment vehicle to be established with a target size of $310 million which will make equity and equity-related investments in established Chinese companies that have strong business fundamentals, favorable growth prospects and viable exits via listings or trade sales. CDH II will be managed by the CDH Team who had worked together since 1995 in the private equity group of China International Capital Corporation (CICC) and raised the first CDH China Fund (CDH I) in 2002, after spinning off from CICC, with a total capital commitment of $102.5 million.
sponsor_shareholders: The CDH Team consists of 8 investment professionals led by Dr. Wu Shangzhi, President of the fund management company (CDH), and Managing Directors Mr. Jiao Zhen and Mr. Stuart Schonberger, who have an average of eight years of China-specific private equity experience each. CDH is jointly owned by the CDH Team, GIC Special Investments Pte. Ltd (GICSI), and Capital Z Investment Partners L.P. (CZIP). GICSI is the private equity investment arm of the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation. CZIP is the New York based private equity fund of funds program affiliated to the Zurich Financial Services. Other potential investors in CDH II are expected to be mainly institutional investors from the US, Europe and Asia. Many CDH I investors are expected to continue to participate in CDH II.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: CDH II expects to raise a total amount of $310 million, of which the proposed IFC equity investment of $20 million will represent no more than 10%.
location_description: CDH II would be established as a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership. Companies with substantial operations in China are the geographic focus of the investments. The investment team will operate out of China with its headquarters in Beijing.
Company Name: CDH CHINA CAPITAL GROWTH FUND II LP

project_description: This project is a modification to an existing IFC project in the Dominican Republic – Domicem No. 20490, which was approved by the Board on July 8, 2003. The original project envisaged partial ownership by Domicem (or the company) of a captive power plant. During construction of the plant, the company has decided that it would be more efficient to fully own the power plant while having an energy equipment supplier operating and maintaining it.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are Colacem, S.p.A. of Italy (49%), SIMEST of Italy (2%) and a group of local partners in the Dominican Republic with substantial knowledge of the local building materials industry (49%). Colacem ranks as Italy’s third-largest cement company and is part of the Financo Holding Group, a private Italian conglomerate owned by the Colaiacovo family of Italy. Founded in the 1950s as a construction and building materials company, Financo today has interests in cement/hydraulic binders; concrete and aggregates; transport, and diversified industries. SIMEST is a publicly owned Italian company supported by the Ministry of Industry and created to encourage Italian investments abroad.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The additional investment required for the full ownership of the power plant is $7.5 million, which IFC is proposing to finance fully by A and B Loans. In addition, the sponsors are funding some enhancements/improvements to the cement plant, which will bring the total cost of the cement plant to $113.5 million.
location_description: The captive power plant will be located at the same site as the Domicem cement plant, which is located 40 km from the capital Santo Domingo, 26 km from the international Port of de Haina and 2 km from the village of Sabana Grande de Palanque. The site is easily accessible, located 2,000 meters away from the Haina Palanque highway.

project_description: The project involves the construction and operation of a greenfield cement plant with a capacity of 4.4 million tons per annum (p.a.) at Obajana, Kogi State, Nigeria. The project is located 220 km southwest of Abuja and consists of the following components: - a cement plant and limestone quarry - a 135 MW captive power plant, - a 90 km natural gas pipeline, - a 351 unit housing complex for staff, - an earth dam and water reservoir to meet the project''s water requirements, and 500 trucks for cement transportation. - The project company is Obajana Cement Company Plc (OCP or the company). The project will fill a supply gap in the Nigerian cement market, where over 75% of the annual consumption of 10.6 million tons is imported. It will use locally available limestone and natural gas to produce cement at a production cost that is expected to be below the current importation cost.
sponsor_shareholders: The project is sponsored by Dangote Industries Limited (DIL or the sponsor), a leading Nigerian producer of sugar, salt and wheat flour and an importer and market leader in cement. DIL is part of a group of businesses controlled by Mr. Aliko Dangote, a Nigerian industrialist.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at $798 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to $75 million.
location_description: The project is located in Obajana, Kogi State, 220 km southwest of Abuja, the Nigerian capital. The central site (cement and power plant) is located 25 Km from the Kabba road junction which will provide access to the roadway leading to Lokoja (the capital of Kogi State) and beyond. The quarry is in Oyo Village and is connected by a 7.5 km conveyor to the cement plant. The gas pipeline will run from the gas manifold at Ajaokuta Steel Complex and will include sections along the Ajaokuta-Okene road and Oben-Kaduna NNPC pipeline route with the last section running from Lokoja-Kabba junction to Obajana.

project_description: The project consists of a loan of up to Euro 10 million (approximately $13 million) to BNI-Credit Lyonnais Madagascar (BNI-CLM, the Bank, or the company), the largest commercial bank in Madagascar. BNI-CLM is an IFC portfolio client and has had a good performance since IFC’s first investment in 1992. The proposed loan would allow BNI-CLM to finance its existing and growing pipeline of FX-earning projects from its broad corporate client base, primarily in the hotel/tourism, agribusiness, textile and fishery industries.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor of the project is Calyon (formerly Credit Lyonnais). BNI (Bankin’ Ny Indostria) was created in 1976, following the nationalization of the financial system, from the merger of the Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) subsidiary in Madagascar and a local investment company. Since January 1, 1991, Credit Lyonnais has held the majority of BNI-CLM capital as shown in the table below: BNI-CLM’s Shareholding Structure Shareholders Percentage of holding Credit Lyonnais Global Banking 51.00% Government of Madagascar (GoM) 32.58% IFC 10.00% Banque de la Reunion 2.00% BNI-Credit Lyonnais Madagascar staff 4.42% Total 100.00% BNI-CLM is predominantly a commercial bank with a network of 20 branches. Despite the difficult economic conditions that have prevailed in the country since the 2002 crisis, as well as the increased competition, BNI-CLM has shown strong and stable growth and profitability to date. Over the past three years, BNI-CLM’s total assets grew from MGF 1,943.8 billion ($305.2 million equivalent) to MGF 2,815 billion ($307.65 million equivalent) and its equity base from MGF 147 billion ($23.1 million equivalent) to MGF 232.5 billion ($25.4 million equivalent). At end of December 2004, BNI-CLM’s ROAA and ROAE were 3.33% and 40% respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s investment will be in the form of a loan of up to Euro 10 million ($13 million equivalent) to BNI-CLM.
location_description: The location of the project is Antananarivo, Madagascar.

project_description: The Industrial Union of Donbass (ISD) is seeking IFC support to help finance CJSC Sofia Kiev (or the company), a 235-room hotel in central Kiev. The hotel is expected to be operated by Hyatt International under the Hyatt Regency brand name.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is the ISD, a privately owned major Ukrainian diversified group, founded in 1995. The group’s main activity is the production and trade of metals (steel).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at approximately $50 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to a $14.5 million A loan and up to a $13 million syndicated B loan.
location_description: The project will be based in Kiev, Ukraine.

project_description: Packages Limited (the Company or Packages) is the leading integrated paper products manufacturer in Pakistan and an IFC client since 1964. It is widely acknowledged as the market leader in terms of its production of sophisticated and higher quality packaging products. Packages plans to undertake an investment program during the period 2005-2008. This investment program involves the following: - establishing a new pulp and paper plant in Kasur, - relocating the existing pulp and paper production facilities from Lahore to the new plant, - increasing production of higher margin printing and writing paper products and - upgrading and expanding the converting lines and tissues lines at the existing plant. With the new and relocated facilities, the company’s production capacity will increase from 100,000 metric tons per year to 300,000 metric tons per year. At the conclusion of the project, all pulp and paper-making facilities at Packages’ existing plant in Lahore will cease, with the exception of the manufacture of de-inked pulp and tissue paper. Other operations at Lahore will, however, continue. The purpose of the project is to achieve the following: - improve the quality of pulp and paper / paper-board production and ensure the supply of quality paperboard at reasonable prices for the company’s growing converting operations; - help the company achieve higher production efficiencies through reduced operating costs; and - improve the company’s overall environmental performance.
sponsor_shareholders: Packages Limited is the sponsor of the proposed project and is Pakistan’s premier integrated pulp and paper mill and packaging materials manufacturer. It is listed on all three stock exchanges of Pakistan. It was originally established in 1956 as a joint venture between the Ali Family of Pakistan and Akerlund & Rausing of Sweden. The original sponsors (i.e. the Ali family) continue to be closely associated with the company. The shareholding structure of Packages as of September 30, 2004 was: the Ali family (18.6%); Packages Group of companies (25.4%), StoraEnso, Tetra Laval Holdings and Finance, and Holgar Crafoord family (12.0%); local financial institutions (18%); IFC (0.8%); and the general public (25%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the proposed project is estimated at $332 million including: $209 million for fixed assets at Kasur, $33 million for capital expenditures for the converting lines and the tissues lines, $32 million for interest during construction, $20 million for contingencies, and $38 for additional permanent working capital requirement and other indirect costs. The proposed IFC investment consists of: - a partial guarantee of local currency loans, - A loan for $5 million and - equity investment of up to $5 million. The IFC guarantee amount is $25 million for a guarantee of a local currency loan of up to 13 years.
location_description: Packages acquired a flat piece of land of about 42 hectares at Kasur, which is about 70 km from the existing plant in Lahore, for the project. The project site is in a rural area and the distance for the straw transportation is shorter than the current site in Lahore. There is a good underground water resource, and about 30,000 m3/day of fresh water consumption will be supplied from four deep well pumps. A public drainage canal is running next to the plant site. The site is close to the public grid and the public substation. The natural gas main supply line is 12 km away from the site. The site is accessible from the main road network.

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: Kronostar (the company or the project) is 100% owned by Krono Holding AG since early 2002. The AOO Sharjadrew combine dates back to early 1900’s with a construction of a saw mill in the Sharja, Kostroma region. Over the years, it has established a particleboard factory, and was privatized in 1992. AOO Sharjadrew filed for insolvency in 1997. In 2002, Krono Holding AG purchased AOO Sharjadrew’s assets. The purpose of the investment is to install a new particleboard line at Kronostar. The project has strong business fundamentals. It will contribute to the modernization of Russian wood panel industry, which is currently characterized by old and inefficient operations, and it will have a potentially strong impact on the revival and development of the following components: - rural area of the Kostroma Oblast; - wood panel industry, and - furniture industry in the Russian Federation. The project is supported by the strong expected demand growth for wood panels. Using modern technology, Kronostar will produce particleboard and will add employment for over 100 direct jobs to the existing operations bringing the total direct employment to over 1000.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Swiss Krono Group (the sponsor), headquartered in Luzern Switzerland, a 100% privately-held and well-established company. The sponsor is a European leader in wood panel board manufacturing with operations in France, Germany, Hungary, Poland, Switzerland, and Ukraine.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $117 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to $45 million A Loan.
location_description: Kronostar (the company or the project) has been established on the existing site of the bankrupt AOO Sharjadrew timber production facility in Wetluschskij, near Sharja in Kostroma Oblast, on a 119.5 hectares of land with access to roads and a connection to Trans-Siberian railway. The project investment will be made primarily in the Kostroma Oblast’s rural area.

project_description: United Riceland Limited (URL or the company) is one of India’s leading rice millers and exporters specializing in the premium segment of Basmati rice. URL was established in 1981 at Samana in the state of Haryana, 150 km north of New Delhi by the Thakrar family to export brown Basmati rice to the United Kingdom (U.K.). The company currently sells its products to the European Union (EU), the Middle East and is also active in the domestic market. IFC entered into a $10 million Loan Agreement with URL in 1996. The purpose of the loan was to finance the construction of a modern Basmati rice milling facility on a new site located 25km southwest of New Delhi, in Gurgaon. Since then actual market developments as well as a positive turn in tariffs for Basmati rice has resulted in URL’s decision to increase the project’s scope. The company plans to increase aggregate capacity from 21 tons per hour to an aggregate nominal capacity of 30 tons per hour with a plant design to produce brown and white rice for sales to the EU, the Middle East, other countries and the domestic markets.
sponsor_shareholders: The company is privately held and is beneficially owned by Mr. N.R. Thakrar and other members of his family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project costs are estimated at $51 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $8.5 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The new plant will be on a 25.01 hectare site in Gurgaon, Haryana State, 25km southwest of New Delhi.

country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: The project involves the modification of Animal Waste Management Systems (AWMS) on swine, dairy or other livestock farms to enable the capture and disposal of methane, produced by animal waste. This capture and disposal of methane will generate a stream of revenues through the creation and sale of Certified Emission Reductions (CERs) or Carbon Credits under the Kyoto Protocol. The project involves modification of AWMS on sites in Brazil, Mexico and other countries over a several-year period.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor and developer is AgCert International Limited and its subsidiaries. AgCert has three (3) key sets of shareholders: Andlinger Capital III (43.39%), XL TechGroup LLC (43.39%), (“XLTG”) and the AgCert employees (12.48%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost will eventually be a function of the number of sites rolled out and the ability of the company to raise cash from debt or equity sources to finance the construction of the sites. Under the current business plan, the company plans to construct 1,596 sites at an approximate cost of $120 million. The total financing needs of the company are expected to be about $150 million over the next 2-3 year period. In addition to the up to $15 million from IFC, $10 million from the existing shareholders, the company is planning to raise a total of $75 million in a combination of equity and debt.
location_description: Initially the Project sites will be located largely in Brazil and Mexico. But the company also plans to roll-out sites in other Latin American countries such as Chile, Argentina, Colombia, and subsequently in other countries in Asia such as China, South Korea, and the Philippines.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: Mironovsky is a leading vertically integrated poultry producer with 45% share of Ukraine’s industrial production and 16% market share of Ukraine’s poultry market. The company was one of the pioneers in developing a chilled distribution system to retailers, it sells chilled poultry products (whole birds, cutup, giblets etc.) under a well recognized brand name, Nasha Ryaba, across Ukraine. The project is to expand CJSC Mironovsky Khleboprodukt’s (Mironovsky or the company) poultry operation from the current production capacity of 126,000 tons of poultry per annum to 227,000 tons in 2008. The project consists of expansion of the existing facilities and construction of new ones along the poultry integration chain, including: - crushing plant with increased specialized processing capacity for sunflower (800 tpd), soya beans (110 tpd), and rape seed (60 tpd) and expansion of existing feed mill; - construction of an additional processing plant to produce a wide range of semi-finished and cooked products; - expansion of the company’s own parent stock farms, broiler growing farms and hatcheries; - construction of a new slaughter plant, with processing capacity of 10,000 birds per hour; - expansion of the company’s transportation system for feed, eggs, day old chicks and finished product; and - investment in working capital.
sponsor_shareholders: The project is sponsored by Mironovsky, a leading, privately-owned poultry integrator in Ukraine. Mr. Yuriy Kosyuk, a local entrepreneur, owns 96% of Merkaba LLC, which in turn owns 96% Mironovsky. Mr. Kosyuk serves as Chairman of the Board of the company. He graduated from the Ukrainian Food Institute in 1991 and that year started his first business, a small sausage production facility. Prior to launching his poultry business, Mr. Kosyuk was involved in various business activities, including exports of metals, import and manufacture of furniture, retail trading, and food processing.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $260 million. The IFC proposed investment is up to $80 million, consisting of A Loans of up to $60 million and equity of up to $20 million.
location_description: The main part of the project, a greenfield Mironovsky poultry factory will include a hatchery, broiler growing facilities and a processing plant and will be located in the vicinity of the town of Kanev. The company will also construct a greenfield further processing plant in the vicinity of Kanev to produce a variety of semi-finished products. To supply feed to the new poultry factory the company will expand and upgrade the existing Mironovsky feed mill and purchase and upgrade a feed mill located in the town of Katerinopol (about 250 km south from Kiev). More specifically, the project consists of the following: - Expansion of the existing Mironovsky feed mill to increase oil crushing capacity to 700 tpd, associated investments in sunflower storage (80,000 m3) and corn storage (60,000 tons); - Acquisition and upgrade of the Katerinopol feed mill with a feed line of 40 tph, soya bean processing line of 5 tph, silo for soya bean storage with capacity of 30,000 m3, and corn storage of 80,000 m3, with cleaning and drying capacity; - Construction of a further processing plant to produce a wide range of semi-finished and cooked products with installed capacity to produce 70tpd (18,200 mt per year, upgradable to 36,400 mt) on one line supplied by CFS (Holland). The product range planned by the company includes cutlets nuggets, wings, meatballs, ready-made chicken meals; - Expansion of Starinskaya parent stock farm to be equipped with 4 rearing and 8 production zones allowing placement of 129,000 DOC per production zone; - Construction of a new slaughter plant (Mironovsky Poultry Factory) in Kanev, with processing capacity of 10,000 birds per hour, upgradable to 20,000 birds per hour, and construction of a new hatchery and broiler growing sheds; - Expansion of transport/distribution capacity for feed, DOC and finished products to accommodate the project volume; and - Construction of new offices in Kiev.

company_name: Societe Burkinabe De Promotion Hoteliere Sa
project_description: The project consists of renovating and expanding Hotel Independance (HI) into a three-star international business hotel with 180 rooms, located in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso (BF). In an effort to revamp the hotel, the Government of Burkina Faso (GoB) has leased the property for fifteen years through an open bidding process to Société Malienne de Promotion Hôtelière (SMPH), an existing IFC client. SMPH created “Société Burkinabè de Promotion Hôtelière" (SBPH) for the purpose of acquiring and operating HI. SMPH sees strong potential in HI because of its size and strategic location, close to the heart of Ouagadougou’s business and administrative district. By modernizing, HI would help raise the standard of the hospitality industry in BF. SMPH seeks IFC’s involvement in the project to obtain long-term financing and support for its first investment and expansion outside of Mali.
sponsor_shareholders: SBPH is owned 60% by SMPH and 40% by Burkinabè businessmen. SMPH is majority owned by Mr. Mossadeck Bally, a Malian businessman with experience in managing hotels. SMPH is an existing client who over the past few years received IFC financing to renovate the Grand Hotel and build the Hotel Salam in Bamako.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at Euro 7.5 million equivalent, which includes an Euro 2.0 million A loan ($2.6 million equivalent) proposed for IFC’s own account.
location_description: 01 B.P. 127 Ouagadougou 01, Burkina Faso HI is an existing site close to the heart of Ouagadougou’s business and administrative district.
Company Name: Societe Burkinabe De Promotion Hoteliere Sa

project_description: Nuqul’s core business is the integrated production, distribution, and marketing of hygienic paper products including tissue paper, baby and adult diapers, feminine pads, table napkins, toilet rolls, and paper toweling. The proposed project is to support the Group’s on-going expansion by providing: - funding for balance sheet restructuring and meeting the 2004-2008 $150+ million core business investment program; and - technical assistance in corporate governance.
sponsor_shareholders: The Nuqul Group (the Group, Nuqul,or the company) is a regional manufacturing conglomerate headquartered in Amman, Jordan. The Group is headed by Mr. Elia Nuqul and consists of a conglomeration of 27 companies operating in 9 countries and selling in 47 markets. The Group is a longstanding client of IFC. The Group is family owned, with Mr. Elia Nuqul, founder, his eldest son, Ghassan, and younger son, Marwan, having the largest individual shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed project is to support the Group’s 2004-2008 $150+ million core business investment program. IFC’ financing involves a corporate loan of up to $25 million to finance the project.
location_description: The project is regional and it comprises the Middle East Region.
additionality: The project will adopt world-class engineering and equipment technology that will lower production cost and maintain the highest quality. The Project will also allow Nuqul and third party converters to avoid imports of jumbo rolls and the associated higher transport costs. The Project will create many job opportunities in the Middle East; for example, the Al Sindian expansion will create approximately 100 jobs at average wages that are almost three times the per capita GDP in Egypt. IFC’s role involves the following components: - IFC’s corporate loan would be supporting the financing needs of a Middle East regional player in its strategy to grow its operations in challenging markets. Moreover, IFC’s flexible long-term financing at the corporate level would help the Group in its efforts to consolidate ownership of the core business companies which would require restructuring of intercompany guarantees, and increasing the average maturity of the Group’s debt to have a better-matched asset/liability position - Nuqul’s management has expressed strong interest in IFC’s value-added approach to corporate governance. IFC’s strength in corporate governance is a strong and timely fit with the needs of this family controlled conglomerate looking to go public.

project_description: The proposed Fund is a closed-end special purpose vehicle, structured as a Collateralized Debt Obligation (CDO), which will invest in emerging market debt issues, both in primary and secondary markets. The Fund is expected to be at least 70% invested at target closing, in a globally diversified portfolio of US Dollar denominated debt issues from approximately 33 countries. Pacific Investment Management Company LLC (PIMCO, or the Fund Manager) will manage the Fund. The Fund is structured to offer investment opportunities both to existing emerging markets investors and to credit quality-sensitive institutional investors who can only invest in investment grade instruments. Against the assets of the Fund, three classes of obligations are expected to be issued in the amount of $300 - 400 million: - Senior Notes, - Second Priority Notes, and - Subordinated Shares (Equity). The Senior and Second Priority Notes will be rated by the rating agencies including Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s. At inception, all three classes of obligations will have a 12-year maturity. The assets of the Fund (the Collateral Pool) will consist of a US Dollar denominated portfolio of emerging market corporate bonds and loans, quasi-sovereign bonds and loans, sovereign bonds and loans, and synthetic securities, and include both investment and non-investment grade securities. The exact composition of the Collateral Pool will be determined after the rating requirements of the rating agencies are met. The expected profile of the Collateral Pool is: - up to 52% invested in emerging markets corporate and quasi sovereign bonds and loans; and - up to 48% invested in sovereign bonds and loans. In addition, IFC will require the Fund Manager to accumulate a minimum of 10-15% bucket of primary issues consisting of credits which are one-notch below their respective sovereign ratings.
sponsor_shareholders: PIMCO is one of the world’s leading fixed income managers with over $394.7 billion in assets under management (as of March 31, 2004). Based in Newport Beach, CA, PIMCO was established in 1971 to offer separate account management services primarily for employee benefit plans, endowments and foundations. PIMCO distinguishes itself as one of the most respected names in fixed income management – due in large part to the success of its innovative total return approach. The PIMCO Bond Team has received numerous accolades, including being named Morningstar’s Fixed Income Manager of the Year twice, in 1998 and 2000.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund’s target size is $300 - 400 million. The proposed IFC investment is $30 million in subordinated and second priority notes.
location_description: Location of the project is not applicable. The project is a global fund which will invest in 33 countries. The Fund Manager will be located in Newport Beach, California.

sector: Household Appliances (Including Refrigerators, Laundry Machine, Dishwashers, etc.)
project_description: Established in 1955, Arcelik A.S (Arcelik or the company) is the market leader in Turkey’s household appliances sector, with revenues of approximately $2.4 billion in 2003. International revenues accounted for approximately 50% of this amount. Its asset size was $1.8 billion at the end of 2003. The company pursues a two-fold strategy targeted at the following components: - maintaining its dominant position in the domestic market and - strengthening its position internationally through brand development, export sales, as well as through acquisitions and greenfield expansions abroad. Arcelik has state-of-the-art production facilities, practices advanced production management techniques, maintains cutting-edge research and development (R&D) capabilities and has experience in implementing new technologies and launching innovative products. In 2002, Arcelik started to develop operational and commercial bases outside Turkey with the acquisition of Romania’s only producer of refrigerators and the purchase of five West European brands. The project supports this strategy through helping the company implement a number of corporate-wide initiatives, including those related to the modernization and capacity increases of existing plants, R&D, information technology, production and the establishment of a green-field washing machine plant in Russia.
sponsor_shareholders: The project will be implemented by Arcelik. Arcelik is 57.3% owned by Koc Group, a leading Turkish industrial conglomerate with investments in consumer durables, automotive, financial services, energy and trade and services. The Burla Group holds 22.3% of Arcelik, while the remaining 20.4% is publicly traded on the Istanbul Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Arcelik would use the IFC financing to fund part of its corporate investment program estimated at €285 million ($379 million). The IFC financing is a loan package consisting of an €80 million ($106.4 million) for IFC’s own account and a loan of up to €80 million ($106.4 million) on the account of participants.
location_description: Arcelik is headquartered in Cayirova, Turkey, approximately 50 kilometers from Istanbul, with 8 other production facilities located in the Istanbul area, Eskisehir, Ankara, Tekirdag (Cerkezkoy), and Bolu in Turkey and Gaesti in Romania. Manufacturing facilities consist of washing machine, refrigerator, cooking appliance, vacuum cleaner, dishwasher, electrical motors, and compressor plants ranging in areas from 18,000 to 57,000 m2/plant. The greenfield washing machine plant contemplated by Arcelik’s corporate investment program will be built on a site located in an industrial zone in the vicinity of a large city in the European part of Russia. Currently, the company is in the process of making its choice among several potential sites.

company_name: Yantai North Andre Juice Co., Ltd.
sector: Fruit and Vegetable Preservation or Processing (Canning, Freezing, Drying, Jams, etc.)
project_description: Yantai North Andre Juice Co., Ltd. (North Andre or the company) is one of China’s leading producers and exporters of apple juice concentrate (AJC). Established in 1996, North Andre has become a major global AJC participant with total processing capacity in excess of 150,000 tons per season. Its net sales rose about 55% in 2003 to $44.0 million and based on year-to-day figures continue to grow robustly in 2004. North Andre is listed on the Growth Enterprise Market of the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong. North Andre has been pursuing an expansion and diversification business strategy within the apple juice and related-products sector. It upgraded and/or expanded plants in the following provinces: Shannxi, Shandong (two plants), and Jiangsu.
sponsor_shareholders: North Andre’s main shareholders are Glory Cause (32.2%), Donghua Fruit (16.8%), Donghua BVI (10.4%), Chengdu Uni-President (5.0%), Mr.Yung Ka Hee Titus (2.0%) and Beijing RAJ (0.7%). The remaining 32.9% shares are held by public shareholders. Glory Cause and Beijing RAJ are controlled by Creat Group, a limited liability company incorporated in China in 1996 with investments in the hi-tech, electronics, communications, pharmaceutical and agribusiness industries. Creat Group’s largest single shareholder (52%) is Mr. Zheng Yue Wen, who serves as North Andre’s Chairman. Donghua Fruit and Donghua BVI were founded by Mr. Wang An, who is also North Andre’s CEO. Donghua Fruit is a diversified company whose scope of activities includes agribusiness, construction materials, and general merchandise.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $95.0 million, including working capital of $43.5 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $15 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Headquartered in Yantai city, Shandong province, North Andre now has four wholly owned operating plants all within proximity to major apple production regions. The four plant locations are: - Muping district of Yantai city, Shandong province; - Baishui county of western Shannxi province; - Longkou county of Shandong province; and - Feng county of Xuzhou city, Jiangsu province.
Company Name: Yantai North Andre Juice Co., Ltd.

project_description: The proposed $150 million project is to establish a Tourism Loan Facility which will provide IFC with a flexible platform from which to support promptly and efficiently tourism companies severely affected by the recent tsunami disaster in South-East Asia. The Facility will be utilized for financing the following components: - the reconstruction/rehabilitation of tourism properties damaged by the tsunamis; - the increased working capital requirements of tourism companies due to slowdown in demand in the region; - the acquisition, by long-term strategic investors, of hotels and other lodging properties that have suffered damages and face uncertain market prospects as a result of the tsunamis; and - the debt restructuring of tourism companies facing financial difficulties due to damaged property and/or slow-down in demand. The Facility will assist established hotel companies in the tourism sector in Thailand, Sri Lanka, Maldives, and Indonesia, who thanks to their distinctive brands, ability to develop attractive properties and well-established relationships with tour operators, will be important in restoring confidence and bringing tourism back to the affected destinations. It is anticipated that the proposed Facility will enable IFC to support a number of companies (the “Sub-projects”) in the Maldives, Sri Lanka, Thailand and other affected countries, and thus ensure diversification of the portfolio. Full utilization of the proposed Facility is anticipated within one year.
sponsor_shareholders: Project sponsors and major shareholders have yet to be determined. It is expected that the proposed Facility will enable IFC to support about 4-5 companies.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project is to establish a tourism loan facility of up to $150 million equivalent that will provide IFC with a flexible platform from which to support promptly and efficiently tourism companies affected by the recent tsunami disaster in South-East Asia. The total project cost is estimated at about $400 million. The proposed IFC investment would be up to $150 million equivalent.
location_description: Tourism companies affected by the tsunami disaster in South-East Asia, especially the Maldives, Sri Lanka, Thailand and Indonesia.

sector: Paper Packaging Products (Including Boxes, Cartons, etc.)
project_description: The project consists of expanding and diversifying the operations of Altyn Ajydar (AA or the company), an existing client of IFC and the leading producer of corrugated carton packaging in the Kyrgyz Republic (KR). It involves the construction, equipping and placing into operation of a cardboard and fluting paper facility with capacity of 8,250 tons p.a., a plastic packaging facility with capacity of 2,400 tons per annum, and the modernization of the existing corrugated packaging plant reaching capacity of 25 million tons per annum. The project will allow AA to diversify into plastic packaging, improve operating efficiencies in the cardboard packaging business through economies of scale and achieve additional savings from import substitution of raw material.
sponsor_shareholders: AA was established in 1995 as a Kyrgyz-Chinese joint venture, and employs 120 staff. AA is owned 68% by the Terehov family and 32% by two Chinese shareholders, Mr. Van Yun Chan (19%), a Chinese relative of Mr. Terehov, and by a business acquaintance, Mr. Lian Mien (13%). Mr. Pavel Terehov is the founder and largest shareholder (20% of shares).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $2.93 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $1.0 million A loan and a $400,000 C loan for IFC’s own account. This is IFC’s second investment after approving in September 1999 a $300,000 A loan to help in the first expansion. The balance of the proposed financing is capital made available through internal cash generation and equity contribution from the sponsor.
location_description: The project is located in existing facilities in the Zapadnaa Promzena industrial site, in the periphery of Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic.

project_description: The proposal is to make an investment of up to $15 million in GP Capital Partners III (GPCP III or the Fund). The Fund has a target size of $200 million and will make control-oriented equity and equity related investments in companies either located in or which have significant business activities in Brazil. The Fund will be structured as a 10-year Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with a commitment period of five years.
sponsor_shareholders: GP Capital Partners III is sponsored by GP Investimentos and will be managed by a team of 8 investment professionals, including 5 Investment Partners. The Fund will follow a similar strategy as GP Capital I closed in 1994 and GP Capital II closed in 1997. GP Investimentos was formed in 1993 to manage private equity investments and its activities today also include hedge fund management and real estate finance. The controlling shareholders of GP Investimentos are: Antonio Bonchristiano, Fersen Lamas Lambranho and Marcelo Peano.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund’s target size is $200 million. IFC’s investment would be up to $15 million for capital contributions as well as management fees and expenses, limited to the investment of the largest other single investor and to less than 20% of aggregate commitments in GP Capital Partners III.
location_description: The Fund Manager is based in Sao Paulo, Brazil and will target investments primarily in Brazil.

project_description: Embraer - Empresa Brasileira de Aeronáutica S.A. (Embraer, or the company) is one of the world’s leading commercial aircraft manufacturers, and is the largest manufacturer located in a developing country. Embraer is currently engaged in a strategically important extension of its product line and consolidation of its position as a global player. The IFC project would help Embraer achieve this goal by providing financing, on commercial terms, for the launch of its program for the new Embraer 170/190 Family of aircraft. The Family comprises four models that seat between 70 and 118 passengers. The company has already delivered some of the first model – the Embraer 170– and expects to receive certification of the other models in the coming years.
sponsor_shareholders: Privatized in 1994, Embraer is listed on the BOVESPA in São Paulo (tickers “EMBR3” and “EMBR4”) and has American Depository Receipts listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker “ERJ”). As of October 30, 2004, the company’s main shareholders include PREVI (a pension fund for the employees of Banco do Brasil) 16.24%; SISTEL (a pension fund for the employees of Telebrás) 7.06%, Grupo Bozano (privately-held Brazilian investment group) 10.61%, Dassault Aviation 2.19%, Thales 2.19%, EADS 2.19%, Snecma 1.16%, and the Government of Brazil 0.33%, with a “free float” of approximately 51.16% ( BOVESPA – 14.15% and NYSE – 37.02% ). Embraer reported $2.1 billion in net revenue in 2003, of which about 85% was derived from manufacturing passenger aircraft, consisting primarily of ERJ 145 jet Family that seat between 37 to 50 passengers. With about 95% of its net revenue derived from exports, Embraer is consistently among the country’s largest exporters. More information about the company can also be found on its internet site ( http://www.embraer.com ).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The end-stage development program for the Embraer 170/190 Family includes the certification and modification process and is estimated to cost approximately $280 million. IFC is considering arranging long-term financing ranging from $75 million to $150 million. The Financing would take the form of: - an “A Loan” of about $30 million, for IFC’s own account; and - a syndicated “B Loan” for the account of international, commercial banks representing the balance.
location_description: All of the company’s production facilities are located in the State of São Paulo, Brazil. The company’s primary production facility is located in São José dos Campos, and Embraer also has facilities in Gavião Peixoto and Botucatú.

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: OOO Kronospan PB would be a limited liability company incorporated in the Russian Federation. The proposed investment program is to set up: - an up to 650,000 cubic meters per year particle board line, and - melamine saturation and facing lines.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Kronospan Holdings Limited, which is the parent company for the Eastern European operations of the Kronospan Group (Kronospan or the group). The borrower is 100%-owned by Kronospan Russia Limited, the parent company for Russian operations of the group. Kronospan is privately owned and is a European leader in wood panel board manufacturing.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at Euro 142 million. The proposed IFC investment would be up to Euro 70 million loan for IFC’s own account including an already committed Euro 42 million loan (Project #21562).
location_description: The project facilities will be located at Egorievsk on a 132 hectare plot about 100 km south-east of Moscow in a recently established industrial zone. The site has good road and rail connections in vicinity and has access to electricity and natural gas.

company_name: CSRC China (Ma'anshan) Chemical Industry Co., Ltd.
project_description: China Synthetic Rubber Corporation (CSRC or the company) is a carbon black manufacturing company with the capacity to produce 60,000 tons per year (tpy) of carbon black and generate up to 9 MW of power from its co-generation facility, located in Maanshan City, Anhui Province, China. The company has requested IFC financing for the debottlenecking and expansion of the existing plant to increase its production capacity to 125,000 tpy. The project will consist of two phases: - debottlenecking of the existing facility (phase I); - installing an additional production line and 12 MW of new power co-generation and building a new warehouse (phase II). IFC financed the company’s original project in 2001 (IFC/R2001-0140), which was to upgrade and modernize the obsolete carbon black plant acquired from a state-owned enterprise, providing $9.0 million in A loan and $2.0 million in equity for a 13.8% shareholding in the company.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is China Synthetic Rubber Corporation (CSRC), that owns 86.2% of the company indirectly through its wholly owned subsidiary, CSRC Singapore Limited. Founded in 1973, CSRC is one of the world’s leading carbon black producers and technology providers. CSRC became a listed company in 1986 and its shares are freely traded on the Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $27.4 million. IFC’s proposed investment is $12 million, consisting of an equity investment of up to $1.0 million and an A loan of up to $11.0 million.
location_description: The project is located in the industrial area of Cihu, a major industrial complex in the northwest section of Maanshan city in the Chinese province of Anhui, about 300 km west of Shanghai. At present, the area of the project site is approximately 137,158 m2 covering the carbon black production lines, power generation facility, feedstock storage, warehouse and administration buildings. As an expansion program, the project company may purchase the land use rights for an additional three adjacent lands to the current project site totaling 47,533 m2 some of which will cover two new production lines and the remainder reserved for future use.
Company Name: CSRC China (Ma'anshan) Chemical Industry Co., Ltd.

project_description: DCM Shriram Consolidated Limited (DSCL or the company) proposes to invest $74.2 million towards capacity expansion and upgrade of the environmental standards of its plants in the Indian state of Rajasthan. The project primarily involves expansion of the company’s PVC and carbide production capacities, the replacement of the company’s chlor-alkali production technology from mercury cells to the environment friendly and efficient membrane cells and supporting capital expenditure to increase captive power generation and expansion of the company’s network of agro-product retail stores. The Delhi Cloth Mills Co. Ltd. (DCM) was founded in 1889 by late Sir Shriram as a spinning mill in Delhi. Subsequently, it expanded and diversified into several industries, including sugar, chemicals, engineering and food products. In 1990, DSCL was carved out as a diversified public limited corporation based in north India with two core businesses: - plastics & chemicals, and - agro-business. DSCL is headquartered in New Delhi and has annual revenues of about $315 million. The company’s production facilities in India are located in Kota (Rajasthan), Bharuch (Gujarat), Ajbapur (Uttar Pradesh), and Rupapur (Uttar Pradesh).
sponsor_shareholders: DSCL and its subsidiaries are owned by three Shriram brothers – the sponsors are Messrs. Ajay Shriram, Vikram Shriram and Ajit Shriram who have a 52.7% shareholding in DSCL. The balance shares are held by the general public (14.1%), banks and financial institutions (22.6%) and other corporates (10.6%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at about $74.2 million which includes incremental working capital and contingencies. The main project components are: - expansion of DSCL’s PVC resin and carbide capacities; - replacement of the Company’s chlor-alkali plant with more environment friendly membrane cell technology; - adding a 40MW power plant; and - expanding DSCL’s network of rural retail stores. Most of the project investment will be made at the company’s existing integrated manufacturing complex at Kota. The proposed IFC investment is $30 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project is located at the company’s existing facilities at Kota, in the Indian state of Rajasthan. Kota, an industrial city about 400 km south of Delhi on the main Mumbai-Delhi railway line, is well connected to both cities: four and a half hours by train to Delhi and overnight to Mumbai. The plant site is 3 km from the main Bombay-Delhi line, has its own siding and is linked to the country’s large railway network, facilitating dispatch of finished goods such as cement, urea and other products to customers as well as to bring in naphtha and other bulk feedstock.
