Though the nearest airport is about 240 km away at Jaipur, Kota is also well connected by road as it is on one of the major north-south national highways, giving the company additional logistical flexibility.

project_description: PT Ecogreen Oleochemicals Limited (Ecogreen or the company), an IFC portfolio company, was established in 1989 and has grown to become the world’s fourth largest and Indonesia’s only producer of natural fatty alcohols. At present, Ecogreen has a production capacity of 122,000 tpa and annual sales of about $105 million. Ecogreen has two production plants in Indonesia, located at Batam and Medan, and affiliated marketing and distribution companies in Singapore, Germany and the USA. The company exports 95% of its production, about 50% to Asia-Pacific and about 20% each to the Americas and Europe. Ecogreen also sells fatty acids, methyl esters and glycerin, which are by-products of the fatty alcohol production process. Ecogreen plans to implement a $50 million project in which IFC will invest up to $25 million as an A Loan, to add 70,000 tonnes per annum (tpa) to its existing fatty alcohol production facility at Batam, Indonesia using technology from Davy, UK. The project would allow the company to improve its international competitiveness.
sponsor_shareholders: The company is owned through a holding company structure whose shareholders are: Messrs. Eddy William Katuari and Fifi Sutanto (representing the Wings group) 47.7%; Mr. Jimmy Masrin and PT Lautan Luas Tbk (representing the Lautan Luas group) 33.3% and Mr. Robert Budi Hartono (representing the Djarum group) 19%. The main sponsor of the company is the Wings group, which is one of Indonesia’s largest producer and marketer of soaps and detergents. The Wings Group has seven main business activities: consumer products; packaging; chemicals; building materials; real estate; agribusiness and financial services. Of these, the consumer products business is the largest in annual turnover. IFC has existing relationships with three of the Wings group companies (PT Sayap, PT Wings, PT Gawi and PT Prakars). The other two members of the consortium are the Djarum group, one of the largest Indonesian cigarette manufacturers, and the Lautan Luas group, which is Indonesia’s leading distributor and manufacturer of basic and specialty chemicals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be about $50 million including contingencies but excluding incremental working capital. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan for IFC’s own account in an amount of up to $25 million.
location_description: The plant will be established at the company’s existing facilities in Batam, Indonesia. Batam is an island off the coast of Singapore connected to it by an hour-long ferry ride. It is also connected by flights to Medan and Jakarta, both about one hour away. The Batam plant is a stand-alone facility with independent power, steam generation and water supply. At Batam, the raw material, diesel, LPG and other feedstock are unloaded through an adjacent public jetty through dedicated pipelines. This jetty is capable of berthing three 12-meter draft vessels simultaneously. The jetty and related facilities also allow movement of material through isocontainers and dry containers.

project_description: Ransa Comercial S. A. (Ransa or the company) is an integrated logistics service company based in Lima, which specializes in handling, storage, and distribution of grains, frozen food, and other general cargoes as well as providing services such as in-bond warehouses, shipping agency, stevedoring services, and trucking. Ransa is the market leader in the distribution and storage business in Peru. It is a 100% subsidiary of the Romero Group. In 1999 IFC approved a $10 million loan (IFC/R99-116) for Ransa’s expansion and improvement of operating efficiency; as of December 31, 2004, $6.25 million remains outstanding to IFC. Ransa’s consolidated USD revenue has grown at an average of 15.2% p.a. from 2000 to 2003, storage volume has increased by 7.8% p.a. for the same period. To accommodate this growth Ransa has been leasing space from Minka, a sister company operating wholesale and retail space in Lima. Minka has given notice to Ransa that it will terminate the lease in 2004. As a result of the lease termination, and to accommodate future growth, Ransa has now decided to embark on a capacity expansion project consisting mainly of the following components: - the construction of a 13,500-m² warehouse for general merchandise, - the construction of a 15,000-m² warehouse for distribution, and - the acquisition of a 86,600-m² plot. In addition the project includes investments in MIS, other capital expenditures, and debt refinancing.
sponsor_shareholders: - The Romero Group: Headed by Mr. Dionisio Romero, the Romero Group (the Group or the Romero Group) is Peru’s largest private business group with the following major holdings: Banco de Crédito, the country’s largest commercial bank; Alicorp (a large agroindustrial company operating in the following segments: wheat flour, pastas and rice; edible oil, margarine, shortenings and laundry soaps; cookies and crackers; animal feed; and other food products and service); Palmas and Industrias del Espino, Peru’s largest palm oil estate (5,000 ha) and crusher; Ransa, the country’s largest integrated logistics company; Romero Trading an export/import trading operation (coffee, cotton, mangoes, soybean meal); Industrias de Aceite in Bolivia representing large soybean plantations (7,000 ha), the country’s second largest soybean crusher, and Bolivia’s largest edible oils operator. The Romero Group also has a few other smaller businesses like auto and truck dealerships. Total direct employment of the group is about 10,000 people. The Romero Group is not an incorporated (holding) company but rather represents the Romero Family interests’ consolidation. Only those Companies in which the Family has a controlling position are included in the Group; hence, the financial sector interests’ are excluded from the Romero Group (refer to “The Romero Family Financial Sector Participation” section below for additional information). To date the Romero Group is composed of the following companies: - Alicorp, - Ransa, - Palmas e Industrias del Espino, - Romero Trading, - Industria Textil Piura, - Universal Textil, - Consorcio Naviero Peruano, - Trabajos Marítimos, and - Terminal Internacional del Sur (the latter three companies are in the shipping sector.) The Romero Family Financial Sector Participation Banco de Crédito del Perú (BCP) was the first bank to be established in Peru (founded in 1889) and is now the largest banking institution in the country. In December 2002, BCP acquired Banco Santander Central Hispano-Perú (BSCH-Perú), whose financials are included in BCP’s consolidated financial statements since such date. BSCH-Perú was merged into BCP on February 28, 2003. BCP is 97% owned by Credicorp, a financial holding company incorporated in Bermuda in 1995 and listed on the New York Stock Exchange. Credicorp is owned by the Romero family (18.7%) and directors and senior officers of the group (3.2%); with the remaining shares held by other investors. The Romero family controls Creditcorp with 25% of the voting rights. Credicorp is now the largest financial services holding company in Peru and is closely identified with its principal subsidiary, BCP. Credicorp is engaged principally in commercial banking (through BCP and Banco Tequendama in Colombia), insurance (through El Pacífico-Peruano Suiza), and investment banking (through Atlantic Security Holding Corporation).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated $20 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $10 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Project funding will be directed to investments in Callao, Peru. The investment will be made at Ransa’s 245,000 m² main operating complex located in Callao, close to the Lima’s international airport and the Callao sea port.

project_description: The project consists of a $50 million financing package to Grupo Financiero Uno (the Group, GFU, Uno, or the company) to support the expansion and consolidation of the Group’s operations in Central America. Founded in the late eighties by a group of Central American shareholders, Grupo Financiero Uno has become the leading retail financial group in Central America with operations in El Salvador, Guatemala, Costa Rica, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama and Mexico. The Group is the largest VISA consumer credit card issuer throughout Central America and Panama, and also offers loans, retail deposits, asset management and insurance products to more than 900,000 customers though six commercial banking subsidiaries and several credit cards companies across the region.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded as a small credit card operation, over the last decade GFU has invested heavily in technology, has considerably expanded its delivery network and has established regulated commercial banks in Guatemala (1990), Nicaragua (1992), Honduras (1993) and more recently in El Salvador (1994), Panama, Costa Rica and Mexico. The group has since been harnessing existing synergies in information technology, regional delivery, marketing and best practices in order to position itself for rapid growth within the region. The Group is controlled by a group of Central American shareholders led by Dr. Ernesto Fernandez Holmann. With more than 35 years of banking and credit card business experience, Mr. Fernandez is one of the top bankers in Central America. Dr. Fernandez Holmann holds a Doctorate Degree in Economics from Harvard University as well as a Bachelor’s Degree in Economics from Georgetown University. Prior experience includes President of Wells Fargo Interamerican Bank, Miami, Florida; Executive Director of Comercial Santa Carla, S.A., Panama; Executive Director & CEO of Banco de America, Managua, Nicaragua. Day to day operations are managed by a team of professional managers, most of them educated in the US.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $50 million.
location_description: The project involves a major regional banking and financial group which operates across Central America, with centers in El Salvador, Guatemala, Panama, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica.

project_description: IFC is considering an equity commitment of up to $5 million to the BioVeda China Fund (the fund or BioChina), an investment vehicle to be established by a select group of institutional investors, to invest in Chinese biotech and life sciences companies. The Fund will be managed by BioVeda Capital (the manager or BioVeda), a Singapore/US headquartered biotech investment firm which currently manages a $32 million venture fund that has invested in the US and Asia. The fund is targeting a first closing in early 2005. BioChina targets to raise up to $25 million to be invested in 3-5 companies to whom the fund would provide both expansion capital and management expertise in order to help to grow their businesses significantly. Exits are expected to be achieved through a stock exchange listing or a strategic sale.
sponsor_shareholders: BioVeda Capital provides venture capital financing to companies in the life sciences with leading proprietary technologies, and outstanding scientific and management talent. BioVeda also plays a role as a business and scientific bridge between companies in the East and West, linking finance and technology between the two markets. With offices in Singapore and San Francisco, BioVeda has a combination of broad scientific and medical expertise, and financial and investment experience to assist investee companies. The General Partners of Bioveda are Dr. Zhi Yang and Mr. Damien Lim. Dr. Zhi Yang has two decades of experience in biotechnology, having held senior scientific and management positions in a variety of US and Chinese biotech and pharmaceutical companies. He holds an M.A. and a Ph.D. in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology from Harvard University. Mr. Damien Lim has over 16 years of private equity and investment banking experience. Mr. Lim received a Bachelor of Business Administration from the University of Houston.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: BioChina targets to raise up to $25 million and the proposed IFC equity investment is up to $5 million. IFC’s ultimate investment would represent less than 20% of the fund’s total capitalization.
location_description: The main legal entity for the fund would be a Cayman Islands limited partnership. The primary geographic focus of the investments would be China. The investment team would operate primarily out of China.

company_name: PALADIN REALTY LATIN AMERICA INVESTORS II, LP
country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: Paladin Realty Latin America Investors II, L.P. (Paladin II or the Fund) is a real estate investment fund which seeks to invest at least fifty-one percent of its capital commitments in affordable and middle-income housing and the remaining capital would be invested in income producing property such as industrial rehabs, retail buildings, offices, etc. in Latin American countries (LAC). Paladin II will be structured as a Delaware limited partnership, with a target size $200 million and an estimated first closing at $100 million. The Fund will seek to make 20 equity investments with average size of less than $10 million, which meet the following criteria: - focus on capital constrained markets; - high value-added business plans; and - clear exit strategies. Paladin’s business strategy mandates for the Paladin team to be involved in the project throughout the entire cycle. This includes: purchase and preparation of the land, acquisition of local permits, underwriting of the property, technical design, construction, sale of property and many other activities that add value to the project. Paladin enters into limited liability partnerships with local partners to execute deals and put in place operating agreements.
sponsor_shareholders: Paladin II is sponsored by Paladin Realty Partners, LLC, a Delaware-registered limited liability company and an institutional investment manager established since 1995. Paladin Realty Partners is owned 51% by Paladin management personnel and 49% by the William E. Simon and Sons Funds Group, LLC. Ten professionals comprise the Paladin team: Mr. James Worms (President) and nine Principals: Messrs. William Dunbar, Philip Fitzgerald, John Gerson, David Gold, Frederick Gortner, Scott Hadley, Jay Hartman, Michael Lenard and Mrs. Whitney Greaves. Paladin Realty Partners has investments in more than 200 real estate assets in North, Central and South America. The General Partner (“GP”) of Paladin II will be Palador Realty-GP, a Delaware-registered limited liability company, and the Fund Manager will be Palador Realty, LLC; both are affiliated with and controlled by Paladin Realty Partners, LLC. In addition to the ten Paladin staff, Messrs. Vincent Carroza (Partner-Mexican Office), Jorj Kalman (Partner-Brazil Office) and Andrew Cummins (Partner-Chile Office) have ownership in Palador Realty, LLC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Paladin II expects to raise $200 million in capital commitments. It is proposed that IFC invests up to $15 million – or 7.5% of Paladin II’s proposed capitalization, assuming the Fund meets its target size of $200 million. Should the Fund raise $100 million (1st closing), IFC’s investment would represent 15% of commitments.
location_description: Initial developments will be located in Central America, Brazil, Chile and Mexico. The Fund is actively seeking developments in other LAC countries. Palador is headquartered in Los Angeles and has offices in Sao Paolo, Santiago, Buenos Aires and Mexico City.
Company Name: PALADIN REALTY LATIN AMERICA INVESTORS II, LP
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: Kuibyshevazot Joint Stock Company (or the company), is the leading producer of caprolactam in Russia and the CIS (caprolactum is the raw material for producing polyamide resins, synthetic fibers and engineering plastics used in textiles, automotive, and many other downstream industries). In addition to caprolactam, the company also produces ammonia, nitrogenous fertilizers and industrial gases. The company is currently executing an investment program aimed at refurbishing, upgrading and expanding its production facilities; the investment to date has been mainly financed by the company’s own resources, a domestic corporate bond issue and a local Russian bank. Kuibyshevazot has a strong credit history and in September 2004 it was given an A+ national scale credit rating by the AK&M-RASO Rating Consortium. IFC has been requested to provide a corporate loan to Kuibyshevazot to help refinance the bond and fund the company’s ongoing capital expenditure program.
sponsor_shareholders: As was common during that time, Kuibyshevazot started its operations in 1965 as a state-owned enterprise (SOE). It was subsequently privatized through an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP). At present, the senior management of Kuibyshevazot owns about 30% of all shares outstanding, while middle management owns an additional 23%. The rest are distributed among other current or former employees.
location_description: The company is located in an industrial area in Togliatti, Samara region, Russian Federation. It is easily accessible by rail, road and river transportation.

company_name: BARING FINTECH PRIVATE EQUITY FUND III LP
project_description: The proposal is to make a $20 million investment in the $350 million Baring Vostok Private Equity Fund III (BVPEF III or the Fund). The Fund will be managed by Baring Vostok Capital Partners Limited (BVCP or the Fund Manager) and will target investments principally in Russia, Ukraine, and, where opportunities arise, in other CIS and Baltic countries. The Fund will be structured as a 10-year Guernsey limited partnership with a commitment period of five years. During the commitment period the management fee is expected to be 2.0% p.a. of total commitments.
sponsor_shareholders: BVCP currently manages three funds in which IFC has an investment: First NIS Fund ($160 million, IFC = $15 million), NIS Restructuring Facility (NISRF) ($15 million, IFC =$10 million) and Baring Vostok Private Equity Fund (BVF) ($205 million, IFC = $15 million). BVCP consists of eight investment partners, headed by Mike Calvey as the founding partner and six principals, project managers and analysts. All members of the investment team live in Moscow. Each investment partner has 10 years of business or investment experience in Russia and CIS, with a focus on various industries and sectors. The investment team also draws on expertise within the Baring Private Equity Partners International network.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund Manager expects the final size of the Fund to be $350 million. IFC’s investment would be the lesser of $20 million or 20% of total commitments to the Fund.
location_description: The Fund Manager is based in Moscow, Russia and will target investments principally in Russia, Ukraine, and, where opportunities arise, in other CIS and Baltic countries.
Company Name: BARING FINTECH PRIVATE EQUITY FUND III LP

project_description: The project involves launching an 8-year, $34 million forestry fund (the Lignum Forestry Fund or the Fund) that will acquire approximately 20,000 hectares of standing radiata pine trees and will plant up to 30,000 hectares of radiata pine and eucalyptus globulus under long-term land-use right agreements with small and medium landowners and farmers mainly in regions VII and VIII of Chile. The Fund will also subsequently introduce a forestry-backed securitized instrument to the Chilean capital markets supported by the net proceeds of the harvest and commercialization of such forestry assets under long-term administrative and off-take agreements with two of Chile’s leading forestry companies. The Fund’s activities will follow the project design of SIF Sociedad Inversora Forestal S.A., a wholly owned subsidiary of Fundación Chile that sold a long term bond backed by forest assets in November 2002. The Fund will pay an annual fee for the land use rights to plant eroded lands and will also share a portion of the net margin of the harvest proceeds with these participating landowners. The owners of standing forests will receive a negotiated price for the land use rights that terminate after the final harvest of the standing forests. The two major forestry companies in Chile, Forestal Celco S.A. and Forestal Mininco S.A. (the Forestry Companies), will administer the Fund’s forestry assets and acquire the harvested logs under long term administration and off-take contracts. The Fund will be created as a Chilean public fund, will be registered in the Santiago’s Stock Exchange in Chile and will be regulated by the Chilean Fund Regulator (Superintendencia de Valores y Seguros or SVS).
sponsor_shareholders: Fundación Chile is the Sponsor. Fundación Chile was established in 1976 and is a private, non-profit institution, created by the Chilean government and ITT Corporation with the objective of contributing to market innovation and technology transfer, essentially in sectors based on renewable natural resources. It’s main areas of activity are in agribusiness, aquaculture/fisheries, forestry/wood products and various other sectors including IT. Fundación Chile’s activities in forestry sector are wide-ranging and include leadership in developing simulation models for radiata pine and eucalyptus plantations, silviculture and forestry biotechnology and certification. Moreover, Fundación Chile has been actively engaged in promoting the use of wood in construction, improving further processing and impregnation of wood to support the competitive wood processing industry in Chile. In this process, it has gained substantial respect from the Chilean business community and various stakeholders in Chile. Fundación Chile has a long-term relationship with Chile’s leading forestry companies and has historically played the role of honest broker in joint forestry/wood development efforts. For the purpose of the Lignum Fund and future forestry fund investments in Chile, Fundacion Chile has partnered Asset Chile and Independencia to leverage the partner’s investment banking experience as well as fund management expertise. Asset Chile is a Chilean boutique investment bank, founded in 1984, providing corporate finance advisory services in a variety of areas including M&A, strategic alliances, divestments, IPOs and general capital. Independencia is a privately-owned Chilean fund manager specializing in real estate investments.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Lignum Fund will be an approximately $34 million equity fund. It is expected that 4-6 Chilean institutional investors will be the primary investors and IFC is considering an equity investment of up to $6.5 million in the Fund.
location_description: The Fund will acquire land use rights mainly in Chile’s VIIth and VIIIth Regions. The average size of the sites is expected to be around 130 hectares and will be in relatively remote locations. The land use rights targeted for new plantations will be dry eroded areas with little or no agriculture value. The Fund will not acquire any land use rights for natural forest or in regions facing indigenous conflicts.
additionality: By supporting the Lignum Fund, IFC will be supporting the introduction of a long-term financial mechanism that will help small landowners and farmers increase their income and overcome a number of constraints that are preventing them from effectively managing and optimizing the value of their properties, including: - relatively small holdings; - lack of access to credit; and - unmechanized management and harvesting procedures. The project will also have an important environmental impact through the afforestation of eroded land with marginal alternative agricultural use, and will ensure that sustainable forestry management practices are applied to all of the land and forestry assets under its management. IFC’s support and fund structuring expertise will help to mobilize investment from Chilean institutional investors and will also help the Project achieve it’s objective of introducing an innovative securitized financial instrument that can be replicated over time, providing Chilean institutional investors an alternative to invest in the forestry sector while also providing a new financing source to Chile’s forestry products industry.

project_description: The project is to establish the Global Trade Finance Program or “GTFP”, a $500 million trade program, that will provide IFC with a flexible platform from which to support the extension of trade finance to under-served clients globally. The objective is for the Corporation to be in position to quickly supplement liquidity where and when it is needed in the system, assist local banks in every region in developing credit relationships with international commercial banks and to arrange training and technical assistance wherever most needed to improve their trade finance capabilities. The program will respond to on-going demand from clients for the Corporation to support trade-related business, both during normal market conditions as well as during periods of liquidity constraints. The inherent flexibility of the proposed framework will permit IFC to respond globally to shifting market and client needs without implementation delays or extra cost. The GTFP will be built up gradually to ensure diversification of the portfolio. Full utilization is anticipated in the fourth year of operations, however, since this is a new program, the rate of growth could be faster or slower. The program will add significant value to local banks, importers and exporters by creating a comprehensive global network of trade finance providers that can be mobilized to extend efficient, responsive, client-driven service. Trade between countries with a limited bi-lateral trade history can be difficult since financial institutions are risk-averse when there is no track record of successful transactions. Hence easy access to a large global network of banks is fundamental to the success of trade finance. Through the GTFP, the Corporation will enhance trade finance capacity in local banks, both by facilitating trade credit as well as through technical assistance. The training of local staff in the practice of trade finance is an important component of this program. In most markets, this will have the greatest net effect on SMEs which are most reliant on the support of local banks as foreign banks typically focus on the larger transactions and top-tier commercial entities. The GTFP will guarantee amounts as low as $10,000 to ensure the SME sector is well supported.
sponsor_shareholders: Project sponsors and major shareholders have yet to be determined.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project is to establish the Global Trade Finance Program or “GTFP”, a $500 million trade program that will provide IFC with a flexible platform from which to support the extension of trade finance to under-served clients globally. The proposed IFC investment would be $500 million equivalent.
location_description: Project comprises of all IFC regions and is global Project, hence no specific locations.

project_description: The project entails the establishment of Kongoni River Farm (Kongoni), an 86 hectare farm comprising 20 hectares of roses under steel greenhouses. The farm, located in the high altitude locale of Timau, on the foothills of Mt. Kenya, will be implemented in two phases of 10-hectares each. The project represents an expansion of the sponsors existing flower operations in response to market demand and the need for geographic diversity of production sites. Additionally, the higher altitude and climatic conditions at Timau will enable the production of a broad variety of roses including large head, long stem roses which command a market premium.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are Mr. Umang Patel and Mr. Bharat Patel. Over the years the Patels have established a successful network of businesses engaged in horticulture and floriculture production, processing and handling services.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project will be implemented in two phases at an estimated cost of €3.6 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of €1.8 million.
location_description: The project is located in Timau, off the main Nanyuki Road, some 200 kilometers north of Nairobi.

sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: Cosmo Films Limited (Cosmo or the company) is an existing IFC client, with total revenue of $69.6 million, at FY04 ended March 31. Cosmo is the largest producer and exporter of BOPP films in India and one of the top 15 players in the world. The company with an existing capacity of 60,600 tonnes per annum (tpa) has plants located in Aurangabad (Maharashtra) and Vadodra (Gujarat). At present, Cosmo has a dominant 35% share of the domestic market and a 75% share of BOPP film exports from India. The company manufactures commodity BOPP films for print lamination, packaging and special value added products like high barrier film, synthetic film, high yield white opaque film, extrusion coated film etc. Cosmo is recipient of various awards for their R&D innovations and exports. The company has requested IFC to invest equity of up to $4 million, to support and strengthen its future growth plans.
sponsor_shareholders: Cosmo is promoted by Mr. Ashok Jaipuria (sponsor), who separated from the Jaipuria family, a large Indian industrial group, and independently established Cosmo in 1976 with personal funds and a ten-year interest free government loan, which was repaid within three years. Mr. Jaipuria's business group also includes Cosmo Ferrites Limited (CFL), in which Cosmo has a 46% shareholding, and one small company - Sterling Oxides Limited. The sponsor, together with associated investment companies, has a 49.02% shareholding in Cosmo. Other shareholders are Indian and foreign financial institutions (3.84%), other corporate bodies (10.42%) and the general public (36.72%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is $4.0 million in equity to fund the company’s normal capital expenditure and long-term working capital requirements.
location_description: While the company is headquartered in New Delhi, plant sites are located in Aurangabad (Maharashtra) and Vadodra (Gujarat). Both sites are pre-existing and have access to the country’s network of roads and airports and ports.

sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: The proposed project involves an investment of up to $20.0 million (combination of loan and equity) in Fangxin Limited (a Hong Kong-based holding company, the Holdco) and its wholly owned subsidiaries (operating in mainland China) to support the Holdco and subsidiaries (together referred to as the Group or Fangxin) expansion program, which is estimated at $37.5 million. The Group is engaged in the development, production and sale of cosmetic packaging components and offers a fully integrated supply chain. The expansion program comprises of the following components: - improving the current technology, facility and working environment of anodizing process and production; - increasing the capacity of the existing operations; and - the development and manufacture of mascara and pump-based line of products. Successful implementation of the project will allow the Group to become better integrated into the global cosmetic and toiletry supply chain and increase its market share in this growing sector.
sponsor_shareholders: Mr. Chun Te Wang (a Taiwanese national) and his family, directly or indirectly control 100% of the Group.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at about $37.5 million. IFC is considering an A Loan of about $15 million to Shanghai Fangxin Metal Technologies Company Limited, a wholly owned foreign entity located in Shanghai, China. IFC’s equity investment of about $5 million will be made at the Holdco.
location_description: The majority of Fangxin’s operations are located approximately 30 km from the city of Shanghai, in the Fengxian District. The company also operates a facility in Shenzhen. The facilities were built on barren land. Fangxin also has an office in Hong Kong. It owns all the buildings on its sites in Mainland China.
additionality: The project is expected to have a significant development impact as follows: It will help Fangxin become a larger and more efficient packager of C&T products. The success of Fangxin will rely on the industry experience, market access and good track record of its founder and the additional capital and operational and debt restructuring provided by this Project. Fangxin is the top quality producer in China and with the new capital should serve as a benchmark in the industry in China. The country will gain from the development of this industry as the major C&T companies turn increasingly to lower cost countries for packaging their products. IFC’s role in the proposed project could be valuable for on the following grounds: - Transfer of International Best Practices: Through the technical assistance initiative, IFC is helping the Group evolve from a family-owned business to a leading manufacturer in China with improved financial and strategic management and corporate governance practices, thereby enhancing its access to international financial markets and setting the stage for a future IPO. - Provide flexible corporate financing: As a young company, it has limited access to long-term funding from local banks for the proposed expansion. IFC will provide the required long term money to Fangxin that will allow it to acquire the scale its operation needs. Moreover, IFC’s involvement has helped attract additional financing from DEG and encouraged Fangxin’s existing local banks to provide longer tenors to the Group. - Supporting the development of a competitive local manufacturer: Fangxin has expressed the desire to work with international experts that provide both financial and strategic advice that will help the Group to grow from an emerging, family-run business to a global player with requisite skills to exploit its competitive advantages. In addition, IFC also provides the stamp of approval that global players like Maybelline, L’Oreal, Revlon are looking for when making critical outsourcing decisions. - Corporate Governance: IFC, through its proposed investment, will help to instill corporate governance that are necessary for Fangxin to evolve from a family business to a professionally managed company with appropriate organizational structure, internal processes and functions. This would also prepare Fangxin for its future IPO.

project_description: The Biotechnology Venture Fund (APIDC Biotech, the Fund, or the company) was formed in May 2003 to make equity, equity-related and mezzanine investments in start-up and early stage life sciences businesses in India. APIDC Biotech is the first fund in India to focus exclusively on the life sciences sector and will seek opportunities in areas such as health care, drug discovery, agriculture, dairy, environmental and industrial applications all over the country. APIDC Biotech plans to take significant minority stakes and build a portfolio of 20 to 25 investee companies with average transaction size of around US$1-1.5 million. The Fund has a 10 year term and a 4 year commitment period.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund’s two main sponsors are Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation Limited (APIDC) and Dyman Ventureast. APIDC was established in 1960, by the Government of Andhra Pradesh for planned development of medium and large-scale industries in the state. In 1989, APIDC set up in a wholly-owned subsidiary to manage venture capital funds. In 1995, APIDC privatized its fund management activity and organized a call for tenders for the selection of a manager. Dynam Ventureast Private Ltd was selected. APIDC formed APIDC-Venture Capital Ltd (APIDC-VCL), a joint venture between Ventureast (51%) and APIDC (49%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: APIDC Biotech’s target size is $35 million and the proposed IFC equity investment is up to $4 million for capital contributions as well as management fees and expenses. IFC proposed investment would represent approximately 11.4% of the Fund’s size.
location_description: The Fund is currently structured as a trust fund under the Indian Trust Act, and is registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). The geographic focus of the investments is India. The investment team operates from Hyderabad, India.

project_description: Founded in 1967 in Espírito Santo, Brazil, Aracruz Celulose S.A. (Aracruz or the company) is the world's leading producer of bleached eucalyptus kraft pulp (BEKP), which is used by paper manufacturers to produce a wide range of products, such as tissue, printing and writing papers and specialty papers. Its two pulp plants located in the cities of Barra do Riacho and Guaiba have a combined annual capacity of 2.4 million tons, corresponding to 31% of the global supply. The company also has 247,000 hectares of eucalyptus plantations in the states of Espírito Santo, Bahia, Minas Gerais and Rio Grande do Sul. The proposed corporate loan from IFC will to support a number of corporate-level initiatives that the company is undertaking in an effort to maintain its ability to compete at the highest levels on a global basis.
sponsor_shareholders: Four major shareholders control the company's voting shares: the Lorentzen, Safra and Votorantim groups (each owning 28% of the voting shares); and BNDES (12.5%). Various other minority investors own the remaining 3.5% of the company’s voting shares. Aracruz’s preferred shares, which constitute over 50% the company's total outstanding shares, are traded on the Sao Paulo, New York and Madrid stock exchanges.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a corporate loan (A Loan) of $50 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Aracruz has corporate offices in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Pulp production is currently distributed between two sites: - Barra do Riacho in the state of Espírito Santo, where the company operates a pulp making complex that is fully integrated with company-owned eucalyptus plantations. The site contains three mills with total capacity of 2 million tons a year of pulp. The industrial complex includes three recovery boilers, three continuous digesters, five bleaching and drying lines, and facilities for chemicals recovery, water treatment and electricity generation through biomass. Environmental control is ensured through modern systems that treat all solid, liquid and gaseous wastes; and - Guaíba in the state of Rio Grande do Sul, where Aracruz operates a high-tech mill with capacity to produce 400,000 tons a year of BEKP. A third unit, Veracel Celulose (Veracel), is being built in the municipality of Eunápolis, in the state of Bahia, in partnership with Stora Enso (a 50% ownership stake each). With startup of operations scheduled for 2005, Veracel will have the capacity to produce 900,000 tons a year of BEKP.

project_description: Corporación Drokasa S.A. (the Corporación or the company) is a leading Peruvian agricultural and industrial conglomerate with three core activities: - the manufacture, marketing and sales of pharmaceutical products; - the production and export of asparagus and table grapes; - and the importation and distribution of chemicals, agrochemical, liquors and health and beauty products. The purpose of the project is to finance maintenance capital expenditure as well as to refinance Corporación and its subsidiaries’s outstanding short-term and long-term debt. The project will be funded through two components: - the issuance of a $25 million equivalent bond and a $5.0 million commercial paper program; and - Corporación’s internal cash generation. The existing debt is the result of a restructuring underwent in 2000 and currently imposes high interest rates and administration costs as well as covenants that inhibit long-term growth.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Corporacion Drokasa, an established Peruvian corporation that started out its operations in 1952. It is owned by local and private South American investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $50 million. IFC will partially guarantee the $25.0 million bond and the $5.0 million equivalent commercial paper program, raising the credit rating of the issuances. The level of enhancement is expected to involve an IFC guarantee of 30% of the bond and 15% of commercial paper respective face values.
location_description: Corporacion Drokasa’s farms are located in Ica. The Corporación has its distribution centers and a pharmaceutical manufacturing plant in Lima.

project_description: Euroventures Management Ltd. (the Fund Manager) is establishing Euroventures Ukraine Fund II LP (EVU II or the Fund) to make direct equity and quasi-equity investments in mid-sized private companies based primarily in Ukraine and in cross-border transactions involving neighboring countries, mainly Russia. The Fund will make investments averaging $4 million to $6 million in a diversified portfolio of companies operating in the unlisted high growth segments.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund is being formed and managed by Euroventures Management Ltd., a private company registered in Cyprus and a representative office in Kiev, Ukraine. The Fund Manager established its first fund in Ukraine, Euroventures Ukraine Fund (EVU), at the end of 1998 with $30 million.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The target size of the Fund will be $50 million to $75 million and IFC’s proposed investment is $7.5 million in equity or up to a maximum of 19% of the total fund size.
location_description: The Fund will be managed by Euroventures Management Ltd. from its office in Kiev, Ukraine. The Fund will make equity investments primarily in Ukraine and in cross-border transactions involving neighboring countries, mainly Russia.

project_description: Proa II (the Fund or the company) is a private equity fund designed to achieve superior returns by acquiring control and/or shared control stakes in undervalued mid-market Chilean companies. Proa II’s target size is $60 million. Proa II will be structured as a “Fondo de Inversiones de Desarrollo Industrial-FIDE”. The Fund plans on making 8-10 investments in mid-size Chilean companies which meet at least one of the following criteria: - being a solid local company with a focus in the local market but wanting to reorient sales to export markets; - being a local company which targets servicing export-oriented companies; - industries targeting local or international markets and whose long-term competitive strategy centers on the development of economies of scales which have not yet been achieved; and - selective companies which received investment from Proa I and are seeking to broaden their businesses through international expansion. In the latter, Proa will have exited its previous investments in the companies before making a follow-on investment. Proa II has an 8-year term, extendable up to two 1-year periods with 2/3 shareholders approval, and a 4-year investment period. The proposed management fee is In line with that of other IFC supported funds. A first closing is expected in late September 2004.
sponsor_shareholders: The General Partner (GP) of Proa II is Proa S. A. Administradora de Fondos de Inversion (Proa S.A), a Chilean joint-stock company constituted on June 7, 1995. The GP has four dedicated senior partners. Combined, the GP team has 30 years of experience in private equity, investment management and investment banking. Proa S.A. is sponsored by and a subsidiary of Moneda, one of Chile’s fastest growing fund managers with $520 million in assets under management. Currently, Moneda manages six investment funds: Pionero, Colono, Proa I, Moneda Deuda Latinoamericana, TOESCA and Chiletech. Moneda partners include Messrs. Sergio Undurraga, Antonio Cruz, Pablo Echeverria and Jose Miguel Musalem, who together hold 80% of Moneda’s ownership. IFC owns the remaining 20%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Proa II’s target size is $60 million and the proposed IFC equity investment is $10 million for capital contributions as well as management fees and expenses. IFC proposed investment represents 17% of the Fund’s size.
location_description: The Fund will be structured as a “Fondo de Inversiones de Desarrollo Industrial-FIDE” in Santiago de Chile. The geographical focus of the investment is Chile. The investment team will be operating from the Moneda offices in Santiago.

project_description: Russia Partners II (or the Fund) will seek to make direct equity and equity-related investments in companies operating in the Russian Federation and other countries of the former Soviet Union (or the Region). The fund structures includes a feeder fund in which a portion of the investors’ capital is guaranteed by OPIC, an agency of the US Government. IFC will not invest in the feeder fund and will not benefit from the OPIC guarantee.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund is being formed and is managed by Siguler Guff & Company, LLC of New York and its affiliate in Moscow, Russia Partners Management, LLC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The target size of the Fund will be $350 million and IFC’s proposed investment is $10 million.
location_description: The Fund will be managed by Russia Partners Management LLC, with offices in Moscow, Samara and New York. Russia Partners is led by Managing Directors Drew Guff, George Siguler and Vladimir Andrienko

project_description: The project consists of establishing a new hotel company or "the Company” using three existing properties fully owned by Occidental in the Dominican Republic (“DR”), refurbishing the facilities of one hotel to re-brand it to a higher standard and upgrading the fire and life safety systems of another hotel. The Company will start operations with 1,316 rooms. The proposed project aims to improve the capital and financial structure of the Company to resume its capital investment program in the DR.
sponsor_shareholders: The parent company is Occidental Hotels Management B.V. (“OHM”), a company registered in the Netherlands. The three main shareholders in OHM are Mercapital (30%), “la Caixa” (31%) and Tamar International Sarl (24%), an investment vehicle that in turn is controlled by the founders of the company. Mercapital is a leading Spanish venture capital group dedicated to the industrial and service sectors. “la Caixa” of Spain is one of the principal saving banks in Europe with interests in several sectors including utilities and telecommunications.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $92 million. OHM has requested IFC’s assistance to mobilize up to $70 million for the financing of the project. The proposed IFC investment would include an A Loan of up to $10 million, a B Loan of up to $40 million and a C Loan of up to $20 million. The A and B loans will be invested directly in a Occidental subsidiary in the Dominican Republic while the C loan will be invested in OHM, the holding company of the Occidental group to help Occidental capitalize its operations in the DR.
location_description: The three hotels comprised in the project are located in Punta Cana, Puerto Plata and Santo Domingo. The properties located in Punta Cana and Puerto Plata are all-inclusive resorts while the one located in Santo Domingo is a city hotel.
additionality: Tourism is largely responsible for strong growth in the DR economy in the 1990s accounting for over 554,000 jobs (16.2% of total employment), $2.8 billion in exports (28.3% of total exports), contributing $5.6 billion in economic activity. The government has identified tourism as a key growth sector and given DR’s competitive advantages, will drive to make tourism more up-market in the future. The proposed project, in line with this strategy, will allow Occidental to re-capitalize three existing hotels on a more sustainable basis and refurbish/upgrade one, and is thus expected to promote further development of tourism in the DR. IFC has an essential role to play in the project by providing the required long-term project finance, thus ensuring that investors with a proven track record, like Occidental, continue to have access to the international debt and equity markets thus sending a strong positive signal to prospective private investors in the tourism sector in the region.

country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: Orient-Express Hotels Ltd. (OEH, or the company), a hotel and leisure group owning and operating about 40 related properties world-wide, plans to invest in a number of small and medium sized hotel and tourism projects in a number of emerging markets. The company has requested IFC to provide a long-term corporate loan in the total amount of up to $50 million to the project companies in target countries. The proposed IFC Loan would support OEH’s expansion in emerging markets.
sponsor_shareholders: Established in 1976, OEH is currently 42% owned by Sea Containers Ltd. (SCL), a market leader in passenger and freight transport and marine container leasing. OEH is listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: OEH estimates an investment of $90 million over the next few years for expansion of existing properties and $50 million per year for new acquisitions. The proposed IFC investment comprises a long-term corporate loan of up to $50 million to the project companies in emerging markets.
location_description: OEH is considering a number of new investments in Asia, LAC and possibly Africa. The exact location of these investments will be determined at a later stage.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

sector: Other Vegetable Oil Crops (Coconut, Rapeseed, Peanut, Sunflower, etc.)
project_description: Aceitera General Deheza (AGD or the company) is one of the major agribusiness groups in Argentina. Its core business is oilseed crushing, where the company ranks in leading market positions for soybean, sunflower, and groundnut. The production comprises crude oil, pelletized meals, and refined oil. In addition to that the Group’s portfolio comprises confectionery peanuts, peanut butter and branded products such as mayonnaise, soybean milk, bottled oil, and other value added products. With a total oilseed volume crushed in 2003-04 of over 4 million tons, AGD is one of the largest crushers in Argentina, exporting over 90% of its production, working with about 6,000 farmers and supplying Argentina and 45 countries in five continents. The company has an annual turnover of about $1.2 billion and employs around 2,250 people. The project sponsor, Aceitera General Deheza S. A. is an Argentine agribusiness corporation whose principal activity is crushing and oil extraction from soybeans, sunflower-seeds, and peanuts. AGD ranks among the leading oilseed crushers in Argentina, exporting over 80% of sales, employing over 2,250 people, working with about 6,000 farmers and supplying Argentina and 45 countries in five continents. The project entails assisting the sponsor with implementation of its 2003-2006 investment program that includes: - construction of new warehouses; - crushing capacity increases; and - high-protein soybean meal production.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is AGD; owned by the Urquía family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated $164 million. The proposed IFC investment includes, for IFC’s own account, an A Loan for up to $50 million and a C Loan for up to $20 million , and a B Loan of up to $50 million.
location_description: Project funding will be directed to investments in the Santa Fé, Santiago del Estero, Córdoba, Chaco, and Buenos Aires provinces in Argentina.

project_description: ABAMCO Composite Fund (the Fund or the company) is a closed-end investment fund, which will be listed on all three Stock Exchanges of Pakistan including the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE), the Lahore Stock Exchange (LSE), and the Islamabad Stock Exchange (ISE) by end-June 2004. The investment objective of the Fund is to invest in large cap publicly listed securities, pre-IPO positions, and local currency debt/money market instruments in Pakistan. The underlying asset pool will be composed of: - a minimum 80% of Net Asset Value (NAV) of the Fund in large cap listed or pre-IPO positions with minimum market capitalization of Rs1 billion; and - a maximum of 20% of NAV in debt/money market instruments. The Fund will be managed by ABAMCO Ltd. (ABAMCO, or the Fund Manager). IFC has an existing 4.2% stake in ABAMCO. The target size of the Fund is $73.5 million equivalent, of which $20 million equivalent has been allocated for over-subscriptions at the time of listing. The Fund Manager will invest up to $7.2 million equivalent in the Fund.
sponsor_shareholders: ABAMCO first became acquainted with IFC in 1995, when IFC participated in ABAMCO as a seed investor with an initial 20% stake. IFC played a pivotal role in establishing ABAMCO, the first asset management company in Pakistan. ABAMCO, currently the largest asset management company in Pakistan, is a subsidiary of JSCL, which is the largest listed financial services company in Pakistan. Due to political upheavals during the late 90s, the Pakistani stock markets remained bearish, stalling progress in the development of this nascent industry. Consequently, ABAMCO did not raise any new funds between 1997 and 2002. As the economy started recovering in 2001, ABAMCO explored opportunities in new products and considered raising new capital. During 2002, ABAMCO raised a fixed income fund (UTP Growth Fund) and an Islamic fund (UTP Islamic Fund), and won a bid to manage a pool of privatized funds (ICP Mutual Funds, Lot “A”) by the Government of Pakistan (GOP). Currently, ABAMCO’s total assets under management are about $180 million. In addition to IFC, other shareholders include Jahanghir Siddiqui & Co. Ltd. (54%), AMVESCAP Plc. (6%), Muslim Commercial Bank Ltd. (4%), and Saudi Pak Commercial Bank Ltd. (2%), and individual investors (29%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The target size of the Fund is $73.5 million with IFC’s proposed investment of $5.0 million.
location_description: The Fund is expected to be listed on all three Stock Exchanges of Pakistan including the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE), the Lahore Stock Exchange (LSE), and the Islamabad Stock Exchange (ISE) by end-June 2004.

project_description: PT Karunia Alam Segar (KAS) and PT Prakarsa Alam Segar (‘PAS’), whose affiliates are existing IFC clients in Indonesia, are expanding into the instant noodle business by establishing plants in Jakarta and Surabaya. They plan to set up several noodle lines in both Jakarta and Surabaya by the end of 2004, with the Surabaya plant also producing beverages and seasonings.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor of the project is PT Mitrajaya Ekaprana, a local private Indonesian company owned by several individuals. Mitrajaya Ekaprana owns almost 100% of KAS and PAS.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $100 million. IFC proposes to finance $45 million in the form of an A Loan and a B Loan.
location_description: P.T. Prakarsa Alam Segar (PAS), Bekasi The Jakarta plant is located on an 11 ha site, formerly a textile factory, in an industrial area of Bekasi, and opened in December 2003. P.T. Karunia Alam Segar, Gresik The KAS plant in Surabaya occupies a portion of a larger industrial site of 75 ha located in north Gresik in a developing industrial area. The area was formerly occupied by brackishwater fish ponds which are now being filled as the city expands. The land was purchased from the previous owners on a willing seller-willing buyer basis, and no residents or land users were displaced. This plant started operation in early 2003.

sector: Man-Made Fibers (Including Nylon, Polyester, Rayon, etc.)
project_description: The proposed project is to build and operate an 18,000 mt/yr acrylic fiber plant in Alexandria, Egypt. The project site is adjacent to the operations of Alexandria Carbon Black (ACB or the company), a member of the Aditya Birla Group of India and a longstanding client of IFC. The facility will be the only acrylic plant in Egypt and ACB will provide utilities (electricity and steam) to the acrylic plant.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is the Aditya Birla Group, one of India’s largest business conglomerates with worldwide sales of more than $8 billion in 2002. The Group is a longstanding client of IFC, in Egypt, India and Thailand and Indonesia. Major group companies include Grasim Industries (fibers, cement, sponge iron, textiles and chemicals); Hindalco (India’s largest aluminum company); Indian Rayon (apparel, yarn, textiles, carbon black) and Indo Gulf Company (fertilizers). The Birla Group has an existing presence in the acrylic fiber business through Thai Acrylic, which started operations in 1989. The Birla Group’s existing operation in Egypt is Alexandria Carbon Black, which started production in 1994 and after successive expansions is now the largest single site carbon black plant in the world. The Aditya Birla Group will own 60% of the equity capital of the new company. Other shareholders are: SIDPEC a subsidiary of Egyptian Chemicals Holding Co. owned by the Ministry of Petroleum of the Government of Egypt; APICORP, an investment company established by the governments of the ten member states of the Organization of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (OAPEC) and Saudi Egyptian Industrial Investment Company (SEIIC) an investment company owned the governments of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and Arab Republic of Egypt. IFC is also proposing to be a shareholder with a 10% equity stake.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $68.9 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of a loan for IFC’s account of $8 million together with a $2.4 million equity investment for a 10% ownership stake.
location_description: The 35 ha project site is located in Ameyra, Alexandria, 25 Km from the main port of Alexandria on the Mediterranean coast. The project site is in an industrial zone adjacent to the existing operations of Alexandria Carbon Black., to Alexandria Tire Company, a major local tire producer and to a number of petrochemical facilities.

project_description: Fushe Kruje Cement Factory sh.p.k. (FKCF or the company) is an existing cement manufacturing company, which was privatized in 2000. The factory was originally constructed as a wet-process plant and had total capacity of about 250,000 tons per year. At privatization the clinker manufacturing plant was not operational and at present, the cement factory operates only as a cement grinding station using imported clinker. The project will construct a modern dry-process, 3,300 tons per day capacity clinker plant, and install additional cement grinding capacity and a captive power plant. Upon completion the project will have a capacity of about 1.32 million tons per year of cement. The project will supply the local market, which currently imports 87% of the total annual cement and clinker consumption of 1.5 million tons.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Seament Holding, a private company 99% owned by Mr. Alexander Bouri, which is engaged in cement trading and manufacture, and shipping. Seament Holding is registered in Lebanon and has been in the cement business for over 35 years.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is $130 million. The proposed investment is a $30 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project is located in Fushe Kruje, 35 km north of Tirana, the capital city, on a site adjacent to limestone and clay quarries.
additionality: The project benefits from its location adjacent to low cost local clay and limestone that allow it to produce clinker and cement at a substantial cost advantage to imports. In addition, it benefits from low capital cost and proximity to the market. The project also benefits Albania by avoiding the high natural import costs associated with poor port infrastructure. Other development impacts include the labor surplus received by the 320 workers to be employed by the company, who would otherwise earn a subsistence income, and health and safety training that workers will receive. IFC’s role in the project is to help complete the financial plan, which would otherwise not be possible because of the size of the project and the lack of domestic lending capacity and appropriate external funding sources. IFC’s presence will give comfort to other financial institutions to participate in the project. The IFC will also ensure the project is implemented in an environmentally sound manner.

project_description: Algerian Cement Company (ACC, or the company) is Algeria’s first and only private cement plant, and is an existing IFC client company. The project consists of increasing ACC’s capacity from 2.0 million tons per year (“tpy”) to 4.0 million tpy, at an estimated cost of $187 million (named Line II). The project represents the second phase of the original ACC project (Line I), which was completed in February 2004 within budget and in a record time of 22 months. The project will be a replicate of the original 2.0 million tpy production line which was supplied by F.L. Smidth (FLS), Denmark. It will be adjacent to Line I at ACC’s production site in Msila, central Algeria, 240 km southeast of Algiers, and will share site infrastructure and utilities already developed for Line I. Construction for Line II started in January 2004 and is expected to be completed in 20 months.
sponsor_shareholders: The project's sponsor is Orascom Construction Industries (OCI), Egypt's largest private sector construction conglomerate and a listed company. OCI is part of the Orascom Group controlled by the Sawiris family, one of Egypt's leading business families. The Orascom Group is a diversified group consisting of three main holding companies: Orascom Projects and Tourism Development (OPTD), for tourism-related investments; Orascom Technologies (OT), for telecom, cellular services and information technology; and Orascom Construction Industries (OCI). OCI has three main business lines: - Construction, providing civil and electro-mechanical engineering and construction services for projects in Egypt and the MENA region; - Building Materials, comprising manufacturing of basic and specialized construction related products such as cement, cement bags and packaging, ready mixed concrete, concrete pipes, steel structures, aluminum and glass curtain walling, paints coatings and industrial gases, and - Infrastructure, consisting mainly of the development of an industrial park and the adjacent port facility in the Ain Sokhna area, and a minority shareholding in a natural gas distribution business. OCI currently has investments in 13 companies including: - its flagship – Egyptian Cement Company (ECC), a joint venture between OCI and Holcim of Switzerland, with an annual capacity of 7 million tons; and - Algerian Cement Company (ACC).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $187 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $20 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The plant site is located near route CW25 (Bourdj Bourerdj – M'sila) about 25 kilometers north of M'sila, 7 kilometers south east of Hamman Dalaa. Wilaya of M'sila is in central Algeria some 240 kilometers from Algiers. The site is located on arid (rock dominated) land and the surrounding land is extremely marginal and is not used for agriculture or cultivation. The location was originally chosen based on technical evaluations and the result of a public consultation, including a focus on avoiding sensitive habitats and avoiding land otherwise used by the local population (hereby avoiding any resettlement), while being as near as possible to high quality raw materials. The sponsor has built a new site access road from the CW25 main road to avoid heavy traffic in the nearby settlement (Debil). Private landowners provided right-of-way access for this purpose and were consulted and provided compensation based on a willing-buyer willing-seller basis. There has been no further physical resettlement or economic displacement caused by the initial project or its infrastructure connections and the expansion will be kept within the existing plant area. The limestone quarry, which is in operation, is located adjacent to the plant, while the clay quarry is located 17 kilometers from the plant site. High quality gypsum is currently bought from domestic commodity suppliers (there are several supply options), but might later be supplied from deposit located 180 kilometers from the plant site. The project includes progressive quarry reclamation plans for gradual implementation during the lifetime of the quarries. As an example the limestone quarry has till date had 3,000 m2 of overburden removed and stored for later application in connection with reclamation to create a landscape (profile) in harmony with the existing and surrounding landscape.

project_description: PT. Astra Otoparts Tbk. (AOP or the company) is the largest manufacturer and distributor of automotive parts for cars and motorcycles in the increasingly competitive automotive component industry in Indonesia. AOP has requested a corporate loan from IFC of up to $24 million to fund the $54 million equivalent project which consists of - capital expenditures of $48.3 million in 2004-2006, to increase production and the product range, at the AOP holding company level and at its nearly 100% owned subsidiaries: PT. Federal Superior Chain Manufacturing, PT. Indokarlo Perkasa and PT. Menara Terus Makmur; and - additional working capital requirement of $5.4 million. The project aims to - enhance AOP’s competencies in product and process engineering; and - strengthening its position in the replacement markets.
sponsor_shareholders: AOP is controlled by PT. Astra International (Astra) with 87.3% shareholding. Astra is a long-standing IFC client and one of the largest Indonesian business conglomerates comprising a holding company with operating activities in six business areas: Automotive (its core business which contributes more than 80% of Astra’s consolidated revenues), Information Technology, Financial Services, Agribusiness, Heavy Industry and Infrastructure. Astra’s consolidated net revenue, for 2002 and 2003, was $3.3 billion and $3.7 billion respectively, while its net income was $393 million and $516 million respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is $54 million. The proposed IFC investment is a loan for IFC’s account of up to $24 million.
location_description: The project will be implemented in the existing plants of the company and its subsidiaries in the greater Jakarta area.
additionality: The project will help the company continue to restructure and improve its competitiveness. AOP began this process in the wake of the removal of duty protection and domestic content requirements on automotive components in 1999. The company is focusing on high volume products with high margins and market share. This project will help AOP expand, de-bottleneck and increase its value-added products. The project will create 551 direct employees through out the project companies. IFC has a strong role in the project by providing long term funding that is not easily available in the local market and by creating a “demonstration” effect to encourage foreign banks to provide long term funds to sound Indonesian companies with proven track records.

project_description: Lojas Americanas (LASA or the company) is one of the most traditional retail chains in Brazil with a broad range of convenience food, apparel and general merchandise items. In activity for 74 years, the company has 121 stores located around 18 states and in the Federal District of the country, with a concentration of 62% of its stores in the Southeast region. The chain employs around 7,800 people and sells more than 80,000 items from 3,000 different companies. In June 1999, the company launched its web-based retail operations (Americanas.com), which currently receives more than 1 million visitors monthly. LASA is also active in providing financial services, through its fully owned subsidiary Facilta Serviços e Propaganda S.A., which has been operating in the market since 1984. In 1998, in partnership with other companies, Lojas Americanas launched the Smart Club, the first multi-loyalty program in Latin America. The proposed project aims to finance the following components: - Capital investments to support the expansion of stores in all regions of Brazil, focusing in the North, Northeast and Midwest; - Expansion of Americanas.com, - Upgrade of management information systems and - Working capital requirements.
sponsor_shareholders: As of December 31, 2003, LASA''s capital consisted of 25,568,119,211 common shares (39%) and 39,990,164,491 preferred non voting shares (61%). Both types of shares are listed in the Bovespa - São Paulo Stock Exchange (72% float). Lojas Americanas is mainly controlled by Jorge Paulo Lemann, Carlos Alberto Sicupira and Marcel Herrmann Telles, the former senior partners of Banco de Investimentos Garantia and current shareholders of AMBEV, who own approximately 52% of the company’s voting shares, through the holding company Varbra S.A.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $70 million. Lojas Americanas has requested IFC’s assistance to mobilize up to $35 million for the financing of the project. The proposed IFC investment would include an A Loan of up to $35 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The company’s new stores will predominantly be located in the North, Northeast and Midwest regions of Brazil. A majority of stores will be located inside existing or new shopping malls. Additional stores will also be opened in the South and Southeast region.

project_description: The project company, PT. Indorama Synthetics Tbk (Indorama), is a large international competitive export oriented producer of polyester fiber and filament yarns, PET resin, spun yarns and finished fabrics. The aim of the project is for Indorama to construct, own and operate a 60 MW captive power plant primarily for its internal use.
sponsor_shareholders: The project company is publicly listed on the Jakarta Stock Exchange and Surabaya Exchange, and is majority owned by the S.P. Lohia Group. The S.P. Lohia Group is a well-established Indonesia business group of India origin and has a 51% ownership interest in Indorama. The balance is widely held by mainly institutional investors and IFC has a 7.34% ownership interest. The S.P Lohia Group’s main business interests include textile related business, cement manufacturing, and commercial property development.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $60 million. The proposed IFC investment involves a corporate loan of approximately $42 million to the project company to help it construct and operate the proposed captive power plant.
location_description: The project is located in Indorama’s main production site in Purwakarta, about 100 kilometers east of Jakarta in Indonesia. It will be located on a vacant 15 hectare site next to the polyester plant.
additionality: The project will secure dependable electricity supply to the project company and ensure that the Indorama continues contributing to Indonesia’s export earnings. Investment climate in Indonesia, although improving, remains largely tenuous, particularly for international investors. IFC’s involvement in the project would demonstrate that it is possible to structure cross-boarder financing transaction in this still difficult business environment. The proposed IFC investment will provide long-term financing to support major capital expenditures which is not readily available in Indonesia. IFC’s involvement in the project also provides in-house expertise in power generation which is valuable to the project company.

project_description: Jointly, Carvajal S.A. and Carvajal Internacional S.A. (or the company), the Colombian and international holding companies of a leading privately-owned Colombian conglomerate founded in 1904, whose core business lines include: - paper manufacturing and conversion; - school and office supplies; - phone directories (yellow pages); - plastic packaging; and - book and textbook editing and publishing (the Project Core Businesses). The company’s expansion, rationalization and modernization plans in the 2003-2007 period, to help its Project Core Businesses to grow (organically and through acquisitions), to become leaders in their sectors, and to achieve international competitiveness. In particular, the project includes the following components: - Paper Manufacturing/Conversion: Modernizing and rationalizing its existing plants; - School/Office Supplies: Modernizing its facility in Brazil, and expanding its operations, mainly in Mexico and Brazil; - Yellow Pages: Rationalizing and growing its operations in Brazil; - Book and Text Book Publishing/Editing: Growing its operations in Mexico and Spain; and - Plastic Packaging: Modernizing its Colombian facilities, and expanding its operations there and in Mexico. In addition, the project will also contemplate environmental and social and health and safety improvements at some of the company’s facilities in and outside Colombia.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are Carvajal S.A. and Carvajal Internacional S.A., respectively the local and international holding entities of the company. Both these holdings are privately-held and registered in Colombia, with the former having its principal business in Colombia, and the latter extending throughout the Latin American region, and with some operations in the US and Spain. Carvajal S.A. is 64.2% owned by members of the Carvajal family of Colombia, and 35.8% by the Fundacion Carvajal and the Fundación Hernando Carvajal B, foundations set up by the Carvajal family in 1961 to do philanthropic / charitable work in Cali, Colombia. Carvajal Internacional S.A. is wholly owned by the Carvajal family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: To be determined.
location_description: The company is headquartered in Cali, Colombia and has operations across 14 sectors in 17 countries throughout Latin America, the United States and Spain, with approximately 36% of its revenue derived from outside Colombia. The intended project investments are expected to be made across several countries for each of the project Core Businesses as follows: - Paper Manufacturing and Conversion: investments will be made at the facilities outside Cali, Colombia; - School and Office Supplies: Capex will be used to modernize/grow the existing facilities in Colombia, Brazil and Mexico, and to expand in Peru, Chile and Brazil; - Yellow Pages: Modernize/expand operations in Brazil, - Book and Text Book Editing/Publishing: Expand operations in Spain and Mexico, and - Plastic Packaging: Expansion in Colombia and potentially building of a new ground-up facility in Mexico.
additionality: The project, which will improve the operational performance of each of Carvajal’s Project Core Businesses, will have several beneficial impacts: - Employment and growth: increased output, productivity and associated rise in income in the relevant countries. This is especially relevant in poor / underprivileged areas south of Cali, which is in the conflict area and which otherwise offers few employment options; - Regional Focus: Carvajal is embarking on a program that will result in investments in most Latin American countries, including those which have limited access to capital markets (such as Central America), and those in which private sector investments have decreased substantially, such as Brazil; - High-quality products / services: the focus on reducing operating costs as well as improving employee training and product quality will result in competitively priced, high-quality products for consumers in the region. In addition, in becoming a more important player in the publishing/editing business, the company is expected to develop into the preferred venue for Spanish-speaking writers or overseas publishing houses wishing to find distribution channels throughout Latin America. Moreover, increasing the supply of written material in Latin America at more affordable prices is expected to have a positive impact in the population’s reading index throughout the region; - Competitiveness: the investment will make Carvajal more internationally competitive, thereby allowing Colombia and other Latin America countries to increase sales to export markets and improve technical know-how; - Environment: the Project will raise the company’s environmental and safety standards, often times also resulting in cost savings and improved employee morale, and - Community development: the success and profitability of Carvajal will help to extend the operations of the Carvajal, Hernando Carvajal B, and Propal Foundations in the communities in Aguablanca and Caloto. IFC’s involvement with the company will signal a strong vote of confidence for the Colombian private sector. Given Colombia’s loss of its investment grade rating in 1999, recent economic recession, political uncertainty and liquidity constraints in the domestic banking sector, consistent access to long-term investment capital (especially from foreign sources) has decreased even for the blue chip companies. IFC’s investment in the company will provide long-term financing for an independent, professionally-managed Colombian conglomerate and show support for the country’s private enterprises. In addition, IFC’s investment is expected to allow the company to accelerate its investment program, notably with respect to acquisitions. IFC’s involvement and advice is also expected to positively impact the Company’s environmental, corporate governance and financial reporting standards with the goal of bringing them in line with international best-practice standards. The project would also extend support to cross-border market operations in Latin America, including those in poorer Andean and Caribbean countries where Carvajal operates.

project_description: Detroit Belarus Brewing Company LLC, (DBBC or the company) is the special purpose vehicle, which was incorporated in New Jersey, USA for the privatization of OJSC Dednovo Brewery (“Dednovo”), a brewery located in Bobruisk, Mohilev Region, in central Belarus. This will be the first privatization of a brewery involving western investors and among the few privatizations in Belarus. In 1990s, Dednovo used to be the second largest brewery in Belarus and the largest employer in the city of Bobruisk. In September 2002, it ceased regular operations in due to lack of working capital and investment funds to implement the necessary capital improvements. The project will refurbish, modernize and expand Dednovo’s facilities to produce a consistent and high quality beer for the Belorussian market.
