The project will also develop a distribution system and brands for Dednovo’s beer.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is DI Belarus Brewing Ltd., a private company incorporated in Cyprus. The sponsor is 100% owned by Detroit Investments Ltd., which is controlled by Eugene Kashper (26%), Edenbury Holdings Limited (51%) and members of the management team (24%) (collectively referred to as the “Individuals”). Edenbury Holdings Limited is controlled by Arkady Livshits. The Individuals have been in the beer business since 1992 and were successful in turning around three Russian breweries, launching and promoting national brands, and establishing a nationwide distribution network in Russia. The Individuals’ Russian brewery arm, Pivovarni Ivan Taranova (PIT) is a fast-growing beer company which captured 5% of the Russian beer market within the first four years of operations. DBBC will be owned by DI Belarus (77%), IFC (20%), and Lebortovo Investments Ltd. (3%) (“Lebortovo”). Lebortovo is a Cyprus-based company wholly owned by Sergei Levin, a Belorussian national and the CEO of DBBC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $31.3 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan for IFC’s own account of up to $7 million and an equity investment of up to $3 million.
location_description: Dednovo is located in on a large site in Bobruisk, Mohilev Region, 100 Km from Minsk in Central Belarus. The production facility was built in the mid 1970s and is in need of refurbishment. Water is supplied from three wells and is of adequate quality. Electricity is supplied from the grid and gas for its boilers is supplied by the local gas company via pipeline. The site is accessible by rail and roads. With the necessary refurbishments, the brewery has the potential to brew significant quantities of high quality beer.
additionality: The project will be the first brewery privatization involving a western investor and among the few privatizations completed in Belarus. IFC’s participation provides political risk cover and comfort to the sponsor. IFC’s involvement as an honest broker will also provide comfort to the government that the transaction is fair to all parties. The successful and visible privatization of Dednovo will have significant demonstration impacts beyond the immediate sector. The project is likely to be a catalyst for further FDI in Belarus where such investments have lagged. In addition to providing long-term financing on terms presently unavailable in Belarus, IFC’s presence would be instrumental in attracting additional financing from a co-financier or equipment supplier to complete the Financing Plan. The project will generate significant benefits to the Belarus economy and create a strong base for economic growth in the beverage industry in Belarus. It will fully rehabilitate the existing productive assets and upgrade and modernize the equipment to international standards. The project will support more than 300 employees, most of whom were laid off when the plant ceased regular operations in 2002. Additional jobs will also be created as the company develops its transport and distribution network. Through procurement of local goods and services, the project will also establish strong linkages to suppliers and other SMEs.

project_description: Sandora Limited Liability Company (Sandora or the company) is the leading manufacturer of branded packaged juices and juice nectars in Ukraine. Having experienced explosive growth in the past several years, Sandora now aims to improve local fruit procurement, expand own puree production and juice varieties and improve product quality. The company has requested IFC’s assistance to provide long-term financing to support its investment and growth plan. The project consists of the following components: - modernization and expansion of the company’s existing juice and puree factory in Mykolayiv; - modernization of recently acquired fruit processing puree plant in Simferopol; - expansion of distribution and - provision of working capital.
sponsor_shareholders: Sandora is owned by Igor Bezzub, Raimondas Tumenas and Sergey Sypko. 1995, Mr. Sypko, at that time professor at the Mykolayiv ship building university, came up with the idea of establishing a greenfield fruit processing/juice packing business in Mykolayiv, Southern Ukraine, an area with abundant supply of quality fresh fruit and vegetables. After searching for investors, he partnered with two Lithuanian citizens, Igor Bezzub and Raimondas Tumenas, who provided start-up capital for the venture and developed marketing and sales. Today, Merrs. Bezzub and Tumenas own each 45% of Sandora and Mr. Sypko, who serves as the company’s General Director, owns 10%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $30 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $10 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Juice and fruit puree production is located outside of Mykolayiv on a site of a former cannery, purchased by Sandora and subsequently refurbished, re-equipped and expanded to a modern state of the art facility. The plant has installed capacity to produce in excess of 500 million liters of juice and nectars per annum. Electrical power is supplied from the national grid and water is drawn from 11 ground wells 60-80 meters deep. The plant drainage is discharged into municipal system. Fruit wastes are sold for industrial use and animal feed. Sandora recently purchased and operates a small fruit processing facility located in Simferopol.

project_description: Rain Calcining Limited (RCL or the company) is an export oriented company located in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. With a capacity to produce 300,000 metric tons per year (tpy) of Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC), it generates up to 49.5 MW of power from its power generation facility using the flue gases evolved during the calcination and combustion of green petroleum coke (GPC). The project entails expanding production capacity to 480,000 tpy and modernizing existing production lines. The venture is scheduled to reach completion by the mid-2005.
sponsor_shareholders: RCL has been sponsored by a group of Indian investors led by Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy (the Reddy Family). RCL is listed on the Indian Stock Exchange. The Reddy Family currently holds about 50% of the company’s shareholding. IFC also holds an 11% shareholding in RCL.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $18 million excluding interest during construction, working capital, contingency and pre-operating costs. IFC has been asked to provide an A loan of up to $10 million. The remaining is expect will be financed by other financial institutions.
location_description: The Project is located in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. The company has been allotted 42.5 acres of land on a lease basis by Visakhapatnam Port Trust for a period of 30 years from August 28, 1992.

project_description: Amaggi Exportaçao e Importaçao Limitada (Amaggi or the company), an existing IFC client, is one of the leading soybean operators in the Mato Grosso state of Brazil. Brazil is the world’s second largest soybean producer and Mato Grosso accounts for 20% of soybeans produced in Brazil. Soybean production in Mato Grosso is expected to outpace the other regions and increase by 10% p.a. in the next few years. To maintain its market share, Amaggi aims to expand its origination activity, particularly to the east of Mato Grosso, where soybean production is growing, replacing other less profitable agribusiness activities. The project involves the following components: - the establishment of soybean collection centers; - construction of silos with 250,000 tons storage capacity and - refinancing a portion of short-term debt that is currently used to support Amaggi’s permanent working capital needs. The company’s permanent working capital consists of soybean inventory and pre-financing provided to farmers in the form of inputs and cash. The project will enable the company to do the following: - lower its financing cost; - sustain its market share; - establish a presence in growth areas in the east of Mato Grosso. Amaggi has played an instrumental role in promoting sustainable soybean cultivation practices in the Mato Grosso state. Pursuant to the first IFC investment, Amaggi has developed and successfully implemented an Environmental Management System (EMS) that fully complies with World Bank Group environmental and social guidelines. The EMS specifies procedures to ensure that no child labor is employed, no negative impacts to the natural habitats, indigenous communities are present in Amaggi’s own operations as well as the operations of third party farmers who receive pre-financing from Amaggi.
sponsor_shareholders: Amaggi is 100% owned by the Maggi family via the holding company, Grupo André Maggi Participacoes (the “Maggi Group”). The Maggi family has been involved in the soybean business since the 1950s. The Maggi Group is involved in cultivation, origination, pre-financing of farmers and transportation of soybeans and power generation in Brazil. Both Amaggi and the Maggi Group is managed by professionals with extensive experience in the soybean industry.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $125 million. The proposed IFC A Loan of $30 million will be used for the following: - refinancing the portion of short-term debt used to meet Amaggi’s permanent working capital requirements and - construction of the soybean silos and soybean collection facilities.
location_description: The company is located in the state of Mato Grosso, Center West Brazil. Amaggi originates all its soybeans from farmers located in Mato Grosso and Rondonia. Hermasa, the transportation arm of the group, undertakes transport services and shipment of soybeans and fertilizers. Hermasa has a barge terminal in Porto Velho, Rondonia and a port facility located in Itacoatiara, in the state of Amazonas. Additionally, Amaggi has two crushing plants, one located in Cuiaba, state of Mato Grosso, and the other in Itacoatiara, in the state of Amazonas.

project_description: Olam International Limited (Olam or the company) supplies raw and processed agricultural commodities, grown mainly by community and SME producers in emerging countries, to well established regional and international clients. It is a fully integrated company that engages in the sourcing, primary processing, transport, warehousing and distribution of a broad range of commodities, including cocoa, rice, timber, cashew, cotton, coffee, sugar, sesame, sheanuts, and spices. The project is to provide Olam with a $150 million multi-country multi-commodity 2-year committed working capital facility, to help Olam International restructure and increase its working capital lines to provide more flexible financing for its supply chain management activities, and allow them to increase trading volumes from Africa (mainly Cameroon, Ivory Coast, Burkina Faso, Benin, Togo and Nigeria), Asia (mainly Vietnam and Indonesia) and other countries where Olam operates.
sponsor_shareholders: Olam is part of the Kewalram Chanrai Group (KCG), which is held privately by overseas Indian family trusts. From the Chanrai family's beginnings in trading in Nigeria and India in 1860, KCG has grown to become a $1.6 billion (turnover) operation with interests in textile, agro-commodities, software development and distribution, automobile, office automation and property development employing over 12,000 people in over 45 countries. Olam is currently owned at 68.8% by KCG and the management team, and 31.2% by financial investors (including IFC for 9.4%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The $150 million facility will be made of three components : - a $50 million 6-month general working capital facility, - a $20 million 60 days pre-shipment facility, and - a $80 million post-shipment / warehouse financing facility. The facility will be managed by Standard Chartered Bank (SCB). IFC is considering to provide a partial guarantee for the facility for up to $50 million. Other institutional investors or banks will be offered to take risk participations in the facility for up to $50 million. SCB will retain full risk exposure for the remaining $50 million.
location_description: Based in Singapore, Olam operates in 36 countries, including 22 frontier countries.

project_description: The project is a $487 million investment in Jiangxi Chenming a greenfield paper facility in the Changbei economic development zone, Nanchang city, China. The facility will produce 350,000 tpy of light weight coated (LWC) paper and will be built and operated by Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings (Chenming or the sponsor), the largest Chinese-owned paper company, and Shinmoorim Paper MFG Company (Shinmoorim), South Korea’s second largest coated paper producer and IFC client. The project will be implemented over an 18 month period and consist of: - installation and operation of an LWC paper machine with an annual capacity of 350,000 metric tons per annum (tpy); - a Bleached Thermo Mechanical Pulp (BTMP) plant with an annual capacity of 187,000 tpy; - a De-Inked Pulp (DIP) plant with an annual capacity of 136,000 tpy; - a co-generation power plant with a total capacity of 100 megawatts; and - ancillary infrastructure, including wastewater treatment and port installations. This purpose of this project is to support Chenming’s strategy of becoming a major international paper company within the next five years and it will also facilitate Shinmoorim’s expansion in China. In so doing, it will bridge a market gap in the availability of LWC paper in the Asia-Pacific region, which is a limited producer and net importer of coated paper. Given that market trends indicate an increasing demand for LWC paper, local Chinese production of this “light-weight” paper will reduce costs for end-users, especially those in advertising and print media.
sponsor_shareholders: Project sponsor: Chenming is the leading Chinese-owned paper and pulp company and is headquartered in Shouguang, Shangdong province, China. The sponsor was established in 1958 as the Shandong Provincial Shouguang County General Paper Mill, and was renamed Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Limited in 1993 when its shares were offered by the government for a public listing. The sponsor is listed on both the Shanghai (A shares) and Shenzhen (B shares) stock exchanges and its ownership structure is as follows: - international investors (42%), - the Shouguang government (31%), - employees (11%), and - domestic investors (16%). While the Shandong government is the single largest shareholder, Chenming is managed and operated independently by a professional management. Its management and organizational structure is completely separate from that of the government, and the sponsor owns its assets, trademarks and patent rights. In 2003, Chenming had an average of 16,292 full-time employees. At December 31, 2003, Chenming had consolidated total sales of $700 million, EBITDA of $185 million, operating profit of $126 million and net income of $79 million (after deduction of $ 8.7 million of minority interests). Its cash balance was $127 million and operating cash generation amounted to $47 million. In all, despite SARS, the company sustained a sound operational performance with sales increasing by 31%, operating income growing by 38% and net income by 69%. Total assets increased to $1.2 billion at year-end 2003 from $1.0 billion in 2002. The company’s equity grew to $485 million from $409 million during the same period. Chenming will hold 75% of the equity ($129 million) of the project company. Shareholders: The project company will be a foreign joint venture owned by the Sponsor, Sappi Limited of South Africa, the world’s largest producer of coated paper, Shinmoorim Paper Manufacturing Company Limited, South Korea’s second largest coated paper producer, and IFC. Based in South Africa, Sappi is the world’s largest manufacturer and supplier of coated wood-free paper and dissolving pulp, with a total annual production capacity of 5.1 million tons of paper and 3.5 million tons of pulp. Sappi brings a high degree of operational experience to the project. Its market share in the coated wood-free paper market is 24 percent in North America, 20 percent in Europe and 60 percent in Africa. Currently, Sappi has a market share of 3 to 4 percent in Asia based solely on its exports to the region. The Project will therefore represent an important step in Sappi’s strategic objective of expanding its current market share in the Asia region. In fiscal year 2003 (ending September 30, 2003), Sappi had net revenues of $4.3 billion and net income of $149 million. Sappi owns and manages approximately 535,000 hectares of timberlands in Southern Africa. It employs 16,000 people mostly in North America, Europe and Southern Africa. Sappi’s shares are listed on the Johannesburg, London and Frankfurt stock exchanges, and have a secondary listing on the New York Stock Exchange. Shinmoorim is South Korea''s second largest producer of coated paper with total capacity of 470,000 tpy and approximately 30% market share. It has 561 employees and was established in 1978 as an affiliated company (through Moorim Paper and Serim Paper) of the Moorim Group, which itself was established in 1956. The group is controlled directly or indirectly by the Dong Wook Lee Family and associates, who together own approximately 60% of the company. IFC holds an 11% stake, Emerging Markets Partnership (EMP) holds 8% and the public holds the balance. Shinmoorim is listed on the Korea Stock Exchange. Over half (52%) of Shinmoorim’s sales are local with the remaining 48% exported to over 60 countries. At December 31, 2003, Shinmoorim has net (unaudited) revenues of $339.7 million and net income of $21.3 million. Cash generation and EBITDA were $31.3 and $44.3 million respectively, indicating strong liquidity and a good cash position. Its total assets were $387.3 million and its total debt was $159.6 million. Shinmoorim will hold 12.5% of the project company’s equity, representing an investment of $21.5 million.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is $487 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of - up to $60 million A Loan for IFC’s own account and - a $21.5 million equity investment for IFC’s own account, representing 12.5% of the project company’s capital. In addition, IFC is arranging a B Loan for the account of participants and ECA-backed financing up to $180 million.
location_description: The project consists of a 350,000 ton LWC plant outside Nanchang city in the Nanchang Economy and Technology Development Area, in Jiangxi province. The project company was registered in Nanchang City on November 4, 2002 and will be located on a 2,000 mu (133 hectare ) site adjacent to the Chang-Jiu Express Highway on the west and the Ganjian River on the east. It has easy access to several modes of transportation with the Changbei Airport only 6 km north of the site, the Jing-Jiu railway 4 km away and the Nanchang International Container Terminal just south of the plant facility. The project is well-located in Jiangxi, which is one of the most forested regions in China, with respect to both access to raw materials and product distribution. It is close to the significant ports in Shanghai and Guangzhou for exports and is also proximate to key local markets, namely Beijing and Shanghai.
additionality: IFC will play a major role in the supporting the project by - working closely with Chenming to educate the sponsor about international financing options, corporate governance, and financial risk management. IFC has helped Chenming identify key risks such as aged receivables and excessive reliance on short-term debt, and will work will the client to optimize its capital structure, - acting as a honest broker between Chenming and Shinmoorim, its technical partner and the project’s other international investor and - ensuring transparency and strong corporate governance at the level of the project company by taking an equity stake. IFC’s advice will also enhance Chenming’s efforts to attain world-class operations, management and governance at the project company. IFC’s role also includes introducing Chenming to international financiers through the B Loan / parallel financing initiative, as well as providing advice related to sustainability practices, particularly with respect to the company’s plantation effort and environmental management policies. In essence, IFC will play a critical role in taking Chenming from the largest Chinese paper company to a leading and ranked player in the worldwide pulp and paper industry. The development impact of this project will help construct a world-class LWC plant to meet the rapidly growing demand for lightweight coated paper in China. Chenming has a competitive advantage over imports due to lower transport, co-generation power, and labor costs. These advantages more than offset the higher fiber in the Chinese market. In addition, The project’s large scale and high quality technical know-how will advantage it over other local suppliers. In addition, the project will have the following benefits: - Regional Development: The project will result in a large-scale investment in China’s paper sector thereby resulting in increased output, productivity, employment and associated rise in income. This is especially relevant in rural areas such as Jiangxi, where there are relatively few employment options for the local population. In addition, the presence of project facility will help develop the local area around the industrial park, creating retail and other business opportunities for the surrounding community. - Technology Transfer: The project will receive equipment and technical advice from Metso (Finland) and Andritz (Austria), which will greatly enhance the technical know-how of the company, which will help improve standards across the local paper industry. - Environment: The project will greatly enhance Chenming’s environmental management system and controls beyond local requirements to achieve standardization among the Group companies and international best practices. All environmental, health, safety and quality activities will be implemented through integrated management systems at all plants to ensure that the environmental conditions are maintained and that the safety and health of the employees is protected, ultimately resulting in cost savings and improved employee morale; - Corporate Governance: IFC’s guidance vis-à-vis corporate governance, especially as it relates to Chenming’s financial risk management policies, will be extremely valuable to the sponsor. At present, Chenming does not adhere to the stringent financial risk mitigation policies put in place by many of the top P&P producers in the world. By supporting the project, IFC will be able to guide the sponsor on corporate governance policies that will allow it compete effectively internationally, implement standards prevalent among global P&P companies, and obtain long term financing from international investors.

sector: Man-Made Fibers (Including Nylon, Polyester, Rayon, etc.)
project_description: P.T. South Pacific Viscose (SPV or the company) is an internationally competitive export oriented Indonesian producer of high quality viscose staple fiber (VSF or Rayon). SPV is an existing client of IFC. The p-roject is to develop and implement necessary capital expenditures for SPV in 2004-2005 to achieve its objectives of increased production sustainability and self-sufficiency in power, as well as provision of working capital.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor of the project is the main shareholder, Lenzing A.G. Details about Lenzing and SPV’s other shareholders are as follows: - Lenzing A.G. (42%) is a publicly owned viscose producer and operator of an integrated pulp plant in Austria. Ashok Birla Group (32%) has interests in steel, machine tools, chemicals, textiles, cement, carpets, and food based industries. Penique (12%) is run by Mr. Mehta, a diamond merchant of Indian origin, based in Belgium. PT Pura Golden Lion - PGL (12%) is the local partner and also acts as the domestic selling agent for SPV. Mrs. Saparsih Noor Luddin (2%) is a private person residing in Indonesia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $19 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $9.5 million A loan for IFC’s own account. DEG will also provide a parallel loan on terms similar to IFC’s.
location_description: The project company is SPV. Established in 1978 and commercially operating since 1983 near Purwakarta, 150 km east of Jakarta, SPV today is one of the largest VSF producers in the world in terms of production capacity.

country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region
project_description: Construtora Norberto Odebrecht (CNO or the company), founded in 1945 in the northeastern state of Bahia, Brazil, is one of the leading Brazilian heavy construction and engineering company in Latin America, and the world leader in hydroelectric dam engineering. Geographically, CNO undertakes projects in all regions of Brazil as well as in South America, Central America, Portugal, the United States and Angola. CNO is a subsidiary of Odebrecht S.A. (ODB), one of the ten largest Brazilian private-sector conglomerates in terms of revenues and Brazil’s leading service exporter, employing almost 30,000 workers. Since it was founded in 1945, CNO has expanded its operations into 13 countries in Africa, Europe, and the Americas. The project consists of a corporate loan of up to $25 million to support the development of CNO’s small and medium enterprises (SMEs) suppliers and subcontractors in Brazil, Venezuela, Peru, Ecuador and Dominican Republic and other Latin American countries where the company currently has operations or is expected to win contracts in the near future (the countries). It will help CNO fund its prepayment financing (advances) to SMEs and will also have a strong capacity-building component, leading to a long-term cooperation and partnership between the SMEs and CNO, including the provision of direct or indirect technical assistance to the SMEs to help introduce financial, environmental, health and safety, social and engineering best practices.
sponsor_shareholders: CNO, a fully-owned subsidiary of the ODB, which in turn is 96.5% controlled by the Odebrecht Investimentors S.A., a Brazilian corporation whole owned by the Odebrecht family. The Odebrecht Group is involved in two main sectors: - CNO engineering and heavy construction, and - chemicals and petrochemicals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $25 million, which is proposed to be funded entirely with an IFC A loan of $25 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Odebrecht Group's headquarters are located in Salvador, state of Bahia, northeastern Brazil, while CNO is headquartered in the city of Sao Paulo. The company also has appropriate, fully owned subsidiaries in those countries where the project will be conducted. The project will cover Brazil, Venezuela, Peru, Ecuador and Dominican Republic and other Latin American countries where the company currently has operations or is expected to win contracts in the near future. When CNO’s project management locations are located in more remote areas, SME subcontracting and supplier opportunities typically originate from nearby cities, or more generally within the country of operation.
additionality: The project is expected to achieve the following objectives in terms of development impact: - expand SME financing in the countries where SME’s direct access to finance is very limited; and - build upon existing supplier linkages to strengthen the SMEs through technology transfer and other best practices such as labor training, and environmental and financial management from CNO. The project would enable CNO to leave its (footprint) in each of their job sites where SMEs are present. IFC’s role in this project includes: - supporting the growth in Brazil’s infrastructure by strengthening the industry’s key players and SMEs concentrated around those construction and infrastructure projects developed by CNO, who is also IFC’s existing client; - reach the SME sector by using CNO as the corporate intermediary allowing it to leverage its extensive experience of working with its suppliers and therefore reducing transaction costs; and - help CNO formalize procedures for screening SMEs and transfer technology and other best practices to its suppliers and subcontractors.
Country: Latin America and the Caribbean Region

project_description: Lebedyansky Experimental Cannery (Lebedyansky or the company) is one of the leading Russian juice and nectars manufacturers. Established in 1967, Lebedyansky (located in Lebedyan, Lipetsk region about 360km South of Moscow), produces fruit purees and concentrates from locally grown fruits, natural fruit juices, nectars, fruit drinks, and canned baby food under several well-established brands. Lebedyansky supplies markets in Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Belarus. Lebedyansky is undertaking an expansion project to: - modernize and rationalize Lebedyansky’s production facilities; - add new capacity in its core juice and nectars business, - introduce new glass and plastic PET packaging, - improve distribution by acquiring a distribution terminal in the Moscow region, and - diversify its product portfolio via acquisitions of new businesses.
sponsor_shareholders: Lebedyansky is owned by Nikolay Bortsov (57%) and his son Yury Bortsov (43%). Nikolay Bortsov, 58 years old, has had a life-long career in the food industry, spanning technical and executive positions and was appointed in 1981as General Director of Lebedyansky, a flagship fruit processing company in the Soviet Union. In 2002, he was elected a Deputy to the Lipetsk Region Duma. Yury Bortsov, 33 years old son of Nikolai Bortsov, joined Lebedyansky soon after he graduated from a university in early 1990’s. He holds the titles of both the Deputy General Director and the Chairman of the Board.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $87.3 million. The proposed IFC investments is an A loan for IFC’s own account of up to $35 million.
location_description: The project is located on the existing site of the Lebedyansky cannery located in the town of Lebedyan, Lipetsk region and its 100% owned subsidiary Progress, also in the Lipetsk region. Production facilities are state of the art, including equipment from Tetrapak. Both sites have own land, adequate rail and road connection as well as utilities. Electricity is supplied from the grid and gas for steam production at own boilers is supplied via pipeline. Both sites use water wells supplying adequate water quality. The company also has four own sales branches covering the whole territory of the Russian Federation: - Moscow area, - the North West (St. Petersburg), - the Urals (Yekaterinburg) and - Siberia (Novosibirsk).

company_name: ADVENT CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE III LP
project_description: This project is a proposed IFC investment of up to €15 million in Advent Central and Eastern Europe III L.P. (ACEEIII), a new regional private equity fund managed by Advent International (Advent). The purpose of the fund is to achieve significant capital appreciation from a portfolio of expansion-stage and buy-out investments in selected countries in Central and Eastern Europe. The approach of ACEEIII will be two-fold. One focus will be on industry restructuring through acquisitions, and particularly buy-outs, in a size range that will enable the fund to invest €20-40 million. The second focus will be on smaller development and expansion opportunities in the €10-20 million range, particularly in second-wave accession countries, which are less-developed in terms of industry restructuring. ACEEIII follows the proven track records of two predecessor funds (in which IFC has invested), and will be managed by a team whose members, in majority, have worked together for more than six years.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor and fund manager for ACEEIII is Advent International, founded in 1984 and one of the oldest private equity firms. Advent is privately-owned, primarily by the firm’s founder and members of the management team, and has a global investment team of over 90 professionals from diverse backgrounds including operations, finance and consulting. Advent has one of the broadest geographic reaches of any private equity player with 14 offices and 10 affiliates in 25 countries. Globally, Advent has raised over $6 billion in aggregate and has invested in more than 500 companies in many different industries. In Central and Eastern Europe, Advent was the first private equity firm to establish a truly regional network, and has helped to establish, sponsor and train a number of local fund managers. Today, Advent has wholly-owned subsidiaries in Poland, Hungary, Romania, and affiliate relationships in Czech Republic and Slovakia, Croatia and Turkey. Other investors in ACEEIII are expected to include multilateral and bilateral development institutions as well as international commercial investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The target fund size for ACEEIII is €300 million. The potential IFC investment of up to €15 million represents up to 5% of the target fund size and up to 15% of the target first closing amount of €100 million.
location_description: ACEEIII will be established as a Delaware, U.S., limited partnership, and its investments will focus primarily on the countries in Central and Eastern Europe where Advent has a local presence, namely: Poland, Hungary, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Romania, and Turkey. It may also invest selectively in Slovenia, Croatia, Bulgaria, Serbia, Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia, and, with specific Advisory Board approval , in Russia.
Company Name: ADVENT CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE III LP

company_name: Shanxi HongAn Coking Technology Co., Ltd.
project_description: The project company will be incorporated in China as a foreign-invested joint venture. It will be owned 75% by Shanxi Antai Group Co. Ltd. (Antai, a company listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange) and 25% by E.K.S. Investments Co., an investment holding company incorporated in Hong Kong SAR. The project is to establish a 1 million tons per annum export-oriented merchant metallurgical coke production plant at a total cost of $119 million. Coke, made from coal, is a major reactive material for iron smelting and its demand is linked to downstream steel production. IFC is requested to provide a loan of up to $70 million.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor and major shareholder of the project company is Antai. Antai is one of China’s six largest merchant coke suppliers, the majority of which are SOEs, and a small pig iron producer. It is a founder shareholder (with a 0.6% stake) of Minsheng Bank, China’s first private bank in which IFC has made a $23.5 million investment for a 1.22% share.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be about $119 million. IFC’s investment would consist of a loan of up to $70 million.
location_description: The new coke plant will be located in in Jiexiu City, Shanxi Province, China
additionality: Development Impact: The project supports the restructuring of the coke production sector in which China has a strong comparative advantage. In line with the Chinese government’s efforts towards modernizing the industry and phasing out notoriously polluting beehive coke production units, the sponsor intends to substitute sales of coke from such facilities with production from a modern plant under their control. The high impact of this project comes from the sponsor’s strong orientation towards an environmentally friendly and sustainable long-term business model. It will further the development of a competitive local company in the interior Shanxi Province of China through increased industrial activity, job creation, and an increase in the direct and indirect demand for goods and services. IFC Role: Although there has been a significant increase in credit growth in China recently, private companies still experience difficulty accessing large loans on a long-term basis for projects in the interior of China. The sponsor has the ambition to develop into a globally competitive coke producer. Despite its solid reputation, it operates in a heavy industry in the poorer interior of China and therefore needs IFC’s long-term financing which will enable the project to maintain a sound balance sheet. Given its long-term goal of listing the project company abroad, it seeks partnership with IFC not only for the provision of long-term capital but also for IFC’s capacity to share best practices in environmental management and corporate governance.
Company Name: Shanxi HongAn Coking Technology Co., Ltd.

project_description: Schwarz Group (the Group or the company) is one of the largest European discount retailers. It operates two types of discount food stores in Europe: - Lidl, limited range deep discount stores; and - Kaufland compact discount hypermarkets. The purpose of the project is for the company to plan a large expansion program, involving the establishment of a number of new stores and hypermarkets in Central and Eastern Europe to be implemented over the next couple of years.
sponsor_shareholders: Schwarz Group is a privately held company based in Germany, with operations in Europe.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC is considering a loan of up to EUR100 million to partially finance the project.
location_description: The Group’s new stores are planned to be located in selected urban areas of target countries in Central and Eastern Europe. All locations for the new stores will have good access to transportation routes and other infrastructure.

company_name: PROCESADORA NACIONAL DE ALIMENTOS C.A. PRONACA
project_description: Procesadora Nacional de Alimentos C.A.-PRONACA (Pronaca or the comany) is a fully-integrated poultry and pork processor. IFC will provide financing for Pronaca to construct a new distribution center in Guayaquil and expand storage facilities in its Quito distribution center; upgrade the environmental standards of its farms and slaughterhouses, refinance short-term debt; and acquire a local company in the packaged meats sector.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Pronaca, a private company founded some 45 years ago. Pronaca currently commercializes leading brands such as Mr. Pollo (poultry), Mr. Chancho (pork), and Fritz (sausages). Pronaca is owned by private local investors. Pronaca owns and operates pork and broiler farms, hatcheries, processing plants, feed mills, and distribution centers across Ecuador. All the company’s food processing plants have HACCP quality assurance systems and certifications, which is the international standard for food safety.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $50 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $20 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The company’s poultry processing plants are located in Quito, Bucay and Valle Hermoso. The company also has a pork processing facility in Valle Hermoso, next to its poultry processing plant. The company’s distribution facilities are located in or around Ecuador’s main urban centers, primarily Guayaquil and Quito. The company’s feed mills are located in Puembo, Durán, and Quevedo. All the above facilities are located on or have good access to the main road. Farms and hatcheries are located in semi-rural areas for bio-security reasons. Pork and broiler farms are located near Santo Domingo de los Colorados. Additional broiler farms are located near Bucay and in the outskirts of Quito.
additionality: Pronaca is the largest private employer in Ecuador. The project will allow Pronaca to increase distribution volume, thus generating significant benefits through linkages. Pronaca’s distribution of additional volumes and larger portfolio of products are expected to provide its more than 60 independent wholesale distributors with the opportunity to increase profits. Pronaca has led the way in the sector in terms of progress towards compliance with pre-existing Ecuadorian regulatory requirements for wastewater management. Pronaca’s current investment to comply with stringent new regulations is expected to have a strong demonstration effect. IFC will play a role in supporting a locally-owned company by providing long-term finance that is not readily available. IFC is providing technical expertise to assist Pronaca in its continuing efforts to reduce costs and further improve its environmental standards.
Company Name: PROCESADORA NACIONAL DE ALIMENTOS C.A. PRONACA

project_description: The Poteza Fund is a closed-end private equity fund formed to make equity and equity-related investments, through majority or controlling stakes, in companies based in southeastern Europe (the Region). Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Serbia, and Slovenia are the primary target countries for investment. In addition, up to 20% of the fund’s capital may be invested in Montenegro, FYR Macedonia, Bulgaria, and Romania. The objective of the fund is to achieve capital appreciation through active management of a diversified portfolio of companies with high growth potential in the Region. An average investment size of €5 million is expected.
sponsor_shareholders: Poteza Nalozbe d.o.o. (Poteza), the sponsor of Poteza Adriatic Fund B.V. (Poteza Fund, the Fund or the company), is part of the Poteza Group, an established financial institution in Slovenia. Between 1992 and 2002, the Poteza Group developed a successful track record investing its own capital in private equity transactions in Slovenia. In addition to private equity, the Group is active in brokerage services (which was the Group’s first business established in 1989), investment banking and asset management. Poteza has committed 15% of the Fund’s total capital commitments.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund’s target size is €75 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to €11.25 million, for up to 15% of the Fund’s total capital commitments.
location_description: The Fund has been formed as a limited liability company (B.V.) in the Netherlands. The Fund is collectively managed by Poteza Capital Management B.V. and Cielo Azul N.V. (the Fund Manager). The Fund Manager retains a local advisory team in Ljubljana, Slovenia. New offices are planned in Belgrade, Serbia & Montenegro and in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

project_description: Ruchi Soya Industries Limited (RSIL or the company) is the premier company of the Ruchi Group. It is the largest oilseed crusher, importer of edible oils, exporter of oilseed meals and producer of textured soya protein (TSP) in India. It entered the edible oil business in 1986, with primary focus on the sale of refined edible oil in the Indian market. The project aims to take advantage of the increasingly growing demand of edible oil in India, especially the trend toward the packaged edible oil. The proposed IFC financing will be used in two main areas: The first is to finance two new facilities: a port based refinery at Patalganga near Mumbai (Bombay) and a crushing plant and associated refinery at Butibori near Nagpur both in the state of Maharashtra. The second part is to finance the company’s maintenance capex and permanent working capital, and upgrade edible oil plants and refineries that may be acquired. The Patalganga refinery will rely on imported crude oils and will benefit from a logistical advantage over its competition by being located close to the JNPT/Mumbai ports as well as being close to the major regional market of Mumbai. The Butibori crushing and refining facility will take advantage of the local production of soybeans.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Ruchi Soya Industries Limited (RSIL or the company), which is a local company listed on the major stock exchanges in India. Its major shareholders are the Shahra family which hold about 34.6% of its shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at Indian Rupees (INR) 2,762.7 million ($60.9 million equivalent). The proposed IFC investment is a INR 1,350 million ($29.7 million equivalent) A loan dominated in Indian Rupees for IFC''s own account.
location_description: The company is registered in Mumbai, India. Its operations are spread across India with emphasis on the south and west of the country. The two new facilities are located at Patalganga near Mumbai (Bombay) and Butibori near Nagpur both in the state of Maharashtra.

project_description: The project consists of expanding the asset base of SugdAgroServe (SAS or the company), an existing client of IFC, to help meet the growing demand for funding by cotton farmers in Tajikistan. In April 2002, IFC helped establish SAS on a pilot basis to alleviate poverty among cotton farmers. SAS allows farmers to become shareholders and capitalize on profits by financing crop inputs at affordable prices and selling their cotton in greater quantities and on better terms. The initial $502,000 was sufficient to provide crop input financing to about 1,200 hectares. As more farmers want to participate, the contemplated expansion and additional funding would enable SAS to service up to an estimated 3,500 hectares.
sponsor_shareholders: SAS is presently owned by 365 cotton farmers, which belong to some fourteen Dehkan farms in the Nov and adjacent Zafarabad oblasts in Northern Tajikistan. Participating farmers were selected based on their land holding and financial condition. SAS is exploring with IFC the opportunity to expand its shareholding and services to an estimated 1,500 additional farmer-owners.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $1.0 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $500,000 A loan for IFC’s own account. This is IFC’s second loan to SAS after approving in April 2002 a $250,000 A loan to help establish the company. The balance of the proposed financing is capital reserve made available through a second grant fund by the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and additional share capital paid in by new farmers.
location_description: The project is located in the Nov and Zafarabad regions of Northern Tajikistan and expands thereafter to other regions.

project_description: The Andhra Pradesh Paper Mills limited (APPM, or the company), with sales of about 157,000 MT per annum of paper, is the fourth largest integrated pulp and paper manufacturer in India. The company was established in 1920 and is listed on the Mumbai and Hyderbad Stock Exchanges. In October 2000, APPM acquired 71% stake in Coastal Papers Ltd. (CP) with a capacity of 55,000 MT p.a. of printing and writing paper from straw pulp and packaging paper from waste paper and newsprint. With the proposed project, it will focus on shifting CP’s production to printing and writing paper based on pulp transferred from APPM. The proposed project consists of: - enhancement of pulp capacity - improvement of the product mix - increase in production capacity and efficiency - improvement of environmental management systems and - increase in the existing farm forestry program. The project also includes the restructuring of part of the company’s existing short-term debt and the recent completion of the company’s privatization through the purchase of the remaining government shares.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is the L. N. Bangur Group which owns 67.8% of APPM. Banks and Financial Institutions own 17.4% and the General Public owns 14.8%. Apart from its interest in APPM, the Bangur Group has an 85% equity interest in Maharaja Shree Umed Mills Ltd. (a company in cotton textiles sector) and a 48% stake in P.K. Tea & Produce Co. Ltd. (P.K. Tea, a small company in the tea sector).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is $139.1 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to $40 million for IFC’s own account including up to $35 million in the form of an A-Loan and up to $5 million in the form of a C-Loan equity investment.
location_description: The company is headquartered in Hyderbad, the capital of the state of Andhra Pradesh. APPM has two existing plants located in Rajamundry, 500 kilometers north east of Hyderabad. Rajamundary is situated on the trunk route, which connects Chennai and Kolkata. Visakhapatnam, a major port, is 200 kms by rail. The plants are located near farm forests and are well connected by roads to various important centers. The finished products can be easily transported to important commercial centers of Andhra Pradesh and other states by network of rail and road transport.
additionality: Development Impact: Farm Forestry: IFC’s Industry, Environment and Social Specialists have visited APPM’s farm forestry nurseries and plantations. Since 1989, APPM has distributed quality seedlings to more than 14,000 farmers to cover a total plantation land of more than 27,000 hectares. The company maintains twelve nurseries and employs 50 to 100 workers per nursery. The total target seedling production for FY03 is 35 million. Approximately 70,000 person days of labor are required for this, which will generate about Rs 4.2 million in wages for local laborers. APPM also provides technical know-how to farmers from low cost planting to post harvest stage, through establishment of demonstration plots, audio, video and printed literature, and personal interactions with the farmers. With this project, APPM’s requirement for wood resources is expected to increase by over 33%, and the company will further increase its farm forestry program. Environment: IFC’s Industry and Environmental Specialists have visited APPM’s plants and have identified significant environmental benefits of the Project. In the Coastal Paper unit of the company, the existing 10,500 MT p.a. rice straw pulping section that is heavily polluting, will be closed down. This will be replaced by pulp from the new Pulp Mill at APPM. The Project will also help to achieve better pollution controls in the APPM plant. The new Pulp Mill will bring down absorbable organohalogens (AOX) in the effluent discharge from present levels of 2kg per MT of pulp to 0.5 kg per MT, and reduce APPM’s water consumption and odoriferous emissions to comply with the World Bank guidelines. This will build on the company’s existing “green” platform and allow it to continue to pursue its commitment to the environment. Employment: APPM will provide direct employment to about 3,200 people, out of which 480 employees will work in the proposed Pulp Mill. Additionally, with the increased wood fiber requirements as a result of the Project, APPM’s farm forestry operations are expected to support over 25,200 farmers and cover over 50,000 hectares of land by 2007. IFC Role Long term funding: IFC will provide long term debt, which is generally not available and without which, it would not be possible to complete the financial plan. In so doing, IFC will play an important role in stabilizing the company’s debt profile, ensuring a proper match of cash from operations with debt service requirements. APPM believes that IFC’s involvement as a lead financier will help attract other local banks for lending long term in the current market scenario. IFC will also inject additional equity in the company, which will provide needed support to the company’s financial plan. Promoting sustainability: IFC’s environmental requirements for forest management will mitigate potential environmental problems and lead to sustainable forestry operations. IFC is expected to assist the company to comply with the new World Bank Group’s Forest Strategy and Policy. The company’s farm forestry operations offer a good example of development at the local farm level. The closure of a straw pulp process will stop high pollution levels.

company_name: Guangxi Baise Fenglin Fiberboard Corporation Limited
sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: The poject cmpany, Guangxi Fenglin Forestry Development Co. Ltd. (Fenglin or the cmpany), is one of the largest medium-density fiberboard (MDF) manufacturers in China with a production capacity of 140,000 m3 p.a.. Headquartered in Nanning, Guangxi province in China, the Company supplies MDF boards to the country’s fast growing furniture and construction industries. The purpose of the poject is to expand the production capacity of the cmpany through the addition of a new 150,000 m3 continuous press medium- and high-density fiberboard line (MDF and HDF), a flooring panel line and a decorative panel line – all in Baise, Guangxi province in China. Another component of the project is to establish and develop an additional 200,000 mu fast growing and high yielding plantation forest to build up sufficient raw material supply for the company.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Mr. Liu Yi Chuan, a Hong Kong citizen and entrepreneur who operates a number of successful businesses in China and abroad. Mr. Liu is a 100% owner of Fenglin International BVI, a private company created in 2003, which owns the project company. Mr. Liu has been in the MDF production business since 1995 through his shareholding in Nanning Sanyuan Property Development Company Ltd. Fenglin International controls two subsidiaries: the project company located in the city of Nanning, China and Guangxi Baise Fenglin Fiberboard Co., Ltd. Located in the city of Baise, China. Fenglin has been producing MDF boards since 1995. At Baise site, the MDF production started in December 2003.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated total project cost is $61 million. The proposed IFC investment would be up to $35 million comprising an A-loan of up to $18 million, a B-loan of up to $14 million and equity of up to $3 million. The remaining project financing amount of $26 million will include equity in the form of internally generated cash and shareholder’s subscription.
location_description: The project site is located in Baise, Guangxi Province, which is approximately 240 km West of Nanning. Baise is a predominantly rural and less developed province in Southern China with vast forest resources.
additionality: The project will have a significant development impact by: - bringing the world-class technology and supporting an expansion of a privately-owned competitive producer of MDF in China; - helping the company bring innovative, lower-cost value-added products to the market; - helping the company establish, develop and manage forestry assets in a long-term and ecologically sustainable way, thereby reducing pressure on the natural forests; - supporting the growth of the less developed Guangxi province, where the company operates; - supporting the job creation in the city of Baise, both in the company’s downstream operations and forestry business; - providing a major source of income to around 2,000 subsistence forestry farmers; - helping the company align its operations and internal policies with international standards, thereby enhancing its access the international financial markets and setting the stage for a future IPO. Following IFC’s reporting requirements, the company has its statements prepared and audited according to IFRS by Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu. IFC Role: - Develop project’s in China’s Less Developed Provinces: In the context of international investors still cautious about investing in poorer provinces and less-known and smaller cities, IFC has a clear role in supporting a competitive private entity in one of the most under-developed areas in China. - Support a Successful and Environmentally Responsible Private Enterprise: IFC will provide long-term financing best suited to the company’s capital expenditure and currency needs. The company owns and develops plantations in Guangxi province, which has vast forestry resources (56% of the province is covered with forests). IFC’s involvement in the project will require the company and the Guangxi province’s commitment to long-term sustainable forestry practices. IFC will seek to raise grant funding to help the company with independent forest certification. - Technical Services: As part of its technical appraisal, IFC is helping the company further improve its operational efficiency. As a prospective shareholder and lender to Fenglin, IFC would assist the company align its policies with best international practices in corporate governance, environmental and social matters. - IFC will seek to mobilize financing from banks and other financial institutions under its B-loan program. IFC would introduce the company to international banks and financial institutions; IFC’s presence would provide comfort to prospective investors and lenders and is expected to enhance the company’s ability to access the international capital markets and eventually launch an IPO.
Company Name: Guangxi Baise Fenglin Fiberboard Corporation Limited

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: Established in April 2002 and July 2002 respectively, OOO Kronospan and OOO Kronohim (together the company or the borrowers) are limited liability companies incorporated in the Russian Federation. The proposed investment program is to set up: - a 140,000 cubic meters per year medium density fiberboard (MDF) line (under construction); - a second 175,000 cubic meters per year MDF line, and - a 80,000 tons/year resin plant.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Kronospan Holdings Limited (Cyprus), which is the parent company for the Eastern European operations of the Kronospan Group (Kronospan or the Group). The borrowers are 100%-owned by Kronospan Russia Limited (Cyprus), the newly formed parent company for Russian operations of the Group. Kronospan is privately owned and is a European leader in wood panel board manufacturing.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at Euro 180 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $50 million equivalent loan (in Euros) for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project facilities will be located at Egorievsk on a 132 hectare plot about 100 km south-east of Moscow in a recently established industrial zone. The site has good road and rail connections in vicinity and has access to electricity and natural gas.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: The proposed project is the construction of a green field glass tableware plant with an annual capacity of 53,000 tons in Targovishte, Bulgaria, at an estimated cost of $60 million. The project, which is expected to be commissioned in 2005 and employ 500 employees in 8 production lines, is located 123 km from the port of Varna on the Black Sea and 313 km from Sofia. It will sell 90% of its production in the Balkans, Central, Eastern, and Western Europe and 10% domestically.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor is the Sisecam Group (Sisecam or the sponsor), Turkey’s leading glass manufacturer and a longtime IFC client. Management and technical assistance to the project will be provided by Pasabahce Cam Sanayii ve Ticaret A.S. (Pasabahce), the flagship company of the glassware division of the Sisecam Group. Established in 1934, over the years Pasabahce has grown to become the third largest player in the tableware industry worldwide.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $60 million. The IFC investment consists of an A loan of $12.25 million, a B loan of $17.75 million, and either an equity investment or a C loan of $2.75 million.
location_description: The site of the project is Targovishte, a town in the northeastern Bulgaria in a longstanding glassmaking region in Eastern Europe. The site enjoys convenient access to Varna, the largest port in Bulgaria and its best port for maritime transportation of container shipments.
additionality: The project will have a strong development impact. It will bring a state-of-the-art tableware facility to Bulgaria, and create direct employment for approximately 500 workers outside the capital and foster additional commercial activity. Approximately 90% of production will be directed to export markets, mainly Balkans, Central-Eastern and Western Europe countries, contributing to foreign exchange generation. The large scale of the plant will capture economies of scale in production and low capital cost. Other non-quantifiable development impacts include the demonstration effect for other foreign investors who are considering Bulgaria for new production facilities and the potential for linkages along the supply chain that could make of Targovishte a glass production center in the region. IFC is expected to play a critical role in the project by: -providing long-term, limited recourse financing otherwise not available to the company, - mobilizing resources from the international debt markets through its B-loan program and broadening Sisecam’s sources of term capital and - encouraging Turkish investors to venture abroad.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: The project consists of the construction of a $100-110 million float glass plant in the town of Targovishte in the northwestern part of Bulgaria. At full capacity, it is expected to produce 200,000 tons of clear float glass annually and employ 200 people. Approximately 90,000 tons of this production will be exported to the nearby Balkan markets, particularly Greece and Romania, 20,000 tons in the domestic Bulgarian market, and the remainder within Turkey.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor is Turkiye Sise ve Cam Fabrikalari A.S. (Sisecam or the sponsor), Turkey’s leading glass manufacturer and a longtime IFC client. Technical and management assistance will be provided from Trakya Cam Sanayii A.S. (Trakya Cam), the float glass division of the Sisecam Group. Established in 1977, Trakya Cam started its operations in 1978 and has grown over the past quarter century into one of the leading glass manufacturers in southern Europe with revenues of $220 million over sales of 650,000 tons of float and processed glass.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $100-110 million. The IFC investment consists of an A loan of $22. 5 million, a B loan of $32. 5 million, and either an equity investment or a C loan of $5.0 million.
location_description: The project site is Targovishte, a town in northwestern Bulgaria, a longstanding glassmaking region in Eastern Europe. The site enjoys convenient access to Varna, the largest port in Bulgaria and its best port for maritime transportation of container shipments.
additionality: The project will have a strong development impact. It will bring a modern float glass plant in Bulgaria, allow the transfer of technological know-how related to float glass production, and make a significant contribution towards developing Bulgaria’s export base. It will create direct employment for 200 workers outside the capital, and will foster additional commercial activity. Approximately 90% of production will be directed to export markets, mainly the Balkans and Turkey, contributing to foreign exchange generation. The project will benefit from low electricity and labor costs as well as good proximity to local export markets. Other, non-quantifiable development impacts include the demonstration effect for other foreign investors who are considering Bulgaria for new production facilities and the potential for linkages along the supply chain that could make of Targovishte a glass production center in the region. IFC is expected to play a critical role in the project by: - providing long-term, limited recourse financing otherwise not available to the company, - mobilizing resources from the international debt markets through its B-loan program and broadening Sisecam’s sources of term capital and - encouraging Turkish investors to venture abroad.

project_description: The project entails an equity investment of the lower of - 10% of the total fund capitalization, or - $50 million in the proposed Colony China Opportunity Fund (“the fund”). Included in this investment, IFC would seek a stake of 10% in the General Partner (GP) of the fund. The fund is a 7-year closed-end distressed asset investment fund, to be established as a Cayman Islands limited partnership. An on-shore parallel fund, which will co-invest pari passu with the fund, will be set up as a Chinese limited liability company to facilitate participation by domestic investors, including co-sponsor Shanghai Industrial Investment Co. (SIIC). The fund will invest in: - acquisition of NPL pools from financial institutions, - direct purchase of distressed real estate assets, and, to a lesser extent, - restructuring of distressed operating companies in PRC, Hong Kong, and Macau (Greater China). The joint sponsors, Colony Capital Asia Pacific Pte Ltd. (CCAP) and SIIC, will leverage CCAP’s global and Asian distressed investment experience with SIIC’s domestic business and government relationships to optimize the fund’s ability to source, structure and execute distressed investments, aiming to achieve a gross IRR in excess of 25%. The joint sponsors are seeking to raise total capital, for both the off-shore and on-shore vehicles, of $250-$500 million, and expect to conduct a first closing by the end of first quarter of 2004. The fund will charge a 2% annual management fee, and will pay the GP a 20% carried interest based on committed capital after achieving a 10% p.a. hurdle rate.
sponsor_shareholders: CCAP, with a potential shareholding of 45-50% in the GP, is a wholly owned subsidiary of Colony Capital (“Colony”). Colony is led by its founder and CEO, Thomas J. Barrack, Jr. (56), and ten other principals, who on average have worked at Colony for eight years with an average of 22 years of relevant business and investing experience. Colony is one of a few unaffiliated, privately-held distressed asset fund organizations having the capability to source, execute and realize investment opportunities in the global markets. SIIC, a potential shareholder with 45-50% stake in the GP, is incorporated in Hong Kong with executive headquarters in Shanghai. SIIC has been the “window” company of the Shanghai Municipal Government since 1981, with the core mandate of attracting global capital to Shanghai. Its flagship operating entity, Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd., is a Hong Kong-listed Hang Seng Index company, 40% owned by the public. SIIC’s total assets of over $4.1 billion (as of December 31, 2002) are invested in real estate, financial services, health care, consumer retailing, infrastructure and logistics, information technology, and the Chongming Development Area. With a dozen offices across China and nine international offices, SIIC has sought to combine local knowledge with global expertise in various sectors through alliances with international players, including Temasek, Salomon Smith Barney and Goldman Sachs. CCAP and SIIC are also committed to ensuring an optimal alignment of all investor’s interests by investing an aggregate of up to 10% of the fund’s total capitalization. If IFC participates in the GP, 10% of IFC’s total commitment would count toward this GP obligation. CCAP has been in discussion with various Asian and U.S. institutional investors about participating in the fund. Initial feedback indicates that IFC’s involvement in the fund is viewed by those institutions as essential to validate the fund concept and mitigate certain risks.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project entails an equity investment of the lower of : - 10% of the total fund capitalization, or - $50 million in the proposed $500 million fund.
location_description: The Fund would be registered as a Cayman Islands limited partnership. SI Colony China (Colony China), a Cayman Islands entity, will be the GP of the fund. The GP is currently proposed to be owned 50:50 by CCAP and SIIC. If IFC takes a stake of 10% in the GP, the shares of CCAP and SIIC would each be reduced to 45%. CCAP controls the daily management of the GP. Mr. Tom Barrack will serve as the interim CEO for the Fund until the local operating team is fully in place. Deals would be sourced through both direct negotiations with domestic banks and asset owners, and auctions by asset management companies (AMCs). Based on the current pipeline, the GP estimates a portfolio mix of 40% NPL transactions, 40% distressed real estate asset workouts, and 20% corporate restructuring transactions.
additionality: This project is expected to make strong impact by doing the following: - Introducing real estate distressed asset resolution techniques to China; - Building local capacity in managing distressed assets, a highly specialized area, by transferring technical expertise from a first tier international player and helping to establish industry best practices in China; - Advocating with policy makers and regulators for more creditor-friendly policies and regulations; and - Building capacity at the municipal level (through SIIC) which supports World Bank and IFC goals. IFC would play various critical roles in this fund, including: - Being the lead sponsor/anchor investor of the first distressed debt fund in China; - Catalyzing private sector investments in the fund; - Acting as the "neutral party/honest broker” between CCAP and SIIC; and - Ensuring best practice corporate governance and helping to establish industry standards in this asset class.

project_description: The $13.0 million expansion project involves the construction and opening in Kiev of 2 new 10,000sq.m DIY (Do-It-Yourself) stores, in addition to the existing 5,000sq.m store, under the name Nova Liniya (NL or the company). The new stores, will follow the best practice of modern DIY format, comparable to those of Home Depot, Lowe’s, and OBI. They will offer a wide range of DIY products, more than 30,000, as well as specialized services. The project, to be implemented in 2 stages over a 20 month period, will address the growing demand in the construction materials, home care products, and consumer electronics. The DIY concept has become well established in Ukraine. Following a slump in the aftermath of the financial crisis in Russia and the subsequent depreciation of the Ukrainian currency, Ukraine’s retail sector, and one of its fastest growing segments, DIY retailing, has posted impressive growth, exceeding 16% in 2002. It is expected that this growth will continue in the forthcoming years and NL, as a first mover, will take full advantage of its established position.
sponsor_shareholders: NL was established in February 2000 as a private joint stock company by its present senior management. In early 2002, an independent investment bank, Dragon Capital, acquired 35% of Nova Liniya’s shares. Currently NL’s management owns 50% of NL, Dragon Capital owns 35%, and individual investors own 15%. Dragon Capital is the leading equity broker and a major M&A (Merger and Acquisitions) adviser in Ukraine.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at about $13 million IFC is considering an investment of about $5 million, comprising an A Loan of about $3.5 million and a quasi-equity investment of about $1.5 million.
location_description: All stores will be located in Kiev, the capital of Ukraine. NL’s existing store, with a total area of about 4.700 sq. m. is located in the densely populated and growing Kharkivsky district. The second store, to be located in the Troyeschyna district, will have a total area of about 10,000 sq. m. The site is unoccupied and is close to residential areas and bus stops. The third store is expected to be identical in size to the second store.
additionality: Development Impact The project is expected to have a significant developmental impact, as follows: - Providing consumers with a wide range of good quality home improvement products at an affordable price. - Upgrading business practices: The project will have a catalytic effect in developing and improving the quality of local suppliers and producers. Since part of the product range is expected to be sourced locally, the company will have to work closely with local suppliers and producers to improve their quality in order to meet NL’s quality standards. - Promoting SME and private sector development: The project would have a positive effect on the development of the home repair/improvement and construction services industry, which was underdeveloped during the years of state planning. - Demonstration effect: The project would provide a significant demonstration effect, as its success would encourage other companies pursuing investment opportunities in Ukraine, as the country' s perceived risk begins to diminish. - Increased employment: The project will create new employment, both directly and indirectly. It will provide direct employment to about 300 employees, mostly women, with a significant multiple of that number expected to be added in the supply stream and in ancillary activities. In addition, temporary employment will be provided to local labor during the construction phase of the project.    Fit With World Bank Group Strategy and IFC Role IFC role in the proposed project could be valuable on several grounds: - In view of the perceived macro-economic and political risks of investing in Ukraine, IFC’s presence in this transaction will help increase investors’ confidence in the country’s business environment. - IFC's proposed financing will enable the company to support its medium-term investments by supplying long-term funds on reasonable terms otherwise not available to the company. - IFC will play an important role in determining the project scope, structuring the financial plan, evaluating the environmental issues, thus reducing the project's risk profile.

company_name: Avenue Special Situations Fund III, L.P.
project_description: Avenue Asia Fund (or the company ) will target single credits in a regionally diversified pool of U.S. Dollar and local currency denominated distressed debt instruments. However, 90% of the Fund’s underlying asset pool will constitute U.S. Dollar denominated credits. The Fund is structured as a closed-end fund, registered in Delaware as a Limited Partnership, with a target size of $500 million. The Fund’s mandate is to make non-control investments in senior debt or debt-related instruments of Asian (Ex-Japan) companies that are: - in reorganization or bankruptcy; - in industries that are in turmoil; - undervalued because of other economic conditions or extraordinary events; or - being sold by non-economic sellers like banks or Asset Management Companies (AMCs).
sponsor_shareholders: Avenue Capital Group is the Fund Manager and has been operating in the Southeast Asian distressed markets since 1999. The Fund is led by its Principals, Marc Lasry, Sonia Gardner, and Malcolm Robinson, who have 45 years of aggregate investment experience in the distressed debt markets in Asia and the U.S. The Principals manage approximately $850 million in Asian distressed debt, through two Asia-focused hedge funds and two closed-end institutional funds (Avenue Asia Capital Partners, L.P. and Avenue Asia Special Situations Fund II, L.P.). In addition to the Asia portfolio, Marc Lasry and Sonia Gardner, together with a separate team of investment professionals based in New York, manage approximately $2.1 billion in U.S. distressed debt. The Avenue Asia team has 17 investment professionals (including 11 based throughout Asia) with approximately 240 years of relevant aggregate investment experience. The Fund has offices and investment professionals in Hong Kong, Thailand and Indonesia, as well as experienced sourcing teams based in Hong Kong, Tokyo and New York. Avenue Asia will draw significant benefit from several key strategic affiliations, including relationships with Amroc (a leading bank loan sourcing firm with operations in Asia and the U.S.) and Texas Pacific Group (a leading global private equity player).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC will make an equity investment of up to 10%, not to exceed $40 million, in Avenue Asia Special Situations Fund III, L.P. (the Fund). The target size of the Fund is $500 million.
location_description: The Fund is structured as a closed-end fund, registered in Delaware as a Limited Partnership, with a target size of $500 million. The Fund has offices and investment professionals in Hong Kong, Thailand and Indonesia, as well as experienced sourcing teams based in Hong Kong, Tokyo and New York.
Company Name: Avenue Special Situations Fund III, L.P.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: Drujba A.D. (Drujba) is the result of the merger in April 2003 of Stind A.D. (Stind; located in Sofia) and Drujba (which originally consisted solely of a plant at Plovdiv, in southern Bulgaria), both of which have been owned by Yioula Glassworks S.A (Yioula), Greece, since their privatizations in 1997 and in 1998, respectively. In 2002, the combined sales of Drujba were Euro 46.9 million ($ 49.8 million) and net earnings amounted to Euro 5.4 million ($ 5.7 million). After the merger, the company’s share of the Bulgarian market is about 72%. The combined capacity at the two plants (after full commissioning of the new furnace in early 2004) will be approximately 264,000 tons per year. The merger of Drujba’s original Plovdiv and Stind operations aimed at more efficient production planning, better capacity utilizations, and more efficient use of management time. Although the sponsor had sought the merger several years ago it was delayed due to lengthy regulatory requirements of Bulgaria’s State Securities Commission and various other regulatory agencies. The proposed project is to refurbish and modernize the operations of an existing Bulgarian glass manufacturer, Drujba. The project involves an investment in a modern 120,000 tpy natural gas fired furnace and related production lines at the company’s plant in Plovdiv. Capacity at the company’s Sofia operation will not increase.
sponsor_shareholders: Project Sponsor: Drujba is 52.6% owned by Bareck Overseas Limited and 46.9% by Glassinvest Limited, both of which are registered in Cypress. Yioula in turn has an 83.3% interest in these two companies through its subsidiary, Yalos Holdings (Overseas) Limited (Yalos), which was set up to purchase companies in the Balkans. The remaining 16.7% of Yalos is owned by the Black Sea Fund (12.0%), the Euromerchant Balkan Fund (3.0%), and Hellenic Industrial Development Bank (1.7%). IFC has a 16.0% interest in the Black Sea Fund and a 18.3% interest in the Euromerchant Balkan Fund. Major Shareholders of the Project: Founded in 1947, Yioula is a privately-owned firm that is now the largest glass container producer in the Balkans. In total, Yioula has 2500 employees, ranks sixth in Europe in glass container production, and has an excellent reputation in the food and drinks glass packaging industry. With two production facilities in Greece, one in Romania, and two in Bulgaria, Yioula holds a strong position in the Balkan glass container market. Yioula’s clients include local wine and beer companies and numerous multi-national companies with business interests in the Balkans such as: Coke, Pepsi, Interbrew, Heineken, Carlsberg, and Glaxo Smith Klein Beecham. Yioula is 59% owned by the Voulgarakis family and 41% by four reputable Greek banks and two investment funds.
