The shareholding structure is as follows: 59.00% the Voulgarakis family, 24.48% Global Capital Investors, 5.96% National Bank of Greece, 4.02% ETVA Bank, 3.36% EFG Eurobank – Ergasias, 1.68% Greek Progress Fund, and 1.50% Commercial Bank of Greece.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated project cost is Euro 47.0 million. This is divided up according to the following components: Equipment and Machinery 20.50 Building and Civil Works 7.60 Contingencies 2.40 Debt Refinancing 16.50 Total 47.00 The proposed project cost is estimated at Euro 47.0 million and consists of building and installation of a new furnace, six production lines, molds and the related warehouses at the plant in Plovdiv. Contingencies are estimated at 9% of the capital cost. Also, the project cost includes Euro 16.5 million to refinance part of Drujba’s existing short-term debt. The financial plan is detailed in the following below: Equity: Internal Cash Generation--15.00 Debt: IFC’s Loan--20.00 Local Banks Loans--12.00 Sub-Total--32.00 Total 47.00 The proposed financial plan includes Euro 15.0 million of internal cash generation and loans of Euro 32.0 million including Euro 20.0 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The new furnace, the production lines and the related assets being constructed as part of the project are located at the company’s plant in Plovdiv, Bulgaria, which is situated about 130 Km southeast of Sofia on an area of 170,000 square meters. The plant’s buildings, warehouses and other facilities occupy about 70,000 square meters. Electricity is provided to the plant from the local grid, which is very reliable. However, in the event that power from that source were to become unavailable, there is a power generator at the plant that can supply the necessary electricity. Water is provided by the city, and the plant also has access to its own water wells. As for transportation, about 70% of the products are transported by trucks and the remainder by rail, and both the roads and the rail facilities are good.
additionality: The proposed project will allow Drujba to improve its production in order to meet the more stringent requirements of the EU and neighboring markets in terms of specifications and quality, while maintaining its dominant position in Bulgaria. Drujba is already a lower cost supplier to its local and export markets and is expected to further lower its production costs by implementing the project. The project represents a low cost expansion of effective capacity. The proposed project will have a positive environmental and social impact. The Dujba plants originally consisted of old equipment and congested workspace. The company’s investment program will upgrade the overall environmental standards and allow both plants to realize about 60% to 75% energy savings and increase the amount of recycled glass used. It will also improve the working conditions of the employees. The proposed project will encourage the development of local enterprises in a commercial way by supporting a small machine tool and mold manufacturer. IFC’s Role: IFC supports Bulgaria’s privatization efforts by focusing on financing recently privatized enterprises, and by supporting manufacturing opportunities in various sectors which have strategic importance for Bulgaria. IFC’s role in the proposed project involves: --providing long-term funding which is not readily available from local financial institutions; --supporting environmental sustainability and higher health and safety standards, --establishing a relationship with a reputable sponsor who has further expansion plans in other emerging markets (e.g. Serbia and Romania), --helping the company address its accounting issues, and --assisting the company to develop an improved capital structure.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: OOO Ruscam (or the company) was founded in 2001 and produces glass containers for the fast growing Russian market. Ruscam’s operations are located in the village of Gorokhovets, about 335 km east of Moscow and the company currently operates two glass furnaces with a total capacity of 580 tons/day. The project entails the installation of a third furnace with 385 tons/day of glass making capacity and bottle-forming lines which will allow the company to expand its production of glass containers in amber and start the production of green containers. The project will address the rapidly growing demand in Russia for beverage bottles manufactured to international quality standards. Currently, most of the bottles manufactured domestically suffer from a high breakage rate when utilized on higher-speed filling lines, which are becoming increasingly common in Russia with the beverage industry’s investment in improved filling technologies and efficiencies.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are Turkiye Sise ve Cam Fabrikalari Group of Turkey (Sisecam) and Anadolu Cam Sanayii (Anadolu Cam), the glass packaging division of Sisecam. Sisecam is the eighth largest glass producer in the world and will provide technical and marketing support to the project. IFC has a long and well-established relationship with Sisecam Group dating back to the 1960s. Ruscam’s majority shareholder is Anadolu Cam with 52% of shares with the remaining balance being held by two local investors who each hold 24% of the shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $35 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A-loan for IFC’s own account for up to $17.5 million.
location_description: Ruscam’s operations are located in Gorokhovets, Vladimir Oblast (about 335 km east of Moscow) and the third furnace will be installed adjacent to Ruscam’s existing two furnaces and production lines. Ruscam is located in its own industrial park, an approximately 15 ha site, separated from adjacent residential areas.
additionality: In addition to strengthening Russia’s manufacturing base in order to domestically meet the demand for quality glass containers, the project is expected to have the following benefits to the local community: - Job Creation: Ruscam has been the only large-scale investment in the Gorokhovets area since the Soviet era and the surrounding area offers very few other employment opportunities. The project is expected to create approximately 200 incremental, sustainable jobs of which over 100 would be direct employment by Ruscam. - Investment in Human Resources: Sisecam has been transferring best technical practice to its local employees at the shop floor-level and international cost, managerial accounting and financial control know-how to the local management cadre it is developing. In addition to the on-the-job training, Sisecam routinely trains local staff at Sisecam facilities in Turkey. - Small and Medium Sized Enterprises: The company is well integrated into the local economy. The project will continue to offer new opportunities for raw materials and service providers (some of which are locally-owned SMEs) and help foster a more competitive market for such materials and services.

sector: Electrical Machinery, Equipment and Components (Electric Lighting, Motors, Batteries, Insulated Wires and Cables, Fiber Optic Cable, Carbon and Graphite Products, etc.)
project_description: Crompton Greaves Limited (CGL; the company; or BSE: 500093) is the flagship company in the BM Thapar Group, and is one of the largest players in India in the electrical equipment and engineering industry. CGL makes a wide range of transformers, switchgear, motors, lighting products, fans, railway-signaling equipment, and undertakes turnkey engineering projects. CGL’s business operations are organized into four Strategic Business Groups (SBGs) namely power systems, industrial systems, consumer products, and digital (networking and telecommunication). The net turnover of the company in FY03 was $328 million equivalent. The company has requested IFC to provide a corporate loan of up to $25 million in support of its ongoing financial and operational restructuring efforts. The proposed corporate investment and debt restructuring program would enable CGL to further cut costs and enhance the competitiveness of its products in both domestic and international markets and increase the average maturity of CGL’s debt. The project is supported by a strong management team. CGL will also benefit from its extensive marketing and distribution network and an established premier brand name in India.
sponsor_shareholders: The current promoter holding is with the Thapar Group (among India’s top industrial houses) and the company forms part of the BM Thapar Group, which presently owns and controls: - Solaris Chemtech Ltd; - Crompton Greaves Ltd; - Greaves Ltd; and - English Indian Clays Ltd. At March 31, 2003, BM Thapar Group owned 38.7% of CGL while Penbryn International Ltd. held 13.7%. Non promoters including institutional investors, corporate bodies, mutual funds etc held 31.7%, while the remaining 15.9% was held by the general public.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $50 million equivalent. The proposed IFC investment is up to $25 million A Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: CGL has 21 plants in 16 operational facilities across 10 locations, which are Mumbai, Malanpur, Mandideep, Nasik, Auragabad, Goa, Pitampur, Baroda, Ahmednagar and Bangalore. In addition, the EPD (turnkey projects divisions) and Luminaries (trading) divisions are based in Chennai and Mumbai respectively.
additionality: The project will help one of the largest players in India in the electrical equipment and engineering industry to continue its financial and operational restructuring. This comprehensive modernization program will help CGL focus on those areas of business where it is most competitive, and also expand its export operations. Parts of the Company that are not strategic or competitive are being sold to other companies that can better utilize them. Other development impacts would include: Local Development: CGL is moving its operations from high costs areas (e.g., Mumbai) to low cost less developed areas. The manufacturing operations will help local economies not only through employment but also through the consumption of privately contracted specialty services, operations and maintenance assistance etc. Benefits to Employees: The project will ensure continued employment for several thousand people, despite rationalization in Mumbai, as well as generate new jobs in low income areas. Formal training, an important benefit to employees, combined with the on-job work experience, will allow workers to increase their skills and improve their earning potential. IFC’s role in this project is manifold. IFC would provide access to much needed long-term capital to assist CGL in implementing the ongoing modernization and restructuring, and in refinancing the company’s high-cost maturing debt, as other sources of long-term financing are generally not available to CGL in the current market scenario. IFC presence would support the turnaround strategy. This would help the company obtain a favorable credit rating in due course and enable it to access the Indian bond market for long-term funds on a sustainable basis in the future. IFC financing would help CGL build the Crompton Greaves brand in the international market in line with its strategy of increased focus on export. IFC will also have a strong role in helping CGL attain global standards in environmental and social issues and corporate governance.

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: Sveza Holding (or the company) is the largest birch plywood producer in Russia and accounts for 10% of the global production of birch plywood. Sveza owns three plywood plants producing birch plywood, particleboard, and bed slats mainly utilized in construction, furniture production and transportation industries, and several logging companies in various regions of Russia. This project will support Sveza’s 2004-2007 investment program, which comprises of: - capital expenditures and modernization program for Sveza’s plywood plants, - expansion of the company’s harvesting infrastructure, and - refinancing of existing short-term debt. This project will enable Sveza to increase the quality of its existing products, widen its product selection, and lower its production costs and raw material consumption through the replacement of older production equipment. The company will further expand its harvesting and sawmilling infrastructure which will improve the company’s raw material self sufficiency. In addition to the above, the refinancing component will help the company reduce its funding cost and lower its maturity mismatch by replacing existing expensive short-term loans by long-term funding.
sponsor_shareholders: Sveza is owned by Severstal Holding, a conglomerate active in steel production, automotive manufacturing, transportation, forestry, insurance, and banking. The largest company in the holding is Severstal Metallurgical Plant (Severstal), a publicly traded steel producer located in Cherepovets. Severstal and Severstal Holding are controlled by Alexei Mordashov, one of the most influential businessmen in Russia. In 2003, Mr. Mordashov was named one of the best managers in Business Week’s list of 25 most prominent European businessmen and is also a member of the Union of Industrials and Entrepreneurs of Russia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $80 million. Proposed IFC investment is a $40 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: Sveza’s existing mills include Fanplit (Kostroma, Kostroma Oblast), Novator (Veliky Ustjug, Vologda Oblast) and Ust Izhora (St. Petersburg, Leningrad Oblast). The Fanplit mill includes two sites, the original mill in the middle of Kostroma, and a new site in an industrial suburb. The Novator plant is located in the industrial area of Veliky Ustiug, in close proximity to good raw material base. The Ust Izhora plant is located in the suburbs of St. Petersburg and close to the Port of St. Petersburg, providing a benefit for export operations.

project_description: The project is intended to enable Wilmar Trading to scale up its offtake of crude palm oil (CPO) from palm oil plantations in Indonesia and process them into refined oil. Wilmar Trading is the merchandising and trading arm of Wilmar Holdings, a leading processor and merchandiser of oilseeds and edible oil in Asia. IFC's support would facilitate Wilmar Trading to finance its 2003/2005 export program and allow continued sustainable long-term growth in a sector where Indonesia has a strong comparative advantage.
sponsor_shareholders: Wilmar Holdings (Wilmar Group or the company) is one of the leading processors and merchandisers of quality edible oils in Asia with net sales in 2002 of approximately $3.5 billion. Its primary business activities include: - Refining crude palm oil and fractionating refined palm oil into other palm-based products; - Crushing oilseeds into meals, edible oils and their derivative products; - Refining soybean and other edible oils; - Merchandizing and distributing edible oils, oilseeds, oilseed meals and their derivative products; - Cultivating and harvesting oil palm trees and processing fresh palm fruit bunches into crude palm oil and palm kernel. Wilmar Group was established in 1991 to trade palm oil and palm products in Singapore and Indonesia. The business then expanded into processing and manufacturing of edible oils and derivative products in Indonesia and China. It also began investing and developing oil palm plantations in 1992. The group’s substantial shareholders include Mr. Kuok Khoon Hong, Mr. Martua Sitorus, Archer Daniels Midland Company (ADM), and China Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export Corporation (COFCO).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC would provide a partial guarantee for up to $33.3 million for a pre-shipment finance facility of up to $50 million extended by a commercial bank. This financing package will be in the form of a committed facility, renewable annually for a maximum of three years.
location_description: Wilmar Trading is located in Singapore, and Wilmar Group’s major palm oil refineries and plantations are located respectively in Dumai, Palembang, Kuala Tanjung, Bitung and Sumatra of Indonesia.
additionality: The project is intended to enable Wilmar Group to scale up its offtake of CPO from palm oil plantations in Indonesia. Not only will this facilitate an increase in exports in Indonesian Palm Oil, it will also have a positive effect on other players along the supply chain, such as farmers who will benefit from increased local demand by Wilmar Holdings refineries and access to international markets, as well as local businesses involved in services. Furthermore, IFC’s involvement in this transaction will be perceived as an endorsement of the Indonesian palm oil industry and will be a good illustration of IFC’s support for good sponsors in a socially sensitive sector.

project_description: Wumart Stores Inc. (Wumart or the company) is one of the leading retail chain store operators in Beijing. The project is for the company to expand its operations in Beijing and its peripheral areas, as well as improve its technological base and logistics.
sponsor_shareholders: The company’s existing ownership structure is as follows: Wumei Holdings, Inc. : 69.76% Beijing Hekang Youlian Technology Company Limited : 3.5% Beijing Junhe Investment Company Limited : 3.26% Beijing Wangshang Shijie E-business Company Limited : 22.48% Beijing Shuangchen Express Company Limited: 1%. Wumei Holdings, Inc. is principally engaged in the retail business in the PRC and through its interests in the Company operates a number of hypermarkets, supermarkets and convenience stores in Beijing. In addition, Wumei Holdings, Inc. is also engaged in import and export trading activities. Wumei Holdings, Inc. is controlled by Dr. Zhang Wenzhong, its Chairman and founder.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $50 million equivalent. IFC is exploring a possible cooperation with the company to finance part of this expansion program.
location_description: The project will be mainly located in urban areas of Beijing, Tianjin and Hebei. The company will acquire or lease retail space in these urban centers located in highly populated areas with good access to public transportation.

project_description: PT Ecogreen Oleochemicals (Ecogreen, the company), an Indonesia based company, is implementing a $84 million project involving establishing a new 60,000 tonnes per annum (tpa) capacity fatty acid production plant, incremental working capital and debt refinancing. The company is one of the leading global producers of natural fatty alcohols, its core product group, as well as co-products and intermediates such as fatty acids, methyl esters and glycerin. The company produces natural or vegetable oil based fatty alcohol, largely used for the production of detergents, shampoos, conditioners, skin applications and similar consumer products. They are also used as stabilizers in the production of plastics and lubricants. The company has 110,000 tpa natural fatty alcohol production capacity at two production plants located in Belawan, Medan (30,000 tpa) and Batam (80,000 tpa) in Indonesia. Ecogreen’s FY02 turnover was $86 million, of which about 95% was from exports to Asia-Pacific, North and South America and Europe. In addition to its production plants, the company has affiliated marketing and distribution companies which have long term lease finished goods storage facilities in Rotterdam, Germany; Houston,Texas; and Newark, New Jersey. The project is part of the company’s long-term strategy to improve its international competitiveness through better utilization of assets and strategic management of raw material inventory. About half of the new fatty acid capacity will be used to support an 8,000 tpa fatty alcohol capacity increase at Belawan, Medan plant through debottlenecking and to supply to an affiliate soap noodle production company. The surplus will be sold in the merchant market. The working capital and the debt refinancing are aimed at helping the company structure a flexible working capital facility with a core component to fund the permanent working capital and a stand-by facility to finance raw material purchases at low price points.
sponsor_shareholders: The company is owned through a holding company structure whose shareholders are: - Messrs. Eddy William Katuari and Fifi Sutanto (representing the Wings group) 47.7%; - Mr. Jimmy Masrin and PT Lautan Luas Tbk (representing the Lautan Luas group) 33.3% and - Mr. Robert Budi Hartono (representing the Djarum group) 19%. The main sponsor of the company is the Wings group, which is one of Indonesia’s largest producer and marketer of soaps and detergents. The Wings Group has seven main business activities – - consumer products; - packaging; - chemicals; - building materials; - real estate; - agribusiness and - financial services. Of these, the consumer products business is the largest in annual turnover. IFC has existing relationships with three of the Wings group companies (PT Sayap, PT Wings and PT Gawi). The other two members of the consortium are the Djarum group, one of the largest Indonesian cigarette manufacturers, and the Lautan Luas group which is Indonesia’s leading distributor and manufacturer of basic and specialty chemicals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be about $84.0 million. IFC’s investment would consist of an A Loan of up to $30 million.
location_description: The new fatty acid plant will be integrated with the company’s fatty alcohol plant at its existing site at Belawan, Medan in Indonesia. Adequate land is available at the plant site and the existing infrastructure can be expanded with marginal incremental investments to support the new project. The site is also located close to a jetty for easy access to movement of material.

company_name: Emerging Markets Global Small Capitalization Fund
project_description: Emerging Markets Small Cap Fund LLC (the Fund or the company) has been newly formed to seek long-term capital appreciation through investing primarily in emerging markets listed companies with market capitalization of less than $500 million. The Fund will have a global focus.
sponsor_shareholders: The Fund will be managed by Emerging Markets Management (EMM), which has its offices in Arlington, Virginia. As of June 30, 2003, EMM managed $5.5 billion in separate accounts and commingled funds, primarily for listed equities in emerging markets. The team will be managed by Felicia Morrow.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The target size of the Fund will be $200 million, although the Fund is likely to be smaller at the initial launch. The Fund will be a quasi-open-ended fund, with the possibility of monthly subscriptions and redemptions. The proposed IFC investment is $10 million, but no more than 15% of the Fund.
location_description: The Fund will be listed in Ireland.
additionality: Through its participation in the Fund, IFC will seek to achieve development impact in several ways. The Fund will respond to an inefficiency that is common to stock markets in developing as well as developed economies: as a general rule, investors and market researchers tend to pay less attention to smaller companies. This is particularly the case for companies that are listed but do not form part of the most commonly used market indexes and, therefore, do not automatically get picked up by investors who want their portfolios to track the market. As a result, market analysts pay less attention to these stocks, which reduces their visibility to investors and consequently limits trading volumes and liquidity. By demonstrating the value of analyzing and investing in these companies, the Fund will contribute to increasing liquidity in this asset sub-class, which is expected to expand the range of stocks available to investors, attract a broader range of local and foreign investors and encourage greater coverage by market analysts. IFC will play a catalyst role in attracting other investors to the Fund. By giving a green light to the project, IFC will serve as an anchor investor, attracting private sector investors that otherwise might not invest in the Fund. In line with the lessons learned from prior funds, IFC’s investment in the Fund will demonstrate our commitment to supporting existing managers with a good track record.
Company Name: Emerging Markets Global Small Capitalization Fund

sector: Miscellaneous and Industrial Ores (Including Magnesite, Fluorite, Sulfur, Soda Ash, Clays, Gypsum, Lime, Peat, Boron, Diatomite, Feldspar, etc.)
project_description: Grupo Calidra S.A. de C.V. (Calidra, or the company) is Mexico’s leading producer of lime and lime-related products, with 2002 revenue of approximately $80 million equivalent. The company operates 17 plants across Mexico and one in Honduras. Its operations comprise the quarrying of limestone, its processing into various grades of quick- or hydrated lime, packaging, and sale to the construction, steel, chemical, mining, agricultural, waste treatment and other industries. The main components of the project include: - the installation of three new kilns, - the consolidation and upgrading of lime hydration capacity, - conversion of existing kilns to dual-fuel capability, and - the decommissioning of inefficient kilns and hydrators. The project aims to rebalance Calidra’s production capacity in favor of regions with limited installed capacity for quality lime, targets faster growing market segments, diversifies its customer base to reduce reliance on the construction sector, and lowers operational risks to Calidra by reducing its dependence on a single fuel type.
sponsor_shareholders: Calidra traces its roots back the beginning of the 20th Century and is majority-owned (52%) by the Riefkohl Family of Mexico. The company’s other shareholders are Graymont Ltd. of Canada (40%) and IFC (8%). IFC’s shareholding dates to 1998, when IFC made an equity investment in the Company as part of the financing of the first project it undertook with Calidra.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The two and one-half year investment program is estimated to cost up to $45 million. The proposed IFC investment would consist of a loan of about $20 million equivalent for IFC's own account. Up to an additional $10 million equivalent may also be raised in parallel from another bank. The balance of funds will come from internal cash generation and a share capital increase, which was recently completed.
location_description: The key components of the project will be undertaken on or adjacent to sites Calidra currently operates in Acajete (near Puebla) and near Colima. The two kilns for Acajete will be installed directly next two existing kilns operated by Calidra. The kiln to be installed near Colima will be on a quarry which is off of an isolated section of an existing highway.
additionality: Development Impact: Calidra is producing a basic industrial input that is important for the construction, steel-making, agricultural and other sectors of the economy, and the project is oriented toward fostering the development of key consuming industries, including glass making, water purification and treatment. The project is aimed at improving Calidra’s operational efficiency, better meeting localized demand, promoting new applications for lime-related products and reducing the Company’s environmental footprint. In particular, the project component to install efficient and environmentally friendly capacity in regions which are experiencing higher demand than supply is expected to at least partly substitute production from inefficient plants associated with high emissions and relatively low-quality product. IFC ‘s Role in the project involves: - support for a second-tier company, - IFC’s value-added with respect to governance, increasing management professionalism and reporting in the company’s development from a family-owned company, - provision of appropriate tenor and currency debt for a long-term investment program, and - substantive, planning (in addition to financial) support of the company’s on-going efforts to reduce its environmental footprint.

project_description: Nanjing Kumho Tire Company Limited (the company or NKT) is a company based in Nanjing, China that produces tires for passenger cars, trucks and buses. Total revenues for 2002 were approximately $115 million. The Company was formed in 1994 as a joint venture between Korea Kumho Tire Co., Ltd. of Korea, local Chinese partners and a consortium of investors. IFC financed the initial green-field project and is now contemplating the financing of the expansion. The company’s current nameplate capacity is 3 million tires per annum, which is insufficient for them to meet demand. In 2002, the company produced almost 5 million tires, by increasing its working days and shifts, optimizing process flow and substituting bias tire production capacity with radial tire production. The project is to expand the company’s nameplate capacity to 8 million tires per annum, with expectations that it can produce up to 10 million tires on the equipment. The company has a 12% share in the national radial tire market share with strong penetration in the south and east regions of China. The expansion project will enable to company to meet ongoing demand for tires, and also to produce to a quality standard adequate to meet the requirements of the most advanced OEM customers in China. NKT will also continue to export a portion of its tires. The company has had strong financial results in recent years, and intends to finance a portion of the project through internally generated cash flow.
sponsor_shareholders: Sponsor: Kumho Tire Co., Inc. (KTC, the Sponsor) was formerly a business segment of Kumho Industrial Co., Ltd. (KIC) and was involved in the manufacture and sale of tires. Effective July 1, 2003, KIC spun-off its tire business into KTC, in which it retains a 30% shareholding. The Korean Military Mutual Aid Association, an investment fund for Korean military personnel holds 50%. The remaining 20% is held by 14 other shareholders that are mostly suppliers or customers of KTC. KTC’s opening balance sheet of July 30, 2003 had total assets equivalent to approximately $1.35 billion, long term liabilities of $679 million and net worth equivalent to $424 million. KTC has two manufacturing plants in Korea, and accounts for about half of the domestic tire sales in Korea with strong international sales. The 2002 sales of KTC (on a pro-forma basis) were $1.23 billion, and 2003 sales are anticipated to be in the same range. Project Company Ownership Structure: As of July 1, 2003, the company is effectively held by KTC (51%), Nanjing Construction and Building Materials Industrial (Group) Corp., Ltd. and Nanjing Investment Corporation (20% and 5%, respectively), and the following shareholders: International Finance Corporation (8%), Kookmin Bank (6%), Asian Finance and Investment Corporation Ltd. (5%), and DEG (5%). The official transfer of shareholding from KIC and another Kumho Group company to KTC will be formalized by Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation (MOFTEC) in early 2003.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $130 million comprised of $87 million in construction cost, incremental working capital and refinancing of short-term debt. The total project cost breakdown is as follows: Project Cost: Total Construction Cost: 87 million, 67% of total; Incremental Working Capital: 5 million, 4% of total; Refinancing of ST loan: 38 million, 29% of to total; Total Project Cost: 130 million, 100% of total. The Financial Plan is made up of $28 million in additional equity, internal cash flow, and $61 million in long term debt from IFC, DEG and parallel lenders. The proposed IFC investment consists of $2.2 million in equity and an A Loan of $30 million for its own account. The Financial plan breakdown is as follows. Financial Plan: Total Equity (Rights Issue): 28 million, 21 % of total; Internal Cash Flow: 41 million, 31% of total; Total Debt: 61 million, 47% of total; Total Financing 130 million, 100% of total.
location_description: The project is located on the existing premises of NKT at 418 Heyan Road in Nanjing, China. There is available land at the existing site for the expansion. Nanjing is a large city of some 3.4 million people with multiple access routes. The city is the capital city of Jiangsu Province and is located about 190 miles due west of Shanghai.
additionality: The project contributes to the restructuring of China’s tire industry, which is a key element of the Chinese government’s plan to develop the domestic automotive sector as well as a modern parts and components industry. NKT’s plan to enter the northern market of China will promote competition in that regional market. The project also benefits from utilizing the technological and marketing expertise of KTC. NKT currently has 1,558 staff which are projected to increase to 2,081 over the project period. NKT will create jobs. In addition, the increased economic output will create wealth in NKT’s value chains which include domestic Chinese suppliers of raw materials and outsourced components, as well as providers of transport, installation and after sales service. In particular, attention will be given to strengthening the linkages with the SME’s which form part of NKT’s aftermarket distribution network. The expansion will generate economies of scale and will bring in new technology, enabling the company to meet the quality requirements of China’s leading automotive OEM’s. Finally, the success of the project will provide a demonstration effect, which will encourage further foreign direct investment into China. IFC’s role in the project includes the following: - to structure the investment and provide long-term capital, mobilize co-financing, including long-term loans from local banks; - to support technology transfer, leading to improved efficiency, quality standards and profitability; - to support ongoing environmental performance at the company; - to support and develop the company’s linkages with distributor SME companies, increasing benefits in the local economy. Such a program might include management training, consulting, and MIS development. In this regard, IFC will leverage its experience in other tire distribution linkage programs developed in the project development facilities.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: The proposed project involves the construction of a 240,000 tons annual capacity greenfield float glass plant in the Russian Federation to meet its growing domestic demand. The project will be located in the Moscow region close to its target markets. Initially sales will focus on the construction industry but later may expand to the automotive sector.
sponsor_shareholders: The project is sponsored by Pilkington plc (Pilkington or the company), and AIG Emerging Europe Infrastructure Fund L.P. (AIG EEIF). Pilkington and AIG EEIF will each hold 50% of the share capital of the project company. Employing approximately 25,600 people globally, Pilkington is a leading worldwide producer of float glass products, automotive glass products and specialty glass. Established in 1826, it is a publicly traded company on the London Stock Exchange since 1970. AIG EEIF is a private equity fund with $550 million capital to invest in selected greenfield projects, companies undergoing post-privatization restructuring and privatization in Eastern and Southern European countries including the Russian Federation.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at EUR190 million of which capital cost is EUR165 million. The proposed IFC investment is a EUR42.5 million A loan for IFC’s own account. Co-financing by EBRD for the project is planned.
location_description: The project site is greenfield in the Ramenskii District, 35 kilometers south east of Moscow. The site is located in rural area along the rail line. A new access to the main road to Moscow will be constructed as part of the project.
additionality: The project would have a substantial impact on the development of the industry and the local economy. Pilkington would bring state-of-the art float glass expertise and the best technological and managerial practices to Russia. The project will increase the competitive structure of the glass industry in the country and consumers will benefit from competitively priced, better quality float glass. It would create jobs and would also positively affect the country's balance of payment account as it results in import substitution. As a large industrial complex, the project would also generate linkages with other industries. IFC Role consists of: - providing long-term funding which otherwise is not available in the country, - ensuring that the project is implemented in an environmentally sound way, - the project could encourage other lenders and investors to consider investments in the Russian Federation.

project_description: Ballarpur Industries Limited (BILT or the company) is the single largest manufacturer of writing and printing (W&P) paper in India. BILT has a total production capacity of 375,000 tons per annum (TPA) of W&P paper and a total pulp capacity of 335,000 TPA, spread across five pulp and paper manufacturing facilities. The company was established in 1945 and is listed on all the major Indian stock exchanges. The proposed $159.7 million project consists of - environmental improvements ($14.4 million); - product quality improvements ($15 million); - production capacity increase ($15.7 million); - expansion of the farm forestry ($6.2 million); - working capital for paper trading ($8.0 million) and for regular operations ($5.7 million); and - Debt Refinancing ($94.7 million).
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is The LM and Gautam Thapar Group (the sponsor or the group) is one of the India’s premier industrial houses with pulp and paper being the core business of the group. The majority of the shareholding of the company is held by the promoters (41.92%), foreign promoters/investors hold 15.63%, Indian Financial Institutions/Mutual Funds hold 26.62% the public holds 12.66% while the rest is categorized under others corporate bodies 3.17%.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is $159.7 million. The proposed IFC investment is $15 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: While the company is headquartered in New Delhi, plant sites are located throughout India. Environmental and farm forestry improvements are planned for sites and plants in Maharashtra, Haryana, Orissa and Andhra Pradesh and Chattisgarh. Production increases and/or product quality improvements will be made to plants in Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh and Orissa. All sites are pre existing and have access to the country’s network of roads. With the exception of the plant in Haryana, all project sites are located in rural areas. Prior to Haryana’s growth in recent years, it was also rural.
additionality: Development Impact: - Social Forestry The company is providing free saplings and other inputs to small farmers close to its plant, providing a stable income to augment otherwise seasonally variable revenue, to nurture the current supply base, to develop farm forestry in the vicinity of each manufacturing unit, raise and distribute seedlings to farmers at subsidized costs, develop site-specific high yield tree varieties and operate purchase depots to ensure fair prices for the produce. This will result in a significant improvement to the income stream of small farmers located mostly in lesser-developed areas of India. In addition, the company''s R&D efforts provide increased know how from a local source. - Poverty Reduction: BILT''s forest operation has a direct and indirect employment effect on a very large number of low income rural people in outlying and depressed areas and social support. - Environmental Improvements: The company maintains high environmental standards, and the project would continue to set a benchmark for majority of the paper companies in India. The company''s investment in the proposed environment project will result in improved emissions control, energy efficiency, and increased bio-mass and farm forestry enterprise. The Fiber Resource Development Program will promote sustainable forest management practices. IFC Role: - Farm Forestry: With this project, IFC will help BILT further develop its linkage program of support for smallholder forestry to raise farmer incomes, and will advise on sustainable forest management practices. IFC''s investment will directly contribute to sustainable forestry operations. It is worth noting here that the social forest program was recommended by IFC while investing in BILT in 2000. - Catalyst for Mobilizing Resources: IFC has been involved with BILT since 2001 when it issued a partial guarantee for BILT’s domestic bond issue. This support enabled BILT to subsequently access local capital markets on its own. IFC''s participation in this project is crucial to build investor confidence and will mobilize the participation of other financial intermediaries. Through this project, BILT will make a mark in the international financial markets and could subsequently access private capital in international capital markets on its own. It will also attract private international investors and thereby diversify BILT’s shareholders. - Corporate Finance: The company''s operations are strong, it has/is in the process of obtaining commitments to refinance approximately $95 million of Foreign and Local currency loans. IFC has made the debt refinancing a condition to the participation in the project. The debt refinancing will strengthen BILT’s financial position.

project_description: Opet Petrolcülük A.S. (Opet or the company) is a retail distributor of petroleum products in Turkey, owned 50% by the Koç Group of Turkey and 50% by Opet’s founding shareholders, the Ozturk family. The project is aimed at strengthening the company’s position in the Turkish petroleum products distribution industry and enhancing its competitiveness in advance of further liberalization. The project is comprised of : - the construction of a greenfield marine terminal and tank storage facility which will increase the company’s oil products storage capacity from 320,000 m3 to 766,000 m3; and, - expansion of the company’s existing retail distribution network, with new stations primarily located in the larger cities of Turkey. The distribution expansion network will enhance the company’s brand recognition in the lucrative Istanbul, Izmir and other larger retail markets. In addition, the project will enable Opet to import larger parcels of products, store in-house, reduce transportation costs and improve the reliability of supply, while simultaneously supporting growth in its fuel distribution business. Opet hopes to take advantage of its strategic location at the mouth of the Black Sea to offer bunkering facilities for Caspian oil products. The intense sea traffic in the region will also give Opet the opportunity to purchase low-cost petroleum products.
sponsor_shareholders: Opet Shareholder Structure: From its inception in 1992 through November 2002, Opet was owned 100% by the Ozturk family, which had over 20 years trading experience in the Turkish petroleum sector. In December 2002, the Koç Group purchased 50% of Opet’s shares from the Ozturk family for $125 million. The Ozturk family collectively retained 50% of the outstanding shares. The Koç Group obtained its shares through Aygaz, its LPG distribution company, as well as through other affiliated companies. The current Opet shareholding structure is as follows: Öztürk Family Members (50%), Aygaz A.S. (40%) and other Koç Group Companies (10%). Aygaz & Koç Group: Aygaz is majority-controlled (52.5%) by the Koç Group, Turkey’s largest diversified conglomerate with operations in energy and numerous other sectors. The Koç Group is one of IFC’s most important global relationships. Aygaz is listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange where 28.5% of its shares are publicly traded.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated to be $150 million and Opet has requested IFC to provide a corporate loan consisting of a $25 million A Loan and a $35 million B Loan.
location_description: The marine terminal and storage facilities are to be located north of the Marmara Sea in Thrace (in a suburban area) and will consist of a marine terminal, tank farm, truck loading units, pipelines between the marine terminal and tank farm, sanitary waste treatment unit, ballast water treatment facilities, auxiliary systems, fire fighting, steam generation, water treatment unit, motor control center, diesel generator and compressed air system. The retail stations will be located all over Turkey, with special concentration in the largest cities.
additionality: Development Impact: The proposed project will have a number of beneficial impacts, including: - enhancing the long-term viability of a Turkish company which operates in a cyclical industry; Opet will gain economies of scale, improve its operating efficiencies, and raise standards resulting in potentially lower fuel prices to consumers when the market liberalizes; - increasing competition in the automotive LPG and retail petroleum and products sectors; - enhancing existing retail distribution offerings and providing cleaner roadside facilities to consumers in the Istanbul and Marmara regions; - enhancing investor confidence in working with a strong Turkish company; - putting the company in a position to take advantage of the market liberalization anticipated under the New Petroleum Law; - allowing oil products to be stored and distributed in compliance with EU quality standards; - allowing Opet to demonstrate its commitment to sustainable business practices; - allowing Opet to continue to be one of the more significant tax paying entities in Turkey. IFC Role: The IFC investment will enable the company to lower its funding cost and secure funding of longer maturities, thus stabilizing its cash flow through periods of cyclicality. Current market conditions in Turkey do not indicate that alternative sources of long-term finance will be available anytime soon. Under these conditions only larger multinational players such as BP and Shell have access to finance for the upgrading and modernization of their distribution networks. IFC has a key role to play in the mobilization of long-term capital under the IFC B Loan program and in assisting parallel lenders such as FMO and DEG. The proposed B Loan aims to provide reasonably priced long-term financing, which is important not only for ensuring profitability in an increasingly competitive domestic distribution market, but also for positioning the company to take advantage of changes in the market expected under the New Petroleum Law. IFC has provided in depth advice on marketing and technical issues pertaining to the proposed Marmara marine terminal, as well as an important role in ensuring proper environmental compliance. Finance facilities provided to the project will also help remove the need for petroleum product distributors in the Thrace region to transport supplies over the two Bosphorous bridges by tanker.

project_description: The proposed IFC investment is a corporate loan to Metrocentro S.A. de C.V. (Metrocentro or the company), a company which owns and operates nine shopping malls in El Salvador, with a total gross leasable area (GLA) of 137,367 m2, including the largest mall in the country, Metrocentro San Salvador. As part of its continuous expansion strategy, Metrocentro has started implementing a $55 million Multiplaza Panamericana project, to address the increasing demand for quality shopping complexes in El Salvador. The proposed new shopping mall will have a total GLA of approximately 41,000 m2; it will host two anchor tenants/department stores, movie theaters, a supermarket, restaurants, financial center and a food court. The mall is planned to become fully operational in December 2004. It will be part of a large diversified complex, including apartments, offices, and hotel, which will be developed at a later stage. As a result, the proposed project is expected to stimulate further development of the selected location, ultimately benefiting the local community.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Grupo Poma, a well established family owned business group, with business interests in automobile distribution, manufacturing, real estate, including hotels and shopping malls, across the Central American region. The Group is also actively involved in community work through the Fundacion Poma, its non-profit organization. The Group is majority owned by the Poma family of El Salvador. Grupo Poma operates its shopping mall businesses through Prisma S.A. (Panama), a trust holding the Poma family’s business interests, which fully owns International Shopping Center Holdings, Inc. (ISC). ISC presently owns 14 shopping malls in Central America with a total of about 250,000 m2 GLA. Metrocentro is 67.4% owned by ISC, 9.4% by the three strategic investors, and the remaining 23.1% is owned by about 150 individual investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at approximately $54 million. The proposed IFC investment is a loan of up to $25 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project site is situated is the southwestern area of metropolitan San Salvador in the jurisdiction of San Salvador and Antiguo Cuscatlan municipalities. It encompasses an area of 145 ha encompassing of the basin of the La Lechuza brook that forms a part of the Acelhuate river basin between coordinates of 13o 40’ N and 89o 15’ West.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment in Metrocentro will enable the following: - improvements in the urban infrastructure of the capital city in El Salvador; - better consumer choices because the clustering of competitors facilitates comparisons of offers and improves consumers knowledge resulting in higher quality goods available at lower prices for the consumer; - improvements in the quality of goods sold; - increase in standards for hygiene and safety in product handling and storage; - improvements in practices among local product suppliers, especially food and fresh products that filter through to other retail formats, including open air vendors; and - creation of more than 5,000 direct and indirect jobs during the construction and operational stage. In addition, as in the Group’s previous malls, the proposed project is expected to attract other development to the area, creating a demonstration effect and contributing to the overall community development. During construction of the shopping mall, strong linkages with the construction and building supply sectors will be established. In addition, once operational, the project will stimulate use of local supplies of goods and services in El Salvador, which will represent more than 40% of the shopping mall supply. IFC’s role in Metrocentro is as follows: - Supporting a successful Central American company to expand its shopping mall business in El Salvador, by establishing Multiplaza Panamericana, a good quality shopping mall and the first of its kind in El Salvador, that would improve the infrastructure in the area where it is located as well as contribute to improvements of the living standard of target customers. - Providing long-term financing to the company that would otherwise be difficult to mobilize from local banks only. and, - Helping the company to improve its environmental standards and establish a training program targeting local retailers who would be located in the company’s malls.

project_description: The project consists of the construction of six luxury guest houses with 8-16 rooms each, at different locations in western Bhutan. The venture is a greenfield project being undertaken by Bhutan Resorts Corporation Limited (BRCL or the company), a company incorporated in Bhutan.
sponsor_shareholders: BRCL will be owned 60% by the Bhutan Hotels Limited which is a fully-owned subsidiary of Silverlink Holdings, a BVI-registered company; 20% by the Bhutan Tourism Corporation Limited, a publicly held company and the third largest tour operator in Bhutan. The remaining 20% will be offered to local financial institutions and the general public at a later stage.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $18.0 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to $6.3 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The six lodges and their associated facilities/access roads will be at the following locations in Bhutan: Paro, Thimphu, Punakha, Gangte, Trongsa and Bhumthang.

project_description: As a vertically integrated poultry producer, Mironovsky Khleboprodukt (Mironovsky, MKP or the company) currently holds a leading position in Ukraine poultry market. The company was one of the pioneers in developing a chilled distribution system to retailers, and rapidly grew in size reaching a sale volume of 43,000mt of ready to cook poultry products in 2002. The company sells chilled poultry products (whole birds, cutup, giblets etc.) under a well recognized brand name, Nasha Ryaba, across Ukraine, with the strongest presence in the Kiev region. The project aims to take advantage of the increasingly growing poultry consumption in Ukraine, low production costs, a robust management team and the company’s leading market position. The project will help Mironovsky to capitalize on the opportunities offered by the rapidly changing consumer preference towards chilled products. By sharing IFC’s global investment experience, the project will enable the company to improve its corporate governance and rationalize its corporate structure. The project will also directly benefit at least 400 outside workers who sell the company’s products through franchise in addition to employing some 4,000 staff on site.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Yuriy Kosyuk, also CEO of the company. Mr. Kosyuk became involved in gas clearing operation with Turkmenistan since 1999. He later decided to invest profits from gas business in the poultry business, and acquired Mironovsky feedmill and Cherkassy broiler complex. Both were facing difficulties and going through bankruptcy. Subsequently the sponsor made additional investments in another two broiler complexes and two parent farms. Currently, the sponsor’s poultry assets include a feed mill with capacity of 230,000 tpa (in Mironovsky), three broiler complexes (which include four hatcheries, three broilers and three processing plants respectively in Cherksassy, Oril Leader and Crimea), two parent stock farms (respectively in Starinska and Shaterskaya), and a chilled distribution system to retail outlets.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated $116 million of which $29 million was already incurred in 2002. The proposed IFC investment is $30 million loans to Mironovsky and its operating subsidiaries.
location_description: The company’s poultry operations spread across Ukraine in six major locations – Crimea (a broiler complex with hatchery, broiler and processing plant), Cherkassy (a broiler complex with hatchery, broiler and processing plant), Oril Leader (a broiler complext with hatchery, broiler and processing plant), Mironovsky (feedmill), Starinska (parent stock farm) and Shahterskaya (parent stock farm).

project_description: The project involves the redevelopment by UACN Property Development Company PLC (UPDC) of a recently privatized hotel complex in Lagos, Nigeria, into: - a 432-room, three-star hotel, targeting the mid-market; - conference facilities; - a business center and health club; and - retail and commercial office space. The project is aimed at the large mid-market in Nigeria that would prefer not to stay in the four/five star accommodations available in Lagos and is underserved by hotels specifically targeted at that sector.
sponsor_shareholders: UPDC Hotels is the project company which is majority owned by the sponsor, UPDC - a Nigerian property development and management company, which engages in the acquisition, development and management of residential and commercial property and listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange, Lagos. UPDC is an associated company of UAC of Nigeria PLC (UACN), which owns 46% of the UPDC.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated up to $32 million. The proposed IFC investment is estimated up to a maximum of $11.0 million A loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The project is located at the current Festac ‘ 77 Hotel site, within Anuwo Odofin Housing Estate. The hotel is well situated in a busy mixed use (residential, commercial and light industrial) area of Lagos, close to the airport, the seaport, some major markets and the main road into Nigeria from the Republic of Benin.
additionality: IFC will provide long-term financing, which is not otherwise available, and will ensure the project is implemented in an environmentally sound manner. The project is expected to have the following key development impacts: - supporting the government’s privatization efforts through the rehabilitation of state assets and creation of employment; - facilitating business by providing quality accommodation at reasonable prices for local and international visitors; - providing quality retail, office and entertainment facilities to the local community, which is currently underserved.

project_description: The Lecico Group (Lecico or the Group), a leading manufacturer of sanitary ware and ceramic tiles in the Middle East, headquartered in Alexandria, Egypt, has requested IFC to provide a corporate loan of up to $20 million. The Group’s holding and main operating company Lecico Egypt S.A.E (Lecico Egypt or the company) is planning to make various investments to expand the Group’s production capacity in Egypt and to refinance the debt of its majority-owned subsidiary the Lebanese Ceramic Industries Co. S.A.L. (Lecico Lebanon) in Lebanon. The proposed investment will help Lecico address sanitary ware export growth opportunities in the region and Europe as well as reduce production costs further in order to make it more competitive.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Lecico Egypt. Its shareholding structure is as follows: Ceramics Holding Middle East (CHME) 75% Egyptian Finance Company 7% Commercial International Investment Co. 4% EFC Holding 3% Others 11% Total 100%   CHME was established in 1997 as a 50/50 % joint venture between the Gargour family of Lebanon and Sanitec, one of the major global sanitary ware manufacturers. The other major shareholders of Lecico Egypt are Egyptian investment companies.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Lecico Group has requested IFC’s support to finance various investments totaling $37 million. The proposed IFC investment is a corporate loan of up to $20 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The Lecico Group is headquartered in Alexandria, Egypt. The Lecico Group’s plants are located in - Khorshid, Alexandria, Egypt, - Borg El Arab, Egypt; and - Kfarshima, Lebanon. The proposed capacity expansion will take place at the Borg El Arab plant, 70 km from Alexandria.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment will help Lecico expand production to increase its exports and build upon its state-of-the-art technology and strong domestic and foreign customer relationships. By helping Lecico address export growth opportunities, the proposed Investment will help increase Egypt’s export competitiveness. By adopting IFC’s environmental, health and safety standards, the Group will improve its practices in these areas. IFC Role: IFC will play a role in: - providing long-term finance that is scarce for mid-sized companies such as Lecico Egypt; - supporting the development of an internationally competitive, majority locally owned and operated company; - improving the Group’s environmental practices; and - strengthening the Group’s corporate governance.

project_description: The project is to design, construct and operate a greenfield, integrated, dry process cement plant of 800,000 tons per year (tpy) clinker capacity and 900,000 tpy cement capacity at an estimated cost of $84 million in the Dominican Republic. The Domicem plant is expected to be commissioned by May 2005 and to sell 90% of its production in the domestic market and 10% as exports. As of March 16, 2005, there has been a modification to this project, which is covered under a new project, Domicem II – Project No.24209. Total Project Cost has also been revised to US$113.5 million.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are Colacem, S.p.A. of Italy (51%) and a group of local partners in the Dominican Republic with substantial knowledge of the local building materials industry (49%). Colacem ranks as Italy’s third-largest cement company and is part of the Financo Holding Group, a private Italian conglomerate owned by the Colaiacovo family of Italy. Founded in the 1950s as a construction and building materials company, Financo today has interests in four operating divisions: - cement/hydraulic binders; - concrete and aggregates; - transport, and - diversified industries. In 2002, Colacem had estimated Net Sales of Euro 398 million, EBITDA (Earnings Before Income Tax and Depreciation) of Euro 145 million and Total Assets of Euro 674 million. SIMEST will acquire a 2% shareholding in Domicem from Colacem, although Colacem will retain majority voting control of Domicem. SIMEST is a publicly owned Italian company supported by the Ministry of Industry and created to encourage Italian investments abroad. Its Board of Directors comprises a range of Italian industrial companies and banks.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $84 million. The proposed IFC investment amounts to $42 million and comprises a $21 million A Loan for IFC’s own account and a $21 million B Loan for the account of participants. As of March 16, 2005, total project cost has been revised to US$113. 5 million. The proposed IFC investment will increase to US$55.5 million (see project Domicem II – No. 24209).
location_description: The Domicem project will be located on a 500 ha site located 40 km from the capital Santo Domingo, 26 km from the international Port of de Haina and 2 km from the village of Sabana Grande de Palanque, where the project’s limestone quarries are located. The site is easily accessible, located 2,000 meters away from the Haina Palanque highway.
additionality: The IFC Role will provide the following: - Access to Long-term Financing. IFC’s involvement will enable the project to obtain long-term financing with maturities otherwise unavailable in the local DR market. As a greenfield project, Domicem requires adequate grace periods on principal repayments to ensure proper capitalization and ‘breathing room’ during construction and start-up. IFC will also play a catalytic role by attempting to mobilize up to $21 million from foreign commercial banks who may be unfamiliar with the local DR market and political environment. In this regard, IFC’s own investment in the project is expected to provide comfort to banks. - Support to Colacem. Colacem seeks to diversify geographically and find growth opportunities in emerging markets. While it has formed a joint venture with strong local partners in the DR, Colacem can benefit from IFC’s involvement in Domicem given that this is its first investment in Latin America. IFC contributes, beyond its ‘umbrella’, regional knowledge and investment experience in the cement industry in the Latin America. IFC has also provided the Sponsors with input such as suggesting improvements in limestone quarry investigation, bulk sampling of raw materials for the turnkey contractor, and guarantee for Nitrogen Oxides (NOx). - Endorsement of CBMI as Turnkey Contractor. IFC has first-hand knowledge of CBMI, the Chinese turnkey contractor, which Colacem will use for the Domicem project after its successful prior collaboration with CBMI. IFC’s endorsement of CBMI would help introduce a new, low cost, competitive supplier to the Latin American market. Development Impact: The Domicem project, a joint venture between Colacem, an industry player with a solid track record and a strong group of local DR investors, is expected to improve the productivity and competitiveness of the DR cement sector. By supplying its own clinker needs through an integrated cement operation in a country where 60% of cement is produced on the basis of imported clinker, Domicem is expected to have a competitive cost structure. The additional production of quality cement is expected to reduce cement prices in the DR, which are among the highest in the world, to more competitive levels. Other development benefits of the project include ‘best practice’ technology transfer, job creation and foreign exchange generation when the project exports a portion of its production. The project will also support infrastructure development and construction efforts, which are critical in a country prone to frequent devastation from hurricanes and in constant need of quality cement and building materials. Colacem has a track record of implementing community development programs in the communities where it operates in Italy and is committed to support similar efforts in the DR. Domicem is expected to operate in line with superior environmental management and safeguard systems, including ‘best practice’ standards for energy efficiency.

project_description: The Project entails the construction and operation of the 124-room Marriott Courtyard Hotel in Port of Spain (POS), the capital of Trinidad & Tobago (T&T), by Caribe Hospitality of T&T (CHTT). Demand for business lodging has grown in recent years as a result of significant investment in Trinidad and should continue to increase with new developments in the natural gas sector and other positive economic indicators. Marriott International will operate the hotel under a Management Agreement and will provide technical assistance in the design and implementation phases.
sponsor_shareholders: Caribe Hospitality of Trinidad & Tobago Ltd. (CHTT), the project company, was incorporated in 2002 as a joint venture between Caribe Hospitality S.A (CH) (60%), Mouttet Capital Ltd (30%) and Poui Holdings Ltd (10%). The purpose of the company is to develop the POS Courtyard hotel. Caribe Hospitality S.A. was incorporated in Panama for the sole purpose of developing and operating small business hotels in Central America and the Caribbean to be managed by Marriott under its Courtyard brand. The intent is to partner with local sponsors for individual hotels on a joint venture basis. Shareholders in Caribe Hospitality are Ramiro Ortiz, Edgar Zurcher and John Keith. Local sponsors in this project are Mouttet Capital Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Victor E Mouttet Limited (VEML) established in Trinidad in 1958, and Poui Holdings Ltd., a shell company that is owned by Joseph Esau, a Trinidadian national.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $11 million. IFC’s proposed investment comprises an A loan of $1.6 million and a C loan of $2.0 million with an income participation feature.
location_description: The POS Courtyard will be located in Invaders Bay, about a mile from the downtown area of the city and across from Hasley Crawford Stadium. Invaders Bay is a former swampland which was filled several years ago by the government to address the need for additional land in Port of Spain. Completed developments in Invaders Bay thus far include a port, PriceSmart and the MovieTowne complex which includes restaurants and shops.
additionality: The Caribe Hospitality concept has an important development impact in demonstrating that regional investment schemes with cross border capital can be successfully implemented in Central America and the Caribbean. Through CH, local and regional investors are able to expand and diversify their business interests. Ultimately the establishment of a chain of business hotels in this area will support regional trade and business development with a network linked by common management and onward reservations, and providing services of known quality and range. More specifically the POS Courtyard will: - provide additional hotel rooms which are clearly needed as part of the country’s basic business infrastructure; - introduce high standards in life and fire safety, energy and water conservation, etc., which should encourage similar upgrading by other hotels; - support a near downtown urban hub that is becoming an important location for modern retailing and social activities; - have strong linkages with T&T’s construction and building supply sectors during construction. Once operational, the project will stimulate local supplies of goods and services used by the hotel and its guests; - provide direct employment for some 60 workers once the hotel is operational and many more jobs will be created indirectly. Hotel employees will benefit from Marriott’s training programs, promotion practices and overall high service standards. IFC’s most important role is the provision of A and C loans with long tenors and grace periods to match market and project risks. IFC has also provided valuable input regarding the Management Agreement and the land lease agreement. In the future IFC may pursue additional CH hotel investments and we can continue to valuable input to improve the viability of CH by ensuring that future hotel projects undertaken are justified on a market basis, that management agreements with Marriott are equitable, that project costs are reasonable and that the financial structures for individual projects are sound.

project_description: The proposed Euros 73.8 million project represents a post privatization restructuring of a Bulgarian steel mini-mill, Stomana Industry A.D. (Stomana, or the company). Headquartered in the Pernik industrial area, Stomana is the largest employer in a depressed region, notorious with the unsuccessful privatizations of a number of big state-owned companies. Moreover, with production of about 600,000 tpy of long and flat steel products and more than 1,300 employees, Stomana is the second largest steel producer in Bulgaria and one of the most important enterprises in the country. The project will be implemented by Sidenor Steel Products Manufacturing Company S.A. (Sidenor or the Sponsor). As part of the project, Sidenor will refurbish the plant, improve production methods and environmental performance, and facilitate transition to higher value-added products. After the completion of the overall investment program, Stomana's production is not expected to divert significantly from current levels as planned investment is in cost reduction and quality improvements, and not in capacity increases.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor, Sidenor (with 75% shareholding in Stomana), is based in Greece and is the largest long steel products manufacturer in the country. It operates two steel mini-mills in Greece and has holdings in several companies which manufacture and market a wide variety of steel products. Established in 1962, Sidenor has been continuously profitable without a single year of financial loss. Sidenor is listed on the Athens Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at about Euros 73.8 million. IFC is considering a financial package of approximately Euros 30 million comprised of: - an A Loan for IFC’s own account of about Euros 20 million, and, - an equity or quasi-equity investment of about Euros 10 million.
location_description: The project will be implemented in Stomana’s existing production facilities, located in the industrial zone of the town of Pernik, Bulgaria. Pernik is situated about 30 kilometers southwest of Bulgaria’s capital, Sofia.
additionality: The project is expected to reduce costs and improve quality and competitiveness. It should result in more efficient use of raw material inputs and labor, and a better overall productivity, due to implementation of new, better technology, and improved management practices. Moreover, the project is expected to have a significant environmental impact as the sponsor is planning to invest about Euros 13 million in environmental improvements. The project will benefit from the management expertise of a strong sponsor, who has significant technological know-how for both investment and production. In addition, the sponsor will bring into the project advanced marketing and sales techniques and a proven quality control system. An important part of sponsor's support will be on-the job training provided by Sidenor, including employee training in Sidenor's plants in Greece. Last but not least, as Stomana is one of the largest employers in the town of Pernik, the successful turnaround of the mini mill is critical for Pernik’s community and its surroundings. IFC has a major role to play in this project by providing long term financing which is scarce in Bulgaria. IFC will play a critical developmental role by ensuring that the project meets World Bank environmental and safety guidelines and hence serve as a model in pollution and dust emission control in Bulgaria. IFC is also playing an important role in structuring the financial plan and bringing other lenders into the transaction while also helping sustain major productive asset and a key employer in the region.

project_description: Olam International Limited (Olam or the company) is an international integrated supplier of both raw and processed agricultural commodities headquartered in Singapore with over 2,300 employees worldwide. Olam operates in 35 countries (primarily in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia) and in nine major agricultural products: cocoa, rice, cashew, cotton, coffee, timber, sugar, sesame and shea nut. The company is involved in varying degrees across the total product supply chain, which can include procurement as close to farmgate as possible, primary processing, inland transport, warehousing, marine transport, and distribution -- using a network of local buying agents, primary processing facilities and logistics. The proposed IFC investment will help strengthen Olam’s balance sheet and support its operations. IFC's financing is therefore expected to help enhance and expand Olam's activities in frontier countries including Ghana, Cameroon, Gabon, Nigeria, Indonesia, Viet Nam and Uzbekistan.
sponsor_shareholders: Olam is part of the Kewalram Chanrai Group which is held privately by overseas Indian family trusts. From the Chanrai family's beginnings in trading in Nigeria and India in 1860, the group has grown into a conglomerate with diversified operations and interests in textile manufacturing, agri-commodities sourcing, processing and trading, international trade, and property development employing more than 12,000 people in over 45 countries. Olam's other shareholders are its management group and the Asia Infrastructure Fund, an IFC investee.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC equity investment of US$15 million is part of a project aimed at helping Olam expand its equity base by approximately US$50 million in order to strengthen its balance sheet and support its operations worldwide, mainly in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia.
location_description: The project will support Olam’s activities mainly in over 20 existing origin countries in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia where the company sources, processes and/or markets its nine major agricultural products.

project_description: Borusan Group is a major Turkish company involved in steel and pipe production, distribution of automobiles and heavy construction equipment, a logistics company and in new technologies. The proposed project consists of: - restructuring the balance sheet; - implementing a number of corporate initiatives to improve productivity; and - strengthening corporate governance. The objective is to improve the company’s overall operational and financial performance. Borusan Group is organized into five divisions: - Steel Pipe Division: comprising three companies which together represent one of the top five pipe manufacturers in Europe; - Distribution Division: comprising the sales and support for Caterpillar construction and earth moving equipment and power systems and also BMW and Land Rover passenger vehicles; - Flat Steel Division: which includes Borçelik, an IFC client, with cold-rolling steel operations; -Logistics Division: which provides logistics, domestic and international transport, port, warehousing and other services to third parties; and, - Technology Division: offering LAN, alternative telecom and other IT services and taking partnerships in high growth IT and telecom companies.
sponsor_shareholders: Borusan Group is organized under a Holding structure, which acts as a parent for its operating subsidiaries. The Borusan Holding is owned by members of Kocabiyik family and is privately held. Borusan history began in 1944 with Istikbal Ticaret, a trading company. By 1972, after integrating steel pipe operations, all Borusan companies were brought together under Borusan Holding. In the 80's Borusan entered a new sector, distributorship, by becoming the Turkish representative for BMW passenger vehicles, as well as for Caterpillar professional earth moving equipment and power systems as the brand's sole representative in Turkey, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Kazakhstan. The 90's also marked the founding of Borçelik, Turkey's first private sector manufacturer of cold rolled flat steel. The partnership with Mannesmann in 1998 placed Borusan among the top five steel pipe producers in Europe.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: IFC’s proposed investment is up to $40 million long-term loans on IFC’s own account and syndicated loans.
location_description: Borusan Group is headquartered in Istanbul, Turkey. Most of the operations are located in Istanbul and within the Marmara region. The Distributorship Division has its representations across the country as well as CIS.
additionality: - Borusan Holding is one of the second tier corporations in Turkey. However, IFC’s track record with its most prominent and profitable operations has been excellent: Borusan’s pipe division since 1976 and Borçelik since 1994. As the Group prepares for the next stage in its evolution against the backdrop of economic and political uncertainty in Turkey, it need access to stable long-term financing. Long-term financing in Turkey is virtually nonexistent, limited to only supplier financing, a problem which is exacerbated in the current crisis environment. - The project includes the implementation of important corporate initiatives as described above, which will build on an established base of achievements in these areas: Group companies already hold various quality certifications, such as ISO 9001, ISO 9002, ISO 14001, OHSAS 18001, QS 9000; in addition, Borçelik has won the European Foundation for Quality Management (EFQM) excellence model award. - The project will strengthen a group employing 3,400 people, most of which are based outside of Istanbul.
