project_description: The Cartones América Group (CAME, the Group or the company) is a leading, privately-owned, Andean Region manufacturer of containerboard, corrugated boxes, clay-coated paperboard, spiral tube board and specialty board packaging products.. The Group traces its roots back to the 1950s in Cali, Colombia. In recent years the company has grown steadily, investing in operations in Venezuela (1993), Ecuador (1998), and Peru (2000). CAME is in an important phase of its development and the project is aimed at helping CAME consolidate recent investments and realize the synergies to be achieved in its operations across the Andean Region..
sponsor_shareholders: Cartones América S.A. (incorporated in Cali, Colombia) directly and indirectly wholly-owns all the companies of the Group. Cartones América is a privately held company which is majority owned (69.8%) by a Colombian family which has been dedicated to the packaging industry for more than 40 years. Citicorp International Finance Corporation is the most important minority shareholder (29.5%) with the balance held by former and current employees (0.7%).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at up to $44 million. IFC is considering extending an A loan for its own account of up to $22 million to CAME, of which up to $5 million could be a quasi-equity instrument. About one-half of the project cost would be allocated to debt refinancing which will extend CAME’s debt maturities, improving its credit profile and strengthening its balance sheet. The balance of the project cost is comprised of investments in operational improvements, environmental upgrades and working capital that is aimed at enhancing CAME’s competitiveness and further reducing its impact on the environment. The most significant of these investments is for a cogeneration plant in Cali, estimated to cost up to $6 million. Other investments include a new printing machine in Ecuador and upgrades in environmental controls at plants in each of the countries CAME operates in
location_description: CAME operates paper mills in Cali (Colombia) and Chincha (Peru). In addition, it operates corrugating and box making operations in Cali and Mosquera (Colombia), Lurin (Peru), as well as near Valencia (Venezuela), and Quito (Ecuador). The two plants in Cali are separate sites within the urban area of the city. The other sites are all located in industrial parks situated on the edge of cities. Some portion of the capital investment comprising the project is allocated for each of these sites. The most significant investment, a cogeneration plant, would be installed at the paper mill site in Cali.
additionality: IFC’s support for CAME will support the Company’s drive to become more efficient and competitive. Impacts on economic development in Colombia are given below. - Strengthening a non-traditional industrial activity to enhance the country’s economic diversification. - Employment Impact- CAME employs nearly 600 people directly. Further, indirectly its operations support the activities of 40 recycled paper collection companies in the Andean Region which employ 800 people directly and an estimated 8,000 indirectly. In Bogotá, CAME is participating in a program with the municipality to build recycled waste collection centers which are operated by street collectors. - Community Development:- CAME actively supports its workers in home purchase. More than 90% of its workers in Cali are homeowners, and it has been implementing the same program for employees at its companies in Ecuador and Peru. CAME has also supported the formation of SMEs in service areas including transportation, maintenance and production of labor intensive items such as dividers. Finally, CAME invests in training at all levels. Its policy is to cover 50% of the cost of educational programs attended by its employees, and many of its employees have acquired technical, university and masters degrees. - Environmentally Friendly.- CAME’s mills use recycled waste as it main raw material. The Group has invested in technology to permit the utilization of lower grades of recycled fibers. They have also made investments to substitute boiler fuel from diesel to natural gas and to increase water consumption efficiency. IFC’s role in the project has the three aspects outlined below. - Access to Long-term Financing.- Recession, liquidity constraints in the domestic banking sector, struggles with narco-terrorist activity, and Colombia’s loss of its investment grade rating have severely constrained access to long-term credit, even for strong credits such as CAME. Many foreign commercial banks have left the Colombian market or conduct short-term trade financing only and IFC remains one of few long-term sources of financing for independent companies. - Catalytic Role.- Given the situation described above, CAME’s current lenders would not be able to extend the maturities of their current loan exposures in individually. However, with IFC taking a lead by extending a loan of up to 9 years maturity, some of these banks have indicated that on the basis of an improved debt maturity profile, they will be able to increase the final maturity of some of their current loans to CAME from about 2-3 years to about 7 years. - Value-Added for next Stage of Corporate Development. Historically a family-owned company, CAME is rising through the ranks of middle market companies to become a more significant regional player. Its next stage of development may include geographic diversification into Central America and the Caribbean and a potential linking with an industrial partner. The company may be able to leverage IFC’s ties in the industry and its experience in neighboring markets to support the pursuit of these objectives. - Support for Cross-Border Operation. IFC’s support for CAME is consistent with the objectives of the governments of the Andean Region to promote cross-border business and financial synergies. In particular, IFC’s engagement is important in backing the Group’s operations in Venezuela, where CAME has extremely limited financing options due to the recent crises.

project_description: Olam International Limited (Olam or the company) is an international integrated supplier of both raw and processed agricultural commodities headquartered in Singapore with over 2,300 employees worldwide. Olam operates in 35 countries (primarily in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia) and in nine major agricultural products: cocoa, rice, cashew, cotton, coffee, timber, sugar, sesame and shea nut. The company is involved in varying degrees across the total product supply chain, which can include procurement as close to farmgate as possible, primary processing, inland transport, warehousing, marine transport, and distribution -- using a network of local buying agents, primary processing facilities and logistics. The proposed IFC investment will help strengthen Olam’s balance sheet and support its operations. IFC''s financing is therefore expected to help enhance and expand Olam''s activities in frontier countries including Ghana, Cameroon, Gabon, Nigeria, Indonesia, Vietnam and Uzbekistan.
sponsor_shareholders: Olam is part of the Kewalram Chanrai Group which is held privately by overseas Indian family trusts. From the Chanrai family''s beginnings in trading in Nigeria and India in 1860, the group has grown into a conglomerate with diversified operations and interests in textile manufacturing, agri-commodities sourcing, processing and trading, international trade, and property development employing more than 12,000 people in over 45 countries. Olam''s other shareholders are its management group and the Asia Infrastructure Fund, an IFC investee.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC equity investment of $15 million is part of a project aimed at helping Olam expand its equity base by approximately $50 million in order to strengthen its balance sheet and support its operations worldwide, mainly in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia.
location_description: The project will support Olam’s activities mainly in over 20 existing origin countries in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia where the company sources, processes and/or markets its nine major agricultural products.
additionality: The project’s development impact include continued direct benefits to rural populations and a demonstration impact on sustainability. Olam''s operations provide substantial benefits to rural areas of many developing countries given the company''s ability to - enhance the efficiency and transparency of agribusiness logistics and - provide knowledge transfer in the primary processing of products which set high standards needed to meet the requirements of international buyers, thereby providing best practices for local companies to emulate. With Sub-Saharan Africa and Asia accounting each for about half of Olam''s production volume, IFC''s investment in Olam complements the World Bank''s efforts in liberalizing the commodity export markets in many developing countries. It also provides support for IFC’s efforts to promote private sector development and the export sectors (including the diversification of export products) in these countries.

sector: Garment and Apparel (Without Fabric , Excluding Footwear)
project_description: The project consists of setting-up a 600 sewing machine, apparel manufacturing factory in Madagascar, Cottonline S. A. (the company or cottonline), specializing in knit and woven casual wear, intimate apparel, sleep wear and active wear products for the US and European markets (the project). The company was incorporated in July 2001 and currently utilizes 300 sewing machines. IFC’s investment will be used for financing the additional capital investment needed to complete the Project and for funding a part of the working capital requirement of the project.
sponsor_shareholders: The company is a joint venture between four partners with an equal (25% each) stake in the company. These include: - Appnell Holdings – It is the investment arm of MAS Holdings which is a leading manufacturer of intimate wear, leisure wear, and casual wear based in Sri Lanka, with manufacturing facilities located in Sri Lanka, Maldives, India, Mexico, Indonesia and Vietnam. - Phoenix Ventures Limited – It is the investment arm of Phoenix Group, which has a large textile operation that includes apparel, fabric and yarn manufacturing through joint ventures with experienced foreign partners in and outside of Sri Lanka. - Unitex Investment Corporation – It is the investment arm of the Socota Group of Madagascar, which is a family owned business, controlled by the Ismail family. The Socota group has been in operation for the last 70 years and is involved in prawn farming, and textiles in the Indian Ocean. - Brandot International Limited – It is a family owned business controlled by Martin Trust family of USA.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $10 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A loan of up to $5.0 million for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The plant is built on a 20,000 m2 site located in Antsirabé, Madagascar, which is 175 km from Antananarivo’s international airport and 530 km away from the main port of Toamasina on the east coast of the country.
additionality: The project will support the creation of a globally competitive export industry with substantial development impact which will include: - contributing to poverty alleviation in Madagascar through direct job creation for approximately 1,750 employees; - utilizing supplies of raw materials from other sub-Saharan African countries which will help develop the local supply base and encourage the growth of SMEs in the Antsirabe area; - creating a demonstration effect with regard to attracting foreign investment into Madagascar; - transferring state-of-the-art technology to the nascent Malagasy garment industry; and - generating net positive foreign exchange inflows to Madagascar by promoting an export oriented project. IFC’s role will be to provide long term financing to the project, which is still largely unavailable from the local financial sector in Madagascar. Its involvement in the project will stimulate the development of a sound linkages programs with local SME’s. IFC will also introduce best practices in sustainable development and environmental protection to the project which could be replicated by some of the sponsors for their other projects.

project_description: Tourism Promotion Services (Afghanistan) Limited -TPS(A)- was established by the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development (AKFED) for the purpose of investing in the Kabul Serena Hotel. TPS(A) will completely renovate and expand the old Kabul Hotel (the project) at an estimated cost of $27.8 million. The hotel development will be phased with 160 rooms total and will be operated by AKFED’s hotel management subsidiary, Serena Tourism Promotion Services (STPS), which trades as Serena Hotels. Originally built in the 1930s, the Kabul Hotel is in a major state of disrepair as a result of war damage and overall neglect over the years but was once an attractive hotel and an important meeting place in Kabul
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor is AKFED and its subsidiary, STPS, now operates 20 hotels in Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique and Pakistan under the Serena brand. As in other hotel projects, STPS has established a separate company in Afghanistan, TPS(A) for the purpose of implementing this project. AKFED is an economic development agency headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland that helps develop economically viable enterprises through equity participation combined with management and technical expertise and support. AKFED is part of the larger Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN), a group of development agencies working in health, education, culture and rural and economic development. AKDN has been active in Afghanistan for a number of years and has a strong local presence.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $27.8 million. IFC’s proposed investment is a loan of up to $ 7 million.
location_description: The project is located in downtown Kabul on Bank Street, across from the Central Bank, and adjacent to Zanegar Park, which will be maintained as a green area. The existing Kabul Hotel currently occupies this site and a new building will be added within the hotel grounds as part of the expansion. To further enhance the quality of the neighborhood in the vicinity of the hotel and facilitate a higher level of security around the hotel , the whole of Bank Street along the boundary of the hotel will be dedicated as a pedestrian zone.
additionality: The development impact associated with the project is strong: The hotel will: - address the lack of accommodation facilities in Kabul to meet the needs of diplomats, government workers, aid organizations, media, NGOs and potential business investors visiting the city. As such it will comprise an essential part of the city’s business infrastructure by providing international standard facilities/services; - provide reliable food & beverage services, business center facilities, communications, meeting rooms, etc., for visitors to Kabul; - restore an architecturally and historically significant building in Kabul and improve this area of the city; - generate much needed foreign exchange for the country and provide revenue to the government by way of import duties, lease payments and taxes; - create linkages with the rest of the economy for building materials, food and beverage and other ongoing operating supplies which will strengthen as the economy diversifies; as well as - provide numerous jobs both during implementation and operations. During implementation, Afghan workers will be used for unskilled and semi skilled labor as well as supervisory positions and craft work. Extensive hotel training will be provided by Serena to maximize the number of Afghanis employed once the hotel is operational. IFC’s primary role will be to provide long-term debt financing which is virtually unavailable for private sector projects in the country currently. The project will have a strong demonstration effect as: - one of the first private sector foreign investments in the country, with all of the related challenges, and laying critical groundwork for future private investment in hotels and other sectors, and - one of the first major building projects in the city’s reconstruction program. IFC's involvement will also ensure compliance with World Bank environmental and social guidelines as well as international standards for fire and life safety.

sector: Garment and Apparel (Without Fabric , Excluding Footwear)
project_description: Founded in 1986, Grupo M is the largest private sector employer in the Dominican Republic with 12,000 employees working in 22 production facilities and is the largest apparel producer in the Caribbean/Central American region supplying to major US brand name companies including Liz Claiborne, Polo, Levis, Hanes and Tommy Hilfiger. The Haiti Project is a phased development of a 500,000 m2 site on the border of Haiti and DR. Phase 1 of the investment program will develop an area of 150,000 m2 for a total investment of $11 million. Upon completion, Phase 1 is expected to generate 1,500 direct jobs and up to 3,000 indirect jobs for Haitian workers in the adjacent area. Subsequent development is expected to include outside customers producing apparel, footwear and other products who would lease or purchase facilities built to order by the zone development company, which will be 100% owned by Grupo M. The total site area would allow up to 40 factory units providing as many as 20,000 direct jobs and 40,000 indirect jobs at full capacity. The project is to provide - a corporate financing to Grupo M (the Group or the company), a vertically integrated apparel manufacturer in the Dominican Republic producing knits and woven products for the US market, to finance ongoing capital expenditures, long term working capital needs and to refinance existing obligations, and - a loan to finance an export zone promoted by Grupo M focusing on garment production in the Republic of Haiti (the Haiti Project).
sponsor_shareholders: The founding companies for Grupo M were established in 1986 by Fernando Capellan, a Dominican Republic (DR) entrepreneur. Grupo M, the holding company, was established in 1993. Fernando Capellan and family members are the controlling shareholders who, together with senior management and company staff hold 82% of the outstanding share capital. Banco Popular, the largest financial group in the Dominican Republic holds 10% of the outstanding shares, while the remainder is held by other local shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the project is estimated at $43 million of which $11 million is the projected cost for the first phase of the Haiti Project. The proposed IFC financing consists of a $20 million loan for IFC’s account to Grupo M to fund ongoing capital expenditures and debt restructuring and a second $3 million loan for IFC’s account to the Haiti Project development company.
location_description: Grupo M’s main production facilities are located in two industrial zones developed by the group in Santiago, Dominican Republic. The Haiti Project is located on the northern border of the Dominican Republic and the Republic of Haiti on the outskirts of the towns of Ouanaminthe (Republic of Haiti, population 56,000 ) and Dajabon (Dominican Republic, population 65,000). The development plan for phase 1 of the Haiti Project will include - site clearing and access roads and utilities, - training center, staff facilities (medical services and cafeteria) and customs clearing offices, and - 3 factory buildings owned by Grupo M.
additionality: Grupo M is the largest private sector employer in the DR. The company has been an innovator in adopting sustainable business practices since its founding. The Group has ISO9002 certification and has won awards for labor practice and corporate citizenship. Financing of Grupo M is an opportunity for IFC to secure the long term growth of the Group. The Haiti Project will have a very significant development impact. This project is the key private sector development in the Republic of Haiti creating an opportunity to rejuvenate the garment sector in the country, which once employed more than 60,000 people but has reduced substantially in the past 10 years. If successful, the development of the zone and the direct investments by Grupo M can be expected to mobilize significant other private sector investments creating as many as 60,000 direct and indirect jobs and thus a dramatic impact to alleviate poverty. IFC is working closely with the Group on additional initiatives in support of sustainability and linkages to the wider community in Haiti. IFC will play a key role in this investment, firstly through its support of a major private investor making a first investment in the Republic of Haiti. IFC’s presence as a long term investor will significantly enhance the attractiveness of the Haiti Project for Grupo M and for other private sector investors who can be expected to follow their lead. The proposed IFC corporate financing of Grupo M will provide otherwise unavailable long term funding to significantly bolster the long term competitiveness and sustainability of Grupo M, the largest employer in the DR and the flagship of the Dominican garment sector.

project_description: The Southern Aluminum Industry (China) Co. Ltd. (the company or SAIC), an aluminum sheet/coil and foil producer in the Fu Jian Province (southeastern China), was established in 1992. SAIC’s products are used in applications such as food and pharmaceutical packaging, condenser and fit stock, cigarettes and beverage packaging, curtain walls and kitchenware. SAIC exports 15% of its products and sells the remainder in the domestic market. SAIC currently employs 500 people. The proposed $38 million is to expand and modernize SAIC, through the installation of a second-hand aluminum hot rolling mill and ancillary new equipment. The planned hot mill, with a capacity of 60,000 tons per year, would allow SAIC to increase its sheet/coil and foil capacity from 12,000 tons to 50,000 tons for sheet/coil (including manufacture of 16,000 tons of foil stock) and from 7,200 tons to 10,000 tons for foil. The proposed project would enable the company to diversify its product mix as well as to reduce its dependency on imports.
sponsor_shareholders: SAIC is owned by Fung Lam Trading Company Ltd., Hong Kong (70%), and Shinyou Shoji Ltd., Japan (30%). Fung Lam Trading Company is owned by Mr. Alim Husin and his family. The Alim Family controls the Maspion Group of Indonesia, which is one of the largest diversified business groups in East Java, Indonesia. Shinyou Shoji, an entertainment company owning game/bowling centers, is owned by Mr. Liu You Rong, based in Japan and a long-time friend of Mr. Alim Husin. The Alim Family has started with a small aluminum kitchenware business in 1962 and subsequently diversified into activities in consumer durables, electronics, chemicals, packaging materials, metal rolling, construction materials, industrial estate development and banking. The Maspion Group currently employs about 25,000 people in 38 companies, 14 of which are joint ventures with well-known multinational corporations such as Siam Cement of Thailand (PVC resin), Kanematsu (stainless steel sheet), and Marubeni (stainless steel pipe).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $38 million. The proposed IFC Investment is an A Loan of up to $12 million.
location_description: SAIC occupies a land area of 240,000 square meters, of which 50,000 square meters are occupied by facilities. SAIC is located in the Rong Qiao Economic and Technological Development Zone, Fu Qing City in Fujian Province, South of China. SAIC is 60 km from Mawei Port and 21 km from Rongqiao Port.; it has a convenient and perfect communication and transport facilities as well as a beautiful environment. SAIC is a large scale and modern aluminum processing set up, employing fully automated and computerized aluminum rolling mills and equipment from Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, and U.S.A., combined with a skilled workforce, including a number of specialists in the field of casting, rolling and finishing processing of aluminum sheet and foil.
additionality: Project Development Impact: The project is expected to: - Enhance the competitiveness of SAIC by enabling the company to significantly expand capacity at low cost. Unit operating costs are expected to decline as better economies of scale are achieved. - Downstream industrial customers, such as house ware, packaging, and construction are expected to gain from the improved quality of production at lower cost compared to imported material. - Provide 60 new jobs, and sustain 500, directly at SAIC and increase employment opportunities indirectly at service providers to SAIC both at the project implementation and production stages. - Develop the network of SAIC's distributors, providing additional employment opportunities. IFC Role: - Support SAIC in maintaining its long-term competitiveness. - Bring higher value added products as a result of the project. - Facilitate a long-term financing to the project. - IFC's involvement in the project would promote focus on corporate governance practices. - IFC's investment would also be instrumental in having an environmental review of SAIC's operations and undertaking necessary measures for improvements in this area.

company_name: GEM VII Targeted Value Income Fund
project_description: Quasi-Equity investment of up to $30 million in GEM VII Targeted Value Debt Fund (the fund or the company). The proposed fund is a closed-end special purpose vehicle, structured as a Collateralized Bond Obligation (CBO), which will invest in emerging market debt issues. The fund is structured to offer investment opportunities both to existing emerging markets investors and to credit-quality sensitive institutional investors who can only invest in investment-grade instruments. The fund is expected to be at least 70% invested in 30 countries at closing in June 2003, in a globally diversified portfolio of US dollar denominated debt issues from emerging markets. Against the assets of the fund, three classes of obligations: - Senior Notes, - Second Priority Notes, and - Preference Shares - are expected to be issued in an amount of $400 million. The Senior and Second Priority Notes will be over-collateralized and credit-enhanced by the Preference Shares and are targeted to receive a higher investment grade rating of Aa2 and Baa2 from Moody's, and AA and BBB- from S&P, respectively. The Senior Notes will be wrapped by a monoline insurer guarantee to achieve a rating of Aaa/AAA. The fund will invest in emerging market corporate, quasi-sovereign, and sovereign debt securities and is a vehicle designed to support the World Bank Group strategy of promoting the development of corporate debt markets in the member developing countries.
sponsor_shareholders: TCW Asset Management Company will be the fund Manager. TCW Asset Management Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of the TCW Group, Inc. (collectively TCW), which is an indirect subsidiary of Société Générale, S.A. As of December 31, 2002, TCW had approximately $80 billion assets under management, including over $3.7 billion in emerging market debt. TCW has 14 debt funds under its management, of which eight are emerging market debt funds with CBO structures.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The expected size of the fund is $400 million. IFC proposes to invest $20 million in the Preference Shares and $10 million in the Second Priority Notes.
location_description: The location of the project is Los Angeles, USA
additionality: The fund is to play an important role in enhancing the status of emerging markets corporate debt as a distinct asset class for international institutional investors. Consequent to the global economic downturn, retrenchment of banks and hedge funds from emerging market debt has seriously affected domestic companies' accessibility to foreign funding. New issuance of corporate paper has declined to $19 billion in 2002 from a high of $41 billion in 1997. Through investment in this fund, IFC will encourage dedicated fixed income fund managers in this asset class to successfully create new products in the form of structured debt funds that are designed to modify the return/risk profile of emerging market assets to tap those investors who are limited to investment grade securities and increase the overall demand for emerging market corporate debt, thereby facilitating emerging markets companies to access the international capital markets either to lower their funding costs or extend their debt maturities or both. Traditionally, the emerging markets investment pool has largely been limited to investors in high-yield bonds, a relatively specialized investor group with limited resources for high-risk classes of assets. By structuring a specialized investment vehicle for large credit-rating-sensitive institutional investors to access emerging market debt securities, IFC would send a strong signal that IFC is committed to develop innovative financial instruments for these investors. According to the fund manager's initial market soundings, investors are hesitant about investing in emerging market debt issues. In order to move the fund forward, TCW must structure the subordinate tranche of the CBO, which is always the most challenging component in such transactions. This problem has been further compounded as institutional investors are trying to reduce risk on their balance sheets and have limited appetite for emerging market exposure. Participation by a strong investor like IFC in the subordinate tranche at the early stage is likely to have a significant catalytic effect and be critical to the distribution and placement of the fund.
Company Name: GEM VII Targeted Value Income Fund

project_description: RAK Ceramics U.A.E. (RAK Ceramics or the company) is one of the largest ceramic tiles and sanitary ware companies in the world with an annual capacity of 2.2 million pieces of sanitary ware and 40 million square meters of ceramic tiles. The company has manufacturing plants in the U.A.E., China, Bangladesh and Slovakia, and sales and distribution offices in France, Germany, Switzerland, and Australia. RAK-UAE''s products are exported to more than 125 countries across 5 continents. IFC’s proposed investment in the company is for financing its expansion projects in Iran and possibly Algeria, with similar plant capacities of approximately 2.5 million square meters of tiles per year. Each of the two individual projects are designed to have state-of-the-art technology and the ability to produce high margin, good quality, affordable tiles for the local markets.
sponsor_shareholders: RAK Ceramics is a public company listed on the Abu Dhabi Stock Exchange. It is owned 33.5% by the ruling family of Ras Al Khaimah (U.A.E.), 27.5% by M/s Emirates Rock and Marbles, 3% by M/s RAK Poultry, 8% by its management, 5% by the Government of Ras Al Khaimah, and the remaining 24% by other institutional and individual investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a corporate loan of $30 million to finance the company’s expansion program in FY03-FY04.
location_description: The company’s factory in the UAE is located in the Ras Al Khaimah Emirate, 75 kilometers from Dubai, in a southern industrial area. The sites for the company’s expansion projects are being identified in the respective countries.
additionality: Development Impact: The proposed IFC investment will enable an internationally competitive enterprise in the sanitary ware and ceramic tiles sector to expand into other developing countries. By introducing good quality, affordable tiles in these countries, it is expected that RAK Ceramics will create a new market for ceramic tiles and encourage replacement of poorer quality tiles. It is expected to create more than 1000 direct jobs in Iran and Algeria, and also stimulate usage of domestic raw materials and energy in these countries. Additionally the proposed IFC investment will stimulate transfer of most advanced production technology, know-how and local staff training by one of the world’s leading ceramic tiles companies. The proposed IFC Investment will: - support a healthy, internationally competitive, global producer in its expansion plans in other developing countries by providing a long-term loan for the financing that would otherwise be difficult to mobilize from the local banks; - ensure that RAK Ceramics conforms to high standards of environmental, safety and social consciousness, as well as to improved corporate governance practices; - provide political risk mitigation to the company for its investments in frontier countries; and - develop linkages with upstream and downstream industries in the respective countries.

sector: Wood Panels and Engineered Wood Products
project_description: Kronostar (the company or the project) is 100% owned by Krono Holding AG since early 2002. The AOO Sharjadrew combine dates back to early 1900’s with a construction of a saw mill. Over the years, it has established a particleboard factory, and was privatized in 1992. AOO Sharjadrew filed for insolvency in 1997. In 2002, Krono Holding AG purchased AOO Sharjadrew’s assets. The purpose of the investment is to upgrade of the existing wood panels plant, and to install a new particleboard and Medium Density Fiberboard (MDF) lines. The project has strong business fundamentals. It will contribute to the modernization of Russian wood panel industry, which is currently characterized by old and inefficient operations, and it will have a potentially strong impact on the revival and development of the: - rural area of the Kostroma Oblast; - wood panel industry, and - furniture industry in the Russian Federation. The project is supported by the strong expected demand growth for wood panels. Using modern technology, Kronostar will produce particleboard and wood panels, and it will create employment for over 600 direct jobs at the peak of the company’s operations. IFC’s role in the project is manifold. IFC will act as a catalyst for foreign investment and private sector participation in Kostroma, and to help the sponsor gain access to long-term financing. The role of IFC’s involvement is also to ensure that the projects benefits trickle down in a sustainable manner to the community.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Swiss Krono Group (the sponsor), headquartered in Luzern Switzerland, a 100% privately-held and well-established company. The sponsor is a European leader in wood panel board manufacturing with operations in France, Germany, Hungary, Poland, Switzerland, and Ukraine.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $190 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to $50 million A Loan for IFC’s own account, and up to $50 million B Loan for the account of the participants.
location_description: Kronostar (the company or the project) has been established on the existing site of the bankrupt AOO Sharjadrew timber production facility in Wetluschskij, near Sharja in Kostroma Oblast, on a 119.5 hectares of land with access to roads and a connection to Trans-Siberian railway. The project investment will be made primarily in the Kostroma Oblast’s rural area.

project_description: Merec Industries Lda (or the company) was founded in 1998 and began producing maize meal and coconut oil in its new factory erected in the Maputo suburb of Machava in January and September 1999 respectively. In December 2000, IFC approved and signed a guarantee to help finance the construction of the wheat mill in Machava-Maputo (Project Number: 10185). The project is successful and achieved 100% of its production capacity two years ahead of appraisal projections. Merec II is a project for the expansion of Merec Industries Lda’s wheat mill processing activities in Mozambique. Merec intends to build a new wheat mill including grain storage silos in Beira, the capital of Sofala Province and the second largest city in Mozambique. A new 140tonne/24h Buhler mill and silos with storage capacity of 12,500 tonnes will be installed in new buildings, with production scheduled to begin in 2005. Following Merec’s success with the first project in Maputo, the company management decided to test the market for Merec’s products in the Beira region to the north of Maputo using a portion of its output from the Maputo wheat mill plant. The good quality of the product and the reliable distribution of Africom (a distribution company owned the sponsors of Merec Industries Lda) have contributed towards the success of this experiment in Beira. Merec is now selling 12,000 tonnes of flour per year in this area but is experiencing demand for this in the South so that once the Beira project is complete there will be no problem switching back. The opportunity in Central Mozambique will be fully exploited through this expansion project.
sponsor_shareholders: The main sponsors of the project are Mr. Mhamud Charania and his mother Mrs Gulsham Ramji. Mr. Mhamud Charania is a 37-year-old British citizen and holds a mechanical engineering degree from the University of Toronto. He is dynamic, enthusiastic and is well respected by his staff. He is an influential member of the Ismaili community in Maputo. Mrs Ramji is 69 years old and is essentially retired. The sponsors came to Mozambique in 1994. They established Africom Lda which has been successfully trading in and distributing basic commodities such as sugar, rice, oil, soap, biscuits, and maize and wheat flour, sourced locally and abroad. They founded Merec Industries Lda in 1998. Part of the Merec complex is rented to Africom.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $4,950,000. The proposed IFC investment is a Guarantee Facility of $ 2.5 million to guarantee the loan that will be provided to Merec by Banco Standard Totta de Mozambique (BSTM).
location_description: The Merec II project will be located in Beira. The location in Beira, the biggest market in Mozambique, is one of the major strengths of this project in addition to the close proximity to the port. The Beira region is one of the most populated parts of the country with an abundant labor force. The site consists of two hectares of unoccupied land within the Beira industrial area. Power, water and other utilities are nearby and available.
additionality: The project development impact can be summarized in the following categories: - Enterprise Development: Merec is interested in participating in supply chain and distributor chain linkages, which with the assistance of IFC can help the growth of small and micro enterprises (MSME’s). This will involve the provision of technical assistance for the local micro and small bakeries, which will use their products. . Merec’s new project will create opportunities for many small businesses to supply goods and services to the plant. A growth in the supply chain will also come about as Merec will be distributing its increased volume through a network of small scale distributors and in some cases directly to new small bakeries. Merec has also requested the support of IFC in the development of the company’s HIV/Aids awareness and treatment programs. - Economic Growth: The World Bank Group’s objectives in Mozambique include supporting the Government’s program for poverty reduction by investing in sustainable industrial projects. The Merec expansion project will add economic value and create 48 new, direct jobs. Merec will provide the necessary on-the-job training for supervision and technical staff in order to improve skills and strengthen the industrial base. Merec will source its packaging locally and will also promote local transport companies which will be subcontracted to carry grain and finished product. - Provision of Finance: IFC is providing financial backing through the guarantee facility thereby enhancing the ability of a local bank in Mozambique to make a long-term loan available to the project. There is a shortage of long term project finance available in Mozambique because of the need for bank liquidity and perceptions of risk.

project_description: Balrampur Chini Mills Limited (BCML or the company) is the largest and the most financially viable sugar producer in India. A public limited company, the ‘Saraogi’ family holds about 47% of its equity capital. The company with its three sugar manufacturing units in East Uttar Pradesh has an aggregate capacity of 25,000 tonnes crushing per day [TCD] Balrampur’s existing mills account for 2.25% of annual Indian sugar production. BCML wants to capitalize on its strengths of excellent management, strong operational and financial capabilities to expand its sugar capacity and diversify its revenue streams through the production of value added products related to sugar production. These include cogeneration and dedicated biomass power plants, ethyl alcohol, and bio-compost fertilizer. The proposed project includes an integrated, Greenfield 4,000 tonnes cane/day [TCD] sugar mill, an associated bagasse-fired 20 megawatts (MW) co-generation plant providing steam and power for the mill’s use and selling 15.45 MW of electric power to the Uttar Pradesh grid. The final element of the project includes construction of new 60 kilo litre / day [ KLPD ] ethanol distillery and an associated biomass fertilizer manufacturing unit, which will employ sugar and ethanol manufacturing waste at the existing 8000 TCD Babhnan mill. The purpose of this project is to build: - a 4,000 tonnes cane per day (tcd) greenfield sugar mill and associated 20MW bagasse fired cogeneration power plant at Haidergarh in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India and - a 60 kilolitres per day ethanol distillery (for blending with gasoline) and associated biomass fertilizer plant at the company’s existing sugar mill at Babhnan also in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Balrampur Chini Mills Limited which is a public company traded on the major stock exchanges in India. Its major shareholders are the Saraogi family which hold about 47% of its shares.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $44 million of which IFC proposes to provide a Rupee loan equivalent of $15 million for its own account.
location_description: The greenfield sugar mill is to be located in Haidergarh in the district of Barabanki in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is a rural site with small holding farms in the area. It is located near the main roadway to facilitate the transportation of sugar cane to the mill and sugar and its by-products from the mill. The proposed ethanol distillery will be located near the company’s Babhnan sugar mill which is also in a rural area. It will benefit from the existing infrastructure associated with the mill.
additionality: T his project is expected to have a high development impact by achieving the following results: - Help a mid-sized company remain competitive and prepare it to take advantage of changes in the Indian sugar industry. The project will support an experienced and successful operator in its drive to become a leading actor in a very fluid Indian sugar sector. The project will also allow the company to take full advantage of newly opened opportunities in the power and the ethanol sectors. - Create strong backward linkages with farmers. The project will support a large number of individual farmers who will gain access to a reliable client for their production. At the Haidergarh location it will help farmers grow sugar which is one of the most profitable crops and should facilitate an increase in farmer incomes. The company enjoys considerable goodwill among sugar cane farmers due to the technical assistance provided and the reliability of its payments. IFC will provide a much needed long term funds to the company as well provide input into enhancing the company’s occupational health and safety program. IFC will also work with the company to increase its farmer extension program through the use of existing trust funds.

project_description: Vietnam Enterprise Investments Limited (VEIL, or the Fund) is a closed-end investment fund incorporated in the Cayman Islands and listed on the Irish Stock Exchange. The Fund has been operating since 1995. It has a capital base of $43.9 million and is managed by Dragon Capital Management Ltd., which is a subsidiary of Dragon Capital Group (DCG). Its investment objective is to invest in publicly or privately issued securities of Vietnamese companies, thereby providing impetus to the development of Vietnamese capital markets by increasing liquidity of Vietnamese securities. The Fund invests in a hybrid asset pool of listed, pre-listed, and unlisted securities and real estate.
sponsor_shareholders: Sponsor - DCG: A reputable investment and advisory firm with a seven year track record of investing in Vietnam and the potential to play a dominant role in developing Vietnamese capital markets. Established in 1994, DCG owns 100% of four subsidiaries: -Dragon Capital Management Ltd. (asset management), -Dragon Capital Markets Ltd. (securities brokerage), -Dragon Capital Ltd. (corporate finance advisory services), and -Dragon Capital Nominees Ltd. (holds assets on behalf of clients). All group companies are incorporated in the British Virgin Islands. Major Shareholders of VEIL: As of December 2002, VEIL had 28 international institutional investors - the top five of which account for 54% of the Fund and include: - Worms Asset Management (16%, UK), - Capital International (10%, US), - British Empire Trust (10%, UK), - Scottish Widows Investment Partnership (9%, UK) and, - Universities Suprannuation Scheme (8%, UK).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund is going through its fourth round of fund raising, targeting to raise $40 million through the issue of 40 million Conversion Shares (C Shares). IFC’s investment into the Fund will be made in a single, one-time disbursement for the lower of $8 million or 20% of the capital increase, mirroring the disbursement procedure for C shares.
location_description: The project is located in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
additionality: VEIL has been virtually the only foreign investor in Vietnamese privatizations. Following the proposed capital increase, the increase in the size of the Fund from $65 million to $105 million should invigorate the securities market. Furthermore, the professional approach and investment perspective of VEIL is expected to have a lasting impact on the Vietnamese market in terms of raising standards of securities research and portfolio analysis in Vietnam. Due to DCG’s complementary businesses of corporate finance and securities brokerage, it is also expected to bring to bear on the investee companies the discipline and perspective of an international institutional investor. IFC’s equity participation in the Fund would support the Government’s financial markets reform initiatives by: - supporting VEIL''s participation in the privatization process by strengthening its capital resources and; - through IFC’s involvement, ensuring the implementation of good corporate governance and industry best practices in VEIL and DCG. In addition, investment in VEIL will signal IFC''s confidence in the future of the Vietnamese market and revive sagging confidence of international institutional investors, thereby providing these investors with opportunities in a market into which they may be unwilling to invest directly. With the demise of most of the dedicated country funds and the absence of any investment bank or broker being prepared to assist formally with placing, the difficulties of raising capital for Vietnam are compounded by global and regional economic downturn. IFC’s commitment to invest is likely to have a greater catalytic effect than if the environment were more benign. Further, through VEIL, IFC would be able to provide a vehicle for institutional investments into Vietnam.

project_description: Larsen & Toubro (L&T, or the company) is one of the largest engineering conglomerates in India. Its main line of business is engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) for large industrial, utilities and infrastructure projects, manufacturing of cement, and manufacturing of electrical and electronics equipment. The company is currently undertaking an operational and financial restructuring for which it has requested IFC’s support. The restructuring involves refinancing of the existing loans as well as the refurbishment and modernization program that would enable the company’s increased focus on exports of its products and services.
sponsor_shareholders: L&T is 40.3% owned by Indian financial institutions, 31% by the public, 3.7% by foreign institutional investors, 20% by Indian companies and the remaining 5% by other investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The proposed IFC investment is a corporate loan of $50 million to support the company’s financial restructuring and ongoing refurbishment and modernization program of approximately $250 million.
location_description: The company is headquartered in Mumbai. It has factories in various locations throughout India, including Ahmednagar, Arakkonam, Awarpur, Chennai, Durgapur, Faridabad, Hazira, Hirmi, Jharsuguda, Kancheepuram, Kansbahal, Kovaya, Mumbai, Mysore, Nashik, Pithampur, Pondicherry and Tadipatri.
additionality: The proposed IFC investment is expected to help L&T to focus on those areas of business where it is most competitive resulting in its further expansion into export markets. The proposed investment will also support: - regional economic activities due to the L&T’s large involvement in infrastructure, utilities and industrial projects; - creation of additional jobs in related manufacturing and service sectors. IFC’s role involves: - provision of long term financing in foreign currency at market rates; - support L&T’s restructuring that would result in its increased international competitiveness; - advising on local partners and possible investors for L&T’s export projects as well as provision of possible financing for these projects; and - ensuring that its environmental and social practices comply with the World Bank Group’s standards.

project_description: The proposed project consists of three potential IFC investments in new small and medium sized enterprise (SME) regional funds in Africa, to be managed by Aureos Capital Ltd.: - Aureos Southern Africa Fund – regional fund targeting South Africa, Mozambique, Zambia, Zimbabwe and the SADC region excluding Tanzania. - Aureos East Africa Fund – regional fund targeting Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda and the East African region in general. - Aureos West Africa Fund – regional fund targeting Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal and the ECOWAS region. The purpose of the project is financing SMEs that demonstrate potential for profitable growth in these three African regions and achieving capital appreciation through dividends and capital gains from these SME investments.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Aureos Capital Ltd., a global fund manager providing risk capital to SMEs in emerging markets. Aureos currently manages 15 funds, with total committed capital of $202 million. Aureos was established in 2001 as a 50%-50% joint venture between CDC Group plc and Norfund, the Norwegian Investment Fund for developing countries, for the purpose of managing and expanding the pool of SME funds originally sponsored by CDC. In Africa, Aureos has an existing portfolio of 9 SME country funds with a total committed capital of $104 million, and an expansive on-the-ground presence in Africa which it plans to increase further upon closing of these funds. Other investors include multilateral and bilateral development institutions, as well as local financial investors.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project costs is as follows: Aureos Southern Africa Fund – $60 million target fund size Aureos East Africa Fund – $40 million target fund size Aureos West Africa Fund – $50 million target fund size The potential IFC investments represent aggregate equity investments of up to $20 million to be allocated between any or all of the three funds (not to exceed 19.9% of any fund), to be determined based on the results of due diligence.
location_description: Aureos Capital Ltd is headquartered in London, UK. Local teams are located in multiple countries in the three African regions.
additionality: The funds will achieve a development impact by improving access to financing to African SMEs, which can, in turn, participate in and contribute to accelerating growth in the regions. The investments will be diversified across a variety of sectors. The funds’ investments in target companies will range from $0.5 million to $4 million and will consist of significant minority equity stakes with board representation and the right to participate in or to influence the conduct of management. This includes but is not limited to, the ability to take a controlling interest or a right of veto on key decisions, should management not meet pre-determined targets. IFC’s participation as an investor in the funds would create more financing capacity available to African SMEs and therefore expand the scope of this impact.

company_name: Inversiones y Valores Milenium, S.A. de C.V.
project_description: Copamex S.A de C.V. (Copamex, or the company) is a leading Mexican producer of paper products for the consumer goods, industrial packaging and printing, and writing (P&W) markets. Located in Monterrey, Copamex is a holding company with 39 subsidiaries (35 in Mexico, 2 in the United States, 1 in Costa Rica and 1 in Nicaragua) of which 36 are wholly-owned and 3 are majority-owned joint ventures. The company is embarking on a debt reduction and refinancing strategy which will enhance its financial flexibility and its ability to compete effectively. As part of this strategy, Copamex has requested IFC’s assistance to refinance part of its long term debt and to fund capital expenditure aimed at rationalizing existing facilities. IFC will help Copamex improve its financial profile in order for the company to become a stronger regional player, better able to compete with multi-nationals. The principal components of the project are as follows: financial restructuring and other measures designed to improve the ability of the company to access national and international sources of finance on competitive terms; rationalization of existing facilities; and measures to improve corporate governance and environmental management and enhance the social impact of the company.
sponsor_shareholders: The Maldonado Quiroga family of Monterrey (Mexico) founded the Copamex in 1928 and still maintains approximately 100% ownership. The Maldonado family has two branches, namely the well known and reputable Maldonado Elizondo and Maldonado Gonzalez families. The members of the Maldonado Elizondo family own in aggregate 92% of the company and play a bigger role in the management of the Copamex than the Maldonado Gonzalez family with 8%. The Maldonado family is active in philanthropic and charitable causes through the Fundación de Beneficiencia Maldonado Quiroga, a 14-year old not-for-profit entity that gives donations to low-income groups in Monterrey.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated Project Cost of $262 million is to refinance part of the company’s debt and to fund capital expenditure for modernizing and rationalizing some of the Copamex’s existing facilities. The capital expenditure component of the project is not part of an expansion program, it consists instead of various investments necessary to keep the facilities competitive. The IFC’s proposed investment would consist of a up to $50 million A loan for IFC’s own account, a up to $107 million B loan for the account of participants banks, and a up to S$25 million quasi-equity C loan for IFC’s account. The company has expressed interest in obtaining Mexican peso financing in order to minimize its foreign exchange exposure and as such IFC is considering providing its A loan in pesos, arranging local currency parallel loans (the “Parallel Loan”, for the account of local lenders) to replace the IFC B loan. In the event that the Parallel Loan is insufficient, IFC will consider swapping any IFC B loan then required to complete the financing plan in pesos.
location_description: The company headquarters are located in Monterrey, in the State of Nuevo Leon, which borders with the United States (Texas). The Copamex’s main facilities are located in the states of Nuevo Leon, Chihuahua, Mexico State, Michoacán and Jalisco. The company also has other facilities in the United States and Central America.
additionality: As the company shifts its production focus toward areas in which it has stronger competitive advantages, Copamex’s profitability will increase. Specifically, consumer and packaging products will be emphasized taking full advantage of the Company’s proximity to the market and its brands. By refinancing US dollar debt with new peso financing with longer maturity, the company’s foreign exchange risks will be reduced and longer maturities will free up resources. Consequently, the enhancement of Copamex’s liquidity will allow its management to better focus on production and market issues and have the resources to invest in improvements. The Project is also expected to support the viability of an important source of employment for 6,878 people in the company. Copamex contributes to the hygienic living standards of the people in the country through the production and distribution of affordable consumer products to all segments of the society. The company significantly contributes to recycling wastepaper and cardboard generated in Mexico and abroad, since around two thirds of its raw material fiber is recycled. By adopting IFC's environmental, health and safety policies and guidelines, the company will improve to stricter international practices and reduce risk to the public, while renewed emphasis on safety will provide its employees with safer working conditions. IFC Role: Provide long-term financing better suited to the Copamex’s business dynamics. While Mexico has enjoyed better access to capital following its investment grade rating, the current market volatility and the recessive environment will make it difficult for the company to raise long-term refinancing without IFC’s involvement; IFC expects also to provide some advisory services to improve corporate governance, environmental and social matters.
Company Name: Inversiones y Valores Milenium, S.A. de C.V.

project_description: SIDER, a state-owned enterprise and Algeria’s sole integrated steel producer, has been privatized in October 2001. In this context, LNM Holdings N.V. has bought a 70% stake in Ispat Annaba (the company), the main steel producing plant and a 70% stake in Ispat Tebessa, its associated mines. LNM/Ispat group is contemplating a project in Ispat Annaba to: rehabilitate and de-bottleneck the existing plant; and upgrade the plant to meet international environmental norms. The investment program is to be phased over a 10-year period, with about $123 million to be invested between 2003 and 2005.
sponsor_shareholders: The project is sponsored by LNM Holdings NV which is part of the LNM Group (the Group). In addition to LNM Holdings NV, the Group includes Ispat International N.V. , a company quoted on the New York Stock Exchange and the Amsterdam Stock Exchange. The Group is the world’s 2nd largest and most global steel producer, with annual sales of over $9 billion and a steel making capacity of 35 million tonnes spread over 12 countries. LNM Holdings is the largest shareholder in Ispat Annaba, with a 70% stake in the company. The remaining 30% are held by SIDER, a state-owned enterprise.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project cost is estimated at $123 million. The proposed IFC investment is a loan of up to $25 million for its own account.
location_description: The project is located in Annaba, in Eastern Algeria near the border with Tunisia. The project site has easy access to major roads and infrastructure, including port facilities in Annaba.
additionality: This project is expected to have a high development impact due to: job creation and employment preservation for the existing 13,500 employees in Ispat Annaba and its ancillary facilities; technology transfer through Ispat’s wide experience in steel processing and treatment facilities; local employees’ exposure to global steel making practices through Ispat’s “Knowledge Integration Program”, a quality and cost improvement program designed to disseminate the Group’s best practices among all subsidiaries; and a substantial reduction of the negative externalities caused by polluting effects of the existing plant. IFC’s role in the project involves: supporting the government’s ongoing privatization program by participating in a highly visible and successful privatization; providing long-term financing to the project which is not available on the same terms in Algeria; assisting the company in formulating its investment program; and devising an Environmental Action Plan with the company to conform with international norms of pollution control.

project_description: In June 2000, Austindo Nusantara Jaya (ANJ), Olympus Capital Holdings Asia managing and JP Morgan Partners Asia managing committed $100 million equity capital and created Verdaine Investment Limited (Verdaine, the company), a dedicated vehicle incorporated in Mauritius, to acquire and manage oil palm plantations in Indonesia. Stakes of the partners are around 31.4%, 35% and 33.6%, respectively. The company’s primary acquisition targets are cash flow positive plantations in Indonesia with growth potential derived primarily from the rehabilitation of ill-maintained areas. Verdaine plans to acquire, rehabilitate and manage 40,000 to 50,000 hectares of palm oil plantation.
sponsor_shareholders: PT Austindo Nusantara Jaya (Austindo, sponsor) is a conglomerate with interests in agribusiness, electric power generation, mining and financial services. Austindo is a 13.11% shareholder of PT Agro Muko a palm oil plantation, where IFC made $2.2 million equity investment for a 7% stake. Austindo is a solid group with virtually no debt ($128 million equity for $145 million assets in 2002). Olympus Capital Holdings Asia (OCHA) is a direct investment firm dedicated to making long-term equity investments in Asia. Armed with some $600 million in committed capital under management, Olympus Capital targets investments in public and private companies operating in the region and has invested in the financial services, communications, and natural resources sectors. Ziff Brothers Investments, L.L.C. (ZBI) is the lead investor in the funds managed by Olympus Capital. ZBI, headquartered in New York, is the primary investment vehicle of the Ziff family and related entities, and has several billion dollars under management across a wide range of industries. In addition to funds from ZBI, its affiliates and other private investors, Olympus Capital Holdings Asia also manages Asia Development Partners, LP, a private equity fund supported by financing guaranteed by the Overseas Private Investment Corporation (OPIC). JPMPA manages the $1.1 billion Asia Opportunity Fund L.P. (AOF), the largest pan-Asia direct equity investment fund. JPMPA has invested in the palm oil, semiconductor, auto parts, mobile telecom, food, internet and technology sectors. In 1999, IFC made a $100 million equity investment in AOF. AOF plays an active role in recapitalizing and restructuring Asian companies affected by the Asian crisis. The fund, which has a 10 year life, invests principally in Korea, Thailand, Philippines, Indonesia and Malaysia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $200 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $40 million loan to Verdaine and/or its operating subsidiaries.
location_description: In June 2000, Verdaine made its first investment in acquiring PT Eka Pendawa Sakti (EPS), a 9,100 hectare plantation located in Kabupaten Tapanuli Selatan, North Sumatra Province. The second investment to be acquired in March 2003 is PT Sahabat Mewah Dan Makmur (SMM), located in Kecamatan Dendang and Gantung, Kabupaten Belitung, in the Province of Bangka – Belitung. SMM has a 15,000 hectare concession with 8,800 hectare mature area out of 12,000 hectare planted.

project_description: Taj Maldives Private Limited (TMPL, or the company) is a subsidiary of Taj Asia Limited affiliated with the Taj Group, one of the leading hotel chains in India and part of the Tata Group. TMPL owns and operates two resorts in the Maldives. The company is proposing to refinance its existing debt of $17 million, on a limited-recourse basis (the project). IFC will consider a long-term loan of up to $8.5 million to TMPL and further assist through a B-Loan syndication of an additional $8.5 million. Due to limited appetite of banks for long-term financing in Maldives, companies operating in the Maldives have found it difficult to raise long-term debt on a limited-recourse basis. In the past, TMPL financed capital expenditure in its two properties with a combination of short term debt, cash generation, inter-company loans and small equity investments. TMPL would now like to refinance these loans totaling $17 million with longer-term loans, on a limited or non-recourse basis.
sponsor_shareholders: TMPL is a 100% subsidiary of Taj Asia (TA), which is a 50:50 joint venture between Taj Group and Cigen Corporation. The Taj Group is the hospitality business arm of the Tata Group and operator of the two properties of TMPL. Taj Group will leverage its hotels and resorts management experience to run the TMPL properties. The flagship company of Taj Group is Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL) which has 50 properties in India and 10 properties overseas. Other companies in Taj Group include Oriental Hotels Ltd, Taj International Hotel Ltd, Taj Asia, and PIEM Hotels Ltd. Cigen Corporation is controlled by Chaudhary Group of Nepal. Chaudhary Group owns 5% of Cigen directly and the balance through associates. Chaudhary Group is engaged in banking, insurance and consumer goods sectors in Nepal.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $17 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $8.5 million A loan and a $8.5 million syndicated B Loan.
location_description: TMPL is located in the Republic of Maldives and operates Taj Exotica and Taj Coral Reef resorts on the islands of Emboodhu Finolhu and Hembadhoo in the Male Atolls.
additionality: Tourism is one of two mainstays of the Maldives economy (the other is fishing) but it relies on expensive and scarce stopgap financing that threatens the long term financial health of firms in the sector. Until now, TMPL has relied on parent support to find reasonably priced mid-term finance. The proposed refinancing will put the company on a sustainable financial structure and the involvement of other financiers will introduce the company to international markets on a stand-alone basis. In addition, linkages with the rest of the economy will also be created in fishing, and food and beverage supplies. Taj Group brings extensive training and international best practices in operating resorts which will increase the skill levels of local employees. IFC has a strong role in supporting the project as it provides: - Access to long-term capital. IFC would provide limited-recourse, long-term debt (ten or nine years) to TMPL, as financing on these terms is generally not available in the Maldives. Such support for TMPL will be a signal to the international commercial finance community of the improved investment climate in the country, as well as of the commercial viability of investment in the key tourism sector. IFC may also help mobilize additional long term financing by way of B-Loan syndication. IFC involvement will help implement an appropriate financial structure in the company. - Attract international financial institutions to participate in investments in Maldives. IFC may also help the company mobilize additional long term financing by way of B-Loan syndication. - Technical assistance in environmental and social best practices. While TMPL has been environmentally responsible in most aspects of operations, IFC has leveraged its ability to mobilize scarce long-term financing by convincing the company to implement a fire, life safety and water treatment improvements. In addition, TMPL will participant in a coral reef restoration program initiated by the IFC. - Encouragement of “south to south” Foreign Direct Investment. Taj Group is a leading Indian company with investments in Sri Lanka, Maldives, Nepal, Goa, and Zambia. The company’s expansion strategy includes investment in other developing countries such as Mauritius and Seychelles that demonstrate an increase in demand in global tourism. IFC’s investment will support foreign direct investment from India to other Part II countries.

project_description: In the end of 2001, Agro-Industrial Complex Agros (Agros, or the sponsor) acquired several poultry farms and processing plants located in the Stavropol region. The acquired facilities needed significant rehabilitation and upgrade to improve production efficiencies. In 2002, Agros began integrating the operations into a single well-coordinated poultry company, Stavropolsky Broiler (the company). The project will introduce modern poultry technology throughout the poultry production chain and optimize capacities to expand the company’s poultry meat production to 40,000 tpa. The project consists of: repairs and upgrade of the company’s breeding and broiler farms; construction of a new hatchery; rehabilitation of processing plants and feedmill; expansion of distribution; and investment in working capital. The project aims to capitalize on the significant opportunities afforded by the poultry industry in Russia, the region’s mild climate favorable to chicken raising and abundant supply of cheap grain.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Agros, an agribusiness holding company established by Interros, one of the largest Russian private business groups. Agros owns 90% of Stavropolsky Broiler.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $33.4 million equivalent. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan of $10 million and a C Loan of $5 million.
location_description: The project is located on 11 sites in the Stavropol region, Southern Russia, approximately 1,250 kilometers southeast of Moscow. Four of the facilities are in mixed industrial/residential areas (Stavropol, Piatigorsk, Nevinnomyssk and Blagodarny) and seven in isolated agricultural areas with few neighbors. All of the existing operations have been in existence for more than 15 years. The sites have proper infrastructure and road access.
additionality: The project will have a widespread developmental impact. It will have a broad impact on the Russian poultry industry by demonstrating the benefits of a vertically integrated system with application of modern management and technology. It will increase demand for the region’s large grain crops. The project will create/save 1,300 jobs, most of them in the newly acquired broiler farms which are currently idle, in rural areas where there is little employment alternatives except for the subsistence activities. The investment will improve product quality, hygiene and bio-security. The venture’s broiler farms will serve as demonstration units to train local farmers in modern broiler outgrow techniques. IFC has played an important role in developing and structuring the project. Using the IFC-British Trust Fund, IFC commissioned consultants to prepare the project’s feasibility study and subsequently advised the company on structuring the project. Drawing on its extensive sector experience, IFC provided in-house advise on livestock operations, which have already helped the company achieve performance improvements. The IFC loan provides extended grace and repayment periods, not available locally. Going forward, IFC’s vital role in the project will be reinforced by extensive supervision required during the implementation phase.

sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: Zhejiang Babei Necktie & Weaving Co. Ltd.(Babei, or the company) is a leading silk necktie and necktie fabric producer in China. It is the largest and most influential company in Shengzhou , which is the necktie production base in China with around 1000 companies engaged in the business. It has existing production facilities with a total capacity of around 2 million square meters of necktie fabric by 2002. The project will increase the company’s market presence in both the export and domestic markets. The project mainly involves: - expanding the weaving facilities from 60 to 168 looms, - building a new dyeing plant, and - relocating the main facilities to a new site.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsor is Babei Hong Kong International Co., Ltd. (Babei Hong Kong), which is a holding company registered in 1999 in Hong Kong, China, and 100% owned by Mr. Jin Yao and his family. The company is currently 76% owned by Babei Hong Kong, and 24% owned by Zhejiang Shengzhou Babei Necktie Co., Ltd. (Babei Shengzhou), which is a holding company registered in Shengzhou, China, and also 100% owned by Mr. Jin and his family.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $24 million. The proposed IFC investment is a $5.0 million A loan and $2.0 million C Loan for IFC’s own account.
location_description: The company is located in Shengzhou, China and currently has three locations; an existing downtown facility, a new weaving plant across the river to the south of the city, and a yarn dyeing facility to the north east of the city. The sites are well accessed to transportation routes. The new weaving plant has 3.3 hectare area, which was formerly low grade agriculture land and had no settlement.
additionality: Following the best corporate practice in accounting, corporate governance, and environment, Babei will have a significant demonstration effect in the local business community. Approximately 400 new jobs would be created by the project when it reaches its production capacity in the next 2-3 years. Babei is a family-owned business. It has expressed a strong willingness to improve the corporate governance and to follow the best corporate governance. IFC will play a role in upgrading the company to the international standard by sharing our experiences and resources in this field. IFC will also play an advisory role in providing technical and financial expertise. Besides IFC’s long-term financing, IFC’s extensive experience and network in textile industry will add value to Babei’s development. In addition, by partnering with local bank in parallel financing, IFC will provide valuable experience to local banks in project financing. The project reflects IFC’s strategic support for demonstration projects that will help Chinese companies adopt international standards for corporate governance, accounting and environmental management. Babei has successfully been exporting quality products and has become highly visible in the local business community; therefore this project fits well with the World Bank Group strategy.

sector: Household Appliances (Including Refrigerators, Laundry Machine, Dishwashers, etc.)
project_description: Arctic S.A. (“Arctic” the "company") is Romania’s only producer of refrigerators, with revenues of approximately $53 million in 2002. The $50 million project consists of : acquisition of Arctic by Arcelik, a Turkey-based home appliance leader, with a turnover of approximately $1.5 billion in 2002; Arctic’s conversion into an efficient production base for Arcelik’s refrigerator sales in Europe. Arcelik will improve Arctic’s performance through: implementing a modernization, quality improvement and capacity expansion program and restructuring Arctic’s existing financial liabilities.
sponsor_shareholders: Founded in 1955, Arcelik, the project's sponsor, is now an established leader in Turkey's home appliance sector and is one of the Koc Group’s flagship companies. In 2002, Arcelik’s consolidated sales amounted to about $1.5 billion. International revenues account for approximately 50% of this amount. The sponsor’s asset base at the end of 2002 was $1.2 billion. Arcelik’s is 57% owned by the Koc Group companies, and 20% of the project sponsor belongs to the Burla Group. The remaining 23% of Arcelik’s stock are public. Public shares are traded at the Istanbul Stock Exchange. Arcelik currently owns approximately 91% of Arctic’s stock. The remaining project company’s shares are widely dispersed among a large number of minority shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated approximately at $50 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan for IFC's own account of up to $25 million equivalent.
location_description: Established in 1970, Arctic’s only 50,000 square meter site is located on the outskirts of Gaesti, a town with a population of approximately 17,000 people. Located approximately 70km from Bucharest, Romania, it serves as the headquarters for the project company. The project investments involving the purchase and installation of tangible assets will be made at this site.
additionality: The project will allow a transfer of Arcelik’s advanced production technologies and top-notch managerial expertise to a Romanian company. The project will contribute to Romania’s export promotion efforts, with its significant focus on international sales, The project will enhance the viability of a major regional employer, which currently provides jobs for approximately 1,400 people. Additional jobs and new business opportunities will be created or preserved throughout Arcelik’s and Arctic’s value chains, which include suppliers of raw materials and outsourced components as well as providers of transport, installation and after-sales services both in Turkey and Romania. Significant synergies will be created as a result of Arcelik’s and Arctic’s coordinating and sharing their value chains. Further, progressive component localization will help develop ancillary engineering and component businesses contributing to SME development in Romania. Finally, the success of this project would provide a demonstration effect, which will encourage more foreign direct investment into Romania.
