Both plants are located in the newly formed state of Jharkhand in India, and are situated in the metallurgical belt of India, close to large deposits of main raw materials, i.e. iron ore, coal, and limestone. Other location advantages available in the state of Jharkhand, such as proximity to suppliers and customers; excellent transportation and logistics facilities; and closeness and connectivity to Calcutta and Haldia ports, are also available at both the plants. The company also has two other smaller plants in India - in Agra and Bangalore. The proposed investment is being planned at its existing plant locations in Ranchi and Jamshedpur.

project_description: The projects consists of the acquisition and upgrade of additional trawlers and upgrading of the processing plant in NovaNam. The investment in trawlers will enhance the company''s ability to catch its full quota. Improving layout of the plant will improve processing capacity, efficiency, yields, quality, and margins. The project follows a US$13.5 million expansion that the company undertook in 1994, partially financed with an IFC loan of US$6.5 million. In 1996 a further US$10 million expansion attracted a US$5 million IFC loan. Repayments of loans I and II have been timely. By establishing the operation in Lüderitz, the company has contributed to the revival of the town and significantly increased its population (c 25,000) following declining economic activities of on-shore mining and crustacean fishing. New fishing operations are now also based in Lüderitz and the town has become an economic center for Southern Namibia. IFC provides long term financing that is not available in Namibia and will thereby ensure that the company maximizes its opportunities within a Namibian quota system that prioritizes allocations to successful, profitable enterprises who maximize on-shore value added production and employment. The project will strengthen profitability and the employment of 1,900 local workers. Employment opportunities in Novanam are highly prized by floor and management staff. Staff is paid above market rates in the area. IFC also seeks to contribute to NOVANAM’s efforts of combating the HIV/AIDS virus.
sponsor_shareholders: Novanam Ltd., 49% subsidiary of Pescanova SA, Spain, is the borrower and main sponsor. Novanam is a hake fishing and processing company in Lüderitz, Namibia. Grupo Pescanova is the market leader in Spain with consolidated group sales of US728 million and a net worth of US$157 million (end of 2001).
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is US$15 million, IFC would provide a US$7.5 million equivalent South African Rand loan to NovaNam Ltd. which would be guaranteed by NovaNam''s mother company Pescanova, Spain.
location_description: Lüderitz, Namibia. Novanam is an existing operation in Lüderitz’s fish processing area.

project_description: CCS is an "anchor bottler" for the Coca Cola Company in the region and is one of the relatively small number of bottling groups worldwide where Coca Cola has an equity stake. The group has over 10 subsidiary companies and 19 bottling plants in the Southern and Eastern Africa region. The group has already invested more than US$100 million in production facilities in East Africa and Mozambique and employs approximately 8,000 people in 7 countries. It also supports a network of SMEs and other businesses which supplies with goods and services so that the multiplier effect is strong. The project consists of the expansion of soft-drinks production and distribution facilities at the CCS bottling companies. The expansions will take place mostly at existing plants, although, CCS is likely to acquire some existing bottling companies over the next year or two, which will also be re-equipped and expanded. CCS wants to reach an agreement with IFC on a master facility between IFC and CCS that can be drawn down as each of the sub-projects is implemented. The project will have a sustainable development impact and will help reduce poverty through the expansion of the number of jobs and business opportunities created by Coca-Cola''s production and distribution networks in Africa. A number of the subsidiaries are joint ventures with local partners who play important operational roles. For example, in South Africa, CCS recently formed a joint venture with Fortune Beverages to enhance the empowerment impact of its operations. CCS is a group which shows strong social responsibility through its support for a wide range of community action projects (eg. road safety, environmental clean-ups, conservation), HIV/AIDS education and health campaigns, youth sports and financial support for schools, and other social services. IFC''s role in the project will be: (a) to provide equity, long term loans and/or guarantees in countries where it is difficult to raise appropriate funds; (b) to help alleviate the relatively high risk associated with the countries where the investment is required by providing informal political risk cover; and (c) to encourage regional integration by helping to make it easier for the South African parent to invest regionally.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsors are: the Gutsche Family Trust (GFI), which owns 76% of the Coca-Cola Sabco Group (CCS), and the Coca-Cola Company (TCCC) of Atlanta, which owns 24% of CCS.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$129 million. IFC is asked to provide a total investment of US$35-40 million which will be split between term loans, equity and guarantees to local banks.
location_description: CCS is headquartered in Port Elizabeth, South Africa. Investment will be made in: Mozambique, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

sector: Other Vegetable Oil Crops (Coconut, Rapeseed, Peanut, Sunflower, etc.)
project_description: The Project: AGD, a long-standing Argentine client, has approached IFC to obtain pre-export financing to complete its soybean purchase program for the 2002 harvest. The unsettled economic environment is preventing AGD from raising the required pre-export financing lines to complete its planned purchasing program of 4 million tons of oilseeds in 2002. This is at a time when the oilseeds sector expects a record crop, and soybean crushing margins are at 10 year highs. IFC''s Role: IFC is assisting a long-standing client and one of Argentina''s top five exporters to access pre-export financing during one of Argentina''s worst economic crises. AGD''s direct competitors are international traders who are able to fund their activities on international markets and remain largely isolated from the Argentine crisis. Syndicate banks have indicated that they would only participate if coming through the B Loan umbrella. Development Impact: i) IFC will provide dwindling pre-export financing to a local company in order to ensure it rides out one of the worst economic crisis faced by Argentina; ii) project funds will also ensure that the company is able to purchase cash its beans from farmers thereby providing urgent liquidity to the latter; iii) IFC''s B Loan umbrella is also key to AGD''s commercial banks, which have expressed their support for the company but are not willing to increase their exposure in the current environment; and iv) the project supports one of Argentina''s top export sectors, the oilseed sector, which today accounts for close to 20% ot total Argentine exports.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Aceitera General Deheza S.A. (the "company," or "AGD"). Owned by the Urquía family, AGD is an Argentine agribusiness corporation whose principal activity lies in the crushing of soybeans, sunflower-seeds, and peanuts. AGD is placed among the leading oilseed crushers in Argentina, exporting over 80% of sales, employing over 1,600 people, working with about 6,000 farmers and supplying Argentina and 45 countries in five continents.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$60 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$30 million A Loan for its own account and up to US$30 million syndicated B Loan.
location_description: Project funding will be directed to continue soybean purchases in the Santa Fe, Cordoba, and Buenos Aires provinces of Argentina.

sector: Other Plastic and Rubber Products (Including Polypropylene Bags, Housing Components, Containers, etc.)
project_description: In 1981, Cosmo set-up India’s first BOPP (Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene) plant with an 800 tpa capacity, and is now India''s largest BOPP producer. BOPP film is primarily used for food and confectionary packaging, lamination, adhesive tapes, pharmaceutical packs, and capacitor film. In FY97-99, to emerge from a domestic BOPP overcapacity situation, Cosmo capitalised on a diversification into exports of niche products to achieve full capacity utilization and a strong recovery of profitability in FY00. In September 2001, because of the continuing growth in domestic demand, facing capacity constraints, Cosmo commissioned a 9,000 tpa production line (Line IV), and, in October 2001, it acquired GP. GP was one of Cosmo''s leading domestic competitors with a production capacity of 13,500 tpa, but, in FY99, it had lost profitability, due to high leverage with expensive debt, which Cosmo now proposes to restructure. Together with the financial restructuring of the recently acquired GP, the proposed project also aims at adding a new 10,000 tonnes per annum (tpa) production line (Line V) . Line V will increase Cosmo''s BOPP capacity from 23,100 tpa to 33,100 tpa. The line, together with the merger with GP, will take Cosmo''s BOPP capacity to 46,600 tpa. The proposed investment will enable Cosmo to consolidate its position in the rapidly growing domestic BOPP market, while serving export markets for niche high-end BOPP applications. The capacity expansion will be at Cosmo’s existing facilities at Aurangabad, Maharashtra, where surplus land, support infrastructure and trained manpower are already available. Cosmo has ISO9001 and ISO9002 certifications, and holds the patent for synthetic paper. The company has a credit rating of ''A'' from Fitch India as of FY01. From being a second-tier company in the domestic BOPP industry, Cosmo is now graduating to become the dominant domestic player, also serving international niche markets. IFC would play a strong role in supporting Cosmo''s strategy by providing long-term foreign currency financing, which is not readily available, to medium sized companies like Cosmo for maturities beyond three years. This financial support will enable the company to better withstand the natural cyclicality of the industry. IFC would also play a key role in assessing and providing advisory support to Cosmo on its merger with the recently acquired GP operations. The acquisition of GP is the first such endeavor undertaken by Cosmo, and the company expects a strong value-addition from the presence of IFC in developing a sound implementation plan for merging GP''s operations and its financial restructuring. The Indian BOPP industry is gradually maturing, and the project will support the dominant player to lead the restructuring process in that industry. Most Indian BOPP manufacturers are diversified companies that entered the market when the demand and price scenarios in the industry were favorable, and the incentives to set up internationally competitive and benchmarked operations of economic size were limited. This situation is quickly evolving with margins coming under pressure as a result of domestic competition, economies of scale, and periods of excess supply as lumpy production capacities come on stream. Similar to other countries, the industry is gradually consolidating to fewer, larger and more efficient players as the less efficient and competitive exit the industry. Companies that take the initiative to proactively benchmark themselves with global standards can create strong value in the economy through demonstration, leadership and creation of viable revenue generating assets. Cosmo has the capability to lead the way in upgrading the entire industry in terms of quality, R&D, productivity and focused customer support.
sponsor_shareholders: Cosmo Films Limited (Cosmo, or the company) is promoted by Mr. Ashok Jaipuria, who, together with associated investment companies has a 51% shareholding in the company. Other shareholders are Indian and foreign financial institutions (12%), and general public (37%). Cosmo is listed on all the major stock exchanges in India.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The project is to finance the US$ 21.8 million expansion and consolidation program of Cosmo. The proposed IFC investment comprises of a US$ 10 million A Loan.
location_description: The project involves expansion of capacity at Cosmo''s existing manufacturing facilities at Waluj in Aurangabad, located in the state of Maharashtra, India. In addition, the company has a second manufacturing site at Chikalthana also located in Aurangabad, and two more manufacturing sites, Baska and Karjan, in Vadodara, located in the state of Gujarat in India, added through the acquisition of Gujarat Propack Limited (GP). All sites are located in the industrial areas near the main cities, and have access to road infrastructure, proximity to ports and access to airports and supporting infrastructure. The corporate office of Cosmo is located at New Delhi.

company_name: COOPERATIVA NACIONAL DE PRODUCTORES DE LECHE
project_description: The proposed project includes: (1) an investment program to rationalize and modernize Conaprole''s industrial, logistic, and distribution operations; (2) labor restructuring; and (3) restructuring of up to US$40 million of short-term debt. The Investment program comprises two phases of which phase one, completed in August 2001, involves the construction of a new milk powder plant. Phase two consists of the creation of a new industrial complex in the outskirts of Montevideo. The project is a key component of a long-range modernization program initiated by the cooperative in 1999 to transform itself into a modern, low cost and world competitive dairy company, in order to survive in the midst of heightened competition and position itself as one of the leading regional dairy players in the medium-term. Significant progress have been achieved over the last three years to that end, through consolidation of manufacturing activities; upgrade of manufacturing processes; adoption of best practices; innovative IT solutions, and improvement of governance practices to become more efficient and proactive with the market. The next major step in this program, the project, will allow the cooperative to achieve significant efficiency gains and realize large cost savings by relocating the production of value added products from two old plants in Montevideo to a new state of the art facility located in the outskirts of the city and two other existing sites where synergies can be achieved. These operations are currently inefficient due to the plants'' antiquated layout, limited automation and low productivity, logistic bottlenecks, and duplication of specialized lines and distribution centers across several sites. IFC will help the cooperative undertake this critical project, by providing it with long-term financing with a tenor that would not otherwise be available from commercial banks. Given the regional economic situation, IFC''s involvement will also provide comfort to the company''s local and international short-term lenders for participating in the restructuring of the company''s short-term debt into long-term debt, thereby reducing refinancing risks. Furthermore, IFC will support the cooperative''s initiatives to improve its corporate governance practices and provide its newly created environment division assistance for institutionalizing environmental best practice standards. The project is expected to have a strong developmental impact given the cooperative''s central role in Uruguay''s dairy sector. It will strengthen the competitiveness of the cooperative in a sector where Uruguay has a strong comparative advantage. By placing the cooperative on sounder operational and financial footings to meet the challenges of an increasingly competitive international market, it will directly benefit the 2,650 farmers supplying milk to the company by increasing the overall efficiency and viability of the dairy sector and enhancing their revenues in the long-term. It will also have a very positive environmental impact including improved effluent quality and reduced environmental nuisances for the inhabitants of Montevideo. Finally, it will enhance the corporate governance of the flagship of the cooperative sector in Uruguay.
sponsor_shareholders: Conaprole is the leading dairy cooperative, second largest private company, and second largest exporter in Uruguay. It operates nine milk processing plants spread across the country, and produces a wide range of dairy products supplying both the domestic and export markets. More than a third of the cooperative''s revenues are derived from exports, mainly to Latin America. In 2001, the cooperative had total revenues of US$232 million.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$107 million including restructuring of up to US$40 million of short-term debt. The IFC loan of US$35 million will finance 33% of the total investment.
location_description: The project is located in the outskirts of Montevideo, where a new industrial complex with an integrated central distribution center will be created.
Company Name: COOPERATIVA NACIONAL DE PRODUCTORES DE LECHE

company_name: YEDI TEPE BEYNELMILEL OTELCILIK TURIZM VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
project_description: Conrad, a five star business hotel, was established with IFC''s assistance in 1989. The proposed project will be the third project with the company. The first investment was approved in 1990 and it involved an A loan of US$24 million, a B loan of US$27.5 million, and an equity of US$4 million. The hotel''s opening in 1992 coincided with depressed market conditions, resulting from the effects of the Gulf war, and strong growth in the number of five-stars capacity, therefore the project was restructured in 1993 when the Board approved an additional US$6.5 million (A loan of US$3 million and B loan of US$3.5 million). Since the restructuring, Conrad Hotel has showed sound operations and has demonstrated its viability. Today, all B-loans have been repaid (in 1998) and in 1998 IFC has sold its equity share to a local sponsor: Aksoy Group. As of March 2002, IFC''s exposure decreased to US$8.3 million. The proposed investment includes a mid-size conference center and a room/accommodation refurbishment program, which is expected: i) to improve Conrad’s competitive position for mid-size conferences; ii) to lead to better utilization of previously dormant and wasted space, converting it into revenue generating property; and iii) to provide higher margins and occupancy rates, thus making the hotel less prone to seasonality. The business/conference segment of the tourism industry provides good prospects for higher occupancy rates. After this investment, Conrad will be better able to face its competitors by providing conference facilities and high level of standards rooms. The project will not increase the 667 room-capacity of the hotel. IFC Role : After the recent political and macro economical turmoil, interest rates in Turkey have skyrocketed, and credits have become very scarce. More importantly, local financial institutions do not provide the financial depth required for the long-term, outward looking strategic development of major corporations in Turkey. Loan maturities, exceeding even a one year range, are currently not available to the Turkish market. Without IFC’s investment, the company would be forced to rely on extremely limited, short-term, and more expensive financing which would adversely affect liquidity. In the context of the uncertain economic environment, the project critically supports the sustained and competitive evolution of the tourism industry, a vital sector for Turkish economy, where total revenues of more than US$8 billion were earned in 2001. World Bank Group Strategy: The World Bank Group and IMF have focused recent efforts on helping Turkey cope with its financial crisis through continuing adjustment lending, support of structural reforms,0 and fiscal stabilization. This project is consistent with both World Bank strategy and with IFC''s country strategy for Turkey, which seeks to: restore stable growth, improve living standards, reduce economic vulnerability and poverty, and aid the private sector to take advantage of the opportunities offered by the reform. By reinforcing the financial structure of an export-earning company, IFC supports an inflow of foreign currency earnings for Turkey. Development Impact: The proposed project will have a significant development impact. IFC’s support of the project is critical at a time when higher inflation, shrinking domestic demand, and price increases have stagnated the economy, especially manufacturing sector, which has brought about massive layoffs, causing severe economic and social instability in the country. The hotel is internationally competitive and has provided export-earnings in the range of US$21 to US$31 million in the past few years. It employs some 400 staff. By providing timely financing, IFC will help the company seize the market opportunity, and adapt to the latest market requirements. It will also enable the hotel to diversify its income base since the business/conference segment of the tourism industry is less prone to seasonality and regional events.
sponsor_shareholders: The major shareholder of Conrad Hotel (Conrad, or the hotel), holding a 49% stake, is Aksoy Group: a Turkish family owned enterprise involved in the construction, real estate and petroleum distribution business. Mr. Erdal Aksoy has been actively involved in the hotel from the very beginning of the its development, and is now the chairman. IFC sold its equity share (19%) in Conrad Hotel to Aksoy Group in 1998. The technical sponsor, holding a 25% shareholding, is Conrad International Corporation, the overseas arm of Hilton Hotels Corporation of California. Hilton acts as technical partner and provides management and other services such as Hilton world wide reservation services. Turkish Social Insurance Fund (SSK) and State Employees’ Pension Fund (Emek) are institutional investors each holding a 15% and 11% shareholding respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$8.8 million. IFC will provide an A loan of US$3.5 million.
location_description: The project will be implemented in Conrad Hotel, a five-star business hotel, centrally located in downtown Istanbul.
Company Name: YEDI TEPE BEYNELMILEL OTELCILIK TURIZM VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI

project_description: FFC will provide financing to primary agricultural enterprises with strong supply links to major food and agribusiness companies in Russia. This project envisages the development of the FFC to begin with the financing of milk suppliers to Campina''s new yoghurt factory in the Stupino District of Moscow Region. IFC is already an investor (USD 10 million loan) in the Campina yoghurt factory which became operational in April 2000 with capacity to produce 28,000 MT of long-life yoghurt for the Russian market. Over time as FFC expands, other food and agribusiness companies are also expected to participate in the FFC, increasing the number of farms serviced. The FFC is an innovative structure which makes it possible to finance primary agriculture because it relies on long-term supply contracts between suppliers/farms and technically and financially strong processing industries. This tightly integrated supply chain provides sufficient comfort to attract investors and makes it possible to finance primary agricultural production. The FFC will also alleviate one of the main obstacle the F&A companies in Russia face -- the inadequate supply of raw materials, both in terms of quality and quantity, from farms. IFC has played a pivotal role in this project, most importantly : Helping develop the innovative project concept and supporting the initial pilot project as a ground breaking means of providing finance to the primary agriculture sector from which investors usually tend to shy away due to the risks of weather, disease & fluctuating commodity prices. Continuing to arrange technical assistance, via the Russia Agribusiness Technical Assistance Project, funded by IFC and the Government of the Netherlands. This support will be essential during the early phases of the company''s operations before it reaches a sufficient size to achieve economies of scale. Providing comfort to Campina and other processors by committing risk capital with other shareholders to a difficult sector which otherwise finds it difficult to attract equity investment. External finance is also not readily available to farms or start-up leasing companies like FFC. The project will have major developmental benefits: Private sector development . This access to finance will enable medium-sized enterprises in the agricultural sector, to expand their production facilities. New investment in essential farm equipment, like cooling tanks for milk, together with technical assistance, will enable these enterprises to improve efficiency in the production, distribution and the quality of raw milk. The project will facilitate the transfer of efficiency-enhancing technologies and business management techniques. Indirect developmental effects are also significant since investment in these enterprises will have a significant multiplier effect on downstream processors, which are severely constrained by the quality and quantity of raw milk. This will foster the development of processing enterprises that will benefit from a high quality and secure supply of raw milk. Poverty Alleviation : Farmers'' standards of living and employment . The expansion of the production capacity is likely to entail a net positive effect on employment and incomes. This effect is particularly welcome in a sector like agriculture that experienced a deep contraction in the 1990s, and in regions which have suffered from high unemployment and poverty. Product safety compliance : technical assistance in the use and maintenance of the equipment, milk handling and hygiene will bring a cleaner, more hygienic product to the processing factory and the consumer market. Foreign exchange earnings : The project will expand the domestic production of products, and thereby reduce the need to import; and will help over time to lower the demand for foreign exchange.
sponsor_shareholders: FFC''s shareholders will be Rabobank International, FMO, and IFC each taking a third stake in the equity of FFC. Rabobank is a AAA rated bank, with its head office in the Netherlands, it has a strategic interest in the food and agribusiness sector, with a worldwide network of offices servicing international and top-local clients. FMO is the Netherlands Development Finance Corporation specialized in medium and long term finance to private companies and banks in emerging markets. The state of the Netherlands owns 51% of the shares with the remaining in the hands of Dutch banks (almost 40%), industries and some individuals. FMO has a pragmatic and business-like approach and FMO''s investments are not conditional upon the involvement of Dutch companies.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$16.5 million, in the form of US$1.5 million of equity investment, a US$5 million A loan and a US$10 million B loan for the newly established FFC. The proposed IFC investment is US$5.5 million in the form of a US$0.5 million equity investment and a US$5 million A loan for IFC''s own account. Furthermore, technical assistance to be carried out by Rabobank International and IFC''s Russia Agribusiness Technical Assistance Project will provide support to FFC during the first three years of its operations. This technical assistance will be funded by the government of the Netherlands (through its development agency Senter International) and by IFC.
location_description: The project company will be headquartered in Moscow, with operations initially focused on the suppliers of milk to the Campina yoghurt factory in Moscow''s surrounding regions. The project company will gradually build up coverage of other Russian regions and different agricultural subsectors, as its business develops.

project_description: Each ASC system will consist of the hub ASC and a number of related kiosks (spokes). Each ASC will be able to provide farmers with: (i) appropriate inputs (seeds, fertilizers, chemicals); (ii) rental equipment; (iii) information (agronomic practices, market information); (iv) contractual farm-input-application and advisory services, and (v) access to crop finance from commercial banks all under a one-stop-shop concept. Each ASC will be staffed with qualified and suitably trained personnel who will transfer knowledge of good agricultural practices to farmers. Developmental Impact: The objective of MSSL’s business model is to improve farming profitability and sustainability by increasing agricultural yields, reducing production costs and chemical pest control dependency. Current less-than-optimal production in India is attributable to the failure to integrate quality agriculture inputs, scientific farming techniques, mechanization, and finance. Indian farmers often do not trust existing input distribution channels because of the prevalence of poor business practices and spurious products. The public extension system’s reach is limited and the contribution of the private sector is typically motivated by the sale of specific products. MSSL’s intention is to become an agent for change in Indian agriculture through an integrated approach that will provide unbiased solutions oriented to individual farmer success. Moreover, the project will benefit the health and well being of farmers and the environment by promoting integrated pest management (IPM) and non-chemical methods and informed management of chemical products. Farmers will be able to access better and more appropriate and fair priced inputs, rental equipment, and extension services as well as assistance in marketing the crops through market information and brokerage services. Farmers will also have access to crop loans from commercial banks at reasonable interest rates enabling investment in modern agricultural techniques and migration to higher value crops. These benefits are likely to spread to non-participating farmers as they will observe the yield improvement and will consequently modify their own crop management techniques. The project is also expected to generate a substantial number of new jobs in rural areas. The venture is expected to cover 180 districts in India creating jobs for rural residents in the areas of agricultural extension, retailing, logistics, and farm equipment operations. In almost all cases the local agricultural service center will employ staff and contractor from the vicinity of the project. IFC''s role IFC''s involvement in the project will assist the company to: (i) enhance its credibility for the expansion of the franchise and client base, (ii) help promote Integrated Pesticide Management plans to reduce the reliance on chemicals and use chemicals only when they are required; and (iii) gain from IFC knowledge/sources on global agri-trends and insights on successful agri-projects across the globe. In addition, IFC''s participation as an equity investor is expected to provide comfort to potential investors when the Company goes public in the future.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd. (M&M). M&M is the flagship company of the Mahindra Group (the group), India’s largest farm equipment conglomerate. M&M initiated its operations in 1945, manufacturing and marketing utility vehicles, tractors and light commercial vehicles. "Mahindra" is the strongest brand in the Indian farm/rural sector and has 450 tractor and 250 vehicle distributors throughout the country. Its market shares are 33% and 46% for tractors and vehicles respectively. The company’s FY2001 (fiscal year ending in March 2001) sales were US$935 million, and total assets and net worth were US$886 million and US$444 million, respectively. The group has also a strong presence in steel, trading, and financial services. M&M presently holds 100% of Mahindra ShubhLabh Services Limited (MSSL), the project company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$6.1 million. IFC is considering investing up to US$2.2 million equity in MSSL.
location_description: MSSL, headquartered in Mumbai, plans to develop 180 Agricultural Service Centers (ASC) in India''s major agro-climatic areas. To further penetrate the local markets, up to 10 internet-based kiosks will be set up around each center. The regions and general locations for the establishment of agri-centers have been strategically selected. One hundred and fifteen will be located in the northern states and sixty-five in the southern states. Currently, two farm centers are operating in four districts (Madurai, Tiruvarur, Nagappattinam, Thanjavur) in Tamil Nadu state; one farm center in one district (Nalgonda) in Andhra Pradesh state; two farm centers in three districts (Kota, Bundi and Alwar) in Rajasthan state; and two farm centers in two districts (Raichur and Kopal) in Karnataka state. In addition to this four more centers, at Tirunelveli district - Tamil Nadu State, Davangere district - Karnataka State, Nagaur and Jaipur districts - Rajasthan State, will be operational soon. All of the centers are and will be located in rural areas in small towns and villages. The sites are on rural roads - in general on agricultural or commercial land.

project_description: - Description and Purpose : The project is to construct and operate Algeria''s first private sector cement plant with total capacity of 2.0 million tons per year (tpy). The project company, Algerian Cement Company (ACC) will use locally available raw materials and inexpensive energy sources to produce and distribute cement in the M''Sila and neighboring region. - Development Impact: The benefits of the project to the economy arise from: - tax revenues generated from the corporate tax levied on the company; - employment generation and incremental earnings of labor - 1,800 semi- and un-skilled jobs will be created during the life of the project at a wage premium of 30% above the prevailing market wage; and - consumer surplus resulting from the project’s ability to drive cement market prices down as low which will greatly benefit consumers who are presently paying high cement prices. Moreover, the venture is expected to have substantial spill-over economic benefits, such as attracting other industries to M’Sila and helping create a more vibrant building materials and construction industry in the country. - IFC''s Role : First, IFC will provide long-term financing, which is unavailable in Algeria. Second, IFC has played a catalytic role in mobilizing financing and guarantees from other international as well as local financial institutions. Third, IFC will play a major developmental role by ensuring that the project meets World Bank environmental and safety guidelines. The investment will serve as a model in pollution and dust emission control in Algeria and will be the first cement plant in the country to meet the latest most stringent international environmental guidelines. Finally, IFC’s presence in a major project involving a foreign sponsor also supports the Algerian government’s efforts to attract foreign investment in the non-oil sectors.
sponsor_shareholders: The project''s main sponsor is Orascom Construction Industries (OCI). OCI is Egypt’s largest private sector construction conglomerate and is part of the Orascom Group controlled by the Sawiris family, one of Egypt’s prime business families. OCI will initially owns 100% of the Algerian Cement Company (ACC), the project company. OCI has plans to bring into the project strategic partners such as Holcim and/or local groups at a later stage.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at $260 million. The proposed IFC''s investment is a $35 million loan for its own account (or guarantee of local loans of the same amount).
location_description: T he plant will be located on the west side of route CW25 (Bourdj Bourerdj - M''Sila) about 25 kilometers north of M''Sila, 7 km southeast of Hammam Dalaa. The wilaya of M''Sila is located in Central Algeria, some 240 km south-east of Algiers.

project_description: Belisce is the dominant packaging paper and packaging material producer in Croatia. Thanks to a long tradition in the wood industry and its proven management capabilities, Belisce has consistently performed well and is a key employer and source of revenue in the Croatian region. The project is to support the corporate expansion and modernization program of Belisce which aims at making the company a leading producer of packaging paper and materials in the Balkan region. Belisce is already a major player in its home market - Croatia - and in the countries of the former Yugoslavia. Most of the modernization of Belisce''s own facilities has already been completed with IFC financing during 1997-98. The proposed project will consist of the following components: (i) further modernizing of Belisce''s internal facilities; (ii) acquiring and modernizing of Valkarton, a Slovenian corrugated box producer with a subsidiary in FYR Macedonia; and (iii) restructuring of existing debt. The proposed investment will have a strong developmental impact as it will: (i) support the development of a locally managed company; (ii) ensure that the most significant employer in the town of Belisce will become a regionally competitive company; (iii) reduce Belisce''s dependence on the domestic market; and (iv) assist the company in the restructuring of its expensive debts and their rescheduling, lending further support to the strategic reorganization and long-term viability of a leading Croatian company. Belisce is the largest employer in the Slavonia County (east Croatia), which is one of the war-devastated regions in Croatia. It plays an active role in the local community through corporate sponsorships of cultural and athletic facilities and bodies. The proposed transaction will help the company to maintain market leadership in Croatia and grow further within the South European region.
sponsor_shareholders: With a major market share in Croatia, Belisce d.d. (Belisce or the company) is the dominant packaging paper and packaging material producer in Croatia. The company has been in the wood processing business for over 117 years, of which in the last 40 years in chemical and mechanical wood processing - production and sales of packaging paper and corrugated products. Since 1993, Belisce has been a joint stock company. The company''''s subsidiaries include a wood processing plant, an electrical equipment plant, and Croatia''s largest paper recycling company. Belisce has a diversified shareholder base: employees (about 42%), Privredna Bank Zagreb - PBZ, a part of Intessa Group of Italy - (15%), Biokalnik - a local box plant (8%), IFC (20%) and local investment and privatization funds (15%). The company has 1,800 employees, less than a half of the number in the mid 1980''s. Production of packaging papers and corrugated board packaging accounts for more than 90% of total operations. Belisce consists of the following units: pulp and paper mills, box plant, spiral and plastic packaging plant, power plant, maintenance department, transport department.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at EUR46 million (US$40.8 million equivalent). The proposed IFC investment is A loan for IFC''s own account in the amount of up to EUR10 million, and a syndicated B loans up to EUR13 million.
location_description: Based in a heavily forested area, Belisce''s production facilities (packaging paper and materials production) are located on the Drava river in Croatia, near the Hungarian and Yugoslav border. Valkarton''s facilities (packaging material production) are located in Slovenia: Logatec and Rakek (close to Ljubljana), and in Skopje, Macedonia.

company_name: Joint Venture with Limited Liability Giavoni
sector: Garment and Apparel (With Primary Textile Operations, Excluding Footwear)
project_description: The project will upgrade Giavoni’s plant and will expand its vertically integrated operations through the construction of a jean manufacturing facility with capacity to produce about 1.3 million pieces per year. IFC''s role in the project is to facilitate foreign strategic investment in Tajikistan. The project is expected to have the following key development impacts: (i) stimulate the growth of the local economy by providing additional private sector jobs; and (ii) demonstration of best operational practices.
sponsor_shareholders: Giavoni (the company) is 56% owned by Carrera USA Inc., which is the holding company of Carrera Group; 32% by Abreshim S.A., which is the largest textile company in Tajikistan; and 12% by Sano S.A. – an investment vehicle. Both Abreshim and Sano are fully state-owned, Tajik companies.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$4.0 million with the proposed IFC equity investment in the same amount.
location_description: The project is located in Giavoni’s existing textiles factory located in the outskirts of Khojand, northern Tajikistan.
Company Name: Joint Venture with Limited Liability Giavoni

project_description: TELCO is among the top ten commercial vehicle (CV) manufacturers in the world and the market leader in the Indian automobile sector. The project consists of a $397.8 million capital expenditure and debt restructuring program, which is an integral part of the operating and financial restructuring of TELCO. This restructuring program intends to make TELCO a globally competitive automobile manufacturer. The project is divided into a $256.3 million program for product development and modernization, and a $141.5 million debt retirement/refinancing program. The main objective of the product development program is to introduce new products and variants of existing products to the commercial vehicle and passenger car segments. IFC has an important role to play in this project. Through its investment, IFC will assist TELCO in moving toward a regional and/or global presence, and will help the company to restructure and modernize in order to become internationally competitive. By providing a partial guarantee, IFC will enhance the credit rating of TELCO''s proposed bond issue and enable the company to access the capital market for long-term funding and obtain more appropriate pricing for long-term risk. By facilitating the development of a market for structured instruments, IFC will also play a key role in promoting the growth and liquidity of the domestic debt market. The development impact of the project is expected to be significant. If TELCO is able to successfully restructure its operations and become globally competitive, it will generate significant economic benefits. The main quantifiable, economic gains will derive from increased production volumes and quality, with lower costs of production at or close to international levels, for passenger vehicles. In addition, as TELCO expands its subcontracting capacity, SME suppliers and other vehicle manufacturers will gain value from improved competitiveness and economies of scale in the domestic auto component industry. TELCO’s global restructuring will also have a significant demonstration effect on other vehicle manufacturers operating in India, as well as on the auto-component industry.
sponsor_shareholders: Tata Engineering & Locomtive Company Limted (TELCO, or the company) is promoted by the Tata Group, India''s premier business house. Tata Sons Limited (TSL), the principal investment and holding company of the Tata Group is the largest shareholder of TELCO with a 14.33% stake. Other Tata companies own 11.32% of the company, bringing the total Tata Group shareholding to 25.65%. Other major shareholders include DaimlerChrysler AG (10.00%), Indian financial institutions & banks (21.14%) and the public (22.90%)
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $397.8 million. TELCO has just completed a rights issue, which will help the company raise $201.9 million over a period of three years to partially finance the project. The proposed IFC investment consists of a partial credit guarantee for a $103 million local currency bond issue to partially finance the project. The IFC guarantee amount will depend on market considerations, but in any event will not exceed $65.0 million.
location_description: TELCO''s main manufacturing facilities are located at: - Jamshedpur, State of Jharkand in East India (manufacture of commercial vehicles) - Pimpri & Chinchwad, Pune, State of Maharashtra in Western India (manufacture of commercial vehicles and passenger cars) - An assembly plant for commercial vehicles is also located at Lucknow, State of Uttar Pradesh in North India All the sites are accessible by air, road and rail transport.

project_description: Founded in 1997, Ramenka has established itself as one of Moscow''s largest retailers. Operating under the name Ramstore, the company currently owns and operates three hypermarkets/mini-malls and six supermarkets. Together the hypermarkets and supermarkets have approximately 27,410 square meters of retail selling space, and 25,850 square meters of leasable retail space. The purpose of the project is to bring Ramenka''s value proposition, which consists of affordable pricing, convenient location, pleasant shopping environment and wide assortment of goods, to a larger number of Moscow consumers. In addition, the project will increase the amount of available retail space in Moscow, which has had the least amount of per capita retail space among all European capitals. The implementation of the project will result in a significant developmental effect. This will include: considerable managerial expertise transfer in the areas of inventory management, marketing, and sales techniques; a switch to more efficient retail formats; a further strengthening of the local distributors, wholesalers and primary food processors (at present Ramenka is sourcing approximately 60% of its product from the local market, working closely with domestic suppliers to ensure a consistent supply of high quality products); an important demonstration effect for retailers in Moscow and Russia more generally; the creation of approximately 900 new jobs for Russian nationals and the doubling of many new jobs in up and down stream activities; and availability of lower-cost, high quality foodstuffs and other consumer goods. IFC’s role in the project will be to provide long-term debt financing in a difficult business environment, and to assist Ramenka in mobilizing a US$30 million B loan, one of very few such transaction to be undertaken in Russia since the 1998 crisis, and among the first syndicated loans in Russia under the guarantee of Turkish sponsors.
sponsor_shareholders: The sponsors of the project are Migros Turk Ticaret Anonim Sirketi (Migros), Enka Holding (Enka) and Entrade GmbH (Entrade). Migros, the largest and the oldest supermarket chain in Turkey, is a part of the Koc Group, one of Turkey''s most important financial and industrial conglomerates. Enka Holding is one of Turkey''s leading industrial group focusing on construction, contracting, property development and retail. Both Migros and Enka are listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange. Entrade is Enka Holding''s wholesale business subsidiary incorporated in Germany. The project company, Ramenka, is a limited liability company incorporated in the Russian Federation. Migros, Enka and Entrade currently own 50%, 38% and 12% of Ramenka respectively.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total cost of the project is estimated at US$100 million. The proposed IFC investment consists of an A loan of up to US$30 million for IFC''s own account and a syndicated B loan of up to US$30 million. Initially the loans will be secured by a guarantee from the sponsors.
location_description: Ramenka''s expansion calls for the greenfield construction of two hypermarkets with attached malls and four supermarkets in Moscow. For the construction of the first hypermarket and mall, Ramenka has acquired a large site on Leningradskiy Prospect (the main highway from central Moscow to Sheremyetevo Airport). A second hypermarket and mall of a similar size is to be located in southern Moscow. Sites for the four new supermarkets will be chosen close to Moscow''s major transportation routes.

sector: Paper Packaging Products (Including Boxes, Cartons, etc.)
project_description: ZAO Stora Enso Packaging is a Russian subsidiary of Stora Enso Packaging OY. The existing company management has proven fully capable in the fast developing Russian corrugated board market, and has emerged as a market leader. This is due mainly to the sponsor, which has extensive experience in corrugated board manufacturing and has extensive experience in Central and Eastern Europe. In order to satisfy increasing demand for its product, the company is undertaking an expansion. The project foresees an increase in the company''s production capacity from current 70 million sqm/year (33, 390 mt/year) to 105 million sqm/year (50, 085 mt/year). IFC''s role in this project is to provide continued, substantive support to its client in an uncertain environment and mitigate political risk. The project will enhance the positive demonstration effect for local businesses that ZAO Stora Enso has already achieved through their best practice production and environmental practices. IFC estimates that as a result of the expansion, ZAO Stora Enso, located in Moscow''s poorer neighboring region, Kaluga, will increase its workforce by an additional 90 people, to a total of 240 people by the end of 2002 (the Company employed 150 people at FYE 2000). Indirectly, the local business community will greatly benefit from the project as a nucleus of regional development. It will also help create jobs and improve infrastructure in many key upstream and downstream businesses.
sponsor_shareholders: Stora Enso Packaging Oy (the sponsor) is a market leader in corrugated board production and a major supplier of packaging machines and systems in Northern Europe. It is a subsidiary of Stora Enso, Finland’s principal forest products company. Its product range includes consumer packages, food and non-food packages, transport packages, display stands, corrugated sheets, paper roll end sheet packing systems, and packaging systems and machines. In addition to its investment in ZAO Stora Enso Packaging (the project company), Stora Enso Packaging Oy has extensive experience elsewhere in Eastern Europe, having already established plants in Hungary, Lithuania, Estonia and Latvia.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: This expansion project has an estimated cost of US$14 million equivalent. IFC has an existing loan of US$6 million and US$1.5 million equity investment in the company. The new project involves IFC providing an additional US$7 million A loan for a total of US$13 million in IFC debt exposure, and a take out of the equity investment. The remaining project cost will be covered by internal cash generation and a sponsor loan.
location_description: The company is located in Balabanovo, 100 kilometers south-west of Moscow. The project site in Balabanovo allows the plant easy access to Moscow, the Russian Federation''s most lucrative market, while at the same time its Kaluga location outside the Moscow region gives it significant taxpayer status in the Kaluga region. Sound infrastructure (rail, road, electricity) is in place and a skilled local staff base has been built.

project_description: The proposed project consists of the refurbishment and repositioning of Hotel Lietuva. The hotel, which targets the conference market currently underdeveloped and underserved in Vilnius, will be operated by Reval Hotel Group, a leading mid-market hotel operator in the Baltics. Opened in 1982, Hotel Lietuva was originally designed as a landmark hotel with 324 rooms on 18 floors, but has suffered from insufficient maintenance and a lack of upgrading. The refurbished hotel will have approximately 275 rooms, as well as restaurant, bar, conference and banquet facilities. The sponsor plans to renew all of the internal infrastructure and upgrade all common areas and the façade. The renovation is expected to start in the second quarter of 2002 and to be completed within 12 months. The renovation of Hotel Lietuva will create high quality mid-market accommodation for business and tourism development in Lithuania, fostering a conference market that will support related industries such as restaurants, retail, and transport, as well as suppliers to the hotel. The project is also expected to bring social and economic benefits in the surrounding area, which the city of Vilnius has targeted for extensive commercial development. IFC''s role in the proposed project is to provide long-term financing which is not currently available in Lithuania at a reasonable cost, and to mobilize additional capital, fostering foreign direct investment flows into the country. IFC’s presence will help ensure that the environmental and fire and life safety standards of the refurbished hotel conform to World Bank Group guidelines.
sponsor_shareholders: Viešbutis Lietuva, the company that owns Hotel Lietuva (the hotel), is 89% owned by Linstow International AS, a Norwegian property company.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated to be US$36.5 million equivalent. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan of up to US$9 million equivalent for IFC''s own account and a B Loan of up to US$9 million equivalent for the account of at least two participant banks.
location_description: The hotel is located in the Šnipiškës district of Vilnius, Lithuania, about 200 meters up from the north bank of the Neris River. A major four lane road (Ukmergës) runs on the north side of the hotel, with a parallel secondary road (Upës) on the south side. The area surrounding the hotel is a mix of shops, offices, public buildings, and parks.

company_name: UNITED JOINT STOCK CO FOR PETROCHEMICAL INDUSTRIES
project_description: The project consists of the construction and operation of a 40,000 mt/year linear alkyl benzene (LAB) plant and the necessary infrastructure outside of Damascus, Syria. Construction of the project has started in June 2001 and is progressing well. LAB is the major feedstock required to produce all kinds of detergents, from liquid soap to dishwasher powder. The venture is an intermediate step towards backward integration of Mr. Daaboul''s detergent operations and will allow Daaboul Detergents to rely on in-house produced LAB instead of depending on supplies from abroad. It will be implemented as a greenfield project and will be incorporated as ''Daaboul Company for Chemicals & Petrochemicals Industries''. The venture will have a number of positive development impacts. The project is competitive locally and within the region, and will generate jobs and increase revenue through taxes. It will aslo support an entrepreneurial and competitive local private sector group of the sort that will be vital if Syria’s more liberal approach to private sector led economic development is to succeed. In addition, as one of IFC’s first financings in the Syrian market, the project will have a positive demonstration impact for local and foreign investors. IFC''s environmental and technical input will be crucial to smoothen the project''s implementation and make the daily operations safe. With this investment, IFC demonstrates its commitment to support local entrepreneurs and to help improve the long-term competitiveness of a family-owned business.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Ahmad Daaboul & Sons Company for Detergents (Daaboul Detergents). Like his other companies, Daaboul Detergents is managed and wholly-owned by Mr. Daaboul and his family. Since its modest beginning in 1974, Daaboul Detergents has developed into the leading producer of detergents in Syria, offering laundry powders, dishwashing paste, and cleaning and disinfecting liquids under established brand names. Production capacities are 35,000 mt/year of powder, 15,000 mt/year of paste, and 15,000 mt/year of liquid cleaners. Roughly, one third of the detergent production is exported to other Arabian countries including Saudi Arabia and Morocco, but also to Gabon and some Eastern European countries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The estimated project cost is US$38.0 million. An A-loan of US$13.0 million is the contemplated IFC investment.
location_description: The project is located 25km south of Damascus in Deir Ali, next the the principal highway connecting Damascus with Amman.
Company Name: UNITED JOINT STOCK CO FOR PETROCHEMICAL INDUSTRIES

project_description: The proposed project consists mainly of refinancing CNO''s existing debt. In order to finance its activities and continued growth, CNO borrowed US$280 million, through a financial structure maturing in June and July 2002 . Due to the political uncertainty in Brazil, the recent crisis in Argentina, and the terrorist attacks to the USA, the international financial market has been adversely affected. It is in this context the company has requested IFC’s assistance in mobilizing US$280 million for the financing of its future operations (the project). IFC Role IFC''s role in this project includes: (i) providing financing that is otherwise currently not available; (ii) "bailing-in" other private sector financing sources through its B-loan mobilization program; (iii) advising the company on a more rational and sustainable financing structure and financial management through appraisal; and (iv) contributing in the improvement of corporate governance practices. Development Impact The Brazilian private sector at present is faced with multiple threats to its stability and prospects of future growth: the depreciation of the Real; the current political and economical uncertainty in Argentina; the political anxiety prior to the 2002 presidential election; the world economic slowdown; and the flight to quality since the September 11 event. These factors are seriously affecting Brazilian firms’ ability to raise financing necessary to maintain the normal course of business, let alone to invest for future growth. Even large companies that previously had access to market financing have lost access. Under the circumstances, demand for financing support from institutions like IFC is mounting and pressing. This requires IFC in the short-run to narrow its focus towards responding to such urgent demand, while remaining within the framework for its medium-term objectives. In relation to this project, the borrower has agreed to earmark US$1 million to finance a social project, acceptable to IFC.
sponsor_shareholders: Odebrecht S.A (ODB) is one of the ten largest Brazilian private-sector conglomerates in terms of revenues, and Brazil’s leading service exporter. It employs almost 30,000 workers in Africa, Europe and the Americas. Construtura Norberto Odebrecht S.A (CNO) is a subsidiary of ODB (99.85% of the voting capital, and 99.82% of the total capital), which in turn is 81% controlled by Odebrecht Investimentos S.A., a Brazilian corporation wholly owned by the Odebrecht family. CNO is the largest Brazilian engineering and construction company as measured by 2000 revenues. CNO provides a variety of engineering, procurement and construction services for infrastructure projects, manufacturing and processing plants and heavy and industrial construction (which includes oil and gas-related construction activities). Together with its wholly-owned construction companies, CNO engages in the construction of large scale infrastructure and other projects, including highways, railways, power plants, bridges, tunnels, subways, buildings, port facilities, dams, manufacturing and processing plants, as well as mining facilities, steel mills, paper and pulp mills, cement plants, and chemical and petrochemical plants . Geographically, CNO undertakes projects in all regions of Brazil, as well as in most South American countries, Central America, Portugal, United States and Angola. CNO was ranked the world''s largest constructor of hydroelectric plants (by revenues) according to ENR- Engineering News Records (in the December 2000 edition) as well as one of the world''s top 20 service exporter in that sector.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total investment cost for the proposed project is estimated at US$280 million to refinance existing debt and support the company''s future operations. IFC will assist CNO by providing a financial package consisting of an up to US$20 million A loan, an up to US$60 million C loan and an up to US$200 million syndicated B loan.
location_description: The Odebrecht Group''s headquarters are located in Salvador, state of Bahia, Northeastern Region of Brazil, while CNO is headquartered in the city of Rio de Janeiro.

project_description: VSTC was incorporated in April 1986 by Mr. Qasim Ibrahim to represent his interests in trading and shipping. In 1988 the company diversified into tourist resorts, which now dominate VSTC''s operations. The company, with US$ 108.4 million in total assets and a net worth of US$ 60.9 million as of June 30, 2001, is one of the larger private companies in the Maldives. Having received land for storage purposes from the government of Maldives, VSTC is now expanding its trading operations by implementing storage facilities at Thilafushi island. VSTC also intends to make its resorts world class by improving environment compliance and safety facilities. VSTC corporate investment program consisting of : i) Infrastructure for Trading Operations (US$23.2 million) including installing storage tanks for diesel, kerosene and petrol (38,000 cubic meters), LPG storage and filling plant (2,538 MT), and cement storage silos and packaging plant (8,000 MT). ii) Energy Saving Equipment (US$4.3 million) including solar water heating systems, heat recovery systems and rationalisation of the installed power generating capacity. These systems would reduce energy consumption by 10-20%, resulting in savings of about US$0.65 million per annum. iii) Environment and Safety Infrastructure (US$3.8 million) including fire detection and safety systems, exhaust chimney systems, and waste water treatment plants. iv) Debt Restructuring of up to US$ 9.5 million of short-term debt. IFC Role IFC would provide long term funding for the proposed project which is not available in the Maldives. The banks operating in the Maldives restrict funding to 3-4 years and offer small amounts at high fixed interest rates of 12% - 14% p.a. in US$ terms. Resort owners have to rely mainly on financing arrangements with tour operators, which have high hidden interest costs of 20% - 30% p.a. IFC would help the company to demonstrate its commitment to protecting the local environment and improving its own environment and safety infrastructure. The Sun Island, partly funded by an IFC loan, has demonstrated good environmental performance (being the first winner of the "Presidential Green Globe Award" in the Maldives) and the current investment is expected to bring the other resorts to similar standards of compliance. IFC would also encourage VSTC to improve its corporate governance and management structure. Development Impact The proposed project benefits tourism, the most important and fastest growing sector in the Maldives with considerable spillover effects on the national economy. The proposed upgrade of VSTC''s environmental and safety facilities and implementation of energy saving measures, will further yield quantifiable and non-quantifiable economic benefits. The expansion of VSTC''s trading activities increases the choices available to the Maldivian consumer and leads to more efficient delivery and market linked prices of essentials goods such as diesel, LPG and cement. The project will extend the fuel distribution network to the more remote islands, which are at present not fully served. World Bank Group Strategy The project is consistent with the IFC strategy for the Maldives which includes encouraging private sector participation in promoting key sectors such as tourism, and related infrastructure, and the World Bank strategy of assisting development in an environment friendly way.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Mr. Qasim Ibrahim, who owns 99.8% of Villa Shipping and Trading Company Private Ltd. (VSTC or the company). The remaining 0.2% of VSTC’s capital is held by Mr. Ibrahim’s wife. Mr. Ibrahim is a well known businessmen in the Maldives and has served as a member of Parliament in the Maldives. He is currently the Vice Chairman of Maldives Association of Tourism Industries, and has been a past President of the SAARC Chamber of Commerce and Industries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$40.8 million. The proposed IFC investment is up to US$15 million, which consist of an A Loan up to US$10 million and a C Loan of up to US$5 million.
location_description: The project site consists of 5 resorts located in the Maldives, namely: Fun Island (Bodufinolhu) in South Male Atoll; Holiday Island (Dhiffushi) in South Ari Atoll; Paradise Island (Lankanfinolhu) in North Male Atoll; Sun Island (Nalaguraidhoo) in South Ari Atoll; and Royal Island (Horubadhoo) in Baa Atoll and (ii) Villa Hakatha on Thilafushi island near Male.

project_description: The project is to modernize and upgrade the existing facilities of a AWMC, a mineral water bottling plant, by installing a PET bottling line including a PET and polyethylene (PE) bag packing facilities. The existing plant (including its underground aquifer sourced water) was in test trial operations for four months since its purchase in 1998, but was shut down because it used PVC technology. The new project will replace it with PET. The venture aim is to achieve a 20-25% share of Yemen''s 100 million liters market by providing a full product size. Distribution will cover the capital of Sana''a, the cities of Aden, Hodeidah, Ibb, Taiz and their surrounding areas. The plant will produce naturally sourced water in 750 ml. and 1.5L. PET bottles including 500 ml. size PE bags. The proposed water bottling project will promote local enterprise in the bottled water sector and increase the supply of safe drinking water. The project would create approximately 100 new jobs, stimulate competition, and introduce healthier PET bottles. IFC''s role in the proposed project involves: (i) providing long-term foreign currency financing which is currently not available from local banks; and (ii) encouraging the development of competitive local manufacturers. IFC''s participation in this investment would create a demonstration effect as an international standard venture that would produce mineral water of high quality and promote sound and modern business practices.
sponsor_shareholders: The main project sponsor is the Salahaddin Industrial & Commercial Group (the group), one of the leading business groups in Yemen, and its chairman, Mr. Yousuf Abdul Wadood Saeed. The group’s activities cover trade, manufacturing of plastic products and household metal appliances, and insurance. The Saeed family owns 33.1% of Al-Ahila Mineral Water Company (AMWC). The group instead owns 11.3% and 6% through Salahaddin Plastic Industries & Marketing Co. Ltd. and Salahaddin Metals Household Appliances Factory (fully owned by the Saeed family). It also owns an additional 2.7% of AMWC through Al-Watania Insurance Company. The remaining 46.9% shareholding is owned by minority shareholders.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$4.0 million. The proposed investment is an A Loan for IFC''s own account of up to US$1.4 million.
location_description: The project is located in Ibb, Yemen.

project_description: This is an innovative pilot attempt by IFC to alleviate the acute poverty of cotton farmers in Tajikistan by enabling them to take control of their own commercial activities. FOM, which will be owned by the farmers, will use the IFC Loan and the SECO grant to: (i) purchase and deliver to the farmers a complete input bundle (including seeds, fertilizers, agrochemicals, tools, implements, grain bags, crop storage, equipment rental, picking charges and transport); (ii) arrange for processing the farmers’ crop; (iii) sell through its marketing service the farmers’ crops directly on the market; and (iv) identify and develop market opportunities and enterprises to assist with improving farmer viability and enterprise diversification. The proposed project will bring management skills and financial support to the agricultural sector and demonstrate the economic benefits to be gained by upgrading the quality and quantity of the cotton crop. The technical assistance will be managed by Private Enterprise Partnership (PEP), who will train the farmers in proper production, irrigation, fertilization and financial management, in addition to appointing the manager. The technical assistance is part of the overall Swiss-IFC Central Asia technical assistance Partnership for Central Asia that has been recently approved by SECO and that will be implemented by PEP. The project is expected to increase cotton yield and revenues for farmers currently living in abject poverty. The venture will also bring an increase of foreign exchange in the country, as over 80% of Tajikistan''s cotton is exported.
sponsor_shareholders: The project company is Farmers Ownership Model (FOM). FOM will be financed on a commercial basis by IFC, and on a grant basis by the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO). The Zafarabad Mcht Association of Farmers (in Zafarabad province) and the Andarasoy Association of Nov Farmers (in the adjacent Nov province) are the most likely candidates to become farm shareholders in the joint stock company. Together, the two associations account for approximately 1,940 hectares. IFC selected farmers who are least indebted and will eventually expand membership to adjacent farmers, and to others in Southern Tajikistan should the pilot program prove to be successful.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$502,000. The proposed IFC investment is a US$250,000 A loan for IFC''s own account. The balance is capital reserve made available through Swiss grant funds and share capital paid in by farmers.
location_description: The project will be located in the Nov and Zafarabad regions of Northern Tajikistan and expand thereafter to other regions.

sector: Miscellaneous and Industrial Ores (Including Magnesite, Fluorite, Sulfur, Soda Ash, Clays, Gypsum, Lime, Peat, Boron, Diatomite, Feldspar, etc.)
project_description: Middle East Regional Development Enterprises (MEREN) was established in 1996 as a private shareholding company to develop investment projects in Jordan and the MENA region. The proposed project is to establish MEREN silica sand plant (MEREN) which will manufacture high quality silica sand to be exported mainly to European glass manufacturers. With an installed annual capacity of 530,000 tons, MEREN is designed to manufacture a number of different quality products, including dried and milled silica for glass, ceramics, sodium silicate, glass fiber, oil and gas fracturing and other industries that use high quality silica sand. The proposed project will promote healthy local enterprise in the silica sand sector, an industry in which Jordan has a natural advantage. It will directly create approximately 30 jobs in the silica sand factory, and indirectly up to an estimated 350 jobs in the transport, storage and handling, and mining sectors. Since all MEREN’s production will initially be for exports, the proposed project will increase Jordan’s export performance and foreign currency earnings. In the longer-term, it may also stimulate establishment of new downstream industries in Jordan such as glass or ceramics manufacturing that use high quality silica sand. The project will involve transfer of the most advanced production technology, know-how and local staff training by Outocumpu to Jordan and it will promote creation of an internationally competitive local enterprise.
sponsor_shareholders: The company''s four shareholders are well established businessmen from Jordan and the Gulf. Mr. Riad Sadik (with 40.4% of MEREN), manages the Al Habtoor Group Engineering Enterprise based in Dubai, with operations in several Arab and European countries and an annual turnover of US$250 million. Mr. Hamid Jafar (with 40.4% of MEREN) is the owner and chairman of Crescent Petroleum Company International, Sharjah. He is a managing director of Intoil Bahrain and the Chairman of Gultainer Co. Ltd. (Sharjah) established in 1976 which manages and operates two container terminals on behalf of the Sharjah Port Authority in the United Arab Emirates. Mr. Hassan Mango (with 14.2% of MEREN) is a prominent Jordanian businessman; he is the Managing Director of Al Emranya Company, active in construction material trading with offices in Dubai and Amman. Mr. Talal Al Hassan (with 5% of MEREN) has served as Jordanian ambassador to several European countries and was Minister of State for Foreign Affairs from 1993 to 1995. The company''s technical partner is Outokumpu, Finland, one of the world’s leading producers of stainless steel and ferro-chrome products, operating in 32 countries worldwide.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$14.6 million. The proposed IFC investment is a loan for IFC''s own account of up to US$5 million.
location_description: The project is located in a uninhabited greenfield area in the Al-Quwarya region in the south of Jordan, 300 km south of Amman and 65 km northeast of Aqaba. The company has obtained a concession for 30 years to explore and extract sand in this area of 12 square kilometers. The proposed plant will be located in this area, close to the sand mines and the main road to Aqaba.

project_description: The project involves the setting up of seven warehouse stores, in different parts of Metro Manila by PS Phils. The warehouse stores are being located within Metro Manila to take advantage of dense populations and relatively high levels of consumer demand. They sell a variety of food and consumer goods with emphasis on quality, low prices, and efficient operations. The warehouses typically carry a much smaller product range compared to supermarkets - 2,500 stock-keeping (sku) units (vs. 25,000-30,000 sku units for supermarkets) including apparel, food services, bakery, photo centers, and tire centers. About 50% of sales are derived from products sourced from the local market. The target customers are consumers and small businesses. IFC''s Role: - Provide long-term financing which is otherwise not available. - IFC presence will help mobilize other medium to long-term sources of funding. Development Impact: - Introduction of a relatively new retailing concept which through increased efficiencies of purchasing, logistics, technology and distribution will provide consumers with lower prices on and wider access to, quality food and consumer goods. - Better value for the mom&pop "sari-sari" stores (largely small and medium enterprises and micro enterprises). - New markets for local suppliers that produce world class products.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is PriceSmart (PSMT), based in San Diego, USA, which owns 52% of PriceSmart Philippines (PS Phils or the company) which operates under the brand name of S&R Price. Modeled after the first membership warehouse shopping chain in the US, the Price Club, PSMT is engaged in merchandising in Central America, the Caribbean, and East Asia. In the US, PSMT operates two buying offices, two distribution centers and a corporate headquarters. As of August 31, 2001, PSMT owned majority interest in 22 warehouse stores with 7 other warehouse stores under licensed agreements in China and Saipan. Other shareholders include the E Class Corporation, which owns 38% of the company and is owned by William S. Go and Robert C. See. Mr. Go is mainly engaged in the import and export business between the Philippines and the US. Both Mr. Go and Mr. See are owners of Century Seafood Restaurant, a high end Chinese restaurant. The remaining 10% of PS Phils is owned by First Metro Investment Corporation, the investment arm of Metro Bank, the largest commercial bank in the Philippines.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$68.7 million. IFC proposed investment totals US$17.2 million with US$12.2 million in the form of an A loan to PS Phils/PSMT and US$5 million in the form of quasi-equity in PSMT.
location_description: The location of the seven warehouse stores are as follows: 1. Fort Bonifacio* 2. Ortigas Extension, Pasig City* 3. Congressional Avenue, Quezon City (to be opened in March 2002) 4. Aseana business Park, Roxas Boulevard, Paranaque 5. Filinvest Corporate City, Muntinlupa 6. Quirino Highway, Novaliches 7. Site of Manila Jockey Club - San Lazaro Racetrack (* existing stores) Each site involves a flat rectangular area measuring approximately 5 acres in order to support a store of about 50,000 sq. ft. and around 300 parking spaces. The locations are situated on main arterial roads with direct access and good visibility. The sites are close to densely populated neighborhoods or commercial centers.

project_description: EKS is one of Turkey’s leading tile manufacturers and exporters with revenues of about US$70 million in 2001. The proposed project includes financial restructuring by providing long-term working capital financing, and investments in capacity and efficiency which will enable EKS to further enhance its overall export competitiveness by increasing high value-added production and reducing costs. IFC Role and Developmental Impact: IFC’s role as a provider of finance for the Turkish corporate sector has increased significantly after the recent economic crisis and financial turmoil. IFC will be providing the necessary long-term finance to enable strong exporters such as EKS to continue to maintain their position in the global market. With IFC’s assistance, EKS will be able to: (i) improve its balance sheet by replacing expensive and uncertain short-term debt with long-term financing; (ii) undertake export-oriented investments in specialty tiles; and (iii) enhance the overall efficiency of its operations by removing bottlenecks in production. IFC''s investment will thus restore the company’s liquidity and enable it to increase exports in direct support of the Turkish economy. Moreover, the project gives IFC an opportunity to support a company belonging to an existing client (Eczacibasi Group) in one of its major business segments at a critical time for the Turkish economy. World Bank Group Strategy: The World Bank Group and IMF have focused recent efforts on helping Turkey cope with its financial crisis through continuing adjustment lending, support of structural reforms and fiscal stabilization.
