Before setting up PAE, Mr. Estrada had a long experience in the oil sector, working for Shell and Mobil among others. He provides Ecomex with capital and strategic support. Mr. Sergio García Palacio . President and CEO of Ecomex. Mr. García got involved in activities related to air pollution in the middle 1980’s. He has been in the engine conversion business since he founded Convertidores Cataliticos Mexicanos in 1991. Prior to this, Mr. García worked mainly in the petrochemical sector in Mexico.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$27.8 million. IFC''s investment consists of a US$ 10 million A loan for IFC''s own account.
location_description: Ecomex currently has a conversion workshop which is located at Fulton No. 5A in Tlalnepantla, State of Mexico and two CNG dispensing stations which are located at: a) Av. 16 de Septiembre No. 255, Naucalpan de Juarez, State of Mexico; and b) Cecilio Robelo, No. 103, Delegacion Venustiano Carranza, Federal District. The project will enable Ecomex to significantly increase the number of conversions undertaken at the conversion workshop and it will also enable the company to build three new dispensing stations. The likely sites for these are: 1) Cerrada de Cien Metros, Delegacion Gustavo A. Madero, Federal District; 2) Rio Becerra s/n, Delegacion Alvaro Obregon, Federal District; and 3) Ecatepec de Morelos, State of Mexico.
Company Name: Combustibles Ecologicos Mexicanos, S.A. de C.V.

project_description: The project is phase I of the Northgate Cyberzone Information Technology Park (Northgate or the project), an expansion of FAI''s existing operations. As the information technology and property development subsidiary of FDC, FAI was established to develop Filinvest Corporate City. FCC includes: (1) Festival Supermall, a well-established regional shopping center for southern Metro Manila completed in May 1998 with over 400 retail locators; (2) Northgate Cyberzone Information Technology Park; (3) Asian Hospital, a 500 bed acute care tertiary hospital and a 350 room medical office building (IFC investment); (4) Spectrum Business District – high rise offices and residential towers; (5) Civic Plaza – national and municipal government offices; and (6) Market Square, a multi-vehicular transportation terminal and wet & dry market. Northgate is located on a 18.7 ha area in FCC and is master-planned to provide a high tech working environment complemented by comprehensive infrastructure. Phase I of the development, covering 2.7 ha, includes: (i) 5 information technology (IT) buildings; (ii) IT infrastructure; and (iii) the Convergence Hall providing a venue for interaction between IT professionals. The Convergence Hall also houses an IT college of De LaSalle University which is not part of the project and will be financed by the Filinvest Corporate City Foundation. Total leasable area of the 5 buildings is about 45,000 sqm available for 35 - 50 locators. This is the first IFC funded project supporting information technology driven infrastructure in emerging economies. IFC’s Role: Providing long-term financing which is otherwise not available Support of the IT sector Development Impact: Reduced barriers to entry for IT companies Enhancement of export potential Foreign direct investment and skills development
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Filinvest Development Corporation (FDC) which owns, directly and indirectly, 92% of Filinvest Alabang, Inc. (FAI), the information technology and property development subsidiary of FDC. FAI is the borrower while FDC is the guarantor of the IFC loan. FDC is publicly listed, but its shares are not widely traded since the Gotianun family effectively owns a significant portion with investment funds holding the remainder. FDC traces its origin to the consumer finance business established by Mr. Andrew L. Gotianun, Sr. and his family in 1955.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$44.0 million. IFC''s proposed investment is US$22.0 million in the form of an A loan.
location_description: The project site will be at Filinvest Corporate City (FCC) in Alabang, Muntinlupa City. FCC is a 244 hectare (ha) fully integrated, self-contained urban development, well situated 16 kms south of Metro Manila, at the gateway of the Calabarzon area (Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal and Quezon provinces), which has experienced significant economic growth in recent years.

project_description: Telecom Technology Limited (the Company) is an exisisting company involved in the business of providing internet services in the city of Dushanbe, Tajikistan. The Company, now wants to expand its activities to other cities of Tajikistan nemely Khujand, Kurgan Tube and Chakalovsk and the Project involves the installation of 4-satellite VSAT stations to establish a network connecting these four cities of Tajikistan. As a result of the Project, a wide range of reliable Internet, Email and private data communications services (currently unavailable or under-served in Tajikistan) will be made available in Dushanbe and three cities of Northern Tajikistan. The Project is a business expansion, sponsored by Telecom Technology Limited. The estimated US$0.7 million cost of the Project includes cost of purchase of new equipment, installation and training and working capital. The Project is expected to be implemented within a period of 6 months after disbursement by IFC. The Project will have the following developmental impacts: (1) expansion of an information service increasingly vital to the development of competitive industry and services; (2) increased competition in a small market; (3) introduction of up-to-date technology in a sector where this is crucial; (4) supporting the emerging Tajik business community; and (5) creation of 30 jobs. The Project is in line with the World Bank Group Country Assistance Strategy, which highlights IFC’s key focus in Tajikistan on promoting investment in small and medium size businesses to foster broad based industrial development and help alleviate poverty. More specifically, the Project complements IFC’s strategy to encourage and support commercially viable Projects in Tajikistan’s emerging SME’s in the private sector by: (a) helping develop new and efficient private sector companies; (b) assisting employment generation; and (c) promoting development of communications. The proposed Project builds directly on these strategies and supports the CAS in private sector development, particularly in the area of SMEs.
sponsor_shareholders: The Project will be owned and operated by Telecom Technology Ltd (the Company). The Company was established in 1994. At start-up, it specialized in development of banking software as well as designing and installation of customized networks for leading Tajik banks and providing networking facility to local businesses. In 1996, the Company became a member and VSAT-operator of INTELSAT, an international satellite communication company and represented Tajik Ministry of Communications in international forums on electronic communications. In 1998, Telecom Technology became the first ISP (Internet Service Provider) and VSAT operator in Tajikistan and today it is the market leader in providing Internet and Email services. In 2000, it opened the first Internet-Café in the country. The Company presently employs some 35 people and is headed by Mr. Shavkat Khalilov (one of its founders). The Company is established as a Tajik limited liability entity and its present shareholding structure is as follows: Private Company “Kon” 11% Mr. Shavkat Khalilov 65% Mr. Bakhtier Khudainazarov 24%
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$710,000.00. The proposed IFC investment comprises an A-Loan of US$315,000 for its own account and represents about 44% of the project cost. This exposure for IFC is within SEF norms for a business expansion. Also, a participating element, which is 2% of Gross Sales, has been included. (This may lead to its re-categorization as Venture Loan, or C Loan, after further negotiation and appraisal).
location_description: The head office of the Company is and will be located in an office building (rented premises) in the City Center of Dushabe and a regional office (also rented space in an office building) will be established in the city of Khujand.

company_name: GUNKOL GUNES ENERJISI VE KLIMA SANAYI A S
sector: Household Appliances (Including Refrigerators, Laundry Machine, Dishwashers, etc.)
project_description: Project : Gunkol Gunes Enerjisi ve Klima Sanayi A.S. (“Gunkol”, or the “Company”), the white goods company of the Teba Group, is Turkey’s leading profitable exporter of cooking ranges and ovens with 2000 revenues of US$60 million equivalent. The project is a US$20 million modernization investment to (i) support the Company''s growth to satisfy the increasing international demand for quality low-cost cooking ovens, and (ii) further increase Gunkol’s export competitiveness through technology improvements and manufacturing cost reduction. The project will raise the Company’s cooking range manufacturing capacity from 360,000 units at present to about 700,000 units, mostly for exports primarily through the rationalization of production processes and equipment modernization. The investment will also support new product development with new designs and features in response to export market demands and specifications. The project is expected to be completed by end-2002. Development Impact : The proposed project will have a significant direct and indirect development impact on the local economy, especially since Gunkol sources products from over 300 local suppliers, mostly in the Izmir area. While direct additional employment at Gunkol will be limited to about 40 people, the project will generate significant indirect employment for about 200 people at local suppliers who are expected to provide higher local value-added and technical inputs to Gunkol. The gradual transformation of Gunkol into a leading global supplier through newer production and design technologies will help the Company and the local suppliers to become globally competitive through increased quality and efficiency demands of export markets. Gunkol could also serve as a model for other Turkish manufacturing enterprises aiming to become competitive exporters to help the economy. IFC Role : The project gives IFC an opportunity to support a new client in Turkey, which is a growing medium-size, second-tier, export-oriented, family-owned company not associated with any of the large industrial groups in Turkey. Access to long-term financing in Turkey is limited, especially for second-tier companies such as Gunkol. IFC will provide a stable longer-term funding base to the Company so that it can instead focus strategically on enhancing production efficiency and exports. This will directly support the Turkish economy, especially in the current economic climate.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is the Teba Group (“Teba”or the “Sponsor”), a second-tier, family-owned business group based in Izmir largely owned by Mr. Teoman Baygan, the founder and his family members. Gunkol is a profitable white goods manufacturing company of the Teba Group. Gunkol has exported cooking ranges and ovens to over 80 countries since the 1980s and is Turkey’s leading cooking appliances exporter with 85-90% of its revenues in hard currency. Gunkol is owned 44.2% by Mr. Baygan, 29% by Tema A.S., a distribution and marketing company of the Teba Group, 26.5% by Ente A.S., an air-conditioner manufacturing company of the Teba Group and 0.5% by other individuals.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$20 million. IFC has been requested to provide a financing package of US$10 million for its own account comprising an A Loan of US$5.0 million and a C Loan component of US$5.0 million, which will be convertible into equity in Gunkol prior to its planned IPO in a few years.
location_description: The project is located in Izmir, Turkey''s third largest city. Izmir is also the second largest port in Turkey with a free trade area for exports. The city has a developed infrastructure in terms of roads, electricity, water and telecommunications. There is an abundant supply of well-educated manpower, including engineers. Gunkol has two separate plant locations in Izmir. The investment will involve the relocation of the old Menderes plant near Izmir airport to the new facility in Pancar nearby covering an area of 110,000 sq.m. within the premises of an organized industrial zone. Gunkol plans to close the Menderes plant because of its older layout and fully transfer the production to the Pancar plant.
Company Name: GUNKOL GUNES ENERJISI VE KLIMA SANAYI A S

project_description: More specifically, the Project consists of the following investments: Alfa Retail Park – a US$44.6 million redevelopment of a former semiconductor factory into a big-box shopping mall, mainly for home appliances and home improvements retailers. The site is located 8 km from Riga centre on a heavily trafficked Brivibas street. It will comprise about 60,000 m2 of retail space through refurbishment of existing buildings and construction of new premises. Riga Central Railway Station – this US$50.1 million project consists of three parts: renovation of the existing station, development of a new shopping mall/department store building, and a new retail building on the station square. The potential for a parking garage underneath the Railway Station square is also being considered. In addition to having commercial merits, the project is expected to strengthen the public transport infrastructure in Riga by making the railway a more attractive means of transportation and helping to relieve traffic congestion. It is estimated that around 170,000 people pass through the Riga Railway Station every day. Mols Shopping Mall - a US$27.4 million extension of the first modern car-based shopping center in the Baltics. This regional shopping center will improve its competitive position through an addition of 10,000 m2 retail space as well as expansion of parking facilities. IFC’s involvement in the Project is central to the Company’s ability to raise the financing necessary for its expansion as there is limited availability of long-term commercial bank financing in Latvia today. In addition to its own funds, IFC would provide a syndicated B loan and work with local financial institutions to raise financing for expansion of the Company’s traditional retail mall. Before IFC''s involvement, a major Scandinavian commercial bank failed to raise financing for the Company on a project finance basis. This Project fits well with IFC’s strategy as it would contribute to the modernization and restructuring of the retail sector in Latvia, including a large number of local SME’s. With IFC’s support, the Project will demonstrate that longer-term financing is available in Latvia on a project finance basis for non-export oriented projects and, perhaps more importantly, that transparent FDI can be successful despite a difficult business environment. The Project will have strong direct and indirect development impact. It will act as a catalyst for private sector development by: establishing “Retail Parks” where local and international retailers are brought together in a symbiotic environment, which promote exchange of information and know-how, thereby contributing to the growth and efficiency of the private sector; providing much needed retail floor space, which currently is in short supply in Riga; delivering consumer benefits by providing wider choice of higher quality merchandise and service at lower prices to a broad cross-section of the Latvian population; improving transparency and good corporate governance, which contribute to the reduction of the size of the informal, unreported sector of the Latvian economy (currently estimated to represent 30-40% of the overall economy) and improve tax collection; restoring and rehabilitating landmark buildings in downtown Riga, cleaning up the environment around the buildings, creating additional parking space and resolving traffic congestion and public safety issues; and hiring and training of Latvian nationals, and job creation in the SME sector.
sponsor_shareholders: Linstow Varner SIA (the "Company") is a wholly owned subsidiary of Linstow Varner AS (Norway), which is in turn owned 50% by Linstow International AS (Norwegian real estate company), 25% by Varner-Gruppen AS (the largest textile retailer in Norway), and 25% by Hakon Gruppen AS (grocery chain owned by ICA/Royal Ahold). Linstow International in turn is owned by the Anders Wilhelmsen Group which, among others, is one of the largest shareholders in Royal Caribbean Cruise Lines. Linstow Varner SIA owns and operates retail centers in Latvia, including "Mols", "Dole", "Minsk", and "Centrs". As part of the Project, the Company is developing the Riga Central Railway Station as well as an abandoned industrial site in Riga ("Alfa") into modern efficient retail parks. Linstow Varner SIA also holds a 10% ownership stake in Narvesen Baltija SIA that operates kiosks, perfumeries and restaurants in the centers as well as other locations in Latvia. Finally, the Company holds 40% of Securitas Latvia SIA that handles security operations in the malls. Varner Gruppen (through through their retail outlets Derssmann, Cubus and Bik Bok) and Hakon Gruppen (through RIMI) occupy close to 25% of the retail space in the existing centers in addition to outlets outside the Linstow Varner centres. A shareholder agreement between the three Sponsors (Varner, Hakon and Linstow), give Varner and Hakon first right of refusal on competitive terms for retail space in new centers. Conversely, Linstow International AS has a first right of refusal on Hakon and Varner’s 25% stakes in Linstow Varner AS. The paid in share capital of Linstow Varner SIA is LVL13 million (US$ 21.6 million). In addition, the Sponsors have provided subordinated loans for a total of about US$35 million as of year-end 2000. The management team of Linstow Varner SIA is composed of Latvian and Norwegian executives. The aim is to maintain a strong management team in Riga, and to support it by the development and operational experience of Linstow Varner AS in Norway. Furthermore, the Board members have a varied and highly valuable experience within the real estate and retailing sectors. They also have extensive knowledge of the Baltic region, especially Latvia and Riga, gained through their long experience in the region. Mr. Petter Salmonsen is the General Director of the Company. Previously, he was a director in Linstow ASA, responsible for shopping mall development and operations in Norway.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at about US$148 million, including contingencies, as well as an estimated US$15 million and US$11 million of interest during construction on the external debt and subordinated shareholder loans, respectively. IFC has been invited by the Sponsors to be the lead financer. On a preliminary basis, it is proposed that IFC provide a US$12 million A Loan and a US$8 million C Loan for its own account. An additional US$70 million would be raised in the form of a B Loan (US$20 million) and parallel loans for the account of commercial banks and NIB. The remaining would be financed through a combination of cash flow from operations and equity/subordinated loans from the Sponsors.
location_description: During the period 1997-2000, Linstow Varner SIA purchased, renovated and started operation of four modern shopping centres in Riga. The total retail area for these centres is about 29,000 m2. As of year end 2000, the total investment was about US$80 million, nearly all (about US$75 million) of which was financed through equity and subordinated loans from the Sponsors. The Company now plans to expand their retail operations in Riga with an additional 100,000 m2 of retail space. Two new sites have been purchased and one of the existing centers will be expanded. The Project involves the redevelopment of an old and abandoned industrial site ("Alfa Retail Park"), promotion of public/private partnership in renovating and improving the old Riga Central Railway Station, and solving traffic problems that congest the Railway station square, as well as developing further successful western retail concepts (Mols), promoting competition and setting industry standards for retailing in the Baltics.

project_description: The project is a greenfield project which will construct a confectionery factory. As well as providing high-quality confectionary to Tanzania, a significant proportion of output is expected to be exported to neighboring countries. The project has a strong development impact: (a) While Kenya''s competitiveness as the industrial center for East Africa has declined markedly in recent years, that of Tanzania has instead improved significantly. Despite this, inward investment in industrial projects has been limited. The proposed project should help demonstrate the attractiveness of Dar es Salaam as an industrial location; (b) The project is forecast to create 150 jobs; and (c) Generate foreign currency earnings of over $ 2 million per annum within five years, as well as saving forex currently spent on confectionery imports. IFC''s Role is : (a) Long-term lending: in Tanzania there is a dearth of term finance; (b) Catalyst: IFC’s participation in the project is expected to be instrumental in bringing in a domestic financial institution; and (c) Marketing and business development assistance: in particular, the IFC consultant has helped the management of 2000 Industries map out an export strategy and refine their business strategy. Also, the IFC project team has been exploring ways in which the distribution and marketing methods used can have a positive social impact.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are comprised of two groups: the first one comprising the Shah and Patel families who are already involved in confectionery production in the region, and the second the Vora family who have been distributors of fast moving consumer goods in the region for more than 30 years. The two groups will be equal shareholders and know each other well.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at US$ 4,750,000. The proposed IFC investment is a US$ 1,600,000 A loan for IFC''s own account.
location_description: A greenfield site of 1.8 hectares in an industrial area in the northern part of Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. It is about 2 km from the main Bagamoyo road.

sector: Oil and Gas Transport or Pipeline
project_description: Gapco Kenya is an oil company that imports, bulk stores and distributes oil products in the East African countries of Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda and Rwanda. The Company began operation in June 1999 with a focus on penetrating the Kenyan wholesale market. The project is to build a fuel oil terminal and blending unit at the port of Mombasa. The project will enable Gapco Kenya to import larger parcels, store in-house, lower costs, provide tailored products, improve reliability of supply and grow its fuel distribution business. The project will have a strong developmental impact as it supports the expansion of the oil distribution sector and improves the availability of fuel oil in East Africa. All oil is imported in East Africa and the project increases and improves the infrastructure for handling oil products, the lifeblood for any developing economy. The project is a natural backward linkage to the IPPs supported by the World Bank Group in Kenya. Kenya over the past three years faced an acute power deficit due to a lack of investment in power generation and a drought that reduced hydro supply. The WB group has encouraged the Kenyan government to allow independent suppliers to generate power to reduce the deficit. These IPPs all use fuel oil to generate electricity. With the revival of the East African Community and the goal of creating a regional market and trading block, there will be a demonstration effect as Gapco is one of the first local companies that is adopting a regional rather than national strategy. The project will provide Gapco Kenya the infrastructure facilities to compete more effectively with the multinationals, leading to better service and lower fuel costs for consumers. IFC will provide long-term debt financing. Availability of long-term financing denominated in foreign currencies is limited in East Africa. Local banks have limited access to long-term funding and focus on short-term trade finance. IFC’s investment will complete the financial plan. To date capital expenditure has been funded from shareholder funds and internally generated cashflow. IFC''s financing will allow the project to be completed in a timely manner and free up the Company''s working capital to grow the business. IFC has assisted greatly in project structuring and implementation. This is Gapco’s first time to construct a greenfield terminal. IFC’s petrochemical engineer has provided considerable input to the sponsors to the requirements necessary to build the terminal to international safety and environmental standards.
sponsor_shareholders: Gapco Kenya''s entire shareholding is held by a holding company, Gulf Africa Petroleum Corporation (Gapco) of Mauritius. The shareholders of Gapco Mauritius are two brothers, Messrs. Yogesh (44%) and Dhiran(44%) Kotak and Africa Growth Fund (12%). The Kotaks, Tanzanian nationals, are well-established, reputable businessmen. Their main business is importation and marketing of petroleum products in East Africa through local Gapco subsidiaries in Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda and Sudan. Gapco Mauritius also own Tranenergy Kenya Ltd., an oil products road haulage company which is an existing IFC client.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$44 million. The proposed IFC investment is a a US$ 15 million A loan for IFC''s own account.
location_description: The Company is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya. The project site is in Mombasa port on the Kenyan coast. The site is on a 3ha leased greenfield site from the Kenya Ports Authority. The site required some filling and leveling. The site is accessed by both both road and rail. Oil pipelines connect the site to the two oil jetties at Mombasa harbour.

project_description: The project is to establish a new 100-ton per hour (about 640,000 tons p.a. of achievable output) grinding unit to produce ordinary Portland cement for the Ghanaian market. Diamond plans to source clinker, the major input in cement manufacturing, from West African Cement S.A., (Wacem), a Togolese company, which has a production capacity of 200 tons of clinker per hour (1.2 million tons p.a.) and in which IFC invested US$6 million in loan and equity (investment #8962). There is a strong demand for cement and a need for additional production capacity in Ghana. Over the past decade, cement consumption in Ghana has increased at an average rate of 11% p.a. Demand is currently estimated at 2.1 million tons and is expected to reach 2.7 million tons by 2005. Ghacem Ltd., Ghana''s only cement producer, with a total nominal capacity of 340 tons per hour (2.1 million tons p.a.), is already operating at high rates. Diamond is expected to have strong economic effects, including (i) a significant reduction in the price of cement due to competition and the contemplated lower price of its clinker, (ii) an improvement in the quality of the cement sold in Ghana, (iii) the creation of some 280 direct jobs and (iv) the development of regional integration and Ghana''s exports. IFC role includes providing project finance, comfort and technical advice. IFC’s investment is critical, as Ghana’s financial sector is not in a position to provide either the long-term financing the project needs, due to the short-term nature of its resources and its very high rates, or the level of foreign currency it requires. IFC will also provide comfort to the sponsors, a useful asset, given that the overall sub-region is still perceived as risky. Finally, IFC has worked with the sponsors to improve the terms of equipment supply arrangements .
sponsor_shareholders: The project is sponsored by two strong and committed private investors, Messrs. Manubhai Jethabhai Patel and Motaparti Prasad, who own Diamond Cement Ghana Limited (Diamond or the company) on a 50%-50% basis. As part of the contemplated project, they intend to associate a few minority investors to the company''s shareholding. Mr. Patel, a Kenyan of Indian origins, has been in business for more than 30 years. He is a major shareholder of: (i) Eastern Rift Sawmills Ltd. (timber) and Pantel Industries Ltd. (chemicals) in Kenya, (ii) Tema Steel Co. Ltd. (TSC) (re-bars and castings) in Ghana and, (iii) Amexfield Togo Steel Sarl (ATS) (re-bars) and Wacem (clinker and cement production) in Togo. Mr. Prasad, an Indian national, is a major shareholder of Martopearl Alloys Ltd. (alloy steel castings) in India. He also has shares in TSC, ATS and Wacem. In addition, Mr. Prasad oversees the management of ATS, TSC and Wacem. The final Diamond''s shareholding structure will include Messrs. Patel (38.57%) and Prasad (30.0%), Hazelbank Ltd. (17.14%) and IFC (14.29%). Hazelbank Ltd. is an investment vehicle belonging to a close business associate of Mr. Patel based in Kenya.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$15.3 million. The proposed IFC investment includes an equity contribution of US$1.0 million and a loan of US$5.0 million.
location_description: The project will be located at Nkorgbuitame, near Aflao, some 6 km from the main border gate with Togo, in a rural area. The two pieces of land Diamond acquired were not occupied at the time of their long-term leases and they did not support any construction or farming activities. Vegetation mainly consisted of typical savanna grass with shrubs and few small trees here and there.

sector: Glass and Glass Products (Including Glass and Mineral Wool)
project_description: The project entails the installation of a furnace for glass production and three manufacturing lines to produce international-quality beverage bottles. The project is expected to have a positive impact on Russia''s transition to a market economy. Sisecam''s proposed investment is the first large-scale investment in and around Garokhovets since the Soviet era. The venture will complete a plant site whose development was halted approximately ten years ago, when a local enterprise ran out of capital to complete its development. The project is expected to provide over 200 direct jobs to the local workforce and may have as large an impact in terms of indirect employment. Once operational, the facility will add a domestic source of competitively priced, quality beverage containers in the Russian market, which is currently a net importer of glass bottles. Sisecam is a world-class bottle manufacturer and the project''s local management cadre and workers can be expected to benefit from the transfer of best practice in cost and managerial accounting and financial controlling. The IFC investment would support the regional expansion of a project sponsor from one of IFC''s countries of operation into another IFC country of operation where the sponsor has comparative advantages based upon the industry know-how it has developed over the past decades. Sisecam has been an IFC client in Turkey and hopes to benefit from IFC''s project finance experience in Russia. Further, through its involvement in the project, IFC is also directly addressing its goal to mobilize relatively scarce foreign direct investment and know-how into the Russian Federation.
sponsor_shareholders: Anadolu Cam Sanayii, a subsidiary of Türkiye Şişe ve Cam Fabrikaları Group of Turkey (Sisecam), is the project''s sponsor and majority shareholder. The project will be undertaken through a joint venture company, ZAO Ruscam, with a group of regional and local investors. Sisecam is the leading glass producer in Turkey, its home market. It has been in business for more than 65 years and is listed on the stock exchange in Istanbul. Sisecam will provide technical and marketing support to the project.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: Total project cost is estimated at roughly US$25 million equivalent. IFC has been asked to provide a loan of approximately US$12.5 million for the project.
location_description: The project will be located 335 km east of Moscow, in the town of Garokhovets in the Vladimir region of Russia. When completed, the plant is expected to operate a furnace with 275 tons/day capacity and three manufacturing lines to produce up to 250 million bottles per annum.

company_name: CSRC China (Ma'anshan) Chemical Industry Co., Ltd.
project_description: The Project Company is CSRC China Corporation, which acquired the carbon black assets from the Maanshan Golden Star Group (“MGSG”), a wholly owned state-owned enterprise (SOE) of the Maanshan city government. The proposed project is to: i) modernize the existing production lines; ii) expand the carbon black production capacity from 25,000 tpy to 60,000 tp; iii) expand the electrical co-generation capacity from 3.0 MW to 4.5 MW; and iv) improve environmental and safety conditions at the plant. The IFC investment will help transform an inefficient SOE into a sustainable, world-class business that will operate according to sound commercial principles, strong environmental performance and good corporate governance. IFC''s investment will also promote the transfer of advanced technology and managerial know-how from the Sponsor to the local workforce. The Project will demonstrate innovative ways in addressing the issue of redundant workers from MGSG. By working closely with the Maanshan city government, and creating a new specialized service Small & Medium Enterprise (SME), redundant employees will be employed by providing catering, security, packaging and janitorial services to the Company.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is China Synthetic Rubber Corporation (“CSRC”), who wholly owns (100%) of the CSRC China Corporation (“Project Company”) indirectly through its wholly owned subsidiary, CSRC Singapore Limited. Founded in 1973, CSRC is one of the world’s leading carbon black producers and technology providers. CSRC became a listed company in 1986 and its shares are freely traded on the Taiwan, China Stock Exchange.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total Project cost is estimated at US$23.4 million. IFC’s proposed investment is US$ 10 million, consisting of an A loan of up to US$8.0 million and IFC equity of up to US$2.0 million.
location_description: The Project is located in the industrial area of Chihu, a major industrial complex in the northwest section of Maanshan city in the Chinese province of Anhui, about 300 km west of Shanghai. At present, the area of the Project site is approximately 91,090 m2 covering the carbon black production lines, power generation facility, feedstock storage, warehouse and administration buildings As an expansion program, the Project Company will purchase the land use rights for an additional three adjacent lands to the current Project site totaling 44,090 m2 which will cover the two new production lines.
Company Name: CSRC China (Ma'anshan) Chemical Industry Co., Ltd.

project_description: The objective of the Fund is advancing and completing privatization of companies in Africa. IFC Role: IFC''s involvement in the Fund is expected to provide credibility given its successful privatization track record in the continent. IFC''s involvement is expected to act as a catalyst in attracting potential investors and strategic partners (when needed) for the privatized entity. As the main sponsor, IFC''s role in structuring and placing the Fund is also crucial. IFC''s reputation and knowledge of the African markets is expected to play a significant role in giving joint investors the comfort to invest in the Fund. Development Impact: The project has a number of developmental impacts. These include: improving management of privatized companies, promoting local ownership through public listing of shares, promoting capital markets'' development in the region and attracting foreign direct investment by improving investment climate in the region.
sponsor_shareholders: IFC is the primary project sponsor.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The Fund is expected to be capitalized up to US$400 million. Proposed IFC investment is expected to be about 15% of the Fund or 25% (if the Fund closes at US$200 million).
location_description: The project will invest throughout Africa.

company_name: Niger Delta Contractor Revolving Credit Facility
project_description: This project involves the establishment of a US$30 million revolving credit facility by IFC, Shell and a local bank. The facility, details of which are still under discussion, would focus on the oil services sector in Nigeria and would provide competitively priced term funding to small and medium-sized local contractors delivering services to the Shell Petroleum Development Company Joint Venture of Nigeria Limited (SPDC JV), primarily in the Niger Delta. Currently, access to term funding is essentially nonexistent for these contractors. Available credit to these companies is only short-term and very expensive. Local banks lack adequate term finance resources in both Naira and US dollars, and tend to limit their exposure to Niger Delta contractors, because they portray high risks. In addition, interest rates charged to these contractors are usually indexed to the Nigerian Inter-Bank Offered Rate (NIBOR), which is highly volatile. Under these conditions, it is difficult for them to acquire and finance equipment, which in turn prohibits them from competing for larger, higher value-added contracts. One of the major developmental benefits of the project would be its positive effect on the Niger Delta. The facility would help support the growth of targeted local contractors, and, as a result, make a contribution to relieve unemployment and poverty. Funding under the facility would also lead to technology transfer and more skilled training, which would provide longer term development gains and movement up the value chain. This would also enable local contractors to compete more effectively with foreign companies on certain contracts, which are not currently accessible to them. Ultimately the project would establish a strong base of local service companies, which would produce all around benefits, such as lowering the country''s production costs and increasing the benefits of oil production to the economy in general. The proposed facility would be the first of its kind for IFC. IFC is actively involved with Shell in working out the structuring and funding arrangements. The facility will also involve a local bank, which is yet to be identified. By financing one third of the required funding for the facility, IFC will play a catalytic role in mobilizing additional term funding, which is not readily available to small oil services contractors operating in the Niger Delta. The facility would also enable targeted contractors to access less expensive US dollar financing and strengthen their financial condition by reducing their borrowing costs. In parallel, IFC''s SME department and APDF are actively working with SPDC JV to put together an estimated US$210,000 capacity building program to support contractors in developing their business.
sponsor_shareholders: The Niger Delta Contractor Revolving Credit facility (the facility) will be structured and funded by IFC together with Royal Dutch Shell (Shell) and a local bank to be identified.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The maximum total lending for qualifying transactions would be US$30 million at a time. The proposed IFC investment is a US$10 million revolving loan for IFC''s own account.
location_description: The target transactions would be in Nigeria. The facility would offer financing to local contractors providing services primarily in the Niger Delta.
Company Name: Niger Delta Contractor Revolving Credit Facility

company_name: TURKISH PRIVATE EQUITY FUND I L.P.
project_description: The Fund, one of the first of its kind in Turkey, will invest in enterprises looking for expansion capital. It will also seek acquisition opportunities for investment. The Fund is expected to create a diversified portfolio in industries driven by growth, exports, and deregulation. Investing in a private equity fund in Turkey has long been a part of IFC''s financial markets strategy in Turkey, as a necessary complement to the loan funding that IFC has made available through commercial banks. The development impact of this project is particularly pronounced in Turkey where the availability of private equity has historically been limited. Currently Turkey is in the middle of a financial crisis, which has greatly reduced the bank credits available to real sector companies in Turkey. Such an environment increases the importance of private equity funds in the economy. IFC has been active in helping structure the Fund and in guiding the project sponsors. In addition, IFC has introduced TVP to Advent. IFC''s participation on the Advisory Board of the Fund will also provide significant comfort to potential investors, who value IFC''s experience in project finance, emerging market venture capital funds in Turkey, as well as its due diligence discipline.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Turk Venture Partners LLC (TVP), which will be the General Partner as well as the Fund Manager for the Turkish Private Equity Fund (the Fund). TVP is controlled by three Turkish entrepreneurs who are the founders of the Fund. The Fund will be affiliated with the global private equity firm Advent International (Advent), and they will jointly develop and invest in deals in Turkey. Advent will actively participate in the management of the Fund and will exercise a veto right on the investment committee. Advent will also assist TVP with fundraising, structuring of the Fund, and training.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$ 40 million. The project consists of a proposed IFC equity investment of up to US$10 million in the Turkish Private Equity Fund for up to 20% of the Fund.
location_description: The project sponsors will be located in Istanbul, Turkey; investments will be made in Turkey only.
Company Name: TURKISH PRIVATE EQUITY FUND I L.P.

project_description: The project’s goal is to establish the US$100 million Brazilian Corporate Governance Fund. IFC would invest less of US$20 million or 25% of the Fund. A first closing of the fund may occur at US$50 million. The Brazilian Corporate Governance Fund will be a closed-end fund with an expected life of six years. Its objective is to create value for investors by identifying, investing in, and supporting mid-sized Brazilian companies committed to implementing the highest international standards of corporate governance, and which are also undervalued at current stock prices. IFC''s role IFC will send a clear signal of support to the Brazilian authorities and to a broad set of private sector actors who are pushing for changes to the legal and regulatory framework for corporate governance. In addition, IFC has a strong role to play by helping the sponsors structure the Fund. Most importantly, as a vocal proponent of improved corporate governance values in emerging markets, IFC''s presence as an investor in the Fund, and as a member of its investment committee and advisory board, will also be crucial to attract other investors both in Brazil and abroad. Developmental Impact Empirical evidence across countries indicates that more developed and more active capital markets are associated with higher rates of economic growth and that well-balanced financial systems with financial intermediation by both banks and capital markets can also absorb shocks better. Efficient capital markets enhance resource allocation, raise long-term financing for investment, and provide diverse financing opportunities for firms both directly and indirectly, by offering exit vehicles for venture capitalists. Addressing the corporate governance problem in Brazil is essential to develop the country’s capital markets and will depend, among other factors, on enhancing minority rights protection, strengthening the corporate governance of institutional investors, and expanding the structure and enforcement of regulation and supervision. If achieved, these improvements would result in higher firm valuation, lower cost of capital, and less profitable investment opportunities being bypassed.
sponsor_shareholders: The Brazilian Corporate Governance Fund (the Fund) general partner will be Bradesco Templeton Asset Management (BTAM), a Brazilian asset management company. Established in 1998, BTAM is a joint venture between Banco Bradesco (50.1%) and the Franklin Templeton Group (49.9%). BTAM is managing a corporate governance equity fund, Fundo de Valor e Liquidez (FVL) of US$170 million, whose main investors are Banco Bradesco and BNDES, the Brazilian National Development Bank. Banco Bradesco is the largest private-sector bank in Latin America, with assets of US$ 45 billion. It is also the largest private asset manager in Brazil, with over US$22 billion under management. Banco Bradesco has been an IFC client since 1991. Today, IFC''s exposure to Banco Bradesco amounts to US$35 million for two operations. The Franklin Templeton Group is one of the largest global managers of mutual funds, with assets under management in excess of US$227 billion and offices in over 30 countries. Its affiliate Franklin Mutual Advisers is a pioneer of investor activism among mutual funds in the United States.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$100 million, with an IFC investment of up to US$20 million in equity.
location_description: The Fund would be organized as a limited partnership in Delaware, and would have offices in Sao Paolo, Brazil. Investments would be made throughout Brazil.

project_description: The project company is a new company formed to establish and run the proposed project. The new 40 room project will be Chingola''s first graded hotel and will cater for business and other visitors to Chingola, the center of Zambia''s copper mining activity. Currently most visitors to Chingola are staying in guesthouses in Kitwe, more than 70 km away. In addition to accommodation, the hotel will provide conference facilities, shop and office space which will be rented out. The project will have the following developmental impacts: (1) form an essential part of the business infrastructure in the Copperbelt and provide important support for mining sector development in the Copperbelt; (2) create 100 new jobs which will improve the lives of over 1,000 people in and around Chingola. IFC appraised the project and advised the sponsor on critical issues relating to design, marketing, competition, financial structuring, management and environmental issues. IFC will also help complete the financing of the project in a country with very little long term financing.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors and their shareholding in the project are Union Gold Zambia Limited (90%) and Mario Guardigli (10%). Union Hotels Limited (UH) is the project company and is 100% owned by Union Gold Zambia Limited (UG). UG is a holding company for a group of companies with interests in construction, trading, retail, manufacturing and tourism. UG is equally owned by Mark O''Donnell, Peter Frangeskides and Nick Frangeskides. Mr.O''Donnell is an established Zambian businessman with a wide range of business interests in Zambia. He is the chairperson of the Chamber of Commerce and past chairperson of the Zambia Manufacturers Association. Messrs. Peter and Nick Frangeskides are qualified and experienced engineers who own and run a major Lusaka based construction and engineering company. Mr. Guardigli is a career hotelier with extensive experience in the hospitality business. He has held several managerial jobs with hotels in the UK, South Africa and Zambia. He holds a diploma in hotel and catering operations from Westminister College, UK, and is a member of the Hotel, Catering and Institutional Management Association.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at $2,393,000. The proposed IFC investment is a US$957,000 loan for IFC''s own account.
location_description: T he project is located in the town of Chingola in Zambia''s Copperbelt. The site is 3.76 hectares and lies about a kilometre southeast of the town center, adjacent to the Civic Center along Kabundi road which links the mining areas with the main prime residential area. The site is opposite the Chingola Golf Club.

project_description: The proposed project is to revamp a nearly idle and ill-maintained copper processing facility, Sofia Med, and to transform it into a modern, cost efficient plant producing 120,000 tpy of copper and copper alloy products. In December 1999, Halcor acquired the assets of the former Bulgarian copper processor, KOCM, and established a new company, Sofia Med. At the time of the acquisition, KOCM was facing bankruptcy, it had ceased production and its creditors were selling the pledged assets. KOCM was notoriously privatized in 1997. The local owner did not put any money into the plant, nor made any effort to reduce production costs. The plant''s losses continued to accumulate, and in 1999 it stopped production and was put in the hands of the court. Halcor will refurbish the plant, inject necessary capital to restart production, and improve production methods to facilitate the transition to high value added products. The project will be implemented in two stages over a five-year period. The first stage will comprise mainly environmental investments (environmental clean-up of the project site, switching the main energy source from fuel oil to natural gas; replacing oil cooling with water-cooling, etc.), and investments needed to facilitate immediate commencement of the facility''s operations. The second stage will comprise investments in the casting, extrusion, and rolling mills departments, which will allow gradual improvement in capacity utilization. The plant is currently producing small quantities of brass tubes and bars. At project completion, the company will be manufacturing 120,000 tpy of copper and brass products, which will be marketed by Halcor, primarily to existing customers through its various global distribution outlets. IFC Role This project is an example of an established Greek company seeking IFC''s help in pursuing pioneering investments in riskier operating environments. Though Halcor has an established market position globally, this would be its first overseas manufacturing investment. IFC''s presence therefore is vital to mitigate some of the risks that Halcor would face in a different regulatory environment. IFC is playing an important role in : (i) structuring the financial plan; (ii) prioritizing important environmental investments; and (iii) helping to revive and sustain a major productive asset and a key employer in the region. IFC would also help the company obtain adequate long term financing at reasonable terms, which is not otherwise available. IFC also expects to do a possible co-financing with Greek banks, thereby serving as an important catalyst in the transaction. Developmental Impact The proposed project will have a significant developmental impact: (i) Positive environmental impact: This will include switching to energy efficient and environmentally friendly energy sources; implementing significantly better employee health and safety practices, compared to past and present practices in Bulgaria. IFC''s participation and expertise will contribute to the implementation of an investment program which meets all World Bank, EU, and Bulgarian environmental standards. (ii) Demonstration effect: In view of the perceived macroeconomic and political risks involved in investing in Bulgaria, IFC''s participation, along with the proposed co-financing from Greek banks, and presence of Halcor and Union Miniere (important and well reputed players in the field of metal processing and distribution) will have a significant demonstration effect in supporting foreign direct investment in Bulgaria''s manufacturing sector. (iii) Know-how transfer: The project will benefit from the know-how and management expertise of a strong sponsor, who has significant technological know-how in investment and production of copper and copper alloy processing. Also, the sponsor will bring into the project advanced marketing and sales techniques and a proven quality control system. (iv) Improved skills base: An important part of the sponsors'' support will be on job training, which will be provided by Halcor. (v) Increased employment: The project will create new employment in Bulgaria, both directly and indirectly, having an important impact in a period of high unemployment in the country. Currently there are 200 employees in the plant, and Halcor expects to increase direct employment to about 500 people within a six-year period. Additional employment is expected to be generated in the supply stream and in ancillary activities. In addition, temporary employment will be provided to local labor during the construction phase. (vi) Supporting sustainable industries producing higher value added products: The project would help the Bulgarian government support sustainable industries with strong sponsors, producing higher value added products. Over the long term, the project is expected to serve as a model for further private-sector development by: (1) providing a clear example of the application of modern management and corporate governance in Bulgaria; (2) attracting a sponsor with first-class expertise; and (3) promoting the development of a key industry for the Bulgarian economy through a strategic alliance with a well established player in the extremely competitive metal alloy processing industry. World Bank Group strategy The project fits well with the World Bank Group strategy for fostering sustainable economic growth by accelerating structural reform and rapid development of the private sector. IFC supports Bulgaria''s privatization efforts by focusing on financing recently privatized enterprises, and by supporting manufacturing opportunities in various sectors, which have strategic importance for Bulgaria.
sponsor_shareholders: Halcor, the project sponsor and major shareholder (89.8%), is a big Greek manufacturer of copper and copper alloy products with more than 50 years industry experience. Part of the Viohalco Group, a large Greek industrial group, the company employs more than 550 people and has been listed on the Athens Stock Exchange since 1996. Based on the high quality of its products and timely delivery, Halcor has already developed a very reputable name abroad and exports more than 50% of its production. The company has been consistently profitable and is financially strong. Minority shareholders in Sofia Med are: Steelmet (0.2%), which is another company of the Viohalco Group, located in Sofia, Bulgaria. It has two major types of operations i) aluminum profile production, and ii) marketing and sales of Steelmet and Halcor products to the Bulgarian market. Union Miniere Pirdop Copper (UM), a subsidiary of Union Miniere S.A., Belgium , which has recently acquired and currently holds a 10% stake in Sofia Med. UM is an international metals and materials group, with industrial operations in Europe, North America, Asia and Africa. UM is one of the leading copper producers in Europe with total output exceeding 500,000 tpy. In Bulgaria, UM operates a smelter with annual capacity of around 150,000 tpy and refinery with 45,000 tpy. A vast modernization and expansion program is currently being implemented at the Pirdop site. The environmental portion of this program is financed by the Bulgarian government and the World Bank.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at Euro 88.7 million. The proposed IFC investment is Euro 13.5 million A Loan for IFC''s own account.
location_description: The project is located in Sofia, Bulgaria''s capital. The project site occupies about 190,000 sq.m, alongside Gara Iskar, at about 10km from downtown Sofia. The area is predominantly industrial, but not far from some residential buildings.

project_description: Akun is a leading high-quality flour producer in the country. It has two flour mills: one with 60 tons/day capacity and the other one with 150 tons/day capacity. Akun''s superior milling technology and the resulting high quality baking flour has proven to be well received by the local market. The new investment project is to establish a pasta/macaroni plant in the Kyrgyz Republic which will be integrated into the existing and profitable flour/semolina plant. At full capacity, yearly production output is expected to be 19,000 tons per year (60 tons per day) of which 70% will be dry short-cut pasta and 30% long-cut pasta. The project has a strong developmental impact. First of all, it will produce high quality pasta at lower prices, thus reducing the need of imports. The much needed hard currency will therefore remain in the country. Second, about 30 new jobs will be created. Also the increasing use of wheat will allow local farmers to stabilize their operations by having a strong and continuous buyer. Finally, state of the art pasta production technology will be introduced to the country and therefore, over time the skill level of local employees will increase substantially. For the refurbishment of the building and site local constructing firms will be used. IFC has a strong role to play since it will provide long-term lending, which is otherwise almost unavailable. Moreover, IFC will ensure that the project is implemented in an environmentally sound manner. It is anticipated that IFC will arrange technical assistance for the company in areas such as management information systems.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is JSC Stock Company Akun Ltd. (Akun, or the company). The company is owned 40% by Mr. Chinibay Tursunbekov, 40% by Mr. Tarik Pekel, and 20% by Mr. Okeev. Mr. Tursunbekov has been a successful entrepreneur and active investor since the Kyrgyz Republic gained independence. He has worked several years in Ankara/Turkey as advisor on investments in the Kyrgyz Republic. Initially, he successfully operated the first privately-owned bakery in the country. Soon after, he acquired two smaller flour mills and produced better quality flour and, on a smaller scale, pasta. In 1997, he acquired the current two larger flour mills with his Turkish partner. Mr. Pekel is a well-known professor in the agricultural faculty of the University of Ankara/Turkey. He is also a freelance consultant for the food-processing sector. Indirectly he owns the Turkish company Orkimsen in Ankara which manufactures/assembles good quality flour mills. He also has a flour mill in Kazakhstan. Orkimsen was involved in the modernization of Akun''s flour mills. Mr. Okeev was the former ambassador of the Kyrgyz Republic to Turkey. He is currently the head of a cultural association in Bishkek and is not involved in the business operations of Akun.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at around $8.8 million. The proposed IFC investment is about $2.4 million A loan for IFC''s own account (portion of this amount could be an equity investment).
location_description: The project site is located in an urban area in Bishkek, the capital of the country with very good access to transportation routes to all directions in the country.

sector: Computer & Electronic Products(Computers & Peripherals, Communications Equip., Elec. Watches & Similar Elec. Products. Integrated Circuits & the application of Miniturization Technologies characterize this sector.)
project_description: The project is to establish Freecom, a company that will focus on providing information technology (IT) solutions to the lower/middle income, first-time buyer, end of the PC market. The objective will be to make IT solutions affordable and accessible to the larger part of the market that is presently excluded on the basis of price, rapid obsolescence, and difficulty of use. This sector is a cause of global concern as the “digital divide” – the gap between technologically enabled countries and the developing country “have nots” – widens, as technology advances. The company will provide personnel computer solutions, based on refurbished used computers retired from corporates due to incompatibility with the latest software. These refurbished PC’s will be bundled with smart software which offers full functionality to the first-time, home or student user, while requiring less computer resources (memory, processor speed), compared to latest windows based software. The bundle provides an affordable solution to first time buyers that will be backed by after sales support and training, not normally available to buyers of used equipment. Freecom will be based in Cape Town, South Africa, but plans to establish distribution points in all the major centres. Future plans include distribution in neighbouring African countries. IFC has played an advisory role in helping to structure the project. IFC has also played an important catalytic role in facilitating the participation of other financiers, in this case the IDC, which have been encouraged to invest based on IFC interest in the project. Limited long term financing is available in South Africa for start-up ventures of this type. IFC participation is key to completing the financing structure. IFC participation in the project is motivated by the positive impact the project can make on helping to reduce the digital divide by making appropriate and affordable technology available to sectors of the population which currently do not have access to PCs.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are the management team of Freecom which comprises Rob Packham, Sooren Ramdenee and Doctor Esther Lategan. Rob Packham (40), a chartered accountant with extensive experience in financial management of retail companies, will be Managing Director of Freecom. Sooren Ramdenee (40), a fellow of the Chartered Association of Certified Accountants, will be Operations Director. Sooren Ramdenee has 14 years experience in international trading activities of manufacturing and information technology companies. Dr. Esther Lategan (55) will be Corporate Development Director. Dr. Lategan has extensive experience in human resource development, including work as social worker and lecturer at the University of Stellenbosch. Dr. Lategan was Executive Director of NICRO; an organisation established to assist abused women and rehabilitated convicted offenders and their families in the western cape region of South Africa. The proposed shareholding of Freecom is as follows: IDC is the Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa. The Freecom Foundation is a shell company formed to invest in Freecom. Shareholders in the Freecom Foundation include management, NICRO ( National Institute for Crime Prevention and Reintegration of Offenders ) , DEC (Disabled Employees Concern), Liberty Life through the Distance Learning Trust and the Freeplay Foundation, a non-profit philanthropic organisation established to assist in community development projects.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at R10,300,000 million (US$1,329,000 equivalent). The proposed IFC investment comprises an equity investment of R1,100,000 (US$142,000 equivalent), and a C loan (venture loan) of R2,000,000 (US$258,000 equivalent) for IFC''s own account.
location_description: The project will be located in Cape Town, South Africa, and will operate from a unit in an industrial park. Freecom will establish distribution/ training outlets in Cape Town, Johannesburg and Durban.

project_description: The project entails the expansion of an existing motor vehicle repair company in Maputo. The company is presently operating from a rented facility with an area of less than 4,000 square meters in an industrial area in Maputo. It needs to move to a new premises and expand its equipment to comply with Motorcare''s (Nissan South Africa) rigorous quality specifications for a full Nissan service centre. Grand Prix Autobody started in 1998 doing body repair and paintwork on all makes of vehicles, and quickly extended its services to cover full car maintenance. Grand Prix has quickly established itself as one of the leading motor vehicle repair companies in Mozambique with the best quality equipment as well as up-to-date materials used in the industry. Its quality workmanship has guaranteed Grand Prix a preferred status amongst all Mozambican insurers as well as international companies in Mozambique. Grand prix will contribute to develop new standards in the country through on-the job training given to the staff, for free, by Motorcare. All the Nissan cars, new or second hand, will have to pass a safety check before cleared to enter the demanding Mozambican traffic and roads, which will improve safety on the roads. Grand Prix will train and employ a minimum of 20 extra people. IFC’s main role will be to provide appropriate financial resources without which the project cannot proceed. The project requires long term financing which is not available from the local banking system. IFC''s co-lender is providing a 5 year loan so IFC will be helping to extend the maturities. IFC’s participation will also ensure that the facilities comply with environmental requirements. The project will be the largest private car repair center in Maputo. It is likely to have demonstration value and to help develop the local transport infrastructure.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsors are Ms. Valarie Banet (70%), a South African citizen who is resident in Mozambique, and the beneficiary of Mr. Bonaventura Langa Cossa (30%), a Mozambican citizen. Ms. Banet, has been in the motor trade industry since 1985 as a manager of a vehicle repair company approved by VW, BMW, Hyundai, Opel and Nissan. She was an Executive Committee Member of the South African Motor Industry Federation (MIF) as well as of the South African Motor Body Repair Association (SAMBRA). Mr. Boaventure Cossa, was a non executive director. He died very recently and his shares will be taken over by his wife.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$1.1 million. The proposed IFC investment is a US$0.4 million A loan for IFC''s own account.
location_description: The existing site is located at Av. Das FPLM 1884, ten minutes drive from the International Airport in the urban area of Maputo in Mozambique.

project_description: The proposed project consists of - For Apolo:The implementation of a new steel pipe line in replacement of an old one. - For Synteko: The implementation of a new resin plant in Uberaba, and the implementation of a three-year expansion and renovation program of its existing resin, adhesives and floor wax facilities in Araucaria, Parana State and Gravatai Rio Grande de Sul State. The proposed project will not result in resettlement or economic displacement. IFC Role IFC has five important roles to play in this project. First, IFC''s involvement in the project will provide the necessary long-term financing for two medium-sized Brazilian companies (SMEs), which access such investment opportunity for the first time. Following the Brazilian economic crisis, long-term financing has been severely restricted to local companies , particularly for middle-market firms and SMEs. The lack of access to such financing has been a major constraint to the development of the Brazilian private sector, hampering productivity increases, broad-based growth, and a broader distribution of the benefits of growth. Under current conditions, in both international and domestic Brazilian financial markets, only larger firms can access financing, while SMEs, such as Apolo and Synteko, are further delayed the necessary investments that will modernize them and enable to mantain international competitiveness. The only way to obtain financing, for a commercially viable and otherwise efficient mid-sized firm, is through the support of sources such as IFC. Second, IFC would introduce the companies for the first time to international lending practices that would serve as an important step to gain visibility and credibility for access further international credit markets in the future. Third, IFC''s involvement would support environmentally sound and socially conscious practices, with a strong demonstration effect in this important area of corporate responsibilities that is still at a nascent stage in Brazil . Fourth, IFC''s involvement in this project would allow two local companies to improve their efficiency in order to better compete with multinational companies, especially in the consumer cleaning segment. Fifth, IFC investment in this project would contribute to the development of the related industries (MDF, particleboard and natural gas) which are experiencing significant demand and pressure to increase their production capacities. Development Impact This is the type of real sector company which is critical to the success of Brazil''s adjustment program. Only if these mid-size competitive producers invest to modernize and expand, will Brazil''s growth recover. This growth is critical for the benefits of the Plano Real to begin to be felt in Brazil. The assistance provided to Apolo would improve the operating efficiency and competitiveness of a medium-sized company and would allow the increase in natural gas consumption, a cheaper and more environmentally friendly source of energy. IFC support would also help Satipel, another mid-sized IFC project with important development impact (including the substitution of hardwood consumption for the benefit of MDF), receive stable and high quality supply of resin at competitive costs. Finally, the project will contribute to a decline in prices of products which will benefit consumers especially in the low and middle income segment of the population. World Bank Group Strategy The World Bank Group''s assistance strategy for Brazil was considered by the Board in a joint IBRD-IFC CAS on March 30, 2000. The principal objective of the country assistance strategy (CAS) is the achievement of sustainable, private-sector led, broadly shared growth, and the priorities for achievement of such growth include: (i) creation of new employment opportunities in internationally competitive private firms; (ii) broadened finance access to the commercial system, both for starting business (i.e. bank lending, leasing, micro-finance), and for participation in their benefits (i.e. broader share ownership); and (iii) delivery of improvements in areas of basic needs and/or visible impact on standards of living: housing, water, health, education, urban transport. IFC''s strategy, consistent with the CAS framework, has the following primary components: (i) backing companies that will create growth, particularly middle-market firms; (ii) supporting activities which demonstrate tangible benefits of liberalization; (iii) investing in financial and physical infrastructure to improve the prospects for sustained growth. IFC''s financing of the project is consistent with this strategy as IFC''s involvement will help this middle-market companies access term-financing it could not otherwise obtain and without which it could not contribute to the supply response that Brazil needs.
sponsor_shareholders: The companies involved in the proposed project are Apolo Produtos de Aco SA (Apolo) and Synteko Produtos Quimicos SA (Synteko). These two companies are owned by GPC Participacoes SA (GPC) a Brazilian publicly traded company and the Peixoto de Castro family (the family). The family owns 62% of GPC. Apolo is a medium size company involved in the production and distribution of steel pipes essentially for the domestic market. Synteko is a medium size company involved in the manufacturing and distribution of wood surface treating products (floor polishing, vanishing, coating and cleaning products) and the production and distribution of resin products for the wood industry.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total investment cost for the proposed project is estimated at US$70.1 million. IFC will assist Apolo, Synteko and GPC by providing a financial package of US$35 million for its own account consisting of the following elements: (i) an A loan to Apolo of up to US$12 million; an A loan to Synteko of up to US$18 million; and a C loan to GPC of up to US$5 million.
location_description: The Apolo project plant site is located in Lorena, Sao Paulo state. The Syntexo plant is situated in Uberada, Minas Gerais state.

company_name: Ningxia Darong Chemicals And Metallurgy Co., Ltd.
project_description: The project will finance:1) an expansion of the calcium cyanamide production from 50,000 tons per annum(tpa) to 150,000 tpa ; and 2) the environmental upgrades of 3 existing calcium carbide furnaces, in oder to reduce air emissions and to recover waste heat to generate steam needed for the expansion. IFC''s investment will help Darong increase economies of scale and further strengthen its position as a low-cost producer of specialized calcium cyanamide, and its derivative products, in both domestic and International markets. IFC''s investment will: promote local private sector development; improve living strandards in Northwest China; and will help alleviate proverty in this remote and less developed region. Through the increased production of the company, the project will provide employment opportunities at a time when local state-owned enterprises are laying off workers.
sponsor_shareholders: The project sponsor is Darong Chemicals and Metallurgy Company Ltd. (Darong or the company). Located in Shizuishan City, Ningxia Autonomous Region, P.R.C, the company was established in 1993. Privately-held, Darong is the largest producer of calcium cyanamide and the only exporter of granulated calcium cyanamide in China. The company is owned by Hong Kong Sheng Rong investment Company Ltd. ( 25.6%) and by Dawukou Ferroalloys Company ( 74.4%) . Both companies are 100% family-owned.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is US$30 million. The proposed IFC investment will amount to US$18 million, consisting of a US$10 million A Loan for IFC''s own account, and a US$8 million B Loan for the account of participants.
location_description: Darong is headquartered in the Dawukou district of Shizuishan city. A major industrial center of Northwest China, Shizuishan city is located in the autonomous region of Ningxia, at about 70km north of Yinchuan city (the region''s capital). The project will be realized within the 112 acres of the company''s plant site.
Company Name: Ningxia Darong Chemicals And Metallurgy Co., Ltd.

company_name: ALEXANDRIA AUTOMOTIVE CASTING FREE ZONE SAE
project_description: The project is to establish Alexandria Automotive Casting Company, which will manufacture medium-technology automotive castings (brake calipers) to be sold under an off-take agreement to Continental Teves. Upon completion, AAC will have a capacity of 20,000 tons per annum. The proposed project will promote local enterprise in the autoparts sector, an industry in which Egypt has a strategic advantage due to its location close to Europe and comparatively lower production costs. The proposed project would create approximately 35 new jobs. As AAC’s production will be mostly for exports, the proposed project will contribute to foreign currency earnings. It will stimulate transfer of the most advanced production technology, know-how and local staff training by Continental Teves to Egypt. IFC’s role in the proposed project involves: (i) provision of long-term foreign currency financing which is currently not available from local banks; and (ii) encouraging the development of internationally competitive local manufacturers. IFC''s participation in this project would create a demonstration effect for other foreign investors to invest in similar export oriented projects in Egypt.
sponsor_shareholders: The main project sponsor is the Mansour Group (the group), one of the leading diversified business conglomerates in Egypt. The group is active in the automotive, heavy equipment, and distribution sectors. Furthermore, it has established joint ventures with reputable foreign partners in the automotive assembly, fast food, and venture capital sectors. The group owns 21% of the Alexandria Automotive Casting Company (AAC or the company) through Mansour Motor Company (fully owned by the group), the leading distributor of General Motors Vehicles in Egypt. Mansour Group also owns the additional 27.5% of AAC through El Mansou r & El Maghraby Investment & Development Company (51% owned by the group). The remaining percentage of shareholding is owned by: -Sid Ahmed family ( 15.%), which has also equity stake in Amreya Metal Company, the major supplier of brake discs, drums and front suspensions to several local automotive assemblers as well as metal castings to cement manufactures; -Commercial International Investment Company ( 15.5%), one of the leading Egypt’s private equity companies; -Olympic Group ( 10.5%), the leader in white goods manufacturing and distribution in Egypt; and -Mr. Said Ahmed Mohsen ( 10.5%), a reputable Egyptian businessman. The company''s technical partner is Continental Teves, Germany, one of the world’s leading suppliers of quality automotive systems. Continental Teves manufactures components for global automakers while localizing vehicle application and development at its manufacturing plants around the world. It operates 25 facilities including 16 plants, high performance acoustic testing labs and 5 development/technical centers in 19 countries.
total_cost_and_ifc_investment: The total project cost is estimated at US$14.5 million. The proposed IFC investment is an A Loan for IFC''s own account of up to US$5 million.
location_description: The project will be located near the Alexandria Port, close to three newly developed industrial zones (Amreya, Borg El Aran and 6th October City).
Company Name: ALEXANDRIA AUTOMOTIVE CASTING FREE ZONE SAE

project_description: In the late 80s, the sponsor created a dairy which produces pasteurised milk packs from cows, camels and goats. Tivisky is today the first camel dairy in Africa, its whole production (mainly from cows) amounts to about 15,000 l./day. This average level can noticeably vary, firmly depending on the season. As pasteurised milk can not be kept more than a few days, the promoter wants to build a sterilised cow milk production unit. The sterilisation process will use the UHT (Ultra High Temperature) technology and requires a specific investment. Target completion date is December 2001. The total production of the whole dairy will amount to about 40,000 l./day. Tivisky will benefit from the technical and commercial assistance provided by the French major milk company SODIAAL.
